merges.body:
Lands the approved round-11 start evaluation on main. `tools/audit/check_scopes.py --round 11` refused the round-11 finder start because `dev/audit/yardstick/round11/EVALUATION.json` was missing from the tree. The evaluation was written, reviewed (evaluation review round 4 approves 83dc948818) and ruled by the owner, but it existed only on `eval/r11`. This is a `--no-ff` merge of `origin/eval/r11` at c04cef7fca50e00fa23466dab28f941a4d5034af into main, so the review sha the record names stays in the history `check_scopes` reads. One commit on top, 8d2bc61ac1, makes `dev/audit/rounds/round11/evaluation/tally.py` find the repository root with the canonical `repo_root` helper: its `here.parents[5]` resolved one directory above the root, and `tests/harness_headers.py` refuses that depth seam. ed87ef7e6d merges this PR's previous head c5ac4df684, which held the older c6ce415b77 copy, and keeps these two files from 8d2bc61ac1 and the delivery row from c5ac4df684. Apart from that fix, `eval/r11` changes only the nine files under `dev/audit/yardstick/round11/` and `dev/audit/rounds/round11/evaluation/`. Nothing else changes. Every new path is under `dev/audit/`, which `tests/closure.py` lists as INERT (`orphan_files()` is empty at this head), and `dev/audit/config/scopes.json` `_coverage_excluded` already classifies `dev/audit/{rounds,yardstick}/**`. Group R11-START-EVALUATION-LAND.

## Head

`98dd1f9ac2e4887b87a9b434a253ecc9c70be82d` merges the authored code head `1110e4cceadba7974aa8e374af7184696e544006`.

`c0847381f73ec0cdfed571b5df6bc244955bf459` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

ed87ef7e6d5af44eb4f6755c4883bd7bab92438c

## Mutation proof

n/a: a record landing with no code change. Two controls. Removing `EVALUATION.json` brings back the original refusal, shown under Null control. Landing the same nine files as a byte-identical copy without the merge (55148fa033, same tree) leaves the gap `review sha '83dc9488180379b859042b5f24b87d94a5a02c95' is not a commit in the ref's history`, which this merge removes.

## Null control

At origin/main e352724335, `python3 -I tools/audit/check_scopes.py --repo . --ref HEAD --round 11` gives `FAIL start evaluation round=11: 1 gap(s)` (`EVALUATION.json is not in the tree`). At this head it reads the evaluation: the review-sha and graded-objects checks pass, and what remains is 14 accepted cards that are not yet merged. Their own groups build those cards; this PR does not.

## Figures

none

## Red checks

`tests / fast (3.14)` and `tests / nightly-status` at c5ac4df684, the previous head of this PR: `tests/harness_headers.py` FAIL depth seams at `dev/audit/rounds/round11/evaluation/tally.py:13: repo = here.parents[5]`. Fixed at 8d2bc61ac1; `harness_headers.depth_root_seams()` returns `[]` at this head. Cheaper detector: none ran. prepr does not run the gate scripts, `dev/audit/` is INERT, so the scoped gate selected nothing, and `harness_headers.py` runs only in CI as `run_always`. The standing cost of a standalone depth-seam scan in prepr is a few seconds per run. It is not built here.

`tests / closures` at c5ac4df684: INERT READS UNDER-APPROXIMATED, because `tests/harness_headers.py` opens the seven new `dev/audit/rounds/round11/evaluation/*.py` files and its committed `inert_reads` does not list them. That same unlisted read is why the scoped gate never selected `harness_headers.py` for this diff. The closures-autofix job owns this repair (`ci-autofix.md`): it re-records the `inert_reads` and pushes the bot commit to this branch. This seat does not duplicate it. Cheaper detector: prepr ran with PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1, and a full `derive_closures.sh` is refused off Linux (`gate-scoping.md`), so none runs on this host.

## Forward-carry

none

## Friction

none

merges.subject: Merge pull request #3602 from tvofi/fix/r11-outside-honest-starts-runs
merges.title: R11-OUTSIDE-HONEST-STARTS-RUNS: r11 outside honest starts runs
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
**Both stacked bases are on main.** Pull requests #3481 (`f46642080b`) and #3532 (`32c768ae03`) are ancestors of `origin/main` `d7004eaa775d` (2026-11-14T21:33Z, `git merge-base --is-ancestor`), and this head merges that main.

**Ruling c1 is confirmed by the owner**: owner ruling D2 (tvofi, 2026-11-15T08:53:01Z, verbatim choice "Yes, as built (Recommended)"; the group's roster carry 11 on `handoff/audit-r10-roster`). A priced start engages on a modulating install too, as this head builds it, and no code change follows from the ruling. The design note marked it `decision: owner` and "decides nothing" (`a63a2ca6cd`), and the design verdict routed it to the owner unread. This head builds arm 1 (engaged on `cycling_cost > 0` or `clamp_planned_levels`), the one the approved note is written on. The other arm is not one predicate. With `_engaged` reduced to `clamp_planned_levels` and nothing else, both fixtures still move against the merge base (the `c1` figure): `cycling_cost` 44.96 to 46.39 kWh, predicted cost 34.48 to 36.39, space steps under the floor 5 to 8; `everything_on` predicted cost 60.27 to 64.88, steps under the floor 12 to 18, edges 4 to 2. The swing term is deleted for every install, so an unclamped priced solve then descends on the true objective with the start count inside it and ships uncommitted levels, and both claims stay owed at those figures. For no fixture to move, the other arm must also restore the swing term for unclamped installs: two cycling terms alive, the switch weight in two units; not built, not measured.

R11-OUTSIDE-HONEST-STARTS-RUNS, group A of the approved design (`design/R11-OUTSIDE-HONEST-STARTS-RUNS` at `a63a2ca6cd`, the round-3 amendment of `0c692c86d2`; `Design review: approve a63a2ca6cde761f9647573b5cfeab2b02f37655a` at `design-verdict/R11-OUTSIDE-HONEST-STARTS-RUNS` `6e5cc74429`): the build of outside pull request #3529 by @Bankaifan, with thanks. The finding, the start count and the commit program are the contributor's. Their design-note commit `054a866c94` is cherry-picked with its authorship kept (`62701bf993`); their build commit `7eeb7cd676` holds groups A, B and C in one commit and conflicts with main in 11 files (the design's routed decision), so group A is rebuilt on the current tree and credits them in `runs.py`, `optimizer.py`, `docs/how-it-works.md` and here. `docs/architecture.md` lists the module and, with #3598's `running_signal.py`, states 94 modules, 60 free of Home Assistant; the round-4 D6 claims harness prints the same.

What changes:
- **A start is priced as one start.** `runs.py` (new, a leaf) owns the start count of a combined draw, the integer edge count, and the commit of a relaxed plan to an on/off mask. The swing term (`cycling_penalty`, its batch twin), `count_compressor_starts`, `_relaxed_starts`, `_scores_rounded` and the relaxed-levels attribute are deleted.
- **An engaged solve ships runs.** Engaged is `cycling_cost > 0` or `clamp_planned_levels`. It descends on the relaxed objective (no start term, no rounding), then `_commit_runs` scores the projection, the commit masks and the relaxed plan where realizable on the true objective, re-solves the best two inside their own runs, and ships the lowest score. A failure in the stage ships the projection.
- **The switch term is weighed in starts** (`switch_weights_batch(level=)`, `p_max` x the running share) in the true objective, so a boundary's start share plus switch weight never passes one start.
- **The published start count** is the edge count with the solve's running reading, on every install: a compressor that keeps running publishes one start fewer.
- The run and pause minimums move from `supply_hold.py` to the leaf; `early_cutoff.py` and `supply_hold.py` import them.
- **The batched gradient simulates no row for a variable its bounds fix** (design note n6; `_batch_fd_gradient`, `_fd_rows`, `_fd_divide`). The batch is the free variables' rows, behind `x0` when the caller asks the batch for `f(x0)`; with every variable fixed and `f(x0)` supplied no batch is run. No gradient and no plan moves (the `gradient` figure). The note's premise, "a pinned re-solve fixes most of the horizon", does not hold as built: the bounds fix 9 percent of the gradients' variables on the two fixtures that engage and none on the other two, so the rows saved are 9 percent and 0, and no solve-time gain is claimed (the `stress` figure).

Departures from the round-2 note, each raised here and not made silently. Departures 1 and 3 are adopted by the round-3 design verdict (`6e5cc74429`: "adopt, as built" and "adopt, with test 3's clause as the amendment replaces it"), with no build change asked for:
1. **One added descent where a switch has a price.** The note keeps the duty-switch operand in the relaxed descent as R10-DUTY-SWITCH-PLANNER-PRICE built it. Measured on that group's fixture (the `descents` figure), the operand's descent alone ships a plan the true objective scores above the plan of a descent without it in 5 of 12 cells, and the other way in 5: the descent weighs a switch at the combined draw, the true objective in starts. So where a switch has a price (`cycling_cost > 0` and a learned stop) the solve commits both descents and ships the lower (`_relaxed_plans`). It costs one more multi-start on those installs only. With an empty learner the solve descends once and ships the plan of a config that never heard of the pair (null control).
2. **The availability vector is built per committed candidate**, as the note's Shape paragraph says ("built from the profile the pinned re-solve starts from"). This supersedes R10-DUTY-SWITCH-PLANNER-PRICE's "built once per space solve": two of its checks are restated (below). Without it the second descent's plan is scored with lost running time at switches it does not make; the `RESCOPE_OFF` mutant is killed by the cold-day check.
3. **Identity on a realizable plan is the stage's, not the commit program's** (the note's test 3). The program buys the cheapest mask within half a floor step of the plan's energy, so it may run a step at the floor where the plan asked for more. The stage keeps the relaxed plan as a candidate, and is the identity where no start has a price and the projection changes nothing.
4. **`cycling_cost` and `everything_on` are suspended, not removed from the may-drift lists** (note r1 asked for `tests/env_drift.py` and `tests/entities.py` to move too). The tree's mechanism is the suspension note `tools/release/stamp.py` restores (`SUSPEND_HEAD_RE`); the two lists are the runner-conditional allow-lists and stay.
5. **`coord_all_features` is not claimed.** It is byte-identical at this head (a coord capture holds no plan), as the note allowed for.

Design choices a reviewer may read as bugs:
- On a clamped install that prices no start, the plan may hold more starts than before (the `grid` figure: 2 to 5 edges at a lower objective). A start with no price costs nothing; the old objective scored the rounded projection and stalled in its flat band.
- Hot-water levels under the floor still ship on an install that can duty-cycle: they are the planner's, group B of the note.
- `everything_on` ends with one more edge and a higher predicted cost than at the base. Its base plan held 12 space steps under the floor that the old count read as no start at all.
- The whole solve is greedy after the first pass (`_co_optimize`, `_avoid_priced_switches`), so one more relaxed plan can still end higher after those passes: 1 of 12 cells (modulating clamped, cold day, 38.11 against the operand's 38.01).

Restated checks of R10-DUTY-SWITCH-PLANNER-PRICE, each with its reason beside it in `tests/features.py` (note n7 asks that a moved value is reported, not rewritten silently):
- the term's value (`_dsp_term`): the true objective's unit is starts, the relaxed descent's the combined draw;
- "a relaxed start carrying a vector" (item r14): no objective rounds the space level now, the true one projects the tank only;
- acceptance, switch weight: asked in starts of both installs (no more switches) and at the combined draw of the duty-cycle install;
- acceptance, cost: the unpriced plan is held to the bound its own stop leaves it (it was scored with heat that stop does not let it deliver);
- the two vector checks (departure 2);
- the duty-cycle install's day is 2 K colder: on the old day its plan now makes no priced switch;
- `_co_optimize`'s refused candidate is driven from an incumbent that asks for the whole compressor;
- the `duty_switch` surface pin gains `running_now`.

Brief carries, by number:
- Carry 0 (the owner's ruling folding this group into round 10): built in round 10, on this dispatch.
- Carry 1 (from r10-cop-learner-draw-floor: group C's low end is read through `DrawRange._run_asked`, never a second statistic): group C, the metered floor, is not built here and `draw_range.py` is untouched; the carry stands for group C's designer.
- Carry 2 (from r10-start-counter-edges: a coordinator's running class comes from that group's running-signal reader, not from the duty-switch record's tracker, which that build removes): answered in this repair. #3598 reached main first, and this repair's merge of main changes the one read: `duty_switch.running_now` reads `running_signal.running_now(rec.signal)`, with the executing-step fallback for a class that has not settled (the design's note n5) and `solved_running` kept (`## Head`).
- Carry 3 (this body's own line on ruling c1): answered by carry 11. Arm 1 stays built, and the paragraph above states the other arm at its measured figures.
- Carry 4 (groups B and C of the note are in no roster; hot-water levels under the floor still ship on an install that can duty-cycle): stands. Neither group is built here; `dhw_planner.py` and `draw_range.py` are untouched.
- Carry 5 (a clamped install that prices no start can plan more starts; a default start price is a product decision): stands, undecided here. The `grid` figure is unchanged.
- Carry 6, on note n6, which the previous body left unbuilt in its own words ("is not built"): built in this pull request at `15681e4438`; the line on note n6 under `## Forward-carry` holds what it measured.
- Carry 7 (friction: test 5 and the acceptance both assumed a priced solve never scores above the unpriced plan): answered by the round-3 note, which replaces test 5 and adopts the second descent. No build change.
- Carry 8 (friction: an owner decision reaches the fixer with no ruling): stands; the line on ruling c1 under `## Forward-carry` holds it, and the design verdict `6e5cc74429` routes c1 to the owner.
- Carry 9 (friction: the note asks that restated checks are reported, not rewritten silently): stands as reported. The restated checks are listed above; round 4 restates two more acceptance clauses, under their own heading below.
- Carry 10 (carry 1's text again, group C's low end read through `DrawRange._run_asked`, never a second statistic): answered at carry 1; `draw_range.py` is untouched.
- Carry 11 (Owner ruling D2 (tvofi, 2026-11-15T08:53:01Z, verbatim choice "Yes, as built (Recommended)"): ruling c1 is confirmed), applied in this body edit: the paragraph at the top and the line on ruling c1 under `## Forward-carry` state the ruling and its date in place of `pending owner confirmation`. No code changes. This repair's dispatch, rendered before the ruling, says the c1 text is not to be changed; the roster carry is the newer of the two and asks for exactly this replacement, so it is followed.
- Carry 12 (owner ruling Q2 on carry 5: measure candidate default start prices for a clamped install, then build the default at the value tvofi picks): the roster marks it moved to R11-OUTSIDE-HONEST-STARTS-RUNS-P3; not built here, and carry 5's line above stands.
- Carry 13 (the running class for a coordinator is `running_signal.running_now(running_signal.signal_for(coord))`, not the duty-switch record's tracker; `None` keeps the executing-step fallback): built in this repair's merge of main. `duty_switch.running_now` reads `running_signal.running_now(rec.signal)`, and `record_for` builds the record with `signal=running_signal.signal_for(coord)`, so it is that read; a `None` reading falls back to the executing step's planned draw (`## Head`; `SETTLED_CLASS` under `## Mutation proof`).

## Departure from the note's test 6, and the switch-weight clause

Ruled (A) on the round-3 question by the round-11 orchestrator under tvofi's mandate 6893738184 (scope all), recorded for tvofi: two clauses are restated by `tests/README.md`'s kernel rule ("A knife-edge optimizer comparison must be measured across BLAS kernels"), keyed on a same-run quantity. (B), production holding the clauses as written, is refused: it ships the plan the true objective scores higher. The restatement changes no production line; the merge with main changes one (`## Head`).

- **The note's test 6, energy half.** Was: "its energy is within one floor step of the relaxed plan it was committed from". Now: the shipped plan scores no higher on its own objective than the projection of the relaxed plan it was committed from (`_hsr_scores`, both in one solve). The energy difference is printed in the check's detail and asserted nowhere. Rule: no line of the stage holds energy to one floor step; a balance outside its band is penalised and never refused (`runs.commit`'s `fine * outside`), and the best two candidates' levels are re-solved inside their runs. The band itself is now pinned at the leaf, where no solve and so no BLAS kernel enters: `a balance outside its band is paid for at every step: ...` (the group's block).
- **R10-DUTY-SWITCH-PLANNER-PRICE's acceptance, modulating clamped install.** Was: the priced plan's switch weight in starts no higher than the unpriced plan's. Now: on both installs every candidate stage of the priced solve returns a plan scoring no higher under the priced objective of the scope it ships in than the projection of the relaxed plan it was handed, strictly lower in at least one call, and the plan that publishes is one a stage returned at that score (`_dsp_stage_scores`). Rule: the old order raced two independent multi-start descents and nothing in the stage holds it. The duty-cycle install keeps both its clauses (no higher weight in starts; a lower one at the combined draw).
- Kept as they stood: no step between the running rule and the floor; priced starts no higher than the unpriced plan's by the same count; the duty-cycle weights; the shipped plan no higher than the old plan under the priced objective.

The measurement, same tree (`f19c16156d`; `99685444a9` read the same), the kernel the only perturbation (`kernels` figure): on SkylakeX the 1.1 kW cell ships one run at 8.0828 on the true objective, -0.4817 kWh against its relaxed plan (one floor step is 0.2750); on Haswell it ships two runs at 8.1664, -0.0500 kWh. Sandybridge and Nehalem read as SkylakeX at 1.1 kW (-0.4815, -0.4816). On the modulating clamped install, SkylakeX's unpriced solve ships 1 switch in starts and the priced solve 2, at 26.9371 against 27.0180 for the unpriced plan under the priced objective, the switches' price included; Haswell 2 / 2, Sandybridge and Nehalem 1 / 1. Credit for the finding, the start count and the commit program stays @Bankaifan's.

## Head

`fbf6e980ce44a6069c2e055ea035531b5b819220` merges main `e352724` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`bca2e138252ed1176e517aca6f3bcb47588cd2af` merges the authored code head `8adb5c5b5f3452daf0772fc54135e514ab224ec4`.

Code head `8adb5c5b5f3452daf0772fc54135e514ab224ec4`. This repair sits on `1c3417a151` (`mutation-autofix`'s merge of `origin/main` `b94425b94f` into the previous head `67e6e16e1e`), first parent:

R11-PRE-HANDOFF-BOOKKEEPING part 1 of 4 (owner ruling 2026-11-13 on card P10): roster carries 0-4. Carries 5-20 are later parts, dispatched at this handoff, and none is answered here.

- **Carries 0 and 1 (the predictor owes the roster fetch).** `pr-contract` fetches `+refs/heads/handoff/audit-r*-roster:refs/remotes/origin/handoff/audit-r*-roster` before `carry_audit.py check`. `ci_predict.py` read whatever remote-tracking ref the seat's checkout last fetched. The tree clone's `fetch_round_rosters` copies that ref from the checkout, so it was just as stale. As a result, a carry to a group the round roster gained since that fetch was predicted `CARRY BAD ... is not a group of the roster`, though CI routes it. `predict` now runs `refresh_round_rosters(root)` whenever it is given a body. That is CI's fetch, into the checkout, so the carry arm and the graders arm's clone both read origin's roster. An unreachable origin leaves the refs alone and adds the note `ROSTER UNFETCHED: ...`.
- **Carry 2 (step replay keyed on what a step reads).** `step_replay_preds` replayed only the `instrument-self-tests` steps whose run text named a changed file, or named a tool whose text names it. It now also replays every step whose recorded closure in `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` holds a changed path under `files` (`recorded_readers`). That is the enumerator the carry names. It is read through `selftest_scope.py`'s own `job_steps` and `covers`, so a `D/**` entry counts. The carry's instance (`queue_pre_flight.py --self-test` over `merge_train.py` at `23b943c987`) is already predicted by main's predictor through the one-level text rule (`## Figures`). What this part adds is the readers the text rule misses (counts in `## Figures`).
- **Carry 3 (the post-push `update-ref` in `write_roster`).** No arm can fail without it, so it is removed, as the carry directs for that case. The callers that reach `write_roster` are `roster_edit.main`, `roster_queue.py`'s batch and `roster_sync.sync`. Each runs `fetch_origin` (`+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`) first, which moves `origin/<branch>` to this run's own last push before the next op's `prepare_worktree`. A lost race re-fetches as well. The planted-defect audit's mutant (the line deleted) left the self-test green. With the line removed, the existing row `P409: two ops in one run both land after our own push` still passes, because the per-op fetch is what lands the second op.
- **Carry 4 (the queue-then-sync duplicate).** `already_carried` compared whole normalised texts. The queue's landing is `From <src>, body item <id>: <text> (items <id>)` and the sync's derived text is `<text> Carry: <G>`, so the two never matched. It now compares `finding_core`: `finding_words` with the queue's prefix, its `(items ...)` tag and a trailing `Carry: <G>` clause stripped. It also matches a carry tagged with the body item's own `carry_audit` id, which `carry_plan` passes. The existing duplicates on the roster are roster data for the orchestrator, not this carry.

Alternatives not taken, and why each lost:
- Carry 0: fetching inside the tree clone straight from the checkout's origin URL. The carry arm itself runs in the checkout (`carry_preds(root, ...)`), so it would still read the stale ref; one fetch into the checkout serves both readers.
- Carry 2: running `selftest_scope.select` (the prelude's selection). On a gate-file diff it returns FULL, every step, which is a replay of all 120 steps rather than the readers of the changed paths.
- Carry 3: a self-test arm with `_on_origin`'s fetch disabled. `main` fetches every head before `write_roster`, so such an arm stays green with or without the line; it would pin nothing.

## Head

`4f3aa7edb38f9818e7ddb5ce2d411c67a35fe8db` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`047ea3fddfdf4e90227010b4dacc2d38ec0b9f0a`, cut from `origin/main` `6d55bf6fd1cd3dd0677d98f6c2da33d259b35b18` (the merge base). It is `275faa2a43` plus one commit answering `prepr.sh`'s 17 survivors and its own self-test row (below). Figures were taken 2026-11-16 06:20Z to 08:40Z. Those the last commit touches are re-taken at this head: the two self-tests it edits, the carry-0 run and its mutants. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` against `origin/main` `f1520e3539` reports no conflict.

One more change, outside the carries. `prepr.sh`'s own self-test failed one row whenever a fixer ran it with `MUTANT_IN_PLACE=1`, as `fixer.md` step 2 directs: `a check needing a git checkout measures nothing in the archive copy, and is refused (got 0, wanted 1)`. The archive-copy rows inherited the caller's variable and ran in place. Those three `mutants_line` calls now clear it (`MUTANT_IN_PLACE= mutants_line ...`).

## Mutation proof

Each mutant was applied in its own worktree at the head (`perl -0pi`), and the named self-test was run there. Failing rows:

- `mut:roundfetch` (`predict`'s `refresh_round_rosters` call deleted, at `275faa2a43`): FAIL `predict calls refresh_round_rosters on one `# mut:roundfetch` line`. At this head that pin is a behavioural row instead. `predict` is called with a body and without one, with the refresh stubbed. Its `if body:` made false, or its note append made false: FAIL `predict with a body refreshes the round rosters and notes a failed refresh`.
- `refresh_round_rosters` returning `None` before its fetch (at `275faa2a43`): FAIL `refresh_round_rosters moves it to origin's branch and returns no note`, and FAIL on the unreachable-origin row. At this head, its one `return` reduced to `return None`, or git's reason dropped from the note: FAIL `an unreachable origin leaves the ref, raises nothing and notes ROSTER UNFETCHED with git's reason (null control)`.

- `mut:dupkey`, in place, `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_sync.py --self-test`:
  - the base's key restored (`finding_words(c) == finding_words(text)`): `98 checks, 2 failed`. The failing rows are `the queue's landing of the same item is not appended again: ...` and `a reworded queue landing tagged with the item's own id is not appended again`. This is the failing test first.

Carry: R9-QID"])`. The row now compares the carry whole, where it compared only a length at `275faa2a43`, which `prepr.sh` reported as the survivor `roster_sync.py:1149`.

- `tools/pr/ci_predict.py:916 CONST_SWAP` (the fetch timeout 60 to 61): an equivalent bound. A value check: the timeout path is `timed out` in the one `return`.
- `tools/pr/ci_predict.py:918 RETURN_DEL` and `:923 RETURN_DEL`: those returns no longer exist. `refresh_round_rosters` has one `return`, killed as above.
- `tools/pr/ci_predict.py:921 CONST_SWAP` (the stderr line index): the index no longer exists. The note quotes the whole stderr, and dropping it is killed.
- `tools/pr/ci_predict.py:558 CONST_SWAP`, `:562 CALL_DEL`, `:562 CONST_SWAP`: the `sys.path` insert position and its `pop` in `recorded_readers`. These are equivalent: `selftest_scope` imports the same either way. A value check.
- `tools/pr/ci_predict.py:565 GUARD_OFF` and `:566 RETURN_DEL`: killed at this head by the no-table row.
- `tools/pr/ci_predict.py:1242 GUARD_OFF`, `:1244 GUARD_OFF`, `:1245 CALL_DEL`: killed at this head by the `predict` with and without a body rows.
- `tools/pr/ci_predict.py:1762 CALL_DEL` and `:1762 CONST_SWAP`: the `sys.path` setup of `roundfetch_self_test`, the self-test's own scaffolding, not a production site.
- `tools/audit/seat/roster_sync.py:1149 STMT_DEL`: killed at this head, as above.

## Null control

- Carry 0: an unreachable origin leaves the stale ref, raises nothing and returns the note (self-test row above). A body-less `predict` runs no fetch: the call sits under `if body:`.
- Carry 2: a closure entry that does not hold the changed path replays nothing (`null control: a closure not holding the changed file is not replayed`). The three existing null rows of `step_replay_self_test` still pass.
- Carry 4: a distinct item for the same group still appends. `R9-QUEUED` ends with `a distinct finding for the queued group. Carry: R9-QUEUED` beside the queued landing. The existing B1 rows (`R9-FROM-2`, `R9-FROM-3`, `R9-PROSE`) still append.

## Figures

- Carry 0, end to end on this checkout. `git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster f20f8b13a797c309719ddb00a853748697f1814f` sets the ref to a roster commit older than the group `R11-OUTSIDE-SELF-SETTING-PUMP`. Then `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/pr/<copy>.py --base origin/main --body <body: one item, Carry: R11-OUTSIDE-SELF-SETTING-PUMP> --only orphans`:

merges.body:
R11-PRE-ROUND-METRICS, part 2 of the group (topic r11-pre-round-metrics-p2): the convergence record of process cards P7 and L1 and decision 0018 sections 2 and 4, built once, with its enumerator `tools/audit/seat/loop_ledger.py`.

Seven roster fields, written only through `roster_edit.py set-field` and refused outside `roster_lib.convergence_why`'s vocabulary: `found_by` (a finder dimension `D<n>`, `reviewer`, `ci-main`, `owner`, `outside`), `owned_by` (`D<n>` or `none`), `caused_by` (`{cause, rca}`: a pull request `#<n>`, another roster group, `external` or `original`, with `rca` a root-cause record of the group under `dev/audit/rca/`: `roster_lib.rca_lists`), `family` (a class of `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`), `cm_kind` (card L1's six words), `parent` and `follows` (other roster groups). `loop_ledger.py` reads them from every `wave-r<N>-groups.json` at the reader ref and prints, per round (each roster) and per ISO week of roster entry (`git blame` of the group's `"group":` line, the first roster holding it), `escapes` by found_by and by owned_by, `injected`, `refix` (a re-report naming the fix it follows) and `loop` (countermeasures by family and cm_kind, k children per countermeasure, groups per generation and each generation's ratio). Which group owes which field is `owed()`: an escape (scorecard line E's two sets, `scorecard.escape_sets`, which `loop_ledger` imports: one definition) owes found_by, owned_by and caused_by; any other hotfix group found_by and caused_by (card P7); a group with an `rca` record caused_by, family and cm_kind (card L1). A read whose owing groups are not all recorded prints `unread (k of n ...)` with the names, never a partial value (0018's NO-READ rule for a partial ledger). `scorecard.py`'s line E gains the owning-dimension split through `loop_ledger.owned_split`, imported inside `scorecard.owned_split` so the scorecard's mutant copies, which run without their siblings, still load (card P7's "the scorecard splits escapes by owning dimension per round": the scorecard's roster is the round's). The enumerator is code-owned in `.github/CODEOWNERS` (carry 0's rule, carried to this part by its text), self-tested in `instrument-self-tests` (step `loop-ledger`), and documented in `tools/audit/seat/instruments/loop_ledger.py.md`.

**`caused_by` is writable on a group with no `rca` of its own, and only on a group a record declares its subject (verdict/3657's two blocks).** `rca_lists(rca, group)` admits the record `dev/audit/rca/<rca>.md` when the file exists, the id is a file stem, and either the id is one of the group's own `rca` list (the group is that record's countermeasure) or the group's name is one of `rca_subjects(text)`: the tokens (`[\w.-]+` runs, trailing dots and dashes stripped) of the record's opening block, which is its first paragraph and, when that is a one-line `# ` title, the paragraph after it, with table rows dropped. That block is where a record states what it analyses ("This is the root-cause seat for R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED", "beside R10-HOTFIX-ROSTER-DRAIN-REPLAY", "The fix is R10-HOTFIX-GATE-STALE-JOBS's", a title's "(R9-EG-B0)"); a group named later is a sibling, a countermeasure or a dispatch-status row. `R10-RCA-TICK-BLIND`, whose opening block names no group and whose status tables name `R10-COMBI-TANK`, `R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE` and `R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE-PERSISTENT`, now admits none of them, so their `injected` stays `unread` until a root-cause seat writes a record about them (0018's NO-READ). Decision 0018's `injected` row requires "the cause recorded by the root-cause seat, which is not the fixer", so the fixer still cannot name a cause no root-cause record carries.

The repair's alternatives (the verdict's options), and why each lost: the "This is the root-cause seat for <group>" sentence as a parsed field is in 32 of the 128 records (`re.search(r"root-cause\s+seat\s+for\s", text, re.I)` over `dev/audit/rca/*.md`), and at the reader ref drops records whose opening says "beside <group>" or "The fix is <group>'s" (`R10-HOTFIX-ROSTER-DRAIN-REPLAY`, `R10-HOTFIX-RESTORE-BASE-SKEW`, `R10-HOTFIX-GATE-STALE-JOBS`, `R10-HOTFIX-FEATURES-WEEKEND-CLOCK`, `R9-EG-B0`), each a record written about that group; a front-matter field is held by no record today (no `dev/audit/rca/*.md` opens with `---`), so it would admit nothing until 128 records were edited, which is the root-cause seat's text and not this group's; requiring the `cause` in the same record does not separate subject from mention, because a cause is a pull request or a group and a process record names many (`R10-RCA-TICK-BLIND` has 31 lines naming a `#<n>`). The opening block admits every one of those five and refuses every status-row, sibling and countermeasure mention the probe in `## Figures` lists. Alternatives the verdict listed, and why each lost: an `rca` arm on `set-field` would make the defect group a countermeasure, since `owed` and the `loop` read take every group with an `rca` as one, so an escape gaining an RCA would also owe family and cm_kind and count in `loop`; narrowing `owed` leaves every escape owing `caused_by` (an escape reached a release, `defect-root-cause.md`'s first trigger), so it alone opens none of the 60 escapes of rounds 10 and 11, and narrowing it further changes card P7's "every hotfix group and every outside group records what caused the defect", a policy text. Round 9's rosters hold `rca` as a bool on 88 groups; `rca_lists` reads own ids only from a list (`rca in True` raised `TypeError`).

Also fixed, in a file this diff touches: `roster_lib._replan_production` joined `tools/plan/replan.py` onto `Path(__file__).parents[2]`, which is the `tools/` directory itself, so the file it loaded never existed, it always failed and returned False, and `group_class` never answered `production` for a group without a `class` (ci_priority's tier 1 reads it). Its self-test check accepted either answer. It now loads the repository's `tools/plan/replan.py`, and the check pins `production` for a lane-less group and `instrument` for one owning only `tools/` files.

Carry 5: built: found-by and owning dimension per escape (`none` a value), the cause named through the root-cause seat's record, and the re-report naming the fix it follows (`follows`, read as `refix`); the per-step denominator and the examining pass over a late merge are cards C1 and C2. Carry 6 is carry 5's text without its source line and is folded into carry 5. Carry 7: built as cards C3 to C5 qualify (the four fields, the closed vocabularies, the per-round and per-week enumerator). Carry 8: built (found_by and caused_by settable on every hotfix and outside group, caused_by once a root-cause record declares the group its subject; the scorecard's E split by owning dimension per round), with the convergence record of carry 5, as one mechanism. Carry 0, Carry 1, Carry 2, Carry 3 and Carry 4 belong to the group's other parts and are not answered here (carry 0's code-owner rule is applied to `loop_ledger.py` above). Carry: dismissed: built in this pull request, cards C1 to C6 below

## Cards

Definitions this part cannot meet as written, returned rather than bent:

- **C1 the per-step denominator has no record to read.** Carry 5 owes "the per-step denominator with an off-cadence dimension reading 0". No tracked record holds a finder step's examined count and universe (`git grep -n -i "denominator\|universe" -- .claude/skills/audit-find dev/governance/roles/COMMON.md dev/audit/README.md` returns only `dev/audit/README.md`'s line naming R11-INTAKE-R10-RESIDUE as the owner of the denominator rule). The read needs the finder's report to carry the step's universe command and examined count first; the ledger then reads it. Owner or orchestrator choice: keep that with R11-INTAKE-R10-RESIDUE's brief rewrite, or define the step record here in a later part.
- **C2 the examining pass over a late merge** is `unexamined`'s read (0018 section 2), which 0018 assigns to R11-PRE-ROUND-METRICS from the roster's group kinds; no record says which finder pass examined which merge, so it is not built here.
- **C3 the fields sit on the roster group, not on the RCA record and the triage ACCEPT.** Card L1 puts `caused_by`, `family` and `cm_kind` on an RCA record and a triage ACCEPT. Both become a roster group (an RCA's countermeasure group lists it in `rca`; an ACCEPT is landed by `append-group`), and the group is where the scorecard, the planner and this ledger already read; a second copy in Markdown would be a parallel record. `caused_by` is tied to the RCA by requiring its `rca` id to be a record that is the group's own or declares it its subject. If the owner wants the fields on the RCA file itself, the ledger reads them through that link.
- **C4 `family` is a bug class.** Card L1 names "the symptom family" with a closed vocabulary but no list; the only tracked closed list of defect families is `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`, so `family` is one of its keys. A family that is no class needs a class first.
- **C5 the prototype was not re-measured.** Card L1 cites the prototype under `$HPO_STATE_DIR/s14/seat/loop-study-1114/data/`; that variable is unset in this container and the scripts are not in the tree, so no prototype figure is reproduced. At the head no roster group carries a convergence field (`## Figures`), so every read with an owing group prints `unread`. The figures exist once the orchestrator sets the fields, and `caused_by` on a group with no `rca` of its own needs a root-cause record declaring it its subject first: at the head such a record exists for 2 of round 10's 48 escapes and for none of round 11's 12 (`## Figures`), so `injected` for those rounds waits on the root-cause seat, which is decision 0018's own NO-READ for an unrecorded cause.
- **C6 the reviewer's `caused_by` check and the fixer rule are policy.** Card L1's mitigation ("the fix reviewer checks `caused_by`") and the audit's row a6 (`fixer.md`) change role contracts; they need the owner's approval and are not drafted here. Until then `set-field`'s refusal of a `caused_by` whose `rca` is no root-cause record of the group is the only check.

## Head

## Block

`loop_ledger.owed` says every escape owes `caused_by`, and so does every other hotfix group (card P7: "every hotfix group and every outside group records what caused the defect"). `roster_lib.convergence_why` admits `caused_by` only when its `rca` id is already in the group's own `rca` list (`roster_lib.py`, the `if rca not in (group.get("rca") or [])` arm). `roster_edit.py` has no op that adds an `rca` entry to an existing group. Only `append-group` writes `rca`, and `set-field` refuses `rca`, because it is not in `SET_FIELDS`. Hand-splicing the roster is ruled out. So for a group that has no `rca`, the only sanctioned writer refuses `caused_by` permanently. The PR's own self-test pins exactly that refusal (`set-field caused_by is refused without the group's own rca record`, on R9-S3).

Measured on the real record at the reader ref, `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster` (`ev/norca.py`, `ev/norca.txt`):
- round 10: 112 of the 123 groups that owe `caused_by` have no `rca`, and so do all 48 of its 48 escapes;
- round 11: 14 of 17 owing groups have none, and so do all 12 of its 12 escapes.

So `injected`, which every escape's `caused_by` decides, and `refix`, which needs the whole ledger, can never print a value for round 10 or round 11. The same holds for every ISO week that contains one of those groups. These two reads are half of what the ledger is built to print. That contradicts two statements in the body: "Carry 8: built (found_by and caused_by on every hotfix and outside group)", and C5's "the figures exist once the orchestrator sets the fields". The orchestrator cannot set these fields. The ledger stays honest: it prints `unread` and never a wrong value. But the mechanism cannot be completed on the record it exists to read.

The fixer chooses the repair. Options include: a sanctioned way to attach a group's RCA record (an `rca` set-field arm, validated against `dev/audit/rca/`); admitting a `caused_by` whose `rca` names any root-cause record that lists the group; or narrowing `owed` so a group the root-cause rule does not reach (`defect-root-cause.md`'s two triggers) does not owe `caused_by`. Whichever is chosen, the repair needs a check showing `caused_by` written on a group that started with no `rca`.

## Block

The previous block (`caused-by-unwritable`) is resolved in mechanism: `roster_lib.rca_lists` admits `caused_by` on a group with no `rca` of its own, and `roster_edit`'s new check writes `caused_by` on such a group, `R9-ESC`, then shows `injected` and `refix` turn from `unread` to values. But the predicate that does it is wider than the invariant it guards. The docstring says a record that names the group is one where "the group is the defect it analyses", and the body says "a record under `dev/audit/rca/` naming the group is that seat's record". The code only checks that the group's name appears somewhere in the file as a whole token.

On the real record this admits records that do not analyse the defect. `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-TICK-BLIND.md` is a process RCA about why the tick board did not prevent dispatch stalls. It names `R10-COMBI-TANK`, `R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE`, `R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE-PERSISTENT` and `R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED` only as dispatch-status table rows and board lines. At this head, `convergence_why("caused_by", {"cause": "original", "rca": "R10-RCA-TICK-BLIND"}, <R10-COMBI-TANK>, names)` returns `None`, and so does the same call for `R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE` (`ev/overbroad.txt`). So `set-field` accepts a cause for those defects that rests on a record never written about them. `injected` then prints a value where 0018's rule ("the cause recorded by the root-cause seat") says it should print NO-READ. This breaks the property the first review credited the ledger with: it prints `unread`, never a wrong value.

Scale (`ev/admissions.txt`): of the 5 round-10 escapes that the body's figure counts as admitted (`round 10 48 5 0`), 3 are admitted only through `R10-RCA-TICK-BLIND`'s status rows: `R10-COMBI-TANK`, `R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE` and `R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE-PERSISTENT`. Only 2 are admitted by a record that says it is the root-cause seat for that group: `R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED` by `R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED`, and `R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK` by `R10-RCA-SETPOINT-LATCH-DEADLOCK`. The body's `5` and `27` therefore overstate where `caused_by` can honestly be written.

The self-test does not reach this domain. Its planted record `R10-RCA-NAMED` ("Cause of R10-D, found again in R10-E-2.") admits both groups it mentions, and no case plants a record that mentions a group without analysing it.

The fixer chooses the repair. Options include:
- a declared subject in the record, such as a front-matter line or the existing "This is the root-cause seat for <group>" sentence, made a parsed field, and admit only the groups it lists;
- requiring the `cause` to be stated in the same record;
- confining the token match to a heading or subject block.

- **(b) The ask judgement reads the level.** `draw_range.ask_evidence`, the one place the draw-floor design makes the judgement, returns `ASK_FOLLOWS` only where the slope of log drawn on log asked is at least `FOLLOW_SLOPE_MIN` **and** the fitted ratio of drawn to asked at the asks' 90th percentile and at their 10th are within `DISAGREE_FACTOR` of each other: `(high / low) ** abs(1 - slope) <= DISAGREE_FACTOR`, from the percentiles and slope the function already computed. ### (b) Why the level is read across the span, not as one figure

A bound on the whole window's level (drawn summed over asked within some factor of 1) was refused: the COP learner reads a departure as an efficiency shift on `ASK_FOLLOWS`, and a pump whose true COP scale is 0.6 draws 1/0.6 = 1.67 x every ask, a level the owner's 1.70 cannot be told from. `cop_duty_floor.py`'s `true_0.6` row is that install and learns the same scale at both ends of this diff (`## Figures`); a whole-window level bound would refuse it every interval (`COP_REFUSED_OFF_ASK`) and its scale would never learn. What separates the two is that an efficiency shift is one ratio at every ask and the owner's draw is not: on the synthetic shape the fitted draw is 2.1 x the ask at the span's low end and 1.4 x at its top.

Downstream, the verdict has three readers (`git grep -n -e ask_evidence -e follows_ask -- custom_components` returns only `draw_range.py` and `accuracy.py`): `MeasuredCop.judge_ratio` (on `ASK_IGNORED` every interval reads `COP_REFUSED_OFF_ASK`), `MeasuredCop.release` (held departures are dropped, not folded), and `accuracy.diagnostics_view` (`draw_follows_ask` False). `judge_ratio` runs only where no heat reading exists (`heat_kw is None` in `_fold_measured_cop`). No solve, optimizer or arbiter path reads the verdict, so no cost figure moves at a fixed learned state, flat price or not; the verdict reaches cost only through which intervals train `cop_scale` on an install with no heat reading.

### (a) Why the ceiling store holds 0 samples

`draw_range.fold` sends an interval to the ceiling store only when all of: `is_running_space`, `experiment_s` not `None` (the interval's own action ran the system-identification experiment), and `DrawRange.takes_ceiling`. Every other interval goes to the window, where a ceiling-written draw is only overdraw evidence against an existing store (`DrawRange._overdrawn`). The experiment is armed only by the **Run System Identification** button (`async_arm_system_identification`, whose one caller is `button.py`), and `sysid.armable` arms the fit, not the probe, while the house learner is unconverged. On the owner's download the experiment gate alone drops every interval, and the window's ceiling-written running samples fall short of `CEILING_MIN_SAMPLES` (counts in `## Figures`), so relaxing the store's rule would not have filled it. The fix belongs to the experiment's arming: owner ruling S3 (2026-11-14) has the button arm the ceiling probe before the fit where the pump's top is unlearned, built in part B.

Each mutant was applied to production lines, `python3 tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py --self-test` run, and the file restored:

merges.body:
R11-PRE-STANDING-SCRIPTS part 1: the `cp-owed` beat row (carry 4, the owner's directive tvofi 2026-11-09, "never let the critical path or outside PRs slip, ever"; triage `dev/programme/triage/s6-batch141.md` P515), built to the approved design (`design/R11-PRE-STANDING-SCRIPTS` 375ce7ff3f, `Design review: approve` at be6cc24cae), section 1's first seam. The new module `tools/audit/seat/owed_watch.py` owns the fired-ledger read, the "a seat is on it" predicate and every owed-by-grace arm. The tick's `_fired`, `_seat_on` and `payloads` (FIRE-OWED) bodies moved into it unchanged. The tick's methods now delegate to it, and the tick's `verdict_kind` reads its verdict line through `owed_watch.FIX_VERDICT`, the one copy of that grammar (the agreement lane refused it written twice). So `orchestrator_tick.py` shrinks and gains no arm (design section 5, L5: "no new arm, ever; it shrinks by extraction"). The beat row `cp-owed` (`beat_jobs.py`, `beatd.jobs.json`, every 300 s, no class lock) writes one `CP-OWED <arm> <subject>` line to the digest for each critical-path or outside step past its grace.

The watched set is computed, never hand-kept. It is every open roster group `roster_lib.is_outside` is true for, plus every group `roster_lib.critical_path_read` publishes at the roster ref (`roster_lib.reader_ref`), plus their open pull requests (`group_for_branch`, else `group_for_pr`). An unreadable critical-path file is `cp-owed: UNREADABLE`, never an empty set. The eight arms and their graces are carry 4's, verbatim: merge verdict at the head with no approval 10 min, approved and unmerged 45, blocked with no fire since 15, a head with no reviewer dispatch 25, UNFIRED, DESIGN-REVIEW OWED 10, FIXER-OWED, and SEAT-SILENT 90.

Decisions, each with its reason:
- The carry states no grace for UNFIRED or FIXER-OWED. UNFIRED takes `FIRE_GRACE_MIN` (15), because it is the same step as FIRE-OWED: published, not fired. FIXER-OWED takes the design-review step's 10 (a verdict is in and the next seat is not dispatched).
- "After a step" compares a FIRED line's leading UTC stamp with the step's commit time. An unstamped line is never "after" anything, so a stale ledger line cannot silence a newer step.
- UNFIRED and SEAT-SILENT clear on a return ref moved since the step (handoff, handoff-wip family, handoff-body, design, design-verdict, verdict/<n>, probe/rev-<n>-*) as well as on a FIRED line. SEAT-SILENT keys on refs, never on a session's status (carry 17's dead session read `running`).
- DESIGN-REVIEW OWED is P510's predicate: no design verdict names the tip. A `seat-refused` verdict counts as no review. A tip whose note opens `Design blocked:` is excluded (design verdict note dr2-blocked-tip-owed).
- Rank: the design's note reads "critical path, then outside, then hotfix". This uses `roster_lib.dispatch_rank` instead, which puts a hotfix first, then critical path or outside: that function is "the one order every queue reader applies" and carries the owner's ruling (triage P420) that a hotfix outranks outside work. Inside one rank, the critical path comes ahead of outside, then the oldest step. That ordering is the rank half of carry 1, and it is pinned by two cases and two mutants.

Every mutant prints `ok   mutant <name> killed by: <case>`. Each arm's mutant drops or inverts that arm's predicate and fails its `planted <arm>: one line at grace 0` case. It watched 11 open outside groups and 0 critical-path groups: the critical-path file at that ref lists only round-10 groups, none open. It printed one line, `CP-OWED DESIGN-REVIEW-OWED R11-OUTSIDE-ROOMS-P2 64m past its 10m grace [OUTSIDE]`, and `git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/*R11-OUTSIDE-ROOMS-P2*'` lists `design/R11-OUTSIDE-ROOMS-P2` and its designer dispatch with no `design-verdict/` ref, so the line is true. The PR arms were not exercised live in this seat.
- Sibling seams, enumerated by `git grep -n "FIRE_GRACE_MIN\|SEAT_WINDOW_MIN\|FIRED_STAMP\|_seat_on\|_fired(\|fire_names\|def payloads\|\.payloads(" -- tools/audit/seat/` (design section 4). Every tick definition moved and each tick call site now delegates: `_fired`, `_seat_on` (two callers, the body-ahead and red-unowned buckets), `payloads`, and the self-test's `FIRE_GRACE_MIN`. The enumeration also returns `sweep_gantt.recent_fired`, a second fire-ledger stamp reader with its own 12 h window. `verdict_audit.recent_lines` is a third, which the grep does not name but `git grep -n "STAMP.match" -- tools/audit/seat/` does. Neither is in the design's section 4 list, so both are carried below and not moved here.

The self-test-reads arm (`--only self-test-reads --record-self-tests`) then predicted `SELF-TEST READS UNDER-SCOPED tests/entities.py: tools/audit/seat/owed_watch.py`. Both `ci_predict.py --base origin/main` and `--only self-test-reads --record-self-tests` now print `CI PREDICT: no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted against 98847b99d7bb`.

## Brief carries

This part's carries are 0 to 4 of the brief, numbered from 0 as the dispatch rendered them.

The approved design (section 5, "L5 decision") builds it as the dispatch drain's classes `not-reviewable-real` and `not-reviewable-deferral` in part 3, not in the tick. CP-OWED lines are ranked by `dispatch_rank`, critical path first inside a rank, pinned by `rank: inside one rank the critical path is ahead of outside` and its mutant `rank_cp_first`. Classification by reason is the dispatch drain's EXCEPTION classes. Carry: R11-PRE-STANDING-SCRIPTS (part 3, named by the approved design)

The design places it with carry 6's readback in part 4 (record_beat.py, postmerge.py). Carry: R11-PRE-STANDING-SCRIPTS (part 4, named by the approved design)

## Summary

Without that filter, a design-reviewer or designer re-dispatch, or a reviewer dispatch newer than the approve, silences FIXER-OWED. No case plants one, so the exclusion is unpinned. Owed: one planted case in which a `dispatch/design-reviewer-<gid>` newer than the approve leaves FIXER-OWED firing. The mutant `fixerowed` covers the arm as a whole, not this conjunct. The PR ranks by `roster_lib.dispatch_rank` instead (hotfix first), and the body states the departure and its reason: the owner's ruling (triage P420; sweep_template 4d) that a hotfix outranks outside work. An owner ruling binds over a design note, and the watched set holds only CP or OUTSIDE groups, so the order changes only for a group that is also a hotfix. merges.body:
R11-PRE-BRIEFS-CENSUS: seven dimension briefs name their step's universe as a command, and the command is built. Policy pull request (dimension briefs, `policy_budgets.json`); finder-critical.

Built from the round-11 start evaluation at `9de7c2bdc73361a5428d85bc444bf973c43bb593`, the tip of `eval/r11`, which the review commit `f6d35cf73f` on `eval-review/r11-4` approves (`review.verdict` `approve` naming that sha, round 4, replacing round 3's approve of `02a48db212`). At that sha all seven cards this group closes carry `decision` `accepted` with tvofi's ruling: E11-D0, E11-D1, E11-D2, E11-D8, E11-D12, E11-D15 ("Accept all 14", made final) and E11-D9 ("Accept all four"). Work began at `7891b714f8` and each card was re-read at `02a48db212` and again at `9de7c2bdc7`: E11-D2 gained one input at the first re-read (a learned draw range fed censored samples), built here; at the second, three proposals changed only to say `escapes and seat-found defects`, with no input added or dropped, and no card was dropped. Merge timing (decision 0018 section 6): this head is not an ancestor of `f6d35cf73f`, and each card's object file is changed here.

**Wording.** A dimension brief is in the owner's words. Every sentence added to `D0.md`, `D1.md`, `D2.md`, `D8.md`, `D9.md`, `D12.md` and `D15.md` was drafted by this seat under mandate 6893738184 (scope all, in force to 2026-12-15T12:00Z).

**Card E11-D9** was built last, in its own commit (`db626fb9dd`), held out until the evaluation recorded its ruling, and is in this head.

**What a brief now names, and the ledger row each new input answers** (`dev/audit/rounds/round11/evaluation/escapes_hand.tsv` at `9de7c2bdc7`; a row marked seat-found is `out` there, a defect a programme seat found with no report from an install, whose input the card keeps; step numbering is kept, and two steps are added):

| brief | universe command(s) | input added, at the step the ledger names | ledger row |
|---|---|---|---|
| D0 | step 4 `enumerate.py d0-grid`; step 8 (new) the same-information oracle per grid cell and per install-day of `d15-installs`, with `C_real`, `C_same` and the model gap side by side | plant `flow-setpoint-behind-valve`; plant `manual-valve-buffer` (step 4) | R10-SETPOINT-POWER; R10-BUFFER-STORE (seat-found) |
| D1 | steps 1 to 6: `d1-lifecycle`, `d1-stores`, `d1-inputs`, `d1-solve-state`, `d1-excepts`, `d1-parsers` | a stored override across restore then resolve (1); a save during the learners' load, and the previous release's persisted record driven to the first actuator write (2); a presence entity changing between two updates, a price fetch raising while the last prices cover now, an input missing and back inside one interval (3) | R10-HOTFIX-AWAY-LIVE; R10-LEARNED-STORE-LOAD (seat-found), R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK; R10-HOTFIX-AWAY-PRESENCE, R10-OUTSIDE-PRICE-OUTAGE-LAST-VALID, R10-INPUT-REAPPEAR |
| D2 | `d2-identities --cells`, read from the new register `dev/audit/config/identities.json` | the switch-back slab (1); the savings identity on a valve house with the buffer above the curve and on a month upgraded mid-month (3); the pump's own power estimate, a moved covariate, the tank's fall after a charge starts, booked against metered space energy, a draw range fed censored samples (5) | R10-COP-GATE-E (seat-found); R10-HOTFIX-SAV-ESTIMATE, R10-SAVINGS-NEGATIVE; R10-HOTFIX-LEARNER-INPUTS, R10-OUTSIDE-DHW-CHARGE-SETTLE, R10-DEMAND-OVERBOOK, R10-SETPOINT-BOOST (second cause) |
| D8 | step 1 `d8-cells` (entity by state by language); step 3 compares every translation file, where it said both | a step's reason above a 1.1 heat-loss scale under flat weather; a merged slot's average power on a non-modulating pump with a minimum power (2) | R10-HOTFIX-PREHEAT-LABEL; R10-MIN-POWER-FLOOR |
| D9 | per metric: `d9-solves` (full solves per cycle), `d9-collections` (retained bytes), `d9-attributes` (payload bytes); each row reports examined over its metric's universe | none: the card names no escape | none |
| D12 | `check_scopes.py --repo . --population` plus the card and the blueprints, printed per cell by `d12-cells [--pairs]`; the cell ledger through `--ledger` | a counter-metered pump whose spans hold hot-water charges, and a short boost (3) | R10-OUTSIDE-LEARNER-ROBUSTNESS |
| D15 | `d15-installs`, read from the new register `dev/audit/config/bundles.json`; a round with no bundle reports 0 of its lines; step 9 (new) the oracle per install-day | a real download whose replay half is empty because one entity id escapes the mask (1) | R10-FLY-REPLAY-MASK |

Intake carry 175 is built by the same rows. D12 declares the two NO-READ axes' levels as the flow row's minimum, default and maximum and says where they are read (`objective.json` `population`, through `--population`); the levels themselves are R11-PRE-OWNER-CRITERIA's file.

**The enumerator** is `tools/audit/enumerate.py`: the prototype at `530cda6a24` ported (`d0-grid`, `d0-modules`, `d1-stores`, `d1-excepts`, `d1-lifecycle`, `d3-sites`, `d14-classes`, `d16-writes`, `d17-features`) and ten universes added. Design choices a reviewer should not read as bugs:

- It refuses in two places only: `run()` turns a missing source (an `OSError`) and a zero-line universe into exit 2. A per-universe guard remains only where its removal changes an outcome, and each has a self-test arm.
- `d1-inputs` is what the code treats as a configured entity slot, not a name shape: every key a `config_flow.py` `_F` row offers through an entity selector (`EntitySelector` or a def returning one, a comprehension's loop name expanded over its tuple), united with the keys `entry_config.py`'s `FACTORY_KEPT` keeps as `an entity assignment` (its comprehension's own `startswith`/`endswith` tests applied to `const.py`, plus its literal entries giving that reason). An entity selector outside an `_F` row, a row keyed by no name, a second comprehension or a wiring test the census cannot read refuses, so a slot added by a new route stops the census instead of leaving it short.
- `d9-solves` climbs callers by name inside the solver's own module and prints, without climbing, a site in another module. Climbing across modules by name prints every caller of any function sharing a name with one on the path; the self-test's not-climbed arm is the control.
- `--ledger TSV` joins any universe to the asserting test of each line, or `not run` (decision 0018 section 1 asks D1 and D8 for the census with its driving test). A generality cell also carries its source, one of 0018's four, and prints `not run` with no ledger.
- `d0-grid`'s plant, zone, hot-water and horizon levels are literals in the script, as in the prototype, pinned by a self-test arm: D0 step 4 no longer types them.
- A self-test line is mutated like any other added line; a survivor there is a mutant of the test, not of the instrument, and is listed without an arm.
- `--briefs` is this group's acceptance as a command: every `enumerate.py <universe>` a dimension brief cites runs non-empty, and a tree citing none is refused.

The two registers hold what no source prints: `identities.json` the identities D2's steps execute with each one's grid, `bundles.json` the one bundle a round has read (round 10's, 2026-10-14, by `dev/audit/rounds/round10/D15/s1/intake.py`; steps from `rotation.json`'s round-10 coverage other than `none`). The install label is opaque.

Files outside the group's list, each because the brief's own terms require it: `dev/audit/config/rotation.json` and `scopes.json` (rows D0.M8 and D15.M9, which `check-wave-script.mjs` requires of an added step), `.github/workflows/governance.yml` (one line: the self-test rides the step that already runs `check_scopes.py --self-test`, as the prototype's did), and the new files.

Alternatives that lost: one enumerator per dimension (seven scripts, seven self-tests, one refusal rule copied seven times); the identity list parsed out of `D2.md`'s prose (a wrapped sentence is no register, and the grid has no place there); cutting D2's identity prose to pay its cap once the register held it (prose moved to an uncapped file is the hole `ratchet-budgets.md` closes).

## Head

merges.body:
Group: R11-PRE-ROUND-CHECK-GATE (topic r11-pre-round-check-gate)
Cards: E11-N-NULL-REVIEWER (accepted by tvofi, "Accept both (Recommended)"); tvofi's 2026-11-15 ruling "Only the finder critical are required for finder start", with his 14:00Z correction that what is still open when the finders finish goes to the architect and planner.
Code-owned and policy: tools/audit/check_scopes.py, dev/governance/decisions/0018-objective-function.md (sections 5 and 6) and dev/governance/roles/architect-planner.md need tvofi's approving review, or one under mandate 6893738184 (issue 3394, scope all, to 2026-12-15T12:00Z).

`check_scopes.py --round N` refused round 11's start on every accepted evaluation card not yet merged, the finder-critical ones and the rest alike: 43 lines at the evaluation's approved head. The owner ruled only the finder-critical ones gate the start. This change makes that ruling a structured field and has the check read it:

- **`gates_finders`**, a boolean on each accepted card, written by the orchestrator beside `ruling`. 0018 section 5 already lets the orchestrator write the owner's ruling into a card; the field records what that ruling decided about finder gating, so it is part of the ruling. The evaluator's `finder_critical` prose stays as the evaluator's argument. It is not parsed, because four cards (E11-K-D4, D5, D9, D10) read "no as the card stands" while the owner's ruling on them is "All four before finders", so the prose does not decide. The check refuses an accepted card whose `gates_finders` is missing or not a boolean ("yes", 1 and null are all refused), so no card stops gating by accident. A rejected or deferred card needs no value.
- **At the finder start**, an accepted card with `gates_finders: false` that is not merged is not a gap. It is printed `PARALLEL <card> accepted, not merged, gates no finder: ...` because it is built while the finders run. Its unset `threshold`/`criterion` is not a gap either: it is built with the card. A non-gating card that is merged gets every check an accepted card gets (after the review, changes its file). A gating card is checked as before.
- **For P3**, `--round N --open-cards` prints `{round, open_cards, unmarked_cards, ref}` as JSON and exits, rc 1 with an `UNMARKED <card>` line on stderr for each accepted card with no boolean `gates_finders` (see `### Repair`). Run at the ref where P3 starts, it lists the non-gating accepted cards still unmerged then. It skips the scope verdict, so it is quick, and it exits 2 rather than printing an empty list when the evaluation is not tracked at the ref. Why a flag rather than parsing the PARALLEL lines: P3 runs at a different moment from the finder start, and the architect needs a parseable list without the 2-minute scope run.
- **The null reviewer** (E11-N-NULL-REVIEWER): `norm(ev.get("reviewer", ""))` turned JSON null into `none`, which is non-empty and so passed the two-seats rule. The evaluator and the reviewer must now each be a non-blank string before they are normalised. A null, absent, blank, `0` or `[]` value is refused for either seat.

Carry 0: this group's part-2 carry (body item 4ffa4b06, landed on the roster). It is built in part 2's own pull request (topic r11-pre-round-check-gate-p2), as the orchestrator ruled, not in this one.

## Approval

Not yet given. These policy edits are kept minimal and await tvofi's approving review at the head, or an approving review under mandate 6893738184 (issue 3394, scope all, to 2026-12-15T12:00Z), declared with the mandate id:
- 0018 section 5: the orchestrator's ruling field now includes `gates_finders` on an accepted card.
- 0018 section 6: Writes and Refuses name the field and the PARALLEL / `--open-cards` behaviour.
- architect-planner.md: Inputs now name `check_scopes.py --round <N> --open-cards` at P3's start. Step 3 places every open card in the plan once, like a finding. Paid within its token cap by dropping two duplicated phrases: "read-only on code", which "You do not write production code" already says, and the Method's "(sensitivity, tradeoff points)", which step 2 already says. The target's holdout bullet now points at step 7's list instead of repeating it.
- evaluator.md is unchanged: "never ... write a `ruling`" already covers a field that 0018 defines as part of the ruling.

## Head

`86a88d394c61d615dcc0107a6189e45ca7b4d219` merges the authored code head `8ad98806e4c824491455b50f05f16eaa09ac7ac9`.

8ad98806e4c824491455b50f05f16eaa09ac7ac9 (handoff/r11-pre-round-check-gate), the merge of the PR branch origin/fix/r11-pre-round-check-gate (691aa86b1e, the relay's tree-neutral merges of 07f969bf3d and fc369d59) into 89f08b6d46; its tree is 89f08b6d46's, byte for byte (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` equal before and after the merge), so every figure taken at 89f08b6d46 describes it. 89f08b6d46 is one commit on 07f969bf3d (the round-2 repair of fix review 3620): the grader stubs part 2 needs, moved here by the orchestrator's route (a) for part 2's bootstrap question. The diff since 07f969bf3d is `tools/policy/check-wave-script.mjs` only, test code, so every figure under the two `### Repair` sections still describes this head: none of them reads that file.

### Delta: the P3 grader stubs for part 2 (#3633)

- **Why**: part 2 (#3633, ec058220b5) restores `audit-plan.js`'s refusal of a plan that leaves an open card or group in no group. main's `check-wave-script.mjs` drives `audit-plan.js` with `plan/read` and `plan/moves` stubs that carry no `--open-cards` listing, so it cannot grade that `audit-plan.js`: `ci_predict.py` reads that as a bootstrap (the base's grader refuses the head's workflow).
- **What moved**: exactly the stub hunks of `git diff origin/main ec058220b5 -- tools/policy/check-wave-script.mjs` (8 added, 4 removed lines): the `OPEN` listing (`open`: one open card E11-X, one open group R11-G, none unmarked; `open_rc` 0) spread into the default `plan/read` stub and the two triage `pthrows` reads; and `MOVES()`, the default `plan/moves` stub, which accounts for both items (E11-X in group A's `open_items`, R11-G in `dropped` with a reason). The refusal's own tests (the five new `pthrows`, the kept-group null control, the `--open-cards` read-prompt assertion) stay in part 2: they fail against an `audit-plan.js` without the refusal. Compared line for line: the delta's `+`/`-` lines are a subset of that diff's, and the remainder is exactly those seven tests.
- **Failing first** (the null control): main's grader, unchanged, against ec058220b5's `audit-plan.js` failed 7: the six `pthrows` named `a triage that drops a verified finding stops P3`, `a triage that keeps one finding twice stops P3`, `a group with no move entry stops P3`, `a publish that is not a 40-hex commit stops P3`, `a reviewer answering for another tree stops P3`, `a recorded verdict that is not a 40-hex commit stops P3`, and `the P3 plan workflow threw`, each with `check_scopes.py --open-cards exited undefined, not 0`.
- **Mutation**: the delta adds no `.py` line, so prepr's step 6d draws no mutant from it. The mutant that matters is the delta's removal, which is the null control above: 7 failures.

### Repair (fix review 3620, round 2)

- **Block**: main()'s `sys.exit(rc)` and its `print(line, file=sys.stderr)` were reached by no arm; M17 (exit 0) and M18 (no UNMARKED line) survived the full self-test.
- **Fix** (the reviewer's first option, at the command line): `open_cards_cli()` builds a scratch git repository in a temp directory with `tests/throwaway_git.py`'s `throwaway_git_init` (7248e2b3's raw `git init` was refused by prepr.sh's throwaway-git step; 07f969bf runs the repository and the subprocess under its environment) with two commits of a round-8 record (minimal objective and round-7 record) and runs `check_scopes.py --repo <tmp> --ref <commit> --round 8 --open-cards` as a subprocess on each. The two records differ only in `gates_finders` on C2 and C3: booleans in the first; absent on C2 and the string `"true"` on C3 in the second. C1 is accepted, `gates_finders: false`, unmerged; C4 is rejected.
- **Arms** (two, in `--self-test`'s coverage table):
  - null control: the all-boolean record exits 0, its stderr carries no `UNMARKED`, and its JSON `open_cards` is `["C1"]`;
  - the unmarked record exits 1, the stderr `UNMARKED` lines are exactly `UNMARKED C2`, `UNMARKED C3` (text before the colon, in order), and its JSON `unmarked_cards` is `["C2", "C3"]`.
- Rejected: moving main()'s print-and-exit into a function the self-test calls; the brief requires the CLI run as a subprocess, and a function arm would leave the `sys.exit` line itself unpinned.

### Repair (fix review 3620, round 1)

- **Block**: `--open-cards` printed `open_cards: []` and exited 0 on a record whose accepted cards carry no `gates_finders`, and nothing tested its output (M11 survived).
- **Fix**: `open_cards_report(rnd, tree, show, merged, anc, changed)` is the function main() prints. It lists the open non-gating cards and names each accepted card with no boolean `gates_finders`. It prints `UNMARKED <card>: accepted, no boolean gates_finders ...` to stderr, adds `unmarked_cards` to the JSON, and exits 1. The no-evaluation path still exits 2.
- **Tests**: the self-test drives `open_cards_report` through the same synthetic record as the other evaluation arms.
  - A non-gating unmerged card is listed: `({"round": 8, "open_cards": ["C1"], "unmarked_cards": []}, 0, [])`.
  - A complete record lists nothing, rc 0 (null control).
  - An accepted card with no `gates_finders`, or with `"no"`, is named, rc 1, whether merged or not.
  - The evaluation arms now hold 62 of 62.
- **Mutants**: `mutant_run.py --spec <scratch mutants3.json> --in-place --cmd "python3 <scratch evtest.py>"`. NULL survived and 4 of 4 were killed:
  - M11: `out` is dropped from the `evaluation_gaps` call, the reviewer's mutant.
  - M12: rc is always 0.
  - M13: no card is ever unmarked.
  - M14: only a missing value counts as unmarked, so `"no"` passes.
- **Live**: `python3 tools/audit/check_scopes.py --repo . --ref f6d35cf73f19a053c99e6627071984ff4190aa04 --round 11 --open-cards` exits 1 with `"open_cards": []` and 43 `unmarked_cards`, and prints 43 UNMARKED lines on stderr. The null control is the same evaluation with every card marked (above): no card is unmarked.
- **After the owner's values landed** (eval/r11 c6ce415b77, `gates_finders` written by the orchestrator from the rulings): the same command exits 0 with no UNMARKED line, `unmarked_cards: []`, and 12 `open_cards`. Those 12 are exactly the cards whose value is false: E11-GATE-REDS, E11-INJECTED, E11-N-GATE-CAUSE, E11-N-INSTRUMENT-YIELD, E11-N-INTAKE-BUILDER, E11-N-NULL-REVIEWER, E11-N-ROLE-CLAUSE, E11-N-RULE-YIELD, E11-R-WORKFLOWS, E11-S-SEATS, E11-SCORECARD and E11-T-product_green_floor.

## Mutation proof

### Round 2 (fix review 3620, at 07f969bf3d)

The reviewer's driver (`verdict/3620:evidence/mut_driver.py`), with M20 and M21 added and M11, M13-M15 (judged in round 1) dropped: each mutant is applied to `tools/audit/check_scopes.py` in place, `python3 tools/audit/check_scopes.py --repo . --ref HEAD --self-test` is run whole, and a mutant is KILLED on a non-zero rc. The file was compared byte for byte with its copy afterwards (`cmp`, printed RESTORED).
- NULL: rc 0, SURVIVED, `marked rc=0, unmarked rc=1 ['UNMARKED C2', 'UNMARKED C3']`.
- M17 main's `sys.exit(rc)` -> `sys.exit(0)`: KILLED (the CLI's unmarked rc reads 0).
- M18 main's `print(line, file=sys.stderr)` -> `pass`: KILLED (no UNMARKED line).
- M20 that print -> `print(line)` (to stdout): KILLED (no UNMARKED line on stderr, stdout no longer JSON).
- M21 main's `sys.exit(rc)` -> `sys.exit(1)`: KILLED by the null control alone (marked rc reads 1).
- M12 and M16 (round 1's function mutants): KILLED, now by the CLI arms as well.
- M19 `"open_cards": sorted(out)` -> unsorted: SURVIVED, an equivalent mutant: `evaluation_gaps` appends to `parallel` while iterating `sorted(cards.items())`, so `out` is already sorted and the `sorted()` is a no-op on every input. No arm can kill it; the reviewer's follow-up is disposed here rather than carried.

Failing test first. The new self-test arms ran against the unchanged predicates, with only the parameter added: `evaluation_self_test` held 54 of 59. These five failed:
- a non-gating accepted card not merged passes and is listed beside
- a non-gating unmerged card's unset value is no gap, it builds with the card
- an accepted card with no boolean gates_finders is refused, in every shape
- an accepted card with no gates_finders is refused even unmerged, and never listed beside
- a null, absent or blank reviewer or evaluator is refused

At the head all 59 hold.

There is one mutant per new predicate, run with `python3 tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --spec <scratch mutants.json> --in-place --cmd "python3 <scratch evtest.py>"`. The driver calls `check_scopes.evaluation_self_test` at HEAD and exits 1 on any failing arm. NULL survived, and every mutant was killed:
- M1 `if not isinstance(gating, bool)` -> `if False`
- M2 -> `if gating is None` (accepts "yes")
- M3 `elif not gating and not (c and merged(c))` -> `elif not gating`
- M4 -> `elif False`
- M5 the `parallel.append(cid)` -> `pass`
- M6 the `continue` after it deleted
- M7 the old `norm(ev.get(k, ""))`

## Null control

The evaluation at origin/eval-review/r11-4 (f6d35cf73f) was run through `evaluation_gaps` at that ref, using a scratch driver that substitutes the card fields:
- **As written** (no `gates_finders`): 92 gaps. These are the 49 of today plus 43 "carries no boolean gates_finders", so an unrecorded card refuses and never passes silently.
- **Every accepted card `gates_finders: true`**: 49 gaps, 43 of them "accepted and not merged". This is line for line identical to `check_scopes.py --repo . --ref origin/eval-review/r11-4 --round 11` on main's code (compared as lists in the driver, printing "identical" only on equality), and 0 PARALLEL.
- **The proposed gating list** (31 true, 12 false; held outside this PR for the orchestrator to record): 36 gaps (31 not merged), 12 PARALLEL.

## Figures

- Delta, the grader matrix. Command: `node tools/policy/check-wave-script.mjs` from the tree root, with `.claude/workflows/audit-plan.js` replaced by `git show <rev>:.claude/workflows/audit-plan.js` and restored after (`git checkout`); the result line is the script's `N passed, M failed` and its rc. Every run also prints `FAIL (probe, expected) threw: deliberate`, the script's own block-harness probe, counted in neither number.
  - main 6aa7ddc712 grader, unchanged, x ec058220b5 `audit-plan.js`: `209 passed, 7 failed`, rc 1 (the null control).
  - main grader unchanged x 416280f5 `audit-plan.js` (blob 0a06aa738b, the same as main's and this head's): `223 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0.
  - main grader plus these stubs x ec058220b5: `223 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0; x 416280f5: `223 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0.
  - this head's grader x ec058220b5: `223 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0; x 416280f5: `223 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0.
  - The brief's 230/230 is part 2's grader: ec058220b5's `check-wave-script.mjs` x ec058220b5's `audit-plan.js`, on main's tree, printed `230 passed, 0 failed`. With the stubs alone the count is 223 at both revisions; the seven tests left in part 2 are the difference.
- Round 2, at 07f969bf3d: `python3 tools/audit/check_scopes.py --repo . --ref HEAD --self-test` printed `evaluation arms: 62/62 held; --round 1 rc=1; --open-cards rc=2, marked rc=0, unmarked rc=1 ['UNMARKED C2', 'UNMARKED C3']` and `SELF-TEST passed (every perturbed scope refused)`.
- Round 2 scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` printed `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out`, the script `tests/entities.py`, and `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` printed `ALL 2723 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`, rc 0; `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reported no conflict; `python3 tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.

## Unpinned sites

`prepr.sh` step 6d, run at 07f969bf3d with `MUTANT_IN_PLACE=1 MUTANT_CMD="python3 tools/audit/check_scopes.py --repo . --ref HEAD --self-test"`, drew the diff's added lines against b880dc914f and printed 7 SURVIVED lines. - `tools/audit/check_scopes.py:685 CONST_SWAP` (round 1, "refused even unmerged", `lambda sha: True` -> `False`): equivalent; the arm states that merged and unmerged give the same refusal, so swapping one input for the other leaves that refusal unchanged.
