merges.body:
R11-PRE-MACHINERY-LIMITER, part 1 of 3: card P2 (owner ruling 2026-11-13) and the group's carries 0-4. Carry 5, Carry 6, Carry 7, Carry 8, Carry 9, Carry 10, Carry 11 and Carry 12 are parts 2 and 3, dispatched at this handoff. Carry 13 (P793, the closure runbook scripts' orch-root default) was homed on the group by tvofi 2026-11-15 after this part's dispatch, so it is in neither this part's brief nor this repair round's (body only); this pull request does not build it, and which part builds it is the orchestrator's assignment.

**P2, the target.** `machinery_ratchet.py` gains THE TARGET (its docstring is the rule): `dev/governance/config/machinery_target_budgets.json` holds `anchor`, `every_merges` and `step`, and the target is `nonproduction_merges - step * floor(n / every_merges)`, n the first-parent merges after the anchor up to the base (PR mode) or head (push mode), never below 0, compared against target plus the existing band. **The schedule:** anchor `b3831ff64e` (this branch's merge base, where the cap was recorded), 48 down every 290 merges: 290 is half the frozen `window_merges` (the owner's seven days of merges), 48 is 10% of the recorded 478 rounded half up (the audit's "e.g. -10% per week", section 6 row a2). **The enumerator:** `python3 tools/audit/machinery_ratchet.py --measure --head origin/main` now prints `target` and `merges_past_anchor`; `--check` prints a `target` line. At a round start the orchestrator records the cap down to `--measure` and asks the owner for the round's anchor and step (`ratchet-budgets.md`); `budget_raise_gate.py` classifies a moved anchor, a longer `every_merges` or a smaller `step` as a raise.

Why a second budgets file and not three keys in `machinery_budgets.json`: `governance.yml` grades a pull request with the BASE's `machinery_ratchet.py`, whose `load_budgets` refuses a key it does not read, so the keys there would turn `policy-docs` red on this pull request (a BOOTSTRAP split, `fixer.md` step 5). The new file is invisible to the base copy, and it is a `*_budgets.json`, so the raise gate guards it; a constant in the program would not be guarded (the program is not code-owned).

Where it binds, a design choice: only a non-production, unexempted candidate in PR mode. A production candidate cannot raise the metric, and the existing code refuses any candidate when the window is over the cap, so a binding target under the old semantics would refuse production work. In push mode the target is a report line: a schedule overtaking the window would otherwise turn a required check on main red with nothing to repair. The two caps stay the ceiling in both modes. **For the owner's review:** a machinery repair of a red required check on main is refused by the target like any machinery merge once the window is past it; its routes are the band, an earned exemption, or an owner-approved change to the schedule. The alternative, a ground the offline ratchet would have to read, was not taken.

**P2, the rest.** `proposal-triage.md`: on severity only a red required check on main or a blocked production pull request skips the machinery bars (`medium`, `high`, `major`, `critical` no longer do); root-cause countermeasure, closeout and owner directive keep their routes, which are not severity. `ratchet-budgets.md`: one in, one out for required checks, the set `merge_train.py owed-reds` prints.

**Carry 0, Carry 1 and Carry 2, the instrument freeze** (`orchestrator.md`, replacing the "proposal waits" bullet; Carry 1's owner and outside items also in the scope bullet and the playbook's round start): local prototype under `$HPO_STATE_DIR/r<N>/proto/<id>/`, each use a sweep-log `WORKAROUND <id> onset=<UTC> cost=<min>` line; the permanent fix a numbered entry of the proposals file in `$HPO_STATE_DIR/r<N>/` citing the prototype and its measured effect; consolidated (duplicates merged, uses and cost summed) and triaged once at round end; ACCEPTs built at the next round's start before its finders, the rest refused with their numbers; a workaround never changes production code, loosens a gate or budget, or skips a review; the exceptions are a production defect, an owner order, a red required check on main, and an owner or outside item. The scope bullet now folds an undeferred owner or outside item into the ongoing round. The playbook's round start gains step 4 (where the prior round's proposals and prototypes are, and that its ACCEPTs are built before finders); step 5 (was 4) already states the deferral record (who, when, their words) and that silence is none.

**Carry 3:** `nonproduction_merges` re-recorded 521 -> 478 (more than its band of 5 below the cap); `churn_per_kilo_product_lines` stays (13785 against 14797, inside its band of 3636). **Carry 4:** `pr_cap.py` classes open pull requests by `machinery_ratchet.is_product` (one predicate), `dispatch-gate --machinery OWNER/REPO` refuses a machinery group once machinery and unread pull requests fill the slots production does not hold (`replan.py` `DEFAULT_CAPS` slots less `PRODUCTION_SLOTS`), and `orchestrator_tick.py`'s cap levels print `pr_cap.class_line` every pass (five lines there; the batch's L5 hold on that instrument covers proposals, and P742 routes this carry here).

Payment for the policy caps: `ratchet-budgets.md` lost three spent sentences (two historical measurements of the CLAUDE.md split and the "deferred, not disabled" motivation); `dev/audit/README.md` lost the organization-transfer item, ruled out by tvofi 2026-11-14 (`dev/programme/HANDOVER.md`, the designer's answers), cut to one line.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant applied alone at the head, its self-test run, the file restored:

bus-nonce: e507e1814e2144e10fd3a6a5ed07a2c8

Round: third. This is a delta review over the reviewed head 56fda94e8568b6ae57d1af8227386f8dc096f61c. The delta is 2fa85b69db, which merges origin/main e30408f788 (#3566, the nudge.md retirement) into the branch, and 43c1c7dbfd, which merges that commit in. The delta touches nothing under custom_components/, so the review is not widened.

## Block

- `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs` at 43c1c7dbfd exits 1 with `ERROR [budgets] tools/audit/briefs/orchestrator.md: about 4286 tokens across its lines exceeds its cap of 4251 tokens (files_tokens)` (`ev/policy_lint_head.txt`). The `--budgets` row for that file (`ev/budgets_orchestrator.txt`, `ev/budgets_prev_head.txt`) reads:
  - 4248 at the previously reviewed head 56fda94e85, inside the cap;
  - 4172 at origin/main e30408f788, inside the cap;
  - 4286 at this head, over the cap.
- Neither side breaks the cap alone. The branch's edits to `dev/governance/roles/orchestrator.md` (`ev/orchestrator_own_diff.txt`, 2608 to 2673 words) left 3 tokens of headroom, and main's #3566 re-pointing then added text to the same file. The auto-merged result is over the cap.
- `dev/governance/config/policy_budgets.json` is not in this PR's diff, so no cap raise covers the overflow.
- The same error is the cause of both new CI reds at this head, and both are in `merge_train.py owed-reds`:
  - `governance / policy-docs` (job 133020850696): `TOTAL: 1 error(s) across 51 policy file(s)`, `by check: {"budgets":1}`.
  - `governance / env-matrix` (job 133020850695): 7 of its 16 declared outcomes fail. Every failing outcome is either `policy_lint rc=0` with that same ERROR line or the follow-on `MUTANTS: the entry point exited 1 on the corpus as it stands`.
- Both checks were green at 56fda94e85, according to the previous verdict.
- The PR body has no `## Red checks` answer for either, and review_packet refuses `red-unanswered` for both.
- To resolve: cut orchestrator.md by about 35 tokens, or raise its cap with the case stated in the body (a budget raise, so the owner's approval under budget-raise-gate). Then re-run `policy_lint.mjs`.

## Findings

- Note: figure: the branch's change to `dev/governance/roles/proposal-triage.md` conflicted with main's #3566 and was resolved by taking main's text verbatim. The head's file equals main's, so the PR no longer changes that file (own-diff stat goes from 13 files to 12: `ev/own_diff_stat_old.txt`, `ev/own_diff_stat_new.txt`). Main's wording carries the same rule (repair at any severity; a red required check on main, a blocked production PR, a root-cause countermeasure, closeout or an owner directive skip the bar). Any body text that claims this PR rewrites proposal-triage.md is now stale. Carry: R11-PRE-MACHINERY-LIMITER
- Note: instrument: the previous verdict's `gate_raise_only` note (classify reads RED, not APPROVAL-OWED, when a gate run was superseded) still stands and was not re-examined here. Carry: dismissed: an instrument defect outside this PR's diff, handed to the orchestrator in the previous verdict

## Evidence

- Head reviewed: 43c1c7dbfd7a642a3543c1912469b2ce30f05584 (`ev/HEAD.txt`), checked out in a detached worktree.
- Merge resolution: `git merge-tree --write-tree 56fda94e85 e30408f788` conflicts only in `dev/governance/roles/proposal-triage.md`. The head tree dfee30d92b differs from that auto-merge only in that file, where main's side was taken. No other hand edit rides in the merge.
- Own diff: `git diff e30408f788...43c1c7dbfd` and `git diff 66865be375...56fda94e85` agree, line for line, in every file except proposal-triage.md, which dropped out. Untouched by this PR: VERSION, the manifest, RELEASE_NOTES.md, tests/golden and custom_components.
- Merge with main: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 43c1c7dbfd` exits 0 with tree dfee30d92b (`ev/merge-tree.txt`). The head already contains origin/main e30408f788.
- Self-tests at the head (`ev/selftest_*.txt`):
  - machinery_ratchet: 72 checks, 0 failed;
  - pr_cap: 32 checks, 0 failed;
  - orchestrator_tick: 322 checks, 0 failed.
- Mutants re-applied at the head (`ev/mutants.txt`), each killed:
  - `pr_cap.py:230` with `and v > PRODUCTION_SLOTS` removed: 1 check fails;
  - `machinery_ratchet.py:359` with `max(0, ...)` removed: 1 check fails.
- `machinery_ratchet.py --check --base origin/main --head HEAD --pr 3627` exits 0 (`ev/check.txt`):
  - ok nonproduction_merges 481 <= 478 + band 5;
  - ok churn 13948 <= 14797 + 3636;
  - ok target 481 <= 478 + band 5 (17 merges past anchor).
- `--measure --head HEAD` prints `merges_past_anchor 3`.
- CI: `merge_train.py classify 43c1c7dbfd --pr 3627` read `WAIT ... pending: gate red: none` from 00:53:09 to 00:59:34 UTC (`ev/classify.log`). The wait was stopped once the block was established. The block rests on the policy_lint failure reproduced locally, not on classify.
- Owed reds (`ev/owed-reds.txt`) include governance / env-matrix and governance / policy-docs.
- I ran the env-matrix driver locally, but it produced no output within 230 s (timeout rc 124). The CI log above is the evidence for that check.

## Friction

- The local `policy_lint_envmatrix.mjs` run exceeds a 240 s tool call. CI's log was read instead.

merges.subject: Merge pull request #3648 from tvofi/fix/r11-pre-relay-rebuild
merges.title: R11-PRE-RELAY-REBUILD: r11 pre relay rebuild
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R11-PRE-RELAY-REBUILD part 1 of 3 (owner card P12, 2026-11-13): roster carries 0-4. Carries 5-12 are later parts, dispatched at this handoff, and none is answered here.

- **Carry 0 (#3358's silent skip).** The skip came from the handoff arm's topic. `cloud_relay.sh` turned `fix/<t>-pr` into `<t>` alone (`topic_grammar.pr_topic`). `review_packet.py`'s handoff-not-applied read tries `<t>-pr` first and then `<t>`. #3358's repair returned under `handoff/r10-combi-tank-pr`, so the arm read only `handoff/r10-combi-tank`. That ref held an older tip, already in the head, whose body the relay had applied (its last update of #3358 ended OK on 2026-11-09). So the arm took the `continue` for "ancestor, body applied", with no line, while `bus.sh dispatch` refused handoff-not-applied. The rule now has one owner, `topic_grammar.handoff_topics`, moved out of `review_packet.py` and used by both readers through `topic_grammar.py handoff-topics`. The first topic that has a `handoff/` ref decides. `handoff_level`'s open and merged topic lists use the same rule, so `handoff/<t>-pr` with an open PR is no longer `handoff-no-pr`. Every other skip of a handoff that the head lacks is now owed on `<log>.level`. A missing body is `handoff-held ... NOBODY`, mirroring HELD-BODY. A hold-file skip is `handoff-held ... HOLD`. An unreadable ref or head, a busy tools tree, a BUSY update and an unreadable body are each `handoff-skipped <ref> <tip> #<pr> <why>`. These kinds are rewritten every pass.
- **Carry 1 (S14-TICK-STALE-SILENT).** `tick_loop.sh`'s `fresh_check` now restarts a branch-backed checkout that is clean and holds no commit outside origin/main (`checkout -q -B <branch> origin/main`). A branch that has commits of its own stays stale, with the why `the branch <b> holds <n> commit(s) origin/main lacks; it is never moved`. When a stale state lasts into a second consecutive pass (counted in `<out>.stale`), the board ends with `-> OWED relay-skipped code=<sha7> behind=<n>: <why> (stale <k> consecutive passes)`.
- **Carry 2 (S14-RELAY-CADENCE).** In the sleep between passes, `relay_gap_sleep` reaps a finished relay and starts the next one under the same lock once `HPO_TICK_RELAY_GAP` seconds (default 120, digits only) have passed since that relay ended. The holder now writes the end epoch as a third field of `<out>.relay.rc`. The tick keeps `--interval`. A stale pass starts no relay in its sleep, and neither does a relay that is still in flight.
- **Carry 3 (HELD-REVIEW over a returned verdict).** `review_freeze` now asks whether the dispatch's own `probe/rev-<pr>-<nonce8>` exists and is in `cloud-relayed.refused` or disposed in the ledger. If so, the review is over: the arm prints `RELEASED-REVIEW` and runs the update. Otherwise the HELD-REVIEW line and its level line name the probe's state: `probe=none (in flight)`, `probe=<sha8> relayed, not yet on verdict/<pr>`, or `probe=<sha8> held by the relay (dispose it to release)`.
- **Carry 4 (owed red text to a cloud seat).** Take a `handoff-wip/<topic>` BLOCKED.md that names `body_push: REFUSED PREDICTOR` and whose `PREDICT <check>` lines name a check in `merge_train.py owed-reds`. For it, the carry-fold arm reads that check at the topic's open PR head (`failure_logs.sh`: name, conclusion, error lines) into `<state>/cloud-owed-red-<topic>.md`, and the `carry-fold` level line names that file for the seat's next message. The carry-fold memo keeps the judged line, so the check is read once for each (wip, body) pair.

Alternatives not taken, and why each lost:
- Carry 0: stripping `-pr` in the relay and adding `<t>-pr` as a second read beside it. That would keep two copies of the rule that diverged once already.
- Carry 0: "any candidate not an ancestor decides". The relay would then disagree with `review_packet.py`'s first-with-a-ref rule.
- Carry 3: a timer release. It would release a review that is genuinely in flight.

## Head

`40cc860dd82b1e81ae8f2492a2796bf2797bc911` merges the authored code head `981cad4189b75d063894454ada80085b872c1b61`.

`981cad4189b75d063894454ada80085b872c1b61`. It is `e9c80fbad11d02cb66f3129bf04a48030ef6bfe1` plus one repair commit for the red `tests / fast (3.14)` at #3648's head `16945f40` (see `## Red checks`): `dev/audit/harnesses/r11_relay_3358_skip.py` finds its root with the canonical `repo_root` walk in place of `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]`. The carries' figures below were measured 2026-11-15 20:20Z to 22:10Z at `e9c80fba` against `origin/main` `98847b99d7bb3238686efd6869f805c89c6d1ff1`; the repair touches only the harness's root line, and its harness figure is re-taken at this head. Merge base unchanged; `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflict.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant is applied in its own worktree at the head by `perl -0pi` on its `# mut:` line, and that file's self-test is run. Failing rows:

- `mut:handofftopics` (`handoff-topics` back to `pr-topic`): FAIL `#3358's shape: fix/<t>-pr behind handoff/<t>-pr, handoff/<t> an older tip in its head, runs update_pr at handoff/<t>-pr`. This is the failing test first: the base's behaviour.
- `mut:nobody` (the NOBODY level line dropped): FAIL `and is owed HELD-NOBODY on the level, never skipped in silence (#3358)`.
- `mut:holdowed` (the HOLD level line dropped): FAIL `and owes handoff-held HOLD on the level, never skipped in silence (#3358)`.
- `mut:skipbusy` (a BUSY update unowed): FAIL `but owed handoff-skipped BUSY on the level, once, never skipped in silence (#3358)`.
- `mut:skiptools` (a busy tools tree unowed): FAIL `a tools tree held by a live relay is busy: no update`, and FAIL `and owed handoff-skipped BUSY on the level, never skipped in silence (#3358)`.
- `mut:reviewrelease` (the release predicate made false): FAIL `the dispatch's verdict refused by the relay releases HELD-REVIEW: update_pr runs`, FAIL `and says RELEASED-REVIEW naming the dispatch`, and FAIL `the dispatch's verdict disposed releases HELD-REVIEW too`.
- `mut:owedred` (the PREDICTOR case deleted): FAIL `a PREDICTOR refusal naming an owed red: the carry-fold level line names the owed red text for the seat's next message`, and FAIL `... which carries the check's name, conclusion and error lines, read at PR #77's head`.
- `mut:owednone` (the no-owed-red return dropped): FAIL `null control: a PREDICTOR refusal naming no owed red adds no text and reads no check`.
- `mut:gapstart` (no in-sleep relay start): FAIL `a relay that ends during the sleep is followed by another after the gap, with no tick pass between`.
- `mut:staleowed` (no board line): FAIL `freshness: a second consecutive stale pass ends the board with one '-> OWED relay-skipped' line: why, code and behind`.
- `mut:branchown` (the own-commit refusal made false): FAIL `freshness: a branch holding a commit origin/main lacks is never moved, and says why`.
- `mut:branchrestart` (`-B <branch>` replaced by `--detach`): FAIL `freshness: a clean branch-backed checkout behind origin/main with no commit of its own restarts on its branch at origin/main`.

For the four `tick_loop.sh` mutants, the nested self-test rows (branch, detached, GIT_DIR, poison, offline_spy) also fail, each naming the same nested row. `mut:tghandoff` in `topic_grammar.py` is pinned by its self-test row `handoff_topics: fix/<t>-pr reads <t>-pr then <t>, ...`. The diff adds no `.py` production line outside that function, and `review_packet.py` now binds the name to it.

## Unpinned sites

`prepr.sh` step 6d is run with `MUTANT_IN_PLACE=1` and `MUTANT_CMD` set to the self-tests of `topic_grammar.py`, `ledger.py` and `review_packet.py`. It leaves two survivors, both `STMT_DEL` of a `ck(...)` row inside `topic_grammar.self_test`: `tools/audit/seat/topic_grammar.py:122` (the `handoff_topics` row) and `:133` (the `handoff-topics` CLI row). Deleting a check row removes a pin, not production behaviour, so no check can kill it. Each row was shown to fail on its production mutant. The CLI row kills the five `main()` survivors that an earlier run at `b38dead5b9` reported, and `mut:tghandoff` is pinned by the `handoff_topics` row. Disposition: a self-test row, not a production site.

## Null control

- #3358's null at both ends: a head that holds `handoff/r10-combi-tank-pr` (`d07f8e9e`, the head the handoff was applied at by hand) gives `null_updated=0 null_owed=0` at both the base and the head. The self-test pins the same case on synthetic refs (`#3358's null control: a head holding handoff/<t>-pr has neither an update nor a level line nor a skip line`).
- A predicted red outside the owed set adds no text and runs no `failure_logs.sh` (`mut:owednone` kills that row).
- One stale pass writes no board line (`freshness null control: one stale pass writes no OWED line on the board`). A fresh pass clears the count.
- A relay still in flight at the gap starts none (`null control: a relay still in flight at the gap starts none`).
- A verdict-less in-flight dispatch still holds, as before: `a dispatch at the head with no verdict holds the handoff: no update_pr call`, its level line now ending `probe=none (in flight)`. A probe that is neither refused nor disposed holds again (`null control: the same probe no longer refused holds again`).

## Figures

- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r11_relay_3358_skip.py --seat <base worktree>/tools/audit/seat`, with the base worktree at `98847b99d7`: `RESULT defect_updated=0 defect_owed=0` and `RESULT null_updated=0 null_owed=0`. This is #3358's silent skip, replayed on its real commits.
- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r11_relay_3358_skip.py` at the head: `RESULT defect_updated=1 defect_owed=0` and `RESULT null_updated=0 null_owed=0`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/harness_headers.py`: at `e9c80fba` `1 of 115 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED` (`FAIL every inlined walk matches the canonical helper and no depth root remains [FAIL depth seams: dev/audit/harnesses/r11_relay_3358_skip.py:34: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]]`), the `tests / fast (3.14)` failure; at `981cad4189` `ALL 115 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`.
- `python3 -c "import sys;sys.path[:0]=['tests'];import harness_headers as h;print(h.depth_root_seams())"`, the depth-seam arm alone: one seam (`r11_relay_3358_skip.py:34`) at `e9c80fba`, `[]` at `981cad4189`, 0.54 s and 0.51 s wall.
- `bash tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh --self-test`: `cloud_relay self-test: 515 checks, 0 failed` (at `1325b217e0`; the commit after it changes `ledger.py` and `tick_loop.sh` only).
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/ledger.py --self-test`: `ledger self-test: 104 checks, 0 failed`. Its census `every kind cloud_relay.sh writes is a ledger kind` failed at `1325b217e0` until `handoff-skipped` was registered as a derived kind.
- Wall time for `bash tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh --self-test`, measured with `time` on one host under the same load: 1m47s at the base and 2m00s at the head. The step replay's bound is `SELF_TEST_TIMEOUT` (180 s). The two relay-gap rows (about 10 s of wall clock) run in the outer run only, as the nesting block already does. The base copy runs itself nested about nine times, and left ungated the rows timed out the replay (rc 124 at `1325b217e0`).
- `bash tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh --self-test`: `tick_loop self-test: 48 checks, 0 failed`.
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/topic_grammar.py --self-test`: `topic_grammar self-test: ok`.
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/review_packet.py --self-test`: `review_packet self-test: 133 checks, 0 failed`.
- The class seams: `awk '/^handoff_arm\(\) \{/,/^}$/' tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh | grep -n continue` enumerates the arm's skip sites. Each is either owed or a head that holds its handoff:
  - no listed row: nothing to apply.
  - no `handoff/` ref under any topic: nothing to apply.
  - unreadable ref or head: `handoff-skipped`.
  - handoff in the head (no body, body applied, seed): nothing owed.
  - no body ref: `handoff-held NOBODY`.
  - hold file: `handoff-held HOLD`, or `handoff-body-unapplied` for a body-only skip.
  - freeze: `handoff-held VERDICT/REVIEW/UNREAD`.
  - recorded failure and backoff: `handoff-update`.
  - no body directory, or unreadable body: `handoff-skipped`.
  - body names another code head: `handoff-body-stale`.
  - body-only with no `Code:` trailer: `handoff-body-unapplied`, or recorded as applied.
  - HELD-BODY: `handoff-held BODY`.
  - tools tree busy or refused: `handoff-skipped`, or `handoff-update`.
  - update BUSY: `handoff-skipped`.
  - update failed: `handoff-update`.
  - BODIED: applied.
  - no new head after the update: the ledger's `dispatch`.

  A PR outside the open-PR listing's 100-row page never enters the loop. Its handoff is owed by `handoff_level` as `handoff-no-pr`, because no listed open PR carries its topic.

merges.body:
R11-PRE-ROUND-METRICS, part 1 of 2 (topic r11-pre-round-metrics): the brief (owner ruling 2026-11-13, cards P3 and P8; process convergence audit d5d7ff81 section 6 rows a3 and a7) and carries 0-4. Part 1 of the group (#3612, topic r11-pre-round-metrics-p1) landed the two held-out instruments; this part lands the flow reads.

- `tools/audit/seat/round_metrics.py` (new, code-owned): 0018 section 2's `lead_time` (clock read from the commit that first added `"group": "<G>"` to a roster file at the roster ref, never a filled field), `product_green` over the window with `tools/ci/gate.py`'s `REQUIRED["push"]` count at the window's two ends beside it, `restore` (time to restore), `runner_s` (job seconds per merge) and `tokens` (`tokens_per_change` over a `tokens.tsv` ledger), per round (`--round N`: tag v(N-1).0.0 to vN.0.0 or now, decision 0016) and per week (`--weeks`). It is the tracked form of the audit's scratch `W/merges.py` and `W/agg.py` (merges by `machinery_ratchet.diff_stats` class), and the scorecard's input producer (`produce`: runs, job listings, verdicts, merges, roster; one REST batch, job listings cached per run attempt).
- `tools/audit/seat/scorecard.py` (now code-owned, as the enumerator 0018 names for `product_green`): its gate read takes a run's latest attempt (shared `round_metrics.gate_conclusions`) and it prints round_metrics' lines over the open round as `R` lines; lead-time percentiles per class, the time-to-restore line and the token line are those.
- `tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py`: the `scorecard` row runs the producer before the report (a failed producer is `scorecard: UNREADABLE produce`, and the report then does not run on stale inputs); a new `ci-attempt` row (carry 4) flags a ci.yml run at attempt 20 or more among the newest 100, naming the run, its branch and its pull request. Both rows are in `beatd.jobs.json`.
- `tools/audit/seat/bottleneck_check.py` (row a7): a held breach prints its live line while the value is more than a quarter worse than the value its first line printed (lower is worse for yield and throughput), its first line otherwise. Merge-wait now prints "hours": the digest's `norm()` blanks "<n> h" as an age, so at the base the digest never showed a merge-wait value at all (Figures).

Carries: carry 0 and carry 2 (same text): every enumerator built here is code-owned in `.github/CODEOWNERS` in this pull request, built to section 2's clock, windows and denominators, a partial ledger is a NO-READ (a concluded run with no job listing makes `product_green` and `restore` unread; one CI run without its listing makes `runner_s` unread; a seat class without a ledger row makes `tokens` unread), and the definitions it cannot meet are the cards below. Carry 1 and carry 3 (same text): the two held-out instruments landed with #3612; this part builds `product_green` over the round's window with the gate's check count beside it, the `lead_time` clock from the roster commit, and runner seconds per merge, each unread on an empty input. Carry 4: the `ci-attempt` row; its self-test fires on the #3287 window (PR #3319's runs 42469369199 and 42469369682, the code run at attempt 44, per `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-SWEEP-SETTLE-LOOP.md`) and is silent at attempts 1 and 19; the fixer.md rule drafted with it is not built, as the carry says. Carries 5-8 are part 2's and are not answered here. Carry: R11-PRE-ROUND-METRICS

## Cards

Definitions of 0018 that cannot be met as written, returned rather than bent:

- **C5 lead_time has no clock for a merge outside every roster.** A hotfix or record branch whose pull request no roster group names (by `resume.pr`, else by branch) never entered a roster, so 0018's clock does not exist for it. merges.subject: Merge pull request #3649 from tvofi/fix/r11-outside-apply-plan-ceiling
merges.title: R11-OUTSIDE-APPLY-PLAN-CEILING: apply plan only up to the manual-plan window
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
Closes #3636

"Apply this plan" failed whenever the published plan had a run starting 20 hours or more from now. The card's `apply()` trimmed the draft at the edit floor only, so it sent runs past the manual-plan window that the editor itself would not let the user touch, and `build_override` in `manual_plan.py` refuses any slot starting past now plus the window. The card now drops every run starting at or after `ceilingParts().applyEnd` (now plus the published `manual_plan_window_hours`) less `APPLY_CLOCK_SKEW_MS`. It does not use `editCeiling`, which also takes the zoomed visible end into account, so a zoomed-in view does not change what is applied. The lower bound is unchanged. A run straddling the window is still sent whole, because the backend frees every step past the expiry itself. The backend refusal is untouched: it protects the stored plan across restarts.

Clock skew: the card measures the window from the browser's clock and the service measures it from the server's. `APPLY_CLOCK_SKEW_MS` is one plan step (`PLAN_STEP_MS`). Runs start on step boundaries, so holding back a run that starts in the last step before the ceiling costs at most one step of pinned time before the expiry, and a browser clock up to one step fast is still accepted. If the browser clock is slow, the card only drops runs the server would also have accepted, so nothing is sent that the server refuses. Alternatives considered: (a) relaxing the backend refusal, which the brief rules out because a slot starting past the window corrupts the stored plan at the next restart; (b) clamping a run's start to the ceiling instead of dropping it, which would invent a slot the plan never had; (c) no skew allowance, which leaves the reported failure reachable on any browser clock that runs fast (mutant M2 below).

No user-facing text changes. Release note for the stamper: credit the reporter, GitHub user rasenschachmatt, for the report and the suggested fix.

## Head

`c57638046f9d2477d761e8da56327369f8a9a4fe` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

Review round 2: the delta since the reviewed head 87a315a355faa219065ed906ed3adbd4d589aacd is one commit that touches only `tests/card.mjs`; no production change. It adds two checks to the #3636 block. `a zoomed-in view does not change the applied runs (#3636)` zooms the view so the visible end is 3 h before the window (`geomAt` returns `windowEnd` 3 h before the ceiling). It requires `editCeiling()` to be at or before that point and the dhw payload to stay `[[-4,-3],[-2,0.5]]`. `a run starting two steps before the window is sent (#3636)` seeds a space run `[-0.5, 1]` h from the ceiling and requires it to be sent. The first check pins the design choice that the ceiling is `applyEnd` and not `editCeiling()`; the second pins that the skew allowance is no wider than one step. The block's `extended()` and `applied()` helpers gained an optional seeded-run set and an optional geometry so the two checks reuse them.

merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
Refs #3616: the planning defect its diagnostics showed, not the issue's multi-zone request, which stays open for the room-level steps the owner's reply lists. No `Closes`.

A floor-return reading seeded the slab estimate every cycle (`ThermalModel.update_slab_from_return_temp`, merged 0.7 sensor / 0.3 model) behind only the `FLOOR_WATER_RANGE_C` range check. A heat-pump return on a buffer plant in that field reads far above any floor loop, so the slab estimate believes heat is stored and the plan holds none. New pure module `slab_seed.py` owns the decision:

- **Bound** `SLAB_SEED_MAX_ABOVE_ROOM_K = 12.0` (argued in its comment): floor-loop water runs 3-9 K above room air (the band the `lower_floor_modelled` repair already states); EN 1264's surface limits (29 C occupied, 33 C bathroom, over 20 / 24 C design rooms) put the floor 9 K above its room; 3 K margin for a manifold sensor and a peripheral zone. A reading more than 12 K above the room is refused.
- **Model estimate**: a refused reading leaves the slab to the model's own estimate, by the exact path an install with no floor-return sensor takes (`_async_learn_interval(slab_unsensed=True)`, then `_propagated_slab` or the room+1 K first seed). Measured identical below (refused arm == unconfigured arm, slab trajectory and plan).
- **Hot-water runs and defrost**: a reading is refused while the pump's observed mode is hot water alone (`slab_seed.hot_water_run`: `mode_observed`, `dhw`, not `space_heat`) or a defrost is flagged (asked of the `defrost_standoff` owner, `freq_control.defrost_interval`, per `tests/entities.py`'s P2 registry).
- **Repair** `floor_return_implausible`, a `ConfigNotices` warning naming the sensor, its reading, the room and the bound; raised on the level alone (a hot-water or defrost refusal is the plant working, not a wrong sensor) and cleared on the next plausible cycle. No stored option is migrated.
- **Texts**: the floor-return option description (config and both options pages, en/de/sv) says which sensor belongs there and states the bound; README's sensor table says the Optimal Setpoint is the step's planned power scaled onto the coldest..warmest acceptable range (`HeatPumpOptimizer._power_to_setpoints`), not a target temperature, and its repair list gives the new repair a home.

Timing (decision): the coordinator seeds the published state before this cycle's pump signals are read, so the first call (`slab_seed.seed`) judges on last cycle's signals, and `slab_seed.judge`, after the signals are read, re-decides on this cycle's before the slab is finalised. Alternatives that lost: moving the pump-signal read above the floor-return read reorders the reader's health snapshot and every learner between; seeding only after the signals are read moves what the learners between see, so plausible installs would not stay byte-identical.

The bound is one-sided: a reading below the room is not refused. That direction plans more heat, not none, and no report shows it; out of this fix's scope.

## Head

`74a57885a3ef178f2556b4b105063a2b3a2edd9a` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

The code below is unchanged from the measured tree; this body re-renders the figure block at this head against the PR's recorded base `5825e1346c14eecace5c87c046558774145a94dc` (origin/main at the re-render is 6aa7ddc712, which `git merge-tree --write-tree` merges with this head without a conflict; 2026-11-16T02:05Z).

## Mutation proof

Block: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/seat/features_block.py --prelude "exec(open('<prelude>').read())" '# --- #3616: an implausible slab seed'`, prelude from `features_block.py --emit-prelude <prelude> '# --- #3616: an implausible slab seed'`. - A plausible floor-loop return (26 C, 6.4 K above a 19.6 C room) still seeds the slab unchanged: it converges on the merge's return + 1 K fixed point (`[26.55, 26.86, 26.96, 26.99, 27.0, 27.0]` at both ends), raises no repair, and plans 11.22 kWh at the merge base and at the head.

Head: `12.689 kWh`, slab equal to the unconfigured install's.

The class is a reading that seeds a model state for a different physical quantity than it measures. `FLOOR_RETURN_TEMP` (water, seeding the slab): closed here. `INDOOR_TEMP`, `LOWER_FLOOR_TEMP`, `OUTDOOR_TEMP`, `DHW_TEMP`, `BUFFER_TANK_TEMP`, `WOOD_TANK_TOP`, `WOOD_TANK_BOTTOM`: each seeds the quantity it measures, outside the class. `MIXING_VALVE_TARGET` (a set-point read as a room temperature): already guarded by the `valve_target_above_comfort` repair. `SOLAR_RADIATION`, `ENERGY`, `POWER`, `HOUSE_POWER`: not temperatures, seed no thermal state.

R11-PRE-PLAN-RENDER (part 1): the plan page shows every phase of the round.
Group R11-PRE-PLAN-RENDER, roster lane IN, size M; owner directive (tvofi, 2026-11-15): "Make the plan html show all phases in the round".
The round's phases are drawn from a tracked, linted per-round file, never from round-specific code.

Until now the plan page drew roster groups only. Between a round's start and its fix roster, it showed nothing of the round. This change adds `tools/audit/seat/plan_phases.py`, which owns the phases file, its refusals and its section. `plan_page.py` draws that section above the group lanes. Round 11's own file, `dev/programme/round11/phases.json`, holds the round's state as of 2026-11-15 13:00Z.

- The file is `dev/programme/round<N>/phases.json`: the round, `as_of`, and one entry per playbook phase (`dev/audit/README.md`, "Running a round: the playbook" and "Round start"). The phases, in the playbook's order, are round start, finders, verify and judge, the architect plan, fix waves, stamps and closure. Each entry carries a status (not started, running, waiting on a named thing, done), started and finished dates, an optional forecast window with its basis, entry and exit text, and items.
- The schema refuses: an unknown status or phase; a phase out of the playbook's order or repeated; `waiting` with nothing named; a date that is not ISO-8601 UTC; a started or finished date on a not-started phase; a finished date on a phase not done; and a forecast with no basis. `plan_phases.py --check FILE` exits 1 on any of them.
- The page draws a phase the file does not list as "not started", never omits it. A date the file does not carry is a dash. The page prints no date or count the file does not carry. Items are drawn under every phase not done.
- One page: the phases section plus everything `plan_page.py` drew before, unchanged (owner, 2026-11-15: "The generic plan page should support showing fixer groups as per normal in addition to the phases"). The phases are drawn on the swimlanes' own time axis (`plan_page.time_axis`, the one axis function both use). A phase reaching past either end is cut there and labelled, for example "since Sun 15 Nov 05:22"; a phase or forecast wholly off the axis is named in its row, not drawn. The section says that the fix waves are the group lanes below; the round-start items name their groups and do not repeat their lanes. The page renders in three cases: groups and phases; phases only (a roster with no fix group yet, as at a round's start); and groups only (no phases file, drawn exactly as before).
- `plan_page.py --phases FILE` draws the named file. Without it, the page draws the checkout's highest-numbered `dev/programme/round<N>/phases.json`. An invalid file draws its section as PHASES UNAVAILABLE and the rest of the page still renders. A checkout with no phases file draws no section, so the page is unchanged.
- The page names the file by its checkout-relative path, never a host path, so `plan_public.py`'s privacy refusal still passes on a page with phases.
- `plan_phases.py --phases FILE --html OUT` draws the section alone as a page in the plan page's stylesheet, for a round with no plan.json at all. The published page is `plan_page.py`'s, with both halves.

What the plan beat needs to pick the file up: nothing new. The beat's `plan-beat` row runs `state_docs.py --plan`, which runs `plan_page.py --repo <its checkout>`. Discovery reads `dev/programme/round*/phases.json` from that checkout's working tree, so the round-11 phases appear once the beat's checkout is at a main that holds this merge. Keeping the phases current is an edit to that file on main: the orchestrator's record step, like the roster.

Roster carries of R11-PRE-PLAN-RENDER, each named. Carry 0 (round filter), Carry 1 (next-round tab with its own preliminary Gantt), Carry 2 (the two-tab prototype as the model), Carry 3 (description, strip and lede counts), Carry 4 (PC-1113-05) and Carry 5 (plan-beat items P753 and P794) are the group's later parts, and this change leaves their text and scope as written. Today's behaviour is byte-identical with no phases file (measured below), the phases section is self-contained so a tab can host it unchanged, and no beat change is needed.

Carry 6 (the owner's directive to show every phase of the round) is built here, apart from two of its items that remain on the group for its next part. First, phase dates from the plan's duration model: this change takes dates only from the phases file, where a forecast must name its basis, and adds no constant and no duration. Second, the page for a round with no plan: this change renders a roster with no groups (the "phases only" arm), but `replan.py` refuses round 10's plan now that VERSION is 10.0.0, so the beat's page stays at its 06:19 snapshot until round 11's roster exists.

## No functionality of today's public page lost

Owner, 2026-11-15: "No functionality from the public plan version today should be lost". This is measured, not asserted.

- Today's public page is `git show origin/handoff/audit-r10-plan:handoff/round10/state/PLAN.html`, the newest state ref's page (state ref ef9c9068, snapshot 15 Nov 06:19 UTC, sha1 3d2752f7b784). It is what `plan_public.py stage` publishes now, because round 10's state ref is the newest.
- Its inputs: the plan.json the beat drew it from (generated.start 2026-11-15T06:19:00Z, roster blob 4b083262, sha1 edc40ce32bfd), the roster at commit 47364eb0 (the commit holding that blob), and one GitHub snapshot taken through `plan_page.fetch_github` (sha1 21875573ab86). The roster ref is a commit SHA, rendered with `--no-fetch` from a scratch clone that holds no phases file.
- The inventory instrument is `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r11_plan_page_inventory.py BASE OTHER...`. It lists every heading, table header row, legend entry, filter control, element id, class name, data attribute, event listener, link shape and the chart-bar tooltip, with digit runs read as `#`. It then prints MISSING and ADDED per other page. Its null control is the public page against itself: `missing=0 added=0`.
- No phases file: origin/main's `plan_page.py` (b3831ff6) and this head's, on the same three inputs, give byte-identical pages. The check was `cmp mainx-nophases.html headx-nophases.html && echo BYTE-IDENTICAL`, which printed BYTE-IDENTICAL. Inventory, public page against this head with no phases file: `RESULT other=headx-nophases.html missing=0 added=0`.
- With `--phases dev/programme/round11/phases.json`: `diff` against main's page shows one hunk, `114a115,129`, which is the phases section inserted and nothing else changed. Inventory: `RESULT other=headx-phases.html missing=0 added=9`. The nine added items are the section's own: heading "Round # phases", the phases table header, `id: phases`, `data-phase`, and the classes forecast, items, nowline, open and phase.
- `plan_public.refusal` over the page with phases returns None, and `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/plan_public.py --self-test` prints "all checks passed".
- Self-test arm "groups and phases: the page is the groups-only page plus the phases section, every section, table and control of it kept" asserts `both.replace(section, "", 1) == groups_only`. Mutant `phases-keep-groups-page` drops the Flow section when phases are present, and is killed.

- class: alerts; bar; barlab; blk; blocked; chip; chk; closed; closelab; closeline; closer; cpnote; d; done; end; filters; g; grid; grp; held; issarea; lane; lanec; lanelab; legend; live; mono; note; occ; pill; ready; scroll; slotcap; st; stamplab; stampline; stat; strip; sub; tick; tier; tip

- table: Batch (UTC) | Skipped | Why | State; Group | Description | Status | Tier | PR | Issues | Blocked by | ETA (UTC) | Wave; Group | Status | PR | ETA; PR | Kind | Wait | Verdict at merged head; Version | Projected (UTC) | Carries | Kind; wave | opens (UTC) | last merge (UTC) | groups | stamp it cuts

Classification: `plan_phases.py` joins `tests/entities.py`'s recorded closure beside `plan_page.py` (`tests/closure.py` INERT_EXCEPT and `tests/closures.json`). The reason: `state_docs.py`'s self-test runs `plan_page.py`, which imports it. The same route was taken for `topic_grammar.py`. The phases file is classified in `tests/layout.json` as `dev/programme/round*/phases.json`. It stays inert under the `dev/programme/` prefix, because no gate script reads a real phases file: the self-tests use fixtures in a throwaway checkout.

## Head

`b0f13c832f425ce5f49df540f0222c5e39ed7b54` merges the authored code head `155036423dab9c6f2724dbfec9df815eb201d7ec` and then merges origin/main `47f0f18a7e` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

155036423dab9c6f2724dbfec9df815eb201d7ec, the reviewed repair head c0db6bce48 merged with origin/main (921214bf42). The only content conflict was `tests/layout.json` (the `dev/programme` entry's `why`), resolved as the union of both sides; the resolution delta is that file alone, plus main's own files. `python3 tests/layout.py` and `tests/entities.py` (2723 checks) pass; `tools/pr/prepr.sh` rc=0 at this head.

## Class repair: a file `--check` accepts is a file the page draws

Defect (reviewer): `plan_phases.violations` left text fields untyped, so a phases file `--check` accepts crashed `plan_phases.section` (reached from `plan_page.render`, `plan_page.py:710`). The instance was `entry: 5`. Measured at the prior head, driving the old validator over every node of a full file with junk values: `entry`, `exit`, `detail`, `note`, `basis` and `waiting_on`/`name` as numbers or lists crashed `html.escape` (AttributeError), and a list, dict or `{}` as `status` or `phase` crashed `violations` itself (TypeError: unhashable), as did `items` not a list (not iterable).

Fix, one owner: `plan_phases.violations` types every text field the section prints (`_TEXT_DOC`, `_TEXT_PHASE`, `_TEXT_ITEM`; a forecast's `basis` and an item's `name` with their presence checks), `items` as a list and `status` as a string before it is a dictionary key. Alternative not taken: `str()` or `html.escape(str(x))` at the draw sites. It would turn a number into text silently and leave `violations` crashing on an unhashable status; refusing at the file is the one place the contract lives.

Enumeration rule (fixer.md step 8): the census `_census` in `plan_phases.fixture_checks` takes every node of a fully populated phases file (`_nodes`, not a list of field names) and replaces it with each of the ten junk values `_JUNK`; each result either earns a violation or draws in `section` (with the plan page's axis and without), and `violations` never raises. It asserts that the fixture populates every field the section reads, so a field the section starts reading has to be in the fixture. Every node the rule returns is closed: the count is asserted equal to `len(_JUNK) * (nodes - 1)` in the check "phases census: null control" (the number it ran is in its `got`, not carried here).

`as_of` in `dev/programme/round11/phases.json` is not refreshed: it records the orchestrator's state as of 2026-11-15T13:00Z (items such as the pull request and card counts), and a seat refreshing the date without re-measuring each item would make the file say something unmeasured. Carry: dismissed: the phases file is the orchestrator's record step, as stated above.

- Under step 6, this is the guard predicate's unguarded domain. The body says no gate script reads a real phases file, and the file is hand-edited on main. So nothing stops an edit that passes `--check` from taking down the beat's page.
- Fix shape, not prescribed: refuse a non-string in each text field inside `violations`, with a self-test arm and a mutant for it.

merges.body:
Main red, instrument (the main-red exception to the round-11 instrument freeze). Every ci.yml push run on main on 2026-11-15 ended `failure` or `cancelled` in `governance / instrument-self-tests`, for two causes, both repaired here.

**(1) The drift step's four refusals.** `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` missed reads main measured: the `dirs` of `dependency-graph-census` and `prepr` and the `.gitattributes` probes of `policy-lint-mutants` under `dev/audit/yardstick`, `dev/audit/yardstick/round10` and `dev/audit/rounds/round10/objective` (directories #3611 added at 646352ff), and `selftest-scope-mutants`' probe `-c`. Re-recorded the way `selftest_scope.py`'s docstring states ("Commit that file, or re-record ... and union the same way"): run 43741911544's `selftest-closures` artifact 14174287444 (main 755b7f57; zip sha256 `21243679cf94a01cb833960c4284ab52db371963081a12c6ff6f690d4b0645da`, the digest that job's log prints) unioned over main's committed table by `selftest_scope.union_record`, so `finder-overlap` and `plant-recall`, gated after that run, keep their committed entries. The diff adds exactly the ten reads the four refusals name and nothing else.

**`selftest_scope`'s own self-test does not fail.** The `FAIL` lines and the `TypeError` in job 132896968023 are the output of `selftest_scope_mutants.sh`, which prints each mutant's failing checks; that step ended "SELFTEST-SCOPE MUTANTS: every mutant refused" and passed, and the unmutated self-test step printed `selftest_scope self-test: 118 checks, 0 failed`. The `TypeError` is the "prune goes on over an unreadable table" mutant: with the `table is None` guard deleted, `prune_entries(None, ...)` raises before its `ck` line, so the mutant is killed by rc 1, not by a named check. No code defect, so no failing test was owed; the union guard of #3551 is not implicated.

**(2) The 60-minute cap on a push.** Six of main's eleven push runs on 2026-11-15 were cancelled at 60.2-60.3 minutes, the other five finished in 34.5-52.9. The variance is the runner host, not the tree: the in-line steps ran about 2.3x slower on some hosts (job 132905064799, `northcentralus`) than on others (job 132896968023, `centralus`) at near-identical heads, while the mutant step (1.0-1.4 min) and the drift fold (4.3-6.0 min) stayed flat. Every cancelled run had reached the mutant step at 57.2-59.8 minutes, which projects to about 67 minutes uncensored.

Slowest steps (min-max over the eleven runs): self-tests-outside-seat 4.9-11.6, policy-lint-mutants 2.9-7.7, the drift fold 4.3-6.0, cloud-relay 2.3-5.1, verdict-bus 1.9-4.9, ci-predictor 1.7-3.9, beat-job-rows 1.4-2.9, merge-train 1.6-2.7.

Options and the wall each buys:

merges.title: R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES: r10 start counter edges
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES: part D of pull request #3420. Thanks to Bankaifan, who reported that the compressor start counter misses short cycles: a compressor that stops and restarts between two samples counts no start. Built on the approved design (`design/R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES` at 18655c84b6; `Design review: approve` at `design-verdict/R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES` 9900aa0068).

The counter used to sample the meter once per refresh in `_record_accuracy` and needed `START_HYSTERESIS_SAMPLES` (2) consecutive samples. It now folds the confirmed edges of `running_signal.py`, a new HA glue module. That module is the one owner of the running signal for a pump in every duty mode, duty mode off included, from the coordinator's construction (`__init__`, after the unload registration) to its release (`_release_registrations`). It owns the state listener, `wear.EdgeTracker`'s debounce, a confirm timer at `EDGE_DEBOUNCE_S`, and the subscribers: the start counter always, and the duty-switch learner while the arbiter listens. The sampled path is deleted, not kept beside it. The coordinator gains no attribute (`coordinator_multiassigned_attrs` 108 -> 107).

- **Stored counts continue.** `lifetime`, `months` and `running` keep their stored shape and `from_dict` reading, so no migration is owed. A counter is unrestored until `_async_load_ledger`'s `finally` restores it. Until then it queues edges, and the restore replays them over the stored `running`: a compressor running across the upgrade is not counted again, and an edge before the read is neither lost nor counted twice.
- **No signal counts nothing.** An unavailable, unknown or non-numeric reading is a `None` class, and the last known class holds across it. On the meter source the reader reads `None` while the immersion element runs: by the coordinator's latch, or by the reading itself being over `thermal_model.immersion_over`, now the one owner of what over means for the latch, the carve-out and the reader.
- **Premise correction (design section 4).** `_effective_cycling_cost` reads `_wear_price` (replacement cost over rated starts) and no count. The counted starts feed the wear ledger line (only at a nonzero price), the month receipt's `compressor_starts` and the insight payload. So the plan is unchanged by construction, and the count is where the null control sits.
- **Source change on an install with both a frequency sensor and a meter**: the counter now reads the frequency sensor, as part A's learner does. The retired path read the meter.
- **Release frees the coordinator.** `running_signal.detach` drops the subscribers and the reader. Both close over the coordinator, which is the weak key of the table holding them. Without that, a released coordinator was never collected (features.py's "a released coordinator is collected" read 8 referrers at the first head of this branch).
- **The refresh-held start (S7, owner ruling D1, 2026-11-15).** On the meter source a confirmed rise is not a start until `wear.HOLD_REFRESHES` (2) refreshes read the signal settled running (`wear.RiseHold`, held in front of `StartCounter.fold` by `StartCounter.hear` and `StartCounter.refresh`). A no-class edge first drops it: an element cut-in on an averaging meter reports one partial average between the on-threshold and the over level, confirmed as a rise, then over, which reads no class. A stop first passes the rise on with the stop when it rose from a stop (a run shorter than two refreshes still counts, at its own time), and drops it when it rose from no class (an element's falling average as it cuts out). The frequency source holds nothing. `running_signal.refresh` owns the per-refresh re-read and hands each subscriber's tick whether the class reads settled running, so the coordinator's refresh path is still one line. Alternatives and why each lost: the residual (owner ruling D1 refused it); the hold in the coordinator's refresh path (+3 coordinator-class lines, +1 `seam_cut_total`, a `_book_starts` call crossing into the ledger seam from `_update_current_state`: refused by `tests/structure.py`, paid by moving the tick into `running_signal`); a stop always passing the held rise on (counts the cut-out partial, killed by the S7 check); a stop always dropping it (loses every run shorter than two refreshes, the short cycles the counter exists for, killed by the blip check and the S7 control). What the hold costs: a meter start is counted up to two refresh periods late, still in the month of its first reading; a start whose rise is dropped by a meter outage inside the hold is counted again only if the meter returns reading running (a rise from no class).
- The module's import set is `wear`, `drift`, `entry_config`, `freq_control`, `inputs` and `thermal_model` (design-review carry v2). `duty_switch` imports it; it imports neither `duty_switch` nor `pump_arbiter` (pinned in features.py).

Carry 0 (owner ruling 2026-11-13, part D fired now; to round 11 if not merged when the stamp is ready): no stamp is held on this branch. origin/main was merged in twice: at 5b8f05ba4e (e8d71a241f), and at 4058469d79 (43227286fc, pull request 3532's leg rule), where `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reported conflicts in `duty_switch.py` and `tests/features.py`; see `## Head`. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 43227286fc` at 4058469d79 reports no conflict. It was merged a third time, at e901e9ef29 (7d3ab93eed), after the fix review's block; see `## Head`.

## Null control

Instrument: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests python3 dev/audit/harnesses/start_counter_edges.py`. It replays the same synthetic meter traces through the production coordinator: at the merge base (a `git archive` export) through the sampled path, at the head through the edge path, with a refresh every `DEFAULT_OPTIMIZATION_INTERVAL`.

- **Control** (every on and off phase spans at least two refresh periods, no start within one period of a month boundary): `control=3` at the base and `control=3` at the head. The same count, and so the same wear lines and month receipt.
- **Perturbation** (one 5-minute stop and restart inside one refresh period): `perturbed=3` at the base, `perturbed=4` at the head. Exactly one more.
- **Lifecycle** (one start before the ledger read lands, stored lifetime 7): `restored=7` at the base, where `from_dict` overwrote the sampled start, and `restored=8` at the head.

- **S7** (owner ruling D1), run at 092746903f (a `git archive` export) and at the head: `s7_60s` 5 / 0 and `s7_30s` 5 / 0, the reviewer's rows unchanged in the harness. Because those rows run no refresh, they would read 0 for a hold that never released, so the harness gains `s7r_60s` 5 / 0 and `s7r_30s` 5 / 0 (a refresh every period, one landing between the partial's confirmation and over, the element running three periods and cutting out through a partial) and their null control `s7r_real` 6 / 6 (the same rig and refreshes with a real compressor start at each offset). Control 3 / 3, perturbed 4 / 4 and restored 8 / 8 between 092746903f and the head, so the rows the verdict reports are unchanged.

The features.py block asserts the head side of each with the production symbols (red at the base, where `running_signal` and `StartCounter.fold` do not exist). Plan invariance is pinned there as a regression ("the counted starts are what the cycling cost and the plan never read"), not claimed as a control. No missed-start figure for real installs is claimed. The sampled path's cadence is a rule, not a measurement: one sample per refresh (`optimization_interval`, default `DEFAULT_OPTIMIZATION_INTERVAL`, plus any requested refresh), two consecutive samples per class change. So any run or stop shorter than about two refreshes was invisible. The contributor's own count was not verifiable from anything in the tree (design carry n4).

`tools/pr/ci_predict.py` replayed each touched instrument-self-tests step at the head under a fixed 180 s bound and turned a timeout into rc 124; `step_replay_preds` read rc 124 at the head and 0 at the base as a predicted red, so `prepr.sh` refused clean branches on a loaded host (#3598's update and the owner-criteria opener, 2026-11-15, CI green for those steps). A timeout measures the host, not the head. Now `replay_step` returns `TIMED_OUT` (-124, never a bash rc), a head timeout is reported as the info line `UNMEASURED <step>: timed out at <s> s on this host` and is not replayed at the base or predicted. The bound is `HPO_STEP_REPLAY_TIMEOUT_S` (default 180, unparseable or non-positive falls back to 180). A real non-timeout red is predicted exactly as before. A base timeout keeps its existing path (non-zero at the base: a note left to CI).

`tools/audit/seat/plant_recall.py` plants a held-out seat's objective bugs into the baseline export and counts recall after the judge; `tools/audit/seat/finder_overlap.py` seats a twin finder on one scopes.json seat's universe and estimates the bugs there from the judged-real overlap, reported with both seats' models. Each is self-tested in `instrument-self-tests` (steps `plant-recall`, `finder-overlap`, read sets recorded by `selftest_scope.py record`), code-owned in `.github/CODEOWNERS` (carry 0), and its run commands, before the Finders phase and after the judge, are in its `tools/audit/seat/instruments/*.py.md` page (the documented command the orchestrator runs; `audit-find.js` is not edited). The plants themselves are not written here.

Carry 0: both instruments are added to `.github/CODEOWNERS` in this pull request and built to 0018's definitions; the ones they cannot meet are the cards below. Carry 3: this part builds its two held-out instruments, recall counted after the judge (a plant lost at the verifier or the judge is a miss) with plants refused unless spread over both the natural universe and the configuration space and refused from a finder, orchestrator or evaluator planter, and the overlap reported with the two seats' models; carry 3's section-2 and section-5 reads (`product_green` over the window with `gate`'s check count, the `lead_time` clock from the roster commit, runner seconds per merge) stay with the group's later parts, as this part's brief scopes them out. Carry: R11-PRE-ROUND-METRICS

## Cards

Definitions of 0018 that cannot be met as written, returned rather than bent:

- **C1 isolated dimensions take no plant.** Section 5 plants into "the baseline export"; `audit-find.js` runs D0, D3, D9, D11, D13, D14 and D15 in `git worktree`s, where `git diff` shows every plant to the finder. `plant` refuses a tree inside a git work tree, meaning the tree itself or any ancestor of its resolved path holding a `.git` directory or file (a linked worktree's or a submodule's), so neither those worktrees nor any subdirectory of one takes a plant; a work tree with no `.git` entry on that path (its git directory named only by `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` or `core.worktree`) is outside the guard, and `audit-find.js`'s `git worktree add` writes the `.git` file it reads. Recall is read over the export's dimensions only and the seven isolated ones have no recall. Owner choice: accept that, or plant those worktrees as a commit the wall hides (not built).
- **C2 when a finding "finds" a plant.** 0018 defines recall as found / planted and names no matching rule. Built: a judged finding names a plant when its `files` hold the plant's file and the plant's `symbol` is a whole word of its `instrumented_symbol`, `title` or `claim`; every match is printed with the finding ids so the rule can be audited per plant.
- **C3 the overlap is counted after the judge.** Section 5 says "finding n1 and n2 with m shared" without a stage. Built as recall is (section 4 item 3): a seat's finding counts when its canonical finding is judged `verified` or `weakened`, and m is the bugs the judge's dedup merged across the two seats.
- **C4 the models are declared, not recorded.** No round record holds a seat's model (`finding.schema`, `JUDGE.json`, `reports-<box>.json`); the pair record carries the models the orchestrator dispatches with, which nothing re-reads.

Answers `Fix review: blocked 56a8a61b92480e770943483d37f08306ae4ee694 class-open` (probe/rev-3612-86286f2c), from ebd654c3.

- **Block: the `.git` guard read only the tree's root.** `refusals()` now walks the tree's resolved path and every parent and refuses at the first holding `.git`, a directory or a file. The table `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` is recorded here as that union over main's own measurement, which turns main's red drift step green.

## Re-cut

Fifth-round body, replaced. Round history is dropped; every figure below is taken at the head named. The re-cut follows P762 and roster carry 9: the table-shrink guard is dropped (`shrink_drops`, `table_base`, `shrink_gaps`, its `static` hook, its fixtures and mutants). The self-test's environment hold and the `main` return-type wrapper go too, because only the guard's base selectors needed them. The union record, `prune` and their tests stay.

The verdict also lists the reviewer's own killed mutants. Two of their predicates stay: the gated-step filter of `union_record` and `prune`'s held-item checks. Both are now pinned by in-tree mutants (below). The third, the probe-is-a-file filter in `union_entry`, is removed as a defect (next paragraph).

Found in this pass and fixed here: `union_entry` dropped a probe that the union also held as a file. `drift` answers a measured probe from `probes` alone, so that union made the next drift run refuse it. Replaying main's measurement against a table written with the filter refused `tools/audit/round4/**` in `open-pr`, `pr-args` and `update-pr`, 3 refusals. Without the filter there are 0. The union is now pure. The `union_record` check expects the probe kept, and it fails on the filtered copy (`FAIL union_record: recording one step over an entry holding reads the trace lacks keeps them`).

## Head

`d95a2bc761b7ce0fb14f3ff4e239a8d045567557` merges the authored code head `8ccc59556f257b52e65c0e364957cf86c9d018c7`.

## Block

- **M3, the barrier's own predicate.** `tools/ci/selftest_scope.py` `shrink_gaps`: `{p for st, p in rows if st == "D"}` -> `{p for st, p in rows}`. This turns "only a path this diff deletes may" into "any path this diff touches may". It is not equivalent. ev/m3_behaviour.txt has a two-commit repository where the diff modifies `tools/x.py` and drops that step's read of it. Unmutated, `shrink_gaps` returns `SHRUNK step s: ... drops 1 files ... e.g. tools/x.py`. Under M3 it returns `[]`. No self-test or driver mutant pins the D-only rule: every `shrink_gaps` fixture's dropped paths are either unchanged or deleted, never modified. - **M1.** `table_base`: `["git", "merge-base", c, "HEAD"]` -> `["git", "rev-parse", c]`. The docstring says the merge base. The only fixture, `table_base(gr, {"SELFTEST_BASE": b0})`, names an ancestor of HEAD, where the two are equal. On a pull-request merge checkout they coincide while `origin/<base>` is the merge's own parent. They differ when the named base has moved past the branch: a local `SELFTEST_BASE=origin/main` on a stale branch would diff main's newer table changes in reverse and report them as SHRUNK. Round 10's objective record, which decision 0018 section 6 has the closing round write and which round 10's close did not write, written now under tvofi's ruling on card E11-N-OBJECTIVE-RECORD ("Write it now (Recommended)"). The record is `dev/audit/yardstick/round10/OBJECTIVE.json`, one row per term of `dev/audit/config/objective.json`. Its by-hand escapes ledger is `dev/audit/rounds/round10/objective/escapes_hand.tsv`; `escapes`, `injected` and `unowned` carry its counts as `by_hand` beside a NO-READ. The ledger sits under the round's directory, as the round-11 evaluation keeps its own under `dev/audit/rounds/round11/evaluation/`. The third change is one glob in `tests/layout.json`. No production, instrument or policy file changes, and nothing is closed by keyword.

## Summary

- **Window.** v7.0.0 (`9cb735dfc6`, 2026-10-14T13:27:06Z, subject `v7.0.0: stamp Round-9 closure`) to v10.0.0 (`13cbe48de4`, 2026-11-15T05:22:47Z): 0018 section 2 reads "from the previous closeout stamp to its own". That is 1210 first-parent commits, of which 1139 are merges.

Every roster-derived command in the record names this sha. The builders named in the record (R11-INTAKE-R10-RESIDUE, R11-PRE-ROUND-METRICS, R11-PRE-TOKEN-LEDGER) are carry-receivable groups of the roster `check_scopes.py` reads at the ref.

The other 12 are `no_read`, each with `would_read` and `builder`. The table in 0018 section 2 gives `none` as the enumerator for `regret`, `operation`, `unowned`, `escapes`, `injected`, `coverage`, `unexamined`, `lead_time`, `closure_slip` and `tokens_per_change`. The examined count of `generality` has none either. `product_green`'s named enumerator prints `A_gate  unread (runs.json)`.

Such a report is neither a judged finding nor an outside report, so it is no objective bug by 0018 section 2's definition. That breaks D2's operating-grid identity. D8 owns a published value, and the fix changed the plan, not only the slot attribute. The difference moves no term's value.

Alternatives that lost: retrying a red self-test once (refused in the RCA: hides a real intermittent defect, costs a job per red); an injected clock in beatd (the race is job ordering, not time). The one production line added to `bus.sh` confirm() touches `HPO_BUS_WAIT_MARK` only when set, so the arm can see the second confirm waiting on a live holder.

## Head

`62abeb4849dbb7443240fd9d879d970ff2f98780` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

## Mutation proof

Predicate mutated in place, then restored: in `bus.sh` confirm() the lock acquisition `until mkdir "$lk" 2>/dev/null; do` replaced by `mkdir -p "$lk"; until true; do`. `bash tools/audit/seat/bus.sh --self-test` then reports FAIL for: "a confirm under a live holder's lock waits and moves nothing (P354)", "two concurrent confirms produce one verdict commit and one post (P354)", "a lock whose pid is not yet written is a live holder inside the settle (P354)" (3 failed). beatd: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/beatd.py --self-test 9` reports "mutant m9_running_ignored turns (9) 'a running instance defers the restart to the next pass' red".

## Null control

Unmodified head: `bus.sh --self-test` 239 checks, 0 failed, including both existing P354 null controls (dead holder's lock taken over; empty pid past the settle taken over). `beatd.py --self-test 9`: 34 checks, 0 failed, including "null: with no restart taken the same job runs" and "null: behind only off the seat paths does not restart".

## Figures

- Instrument: 12 concurrent `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/beatd.py --self-test 9 --no-mutants` on one 4-core host with 6 CPU burners, counting runs with any FAIL line, `grep -l FAIL`. merges.body:
Round-11 record: the round-10 round-end proposal triage, as `proposal-triage.md` (on main since #3451) shapes it: one consolidated batch, ruled once per instrument, over three inputs together (tvofi, 2026-11-15: "it should triage all its instrument groups together with your proposals and local prototypes before starting instrument work, some might be unnecessary"), plus one root-cause record per tooling-friction family (loop card L8). tvofi ruled every decision card the batch raised on 2026-11-15; the rulings are recorded in the entries. It adds record files only and closes nothing by keyword.

## Summary

- **The batch.** `dev/programme/triage/r10-round-end.md`, entries P742-P795 (54). Inputs: the 47 unfinished groups on `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster` `80c1fb32c7` (every instrument group among them, the eight `deferred` ones, #3551, #3566, and the instrument carries on R10-PROCESS-SLIM, R10-SEAT-IDENTITY-P5, R10-OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE and R11-INTAKE-R10-RESIDUE); the round-10 orchestrator's proposals (PC-1113-01 to -23 and the unnumbered sweep candidates after the 2026-11-13 triage seat); the local prototypes and workarounds (HANDOVER's inventory, the landing chains, the wake filter, the closure runbook, the dispatch seats' scripts); the pickup seat's proposal, read as a lead. Rulings are checked against the code at `origin/main` `a39627da59`, not the logs' accounts.
- **Outcome.** Thirteen existing groups kept (several narrowed or widened by merged items), four new S groups (three hotfixes, each with a freeze ground, and R11-OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE-P3 as outside work), five deferred groups `absorbed` into kept ones, R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P3 `refused` with all 34 carries re-homed by index, R11-PRE-OBJECTIVE-FUNCTION closed as done (#3575), R11-INTAKE-R10-RESIDUE's instrument carries split by seam (P768), and every PC-1113 proposal ruled or shown owned.
- **Owner rulings.** tvofi answered all cards (C1-C15, O1, O2, Q1, Q2) on 2026-11-15 about 09:50-09:57Z; 18 entries carry an `Owner:` line with his verbatim choice. All took the recommended option except C9 ("Keep them locally and benchmark them against the train"), which changed P789 and P790 from a drop to a DEFER: the landing chains and `land.sh` stay session-local and R11-PRE-PARALLEL-PIPELINE owes a benchmark of per-pull-request merge wait (verdict-and-GREEN to the merge commit), chain against train, with the train's own entries as the null control and a decision rule fixed in advance. P750 and the scratch-instruments record were corrected to match. O1 admits the two kept round-10 groups (P755, P761) into the pre-finder set; Q1 and Q2 are production rulings recorded in the batch's header for findability.
- **Root-cause records.** Seven under `dev/audit/rca/`, one per friction family with three or more instances: `R10-RCA-FAMILY-SELFTEST-SCOPE-DRIFT.md`, `-POLICY-DOCS-TIMEOUT.md`, `-FIGURE-BLOCK-STALE.md`, `-PIPEFAIL-SIGPIPE.md`, `-FLAKY-SELFTEST.md`, `-RELAY-SERIAL-UPDATE.md`, `-SCRATCH-INSTRUMENTS.md`. Each names the cause, the process state with its evidence, a cost test with numbers and a countermeasure or a recorded refusal. Three of the families turned the required `gate` red (policy-docs timeout, figure block, flaky self-test). Families under the threshold get one line each in the batch's Part E; one count the round-10 orchestrator stated ("relay release line not honoured") did not reproduce and is recorded as such.
- **Classification.** Both new paths sit under prefixes on `INERT` in `tests/closure.py` (`dev/programme/`, `dev/audit/`) and under `tests/layout.json` globs (`dev/programme/triage/*.md`, `dev/audit/rca/**`).
- **Nothing built.** No production, test or instrument code; no roster edit. The orchestrator routes each ACCEPT through `roster_edit.py`, citing `triage: dev/programme/triage/r10-round-end.md#P<n>`.

## Head

`caa32492bc7a7b0512957f8df4f5d6153349dd6d` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`2e17928032f2d9b662cf5d771a4e0192f5a2def5`. Two commits on `origin/main` `a39627da59`: the batch with the seven records, then the owner rulings. Read the diff three-dot.

## Null control

The rulings are checked against the tree, and where the tree already answers a carry the batch says so rather than ruling it: R10-SEAT-IDENTITY-P5 carries 0-3 are on main (`tools/audit/seat/seat_gen.py`, the `loop-cwd` row in `tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py`), the scorecard's beat row is on main (`beat_jobs.py`, row `scorecard`), and R10-PREPR-DARWIN-SELFTEST-LANE's lane is replaced by the `darwin-selftest` row already merged by #3565. Of the 26 cards P1-P14, R1-R3 and L1-L9 checked, P13 alone reads fully built (`beat_jobs.py`, `0bfec38fa3`).
