merges.title: R10-COP-LEARNER-DRAW-FLOOR: r10 cop learner draw floor
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-COP-LEARNER-DRAW-FLOOR, built on the approved design (`design.md` at 94d2c9f06576693b31996d21d18af241d41640b2 of design/R10-COP-LEARNER-DRAW-FLOOR; `Design review: approve`, design-verdict at 732212c268). Three carries on the COP learner's one judgement seam, `MeasuredCop` in `accuracy.py`. `Carry N` below is entry N (0-based) of this group's `carry` list on handoff/audit-r10-roster at 30097de04722.

What ships, by carry:

- **Carry 0 (84e73ec4), the capped floor.** `draw_range.power_floor_kw(draw, params)` is the one floor `MeasuredCop.judge_floor`, `coordinator._fold_flow_lift` and `accuracy.diagnostics_view` read, each on the same window object. It is `flow_lift_power_floor_kw` capped by the low end (`LOW_PERCENTILE`) of the draws metered under a run ask, never under `on_threshold_kw`. A run ask is an ask at or above the window's configured minimum and above zero: `DrawRange._run_asked`, the pair reader `follows_ask` built inline and now shares. Invariants (a) to (f) of the design are each a check in `tests/features.py`.
- **Carry 1 (35931f4b), hold-then-replay.** `draw_range.ask_evidence` returns one of four states; `follows_ask` is that state as a tri-state, results unchanged. `MeasuredCop.judge_ratio` is an instance method on the interval's row (`accuracy.CopInterval`): a departure beyond `COP_ASK_TOLERANCE` is held while the evidence is pending and reads `COP_REFUSED_NO_EVIDENCE`, no new code. `MeasuredCop.release` is the one place a held row is judged: all fold on follows, none on does-not-follow, base's rule where the evidence is unobtainable, and while it is pending base's rule for a row older than `COP_HOLD_HORIZON_S` (a week) or pushed out of a hold of `draw_range.WINDOW` rows. A released row folds against the scale it was read at. `diagnostics_view` gains `held_intervals`.
- **Carry 2 (R10-COP-GATE-E band), measurement, no build.** Re-run at this head, `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_cop_gate_band.py` reads `fit=none` on both fixtures under `tests/replay/` and its `--synthetic` control fits. The carry stays open on the named owner data (`## Forward-carry`).
- **Carry 3 (issue 3106 item 4, the set-point-to-draw map), not built here.** It is the brief of R10-DRAW-MAP-EVIDENCE, a live group ordered after this one and built on this handoff; nothing in this diff touches `thermal_model.flow_setpoint_for_level` or `follows_ask`'s slope test. Carry: R10-DRAW-MAP-EVIDENCE
- **Carries 4 to 9 are this body's own items, routed back to this group for a ruling**, each still under `## Forward-carry` or `## Friction` with its text unchanged: Carry 4 (09c5aa75, departure 1), Carry 5 (5b2b2810, departure 2), Carry 6 (ade1b168, note n2), Carry 7 (870278d1, the unobtainable arm), Carry 8 (28d8e538, the cap reads run-asked draws only), Carry 9 (b4659e0c, the `fixer.md` contradiction). None is built in this round: each waits on the owner's or the orchestrator's decision.
- The walking metered/asked ratio moved from the coordinator to `MeasuredCop.walk_ratio` (design note n1), which pays for the coordinator lines the release adds.

**Departures from the design note, each made because the tree refused the note's letter. They are disclosed here for the reviewer and routed under `## Forward-carry` for a ruling.**

1. **Where the release runs.** The note calls `release` from `_learn_measured_cop`, after the interval's own refusal is written. There, the check "#1523 class check: every learner feeder in coordinator.py consults the freeze or carries a disposition" went red (`undispositioned ['_learn_measured_cop']`): a cycle the learners are frozen on would have moved the COP scale. The census accepts a disposition, but its key is the function name, and an entry for `_learn_measured_cop` would also excuse any later fold of present evidence written there (`fixer.md` step 14). So the route changed: the release runs in `_fold_measured_cop`, past the freeze gate and the missing-reading guard and ahead of the interval's own judgement. The census passes with no new disposition. Consequences: a frozen cycle and a cycle with no power reading release nothing, and the hold cannot grow on such a cycle either; released rows fold before the cycle's own interval, not after; the interval's code is still its own, because the replay's return value is discarded.
2. **A replay trains the scale alone.** The note folds each released row through `_fold_cop_evidence`. That function's tail feeds the capacity envelope from this cycle's `_measured_power`, `_commanded_power()` and outdoor bucket, none of which is the held interval's. A replay returns before that tail. Cost: a held departure asked at or above 0.95 of nameplate no longer feeds the envelope, which it did when base folded it at its own tick.
3. **The cap is keyed to the configured range.** `power_floor_kw` returns the configured figure while the window's `config` differs from the live parameters' range. The note's invariant (e) reverts the floor when `DrawRange.observe` clears the window, which is at the next running sample; until then the window's pairs were asked under the old minimum, and a raised minimum would read them as run asks. The check for (e) pins both.
4. **`thermal_model.py` is touched, docstrings only.** The note lists it as not touched and its note n3 asks for `flow_lift_power_floor_kw`'s reference to the judgement to be updated; that reference was false at the head, so two docstrings changed and no code.
5. **One harness row the note lists as a null moves.** `p4_follow_lag1tick` folds fewer intervals than at the base (`## Figures`). Its draw is the previous interval's ask, the window reads that as not following, and the departures base folded before the evidence are now held and dropped. That is carry 35931f4b's stated behaviour on a draw that does not follow its ask; the note's spike did not show the row.

One existing check changed its expectation: "with no draw evidence a departure folds only past the nameplate third ... folds on 4 kW, as base" asserted the base behaviour this carry removes. It now pins both arms: pending holds on 4 kW and on 14 kW, and with no window base's rule stands.

The save cadence of the thermal learning store reads `_cop_samples // 10` crossing, where it read `% 10 == 0`: a release folds several intervals in one cycle and can step over a multiple of ten.

## Head

`5723ce192e589a344de0ddb3b50929b19e90fec7` merges the authored code head `a472503fe19d7237d3701d9ac6b23e16bd0fb675`.

No finder harness: the group is an owner report (triage batch 238, P714). Part 1 is on main; the diff against main is this part's seven files.

## Re-cut

Replaced after the third blocked verdict (`Fix review: blocked 35ebd383cdc6909a17e808ba656b249e615b157e self-test-red`, nonce 06f0734c). Every figure below was taken in this pass at the head named under `## Head`; earlier rounds' text is deleted. The carries keep their numbers and wording, which the roster's folded items are keyed to.

What this round changes, against the verdict's one block:

1. **The cause.** `Train.policy_approval_due` asks `Train.fork_head` before any approval is due (this part's first commit `23b943c987`, decision 0017). The pre-flight's self-test world, `fake(world)` in `tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py`, answered no `gh api repos/o/r/pulls/7` read, so `fork_head` failed closed on every row reaching it under `--mandate`, and the self-test's own `due()` died on the uncaught Stop. The production path is not the defect: `PreFlight.entry` turns that Stop into `PARK outside`, and a head the pulls API does not answer for must park.
2. **The repair.** The fixture answers that one read with a pulls object, a branch of ours unless the case names another head repository, read by the real `tools/pr/outside.py`. No expectation of main's rows moved: the five failing rows pass unedited. Four rows are added: a cross-repository policy head under the `--mandate` parks at `policy` naming the head as cross-repository, `policy_approval_due` names no mandate for it, an unanswered pulls read parks at `outside`, and with no `--mandate` the pulls object is not read.
3. **The closures table.** `carry-check-and-the` re-recorded by `selftest_scope.py record --step carry-check-and-the` (strace): its entry gains the file `tools/pr/outside.py` and the probe `tools/pr`. The record's write also re-ordered the `probes` of six other entries with equal sets; those six are kept as main's bytes, so the table differs from the PR head `35ebd383`'s in that one step.
4. **The dispatch's premise is corrected.** The brief read the red as an interaction with what main merged since the reviewed head `b372f8e9`. It is not: the pre-flight rows are main's commit `9350dc7ce1` (2026-11-10), an ancestor of `23b943c987`, and the red starts at `23b943c987` itself (Null control). No main merge introduced it.

Alternatives, and why each lost (`fixer.md` step 17):
- **Stub `Train.fork_head` in the pre-flight self-test, as merge_train's older rows do.** That leaves the pre-flight's world blind to the read the train now makes, and the fork and unread arms unpinned from the pre-flight's side.
- **Move the `fork_head` call below the mandate read in `policy_approval_due`.** The five rows hold a mandate in force, so they reach the call in either order; and a refused fork head would first cost a mandate read it never needs.
- **Catch the Stop inside `policy_approval_due` and answer "ours".** That is the unread head taken for ours, which decision 0017 refuses.

## Head

In place at `6f41f0b563c3ba55371310b3c9bd567d67007d2f`, one predicate replaced, `python3 tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py --self-test` run, the file restored and the restored run printed. A kill is the self-test's `FAIL` lines and rc 1.

- `policy_approval_due`'s `if self.fork_head(pr) is not None:` to `if False:` (merge_train.py): `queue_pre_flight self-test: 57 checks, 3 failed`: `FAIL a cross-repository policy head under the --mandate PARKs on the review ...`, `FAIL ... and policy_approval_due names no mandate for it`, `FAIL a policy head whose pull request the pulls API does not answer for PARKs at \`outside\` ...`.
- `fork_head`'s unread-pull `raise Stop("outside", ...)` to `return None` (merge_train.py): `57 checks, 1 failed`, the unread row.
- `fork_head`'s `cross = _outside_gate().cross_repository(facts, self.repo)` to `cross = False` (merge_train.py): `57 checks, 2 failed`, the two cross-repository rows.

Four run, four killed. merge_train.py, merge_pr.sh and the remerge files are byte-equal to `35ebd383`'s, where the reviewer ran three of their mutants (three killed); none is re-run here.

## Red checks

- `governance / instrument-self-tests` at `35ebd383cdc6909a17e808ba656b249e615b157e`, step `carry-check-and-the` (`Show the carry check and the queue pre-flight refusing their own fixtures`), red at the head and green at the merge base: the pull request's finding (`defect-root-cause.md`), outside the `merge_train.py owed-reds` set. **Cause:** items 1 and 4 above. **Cheaper detector: exists, and was in no local path.** The step's own second command, `python3 tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py --self-test`, 0.15 s wall here, reads only the checkout. The detector the dispatch asked to be evaluated, that self-test at the handoff after a main merge, would have caught it but names the wrong moment: the red is this part's first commit's, so the detector is keyed on the diff, not on a merge. Its general form: at the handoff, run each `instrument-self-tests` step whose recorded `files` hold a path the diff changes. `prepr.sh` step 6d's self-test arm re-runs only each changed file's own self-test, and `queue_pre_flight.py` is unchanged by a diff to `merge_train.py`. **Standing cost:** for a diff changing `merge_train.py`, 23 steps, 1686 s summed over the `OK` lines of the traced run above (strace; `prepr` 461 s, `update-pr` 536 s, `merge-train` 186 s, `hooks-setup` 158 s, `pr-args` 120 s, `beat-job-rows` 106 s, the other 17 under 37 s each), per handoff; a diff to a file fewer steps read costs less. **Process state: (c).** Step 6d ran and passed at every head of this part while its self-test arm read one direction, the changed file's own self-test, and not the self-tests that read the changed file. merges.subject: Merge pull request #3599 from tvofi/fix/r10-hotfix-reference-basis
merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-REFERENCE-BASIS: bump the savings reference basis for the reference #3587 changed
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-REFERENCE-BASIS: a production hotfix that gates the v10.0.0 stamp. Pull request #3587 (merge 931970141c) changed the savings reference the ledger books for one install class, but `ledger.REFERENCE_BASIS` was not bumped. The class is a two-zone house behind a throttling (manual) valve whose curve is the bound. In cold hours with no sun, the first-step reference power rose by 1.12 to 1.15 %. Controls are bit-identical. The verification seat measured this at origin/main d7004eaa77 by calling `_compute_baseline_power` at 931970141c^1 and at 931970141c: +5, 0, -5 and -15 °C give +1.15 %, +1.13 %, +1.13 % and +1.12 %. Sun at 300 W/m2, an unvalved install, a single-zone valve and a plain house are all bit-identical.

The in-code rule at `ledger.py` says "Bump when the booked reference changes". `docs/dashboard-card.md` promises that "when an update changes how the baseline is booked, every month up to the update stops stating a saving". v7.1.17 shipped basis 2 with the pre-#3587 reference. Without this bump, a month first booked on v7.1.17 that keeps booking after the upgrade would sum two references into one saving.

**The change.** It mirrors the previous bump, 194625754d (basis 1 to 2), and its stale-pin deletion, fc372c8094:
- `REFERENCE_BASIS = 3` in `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/ledger.py`. Its comment now records what basis 2 was: a valve-limited two-zone house held at level floors below the plant's ceiling, released in v7.1.17, where #3587 holds it at the valve top.
- The features check `a month's first savings booking stamps the reference in force, once` pins the literal 3.0 and `_SB_NOW == 3`, so a bump stays deliberate.
- A new check reads a persisted stamp 2.0 as the old basis after a booking: no saving or percent, both columns kept, the stamp unchanged.
- A null-control check reads a stamp 3.0 as current after a booking.
- The killed-by pin `tests/mutation_ledger/killed_by/ledger.py/@module.CONST.1e17aeec.json` (`old: REFERENCE_BASIS = 2`) is deleted, as fc372c8094 deleted the pin on `= 1`. Its line no longer exists, so `ci_predict` would read it as STALE PIN.

**Docs.** No sentence in `docs/dashboard-card.md` or README.md names the basis number or which releases count as old, so nothing in them became false. The *old basis* paragraph (dashboard-card.md, "So does a month booked, wholly or in part, against an earlier baseline ...") is what this change makes true again. No strings change.

**User cost.** On an install whose current month was first booked on v7.1.17, the Savings tab's row for that month shows *old basis* after the upgrade. It states no saving and no percent, and it keeps its two cost columns (baseline and paid). Every month first booked before v7.1.17 already reads *old basis*, so this costs nothing more there. The next month is stamped fresh and states its saving. Single-zone and unvalved installs in that small set also lose the open month's stated saving, because the basis is global. That is the same trade 194625754d made.

## Release note

### A month first booked on v7.1.17 shows "old basis" after this update (R10-HOTFIX-REFERENCE-BASIS)

This release changes how the savings baseline is booked for a two-zone house behind a throttling valve: in cold hours with little sun, the baseline is about 1 % higher than before. The month that is open when you upgrade, if it was first booked on v7.1.17, shows *old basis* on the Savings tab. It keeps its baseline and paid columns but states no saving, because those two baselines cannot be added into one figure. Earlier months are unchanged, and next month states its saving again. Nothing to do.

## Root cause

Per dev/governance/rules/defect-root-cause.md: the defect did not reach a release (#3587 merged after the v7.1.17 tag and is in no tag) and turned no check red. This section is the record the verification asked for, not a triggered analysis.

- **Cause.** #3587 replaced the held state of `_thermostat_held_state` with `valve_top_equilibrium` for a valve-limited two-zone house. That changed `baseline_power`, which `_settlement_schedule` books into `savings_baseline`. bus-nonce: 3a4f648d09f0f438f5d5f8d9c7aa3f2d

Round 1 of this review. Measured at f7efa4be885e53556a6bfa02ad22a9b22c417b2a from a detached worktree; `git ls-remote` printed the same head for `handoff/r11-pre-objective-function` before this verdict was written. Body read: BODY.md at d578ba0b35179fa4f4bd6fc0e61672783767e850. Roster carries read at `handoff/audit-r10-roster` ec9295930700401e83d86f2e98a1648be84d7d12.

## Block

The mechanism half (the `--round` refusal, its self-test, the playbook pointer) holds and is not the block. The block is the definition's sufficiency, on the brief's fifth and seventh points. Each item names the sentence that would clear it.

1. **Three thresholds live only in the handoff body.** 0017 section 2 decides "moved" for `lead_time`, `closure_slip` and `tokens_per_change` by "the owner's percentage", and targets `product_green` at "the owner's floor" and `closure_slip` at "the owner's ceiling". No value is in 0017, `objective.json` has no field for one, and 0017 does not say where the owner's value is recorded; the values proposed (0.90, 0.2 days per day, 20%) are body Decisions 1 to 3, which a reader of the file and the tree never sees. So ordering rules 2 and 3 cannot be applied from the file for three of the four layer-2 and layer-3 terms. Clears with: a field per threshold in `objective.json`, and one sentence that an unset one makes the comparison undecided and is carded (section 1 already says this for a dimension's missing criterion, and only for that).
2. **The ordering does not say how a NO-READ compares.** "A round holds layer 1 when no term is worse" is undefined when a term is NO-READ on one or both sides, which at round 11's baseline is every layer-1 term (the body: twelve of thirteen NO-READ). Read one way nothing is ever admissible; read the other, from round 12 `first_pass` alone ranks process changes while both catchers section 5 names for its false move (`injected`, `escapes`) are NO-READ. A reader cannot tell which the owner meant. Clears with one sentence in section 2.
3. **`regret`'s information set is not defined, and as written the integration's own model error lands in the floor.** The target is "0 against the same-information oracle" for "the same prices, weather, house and comfort bounds". The file does not say whether "information" is the exogenous input at decision time (published prices, the provider's forecast, sensor readings) or the integration's own forecasts and learned house model, nor whether "house" is the measured house or the model of it. Under the second reading a wrong demand forecast or a mis-identified thermal model costs zero regret, which is savings defined against the integration's own model. The residual row adds to this: it lists "forecast error in price and weather, sensor error" as irreducible for a term whose oracle by definition shares that information, so the floor and the removable loss are not separated (the provider's forecast error is floor; the integration's own demand and house model error is removable). The measured-against-modelled gap, the one read that would catch the own-model case, is named as D0's and as a catcher in section 5 but is in no term's definition or target and has no enumerator and no builder. Clears with: the information set and "house" defined, the residual split along that line, and the gap made part of the term.
4. **The install population is not enumerable from the file.** Section 1 defines it by the configuration flow (enumerable: control kind, tank and valve layout, price source, unit system) and then makes the cells the product of axes the flow does not enumerate: climate, house and tank size, tariff and price shape have no levels, Home Assistant version has no range, and the levels are said to be "each enumerated in D12's scope", which this diff does not change (`git diff` touches no dimension brief) and which D12's brief does not carry today (`ev/tree_claims.txt`: its axes are layout and heat-pump kind). `generality`'s denominator is therefore whatever bins the reader picks. Clears with: the rule that fixes each axis's levels from tracked files (the flow's option lists, `tests/profiles.py`, the translations directory, the manifest's version floor) or the command that prints the cells.
5. **Section 1's dimension table has an end state per dimension and no distance, enumerator or floor per dimension.** The owner's first carry asks, for every dimension, the perfect result "each with the measured distance from it". The file gives distance and residual per term only; a dimension's distance is reachable only through `coverage` and `escapes`, which measure examination and reports, not the stated result. For D2, D3, D7, D8, D9, D10, D11, D14 and D15 the perfect result names no command that would print how far the code is from it and no NO-READ. Clears with: a column naming the enumerator or NO-READ and what would read it.
6. **Three product reads are NO-READ with no builder, and two of the three carries do not name what they carry.** The brief asks that every enumerator be a tracked command or name the roster group that builds it. `regret` ("none whole … no record holds realised cost per install") and `operation` ("none. The actuator-write dimension, once briefed") name no group; the same-information oracle, the realised-cost record, the write-and-hold cell ledger and D12's axes and cell ledger ("D12's brief must gain these") are carried to no brief. At ec92959307 the carries on R11-PRE-TOKEN-LEDGER and R10-DIMENSIONS-FULL-COVERAGE open "The same, for …" with no antecedent in their own group: neither names decision 0017 or its section, so the control the next stage needs is not stated where that seat reads (`fix-review.md` step 10). Only R11-PRE-ROUND-METRICS's carry is self-standing.

Also owed at the re-handoff, on this diff's own instrument, none the block by itself (`ev/probes.txt`, `ev/mutants.txt`):

- The evaluator's independence is a string compare. `evaluator: "orchestrator-r10"` and `evaluator: "the orchestrator"` with `reviewer: "Orchestrator"` are accepted (probes P1, P2); only the exact token `orchestrator` is refused. Nothing reads who dispatched the seat, whether it worked the graded round, or that the reviewer returned `approve`: `reviewer` is a name, not a verdict.
- 0017 says who may not write the owner's decision (the evaluator, `evaluator.md` last paragraph; the orchestrator "never edits them", section 5) and names nobody who does; section 6 has the orchestrator write `OBJECTIVE.json` while section 5 says it never edits a round's objective record. One of the two sentences is wrong.
- `merged` accepts any ancestor of the ref: an accepted card naming the repository's root commit passes (P3). Nothing ties the commit to the card.
- A `value` whose `enumerator` is `by hand` passes, as does a null value (P4, P5), against section 6's "per term a value with the enumerator that printed it".
- A `remove` on evidence `NO-READ: none` passes (P6), against section 3's "Never on a NO-READ".
- Section 6's "every `unowned` item, and every owner-decided result with no written criterion, yields a card" is checked by nothing: the all-keep, all-NO-READ, zero-card record passes (P0, P7). That record is what round 11's start will most cheaply be.
- Survivor of my own: with the verdict's membership in keep/change/remove untested, the self-test still passes (`ev/mutants.txt` R12). A verdict of any other word with a card is accepted under that mutant; no arm pins the set.
- The object set is the 168 guide, contract, rule, brief and workflow files. `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/workflows/*.js` (the files that run a round, `audit-find.js` among them), `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/skills/`, and every script with no guide under `tools/audit/seat/instruments/` (`policy_lint.mjs`, `brief_lint.mjs`, `stamp.py`, `closure.py`, `structure.py`, `mutation_table.py`, `budget_raise_gate.py`, `carry_audit.py`) get no verdict, so "every dimension, contract, rule, instrument and gate" is narrower than the machinery.
- 0017's Context cites the two pre-studies at `dev/audit/rounds/round10/`; neither is in the tree at this head (the body says they are on step refs), and `operation` is assigned to "the actuator-write dimension the coverage audit proposes". The universe is defined in the file, so the term survives, but the citation resolves to nothing.

## What holds

- End states exist: per dimension (section 1), per term and for the process (section 2's second table and "the perfect round"). The file does not define directions only.
- The function is anchored on `custom_components/` and `blueprints/` at the close; perfect code is the conjunction of every dimension's result, the completeness term `unowned`, and the three product terms.
- The chain is six links with a measure and a failure chance each, and the file states that "one round guarantees perfect code under no condition this record can check". It does not make the stronger claim; section 5 claims section 4 for no round until the held-out checks exist.
- The flat-price null control and the perfect-foresight bound are in the definition of `regret`; comfort bounds are the delegated ones, and a plan that leaves one is an `operation` defect, never a saving.
- Each process term has its residual separated from removable cost.

## The convergence argument

The inequality N' <= (1 - p(1 - q)) N + g is right under its own terms. It does not follow that the function moving the right way means fewer objective bugs. Unstated assumptions:

1. **p is an infimum over bugs and the sensor measures a mean.** The geometric rate needs the least per-bug detection chance to be positive; planted-defect recall estimates the average over kinds someone thought to plant. Survivors of each round are selected for low p, so the tail's rate is not the measured recall, and a kind the finder model cannot see has p = 0 with no sensor moving.
2. **The two-finder estimate assumes independent finders with equal catchability.** Two seats of one model on one brief are positively correlated, which biases (n1 + 1)(n2 + 1) / (m + 1) - 1 low; the "escapes are seen" sensor then reads better than the code is.
3. **Found means survived the verifier and the judge.** A real defect voided or refuted is lost with no link and no term; recall is "found / planted" without saying at which stage found is counted.
4. **q counts injection per bug removed; g counts new surface.** A refactor (D7's moves), a documentation or process fix, or a fix of a false positive injects with no bug removed and no new surface. The `injected` term's denominator covers them; the model's two parameters do not.
5. **Link 3 has no term.** "Every finding was fixed correctly" is measured "only once a re-report names the fix it follows"; nothing in the thirteen terms reads a fix that did not fix, and `injected` is defined as a new defect.
6. **The claim covers objective bugs only.** Section 1's perfect code also holds the three product terms and the owner-judged dimensions; nothing argues they converge, and `regret`'s floor means it cannot reach its stated end state. The file should say the convergence claim is not a claim about section 1.
7. **`escapes` depends on a reporting rate nobody measures.** Releases per day is beside it; installs reporting is not, and the residual row admits this.

## Gaming, term by term

Moved without improving what is measured, and not caught by a control that exists at this head:

- `first_pass`: approve weakly. Its catchers are `injected` and `escapes`, both NO-READ; real-catch incidence is beside it but in no rule.
- `coverage`: the universe is "a command the reviewer re-runs"; re-running a command that prints a narrow universe reproduces the narrow universe. The control that would catch it (planted defects over the natural universe) has no instrument.
- `generality`: the share rises when a cell is "examined" by one property test over the configuration space or a stub simulation, with nothing asserted about the result; "no defect found" is met by not finding. The term measures examination, not correctness per cell.
- `operation`: "the value written equals the documented target" moves by editing the document to match the code. No false move of this shape is listed.
- `regret`: block item 3.
- `unexamined`: "a fix names the judged finding it closes" stops a feature relabelled as a fix; it does not stop a late merge being "examined" by a pass that reports it read.
- `injected`: the cause is named by the fixing group, which is the party whose predecessor it indicts; "checked in review" is the only control.
- `lead_time`: the clock starts at the roster entry, which the orchestrator writes; entering a group when its fixer is ready moves it. "Enter the group late" is listed and its catcher restates the definition.
- `tokens_per_change`, `closure_slip`, `product_green`, `escapes`, `unowned`: I found no move beyond those section 5 lists, and each listed catcher is a stated companion figure, not a refusal.

## Items for the owner, not blocks

Where the draft limits what a mandate may approve:

1. Section 5: "no mandate scope covers" 0017, `objective.json`, `check_scopes.py`, each enumerator once built, and every round's `EVALUATION.json` and `OBJECTIVE.json` (body Decision 8). This narrows decision 0013. It is stated and not enforced: the diff adds four CODEOWNERS lines and changes nothing that reads a mandate, so under 0013's grammar a mandate scoped `code-owned` or `all` still reaches these paths.
2. Section 2 rule 1: a change moving a layer-1 term the wrong way is accepted by "only the owner … by card".
3. Section 6: "the owner decides each card", and the check refuses a round start with an undecided card. No agent under any mandate can clear a card, so a round cannot start while the owner is away and one card is open. Every `change` and `remove`, every `unowned` item and every missing criterion is a card.
4. Section 1 and section 3: the supported population, the comfort bounds, the gate and the review rule are "the owner's"; "neither is a tunable the evaluated round may loosen".
5. Section 5: "Adding a term or an object class removes one" (body Decision 17), and from round 12 a process change is kept only on a measured before and after with its null control, which removes from any approver a change whose named term is NO-READ.
6. `/tools/audit/check_scopes.py` becomes code-owned. R10-DIMENSIONS-FULL-COVERAGE owes a territory check in that file, and every closing orchestrator's `OBJECTIVE.json` needs the owner's review before the next round can start.
7. The budget entry for `evaluator.md` was pushed with no owner confirmation first; the body says so under `## Red checks` and leaves it to `budget-raise-gate`.

The model the draft assigns the evaluator seat: `evaluator.md` line 3, "One opus seat per round" (body Decision 9; its alternative is "a model at least the orchestrator's"). The owner's instruction quoted in 0017's Context asked for "a fable seat" to define the function, and this group's roster models are fable for fixer and reviewer. The reviewer of the evaluation is "a second seat" with no model named.

## Findings

- The planted-defect recall and the two-finder overlap, which sense four of section 4's six assumptions, have no instrument and no group; 0017 sends them to round 11's first evaluation as cards, so round 11 runs with the convergence claim unverifiable. Carry: R11-PRE-ROUND-METRICS
- Link 3 of the chain (a fix that did not fix) has no term and no record that would read it; a re-report must name the fix it follows. Carry: R10-DIMENSIONS-FULL-COVERAGE
- No instrument measures per-bug detection as an infimum or the correlation of two same-model finders; the overlap estimate is biased low under it. Carry: R11-PRE-ROUND-METRICS
- `scorecard.py` line `A_gate` reads the last 20 runs and 0017 defines `product_green` over the window; the proxy and the term will disagree until the window is added. Carry: R11-PRE-ROUND-METRICS

## Evidence

- No review packet exists and no CI has run: no pull request is open for this head. `## Red checks` in the body answers `budget-raise-gate` in advance; nothing was red to read.
- Merge with main: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main f7efa4be88` exits 0 (tree 3d6c5a2771); the merge base is origin/main e23124ff6e, so the head is 0 behind.
- `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty: my contract copy is current.
- RESULT self-test at head: 15/15 evaluation arms held, rc 0 (`ev/checks.txt`).
- RESULT `--round 11` at head: rc 1, 2 gaps naming `round10/OBJECTIVE.json` and `round11/EVALUATION.json`; without `--round` rc 0.
- RESULT the body's six mutants: each rc 1 with the arms the body's table names (`ev/mutants.txt` M1 to M6); unmutated rc 0 before and after.
- RESULT my eight further mutants over the nine arms the body left unmutated: seven killed, R12 survives (above).
- RESULT bypass probes P0 to P8: all nine accepted (`ev/probes.txt`).
- Figures re-derived: 13 terms; 168 objects (16, 19, 10, 105, 18); 0017 is 352 lines; corpus 69092 against 68618 plus band 500; `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`; `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`; the check's wall clock 1.3 s here against the body's 1.8 s on its container; `rules_sync --check` ok.
- Not re-derived: `tests/entities.py` (this container's interpreter has no `homeassistant`), `prepr.sh`'s three survivors, and every round-10 hand figure in the body's worked example, whose sources are two audits on step refs outside the tree. `first_pass` 412 of 817 has an enumerator (`flow_metrics.py --window`) that I did not run, having no window bounds in the body.
- `VERSION`, release notes, `custom_components/` and `tests/golden/` are untouched by the range; both claim files are byte-identical to the merge base. No production line changes, so `mutation` on `--scope changed` draws no mutant here.
- Tracked commands 0017 names that exist: `tools/audit/seat/scorecard.py` (lines `A_gate`, `H`, `E`), `tools/audit/seat/flow_metrics.py --window`, `tools/audit/seat/review_strength.py --window`, `tools/audit/machinery_ratchet.py --measure`, `tests/ha_contract.py`, `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`. `governance_cost.py` exists only as `tools/audit/round4/D11/governance_cost.py`, a round-4 evidence script. Roster groups named and present, not started: R11-PRE-ROUND-METRICS, R11-PRE-TOKEN-LEDGER, R10-DIMENSIONS-FULL-COVERAGE.

The packet printed `Review scope: full`, because `verdict/3575` holds round 1's verdict only. I read the whole three-dot diff (13 files, merge base 23cc7b8e1d, which was origin/main's tip at render) and ran my own mutants over all of `check_scopes.py`'s new predicates, and answered the dispatch's three delta items and the round-3 block against the probe ref's verdict. Role contract read from the role pack rendered at origin/main.

## Block

Neither item needs a commit on the pull request's branch: both are edits of the roster branch, by `roster_edit.py`.

1. **The D6 register carry is in no group that can receive it.** The body's sixth `## Forward-carry` item (section 1's table reads D6's distance from `tests/doc_claims.py` only for the claims it registers; the enumeration of the rest is owed) ends `Carry: R11-INTAKE-R10-RESIDUE`. On `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster` at 5eaef97ee4 its text is held by `R10-D5-D6-FULL-SCOPE` alone, carries 2 and 3, a group at stage `done` that `roster_lib.carry_receivable` reads false; carry 2 is marked `[moved: R11-PRE-OBJECTIVE-FUNCTION]` and carry 3 `dismissed: duplicate of carry 2 ... moved to R11-PRE-OBJECTIVE-FUNCTION`. `R11-PRE-OBJECTIVE-FUNCTION`'s six carries do not hold it (and it is this pull request's own group), and none of `R11-INTAKE-R10-RESIDUE`'s 175 carries does. Control: the same search finds the D12 item in `R11-INTAKE-R10-RESIDUE` carry 115 (`ev/roster_carries.txt`). `carry_audit.py ... landed` prints `CARRY-LANDED: 0 missing` (`ev/carry_landed.txt`) because its source rule passes an item whose destination holds any carry from `#3575`, and carries 114 and 115 are from it. 1. **docs/configuration.md (Pump duty control, "A switch that stops the compressor is priced") and docs/how-it-works.md (cycling-cost section) state the off time is charged as heat not delivered for any latched direction.** The configuration bullet says "Once a direction has stopped the compressor ... the plan ... expects the median measured off time as heat not delivered in the step that follows"; how-it-works says the optimizer learns "per direction" and "counts the off time as heat not delivered". Executable code charges lost heat for one direction only: `duty_legs.lost_share` returns `min(1.0, stop_probability[0] * off_seconds[0] / (step_minutes * 60.0))` (custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/duty_legs.py:161), index 0 being `dhw_space` (`duty_switch.DIRECTIONS = ("dhw_space", "space_dhw")`, read in that order by `planner_pairs`). A latched heating-to-hot-water direction is priced in `switch_weights_batch` but never reduces availability. Fix: name the direction (hot water to heating) in both sentences.

2. **docs/configuration.md, Heat pump on/off switch row: "a run the plan would end within 10 minutes is not started unless the tank needs heat now (below its minimum, or a disinfection hold)".** `supply_hold._ends_soon` (supply_hold.py:156) exempts the start only when `step_duty(inp.plan, now) in ("dhw", "both") and tank_reason(inp)`: a cold tank or disinfection hold on a space-only step is still held. The page states the tank condition alone. Fix: "unless the step heats the tank and the tank needs heat now".

3. **The body's `## Null control` does not re-derive.** It claims the `git grep -c -E ...` command prints "one or more lines per page at the head"; at the head it prints README.md:1 and docs/configuration.md:3 and nothing for docs/how-it-works.md (none of the four patterns appears in the added how-it-works paragraph). Origin/main side prints nothing, as claimed. ev/checks.txt. Fix: add a pattern that occurs in the how-it-works paragraph (e.g. `min\(a, b\) / p_max`) or correct the sentence.

merges.subject: Merge pull request #3592 from tvofi/fix/r10-hotfix-carry-tip-sigpipe
merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-CARRY-TIP-SIGPIPE: the carry check reads an own branch tip among many heads
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
Hotfix R10-HOTFIX-CARRY-TIP-SIGPIPE. Since #3514 (decision 0017), `carry()` in `tools/pr/app_approve.sh` checked whether a head is a branch tip of origin with
`printf '%s\n' "$heads" | grep -q "^$h[[:space:]]refs/heads/" || ours=0` under `set -uo pipefail`. origin lists 7937 branch heads. `grep -q` exits at its first match, the `printf` writer then gets SIGPIPE, and under pipefail the pipeline returns 141. So `ours=0`: a head that **is** a branch tip of origin was read as a fork's head, and every range with a row or bot commit answered `FRESH-REVIEW` / `CARRY: no`. This blocked every verdict carry on main's tools.

How the cause was confirmed:
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/review_carry.py 2b8893814da8e6cf0a5fd8b33c05d849f2717d45 341677c1974c819ee417226897047192b703014c` at origin/main prints `FRESH-REVIEW ... on a head that is no branch tip of origin`. At the same time, `git ls-remote --heads origin` lists `341677c1... refs/heads/fix/r10-hotfix-main-selftest-scope`.
- The pipeline in isolation, under `set -uo pipefail`, with the match first: 8001 heads give `PIPESTATUS=141 0`, and one head gives `PIPESTATUS=0 0`.

The fix uses here-strings (`grep -q ... <<<"$heads"`). A here-string has no writer process that a closing reader can kill, the trailing newline is the same as `printf '%s\n'`, and it works on bash 3.2.

The coordinator also added the `gh_transient` census flake to this hotfix. The row `and gh_transient prints nothing on either stream` failed in CI job 132518925875. `gh_transient` ends in the same shape: `printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qE '^Get ...|^error connecting to '`. The CI runner ignores SIGPIPE: the same job log prints `printf: write error: Broken pipe` from `tick_loop.sh:224` and `pr_args.sh:454/464`. So when grep exits at a first-line match while printf is still writing, printf writes that message to stderr, and the census captures it with `2>&1`. When SIGPIPE is not ignored, the same race returns 141 and a transient read is refused. I could not reproduce the race on the census's own two-line inputs locally: 2000 iterations on macOS bash 3.2 in both signal regimes gave 0 hits. With a long input the mechanism is deterministic. The fix makes the race impossible, because the function has no pipe left.

Sweep (tools/pr and tools/audit/seat). Enumerated with
`git grep -nE '\|[[:space:]]*grep[[:space:]]+-[a-zA-Z]*q' -- tools/pr tools/audit/seat`: 236 lines, all at origin/main 6858b4abc1.
Fixed, because each can take an input larger than a pipe buffer (16 KB on macOS before it grows) with the match early:
- `tools/pr/app_approve.sh` `carry()` heads (the defect), `gh_transient` gh stderr (the flake), and the bot-commit name list `$bt`.
- `tools/audit/seat/bus.sh` re-cut check: a PR body can be up to 64 KB, with `## Re-cut` near the top.
- `tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh` `pr_pushers`: whole script texts (app_push.sh and others are far above 64 KB). This is the source of the CI `Broken pipe` lines; under `pr_trap`'s pipefail it would report a false OPEN.
- `tools/audit/seat/handoff_push.sh` note: the diff names over a main merge. It uses a grep without `-q`, which reads to the end, because a here-string of an empty diff would match the empty line.
Dismissed, with the reason:
- `app_approve.sh:154`: one status line from `tail -1`.
- `bus.sh:827`: one review_packet message.
- `bus.sh` self-test rows 1267 and later (151 lines): stub output of a few lines from one single-argument printf. Locally, 2000 runs of that shape lost no race. It is still the same class with a narrow window, so it is left to the class barrier under Forward-carry rather than rewritten in a hotfix.
- `tick_loop.sh` (37): the self-test turns pipefail off on purpose (line 216), and row 224 is that guard's own test. The production rows read short `$out`.
- `pr_args.sh:457/460` tails (`grep -E ... | grep -qv`): the upstream grep emits a few matching lines, which fits any buffer.
- `pr_args.sh:471` (`printf '%s\n' $found | grep -qxF`) is **fixed** as well, although its list is only about 20 paths. With one argument per path, printf writes once per line, and a local `pr_args.sh --self-test` printed `line 473: printf: write error: Broken pipe` from this line. So a large input is not the only way to trigger the race: a writer that makes several `write()`s can lose it on small input too.
- `pr_args.sh:1397`: the `## Head` section.
- `cloud_relay.sh` (9): single 40/32-hex values, or self-test fixtures (`owes`, `dbtree`).
- `ci-watch.sh`: no pipefail of its own, and it neither sources `pr_args.sh` nor calls `pr_trap`.
- `update_pr.sh:69` (`git worktree list | grep -F "[$BR]" | grep -vqF "$WT "`): it runs under `pr_trap`'s pipefail, but both upstream stages read to the end, and the early-exit `grep -vqF` sees only the few lines naming `[$BR]`. That output fits any pipe buffer in one write.
- `heartbeat.sh`, `seat_venv.sh`: self-test `$out` of a few lines.
- `app_push.sh:930/945`: one `ps` character.
- `prepr.sh:3198/3200`: the match is the last trailer line, so no early exit.
- `push.sh:170/206`: the `## Head` section of a body.

Changed since cb803e9e (review round 1, verdict probe/revt-r10-hotfix-carry-tip-sigpipe-a366776e, blocked class-open):
- `tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh:125` (`op_clear_leftover`) is fixed. Round 1 dismissed it as "no pipefail", and that was wrong: `open_pr.sh` calls `pr_trap`, which sets `set -Eeo pipefail`. `git worktree list --porcelain | grep -qxF "worktree $WT"` read a registered left-over checkout as absent once the list outgrew the pipe. It now uses a here-string. A deterministic probe, with a git wrapper appending 3000 worktree entries after git's own list and `set -Eeo pipefail`, gives `pipe:MISSED 141 0` 5 of 5 and `here:found` 5 of 5.
- `open_pr.sh:48` (`OP_REG=$(git worktree list --porcelain | awk '... exit')`) is fixed as well. The new row found it: awk's `exit` is an early-exit reader on the same list, and under `pr_trap` the 141 stopped the run through errexit before line 125 was ever reached. It now uses a here-string. If `git worktree list` itself fails, that is now read as "no registration" (the lone-run path) rather than stopping the run.
- `pr_args.sh:448` (`kind=$(printf "$PR_PUSHERS" | awk '... exit')`, inside `pr_pushers`, which runs under `pr_trap`) is fixed as well, with a here-string.
- The other early-exit readers in the `pr_trap` scripts (`| head`, `| awk ... exit`, `| sed q`, `| grep -m`, over `open_pr.sh`, `update_pr.sh`, `delivery_row.sh` and `pr_args.sh`) are disposed: `open_pr.sh:170` (`grep -oE 'pull request #N' p1.log | head -1`) reads a grep that emits a line or two in one write, and `pr_args.sh:1532` is a `head -n` on a file, not a pipe.
- New row in `pr_args.sh --self-test` (open_pr's self-test): `open_pr: the same re-run with 3000 more worktrees listed after the left-over one still clears it and opens`. It uses the existing closed-after-p2 re-run harness, with that git wrapper on PATH.

It prints 232 lines at 7d186ed4 and 236 at 6858b4abc1 with macOS git; the counts include comment lines that name the pattern. Every script that calls `pr_trap` (`open_pr.sh`, `update_pr.sh`) or is sourced into one (`pr_args.sh`, `delivery_row.sh`) was re-read: open_pr.sh:125 was the one open `grep -q` site. The early-exit-reader sites the new row then exposed are listed above. The only new file it reaches is `tools/coverage/coverage_tree.sh:300` (`printf "$_grade" | grep -qE`). It is dismissed: the script is executed, not sourced, it sets no pipefail, and a new bash does not inherit a caller's pipefail, so grep's status decides.
- Answer to the verdict's surviving-mutant note (the `$bt`, bus re-cut, handoff_push and census rewrites have no row that fails on the old line): the verdict routes it to R11-INTAKE-R10-RESIDUE, and the class lint pins it there. This hotfix pins the two lines that broke (carry, gh_transient) and the open_pr site.
- Answer to the verdict's count note: the round-1 figure 236 was measured on macOS at 6858b4abc1, and the reviewer's Linux count differs. The widened command's count at this head is given above. A later reader re-measures at their own base.
- Answer to the dismissal note on `update_pr.sh:69`: the reason is rewritten above.

Leaves #3394 open.

## Head

`897c777b23ca69cac35183ff1a88f1483a8ccdb1` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

7d186ed4a5fe4f7097332e05562f0870b3e3f1aa

## Mutation proof

Each mutant is a copy of `app_approve.sh` with one old line restored, run with `--self-test`:
- carry line restored (`printf '%s\n' "$heads" | grep -q ...`): `FAIL CARRY on a head of ours listed first among 20001 branch heads of origin (got '1', want '0')`, `app_approve self-test: 353 checks, 1 failed`.

The second FAIL reproduces the CI flake's message class.

Round 2 (open_pr.sh). The new row is `open_pr: the same re-run with 3000 more worktrees listed after the left-over one still clears it and opens`, in `pr_args.sh --self-test` on macOS:
- Both lines old (red first): `FAIL`, `260 checks, 12 failed`.
- Head 7d186ed4: `ok`, `260 checks, 11 failed`. The 11 are the same FAIL lines as origin/main's own run on this host (BSD sed, pr_bounded, host_refusal), with a `diff` of the FAIL lines against the base run that is empty.
- Mutant, line 125 restored alone: `FAIL` (the left-over checkout is read as absent), `12 failed`.
- Mutant, line 48 restored alone: `FAIL` (awk's exit gives 141 under errexit), `12 failed`.

Failing test first: the new carry rows on the unfixed tree gave `FAIL CARRY on a head of ours listed first among 20001 branch heads of origin (got '1', want '0')`, `app_approve self-test: 351 checks, 1 failed`.

## Null control

- Unmodified origin/main 6858b4abc1: `app_approve self-test: 348 checks, 0 failed`. This tree has no row with more than a handful of heads, so the defect passed silently.
- The new null-control rows pass both before and after the fix: `ok   NO CARRY: the same 20000 heads without it (null control)` and `ok   refused as a head that is not ours`. A head that is not a tip still refuses.
- Touched instruments on macOS: `handoff_push self-test: 6 checks, 0 failed`. `pr_args.sh` and `bus.sh` show the same FAIL lines at origin/main as on this head. These are host failures: BSD `sed -i` in the census fixture, and APFS case-insensitivity in bus's case-collision row. I re-ran the census rows by hand with BSD `sed -i ''`: no trap gives `OPEN ... no pr_exit_trap`, a foreground push gives `OPEN ... runs in the foreground`, and no push hold gives `OPEN ... holds no push lock`. Its null control (no branch lock) returns rc 0, and the clean tree returns rc 0. CI on Linux is the authority for those rows.
- After the fix: `app_approve self-test: 353 checks, 0 failed`. `tools/audit/seat/bare_array.py --check` exits 0.

## Figures

none

## Red checks

The defect turned main's carry red with no check catching it. The cheaper detector is the self-test row this PR adds: a stubbed `ls-remote` lists the head first among 20000 heads, so any early-exit reader fails deterministically, in seconds, in the existing `app_approve` self-test step, at no new standing cost. The census flake's detector is the paired long-stderr rows, which are deterministic where the two-line census rows were not. Cause: #3514 added a pipe into `grep -q` over an unbounded producer under pipefail. This class is already named in comments in `prepr.sh:216/1881/3664`, `app_push.sh:1088`, `cloud_relay.sh:308`, `seat_venv.sh:254` and `tick_loop.sh:213`. The fixture had only a few heads, so the row could not see it.

The checks below are red on commits in `6858b4abc1..origin/fix/r10-hotfix-carry-tip-sigpipe` that are not this hotfix's. They arrived when the PR branch merged main at 5c4a7a0fc6: main's own commits since the hotfix's base, and other PRs' branch commits that main carries. None is on cb803e9e or 7d186ed4, which carry no failed run. Each was measured with the check-runs API per commit:
- `governance / instrument-self-tests`: red on 070118088a and ff8b073827, which are other branches' commits merged into main. This branch did not cause it, so it owes no detector.
- `tests / ci-ratchet`: red on 5cd7b87413 (main's merge of #3588). Not this branch's, so it owes no detector.
- `tests / fast (3.14)`: red on 070118088a. Not this branch's, so it owes no detector.
- `tests / mutation`: red on 837ead0bd7 and 5b197bd685. Not this branch's, so it owes no detector.
- `tests / nightly-status`: red on the record commits and main-side merges (63ca72623e, 16ee88317b, 65a5a17301, 341677c197, e81c5ac940, 1506411191, 837ead0bd7, 5b197bd685, 070118088a). It reports the nightly run's state, not this diff, so it owes no detector here.

## Forward-carry

- Recurring class, a barrier owed: `printf | grep -q` (or any pipe into an early-exit reader) breaks on a precondition, "a producer larger than the pipe buffer feeding an early-exit reader under pipefail, or where SIGPIPE is ignored". It is named in comments at `prepr.sh:216/1881/3664`, `app_push.sh:1088`, `cloud_relay.sh:308`, `seat_venv.sh:254` and `tick_loop.sh:213`, and now in this defect. Control: `git grep -nE '\|[[:space:]]*grep[[:space:]]+-[a-zA-Z]*q' -- tools/pr tools/audit/seat` prints 236 lines at 6858b4abc1. The evidence is `PIPESTATUS=141 0` with the match first among 8001 lines against `0 0` with one line, and `printf: write error: Broken pipe` in CI job 132518925875, where SIGPIPE is ignored. This PR fixes 11 of those lines. The rest are listed as dismissed in the sweep above, and the 151 `bus.sh` self-test rows, the `tick_loop.sh` / `heartbeat.sh` / `seat_venv.sh` self-test rows and `pr_args.sh:457/460` still hold the shape with a narrow window. The barrier is a lint over the pattern, which an owner freeze keeps from being a new instrument group before closure. Carry: R11-INTAKE-R10-RESIDUE

The body's macOS mutant run (`12 failed`) is plausible but I could not re-derive it here. CI's runner awk decides whether CI ever pins this line. merges.body:
R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING-PR-B, second pull request: the arbiter's split of a step serving both duties reads the learned estimate, as the group's ruling on rule c states. With thanks to Bankaifan, whose pull request 3420 found the duty-switch restart; its split function (order latched per step, the whole step given to the first duty when the second share is shorter than the minimum split plus the learned off time) is the starting point of `DutySwitchLearner.split` and `duty_switch.both_step_duty`, narrowed here by the ruling: the whole-step rule applies only where the plan's next step serves the denied duty, and `n` has a ceiling.

- **The reader and its first caller** (roster carry 0, item 1b22f416). `duty_switch.both_step_duty` takes the pump's record, the step's start, the plan's split and the plan's next step; `_share` in `pump_arbiter.py` delegates to it. The decision is `duty_legs.both_step_legs` under the leg rule `DutySwitchLearner.split` returns, latched on the record per step start; a record not yet loaded splits as before and latches nothing. The arbiter holds no learned state.
- **The rule.** Space goes first only where hot water to space is the one usable direction. The first duty keeps the whole step only when the switch into the second is usable, the second share is under `SPLIT_MIN_MINUTES` plus that direction's median off time, and the next step serves the second duty (or both). With no usable direction the decision is hot water first, not whole: today's split.
- **`n` has a ceiling**, `N_CAP` (twice `N_ON`), held at each booking and on each pass's decay by scaling both counts alike, so `p` does not move. A latched direction with no further episode unlatches just past two half-lives, and the default split re-tests it (verdict item n11).
- **Factory reset voids the duty-switch store** (roster carries 1 and 6, items 3c666f5b and 893e80d2), under the orchestrator's ruling under mandate 6715477401 of 2026-11-12T19:51:09Z. The store joins `_restored_stores` and `_FACTORY_VOID` as voided whole, so the existing mechanism also puts it in the undo point and the undo restores it. The entry is set up again with a new coordinator, whose record loads the voided store empty: that is the in-memory learner emptied in the reset's own step. The planner of R10-DUTY-SWITCH-PLANNER-PRICE, now on main, reads the same record (`planner_fields`), so after a reset it prices from the voided record too. A reversal is the `("duty_switch", None)` row, its `_FR_STORES` line and the reset check.
- **What the reader reads** (roster carries 4 and 5, items 90bc5153 and d088605d). Only the latches and the median off time. It reads no `n`, tally, `span_days` or published key, so a `span_days` of 0 beside non-zero tallies, or evidence accruing faster on one set-point unit, moves the split only through a latch.

**Reconcile round (early, owner ruling 2026-11-14).** This branch contains PR 3561's head 30b069508f194240f90ddd05cb5cfee0613814e1 (R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK), merged first, then origin/main at 50373173d486faf394b24637c177ab38b691b394, which merged clean after it. If 3561's head moves before it merges, the successor merges the new head and nothing else.

- **One leg rule for planner and arbiter** (carry c3ad1545, binding the branch that merges second; this one). R10-DUTY-SWITCH-PLANNER-PRICE, now on main through 3561's head, made `duty_legs.py` the owner of the both step's legs; this branch's `split` put a learned order and a whole-step decision in the arbiter. Union: `duty_legs.leg_rule(stop_probability, off_seconds)` returns `(first duty, minutes the second share must clear past SPLIT_MIN_MINUTES, or None)`; `both_step_legs` and `leg_ends` take that rule (and the next step's duty, `leg_ends` reading it from the plan itself); `DutySwitchLearner.split()` is `leg_rule(*planner_pairs())`, the very pairs `planner_fields` hands the solve, so the planner prices the legs the arbiter serves. `switch_weights_batch` weighs the inside switch in the rule's direction, `availability` charges a two-leg step only when hot water goes first, and `switch_ban` under space first bans only the step before heating. With no stop priced the rule is `DEFAULT_RULE` and every array is main's: no golden moves.
- **Order in `pump_arbiter.py`.** 3561 owns the set-point-stuck behaviour (its `_lead_mode`, `_step_duty` and `_served` helpers, kept whole); this group owns the duty-switch delegation inside `_share`, which `_served` calls after the block. Order per pass: planned duty, block, hot-water lease (`_step_duty`), then `_share` → `duty_switch.both_step_duty` → `duty_legs.both_step_legs`, then the block again (`_served`).
- **Superseded deliberately.** main's `if self.n > N_CAP` booking cap gives way to this branch's comparison-free `min()` (reviewed at 29370fdb), also held on decay, so its two ledger pins (`Direction.book` GUARD_OFF and CMP_BOUND 3e106b06) are removed as stale. main's `_share` body (legs read inline) gives way to the delegation. Three planner-price checks that assumed hot water first under the hot-water-to-heating pair alone keep their assertion under a pair priced both ways and state the space-first outcome beside it.

The group's roster carries, by index:

- Carry 0 (item 1b22f416): implemented; `both_step_duty` is the reader and `_share` its first caller, and `dead_top_level_symbols` does not move.
- Carry 1 (item 3c666f5b): implemented per the ruling in Carry 8; the store is voided by a factory reset.
- Carry 2 (item ef5d3875): settled in part 1 (`N_ON` is a decayed weight); the split reads the latch it sets and adds nothing.
- Carry 3 (item c7d068a1): settled in part 1 (the publication's resolution); the ceiling now also bounds the published `n` at 10.
- Carry 4 (item 90bc5153): implemented; the reader reads no `span_days` and no published key, pinned by "the split reads the latches and nothing published…".
- Carry 5 (item d088605d): implemented; the reader reads no `n`, so a unit gating fewer switches moves the split only through a latch, same check.
- Carry 6 (item 893e80d2): implemented by the void; the planner's read (`planner_fields`, now on main) reads the same record, voided alike.
- Carry 7 (item b30e2dd2): implemented in this round: the order and the whole-step rule are `duty_legs.leg_rule`, read by `both_step_legs`, `leg_ends`, the weights, the charge and the ban; the harness mutant "arbiter: the share serves the legs in reverse order", re-anchored on `both_step_duty`, turns 3 section checks red.
- Carry 8 (the orchestrator's ruling of 2026-11-12T19:51:09Z): implemented with its owed failing-first test and its restart null control.

merges.body:
**A policy change, awaiting the owner's review.** It changes what the D5 and D6 finder seats must do from round 11 on, and the finder scopes that size them; I drafted it, and merging needs the owner's approving review (`CLAUDE.md`, "Where the policy is").

The owner's rulings of 2026-11-13, verbatim (1 = all user facing text in production; 2 = every single sentence in all documentation; 3 = all code comments):

1. "Do 1 in round 10, and 2 and 3 in round 11 sequenced as you recommend. Code comments in instruments and the documents that describe the instruments, developer and other non-static documentation also in scope for 3."
2. "The test suite comments are in scope. Also, since 1-2 is done before 3, they may not trust code comments, only the actual code behaviour"
3. "Go by your recommendation, but I would like the scope of d5 and d6 to always cover that full scope"

What changes:

- **`tools/audit/text_ledger.py`** (new instrument) enumerates every unit a seat must judge. For D6 that is each sentence of a document, each fenced block, each sentence of every JSON string leaf (strings.json and translations), and each user-visible literal in the Python and card JavaScript (two words or more, with markup, interpolation and CSS dropped). For D5 it is each comment block and each docstring in Python, JavaScript and shell. A file with no text is one `file` unit, and a unit's id is the sha1 of its text, so ledgers diff across rounds. `check` refuses an unrowed unit, an orphan row, a claim without an executed command and result, a verdict outside true/false/stale/unverifiable, and a non-true verdict without the truth. `--plant` writes one sentence into a copy of a file and must see that sentence refused as unrowed: the per-seat null control that an omission is visible.
- **`dev/audit/config/scopes.json`.** D5's universe grows from production Python and the card to production, `tools/**`, `tests/**`, the instrument scripts under `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/workflows/` and `dev/audit/harnesses/`, and the `docs/img/` generators (`.py`, `.sh`, `.js`, `.mjs`), in ten seats. D6's universe gains RELEASE_NOTES.md, production Python and the card (user-visible strings), the instrument documents, READMEs under tools/, tests/README.md, dev/audit/README.md, role contracts, rules, dimension briefs, the living handover and the plan, in seven seats. D6's `static` map names the records it leaves out, each with its reason: round evidence and RCAs, the archive, delivery, register and triage rows, decision records, dated design records, the generated `.claude`/`.cursor` rules, and the linters' fixtures. A new `ledger` key per dimension caps each seat at `max_units` text units (4500, chosen so the largest single file, tests/features.py, fits with room), so a seat's cell can be finished.
- **`tools/audit/check_scopes.py`** enforces both, and its `--self-test` refuses each perturbation. A seat over the cap is refused by name. So is a path matching D6's `classify` globs (`**.md`, `**.mdc`, `**.html`) that is in neither the universe nor `static`, a path in both, and a static entry that names nothing or carries no reason. A new README or role file therefore cannot slip out of D6 unnoticed, and D5's own `classify` line does the same for a comment-bearing script.
- **D5's comment line (repair of the class-open block at ac1607ad).** D5 now draws the line D6 draws for documents: `scopes.json`'s D5 `classify` is `**.{py,sh,js,mjs}`, the suffixes `text_ledger.py`'s D5 rule reads comments from (one constant, `text_ledger.D5_SUFFIXES`), and its `static` map names the frozen evidence it leaves (`dev/audit/{rounds,rca,waves}/**`, `dev/archive/**`), each with its reason. `check_scopes.py` refuses a carrier in neither, a ledger dimension drawing no `classify`, and a D5 `classify` missing any suffix the ledger reads. The three instrument seams the verdict named are measured, not dispositioned away: `.claude/hooks/*.sh`, `.claude/workflows/*.js` and `dev/audit/harnesses/**` join D5's universe in a new seat, D5-s10 (box B12), because `CLAUDE.md` names the harnesses as instruments a later seat reruns (fixer.md step 18), so they are not frozen evidence the way `dev/audit/rounds/**` is. The `docs/img/` image generators join it too, in the docs seat s2, whose `docs/**` glob already reaches them.
- **`dev/governance/dimensions/D6.md`, `D5.md`.** D6 rows every unit and runs one executed check per claim against the code that decides the behaviour, never a comment. D6 runs before D5's comment pass. A finding covers one file, and its harness output is `check`'s. D5 step 4 stops sampling: every comment and docstring in its cells is judged true or false of the code it sits on by an executed check of that code, and the concision judgement is kept. D6 carries the rulings verbatim and D5 cites them, so there is one copy.
- **`.claude/workflows/audit-find.js`.** Boxes B11-B13 hold the eleven new light seats (D5-s10 in B12). `CADENCE` stays at 2 for D5 and D6, and **that is wrong for ruling 1**: at 2, D5 and D6 are off in round 11, while the ruling puts "2 and 3 in round 11". The base's `check-wave-script.mjs` named D5 as its cadence-off arm, so it refuses `D5: 1` (`ci_predict` BOOTSTRAP). Following fixer.md step 5, this pull request is p1. It carries the grader hunk, which now reads every dimension's activity off `CADENCE` and so passes at either value, plus the policy. p2 is the one-line `CADENCE` move, `D5: 1, D6: 1`, which can land once p1 is on main (Forward-carry).

**Why round 10 missed "The optimizer never writes a recommended space set-point."** I established this from the record rather than assuming it. The sentence is `space_setpoint_entity`'s description in strings.json and translations/en.json, added by 6f02b8a71e (#483). No round-8, -9 or -10 D6 output contains it (`git grep` below, rc 1). Round 9's claims table (`dev/audit/rounds/round9/D6/s1/claims_table.txt`) has four strings.json rows, C50, C53, C54 and C59, all about field keys and labels. Round 10's D6-s3 owned strings.json, and its `claims_checked=3741` (`dev/audit/rounds/round10/D6/s3/REPORT.md`) counted key parity between strings.json and en/sv, plus services.yaml against the registered schemas. That is a check that keys exist, not that their sentences are true. The method extracted only sentences that looked claim-bearing and kept no record of the ones it skipped, so the skip left no trace. Under the amended method the miss is impossible in two places. First, `text_ledger.py units --dim D6` lists that sentence as a unit, and `check` refuses any ledger without a row for it; the self-test pins that sentence as a unit. Second, the row is a claim about behaviour, so its check must run the code: D6.md step 2 says "A key-parity check is no truth check".

**Finding shape and COMMON.md: it fits as written, so this PR does not change COMMON.md.** A finding covers one file with false or stale rows. Each COMMON.md requirement maps onto it:
- Item 1, the executed number: `text_ledger.py check`'s counts over the seat's ledger, which is TSV under the round directory.
- Item 2, the instrumented symbol: the production symbol that the false row's own check drives.
- Item 3, the perturbation: the one-line production edit that makes that row's check return the sentence's claim. The count moves down by one when that row is re-run.
- Item 4, the metric: false or stale rows per file.

The planted unit is an extra null control on completeness. COMMON item 5 asks for one only for cost, gain or time, so it fits beside that item.

The truth-side control the dispatch proposed, a known-false sentence planted where the seat cannot see it, is **not built**. Planting it blind means editing the export before the fan-out, and every dimension's seats read that same export (`audit-find.js` `workdir`), so a planted sentence would corrupt other dimensions' measurements. Forward-carry asks the owner for a ruling.

Generated scope-line block: The generated scope-line block is left out of this body: update_pr.sh verifies it against its own merge head, which no body can name in advance (R10-HOTFIX-UPDATEPR-FIGURE-REFRESH); the scope line is the gate's own MODE line at the head.

## Re-cut

Round-3 repair by the cloud fixer seat, against reviewed head 09c0bc5ce99c4ed0b27e780d08aa6be28bf06bbd (verdict `mutant-committed`). One commit, c2508883c4, changes code: it restores `classify_errors`' line `errs += [f"static and in the universe: {f}" for f in sorted(stat & uni)]` in `tools/audit/check_scopes.py`, which ff9b385bcd had replaced with `pass`. Nothing else in the function changes: `git diff ff9b385bcd^ HEAD -- tools/audit/check_scopes.py` prints nothing. Every figure below was re-taken at c2508883c4. Figures that moved since 38f90d9be7 moved because main moved under them (the merge of c987209cc7): D5 universe 851 to 853, the cadence grader 226 to 227 passed, and strings.json 2234 to 2250 units.

**Leftover-mutant sweep.** The whole branch was read: `git diff c987209cc7...HEAD` in full (13 files, 849+/65-), every code hunk by eye. That covers `tools/audit/check_scopes.py`, `tools/audit/text_ledger.py` (new), `tools/policy/check-wave-script.mjs`, `.claude/workflows/audit-find.js`, `.github/workflows/governance.yml`, `tests/layout.json` and `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json`; the remaining files are briefs, instrument docs and `scopes.json` data. Each removed code line in the three-dot diff is replaced by an extended form of itself (the import line, the `check`/`verdict` signatures, `status`, `sizes`, the `live = verdict(...)` and final `sys.exit` calls, and the cadence assertion). Per commit, `git show -U0 <c> -- '*.py' '*.js' '*.mjs' '*.yml' '*.json'` grepped for an added bare `pass`, `return`/`return None|True|False|0|1`, `continue`, `break`, `exit 0` or `|| true` over the 8 non-merge commits. It returns ff9b385bcd's `pass` and, in e130ee97a4, `text_ledger.py`'s `except ValueError: pass` in `plant`, its `return None` returns (`user_text`, `parse_ledger`), its tokenizer `continue`/`break` and `run_check`'s header-refusal `return 1`. Each of those is new code whose path the self-test drives, not a replaced line. `git status --short` is empty. Found: no other mutant.

**How the mutant got committed (defect-root-cause.md, second trigger).** The round-2 fixer ran a hand mutation of `classify_errors` in place in the branch worktree, with no `mutant_guard` (`dev/audit/harnesses/mutant_guard.py`, which refuses to start on a dirty path and restores from `HEAD` on exit) and no restore check. The next commit, ff9b385bcd ("D5.md: the scope line fits the brief's line cap"), was made with the mutant still in the working tree, so it swept `check_scopes.py` in beside the D5.md edit. Two things should have caught it before the handoff, and neither did:
- `tools/pr/prepr.sh` does not run a changed instrument's own self-test. It runs fixed self-tests (its own, `fold_ledger.py`, `tmp_paths.py`) and the diff-mutant lane only when `MUTANT_CMD` is set, which it was not.
- The body's `SELF-TEST passed` figure was taken at an earlier head and carried to 38f90d9be7, not re-taken there as fixer.md step 6 requires.

Process state: **(b), the process existed and was not followed**. fixer.md step 2 says "paste the failing check names, restore" and step 6 says re-take the evidence on each new tree. Both were obeyed for the recorded proofs but not for this unrecorded extra mutation. Cheaper detector: running `python3 -I tools/audit/check_scopes.py --self-test --repo .` locally before the push. It fails at the mutant head (rc=1, below) and costs 50 s per run on this container (`date +%s.%N` around the run). The gate that did catch it was CI's `governance / instrument-self-tests`, plus the owed `gate` it feeds, and a third review round. Cost test: cost(countermeasure) is about 50 s for each prepr run on a branch that touches `check_scopes.py`. cost(defect) is one review round, measured in hours per occurrence. P(recurrence) has no measured class frequency; this is the first mutant-committed verdict this fixer knows of. Countermeasure, for this seat: every hand mutation in this repair ran in a detached scratch worktree at the head (`git worktree add --detach`), so the branch worktree was never edited, and `git diff --quiet HEAD` printed `BRANCH_CLEAN` afterwards. A tree-wide check (prepr running each changed instrument's own `governance.yml` self-test line) is a tooling change outside this group's files and is not built here. It goes to the root-cause seat as a separate seat's call, per defect-root-cause.md "What is owed" item 2. Carry: dismissed: the root-cause seat beside this fix owns the process countermeasure (defect-root-cause.md item 2), and this body records the state and the cost numbers it starts from

## Head

`3230ac7113e513864159360d16a6fd35828997ad` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

59d971b5a5efe936f3212aa3ce0e93d2ea40a69d: the repair commit c2508883c4 merged with the PR branch origin/fix/r10-d5-d6-full-scope at 09c0bc5ce9 (it adds only `dev/programme/delivery/3571.md`, the orchestrator's delivery row). Resumed from handoff/r10-d5-d6-full-scope at 02d55e2812 (merge base c987209cc7a891e0e4066d4ad8dc5cf55357c5ae, which carries main's weekend-clock fix). origin/main was 513a07dfdc0daf09a054826974dbb64bfea9de27 at 2026-11-14T03:56:19Z, and `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` prints one tree, with no conflict.

## Mutation proof

Re-taken at c2508883c4. Each mutation ran in its own detached scratch worktree at that head, never in the branch worktree:
- The reviewer's mutant (ff9b385bcd's `pass` in place of the static-and-in-the-universe line), at 02d55e2812: `python3 -I tools/audit/check_scopes.py --self-test --repo .` prints `SELF-TEST FAILED` with arm `'a static path in the universe is refused': False`, rc=1. Restored at c2508883c4, it prints `SELF-TEST passed (every perturbed scope refused)`, rc=0.
- `text_ledger.py`: with `unrowed = sorted(ids - set(by_id))` changed to `unrowed = []`, `python3 -I tools/audit/text_ledger.py --self-test` prints `FAIL a dropped row is refused by its unit id` and `17 checks, 1 failed`, rc=1. At the head it prints `17 checks, 0 failed`.
- `check_scopes.py` cap: with `if n > d["ledger"]["max_units"]]` replaced by `if False]`, the self-test prints `SELF-TEST FAILED` with `'a seat over ledger.max_units is refused by name': False`, rc=1.
- `check_scopes.py` line: with `errs += [f"classified in neither ...` made `errs += [] and [...]`, the self-test prints `SELF-TEST FAILED` with four arms false: the D6 unstatic arm, the D5 outside plant, the D6 null plant and the D5 round-evidence arm. rc=1.
- D5 carrier probe: with the `classify misses a D5 comment carrier` comprehension's `if dim == "D5"` made `if False`, the self-test prints `'a D5 classify missing a comment carrier is refused': False`, `SELF-TEST FAILED`, rc=1.
- Not re-taken in this repair, and recorded by round 2 at 38f90d9be7: the cadence-control mutation (`activeIn` reduced to `!!CADENCE[dim]`, `node tools/policy/check-wave-script.mjs` 2 failed) and the fix-reverted D5 comment-line copy with its committed plant. Neither file changed in this repair.
- The self-test's own arm against a vacuous `--plant`: a ledger that already rows the planted unit must fail `--plant` (`--plant fails a ledger that already rows the planted unit`).

## Null control

- D6's documentation line is unchanged by the D5 repair: the self-test arm "null control: a document in neither D6 universe nor static is still refused" plants a committed-shape `dev/zz-planted.md` and reads `classified in neither universe nor static: dev/zz-planted.md` from D6.
- The self-test's complete ledger passes `check` with and without `--plant` (arm "null control: the complete ledger passes, and its plant is refused"). Its live D5 and D6 pass the cap and the line (arm "null control: the live D5 and D6 pass the cap and the line").
- The base, carried from round 2 and not re-taken: base scopes at 90c6bc3b07 have no `ledger` key, so `check_scopes.py` prints no unit column there.

## Figures

All taken at c2508883c4, whose tree differs from 59d971b5a5 only by the delivery row, 2026-11-14T03:56Z.
- Self-tests, in governance.yml's `self-tests-outside-seat` order:
  - `python3 -I tools/audit/check_scopes.py --self-test --repo .` prints `SELF-TEST passed (every perturbed scope refused)`, rc=0. Its control is the reviewer's mutant above, rc=1.
  - `python3 -I tools/audit/text_ledger.py --self-test` prints `17 checks, 0 failed`.
  - `node tools/policy/check-wave-script.mjs` prints `227 passed, 0 failed`, its cadence line reading `off at 11: D5, D6, D11, D13; every dimension on at 12 as its cadence says`.
  - `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/selftest_wiring.py --check` prints `selftest_wiring: 0 index gap(s)`.
  - `python3 -I tools/ci/selftest_scope.py --self-test` prints `120 checks, 0 failed`.
- D5 and D6 seats, units per seat (rule: `text_ledger.py`'s units over each seat's files for the ledger step): `python3 tools/audit/check_scopes.py --repo . --ref HEAD` exits 0.
  - D5 prints `seats=10 universe=853`, with units per seat from 0 (s1) to 3809 (s7), and D5-s10 at `312f/1704u`.
  - D6 prints `seats=7 universe=344`, with units per seat from 2246 (s6) to 4005 (s2).
  - Coverage prints `unclassified=0`.
  - Every seat is under `max_units` 4500. The null control is the self-test arm that caps D6 at 1 and is refused by seat name, and the cap mutant above.
- The class the round-2 verdict named, enumerated by rule (tracked paths matching D5's `classify` less D5's universe less `static`): the live D5 line prints `ok` at this head. Its control is the self-test's committed-shape plant, a comment-bearing .js file planted directly under .claude/ (the path is the self-test's `POUT`, never committed), which the same rule returns and refuses (arm `a comment carrier in neither D5 universe nor static is refused`, True here and False under the line mutant). The per-directory census at ac1607ad is round 2's and was not re-taken; the dispositions it lists are in `scopes.json`, unchanged here.
- Round-10 sentence enumerated: `python3 tools/audit/text_ledger.py units --dim D6 custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/strings.json | grep -c "never writes a recommended space set-point"` prints 1, out of 2250 units in that file (`| wc -l`).
- Absent from every earlier D6 output: `git grep -c "never writes a recommended" 90c6bc3b0756475e28d4ace8d8e31c4788474933 -- dev/audit/rounds/round9/D6 dev/audit/rounds/round10/D6` exits 1. With `priority_cancel` on, it asserts that only #11's queued run is cancelled, and that unreadable comments cancel nothing.

**Part two (advisory on push) is already on main, so this diff builds nothing for it.** The owner's 2026-11-11 ruling, as triage recorded it (`dev/programme/triage/s6-batch218.md#P666`: "on push, ci-ratchet is reported advisory (its result printed, never a gate failure); on pull requests it stays as today"), was built by R10-GATE-PUSH-RATCHET at ef4556bb42 (2026-11-12T08:55Z, before the four red pushes of 2026-11-14): `tools/ci/gate.py`'s `PUSH_REPORT_ONLY` holds `ci-ratchet`, and `machinery_line()` prints its conclusion while the gate passes.
