merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-MAIN-SELFTEST-SCOPE: union main's traced self-test read sets into tools/ci/selftest_closures.json

Main is red on `governance / instrument-self-tests`, step "Refuse a self-test read set the committed table misses", on every push since f7e7a0244a (#3573). The last green run of that step is 43553916206 at 0f37833e21 (#3547). At origin/main 9fdba3b854 (run 43611495159, job 132497640978) it prints `selftest_scope check: 114 gated step(s), 11 refusal(s)`, every one an UNDER-SCOPED line. Five merges added the reads. The first run that refuses each one names the merge:

- #3573 (f7e7a0244a): pr-merger misses `tools/audit/seat/proof_watch.py`; ci-prelude and gate-predicate miss `tools/ci/fixtures/gate_requeued_needs_runs.json`.
- #3544 (a77d71fb75): verdict-bus misses `dev/governance/roles/fixer.md`.
- #3584 (1791869fdb): gate-sweep misses `tools/ci/gate.py`, `tools/ci/ghapi.py`, `tools/ci/prelude.py`, and the probe `tools`.
- #3567 (5e3274a19f), which adds the tracked directory `dev/audit/rounds/round10/user-text`: policy-lint-mutants (probe `.gitattributes` there), dependency-graph-census and prepr (dirs).
- #3565 (6b61e47cc2): beat-job-rows misses 371 files and 46 dirs.

The repair is the one `tools/ci/selftest_scope.py` states: commit the table the drift step itself writes. Two traced push runs each uploaded a `selftest-closures` artifact. Each artifact is the committed table unioned with that run's measurement: 43607468927 at 6b61e47cc2, and 43611495159 at origin/main 9fdba3b854. Both are folded into the table with the instrument's own `union_entries` and written by its `write_table`. Nothing is edited by hand, and the check is not touched. The fold is `union.py`: it loads the committed table, unions each artifact's `steps` over it with `selftest_scope.union_entries`, and writes the result with `selftest_scope.write_table`. No entry loses a read. A per-step comparison of the old table against the new one, using `selftest_scope.covers`, finds two items gone. Both are beat-job-rows probes, `tools/audit` and `tools/audit/seat`. `write_table`'s `compact_probes` folds them into directories the step now lists (`tools`, `tools/audit`, `tools/audit/seat`). `drift` excuses a probe under a listed directory, so the fold does not change what main refuses.

What a PR run proves here, and what it does not: `SELFTEST_TRACE` is set only on `push` (governance.yml, the job's `env`). So a pull-request run never traces and never runs the drift step, and no PR run can show this repair green. This change touches a `GATE_FILES` member (the table), so the PR's instrument-self-tests run is FULL. It proves every step still passes, that `static` finds the table consistent and not stale against the workflow, and that the scope self-test passes. Only the first push to main after the merge proves the drift step green. Until then, the proof below replays the traced step's own comparison (`selftest_scope.drift`) with each run's CI-measured artifact as the measurement. The function documents that the compacted artifact and the live fold refuse the same lines. On origin/main's table, the replay reproduces the CI step's 11 refusals line for line.

## Head

`341677c1974c819ee417226897047192b703014c` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3589.md`. The authored code head is `2b8893814da8e6cf0a5fd8b33c05d849f2717d45`.

`f454b6fa70e6c8e56699dbd3b0aec499fea53b6f` merges origin/main `931970141c` into the authored code head `2b8893814da8e6cf0a5fd8b33c05d849f2717d45` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below).

2b8893814da8e6cf0a5fd8b33c05d849f2717d45, measured against origin/main 9fdba3b854 at 2026-11-14T16:41Z (`date -u`).

## Mutation proof

n/a: no production line changes. The diff is the measured table alone. The table's role in the check is shown both ways under Null control: the origin/main table refuses 11 lines and the head's table refuses none, over the same measurement.

## Null control

The unmodified tree, origin/main 9fdba3b854. Replaying `selftest_scope.drift` with run 43607468927's artifact as the measurement prints `replay: 114 gated step(s), 11 refusal(s)`. These are the same 11 UNDER-SCOPED lines that CI job 132485295279 printed. The CI step at the same tree (run 43611495159, job 132497640978) prints `selftest_scope check: 114 gated step(s), 11 refusal(s)`. At the head, the same replay with either run's artifact prints `replay: 114 gated step(s), 0 refusal(s), 0 note(s)`.

## Figures

<!-- figure-block: scope-line mb=931970141cf9e213ab0f5283bdcfdb128a0f127c head=341677c1974c819ee417226897047192b703014c -->

MODE: FULL -- every test script runs, nothing is scoped out.

The CI step at the same tree printed 11 (job 132497640978).

- Gate scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` prints `MODE: FULL` (the table is a gate file). CI runs it.

- `governance / instrument-self-tests` (main push runs 43603039666, 43607468927, 43611495159, and every main push run since 43556918153), step "Refuse a self-test read set the committed table misses". It fails with 11 UNDER-SCOPED refusals and is repaired by this diff. Root-cause answer: the cheaper detector is to trace each pull request's selected self-test steps and run `check` over the steps that ran. The PR job already runs those steps through `tools/ci/selftest_step.sh`, but `SELFTEST_TRACE` is push-only. Its standing cost is strace overhead on every PR's selected steps, up to one traced 60-minute run per PR that selects many steps, as R10-RCA-MAIN-SELFTESTS-RED section 2d priced it. Its alternative, countermeasure A of that RCA (main commits the measured table mechanically), is ruled to round 11. Section 2d recorded "the record stands until a second instance". This red is at least the fourth instance (R10-HOTFIX-MAIN-SELFTESTS, R10-HOTFIX-MAIN-IST-READSET-2, R10-HOTFIX-SELFTEST-SCOPE-RERECORD, this one). The analysis belongs to the root-cause seat beside this fix, not to this PR.
- `tests / ci-ratchet` (main push runs 43603039666 through 43607708534) is not this diff's red, and this diff does not repair it. On a push it is report-only by design: the owner's 2026-11-11 ruling was built by #3500 (merge cbe8d93bd8) as `PUSH_REPORT_ONLY` in `tools/ci/gate.py`. Main's `gate` job succeeds in the same runs where ci-ratchet fails, as the ruling specifies. This red prints `ci-ratchet: CI push run 43602217369 has no completed `tests / *` job (fail closed)`. Run 43602217369 (97a3a921e0, #3570) was cancelled at `prelude` with every `tests / *` job skipped. `tests/ci_ratchet.py` `_walk` returns None for a run with a cancelled `tests / *` job, but refuses a completed run whose `tests / *` jobs never ran. It is not a budget overrun. That walk belongs to the live group R10-HOTFIX-CI-RATCHET-SKIPPED-RUN. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-CI-RATCHET-SKIPPED-RUN

## Forward-carry

- beat-job-rows now records 371 files and 46 dirs, nearly the whole `tools/` and `.github/workflows/` tree. The cause is #3565's self-test check "the wired set is the real tree's seat self-tests". It calls `beat_jobs.darwin_instruments(<repo root>)`, so `selftest_wiring.self_testing` walks all of `tools/`. This re-record records that read set as-is, because the measurement is the authority, and does not bless it. The step will now run on nearly every pull request that touches `tools/` or a workflow. A hermetic fixture tree would let the step scope again. No live roster group owns `tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs*.py` (R10-BEAT-JOB-TABLE and R10-HOTFIX-MACOS-SELFTEST-LANE are done), so it is reported to the orchestrator for routing. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-MACOS-SELFTEST-LANE | dismissed: deliberate real-tree wiring check recorded as measured, the routing of a hermetic fixture is the orchestrator's
- Open PR #3551 (R10-SELFTEST-SCOPE-UNION-GUARD) also edits `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json`. Whichever lands second re-unions with `union_entries` over the other's table. #3551's shrink guard should treat a `compact_probes` fold, a probe dropped because a listed ancestor directory answers it, as no drop: this re-record contains two such folds. Carry: R10-SELFTEST-SCOPE-UNION-GUARD

Carry 10 (R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE, part 3): on a combi store the plan's hot-water figures now say which split they show. The carry accepts "count the store's charge as one channel" or "say which split it shows"; under the orchestrator's ruling on the predecessor's BLOCKED question (2026-11-14T10:45Z) this part delivers the second and forward-carries the first.

On an install whose `ThermalParameters.combi_tank_active` holds, DHW Heating Cost (next 24 h), DHW Energy (lifetime), DHW Cost (lifetime) and the climate entity's `dhw_heating_cost` attribute each publish a static `dhw_split` attribute: "what the heat pump spends in hot-water mode; with a combi store this includes space heat drawn from the store" (`entity.COMBI_DHW_SPLIT`, through `entity.dhw_split_attributes`). It is kept out of the recorder the same way as `split_method` (`_unrecorded_attributes` on each class). No entity is renamed, no figure moves, and strings.json and the translations are untouched. On every other install the attributes are what they were. README.md's three sensor rows and docs/configuration.md's combi-tank option say the same thing. tests/doc_claims.py pins the docs to the code's sentence, and tests/entities.py pins the attribute, its null and its unrecorded status.

Edit set: the ruling widened it by sensor.py, climate.py, README.md, the one docs page, tests/entities.py and tests/doc_claims.py. This diff also adds the helper to custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/entity.py, beside `has_hot_water`, because both platforms read it and no platform module imports another. The alternatives were the helper in sensor.py with climate.py importing a sibling platform, or the predicate copied into both, and each lost on that ground. The helper takes the thermal parameters rather than the coordinator. Handing it the coordinator charged its body to `coord_footprint` (+3, inadmissible). Passing the input it reads in is the contract's own rule, and the score reads NULL. No file on the ruling's not-editable list is touched: coordinator.py, heat_energy.py, dhw_planner.py, the exchange (`_combi_flux_exchange`) and the hot-water LP (`_plan_dhw_min_cost`).

## Head

`837ead0bd75a34e576bf266847019725b2fcd104` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

4edd4f2d24 (merge): the merge of origin/main fafd6a9ff5 into 8341359750, with tests/doc_claims.py resolved by hand (authorised); README.md, docs/configuration.md and tests/entities.py auto-merged. The union keeps both whole, and `main()` calls both. The three Carry 10 checks still read the real text: README.md's rows, configuration.md's combi option and `entity.COMBI_DHW_SPLIT` in the merged tree, whose dhw_split lines the merge left unchanged, so none needed a new anchor. `python3 tests/doc_claims.py` passes all 390 checks. Under `mutant_run.py --in-place`, SURVIVED NULL, then KILLED for each Carry 10 perturbation: a README hot-water row loses `dhw_split`, the space row gains it, the combi option loses it, and the code sentence changes. Each fails only its own check. Main's flow pin is also KILLED ("sent again every 5 minutes" made 7 fails "every quoted figure in the flow help (19 pins)"), so the union did not hollow it out. `git diff fafd6a9ff5 HEAD --stat` names only this part's eight files.

8341359750 (code): the branch merged with origin/main at a2ef25b4b2 (PR 3574 landed), which is the merge base every figure below is taken against, at 2026-11-14T13:07:27Z. The code's own commits are unchanged by the merge: `git diff cb97628f08 8341359750` over entity.py, sensor.py, climate.py, tests/entities.py and dev/audit/harnesses/r10_combi_tank.py prints nothing.

`python3 tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --spec <16 named mutants> --cmd '<the Carry 10 block of tests/entities.py>'`. The command ran tests/entities.py's header (through `DATA`) and then the block from the `# R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE Carry 10` marker, the way `features_block.py` runs a features.py block. Running the whole of `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` per mutant reproduces the same kills, more slowly. `SURVIVED NULL`, then KILLED on each of:
- entity.py: `COMBI_DHW_SPLIT` text changed (entity_const_text), the combi guard `if False` (entity_guard_off), the guard without `combi_tank_active` (entity_guard_on), the `dhw_split` return deleted (entity_return_del).
- sensor.py: DHW Heating Cost's attribute property returns None (sensor_cost_attr_del), drops `or None` (sensor_cost_or_none), is handed no parameters (sensor_cost_params_none), or loses `dhw_split` from `_unrecorded_attributes` (sensor_cost_unrecorded). The accumulator's `_unrecorded_attributes` loses `dhw_split` (sensor_acc_unrecorded). The `_ledger_line == "dhw"` guard is `if False` (sensor_acc_guard_off) or `if True` (sensor_acc_guard_on, killed by the space-figure null). The update call is deleted (sensor_acc_call_del) or handed None (sensor_acc_params_none).
- climate.py: the `_unrecorded_attributes` line is emptied (climate_unrecorded), the update call is deleted (climate_call_del), or it is handed None (climate_params_none).

`mutant_run.py --diff a2ef25b4b2...HEAD` with the same command printed no `SURVIVED` line (rc 0) over the 12 mutants it draws from the added production lines (`--list`).

1. Card DHW kWh tile: none exists. The card's tiles are `tiles.price_now`, `tiles.planned`, `tiles.cost` and `tiles.indoor` (custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/www/heatpump-optimizer-card.js). Its DHW series is the `dhw_slots` power bars, and the receipt shows `BILLED_LINES` only.

merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE part 4: Carry 9. Behind a throttling valve whose curve cannot hold the target, `_thermostat_held_state` bisected a family of states with both floors at one temperature (`_held_zones`). On a two-zone house the plant at its pump settles with the floors apart: radiators above, slab-fed floor below, and the mean is warmer than any level state the curve can feed. The reference therefore started below its own ceiling, and its 96-step day warmed to that ceiling, so every booked day bought the warming. That affects `baseline_cost` and the saving against it on every two-zone valved install whose curve is the bound.

The fix adds `thermal_model.valve_top_equilibrium`, which solves the plant's own rates (`_two_zone_rates`, affine while each zone sits below its circuit's top) with every circuit at the curve's top. `optimizer._held_at_valve_top` takes that equilibrium only where the valve's top draw is the bound and the pump can make that draw (`_pump_unreachable`, now shared with `_held_unreachable`). Anywhere else, the level bisection (`_held_bisected`, moved out unchanged) holds as before.

The three measurements the brief puts first:
- **(0) The harness.** Pull request 3481 has not merged (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 9a543f44d696 origin/main` is false at `a77d71fb755f`). Its `fields` arm was run from that head in a detached worktree. Its imports (`whatif`) and `_compute_baseline_power(start=)` do not exist on main, so it cannot run against the merge base. The install row is in this pull request's own harness, `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_held_install.py`.
- **(1) The `fields` arm at 3481's head.** That head's base is main `c987209cc7`, whose production code equals `a77d71fb755f`'s (`git diff --quiet c987209cc7 a77d71fb75 -- custom_components/` exits 0); 3481's own diff adds the `start=` hook and touches neither `_thermostat_held_state`'s body nor `_held_unreachable`. Second-pass room: single-zone 21.00, valve one tank 19.88, two-zone valve two-tank 21.01 (`## Figures`).
- **(2) Install-parameter reproduction.** The 3574 body reports a scratch probe on `tests/replay/owner-2026-10-30-away.json` (two zones, valve `manual` at 21 C, a 4 kW pump). Its probe is not in the tree, so this pull request builds the reproduction as `tests/profiles.py` `replay_install()`, used by the new harness and the new checks. At the merge base, +5 C reads: held 20.527, day's end 20.719, plant's ceiling 20.719. At -15 C: held 19.532, end 19.982, plant 19.980. 3574 read 20.557 against 20.749 at its own base, the same shape.
- **(3) The cause, from the code.**
  - **The synthetic one-tank fixture is the unreachable case part 1 models.** No behaviour changes there. The plant at its pump settles where the reference holds: 19.888 at 0 C, 20.662 / 19.115 / 17.568 at +5 / -5 / -15 C (`## Figures`). The bound is the derived curve, `mixing_valve.flow_setpoint`. Its draw is `_single_valve_rates`' `ua * (min(T_buf, flow_set) - T_slab)`. The curve adds the house's loss over the emitter UA to the target, but the single-zone emitters feed the slab, so the slab-to-room resistance is not in it, and the room settles below target even with the target at `comfort_ceiling`. The plan cannot do better: `_derive_hold_schedule` only ever lowers the valve target below `mixing_valve_target or comfort_ceiling`, and `manual` mode sets none. This part's files leave that alone; the plant-curve finding is carried (`## Forward-carry`). The new check's one-tank control and the 3481 `fields` row pin that the reference equals the plant there.
  - **On the install it is the held state.** The cause is `_thermostat_held_state`'s unreachable branch: `held_at` builds every candidate through `_held_zones`, `upper_floor_temperature = lower_floor_temperature = temp`. `_held_unreachable`'s valve half (`need_kw > valve_top_draw(...)`) is right. The family it is tested on is what is wrong: the curve's top draw at level floors is less than at the plant's own split.
  - **`valve_top_draw` is right**: the plant's draw is the same `_circuit_draw` at the same tops.
  - **`_compute_baseline_power`'s use is right**: from the corrected held state its day ends where it starts (gap 0.000, `## Figures`).

## Head

`af01d592585120f546221394cb694bf6e51a94b1` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`8fac4e7e5b18dff2973f3cf35848199b9de26fb1`, seven commits on origin/main `a77d71fb755f231934e5e59ce1c38c51f86b6439`, measured 2026-11-14 (UTC). The last commit adds only `tests/closures.json`'s INERT entry (`tools/pr/ci_predict.py --apply-inert`) and deletes the moved pin; every other figure was taken at `193b86d9d0`, whose production code and checks are the head's (`git diff --stat 193b86d9d0 8fac4e7e5b` names those two files alone). `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflict. Pull request 3574 had not landed at that tip, so origin/main was not merged. VERSION, the manifest and RELEASE_NOTES are untouched.

## Mutation proof

Command: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components python3 tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff a77d71fb755f...HEAD --report-only --cmd "python3 tools/audit/seat/features_block.py '# --- R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE: stored heat bought back' '# --- R10-WATER-SETPOINT-FEEDBACK (outside report #3380'"`.
- 35 mutants are drawn (`--list`). 32 are killed. The 3 survivors are the three `>` to `>=` equality bounds, each triaged equivalent under `tests/mutation_ledger/survivor_triage/`:
  - `optimizer.py` `_held_at_valve_top` CMP_BOUND db7fdb5e;

  - `thermal_model.py` `valve_top_equilibrium` CMP_BOUND 43d78bdc.

- Failing first: at `6fcca20502` (the checks alone, base production code), the same block reads `FAIL R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE Carry 9: on an install whose valve curve cannot hold the setpoint, ...` with the held floors level at 20.527 against the plant's 20.719 / 21.009 / 20.428 at +5 C, `1 of 12 FEATURES BLOCK FAILED`.
- At the head: `ALL 13 FEATURES BLOCK PASSED`.
- Three first-round survivors were removed by changing the code, not by triage. The tank line re-derived the tank `held_at` had already placed at the curve's top. The steady charge's `dt` multiplied a zero; it is now `math.inf`. The solve's zero origin is now the state's own zones.
- That last edit exposed a real gap, which part 1's pump check (4 kW, valve at 40 C, -25 C) caught at 36.9 C: the valve's ceiling was taken where the pump, not the curve, was the bound. `cdbd4c6f56` gates it on the valve's own bound.
- The stale `_held_unreachable` CMP_BOUND triage and RETURN_DEL pin at ebd24b04 are deleted: their line moved unchanged into `_pump_unreachable`.

## Null control

- Bit for bit, merge base against head, `_thermostat_held_state`'s room and the day's summed `_compute_baseline_power` (float hex, a scratch probe over 4 outdoor temperatures x 6 houses). 20 of 24 rows are identical: single-zone, two-zone, the one-tank valve, the two-zone valve two-tank control, and the install with its valve off. The 4 install-valve rows move (`## Figures`).
- The install with the valve off holds 21.000 on both floors at every temperature; that is the new check's null and the harness's `valve off` rows.
- Flat price: `tests/golden/flat_prices.json` (`baseline_cost` 100.179654) and its valved twin `valve_storage_flat_prices` (two-zone, valve `manual`) are unmoved. Neither reaches the changed branch: a counting probe over `golden.capture` reads `_held_at_valve_top` called 0 times in each (2 held-state calls each), because both curves hold the target there.
- Golden drift: no scenario moves (`## Figures`).

  - Base (base production code, this tree's `tests/`):
    - install +5 C: `held 20.527/20.527/20.527 end 20.719/21.009/20.429 plant 20.719/21.009/20.428 gap 0.482`

merges.body:
R10-OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE, part 1 of 2: an allowlisted outside contributor's fork pull request is adopted on our machine from main's copy of the contract. Built to the design note at `design/R10-OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE` 142e70df1b77cf9e7f63d6675b9ad560941e20c9 and its approval at `design-verdict/R10-OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE` fb36c832b6eeb3307bb07502d9a2529b36474535. No finder harness: owner report (tvofi, 2026-11-12, triage batch 238, entry P714). `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py`, `remerge_main.sh` and `merge_pr.sh` are part 2's and are not edited.

**Three things a reader must know first.**

1. **This pull request raises one budget, and the owner has not confirmed it in person.** `files_tokens` for `dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md`, see `## Raise justification`. It rests on `CLAUDE.md` rule 2's mandate exception and merges only if `budget-raise-gate` admits it.
2. **Three checks the design owes were not run, because this seat holds no owner credential and no test fork:** the two live checks (design items 8 and 20) and the account behind `secrets.CLOSURES_PUSH_TOKEN` (design item 19). Decision 0017 lists them under "Before the first allowlist entry" and the allowlist's own comment points there. Class O's condition 3 is written to both answers GitHub can give and to the intermediate-commit case (verdict item 25), so no answer of the live check changes the code; which answer GitHub gives is not recorded here.
3. **The mechanism is inert at merge:** the allowlist merges empty and the owner adds the entry after part 2.

What was built, by file:

- `tools/pr/outside.py` (new): admission, the three path classes with default deny, the manifest version, class O in both forms, and `approve`, the one writer of the mandated class-O approval.
- `dev/governance/config/outside_contributors.json` (new, empty) and two `.github/CODEOWNERS` lines (the allowlist, `outside.py`).
- `tools/audit/seat/bus.sh`: `adopt <pr> <comment id>`.
- `tools/pr/app_approve.sh`, `carry` only: a head that is no branch tip of origin carries only the automatic merge of main; verdict item 21's merge arm. `--carry` now asks origin for its branch heads whenever the range holds a commit, so a carry test of a local head never pushed refuses every non-merge commit in it; the instrument guide says so. Four other instruments run the real `--carry` in their own self-test over a head their fixture never put on a branch of origin, so their fixtures are repaired, in `tools/pr/app_comment.sh`, `tools/audit/seat/review_carry.py`, `tools/audit/seat/ledger.py` and `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py`, self-test code only: the carried head sits on a branch of origin, as a pull request of ours holds it, and each self-test gains the fork arm as a new pin. The alternative, a seam in `carry()` that a fixture switches (an environment variable or an argument naming the head as ours), lost: it is a switch on the one question the rule exists to ask of origin, reachable by any caller, and it would leave the four self-tests proving the seam instead of the rule. The new `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` sits in the D5 and D6 universes of `dev/audit/config/scopes.json`, beside the other `docs/*.md`; an exclusion lost, because the guide states how the project works and those two dimensions measure exactly that.
- `tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`: `--outside-author` (adoption's form), `--outside-pull` with `--outside-ref` (pr-contract's, spawning `outside.py`).
- `.github/workflows/pr-contract.yml`: the pulls answer saved to a file and two arguments on the `policy_lint.mjs` line. `.github/workflows/tests.yml`: the head ref name through `env:` and the same-repository conjunct on the `laneskip` step (verdict item 22). `.github/workflows/governance.yml` and `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json`: the `outside-contract` self-test step, placed ahead of `tick-loop`. `tests/closure.py` and `tests/closures.json`: `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` leaves the INERT prefix by an exact exception, beside the other reader docs, and enters the recorded closures of `tests/doc_claims.py` and `tests/harness_headers.py`.
- Decision 0017, `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`, two paragraphs in `dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md`, the instrument guides.

**Departures from the note, each raised here for the reviewer rather than made silently:**

- **Main's copy is a throwaway worktree of the fetched main commit, not six `git show` files.** `policy_lint.mjs --pr-body` and `carry_audit.py` import siblings and read the tree, so single files do not run. `adopt` then re-runs main's own `bus.sh` (`adopt-from-main`), which refuses unless its tree is the commit just fetched: the adoption logic itself, and every `push-verdict` gate, is main's too. The data (allowlist, CODEOWNERS) is still read with `git show <main sha>:<path>`.
- **Class R is tested before class F.** The note's table lists F first. The self-test holds, over the tracked tree, that no R path lies under an F rule, so no answer differs today and a later R rule cannot be shadowed.
- **pr-contract gets no new step: `policy_lint.mjs --pr-body` spawns the pinned `outside.py` itself** (`--outside-pull`, `--outside-ref`), over the pulls API's answer saved as a file, with no token and no API call. The note asked for four values through `env:` and one flag; this passes the whole answer as a file, so no contributor-named value reaches a shell either. Two earlier cuts were refused by the tree's own checks and are why: a step holding the job's token (`tests/entities.py`: "every pinned grader given a token runs its own copy under the Actions token on the pull request"), then a tokenless step whose shell broke `codeowners_gap.py`'s proof that the job runs `policy_lint.mjs` pinned (nine files read uncovered; back to zero now). Consequence, stated: the early signal reads neither the reviews (class O prints `PENDING:`) nor the other pull requests at the head, and reads `GATE_FILES` from the head's `tests/closure.py`, which pr-contract does not restore; adoption reads all three from main.
- **The allowlist is `dev/governance/config/outside_contributors.json`, one directory below the path the note and the dispatch name.** `tests/layout.json` places a governance data file under `config/` and refuses one beside it, and `policy_lint.mjs` already excludes that directory's JSON from the prose corpus, so the base's copy of the linter accepts the file with no edit.
- **The pull request's author and the verdict comment's author must be the SAME allowlist entry.** The note says "match one entry"; the stricter reading is taken.
- **fix-review.md gains two paragraphs, not a headed section:** the file sits at its line cap.
- **`adopt` reads the body lint and carry audit through `HPO_BUS_BODYLINT` and `HPO_BUS_CARRYAUDIT` in the self-test,** the file's existing stub convention (`HPO_BUS_CLASSIFY`, `HPO_BUS_PACKER`). The self-test therefore proves they are called and that a refusal refuses, not that main's real `policy_lint.mjs` passes a real body from a worktree.

Carries answered (design note items, then verdict items):

- 1, 10: the allowlist id is data; the head ref name is matched with `re.fullmatch` and reaches no shell string. 2: the review commit is read with `ls-tree` and `cat-file` only. 5, 6: `setpr` pushes a branch ref; `ls-remote` goes through `retry_with` and an unreadable one refuses. 7: `check --comment` refuses a comment that is not an issue comment of that pull request. 9: `checkPrBody` reads commits only in its Dependabot branch; the flag changes the author arm alone, and the in-file test compares the refusal count of another fixture with and without it. 12, 13: decision 0017 corrects 0011's citation and states three autofix jobs. 14: `approve` writes "mandate comment <id>" and the self-test proves `MANDATE_CITE` reads exactly that id. 15: the review list is read with `--paginate --slurp` and a non-list refuses. 17: the gate module is the running tree's (main's at adoption), loaded by path. 18, 27: fix-review.md's second paragraph.
- Round-2 verdict 14, 15: `adopt` runs main's `policy_lint.mjs --pr-body` and `carry_audit.py` over the live body, fetches main itself, and `check` refuses a base that is not `main` of ours. 16, 26: `check` refuses another pull request of any state at the head (the commit's associated pulls, and the head branch's pulls with `state=all`). 17: a manifest `version` diff refuses; the `docs/img/` scripts class O. 18, 19: latest decisive review; a review at L is accepted when L carries to the head.
- Verdict 21, 22, 24, 25, 28, 29: built, each with a self-test case named under `## Mutation proof`.
- Not this part's: 11, 16 (design), 23 (verdict). Part 2 imports `outside.py` by path; if that moves the recorded closure of the train's self-test, the verdict's Build parts already give part 2 the re-record.

## Carries received from part 2

Part 2 (`r10-outside-contributor-cycle-p2`) was built before this part published anything and left seven carries on this group's roster entry. Each, by its index there:

- Carry 0 (item d4703cd1, the interface to this module): built. What part 2 reconciles `Train.fork_head`, `Train.outside_contract` and merge_pr.sh's `head_is_ours` to, in `tools/pr/outside.py`: `pull_facts(repo, pr)` reads the pull request; `cross_repository(facts, repo)` is the one definition of a cross-repository head; `check(repo, pr, ref)` returns `(rc, lines)` with rc 0 admitted, 1 refused, 3 not an outside pull request, and is the whole contract with class O (verdict item 23's call at the landing head); `Rules(ref).classify(path, pr)` answers F, R or O; a shell caller runs `outside.py cross --repo O/R --pr N` (rc 0 cross-repository, 3 ours, 1 unread). Every read that fails raises `Refuse` or answers rc 1, never a default.
- Carry 1 (item 8da136bb, the self-test closure re-record): not this head's. This part records `outside-contract` and re-records `verdict-bus` and `app-approval`; at this head the train does not import `outside.py`, so its two steps cannot be traced reading it. Part 2 re-records them once this is on main, as the design verdict's Build parts say.
- Carry 2 (item 53108d53, the live checks): built as a written precondition. Decision 0017, "Before the first allowlist entry", lists the fork-head merge and its identity, the end-to-end approval of an adopted verdict, and the `commit_id` read; none was run by either part.
- Carry 3 (item aa80140a, the guides and decision 0017): built in part. Carry 29's sentence is in decision 0017 and in the guides of `outside.py` and `app_approve.sh`; decision 0017 point 7 says the train merges main into the fork branch itself or parks naming the fork. Not written here: remerge_main.sh's head-repository flag and the train's outside block class. Neither exists at this head, and a guide naming a flag the tree does not hold is a false claim; they go into those two instruments' guide pages with the code, in part 2's pull request.
- Carry 4 (item f7754778, the train's approval body under a bare mandate id): not this part's change. `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py` is not this part's to edit; `outside.py approve` writes "mandate comment <id>" and its self-test proves `MANDATE_CITE` reads exactly that id, and its case "class O REFUSE: _agent_approval_body under a bare mandate id" is the control that the train's body cites nothing. Whether our own heads' approvals should cite "mandate comment <id>" is a question for the group that next owns that file's seam; R10-GATE-DEFER-BARRIER, which the earlier body named, no longer receives carries (`carry_audit.py` reads it as carries-open). Carry: R11-INTAKE-R10-RESIDUE
- Carry 5 (item cc5c19fe, the predictor's missing roster fetch): held by main's mechanism, not by code of this branch. The carry requires that the clone `ci_tree_run` builds holds the round-roster refs `pr-contract.yml`'s fetch gives the job. Main's 68e1704e2b (pull request 3549) built that as `fetch_round_rosters(run)`, called in `ci_tree_run` on the line tagged `# mut:roundrefs` and pinned by `roundref_self_test(root)`; this branch's own helper for the same refs is removed at this head (`## Head`), and the requirement is measured on the merged tree under `## Figures`.
- Carry 6 (item 3518898b, the dispatch gave no interface): answered by Carry 0.
- Carry 7 (item 67320eeb, from r10-closeout-prep-p2, not part 2; read on `handoff/audit-r10-roster` at 5db6c975a7159f0a59341ceb2a0ddb448e2ad046 during repair round 3): not built at this head, and not answered by anything in it. ## Block

`carry()` in `tools/pr/app_approve.sh` now runs `git ls-remote --heads origin` and treats a head that is no branch tip of origin as not ours. Four other instruments call the real `--carry` inside their own `--self-test`, over fixture heads that are never pushed to `refs/heads/*`; the diff edits none of the four files. `instrument-self-tests` step red at the head and not at the merge base (fix-review.md step 11), each one:

The fixture's origin holds only `main`.
- `tools/audit/seat/ledger.py --self-test` (step `obligations-ledger`): base 0 failed, head `102 checks, 1 failed`: "REVIEW OWED skips a head its newest merge verdict carries to (a clean main merge); a branch-own commit after it is owed (null control)". The fixture repository has no `origin` remote, so the listing fails closed.
- `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` (step `merge-train`): base 0 failed, head `656 checks, 2 failed`: "add, a train live: a CARRIED single ... passes app_approve.sh --carry under the queue lock and is spooled for the NEXT batch (ADDED)" and its null control "a head carrying a non-main delta past its verdict is refused by the `carry` rule". No `origin` remote in the fixture.

All four steps list `tools/pr/app_approve.sh` in `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` at this head, so the scope selects them for this diff: the pull request would open red on them, and a forced-full `main` would be red after it. `tools/pr/prepr.sh` does not run the instrument self-tests, which is why the handoff did not see it.

The enumeration rule for the class: every caller of `app_approve.sh --carry` (`git grep -n -e '--carry' -- tools | grep app_approve`). Callers whose self-test I ran and found green at the head: `orchestrator_tick.py` (315 checks), `review_packet.py` (123), `cloud_relay.sh`, `bus.sh` (203), `outside.py` (212). `queue_pre_flight.py --self-test` under `python3 -I` stops on `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'merge_train'` at the head; I did not run it at the base, so it is not counted either way.

The repair is the fixer's choice between giving those fixtures an origin branch at the carried head (as this diff's own `ourcarry` does inside app_approve's self-test) and a seam in `carry()`; either way the four self-tests are re-run at both ends and their closures re-recorded.

## What this part defines for part 2

In `tools/pr/outside.py`, imported by path:

- `pull_facts(repo, pr, pull=None)` -> dict with keys `author`, `state`, `head_repo`, `head_ref`, `head_owner`, `head`, `base_repo`, `base_ref`.
- `cross_repository(facts, repo)` -> bool, the one definition of a cross-repository head (`facts["head_repo"] != repo`; a head repository that is gone is cross-repository).
- `check(repo, pr, ref, gate=None, fetch=True, early=False, comment=None, pull=None)` -> `(rc, lines)`: 0 admitted, 1 refused, 3 not an outside pull request.
- `Rules(ref).classify(path, pr)` -> `"F"`, `"R"` or `"O"`; `Rules.is_owned`, `Rules.refused`, `Rules.free`.
- `approve(repo, pr, head, mandate, ref, role, gate=None, fetch=True)` -> `(rc, lines)`; `owner_read(reviews, head, gate, repo, carry)`; `allowlisted(user, allow)`; `read_allowlist(ref)`; `carries(lsha, head, ref)`; the exception `Refuse`.
- Shell form: `python3 -I tools/pr/outside.py cross --repo O/R --pr N` (rc 0 `CROSS-REPOSITORY`, rc 3 `SAME-REPOSITORY`, rc 1 `REFUSE:`), `check`, `classify`, `approve`.
- Constants: `ALLOWLIST`, `CODEOWNERS`, `MANIFEST`, `HEAD_REF`, `READ_WORDS` ("Outside read:"), `READ_LINE`, `DECISIVE`.

Data paths: the allowlist is `dev/governance/config/outside_contributors.json` (key `contributors`, entries with `login`, integer `id`, `since`, `decision`), read with `git show <ref>:<path>`; the fetched fork head is `refs/hpo-outside/<pr>`; `bus.sh adopt <pr> <comment id>` is the adoption entry and `policy_lint.mjs --outside-author <login>` its body-lint form.

This part defines none of `Train.fork_head`, `Train.outside_contract` or `head_is_ours`; `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py`, `remerge_main.sh` and `merge_pr.sh` are untouched by the diff.

## Can this part alone stop the train

Yes, as it stands, and for our own pull requests: the four red self-test steps above stop this pull request itself, and after it any pull request whose diff reaches one of those four closures.

In production paths a same-repository pull request is otherwise unaffected, by reading and by measurement:

- The train's four `--carry` calls (`merge_train.py` admission, add, the head wait, `admit_verdict`) pass the live `headRefOid`, which is a branch tip of origin for a same-repository head, so `ours` stays 1 and every arm below is the base's. The extra cost is one `git ls-remote --heads origin` per carry whose range holds a commit: 7216 heads, 0.63 s from this seat.
- `policy_lint.mjs`: `outsideAdmission` returns before any spawn for the App (both spellings), Dependabot and an absent author. The base's copy of the linter, given this head's two new arguments, prints the same summary line as without them (`PR-BODY: 2 error(s)` both ways on the handoff body with no `--base`), so the head's `pr-contract.yml` line does not break the base's restored grader.
- `tests.yml`: the added conjunct is true for a same-repository head and `HEAD_REF` holds the value the inline expression held.
- A carry of a local head never pushed now refuses, with or without an `origin` remote; the body says so for non-merge commits. It holds for a merge of main too wherever the branch changes a merge-driver file, since on `ours=0` each such file must be main's bytes.

For a fork pull request this part admits nothing at merge: the allowlist is empty and `check` answers rc 3.

merges.body:
Part 3, the last part, of outside pull request #3435. Thank you, Bankaifan, for #3435 and the live-install report behind it. Your commit b785556645 (the DEBUG reasons, the frozen phase and its card strings) is kept with your authorship. It was cut from your one commit, as part 1 and part 2 cut theirs, and our changes are separate later commits. This delivers the remainder of pull request 3435 and leaves #3435 open for the orchestrator to close with thanks. Part 2 is on main as 0731b35877 (pull request 3505), so the diff against main is this part's alone. Part of #201.

**Round 3: handoff repair.** The opener's prepr refused c725250734 when it merged it with main, on three counts:
1. `ci predict`: unpinned sites were added in `learner_progress.py`.
2. `preflight`: a closing keyword beside #3435.
3. The open first-review block.

What this round changes:
- origin/main is merged as plain merge commits. e8e34b05fd was pushed to the step ref by another writer under the same seat identity, and this branch builds on it fast-forward.
- Merging main exposed a semantic conflict. On main, part 2's check X7 ("a settle ending before the running tail's end leaves it; one ending later moves it") failed against this part's scaled tail, so the pin run's `tests/features.py` baseline was red (`MUTATION TABLE INCONCLUSIVE`). X7 seeded `BoostState` at the default `space_boosted` of 0. Under the scaled tail its first settle then owes about 7.8 h, so the half-second-later end never reaches the held 12 h end. X7 now seeds the sum at a full window, so both settles owe the full tail and its two arms test what they did on main (c90588dcf4).
- Every added mutation site is pinned by a real kill or triaged as equivalent (`## Unpinned sites`).
- No closing keyword remains in this body or in any commit message on the branch.

**The first review's block is answered by c2a379d493, which descends from the blocked head 6caf7df2fa** (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 6caf7df2fa c725250734` exits 0). Block: class-open, a lower-floor probe problem the lower learner recorded paused the house, solar and gains learners on the card. Each learner now records its own freeze, and each card learner reads only the record of the learner it folds in. The class census is under `## Figures`, and the test that fails with the fix reverted is under `## Mutation proof`.

What ships, by brief item:
- Reasons at DEBUG. `close_span` logs one line for a span the counter closed or refused, through `log_close`, which returns before any formatting with DEBUG off. The house heat-loss learner's gates return through `learner_progress.log_skip`, which passes the reason's values to the logger as arguments (CHANGE b). Nothing is logged above DEBUG.
- (a) No helper and no reason string is added to `coordinator.py`. `log_skip`, `pauses` and `Freeze` live in `learner_progress.py`. `learning_freeze` and `freeze_end` live in `boost.py`. The coordinator passes what it already holds: `learner_freeze_reason`, and itself to `boost.learning_freeze`. `tests/structure.py` passes with no budget raised.
- (c) One source. Each learner records the freeze it obeyed in the coordinator's `FreezeRecord` (`learner_progress.py`), under its own name: `house`, `lower`, `dhw` or `buffer`.
  - A card learner's phase reads the record of the learner it folds in, `learner_progress.HELD_BY`: house, solar and gains read `house`, and lower reads `lower`.
  - The sensor's `learner_freeze_reason` is `FreezeRecord.last`, the reason recorded last this cycle; a learner that records again moves to the end.
  - Asking `_learning_frozen` again from the payload builder measured +2 on `seam_cut_total` in round 1, so it was not taken.
  - When two reasons hold at once, `_learning_frozen`'s own order picks the one a learner records. An unusable reading ranks above the boost, so the learner shows frozen with no end, and the card says "Paused until its inputs are usable again.", never "after a boost".

merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-BOOST-FLOW-CEILING: a production hotfix for a defect the owner (tvofi) reported on 2026-11-13 from his v7.1.15 install, a Tuya Rotenso Windmi under Pump duty control at Control with a flow set-point. After he released the stuck set-point by hand (R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK), a live space boost wrote 41, then 43, and then rose gradually to 53 °C, instead of his maximum. His direction, verbatim: "it should not be hard coded to 55 but rather set at the maximum value (if sensible, otherwise today's gradual rise is ok)". On "sensible": "in a control and comfort sense".

This branch is stacked on the R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK handoff head 90eb45f69f and merges after it.

**Cause.** A space boost and the global boost mode change the step's duty (`pump_arbiter._planned_duty`) but not the level the flow set-point maps. `_flow_target` mapped the plan's own `power_schedule` level through `thermal_model.flow_setpoint_for_level`. A boost over a step the plan books at a partial positive power therefore wrote floor + fraction × (ceiling − floor), and the floor (measured inlet + lift) climbed as the system water warmed. That is the gradual rise the owner saw. Only an idle step (level ≤ 0) or a step at the band top gave the ceiling. `boost.overlay` sets the action's power to the maximum, but the arbiter does not read the action's power: only the system-identification experiment overrides the plan's level. Latent since 0a58990088 (R9-SW-6, first shipped in v6.7.17), which made the set-point follow the planned level.

**Repair round (review verdict held at 7db7de155f; CI red at the pull-request head 9e02464877).** The delta from the reviewed head:
- the repaired lower branch merged in;
- #3404's harness M03 re-anchored on this branch's `boosted=False` arm line;
- one unit of `coord_footprint` paid (see `## Architecture score`);
- the pins and one equivalent-survivor triage.

No other production change: the payment removes `_space_boosted` and the `water` local and reads the same fact inline in `desired()`. The pump-duty arbiter block prints `ALL 61 FEATURES BLOCK PASSED` at this head.

**Conflict round (origin/main `cc0fb254` merged into `ece83280`, after #3561 and #3564).** Git conflicted in `strings.json` and `translations/de.json`, `en.json` and `sv.json` only, one hunk each, all on the `space_setpoint_unit` help text of the options entities step; `tests/closures.json` merged through its ledger driver and every other file merged automatically. Each hunk was resolved as a union, key by key against the merge base `ec964501`: a key only one side changed keeps that side's value, and a key both sides changed keeps main's. In `strings.json`, `en.json` and `de.json` only main changed `space_setpoint_unit` (#3564's appended sentence on what Control writes), so main's text stands. In `sv.json` both sides changed it: this branch's "entitet" wording and #3564's appended sentence. Main's value already contains that wording, so main's text stands and nothing of this branch's is lost. Enumerated by flattening each file's three versions to leaf keys: the merged key set equals the union of both sides in all four files, every merged value equals one side's, and de, en and sv keep the same key set as `strings.json`. This branch's `flow_heat_c` and `space_setpoint_entity` texts are unchanged.

## Design

**What a boost writes.** `_boost_ceiling_c(inp)` decides the target: the set-point entity's own maximum, capped by a heating ceiling (`flow_heat_c`) set to anything but its 55 °C default and by the controller's upper-limit sensor (`space_setpoint_high_limit_entity`, read through the `_setpoint_limits_c` the feedback loop already uses) where it reads. The maximum and the cap are both in the entity's own terms, so a return target is not moved: no offset is applied twice. The boost keeps following the planned level, as before, when the maximum does not read, sits at or below the gate, or sits above `FLOW_HEAT_C_MAX`. That constant is 70 °C, the options flow's own upper bound for `flow_heat_c`. It was a literal at config_flow.py and is now named in const.py and used there too. An entity reading 80 or 100 (a generic number helper) is no heating-flow set-point to drive to its top.

**Explicit versus default `flow_heat_c`.** An absent key reads as `DEFAULT_FLOW_HEAT_C`. `tests/config_flow_steps.py` proves that an untouched options page changes nothing (`_ABSENT_FALLBACKS is exactly the proven set`), which requires a stored default to behave exactly like no setting. A first cut that read the key's presence as "explicit" broke that proof (2 of 580 failed: `flow_heat_c` listed but unproven). So the ceiling caps a boost when it is anything but the default. The one thing lost: a person cannot cap a boost at exactly 55 °C through this option. 54.5 °C, or the controller's upper-limit sensor, does it. An upper-limit sensor reading at or below the gate leaves no heating value and is ignored, as the feedback loop's bounds ignore it.

**The seam is the level.** `_level_kw(inp, now, boosted)` is the one owner of the level a heating step maps:
- the experiment's commanded power, where the action is the experiment's;
- the band top under a boost with a ceiling to write;
- otherwise the plan step's level.

`_flow_target` maps that level with the boost's ceiling in place of the configured one. At the band top, `flow_setpoint_for_level` gives frac = 1 and returns the ceiling exactly, so "the maximum at once" and "the level at the band top" are the same write. `_bounded` then clamps it to the entity's range as for any heating write. `_space_boosted(coord, inp, now)` reads the fact from the live boost record and `inp.mode == MODE_BOOST`, only for a water set-point, so a caller with no coordinator on an indoor set-point (the °F checks) reads nothing. `_space_target` takes it as a required keyword, so every caller states it.

Two alternatives were refused:
- A special case at the write would bypass `_bounded`'s `lo`/`hi` and give the boost row a second formula.
- Reading the overlaid action's power would follow the cycle's snapshot, which lags the one-minute tick.

**Is stepping straight to the maximum sound control and comfort? Yes, on this evidence:**
- (a) Control. The arbiter's premise is that the set-point is a power command. `_full_draw_c` says "a supply target at the ceiling sits far above the water, so the pump may draw its top". The `FLOW_HEAT_C` comment says the heating set-point is high so "the pump's own water thermostat never cuts a planned heating step short", and that the supply "settles where the emitters take the pump's output". A higher target therefore buys the nameplate draw a boost is for (README: "apply maximum heat ... for two hours") and fewer thermostat cut-outs, not water overshoot.
  - The minimum run and minimum pause (supply_hold.py) govern only the supply switch, and `supply_hold._passes` exempts a boost.
  - The power-feedback loop is off under a boost (`_feedback_on`).
  - No set-point ramp exists on any path to protect: the gradual rise was a side effect of the partial level, not a mechanism.
- (b) Comfort. A boost lasts `boost.BOOST_HOURS` = 2 and expires on its own. On a flow or return set-point nothing trims it on the room temperature (the action's comfort-ceiling set-point reaches only an indoor-unit entity), and the model has no emitter limit. A step to the maximum can therefore overshoot the room target within the two hours. That exposure already existed at the fixed 55 and is the documented intent. The owner ruled it out of scope today (see Forward-carry). The guards a person controls are `flow_heat_c` set off its default and the upper-limit sensor; docs and the option's help text say to set `flow_heat_c` on a low-temperature floor heating.

**Docs.**
- docs/configuration.md: what a boost writes, under Pump duty control and in the `flow_heat_c` row.
- `flow_heat_c` help text in strings.json, en, sv and de.
- The sentence "Boost mode writes Heating + DHW with the heating-flow ceiling (55 °C, or `flow_heat_c`)" no longer holds and is corrected.
- README.md's "Boost Space Heating ... apply maximum heat on that channel" is now true and stands.

**Re-pinned, by name.** On the arbiter fixture's entity, whose maximum is 63, three checks pinned a boost writing 55. They now pin 63:
- `the global boost mode writes Heating + DHW and the set-point entity's maximum, 63 ...`
- `a boost writes its own single duty where the pump offers it ... a space boost writes the set-point entity's maximum, 63 ...`
- `R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK: a boost over an idle step writes the entity's 63 maximum ...`

## Release note

### A space boost writes the set-point's maximum on every step (R10-HOTFIX-BOOST-FLOW-CEILING)

Under Pump duty control at Control with a flow or return set-point, Boost Space Heating and the global Boost mode used to write the full heating flow only on steps the plan left idle or booked at full power. On a step the plan booked at part power they wrote a set-point between the floor and the ceiling that rose slowly, for example 41, then 43, then 53 °C. Both boosts now write the set-point entity's own maximum on every step they cover. A heating flow ceiling set to anything but 55 °C, and the controller's maximum set-point sensor when configured, cap it. An entity whose maximum cannot be read, or one above 70 °C, keeps the previous behaviour.

## Root cause

Root cause per dev/governance/rules/defect-root-cause.md: the defect reached a release (v6.7.17 through v7.1.15).

- **Cause.** When 0a58990088 (R9-SW-6, 2026-10-06) made the flow set-point follow the planned level, it changed what a boost writes, and it covered only one of the two cases. Its `flow_setpoint_for_level` docstring states the idle case ("a boost over an idle plan still holds heat_c") and not the partial one. The boost changed the duty, but the level stayed the plan's.
- **Why the existing test passed.** The boost test (`the global boost mode writes Heating + DHW and the heating flow ...`, from 06bd2452f8, 2026-09-27) predates level-following. When it was written, any heating step wrote a fixed 55, so an idle plan was a full test. It stayed green after R9-SW-6 for two reasons, either sufficient: its plan is idle (`duties="--"`), and its `_PaCoord` fixture carries no `max_electrical_power`, so the band is not ready and the slide is skipped on every plan.
- **The cheaper detector.** It is the check added here: a boost on a step booked at a partial level with the band ready, for both boost surfaces, inside the existing pump-duty arbiter block. No new script or job.
- **Process state.** Nothing asked that a change to the level mapping re-run the duty rows (boost, experiment, comfort) on a partial level. Accepting the idle-only test was not a recorded decision: the test was right when written and went stale when the mapping changed under it. No separate countermeasure is proposed; the orchestrator decides whether a root-cause seat runs beside this fix.

## Head

`6251038ff35f31d9e37b0c7cee0435187724657c` merges the authored code head `2486dc6da9cd53e8cfdf0aa12220698600d6a419` and then merges origin/main `fafd6a9ff5` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`2486dc6da9cd53e8cfdf0aa12220698600d6a419` merges origin/main `cc0fb254` into `ece83280`, with the four string files (`strings.json`, `translations/de.json`, `en.json`, `sv.json`) resolved by hand as a union: one hunk each, on `space_setpoint_unit`, where main's text is kept (in `sv.json` it already carries this branch's wording). No other file was resolved by hand.

`ece8328001608ff93f5138392f6e6c15420c8929` merges the authored code head `ac31599707556415beaaaab8b6f7acfd2b04a7cf`.

`ac31599707556415beaaaab8b6f7acfd2b04a7cf` is stacked on the train heads `ec9645014c773759edfbf632829c7cbef272ba33` (#3580) and `8317d9e1b282fce0dfa342465470921a3e4b4e8f` (#3576) and lands after them; the conflicts were resolved by union in `strings.json` and `translations/de.json`, `en.json` and `sv.json` (this PR's `space_setpoint_entity` beside their `space_setpoint_unit`), and the reviewed head is `ced9b233580709f530d5dc402dc12344697fef87`.

## Mutation proof

Failing first. Commit d6b439956e adds the partial-step boost check before any code. At it, the pump-duty arbiter block (`tools/audit/seat/features_block.py` from `R.section("pump-duty arbiter — mode and set-points per plan step` to `_pa_subs = _PaCoord(`) printed `1 of 59 FEATURES BLOCK FAILED`, with a channel boost and the global mode both writing `[42]` on the partial 1.0 kW step. At the head the block prints `ALL 61 FEATURES BLOCK PASSED`, and `tests/config_flow_steps.py` prints `ALL 580 checks PASSED`.

`python3 tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff 90eb45f69f511811ddd2ed9e7c6570ab8b2abdd1...HEAD --cmd 'bash <three blocks>'` diffs from the stuck-set-point head this branch stacks on. The command runs three blocks: the arbiter block, the water-setpoint feedback seam block (`# --- R10-WATER-SETPOINT-FEEDBACK (outside report #3380` to `_fb_floor = _fb_sim(clamp=(26.4`), and the R10-CEILING-PROBE block (`R.section("R10-CEILING-PROBE: the experiment` to `R.section("R10-PROD-RESIDUE-PINS`, with its prelude from `features_block.py --emit-prelude`). It generated 36 mutants at 20b310b063 (the same code as this head; later commits add checks and drop two pins) of the added production lines (pump_arbiter.py, const.py, config_flow.py). 34 are killed and 2 survive, both equivalent:

- `_boost_ceiling_c`'s `_gate_floor_c(...) < high` moved to `<=`. At `high` equal to the gate, the entity's own range clamps every heating write to the gate whichever branch runs, so no input can tell the two apart.

Mutants this round's checks were added to kill:

## Null control

- The same partial step with no boost writes its partial value, below each boost target.
- An entity maximum of 90, or none, leaves a boost on that same partial value.
- With no boost, a band-top step writes the heating flow, 55, and an idle step the gate, 25.
- The power-feedback loop is on for the partial step with no boost and off under the space boost.

The investigator's probe `probe/boost43.py` in the session's `seat/boost-43/` scratch directory (out of tree; the orchestrator holds the path) can be re-run by the reviewer against this head.

The generated scope-line block is left out of this body: update_pr.sh verifies it against its own merge head, which no body can name in advance (R10-HOTFIX-UPDATEPR-FIGURE-REFRESH); the scope line is the gate's own MODE line at the head.

## Architecture score

- `coord_footprint` 2505 -> 2506 (this seat's measure at merge base 154dbb4c61 and 416147bb56; CI read 2503 -> 2505 at 9e02464877 before the payment): `desired()` now passes the live boost fact to `_space_target` as a computed argument, `boosted=_flow_unit(inp.config) and (inp.mode == MODE_BOOST or boost.held_for(coord).active(...))`, where the call was a plain delegation the footprint does not charge. The fact needs the coordinator's boost record, and `desired()` is the one function that holds both it and the call. Payment tried: the first cut's `_space_boosted(coord, inp, now)` helper and `water` local charged 2 units (`pump_arbiter._space_boosted:1`, `desired` 7 -> 8); both are removed (commit "read the boost fact inline in desired()"), paying 1 of the 2. A local `boosted = ...` costs the same unit and turns the call back into plumbing, so it pays nothing. Carrying the fact on `ArbiterInputs` would move it into the coordinator's published builder, coordinator.py, held by open pull requests, and charge the builder instead. No payment that improves the architecture exists for the remaining unit (per-function measure: `tools/audit/archscore/metrics/footprint.py`'s `measure`, base and head, the only charged difference being `pump_arbiter.desired:7` -> `:8`).

## Red checks

Each check that was red on a commit of this branch (pull request #3562, head 9e024648777c), answered per dev/governance/rules/defect-root-cause.md:

- `arch-score / arch-score`: `dS -0.0012 WORSENS; unexplained: coord_footprint 2503->2505`. The cause is this branch's boost fact in `desired()`: the `_space_boosted` helper and `water` local, 2 units. One unit paid and one explained under `## Architecture score`. Cheaper detector: `python3 -I tools/audit/archscore/gate.py --base <merge base> --head HEAD --body <body>`, about 2 minutes locally; prepr does not run it. The handoff did not run it, which is why it reached CI. Standing cost: one run per handoff whose diff touches a function handed the coordinator.
- `tests / fast (3.14)`: `tests/doc_claims.py` failed `no user page carries a history phrase outside a reasoned exemption` on the "as before" in docs/configuration.md, a sentence the lower branch (#3561) added. It is fixed there and merged in here. Cheaper detector: `tests/doc_claims.py` itself, 9 s; it is answered in full in #3561's Red checks.
- `tests / mutation`: REFUSED, 21 unpinned sites added by this diff: 6 from #3561, which that branch now pins, and 15 of its own. The sites left at this head after the payment are now settled by `python3 tests/mutation_table.py --pin-killed --base origin/main` (features.py, config_flow_steps.py, guard_pins.py). Of 13 mutants, 11 are pinned killed. The two on the range test's line share one anchor: its `<= FLOW_HEAT_C_MAX` comparator is killed, and its gate comparator lives and is equivalent. That anchor is triaged `equivalent` in tests/mutation_ledger/survivor_triage/, with the reason. `ci_predict.py --base origin/main` now predicts no red. Two pins this branch's rewrite made stale (`_space_target` RETURN_DEL 268586e3, `desired` GUARD_OFF 0082e8a4) were already deleted. Cheaper detector: ci_predict's ADDED UNPINNED lines, printed as a WARN at the handoff. The body answered them "pinned by mutation-autofix", which the next row shows could not happen.
- `tests / mutation-autofix`: AUTOFIX skip-measure-failed. The shard jobs' baseline found `tests/doc_claims.py` red (the same sentence), so no mutant's verdict meant anything and no bot commit followed. No separate detector exists: it is the doc_claims red above.
- `governance / instrument-self-tests`, `tests / briefs`, `tests / nightly-status`: red on main commits that the pull-request branch's merges of origin/main brought into its ancestry, not on any commit of this diff. For example, `governance / instrument-self-tests` is red at main 154dbb4c61 itself. They grade `main` and are the orchestrator's there (`defect-root-cause.md`, Enforcement).
- `pr-contract` and `gate`: red at 9e02464877, aggregating the reds above. This section answers them.

## Forward-carry

- On a flow or return set-point a space boost is bounded only by its two-hour window (`custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/boost.py`, `BOOST_HOURS`): nothing trims it on the room temperature, and the model has no emitter limit, so a boost can overshoot the room target (pre-existing at the fixed 55 °C; a design question for the owner, not a hotfix). calendar day and asserts the weekday day type for that arm. So the check is red
on every Saturday and Sunday, on main and on every head. This pull request adds
only the record: `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-FEATURES-WEEKEND-CLOCK.md` and its
`_rca` entry in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`. The test fix is
R10-HOTFIX-FEATURES-WEEKEND-CLOCK's. The countermeasure is specified for a
fixer and carried to R10-SUITE-ENV-RESIDUE; it is not built here.

- Process state: (c). R10-SUITE-HOST-DETERMINISM's nightly step changes the
  zone and never the calendar day.
- Class: a suite verdict that follows a host property the gate does not pin.
  It has three instances in round 10 (CPU load, zone, calendar day), so it owes
  a class barrier.
- Cost test: the recommended countermeasure runs the existing nightly Kolkata
  step under `faketime` on the other day type, for about 10 to 20 s a night (an
  estimate). The defect

merges.body:
HOTFIX (R10 batch 246, P744), repair round after "Fix review: blocked 8a05961b" (probe/revt-r10-hotfix-macos-selftest-lane-dfbc393a). Main CI is Linux-only, so a Darwin-only self-test regression (PR 3475: `mutant_run.py` listing /proc) was found only when an opener failed. This adds a `darwin-selftest` beat row: Darwin hosts only, one cycle per new origin/main tip, heavy-slot lease per pass, a detached worktree the row owns, `prepr.sh --self-test` plus each wired seat self-test, one `darwin-selftest: RED <instrument> <first FAIL line>` per red, nothing when green. No workflow file touched (owner ruling 2026-11-12: macOS checks are local seats or beat rows). It detects after merge and does not prevent; a pre-merge arm is round 11.

This round was run on the Mac, so both blocked items are measured below. Those measurements exposed two lane defects in this group's own seam, and both are fixed in this head:
- One whole run took 80 to 109 min, which is past the row's beatd `timeout_s` of 3600. beatd would kill every pass, and because the tip was never remembered, the row would take the heavy slot again every 900 s. A run is now a resumable cycle. Each pass starts no self-test past `DARWIN_PASS_BUDGET_S` (900 s), remembers what ran and gives the slot back. The next pass resumes the same tip, and a finished cycle writes its RED lines once.
- `python3 -I` drops the script's directory from sys.path (Python 3.11+, `-I` implies `-P`). That made `queue_pre_flight.py` read as a false Darwin red (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'merge_train'`). The row now runs a `.py` self-test with CI's plain `python3`.

Closes: none (no issue; triage P744).

## Head

`4d5b7e94d1807b987fac5323e9129f9359d6b7a9` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

5c7b8a82c53d2259296dd43da81212f85e69eaed

## Re-cut

Round 4 follows the round-3 verdict `blocked a55158085ed8cd6517113af8b77af07492a6634e mutation-vacuous: red_carried_to_next_cycle, no_per_run_remember survive`. Relative to the reviewed head this repair changes only `tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs_selftest.py`: two cases and two MUTANTS rows, production code unchanged. It also merges origin/main c987209c, which carries the weekend-clock fix.
- `darwin-selftest: a new cycle starts with an empty red list after a cycle that had REDs`: cycle 1 on tip A ends with one RED, cycle 2 on tip B runs green, and the digest must be empty.
- `darwin-selftest: a pass killed partway keeps the runs it finished`: the second self-test run raises, and the remembered state must hold `done == [prepr.sh]`, `complete` false and the cycle's tip.

## Mutation proof

Seventeen mutants in `beat_jobs_selftest.py` MUTANTS. Each one is killed by the case named in its entry, and the self-test prints `ok mutant <name> killed by: <case>` for each. The command is `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py --self-test` at the Head, and its final line is `beat_jobs self-test: 242 checks, 0 failed`.
- The ten from earlier rounds: `darwin_gate_dropped`, `darwin_first_fail_is_last_line`, `darwin_tip_not_skipped`, `darwin_red_dropped`, `darwin_cwd_repo`, `darwin_keep_state_dir`, `darwin_wired_filter_dropped`, `darwin_remember_on_wt_fail`, `darwin_slot_take_ignored` and `darwin_lease_not_released`. The sites of `darwin_tip_not_skipped` and `darwin_red_dropped` were re-anchored to the restructured lines. They mutate the same predicates.
- New this round:
  - `darwin_budget_ignored` drops the pass-budget check. Killed by "a pass starts no self-test past DARWIN_PASS_BUDGET_S; the next pass resumes the same tip".
  - `darwin_cycle_follows_main` makes every pass restart at the newest tip. Killed by the same case.
  - `darwin_done_rerun` makes an already-run self-test run again. Killed by the same case.
  - `darwin_red_each_pass` writes the RED lines at every pass. Killed by "a cycle's RED lines are written once, when it completes".
  - `darwin_py_isolated` puts `-I` back. Killed by "a .py self-test runs as CI's plain python3, never -I (which drops the script dir)".
- Round 4 adds `red_carried_to_next_cycle` (the new cycle's `red` seeded from the old one's, killed by the empty-red-list case) and `no_per_run_remember` (the per-run `ctx.remember` line deleted, killed by the killed-partway case). The self-test prints `ok mutant red_carried_to_next_cycle killed by: ...` and `ok mutant no_per_run_remember killed by: ...`. Both new cases pass on the unmutated code (242 checks, 0 failed).
- Failing test first: with the new cases added and the Head's production code still at 8a05961b, `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py --self-test --no-mutants` gave rc=1 and `139 checks, 5 failed`. The five failures were the pass-budget, written-once, per-pass-slot, budget-at-most-half-timeout_s and plain-python3 cases.

## Null control

- Pass budget: at 8a05961b the same fake run, three 600 s stubs plus prepr, ran every self-test in one pass, and the budget case FAILED, as above. At the Head, pass 1 runs exactly ceil(900/600) = 2 self-tests. Every later pass adds a worktree of the first tip, even after the fake origin/main moves. The cycle ends with each self-test run exactly once.
- `-I`, on this Mac at main 50373173 (output in <scratch>/qpf.txt, scratch):
  - `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py --self-test` gives rc=1 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'merge_train'`.
  - `python3 tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py --self-test` gives rc=0 with `queue_pre_flight self-test: 53 checks, 0 failed`.
  - Not re-measured: whether any other self-test that is green under `-I` changes without it. Dropping `-I` only adds the script's directory to sys.path.
- Reviewer survivors from earlier rounds: unchanged from the prior body. All are killed (probe/revt-r10-hotfix-macos-selftest-lane-dfbc393a Evidence).

## Figures

Machine class for every run below: Apple M1, 8 cores, 8 GiB, macOS 27.2, Python 3.14.7, /bin/bash 3.2.57. The box was not idle. Another seat's `prepr.sh --self-test` (pid 16778), two to three further `prepr.sh --self-test` processes and a `ci_predict.py --record-self-tests` ran during these runs, beside the merge train.

Each run uses row code 8a05961b, the blocked head, which carries the defect-detecting row unchanged. The row runs from a scratch clone at <scratch>/repo whose `refs/remotes/origin/main` is set to the tip under test. The body's former command, `beat_jobs.py --run darwin-selftest`, was wrong: the CLI takes the row as a positional. The command, from that clone, is:

    time python3 -I tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py darwin-selftest --state <scratch>/state-<red|green> --repo <scratch>/repo
    cat <scratch>/state-<red|green>/digest/jobs/darwin-selftest

**RED at main 19baca76181cb019d9b1cfd93ee6bc0a08e20047** (2026-11-13T22:57:53Z to 2026-11-14T00:18:24Z). Result: `real 80m30.649s`, rc=0, and the digest holds 13 lines:

    darwin-selftest: RED tools/pr/prepr.sh FAIL and the refusal quotes mutant_run's own reason (got 0, wanted 1)
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/bus.sh FAIL push-verdict refuses evidence names that differ only by case, naming both
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh: line 124: vars[0]: unbound variable
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/gh_calls.py FAIL gh api dot segments resolving to #201 is refused
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/heartbeat.sh FAIL null control: the same host's message naming another path is pushed
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/hooks_setup.py FAIL beatd: run at the floor starts, and records its cwd, argv and HPO_* environment (null control for the refusal)
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py FAIL spec: the NULL mutant reports SURVIVED and a pinned mutant KILLED
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh FAIL   a runner without pr_exit_trap is refused
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh FAIL   a runner without pr_exit_trap is refused
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'merge_train'
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh FAIL a seat bin dir with no gh shim: one TICK-GH flag line naming the gh found, beside the banner
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/train.sh train.sh: REFUSE: self-test: TERM to the train (pid 42762, launcher 42762) left 0 of 0 pids of its tree alive (pidfile removed, none)

The defect the row was written for is named: `RED tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py`. `RED tools/pr/prepr.sh` is the same defect seen through prepr's own self-test, because it quotes mutant_run's reason.

**GREEN for that defect at main 50373173d486faf394b24637c177ab38b691b394**, which carries the mutant_run Darwin hotfix f3ccd1a5 ("mutant_run: wait for the self-test's zombie by polling the table, as macOS has no os.waitid"). The run went from 2026-11-14T00:18:49Z to 02:07:37Z. Result: `real 108m47.673s`, rc=0. The `mutant_run.py` and `prepr.sh` lines are gone, and so is `tick_loop.sh`. The digest holds the 10 lines below. The row is not silent, because main still carries other Darwin reds:

    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/bus.sh FAIL push-verdict refuses evidence names that differ only by case, naming both
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh: line 124: vars[0]: unbound variable
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/gh_calls.py FAIL gh api dot segments resolving to #201 is refused
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/heartbeat.sh FAIL null control: the same host's message naming another path is pushed
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/hooks_setup.py FAIL beatd: run at the floor starts, and records its cwd, argv and HPO_* environment (null control for the refusal)
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh FAIL null control: open_pr with the code sha passes every check, and its failed push names its log
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh FAIL null control: open_pr with the code sha passes every check, and its failed push names its log
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'merge_train'
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/train.sh train.sh: REFUSE: self-test: TERM to the train (pid 68229, launcher 68229) left 0 of 0 pids of its tree alive (pidfile removed, none)
    darwin-selftest: RED tools/audit/seat/update_pr.sh FAIL null control: open_pr with the code sha passes every check, and its failed push names its log

Classification of the 10 lines at 50373173:
- `queue_pre_flight.py` is the lane's own `-I` artifact, fixed in this head (Null control).
- These four were re-run directly on this Mac at 50373173 with CI's command, outside the row: no slot, no HPO_STATE_DIR, plain `python3`/`bash`. Each one reproduces:
  - `python3 tools/audit/seat/gh_calls.py --self-test` gives rc=1 and `221 checks, 1 failed`, with the same FAIL line.
  - `bash tools/audit/seat/heartbeat.sh --self-test` gives rc=1 and `8 checks, 1 failed`, same line.
  - `python3 tools/audit/seat/hooks_setup.py --self-test` gives rc=1 and `46 checks, 1 failed`, same line.
  - `bash tools/audit/seat/train.sh --self-test` gives rc=2 with the same REFUSE.
  They are real Darwin reds on main and not artifacts of the row.
- `cloud-setup.sh` is a real Darwin red. It calls `mapfile`, which /bin/bash 3.2 lacks, so `vars` stays unset under `set -u`. It is carried (Forward-carry).
- `bus.sh`, `open_pr.sh`, `pr_args.sh` and `update_pr.sh` were not re-run outside the row. They take 388 to 692 s each, and the box's heavy capacity was left to other seats. They are not classified, and they are carried with the four above (Forward-carry).

**Wall time of one whole run, by this machine class under the load above:**
- RED: 4830.6 s. Slot wait inside it was not measured separately.
- GREEN: 6527.7 s. Of that, 779 s was slot wait (slot-take returned at 00:31:48Z, polled every 2 s on its pid) and 5749 s was self-tests after the slot.
- What the row runs is enumerated by `python3 -I -c 'import sys; from pathlib import Path; sys.path.insert(0,"tools/audit/seat"); import beat_jobs; print(len(beat_jobs.darwin_instruments(Path(sys.argv[1]))))' <tree>`, run from the Head on a `git archive` of each tip. It gives 80 at 19baca76 and 81 at 50373173, plus `prepr.sh --self-test`, so 81 and 82 runs.
- Per-run seconds come from sampling the row's child processes every 2 s. Each run counts from its start to the next run's start. 51 runs were seen; the rest finished within one sample. The sampled sum is 5746 s, against 5749 s measured.
- The largest runs: `prepr.sh` 1104, `pr_args.sh` 692, `open_pr.sh` 685, `update_pr.sh` 676, `beatd.py` 406, `bus.sh` 388, `merge_train.py` 381 and `cloud_relay.sh` 370. Every other run took under 200 s.
- No unloaded figure was taken: the train and openers run on this box all the time.

**Scope choice.** Even half the loaded figure, about 2900 s, would be past the 900 s interval, and close to the 3600 s timeout. So the row needed a scope that fits a pass, and raising `timeout_s` alone would not do. Two scopes were considered:
- Diff-scoped: only the self-tests the diff since the remembered tip can reach. Not taken. This defect class breaks that rule: `prepr.sh --self-test` went red from a change to `mutant_run.py`, a different file, and no measured closure maps seat self-tests to their inputs.
- A slower cadence alone: not taken. The pass would still outlive `timeout_s`.

Taken: a resumable cycle per tip, with a pass budget. The bound is 900 s plus the longest single run, measured 1104 s, so about 2004 s per pass. That is under the 3600 s `timeout_s`. A pass holds the heavy slot at most that long and then gives it back to other seats' prepr runs.
