## Scope

This review covers the round-4 repair (commits 444c39aa7a and 9b6fdcd4fc) and runs over the previously reviewed head d95a3490ef0a1ae41a1bd20095f665a44e40d40a. The previous verdict blocked on `mutation-vacuous: fixer-guard-off readback-nonce legacy-refusal-swallow`. The delta `git diff d95a3490ef..9b6fdcd4fc` touches two files. It adds 3 harness entries to `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_flow_dispatch_mutants.py` and 3 self-test checks inside `_group_checks` in `tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py`. It adds no production line and touches nothing under `custom_components/`, so nothing widens the scope (fix-review.md step 12). As the brief directs, the diff-mode mutants were re-run over every line the branch adds since its base cbd23f1c8b. Every survivor is listed below.

## Findings

- Survivor `tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py:635 CMP_BOUND` (`len(group.get("carry") or []) > PART_CARRIES` changed to `>=`). This is production code and it is not equivalent, so the body's disposition "equivalent on output" is wrong. Take a fixer dispatch of a group with exactly five raw carries whose cut-over roster the clone cannot read. The unmutated code skips the legacy read and dispatches. The mutant enters the branch, `roster_lib.read_legacy` raises `RosterNotFound`, and it refuses. This head's own new check, "a --part dispatch whose cut-over roster the clone cannot read refuses naming the cut-over", shows that the legacy read refuses on an unreadable cut-over. The difference fails closed, and the line has been on main since #3450 merged d95a3490. This delta neither adds nor changes it, so it does not block here. The pin it needs is a five-raw-carry group with an unreadable cut-over that dispatches unrefused. Derived from the code, not executed. Carry: dismissed: the producing group R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE is carries-open, so carry_audit refuses it as a destination (probed), and no other live group owns the seam; the gap is a fail-closed corner already on main, and it stays recorded here and in the body's Unpinned sites for the group's next part
- Survivor `tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py:600 CONST_SWAP` (`carry_only: bool = False` changed to `True` in the `dispatch_group` signature). The default was already `False` at cbd23f1c (line 547 there), and the line is in the diff only because it was re-flowed. The CLI passes `carry_only=args.carry_only` explicitly (line 1530), so the default matters only to an in-process caller that omits it. Carry: dismissed: pre-existing default, re-flowed only, answered in the body's Unpinned sites
- Survivor `cloud_dispatch.py:767 CONST_SWAP` (R10-CLASH fixture `range(14)` changed to 15): self-test fixture size. 15 carries is still over five, so the collision check keeps its meaning. Carry: dismissed: self-test fixture constant, not production
- Survivor `cloud_dispatch.py:771 CONST_SWAP` (R10-SELF-P2 fixture `range(9)` changed to 10): self-test fixture size, still two parts. Carry: dismissed: self-test fixture constant, not production
- Survivor `cloud_dispatch.py:887 RETURN_DEL` (`why_any`'s exception `return` changed to `pass`): an exception-to-text adapter in the self-test. Under the mutant a crash reads as `None` and still fails the check that uses it. Carry: dismissed: self-test helper, not production
- Survivor `cloud_dispatch.py:893 RETURN_DEL` (`split_any`'s exception `return` changed to `pass`): the same adapter shape as line 887. Carry: dismissed: self-test helper, not production

HOTFIX R10-HOTFIX-PLAN-OWNER-PRICE. The planner had no way to take an owner-stated price: `group_hours` read only size, class, resume stage and pending carries, so R10-CATALOG-PR (the owner's step that opens the hacs/default PR) was priced as a fresh small production fixer and closure sat past the owner's 2026-11-15 deadline. Owner ruling, tvofi 2026-11-12, verbatim: "Price it at 4h". The 240 minutes is the owner's value: the fixer did not choose, round or second-guess it.

What changed:
- Roster fields `owner_price_minutes` (positive minutes) and `owner_price_cite` (the owner's words, mandatory beside it). One definition, in `roster_lib.owner_price_why` / `roster_lib.owner_price`; a half-written pair is a `SchemaError`, never read as no price.
- `replan.group_hours` returns the price in hours before the size lookup, basis `owner-stated N min (not measured): <citation>`; a malformed price is a `PlanError` naming the group. The plan group row carries `owner_priced` (and, for a post-closure group, `duration_basis`) only when priced.
- Roster editor op `set-price <group> <minutes> --price-cite <text>` (`roster_edit.op_set_price`): refuses a missing or blank citation, non-positive, non-numeric or infinite minutes; the old price and citation go to `resume.note`; the price already held writes nothing. Not a queue-only op, like `set-size`.
- `plan_page.py` draws "owner-stated price, not measured" on the ETA cell of a priced row.
- Last step: R10-CATALOG-PR set to 240 min with citation `owner-stated price, tvofi 2026-11-12: "Price it at 4h"`, written through `op_set_price` and the editor's own `dump` (the diff is the two fields, the trailing comma and the `resume.note` record).

The durations model, the definition of closure and every other group's price are untouched.

Alternatives that lost: a per-size override in `durations.json` (changes every group of that size, which the brief forbids); a separate prices file (a second roster-shaped source to keep fresh).

`65045129d08d5bc47fa1e89a6085784a8600fed1` merges the authored code head `08caf4d1c3c04925be2d4172fcd9e70d7a3d03b7`.

08caf4d1c3c04925be2d4172fcd9e70d7a3d03b7

## Repair of `instrument-self-tests` (Show the tick loop refusing its own fixtures)

The step went red at `5d647dd0` (run 43242542423, job 131266913985: `30 checks, 1 failed`, `FAIL a seat bin dir with no gh shim…`). The earlier body attributed this to a defect in an older `tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh` repaired on main by `e899dde4ab`; that was false: the review measured `e899dde4ab` an ancestor of both `6e8db8d8` and `5d647dd0`, and `tick_loop.sh` byte-identical at `5d647dd0` and `b131ad0a`.

The red is not introduced by this diff, which touches nothing the self-test reads; it recurs whenever main moves more than 25 commits on those paths before CI runs. That self-test isolation defect is carried as R10-HOTFIX-TICK-SELFTEST-CHECKOUT (`handoff-wip/r10-hotfix-tick-selftest-checkout`), not built here.

At this head, branch `work` checked out, 0 commits behind `origin/main` (`git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main`): `env -u BASH_ENV bash tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh --self-test` printed `tick_loop self-test: 30 checks, 0 failed`. `instrument-self-tests` is not in `merge_train.py owed-reds`, so it owes no `## Red checks` entry.

## Red checks

Read per commit from the PR's check-runs (runs 8032-8036, 8059/8060, 8069/8070/8072), not from the earlier body. Every check that concluded red on any commit of the branch:

- `tests / closures`: red at `b7a838c1ef516f840530eb85b4c94c6fdfdab0f1` (run 8060, job 131170648315), `INERT READS UNDER-APPROXIMATED`: `tests/harness_headers.py` opened `dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/main_reds.py`, which the committed `inert_reads` did not list. Repaired by the `closures-autofix` bot commit `5d647dd055d7e08e1073bedbe570257c606b98b3` (one added `inert_reads` line in `tests/closures.json`), which the repair head `b131ad0a` dropped and this head carries again through the merge of `29996fad`. The earlier body said `none` here, which is why `pr-contract` went red. **Cheaper detector:** `python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --apply-inert` before the handoff, but it does not exist for this red: run on a clean worktree at `6e8db8d8` (base `02a73718`, then `origin/main`) it printed `CI PREDICT: no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted` in 2.6 s and wrote nothing, and `--apply-inert` the same (a data-file read is not seen). The detector that does reproduce the red is `env -u BASH_ENV ./tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/harness_headers.py`: it wrote exactly the one missing line (`main_reds.py`), 169.6 s wall (2m49.6s) on this diff, against the CI closures job's 25 min (12:08 to 12:33) plus one bot commit and a second full run. **Process state: (c)**, the process existed and ran and did not produce the intended result: the step 6d predictor is the pre-handoff path `ci-autofix.md` names for INERT READS, and it is blind to a file a harness reads at run time by directory, so a green `ci_predict` said nothing about this red. **Cost test:** adding a standing `--single tests/harness_headers.py` (about 170 s) to every handoff costs more than it saves, because the red is repaired mechanically by the `closures-autofix` job with no seat action and no manual cost; the defect cost here was wall-clock only (about 25 min of one CI cycle). - `pr-contract / pr-contract`: red at `b7a838c1` and `5d647dd0` (`Check the body against the contract`), because the body above said `none` for `tests / closures`. A consequence of the same answer, cleared by this body; the contract excludes its own verdict from the set it asks a body to answer.

Runs 8032, 8033 and 8035 at `2c803484` and `7033a7e4` concluded `cancelled` (superseded by the next push), not red.

merges.subject: Merge pull request #3518 from tvofi/fix/r10-hotfix-mutant-run-darwin-pr
merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-MUTANT-RUN-DARWIN: r10 hotfix mutant run darwin
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
HOTFIX r10-hotfix-mutant-run-darwin. Since #3475, `tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py` lists `/proc` in `family()` and `_reap()`. macOS has no `/proc`, so every run there raised `FileNotFoundError`, `tools/pr/prepr.sh --self-test` failed its `mutants_line` fixtures on the orchestrator's macOS host, and every pull request opened from that host was refused.

The fix has two halves.

**The readers.** One process-table reader, `_ptable()`, returns `(pid, state, ppid, pgrp, session)`. It lists the procfs root; on `FileNotFoundError` it reads `ps -axo pid=,stat=,ppid=,pgid=`, takes the session from `os.getsid`, and drops the `ps` process's own row. `family()` and `_reap()` both read that table. The environment-token read is `_carries()`, False where no `<root>/<pid>/environ` exists. A `ps` that fails raises `OSError`, never an empty table, which would switch the fork cap off silently.

**The platform is injected, not patched.** The procfs root is `PROCFS[0]`, taken from `MUTANT_RUN_PROCFS` (default `/proc`); a root that does not exist is a host without procfs. The first seat's self-test emulated macOS by monkeypatching `os.listdir` and `Path.read_text`/`read_bytes`, and its null control read the host's real `/proc`: on macOS that control could not hold (2 of 64 checks failed). The self-test now reads the table three ways on every host: with no procfs root, through a faked procfs root it writes from the live table (`<pid>/stat`, `<pid>/environ`), and through the host's own `/proc`. Where the host has none, that third leg is one printed, counted `skip`. A staged `ps` on PATH supplies the rows no live table yields on demand: a row whose session `os.getsid` refuses, a line that is no row, a `Zs` zombie in the command's group. Two driver runs pin that the root the environment names is the one the driver reads.

Skips are counted. Every case the host cannot run goes through one `skip()` and the self-test prints `mutant_run self-test: <n> skipped` above the summary line, whose text `governance.yml` greps and which is therefore unchanged in shape. A check pins the count against the two host facts it depends on: four without a child subreaper, one without `/proc`, none on a Linux host with both.

Carry 0 of the roster group (the orchestrator's macOS run: at fdfd99d535 the driver's self-test fails 2 of 64 checks on Darwin, both null controls that need a real proc filesystem; owed, a stated precondition and a skip named in the tally, or an emulated table, with no skip hiding a Linux failure) is built in this pull request, both ways: the table is emulated through the faked root on every host, and the host-`/proc` leg states its precondition and is a counted, printed skip where the host has none. Re-measured on this Mac: 64 checks, 2 failed at fdfd99d535; 71 checks, 0 failed, 5 skipped at this head. The Linux half of its control (the host leg runs unskipped and the tally reads 0 skipped) is Linux CI's to confirm.

Alternatives considered:
- Skip the two null controls on a host without `/proc` and stop there. It lost: the procfs readers would then run nowhere but Linux CI, and the defect this hotfix repairs is exactly a reader one platform never ran.
- Keep the monkeypatch and add a fake `/proc` by patching more calls. It lost to one injectable root: the production readers take the root as data, so no test patches the standard library.
- The brief's candidate patch (a second `ps` loop inside `family()`, `_reap()` returning nothing). It lost at the first seat: it duplicated the descendant walk, `ps` counted itself as a child, and a refused `getsid` dropped the whole row.

Scope beyond the brief's two files, by the orchestrator's ruling of 2026-11-12: `dev/audit/harnesses/mutant_run_diff_shards.py` (the shard runner the survivor figures below came from, fixer.md step 18) and its one `tests/closures.json` inert-read entry, written by `python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --apply-inert`.

## Head

`7c15eaf837f61d798d08c598770ca3b8ce3838ef` merges the authored code head `b49a16c2f7a11194e9eb2662d3e992c864c6fb7d`.

b49a16c2f7a11194e9eb2662d3e992c864c6fb7d. Every figure below was measured at its parent 3dccd18a95617b752a1be6fce24f5dc7df3bd57f, and so was the `Prepr:` receipt (full `tools/pr/prepr.sh`, rc 0, at 3dccd18a95); the delta to this head is one file, `dev/audit/harnesses/mutant_run_diff_shards.py`, which now finds the checkout with the canonical `repo_root` walk in place of `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]`. That delta answers a red the scoped gate found after the first handoff: `tests/harness_headers.py`'s inline scan refused the depth root (`harness_headers.inline_scan()` rc 1 at 3dccd18a95, rc 0 at this head). No full prepr was re-run at this head. 3dccd18a95 was measured on macOS (Darwin, arm64) with origin/main 19baca76181cb019d9b1cfd93ee6bc0a08e20047 as merge base, at 2026-11-12T17:35Z. `tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py` is byte-identical between d823c55e4d, where the mutant figures were taken, 3dccd18a95 and this head: `git diff --quiet d823c55e4d HEAD -- tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py && echo IDENTICAL` prints `IDENTICAL`.

## Mutation proof

Command: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --spec <spec> --cmd '<the self-test, its output kept per run>'`, the spec being the twelve edits below. Output: `SURVIVED NULL`, then one line per mutant; the failing checks are from the kept output of the same runs, on macOS.

| mutant | edit | result | checks that go red (macOS) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `procfs_leg_reads_ps` | `os.listdir(PROCFS[0])` lists a path that never exists, so the table is always `ps` | KILLED | faked root: `a failing ps is never read: the table is procfs`; `a driver whose MUTANT_RUN_PROCFS names an empty root sees no process` |
| `no_procfs_leg_no_ps_fallback` | `except FileNotFoundError:` becomes `except NotADirectoryError:` | KILLED | the no-procfs leg ends in `FileNotFoundError` at its first `family()` call, rc 1, no summary line |
| `no_procfs_leg_failed_ps_is_empty_table` | `if ps.returncode:` becomes `if False:` | KILLED | no procfs: `a failing ps refuses (OSError), never an empty table that turns the cap off` |
| `host_leg_never_skipped` | the skip predicate of the host-`/proc` leg becomes `if False:` | KILLED | host leg: `found by its token (the environ leg)`, `a failing ps is never read`; and `skip: each case this host cannot run is counted, once` |
| `skip_not_counted` | `skips += 1` becomes `skips += 0` | KILLED | `skip: each case this host cannot run is counted, once` |
| `env_root_ignored` | `PROCFS` no longer reads `MUTANT_RUN_PROCFS` | KILLED | `a driver whose MUTANT_RUN_PROCFS names an empty root sees no process` |
| `zombie_state_not_sliced` | `state[:1]` becomes `state` | KILLED | no procfs: the staged-`ps` check (`a Zs zombie in the command's group is not counted`) |
| `refused_getsid_keeps_last_session` | `session = None` becomes `pass` | KILLED | no procfs: the staged-`ps` check (`a row whose session os.getsid refuses takes no other row's`) |
| `reap_collects_nothing` | `_reap`'s predicate becomes `if False:` | KILLED | `_reap() collects a dead child it does not skip`, with no procfs and through the faked root |
| `token_matched_as_substring` | `mark in env.split(b"\0")` becomes `mark in env` | KILLED | faked root: the session, ppid and token arms (the near-miss token is found) |
| `ps_counts_itself` | `if int(pid) == ps.pid:` becomes `if False:` | KILLED | `family() finds the driver's descendants by ppid, zombies excluded`, with no procfs and through the faked root (whose table is written from `ps` here) |
| `stat_split_after_first_paren` | `stat.rindex(")")` becomes `stat.index(")")` | KILLED | faked root: the session, ppid, token and `_reap` arms (every faked comm holds `) `) |

A mutant per leg: `no_procfs_leg_*` fail the no-procfs leg, `procfs_leg_reads_ps`, `token_matched_as_substring` and `stat_split_after_first_paren` fail the procfs leg through the faked root, and `host_leg_never_skipped` shows what the skip guards on a host without `/proc`. On Linux the host leg runs unskipped, and the same procfs mutants are expected to fail it there; that is Linux CI's to confirm.

Failing test first: at the merge base 19baca7618 `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --self-test` on this Mac prints 4 `ok` lines and 5 `FAIL` lines and then ends in a `FileNotFoundError` traceback with no summary line, rc 1. At the first seat's tip fdfd99d535 it prints `64 checks, 2 failed`, both `no-procfs: with /proc present (null control)` arms (the environ leg, and a failing `ps` never read).

## Unpinned sites

Measurement: the diff's mutants are `mutant_run.py`'s own `diff_mutants` over `19baca7618...HEAD`, which is exactly the lines the two seats added (the narrowest base there is); the command is `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --self-test`. One self-test takes about a minute on this host, so the full list was run in four shards with `dev/audit/harnesses/mutant_run_diff_shards.py`, which calls the driver's own `added_lines`, `diff_mutants`, `Workspace` and `run_cmd`; no full serial `--diff` pass was run. `tools/pr/prepr.sh`'s diff-mutant step (`MUTANT_CMD`, the serial driver, the first 40 mutants) is the cross-check. The survivor triage ledger cannot hold these: `tests/mutation_table.py`'s key grammar admits only `custom_components/` anchors, so each survivor is answered here.

Result on macOS at d823c55e4d: 128 mutants, 92 KILLED, 36 SURVIVED, 0 FORKCAP. All 36 are in `tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py`'s self-test half (line 640 on); no survivor is in a production reader (`_ptable`, `_carries`, `family`, `_reap`, `PROCFS`). The first seat reported 16 on Linux at fdfd99d535; the count is higher here because this seat added checks, and every added `check(...)` call is one deletable statement. One of the first pass's survivors was a real gap, now closed: deleting `session = None` in `_ptable` let a `ps` row whose `os.getsid` is refused keep the previous row's session; the staged-`ps` check kills it (`refused_getsid_keeps_last_session` above).

Each line is `line OPERATOR`, the mutated statement, and its disposition.

Unmeasured on macOS (Linux-only arm), 12. The cloud reviewer measures these on Linux; none is claimed killed or equivalent here:
- `656 CONST_SWAP` `prev = _subreaper(2)` in `_can_subreap`: unmeasured on macOS (Linux-only arm); `prctl` is absent here, so the probe returns -1 whatever its argument.
- `657 CMP_BOUND` `return prev > 0 and ...`: unmeasured on macOS (Linux-only arm); `prev` is -1 here.
- `657 CONST_SWAP` `return prev >= 1 and ...`: unmeasured on macOS (Linux-only arm); same line.
- `1026 STMT_DEL` `name = f"forkcap: a daemon that ..."`: unmeasured on macOS (Linux-only arm); here only the `skip` line reads `name`, and no check reads a skip line's text.
- `1030 CALL_DEL` `write_spec([bad])`: unmeasured on macOS (Linux-only arm); the daemon cases are skipped here.
- `1031 STMT_DEL` `rc, out, _ = drive(...)` of the daemon cases: unmeasured on macOS (Linux-only arm).

A command substitution's status is its last command's, `echo x`, so it is always 0, and the `BUS carry-landing UNREAD #<pr>: the body could not be read` branch can no longer fire. When gh fails, `raw` becomes empty, there is no `HEADREF:` line, and `carry_audit.py landed` runs on an empty body and returns rc 0. The gate passes with nothing printed where it used to say UNREAD. It still lets the dispatch go on either way, but the one signal that the gate judged nothing is gone. Under `## Evidence` of a merge verdict, the base flags this item `carry` and the head drops it.

n/a: record-only diff -- every file in this pull request is a `dev/programme/delivery/<N>.md` row file; there is no production, test or check code here to mutate.

## Null control

n/a: no quantified production claim; the one figure names its instrument and re-derives at the head.

## Red checks

`governance / record` (`record`), `tests / nightly-status` (`nightly-status`) and `governance / delivery-status` (`delivery-status`) may stand red on main at the base this beat was computed against; each is answered here.

- `governance / record` (`record`): a rowless merge is the batch interval the record protocol promises, and this pull request is that batch, which is the answer the check's own refusal text names. No cheaper detector exists than the check that already fired; its standing cost is one beat per batch.
- `tests / nightly-status` (`nightly-status`) and `governance / delivery-status` (`delivery-status`) grade `main`, not this pull request. This beat's delivery rows are precisely the drain `delivery-status` batches, so the red is the batch this beat exists to close; `nightly-status` executes nothing this diff changes and is answered because the shared reporter-input rule counts a row the diff rewrites. No cheaper detector exists than the check that already fired; its standing cost is one beat per batch.

none

none

Opened by the hpo-author App. No review seat: where `record_row.py --automerge-check` passes at the head, the approver App approves and the beat merges it at that head once its required checks pass (tvofi, 2026-10-07); where it refuses, the review stays manual. R10-HOTFIX-CARD-HEALTH-TEXT, carries 0 and 1, cut from main after #3485. This PR changes only `tests/card_browser.mjs`, and no production line.

**Carry 1 (P662).** `themeMismatch`'s cases now include the two matched arms: light variables with darkMode false, and dark variables with darkMode true. One unit therefore measures every own-text run on the tile and on every dialog page, Health and Advisor rows included, in all four theme/darkMode pairings. Before this PR, the matched arms were measured only by the P9 grid's lockstep cells. The own-text sweep moves out of `themeMismatch`'s page script into `hpoContrastKit`, which `themeLiveSwitch` also reads. That keeps one copy of the WCAG unit.

**Carry 0 (owner fact: default theme, auto, following macOS).** `themeLiveSwitch` mounts the card on HA's default theme tokens (`THEMES.light`/`THEMES.dark`) and opens the Health dialog. It then switches the OS colour scheme live, light to dark and back, with `page.emulateMedia`. In the page, a `prefers-color-scheme` change listener does what HA's themes mixin does, in the same order. It writes the theme's variables onto the document. One microtask later, it gives the card a hass whose `themes.darkMode` is the new scheme. The Health dialog is measured twice per direction: between the variable write and the hass update, and on the frame after the card's re-render. Reach requires each of these:
- at the first point, the card still holds the old darkMode and the old row surface, so that measurement is the mismatched pairing;
- after the re-render, the dialog is still open on Health;
- the row surface flipped;
- at least 10 `span.fact-text` labels are measured at both points.

**Which state the owner's install was in.** Steady state is the matched arm: dark variables with darkMode true (or light with false). HA writes the variables and darkMode together on every OS switch. The card reads no OS scheme itself: the card has 0 `@media (prefers-color-scheme` rules, and its 2 `matchMedia(` calls are `pointer: coarse` and `prefers-reduced-motion`. So the P9 grid's off-lockstep cells (OS scheme varied, darkMode fixed) do not change the card's paint, and they are not the live state.

On the released pairing, the steady arms are green, so this contrast check cannot be red in the owner's steady state. The released pairing is red only in the window between HA's variable write and its hass update, at 1.24:1 (light to dark) and 1.11:1 (dark to light). In this model the hass update lands one microtask after the write, so no frame is painted inside that window. Whether HA's frontend paints one is not measured here. The orchestrator's hypothesis is therefore refuted as an explanation of the screenshot: the owner's install was in the matched arm, where the released rows read 11.08:1 (RCA second pass). The screenshot's box-less labels are #3485's blocker cause, and `blockerHide` is red on the released card in that matched dark arm (#3485 body). The new check still pins the transient. A fix that moved the rows back onto a darkMode literal under theme text would go red there, as the mutation below shows.

## Head

`c3857c8fbc220dbe2466662e8233f2c3ebb4d999` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3509.md`. The authored code head is `e5e6c81b8ee7fe91a2599ae6d021bb6a471a4890`.

e5e6c81b8ee7fe91a2599ae6d021bb6a471a4890, merged with origin/main 19baca76181cb019d9b1cfd93ee6bc0a08e20047 (merge base 19baca76181cb019d9b1cfd93ee6bc0a08e20047) at 2026-11-12T13:38:51Z. The two merges of main (at cbe8d93bd8 and 19baca7618) brought in no card or browser-lane file (`git diff --name-only e1361b108c HEAD`: gate, stamp, merge-train, plan-tooling and delivery files only). The browser-lane run below was taken at the pre-merge commit e1361b108c, on the same card and test tree.

## Mutation proof

Planted the released defect as Carry 1 specifies: `.health-row, .fact-inbox-row` back on `--hpo-surface-2` with `--hpo-text`, as at 906fee95e. In the card's surface-2 rule, the two row selectors leave the ink re-point and get a background-only rule. I ran a scratch driver that calls only `themeLiveSwitch` and `themeMismatch` from `tests/card_browser.mjs`. Four checks go red:
- `R10 live light to dark: every Health text run clears 4.5:1 between HA's theme write and its hass update`: 40 of 59 runs under 4.5:1, `span.fact-text` / `span.fact-sub` at 1.24:1
- `R10 live dark to light: every Health text run clears 4.5:1 between HA's theme write and its hass update`: 40 of 59 runs, 1.11:1
- `R10 every own-text run on every dialog page clears 4.5:1 with dark theme variables, darkMode false`: 65 runs, Advisor `span.fact-text`, `span.fact-sub`, `span.fact-value` and `button.fact-act` at 1.24:1
- `R10 every own-text run on every dialog page clears 4.5:1 with light theme variables, darkMode true`: 65 runs, the same elements at 1.11:1

Card restored with `git checkout custom_components/`.

## Null control

Under the same planted defect, these stay ok:
- both matched arms of `themeMismatch`, with their tile and chart checks;
- both `after the card's re-render` checks;
- both reach checks;
- the start check.

The matched arms and the post-render frames are the steady states the RCA found clean, so the red comes from the mismatched pairing and not from the sweep. On the unmutated tree, all 7 `themeLiveSwitch` checks and all 12 `themeMismatch` checks are ok.

## Figures

- 59 runs measured on the Health dialog per live switch, and 40 under 4.5:1 on the planted defect. Instrument: `themeLiveSwitch` in `node tests/card_browser.mjs`. Measured through a scratch driver that patches the file's driver to call only that function after `chromium.launch()`; it is not in the tree.
- 65 runs under 4.5:1 per mismatched arm on the planted defect, and 0 in the matched arms. Instrument: `themeMismatch` in `node tests/card_browser.mjs`, same driver.
- Full browser lane: `node tests/card_browser.mjs` printed `P9 grid MODE: FULL (HPO_BROWSER_SCOPE=full)` and `ALL BROWSER CHECKS PASSED`, rc 0, at e1361b108c. Payload from `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/plan_view.py`.
- The card has 0 OS-scheme rules and 2 `matchMedia(` calls, neither of them the colour scheme. Instrument: `python3 -c` with `re.findall(r'@media[^{]*prefers-color-scheme', s)` and `s.count('matchMedia(')` over `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/www/heatpump-optimizer-card.js`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.

merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-OPENER-UNBLOCK: the opener's two blockers, in two seams and disjoint files. Hotfix by owner ruling (tvofi, 2026-11-11T20:13Z).

- **Part A, BEAT-STALE-CHECKOUT (P581), `tools/audit/seat/beatd.py`.** After every PASS (never under `--once`), the beat counts origin/main's commits over its own checkout on `tools/audit/seat` and `tools/pr`. Those are `pr_args.sh` `pr_tools_fresh`'s paths, whose STALE CHECKOUT refused the opener. If the checkout is behind, no job instance is running, the tracked tree is clean, `git rev-list origin/main..HEAD` is empty, origin/main's `beatd.py` compiles, and the beat has not already restarted to that origin/main sha (guard `HPO_BEATD_RESTARTED`), the beat restarts. It runs `git checkout -q -B <branch> origin/main` (`--detach` on a detached head), journals STOP, prints `BEAT-RESTART`, and re-execs itself in place with the same arguments. Once the restart is taken, `run_one` starts no new instance. Any other outcome prints `beatd: NO-RESTART behind=<n> code=<sha12>: <why>`, and from the second consecutive refusal also `BEAT-STALE <utc> ...`. A running instance only defers the restart to the next PASS. STATUS's `STALE-CODE`, which counts every commit, stays the alarm. The checkout path does not change, so beatd.tools, the orch checkout and the launch files are untouched. There is no separate rotate instrument (rejected in the ruling).
- **Part B, OPENER-LIVE-TIP (P603), `tools/audit/seat/open_driver.py`.** When origin's handoff tip differs from the board line's sha, the pass logs `RETIP <topic> <board sha8> -> <tip sha8>`. It then runs every candidate check (batched, no-body, seen, landed, fix-branch, live, stuck, backoff) and the open at the live tip. `SKIP moved` stays only when origin has no handoff ref for the topic. `ct` stays the board line's, so STARVED ages from the line's commit.

- **Test hermeticity, `tests/gate_lock.py` `_priority_cases`.** `prepr.sh` exports `HPO_GATE_PRIORITY` from the branch name, and it is 2 on a hotfix branch. The arms `priority_first` and `slot_priority` started their normal waiter outside `_Env`, so it inherited 2, both waiters were urgent, and the queue released them in FIFO order. As a result, `tests/entities.py` failed under prepr's closures recording (`2 of 2705 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`, three runs of three on this branch), but not when run standalone. Each normal waiter now enters under `_Env(None)`.

Alternatives considered: Part A could poll on a timer thread instead of after each PASS. That lost because it adds a second scheduler beside the job loops, and "between passes" is exactly the PASS boundary. Part A could also exec from inside `Beat.run`. That lost because `cmd_run` must drop `beatd.lock` first, which its `finally` does.

## Head

`8335dbdb197fdb58a04499857a611d9b1530805f` merges main `19baca7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`190ec599dac05e7a19e7639376c737d53ba40685` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`92ecb6c16ea264a2b468f2a30a932d3c22068e88`. Merge base and origin/main are both `5365b1843702465563fd330623464769777c8c06`, at 2026-11-12T11:24Z.

Merge repair: `cf26b254e6` merges origin/main `5365b18437` (past the v7.1.12 stamp `4596f721f6`) into the previous head `93e4697879`. Its one conflict, `tools/audit/seat/beatd.py` `cmd_run`, is resolved by union: main's `launch.json` write (what `liveness.py` relaunches a dead beatd from) runs first, then this branch's `beat = Beat(...)`, `rc = beat.run(...)` and the in-place `os.execve` restart. Read-back: every line each parent added over the merge base is present in the merged file (a `grep -qxF` per added line of `git diff -U0 <base> <side> -- tools/audit/seat/beatd.py`, which prints `MISSING:` per absent line; it printed none for either side). The reviewer's delta is the `cmd_run` hunk of `git diff 93e4697879 92ecb6c16e -- tools/audit/seat/beatd.py`; `tests/closures.json` is byte-identical to origin/main's (`git diff --quiet origin/main HEAD -- tests/closures.json`).

`env -u BASH_ENV ./tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/entities.py` ran at `cf26b254e6`, rc 0, and its recording was committed as `f08baa3673`, then withdrawn by `92ecb6c16e`. It raised `inert_reads["tests/entities.py"]` from 75 to 1644 entries (1569 new: 799 under `dev/audit`, 663 under `dev/programme`, 6 under `dev/governance/decisions`). At that head `prepr.sh` refused twice. Its self-test failed 3 of 542 on the 6b skip arm (`6b skips a diff that reaches no selectable script, recording nothing (got 1, wanted 3)`): a new `dev/governance/rules/` file now reaches `tests/entities.py`. `ci_predict.py` also predicted a closures red, because the recording dropped `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_open_driver_mutants.py` from the entry. The same self-test exits rc 0 at origin/main (null control). With main's `closures.json`, `ci_predict.py --apply-inert` writes nothing and predicts no red. A recording that widens the gate's reach belongs to the closures lane, not a merge repair. Carry: dismissed: the recording is CI's `closures` job and `closures-autofix`'s to commit on Linux, not this repair's.

Figures re-taken at this head: the beatd self-test, the scope, the structure ratchet and prepr.sh. The others below were taken at `80779d2e74` and describe code the merge did not touch.

## Mutation proof

Part A, `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/beatd.py --self-test 9`. Each of the 10 mutants turns its named case-9 check red:

`tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh` `carry_fold_arm`, R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE part 1 of 6: **Carry 14** (P556, S14-CARRY-FOLD-WRONG-CHECKOUT) and **Carry 22** (P580, CARRY-FOLD-ARM-REJUDGES-EVERY-PASS), built as one change to the arm. Carry 17 (same arm, the handoff-wip dispose) is part 6's and is not touched; dispose is not widened to `handoff-wip/`.

- **Carry 14.** At the base the body push ran from `git worktree add --detach "$wt" FETCH_HEAD` (base line 838, `git show a7628041dc:tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh | grep -n FETCH_HEAD`). The worktree is now added at a private ref, `+refs/heads/handoff/<topic>:refs/hpo-relay/fold/<topic>`, deleted after the push. Before `body_push.sh` runs, the worktree's HEAD must equal `handoff/<topic>`'s tip from the arm's own `ls-remote`, which now lists `refs/heads/handoff/*` as well as `refs/heads/handoff-wip/*`. Otherwise the arm prints `OWED carry-fold <topic> worktree at <a>, handoff at <b>`, puts that on the level and pushes nothing, so a failing pass logs the fold worktree's head, as reproduce step (1) asks. `HPO_RELAY_BODYPUSH` now replaces only the `body_push.sh` call inside that worktree. At the base it skipped the worktree entirely, so the self-test never exercised the real checkout. A missing handoff is now on the level; at the base it was only printed, with no level line.
- **Carry 22.** A new state file, `cloud-fold-judged`, holds one line per topic: `<topic> <wip sha> <body sha|-> <outcome> <epoch> [<its OWED level line>]`. The outcome is one of `blocked`, `fold-failed`, `push-failed` or `folded`. Both shas come from the `ls-remote` the arm already makes. A memoed pair is neither fetched nor shown (base line 818 fetched every one), and its stored OWED line goes back into `cloud-level-fold.$$`, because `level_set carry-fold` (base line 849) replaces the whole kind. `fold_memo_stands` lets `fold-failed` and `push-failed` expire after 3600 s, because an ancestry red can clear with no ref moving. Success still appends to `cloud-folded` (base line 843). The memo is rebuilt each pass from the topics listed in that pass.

Alternatives not taken. Storing the OWED line in the level file was rejected: the level is per `--log`, so a pass with another log would silently drop an owed item. An env-tunable TTL was rejected: the self-test ages the memo entry instead, so no knob was added. Moving the worktree check ahead of `carry_fold.py` was also rejected. It would change the order the brief prices as "a failure after the fold", and the cost it would save happens only when no handoff exists.

Carry numbers in this body are 0-based roster indexes, as the part-1 dispatch gives them: "This part: Carries 14, 22 (0-based roster indexes)". The check now de-duplicates the globs and pins `len(globs) == 2`, the set the handoff machinery lists; its wip-invisible and handoff-visible assertions are unchanged. `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py --self-test` now prints `169 checks, 0 failed`; `bash tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh --self-test` prints `452 checks, 0 failed`. `tests/closures.json` is re-recorded by `env -u BASH_ENV ./tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/entities.py` (entities `rc` 1 to 0).

Round 2 was blocked `mutation-vacuous` at c562b07972 on two survivors. Both are now closed in `carry_fold_arm` and its self-test; round 2's triage of them is withdrawn.

- Rewriting that line exposed a third survivor, `r3-folded-skip-off`: replacing `&& continue` with `&& true` survived the round-2 suite. The self-test now moves `handoff-wip/cf-a` after its fold and asserts that `carry_fold.py` ran once for cf-a. That mutant is KILLED.

The alternative to deleting the memo write was a check that the `cloud-fold-judged` line survives a pass. It lost because nothing reads that line for an already-folded topic: the check would pin a write with no consumer.

SURVIVED: r3-folded-skip-off.

- The cost figures (27-33 s, about 181 s a pass) are the triage's, from the live relay. This seat has no relay state, so they are not re-measured. The self-test pins the mechanism, which is that a memoed pair is not fetched.

merges.body:
Part A of the duty-switch restart learning, built from Bankaifan's pull request 3420 with thanks: the finding, the install's table and the first implementation are theirs, and their ten commits are this branch's first ten, authorship kept. On a Luxtronik install driven over the smart-home interface, a hot water to space mode write while the compressor runs stops it; nothing priced or observed that. This pull request observes each such switch, estimates per pump and per direction how often it ends in a stop and how long the pump then stays off, persists the estimate and publishes it on the compressor-starts sensor. **Nothing reads the estimate to change a plan or a write**: that is parts B and C of the design approved at `design/R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING` abc575172ca1e6758c58ca8d1f265a2dc7c4fa23, which `docs/design/2026-11-10-duty-switch-restart-learning/design.md` now carries. No issue is closed: the finding arrived as pull request 3420, which the orchestrator closes with thanks after the merge.

## Re-cut

The seventh repair, answering the seventh review, past the three-round bound by owner ruling: outside request, drive to merge. This body replaces the earlier ones under `fixer.md`'s re-cut rule: round history is deleted, and every figure below was re-taken at the head named under Head, but where a line says it was not re-run. The round-7 review (`Fix review: blocked 112f0d777b8f8c921a75982d36305e94ffd2f7f4 mutation-vacuous: r7v_unsettled_with_pending_runs`, `verdict.md` on `probe/rev-3461-ba74baae`) is answered under "Review round 7, answered". Since 112f0d77 the branch adds two checks to the duty-switch section of `tests/features.py` and a `fresh` argument to its `_ds_wrapped` driver, merges `origin/main` three times, last 19baca76181cb019d9b1cfd93ee6bc0a08e20047, and gives the section's arbiter fake the `dhw_max_temp` that main's 4498df97 made the arbiter read; no production line moved.
## Head

`2e1e33a70a4c09db239d8814e3a645a90d9a2cfd` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

9453c5e25523a963106e27aad6e9fe16846aa367

The merge base is 19baca76181cb019d9b1cfd93ee6bc0a08e20047 (`git merge-base origin/main HEAD` at this head), which is `origin/main`: this head merges it. Every command below compares three-dot against the merge base. The mutant runs, the drift, structure and architecture figures and the diff pass ran at a5e0e78df906e41e3a59b503a0b9531a8edadf22, which merged `origin/main` 6e100ef6980216a81eaa0438bdc215d62b19271f; this head differs from it by the merges of `origin/main` cbe8d93b and 19baca76 alone, whose delta from 6e100ef6 touches nothing under `custom_components/` and not `tests/features.py` (`git diff --stat 6e100ef69 19baca761 -- custom_components tests/features.py` prints nothing), so the diff pass's mutant set and the section are the same. The scoped gate (`GOLDEN_REF=cbe8d93b`) ran at f6b7356ef7dc89555f5182f5a3a5e0f830f4c503, which merged `origin/main` cbe8d93b; this head adds only the merge of `origin/main` 19baca76, whose delta from cbe8d93b is seven files under `tools/plan/`, `tools/audit/seat/`, `dev/audit/harnesses/` and `dev/programme/delivery/`, and nothing under `custom_components/` or `tests/`. `tools/pr/prepr.sh` with this body ran at this head.
## Brief carries

- Carry 1 (the build input; the brief prints it as carry 0): done as asked. The branch starts from pull request 3420's ten commits at e05c6b1ccc17f2486160669f4a64a33b79ea6a17, the head `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/3420/head` still printed at the start, re-committed with author and author date kept; the build was measured against the approved design and the reviewer's comparison section, as the next section answers line by line, and not rebuilt from scratch: the episode and void logic, the pass-confirmed debounce, the store's three census registrations and the stop, kept, defrost and reload tests are the contributor's, moved behind the design's seam.
- Carry 2 (this body's own round-1 item be768cab, folded onto the roster): done in the tree. `docs/design/2026-11-10-duty-switch-restart-learning/design.md`, section "Part A as built", now holds it: no read API and where the first reader goes, the conditional keys, the wider loop void, n with no ceiling but the load bound. The groups it constrains are parts B and C, so it is carried on to their briefs under Forward-carry.
- Carry 3 (round-1 item 25e8fe39, folded likewise): done in the tree, in the same section of the design note: the supply minimum-run hold of pull request 3420 is removed and built nowhere. Where it is built is the orchestrator's decision and is not made here.

## What was cut from pull request 3420, and what moved

Each line answers one conflict of `verdict.md`'s section "Pull request 3420 at e05c6b1ccc against this design" on `design-verdict/R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING`.

- Scope: `supply_hold.py`, `cycle_supply`, the retry in `supply_tick`, the split hook in `_share`, and the edits to `coordinator.py` and `early_cutoff.py` are removed; `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat -- custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/early_cutoff.py custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/diagnostics.py` prints nothing.
- Seam: `ArbiterState` gains no field; `duty_switch.py` holds a `WeakKeyDictionary` registry of its own and no longer imports `pump_arbiter.py`. The arbiter makes four calls into it (`attach`, `detach`, `note_mode_write`, `note_pass`) and builds the context in `_switch_context` and `_report_write`.
- Running signal: `wear.compressor_running` and `wear.EdgeTracker`. The floor is `RUNNING_FLOOR_HZ`, the line `freq_control.FrequencyMap.observe` already refuses a sample under (item n9: no install's stopped reading was available to this seat; the constant says so).
- Estimate: two decayed weights per direction, a stored latch with the four thresholds, an off list capped on write and refused on load when longer.
- Load: a record loads whole or empty (`DutySwitchLearner.from_record`); a failed read is not marked loaded.
- Heated gate: `_flow_inlet_c`, per direction (below).
- Void list: the feedback loop and the same-option re-send are added.
- Publication: the sensor's attributes; the diagnostics key is removed.
- `tests/guard_pins.py`'s two coordinator stubs gain an `entry`: the learner's store is keyed on it as the arbiter's is, and the stubs had none because the arbiter's own persist swallows the `AttributeError`.

## Departures from the approved design, each for the owner or reviewer to overrule

- Store encoding. The design stores k and n. `Direction` stores k and the kept weight, n their sum: with k and n, `tests/finite_boundary.py`'s in-domain probe of k exceeded n, was refused as k > n and read as unreached; two addends make every in-domain pair valid. Published attributes are still k and n.
- Tallies. `stopped` and `kept` are stored integers beside `void` and `censored`: the design publishes them and its store list omits them.
- Read API. The design lists a read API "unused in A". It is not built: an unused module-level function raises `dead_top_level_symbols`, which sits at zero headroom. `Direction.usable`, `.p` and `.median_off_s` hold the three values.
- Origin (share, lease, other) is not in the context: nothing in A reads it.
- 3405's loop voids on any target the loop moved off the open-loop one (`FeedbackRun.sent_c` set), raised as well as lowered: the base is not in reach of the pass, and a wider void costs evidence only.
- Source-leg age is the replaced mode record's age, not `dhw_since`, which `_leased` has already reset on the pass that leaves hot water.
- The space set-point the heated gate reads is the command's, written right after the mode, not the written record, which at that instant is still the hot-water leg's.
- Publication is conditional. Five `coord_*` goldens snapshot the starts sensor's `extra_state_attributes`, so the design's premise that the sensor is off the goldens does not hold, and fourteen always-present keys read as five stale fixtures in `tests/env_drift.py --all`. A direction publishes its keys only once it holds a stopped, kept or void episode; an install that never switches duty while running publishes what it did before, and no golden moves. Mutant `publish_only_observed`.
- Factory reset keeps the store (`_FR_STORES`, the contributor's disposition). Learned state elsewhere is voided there; the owner may want this voided too.

## Review round 7, answered

1. mutation-vacuous. The survivor is killed by one check added to the duty-switch section, beside its null control; it is not triaged.
   - `r7v_unsettled_with_pending_runs` (`duty_switch.note_mode_write` counting an unsettled tracker with an edge pending as running): "through duty_switch.note_mode_write, a mode write on a record just loaded whose first reading, 50 Hz, came inside the debounce before the write and is still pending opens nothing and books nothing". Driven through `_Record`, `note_signal`, `note_mode_write` and `note_pass`: `_ds_wrapped`'s new `fresh` argument skips the settling reading and pass, so the record is as loaded (`settled is None`); its first reading, 50 Hz, is taken `_DS_START_LEAD` (10 s) before the hot water to heating write with no pass between, so it is pending at the write; nothing opens and nothing is booked, whether the reading holds through the window or reads 0 Hz 15 s after the write. The check asserts `0 < _DS_START_LEAD < wear.EDGE_DEBOUNCE_S`. Null control: the running row of the round-5 check, the compressor settled running at the write, books it kept through the same passes. `fresh` defaults to False and leaves every earlier call unchanged.
   The failing check, from applying the mutant to a `git archive` copy of this head and running the section:
   ```
     FAIL through duty_switch.note_mode_write, a mode write on a record just loaded whose first reading, 50 Hz, came inside the debounce before the write and is still pending opens nothing and books noth
   1 of 59 DUTY-SWITCH SECTION CHECKS FAILED
   ```
   The reviewer's command, `python3 tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --spec <spec> --cmd 'env PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_duty_switch_section.py'`, with each of the verdict's two round-7 specs read from `probe/rev-3461-ba74baae` (`ev/reviewer_mutant_spec_round7.json`, `ev/reviewer_mutant_spec_round7b.json`), at the repair commit, before the merge:

2. The whole-branch diff pass, run by this seat before the handoff, found one survivor beyond the three recorded: `duty_switch.py:396 STMT_DEL`, the alias `Reader = Callable[...]` deleted, an operator `mutant_run.py` gained on main since the last body. The check "the reader's annotations resolve, as Python 3.13 resolves the arbiter's at import" resolves `_running_signal`'s and `attach`'s annotations with `typing.get_type_hints` and asserts they name one reader type; null control, a seam annotated with a name no module binds does not resolve. Under the mutant (spec entry `r8f_reader_alias_deleted`), in a `git archive` copy:

   ```
3. The merge of `origin/main` 6e100ef6 broke the section on a line git reported nowhere: main's 4498df97 has `pump_arbiter._dhw_write` read `params.dhw_max_temp` and gave main's fakes the field, and this branch's `_DsArb` fake lacked it (`AttributeError` in the section). The fake now carries `dhw_max_temp=60.0`, above the 50 C set-point the censor check writes; a limit equal to the 48 C set-point, as main's fakes carry, capped that write away and failed the censor check. The diff pass at the merge is how it was found, refusing on its baseline.
4. Findings: the fence of the body's `## Mutant spec` opens `json` again; the round count is the seventh review, answered by this repair; no finder harness exists, as in rounds 1 to 6.

- n10: the heated gate is per direction (`duty_switch._heated`): inlet minus water set-point into space (round 2: only where the set-point is a water temperature), the source leg's age into hot water; the table's three kept rows pin it with an inlet under the set-point. - n13: `DutySwitchLearner`, `Direction` and `SwitchContext` take no Home Assistant object; the tests drive them directly.
- n14: one call, `duty_switch.starts_attributes`, returns the finished dict; the check the note asks for found the opposite of what the design assumed: the five `coord_*` fixtures do hold that sensor's attributes. See the conditional publication above.

`7336628bcbdcc661765275544bba49f646e8a5b6` merges main `6e100ef` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

merges.body:
R10-OUTSIDE-DISINFECTION-SETPOINT part 2, the round-down ruling (`dev/programme/triage/s6-batch226.md#P681`, ruling (1)): the no-cycle hot-water write never exceeds the charge limit `dhw_max_temp`, and the set-point repair's Fix never exceeds the hard maximum its row is judged against. Carry 0 (#3452's no-cycle ceiling item 7052beca) and Carry 2 (that ruling) are built here; Carry 1 (#3452's credit-threshold item 9ac8c410) moved to R10-DISINFECTION-STEP-NOTICE, which owns the ruling on `dhw_hard_max_temp`.

The no-cycle hot-water write (`pump_arbiter._dhw_write`) rounded an off-step everyday set-point to the nearest step, so it could hold the tank above the user's own charge limit for good (everyday 58, step 5: 60). It now goes through `_bounded`'s existing ceiling, `hi=` the parameters' `dhw_max_temp`, which `quantise_setpoint_c` rounds down onto the entity's step in the entity's own unit: no second statement of the cap. The ceiling is the charge limit, not `dhw_hard_max_temp`, which rises to the disinfection temperature while the cycle is enabled and not running (mutant M14 below).

Class seam, the set-point repair (`setpoint_check._dhw`): its Fix rounded the floor up with no ceiling (offstep install, disinfection 60.3, step 1: Fix 61 against a hard maximum of 60.3, which the arbiter writes back as 60, so the notice stood for good on an install whose arbiter writes nothing but whose user pressed Fix). The floor is now quantised once, up onto the step and never above `dhw_hard_max_temp` (`quantise_setpoint_c`'s `hi_c`, rounded down), and the reading is judged against that quantised floor, so a Fix never exceeds the ceiling its row is judged against and a pump at that step raises nothing. An on-step floor at or below the ceiling is unchanged: rounding up only moves an off-step floor, and a reading on the step at or above the floor is at or above its step-up.

A ceiling can now sit under the entity's own minimum (`tests/features.py`'s L2 row: everyday 3 °C on a climate entity whose minimum is 44.6 °F), where `quantise_setpoint_c` applies `hi_c` last and would write below the range the entity accepts. `_bounded`'s contract is a value inside the entity's range, so a caller's ceiling under the entity's minimum rounded up onto its step is dropped (the `hi` test in `_bounded`) and that minimum is written, as at the base (45 °F there). Two earlier forms were refused by their own checks and replaced: clamping the ceiling to the minimum (`4498df97`) rounded an off-step minimum down, under the range (44 °F, the L2 check); comparing the ceiling with the raw minimum (`ec29e0dd`) kept a ceiling between an off-step minimum and its step-up and rounded it under the range (30.6 over a 30.4 minimum, step 1: 30; mutant M20).

The ruling's `lo=` (the write at or above `dhw_min_temp` plus `DHW_MIN_TEMP_SETPOINT_MARGIN`) is not added: it cannot change any write. With `hi=` the everyday set-point (`dhw_max_temp` is `min(70, dhw_setpoint)`) and the value the everyday set-point, the nearest step is at or above the step-down of `hi`; where the step-up of `lo` is at or below the step-down of `hi`, the `max` with it is therefore a no-op, and where it is above, `quantise_setpoint_c` applies `hi_c` last and the ceiling wins. A `lo=` would be an always-surviving mutant. The ruling's alternative, reporting the rows where the two bounds leave no step, is taken: the harness's `below_floor` field (`## Figures`).

Alternatives not taken: `rounding="down"` with no `hi=` (a second statement of the cap that `dhw_max_temp` owns, and it would not hold a set-point above 70 at 70); `hi=dhw_hard_max_temp` (mutant M14: survives a census keyed on the hard maximum with the cycle disabled, counts 64 of the 104 rows with it enabled); for the repair, extending `dhw_gated` alone (covers an arbiter install, where the arbiter's own write is already excused, but not the Fix value above the ceiling on an install the arbiter does not write).

## Head

`4391a6c8d89445c5b6e543628ac5b01a7d170374` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3497.md`. The authored code head is `c5b48730d9063440e8df53a5a14928d9e96f0078`.

`4d4d71488f557a2d9d0b979d423b83cca09cf94f` merges origin/main `dca53dc6ff` into the authored code head `c5b48730d9063440e8df53a5a14928d9e96f0078` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below).

c5b48730d9063440e8df53a5a14928d9e96f0078 (the authored head 43095bdec3bba091bfe1a5a38abf172987e7ceb8 merged with origin/main 7617c7cf4a, conflict-free, review_carry.py CARRY), seven authored commits on origin/main ef579d9ba689 (`c9258994` the failing checks, `20d22eae` the fix with the harness and runner, `05a56e58` M11 retired, `4498df97` the entity-minimum clamp in `_bounded` and the test fakes, `ec29e0dd` that clamp replaced by dropping a ceiling under the minimum, `4342f022` the minimum taken on its step and the diff's survivors killed, `43095bde` the repair's redundant guard dropped and the killed sites pinned); merge base ef579d9ba689dcb48b0d4aa95222f1ce83d99c2d, origin/main's tip at 2026-11-12T03:33:29Z (`date -u`).

## Mutation proof

`python3 tools/audit/seat/r10_disinfection_setpoint_mutants.py` (each mutant applied to a detached worktree of HEAD, `tests/block_duty.py` run there; exit 0 only when NULL survives and every other mutant is killed), at 43095bde (exit 0), and at 20d22eae for M11:

- `M14-limit-hard-max` (the no-cycle `hi=` set to `dhw_hard_max_temp`), `M15-limit-dropped` (`hi=` dropped: main's nearest step), `M16-limit-round-up` (`rounding="up"` in place of `hi=`): killed by "no no-cycle write exceeds the charge limit (dhw_max_temp), the cycle enabled and not running or disabled, ..." and "an off-step everyday set-point is written on the step at or below it, never rounded up ...".
- `M17-fix-uncapped` (`setpoint_check._dhw`: `hi_c` dropped, #2805's uncapped round-up) and `M18-active-raw-floor` (the reading judged against the unquantised floor): killed by "the hot-water repair's Fix never exceeds the tank's hard maximum it is judged against, ...".
- `M19-ceiling-under-min` (`_bounded`'s ceiling kept under the entity's minimum) and `M20-ceiling-under-raw-min` (compared with the raw minimum, not its step-up): killed by "a charge limit below the entity's minimum writes the entity's minimum, never a value it refuses" (that check also holds at the base, where no ceiling reached under the minimum).
- `prepr.sh`'s diff mutants (`MUTANT_CMD="python3 tests/block_duty.py"`) at ec29e0dd left three survivors, each now killed or removed: `pump_arbiter.py` `_bounded` CMP_BOUND (`>=` to `>`; killed by the same check's 72 °C everyday on a 70 °C minimum, whose ceiling sits exactly on the minimum's step); `setpoint_check.py` `_dhw` CMP_BOUND (`<` to `<=`; killed by a reading exactly one `MIXING_VALVE_WRITE_EPSILON` under the floor, in "the hot-water repair's Fix never exceeds ..."); `setpoint_check.py` CONST_SWAP on the Fix value's `round(..., 6)`, a line this diff no longer changes (the name `on_step_c` is kept).
- M1-M10, M12, M13 of part 1: killed as before.
- `M11-everyday-cycle-nearest` (route a cycle at or below the everyday set-point through the no-cycle return) SURVIVED at 20d22eae and is retired in `05a56e58` as equivalent: on those rows `dhw_cycle_temp` is the everyday set-point, so `dhw_hard_max_temp` equals `dhw_max_temp` and both returns are the same `_bounded` call.

Failing first: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/block_duty.py` at c9258994 (origin/main's production code) prints `4 of 69 BLOCK DUTY CHECKS FAILED`: the three checks above and part 1's "an everyday set-point the nearest step rounds up is held below it on a cycle ...", whose everyday-step conjunct pinned main's nearest write (58 on step 5: 60) and now asserts 55. At 20d22eae: `ALL 69 BLOCK DUTY CHECKS PASSED`.

## Null control

`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_disinfection_setpoint.py` (this PR, sha1 6ced0aeb71d5fc00734eaf4098e65e5e665891e8) copied over a worktree of origin/main ef579d9b and run there and at 20d22eae (both outputs byte-identical at 43095bde: `cmp`), default mode and `--grid` (2340 lines: arms `held`, `idle`, `disabled` x 5 steps x 12 everyday set-points x 13 disinfection temperatures):

Carry 1 (the brief's Carry 0, MUTVAC-STMT-DEL) is implemented here as STMT_DEL, after the fork cap.

Carry 2 is the acceptance carry (item 803fdcf8, below) has landed on the group's roster entry at roster commit c25798dfec (origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster, dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json).

mutant_run.py bounds the command's process tree and gains a STMT_DEL operator (P604 FORKCAP; carry P607 STMT_DEL). The command's family is polled every 0.5 s and SIGKILLed whole past `--fork-cap` (default 256) processes, and again at the command's exit, on timeout and on a signal; the outcome is `FORKCAP`, never KILLED, since a cap stop proves no test pins the mutant. Family is four legs: the command's session, its process group, every process carrying the run's `MUTANT_RUN_TOKEN` environment mark, and every descendant of the driver, which sets `PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER` for the command's lifetime (restored after) so an orphan reparents to it rather than to init. The ppid leg is the one no descendant can leave: setsid, setpgid, a cleared environment and an exited parent all keep a process under the subreaper. Children the driver had before the command are excluded; reparented orphans that die are reaped each poll, and zombies are not counted. Diff mode's STMT_DEL replaces each simple statement an added line falls in with `pass` (compile-checked, deduped against CALL_DEL/RETURN_DEL). No reproduction ran an unbounded self-test; all runs were under `ulimit -u` in a subshell with a timeout.

Alternatives: an RLIMIT_NPROC soft limit lost (not enforced for root, counts the whole user, and a fork failure would read as KILLED rather than FORKCAP). A per-command cgroup lost to the subreaper: it needs a writable, delegated cgroup v2 hierarchy, which a seat container does not guarantee, while prctl needs no privilege. A FORKCAP diff run exits 1 (0 under --report-only); survivor_list.py reads only SURVIVED lines, and its pinned producer strings are unchanged.

Fix review: blocked d68d307421b117a807b0734ccea1e9d57f8b09b6 class-open: fork cap misses descendants that leave the process group (counted, never killed) or the session (never counted)

bus-nonce: 6b2ac7fd24492517b506aa24d3a707d6

Round 1. Handoff review from a detached worktree at the handoff tip d68d307421b117a807b0734ccea1e9d57f8b09b6 (`ev/HEAD.txt`), merge base ee64358be7eeccaec5178a923cb3b83a18a924a0.

## Block

- Process-group escape: the cap counts the whole session (`session_pids`, by `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 6), but the FORKCAP branch kills only the leader's process group (`_killpg` -> `os.killpg(p.pid, SIGKILL)`). A descendant that calls `setpgid` stays in the session, so it counts toward the cap, and survives the kill. `ev/escape_test.txt` chainB: a 150-deep chain whose levels call `os.setpgid(0,0)`, `--fork-cap 32`. It reports `FORKCAP m` in 3 s, then leaves 38 processes running, and 83 three seconds later, still forking. This breaks the brief's acceptance ("leaves no process of its session") and the docstring's "SIGKILLed whole". The fix is to SIGKILL every pid `session_pids` returns, repeating until the list is empty, plus a self-test chain that changes its group.

Anchor `tests/harness.py` to its own tree so a harness run from another root no longer measures the cwd's tree (Carry 3, R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED item 6d58568e), and settle the cloud-seat environment carries. Topic r10-suite-env-residue.

## Head

`a050364ac19472a1572c12aa5e9b977b17bc6f83` merges main `0b276e8` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`3861ae76214c26900658bfa52c91d880fe8865a1` merges the authored code head `7215e37c7136142c6d6c479babf462c8f69ac569`.

7215e37c7136142c6d6c479babf462c8f69ac569 (code head of this branch), measured on origin/main a7628041dc02e298c5399003d4c0576391dd5c4e (merged in by 628e9d3058, a clean merge), 2026-11-11T06:57Z.

## Mutation proof

Carry 3. The production change: `tests/harness.py` anchors its two `sys.path` inserts and its translations listing to `_ROOT`. The pins are in `tests/harness_headers.py`. They run `import harness, heatpump_optimizer, profiles` from a decoy cwd that holds `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/__init__.py` and `tests/profiles.py`. `dev/audit/harnesses/learner_inputs_swap.py` imports `profiles` straight after `harness`, which is why the decoy holds that module. Three checks pin the change:

- (P1) `tests/harness.py from a foreign cwd finds its catalogues and its own tree's package`: `heatpump_optimizer.__file__` is under this tree's `custom_components`.
- (P2) `tests/harness.py from a foreign cwd resolves a module the cwd's tests/ also holds to its own tests/`: `profiles.__file__` is under this tree's `tests`.
- (P3) `tests/harness.py's sys.path inserts are exactly its own tests/ and custom_components/, absolute`: the entries `import harness` adds to `sys.path` are exactly those two absolute paths.

So each insert is pinned on its own, twice. The `tests` insert is pinned by P2 and P3, and the `custom_components` insert by P1 and P3.

The reviewer's own mutants are taken verbatim from `origin/probe/rev-3431-677c1ae0:ev/mutant-*.diff`. Each is applied with `git apply` to a `git archive` copy of 8933c424. Its `tests/harness.py` and `tests/harness_headers.py` are byte-identical at the head: `git diff --stat 8933c424 7215e37c` lists only `tests/arch_score.py`. Each copy is git-initialised before the apply so that the register-status check reads a repository. Each copy is run as `PYTHONPATH=<copy>/tests/hastub python3 <copy>/tests/harness_headers.py`, once with cwd = the copy's root and once with cwd = a directory outside it:

| mutant | cwd = copy root | cwd = outside | failing checks | vs the d710f5dd verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| null (unmutated head) | `ALL 115 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED` | `ALL 115 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED` | none | null still survives |
| M1a (`tests` insert alone back to `"tests"`) | `2 of 115 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED` | `2 of 115 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED` | P2, P3 (`added=['<copy>/custom_components', 'tests']`) | **changed**: survived (113 of 113) and is now killed |
| M1b (`custom_components` insert alone) | `2 of 115 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED` | `2 of 115 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED` | P1, P3 | unchanged: killed |
| M1 (both inserts reverted) | `3 of 115 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED` | `3 of 115 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED` | P1, P2, P3 | unchanged: killed |
| M3 (`tests/harness.py` at the merge base) | `3 of 115 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED` | no result line: `import harness` raises `FileNotFoundError: ... 'custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/translations'`, rc=1 | P1, P2, P3 at the root | unchanged: killed |

Every mutant changes the production line in `tests/harness.py`; `tests/harness_headers.py` is the same file in every row. A first pass ran from plain `git archive` copies with no `.git`. There, every row, the null included, also failed `the executed harnesses leave their committed output byte-identical` (`git status failed rc=128`). That is the runner, not the mutant (fixer step 2), and the git-initialised re-run above removes it.

`mutant_run.py --diff` is not pin evidence here: it skips `tests/`, and this PR changes only `tests/` and one seat script.

## Null control

- The check pins the defect, not the decoy. With the head tree, P1 to P3 pass from the decoy cwd (the null row above). With the base `tests/harness.py` (M3), the same import from a foreign cwd raises `FileNotFoundError`.
- The finder's harness at both ends. `learner_inputs_swap.py`'s pattern is `sys.path[:0] = [T/tests/hastub, T/custom_components, T/tests]`, then `import harness`, then `profiles`. I ran it with cwd = a `git archive` export of the merge base 40fe1cae2e:
  - T = head copy (8933c424): `profiles <T-head>/tests/profiles.py`.
  - T = M1a copy: `profiles <base-export>/tests/profiles.py`. That is the cwd's tree, the defect of item 6d58568e.
  - `heatpump_optimizer` resolves to T in both runs.
  - The capture is a scratch probe that reuses the finder's sys.path lines. No finder's harness is committed for 6d58568e.

## Figures

- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/harness_headers.py` at 8933c424 in the worktree: `ALL 115 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED` (instrument: that script; scope: its 115 checks, which are the 113 of d710f5dd plus P2 and P3).
- Scoped gate: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff a7628041dc` printed `MODE: SCOPED -- 21 script(s) run, 12 scoped out` at 8933c424. `GATE_SCOPE=auto PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub bash tests/run.sh` reported `ok` for every script it reached. It stalled in `tests/arch_score.py` and was stopped at the 30-minute background limit before `harness_headers.py` and `stress.py` ran in it. `harness_headers.py` passes separately (above), `tests/arch_score_head.py` alone prints `ALL 18 ARCHITECTURE SCORE HEAD CHECKS PASSED`, and `tests/arch_score.py` is the Carry 6 fix below. `tests/stress.py` is left to CI's required run.
- Structure ratchet: `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`; no metric moved up.
- Seam enumeration for the cwd-capture class: `git grep -l 'from harness import\|import harness' -- dev/audit/harnesses/ | xargs grep -l sys.path`, less `git grep -l os.chdir -- dev/audit/harnesses/`. Every file it lists imports `tests/harness.py`. P3 now pins that the shared module's inserts are absolute and inside its own tree, so the class is closed at the shared module, not per harness. A harness that inserts its own relative `sys.path` entries for other modules (e.g. `cop_duty_floor.py` inserts `tests`) is its own seam and is not changed here. Carry: dismissed: those inserts resolve a harness the caller already placed in the intended root, and the shared module no longer captures the cwd.

## Red checks

- `governance / policy-docs` (run 43176982649, job 131044069880, failure at 07:49Z at the earlier commit 3861ae76 of this branch): the job's field-coverage step graded a head that lacked main with main's pinned `field_coverage.mjs` and refused (`DEAD registry: DECLARED pinned tools/pr/figure_block.py is no longer in the derived set`; `REFUSED replay_cuts: ... module 'replay' has no attribute 'COST_CUTS'`). It is green at head a050364a (job 131063576099, 08:36Z) after main was merged in. No cheaper detector exists than re-merging main; this is the stale-base class, and a proposal is recorded for round 11.
- `tests / fast (3.14)` (check run 130474184553, failure at 11:05:07Z at this head): inherited from main, not this diff's. The one failing check is `tests/features.py`'s `combi_type_branch census` (`1 of 5237 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`), whose vendor hits are in const.py, heat_curve.py, pump_arbiter.py and thermal_model.py; this PR's three-dot diff touches none of them and nothing under `custom_components/`. Main has been red on that census since #3398 and its hotfix (r10-hotfix-combi-census-main-red) is in flight. A re-run of `tests / fast (3.14)` at this head (130501374703) concluded success at 12:37:52Z. The cheaper detector is `python3 tests/features.py` on main, already run by the gate; none is owed beyond the hotfix.
- `policy_lint` budgets (`tests/entities.py` D11-05 arm), from an earlier round: an intermediate commit added a note to `.claude/workflows/web-fragments.md` and then to `tests/README.md`. Both are at zero token headroom. With the note removed, `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs` prints TOTAL: 0 error(s). The cheaper detector is that same command, already in `prepr.sh`; its standing cost is nil.
- `tests/arch_score.py` failed in this seat at 8933c424 (`1 of 279 ARCHITECTURE SCORE CHECKS FAILED`, on `arch-score.yml: a head edit to tests/structure.py is not what the gate loads (the #2068 plant)`: `fatal: '/opt/hpo/runner-temp/base' already exists`), and `prepr.sh` refused `closures` on it. It is not a required check, and it went red in no CI run of this branch. It is fixed in this PR, not answered as residue: see Carry 6. The cheaper detector is that script itself run twice in a seat, which `prepr.sh`'s closures step already does; its standing cost is nil. Carry: dismissed: fixed here (Carry 6).

## Forward-carry

- Carry 4 (cloud-setup venv-ha lacks scipy and paho): the header of `tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh` now states that venv-ha is typing-only by design, and that the suites run under venv-ci with `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`. Measured: under venv-ci with the stub, `import harness` succeeds from a foreign cwd. Adding paho or scipy to venv-ha would need a new hash-pinned lock entry, which the typing lock does not carry; not built. Carry: dismissed: premise stale, venv-ha is not a suite interpreter.
- Carry 2 (no-`pr` dispatch form for a CI-cost hotfix): `.claude/workflows/web-fragments.md` and `tests/README.md` are both at their token caps (`node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --budgets`). The one sentence has no home without a cap raise or a payment. Carry: dismissed: needs an owner ruling on a cap raise; the fact is `ci.yml` `workflow_dispatch` with `-f base=<ref>` and no `pr` input.
- Carry 1 (nightly heartbeat respawn): not buildable here. The measurement recipe needs `gh run list --workflow nightly.yml`, which is unavailable in this seat. The brief's own rule closes the group as superseded unless `hb:positive_control` goes red at a main that carries the unwinder fix. Carry: dismissed: no red measured; `tests/nightly_ha.py` already samples with `_remote_debugging` where it exists.
- Carry 5 (stress memory-peak precondition, traced bump on 3.14): addresses a group whose roster stage is done, and it is not this group's seam. Carry: dismissed: no destination is live. The precondition stays in the carry text of the brief: re-measure base beside head on one box before reading a 3.14 stress memory red.
- Carry 6 (cloud prepr.sh environment faults, item ec93383a): one fault reproduced on this seat, and it is fixed here.

merges.title: R10-OUTSIDE-DHW-CHARGE-SETTLE: r10 outside dhw charge settle
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-OUTSIDE-DHW-CHARGE-SETTLE: the build of outside pull request #3434 by @Bankaifan, whose commit opens this branch with its authorship kept. A DHW charge start drops the tank reading 3-5 K within minutes. Main books that dip as a draw on the heated interval in the draw statistics, and as usage on the unheated intervals after a short charge. Both inflate the heavy-day p90 that the planner reads through `DrawStats.quantile`.

Repair round 3. Review blocked `8fe714779` as regression-unmeasured. At the learner's production cadence, the take-back erased real draw. The learner runs once per coordinator refresh, `optimization_interval`: 30 min by default, 10-120 min in 5-min steps. Every harness arm and test sampled at 5 min. The cause: the interval that *ends* at the first heated sample was folded as charge energy. At a 10-120 min refresh that interval holds the draw made before the charge. A later dip recovery then took that draw back.

The fix rests on one physical fact: the dip recovers once the charge stops, and a draw does not. In `dhw_learning.py`, `ChargeSettle` (in memory) holds the open charge's transient:
- **Draw statistics.** `ChargeSettle.classify` now returns the interval's class. Only an interval that *started* on a heated sample, or ends within `DHW_CHARGE_SETTLE_HOURS` of the last heated sample (settling), is folded as charge energy (`DrawStats.fold(..., charge=True)`). The plan's flag marks the charge no earlier than its slot, so an interval ending at the first heated sample holds the pre-charge draw. It is folded as plain draw, which no take-back reaches. A later unheated rise takes back what it recovered (`DrawStats.take_back`). Two caps bound it: the charge-folded energy left in the open occurrence, and `DHW_CHARGE_DIP_MAX_K` (5 K) per charge.
- **Usage learner.** A settle interval's drop is deferred instead of skipped. Later unheated rises cut it. The first unheated interval past the window that does not rise closes the charge and learns what is left. This part is unchanged this round.
- **Cooling learner.** Gated as on main, on a heated interval (starts or ends heated).
- **Restore refactor.** The author's `_restore_daytypes` fold of the two duplicated restore loops stays. `apply_payload` takes an overflowing day count as zero, as the loader does.

Design choices a reviewer may read as bugs:
- A heated rise is never credited, because it is charge heat. So a dip that recovers while the charge still heats stays booked, as on main.
- A draw that overlaps the recovery hides the rise, so the phantom stays as on main (draw-0745 dip, below).
- A restart forgets the open charge, so that charge is booked as on main. A take-back only reaches the occurrence still open.
- A real draw *during* a charge is folded as charge energy, and a later dip recovery can take it back. The charge heat that hid part of the dip makes the recovery larger than the dip the charge folded. This is measured below (5-min draw-0735: −0.30, against main's +0.39). At every production cadence, 10 to 60 min, no dip cell reads further from its truth arm than main.
- At 10, 15 and 60 min the fix removes none of main's phantom (N equals B in every dip cell). There the dip lands inside a heated interval, or past a settle window shorter than the refresh. The gain at production cadence is the 30-min draw-0735 and draw-0745 cells, +0.23 to +0.01. Every other production cell reads as main.

Alternatives considered:
- (a) Fold the drop only where it exceeds the dip bound: this costs every real draw near a charge up to 5 K.
- (b) Lengthen `DHW_CHARGE_SETTLE_HOURS` to the refresh interval, so the settle window catches the dip at 30-60 min: that widens the window that defers real usage. With no production trace at those cadences, I did not measure it and did not take it.
- (c) Persist `ChargeSettle`: a store field for one transient per restart.

## Head

`8da2a871a48ae728a571bd2f63eac18fb6d73f3b` merges main `4f3b94f` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`c68aec3a7a9a568cfc95a72c0f33f3358366f7e9` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

Code head `c68aec3a7a9a568cfc95a72c0f33f3358366f7e9`, on merge base `ef579d9ba689dcb48b0d4aa95222f1ce83d99c2d` (`origin/main`, which this head merges). It is the `merge-main` bot's merge of `origin/main` into `7236c8a2c`, the head that holds the merge verdict; `7236c8a2c` merges `9b5c699a4` (the earlier handoff, whose history is unchanged) into the PR branch. The bot's merge conflicted in `tests/structure_budgets.json` only, on the `class_excess_loc` row. Its resolution was measured on the merged tree: `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `class_excess_loc = 17529` and `ok   class_excess_loc 17529 <= 17529`. Main's own row is 17531 and this branch's is 17532. From their common base `6d16af36c` (17534), the branch paid 2 and main paid 3, and the merged measurement is the sum. The merged row is below main's, so no budget was raised. Against `origin/main`, `git diff origin/main HEAD -- tests/structure_budgets.json` changes that row alone. Main's delta since `7236c8a2c` (`git diff --stat 7236c8a2c HEAD -- custom_components`) touches neither `dhw_learning.py` nor `dhw_draws.py`, nor the harness, so the fix and its figures are unchanged since `d6564e1ea`, where they were measured.

## Mutation proof

Failing test first. Two checks were added to the block: `at the learner's production cadences a charge-start dip's recovery takes back no draw made before the charge` (10, 15 and 30 min) and `a charge's take-back stops at the energy its charge folded and at the dip bound`. The same block CMD (below) was run with the rest of the head and with three versions of `dhw_learning.py`/`dhw_draws.py`. Values are cadence: (dip open kWh, truth with no dip, no DHW charge on record):

```
