Main fails because it keeps the phantom, and the old head fails because it erases the draw. The second check fails at main on both arms (`esc` 0.9148 against 0.689, `cap3` 1.849 against 0.6825). Fix review: blocked 8fe714779710e5f56c6eb353ab8b2cea00fcaddd regression-unmeasured: at the learner's production cadence the take-back erases real draw (15-min p90 1.8777 to 0.9868 kWh, 30-min sequence 0.6542 to 0.3847 kWh), unmeasured because every harness arm and test samples at 5 min

bus-nonce: 1be12d5d56ad938d69920390d5a4f45c

## Block

Round 2. The delta against `8e2b7d99` (the authored handoff `b6696bd6`, plus a main merge and a bot pin commit) rewrites `dhw_learning.py` and `dhw_draws.py`, so this review covers that production code in full.

The round-1 regression is held: every truth arm (no dip) is identical between base and head. That holds in the fixer's harness at 5 min, and in my probes at 5, 10, 15, 30 and 60 min. The repair still introduces a new regression of the same kind (real draw removed from the heavy-day p90). The body never measured it, because nothing in the PR runs at a cadence production can use.

- **Cadence.** `async_learn_dynamics` runs once per coordinator refresh: `update_interval=timedelta(minutes=config.optimization_interval)` at `coordinator.py:3546-3548`, default `DEFAULT_OPTIMIZATION_INTERVAL = 30` (`const.py:1632`). The options flow allows 10 to 120 min in 5-min steps (`config_flow.py:1854`). The fixer's harness (`STEP_MIN = 5`) and every `_chg_seq` case in `tests/features.py` (5 min apart) sample faster than any configurable interval. At the 30-min default, `DHW_CHARGE_SETTLE_HOURS = 0.25` can never mark an interval as settling.
- **Mechanism.** The interval that *ends* at the first heated sample is flagged as charge (`heated_interval = self.heating_since_sample or heating`). So a draw made before the charge starts is folded as charge-folded energy. The heated interval's own charge heat also hides part of the dip, so the later unheated rise (the full dip recovering) is larger than the dip energy that was folded. `take_back` then removes the difference from real draw. This contradicts the body's claim that the take-back can erase "never draw folded outside the charge".
- **Minimal sequence, 30 min apart (the default).** Script `ev/seq30.py`, output `ev/seq30.txt`. Readings 07:00 50.0, 07:30 47.0 (plan flag on, a 3 K draw before the charge), 08:00 44.0 (charge heat +1 under a 4 K dip), 08:30 48.0, 09:00 48.0. Open occurrence:

  | arm | base `ee64358b` | head |
  |---|---|---|
  | truth (no dip) | 0.6542 | 0.6542 |
  | dip | 1.3127 | **0.3847** |
  | no-charge control (flag never set) | 1.3127 | 1.3127 |

  The head removes the 0.66 kWh phantom and 0.27 kWh (41 %) of the real draw on top.
- **Simulation.** Script `ev/cadence.py`, output `ev/cadence_{base,head}.txt`, moved cells in `ev/cadence_moved.txt`. Per-minute tank physics, the learner sampled every 10/15/30/60 min, charges of 10, 40 and 15 min, draws at six offsets, 14 days. At 15 min (a configurable setting), a 07:30 10-min charge with a draw starting 10 min before it reads:
  - truth 1.8777;
  - dip arm at base 1.8753 (error −0.002);
  - dip arm at head **0.9868** (−0.89, −47 %).

  At the 30-min default the head moves four dip cells: two improve (+0.23 to +0.015) and two newly under-count (0.000 to −0.19). At 10 and 60 min the head equals the base in every dip cell. So at those cadences the fix removes none of the phantom it was written for: at 10 min, offset +5, the dip arm reads 2.6261 at both ends against truth 2.1156.
- **What the repair owes.** At least the 30-min default and the 10-min floor, in the harness and in a features case:
  - a draw ending in the interval that closes at the first heated sample, beside a dip;
  - a take-back that cannot exceed the energy the charge's dip actually folded;
  - the gain at production cadence stated against these losses.

  Five-minute arms are not production evidence. They may stay as a sub-cadence check, but the body must say so.
- **Mutation survivors (`--spec`, my own mutants).** Two of the three survivors below change the booked energy. Both target a claim the body makes. `ev/mutants_r2.txt` is the block command at the head. The concrete sequences are `ev/seq.py`, with output in `ev/seq_survivors_head.txt` and `ev/seq_survivor_{esc,cred}.txt`.

  | mutant | edit | head | mutant | control |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `R2_ESCROW_DEC_OFF` | `dhw_draws.py` `self._open_charge_kwh -= taken` → `pass` | 0.689 | 0.4633 | 0.689 |
  | `R2_CREDIT_PER_INTERVAL` | `dhw_learning.py` `if (heated_interval or settling) and not self.open:` → `if heated_interval or settling:` | 0.689 | 0.457 | 1.849 |

  - `R2_ESCROW_DEC_OFF`: the take-back escrow is never decremented. A 3 K pre-charge draw, a 1 K dip and two +1 K settle rises (sequence A) lose 0.226 kWh of the pre-charge draw under the mutant. This breaks "never draw folded outside the charge".
  - `R2_CREDIT_PER_INTERVAL`: the credit resets on every charge-affected interval. Sequence B (an 8 K drop, then three +3 K rises inside the settle window) takes back about 7 K under the mutant, past the per-charge `DHW_CHARGE_DIP_MAX_K` of 5 K the body states.
  - `R2_SETTLE_INCL_HEATED` (`return not heated_interval and (` → `return True and (`) is equivalent by reading. On a heated interval, `async_learn_usage(..., heated=True)` returns at its first guard, and `advance` returns before the pending branch.

  The wider-closure re-run of the three is reported under Evidence.

## Findings

- Residual: quantised sensor jitter (±0.1 K, rounded to 0.1) in a truth trace at 5-min cadence. A positive jitter inside the settle window takes back charge-folded draw. The p90 falls 5.2218 to 5.2085 at a draw 10 min before the charge and 5.155 to 5.1365 at a draw starting 2 min after it (−0.25 % and −0.36 %); every other jitter cell is B = N (`ev/probe_{base,head}.txt`). This is bounded by the jitter amplitude over at most three settle intervals, and it lies inside the cadence repair above. Carry: dismissed: 0.4 % at most, below the sensor resolution, and the regression-unmeasured block re-scopes the mechanism it rides on
- Out of scope: the body's second class enumerator (`git grep -n "async_learn_dynamics\|CONF_DHW_TEMP_ENTITY\|draw_stats.fold" -- custom_components/`) also returns `config_flow.py` (89, 543, 1409, 1444, 1683) and `const.py` (84, 297, 1858), which the body's disposition list does not name. Every hit is the entity key's definition, form field or staleness/plausibility table, not a consumption attribution, and no perturbation of these moves any harness figure. Carry: dismissed: void under judge.md (definitions only, no drop attribution); the body should name them next round

## Evidence

- Head reviewed: `8fe714779710e5f56c6eb353ab8b2cea00fcaddd` (`ev/HEAD.txt`). Merge base `ee64358be7eeccaec5178a923cb3b83a18a924a0`. Round 2 (delta against `8e2b7d99d0e99f3cbd00d49ceb9b4a1458b87257`).
- `review_carry.py 8e2b7d99 8fe71477` prints `FRESH-REVIEW`.
- `review_carry.py df632c8dd 8fe71477` prints `CARRY`. The body's `## Head` names `df632c8dd`, and the one commit past it is the bot's `ci: pin killed mutants` (a ledger file only). `review_packet.py` refused with `head-note` for the same reason.
- RESULT harness (the fixer's `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_dhw_charge_settle_p90.py`, sha1 `24cfb411cf98c620a321bc8a9e3d32cc7beb18e3`, run from the head's copy against the base and head trees; `ev/harness_{base,head}.txt`, side by side in `ev/harness_BvN.txt`): every B and N cell of the body's table re-derives except one. draw-0745 dip@max usage points read 81 at N against the body's 82; p90 5.3865 matches. The body measured on merge base `a7628041`, and main has moved since. Truth and flat arms are B = N in all six geometries and both rates.
- Harness provenance (step 9): this PR adds the harness, so the instrument is the builder's, not the finder's. No finder harness is named (packet: "Finder's harness: none named"). `ev/probe.py`, `ev/cadence.py`, `ev/seq.py` and `ev/seq30.py` are mine (reviewer-built) and not in the tree.
- RESULT probe (`ev/probe_{base,head}.txt`, 5/10-min cadence, draws at 07:20/07:32/07:40/07:45, ±0.1 K jitter on and off): noise-free truth cells are B = N. Note that a 1-min cadence is below the learner's `dt_h <= 0.02` floor and learns nothing at either end; those rows are void.
- RESULT cadence (`ev/cadence_BvN.txt`): all 72 truth cells are B = N; the dip cells that move are listed in `ev/cadence_moved.txt`.
- Mutants, the block command from the body at the head (`ev/mutants_r2.txt`): `SURVIVED NULL`; `KILLED` R2_FLUSH_AS_HEATED, R2_CHARGE_HEATED_ONLY, R2_TAKE_AFTER_FOLD, R2_CLOSE_KEEPS_PENDING; `SURVIVED` R2_ESCROW_DEC_OFF, R2_CREDIT_PER_INTERVAL, R2_SETTLE_INCL_HEATED.
- The three block survivors were re-run over a wider closure: `mutant_run.py --in-place` over `tests/entities.py`, `guard_pins.py`, `finite_boundary.py` and `features.py` in series (the scripts that kill this file's other ledger pins). The run refused at `KILLED NULL` (rc 3): one of those scripts is red on the unmutated head, which fits the inherited `tests / fast` red. So the survivors are established against the PR's own block command only. Whether another gate script kills them is not verified here; the concrete sequences above show they are not equivalent.
- The body's own 25 + 3 + 6 + 4 named mutants were not re-run. The body runs them through the same block command at `b5a0f877`, whose production files match the head.
- `python3 tests/structure.py` at the head: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`, `class_excess_loc = 17532`. The budget row reads 17534 → 17532 against the merge base `ee64358b`. The body's "17537 to 17535" was measured on the older base; the direction and size (−2) are the same.
- `VERSION`, `manifest.json` and the `RELEASE_NOTES.md` heading are untouched (`git diff ee64358b...HEAD` prints nothing). No golden or claim file is in the diff.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 8fe71477` exits 0 against origin/main `0a2139b1` (`ev/merge_tree.txt`).
- CI at this head, read live: `tests / mutation` failure (the body answers it under `## Red checks`); `tests / fast (3.14)` failure (the dispatch rules main's `tests / fast` census red inherited from main); `governance / instrument-self-tests` failure (outside `merge_train.py owed-reds`, so not this PR's). `merge_train.py classify` was still WAIT when this verdict was written (`ev/ci_classify.txt`). The block does not turn on CI.
- Class enumerator: the first grep returns `boost.py`, `climate.py`, `coordinator.py`, `dhw_learning.py`, `optimizer.py`, `payload.py` and `sensor.py`, all named in the body's dispositions.

- Finder-class harness at both ends, my cadence probe over 72 cells (10/15/30/60 min, 3 charges, 6 draw offsets): truth is identical to base in all 72. Dip cells that move against base: only step=15 charge 07:35+15 off+5 (truth 1.2527, base 1.594, head 1.1481), step=30 07:30+10 off+5 (truth 1.6087, base 1.84, head 1.6238) and off+15 (truth 1.9994, base 2.2303, head 2.0143); none is further from truth than base. merges.body: The product page (`docs/index.html`) rebuilt to the design note design/R10-PRODUCT-PAGE-REDESIGN at 2f56c2e6a9a2d280a1ab741ad768dec2d8ced89f: one illustrative day drawn by a generator (`tools/site/day_chart.mjs`) and pinned by `tests/doc_claims.py`, a scroll story over it, a first-week timeline, and a control-path chooser in place of the table. The note's acceptance list is `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_product_page.mjs`. The first fixer stopped on four points where the tree contradicted the note (BLOCKED.md at c7b0b4611d88, build 3bfb1990c83c); this head applies the orchestrator's rulings on them, given under mandate 6715477401. A fix review at 1a35b70dbf2c blocked on five note requirements the harness did not test; this head answers all five. ## Head `438d15f1926d713925c2b00f2fcbd0dcf20b5a72` merges the authored code head `fcc7f07e673a200cfbaf89b2a00fb28c0b18b749`. fcc7f07e673a200cfbaf89b2a00fb28c0b18b749: the blocked head 1a35b70dbf2c9225c7a2d946be27c5620e0322f1 plus three commits (d3f9e96d7, 38cb8e3fa, fcc7f07e6) that touch `docs/index.html` and `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_product_page.mjs` only. Its merge base with origin/main is 6cc15e9b8f53b5393bb4ed7297bfc12747d6e2f6. origin/main's tip at 2026-11-12T01:12:43Z is 47788534daffab7a199a132c5f2ca118951018dc; `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0 against it, so main was not merged in this round. Entries marked "this round" were taken at this head; the Rulings, and the entries that name 11c5dfb170be, d5afce01d6d9, dd31ed3599c8 or 45a5053c62cd, are as the reviewer re-derived them at 1a35b70dbf2c, and this round's diff touches none of the lines they mutate. ## Answer to the blocked verdict Verdict: `verdict.md` on probe/rev-3458-4454bc77 at d5998f40efbf8c4761184db5503ccc94dc320e7d, five design-note requirements with no check. Each now has a check in `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_product_page.mjs`; none is waived. Each row's proof is the mutation named, under Mutation proof; its null control is the unmutated run, `RESULT fails=0`. | item | check | proof (page mutation, check goes red) | |---|---|---| | 1 targets at least 40 px | `floor : every target outside a line of text is at least 40 px in both dimensions`, four widths, two themes, and again at two widths with the page's fonts refused | M1, M1b, M1c; and the blocked head's page itself | | 2 no scroll-driven animation | `10 no scroll-driven animation `: the progress line gone, and every other element's display and box identical | M2a, M2b | | 3 reads in order with styles off | `floor styles off` | M3, M3b | | 4 keyboard reach and ring | `floor keyboard`: the Tab walk, and the operation by key | M4a, M4b | | 5 no relational selector | `10 no relational selector `, rendered; the source-text match is deleted | M5a, M5b | Item 1, the page gives way, not the note. The harness's rule over the blocked head's page returns the story link at 26 px, the header brand at 30, the eight section links at 37, the four footer links at 23, the coffee link at 38 and the HACS link at 22: the reviewer's instance and every other member of its class. All are raised in this diff: `min-height: 40px` on `.next` and `.brand`; the section links' block padding 7 px to 9 px; a `footer a` rule with 9 px of block padding; the coffee link's block padding 8 px to 11 px; `padding-block:11px` on the HACS link. `.next` therefore departs from the note's line 508 by that one declaration. ## Block

The merge train's object-page reads take their list key from the `key` argument (`--jq .<key>[]`). No merge_train check pins that key: the self-test stubs answer one JSON item per line whatever `--jq` the call carries. Each of these production mutants passes `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` with `611 checks, 0 failed`, rc 0:
- `Train.pages`: `gh_read.read_pages(self.run, path, key)` changed to `gh_read.read_pages(self.run, path)` (ev/mutant-pages-drop-key.txt)
- `_check_runs`: key `"check_runs"` changed to `"checkruns"` (ev/mutant-key-typos.txt)
- `bot_head`'s pull_request runs read: `"workflow_runs"` changed to `"workflow_run"`
- `_gate_busy`'s ci.yml runs read: `"workflow_runs"` changed to `"runs"`
- the infra re-run jobs read: `"jobs"` changed to `"job"`

These mutants are not equivalent. With the `_check_runs` typo, the finder's harness at this head, `merge_train.py classify 381b01147f24f36f474c443406b908028ca021f2 --pr 3427`, prints `REFUSE ci: the check runs at 381b01147f24 could not be read`, rc 2 (ev/mutant-checkruns-typo-live-classify.txt). That is the base's failure, the one this PR exists to fix. Only a live run of the classify harness catches it, and no committed check does. gh_read's own self-test does check the `--jq` expression, but only for `read_pages` called directly. The PR's merge_train mutant (`_check_runs` reverted to `--paginate`) is killed only by the `page=`/no-`--paginate` argv check, and that check ignores the key.

Remedy, kept to what the block needs: make the merge_train stubs (and queue_pre_flight's and orchestrator_tick's stubs for the paged reads) honour the call's `--jq`. For example, serve the object page `{"check_runs": [...]}` and refuse any `--jq` other than `.<expected key>[]`, as gh_read's `server` stub already does. Then re-run the five mutants above, and expect each to be killed.

merges.body:
R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE. Under a part-load derate, `_terminal_cost` and `_deferred_energy_cost` bought stored heat back at a COP with no draw. Both now buy it back through one law, `optimizer._refill_law`. The law is `thermal_model.refill_power_kwh`, the tree's own inverse (`power_for_heat_per_cop_kw`), applied with the heat spread evenly over the cheapest quarter of the horizon. Those are the hours the 25th-percentile refill price (`_refill_price`) is drawn from. The terminal and the deferred figure change together, as `_terminal_cost`'s docstring binds them. With no derate `_refill_law` is `None` and every figure is the linear one, bit for bit.

Decision (Carry 2's "price refill at a stated rate's derated heat, or segment the hot-water LP"): the stated rate. The LP segmentation was built, measured and refused: see `## Forward-carry`. The unattributed savings residual (Carry 1) is now attributed. It belongs to the booked reference, not to stored heat and not to COP.

Alternatives and why each lost:
- (a) The rate at max power: one figure for every deficit. It over-charges every refill a floor run would buy (the carried `at-max` bound).
- (b) The plan's own energy-weighted draw `P_r` (`r10_partload_residue.py refill`): unknown when `_terminal_cost` is built, before the plan exists, so the objective and the settlement could not share it.
- (c) Segmenting the hot-water LP: measured worse (`## Figures`).
The rate taken is a property of the deficit and the window, known to both twins at build time.

The brief's three carries:
- Carry 1 (the residual): attributed in `## Figures`; its fix is carried in `## Forward-carry`.
- Carry 2 (part-load refill pricing): built for `_terminal_cost` and `_deferred_energy_cost` together. The hot-water LP's secant was measured, and its segmentation refused and carried.
- Carry 3 (Carry 2's segmenting and refill-rate decision, and its zero-derate control): the decision is the paragraph above; the control is `## Null control` and the companion's `d = 0` rows.

Carries 4, 5 and 6 on the roster entry are this body's own `Carry: R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE` items, landed by the carry fold, not further work:
- Carry 4 is the merge-base residual in `## Figures` (-3.90 % flat, -8.02 % varying).
- Carry 5 is the residual's attribution in `## Forward-carry`.
- Carry 6 is the hot-water LP's secant in `## Forward-carry`.
- Carry 7, Carry 8 and Carry 9 are this body's own `## Figures` residual line and its two `## Forward-carry` items, folded back from #3442 verbatim. They repeat Carries 4, 5 and 6, so nothing further was done for them: Carry 7 is the merge-base residual (-3.90 % flat, -8.02 % varying), Carry 8 the residual's attribution, Carry 9 the hot-water LP's secant. The two Forward-carry items stay pending the orchestrator's ruling on their owner.

## Head

`ffd88ef8d2be28dc2a06def904ef5c1ae2cc3873` merges main `289c9b9` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`3655f1edfc1ced447acedc4252adf65e522222ef` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

611102f07624b45af9e434ec4359f6db3f8e5b14 (repair). It is `f1e49686bc911dff1a6e573c681524d4cbbcc792`, the PR head that merges round 2's 61241004, plus one commit: the `killed_by` row for `optimizer.py:2712 GUARD_OFF`. No production or test line changed. `origin/main` was at ee64358be on 2026-11-11 (UTC); `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflict, so main is not merged.

Round 2's head, 61241004989d6a432faf2e4d8523b8a2883439e8, is cut from 9394a652, round 1's head, with `origin/main` cbd23f1c8bf6185c3a6c10f6e4aaf562417e75bf merged in at 56a5572a.

That merge had one textual conflict, `tests/structure_budgets.json`'s `class_excess_loc`. The ledger merge driver resolved it (`17537 + both deltas = 17533`), and it was re-measured on the merged tree: `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `ok class_excess_loc 17533 <= 17533` and `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`. No cap was raised. VERSION, the manifest and RELEASE_NOTES are untouched (`prepr.sh` `no version edit` ok).

Base figures are at 32aea942, the branch's cut. Round-2 figures were re-taken at 61241004 on 2026-11-11 (UTC), with main at cbd23f1c.

## Round 2

Round 1's block (`Fix review: blocked 9394a652 mutation-vacuous`) named three gaps:
- The split buffer/building arm of `_terminal_row_cost` was unpinned: the `if refill is not None:` inside `if cop_buffer != cop_end:`.
- The 2723 `CLAMP_DROP` survivor had no triage.
- The `hours <= 0.0` arm of `refill_power_kwh`'s guard survived and had no triage.

What this round did:
- **Valved arm.** A new `tests/features.py` check, `R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE: on a valved install ...`.
  - The install is two-zone, with a `manual` valve, a 300 L tank and `cop_flow_carnot`. So `buffer_is_store` holds, and `cop_buffer` 1.4551 differs from `cop_end` 2.4500.
  - Both conditions are asserted as preconditions, read off `_terminal_row_cost`'s own arguments through a spy.
  - The check asserts that the derated terminal (`d = 0.2`) equals the law applied to the split linear figure, within 1e-9. The law is `power_for_heat_per_cop_kw` at the refill hours.
  - It also asserts that `_terminal_cost_batch`'s row equals the scalar at both derates.
  - Head readings: linear 65.425760, derated 81.782200, law 81.782200.
- **`refill_power_kwh`'s guard deleted, not triaged.**
  - `power_for_heat_per_cop_kw` already returns its input unchanged when `d == 0` or `band <= 0`, and `hours <= 0` makes `band <= 0`. So neither arm of the guard could change a result.
  - Both mutants survived even a direct contract check: the guard made `if False:`, and the `hours` arm dropped.
  - Deleting the guard removes both sites.
  - A third new check, `refill_power_kwh returns its input bit for bit ...`, pins the pass-through and the `copysign` that carries the sign. The pass-through is checked with no derate at either sign, and at `hours` 0 and -1.
- **Clamps triaged as equivalent.** The three sites are `optimizer.py` 2718, 2719 and 2723, all `CLAMP_DROP`.
  - Triage rows: `tests/mutation_ledger/survivor_triage/optimizer.py/_terminal_row_cost.row_cost.CLAMP_DROP.{374beae5,bce793a5,9e69f3b6}.json`, written by `mutation_table.row_text` at the inventory's own anchors.
  - `cop_end` is `compute_cop(...)`. `cop_buffer` is `marginal_cop(..., "buffer", ...)`, which is `compute_cop(..., flow_temp=...)`.
  - Both end in `_cop_law`'s `return max(cop, 1.0)`, so the 1e-6 floor never binds.

Alternative that lost: triaging `refill_power_kwh`'s two guard arms as equivalent. Deleting the guard won because it duplicated the inverse's own pass-through, and a triage on a deletable line keeps dead code (`fixer.md` step 17).

Class sweep. Rule: `git grep -n -E "_refill_law|_bought_back|refill_power_kwh|refill\(" -- custom_components/` enumerates every site that applies the law. Every site it returns, with its disposition:
- `optimizer.py:2713`: the split arm. Closed in this diff by the valved check (M7 below).
- `optimizer.py:2723`: the single-sum arm. Already guarded by round 1's check (round 1 M8).
- `optimizer.py:3081`: `_terminal_cost` builds the law both terminal arms receive. Already guarded (round 1 M2).
- `optimizer.py:5640`: `_deferred_energy_cost` applies the law once, to the total after the per-store COP corrections (`for store, ... in tanks`). It has no split arm. Already guarded (round 1 M1).
- `optimizer.py:2647` and `2655`: `_refill_law` and `_bought_back`, the law's definition and its one wrapper. Already guarded (round 1 M3, M4).
- `thermal_model.py:2601`: `refill_power_kwh` itself. Closed in this diff (guard deleted; contract check; M11 below).

The rule's other hits are `config_flow.py`'s `async_step_*_prefill`, which match on the name only.

## Mutation proof

Round 1, at 5c368ab. Each production line was neutralised in turn, the new `tests/features.py` check run (its block standalone), and the line restored. Each run printed FAIL `R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE: under a part-load derate the terminal cost and the deferred settlement ...`. The four mutants were: `_deferred_energy_cost`'s conversion made the identity (at the first commit, `electrical = refill(electrical)` to `pass`); `_terminal_cost` passing `None` for the law; `_refill_law`'s derate guard made always-`None`; and `refill_power_kwh` returning its input.

Round 2, at 61241004. The block was run standalone: `tests/features.py` from `# --- R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE` to the next block, under `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`. Each production line was neutralised in turn, then restored:
- M7, `optimizer.py:2712` `if refill is not None:` to `if False:`: FAIL `... on a valved install ...`.
- M11, `refill_power_kwh`'s `math.copysign(...)` to its bare first argument: FAIL `... under a part-load derate ...` and FAIL `... refill_power_kwh returns its input bit for bit ...`.
- M8b, the 2723 clamp `max(cop_end, 1e-6)` to `(cop_end)`: all three PASS. Equivalent; triaged in `## Round 2`.
- NULL, a comment line added inside `_terminal_row_cost`: all three PASS.

At the head all three PASS.

## Null control

At `d = 0` the companion harness reads every terminal, deferred and LP gap as 0, over 32 solves at both ends (`null rows not zero 0`). The check asserts `_refill_law` is `None` with no derate, and the valved check's `d = 0` figure is the split linear one, which its batch row equals. The base tree reads the defect: the same check FAILs at 32aea942, where the derated terminal equals the linear one.

Flat-price null (mandatory): the flat day's rows are printed beside the spread day's. The derated refill's move of the savings figure is the `predicted_savings` column of `r10_sav_valuation_residue.py` at both ends, apart from the stored-heat term. The residual attribution runs at `d = 0`, so it reads the same at both ends: no part-load term is in it.

## Figures

- **Carried figures**, re-measured at the merge base: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_partload_pricing.py`.
  - Flat `d=0.112`: lp_err max 0.267290 (dhw cost max 7.0145), terminal-at-max max 4.368455, deferred-at-max max 2.140129; `null rows not zero 0`.
  - The harness applies the linear rule's bound to the production figure. So at the head its terminal and deferred columns still print a bound: it measures what this fix replaces, and the companion below reads the defect.
- **Companion**, `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_valuation_residue.py`. It compares the production figure against `power_for_heat_per_cop_kw` at the refill hours, applied to the zero-derate figure.
  - Base 32aea942: spread `d=0.112` terminal gap max 3.150490, deferred gap max 0.440868; flat `d=0.112` terminal gap max 2.835283, deferred gap max 0.187447.
  - Head 5c368ab, and again at 0edaebae: all four 0.000000.
  - LP gap (left by this fix): spread 0.202595, flat 0.335995 at both ends.
  - `d=0` rows read 0 at both ends; `null rows not zero 0`, `failures 0`.
  - 7b60fb7 and 21f178bc change only `tests/`.
- **Companion, round 2**, at 61241004 (sha1 146c08d9faf2823f2779f01b68cf44f6f1b62648): `spread d=0.112 ... terminal gap max 0.000000 deferred gap max 0.000000`, and `flat d=0.112` the same; LP gap 0.202595 / 0.335995; `null rows not zero 0`, `failures 0`. Its 16 cells set no `cop_flow_carnot`, so none takes the split arm. The valved check in `## Round 2` is the split arm's reading.
- **Residual** at the merge base, `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_wood_reference.py valve-flat` and `valve-vary`: -3.90 % (flat), -8.02 % (varying). These arms run at `d = 0`, unchanged by this diff. It is attributed below; the finding is the first `## Forward-carry` item. Carry: R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE
- **Attribution** (carried in `## Forward-carry`), `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_residual_attribution.py flat` and `winter_typical`. Units are kWh_th over the arm's plant steps (`plant steps seen 192 of 192`).
  - Flat: the booked reference, stepped from its held state, draws -34.85 from its stores and loses +12.52 beyond the steady comfort term. Together that is -22.33 kWh_th, the residual.
  - Varying: -34.85 and +11.89.
  - The store term is price-independent; a reference at equilibrium reads 0 on it.
  - Ruled out first by a probe on the same loop: the buffer tank's standby loss, plan less held reference, is +0.07 kWh_e against the flat arm's -5.21 kWh_e gap.
- **LP segmentation, refused.** The hot-water LP was cut into four equal draw slices of the band, each step's energy priced at its slice's slope, and `r10_partload_pricing.py` run at that tree.
  - Every derated hot-water cell's published hot-water cost rose: flat 7.0145 to 7.8780, spread 8.0681 to 8.8053 (every draw at the floor, 1.500 kW).
  - The base LP publishes the true inverse of the energy it buys, so its secant is a valuation error, not a delivery one.
  - A convex-exact program cannot cost more in truth, so the chord model misprices. The segmentation was reverted.
- **Repair: the 2712 pin**, at f1e49686 through `python3 tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --in-place --spec <spec> --cmd 'bash <killcmd>'`. The spec mutates `optimizer.py:2712` `if refill is not None:` to `if False:`; the command runs `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` and fails only on `mutation_table.py`'s `killed()` rule against the measured baseline (rc != 0 and more `FAIL` lines than 1).
  - Baseline, unmutated: `1 of 5240 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`, rc=1, the inherited `combi_type_branch census`.
  - `SURVIVED NULL` (rc=1 failed=1), `KILLED row_cost_split_refill_GUARD_OFF` (rc=1 failed=2); the added FAIL is `R10-SAV-VALUATION-RESIDUE: on a valved install, where the tank's deficit converts at its own flow-derated COP ...`. Run twice, the same both times.

merges.body:
R10-INTRODUCED-REDS-BARRIER, the class barrier for R10-RCA-PUSHER-CENSUS-ESCAPE (triage `dev/programme/triage/s6-batch200.md#P626`): a step of `governance / instrument-self-tests` red at the head and not at the merge base is INTRODUCED, a finding of the pull request that the reviewer blocks on. A red inherited from `main` stays unowed, as the 2026-11-07 ruling (`234ff52c75`) holds.

**This pull request is POLICY.** It changes what a fix reviewer must block on (`dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md` step 11, `dev/governance/rules/defect-root-cause.md`). It merges on the approval under the owner's mandate (policy scope), after a merge verdict. No budget is loosened. The added sentences are paid by cutting spent prose in the same two files: `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --budgets` exits 0 with both files under their per-file caps.

- `merge_train.py`: one rule, `introduced_at` (`introduced_reds` pure). A step is red by `RED_CONCLUSIONS` (`review_packet.RED`, a self-test pins the two equal), so a step `cancelled` or `timed_out` counts, not only `failure`. A head job concluding `timed_out` where the base's did not adds `(the job concluded timed_out)`: a hang the pull request makes behind a step already red at the base hides every later step. The latest run by id is read at each side, concluded or not. A head job still running reads WAIT (rc 3) under `classify --pr` where the required set is green, never GREEN. A job-level `cancelled`, `startup_failure` or `action_required`, or a red job with no red step, is a Stop (rc 2): it reads no step. No base run counts every head red. The push-only drift step (`Refuse a self-test read set the committed table misses`) is excluded. A step skipped by scoping concludes `skipped` and is never red. An unreadable listing or job is a Stop (rc 2), never an empty list. `classify --pr` reads an introduced red as RED with one `INTRODUCED <step>` line each, so `bus.sh dispatch` and a cloud reviewer's `classify --pr` wait both stop on it. The new `introduced <sha> [--base <sha>]` subcommand prints those lines alone.
- `review_packet.py`: `introduced_reading` defers to `introduced_at` alone (the failure-only gate in front of it is gone) and refuses each name as `introduced-red`. An unreadable input, or a job still running, refuses too (fail closed). `gather`'s check-run keys come from `ci_facts`, the seam its self-test drives.
- `bus.sh dispatch`: an INTRODUCED red's REPAIR-OWED message names the INTRODUCED lines, not a required context.
- The base and head job are read through `?check_name=` filtered check-run reads. A main commit carries over 100 check runs, so the packet's unfiltered first page can miss the job.
- `.github/workflows/governance.yml`: the comment above `instrument-self-tests` no longer says `pr-contract` makes the body answer its red. It now says what holds.
- `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`: class `R10-SELFTEST-RED-INTRODUCED`, barriered by this rule, with `_rca` entry R10-RCA-PUSHER-CENSUS-ESCAPE. The class id also lands in `dev/audit/config/finding.schema.json`'s `class_guess` enum, and `fold_ledger.py sync` regenerates `.claude/workflows/audit-find.js`'s `CLASS_GUESS` from it. The RCA is landed as `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-PUSHER-CENSUS-ESCAPE.md`, its figures re-measured at this merge base.
- `.claude/rules` and `.cursor/rules` were regenerated by `node tools/policy/rules_sync.mjs`. Both instrument pages are updated.

Alternatives: C2 (a `prepr.sh` census arm) covers one step, not the class. C4 (making the job required) conflicts with decision 0013's `HPO_JOB_GRADES` boundary. C3 and C5 were refused by the RCA. A body-answer obligation (restoring the pre-ruling rule for this job) would re-owe inherited reds, which the ruling removed. Folding the rule into `classify` (the train's merge predicate) would change the train's merge rule. It is left to `classify --pr`, the reviewer's and dispatcher's read.

## Head

`54326b764f733ff7af6f97870429ae20ed2ae3a1` merges the authored code head `c67a466bf8df055f8791d8fb3aec7dc191a32ff9`.

c67a466bf8df055f8791d8fb3aec7dc191a32ff9

## Repair (round 1 verdict at fbf6c4dcd9)

The block: `introduced_at` read only a job concluding `failure` and steps concluding `failure`, so a hang the PR makes (job `timed_out`, step `cancelled`) read 0 and clean. Closed by reading every conclusion in `RED_CONCLUSIONS`, adding the job-level timeout, and refusing what reads no step. The three findings are built here, not carried: M7 (a re-run arm at one head, both directions), M9 (`ci_facts` arm), and the REPAIR-OWED message (bus self-test arm).

Class enumeration (fixer.md step 8), rule: every value a GitHub check run's `status` and `conclusion` and an Actions step's `conclusion` can take, each driven through `introduced_at` by a self-test arm or the harness below. Dispositions: `success`, `skipped`, `neutral` job: clean at no job read (arms). `failure` job: steps read (arms). `timed_out` job: steps read plus the job timeout, subtracted by a base `timed_out` (arms, and its null). `cancelled`, `startup_failure`, `action_required` job, at the head or base: Stop (arms for cancelled at both sides and startup_failure; action_required is the same branch, `hc not in SELFTESTS_STEP_READ`). `queued`/`in_progress` job: WAIT at the head (arm), Stop at the base (same branch as base cancelled). Step `failure`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`: red (arms); step `skipped`, `success`: not red (arms). No run: clean (arm: the prelude skips the job whole). The readers of the rule: `classify --pr`, `introduced`, `review_packet.introduced_reading`; all three now call `introduced_at` with no gate of their own in front of it.

## Mutation proof

Driver applies each mutant to the committed tree at `537d9f048`, runs the owning self-test(s), restores by `git checkout`; tree clean after. Every mutant KILLED:

- N1 `RED_CONCLUSIONS` reduced to `failure` only: 3 failed (merge_train and review_packet): "one notion of red: merge_train.RED_CONCLUSIONS is this file's RED", "a hang the PR makes (job timed_out, step cancelled) is INTRODUCED: the step and the timeout, refused", "a cancelled step inside a failed job is INTRODUCED".

- N3 `JOB_TIMED_OUT` never added: 3 failed, incl. "a hang behind a step already red at the base: the timeout alone is INTRODUCED".
- N4 a running head job returns `[]`: 2 failed, "a head job still running (a hang before its timeout) is WAIT under classify --pr (rc 3), never GREEN", "fail closed: a job still running at the head refuses introduced-red, never reads clean".
- N5 (verdict M7) `selftest_job` `max` to `min`: 3 failed, "a re-run at one head that went red: the latest run (highest id) is read, its red INTRODUCED", "a re-run at one head that went green reads clean at no job read", and the WAIT arm.
- N6 a job-level cancelled read as steps: 2 failed, "fail closed: the head's job concluded cancelled is a Stop (rc 2), never a clean read" and the packet's.
- N7 a red job with no red step not refused: 1 failed, "fail closed: a red head job with no red step is a Stop (rc 2), never a clean read".
- N8 `classify_cmd`'s WAIT branch dropped: 1 failed, the WAIT arm.
- N9 (verdict M9) `ci_facts`'s reading replaced by `([], "")`: 1 failed, "gather's ci_facts carries the INTRODUCED reading build refuses (M9: its wiring)".
- N10 the packet's running-job refusal re-prefixed `pending:`: 1 failed, "fail closed: a job still running at the head refuses introduced-red, never reads clean".
- N11 `bus.sh` ignoring INTRODUCED lines: 1 failed, "an INTRODUCED red (classify --pr RED, the required set green) owes REPAIR-OWED naming each INTRODUCED line, never a required context".

Failing test first: each arm was added before its production line and run red (merge_train: `NameError: JOB_TIMED_OUT`; review_packet: `TypeError: 'list' object is not callable` at the old eager base read; bus: 1 failed of 175).

## Null control

- The verdict's harness (its `ev/unguarded-domain.txt` cases, re-driven through `introduced_at` at each tree), with two nulls:
  - at `fbf6c4dcd9` (before): job failure + step cancelled, base green: `[]`; job timed_out + step cancelled: `[]` at 0 job reads; job cancelled: `[]` at 0 job reads; step timed_out/cancelled in a failed job: `[]`.
  - at `537d9f048` (after): `['hang']`; `['(the job concluded timed_out)', 'hang']` at 2 job reads; Stop ("concluded cancelled, which reads no step"); `['a', 'b']`.
  - nulls, identical at both trees: job failure + step failure, base green: `['hang']`; the same step failing at head and base: `[]`.
- A timeout the base had too, on the same step, is inherited: GREEN, introduced rc 0 (self-test arm).
- No `instrument-self-tests` run at the head (the prelude skipped it): GREEN (self-test arm).
- `classify` without `--pr`, and with `--main`, unchanged (self-test arm).

## Figures

Measured at origin/main `0e28afd38b`, 2026-11-11 16:20Z (`date -u`). Real data through `review_packet.introduced_reading(head, base)` (filtered reads only):

- (a) `c93903f075` (#3425 head) against `cbd23f1c8b`: the 4 INTRODUCED steps (sweep template render; PR argument builder; PR opener; PR updater census), head job 130479299736 failure, base job 130415622883 failure, 2.44 s.

That is the fail-closed arm, not a clean read; the code path is unchanged from the round reviewed.
- Self-tests: `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` 638 checks, 0 failed; `python3 tools/audit/seat/review_packet.py --self-test` 109 checks, 0 failed; `bash tools/audit/seat/bus.sh --self-test` 175 checks, 0 failed.
- Gate scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` reads `MODE: SCOPED -- 3 script(s) run` (doc_claims, entities, harness_headers). `python3 tests/structure.py` passes. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflict.

## Block

- class-open, a predicate's unguarded domain (fix-review.md step 6). `merge_train.introduced_at` returns [] when the head's job concluded anything but `failure`, and `introduced_reds` counts only steps that concluded `failure`. A PR that makes an instrument self-test hang or slow down past the PR timeout (`timeout-minutes: 30` on a pull request against 60 on a push, `ev/selftests-timeout.txt`) produces a red `instrument-self-tests` job that concludes `timed_out`, with the running step `cancelled`. The barrier reads that as 0 introduced at no job read, and `classify --pr` and `review_packet` both pass it (`ev/unguarded-domain.txt`). Main's own push job has 60 minutes, so the same diff can be green or failure at the base while timed_out at the head: the asymmetry is in the head's favour. A job concluding `failure` whose only new non-success step is `cancelled` or `timed_out` also reads 0. The same file's `review_packet.RED` already names {failure, cancelled, timed_out, action_required, startup_failure} as red, so the rule is narrower than the repository's own definition of a red. The body claims the rule fails closed, and here it fails open. Owed: a head job that concluded `timed_out` (and steps that concluded `timed_out` or `cancelled`) count as red under the same base subtraction, and a job-level `cancelled` is a wait or a Stop, never a clean read. Each needs a self-test arm and its mutant.

## Findings

- Surviving mutant M7: `selftest_job`'s `max` changed to `min` (the earliest concluded run, not the latest) kills no check in either self-test. Real data has re-runs: #3425's head job 130479299736 is `run_attempt` 3. Under M7 a re-run that turned green still reads its older red, and a re-run that went red reads the older green. ## Block

Round 1. The three files the re-record removes are not a real narrowing. They come from a trace gap in the recording environment, and the gap depends on that environment.

- The path: `tools/pr/prepr.sh:1980` (inside `--self-test`, cwd at the repo root) runs `bash .claude/hooks/session-start.sh --self-test`. That reaches `report()` (`.claude/hooks/session-start.sh:89-104`). When `git config --get merge.claimnotes.driver` is empty, `report()` runs `python3 tests/env_drift.py --install-merge-driver`. When `merge.ledgermerge.driver` is empty, it runs `python3 tools/merge/ledger_merge.py --install`. Those installs read `.gitattributes`.
- Why the recording missed them: the fixer's seat, like mine, had both drivers set in `.git/config` because the session-start hook installed them when the session opened (`git config --show-origin` gives `file:.git/config` for both). So the 861 s record never took that branch, and the three reads vanished. The same applies to "the first seat's independent run gave the identical diff": both seats share this environment, so the second run is not an independent check.
- CI takes the branch: the job uses `actions/checkout`, `governance.yml` installs neither driver anywhere (no `install-merge-driver` and no `ledger_merge.py --install` in the file), and a fresh checkout has no `merge.*.driver` config. On main's red run the refusal listed only `mutant_guard.py` and `mutant_run.py` as misses. That fits CI having read the three files, which the old table still covered.
- Measured (my own instrument; strace, not the finder's whole-job trace): in a fresh `git clone --no-local` at the head, with no driver config (`git config --get-regexp 'merge\..*\.driver'` rc=1), `strace -f -e openat,execve bash .claude/hooks/session-start.sh --self-test` opens `.gitattributes` (2 calls), `tests/env_drift.py` (2 opens + 1 exec) and `tools/merge/ledger_merge.py` (2 opens + 1 exec), and exits rc=0: `ev/hook.reads.txt` (8 lines). Null control: the same command in the same clone, once the drivers are installed, opens none of the three (0 lines, `ev/hook2.reads.txt`). Every path that differs between the two runs is one this diff deletes.
- The consequence: once merged, the first main push re-runs instrument-self-tests on a fresh checkout. It will measure those three reads against an entry that no longer names them and refuse `UNDER-SCOPED step prepr: files misses ['.gitattributes', 'tests/env_drift.py', 'tools/merge/ledger_merge.py']`. That swaps one red on main for another.
- The cure, cheapest first: keep the three files in the prepr entry beside the three it gains, so the entry is the old one plus `mutant_guard.py`, `mutant_run.py` and `figure_block.py`. Or re-record in a clone where `git config --unset merge.claimnotes.driver` and `git config --unset merge.ledgermerge.driver` were run first. A record taken where the hook has already set up the clone cannot see this branch.

## Findings

- Follow-up: `selftest_scope.py record` measures whatever per-clone git config the recording seat has, so a seat whose session-start hook already installed the merge drivers drops reads that CI's fresh checkout makes. The same gap can narrow any gated step that runs the session-start self-test. One countermeasure would be for `record` to run against a scratch clone with no `merge.*.driver` config, or to refuse while those drivers are set. This review does not settle it. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-MAIN-IST-PREPR-SCOPE
- Follow-up: the body's root-cause countermeasure (run `selftest_scope.py check` in prepr/ci_predict when a gated step's script changes) is unbuilt, and the body names R10-HOTFIX-PREPR-WC-PAD as the owner of prepr.sh. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-PREPR-WC-PAD

- There is no pull request yet, so there is no review packet and no CI on this head to read. No red is owed a `## Red checks` answer (`instrument-self-tests` is not in `merge_train.py owed-reds`).
- The body's figures, re-derived in my seat's environment, where the drivers are set: `selftest_scope.py record --step prepr --out <scratch>` gave OK 901.5 s, 0 failed, 0 broken traces (`ev/record.log`). The recorded prepr entry equals the head's on files, probes, dirs, run_sha, index and objects. `drift()` on that measurement with main's b737e88ee table gives `UNDER-SCOPED step prepr: files misses ['dev/audit/harnesses/mutant_guard.py', 'tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py', 'tools/pr/figure_block.py']` plus `note: over-scoped step prepr: 3 files no longer measured`. Builds outside pull request #3437 (Bankaifan, accepted into round 10; its commit is adopted with the author's authorship, its tool-attribution trailers dropped). A failed price fetch in `_fetch_tibber_prices` always raised `UpdateFailed`, so every entity went unavailable and the optimizer stopped steering, though the last fetched prices still covered the current step. Now, while `_known_prices_for` still returns a price for the current plan step, the failure is a WARNING plus the `price_feed_stale` repair and the update carries on; once no published price covers now, the update fails as before (D10-07) and the repair stays until a fetch succeeds. A refused token always fails and raises no repair. Closes nothing.

Design, against the alternatives:
- `issues.note_price_outage` owns the outage's logging and the repair, and returns whether planning goes on; the coordinator passes the post-increment outage count and the covering prices. The author's version stored `bridged` in the coordinator and passed `not cycles`: two counted statements, `coord_footprint` 2497 -> 2499, inadmissible under `score.py`. Returning the verdict pays both.
- The coverage decision stays a coordinator read (`_known_prices_for`), not a copy in `issues.py`: no price concept duplicated, and `issues.py` keeps no price import (its leaf contract).
- `price_model.py`, which owns `pull_prices`, was refused as the home: it imports no `homeassistant`, and a repair call there would add the issue registry to a model module (fixer step 17).
- The recovery clear runs inside the latch's own branch (`if self._tibber_outage_cycles:`), not on every healthy cycle as the author's did; the repair is not persistent, so no restart leaves one behind.
- Corrected claims: `_fetch_tibber_prices`'s and `_tibber_fetch_failed`'s docstrings and the update loop's comment said every failed fetch raises; they now state the coverage condition. `README.md`'s repair-notice list gains the new notice (`doc_claims.py` refused it with no home). The strings.json/en text, de and sv say the same four things: no new prices (with the error), planning goes on on the last published prices covering now, unavailable once they run out, clears on a successful fetch.

Builds outside pull request #3443 (Bankaifan, fork head 01188a68b0, kept as the first commit 698f643b65 with the contributor's authorship, date and tree; its message lost only the session-link and co-author trailers `ref_privacy` refuses) into one seam. Home Assistant 2026.11 serves the climate temperatures under the native names and logs every class still defining the old ones (removal stated 2027.11); the supported floor 2025.2.0 reads only the old ones. The contributor's plain rename breaks the climate entity on every core below 2026.11: on 2025.2.0 it reads `AttributeError` for the unit (Figures, harness at 01188a68b0).

The entity's logic lives once, under the native names. `HeatPumpOptimizerEntity._PRE_NATIVE`, beside `_PUBLISHED` in `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/entity.py`, maps each native member to its pre-native spelling; `__init_subclass__`, after the finite scrub, installs the old name as the same member object only where no `homeassistant` base of the class carries the native member. Detection is on the base class, never a version. On a core whose base carries the native names the class holds none of the old ones, so `migrate_deprecated_entity_members` reports nothing. A later platform with the same deprecation gets its alias from the table.

Alternatives not taken: a module-level patch in `climate.py` after the class statement (the shape #3443's body describes; a second helper outside the mechanism owning the published names, and the scrub would not cover it without repeating it); two property bodies per name (the logic twice); a version comparison (the brief refuses it: the base class is what the core reads); raising the floor (out of scope by the brief).

`tests/nightly_ha.py` gains `log:no_deprecated_member` (OUTSIDE_CHECKS), failing a run whose Home Assistant log carries `provides the deprecated` beside this package's name: the WARNING has no traceback, so no existing scan read it. It runs on both images of CI's `nightly-ha` matrix at this head.

merges.body:
The CI gate livelock behind #3445 (held in the train 75+ min) and #3446 (code suite run five times at one head), ruling P620 (`dev/programme/triage/s6-batch196.md`). Two seams, each with a failing self-test first and a null arm.

1. `tools/ci/gate.py`, the source loop in `gate()`: a run whose unit's jobs concluded only `cancelled` or `success`, at least one `cancelled`, is no source for that unit, and the loop falls through, as it already does for a deferred (all-skipped) unit. A cancelled newer run sorted first by `fresh()` (its jobs started latest) and the gate read its CANCELLED. A red beside a cancelled job (fail-fast) keeps that run the source.
2. `tools/ci/sweep.py`, `Sweep.fresh()`: a `workflow_dispatch` run at the head that is not completed (`NOT_COMPLETED`) or concluded `success` is the head's fresh judge whatever its `created_at`. Keying on creation at or after the stale gate's completion re-dispatched each time an old pull_request or pull_request_review gate was re-run.

Alternatives: (gate) skipping only an all-`cancelled` unit, the brief's literal wording, leaves a run cancelled mid-unit (some jobs already `success`) as the CANCELLED source, so the livelock survives a late cancel; skipping any unit with one `cancelled` job hides a fail-fast red behind an older green. (sweep) keeping the creation key and adding the re-run's attempt start loses to a stateless one: any live or green dispatch is a judge, so nothing about gate timing can re-open the loop.

Merge note for the orchestrator: a change under `tools/ci` makes every open PR whose base predates it stale-pinned (`Sweep.stale_pin`), costing one fresh dispatch per open PR once; time the merge accordingly.

Fixture fidelity: `sweep_selftest.run()` and `finish()` now set the run's own `conclusion` (the gate job's when the run completed), which GitHub always lists and the new predicate reads; no prior check changed verdict.

## Head

`d62aaa031c00359ba5867d2c7b8b006d49d669f2` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

97e6011948c9dd967888050fcb5ad4bc4a17c94b, on base ee64358be7eeccaec5178a923cb3b83a18a924a0 (origin/main at 2026-11-11T13:06:51Z).

## Mutation proof

Each production predicate removed alone, then the self-tests:

- gate.py, the whole new `continue` deleted: `python3 -I tools/ci/gate.py --self-test` fails `a newer cancelled run over an older green one at the head is no source: green` and `null: with only the cancelled run at the head the unit has no source: red` (2 of 85 failed).
- gate.py, `"success"` dropped from the allowed set: fails `a newer run cancelled after part of its unit passed is no source either: the older green judges` (1 of 87).
- gate.py, the `any(... "cancelled" ...)` clause deleted: fails 19 of 87, among them `null: a newer green run over an older red one is the source: green` and `null: a newer failed run over an older green one is the source: red`.
- sweep.py, `later` restored to the `created_at >= completed_at` key: `cd tools/ci && python3 sweep.py --self-test` fails `stale pin, one judge per head: a dispatch listed completed|queued|in_progress, created before the stale gate's re-run completed is the fresh judge; nothing dispatched` (3 of 85).

Restored: gate 87 checks, 0 failed; sweep 85 checks, 0 failed.

## Null control

At ee64358be7 with only the new checks applied: gate self-test 2 of 85 failed (the cancelled-over-green arm reads `(False, ['tests / fast (3.14): cancelled (run 95)', ...])`); sweep self-test 3 of 85 failed (the three one-judge-per-head arms dispatch). The null arms passed at the base and pass at the head: a newer failed run over an older green one reads red; a fail-fast unit (one failure, rest cancelled) reads red; a newer green run over an older red one reads green; with only a `failure` or only a `cancelled` dispatch at the head the sweep dispatches exactly once (`dispatches=1`).

## Figures

- gate self-test: `python3 -I tools/ci/gate.py --self-test` prints `gate self-test: 87 checks, 0 failed` at the head; 81 checks, 0 failed at the base before the new checks.
- sweep self-test: `cd tools/ci && python3 sweep.py --self-test` prints `sweep self-test: 85 checks, 0 failed` at the head.
- scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` prints `MODE: FULL` (reason: `tools/ci/gate.py changes the gate itself`); the full suite is CI's.
- structure: `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- Class enumeration (fixer step 8): the seams that pick a run as a judge of a head are the source loop in `gate.gate()` and `Sweep.fresh()` (both closed here); `sweep.settled`/`undecided` read gate jobs, not run conclusions, and are already guarded by the #3308 and settle checks. The P620 measurement (10 of 43 code dispatches) is the ruling's and not re-taken here.

## Red checks

- `tests / fast (3.14)`: red on fc3af2f9a4 because `tests/features.py` failed its `combi_type_branch` census (vendor names at const.py:812 and five other lines), which the base 60413046e3 already failed on the same line; the diff touches only `tools/ci`, so it cannot reach it, and the head is green. No cheaper detector for the branch exists: the census belongs to the base's own run and was caught by it.
- `governance / instrument-self-tests`: main's own red until merge 6d16af36c2; no detector is owed for a red this branch did not introduce.
- `tests / nightly-status`: grades main's nightly (cancelled lanes), outside the required set, so owed no answer under defect-root-cause.md Enforcement.

- RESULT head: gate self-test 87 checks, 0 failed; sweep self-test 85 checks, 0 failed (ev/head-selftests.txt). Matches the body.

None can be red at a head with no runs. Main's inherited tests / fast combi-census red and governance / instrument-self-tests failures are not this PR's.
- Forward-carry: the body has none, and the roster assigns this hotfix no carry that I was handed.

## Findings

- Follow-up: the sweep.py module doc (lines 50-52 at the head, ev/sweep-module-doc-48-53.txt) still states "A dispatched run created after the stale gate concluded is that fresh judge already". That is the creation key this PR removes, so the module doc now contradicts Sweep.fresh(), whose own docstring was updated. Carry: dismissed: one-sentence doc drift in a file this PR already edits; the fixer can fold it in before the PR opens, and a doc-only delta never widens a review (fix-review step 12)
- Follow-up: some body figures do not reproduce. Mutation proof "whole continue deleted ... 2 of 85" measures 3 of 87, and null control "gate self-test 2 of 85 failed" also measures 3 of 87. No self-test covers a gate whose own run carries a cancelled-plus-success unit. Carry: dismissed: parity with the base line's untested own-run guard; it is outside both livelock arms and kept conservative, so the gate's own unit always judges

A green dispatch created before a later tools/ci change on main still counts as the head's fresh judge, so the merge note's "one fresh dispatch per open PR" is an upper bound (a PR with a live or green dispatch at its head gets none), and such a head is not re-judged with newer programs by the sweep. Now `pass()` takes the one open-PR listing first (`open_prs`, into `cloud-prs-open.$$`), then runs probe_arm, confirm_arm (with --confirm), handoff_arm, carry_fold_arm, stuck_arm, noreturn_arm. `handoff_arm` and `confirm_arm` reuse the listing; a failed listing leaves no file and each arm lists for itself as before. Updates are not detached (update_pr.sh already answers BUSY per branch). Repair round: the self-test now pins the arm order itself, killing mutants m7 and m8 that survived.

Closes nothing (triage s6-batch182 P601).

- m8 `confirm_arm` after `handoff_arm`: 1 failed (`pass --confirm runs the arms probe, confirm, handoff, carry_fold, stuck, noreturn in that order`)

- m11 `carry_fold_arm` before `handoff_arm`: 2 failed
- m12 `confirm_arm` dropped: 9 failed

merges.title: R10-OUTSIDE-DISINFECTION-SETPOINT: r10 outside disinfection setpoint
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-OUTSIDE-DISINFECTION-SETPOINT, built on outside pull request #3439 (Bankaifan, fork head f9a7bcb4ee; adopted as feeb0b6b39 with the author kept and the tool trailers dropped by the ref_privacy.py guard's attribution classes). With Pump duty control writing the hot-water set-point, a disinfection cycle wrote the everyday set-point (stock pair 55/60: 55.0 on a booked and on a held step), so the pump's own thermostat ended the cycle below its target; and the set-point repair stood permanently against the arbiter's own 55, its Fix (60) rewritten to 55 at the next step.

The rule for a cycle's temperature now has one owner on `ThermalParameters`: `dhw_disinfection_temp` (the disinfection temperature where #3398's `legionella_cycle_active` holds, else `None`: the one cycle predicate) and `dhw_cycle_temp` (the higher of the everyday set-point and that). `dhw_hard_max_temp` and the repair's `_dhw_floor` read them instead of each restating the predicate and the max. The arbiter decides when (`_dhw_write`: the step's action books `dhw_reason` legionella, or `disinfecting` holds) and every row of `desired` that writes hot water takes that one answer; the cycle's target is written on the entity's step at or below the tank's hard maximum (`dhw_hard_max_temp`: the cycle's temperature capped at 70 °C) and bounded by its range (above the range is left to the guard's unreachable notice). `dhw_gated` is generalised from "the arbiter's gate, below the everyday set-point" to "the arbiter's own write, still as written": a record exists only while the arbiter controls the pump (`_forget` clears it when Control is left), so an install where the arbiter writes nothing keeps the repair unchanged.

Alternatives not taken: the contributor's private helper computing the max inside the arbiter (a third copy of the expression the ceiling and the floor already held); a special case in the repair for the cycle (the brief asks the existing exemption to generalise, and a special case would restate the arbiter's when-rule in a second module); folding the repair's floor onto `dhw_cycle_temp` (changes the repair on an install whose everyday set-point is above the disinfection temperature with the pump reading between them, which the null controls forbid).

Repair for the blocked verdict at 0aed6ccb (null-control-leak): `8da43a2f` routed every cycle write through the round-up, so an off-step everyday set-point above the disinfection temperature was written a step above itself (everyday 57, disinfection 50, step 5: 60, where 49a45dd8 and the no-cycle row write 55), above `dhw_hard_max_temp` 57; and `feeb0b6b`'s round-up already did the same for an off-step disinfection temperature above the everyday set-point (60.3 at step 1: 61). `de817c3a` bounds the cycle's write by the hard maximum through `_bounded`'s existing ceiling (`hi=`, rounded down onto the step, in the entity's own unit): no cycle write exceeds it, every row where 49a45dd8 stayed within it is unchanged, and the no-cycle write is untouched. This reverses `8da43a2f`'s row (everyday 60.4, disinfection 60.2, step 1: 60 again, 49a45dd8's value): the only on-step values are 60, below the disinfection temperature, and 61, above the hard maximum, and the hard maximum wins. Alternatives not taken: restoring `cycle <= everyday` (keeps 49a45dd8's nearest step, which writes 60 over a hard maximum of 58 at everyday 58, step 5); a ceiling at `dhw_cycle_temp` (drops the 70 °C cap, mutant M13); rounding down without the ceiling (a second statement of the cap, which `dhw_hard_max_temp` owns).

`dhw_target_temperature` (`optimizer.py` predictive_info, copied onto every step's action) is left the everyday set-point: it is published beside `dhw_min_temperature` as the configured target, no production code reads it to act (`git grep -n dhw_target_temperature -- custom_components`: the optimizer's two writes, the sensor attribute, the payload type), and a cycle step already says so through its `dhw_reason` legionella; moving it would move every golden fixture that records it for a label change.

The space-only gate row (`DHW_GATE_C`) stays a gate on a step the plan booked for a cycle only when a block removed hot water from it; a held cycle turns a space step into Heating + DHW, whose write is the cycle's temperature (pinned).

## Head

The widened scope is that function's cycle write.

`8da43a2fe` drops `or cycle <= everyday`, so every cycle write is now rounded up. The body justifies this for one case: everyday 60.4, disinfection 60.2, step 1. There the nearest step (60) falls below the disinfection target, which the guard's credit test needs. But `dhw_cycle_temp` is `max(dhw_setpoint, disinfection)`. So the change also rounds up every install whose everyday set-point is at or above the disinfection temperature and off the entity's step. On those installs, the nearest step already meets the disinfection target. This is the body's own null-control class ("an everyday set-point at (60) and above (62) the disinfection temperature ... Had the fix leaked into them the diff would print those lines"). The harness puts that class only on-step, so it cannot see the leak (its output is byte-identical at 49a45dd8 and at the head, `ev/harness_prev_49a45dd8.txt` and `ev/harness_head.txt`).

Measured with the PR's own `_dhw_snap` and `written` helpers inside `tests/block_duty.py`'s `disinfection_checks`. The probe is spliced in temporarily (`ev/probe2.py`) and output is in `ev/probe_overshoot.txt`. The install is everyday 57, disinfection 50, entity min 30, max 65, step 5.

- RESULT head 0aed6ccbc: held cycle write 60.0; booked cycle write 60.0; null (no cycle) write 55.0
- RESULT prior head 49a45dd8: held cycle write 55.0; booked cycle write 55.0; null (no cycle) write 55.0

The cycle's target here is 50, and 55 already meets it. The head instead writes 60. That is a full step above the everyday set-point and above `dhw_hard_max_temp`, which is `min(70, dhw_cycle_temp)` = 57, the ceiling the plan models the tank under. The pump heats the tank 3 °C past what the plan accounts for on every cycle step. Before this delta, the reviewed head did not do this. The overshoot equals the entity's step: 1 °C on a step-1 entity with a 0.5 °C everyday set-point (52.4 → 53 against 52), and 5 °C on a step-5 entity.

The defect `8da43a2fe` fixes is real (M11 reproduces it below). The repair needs to round up only where the nearest step falls below the disinfection temperature. Something like `max(nearest(everyday), up(disinfection))` through `_bounded`'s existing `lo` argument would do it. That `lo` already rounds a floor up, so it adds no second rounding rule, which was the reason the body gave for rejecting the quantised comparison. It also needs a `tests/block_duty.py` null-control check on an off-step everyday set-point above the disinfection temperature, which fails at this head.
