merges.body:
R10-COMBI-TANK PR B (M; design `a605014bff4478f470853109060f4ff7ef605d4c`, approved by `design-verdict/r10-combi-tank` `56810263b`, Cost and Order section's PR B scope). Stacked on PR A, #3358 head `577c6974205926e7dbaa178b91af96a229ea02f3` (workaround ruling: outside work may stack on an unmerged base). Issue #3225 (outside user Bankaifan): a combi store, one body of heating water serving the space circuit and hot water through an exchanger, could not be configured. PR A landed the store's physics behind fields only a test could set; this PR makes it reachable by an install and closes the issue.

Closes #3225

What changes:
- **The option.** The building page gains a `combi` section: the switch, the tank type, the exchanger effectiveness, the potable volume and the legionella force. The switch is refused (`combi_needs_store`) by the model's own `combi_tank_active` predicate over what would be stored, never a copy of it. The type is the flow's pre-fill of the two numbers the model reads (`_combi_preset_fill`: a changed type writes its preset, a kept type keeps edited numbers, `custom` writes nothing); `COMBI_TANK_PRESETS` in const.py is keyed by physical construction, never by product (design §T.4). Strings in every shipped language (en, sv, de), the configuration doc's building table, and the card's setup diagram (a combi caption and the hot water pipe leaving the buffer).
- **The loader.** `ThermalParameters._tabled_values` reads the four fields from their own keys; PR A's `unwired_combi` exemption is replaced by a check that each field is reached by its own key (carry 8).
- **The seed (carry 6).** `tank_levels` and `combi_tank_seed` (coordinator.py, module level beside `_seed_store`): a combi store is one node, so both levels carry the buffer probe, else the hot water probe, else the previous plan's buffer trajectory, which is `_seed_store` over the DHW reading. Off combi each tank seeds alone, as before.
- **The learners.** The separate tank's DHW learner takes no sample of a combi store. The buffer cooling learner needs no gate: combi implies a throttling valve, under which `_async_learn_buffer_cooling` already returns (pinned by a check over every valve mode).
- **The legionella default (design §L, as the folded web report item 6 corrects it).** `ThermalParameters.legionella_cycle_active` is the flag's one behaviour read: a combi store holding at most `COMBI_LEGIONELLA_POTABLE_LIMIT_L` (3 l) of potable water runs no cycle unless `dhw_combi_legionella_force` is on; off combi it is `dhw_legionella_enabled` itself. Its nine behaviour readers moved to it (dhw_planner, legionella, setpoint_check, the coordinator's elastic block, the rating's top); diagnostics publish `dhw_legionella_cycle_active` beside the raw flag. The W 551 exemption citation is gone; the default rests on physical grounds (no potable water stands to disinfect), and the help text states W 551's delivery temperatures.
- **Setup and advisor.** `describe_setup` gains `dhw_source` (`combi` / `tank`) and the hot water edge leaves `buffer_tank` in combi; `rank_sensor_gaps` prices no hot water probe over a combi store with a buffer probe.
- **Main's de gaps, disclosed.** `de.json` and the card's de strings lacked five keys main gained from PRs that crossed #3331; `tests/entities.py`, `tests/card.mjs` and `claims.py`'s C112 were red on main's own tree for them (null control below), so `82d5ba034` filled them. Main filled the same keys independently before the handoff; the merge `baac8a0a2` resolved each conflicting hunk to main's text, so this PR's diff against main carries none of them.

Departure, disclosed: `origin/main` was merged at the start (`fa38b58c2`) although `git merge-tree` reported no conflict, because the brief's de translations need the de catalogue and `SHIPPED_LANGS`, which exist only on main (`git ls-tree origin/main custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/translations/` lists de.json; PR A's head does not). It was merged again (`baac8a0a2`) when `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reported CONFLICT in de.json and the card, the de-gap keys above, and a third time (`27fa6918c`) for the merge train's skip, `## Merge resolution only`.

## Head

`141f8af1b1a59840ec18522dd4e44ad321d4c397` merges the authored code head `52ab77dc206962c162ee9abd475361455c0c3f68`.

`52ab77dc206962c162ee9abd475361455c0c3f68` is this PR's head (see `## Head note`). Earlier heads: `a47cddfebf07840156d6f6dfa64b29ade3371d67` (blocked `merge-conflict`), `a1b268838ee527fa669abcaba5c97ba542b03d3c`, `1d4aec21aa0828412077708a9e74453acaef12e2`, `e020a1d23d87c707f2a3070e0e77a724fff4b127`. The figures in `## Figures`, `## Mutation proof` and `## Null control` were re-taken at this head unless a line names another.

## Head note

`52ab77dc206962c162ee9abd475361455c0c3f68` is the merge of `origin/main` `d08ed31049cd3636cde4d2fdeb3bd7cd4b3c842a` (v7.1.10's stamp; read 2026-11-11T01:05Z) into `a47cddfebf07840156d6f6dfa64b29ade3371d67`, taken because `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main a47cddfeb` reported a conflict (`Fix review: blocked a47cddfeb... merge-conflict`). One path conflicted, `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` (`## Resolution` section 3); the merge changed no other file by hand. `VERSION`, the manifest and `RELEASE_NOTES.md` are main's (`git diff --quiet origin/main HEAD -- VERSION custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json RELEASE_NOTES.md` exits 0).

## Resolution

The merge at `a1b268838` conflicted in four files, not one (the brief named the first); sections 1 and 2 are that merge's and both parents' entries are present in each result. Section 3 is the merge at this head, the only path that conflicted in it.

**1. `dev/audit/rounds/round3/D5/option_doc_coverage.py`** (EXPECTED header). Parent HEAD (this branch) carried: `R10-MIN-POWER-FLOOR ... 204 -> 205 and 237 -> 238 ... R10-COMBI-TANK (#3225) moved them 205 -> 210 and 238 -> 244` and `RESULT option_fields_rendered=213 ... option_schema_keys_rendered=247`. R10-MIN-POWER-FLOOR ... 207 -> 208 and 240 -> 241` and `RESULT option_fields_rendered=211 ... option_schema_keys_rendered=244`. Kept result: main's chain (204 -> 207 -> 208 for fields, 237 -> 240 -> 241 for keys, plus its 211 / 244 heat-curve step) followed by this branch's sentence re-based on it: `R10-COMBI-TANK (#3225) moved them 211 -> 216 and 244 -> 250: the building page's combi section (one section key, five fields), each with its row`, and `RESULT option_fields_rendered=216`, `option_fields_undocumented=0`, `option_schema_keys_rendered=250`. Check: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round3/D5/option_doc_coverage.py` prints `option_fields_rendered=216`, `option_fields_undocumented=0`, `option_schema_keys_rendered=250` (main's 211/244 + this branch's 5/6).

**2. `dev/audit/rounds/round4/D6/claims.json` and `claims.md`** (C125). HEAD: `(48 selects)`, `48 selects, untranslated=[]`. origin/main: `(49 selects)`, `49 selects, untranslated=[]`. Kept result: regenerated by `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round4/D6/claims.py`, not hand-merged: C125 reads `50 selects, untranslated=[]` (main's 49 + this branch's one), C30 `97 rows` (was 94 on main), C31 `104 rows` (was 102 on main). `claims.py`'s header counts moved to `config_defaults_compared=97` and `config_ranges_compared=104` in the same regeneration; prepr's `claims register` step confirms the script rewrites both files byte-identical.

**3. `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt`** (re-stated at `52ab77dc2`; it replaces the 12-line resolution of `a1b268838`). The claimnotes driver refused the merge of `d08ed3104`: main's v7.1.10 stamp emptied its claim list and moved `claims-for:` to 7.1.10, while this branch held twelve lines under `claims-for: 7.1.9`. Kept result: main's file plus this branch's six `R10-COMBI-TANK (#3225)` lines (`config_flow`, `coord_all_features`, `coord_dhw`, `coord_grid_fee`, `coord_minimal`, `coord_two_zone`), 6 claim lines, `claims-for: 7.1.10`. No `R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE-PERSISTENT` line is carried. Rule for the count: lines of the file that are neither blank nor comment (`grep -cvE '^\s*(#|$)' tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt`), 6 at this head and 0 on `origin/main`; of those, lines not naming `R10-COMBI-TANK (#3225)`: 0. `diff <(git show origin/main:tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt) tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` prints those six additions and nothing else. Check that each claim is still owed and none is missing: `python3 tests/env_drift.py --all origin/main` prints `CLAIMED` for exactly those six scenarios (`config_flow: 4 leaves moved`, each `coord_*: 3 leaves moved`), then `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 56 scenario(s) checked against origin/main` and `NO STALE FIXTURE: 56 committed fixture(s) still match what this tree computes`; a dropped line still owed would print unclaimed drift, a kept line not owed a stale claim. `tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt` is byte-identical to main's (`git diff origin/main...HEAD -- tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt` prints nothing). No golden fixture was re-recorded in this round.

**Auto-merged and not conflicting:** the `tests/golden/*.json` fixtures (main's string moves and this branch's additive keys), `custom_components/**` and the translations.


## Repair round

The previous head could not be applied: merged with main, `python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py` printed `PREDICT ledger   STALE PIN custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/thermal_model.py:ThermalParameters.dhw_hard_max_temp GUARD_OFF 07409d20: disposition names no site the inventory generates (old pin '        if self.dhw_legionella_enabled:')`. Cause: this branch rewrote the site, `dhw_hard_max_temp` now guards on `self.legionella_cycle_active`, so the old line no longer exists. The current guard already carries its own pin (`...GUARD_OFF.f3c560aa.json`, killed by tests/guard_pins.py, `--pin-killed`). Repair as ci_predict prints it: the stale pin file `tests/mutation_ledger/killed_by/thermal_model.py/ThermalParameters.dhw_hard_max_temp.GUARD_OFF.07409d20.json` was deleted (`git rm`), not edited. After it, `python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py` prints `CI PREDICT: no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted against 5d09dedf69eb`. Cheaper detector for the red: `ci_predict.py` itself (this branch's prior bodies already name it); process state (d), main's merge changed nothing here, the earlier pin set was stale against this branch's own rewrite once re-checked on the merged tree.

## Merge resolution only

The merge train skipped #3398 (`SKIP #3398 recarry: main does not merge without a resolution`): `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 249d76dd6` reported CONFLICT in the paths below. R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE had landed on main, adding to the same lists as this branch. Each path was resolved against both parents (figures in this section are those at `27fa6918c`; `## Resolution` above gives the current ones):
- `strings.json`, `translations/en.json`, `de.json`, `sv.json`: both sides appended an `options.error` key (this branch `combi_needs_store`; main `heat_curve_not_offset` and `heat_curve_entity_in_use`) and a `selector` block (this branch `dhw_combi_tank_type`; main `heat_curve_target_kind`). - `dev/audit/rounds/round3/D5/option_doc_coverage.py` (EXPECTED header): base 205/238; this branch +5/+6, main +3/+3, giving `option_fields_rendered=213` and `option_schema_keys_rendered=247` at that merge.

## Mutation proof

Re-executed at `52ab77dc2` after the merge: each mutant applied in a detached worktree at that head, `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/seat/features_block.py --through "# --- round-5 D3-04 (#1312): the valve ratio's two-price floor"` run (`tests/features.py` from its top through the PR B block), and the file restored by `git checkout -- .` (`git status --short` empty after the last). merges.body:
Main-red hotfix: `governance / instrument-self-tests` red on main. Its step "Refuse a self-test read set the committed table misses" refuses read sets the committed `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` misses. There are two causes, and this PR closes both.

**Cause 1: a racily clean git index (prepr's moving read set).** A fresh checkout leaves every file it wrote in the index's own mtime second "racily clean". Those are the alphabetical tail of the checkout, because git writes files in index order. The first index-refreshing git command (`git status`) run in the real checkout opens and hashes each racy file. Under strace those opens fold into whichever traced step ran that command first. In run 42780661829 that was prepr's `WIRE_PORC=$(git status --porcelain)`, in the red-check-arm wiring block of `tools/pr/prepr.sh`. The read set moves with scheduling and checkout timing, not with the tree.

**Fix 1: `selftest_scope.py settle`.** It waits until the clock is past the newest tracked file's mtime second, then runs `git update-index -q --really-refresh --force-write-index`. It verifies with `racy_entries`, retries up to three times with a 1.1 s margin, and refuses (rc 1) if any entry is left or a file is stamped in the future. It runs untraced in CI's `strace` step, before `launch`, and as `record`'s first act.

**Repair for the round-1 block (mutation-vacuous).** Two lines were pinned by nothing: the CI settle call in `governance.yml` and the `settle` CLI dispatch. They are pinned now:
- `settle_gaps()` refuses a job in which no untraced step ordered before the first traced one runs `python3 -I tools/ci/selftest_scope.py settle` on a line of its own. The first traced step is a gated step, or `launch`, which starts traced steps. A swallowed `|| true` is refused too.
- `static_check` (the pull-request side) and the self-test's live-job check run `settle_gaps`. The self-test reads the job file passed with `--self-test --workflow PATH`, so `selftest_scope_mutants.sh` can hand it a mutated `governance.yml`.
- The self-test drives `main(["settle"])` over the racy fixture.

Design choice: the settle call is pinned by a static read because the strace step runs only when `SELFTEST_TRACE` is set, which it never is on a pull request.

**Cause 2: steps whose read sets main's own changes widened.** Many steps read files their committed entries miss. `post-merge-record-line`, `plan-page`, `handover-prompt`, `state-doc-writer`, `roster-queue-runner` and `post-merge-bookkeeping` miss `tests/layout.py` and `tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py`. `open-pr`, `update-pr`, `pr-args`, `hooks-setup`, `field-coverage` and `selftest-wiring` miss `tools/audit/seat/survivor_list.py`. `beat-job-rows`, `cloud-relay`, `verdict-bus` and others miss other files. **Fix 2:** each refused step is re-recorded by the instrument's own path (`python3 -I tools/ci/selftest_scope.py record --step ID ...`, Linux, strace). Each was recorded in a fresh worktree of this branch merged with origin/main, so it measures the tree main will have after the merge. No read set was hand-edited, and `tests/closures.json` was not derived.

Alternatives that lost:
- **Re-record prepr from a run's `selftest-closures` artifact, without `settle`.** That bakes one run's racy tail into the table, and the next run's tail starts elsewhere.
- **Scope `WIRE_PORC` to its fixture directory.** That weakens the whole-worktree guard and only moves the first index refresh to another step.
- **Drop opens by `git status` in `fold_trace`.** That hides real content reads in a dirty tree, and `git diff` pays the same racy reads.
- **Commit main's uploaded `selftest-closures` artifact via `check --write`.** That replaces every entry with one CI run's measurement, which carries cause 1's racy tail (no settle on main). `record --step` re-measures only the refused steps.

Root cause: `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-MAIN-SELFTESTS-RED.md` (group R10-RCA-MAIN-SELFTESTS-RED, already run). Cause 1 is its shape 2 (a read set that moves between runs of one tree).

## Head

`969106255818a1279e2decdd53626b47f3cacb39` merges main `dbd1ab5` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`cd13fd1f345086d79eefe4f968f646b55a00d84d` merges the authored code head `6eaabd8038151452dc9496ec38c2eb82befe8953`.

The merge base with origin/main is 30c785330fc727ae26d6a6d2d51b38f1856fe87c. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` is clean at origin/main d08ed31049cd3636cde4d2fdeb3bd7cd4b3c842a. R10-HOTFIX-DELTA-REVIEW, repair of #3379 after it went DIRTY against main. Owner ruling (tvofi 2026-11-09): "I though it was always only the delta that was reviewed in later review rounds? If not, make it so", with the exception "only if the delta touches production code in a way such that the functionality of the other already reviewed code has a risk of being affected in a non obvious way that CI would not detect". A later round covers `git diff <reviewed-head> <head>`, each prior finding resolved and the live required checks. Only a delta touching production code (`custom_components/`) that puts already-reviewed code's functionality at non-obvious risk, in a way CI would not detect, widens it, to exactly that code; the verdict names the path and the risk. Instrument, test, policy and body deltas never widen it. The same rule is stated in fix-review.md step 12, the packet's scope line (review_packet.py) and the reviewer prompt (cloud_dispatch.py).

## Head

`762fd619773d8e6291ab0d339454bc1a8d74ed55` merges the authored code head `f26d038f142a35b09ea309ca6b50989df4ef6a44` and then merges origin/main `63bcdcaad8` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

Head f26d038f142a35b09ea309ca6b50989df4ef6a44, measured against origin/main d08ed31049cd3636cde4d2fdeb3bd7cd4b3c842a at 2026-11-11T01:31Z. This round's delta over the last reviewed head 1875f3ed3b0f38234ae30e11299c2e4632a4c422 is two commits:

- 4b7a5fc40bf82e1611ef3fd8d7a96bd9d1c0fb3e merges origin/main (a merge, not a re-cut: orchestrator.md section 7). `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only origin/main 1875f3ed3b` named one conflicted path, tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py, in five hunks. Main's side added `carry_only`/`record_pr` to `dispatch_group`, `GROUP_FLAGS` and the `--group` call, passed `roster`/`fixer` to `group_brief`, and moved the reviewer prompt's packet sentence into a `where` string that branches on a handoff review (`at_handoff`). The resolution keeps both sides: every hunk carries main's arguments and `reviewed_head`. `--reviewed-head` is now spliced into the PR branch of `where`, beside the review_packet render command, and the later-round scope sentence follows `where`. Read back: each line either parent added to cloud_dispatch.py relative to the merge base is in the merged file, or re-wrapped into a union line that keeps every one of its arguments.
- f26d038f142a35b09ea309ca6b50989df4ef6a44, policy-only: main's compression of fix-review.md left the merged file at 139 lines and 2551 tokens. Dropping "of being affected" from step 12 makes it 138 lines and 2546 tokens. The lines cap goes back to main's 140, which withdraws the earlier raise to 143, and the files_tokens cap is re-recorded at the measured 2546 (it was 2549 on this branch).

## Mutation proof

`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_hotfix_delta_review_mutants.py` at f26d038f142a35b09ea309ca6b50989df4ef6a44 ends `MUTANTS: 9 run, 0 not as required`. M0 (unmutated head) passes; M1 to M8 are KILLED. M6 removes `--reviewed-head` from the reviewer prompt, which now lives in the merged `where` string, and is killed by `FAIL a later round's reviewer renders its packet with --reviewed-head and is told its scope is the delta (fix-review.md 12); null: a first round's render names no reviewed head`. M7 and M8 are killed by `FAIL the packet's scope line: the exception names production code, non-obvious risk and CI's blindness, and the wider trigger wording is absent`.

## Null control

M0, the unmutated head, passes every self-test the mutants turn red. A first-round render names no `--reviewed-head` (the same cloud_dispatch self-test check), and a first round still renders the full diff (review_packet self-test).

## Figures

All at f26d038f142a35b09ea309ca6b50989df4ef6a44:

- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/review_packet.py --self-test`: `94 checks, 0 failed`.

The first run reported `1 of 2707 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`; the failure was `hb:positive_control`, a timing positive control whose sampler did not name a 600 ms spin. A re-run at the head passed, and so did a run at origin/main d08ed31049cd3636cde4d2fdeb3bd7cd4b3c842a started in parallel as the control. This diff touches no file in that check's path.

merges.body:
deps(tests): the pip group's bumps from Dependabot #3414, re-applied with hashes that install, homeassistant-stubs, zeroconf and cronsim held

Supersedes pull request 3414. The orchestrator closes it as superseded after the merge; this body carries no closing keyword for it.

Dependabot's branch cannot be edited, so this branch re-applies #3414's version changes (head 4182e75d7, base 32aea942e) to `tests/requirements-typing.txt`, the only file #3414 touches. It is cut from 32aea942e, an ancestor of origin/main d08ed3104. This is the third instance of the class (#3088, #3323 / pull request 3408, now #3414). The reds at #3414's head come from two causes:

1. **A stale hash on the homeassistant pin.** Dependabot moved homeassistant 2026.10.4 to 2026.11.0 and kept the previous version's `--hash` lines. pip's hash-checking mode refuses the install, which turned `tests / typing` red.
2. **homeassistant-stubs 2026.10.0.** `tests/typing_ruler.py`'s source-only lock check refuses a lock whose stubs pin disagrees with `tests/typing_budgets.json`'s `ruler`. The stubs stay at 2026.9.3 (2026.10.0 is the empty deprecation release and changes what the census measures); no budget moves.

Of #3414's seven bumps, boto3 and botocore 1.43.126 and regex 2026.11.7 land as written, and homeassistant 2026.11.0 lands with its own hashes. homeassistant-stubs is held at 2026.9.3. zeroconf and cronsim cannot be compiled under the lock's rule: homeassistant 2026.11.0 pins `zeroconf==0.152.0` and `cronsim==2.7` exactly, so #3414's 0.154.0 and 2.8 stay at homeassistant's pin and the override set does not grow. It shrinks: homeassistant 2026.11.0 stopped pinning cryptography, pillow, hass-nabucasa, orjson, python-slugify, securetar and pyopenssl lower, so the compile resolves without those seven overrides and the header names the six that remain. The lock gains httpcore2, httpx2, pyserial and truststore, which homeassistant 2026.11.0 requires, and loses nothing else. The body is the header's compile from `typing_ruler.py --print-requirements` with the override set above; the pins it resolved are the committed ones (see `## Figures`).

The header's text the bump made false is corrected (override list, the held pins, the generic PyJWT, aiohttp and yarl sentence). `.github/dependabot.yml` is untouched: triage ruled P543 (a Dependabot `ignore:` for homeassistant-stubs, zeroconf and cronsim) REJECT in batch 141, because the ignore would not have made #3088, #3323 or #3414 green (stale hashes in all three), and an ignore of zeroconf would also block the 0.152.0 move homeassistant itself needs.

## Head

`6ed9c598f2b190e3cd25153ac0f156c25d17be84` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

## Mutation proof

- The stale-hash repair: put #3414's `tests/requirements-typing.txt` (4182e75d7) in this tree. Its homeassistant 2026.11.0 block carries 2026.10.4's hash lines, none of them PyPI's for 2026.11.0, so `pip install --require-hashes --no-deps` stops with `THESE PACKAGES DO NOT MATCH THE HASHES` (CI's `tests / typing` log at 4182e75d7 shows the same refusal). This branch's block passes the per-pin PyPI comparison below.
- The comparison itself can see a corrupted pin: change one hex digit in the first homeassistant hash of this branch's body. The comparison then reads `blocks 116 bad 1` with `MISMATCH` on `homeassistant 2026.11.0`. Restored, `bad 0`.

## Null control

- The bot head is the unmodified tree for the hash claim: the same per-pin PyPI comparison on #3414's body reads `blocks 112 bad 1`, the one bad block being `homeassistant 2026.11.0`. So the zero on this branch comes from correct hashes, not from a comparison that never fires.

## Figures

- Per-pin hash check, 116 `name==version` blocks in this branch's body: for each block the `--hash` sha256 set was compared with the sha256 set of `https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json`'s `urls`; every block's set is a subset of PyPI's. Result `blocks 116 bad 0`. On #3414's body (112 blocks) `bad 1`, on main's body (112 blocks) `bad 0`. The script is an ad-hoc 20-line `urllib` loop kept in this seat's scratch, not committed (triage P544 rejected a PyPI hash checker as a `tools/` instrument; CI's `--require-hashes` install is the standing detector).
- Reproduction of the body, pin route: take this branch's body, keep only each block's `name==version` line (116 lines), and run `uv pip compile <those lines> --python-version 3.14.7 --python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_28 --generate-hashes --no-header --no-annotate --override <the six overrides: homeassistant==2026.11.0, uv==0.13.7, astral==3.2, sqlalchemy==2.1.8, acme==5.9.0, python-dateutil==4.0.0>` (uv 0.12.11 on this host). `diff` of the output against the committed body is empty (byte-identical).
- Reproduction of the body, fresh route (`python3 tests/typing_ruler.py --print-requirements` as input, same options): NOT byte-identical today, and it cannot be, because the route re-resolves unpinned names against live PyPI. Differences are exactly: bleak 3.0.2 to 3.1.0, boto3 and botocore 1.43.126 to 1.44.0, josepy 2.2.0 to 2.3.0, regex 2026.11.7 to 2026.11.9 (all released after the fixer's compile, so they are newer than #3414's proposals), and greenlet, httpcore, httpx, pytz and six present in the committed body and absent from the fresh one. The header documents this (`--print-requirements` moves unrelated packages), which is why the pin route is the reproduction claim. The five absent packages are dependencies of the newer josepy / boto3 / bleak resolutions and are not required by anything pinned at this lock; I did not verify that mechanism package by package, so it is stated as the observed difference only.
- Diff of the body against main's body (`diff` below each header): version changes are #3414's boto3, botocore, homeassistant, regex plus the zeroconf move 0.151.5 to 0.152.0 homeassistant pins; added packages are httpcore2, httpx2, pyserial, truststore.

Result: exit 0, `ALL 9 typing-ruler checks PASSED`, environment mypy 2.4.1, homeassistant-stubs 2026.9.3. `uv pip check` on that venv lists exactly the header's override set (acme, astral, sqlalchemy, uv, python-dateutil). merges.body:
Builds R10-WATER-SETPOINT-FEEDBACK from the approved design note (design/R10-WATER-SETPOINT-FEEDBACK at 1442f9067ab3592ef5ed7c3389809539324c4ad1, `Design review: approve` at d3623f5b35777e4461fe62359e03ba84997fefc6), adopted from outside pull request 3380 (contributor Bankaifan, fork head 0adb47be25e18024f4591965ad72cf4ec0b8492a, a design note only). With Pump duty control at Control and a water space set-point (`space_setpoint_unit` flow or return), `pump_arbiter._flow_target` wrote the live inlet plus `flow_min_lift_k`, re-anchored every pass, and never compared `ArbiterInputs.measured_power_kw` with the planned level, so a controller that integrates on set-point minus return ramped for the whole heating block (the contributor's Luxtronik 2.1 runs: planned 0.53 kW, measured 1.13-1.58 kW). The arbiter now closes that target on measured power: `pump_arbiter._feedback`, its run record `FeedbackRun` on `ArbiterState` (unpersisted), the qualifying predicate `_feedback_on`, and the controller-clamp adoption `_clamp_cut` in `hold`. Gated by the new option `space_setpoint_power_feedback` on the advanced Sensors and entities page, default on (tvofi 2026-11-09, Carry 4), shown for a water unit and acting only with `heat_pump_power_entity` configured; every other install writes as before (I1, pinned below). No issue: roster group R10-WATER-SETPOINT-FEEDBACK, issues `[3380]`. Close 3380 with thanks once this merges.

Contributor ask (design note's fixer item 6, not waited on): @Bankaifan, please run the note's §Acceptance on the install and report the same history tables, with the controller preconditions now in `docs/configuration.md` (heating hysteresis at most the lift; parameter 979 below the heating-season return; the integration polling within 600 s and restoring heating mode after a controller restart; no second writer of 10000/10001). The simulation below says the wind-down from the 52 Hz start programme to a 0.53 kW plan takes about two hours on a 0.5 K hysteresis; read acceptance's "±20 % after the start-hold" against the last 30 minutes of a long block, not the first.

Co-authored-by: Bankaifan <476059+Bankaifan@users.noreply.github.com>

## Design items answered in code

- Shape (§3): per qualifying pass, after `FEEDBACK_START_HOLD` (5 min) of today's target, the target moves `FEEDBACK_RATE_K_PER_MIN` (0.2 K/min, time-based, from the run's last pass) against the error of the `FEEDBACK_WINDOW` (3 min) mean draw, is held inside the deadband, and stays in `_feedback_bounds`: at most `FEEDBACK_DOWN_K` (0.3 K) below the inlet, past no stop bound or controller cut, one entity step above the gate, at most the ceiling. Unrounded `w_c` accumulates.
- Seam: `pump_arbiter.py` only computes; `coordinator.arbiter_inputs` publishes one field, `ArbiterInputs.defrosting`, the raw `PumpSignals.defrosting` (§2 design finding: `coordinator.py` joins the group's files). The arbiter asks `freq_control.defrost_interval` itself, the P2 registry's owner of that decision (`tests/entities.py` `defrost_standoff`); no new read path.
- Departure, named: the feedback is applied in `desired` around `_space_target`'s value, not threaded into `_flow_target`/`_space_target` as the note's interface section says. `_flow_target` stays the pure open-loop feed-forward that `_flow_command`, `draw_range` and the existing checks read; the loop's state is touched in one caller.
- R1 (anti-windup): `_clamp_cut`, called in `hold`'s held branch for the space slot. A reading inside `[record the loop write replaced, the write] ± SETPOINT_TOLERANCE` is adopted as the record and as a one-sided cut bound for the run; `hold` reads it as held (no rewrite, miss or `ISSUE_IGNORED`). A cut of today's write keeps today's miss and repair. Design note 10: both sides pinned in one check (0.2 K under: held, no cut; 0.4 K under: cut adopted; 35.0 °C: dropped, run reset).
- R2: option (a), today's start write kept; docs line on hysteresis. Self-caused stop: `_note_stop` records the inlet-to-write gap at a running-to-stopped edge under a loop write below today's target, and `_feedback_bounds` holds the target `FEEDBACK_STOP_MARGIN_K` closer to the inlet than that gap for the life of the `ArbiterState`.
- Design note 7 (the loop's write quantum): taken as the reviewer offered, "force a write". `_note_sent` drops the space record when the loop's target differs from it at all, so `_write`'s `SETPOINT_TOLERANCE` skip cannot leave the controller 0.3 K from the loop's value; an equal value is still not sent, so a held target stays silent (design note 5's purpose kept; `_write` and `hold`'s echo grace unchanged). Without it, the main repeat stalls (mutant "sub-tolerance resend removed", below). With it, the design's 0.3 K margin holds: one 0.1 K step plus a 0.1 K inlet rise between passes, under the 0.5 K minimum hysteresis.
- R3: the integration's polling is a docs precondition; no HPO re-write. A revert to 35.0 °C falls outside the bracket, so `hold` drops the record and `_clamp_cut` resets the run (start hold re-entered). A heating-mode revert is a docs-recorded limitation.
- R4/R5, F1-F6: the fixture below models start at return <= register - hysteresis (0.5 K and 2 K), stop at return >= register + stop hysteresis (0.5 K and 0.1 K), the [979, return limit] clamp with readback, the 35.0 °C revert, and k = 0.9 Hz/min per K cited to #3372's comment of 2026-11-09T20:39:05Z as an install measurement, not firmware. F3: the main run uses 0.1 K steps and no deadband is in kelvin. F5: docs line on a second writer; the rate limit is per loop. F6: the 5 min start hold covers the 3 min start programme.
- Deadband: `FEEDBACK_DEADBAND_SHARE` (10 %) of the planned level, or of the band floor where the plan asks less. The note's absolute 0.05 kW floor was a second module-level 0.05 kW line constant, which `tests/entities.py`'s P2 `channel_active_kw` rule refuses; the band floor is scale-free and gives 0.053 kW on the reporting install.
- Qualifying predicate: duty exactly `space`, water unit, power entity, option on, no defrost, no experiment, no space boost, planned level below the band top. The note's conjuncts for mode, plan staleness and a positive level are implied by `duty == "space"` (`_planned_duty` returns space only from a fresh Auto/Economy plan step that runs, an experiment or a boost), so each would be an unkillable mutant; they are not written.
- Design note's fixer item 2: `power_schedule` is electrical kW: `_band_kw` maps it on `min/max_electrical_power`, and `thermal_model.planned_draw_runs` reads it against the electrical floor; `_nudged` compares it with the meter directly.
- Design review note item 9: `tests/golden/config_flow.json` does not move (the seeded unit is indoor, so the `when=_water_space_setpoint` field does not render, as `flow_min_lift_k` does not), so both claim files stay byte-identical.
- Files outside the roster's `files` list, each owed by the note or the option: `coordinator.py` (§2), `entry_config.py` (the option's typed read), `translations/de.json` (Carry 4's parity), `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_water_setpoint_feedback.py` (fixer.md step 18).

## Recorded limitations, measured by the fixture

- The wind-down is bounded by k x the 0.3 K the target may sit under the inlet: from the 52 Hz start programme (1.2 kW, 2.3x a 0.53 kW plan) the main repeat reaches every-minute-within-20 % only in the block's last 30 minutes of three hours.
- At a higher level the start hold writes the level map's value (31.9 °C at 1.2 kW on a 40 °C ceiling), which drives the compressor to 90 Hz before the loop starts; that repeat needs a four-and-a-half-hour block. Changing the start write is I3, the approved design's; not changed here.
- A 0.5 K entity step: the loop stops the ramp and the speed falls, but the coarse grid rounds the 0.3 K margin away, so the draw does not reach ±20 % of plan in three hours.
- A controller that stops at register + 0.1 K: one extra start, then the learned stop bound holds the target above the inlet, where an integrating controller ramps as today. Bounded, not fixed.

## Carries

- Carry 1 (the contributor's trailer): the `Co-authored-by: Bankaifan <476059+Bankaifan@users.noreply.github.com>` line above, for the squash commit; no commit on the branch carries it, as the seat's dispatch forbids trailers in its own commits.
- Carry 2 (#3372's start-then-hold and anchor-once-per-step): closed here. The start hold (`FEEDBACK_START_HOLD`) writes today's start value, and the deadband branch of `_nudged` holds the target instead of re-anchoring it to the rising inlet; pinned by `R10-WATER-SETPOINT-FEEDBACK: a draw on plan holds the target ...` and the start-hold mutant. Design §4 A1 records why neither alone is the fix.
- Carry 3 (F1-F6, the SHI facts): answered under `## Design items answered in code` (R1-R5 and the F lines) and in `docs/configuration.md`'s preconditions; each fixture condition (start and stop hysteresis, [979, return limit] clamp with readback, 35.0 °C revert, k cited as an install measurement) is a repeat in `tests/features.py`.
- Carry 4 (owner decision: an advanced option, on by default for qualifying installs): `const.CONF_SPACE_SETPOINT_POWER_FEEDBACK`, default `True`, `EntryConfig.space_setpoint_power_feedback`, the `entities` page row with `when=_water_space_setpoint`; `strings.json`, `en`, `de` and `sv` translations; `docs/configuration.md`. A non-qualifying install keeps I1 whatever the option says (I1 check, option-off arm and no-power-entity arms). The config_flow golden does not move (indoor seed), so no claim.
- Carry 5 (design round 2 and the reviewer's notes for the fixer): R1-R5 answered as the approved note says; review note 7 (write quantum) by `_note_sent`'s sub-tolerance send, note 8 (stop model at W + 0.1 K) as its own repeat beside the W + hysteresis model, note 9 (golden claim) as above, note 10 (both sides of the bracket) in one check. The orchestrator's GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE assumption (config_flow refuses a heat-curve displacement entity with a water unit) is not built here: it is the orchestrator's routing, and this branch adds no such refusal.
- Carry 6 (r10-arbiter-off-restore's ordering note, item 0b0152d5: this group goes first on `pump_arbiter.py`, and a record it adds for the space write extends `ArbiterState.written["space_setpoint"]` and `ArbiterState.space_before` rather than adding a second): satisfied at this head. `space_before`, `_arm_space` and `_edited` are that group's and exist on neither side here (`git grep space_before` over `custom_components`: 0 files at origin/main and at 5a03cadb3, measured 2026-11-10T03:12Z; they are on `handoff/r10-arbiter-off-restore`). Every space write this branch sends, the loop's included, lands in the one persisted record `ArbiterState.written["space_setpoint"]` (`_write`, and `_clamp_cut` on a controller cut); `_persist` stores `held.written` and nothing this branch adds. What it adds beside that record is run-scoped and in memory only: `FeedbackRun.sent_c`/`prev_c` (the loop's last target and the record it replaced, read by `_clamp_cut` and `_note_stop` alone) and `ArbiterState.feedback`/`stop_gap_k`. None is an own-write refusal or an edit-adoption record, so that group's two readers stay on `written["space_setpoint"]` plus `space_before` and do not move. The one interaction they must survive, `_note_sent` dropping the record when the loop's target moves, is under `## Forward-carry`, destination that group's brief; its controls M03 and M04/M16 run on that group's branch, after this one merges.

merges.subject: Merge pull request #3417 from tvofi/fix/r10-carry-sink-barrier
merges.title: R10-CARRY-SINK-BARRIER: r10 carry sink barrier
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-CARRY-SINK-BARRIER: the owner-approved barrier (tvofi 2026-11-10). A carry goes to the live group owning the seam; where none exists, the producing group keeps the fix. Before this change `carry_audit.py` refused only a destination gone or at a `CARRY_CLOSED` stage, and `roster_edit.py append-carry` and `roster_sync.py carry_plan` accepted any open group, so a carry could be parked on a group whose pull request had already merged (`carries-open`) or on a group created only to receive carries.

This is policy (`finding-propagation.md` changes what a seat must do). It is merged under the mandate and surfaced to tvofi.

The fix is one predicate, `roster_lib.carry_receivable`, read by every destination reader:
- `carry_audit.Dests.live`, which `Dests.check` uses for the group token, for the issue token (`Dests.receiving`, round 2) and for the refusal's valid-target list;
- `roster_edit.py` `append-carry`, `mark-carry moved` and `set-stage absorbed --into`;
- `roster_sync.carry_plan`.

`carry_receivable` refuses two things:
- a stage in the new `roster_lib.CARRY_DEST_CLOSED`, which is `CARRY_CLOSED` plus `carries-open` and `refuted`;
- a receiver-only sink: a group with no `resume.pr`, no `issues`, no `fixes` and a recorded `files` list that is empty.

Every refusal names the rule.

Design choices the reviewer should check:
- **`CARRY_CLOSED` itself is unchanged.** It also decides what a group still *holds* (`stranded`, `legacy_carries`, `roster_report`). A carries-open group must keep holding and discharging its own carries, so the destination set is a separate tuple derived from it.
- **The sink test does not count a brief as work.** All 431 groups on the round roster have a non-empty brief, and `append-group` requires one, so a "no brief" test could never fire on a real group.
- **The sink test keys on `files == []`, not a missing key.** A group with no `files` key has an unrecorded seam, not an empty one. The self-test fixtures that omit the key stay live.
- **No live group on the round roster is a sink today** (harness below), so that arm guards the next sink and takes nothing away now.

Alternatives considered:
- Widening `CARRY_CLOSED` would have stranded every pending carry on the 10 carries-open groups in `carry_audit.py roster`, and changed `set-stage` closing.
- Fixing `carry_audit.py` alone, as the brief scoped it, would have left `append-carry` and `roster_sync` writing the carries the audit then refuses. That route is the one that parked them.

Closes no issue: the group lists none.

## Round 2

Answers verdict/3417 (blocked 34a9cf1251fa6046f3182a21aea60a84b477609f, class-open).

- **The block.** `Dests.check` accepted `Carry: #N` whenever `owns(n)`, and `Dests.__init__` fills `owned` from every `is_open` group, carries-open and refuted included. So a carry refused on the group token passed when re-spelled as the group's issue (#3313, #2728). The round-1 census below misfiled `Dests.__init__` as "issue ownership"; it is also the destination test for `#N`.
- **The fix.** `Dests.__init__` now also builds `receiving`: the issues of every group `Dests.live` (that is, `roster_lib.carry_receivable`) accepts, plus every carry-file issue and every issue an O-brief names. `check` refuses an owned `#N` outside `receiving`, naming the owner, its stage and the rule. There is one rule and no second copy: the issue arm calls the group arm's `self.live`. `owned` and `owns` are unchanged, so `sweep --issues` and `orphaned` behave as before.
  - **A design choice to check:** an issue counts as receivable if *any* open group listing it is live, a carry file owns it, or an O-brief names it. A carries-open group that shares an issue with a live group does not block a carry, because that issue has a live owner.
- **Merge.** origin/main was merged into the handoff (44c77b585, claimnotes driver, no conflict). That brings in #3409/#3410's selftest-closures changes.
- **The reviewer's ci_predict.py finding** (Carry: R10-CARRY-SINK-BARRIER) is in this group's own seam, so it is built here. `ci_predict.self_test` picked the first `is_open` group as the carry destination it predicts green. It now picks with `carry_audit.Dests.live`. Commit a8563e945 restores that line: a mutant-restore race in this seat's own run left the `is_open` mutant in 27a61185f's copy of `ci_predict.py`. The three-dot diff at the head carries the fix.

## Approval

This is a policy change: `dev/governance/rules/finding-propagation.md` and its generated copies. The barrier is owner-approved per the group's brief (tvofi 2026-11-10), which says it merges under the mandate and is surfaced to tvofi. The approval itself is recorded at merge, by one of:
- tvofi's approving review at this head;
- an approving review citing mandate 6329234399 (scope all), if that mandate is in force when it merges.

This seat holds no approval.

## Head

`37555ea332a069d698366d7c41341d971ce3a613` merges the authored code head `a8563e94535f3838b0f43ff4ce2dfe6645c0fdb0`.

a8563e94535f3838b0f43ff4ce2dfe6645c0fdb0, merge base 04dfcafccdde1ee5df21a02fe4f06a5bc1083ea0 (origin/main at 2026-11-10T11:18:11Z). Round 1 was measured at 22f3ba79a7a6f2832bb37d4bfa97b627459226db and reviewed at 34a9cf1251fa6046f3182a21aea60a84b477609f.

- M1, the issue-token predicate `if n not in self.receiving` changed to `if False`: the same 2 FAIL, rc 1.
- M2, `receiving` filled by `roster_lib.is_open` (the base rule) instead of `self.live`: the same 2 FAIL, rc 1.
- M3, an O-brief's issue not added to `receiving`: 2 FAIL, `an O-brief owns the issues its file name carries` and `sink barrier (null control): a carry to #906 passes, an O-brief names it`, rc 1.

This mutant is killed only while the in-tree roster's first open group is not receivable. At this merge base that group is R10-PREPR-CAP, at carries-open.

- `W6` (append-carry check → `if False`): rc=1, fails=6, first `append-carry to a done group refuses and writes nothing (carry 3)`.
- `W12` (absorb `--into` check → `if False`): rc=1, fails=3, including `sink barrier: set-stage absorbed --into R9-WC is refused` and `... --into R9-WS is refused`.
- `L7` (new: `CARRY_DEST_CLOSED = CARRY_CLOSED`): rc=1, fails=1, `carry_receivable: carries-open, refuted and every CARRY_CLOSED stage take no carry`.
- `L8` (new: sink clause dropped): rc=1, fails=1, `carry_receivable: a receiver-only sink (no PR, issue or fix; files []) takes none`.

Both stages that projection chooses between (done, carries-open) now refuse the carry, and the write path discards the refusal text (`appends, _`). At base: rc=1, fails=1. Here: rc=0, fails=0.

MUTANT-SYNC, tree 22f3ba79a: `roster_sync.carry_plan` reads `is_open` again. `roster_sync.py --self-test`: 2 failed of 96:

`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_carry_parser_mutants.py`: `L-landed`, `L-words` and `L-source` matched nothing at main (`landed()` was reworded by 67a823c2e) and are re-anchored here. Each is killed: failed=12, 4 and 2, `survived=0`. Its 6 `UNMAPPED` sites are all in `seg_dests`, which this diff does not touch.

Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's releases.

v4.39.3

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

v4.39.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode.   • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

Bumps the site group with 1 update in the /tools/site directory: [mermaid](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid). Updates `mermaid` from 12.2.0 to 12.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from mermaid's releases.

mermaid@12.3.0

Minor Changes

  • #8164 592d0e4 Thanks @​filipsajdak! - feat: add the open-arrow and hollow-circle edge markers, so a notation can tell two kinds of flow apart by whether the head is filled

  • #8165 5c8aa5d Thanks @​filipsajdak! - feat: add the BPMN element shapes - events, gateways, activities, data objects, data stores and text annotations - each reporting where a line meets what is drawn

  • #8470 692d22a Thanks @​openmindednewby! - feat: flowchart edges accept a step number (e1@{ step: 1 }); a dot travels the edges in step order and loops, hidden under prefers-reduced-motion

  • #8478 56aa105 Thanks @​openmindednewby! - feat: add flowchart.stepDuration to set how many seconds each step of the flowchart step animation lasts

  • #8479 800f7ef Thanks @​openmindednewby! - feat: highlight the flowchart edge whose step is playing, in sync with the step animation dot

  • #8480 50d6294 Thanks @​openmindednewby! - feat: add flowchart.stepNumbers to show each step edge's number in a badge

Patch Changes

  • #8443 2ff8286 Thanks @​knsv-bot! - fix: agentflow renders the a[/…/] short form as an input instead of falling back to a task with a SHAPE_UNSUPPORTED warning

  • #8661 b200b27 Thanks @​pbrolin47! - fix: Bump DOMPurify to 3.4.17 to address GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7 and GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2

  • #8633 686f350 Thanks @​sidharthv96! - chore: Remove the uuid dependency and the unused legacy ER diagram renderer

  • #8661 7eec083 Thanks @​pbrolin47! - fix: Stop an edge from a node inside a subgraph from crossing an edge from the subgraph itself to the same node with ELK 0.10+ (e.g. outer --> a with da --> a, or three --> two with two --> c2)

  • #8532 42d3760 Thanks @​Devehab! - fix: upgrade bundled elkjs from 0.9.3 to 0.12.0, which is licensed EPL-2.0 OR GPL-3.0-or-later, so GPL-3.0 projects can ship mermaid with ELK

  • #8162 d5ca27a Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix(swimlanes): size a lane that holds a nested subgraph (TB drew it as an empty 0x0 box, and likewise an outer group holding lanes), and grow LR and RL lanes by the nested group's padding

  • #8405 b4299f2 Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix: do not draw a stray empty swimlane when a node is listed in two lanes, and warn about it and about a subgraph nested in a lane

  • #8385 37d0ace Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix(swimlanes): keep two arrowheads that land on one face of a node apart when a sibling edge is straightened

  • #8385 38e810a Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix(swimlanes): an edge routed round the outside of a diamond now arrives at one of its vertices instead of ending in empty space beside it

  • #8385 25d7e31 Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix(swimlanes): a second edge leaving a diamond on the same level as its target now leaves from a free vertex instead of running beside the first

  • #8171 a4750b4 Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix: dock a swimlane edge on the shape it points at, so a line reaches an event's ring instead of stopping at the room its caption reserves

merges.body:
R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE-PERSISTENT, kind `persistent` of the heat-curve number-entity control, and `off_restore`'s C1–C4, built under the owner's ruling (tvofi, #201, 2026-11-07: "Offset kind and a later persistent kind, both in this round. Turning the optimizer off should restore the baseline") and the approved note `design.md` on `design/R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE-PERSISTENT` at `a64af2b343b826d253eb86ce2dfe4f12f67da9b9` (`design-verdict/R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE-PERSISTENT` `c47d6e5e27b22a84c8981ead52f506ac87510f83`). Stacked on #3299 (R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE) under the owner's 2026-11-09 workaround ruling; see `## Head`. Outside contribution: PR 3284 by Bankaifan, read as data. There is no finding and no issue to close: the build is the owner's ruling. No finder harness: owner report.

**Fix review 1 (`verdict/3402`, nonce `ebe7cc587c7af6e31ee31c16557d769e`, blocked, config-attack), repaired in this round.** A hand edit adopted while displaced (P6) stored `reading - (written - b)` with no bound, so an edit near the range's edge armed a baseline the entity cannot hold and off wrote it. `write_persistent` now adopts `_within_range(reading - (written - b), reading)`: the edit's own difference, bounded to the entity's declared range. `_within_range` is the clamp `persistent_target` already applied to every plan write (I1), moved into one helper both call, so the bound has one owner. The candidate fix the brief names, taken as named; the alternatives and why each lost:
- Refuse the adoption (keep the old baseline): the next plan write re-sends 25 over the user's 21, fighting the edit by 4 K where the bound fights it by 2 K; and the stored baseline stays one the user overrode.
- Bound the restore value instead of the stored baseline (keep 18, write 20 at off): the user's 21 is then held at displace +3 with no write, but the record keeps a baseline the entity cannot hold, so `async_forget`'s "set it to 18 by hand" stays wrong, every plan write from it saturates and latches the range warning, and the shared `off_restore` restore path (the arbiter's too) would need the entity's range at restore time, when an unload may find it unavailable. Two values for one concept, and a change to the shared hook this group does not own alone.

**Departure from the note's P6, stated for the owner's mandate.** P6 adopts the edit's whole difference. At the range's edge it now adopts the nearest value the entity holds, and the optimizer displaces from there: range 20..35, 22 displaced +3 to 25, set to 21 by hand, adopts 20 (not 18), the plan's +3 then writes 23, and off restores 20. So at the edge a hand edit is not held unwritten at the displace in force, as P6 holds it inside the range: the plan's next write moves it by `b + d - reading` (2 K here). That is the bound's price, and the check pins it, so a later seat reads it as a choice and not a bug. Verdict consequence (b), "a later displace 0 writes 20, not the user's 21": the neutral still writes 20, and that is P6's own behaviour, now no longer the range's saturation. Inside the range P6 moves the user's setting by the whole displace in force at neutral (the null control: an edit to 24 at +3 adopts 21, and the neutral writes 21, 3 K below the user's 24). What the bound changes is that the neutral, the armed baseline and the off restore are now one value (20, 20, 20), where before they were 20 (saturated, warning latched), 18 and 18.

**Budget 1 (the verdict's residual).** `heat_curve_persistent_writes_per_day` = 1 writes nothing, as 0 does, because one write is always kept back for the restore (I2). The minimum stays 0 (a number selector cannot skip 1, and 0 is the documented off); `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/ecl110.md` and the en/sv/de descriptions now say "0 or 1 writes nothing", and the budget-0 check now drives 1 beside it.

**What changed over #3299's head** (round 1).
- `off_restore.py` (the one owner of the record, C1–C4). C1: a `neutral=None` consumer's armed entry is `{"entity_id", "value"}`; it is restored by rule R (its value to its own entity, whatever the config now names), through the consumer's `Restorer.write` or, when the factory answers None, the writer registered by `register_consumer(key, factory, write=)`. An arm naming another entity, or a neutral kind, restores the recorded entity first and refuses the write when that fails; a `None` entry under a `neutral=None` restorer is dropped unwritten. A baseline restore whose write answers False is a failure. A neutral entry keeps #3299's `None` and every path it had (ruling (a)). `restored(entry, entity_id, value)`. C2: `async_rebaseline`. C3: a `state` section of the same record (`async_consumer_state`, `consumer_state`, `async_save_state`), written only when a consumer has one. C4: `async_forget` names each still-armed baseline once and writes nothing. `OFF_RESTORE_STORE_VERSION` stays 1.
- `heat_curve.py`: kind `persistent` is a second `Restorer` of the consumer `heat_curve` (`neutral=None`, `baseline_of` the entity's own reading, writer `write_setpoint` registered). `write_persistent`: the P7 refusals at every write, `classify` (ours / in grace / missed / edit), the edit adopted through `async_rebaseline` (P6), `persistent_target` (baseline + displace in whole steps toward the baseline, inside the band and the range: I1), then W1, the wall-clock dwell (P5), the W3 latch on a second miss, the per-local-day budget with one write kept back for the restore (P4, I2), `async_arm`, the write-ahead record and the write. W4 is not consulted for this kind (ghcp-r2). Kind `offset` is unchanged in behaviour; its write tail is now `_send`, shared by both kinds.
- Options: the kind selector offers `persistent`; three rows (`heat_curve_persistent_band_k` 3 K in 0.5–5, `heat_curve_persistent_writes_per_day` 12 in 0–48, `heat_curve_persistent_min_dwell_minutes` 60 in 15–360) shown only under the stored kind `persistent`; `_heat_curve_errors` applies P7 (unreadable, or a reading outside its own range) to kind `persistent` and T2 to kind `offset` only. Strings en/sv, `docs/ecl110.md` "Kind persistent", `docs/configuration.md` rows, `README.md` surface row and removal note.

**Departures from the note, raised here for the reviewer.**
1. The reserve rule is `count + 2 > writes_per_day` for every write, not the note's `count + 1 + (target ≠ b)`. The note's form breaks its own I2 when the plan returns to the baseline while armed: at budget 2, displace 24 (count 1), then displace 0 writes 22 (1 + 1 + 0 = 2, allowed, count 2), and the off restore writes 22 again (count 3 > 2). The return write leaves the key armed, so a restore always follows. Check "budget 2: one displace and its restore; a second displace, or a return to the baseline the restore would repeat, is refused" pins it, and mutant M02 (the note's `+ 1`) fails it.
2. The record accessors load on demand, so they are async and take `hass`: `async_armed_entry(hass, entry, key)` and `async_consumer_state(hass, entry, key)`, plus a sync `consumer_state(entry, key)` for the `restored` callback, which runs inside a restore whose record is loaded. The note's sync `armed_entry(entry, key)` would read None before the record's first load after a restart and re-capture the displaced value (O3).
3. `previous` is the reading before the write, not the last `written`, so a first write that never landed reads as missed, not as the user's edit (check "a reading still at the write before is the write missing").
4. The persistent restore callback is `_persistent_restored`, beside kind offset's `_restore_recorded`; the consumer state also holds `entity_id`, `misses` and `refused_day`.
5. `_Held`'s consumer-state field is `consumers` (persisted under `state`), because a second class attribute named `state` untyped `self._external_heat.state` and raised `name_kept_members` (`## Figures`).

## Head

## Forward-carry

- The range bound at adoption binds any baseline the arbiter rebaselines from a hand edit: an adopted baseline must be a value the entity holds, or off writes one it refuses. Control: this PR's M21 (floor 18, ceiling 37). Carry: R10-ARBITER-OFF-RESTORE

A baseline consumer's record must not key its own state on an attribute named `state` of a class (the `name_kept_members` ratchet). Lands in that group's entry in `dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json`. Carry: R10-ARBITER-OFF-RESTORE

comments.body:
Fix review: blocked b10beaad55c9fdb50ec8446bb3593c3ca11d8bd0 config-attack: an edit adopted near the range floor rebaselines outside the entity's own range, so off writes a value the entity refuses

bus-nonce: ebe7cc587c7af6e31ee31c16557d769e

Round 1 (no earlier `Fix review:` on #3402). Measured head `b10beaad55c9fdb50ec8446bb3593c3ca11d8bd0`, the head the body names (step 7). #3299 has merged (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e066a630 origin/main` exits 0), so the three-dot diff from merge base `b0762725099f` is this group's alone.

## Block

P6's adoption, `baseline = reading.value - (state["written"] - baseline)` in `heat_curve.write_persistent`, and the `async_rebaseline` it feeds store a baseline with no bound to the entity's declared range. `persistent_target` clamps every plan write to the range (I1), but the restore writes the adopted baseline unclamped. The persistent kind's own refusal rule (P7, `outside_own_range`) is about the value the entity reads, and the restore then writes it a value outside that range.

Measured with the block driver (`ev/probe_range_floor.diff`, `ev/probe_range_floor.out`; the fixtures are the block's own `_ghcp_coord`, `_ghcp_reads`, `_ghcp_age`, `_ghcp_off`): number.x with step 0.5 and range 20..35 reads 22, displace +3 writes 25, and the user sets 21 by hand. After the dwell the next publish adopts the edit: armed `{'entity_id': 'number.x', 'value': 18.0}`, and off then sends 18 (`all writes [25, 18]`), below the entity's min 20. Null control: the same sequence with an edit to 24, inside the range, adopts 21 (`armed {'entity_id': 'number.x', 'value': 21.0}`).

Consequences:
- (a) In Home Assistant the restore fails. The fixture's stub service accepts 18, but `inputs.write_setpoint` calls with `blocking=True` and does no clamp (inputs.py:597-616), and HA's `number.set_value` and `input_number.set_value` refuse a value outside min/max. That refusal is from reading HA, not measured here. The restore is then latched and the key stays armed for good: every later off retries, and `async_forget` tells the user to "set it to 18 by hand", a value the entity cannot hold.
- (b) The plan is wrong while armed. After the same edit a later displace 0 writes 20, not the user's 21 (`floor, then displace 0: writes [25, 20]`), so the optimizer's neutral moves the user's own setting 1 K down and spends budget doing it.
- (c) The same applies at the ceiling, by symmetry (not run).

Trigger: a hand edit, made while displaced, that comes within the band of the range's edge (≤ 5 K, the band's maximum). It reaches the owner's ruling "Turning the optimizer off should restore the baseline". The candidate fix is small: bound the adopted baseline to `[reading.lo, reading.hi]` at adoption, or refuse to adopt. It is a departure from the design note's P6, so the fixer raises it with the designer. Its proof is the probe above turned into a check, with a mutant that drops the bound.

## Findings

- Follow-up: surviving mutant R21 (`ev/mutants_independent.log`): `_write_persistent_target` with `_send` moved ahead of `_record_write` and `async_save_state` (no write-ahead) passes all 102 checks of the block. No check observes the order. The order is what keeps a crash between the send and the record from reading as the user's edit on restart, which would rebaseline onto the optimizer's own write. The design's "write-ahead crash (reading = previous)" check sets up the residue and never the order. A check whose writer reads the persisted record at call time would pin it, and the arbiter's own write-ahead of its consumer state owes the same check. Carry: R10-ARBITER-OFF-RESTORE
- Residual: `heat_curve_persistent_writes_per_day` = 1 writes nothing, the same as 0, because the reserve rule is `count + 2 > budget`: the probe shows `budget1 writes []` against `budget2 writes [24]`. The options range is 0-48, and `docs/configuration.md`'s row and the en/sv descriptions say only "0 writes nothing", so 1 reads as one write a day. The fixer can fix it in this re-cut: name 1 beside 0 in the docs, or raise the minimum to 2. Carry: dismissed: owed by this same PR's re-cut under the block above, not a later stage

## Evidence

merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-RECORD-ISSUE-CONTINUATION: post #201 records to a continuation issue
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-RECORD-ISSUE: #201, the programme's coordination and record issue, hit GitHub's 2,500-comment cap. Every comment on it is now refused with `HTTP 403: Commenting is disabled on issues with more than 2500 comments`, so `record_beat.py` printed OWED for #3350's record line and every later merge would do the same. Owner ruling (tvofi, 2026-11-09 ~22:35Z), answering whether to open a continuation issue and move the policy and tools to it: "Yes". The continuation is #3394, "Programme coordination and record (continuation of #201)". #201's body now starts with a line pointing to it. A body edit is not a comment, so it still lands.

The design is one definition. `tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py`, which already owned the tracking-issue constant (`MANDATE_ISSUE`) that `gh_comment.py` and `merge_train.py` import, now holds `RECORD_ISSUES = (201, 3394)` and `RECORD_ISSUE = RECORD_ISSUES[-1]`, plus `on_record_issue(comment)`. Writers post to `RECORD_ISSUE`. Readers of the record (a mandate grant, its revocation) read every issue in `RECORD_ISSUES`. Mandate 6715477401 is on #201 and still resolves by id, since comment ids are global. A revocation the owner posts on #3394 still voids a #201 grant. Before this change, the kill switch could only be read on #201, which can no longer take a comment, so it would have been dead.

- Writers: `record_beat.py` (the merge line; the template now ends `Leaves #3394 open.`), `nightly.yml`'s record-autofix comment (it reads the constant through `python3 -I -c ... from budget_raise_gate import RECORD_ISSUE`, pinned by `tests/entities.py`), and `handover_prompt.py`'s coordination step.
- Readers: `budget_raise_gate._mandate`, `merge_train._mandate_read` and `orchestrator_tick._thread` read every record issue. `plan_page.py` and `carry_audit.py` leave both issues out of the open-issue and orphan counts, so #3394 does not show up as an unplanned orphan.
- Guards: `gh_comment.py`'s mandate guard covers a post or patch on any record issue, with the grants read from every record thread. A new `closed_record_guard` refuses a post to #201 and names #3394 instead of returning a bare 403. A patch to an old #201 comment still passes, because edits still land. The seat-gh shim's deny-by-default guard is now `trackers='201 3394'`. `gh_calls.py`'s self-test pins that line to `RECORD_ISSUES`, refuses a raw post and a `gh issue comment` on #3394, and runs a mutant that drops it.
- Policy: `CLAUDE.md` (index rows), `delivery-status-tracking.md` item 3, `writing-for-agents.md`, `orchestrator.md`, `nudge.md`, `HANDOVER.md`, instrument pages, `sweep_template.md` and the two web workflows now name #3394. `.claude/rules` and `.cursor/rules` were regenerated.
- Kept deliberately: `governance.yml`'s `delivery-status-publish` still splices the ledger region into #201's **body**. Body edits are unaffected by the cap, and `tests/delivery_status.py` and `tests/entities.py` pin that region where readers look for it. Historical citations of the form `#201 comment <id>` are reads of the record and stay as written. Decision records (0009, 0011-0016) record what was decided and are not rewritten.

Repair after prepr refused the first open: `carry_audit.py` imported `RECORD_ISSUES` from `budget_raise_gate` at module level. pr-contract's carry step runs the head's `carry_audit.py` beside the base's restored `budget_raise_gate.py`, which has no `RECORD_ISSUES`, so `check --body` died with `ImportError` (prepr's `ci predict` predicted pr-contract red). prepr's own self-test copies `carry_audit.py` with `roster_lib.py` alone into a fixture, so that would have stayed red on main after the merge. Only the roster arm reads the record issues, so `carry_audit.log_issues()` now imports them when called, and `check --body` needs no gate. The `R3` plant in `r10_roster_ops_mutants.py` moves to the new line.

Alternatives considered:
- A second constant per writer. Refused: it is the drift this replaces.
- A new `record_issue.py` leaf module. Refused: a new tracked file needs a measured closure re-derived off Linux, and `budget_raise_gate.py` was already the module the guard and the train import "for one definition of the revocation test, the grant reading and the tracking issue" (gh_comment.py `_gate`).
- Having the shim read the number at run time from `budget_raise_gate.py`. Refused: it costs a python spawn on every gh call, and an unreadable file would need a fail-open or fail-closed choice. The literal plus a self-test pin is the mechanism already in the tree.

After the merge (an action, not a carried finding):

- After this merges, the orchestrator re-runs `tools/audit/seat/seat_venv.sh --install-shims <bin dir>` on each host. Installed shim copies keep the old `tracker=201` until then, so #3394 is unguarded on that host. The install is a host action, not a tree change.
- `budget-raise-gate` runs the gate from the base commit, so a mandate or revocation on #3394 is read by that gate only from the first base that carries this merge. Until then, every grant in force (6715477401) is on #201, which the old gate reads.

## Head

`823d472de04391e40f80468e0b17073d94ccbe25` merges main `04dfcaf` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution (the branch predates main's governance.yml and selftest_closures.json changes (#3409/#3410/#3416); no conflict). The reviewed code is unchanged.

`9b903a91ab9e1ed5d439729aa09b67766492ff5f` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`bda8bdf60248e8a5f7ae28a35928bc4275271c73`, origin/main `e3295ba4621f524a1aa4377f7ee219a4ade59efb` merged in (merge base `e3295ba462`). Figures below without a repair note were measured at the first handoff, `6604ac0856`, on merge base `b8f67a7751`.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant edits `tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py`, the one definition. The four self-tests listed below run against it, and the file is restored with `git checkout` after each mutant:
- **M1**, writers back to #201 (`RECORD_ISSUE = RECORD_ISSUES[0]`): killed. `record_beat` fails `the comment goes to the record issue, never #201 (closed to comments at its cap)`. `gh_comment` fails `arm6_a_grant_on_the_continuation_issue_is_guarded`, `arm6_record_issues_are_201_then_its_continuation` and `arm7_a_post_to_201_is_refused_naming_the_record_issue`. `budget_raise_gate` fails `mandate: the record issue is the last of RECORD_ISSUES, and #201 one of them`.
- **M2**, #201 no longer read as a record issue (`on_record_issue` over `RECORD_ISSUES[-1:]`): killed. `budget_raise_gate` has 9 failures, among them `mandate: a mandate on #201, the record before the comment cap, still passes` and the e2e `a raise approved at the head under a mandate in force exits 0`. `gh_comment` has 6, among them `arm6_brief_row_refused_on_post`. `orchestrator_tick` has 5, among them `record issues: null control: the same #201 grant with no revocation is in force` and `MAIN mandate: mandate in force`.
- **M3**, the gate's revocation thread reads #201 only (`for n in RECORD_ISSUES[:1]` in `_mandate`): killed by `budget_raise_gate` e2e `... after reading the comment, every record issue since it was written, then the body`.
- **Repair**, carry_audit's module-level import back (`git show f583ccfc9a^:tools/audit/carry_audit.py`) in a tree with origin/main's `budget_raise_gate.py`: `check --body BODY.md` exits 1 with `ImportError: cannot import name 'RECORD_ISSUES' from 'budget_raise_gate'`. `r10_roster_ops_mutants.py R1 R2 R3 R4 R5`: `plants: 5, without a FAIL line: none`; R3 (record issues reported) fails `roster (null): an issue a live group lists, in issues or fixes, and the record issues are not reported`.
- **Shim**: `gh_calls.py --self-test` carries its own mutant, `mutant: the continuation dropped from the trackers lets its planted post through`, which is killed. That self-test also pins `trackers=` to `RECORD_ISSUES`.

Script that ran M1 to M3 and the null, with the four self-tests named in the null below: a bash loop of `sed -i` on the line, then `timeout 600 python3 <tool> <self-test flag>`, then `git checkout -q -- tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py`. `git status --short | wc -l` printed `0` after it.

## Null control

Repair: the same tree with the fixed `carry_audit.py` exits 0, `CARRY-AUDIT: 0 finding item(s): 0 routed, 0 unrouted, 0 bad destination(s)`.

The same four self-tests on the unmutated head: `record_beat self-test: 17 checks, 0 failed`; `gh_comment.py self-test`: `TOTAL: 0 failed`, `SELF-TEST PASSED`; `budget_raise_gate self-test: 277 checks, 0 failed`; `orchestrator_tick self-test: 304 checks, 0 failed`. A post or a `gh issue comment` on the issue after the continuation (#3395) still reaches the real gh (`gh_calls.py` `null control: a gh issue comment on the issue after it reaches the real gh`), and a #201 post to another repository is not refused (`arm7_a_post_to_201_of_another_repository_passes (null control)`). A #201 grant with no revocation is in force (`record issues: null control` in the tick).

At `origin/main` (`git archive` of tools/ into scratch) the same failure appears: `196 checks, 1 failed`. CI runs Linux bash.
