merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-COMBI-TANK-STORE (R10-COMBI-TANK PR A, L; design `a605014bff4478f470853109060f4ff7ef605d4c`, approved by `design-verdict/r10-combi-tank` `56810263b`, Cost and Order section's PR A scope). Issue #3225 (outside user Bankaifan): a combi store, where one body of heating water serves the space circuit and hot water through an exchanger, cannot be modelled; entering the store as both tanks counts its heat twice. This PR lands the store physics. **No loader or option sets `dhw_combi_tank_enabled`**, so no install can reach combi, and with the option off every plan is byte-identical (golden drift, below). Refs #3225; PR B (R10-COMBI-TANK, topic `r10-combi-tank-b`) makes it reachable and closes it. This PR closes no issue.

What changes:
- **`thermal_model.py` owns the store.** `DhwStore` (frozen, module level) is the one view every hot-water recursion reads, through `ThermalParameters.dhw_store`. Off combi it is the separate tank's own values and both transforms return their argument itself. In combi it is the buffer store over `buffer_store_volume` (buffer plus potable litres), with the buffer's UA, the tighter of the DHW and buffer limits, and the exchanger effectiveness `combi_dhw_effectiveness` (floored at `COMBI_DHW_EFFECTIVENESS_FLOOR`, capped at 1). `combi_tank_active` is the design's predicate. The tank type is two numbers (`combi_dhw_effectiveness`, `combi_potable_volume_l`), never a code branch.
- **One step, both stores.** `store_step` is the hot-water step for the separate tank and the combi store alike; `simulate_dhw_step`'s body was a second copy of exactly this physics and now calls it, bitwise identical off combi. The draw is debited at the tap temperature (`tap_temp_for_store`), the rating clamp and inlet floor book what they refuse or inject, so `C·dT = (heat_in − draw − loss − refused + injected)·dt` per step.
- **The flux exchange (design, Solver).** The space steps (`_simulate_step_single`, `_simulate_step_two_zone`, `simulate_trajectory_batch`) take the hot-water side's net flux as `WeatherSeries.buffer_exo_kw`, joined to the tank's input behind the valve; every DHW recursion takes the space side's as `tank_exo_kw`. The published walk (`simulate_trajectory_with_dhw`) is one node: its DHW trajectory is its buffer trajectory.
- **Departure, raised: the exchange is a bounded repair, not a scored candidate.** The design's one extra iteration under the "adopt only if it scores better" gate never adopts: the replan buys more hot water, so it always scores worse on the space objective, and the space side drains the store below the DHW floor. `_combi_flux_exchange` re-plans hot water against the fixed space plan's net flux until the plan stops moving, at most `_COMBI_EXCHANGE_ROUNDS` DHW builds, and keeps the space plan it was computed against: a space re-solve would draw the repair straight back out.
- **Readers moved to the view** (census `combi_store_view`), **tap limits enter the store frame and the legionella target never does** (census `combi_tap_limit`), and **every DHW walk carries the space flux** (census `combi_flux_live`). `buffer_store_volume` keeps the `dhw_combi_tank_enabled` conjunct ahead of `combi_tank_active`: off the option its two per-step readers then evaluate no predicate, which `tests/stress.py`'s production-call channel reads.

## Re-cut

Fourth round (`fixer.md`, "Past three rounds"). Round 3 blocked `577c6974205926e7dbaa178b91af96a229ea02f3` on CI state alone (`verdict/3358` `36f106fd9`): no code change was owed. This head merges `origin/main` `b8f67a775137a8032d5c71b34ea64165c1d4613a` into it with no conflict and no resolution, so the reviewed patch is unchanged (`## Figures`, patch identity). Every figure below was re-taken at this head; round history is deleted.

**Disclosed self-correction, kept:** round 1 said the `and` in `buffer_store_volume` "carried two BOOLOP sites no input could separate"; the production-call count separates them, `tests/stress.py` read it red in round 2, and the conjunct was restored there.

## Head

`d07f8e9ea5a78bf44ea405ef233ae11ad7e1c211` merges the authored code head `6254262796cdec57bec1dec5c0d038ba933a215a`.

Head 6254262796cdec57bec1dec5c0d038ba933a215a: `Merge origin/main into fix/r10-combi-tank-pr`, parents `577c6974205926e7dbaa178b91af96a229ea02f3` (the round-3 head) and `origin/main` `b8f67a775137a8032d5c71b34ea64165c1d4613a`, merged 2026-11-10 UTC. Every figure below was taken at this head.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant of `thermal_model.py:329` (`buffer_store_volume`'s guard) was applied in a detached worktree at this head and the whole of `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` run:
- Unmutated: `ALL 5071 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, rc 0.
- **MA**, the conjunct dropped (`if self.combi_tank_active:`): `1 of 5071 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`, rc 1: `off the combi option the buffer's store volume, capacity and UA evaluate no combi predicate; null control: with the option on the volume evaluates it and adds the coil` `[off: 3 predicate evaluation(s), ...; on: 1, 544.0]`.
- **MB**, the predicate dropped (`if self.dhw_combi_tank_enabled:`): `1 of 5071 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`, rc 1, the same check by its null arm `[off: 0 ...; on: 0, 544.0]`.

The store physics, the flux exchange and the three censuses are killed by the `R10-COMBI-TANK-STORE` block of `tests/features.py` and the pinned and triaged sites in `tests/mutation_ledger/` the earlier rounds landed; this pass re-took none of those per-mutant runs, because the merge changed no line of this diff (`## Figures`, patch identity). Two of them, named M2 (the exo term dropped from the LP's free recursion) and M4 (dropped from the legionella run-up walk) in the round that ran them, fail only the `combi_flux_live` census, which `## Forward-carry` cites.

## Null control

- **Option off, the whole plan:** golden drift against the merge base (`## Figures`); no claim file is touched.

merges.body:
This is the root-cause seat for R10-RCA-ROSTER-DRAIN-REPLAY, run beside R10-HOTFIX-ROSTER-DRAIN-REPLAY and never inside it. It names the cause, process state **(d)**, the cost test, and a countermeasure built here. The analysis is `dev/audit/rca/r10-rca-roster-drain-replay.md`, and its `_rca` entry is in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`. `beat_jobs.py` and `beatd.jobs.json` are untouched; they belong to the hotfix.

**Cause:**
- The beat's drain runs each queue line at least once. A pass killed at `timeout_s` 900 had pushed its ops but never written `roster-done.json`, so the next pass re-ran them.
- `drop-carry <group> <index>` resolves its index again on every run. Each replay therefore deleted whatever entry had shifted into that index.

**Why the index form exists:** `9969e3ca8` (2026-10-18, #2513) added it for a caller that runs an op once. That caller is a human who has just read `jq '.carry[N]'`. Nothing ran a queue automatically until #3197 on 2026-11-05.

**Countermeasure:** `roster_queue.replay_unsafe` refuses `drop-carry` and `mark-carry` without `--match` on both run paths, before the editor runs. The report line says `refused rc=2 ... key it --match TEXT`, and the queue line is marked `#refused`. A hand run of `roster_edit.py` keeps the index form.

## Head

`a7f37e665413650685c3930ccaf635b7c83eeb9c` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`f4fecc828bca91b403cf9395f2b00fa28a713c03`, on `origin/main` `5d09dedf69eb9fe9bcab6bd9e5ddbde04a387ecb` (2026-11-10). The roster history was read on `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster` at `c444a6995`.

## Mutation proof

`python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_roster_drain_replay.py mutants` plants each mutant in a copy of `tools/` and runs `roster_queue.py --self-test` there. The baseline copy passes. Each mutant fails the checks listed:

- M1, the predicate never refuses: `run: drop-carry and mark-carry by index are refused and marked, never pushed` and `run --batch: drop-carry by index is refused before the batch, and marked`.
- M2, the single-op path skips the check: `run: drop-carry and mark-carry by index are refused and marked, never pushed`.
- M3, the batch path skips the check: `run --batch: drop-carry by index is refused before the batch, and marked`.
- M4, `mark-carry` is left out of the predicate: `run: drop-carry and mark-carry by index are refused and marked, never pushed`.

## Unpinned sites

`replay_unsafe`'s predicate and its two call sites in `tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py` are pinned by the in-tree mutant harness `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_roster_drain_replay.py mutants`, which kills all 4. `mutation-autofix` mutates `custom_components/` only, so it does not reach these sites.

## Null control

- **The unmodified op replays destructively.** `replay` applies `drop-carry G 1` twice to a five-entry fixture through `roster_edit.apply_op`. Both runs apply, and two entries are removed.
- **The `--match` form is the control.** Run twice, it removes one entry, and the replay refuses with `no carry entry matches`.
- **The check does not fire on replay-safe lines.** The `--match` forms of `drop-carry` and `mark-carry` print `runs`. The self-test's `drop-carry G --match one` line is pushed.
- **The census rule is checked independently.** The orchestrator's hand restorations are the control: they restored 14 of the 18 rule-replays and none of the 14 first drops (`firsts_restored=0`).

## Figures

- `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_roster_drain_replay.py replay`: index form `removed=2`, `--match` form `removed=1`. Both index lines are refused by the check, and both `--match` lines run.
- `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_roster_drain_replay.py census 43495fb61 c444a6995`: `drops=32 replays=18 replays_restored=14 replays_unrestored=4 firsts=14 firsts_restored=0`.
  - The rule: a drop is a replay when an earlier drop in the window removed an entry at the same (group, index).
  - The 4 unrestored drops are in R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER: `6027d13ff`, `76d95c36a`, `c7c424169`, `dfbc636b9`.
  - Pair replays fall 13 to 15 minutes apart (the `PAIR` lines).
  - 8 of the 14 first index drops were replayed at least once: 8 is the count of `PAIR` lines, 14 is `firsts`.
- `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_roster_drain_replay.py contained c444a6995`: `entries=1690 contained_in_a_sibling=23`.
  - These are entries whose full text also sits inside a sibling entry of the same group. `--match` cannot name them, so only a hand run by index can.
  - The same arm at `5d09dedf6` prints `entries=1337 contained_in_a_sibling=24`.
- `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_roster_drain_replay.py cost`: the check's per-line cost in µs, over 100000 calls. It reads below one microsecond.
- `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_roster_drain_replay.py mutants`: `mutants=4 killed=4`.
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py --self-test`: `65 checks, 0 failed`. Three of those checks are new.
- Cost test, from section 5 of the RCA doc:
  - The defect costs at least 600 s per occurrence. That is the restoration commits `54f325471` (09:35) to `e4ab4a9f8` (09:45), and it leaves out the 4 losses nobody noticed.
  - The countermeasure costs under 1 µs per line, plus at most one 120 s `interval_s` requeue per index line written.
  - It breaks even once P(an index line is replayed) exceeds 0.2. In this incident that rate was 8/14. **Passes.**
- Class search: `Grep` for `(drop|mark)-carry +<group> +<index>` over the tree, JSON excluded.
  - Outside this diff it returns only the usage lines of `roster_edit.py` and `instruments/roster_edit.py.md`.
  - Each other runner that applies first and records afterwards is dispositioned in the RCA doc, section 4: closed here, already guarded, or the hotfix's.
- Scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff 5d09dedf69eb9fe9bcab6bd9e5ddbde04a387ecb` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run`.
- Ratchet: `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.

## Red checks

none

## Forward-carry

- **Restore four lost carries.** R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER (stage `done`) lost four carries to replays that nobody restored: `6027d13ff`, `76d95c36a`, `c7c424169`, `dfbc636b9`. `76d95c36a` removed the item-453f6578 carry that `83ba995b6` had marked implemented. They are recovered from each commit's parent with `git show <sha>^:dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json`, and re-appended with `roster_edit.py append-carry`. Carry: R10-TICK-RESIDUE
- **Correct carry[11]'s premise.** R10-TICK-RESIDUE carry[11] judged the drain's replay harmless because "the ops come back as refusals". That premise is false for `drop-carry` and `mark-carry` by index: the census above counts 18 destructive replays. A queue now refuses those forms, so a carry, brief or orchestrator note that writes a queued carry op must key it `--match TEXT`, and an entry inside a sibling's text (the `contained` arm) is edited by hand, once. Carry: R10-TICK-RESIDUE

## Friction

none

merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-ROSTER-DRAIN-REPLAY: r10 hotfix roster drain replay
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
Hotfix R10-HOTFIX-ROSTER-DRAIN-REPLAY. `beat_jobs.py` `roster_drain` saved its done set (`roster-done.json`, `roster-queue-lines.json`, `roster-hold.json`) only after the whole queue: beatd kills the row at its `timeout_s` in `beatd.jobs.json`, so a pass with more pending ops than fit replayed every applied op on the next pass (the orchestrator observed drop-carry ops re-landing on handoff/audit-r10-roster, 2026-11-10). Fix: a `save()` after every op that is marked done (each `ctx.remember` is an atomic write and only on change), and `ROSTER_PASS_BUDGET_S`: no op starts past it, so the kill does not land mid-queue; the self-test pins it at most half the row's `timeout_s`, leaving an op started just before it as long again.

Alternatives: (1) save only, no bound — a kill still replays the op it lands in, and a drop-carry replay is the observed harm, so the bound is kept; (2) an op count cap per pass — a count does not track the op's duration, the time budget does; (3) reading `timeout_s` from `beatd.jobs.json` at run time — couples a row to beatd's table file at every pass; a constant pinned against the table by the self-test gives one source checked at every self-test run.

The root cause is owed in its own seat, the orchestrator's R10-RCA-ROSTER-DRAIN-REPLAY (the defect reached a live state document), and is not written here.

Residual: the digest lines of the ops a killed pass applied are not written (`write_job` stays at the pass end); with the bound a kill needs one op to outlast half the timeout. Carry: dismissed: digest-only loss, the done set is the state that must survive, and the bound makes the kill the exception.

## Head

`ad85ca26787316f16bad588d9aa01391589c0c46` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

b4660fa4f9632632f4ff9d69e9f344b28800309c, merge base 5d09dedf69eb9fe9bcab6bd9e5ddbde04a387ecb (origin/main at 5d09dedf69eb9fe9bcab6bd9e5ddbde04a387ecb, 2026-11-10T08:42Z).

## Mutation proof

Deleted the per-op `save()` after `holds.pop(key, None)` and the `if ctx.clock() - start >= ROSTER_PASS_BUDGET_S: break` lines, ran `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py --self-test --no-mutants`, restored:

    FAIL roster-drain: a pass killed mid-queue keeps its applied ops; the next applies each once
    FAIL roster-drain: a pass past ROSTER_PASS_BUDGET_S starts no op; the next pass resumes
    beat_jobs self-test: 112 checks, 2 failed

The same edits stay in the self-test's MUTANTS (`roster_saved_at_pass_end`, `roster_pass_unbounded`, plus `roster_budget_over_timeout` raising the constant to 451), each killed by its named case in `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py --self-test`.

## Null control

Failing test first, at the merge base with only the self-test changed: the two cases above and `roster-drain: ROSTER_PASS_BUDGET_S is at most half the row's timeout_s` FAIL (`beat_jobs self-test: 112 checks, 3 failed`), while the new `roster-drain null: a pass that completes applies each op exactly once` passes — a pass that is not killed applied each op once before the fix too, so the killed-pass case separates the defect from a working drain. No finder harness exists for this hotfix (orchestrator observation); the self-test case is the harness, run at both ends above.

## Figures

- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py --self-test --no-mutants` with the self-test alone at the merge base: 112 checks, 3 failed (the three cases above).
- Class seams, rule `grep -nE "ctx\.remember\(|atomic\(" tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py` (a row's persisted memory, by row), against the property "a loop of non-idempotent side effects whose done record is written after the loop":

  - `gantt`, `pulse`, `fold`, `write_job`, `atomic` itself: input snapshots or digest files, rewritten whole each pass. Not the class.

- Focus (replay idempotence, no dropped op, queue intact), read against the code at the head: `S/roster-drain.queue` is only read by `roster_drain`, never written, so a killed or failed pass leaves it intact; an op is added to `done` only after `roster_queue.py run` reports or marks it, and `save()` follows each such add, so a landed op is persisted before the next op starts; the budget `break` leaves the remaining keys out of `done`, so the next pass runs them (budget-resume case); `UNRUN`/`CASCADE` paths `continue` without marking. Owner ruling (tvofi, 2026-11-07, waste-study decision cards, card 2, ruled NARROW): a fix reviewer that returns `blocked` with class `mutation-vacuous` or `class-open` lists, in that one verdict, every survivor or open seam it found at that head. It no longer names one per round. The repair fixer then answers the whole list in one repair.

This is **policy**. It changes what a reviewer seat must do (`dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md` steps 1 and 6), so it merges only on tvofi's approving review.

What changes:

merges.subject: Merge pull request #3401 from tvofi/fix/r10-hotfix-train-policy-mandate
merges.title: R10-HOTFIX: the train's pre-flight judges a policy head with the mandate's due approval
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
The merge train parked a policy head that its own `--mandate` should have carried. On #3366, at head 97839ed60f8b59cd59adc99d106b4e94ac4dccab with a merge verdict at that head (comment 6754586447), the live train (state dir `mandate` file 6715477401) logged `PARK #3366 policy: policy paths changed (...): no decisive review by tvofi (id 70032254) on this pull request`. A re-add under `--mandate 6715477401` then answered `ADD REFUSED #3366 policy: ... (the pre-flight park at this verdict still holds)`.

Root cause: an ordering defect between the train's two policy steps. The batch admission (`Train.at_head`) and `Train.land` both call `policy_approve` (post the citing approval under the mandate) and then `policy_gate` (judge it). The `--pre-flight` read, `queue_pre_flight.PreFlight.entry`, called `policy_gate` alone, so it ran before anything was posted. A policy head with no review yet therefore parked on "no decisive review" before admission could post the approval that cures it. `train_add`'s re-admission of a `PRE-FLIGHT` park at the same verdict re-runs that same read (`Train.preflight_entry`), so it refused #3366 again for the same reason. Both symptoms come from one seam. The park memo itself is correct: it re-asks the pre-flight, and the pre-flight gave the wrong answer.

The mandate covers this act. Comment 6715477401 on #201, by tvofi, created 2026-11-08T01:12:45Z and never edited, reads `MANDATE: agents may approve as tvofi, scope all, from 2026-11-08T01:12Z until 2026-11-16T18:00Z`. budget_raise_gate's own reader, `mandate_state(..., "merge", MANDATE_COVERS_POLICY, "policy merging")`, run on the live comment and the #201 thread since its creation, returned `(True, 'mandate 6715477401 (scope all, from 2026-11-08T01:12Z until 2026-11-16T18:00Z)')`. With one tvofi revocation comment appended, it returned `(False, "mandate 6715477401 was revoked by tvofi's comment 1")`.

The fix, in `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py` and `tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py`:
- `Train.policy_approval_due(pr, h, files)` decides whether `policy_approve` will post. It is a read, holding policy_approve's own decision unchanged: no policy path, no `--mandate`, a budget file beside the policy, the owner's approval already at the head, or a mandate that `mandate_state` does not read as in force for policy merging each mean no post. `policy_approve` now posts on its answer.
- `Train._agent_approval_body` is the body `_post_agent_approval` posts, factored out so the pre-flight can judge the same body without posting it.
- `Train.policy_gate(..., posting=None)` judges the reviews it reads plus, optionally, the review about to be posted, appended last as GitHub would list it. Every caller but one passes none.
- `Train.policy_admits(pr, h, item, files)` is the pre-flight's policy read: `policy_gate` as admission reaches it, with the due approval judged unposted. It posts nothing. When a `--mandate` is set but nothing is due, the park names the mandate's own reason (revoked, expired, scope) beside the gate's.
- `PreFlight.entry` calls `policy_admits` in place of `policy_gate`.
- `land` still re-reads the real reviews at the merge, so the merge decision is unchanged and `policy_gate` stays the only judge.

Alternatives rejected:
- (a) Post the approval inside the pre-flight. That makes a read-only instrument write, and it would post an owner-account approval for an entry a later pre-flight step (row, findings, raise) then parks.
- (b) Skip the policy read in the pre-flight under a mandate. That passes heads the merge would refuse, such as an owner `CHANGES_REQUESTED` (pinned below), because it bypasses the judge where (c) consults it.
- (c), taken, keeps one decision (`policy_approval_due`) and one judge (`policy_gate`), shared by the post, the pre-flight and the merge.

## Head

`55dfa880d1cd779356cef493eb59cf73ca7818bc` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

593a28c96e54a64c3ce25d99dfd4850be6094e4b. This is the repair of the CI block at f0b7564596d2725f87090f921e0d3ceb51ceec8b (hpo-approver comment 6758409766): one commit over that head, 593a28c9, adding the line `    from pathlib import Path` to the harness's inlined `repo_root`. Its `def repo_root` through the `raise RuntimeError` line is now byte-identical to `tools/audit/repo_root.py`'s, compared by regex extraction of both texts. The earlier commits are unchanged:
- 9350dc7c: the fix and the failing tests;
- 8e795cda: the mutant harness;
- b4f272a6: the guides and the inert classification;
- e414ab71: a direct pin on `policy_approval_due`;
- 20f3028f: origin/main b0762725 merged in;
- f0b75645: the delivery row.

The merge with main changed `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py` (+16/-12, other pull requests' lines), so every figure below that names 593a28c9 was re-taken at this head. The ones naming an earlier SHA say so.

## Mutation proof

Failing first: the new `queue_pre_flight.py` self-test checks were run against the unfixed `merge_train.py` and `PreFlight.entry`, in the working tree before the fix was written. `python3 tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py --self-test` printed `52 checks, 2 failed`:
- `a policy head with no review yet passes under the train's --mandate in force for policy merging (the approval policy_approve posts, judged by policy_gate)`;
- `null control: under a --mandate tvofi revoked it still PARKs, named as revoked` (the unfixed park did not name the revocation).

Mutant P1 below restores that unfixed call at the head, and it fails the same two checks.

`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_hotfix_train_policy_mandate_mutants.py` at 593a28c9 makes one in-place mutant per arm under `mutant_guard`. It runs `queue_pre_flight.py --self-test` for each mutant. The tree was clean afterwards: `git status --porcelain` printed nothing. It printed `8 mutant(s), 0 not as required`, rc 0:
- P0, unmutated: PASS.
- P1, `PreFlight.entry` calls `policy_gate` alone (the defect): KILLED. Both checks above fail.
- P2, `policy_admits` builds no posting: KILLED by the pass check.
- P3, `policy_approval_due` returns the id even when the mandate is not live: KILLED by `policy_approval_due names the mandate in force for policy merging; revoked, expired or scope code-owned it names none`. At 8e795cda this mutant SURVIVED, because `policy_gate` re-judges the simulated review and still parks. e414ab71 pins the function directly, since `policy_approve` posts on the same answer.
- P4, the no-mandate arm (`cid = self.mandate_id() or MID`): KILLED by `null control: the same head with no --mandate still PARKs on the review`, and by the existing `a policy head with no owner review at its head PARKs`.
- P5, the mandate's reason dropped from the park: KILLED by the revoked null control.
- P6, the posting judged instead of the reviews read: KILLED by `an owner CHANGES_REQUESTED at the head still PARKs under the --mandate`.
- P7, the pre-flight posts (`policy_approve` called inside `policy_admits`): KILLED by the pass check and the CHANGES_REQUESTED check.

Re-anchored: `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_train_upgrade_mutants.py` M3 and M5 named spans in `policy_approve` that moved into `policy_approval_due`. Their mutations are unchanged, re-pointed at the new spans (M3 `return cid, pol, why`; M5 `pass` over the at-head return). `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_train_upgrade_mutants.py M3 M5`, run at b4f272a6, printed `M3 KILLED` and `M5 KILLED`, rc 0. It was not re-run at 593a28c9. The main merge did not touch the spans either mutant names; CI's mutation lane judges the head.

The repair's own control: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/harness_headers.py` at f0b75645 (the blocked head) printed `1 of 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED`, rc 1: `every inlined walk matches the canonical helper and no depth root remains [FAIL python copies=174 differ=['dev/audit/harnesses/r10_hotfix_train_policy_mandate_mutants.py']`. At 593a28c9 it printed `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`, rc 0.

## Null control

- No `--mandate`: the same policy head with no review still PARKs `policy`, with `no decisive review`.
- A mandate tvofi revoked: it still PARKs, naming `revoked`.
- A mandate with scope `code-owned`: it still PARKs.
- An expired mandate: it still PARKs.
- An owner `CHANGES_REQUESTED` at the head under a live mandate: it still PARKs.
- Each check above passes at 593a28c9 (`queue_pre_flight` self-test below), and its own mutant (P3 to P6) turns it red.
- The pre-existing policy and raise arms of the pre-flight self-test stay green at the head. These are: a cited approval passes, an uncited one parks, no review parks, a revoked mandate parks, and the raise arms.

## Figures

- `python3 tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py --self-test` at 593a28c9: `queue_pre_flight self-test: 53 checks, 0 failed`, rc 0.
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` at 593a28c9: `merge_train self-test: 608 checks, 0 failed`, rc 0.
- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_hotfix_train_policy_mandate_mutants.py` at 593a28c9: `8 mutant(s), 0 not as required`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/harness_headers.py` at 593a28c9: `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py`, at e414ab71: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`, at e414ab71: `1 of 2706 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`, rc 1.
  - The one failure was `a measured script's late-writing descendant is waited for, not recorded as nodata`, the coverage stage's wait-bound check.
  - Its waiting arm recorded every script as `nodata`, `entities` included. The host was at load average about 350 (`uptime`).
  - Its inputs are the coverage stage and planted scripts, none of this diff's files.
  - It is left to CI's run at this head.
- The class rule: `git grep -n "policy_gate(\|\.policy_admits(" -- tools .github` printed 5 lines at 593a28c9. Each line, with its disposition:
  - `merge_train.py` `def policy_gate`: the judge itself, taking the new optional `posting`.
  - `merge_train.py` `policy_admits`: new; it calls the judge with the unposted approval.
  - `merge_train.py` `land`: after `policy_approve`, unchanged.
  - `merge_train.py` batch admission: after `policy_approve`, unchanged.
  - `queue_pre_flight.py`: now calls `policy_admits`, this diff.
  - No caller judges policy before the post.

## Red checks

- `tests / fast (3.14)`, red at f0b75645 in `tests/harness_headers.py`. The new harness's inlined `repo_root` lacked the canonical line `    from pathlib import Path` from `tools/audit/repo_root.py`, so the header check refused the copy. 593a28c9 copies the function verbatim (see `## Mutation proof` for the before and after).
  - Root-cause trigger answer: a cheaper detector existed. It is `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/harness_headers.py`, run locally in about 188 s, against about 13 min of the fast lane.
  - It was not run before the handoff because `tools/pr/ci_predict.py` predicted no `fast` red: `CI PREDICT: no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted`. ci_predict does not run the `run_always` script `harness_headers.py` over a new harness.
  - That predictor gap is the countermeasure's place, carried below to R10-PREPR-RESIDUE. It is not fixed here: it is a different seam (`tools/pr/ci_predict.py`), and not one line.

## Forward-carry

- ci_predict does not run the `run_always` `tests/harness_headers.py` over a new or changed `dev/audit/harnesses/*.py`. So a harness whose inlined `repo_root` drifts from `tools/audit/repo_root.py` passes prepr step 6d and `body_push.sh`'s predictor, and turns `tests / fast` red in CI (this PR, at f0b75645). Carry: R10-PREPR-RESIDUE
- The ambient `gh` account is never checked against the owner before the train acts as the owner. `policy_approve` posts an approval as whatever account `gh` holds, and `policy_admits` judges an unposted review it labels with the owner's pinned identity. A train run under a non-owner token would post a non-owner approval, which `policy_gate` then refuses at the merge, and the pre-flight would have passed it. Not fixed here: it predates this PR (`policy_approve`'s post) and wants one owner check shared by the post and the simulation, not a line. A barrier exists to reuse: `tools/audit/seat/ci_probe.py` `owner_check` (`GET /user`, refuse unless the login is the owner). Carry: R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE
- `policy_approval_due` ignores the owner's own `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Where tvofi's latest decisive review requests changes, `policy_approve` still posts a mandated approval. `budget_raise_gate.approval` then refuses it ("a mandated approval does not override it"), so nothing merges, but a needless owner-account approval is posted. The pre-flight already parks this head (P6's check), so this PR's read is correct. The post's decision is the owner's-latest-decisive rule, which lives in `approval()`, and sharing it is more than one line. Carry: R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE

My differential harness finds no pre-flight PASS that the real gate refuses, except under an unchecked precondition carried below. The block is CI: a required check is red because of a file this PR adds, and the body does not answer it.

## Block

- `tests / fast (3.14)` concluded `failure` at this head (job 129597668418, run 42743953498): `1 of 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED`, `>>> FAILED: python3 tests/harness_headers.py`. ## Findings

- Follow-up: `python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --apply-inert` printed `CI PREDICT: no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted` for this branch, beside `APPLIED inert_reads tests/harness_headers.py: dev/audit/harnesses/r10_hotfix_train_policy_mandate_mutants.py`. So a new harness whose inlined `repo_root` drifts gets a clean prediction. Control: predicting on this head (or on any harness whose `repo_root` lacks `from pathlib import Path`) must predict the fast red. Carry: R10-FLY-CIPREDICT-RESTORING
- Follow-up: the pre-flight's simulated review (`policy_admits`, merge_train.py:2457) is built with the owner's pinned identity, and nothing checks that the train's ambient `gh` account is that owner. `_post_agent_approval` (merge_train.py:2381) posts with whatever account `gh` is logged in as, and no `gh api user` read happens anywhere in the train. Under a non-owner account, world A17 in `ev/reviewer_differential_a17.txt` gives `preflight=PASS real=PARK posted=1  <-- SLIP`. Before this diff that head parked at the pre-flight before anything was posted. Now it is admitted, a stray approval is posted, and `land`'s `policy_gate` then refuses it, so the merge still fails closed. A cheap barrier already exists: `ci_probe.py:154-161` `owner_check` refuses when `GET /user` is not tvofi. Applying it once per train run, before `policy_approve` or `policy_admits` runs, would close this. Control: world A17 must PARK at the pre-flight. Carry: R10-TRAIN-MERGE-LOOP-2
- Follow-up (pre-existing, outside this diff): the real path posts the mandated owner-account approval even when the owner's own latest decisive review is CHANGES_REQUESTED. Worlds N5 and A1 give `real=PARK posted=1`: `policy_approval_due` does not consult `approval()`'s CHANGES_REQUESTED rule. The train still refuses at `policy_gate`. But GitHub now reads the owner account's latest review as APPROVED, so the PR's GitHub-side code-owner state no longer shows the owner's request for changes. This diff's pre-flight posts nothing in those worlds (`posted=0` in pre-flight runs; check "... and the pre-flight posts nothing"). Control: worlds N5 and A1 must give `posted=0` in the real path. Carry: R10-TRAIN-MERGE-LOOP-2
- Out of scope: the body's class-rule figure says `git grep -n "policy_gate(\|\.policy_admits(" -- tools .github` gives "4 lines at e414ab71". At both e414ab71 and f0b75645 the enumerator prints 5 (`ev/class_rule.txt`). The fifth line is `policy_gate`'s own `def` (merge_train.py:2049), not a caller. The body's four dispositions cover every call site, so the class is closed and only the stated count is wrong. merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED: hotfix cop unmeasured
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED (hotfix, owner-reported, user-visible). The Health tab graded the heat pump from "measured COP" samples on installs that cannot measure COP. With no heat input, `flow_meter.cop_evidence` infers COP = model COP x (plan's ask / power reading), and the coordinator recorded that as the measured COP and fed it to the COP health watch, so a hot-water interval drawing exactly its ask stored `compute_cop_dhw(outdoor, tank)` itself. On the owner's install both inputs are now Tuya vendor models ("Estimated Heating Output", "Estimated Power Draw"), so heat over power is the vendor's own fitted COP on every interval: the same self-comparison through the other door.

What changes (owning seam: the COP observation path):

1. **A COP sample is measured only from metered heat over metered power.** `thermal_model.InstallCapability.cop_measured(dhw)`: a heat reading (heat counter, or thermal power entity) over an electrical one (the electric counter for a counter's span, else the power entity), neither a vendor estimate, and for a hot-water interval a heat reading declared to see that circuit. `InstallCapability.cop_sample(heat_kw, dhw)` turns it into the fold's answer per interval: `True` (record and grade), `False` (scale only), `None` (refuse). `coordinator._fold_cop_evidence` gates `MeasuredCop.record` and `_observe_cop_health` on it, together, in one `if measured:`.
2. **The card and the diagnostics say it cannot be measured, and name what would.** `accuracy.cop_observability` publishes `not_measurable` with no heat reading (whatever the draw does) and the new `estimated_inputs` for an estimate on either side; `draw_follows_plan` is retired. `machine_score` returns the new reason `cop_unmeasurable` instead of `cop_watch_learning` ("not enough data yet"). Card: `health.cop_reason_not_measurable` / `estimated_inputs` and `score.reason_cop_unmeasurable` (en, sv) say "COP cannot be measured on this install" and name a heat energy meter or thermal power meter covering the heating circuit, hot water included (and a power meter, neither an estimate); `score.part_machine` says a measured COP is metered heat over a power meter. The observed-COP sensor waits for `metered_inputs` on an estimate.
3. **Estimate versus meter, on both sides.** New options on the metering page: `heat_pump_power_source` and `heat_pump_thermal_power_source` (auto / meter / estimate, default auto) and `heat_meter_sees_dhw` (default off). No Home Assistant signal distinguishes a vendor estimate from a meter (both are `power` sensors), so the marker is config-level. `auto` reads an entity whose id contains `estimat` as an estimate (`const.ESTIMATE_ID_MARK`). Why name detection is sound here, and only here: it is a default the user can override either way, and its only effect is on the COP observation path. A false positive only withholds a COP grade. It never changes a plan or a learner. A false negative is today's behaviour. It catches the Tuya integration's "Estimated Power Draw" / "Estimated Heating Output" entity ids on the owner's install with no action from them. A heat counter outranks the thermal power entity and is read as metered.
4. **A negative or missing heat reading stops the fold.** A configured thermal power that reads no heat this interval (`read_heat_output_kw` turns a negative into `None`, as it does an unavailable one) now refuses with `no_heat_reading` instead of falling into the commanded inference.
5. **Migration: the stale bands are not read.** The watch's memory moves to `cop_baseline_measured` / `cop_health_cusum_measured` (`coordinator._COP_BASELINE_KEY`). The pre-fix `cop_baseline` bands carry no provenance, so no per-sample split is possible, and they are never loaded: every band restarts from measured samples alone, and real samples are never averaged with model ones. A pre-fix store's last COP (`measured_cop`) is not shown as measured either: `_async_load_thermal_learning` reads it only from a payload that carries `cop_baseline_measured`. Why a key rename and not a store version bump: a major bump of the thermal-learning store would reset every learner on a downgrade (`QuarantiningStore` surfaces a newer version and starts afresh). The rename resets only the contaminated field, in both directions: an older release reads no `cop_baseline` and starts that watch empty. The cost is that a genuinely metered install re-learns its bands (20 samples each, `COP_BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES`).

**Owner ruling, retained.** tvofi, 2026-11-07: "Training on estimated power should be good enough and better than nothing though so retain that". No learner is gated on the estimate marker. The COP scale (`_apply_cop_scale`) and the capacity envelope (`_fold_capacity_envelope`) still fold every interval they folded before, inference and estimates included (pinned: the null-control check asserts `_cop_samples == 1` on the no-heat interval; the Tuya check asserts 3 scale samples over 3 estimated intervals). The new `no_heat_reading` refusal (item 4) is the one change to what reaches them, and it fires only on a configured thermal power that read nothing.

**Learners consuming estimated inputs (information only, unchanged by this PR).** Heat reading: the house heat-loss learner (`_async_learn_house_heat_loss`, via `heat_energy.space_heat_kw` / `close_span`), the lower-floor loss learner (`_async_learn_lower_floor_loss`), the capacity envelope (`_fold_capacity_envelope`, thermal kW), the COP scale (`cop_evidence`), and the COP reference curve's supply-lift judgement (`_cop_reference_curve`). Power reading: the COP scale (`_fold_measured_cop`), the draw-range window (`draw_range.fold` in `_record_accuracy`), the slab propagation (`draw_range.space_draw_kw`), immersion detection (`_detect_immersion`), the capacity envelope, the accuracy tracker's actual cost, the compressor start counter and the frequency map (`_freq_map.observe`). Found by reading every reader of `_flow_bias.heat_output_kw`, `close_span` and `_measured_power` in `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/`.

**Carry 1 (owner addition, tvofi 2026-11-07), point by point.**
- (a) Purging the stale baseline: done by the key rename in item 5. The owner's `"0:dhw" [2.30, 2]` and `"2" [2.52, 2]`, and any older bands, sit under the pre-fix `cop_baseline` key, which is never read again, so they can never be averaged with the real samples now accumulating. Pinned by "a COP baseline stored before measured provenance loads empty with its CUSUM reset; one stored since round-trips", whose payload is the owner's two bands, and now also by "a last COP stored before measured provenance does not load as measured; one stored since round-trips" (this round). Mutants M5 and G kill them.
- (b) Estimate versus meter, on the thermal power input too: `heat_pump_thermal_power_source` mirrors `heat_pump_power_source`, and `auto` reads the Tuya "Estimated Heating Output" id as an estimate.
- (c) Hot-water coverage is explicit, never assumed: `heat_meter_sees_dhw`, default off. A ":dhw" sample needs it on. Pinned by "metered heat over metered power records a space sample; a hot-water sample only where the heat meter is declared to see the hot-water circuit". Mutant M7 kills it.
- (d) Either side estimated is not measured, learners are not gated, and the consumers are reported: `cop_measured` refuses an estimate on either side. The Tuya null control (heat over power equals the fitted COP on every interval) is in `## Null control`. The owner's ruling and the learner list are above.

Alternatives considered: (a) a store major-version bump. It lost on the downgrade reset described above. (b) Per-sample provenance inside the existing bands. It lost because the old samples have none, so they would still need dropping, and it adds a field per band for no reader. (c) Gating the COP scale on a heat reading too. The owner ruled that out. (d) Name detection alone, without the option. It lost because nothing could override a misread id. (e) Leaving the coordinator helper as a module function. It lost because the decision is install capability, so it lives on `InstallCapability`, pure and testable without the coordinator.

**Repair round 2 (fix review blocked 9cf0b6108, mutation-vacuous on the `measured_cop` provenance gate).** The production line the review mutated, `MeasuredCop.from_dict(stored.get("measured_cop") if _COP_BASELINE_KEY in stored else None)` in `_async_load_thermal_learning`, was right but unpinned: the migration check's pre-fix payload carried no `measured_cop`. This round changes tests only (`git diff --stat 9cf0b6108 HEAD` lists `tests/features.py` alone), in the R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED section:
- `_cu_old_payload` now carries a pre-fix `measured_cop` record (a 2.55 hot-water COP, the null-control fixture's model value, with its old `at`), and the new check "a last COP stored before measured provenance does not load as measured; one stored since round-trips" asserts `_cu_old._measured_cop.cop is None` (and its `at`), that the since-fix payload carries a `measured_cop`, and that it loads back equal (`as_dict()`).
- Two further checks kill diff mutants the mutation step found in the same loader seam: "a COP health CUSUM stored since measured provenance loads with its state" (the CUSUM under the since-fix key is kept, the reset check's null control), and "the store's domains admit a since-fix COP payload: the one the fold wrote, and a one-sample band beside a CUSUM part-way to its alarm" (`store.off_domain` over both payloads).
No production line changed, so `coordinator.py` lines did not shift and the roster brief's line anchors need no re-pin.

**Conflict resolution (the merge train skipped #3297: the recarry conflicted with main).** Merge commit bdeefc51c merges origin/main 73365699a into the PR head 2d010b091. One conflict, `tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt`, scenario `score_open`: main's line was `score_open  # R10-WHY-NOW-WIDGET: Why now block added, showing the no-data line`, written for the why-now widget's diff, which main now carries; the branch's was a bare `score_open` written for this diff. After the merge `score_open` moves only for this branch's grade explanation (`node tests/card_drift.mjs` against the merge base: `1 state(s) moved and claimed, 44 identical`), so the file keeps one `score_open` line, with this branch's reason: `score_open  # R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED: grade explanation says measured COP is metered heat, no grade without it`. Every other line is byte-identical to main, main's R10-WHY-NOW-WIDGET comment block included (`git diff origin/main -- tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt` adds this branch's comment block and swaps that one line, nothing else); `claims-for:` stays 7.1.5, equal to `VERSION` at 73365699a. Every other file auto-merged; no production line of this branch changed in the merge (the survivors below are the same eight at shifted line numbers).

**Conflict resolution 2 (the merge train skipped bdeefc51c: main was stamped v7.1.6 and the recarry refused on the claim files).** Merge commit 68b0735be merges origin/main 2a3c05644 (VERSION 7.1.6) into bdeefc51c. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main bdeefc51c` reported `MERGE-CLAIM: refused` on both `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` and `tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt`: both sides changed claims under different `claims-for:` stamps (base 7.1.5, main 7.1.6). Main's stamp emptied the v7.1.5 lists, and the R10-SAV-WOOD-HEAT `coord_*` lines and the R10-WHY-NOW-WIDGET `score_open` reason the earlier merge carried belong to the release v7.1.6 now stamps. Each file is resolved to main's bytes plus this branch's own claims only: in `claimed_drift.txt` the five `coord_* # R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED` lines (machine reason `cop_watch_learning -> cop_unmeasurable`) and `config_flow # R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED` (metering-page leaves added), and in `card_claimed_drift.txt` the R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED comment block and `score_open  # R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED: ...` (the score_open resolution from bdeefc51c is kept). `git diff origin/main -- tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt` adds 6 lines to each and deletes none; `claims-for:` is main's 7.1.6, equal to `VERSION`. Every other file auto-merged. VERSION, the manifest version and the RELEASE_NOTES heading are main's own (`git diff origin/main HEAD -- VERSION RELEASE_NOTES.md custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json` prints nothing). No production line of this branch changed in the merge: the diff-mutant survivors are the same eight, at the same lines.

**Conflict resolution 3 (fix review blocked 7fe24f9f6: merge-conflict).** Merge commit 9c59a9ea9 merges origin/main 20e83746f into 7fe24f9f6. Before the merge, `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 7fe24f9f6` printed four `CONFLICT (content)` lines; the claim driver (`python3 tests/env_drift.py --install-merge-driver`) resolved both claim files. Each conflict is resolved by union:
- `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/thermal_model.py`: `InstallCapability` keeps the branch's `heat_estimated`, `power_estimated` and `heat_sees_dhw` fields and main's `on_off` (R10-MIN-POWER-FLOOR), in that order. `probe_install` passes all four. Main's `declared_modulation` follows `probe_install`, ahead of the branch's `_estimated`.
- `dev/audit/rounds/round3/D5/option_doc_coverage.py`: the header's history keeps both moves, the branch's 204 -> 207 / 237 -> 240 and then main's +1 (the compressor modulation select), so the EXPECTED lines read `option_fields_rendered=208` and `option_schema_keys_rendered=241`. The harness prints those two values at 9c59a9ea9.
- `dev/audit/rounds/round4/D6/claims.json` and `claims.md`, C125: base 45 selects, the branch +2 (the two meter-source selects), main +1, so 48. `claims.py` regenerates both files, and its run at 9c59a9ea9 leaves them reading 48 selects with `claims_false=0`.
The claim files hold main's bytes plus this branch's own claims only: `git diff origin/main -- tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt` adds the same 6 lines to each that the earlier merges carried and deletes none. Every other file auto-merged. `git diff origin/main HEAD -- VERSION RELEASE_NOTES.md custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json` prints nothing. origin/main was 20e83746f when this round began. The brief named 7812357d5, and main had already moved past it.

**Carry 2 (moved from R10-MIN-POWER-FLOOR, items de37a181/df5196cc): re-read `probe_install` and `InstallCapability` against the `on_off` early return.** This branch changes neither `can_duty_cycle` nor `fully_metered`. Rule: `python3 <scratch>/fnbody.py <ref>` prints `ast.dump` of both `InstallCapability` methods from `thermal_model.py` at a ref; its output at `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` and at ad3d8a561 is byte-identical (`cmp` exits 0). Their inputs are unchanged too: `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD -- custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/thermal_model.py` adds 55 lines and removes none, and no added or removed line names `measured_power`, `frequency`, `on_off` or `writes`. Null control: a diff that touched either method or one of those fields would make `cmp` fail or the grep print a line. The `on_off` early return and its checks need no revalidation for this pull request. Carry: R10-MIN-POWER-FLOOR

## Head

`b72efecda93d11758d4883335c1a2579ad76d353` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

Code head `1002809eaefd53be30ca0583f98ce4d19dffbe67`: the previous PR head `9c92e927bf4b75d84420ce1d2ad4906be116d06b` (which merges the authored code head `ad3d8a56178f9f0aa81232749130ac111219d791`) merged with origin/main `b0762725099fefd337fc74ecff161cb487a992bc` (a two-parent merge).

**Merge resolution only (delta reviewer: judge this alone; no code change beyond it).** `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 9c92e927` reported five conflicts, the claimnotes driver installed (`python3 tests/env_drift.py --install-merge-driver`: already-installed):
- `tests/golden/config_flow.json`, one hunk in the seeded options map: union, `heat_curve_displace_entity` (main, R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE) then `heat_meter_sees_dhw` (this branch). Control: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/golden.py --record --only config_flow` on the merged tree, then `cmp` against the hand union, printed equal.
- `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt`: the driver refused (both sides rewrote `config_flow`'s claim). This branch's six lines kept; main's `config_flow # R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE ...` line dropped, per the driver's own instruction and `claim-files.md` (main's lines are inert; the branch excuses only its own diff).
- `dev/audit/rounds/round3/D5/option_doc_coverage.py`: the header's RESULT assertions. Branch prose kept; values re-measured on the merged tree by running the script: `option_fields_rendered=211`, `option_schema_keys_rendered=244` (branch +3 and main +3 over the base's 205/238), main's annotation re-based to "(208 until R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE ...)" / "(241 until ...)".

The body's item 5 says "A pre-fix store's last COP is not shown as measured either". The production line that does this is `coordinator.py:4575`, `MeasuredCop.from_dict(stored.get("measured_cop") if _COP_BASELINE_KEY in stored else None)`. I replaced it with the ungated `MeasuredCop.from_dict(stored.get("measured_cop"))` (mutant G). The result:

- `tests/entities.py` rc=1 with 3 of 2645 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED, the same three environment failures the unmutated head prints (coverage-job reuse, release ZIP, Pages workflow).

The gate carries weight on the owner's own install. Without it, the pre-fix `measured_cop` (a model value: 2.55 on the null-control fixture) loads back after the upgrade, with its old `at`. Two surfaces then read it:

- Diagnostics `cop_learner.measured_cop` (`accuracy.diagnostics_view`) reports it as measured.
- The card's Health COP row appends "Measured {age} ago." from `measured_cop_at`, right under the new "COP cannot be measured on this install" text.

This is the "do not report a model value as measured" requirement of brief items (2) and (5) and carry (a). The ObservedCOPSensor masks it only because it is unavailable while `waiting_for` names a reason.

Cure, small, and inside this group:
- Add a `measured_cop` record to `_cu_old_payload` in the R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED section.

A Riemann-sum counter integrated from the Tuya "Estimated Power Draw" or "Estimated Heating Output" therefore still records a measured COP through the span route (`heat_energy.close_span` -> `_fold_cop_evidence`), and that COP is the vendor's own fitted COP. This is carry (d)'s "an estimated input on EITHER side", reached through the counter pair. The body discloses that a heat counter "is read as metered" but gives no reason. The owner's install has both counters unset, so this does not reach the owner today. It is not the cause of the block. Carry: R10-COP-GATE-E

Deleting it passes the whole `tests/features.py` (ALL 4915) and leaves `tests/entities.py` at its three environment failures (`ev/whole_R-electric.txt`, `ev/whole_R-electric_entities.txt`). On the sample paths it is equivalent: a heat-counter span with no electric delta refuses `unaligned_meters` in `heat_energy.close_span`, and a thermal power with no power entity refuses `no_power` first. The grade is None either way, and the production line is correct, so this does not block a hotfix. merges.body:
Bumps the pwlane group in /tests/pwlane with 1 update: [playwright](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright). Updates `playwright` from 1.64.1 to 1.65.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.65.0

🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under Bun. Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the --bun flag, because without it bunx playwright test runs on Node.js:

bunx --bun playwright test

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

  • There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and --only-changed does not follow imports.
  • Bun loads modules itself, so --tsconfig and the JSX options in tsconfig.json have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported.
  • Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: click instead of locator.click. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages.
  • Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

🚨 Reports with only failures

New failures reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New onlyFailures option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters keeps only tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
reporter: [
['failures'],
['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
],
});

🎯 Test runner

  • New built-in -exclusive- test lock runs a test only when no other tests are running. All other tests continue to run in parallel with each other:

    test('restart the server', { lock: '-exclusive-' }, async () => {
  // No other test runs while this one is running.
});

  • test.skip(), test.fixme(), test.fail() and test.slow() now accept only a description. It is recorded in the test annotation:

    test('upload a file', async ({ page }) => {
  test.skip('Not implemented yet');
});

129582549659, main b076272509): `selftest_scope check: 109 gated step(s), 38 refusal(s)`
at the step `Refuse a self-test read set the committed table misses`. It has
not been green on main since #3315 (ba6fd7e8b0) introduced the check: until
#3375 (2cf0f129bc) restored tracing the job hung or was cancelled, and after
that every main push failed this step (37, 37, 37, 38 refusals at 2cf0f129bc,
9b1bb58db7, 20d96598c9, b076272509). From 8652aa65ce (#3361) a second cause
also fails the selftest_scope self-test and its mutants step (job 129633096425:
`selftest_scope self-test: 96 checks, 1 failed`, `selftest_scope check: 109 gated step(s), 39 refusal(s)`).
Not infrastructure: no rate-limit or network line; each step printed its
refusals and exited 1.

## Causes

1. **A probe no table can hold.** `ref_privacy.added_lines` ran
   `git show REV:path` on the side of the diff where the path is absent (an
   added file at the base, a deleted one at the ref). Git lstat()s the worktree
   path to word that error, so on main's push `push-names-the-host` probed
   each merge's new files: `dev/programme/delivery/3375.md`, `3396.md`,
   `3299.md` (with `heat_curve.py`, `off_restore.py`), `3399.md`, `3400.md`,
   `3361.md` in successive runs, one new path every merge. A re-recorded table
   alone would go red again at the next merge.
2. **The committed table drifted.** `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` missed
   files, dirs and probes that merges since #3315 added (`topic_grammar.py`,
   `bottleneck_check.py`, `tools/audit/seat/hooks/`, the new
   mutation-ledger dirs, ...).
   - **2b. An ungated step.** #3361 (e79a0e78bc) added `Show the workflow read
     runner refusing its own fixtures` with an `if:` that does not read
     `steps.scope.outputs.<id>`:
     `UNGATED step 'Show the workflow read runner refusing its own fixtures': its if: does not read steps.scope.outputs.<its own id>`.

## Fixes

1. `tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py`: the content arm reads the diff's
   `--name-status` and shows only the present sides. Its output is unchanged,
   because an absent side was already read as no lines.
2. `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json`: re-recorded as the union of the
   committed table and main's own measurement at b076272509 (artifact
   `selftest-closures` 13730213593 of run 42741176573), less that run's one
   cause-1 probe `dev/programme/delivery/3399.md`. The union keeps the
   committed over-approximation, which drift reports and never refuses.
3. `.github/workflows/governance.yml`: the step gets `id: gh-read-run` and is
   gated on `steps.scope.outputs.gh-read-run` (precedent d9990a12f2). Its table
   entry recorded on Linux by
   `python3 -I tools/ci/selftest_scope.py record --step gh-read-run`
   (`0 failed [], 0 broken trace(s)`).
4. **A timing-dependent read set, fixed at its cause.** `beatd.py`'s self-test
   case (a)6 ran `git status --short` on `ROOT`. Status re-reads the content of
   every racily clean index entry (mtime not older than the index), so the
   files it reads follow the checkout's timing: main's measurements recorded
   80, 20 and 235 `beatd` files, mostly `dev/audit/**` logs and PNGs, for one
   unchanged step. The status now runs in the case's own throwaway repo
   (`w / "plain"`, initialised before it); the check, that a non-fetch command
   through the shim logs no retry, is unchanged. Fixed rather than narrowed:
   a narrowed recording would still need the step to read `ROOT`'s index and
   665 dirs, and any file a later checkout leaves racy would refuse again.
   The `beatd` entry is re-recorded from the fixed code.
5. Union with main's later measurements (artifacts 13735714488 and
   13737089304 of `selftest-closures`): `tools/audit/seat/gh_read_run.py`
   added to field-coverage, hooks-setup, open-pr, pr-args, selftest-wiring and
   update-pr (real drift from #3361). Not unioned: their `beatd` sets (the old
   case (a)6, fix 4) and `push-names-the-host`'s probes
   `dev/programme/delivery/3400.md`, `3361.md` and
   `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_red_list_lag.py`, each a path the measured push
   added (`git log --diff-filter=A`: 7326025c8, 5a5b2c4fc, d3deec006), i.e.
   cause 1, fixed by fix 1.

Roster carries: Carry 1 and Carry 2 are one item (22f9186f from
r10-rca-main-selftests-red) recorded twice. Both instances it names are built
here: `ref_privacy.added_lines` as fix 1, beatd's timing-dependent read set
as fix 4.

## Head

`64e6ff57bbd6008f221ec1c39335ba8599be407d` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

79f25fdb3bc296091a1b48d64549927f5391c262

## Mutation proof

New self-test check in `tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py`: a subprocess spy
over `content_check`, on a diff with an added, a modified and a deleted file,
refuses any `git show` of an absent side.

- Before fix 1 (the check added, `added_lines` unchanged):
  `FAIL the content arm never shows a side the diff says is absent ...`,
  `ref_privacy self-test: 125 checks, 1 failed`.
- Mutant `if not present:` -> `if False and not present:`: `125 checks, 1 failed`.
- Mutant ref side `status != "D"` -> `True`: `125 checks, 1 failed`.
- Fixed: `ref_privacy self-test: 125 checks, 0 failed`.
- Fix 3: before it, `FAIL the live job parses (118 steps) and its gating is consistent`
  (main's job 129633096425); after it, `selftest_scope self-test: 96 checks, 0 failed`.

- Fix 4, perturbation: two tracked files touched
  (`dev/audit/rounds/round9/D4/s1/shots/expanded_plan__1280__light__en.png`,
  `dev/audit/waves/w5-g5-195-coverage/coverage/logs/entities.log`), then
  `selftest_scope.py record --step beatd --out <scratch>`. Old case (a)6:
  the entry reads both touched files, `index: true`, 665 dirs. Fixed: neither,
  `index: false`, 1 dir. Unperturbed control, bare `git status --short` under
  `strace -e openat` on this checkout: 0 opens of `dev/audit/*.{png,log,tsv}`
  on a fresh index, 2 after touching those two files, 0 on the next run.

## Null control

On the unmodified tree the new check fails (above), and the other 124 checks
pass, so fix 1 changes no refusal `--check` makes. Table: main's own
measurement (artifact 13730213593) fed to `selftest_scope.drift` gives the
job's 38 refusals against the committed table, and none against this table
once the cause-1 probe is removed from the measurement.

## Figures

- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py --self-test` -> `ref_privacy self-test: 125 checks, 0 failed`
- `python3 -I tools/ci/selftest_scope.py --self-test` -> `selftest_scope self-test: 103 checks, 0 failed` (at 79f25fdb3)
- `python3 -I tools/ci/selftest_scope.py static` -> `selftest_scope static: 110 gated step(s), 0 problem(s)` (at 79f25fdb3)
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/beatd.py --self-test` -> `beatd self-test: 119 checks, 0 failed` (at 79f25fdb3)
- Union check: each artifact's steps against this table, by `selftest_scope.covers` and the dirs rule `drift` uses, misses only in `beatd` (old code) and `push-names-the-host` (the three cause-1 probes above); every other step 0.
- Scoped gate: `tests/closure.py select` -> `MODE: FULL` (`tools/ci/selftest_closures.json changes the gate itself`); left to CI.

## Red checks

`governance / instrument-self-tests` on main (steps `Refuse a self-test read
set the committed table misses`, `Show the self-test scope
(tools/ci/selftest_scope.py) refusing its own fixtures`, `Show the self-test
scope refusing each mutant of its trace rules`). Cheaper detector:
- Cause 2 (table drift) and fix 4 (beatd's timing): none cheaper; only the
  strace measurement of the whole job sees a read set, and it runs on a push
  to main.
- Cause 2b (ungated step): `selftest_scope.py static` / `--self-test`, under a
  second each, would have refused it on #3361's own PR.
- Cause 1 (absent-side probe): a second recording at a different head diff.
Process state (a), no such process: nothing commits main's uploaded `selftest-closures`
artifact when the drift step goes red (`closures-autofix` repairs
`tests/closures.json` only), so main stayed red across merges with the repair
already uploaded. The root cause is owed in a separate seat
(`defect-root-cause.md`).

## Forward-carry

none

## Friction

none

Each: `ref_privacy self-test: 125 checks, 1 failed`, the failing check `the content arm never shows a side the diff says is absent ...`. Not vacuous.

Deleting the `gh-read-run` table entry -> `STALE ... missing ['gh-read-run']`, `110 gated step(s), 1 problem(s)`.

Fixed code: files 3, index false, dirs 1, neither touched file read; covered by the head table (no missing files, dirs or index, run_sha equal). Mutant (status back on `ROOT`): files 7 incl. both touched files, index true, dirs 665; against the head table it misses 4 files, 664 dirs and the index, i.e. drift would refuse. Matches the body's 665 dirs / index figures (ev/fixed.json, ev/mutant.json).
- Table re-record (fix 2/5): my own semantic diff of `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` origin/main vs head, using `selftest_scope.covers` and drift's dirs/ancestor rule with main's committed table as the measurement: every step of main's table is covered by the head table except `beatd` (`.gitignore`, 656 dirs, index), the read set fix 4 removes. All other changes are additions (the textual 1610-line diff is mostly key reordering). The body's union check against main's uploaded artifacts 13730213593, 13735714488, 13737089304 was not re-derived: those artifacts are not reachable from this seat; the CI `governance / instrument-self-tests` run at this head (job 129677221345) concluded success.
- Class (step 6): the body's cause 1 is the one absent-side `git show` in `added_lines`; the fix routes both sides through `--name-status` with `--no-renames`, so no R/C two-path record can misalign the `zip(fields[0::2], fields[1::2])` pairing. No enumeration rule named; the class is one seam.
- Claims/version (steps 4, 5): diff touches no `tests/golden/`, claim file, `VERSION`, manifest or `RELEASE_NOTES.md`; no fixture can move.
- Metrics (step 14): no `*_budgets.json`, `tests/closures.json`, mutation ledger or archscore file in the diff.
- Merge: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 64e6ff57...` exit 0 at origin/main 699f4d9ef4 (ev/merge-tree.txt).
- CI: `merge_train.py classify 64e6ff57bbd6008f221ec1c39335ba8599be407d --pr 3409` -> `GREEN 64e6ff57bbd6008f221ec1c39335ba8599be407d pending: none red: none` (ev/classify.txt). The digest's early `gate` failure (job 129677715544, 06:47) is superseded; classify reads no red. No owed red (`merge_train.py owed-reds` set) is red at this head, so no `## Red checks` answer is owed by this PR's runs; the body answers main's `instrument-self-tests` red anyway, naming process state (a) and a separate RCA seat (roster item r10-rca-main-selftests-red).

merges.body:
deps(tests): the pip group's bumps from Dependabot #3323, re-applied with hashes that install, homeassistant-stubs, zeroconf and cronsim held

Supersedes #3323

Dependabot's branch cannot be edited, so this branch re-applies #3323's version changes (head da3a5cfb8, base 4fe7d5934) to the five test locks. It is cut from main b07627250, and the five files are byte-identical between 4fe7d5934 and that main. This is the same shape as #3088 / #3147. The reds at #3323's head come from two causes:

1. **Stale hashes on five pins.** Dependabot changed the version and kept the previous version's `--hash` lines for coverage 7.17.2 (`requirements-coverage.txt`), and for acme 5.9.0, python-dateutil 4.0.0, sqlalchemy 2.1.8 and uv 0.13.7 (`requirements-typing.txt`). The last four are exactly the typing lock's overrides that the PR moved, the same pattern as #3088's cryptography and uv. pip's hash-checking mode refused the install, which turned `tests / typing` red and `tests / coverage` red. `tests / coverage-ratchet` then had no `coverage-json` artifact. The coverage block is now its header's compile. The typing body is the header's single-package route: this lock as input, those four packages' hash lines deleted, and the override set moved to the new versions.
2. **homeassistant-stubs 2026.10.0.** `tests/typing_ruler.py`'s source-only lock check refuses a lock whose stubs pin disagrees with `tests/typing_budgets.json`'s `ruler`. That was the one failed script in `tests / fast (3.14)`. b9c009a6b held the stubs at 2026.9.3 on purpose: 2026.10.0 is the empty deprecation release, and it changes what the census measures. The stubs therefore stay at 2026.9.3 and no budget moves.

Two of #3323's bumps cannot be compiled under the lock's own rule. homeassistant 2026.10.4 pins `zeroconf==0.151.5` and `cronsim==2.7` exactly, so 0.153.0 and 2.8 are unsatisfiable unless each becomes a new override. Both stay at homeassistant's pin. The override set does not grow, and nothing here needs either version. Every other bump lands as #3323 wrote it: anyio, boto3, botocore, grpcio, mypy-extensions and threadpoolctl in the typing lock, threadpoolctl 3.8.0 in the ci lock, and cython 3.3.1 in the build lock. The ci and build locks are byte-identical to #3323's. py-spy 0.4.3 keeps the nightly-ha lock's documented shape, the two Linux wheels, instead of #3323's nine distributions, so that lock's header stays true.

Text the bump made false is corrected. The typing header names the moved overrides and the held pins. `.github/dependabot.yml` said Dependabot rewrites every hash line of a package it bumps, which was false twice. It now says which pins Dependabot leaves stale and how such a pull request is re-applied.

## Head

`6d894955cfb79f65a64e445acacb8f159342b237` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

a555d52ae875732c290b1847e0b4709826711335

origin/main at b0762725099fefd337fc74ecff161cb487a992bc (`date -u` Tue Nov 10 02:35:05 UTC 2026).

## Mutation proof

- The stale-hash repair: put #3323's `requirements-coverage.txt` back. Then `pip download --require-hashes --no-deps --only-binary=:all: --platform manylinux_2_28_x86_64 ... --python-version 3.13 -r tests/requirements-coverage.txt` exits 1 with `THESE PACKAGES DO NOT MATCH THE HASHES` for `coverage==7.17.2`. The typing lock does the same at 3.14.7 for `acme==5.9.0`: pip stops at the first mismatch, and the per-pin comparison in `## Figures` names all four. This branch's locks exit 0. CI's `tests / coverage` and `tests / typing` logs at da3a5cfb8 show the same refusal, with the same `Got` digest for coverage.
- The stubs hold: put #3323's `requirements-typing.txt` in this tree. Then `python tests/typing_ruler.py` reads `FAIL the typing job's hashed lock installs the recorded pins [homeassistant-stubs==2026.10.0 in the lock, ==2026.9.3 in the budget ...]`, `1 of 11 typing-ruler source checks FAILED`, exit 1. That is CI's `tests / fast (3.14)` failure at da3a5cfb8. Restored, it exits 0.

## Null control

- The census can see an error under this toolchain: append `_HPO_NULL_CONTROL: int = "not an int"` to `const.py` and run `tests/typing_ruler.py --mypy` with this branch's pins. It reads `FAIL errors did not grow [recorded 0, measured 1 (+1)]`, by_code `assignment: 1`. Restored, it reads errors 0.
- The hash comparison can see a correct pin: on #3323's locks the same script reads 127 of 132 pins `OK` and 5 `STALE`. So the zero on this branch comes from correct hashes, not from a comparison that never fires.
- main's typing lock passes the same `pip download --require-hashes` run (exit 0, 111 packages).

## Figures

- Stale hashes, 5 of 132 pins in #3323's five files. For each `name==version` block, the `--hash` set was compared with the sha256 set from `https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json`'s `urls`. coverage 7.17.2: 119 listed, 0 of them PyPI's. acme 5.9.0: 2, 0. python-dateutil 4.0.0: 2, 0. sqlalchemy 2.1.8: 72, 0. uv 0.13.7: 19, 0. Every other pin's set is a subset of PyPI's. At this head the same comparison over all five files reads `STALE pins: 0` (132 pins `OK`).
- `pip download --require-hashes --no-deps --only-binary=:all:` for linux x86_64 (CI's runner platform; PyRIC, sdist-only and unchanged, dropped): the coverage lock on 3.13 and the typing lock on 3.14.7 each exit 0 at this head and exit 1 at #3323's.
- The typing body diff against main (`diff` of the bodies below each header) changes exactly 10 version lines: acme, anyio, boto3, botocore, grpcio, mypy-extensions, python-dateutil, sqlalchemy, threadpoolctl, uv. These are #3323's typing bumps minus homeassistant-stubs, zeroconf and cronsim. The compile was `uv pip compile <lock> --python-version 3.14.7 --python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_28 --generate-hashes --no-header --no-annotate --override <the 13 overrides the header names>`. With #3323's zeroconf it is unsatisfiable (`homeassistant==2026.10.4 depends on zeroconf==0.151.5`), and the same holds with its cronsim (`depends on cronsim==2.7`).
- Typing census at this head: `tests/typing_ruler.py --mypy --emit <file>`, run by a CPython 3.14.7 venv holding this branch's 112 typing pins (macOS wheels, installed `--no-deps` without hashes, because the lock is Linux-only). Result: exit 0, errors 0, by_code `{}`, environment mypy 2.4.1, homeassistant-stubs 2026.9.3, threadpoolctl 3.8.0. CI's `typing` job, on the hashed Linux install, is the authoritative run.
- `python tests/typing_ruler.py` (source-only): exit 0, `ok the typing job's hashed lock installs the recorded pins`. `python3 tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`. `python3 tests/layout.py`: exit 0.
- `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff <merge base> HEAD`: `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`.
- Gate scope, `tests/closure.py select --diff <merge base>`: `MODE: FULL` (`tests/requirements-build.txt changes the gate itself`). The suite is CI's. The ci and build locks are byte-identical to #3323's, and at da3a5cfb8 `tests / fast (3.14)` failed only `typing_ruler.py` (`1 TEST SCRIPT(S) FAILED`). Its `env_drift.py` read `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 56 scenario(s)` and `NO STALE FIXTURE: 56 committed fixture(s)`. Both claim files, `VERSION`, the manifest and `RELEASE_NOTES.md` are byte-identical to origin/main.

## Red checks

There are three causes, none in this branch's files: `tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py`'s read of absent diff sides, drift in `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json`, and #3361's ungated step.
