merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-TRAIN-STALE-VERDICT-GUARD: the merge train refuses a merge verdict when a blocked verdict at the same head was dispatched later (triage batch 127, P393).

The defect, as the triage found it: the train admitted the newest posted `verdict/<pr>` tip. A stale reviewer seat can post its merge verdict after a later-dispatched reviewer has already blocked the same head, and the train admitted it. PR 3232 at `bba5b4d4` is the instance:
- the merge verdict's nonce `2a9f4501` is recorded as dispatched at 2026-11-06T20:50:26Z;
- the blocked verdict's nonce `cc3bfb99` is recorded as dispatched at 22:13:28Z.

Those two times are the triage's record. Both logs that hold them are host-local, so this seat could not re-read them.

The fix, in tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py:
- `Train.posted_verdict` makes one more read after it reads a `merge` verdict: `Train.stale_verdict(n, tip, head)`. Both admission paths share `posted_verdict`: the queue builder (`admit_verdict`, so `queue`, `sweep` and `ready_batch`) and `admit_add`'s `verdict` rule (and through it bus.sh's `add --auto`).
- `stale_verdict` fetches `verdict/<n>` and reads its history from the tip (`git log --format=%H%x00%s`). Every older commit whose subject parses (`proof_watch.parse_verdict`) as `blocked <head>`, at the merge verdict's head, is a finding at that head. If the fetch or the log fails, the merge is refused. A failed read is never taken to mean there is no blocked verdict.
- Nonces: each verdict commit carries its review tree, so the nonce is read from that commit's VERDICT.md by `proof_watch.verdict_nonce`. That function is new: it is the one Python reader of the line bus.sh's `verdict_nonce` reads, the first whole `^bus-nonce: <32 hex>$` line.
- Dispatch times: `dispatch_order` reads them from bus.sh's worker registry, `$HPO_BUS_STATE/dispatched` (else `~/.zcode/bus/dispatched`), which is the source the brief names. It takes the nonce's first record for that PR and head (its mint). It validates the time with `strptime` against bus.sh's `date -u +%FT%TZ`. A same-second pair is ordered by append order.
- `stale_merge` is the rule:
  - same nonce: admitted;
  - the merge verdict's dispatch is before the blocked verdict's: refused, `stale merge verdict: ...`;
  - either time is missing: refused, `stale merge verdict undecidable: ...`, naming which. Missing means no record, a time-less record from before R10-ORCH-DISPATCH-REG (also not dated by a later `--nonce` re-record), a malformed time, no registry file, or no nonce line;
  - later dispatch: admitted.

The seam choice. I put the check on the `posted_verdict` read, not in a new `merge_train.py admit` subcommand. The brief rules that a subcommand is not to be added only to match the carry wording. `posted_verdict` is the one read both admissions share, so one call site covers both. Two alternatives lost:
- `admit_add` alone: the queue builder and the sweep would stay open;
- the events log: the brief rules it out because it keeps only 8 nonce characters.

Design choices:
- An undecidable case refuses rather than admits, as the carry text says. On the orchestrator's host this should cost nothing live. The registry has had its utc field since de66f00bd (R10-ORCH-DISPATCH-REG, 2026-10-26), and the triage records every open PR's dispatches inside that window.
- The guard needs the registry, which lives only on the host where bus.sh dispatches. The instrument entry says to run the train there.

Beyond merge_train.py:
- tools/audit/seat/proof_watch.py, tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py: the agreement lane refused my first cut. It had copied `^bus-nonce: ([0-9a-f]{32})$`, a grammar cloud_dispatch already wrote twice inline, without registering it. I did not register the copy, because CI grades with the base's `SHARED_GRAMMARS` (#3100). Instead, `proof_watch.py` now holds the grammar (`NONCE_LINE`, `verdict_nonce`), and cloud_dispatch's two inline copies call it.
  - cloud_dispatch's self-test reads 129 checks, 0 failed at main 661d26a5d both before and after this change.
  - Importing `review_strength.NONCE_RE` lost: it would add a file outside `agreement_py.py`'s restore closure (`UNRESTORED tools/audit/seat/review_strength.py`), and its rule is looser (`\s*`, no `$`) than bus.sh's.
  - The registry timestamp regex, which gh_calls.py also writes, became a `strptime` parse. That parse also refuses a time that is not a real time.
- tools/audit/seat/instruments/merge_train.py.md: the instrument entry.
- dev/audit/harnesses/r10_triage_p393.py, the finder's harness:
  - a `guard` arm drives the production `Train.stale_verdict` over every historical instance;
  - its nonce reader now imports `proof_watch.verdict_nonce`.

A defect in the harness, found here and fixed in it. Its unanchored `bus-nonce:\s*([0-9a-f]{8})` read the nonce that PR 2465's merge verdict quotes in a finding's prose (round 2's `bus-nonce: 0f1f8919...`) as that verdict's own nonce. The verdict's own trailer is `f8b99351`. So the triage's "4 same" counts one false SAME. At the same bus snapshot, the base harness prints `same=4` and the head harness prints `same=3`.

## Head

`f3810f1c0ce93775298845470e15039a21e8c746` merges main `1cabb84` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution (main's tests/fast red fixed by #3378 (1cabb845)). The reviewed code is unchanged.

`562f446787776e2a77367833f95a4489a1ac7ae7` merges main `2f6d699` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`535182155b21a7c7bbfd8aebb35b76ae58f6e055` merges main `f365ce7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`670b7ccf3fd33a6b2d31befe68ff9c3608a6d647` merges main `3231c07` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`f29c16fac7d846ac098fb30eb466c6961c7f9038` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`fb39908639d83652b8d469da87d90891edac7da8`. It merges origin/main `19865e5a866ce066eaa52f7167a7d901fd1d5968` into `0c1bfeef8`, with no conflict and touching no file this diff changes. The branch was cut from `17e621f08c4feec724478573741fbd8b596ceaba`, the base I was given, and merged main three times. Each merge was made because main had moved since the last `prepr.sh` run, and each was followed by a re-run:
- `a41d9f110` merged `661d26a5d2e655f32391048605db5970d133db1d`;
- `0c1bfeef8` merged `fdc8d21adaa50a7feee534f08ee5edde9bda81ed`;
- this head merged `19865e5a8`.

What was taken where:
- The self-tests, the scope and the final `prepr.sh` run are at this head. The hand mutants are at `962aad515`, which has the same production lines. The prepr run's start, end and origin/main at the start are in `## Figures`.
- The harness figures are at `a41d9f110`. The merges since then brought in no file the harness or `stale_verdict` reads; main's cloud_dispatch.py changes are the only overlap with this diff, and its self-test is green.
- The diff-mutant run is at `a41d9f110`. Since then the branch added one test line (962aad515), whose own survivor is killed by hand below.

## Mutation proof

Failing first, at b9a510304 (the self-test only, before the fix): `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` printed `merge_train self-test: 576 checks, 9 failed`. That run was before later arms were added. The failing checks were:
- `stale verdict: STALE -- ...`;
- the six `stale verdict: a missing dispatch time is refused with its reason (...)` cases that existed then;
- `stale verdict: a same-second tie is ordered by the registry's append order (...)`;
- `stale verdict: an unreadable verdict/<pr> history is refused ...`.

The hand mutants were re-taken at the pre-merge tree of this head (`962aad515`, the same production lines). Each was one single-occurrence replacement in the file, then `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test`, then a restore. Afterwards, `cmp` against the saved copies printed nothing.
- Baseline: `579 checks, 0 failed`.
- M1, the comparison dropped (`if mt < bt:` -> `if False:`): `3 failed`:
  - `stale verdict: STALE -- ...`;
  - `stale verdict: a same-second tie ...`;
  - `stale verdict: the dispatch time decides, not the registry's line order ...`.
- M2, the same-nonce admission dropped (`if merge is not None and b == merge:` -> `if False:`): `1 failed`, `stale verdict: SAME (null control) -- ...`.
- M3, proof_watch's `NONCE_LINE` unanchored (`^bus-nonce: ...$` -> `bus-nonce: ...`): `5 failed`, among them STALE and LATER. The fixture's VERDICT.md quotes the other verdict's nonce in prose, in PR 2465's shape.
- M4, a time-less mint dated by a later re-record (`return None` -> `continue` in `dispatch_order`): `1 failed`, `... (a mint before the utc field is not dated by a later --nonce re-record)`.
- S1, `return f[4], i` -> `return f[5], i`: `1 failed`, `... the dispatch time decides, not the registry's line order ...`.
- S5380, the fixture's `calls.append(argv)` dropped: `1 failed`, `stale verdict: a blocked verdict at another head is not this head's finding (admitted, no nonce read)`.
- Killed at b8a801aea by the same method:
  - the fetch guard off (`if False:`): `1 failed`;
  - the fetch guard's `[0]` -> `[1]`: `6 failed`;
  - the no-blocked early exit off: `1 failed`.

Diff mutants: `prepr.sh` step 6d at `a41d9f110`, with `MUTANT_CMD` set to the merge_train, proof_watch and cloud_dispatch self-tests, printed `6 survivor(s) on the diff's added lines`. Each is answered under `## Unpinned sites`. The same step at `e53b46eda` had printed 11. The 5 killed since are S1, the fetch guard's GUARD_OFF, CONST_SWAP and RETURN_DEL, and the early-exit GUARD_OFF and RETURN_DEL, killed by the tests in b8a801aea.

## Null control

- The two arms the rule must admit:
  - `stale verdict: LATER (null control)`: the merge verdict dispatched after the blocked one is admitted, by `posted_verdict` and by `admit_add`;
  - `stale verdict: SAME (null control)`: one nonce posted both verdicts, with an empty registry, and it is admitted.
- `stale verdict: a blocked verdict at another head is not this head's finding`: admitted with no registry file. The check also asserts that the history read ran, so it is not vacuous, and that no nonce was read.
- The unmodified tree: at the base, the guard arm admits every one of the 64 historical instances (`guard=absent admitted=64`; `## Figures`). That is the defect.
- The existing fixtures pass unchanged: merge_train `579 checks, 0 failed`, against `564` at main. Their stubs answer `git log` with nothing, so no verdict in them has a blocked predecessor.
- proof_watch prints `47 checks, 0 failed` and cloud_dispatch `131 checks, 0 failed` at this head. The same scripts at main `fdc8d21ad` print 47 and 131; main added cloud_dispatch's two extra checks since 661d26a5d, where it printed 129 both with and without this diff.

## Figures

- Self-tests at the head:
  - `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` prints `merge_train self-test: 579 checks, 0 failed`. At main it prints `564 checks, 0 failed`; this diff adds 15 checks in `_stale_verdict_self_test`.
  - `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/proof_watch.py --self-test` prints `proof_watch self-test: 47 checks, 0 failed`.
  - `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py --self-test` prints `cloud_dispatch self-test: 131 checks, 0 failed`.
- The finder's harness at both ends.
  - Setup:
    - The base copy is dev/audit/harnesses/r10_triage_p393.py at main 661d26a5d (unchanged since 17e621f08), sha1 aad12c7b1a754c181fa49ae348840676ea9e04e4. The head copy has sha1 040151ecdc06d0f7cdf45cbb7e0311056b9353de.
    - The runs were taken back to back, 2026-11-08T22:36:22Z to 22:36:42Z, over one fetch of every `verdict/*` and `review/*` ref. The bus moves (703, 704 and 705 refs across this session's runs), so a later run re-derives its own counts.
    - The `stale` arm's events log is host-local and absent here, so it was given an empty file. That is why the brief's `1 stale, 21 later` cannot be re-taken here: STALE and LATER need a time, and SAME does not.
  - `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_triage_p393.py stale <empty events.tsv>`:
    - base: `verdict refs=705 instances=64 stale=0 later=0 same=4 unknown=60`;
    - head: `verdict refs=705 instances=64 stale=0 later=0 same=3 unknown=61`.
    - `diff` of the two outputs differs only on PR 2465's line (`SAME ... merge=0f1f8919` -> `UNKNOWN ... merge=f8b99351`) and on the tally.
  - `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_triage_p393.py guard <state dir>`, with the head harness copied beside the base tree's merge_train (removed afterwards):
    - base merge_train, empty state dir: `guard=absent admitted=64 refused-stale=0 refused-undecidable=0`.
    - head, empty state dir (no registry): `guard=yes admitted=3 refused-stale=0 refused-undecidable=61`. The 3 admitted are exactly the head `stale` arm's 3 SAME: PR 2323, 2329 and 3045.
    - head, with a registry of PR 3232's two dispatches only, at the triage's recorded times, with full nonces read from that PR's verdict commits b09e48026 and 8000a4f5d: `admitted=3 refused-stale=1 refused-undecidable=60`. The refusal line is `refused-stale pr=3232 head=bba5b4d4 merge=b09e4802 stale merge verdict: its nonce 2a9f4501 was dispatched at 2026-11-06T20:50:26Z, before the blocked verdict's cc3bfb99 at 2026-11-06T22:13:28Z`.
    - null control, the same registry with the merge dispatch moved after the blocked one (23:50:26Z): `admitted=4 refused-stale=0 refused-undecidable=60`, PR 3232 admitted.
    - base merge_train with the PR 3232 registry: `admitted=64`, so the base admits the stale verdict.
  - The real 1/21 split needs the host registry. The reviewer or orchestrator runs `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_triage_p393.py guard ~/.zcode/bus` on the host where bus.sh dispatches.
- Class enumeration. The rule: `git grep -n -E 'parse_verdict\(|posted_verdict\(|VERDICT_MERGE' -- tools`, less self-test lines. Every seam it returns, and its disposition:
  - `merge_train.py` `admit_verdict` -> `posted_verdict` (queue, sweep, ready_batch): closed in this diff.
  - `merge_train.py` `add_verdict` -> `posted_verdict` (`admit_add`, and bus.sh's `add --auto` at post time): closed in this diff.
  - `merge_train.py` `stale_verdict`'s own `parse_verdict` call: this diff.
  - `orchestrator_tick.py` `MERGE-READY` and `REVIEW STALLED`: unchanged on purpose. These are report lines that merge nothing, and a stale verdict flagged MERGE-READY is still refused at the train's admission.

  - tools/pr/app_approve.sh's evidence gate: the rule does not return it. It runs only after the train has admitted the entry, and the train now refuses the stale case first.
- Scoped gate at the head: `D=$(mktemp -d); python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out` and names tests/entities.py.

- run_always lines, at cc7dc09ff:
  - `tests/env_drift.py --claims-only` printed `claims hygiene: 17e621f... ok`;
  - `tests/closure.py selftest` printed `ALL 118 closure shrink pins PASSED`;

- Agreement: `python3 -I tools/policy/agreement_py.py --out <f>` then `node tools/policy/agreement.mjs --py-json <f>` prints `RESULT divergent=0 unregistered=0 dead=0 refused=0` and `AGREEMENT ok`. The restore line reads `18 closure file(s), 18 covered`.

It ran 2026-11-09T00:13:24Z to 00:34:34Z, with origin/main at `19865e5a8` at its start and still there at its end, so no merge or second run was owed. Its `diff mutants` step was skipped (MUTANT_CMD unset); that step's figures are the `a41d9f110` run under `## Mutation proof`, with the same production lines. ## Unpinned sites

The six survivors from `prepr.sh` step 6d at `a41d9f110`. Each is equivalent; none is a skipped test.
- `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py:1224 RETURN_DEL`, the closing `return None` of `dispatch_order`: falling off the end returns None. Carry: dismissed: equivalent mutant, an implicit return is None

It is kept so the arm holds when run on its own. Carry: dismissed: equivalent mutant under the self-test's call order
- `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py:5380 CALL_DEL`, the fixture's `calls.append(argv)`: killed at 962aad515 by S5380 above. The no-nonce-read null now asserts that the history read was recorded. Carry: dismissed: killed by 962aad515, the step ran before it

The cheaper detector exists and is not a new cost: the scoped gate on the merged tree, which `tests/closures.json` already points at those scripts (#3378's body names it and leaves the train re-proof question to the root-cause seat). No countermeasure is built here.

merges.body:
Outside work orders ahead of audit and owner work in every orderer, after main and hotfix. Round 3 repairs the round-2 verdict (class-open at 2bf0e026): every orderer now reads the hotfix tier from one predicate, `roster_lib.is_hotfix`.

Owner ruling (tvofi 2026-11-07, triage batch 134 P420), verbatim: "all accepted outside issues or contributions should be prioritized higher than audit or owner submitted ones unless i call the owner one a hotfix."

## Head

`dc9a22f468e84541f12b56d3a51f766dbf7bccf9` merges main `1cabb84` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution (main's tests/fast red fixed by #3378 (1cabb845)). The reviewed code is unchanged.

`62f90fcb3bd8a45775642d290bf86b3274cb040d` merges main `2f6d699` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`aff9f1393aec11bc0f5fc745d34a9161c09b695a` merges main `7bdc8aa` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`cc0b58ff5be5b428a73d3b5b7e8caa184404d0ea` merges main `f365ce7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`0e307d59e495c56eb705ee9484f83311b38ce8d9` merges main `c782949` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`43136fbca4b5ba2a6f7f137f60cf67951a305c94` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`a0bad333ed4e0db2a7609c3b6a1df18625242011` merges origin/main `daf8b349fd30cc60786eeca333a426b693aa4c5f` into `f7161d2030a7cb6265eff2f22408e6457a3e00bc`. f7161d20 merged origin/main `51cd5ec8a42abde3c223f22e9f4a0d5f35f8844a` into the repair commit `2135d8b92f24f1020dd2016b46f99249ae7af57c`, which sits on the round-2 head `2bf0e026397c99378c53d47a0a49c30927deefd9`. Neither merge had a conflict. The figures below were taken at f7161d20 unless a line names another head. `git diff --name-only f7161d20 a0bad333` lists only `dev/programme/delivery/3346.md` and `tests/card_browser.mjs`, so the second merge reaches no file these figures read, and no self-test re-ran for it. prepr re-ran at a0bad333 (Figures). origin/main daf8b349 at 2026-11-08T21:13Z.

## Round-2 repair (commit 2135d8b92f24)

The verdict: `tools/plan/replan.py` `dispatch_tier` kept the base's hotfix predicate, `k == "bug" or "HOTFIX" in g and cls == "production"`. Under it an instrument-class R10-HOTFIX group fell to the instrument tier (6), below outside (3). Every other orderer ranked it above outside. Chosen fix: `dispatch_tier`'s hotfix arm is now `roster_lib.is_hotfix(group)`, the predicate `dispatch_rank` already applies. Rejected alternative: keep the class condition and get the owner's word that a non-production hotfix ranks below outside in the plan only. The ruling says "unless i call the owner one a hotfix", and a HOTFIX name is that call, so the plan has no reason to differ from the opener, the gate lease or the OWED list.

Enumeration rule for hotfix predicates, a different rule from the ordering-site grep in round 1: `grep -rnE '"HOTFIX"|R10-HOTFIX-|r10-hotfix-|is_hotfix|== "bug"' tools/ --include=*.py --include=*.mjs --include=*.sh`, with `_selftest.py` files and comment lines dropped. Each seam it returns, and its disposition:
- replan.py `dispatch_tier`: closed in this diff (`roster_lib.is_hotfix`).
- roster_lib.py `is_hotfix` / `dispatch_rank`: the owner of the predicate, unchanged. gate_priority `derived_priority` and orchestrator_tick `owed_levels` reach it through `dispatch_rank`, so they were already guarded.
- open_driver.py `default_class`: closed in this diff. It took a hotfix by topic or group name only. It now also takes the roster's `is_hotfix` set, passed through `order` and `run_pass` the same way the outside set is, so a `kind` "bug" group counts too. This is the verdict's minor finding.
- merge_train.py `drain_order`: closed in this diff. The rule returned it, and the verdict did not name it. Before this commit the drain read a hotfix only from the `--priority` flag, so a roster hotfix spooled without the flag drained behind outside entries. `Train._hotfix` (`roster_lib.is_hotfix` through the same `_roster_group` mapping, branch then `resume.pr`) now puts it in the `--priority` tier. `_outside` and `_hotfix` share one `_roster_is` reader.
- The other hits are comments, strings in fixtures or messages, or group names quoted as provenance: agreement.mjs:590, gh_comment.py:506, and merge_train.py at the R10-HOTFIX-TRAIN-DEFER-WAIT docstrings and comment. None of them decides an order.

Other verdict findings, closed in commit 2135d8b9:
- orchestrator_tick `owed_levels` maps a PR to its group by `group_for_branch`, else by `group_for_pr(roster, n)`, as `merge_train._roster_group` does, so a fork-head outside PR keeps its rank. gate_priority `derived_priority` gets no fallback: it runs before a pull request exists (prepr step 1b0) and receives a branch, not a PR number.
- `tools/audit/seat/instruments/merge_train.py.md` now states the drain order: `--priority`, roster hotfix or `--front`; then outside; then critical path; then arrival. It also states the branch-then-`group_for_pr` mapping.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant ran from a `git archive` of f7161d20 with the owner file's own `--self-test`. The script is `mut.sh` in the seat's scratch, a one-off, so it stays out of the tree. Lines are `name: mutation -> result, failing check`:
- replan-base-arm: `if roster_lib.is_hotfix(group):` restored to the base's `if k == "bug" or "HOTFIX" in g and cls == "production":` -> KILLED. It fails `an instrument-class R10-HOTFIX group is the hotfix tier and holds the one real slot at t0 ahead of an outside group ...` with `{'OUT': ('2026-01-05T00:00:00Z', 0, None, 3), 'R10-HOTFIX-X': ('2026-01-05T18:00:00Z', 0, None, 6)}`. That is the verdict's misordering: OUT holds the slot and the hotfix waits 18 h. The in-tree `tier-hotfix` mutant check also fails, because its anchor is the line this mutant removed.
- od-hotfix-set: `if group and roster_lib.norm_group(group) in hotfix:` -> `if False:` -> KILLED. It fails `run_pass: a kind-bug group with no HOTFIX name opens ahead of an outside group, cap 1`.
- od-hotfix-wiring: `run_pass` drops the `hotfix` argument to `order` -> KILLED by the same check.
- ot-fork-fallback: `or rl.group_for_pr(roster, n)` deleted -> KILLED. It fails `OWED buckets: a fork-head outside PR, mapped by resume.pr, prints before the critical path's; unrecorded, after it`.
- mt-drain-hotfix: `or self.hotfix(items[id(e)])` -> `or False` -> KILLED. It fails `P420 drain_order: a roster hotfix with no --priority flag (#8) drains ahead of an outside entry (#31)`.
- mt-hotfix-pred: `_hotfix` reads `is_outside` instead of `is_hotfix` -> KILLED by the same check.
Restored, each of these self-tests is 0 failed at f7161d20 (Figures). The earlier rounds' mutants stand as recorded at d21a15eb and 51838e6d, including the overflow-arm-order proof.

## Null control

Each new check has a null arm that would print the opposite result had the predicate been absent:
- replan: `null control: the same instrument without a HOTFIX name stays the instrument tier`.
- open_driver: `run_pass null: the same group with no kind waits behind the outside group` (it launches `r10-out`).
- orchestrator_tick: the same fork PR with `resume.pr` unrecorded prints after the critical path's (`[#100, #104]`).
- merge_train: `P420 drain_order null: the same group without a HOTFIX name drains behind the outside entry` (`[31, 7, 8]`).
The live-roster count below has its own null control: the pre-repair head 2bf0e026, run with the same script on the same roster, prints 7.

## Figures

- Live roster, command `python3 -I tiers.py <tree> wave-r10-groups.json`. The script is a one-off in the seat's scratch. Rule: for every roster group where `roster_lib.is_hotfix` and `roster_lib.is_open` hold, count those whose `replan.dispatch_tier(g, False, g.get("savings"))` is not `TIER_HOTFIX`. Roster `handoff/audit-r10-roster` 93fd3041c1f1 at 2026-11-08T20:51:39Z. At f7161d20 it prints `open is_hotfix groups 9; not TIER_HOTFIX in replan 0`. At 2bf0e026 it prints `... 9; ... 7`, the same seven groups the verdict lists: GATE-BUSY-DEFER, CODEQL-HEADROOM, TRAIN-DEFER-WAIT, AUTHOR-EMAIL, NONREQUIRED-REDS, ROSTER-LINT-REFRESH and PREPR-SELFTEST-DARWIN. The verdict counted 8 open at roster 6fb2599d. The roster has moved since, so the open count is the roster's, not this diff's.
- Two-group fixture with slots=1, R10-HOTFIX-X (kind instrument) and OUT (source outside), read with `build_plan`. At 2bf0e026: OUT is on slot 0 at t0 and the hotfix starts at t0+18 h, tiers 3 and 6. At f7161d20: R10-HOTFIX-X is on real slot 0 at t0, tier 2. OUT is the taller group, so it is the critical path, and it starts beside the hotfix at t0 flagged exempt.
- Self-tests at f7161d20, each printed by its own `--self-test`, all 0 failed: replan `self-test: 0 failed`; gate_priority 15 checks; roster_lib 71; orchestrator_tick 286 (285 plus the fork-head check); merge_train 574 (main's checks plus this diff's two drain checks); plan_page 67; open_driver 86 (84 plus the two run_pass checks).
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED. `tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff 2bf0e026` at 2135d8b9: `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`.
- Scope: `tests/closure.py select --diff 51cd5ec8` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out`, and `scope.run` names `tests/entities.py`, which needs the real Home Assistant package (see the round-2 evidence) and is left to CI.
- `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1 bash tools/pr/prepr.sh <body.md>`, body check included: rc=0 at f7161d20. Main then moved to daf8b349, so origin/main was merged and prepr was re-run at a0bad333 (next line).
- `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1 bash tools/pr/prepr.sh <body.md>` at a0bad333, body check included: `PRE-PR: a0bad333ed4e... rc=0` at 2026-11-08T21:14:57Z, and origin/main was still daf8b349 when the run ended.
- The three-dot diff against 51cd5ec8 touches no `VERSION`, manifest, `RELEASE_NOTES.md`, `tests/golden/` file or `*budgets.json`.

## Red checks

At the round-2 head 2bf0e026, every check run concluded success, skipped or neutral (verdict evidence, 55 runs). The three reds below come from earlier heads and are answered as they were.

`governance / instrument-self-tests` (job 128661348216): red. Cause: `python3 -I tools/plan/replan.py --self-test` failed on the PR merge ref (refs/pull/3304/merge, 5259a4c4) with `FAIL dispatch follows the owner's order ... ['CPA','CPB','CPC','R10-HOTFIX-H','OUT',...]`, then `FAIL the unmutated copy's self-test exits 0`. The head alone passed and origin/main alone passed; the merge failed. Main's build_plan ran its critical-path overflow arm before the tiered pick, so critical-path groups took the real slot ahead of the hotfix and outside groups this diff ranks above them. This diff owned the red. Repaired above: origin/main merged in, the tiered pick runs first, replan self-test 0 failed at 4c4dd755. Cheaper detector: running the self-test on `git merge origin/main` of the head. It exists as this CI job; tools/pr/prepr.sh runs on the head unmerged. By the owner ruling of 2026-11-07 it is not rerun when main moves, so no pre-push detector covers a main-side scheduler change landing after the push. Standing cost of a merged-tree self-test pass in prepr: one replan.py run, about 85 s. Carry: dismissed: the merge train recarries and re-proves the head on current main under the owner ruling, so a prepr merge step would repeat that proof.

`pr-contract / pr-contract` (job 128661350034): red. Cause: `[pr-body] check governance / instrument-self-tests is red and ## Red checks does not name it`, the only error; the body said `none`. This diff did not cause it beyond the red above; this section names the check. Cheaper detector: `tools/pr/prepr.sh --body-check`, which exists and reads the red-history from the check-runs. It ran before the red existed, so it could not name it.

`gate` (job 128661143751): red at `Judge this head`, one line: `FAIL pr-contract / pr-contract: failure`. A consequence of the pr-contract red above; no separate cause and nothing to detect.

`tests / fast (3.14)` (check-run 129330845342, job 129330845342, head `62f90fcb3bd8`): red, and it is main's red inherited at 2f6d699e, not this diff's. Cause: `tests/entities.py` (3 of 2707 checks) and `tests/harness_headers.py` (3 of 112) failed; the log shows `FAIL de.json has exactly strings.json's keys` for `options.step.entities.sections.indoor.data.flow_heat_c`, `flow_min_lift_k` (data and data_description) and `selector.space_setpoint_unit.options.return`, the two flow-field label/description checks in de.json, and D6 claim C112 false (`claims_true` 122 against 123), which fails the byte-identical harness output check. Main's own tests/fast run at 2f6d699e (job 129291622423) prints the same de.json and D6 lines. The skew is between #3372/#3360 and #3331: keys missing from de.json and from the card's German dictionary. The fix is hotfix #3378. This branch inherited it through a recarry onto red main and touches none of de.json, strings.json, the card or D6. Process state (d): the process was sound and main's state changed underneath the recarry. Cheaper detector: none on this branch, since the branch does not touch those files; the detector for the skew is the tests/fast run that caught it on main. Carry: dismissed: the fix is #3378 on main and the train recarry re-proves this head on the repaired main.

## Forward-carry

Splitting hotfix from outside inside the gate lease needs PRIORITY_MAX above 2 in tests/gate_lock.py (a different seam); not done here, hotfix and outside share band 2. Carry: dismissed: the lease has three bands and arrival orders within one, a hotfix waits behind an older outside run for one lease at most, and raising PRIORITY_MAX changes the aging rule for every waiter, so the split is not worth building without a measured wait

## Friction

fixer-step-push: contradiction: refs/heads/handoff-wip/r10-outside-first still holds a prior seat's BLOCKED commit 4a66cde5, which is not an ancestor of this head. A fast-forward step push is impossible, so none was made and nothing was forced. This seat hands off directly. Carry: dismissed: the brief deletes the step ref after the handoff, which clears it for the next seat
mutant-cmd-scope: cost: one MUTANT_CMD runs one self-test over the mutants of every changed file, so on a multi-file diff the prepr count reports the command's reach, not the pins. This round's proof is per file (above). Carry: dismissed: per-file runs by `--path` already exist in mutant_run.py, and a seat that reads its survivors per file finds the gap in one listing

## Unpinned sites

Every remaining survivor from the per-file runs, by disposition:
- Self-test lines (a mutant there weakens a fixture or deletes one check; no production behaviour moves). These are value checks in the instrument's own self-test, and `mutation-autofix` mutates `custom_components/` only. gate_priority.py:231 (`>` to `>=` in the check). roster_lib.py:894 and :914 (fixture constants in the is_outside and group_for_pr checks). replan.py:755, :761, :762 and :766 (tier-check bounds and constants). replan.py:792 is tightened from `slot < 1` to `slot == 0` at 4c4dd755 and not re-run by the instrument. All 9 open_driver_selftest.py sites (:114, :118, :119 x2, :120 x2, :122, :124, :126), a test-only file. All 15 merge_train.py sites (:4010 x2, :5572, :5574, :5585, :5588, :5591, :5592, :5597, :5605 x2, :5607, :5615, :6961 x2), all inside `_self_test` (lines 3836 to 8396): the fixture default `outside=lambda it: False` and fork-head fixture constants.
- Equivalent: roster_lib.py:657 RETURN_DEL. `continue` becomes `pass` as the last statement of the loop body, so the next iteration follows either way. orchestrator_tick.py:897 CONST_SWAP. The no-roster default rank `3` becomes `4` only on the arm where every item gets the same constant, so the sort by PR number is unchanged.
- Round 3 (2135d8b9): every production line this commit adds is pinned by a killed mutant above: replan's hotfix arm, open_driver's hotfix set and its wiring, the tick's fork-head fallback, and merge_train's drain term and `_hotfix` predicate. `_roster_is` is the body `_outside` already had, and the P420 `_outside` checks pin it. The new lines in the test files and the instrument doc are fixtures and prose.

## Block

This is round 2, a later-round review. I reviewed head 2bf0e026397c99378c53d47a0a49c30927deefd9 against merge base 73365699a135fb813a43380096b6776d57f8ff4c, using the three-dot diff. Every Block and Finding item from round 1 (verdict/3304 at 429c7eaab) is closed at this head (see Evidence). One new item blocks.

The brief defines the order as "main, then hotfix (an R10-HOTFIX- name or kind bug), then outside, then today's order". The PR adds `roster_lib.is_hotfix`, which follows that definition: kind `bug`, or `HOTFIX` in the name. It also adds `dispatch_rank`, whose docstring calls it "the one order every queue reader applies". gate_priority and the tick's OWED order use it. open_driver gets the same result by name.

`tools/plan/replan.py` `dispatch_tier` does not use it. The diff moves its hotfix line ahead of the new outside arm but keeps the predicate `k == "bug" or "HOTFIX" in g and cls == "production"`. So an R10-HOTFIX-named group that is not production class is not a hotfix in the plan. It falls to the instrument tier (6), below outside (3) and below the critical path (4).

On the live roster (`handoff/audit-r10-roster` 6fb2599d), 8 HOTFIX-named groups are not done. 7 of them get replan tier 6 and dispatch_rank 0 (`ev/live-hotfix-tiers.txt`): GATE-BUSY-DEFER, CODEQL-HEADROOM, TRAIN-DEFER-WAIT, AUTHOR-EMAIL, NONREQUIRED-REDS, ROSTER-LINT-REFRESH and PREPR-SELFTEST-DARWIN.

A two-group fixture shows the effect (`ev/hotfix-predicate.txt`). With slots=1, R10-HOTFIX-X (kind instrument) and OUT (source outside):
- replan dispatches `['OUT', 'R10-HOTFIX-X']` (tiers 3 and 6);
- dispatch_rank gives `{'R10-HOTFIX-X': 0, 'OUT': 1}`;
- open_driver orders `['r10-hotfix-x', 'r10-out']`.

The plan therefore starts an outside group ahead of a group the owner named a hotfix. The opener, gate lease and OWED list put that hotfix first. That breaks the ruling's "unless i call the owner one a hotfix" in the one orderer that decides fixer starts. It also contradicts the PR's own claim of a single order.

The body's enumeration rule (`critical_path|critical_path_groups|CRITICAL_PRIORITY`) finds ordering sites, not hotfix predicates. So this seam is neither in its output nor dispositioned. The `production` condition was inherited from the base, where it decided only "urgent or not". This diff gives hotfix its own tier above outside, so the old predicate now decides an order the ruling settles.

To settle it, do one of these:
- make `dispatch_tier`'s hotfix arm `roster_lib.is_hotfix(group)`, with a fixture that has a non-production R10-HOTFIX group and an outside group, plus its mutant;
- or disposition in the body why a non-production hotfix should rank below outside in the plan only, with the owner's word for it.

Carry: R10-OUTSIDE-FIRST

## Findings

Carry: R10-OUTSIDE-FIRST
- Defect (minor, same seam): `open_driver.default_class` treats a hotfix by name only (`r10-hotfix-` topic or `R10-HOTFIX-` group), never by kind `bug`, which the brief and `is_hotfix` both count. No live non-done group is kind `bug` without a HOTFIX name today, so nothing is misordered now. Passing `is_hotfix` through as the outside set is passed would close it. Carry: R10-OUTSIDE-FIRST
- Defect (doc): `tools/audit/seat/instruments/merge_train.py.md` is in the group's roster `files` list. It describes `Train.drain_order` and the `--front`/`--priority` tier, but not the new outside term between priority and the critical path. Carry: R10-OUTSIDE-FIRST
- Follow-up: `orchestrator_tick.owed_levels` and `gate_priority.derived_priority` map a PR to its group by `group_for_branch` only. A fork-head outside PR, whose branch no group claims, gets rank 3 / priority 0 there, while `merge_train._roster_group` falls back to `group_for_pr`. The brief requires that fallback only in merge_train. The tick has the PR number, so the same fallback would cost one call. Carry: R10-OUTSIDE-FIRST

merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-RCA-SWEEP-SETTLE-LOOP is the root-cause seat for the sweep settle loop. It ran beside the R10-SWEEP-SETTLE-LOOP fixer and did not edit `tools/ci/`. Part of #201. The analysis is `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-SWEEP-SETTLE-LOOP.md`, indexed in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json` as `_rca.R10-RCA-SWEEP-SETTLE-LOOP`. Trigger: release (#3287, `52f9fc5b34`, shipped in v7.1.6).

- **Cause.** `tools/ci/sweep.py` `undecided()` arm 1 treats any non-gate job of another run whose `completed_at` is later than this gate's start as a source that finished late. When GitHub re-runs a `gate` job, it re-stamps every skipped job of that run seconds before the new gate starts. Every job that ran keeps its stamps. This was measured on #3319's runs 42469369199 and 42469369682, attempts 1 to 6. As a result, two red gates at one head re-run each other until the cap (attempt 44).
- **Process state (c).** #3287 pinned "the branch cannot loop" with one-pass nulls. Those nulls ran over hand-written units that have no `conclusion` field and that a re-run never moves. Its recorded replay ran one open-loop sweep, even though its own fixture's attempt-10 rows already showed the re-stamp. The review accepted the nulls, and the live head it watched re-ran green, which ends the loop at the first step.
- **Countermeasure A (state c), adopted and carried to the fix.** The convergence claim is pinned closed-loop over a recorded attempt-to-attempt transition. The harness added here is offered as the finder's harness at both ends.
- **Countermeasure B, proposed to triage, not built.** A beat row that flags any ci.yml run at attempt 20 or above.

## Head

`ebae602abf29240285d792c662f985860d5338ac` merges main `1cabb84` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution (main's tests/fast red fixed by #3378 (1cabb845)). The reviewed code is unchanged.

Head 97b15d1667506caf05a78e1548859e29f837a5d7: two github-actions[bot] 'ci: merge main' commits over 4818b1a2 (review_carry CARRY); no code change since that head.

`4818b1a254b8e34c15a08af342957e17026de04c` is `github-actions[bot]`'s `ci: merge main` of origin/main `c782949e34` into the reviewed head `1310d182e16b`: an automatic merge, no resolution, no branch-authored commit (`review_carry.py 1310d182 4818b1a2`: CARRY). The code reviewed at `1310d182` is unchanged.

`1310d182e16b613937de0e200f03f2aa15c65785` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`3aa0616e7b29c421d00bb3054922275717e44625` merges origin/main `daf8b349fd30` into `1b2307959d53`: an automatic merge, no resolution. Main's delta since `51cd5ec` touches only `tests/card_browser.mjs` and `dev/programme/delivery/3346.md`, which nothing in this diff reads. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`1b2307959d535b0400dc25fc9891a190a76db8a2` merges main `51cd5ec` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`50a78a49ba19061c5d4e6e4a8f5efae62da64aab` merges the authored code head `95f3e79e7af9a4dbe2e18be5078eeaf89d23bd53`.

`95f3e79e7af9a4dbe2e18be5078eeaf89d23bd53` (the repair of blocked 8db2e568; origin/main `bb7dfb9bd6c6` merged, prepr.sh rc=0 on it), branch `fix/r10-rca-sweep-settle-loop`, two commits on origin/main `4fe7d5934b`, which is the merge base. The three-dot diff adds:
- the RCA document;
- the harness `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_sweep_settle_loop.py` and its recorded fixture `.json`;
- the `_rca` entry;
- the harness's `tests/closures.json` INERT READS entry, written by `ci_predict.py --apply-inert`.

It has no production line, and no delivery row because no PR exists yet.

## Mutation proof

This handoff adds no production line. The detector it adds is the harness's `replay` arm. It was run against real program copies made with `git archive <sha> tools/ci`:
- **Red on the defect.** At `origin/main` `4fe7d5934b` and at `52f9fc5b34` it prints `RESULT replay reruns=86 max_attempt=44 sim_minutes=72 alarm=yes`.
- **Green once fixed.** On a candidate copy where arm 1 ignores `conclusion == "skipped"` it prints `reruns=1 max_attempt=2 alarm=no`. This candidate is a control for the harness, not the fix. It also passes the current `sweep.py --self-test` (52 checks, 0 failed), so today's self-test cannot tell a fixed arm 1 from a broken one.

## Null control

- `--no-restamp` (the hand-written fixtures' world) at `origin/main` prints `reruns=1 max_attempt=2 alarm=no`. The arm's power comes from the recorded transition. A world without it hides the defect.
- `52f9fc5b34^` (before `settle` existed) prints `reruns=0` on the same real-red head, which is correct: a genuine red is not re-run.
- The census predicate at alarm 20 flags 0 runs in the 21.2 h before the merge and 32 runs in the 16.6 h after it. At alarm 10 it flags 4 runs before the merge (the predecessor design's 10-17-attempt runs), which is why the proposed threshold is 20.

## Figures

- Replay: `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_sweep_settle_loop.py replay [--ci <export>/tools/ci] [--no-restamp]`, with results as above. Runtime is 0.12-0.25 s (`time -p`).
- Census: `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_sweep_settle_loop.py census <tsv> --since ... --until ... --alarm N`. The TSV is `gh api --paginate repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?per_page=100&created=>=2026-11-06T22:00:00Z`, read at 2026-11-08T11:52:46Z.
  - Pre-merge: `runs=465 reattempts=428 at_cap=0 max_attempt=17`.
  - Post-merge: `runs=324 reattempts=1618 at_cap=17 max_attempt=45`.
- `gate-sweep.yml`: 1000 runs (the API cap) were created between 07:53:04Z and 11:50:13Z, totalling 904 run-minutes, median 23 s each.
- Detector probe: one `gh api ...ci.yml/runs?created>=...` call takes 2.84 s.
- The brief's 1089 re-attempts and 810 runner-minutes are the orchestrator's figures over its own window. They were not re-taken here.
- Re-taken at `3aa0616e7b29` (`date -u` 2026-11-08, origin/main `daf8b349fd30`): `replay` prints `RESULT replay reruns=86 max_attempt=44 sim_minutes=72 alarm=yes`, and `replay --no-restamp` prints `RESULT replay reruns=1 max_attempt=2 sim_minutes=1 alarm=no`. `tests/closure.py select` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out` (`tests/entities.py`). `tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- Local checks at the earlier head:
  - `python3 tools/audit/fold_ledger.py check` prints `0 violation(s)`, 138 rca entries.
  - `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
  - `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out`.
  - `ci_predict.py --base origin/main` predicts no red.
  - `tests/entities.py` could not run on this host (it has no `homeassistant`); `tests/harness_headers.py` was not run to completion here, and this harness carries no EXPECTED RESULT lines, so it executes nothing of it.

## Red checks

Train skip at `1b2307959d53`, run 42519917698: `governance / instrument-self-tests`, `pr-contract / pr-contract` and `gate` red.

- `governance / instrument-self-tests`: the one failing check in job 128852059264's log is `FAIL   mutant mut:unlock (its line deleted): the holder is still alive when the run returns`, giving `pr_args self-test: 184 checks, 1 failed` in the `update-pr` step. That is a timing-dependent arm in `tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh`, a file this diff does not touch (`git diff --stat $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD` lists six files, none under `tools/`). The arm reads the lock holder inside its 0.2 s `mut:watch` poll, so under load it can read a holder that already exited. Not this diff's: in the same job, the `pr-args` and `open-pr` steps ran the same self-test and printed `pr_args self-test: 184 checks, 0 failed`, and `governance / instrument-self-tests` is `success` at main `51cd5ec8` (run 42519600464). The deterministic arm is open #3317's carry 19/40 (R10-HANDOFF-PATH part 3). No cheaper detector is owed: the arm is itself the detector, and its flake is already being fixed there. Carry: R10-HANDOFF-PATH|#3317
- `pr-contract / pr-contract`: its only `ERROR` is `[pr-body] ... check \`governance / instrument-self-tests\` is red and \`## Red checks\` does not name it`. This section now names it. No cheaper detector: the body could not name a red that did not exist when it was written. Carry: dismissed: answered by this section
- `gate`: red because the two checks above are red; it carries no failure of its own. Carry: dismissed: follows the two above

Earlier round:

Verdict "Fix review: blocked 8db2e568 root-cause-detectable: tests / fast (3.14)", red `tests/harness_headers.py`.

- Cause, mine: `harness_headers.py` check "every inlined walk matches the canonical helper and no depth root remains" failed at 8db2e568 on `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_sweep_settle_loop.py:37: ROOT = HERE.parents[2]` (run locally: `1 of 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED`, the only FAIL line). Fixed in a0ee437f: the harness inlines the canonical `repo_root`. After: `harness_headers.inline_scan()` rc 0 and `depth_root_seams()` is `[]`; `replay` still prints `RESULT replay reruns=86 max_attempt=44 sim_minutes=72 alarm=yes`.
- The named `a3:roster`, `a3:orjson`, `a3:finite` are `tests/nightly_ha.py` checks driven from `tests/entities.py`, not `harness_headers.py`; my diff touches neither, and the local `harness_headers.py` run lists no a3 line. I did not reproduce them and do not claim them fixed; if they are red at this head they are not caused by this diff.
- Root-cause trigger: cheaper detector exists and is standing: `prepr.sh` "ci predict" ran `harness_headers` seams only on a changed file's self-test, and a new harness under `dev/audit/harnesses/` has none, so it missed this. Standing cost of running `depth_root_seams()` in prepr for any added file in that scope: one in-process scan, well under a second (`python3 -c "import harness_headers as h; h.depth_root_seams()"`). No countermeasure built here; recorded as a refusal to widen prepr inside a repair PR, for the orchestrator to cost.
- Remaining: no CI has run on `3aa0616e7b29`.

## Forward-carry

- Carry 1, to the R10-SWEEP-SETTLE-LOOP fixer through the orchestrator. This must reach the fix before it merges (`finding-propagation.md`). It covers:
  - countermeasure A, a closed-loop convergence check over a recorded attempt-n/n+1 pair;
  - the harness, offered for both ends;
  - the fact that the current self-test passes a fixed arm 1;
  - the design question in RCA section 3: whether a re-run should require an input change since the previous attempt.

  Carry: #201
- Carry 2, to proposal triage: countermeasure B, the `attempt-watch` beat row at attempt >= 20, polled every 1800 s, using RCA section 4's numbers. Carry: #201
- Carry 3, to the tick's owner: `orchestrator_tick.py:1441` counts any check run completed after dispatch as worker CI activity, so a sweep re-run reads as the worker's. Whether check runs are re-stamped was not measured. Carry: #201

## Friction

## Block

The PR's own harness fails a required check. `tests / fast (3.14)` concluded failure at this head (12:52:10Z to 13:03:33Z), and `gate` concluded failure (12:53:19Z). The failing script is `tests/harness_headers.py` (log `ev/fast-log.txt` line 8132), check "every inlined walk matches the canonical helper and no depth root remains": `FAIL depth seams: dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_sweep_settle_loop.py:37: ROOT = HERE.parents[2]`. I confirmed the matcher: `depth_root_seams` flags a `ROOT =` line holding `.parents[`, which line 37 is. The change is to resolve the repository root through the canonical helper that check names, not a parent count.

The body says "## Red checks: None. No PR exists and no CI has run on this head". That was true at push and is stale now, so the red is unanswered. A cheaper detector existed: the body itself says `tests/harness_headers.py` was not run to completion on the fixer's host (no `homeassistant`). The depth-seam scan (`depth_root_seams`) is a pure text scan of the harness files and needs no Home Assistant. It would have shown this red before the push. Name it as the detector and run it (or the scan alone) before handoff.

Carry: built-here

merges.title: R10-TRAIN-REJOIN-NO-RECARRY: train rejoin no recarry
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
Two merge-train changes on one seam, under the owner's waste-study rulings (tvofi, 2026-11-07, cards 1 and 5, both accepted). The ruling's lead-time and recarry figures are the brief's (the waste-study scripts live in the orchestrator's s12 directory, outside the tree), and this seat did not re-take them.

Card 1, the rejoin. Under `--skip-bad`, an entry the train skips on a head red that includes `gate` now rejoins the same train. `at_head` and `admit` raise a new `HeadRed` (a `Stop` carrying the head and the red names), and `Train.rejoin_candidate` queues that skip. After the batch's own merges and serial entries, `Train.rejoin` reads each queued head through `classify_at` (the reading the `classify` CLI prints, deferral and sweep settle included). On GREEN the entry runs the serial path (`one`), with no `add` and no merge seat. On RED it stays skipped: a real red never rejoins. It also stays skipped if the head is still WAIT `wait_cap_s` after its skip, or if the branch moved off the skipped head (a new head owes a new verdict). Each outcome is logged as `REJOIN #<pr>: ...`. A rejoined merge is `CURED` by the existing `skip_report` rule, and a refused rejoin replaces its earlier skip row. `wait_cap_s` is `polls x (REVIEW_POLL_SECONDS + POLL_SECONDS)`, the review-run wait's ceiling, 7320 s at the default 24 polls. It is now one method, read by `review_settle`'s log and by the rejoin.

Card 5, no recarry. `Train.recarry` now asks `Train.merges_as_is` before it recarries a head that lacks origin/main. Recarry still happens in four cases:
- `main-protect-checks` requires an up-to-date branch: `strict_update`, read live, where unreadable counts as required. This is the brief's "behave as today wherever the ruleset forces an up-to-date branch".
- git's merge of origin/main and the head conflicts (`merge_tree`, the train's driver-free text merge). This is the one content reason.
- The head is a GITHUB_TOKEN tip, whose cure is the recarry's App push.
- A graded red holds the car (`grade_held`), so its recarry and CI are still owed.
Otherwise the head merges as it stands. The train logs `#<pr> no recarry: ...` and records the merge base as `nr_base`. `one`, the MainMoved recovery in `serial` and `--overlap`'s up-front loop hand that base to `at_head` as `rb`. So `grade_merge` grades the tree about to land, origin/main merged with the proven head, at the merge and again in its guard, as R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE already does for an overlap car. A batch's proved entries never recarried, so card 5 changes the serial path only.

Carry f7d2bf7c (from #3288): remerge_main.sh printed `MERGE CONFLICT` for any failure of its fetch, reset and merge chain. Now it prints `MERGE CONFLICT <pr>` only when the merge left unmerged paths. Any other failure prints `REMERGE FAILED <pr> at <fetch|reset|merge> (rc=N)` under git's own words. `recarry` stops on that line as a git failure, never as "main does not merge without a resolution".

Design choices:
- The rejoin runs after the batch's own merges rather than as a re-spool. A re-spool would need the next drain to wait on a classify, and nothing drains while a train idles. Running in-train keeps the "no add" property and holds none of this batch's merges (test (b), WAIT).
- No recarry grades against the merge base rather than main's tip. With main's tip as `rb`, `grade_merge` returns ungraded whenever the batch itself moved nothing, and a foreign main would land unread. M14 kills that form.
- The live ruleset needs no change today (below), so the strict read is the "until it is applied" arm and costs two ruleset reads per recarry decision.

## Ruleset change

Live read at 2026-11-08T20:08Z: `gh api repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/rulesets/23698884 --jq '{updated_at, rules: [.rules[] | {type, parameters}]}'` returned `updated_at` 2026-10-27T22:36:19.629Z, a `required_status_checks` rule with `required_status_checks: [{"context":"gate","integration_id":15368}]` and `strict_required_status_checks_policy: false`, and a `pull_request` rule (one approving review, code-owner review required, `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push: false`).

The exact change that lets a proven batch merge without a per-PR rerun is none. `strict_required_status_checks_policy` is already `false`, so GitHub does not require a branch to be up to date with main. The one required context, `gate`, is the one the head's own CI already concluded at the verdicted head. With `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push: false`, no recarry is needed to keep an approval either. tvofi has nothing to apply. If `strict_required_status_checks_policy` is ever set to `true`, `strict_update` reads it at the next recarry decision and the train recarries every head that lacks main, as before this change. The null control under `NO RECARRY null control: under a strict policy` pins that.

## Head

`dcb78bf17600b73f729ba04356ae9bdd0bae11b9` merges main `f365ce7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`6ccb12bd7ef5ba9f1d1b7fbd7b2b13d76c0f7cf8` merges main `3231c07` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`40c79702c72359f00a0a932eabf727a942b1f9eb` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

1dae7f1c96b548cfc35292209d0e4076a0abcc18, cut from origin/main 17e621f08c4feec724478573741fbd8b596ceaba. 5358f7b1 was the first prepr-clean head. 1dae7f1c adds only tests and harness entries, pinning step 6d's survivors, with no production line. origin/main stood at 51cd5ec8a42abde3c223f22e9f4a0d5f35f8844a at 2026-11-08T20:40Z, with `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` clean with the ledger driver and without it (the same tree, 1faf4d8d). It stood at 661d26a5d2e655f32391048605db5970d133db1d at 2026-11-08T22:27Z, again clean (tree 5ca0cada). The brief's owner ruling (2026-11-07) is to merge origin/main only on a merge-tree conflict, so nothing was merged, and the dispatch's merge-when-moved step yields to it. prepr's `merged structure` step graded the merged tree (`STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`). Every figure below was taken at this head, except the failing-first runs, taken at the tests-only tree before the fix.

## Mutation proof

Failing first. The tests were added with production unchanged, at the tree before the fix commit (folded into fcdfb82b): `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` printed these FAIL lines:
- `NO RECARRY (c) --overlap: a clean merge tree against origin/main and an unchanged proven head merge with no recarry ...`
- `NO RECARRY (c): ...`
- `NO RECARRY null control (d): a merge-tree conflict against origin/main still recarries ...`
- `REJOIN (a): an entry SKIPped on a red gate whose head turns GREEN within the cap rejoins the train ...`
- `REJOIN null control (b): a head whose classify reads RED stays SKIPped ...` (at the base no `REJOIN` line exists)
The run then stopped on a TypeError in my own WAIT check (`rj and ...` handed a list to `check`), corrected to `bool(rj)`.

`bash tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh --self-test` at the same point printed `pr_args self-test: 185 checks, 1 failed`, the failing check being `null control: a fetch git rejected is not fetched again ..., and is named REMERGE FAILED at fetch, never MERGE CONFLICT (carry f7d2bf7c)`.

Mutants: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_train_rejoin_no_recarry_mutants.py` (in this diff: one exact single-occurrence span per mutant, run through `merge_train.py --self-test`) printed `MUTANTS: 20 run, 0 not as required` at the head:
- M0, the unmutated head: PASS.
- M1, the rejoin fires on RED (`if state == "green":` -> `if state in ("green", "red"):`): fails `REJOIN null control (b): a head whose classify reads RED stays SKIPped`.
- M2, the batch's `self.rejoin(rejoin, head_req)` deleted: fails REJOIN (a), (a) serial and both (b) cases.
- M3, every `HeadRed` a candidate, GATE or not: fails `REJOIN null control: a skip on a red that is not GATE is no rejoin candidate at all`.
- M4, cap 0: fails REJOIN (a).
- M5, cap x100: fails REJOIN (b) WAIT. That check bounds the check-run reads at the skipped head by the cap.
- M6, the moved-head guard off: fails `REJOIN: a skipped head the branch moved off does not rejoin`.
- M7, the serial loop's `rejoin_candidate` deleted: fails `REJOIN (a), serial`.
- M8, a recarry on every main move (`and not self.merges_as_is(item, h)` dropped): fails NO RECARRY (c) both, the merge-base grade, and (d).
- M9, the strict read ignored: fails four of today's recarry checks, among them `--overlap: every serial entry is re-carried UP FRONT` (the world's ruleset reads strict, as today's tests assume).
- M10, the conflict ignored: fails (d).
- M11, a bot tip ignored: fails `NO RECARRY keeps a bot head's cure`.
- M12, `grade_held` ignored: fails `NO RECARRY never skips the recarry a graded red holds`.
- M13, `one` passes `rb` None: fails NO RECARRY (c) and REJOIN (a) serial.
- M14, `--overlap` uses main's tip as `rb`: fails `NO RECARRY grades the un-recarried car against its merge base even when the batch moved nothing`.
- M15, `strict_update` always False: fails the same four checks as M9.
- M16, the `REMERGE FAILED` stop off: fails `carry f7d2bf7c: a remerge that failed before any conflict stops as a git failure`. With the stop off, the moved head reads as a push that landed and the entry would merge.
- M17, the rejoin's re-skip deleted: fails `REJOIN: a rejoin refused again (red at its own CI wait) is skipped again, its row replaced`.
- M18 and M19, the rejoin's sleep guard off or its sleep deleted: both fail REJOIN (b) WAIT, which pins one poll-grain sleep per WAIT read.

remerge_main.sh's `# mut:remergeconflict` line is pinned in pr_args.sh's own self-test. Its arm `mutant mut:remergeconflict (its line deleted): a rejected fetch is misreported as MERGE CONFLICT` passes at the head, where pr_args prints `185 checks, 0 failed`.

## Null control

- `REJOIN null control (b)`, RED: merged [1], one SKIP line for #2, no recarry, `skipped.json` still names #2.
- `REJOIN null control (b)`, WAIT: #1 merged before the rejoin's first read, #2 stopped at the cap, `TRAIN DONE`.
- `REJOIN null control`: a non-GATE red is never a candidate.
- `NO RECARRY null control: under a strict policy` and `... under an unreadable policy`: every serial head that lacks main is recarried, as today.
- `NO RECARRY null control (d)`: a merge-tree conflict still reaches remerge_main.sh.
- pr_args `null control: remerge_main on a clean merge keeps that merge`, and the conflicting-main arm still prints `MERGE CONFLICT 7`.
- Every pre-existing merge_train check passes unchanged: 564 checks at the base and 580 at the head, 0 failed at both.

## Figures

- merge_train at the base: `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` at 17e621f0 prints `merge_train self-test: 564 checks, 0 failed`. At the head the same command prints `merge_train self-test: 580 checks, 0 failed`.
- pr_args at the head: `bash tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh --self-test` prints `pr_args self-test: 185 checks, 0 failed`.
- Mutants: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_train_rejoin_no_recarry_mutants.py` prints `MUTANTS: 20 run, 0 not as required`.
- Structure: `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- Architecture: `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` prints `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`.
- Scoped gate: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out`, naming tests/entities.py. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` prints `ALL 2668 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`, and the run_always scripts pass: `tests/harness_headers.py` prints `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`, `tests/closure.py selftest` prints `ALL 118 closure shrink pins PASSED`, and `tests/layout.py` and `tests/env_drift.py --claims-only` pass. A first `closure.py selftest` read `1 of 118 ... FAILED` while the mutant harness's `_mutant_M*.py` copies stood untracked in tools/audit/seat; it passed once they were gone.
- CI prediction: `python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --apply-inert` wrote the harness's INERT READS entry (tests/closures.json) and then printed `CI PREDICT: no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted against 17e621f08c4f`.
- The rejoin's bound: `wait_cap_s` is `polls x 305` s, 7320 s at the CLI's default `polls` 24 (`Train.__init__`).
- Class enumeration, the rule `git grep -n "self\.recarry(" -- tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py`. It returns four call sites, all closed in this diff, because each hands `nr_base` on:
  - `one`;
  - `serial`'s MainMoved recovery;
  - `one_overlap`;
  - `_batch`'s `--overlap` up-front loop.
- Class enumeration, the rule `git grep -n "self\.skip(" -- tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py`. It returns five sites:
  - the admission skip and the serial skip, which can carry a `HeadRed`, closed (`rejoin_candidate`);
  - the up-front recarry skip and the merge-loop skip, which can carry no `HeadRed` (no CI read there), no candidate by construction;
  - the rejoin's own re-skip, which is final.
- Class enumeration, the rule `git grep -n "MERGE CONFLICT" -- tools/`, outside tests and docs. It returns remerge_main.sh (closed here) and handoff_push.sh's main merge. handoff_push.sh's chain is the merge alone, with no fetch or reset in it, so the transport misdiagnosis carry f7d2bf7c names cannot occur there.
- prepr: `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh` printed `PRE-PR: 5358f7b1fd67fbcf57be5c125d0f438c92e027e3 ... rc=0` (no body). At the head, with this body, `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh <body>` passes, its body check included (rc 0). Its diff-mutant step was run on its own, because a body run that included it passed the container's 30-minute background bound: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff 17e621f08c4f...HEAD --cmd "python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test" --max-mutants 40 --report-only`, at 5358f7b1, 21:20:55Z to 22:15:37Z. ## Unpinned sites

The rule is the step 6d survivors at 5358f7b1 that no test added after them kills. Production lines are unmoved at 1dae7f1c.

A real recarry left holding an earlier no-recarry base hands `at_head` that merge base as `rb` instead of None. `grade_merge` then grades the merge of main's tip and the recarried head, which contains main, so it grades tree(h) with a superset of touched files. The outcome is the same grade. The pop is kept so `rb` names the tree the head's CI read. Carry: dismissed: outcome-equivalent, a stale base widens the grade's file set and never narrows it

The count, its re-measure command and its null control are written into dev/programme/carries/carry-201.json, last entry, for the orchestrator seat that holds the logs. Carry: #201

merges.body:
R10-I18N-DE: German as a third UI language beside English and Swedish, through the two i18n mechanisms the tree already has: `translations/de.json` key-for-key with `en.json`, and a `de` dictionary in the card's `STRINGS` table key-for-key with `en`. No new mechanism. The per-language production tables that already had `sv` (`narrative.TEMPLATES`, `topology._TRANSLATIONS`, `config_flow.PRESET_WARNING`) gained `de`. Every check that pinned en/sv parity now iterates the shipped catalogues (`tests/harness.py`'s `SHIPPED_LANGS`, derived from the files under `translations/`) or `Object.keys(STRINGS)`. The docs that list UI languages name German.

**Repair round (this pass).** The train skipped this PR on a real red in code run 42507800236 (head `56063679e`, merge ref `c5ebc4058`). Main's R10-MIN-POWER-FLOOR work (merged since this branch's previous authored head) added the `compressor_modulation` option to `strings.json`: its label and description on the `thermal_model` options page, plus the `selector.compressor_modulation` options `auto`, `on_off` and `modulating`. `de.json` had no German leaves for them. The previous body's Carry 1 predicted this: whichever of the two pull requests merged second would be refused until the German leaves existed. This pass adds the five German leaves in strings.json's key order, using the catalogue's existing terms: Verdichter, Mindestleistung, Ein/Aus (the catalogue's `heat_pump_switch_entity` label is "Ein/Aus-Schalter der Wärmepumpe"), Raumheizung, Warmwasser, Sollwert and the informal *du* address. Commit `75fc7e4b4` touches only `translations/de.json` (9 added lines). No production code, test or other file changed in this pass.

**Roster carries.** Both of the group's roster carries are r10-min-power-floor's item c7e2fe29, "the new option's German label". Carry 1 is the entry routed from that body; Carry 2 is the same text as the orchestrator restated it. Both are discharged by commit `75fc7e4b4`: the option's label (`options.step.thermal_model.data.compressor_modulation`), its description and its three selector options now have German text. `tests/entities.py`'s "de.json has exactly strings.json's keys" pins them, and its null control is under `## Mutation proof`.

Earlier rounds' substance is unchanged and still holds at this head:

- **Card strings.** The 18 `whynow.*` keys have German text, and `tests/card.mjs`'s every-language parity check is green.
- **Widened tests.** The why-now key-twin check compares `en` with every card language. The setup-text, narrative and `reasons.scheduled` language checks in `tests/features.py` equal the shipped catalogue set. A German why-now render check sits beside the Swedish one.
- **Terminology.** Each concept has one German term: Flüstermodus, Ruhezeiten, Feiertag, Mindestleistung / Maximale Leistung / Leistungsaufnahme.
- **Stub-killer repair.** `tests/entities.py`'s `--anchor` stub killer spares the anchor run's null control by the production null-control edit (`_mut_an_nulled`), not by its marker words. The `--anchor` fixture names the live `_tr` RETURN_DEL row `86fae85d`.

German address is the informal *du* that Home Assistant's own German UI uses. Wire values stay untranslated: entity ids, config keys, service and attribute names, reason codes and enums. `name_match.SYNONYMS` and `grid_fee`'s input parser stay English and Swedish by design, because they parse user input and are not UI text. `tests/card_browser.mjs`'s P9 grid stays `["en", "sv-SE"]`.

## Head

`070425a79e84d9d4ce652209c194a596f9fac7ed` merges main `f365ce7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`59f1e158a2078562b282fa7e2e67804b426a2fad` merges main `6457496` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`cc40997d8768b76dc4efc9ec7414346b447b35be` merges main `19865e5` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`9b9c4ffc7d168af9dc7007f361e9402ad32065db` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`41d98b8e9e5446b9b6fcdbbddebe069b9e66e450`. It is the PR head `acbd1ea912b551ea5f9b3ed51294f7ba5ed57605` plus three commits:

- `75fc7e4b4`, the five German leaves;
- `498188ef9`, a clean merge of `origin/main` `17e621f08` (#3318: `tools/audit/carry_audit.py`, `tools/audit/seat/body_patch.sh`, a delivery row);
- `41d98b8e9`, a clean merge of `origin/main` `51cd5ec8a42abde3c223f22e9f4a0d5f35f8844a`, `origin/main` at 2026-11-08T20:38:34Z (#3316, #3333, #3340: `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED.md`, `tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py`, `tools/audit/seat/instruments/tick_loop.sh.md`, one `tests/closures.json` harness row, delivery rows).

Neither merge touches a file this branch changes. Main moved twice while this pass ran. The translation figures (key gap, `claims.py`, `harness_headers.py`, `card.mjs`, the scoped gate, the mutation proof and its null control) were taken at `75fc7e4b4` on base `996ded2a6`, because neither merge changes a file they read. `tests/entities.py` and `tests/structure.py` were re-run at `498188ef9` and again at `41d98b8e9`, and `tools/pr/prepr.sh` at `41d98b8e9`. `git merge origin/main` at the start of this pass printed `Already up to date.`, because `acbd1ea9` already merged main `996ded2a`.

## Mutation proof

- **The fix's lines deleted (the PR head `acbd1ea9` is that tree).** At `acbd1ea9`, `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round4/D6/claims.py` printed `claims_true=122`, `claims_false=1` and `FALSE C112 … every translation file carries exactly the keys strings.json declares`. `tests/harness_headers.py` reads that output against the header (`header='123' printed='122'`), which is CI's harness_headers red. CI's run 42507800236 reported `de.json has exactly strings.json's keys` red on the same five keys.
- **One leaf deleted at `75fc7e4b4`.** I removed `selector.compressor_modulation.options.on_off` from `de.json` in a separate worktree at `75fc7e4b4` and ran `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`. It printed `1 of 2703 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED` and exited 1. The one failing check is `FAIL de.json has exactly strings.json's keys  [selector.compressor_modulation.options.on_off]`. With the leaf restored, the same command printed `ALL 2703 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` and exited 0.

## Null control

- **`75fc7e4b4`, unmutated.** `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` printed `ALL 2703 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` (exit 0). `ok de.json has exactly strings.json's keys` is among the passing checks, beside the en and sv rows. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round4/D6/claims.py` printed `claims_true=123` and `claims_false=0`, matching the header. It left `claims.json` and `claims.md` byte-identical: `git status --short` printed nothing.
- **CI's own merge tree, `c5ebc4058`.** It is the merge ref run 42507800236 ran on, fetched and checked out detached. The same `claims.py` command printed `claims_true=122`, `claims_false=1`, C112 false with `missing={'de': 5, 'en': 0, 'sv': 0}`, and it rewrote `claims.json` and `claims.md`. So the local instrument reproduces CI's red at CI's tree, and the fix is what clears it, not the container.

## Figures

- **Key gap, re-derived three-dot.** The command was a scratch script. It flattened `strings.json` and `translations/de.json` to dotted leaf paths and printed `set(strings) - set(de)` and `set(de) - set(strings)`. At `acbd1ea9` (whose merge base with `origin/main` is `996ded2a`, so three-dot and two-dot agree) it returned 5 missing and 0 extra. The 5 were `options.step.thermal_model.data.compressor_modulation`, `options.step.thermal_model.data_description.compressor_modulation` and `selector.compressor_modulation.options.{auto,on_off,modulating}`. At `75fc7e4b4`, `498188ef9` and `41d98b8e9` it returned 0 missing and 0 extra. The in-tree instrument for the same property is `python3 tests/entities.py`'s "de.json has exactly strings.json's keys", whose null control is the one-leaf deletion under `## Mutation proof`.
- **CI job conclusions, run 42507800236.** Read with `mcp__github__actions_list list_workflow_jobs`, keyed on each job's `conclusion` and its failed steps' names. The failures were `tests / fast (3.14)` (step "Run the suite"), `pr-contract / pr-contract` (step "Check the body against the contract") and `gate` (step "Judge this head"). The one cancelled job was `codeql / Analyze (python)` (step "Perform CodeQL Analysis"). Every other job read success or skipped.
- **The a3:* FAIL lines are planted fixtures.** Today's `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` at this head printed 8 `FAIL a3:` lines and still ended `ALL 2703 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` with exit 0. Each FAIL line is the planted negative of the self-test after it, for example `FAIL a3:roster [1 registered, 82 …]` followed by `ok a3:roster fails when the registered ids are not collect()'s set`. The script's exit, not the log text, is the verdict.
- **`node tests/card.mjs`** (after `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/plan_view.py` wrote its payload) printed `ALL CARD CHECKS PASSED`.
- **Scoped gate.** At `75fc7e4b4` against base `996ded2a6`, `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub GATE_SCOPE=auto GATE_SCOPE_BASE=996ded2a6dc52816bd4c7dd873c048d85fc6adad GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=996ded2a6dc52816bd4c7dd873c048d85fc6adad bash tests/run.sh` printed `MODE: SCOPED -- 27 script(s) run, 6 scoped out`. Every script in the three lanes printed `ok`, including `tests/entities.py` (559s), `tests/features.py`, `node tests/card.mjs`, `tests/structure.py`, `tests/golden.py`, `tests/env_drift.py --all 996ded2a…`, `tests/arch_score.py` and `tests/arch_score_head.py`. `tests/stress.py` then FAILED one check, "the probed scenarios' memory peaks stay within their recorded budgets". The run was then stopped by this seat's 30-minute background limit, so I ran `tests/harness_headers.py` alone: `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`, with every `dev/audit/rounds/round4/D6/claims.py RESULT … matches header` row ok.
- **The stress memory red is the container's.** `tests/stress.py` alone at `75fc7e4b4` read `1 of 113 STRESS CHECKS FAILED`, that one check, with every scenario at a traced peak of 5.3 MiB against a recorded 3.4-3.5 MiB. The probe it runs, `PYTHONPATH=custom_components:tests/hastub python3 tests/stress.py --memory-probe '{"season":"winter","building":"typical_slab"}'`, run three times on each tree, printed `traced_mb` 5.27, 3.44, 5.27 at `75fc7e4b4` and the same 5.27, 3.44, 5.27 at unmodified `origin/main` `996ded2a6`. The draw is bimodal and identical across the two trees. A full `tests/stress.py` at `996ded2a6` drew the low mode and printed `ok` for that check; its 7 reds are all "origin/main IS this commit" self-comparison arms. CI's `tests / fast (3.14)` in run 42507800236 passed `stress.py` at this branch's previous head. I did not establish what selects the mode. The diff adds no code that `build_case` runs.
- **At `498188ef9` and at `41d98b8e9`.** `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` printed `ALL 2703 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` (exit 0), with `ok de.json has exactly strings.json's keys`. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/structure.py` printed `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- **`tools/pr/prepr.sh` with this body.** `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh <this body>` at `41d98b8e9e5446b9b6fcdbbddebe069b9e66e450` printed `PRE-PR: 41d98b8e9e5446b9b6fcdbbddebe069b9e66e450 … rc=0`, run with `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub` and `MUTANT_CMD="python3 tests/guard_pins.py"` exported. It ran from a local branch not named `fix/r10-i18n-de`, so its push-order and ancestry-reds steps printed `skip`; `pr-contract` re-executes both against the pull request. Its `diff mutants` step drove the diff's added lines and read no survivor, and step 6d listed no unpinned site.

## Unpinned sites

none: this pass adds no code site. The five German strings are data, which `tests/entities.py`'s key-parity and placeholder checks pin.

## Red checks

- **`tests / fast (3.14)`: `tests/entities.py`, "de.json has exactly strings.json's keys" (run 42507800236).** It is this branch's red. It went red at the merge with main, not at an authored commit: main gained five `strings.json` keys (R10-MIN-POWER-FLOOR) that the German catalogue, unique to this branch, did not carry. It is repaired here. The detector that caught it is the right one, and it is already the cheapest that exists. The check is a set comparison inside an `entities.py` run that happens for every catalogue diff, and the previous body had named it as the mechanism that would enforce this exact item (Carry 1). A cheaper detector would need the second-merging PR to know the other's keys before either merged. That is a cross-branch key census on every push, at the standing cost of one more cross-branch read per push, to save a red the existing check already turns up within one CI run. None is worth building.
- **`tests / fast (3.14)`: `tests/harness_headers.py`, `dev/audit/rounds/round4/D6/claims.py` RESULT claims_true / claims_false and "the executed harnesses leave their committed output byte-identical".** Same cause: the harness's C112 claim is the same key parity, and the five missing de leaves turned it false (122/1 against a 123/0 header) and rewrote its committed `claims.json` and `claims.md`. I diagnosed it on CI's merge tree `c5ebc4058` (see `## Null control`). The cause is this branch's: `claims.py`'s C112 row reads `translations/*.json`, which includes the branch's `de.json`. The same `de.json` repair fixes it; no harness or header changed. Cheaper detector: none beyond the entities check above, which fires on the same input earlier in the same job.
- **`tests / fast (3.14)`: the `a3:*` FAIL lines.** Not a red: they are `tests/entities.py`'s planted negatives (see `## Figures`), and the step's exit is decided by the real failures above.
- **`tests / mutation` at 86f40880 (run 42485521754, previous round): null control killed by `tests/entities.py`.** It is green at `acbd1ea9` (run 42512291787, job 128827902612, success); this pass adds no code site. It was a refusal, not a survivor: `mutation-autofix` printed `skip-not-unpinned` and named no site. The cause was a test-stub defect on main since `f5d665f58`, reached because this diff edits `topology.py`. `tests/entities.py`'s `--anchor` stub killer spared the anchor run's own null control by the words `(null control)` anywhere in the file, so a lane null control in `topology.py` spared every mutant. Commit `48edf9524` repaired it, keying on the production null-control edit (`_mut_an_nulled`), and added a regression check that re-drives the pin from a pre-nulled file.
