bus-nonce: 75e07da349fe8245825db04e24bba166

## Block

CI on this head never concluded. `merge_train.py classify 1c29e5ab7733d9c72d1773b649c97291b8b5dfb2 --pr 3345` printed `WAIT ... pending: gate red: none` (rc 3) on every poll, about 50 minutes. The runner queue is the cause: `tests / closures`, `tests / fast (3.14)`, `tests / browser`, `tests / coverage`, `tests / typing` and `tests / arch-instrument` were still `queued` at the last read. No gate check was red. This is a hand-back, not a defect finding: I found nothing to block on in the code. Re-dispatch the review, or carry this one, once classify exits 0. The sections below hold what I measured.

## Findings

- Residual: `owner_topic`'s `name.startswith(t + "-")` boundary in tools/audit/seat/topic_grammar.py is not pinned by topic_grammar's own self-test; mutating it to `startswith(t)` leaves that self-test green (rc 0). The caller's `roster_sync.py --self-test` does kill it (1 failed), so the rule is pinned, one module away. Carry: dismissed: pinned by the consumer's self-test; the PR body says the rule moved unchanged.

## Evidence

- Head measured: 1c29e5ab7733d9c72d1773b649c97291b8b5dfb2; PR head re-read at the end of the review and unchanged.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 1c29e5ab7733d9c72d1773b649c97291b8b5dfb2` exits 0 (ev/merge-tree.txt); no `MERGE-CLAIM` line, no conflict. `git diff` of dev/governance/roles/ between the merge base and origin/main is empty.
- Self-tests at the head, all pass (ev/selftests.txt): topic_grammar ok; pr_cap 22/0; open_driver 79/0; owed_unactioned 57/0; orchestrator_tick 297/0; ledger 102/0; cloud_relay 385/0; cloud_dispatch 132/0. The cloud_relay count matches the body's 385.
- Mutants on topic_grammar.py, each restored with `git diff --quiet` clean (ev/mutants.txt): prefix match instead of full match: self-test rc 1 (killed). Bare `-<N>` counted as a family member: rc 1 (killed). `owner_topic` prefix without the dash: topic_grammar self-test rc 0 (survives), roster_sync self-test fails 1 row (killed there). The body's claims "bare -<N> fails 2 rows, prefix fails 5" were not re-counted row by row; I confirm only that each is killed.
- I did not re-run the body's tick-level mutants (orchestrator_tick, pr_cap, open_driver, owed_unactioned, cloud_dispatch), the closure INERT_EXCEPT mutation or the `closure.py check` null control. I did not use the diff-mutant run or its 20 survivors; `tests / mutation` was green in CI. The body's remaining figures were not re-derived.
- Packet figure_lint: 18 resolved, 0 not verified, 0 refused. carry_audit: 3 finding items, 3 routed, 0 unrouted. The forward-carry destination R10-FLY-CIPREDICT-RESTORING is present in wave-r10-groups.json on origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster.
- CI at last read: green are `tests / mutation`, `tests / briefs`, `tests / closure-scope`, `tests / nightly-status`, `governance / wave-script`, `governance / instrument-self-tests`, `governance / policy-docs`, `arch-score`, `budget-raise-gate`, `hassfest`, `validate-hacs`. Red: `governance / delivery-status`, repo-wide per the brief and not required. Pending: `governance / env-matrix`, `codeql / Analyze (python)` and the queued tests jobs above. `tests / mutation` green is not proof the baseline was green; I did not read its log.
- Not checked: claim-file drift (`env_drift.py --all`), VERSION/manifest/notes untouched, and step 15 architecture. The diff touches no VERSION file, and no claim file is in the 18-file list (tests/golden/ absent). Step 15 and the `pr-contract` re-run were not completed.
- Round: first review of this head.

Fix review: blocked fd973e035d6044ac55a105a7156af5b46ce5838f semantic-conflict: the merge of main makes governance / instrument-self-tests red; the new topic_grammar step is ungated under main's selftest_scope

bus-nonce: 569d8518b37bf7b3ab928471152b63e3

## Block

The head's merge of origin/main has no textual conflict, but it combines two changes that break each other. Main brought in `tools/ci/selftest_scope.py` and `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` (R10-CI-SELFTEST-SCOPE, between `1c29e5ab7` and `806e952ca`). That code requires every instrument-self-tests step to have an `id:` and an `if:` that reads `steps.scope.outputs.<id>`. This branch's governance.yml step "Show the topic grammar refusing a bare number and a prefix as family members" has no id and is gated only on `!cancelled()`.

- CI at this head: `governance / instrument-self-tests` (check-run 129104657944, run 42600800913) fails with `FAIL the live job parses (115 steps) and its gating is consistent` / `selftest_scope self-test: 90 checks, 1 failed`.
- Reproduced here: `python3 tools/ci/selftest_scope.py --self-test` at this head gives 90 checks, 1 failed. At origin/main `f365ce757` and at the merge base `806e952ca` it gives 90 checks, 0 failed. `wiring_gaps` at the head returns exactly `UNGATED step 'Show the topic grammar refusing a bare number and a prefix as family members'`, and `selftest_scope.py static` reports 1 problem (ev/selftest_scope_*.txt, ev/wiring_gaps_head.txt).
- The context is not in `gate_required` (ev/required_contexts.txt), so `merge_train.py classify` reads GREEN and the gate is green. But the job runs on pushes to main (only product-only PRs skip it). Merging this head would turn main's instrument-self-tests red, and that red would belong to this PR.
- The body's `## Red checks` says `governance / instrument-self-tests` was "repaired at the previous head". At this head that is no longer true, and the body does not name this new cause.

Repair: I probed this in a scratch worktree only; nothing was pushed. Adding `id: topic-grammar` and `if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.scope.outputs.topic-grammar == 'true' }}` makes the self-test pass (90 checks, 0 failed). `static` then reports one remaining STALE line: `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` lacks `topic-grammar`, re-record with `python3 tools/ci/selftest_scope.py record --step topic-grammar`. That command needs strace, on Linux. The launcher may also need a `sel topic-grammar` arm if the step is meant to run in the background; the fixer should check how the other gated foreground steps are wired (ev/repair_probe.txt). After the repair, the fixer should re-run steps 2-8 and update the body's Red checks entry.

## Findings

none

## Evidence

- Round: this PR has been verdicted before. The previous verdict, at `1c29e5ab7733d9c72d1773b649c97291b8b5dfb2`, was blocked ci-pending only. This review covers the resolution delta from `1c29e5ab` to `fd973e03`; `review_carry.py` prints FRESH-REVIEW (632b3764 is not an automatic merge).
- Head: `fd973e035d6044ac55a105a7156af5b46ce5838f` is the PR head (pull request read and `refs/pull/3345/head`) and the head the body names in `## Head`. Its merge base with origin/main is `806e952ca`. origin/main has since moved to `f365ce757`.
- Merges with main: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main fd973e03` exits 0 (tree `52188550a`), with no conflict.
- Roles current: `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty.
- Resolution delta, merge by merge. I compared each merge's tree with `git merge-tree --write-tree` of its parents:
  - `f3633ad2a` (1c29e5ab + main 79b7356f3): the only hand-resolved hunks are `.claude/workflows/audit-find.js` (FINDING-SCHEMA block lines 184-185, CLASS_GUESS and FINDING_REPORT) and `dev/audit/config/finding.schema.json` (the class_guess enum line). `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json` was resolved by the driver (`LEDGER-MERGE: resolved`).
  - `632b37641`: its tree equals `f3633ad2a`'s. The automatic merge would have added `BLOCKED.md`; `-s ours` dropped it, as the body says.
  - `0b8d0c2b4` and `fd973e035`: their trees equal the automatic merge of their parents, so neither has a hand-resolved hunk.
- Both parents' clauses are present (ev/union.txt). I compared JSON leaves against the merge base of the two parents:
  - bugclasses.json: the branch added 31 leaves and main added 44. None is missing, and no head leaf is absent from both parents.
  - finding.schema.json: each side added 1 leaf (`R10-TOPIC-FAMILY` and `N-relay-handoff-starvation`). Neither is missing, and nothing extra was added.
  - audit-find.js CLASS_GUESS: the branch added `R10-TOPIC-FAMILY` and main added `N-relay-handoff-starvation`. Nothing is missing or extra.
  - `fold_ledger.py check`: 0 violations. `fold_ledger.py --self-test` passes.
- Scoped gate: `tests/closure.py select --diff 806e952ca` prints `MODE: FULL -- every test script runs` (`tests/closure.py changes the gate itself`). The suite is CI's and I did not re-run it. CI's `gate` (check-run 129126185452) reads success.
- Self-tests at this head (ev/cheap.txt):
  - `tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED.
  - orchestrator_tick 297/0, topic_grammar ok, owed_unactioned 57/0, open_driver 79/0, pr_cap 22/0, cloud_dispatch 132/0, ledger 102/0, cloud_relay 397/0, roster_queue 62/0.
  - `tests/closure.py selftest`: ALL 118 closure shrink pins PASSED.
- The body's figures say each self-test "exits 0, 0 failed" without giving counts, so there are no counts to re-derive. The counts above are my own.
- Mutation pins re-taken at this head, where main moved their files (ev/mutants_head.txt). Each mutant matched once and the tree was restored clean:
  - Mutant A (the fixer's BLOCKED.md clause) fails "the fixer is told to push BLOCKED.md with a Question line before stopping on a question" (132 checks, 1 failed).
  - Mutant B (the reviewer's "never on a head ... merges cleanly" clause) fails "the reviewer blocks on main only for a merge-tree conflict, never a clean head behind main" (132 checks, 1 failed).
  - Deleting the `handoff-wip/` blocked-stop arm makes ledger's self-test exit 2 with `refused: 'refs/heads/handoff-wip/x' matches no ledger arm`.
  - The closure.py `INERT_EXCEPT` pin was not re-taken. Its entry (line 626) is untouched by main's delta, which is the body's own reasoning.
- VERSION, the manifest, RELEASE_NOTES and both claim files are untouched in the three-dot diff (ev/untouched.txt).
- CI: `merge_train.py classify fd973e03 --pr 3345` exited 0: `GREEN ... pending: none red: none` (ev/classify1.txt). Non-required reds at this head:
  - `governance / instrument-self-tests`: the block above.
  - `governance / delivery-status`: not this PR's (defect-root-cause.md).
- Review packet: rendered with refusal `hot-file: #3326 holds an unboarded merge verdict and shares tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py`, with the advisory that HPO_BUS_TRAIN_STATE is unset. It is the train's concern and not a defect of this head. The packet's carry_audit reads 4 routed, 0 unrouted, and figure_lint reads 19 resolved, 0 not verified.
- CI was re-read with a second `merge_train.py classify` run, more than 60 s after the first, and again read GREEN, `red: none` (ev/classify2.txt).
- I did not get a local result for `tests/entities.py` (`PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`): it hit this seat's own 230 s timeout (rc=124; ev/entities.txt holds the partial log). Its result is cited from CI's green `tests / closures` and `gate` instead.

merges.body:

merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER, the carries part (topic r10-hotfix-gate-busy-defer-p5). Every one of the 13 carries ends below in a fix with its controls, a `covered by <sha>` line naming the code and test that prove it, or the owner's recorded dismissal.

**Carry numbering.** Each carry line names the roster's 1-based number and the brief's 0-based one. Everywhere else in this body, "carry N" is the brief's number.

**What the tree already did, and what was left.** The deadlock this group was cut for is closed on main:
- #3246 (355d9965a) added `busy()`'s id tie-break.
- #3276 (812bb8747) made `judging()` read a deferring run's skipped caller as judging.
- #3287 (5c1fa41fb) publishes a deferral at once and lets `gate-sweep.yml`'s `settle` re-judge it.
- #3290 (48af0864a) made the train and `ci-watch` read a deferral red as a deferral, not as RED.

Three defects were left, and this diff fixes them:
1. **A stale pin (carries 3 and 5).** A gate re-run executes the programs of its event's original `base.sha`, so the sweep's job re-runs kept replaying a pre-fix `busy()`. The recorded #3244 triple deadlocks under its live pin 9cbd7dd0 and decides under main (`## Figures`). The fix is `sweep.py`'s `stale_pin`/`fresh`: where the base changed `tools/ci/*.py` after the pull request's `base.sha`, the sweep dispatches ONE fresh `ci.yml` run (`pr`, `base`) instead of re-running. That run rev-parses `origin/<base>` when its job starts, and its gate is the newest check run at the head. A dispatched run created at or after the stale gate's conclusion is that fresh judge already, so nothing is dispatched twice and the branch cannot loop. It lives in the sweep because the sweep runs main's copy (`gate-sweep.yml`, `ref: github.sha`), so it reaches every PR at once. `gate.py --refresh` runs the pinned copy itself, so a change there could not reach the PRs it is for.
2. **A source shadowed by run id (carries 11 and 10).** `gate.gate` took each unit's source from the highest-id run, so a body run that GitHub numbered below its code run had its read of the latest body shadowed. The source is now the run whose jobs for the unit started LAST, then the higher id. `arch-score` reads the PR live at its start (`arch-score.yml`, `gh api .../pulls/$NUMBER`), so a later start is the fresher read. This run's own unit, while its listing lags, is never displaced: that is fail-closed, and it is a design choice. Before, a higher-id sibling's green could cover a lagging own unit; now the gate re-reads its own listing inside `lag_bound`. `prelude.run_jobs` fills an optional `starts` map from the listing it already reads, so no request is added.
3. **No pin for the three-gate shape (carry 1).** A self-test case and a recorded replay scene now pin #3244's three-gate mutual deferral. Two stale parts of the proof instruments were retired as #3287's design: the RCA replay's `C3-AT-ONCE` defect class, which failed every replay at main, and `r10_ci_gate_core.py`'s M26, whose anchor no longer exists.

**Alternatives.**
- **Stale pin:**
  - Change `ci.yml` to restore from the live base on a re-run. `ci.yml` is outside this group, and the pin is deliberate (a PR judges with its base's programs).
  - Read each gate's `programs restored from` log line. The logs endpoint redirects to a blob, which `ghapi` does not follow as JSON. The PR's live `base.sha` equals that line on every pull_request-event gate measured (`## Null control`).
  - Re-run and accept the old program. That is the #3261 attempt-10 loop the carry records.
- **Source order:** order by run `created_at`. A same-second push and edit tie on it, and a re-run executes a unit afresh without moving it, so a job start is the only stamp that orders the reads.

**Order against #3243 (R10-GATE-LEASE-TOCTOU).** #3243 merged first (5421413b). It touches `tests/gate_lock.py` alone, and this diff does not touch that file, so neither order conflicts.

Carry 1 (the brief's carry 0): covered by 355d9965a (#3246). `busy()`'s clause `and not (r["id"] > ctx["run_id"] and started(r))`, tools/ci/gate.py. The self-test `busy-defer: of two started gates at one head the lower id defers to none, the higher to the lower` drives runs 42192623509 and 42193153511 and reads `([], [lo])`. Mutant M17 (r10_ci_gate_core.py) is killed by it.

Carry 2 (the brief's carry 1): partly covered, remainder fixed here.
- Covered by 355d9965a (the tie-break) and 812bb8747 (`judging()`). At main the recorded #3244 triple replays `DECIDED`, all three PASS (`## Figures`).
- Covered by 5c1fa41fb (`sweep.settle`), so a deferral resolves without a hand re-run. Self-test `#3282: the sweep for the code run's completion re-runs that deferring gate, no human`.
- Covered by 48af0864a: the readers take that transient red as a deferral (`merge_train.classify_at`).
- The red itself stays, #3287's design: a job that holds no runner can only conclude, and a skipped required check reads as passing.
- Fixed here:
  - The three-gate shape is pinned: `busy-defer, three gates (#3244)`, red under M17 and M18.
  - The scene `3244-triple` replays DEADLOCK at the live pin and DECIDED at main and at this head.
  - The stale-pin dispatch, the reason #3244's and #3261's reds outlived the fix.
- The scratch `rerun-gate.sh` is in no tree path (grep below). With the sweep re-judging deferrals and dispatching stale pins, nothing is left for it.

Carry 3 (the brief's carry 2): covered by 5c1fa41fb. `judge()` re-reads only for `lag_bound(why)`, which is 0 for a deferral, so no deferral waits 720 s. Self-tests `#3282: the deferring edit gate publishes CI's deferral at once and holds no runner` and `C3: a deferring edit gate beside a busy code run defers at once, no nap; re-run once the code run ends, it judges its sources`. A code run longer than any bound is re-judged by the sweep when it completes, so the bound question is moot.

Carry 4 (the brief's carry 3): fixed here (stale pin, above). The orchestrator step it proposed ("re-judge only after a fresh event") is now the sweep's own dispatch, so no policy text is owed.

Carry 5 (the brief's carry 4): covered by afc1586a, the merge base: no defect. `governance / instrument-self-tests` is not a required context. The gate's governance names are `UNITS["governance"] = ("policy-docs", "wave-script", "env-matrix")` (tools/ci/prelude.py), and `REQUIRED` is built from `UNITS` alone. The gate job 128321406871 read `WORKSET: ... governance ...` and printed `PASS` under pinned 294a880d with the same names. The cancelled job is reported under "Not gating" by design. Making it required is the gate owner's call, not raised here.

Carry 6 (the brief's carry 5): fixed here. The first item (re-prove with `replay --ci <export>`) is under `## Figures`. The second item, RCA 5.2's countermeasure, is built in `sweep.py`, so the manual 5.3 dispatch is retired once this merges.

Carry 7 (the brief's carry 6): dismissed by the owner (bar 2026-11-08, triage batch 136 entry 425); no work.

Carry 8 (the brief's carry 7): covered by 5c1fa41fb. "Nothing re-judges it" is false by construction: `Sweep.settle` and the green branch re-run a deferring gate with no human. The self-test #3282 replay posts the re-run with tvofi's human re-run removed.

Carry 9 (the brief's carry 8): dismissed by the owner (the same ruling as carry 6, which it repeats); no work.

Carry 10 (the brief's carry 9): covered by 5c1fa41fb, the same as carry 7, which it repeats.

Carry 11 (the brief's carry 10): measured first, then fixed here through carry 11's source order, not the re-run the carry proposed.
- **The measurement.** `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_codescan_wait_race.py --since 2026-11-01T06:21:44Z --until 2026-11-08T06:21:44Z --rows`, over the 7 days before the merge base, reads 1821 runs and 5 ORDERED red edit runs. That count is a superset: it counts any failure of the codescan step.
- **Narrowed to the carry's rule** (an ordered pair; the job log carries `no run at this head owns a finished codeql unit`; a codeql leg of the code run succeeded after that red) by a probe over those runs (scratch `probe10.sh`; its rule is the three conditions just named). It reads **3** edit runs on 2 heads: 42373556850 (head 97786d25), and 42385417686 and 42387066581 (#3252, head 31347980).
- **The other two** (41952981275, 42246412814) carry the line, but the code run's codeql legs had succeeded before the red, so no source finished later.
- **3 meets the build threshold.**
- **What was built.** Only `gate` is a required context (tools/policy/fixtures/required-contexts.json), so the stale red mattered only as the gate's source. Under id order, the higher-id edit run's red outranked the code run's later green. #3252's code-run gate at 17:14:38Z (attempt 2) failed on `pr-contract / pr-contract: failure (run 42387066581)` while its own `pr-contract`, started 17:13:48Z, was green. `pr-contract` reads the body live at its start (pr-contract.yml, "THE BODY IS READ FROM THE API AT RUN TIME"), so the later start is the fresher read, and carry 11's source order takes it.
- **The replay of that recorded gate** (scene `3252-nosource`): `FAIL pr-contract / pr-contract: failure (run 42387066581)` at main, the live verdict, and PASS at this head. The sweep then re-runs the edit runs' red gates through its green branch, and they read the same fresher source.
- **Why not the proposed log-keyed re-run.** It would need the sweep to read job logs (a raw, redirect-following mode in `ghapi`) and re-run whole `pr-contract` jobs. It would still leave the gate taking the higher id's red until that re-run finished.
- **Arms:**
  - The #3252 shape passes once the code run's pr-contract is green: the replay.
  - The null, a fresher red is still the source, never passed over: self-tests `C3: a body edited after the code run's gate passed is still judged (this run's own pr-contract)` and `source order: ... null`.
  - M27 (id order) reads `MISREAD` on the scene, replay exit 1.
- **The residual, stated.** The red stands until the code run's own `pr-contract` runs. At #3252 that was the code run's re-run, about 1.5 h after the first red, against 3 h 10 min live.
- **Two harness defects fixed on the way**, both now in its selftest (15 checks after the merge of main, below):
  - The run listing truncated silently at GitHub's 1000-run cap, and the 7-day window holds 1821. It now reads day windows and refuses a window at the cap.
  - Run 42425147012's `filter=all` jobs listing answers HTTP 502 on pages 2-6 every time. It is now read per attempt after a 5xx.

merges.body:
Adopts outside pull request 3356 (contributor Bankaifan, fork branch `feat/water-setpoint-lift-ceiling`, fork head e9dc72be09b9fc16fdde3508b1816ca5b4f5c9d5): with Pump duty control at Control and a water space set-point, the modulation floor's lift over the measured inlet (`flow_min_lift_k`, else `thermal_model.FLOW_MIN_LIFT_K`) and the full-power ceiling (`flow_heat_c`, read by the arbiter since #1955 but not offered) become options on the Sensors and entities page, shown for a water unit; `space_setpoint_unit` gains `return`, a controller taking the number as its return-water target. For a return target the hold, the weather curve and the gate move down by `pump_arbiter.RETURN_SUPPLY_OFFSET_K` (`_as_target`, `_gate_floor_c`), the valve outlet is skipped as the lift's anchor (`RETURN_SKIPPED_RUNG`), and `_full_draw_c` withholds the full-draw set-point from `draw_range` while the return-side inlet has less than `FLOW_MIN_LIFT_K` of headroom under the ceiling. The contributor's four commits are kept with their authorship, except one: the fork's c73b0e015 ("tests: review checks for the return set-point unit") was authored by the assistant identity the contributor ran, which `ref_privacy` refuses to publish, so it is re-authored to the contributor's own identity from the adjacent commit of the same fork session (Bankaifan <bankaifan@users.noreply.github.com>); their assistant-session trailers were dropped from the messages, and the contributor is credited by the Co-authored-by trailer below. The fork's `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` hunk, which restated the R10-MIN-POWER-FLOOR line under claims-for 7.1.7 that the 7.1.8 stamp emptied, is dropped; one added commit writes this branch's own config_flow claim, a default-options null-control grid, and makes `_or_hold`'s config argument required. No issue: the build is the outside-intake adoption, roster group R10-WATER-SETPOINT-LIFT.

Close 3356 with thanks once this merges. Plan page link for the outside-intake ruling (tvofi 2026-11-06): owed on 3356 by the orchestrator. After: R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE (#3299), open at this head; if it merges first with its own config_flow claim, the combined claim line is restated on this branch (claim-files.md).

Co-authored-by: Daniel <476059+Bankaifan@users.noreply.github.com>

## Independent review of the fork (fix-review.md, detached at the fork head, rebased onto main)

Sound, adopted. Judged on the added production lines (238 added, 39 deleted under `custom_components/`, `git diff --numstat origin/main HEAD -- custom_components`):

- One owner per concept: `const.SPACE_SETPOINT_WATER_UNITS` is the one definition of "a water set-point", read by `pump_arbiter._flow_unit`, `thermal_model.flow_setpoint_driven` and `config_flow._water_space_setpoint`; the supply-to-target shift lives in `pump_arbiter._as_target` alone; the lift's read in `thermal_model.configured_flow_min_lift_k`, beside `configured_flow_heat_c`. No `homeassistant` import added below the glue; `entry.options` is read only through the config mapping the arbiter is handed.
- Missing or invalid input refuses rather than guesses: a non-positive, non-finite or non-numeric lift reads as the rated lift; a return target with no return-side reading anchors nothing and takes the no-inlet hold.
- **Full-draw withholding — kept as the fork encodes it, the finite value `ceiling + FLOW_MIN_LIFT_K` in `FlowCommand.ceiling_c`, not an explicit representation.** Every reader is in `draw_range.py` and reads the pair as `written_c >= ceiling_c - CEILING_TOLERANCE_K` (`takes_ceiling`, `_overdrawn`, `_evidence`); the stored rows persist `(written_c, ceiling_c)` and `_command_cells` re-reads them only when both are finite. The explicit alternatives each lose: `None` already means "nothing commanded the draw" and `_evidence` reads it as **full** (`cmd is None or ...`), the opposite of what is meant; `math.inf` compares right live but `_command_cells` drops a non-finite row to `None` on reload, so a restart turns every withheld sample into a full one; a separate `full_draw` field on `FlowCommand` changes all three predicates and the stored-row schema with its back-compat read, which is widening into `draw_range`'s seam. The finite value persists and reloads with the meaning it was written with, and is unreachable by any write: `_flow_target` caps every heating write at the ceiling (`hi=heat_c`) and the gap, `FLOW_MIN_LIFT_K`, exceeds `CEILING_TOLERANCE_K` plus one entity step. Cost of the choice: a return target's stored row holds `ceiling + 5` rather than the configured ceiling while withheld, which a diagnostics reader of the raw rows sees.
- **Silent behaviour change, named:** `pump_arbiter._heat_ceiling_c` reads a stored `flow_heat_c` at or below `FLOW_GATE_C` (25 °C) as `FLOW_HEAT_C` (55 °C) at all three arbiter sites. On main such a value made every heating step write the gate, i.e. off; at this head it heats to 55 °C. The options flow offers 30–70 °C, so only a hand-edited entry reaches it; `docs/configuration.md` states it.
- `configured_flow_heat_c` now reads an absent key as `const.DEFAULT_FLOW_HEAT_C` and keeps `default` only for an unreadable value; every caller passes `pump_arbiter.FLOW_HEAT_C`, the same 55.0, so no caller's result moves (the null-control grid below runs the absent case).
- Assumptions the code labels as assumptions, not measured: `RETURN_SUPPLY_OFFSET_K` (the W35 30/35 °C rating spread) and the 5 K full-draw headroom. The fork's evidence (one install's recorder, a firmware decompilation not in the tree) was read as data; no figure from it is restated here as a measurement.

## Head

`4970f24c47bae8e768b0f36df647e6741d2eaedf` merges main `f365ce7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`981b31024e43a40a88552f08208809dcbbbf5512` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

- Null-control detector: `_return_unit` widened to every water unit (a flow target treated as a return one): `20 of 5011 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`, among them `null control: with default options every set-point an indoor or flow unit writes, and every held FlowCommand, is main's, cell for cell` (`2688 cells, moved at [1344, 1347, ...]`, the first flow cell onward), and the pre-existing flow-path checks (on the real curve a space-heating step writes the level's flow; the baseline holds the rated 35 degC flow; a flow set-point never goes below 25 °C).

The `_as_target` mutant leaves the grid green, as it should: it changes only a return target.

The default-options grid, pinned in `tests/features.py` as `_NC_AT_MAIN`: `_nc_cells()` drives the production `pump_arbiter.desired` for the baseline and each duty, and `_flow_command`, through a real coordinator, for unit indoor and flow × four inlet-rung sets (none, pump return, valve outlet, both) × inlets 18/27/52/60 °C × plan levels 0/1.5/3.5/6 kW × weather curve absent/30/42/61 °C: 2688 cells. Recorded by the same block on origin/main's production tree and on this head: byte-identical (`cmp`). Flat-price null control: not applicable (no cost figure).

merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-STRESS-MEM-PEAK: `tests / fast (3.14)` failed `tests/stress.py`'s "the probed scenarios' memory peaks stay within their recorded budgets" on #3297. The cause is not #3297's diff and not the interpreter version. It is the BLAS thread pin in `optimizer._scoped_minimize`, which built a fresh `threadpoolctl.ThreadpoolController` on every minimize call. The work each build did inside the solve forced CPython to rebuild its interpreter-wide interned-string table in one 1.83 MiB step, and the memory probe's traced window charged that step to whichever scenario's solve crossed the rebuild point. This change builds one controller at import, and the probe now asserts its own precondition: no import inside the traced window.

This repair round answers the three reds at 0f84b0fe8b (`gate`, `tests / mutation`, `tests / replay`).
- It pins the new guard's mutant in the ledger.
- It re-records one replay CPU budget down. The single controller made a replay cycle cheaper, so the old budget could no longer see a doubled cycle.
- It restores a replay null control that the tighter budget had silenced.

A local Linux finding limits what this PR closes. It is under `## Forward-carry`, carried to the two live stages that read a stress red. This round changes no code: it repairs the body against the review verdict at 00d12cad0f (verdict/3349 61a90cfce8).

## Head

`56a214c8bd8f72dfc4839234dc749cc53ec6813c` is the orchestrator's recarry of main into the previous head (#3367 raised the CodeQL python cap on main). It is not a clean merge of the live head and main (the body file is not the live pull-request body), so prepr checked this head.

`aeb5d2bdd62bec196fb2b736dcb2143e15d10b9b` merges main `f365ce7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution (#3367 raised the CodeQL python cap on main). The reviewed code is unchanged.

`00d12cad0f12bb8eb7da1010a720f7576fd4a552` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`00d12cad0f12bb8eb7da1010a720f7576fd4a552`. Its tree is 6286dfef5e's (`git diff --stat 6286dfef 00d12cad` prints nothing); 6286dfef5e merges origin/main `425b858495432c8dceb89d8d13866550352ba54f` into round 2's 0eb862d2 (giving 4dc05fad, where the scoped gate ran), then `fdc8d21adaa50a7feee534f08ee5edde9bda81ed` (#3338: governance and tools only, no file of this diff). Both merges are clean. No merge this round: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 00d12cad` exits 0 against origin/main 6457496aba (stamped 2026-11-09T02:52Z), so the branch is not re-cut or moved. The merge base stays fdc8d21ada and the scope is unchanged (`MODE: SCOPED -- 27 script(s) run, 6 scoped out`, re-derived at this head).

## Root cause

**Reproduction.** The red is CI job 128711769266, #3297 head 7fe24f9f61, CPython 3.14.10 on an AMD EPYC 7763. It traced heavy_old/shoulder and winter/pv+cycle at 5.3 MiB against a 3.46 record. A second run at the same SHA (job 128751219984, CPython 3.14.10 on a Xeon 8370C) traced those two at 3.5. On that run typical_slab/winter read 5.3 (record 3.4) and typical_slab/shoulder 4.0 (record 1.8). Same tree, different scenarios bumped, each bump about +1.8 to 2.2 MiB.

**Not the interpreter, not the hardware.**
- Main's own full runs on CPython 3.14.10 passed stress.py on every runner CPU class in the sample after #3274 merged, including 4fe7d5934b (#3297's main parent) on an EPYC 7763 and 72940b7954 on a Xeon 8370C.
- Locally on 3.14.7, stress.py's own `--memory-probe` at origin/main reads 3.47 on heavy_old/shoulder, winter/pv+cycle and winter/cycle (3 of 3 each). At the #3297 head it reads 5.31 on all three (2 of 2 each).
- On 3.12.14, origin/main reads 3.49 and 3.50.

**Mechanism.**
- On 3.14 a process's first `ThreadpoolController()` traces 199 KiB at main and 2076 KiB at #3297, after identical imports. Interning 100 throwaway strings before tracemalloc starts takes #3297's figure back to 199 KiB.
- The traced 1888 KiB sits in 93 blocks allocated under `marshal.loads` of a tiny stdlib module (`ctypes.macholib.dyld`, imported by `ctypes.util`). That is a global table being rebuilt at that moment, not the module.
- A churn harness (intern a fresh attribute name, then free it) shows the step directly: 1.83 MiB at intervals on both 3.14 and 3.12. With a constant name the peak is 0.002 MiB.
- So #3297 changed no solve. Its added strings moved the import-time table to just under a rebuild point, and the solve's own interning crossed it.

**What interns inside the solve.** `threadpool_limits(limits=1)` constructs `ThreadpoolController()` per call: 8 calls per typical_slab/shoulder solve, 10 per heavy_old/shoulder. On Linux (`_find_libraries_with_linux`, `/proc/self/maps`) each construction opens fresh `ctypes.CDLL` handles. Their symbol names are built at runtime (`f"{prefix}openblas_get_num_threads{suffix}"`, `_get_symbol`), interned by `CDLL.__getattr__`'s `setattr`, and freed with the handle. Off Linux on 3.14, the first call also imports `ctypes.util` (`dllist`) inside the solve. The Linux arm is read from threadpoolctl 3.7.0's source; it was not measured on Linux in this seat. The review's Linux measurement does not confirm it: base and head each ran red 1 of 3 interleaved on one box (`## Forward-carry`), so on Linux the harness does not move under the fix. CI's `fast (3.14)` read green at this head (job 128914863009, `ok python3 tests/stress.py`), which is one more sample of that flake, not a confirmation.

**The claim it reached several PRs is not supported.** Of 300 failed CI runs back to 2026-11-06, the only fast-job failures naming this check are #3297's two. The fast reds on #3181 and #3198, and #3299's earlier heads, were `tests/entities.py` and `tests/env_drift.py`. Their stress.py lines read `ok`.

**Process state: (d), sound under a precondition that changed beneath it.** `_memory_probe_main`'s docstring states the precondition: "A fresh process gives each scenario an honest high-water mark". That holds for RSS. It held for the traced arm only while the solve left interpreter-global tables alone and the import-time interned table sat far from a rebuild point. Nothing asserted it, so a tree landing near the rebuild point read as a scenario regression. Green runs print no memory figures (`run.sh` shows only a failing script's output), so the shrinking margin was invisible until the red. The countermeasure is two checks, and only one reaches Linux. `solve_window_imports` and the stress check that refuses it notice the precondition off Linux only: there the unfixed optimizer imports `ctypes.util` and four `ctypes.macholib` modules inside the window. On Linux it reads `[]` with the unfixed optimizer too (the reviewer's ev/linux-inwindow-imports.txt on verdict/3349: `mutA in-window imports: []`, `wt in-window imports: []`), so it cannot fire there and does not notice this precondition on Linux. The churn shape has no import to observe. On Linux the fix's one guard is the features pin on the shared controller (`_blas_pin_shared_controller`), which the reviewer's mutants A, B and C all fail.

**Class reach.** The rule is `git grep -n "tracemalloc.start"`. It returns 9 windows:
- `tests/stress.py`: closed here.
- `tests/replay.py`: memory cycles are the odd cycles after cycle 0 has already solved, so first-call setup is paid before any traced window. Already guarded.
- The seven `dev/audit/rounds/*/D9/*` harnesses, including `round4/D9/h7_memory_gate.py`, which `harness_headers.py` executes: all trace a solve after importing optimizer.py, so this change removes the per-call controller from their windows too. They are evidence records, and their thresholds are not touched.

**Cost test.**
- Defect: one production PR (#3297) blocked on both of its runs, plus this fixer and an RCA seat.
- P(recurrence): the step recurs at every rebuild point the tree's growth passes. In the churn harness they sit about 7 000 and 50 000 interned names apart on 3.14, about 14 500 and 58 000 on 3.12. Any diff can land near one.
- Countermeasure: one set difference per probe and a three-call features check. Passes.

## Mutation proof

- **Delete the production fix** (the stress.py change applied to main's unfixed optimizer.py; mutant worktree at bb7dfb9bd6+wt): the probe's `imported` field reads `["ctypes.macholib", "ctypes.macholib.dyld", "ctypes.macholib.dylib", "ctypes.macholib.framework", "ctypes.util"]` on typical_slab/shoulder (traced 2.06 MiB). The new memory-pass check "no probed solve imports a module inside the traced window (first-call setup is the import's cost, not the scenario's)" fails on it. The full stress.py run per mutant is left to CI's mutation check (`fixer.md` step 5).
- **The features pin, driven against the same mutant**: `FAIL the BLAS thread pin reuses optimizer.py's one ThreadpoolController ... | constructions=4 (want 1: the null control's alone), _blas_threads=NoneType`.
- **A second mutant that keeps `_blas_threads` but calls `threadpoolctl.threadpool_limits(limits=1)` again**: `FAIL ... constructions=4 ..., _blas_threads=ThreadpoolController`.
- **GUARD_OFF on the new guard** (`if _blas_threads is None:` made `if False:`, a copy of the head's custom_components): `FAIL without threadpoolctl the scoped minimize runs unpinned and still solves (x -> 0 on the bowl) | error=AttributeError("'NoneType' object has no attribute 'limit'") x=None`.
- **At the head**: both arms `ok`.

- **This round, the ledger's own mutant**: `python3 tests/mutation_table.py --pin-killed --base origin/main` drove `optimizer.py:887 GUARD_OFF` (`if _blas_threads is None:` as `if False:`). It took `tests/features.py` from rc=0 failed=0 to rc=1 failed=2: `pinned custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py:887 GUARD_OFF -- killed by tests/features.py`, `PIN KILLED: 1 pinned, 0 left unpinned`. Its null control (`optimizer.py:552 NULL_COMMENT`) survived every driver.
- **The replay re-record, before and after**: `replay.draw_offenders(replay.cost_draws())` with job 128866186676's rows appended and ref47 still at 3.3424 names that job (`clean cpu_ratio 1.551: budget 3.342 cannot see a 2x cycle`; `cpu arm not over budget`). At 2.7713 it names none.
- **The draws null**: moving job 125051003592 under the ref53 border (into ref47) names nothing at 2.7713. Moved into ref40 it is named (`clean cpu_ratio 1.444: budget 3.987 cannot see a 2x cycle`). Moving 127046649273 over the border into ref53 is still named (`clean cpu_ratio 2.256 over its budget 2.076`).

## Null control

At origin/main the traced peaks match the record (3.47 against 3.46 on heavy_old/shoulder), and only a tree near the rebuild point bumps. With the fix, #3297's tree and main read the same: typical_slab/shoulder 1.87 / 1.87, heavy_old/shoulder 3.29 / 3.29, winter/pv+cycle 3.29 / 3.29. Both report `"imported": []`. The 3.29 against a 3.46 record is 0.95x, inside the stale rule. The 0.18 MiB fall is the in-window `ctypes` import that this Mac no longer pays; on Linux, which has no such import, a fall is not expected. In the churn harness a constant (already interned) name peaks at 0.002 MiB against 1.83 MiB steps for fresh names. In the pin, the counter sees a direct construction (1), so a 0 cannot come from a dead counter.

## Figures

Local runs: macOS arm64, uv CPython 3.14.7 and 3.12.14 venvs with `tests/requirements-ci.txt` installed `--no-deps`. Scratch instruments are cited by sha1 (`$S` = this seat's scratch directory).
- traced peaks per tree: `$S/probe1.sh <repo> <python> <label>...` (sha1 1aedffce5a465ce6fa27a35936cf5916f8c77e11), which runs `python3 tests/stress.py --memory-probe <spec>`. Main 3.47; #3297 5.31; main+fix and #3297+fix 1.87 / 3.29 / 3.29; mutant 2.06 with five ctypes modules imported.
- repetition at main and #3297: `$S/memprobe.py <repo> <n> <labels>` (sha1 e3457e990305a17dd798b80980749ec079321a40). Main 3.14.7: [3.47, 3.47, 3.47] / [3.47, 3.47, 3.48] / [3.47, 3.47, 3.47]. #3297 3.14.7: [5.31, 5.31] / [5.3, 5.31] / [5.31, 5.31]. Main 3.12.14: [3.49, 3.49] / [3.5, 3.49].
- first-controller trace and the 100-string padding: `$S/importpeak.py <repo> controller <pad>` (sha1 d1d62b5d929fa50e3dd650ce79ff5114e8363627). 199 / 2076 / 922 / 922 KiB; #3297 at pad 100 gives 199.
- allocation site: `$S/tbdiag.py` (sha1 d3fdab1a419f144015bb2f38023d05e759551c9d). 1888 KiB in 93 blocks under `_compile_bytecode` (`marshal.loads`) of `ctypes.macholib.dyld`, reached through `threadpool_limits` and `_load_libraries`.
- in-window imports and hash-seed independence: `$S/impdiag.py` (sha1 ec9be2b1d49047cbfdf7dd8f70612d692c481f2f). Seeds 1 and 2 both read 3.88 at #3297; main reads 2.05.
- no cyclic garbage in a solve (refutes a GC-timing cause): `$S/gcdiag.py <repo> <label> saveall` (sha1 7f8f62811489bbd7a7a7b9c92ae6adfb89f91d93). `unreachable: 0`.
- the rebuild step: `$S/churn.py` (sha1 b9a3037a4d12d53fc84702d221541245e438c5ea). 1.83 MiB at 7 000 / 57 000 (3.14.7) and 14 500 / 72 500 (3.12.14); null control 0.002 MiB.
- per-call CPU: `$S/tpbench.py` (sha1 6938d9ca4852064d1c3f0a82e42f3fb08fd4366a). Fresh `threadpool_limits` costs 1.141 ms (3.14.7) and 1.838 ms (3.12.14) per call; shared `controller.limit` 0.002 ms. merges.body:
Repair round for the three planner defects of the 2026-11-08 replan study (a name-prefix lane collision, b refused/deferred groups still scheduled, c the critical-path coordinator-cap exemption). Group R10-FLY-REPLAN-DEFECTS. Blocks of `Fix review: blocked b59abf37196379f3264b3aaad42e199aaf053207` answered: class-open, mutation-vacuous, red-ci, and the owner question.

(a) `roster_lane` matches `INSTRUMENT_NAME_STEMS` as the exact group or `<stem>-...`, so `R10-I1` no longer takes `R10-I18N-DE`. (b) `roster_lib.CLOSED_STAGES` gains `refused` and `deferred`; `refuted` stays open. (c) `build_plan` exempts a ready critical-path group from the coordinator cap, flags it `exempt_coordinator`, and `check_plan` leaves flagged groups out of its coordinator count.

## Re-cut

Round 3 of review: `Fix review: blocked 8f073db70d18895d0962924ac8da72647a02090a mutation-vacuous`. Two non-equivalent mutants survived; this head adds the owed checks and no production change (neither mutant revealed a defect). Disclosed self-correction: the Mutation proof line below that says `deferred-holds-dependent` was retargeted to the producing line did not kill `open_ = open_ - set(held)`; that site is now killed by its own row.

## Round-3 mutation proof (head 2305095d2b61ccac83157333719f3124bc73be7c)

Driver `tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --spec`, NULL mutant first (reported SURVIVED = the command passes unedited), then the mutant.

| site | mutant | check added | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tools/plan/replan.py` `build_plan` | `open_ = open_ - set(held)` -> `pass` (spec `--in-place`, cmd `python3 tools/plan/replan.py --self-test`) | row "refused/deferred: a held dependent is in no wave and no batch", plus in-file mutation arm `held-subtraction` | `SURVIVED NULL`, `KILLED replan-held-subtract` |
| `tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py` `held_behind_deferred` | `elif a in held and gates(G[a]):` -> `elif a in held:` (spec `--copy-tree`, cmd `python3 tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py --self-test`) | row "a held group that is itself released (refuted) does not hold its dependent" (fixture P deferred, Q refuted after P, S after Q; expects `{"Q": "P"}`) | `SURVIVED NULL`, `KILLED held-gates-conjunct` |

Null controls: the replan row asserts the released (`refused`) case keeps R10-Y and R10-Z in waves/batches, so it is not satisfied by emptiness; the roster_lib row's null is `chain` (queued Q holds S) in the preceding row. The weakened form (`set(list(held)[:0])`) is the same deletion. Why the old rows missed it: the output loop's `if n in held` branch relabels a scheduled held group, so start/held_behind read the same; only wave/batch membership separates them. Ledger: both sites are `tools/`, outside `mutation-autofix`'s lane; the in-tree harness is replan's `held-subtraction` arm and the roster_lib row; no `tests/mutation_ledger` entry applies.

`tools/pr/prepr.sh` at this head: `rc=0` (gate mode FULL, structure ratchet passed, ci predict clean).

## Head

`7df25328455b21659d3c74c44419920cf1adfa38` merges main `f365ce7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`09f0b6d9ce030676bd513e77a8b7318b53632b7c` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

2305095d2b61ccac83157333719f3124bc73be7c: the PR head 8f073db70d18895d0962924ac8da72647a02090a plus the round-3 repair (two self-test rows, one in-file mutation arm). `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0 against `origin/main` 82a2c142f (2026-11-09T05:57Z), so there is no merge; the one resolution it reports is the `tests/closures.json` ledger merge driver. Main moved after the last `tools/pr/prepr.sh` run; the figures stamped below are at merge base 20e83746fe91.

## Owner ruling carried (Carry: R10-FLY-REPLAN-DEFECTS)

The open owner question is ruled by the orchestrator under mandate 6715477401: "a group whose `after` names a DEFERRED group stays held behind it (deferred means postponed, not done); a group whose `after` names a REFUSED or REFUTED group is released (that predecessor never lands)." Implemented in `roster_lib.gates` (the one predicate: a predecessor in `RELEASING_STAGES` = finished + `refused` + `refuted` no longer gates), `roster_lib.held_behind_deferred` (transitive), `roster_lib.depth_of`, `replan.dependency_graph` and `replan.build_plan` (a held group is emitted unscheduled with `held_behind`, `done` true so every reader that skips a done group skips it), and the readers named under Figures.

## Block 1: class-open (closeout)

Cause: adding `refused` and `deferred` to `CLOSED_STAGES` dropped them from `open_groups`, which `closeout_exempt` and `closeout.roster_blockers` read, so the `resume.host` rule was dead for `refused` and a hosted `deferred` group stopped blocking. Fix: `roster_lib.unfinished_groups` (every group not in `FINISHED_STAGES` = done + `absorbed`), read by `closeout_exempt` and `roster_blockers`. Alternative rejected: reading `groups_of` at each closeout call site duplicates the rule. Closeout therefore behaves as at the merge base for every stage.

Reviewer's harness `evidence/probe_closeout.py` (sha1 123d68927f7c435b15336da810a8dd409433e8f8, verdict/3326), both ends, same fixture, `H` in-progress, `R` hosted by `H`:

| tree | refused | refuted | deferred |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3cf879467 (before) | `['H']` | `['H','R']` | `['H']` |
| this head | `['H','R']` | `['H','R']` | `['H','R']` |
| merge base 20e83746 (control) | `['H','R']` | `['H','R']` | `['H','R']` |

Self-test rows: `closeout.py` "a refused group whose host is still open blocks", the deferred twin, and "a deferred group with no host still blocks" (its null); `roster_lib.py` "a refused or deferred group stays unfinished ... closeout_exempt exempts it only when its host is not open".

## Mutation proof

Mutants applied to the production line, then the self-tests run; each line is the mutant and what it turned red (`$HOME`-local driver `mut2.py`, sha1 not in tree; the `replan.py` ones are the in-file harness).

- `closeout_exempt` reads `open_groups` (`set(unfinished_groups(roster))` -> `set(open_groups(roster))`): `roster_lib.py`, `closeout.py` red.
- `roster_blockers` reads `open_groups`: `closeout.py` red (the hosted refused/deferred rows).
- `RELEASING_STAGES` plus `deferred` (deferred releases): `roster_lib.py` red.
- `RELEASING_STAGES` without `refuted`, then without `refused`: `roster_lib.py` red, each.
- `held_behind_deferred` not transitive (`elif a in held and gates(G[a])` -> `elif False`): `roster_lib.py` red.
- `critical_path` reads every open edge again (`if a in G and gates(G[a])` -> `if a in G`): `roster_lib.py` red.
- `depth_of` reads `is_open` again: `roster_lib.py` red.
- `handover_prompt.ready_next` back to `a not in open_`: `handover_prompt.py` red, two rows ("a group after a deferred group is held", "after a refuted group is released").
- Block 2: `check-ignores-flag` (`if g.get("coordinator") and not g.get("exempt_coordinator")]` -> `if g.get("coordinator")]`), new in-file mutant: KILLED by the new row "--check passes a flagged critical-path start that overlaps a running coordinator group".
- `edge-releases-ruled` (`dependency_graph` back to `if a in open_:`) and `deferred-holds-dependent` (`held = roster_lib.held_behind_deferred(G)` -> `held = {}`), new in-file mutants: both KILLED. The first version of the second targeted `open_ = open_ - set(held)`, which survived (the held branch of the output loop masks it); retargeted to the producing line.
- Earlier mutants (`lane-stem-boundary`, `coordinator-cp-exempt`, `coordinator-cp-flag`, the updated `coordinator-cap`/`cp-first-in-tier`) still KILLED: `python3 tools/plan/replan.py --self-test` prints `self-test: 0 failed` with every mutant killed.

## Null control

- Block 2 fixture: X3 (L, coordinator) runs while CP1 (XL, coordinator, after D) starts flagged; the row asserts `X3.start < CP1.start < X3.finish` so the overlap is real, and its null is the same plan with the flag removed, which `check_plan` refuses with `coordinator cap`. The reviewer's probe `evidence/probe_check.py` gave `[]` at the head and the cap message under the mutant.
- Ruling arms, replan: `deferred` -> dependent and its own dependent `held_behind` the group, `start` null; `refused` -> dependent starts at 0 and is not held; `refuted` -> the group is still scheduled, its dependent released with `after == []`; null: a `queued` predecessor still gates (`after == ["R10-Q"]`, starts later).
- Ruling arms, `roster_lib`: `gates` / `held_behind_deferred` / `depth_of` for `refused`, `refuted`, `done`, `absorbed` (released) against `deferred` (held), and the transitive case.

## Figures

Each command is the instrument; counts are not carried.

- Seam rule for the changed predicates (`CLOSED_STAGES`, `open_groups`, `is_open`, now also `gates`, `unfinished_groups`): `grep -rnE "open_groups|is_open\(|closeout_exempt|roster_blockers|CLOSED_STAGES|DONE_STAGES" tools tests` (null control: it returns `closeout.py`, which the first body's list lacked). Dispositions:
  - `closeout.py` (`roster_blockers`, `step_issues` via `closeout_exempt`): fixed in this diff (Block 1).
  - `plan_table.py` (all five `open_groups` calls), `resume_doc.py` open counts and waves, `handover_prompt.py` `in_flight`, `prune_refs.open_group_ids`, `size_durations.py`, `ci_predict.py`, `carry_audit.py`, `merge_throughput.py`, `roster_sync.py`, `roster_edit.py`: read the open set as work still owed; a refused or deferred group dropped from it is the intended reading (deferred stays owed only through the edge rule and closeout). Self-tests of each: 0 failed.
  - After-edge readers, changed to `roster_lib.gates` so they follow the ruling: `resume_doc.py` "Ready next", `handover_prompt.ready_next`, `plan_page.py` `blk`, `orchestrator_tick.py` `blockers` line; `roster_lib.depth_of`. Pinned only for `handover_prompt.ready_next` (rows above) and `depth_of` (`roster_lib.py`).
  - `roster_lib.critical_path` and the `plan_table.py` mermaid dependency drawing now skip an edge to a refuted group (`gates`); `critical_path` is pinned by the `roster_lib.py` row "critical_path: an edge to a refuted group is released" (mutant: `if a in G and gates(G[a])` -> `if a in G` goes red), the drawing by no row. Not drawn: an edge to a deferred group (the group is not in the open set), display only.
- Block 3 closures, `python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --base origin/main`: `no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted`. Cause of the red: the new `tests/entities.py` edge runs `orchestrator_tick.py --self-test`, opening four INERT files (`orchestrator_tick.py`, `pr_cap.py`, `budget_raise_gate.py`, `app_approve.sh`). Repair, by the route `INERT_EXCEPT` documents: the four join `INERT_EXCEPT` in `tests/closure.py`, then `./tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/entities.py` twice (the first recording fails its own "every tracked file is measured or classified" check, since the table does not yet list them; the second is the fixed point and records `rc` 0). Alternatives: classify the reads out of the tick edge (drops the edge that catches the CLOSED_STAGES regression), or `--apply-inert` (it files them under `inert_reads`, which the self-test-reads arm names UNDER-SCOPED for a script whose self-test reads them).

- Replan before/after figures of the first body (R10-I18N-DE lane, R10-FLY-CLOUD-FRUGAL-OFF done) are unchanged by this round except that a dependent of a deferred group is now held.

The diff's added guards are pinned by the self-test rows above; `prepr.sh` step 6d lists any it finds unpinned and each is named in the Mutation proof section as killed. The `plan_page.py` `blk`, `orchestrator_tick.py` `blockers` and `plan_table.py` drawing edge reads carry no row: Forward-carry.

Round: 1 (first review of this PR at this head).

## Block

1. class-open: `tools/audit/seat/closeout.py` `roster_blockers`, through `roster_lib.closeout_exempt`. `closeout_exempt` was written so that a ruled group (`RULED_STAGES = ("refused", "refuted")`) whose `resume.host` names a group still open blocks the closeout ("The roster keeps a ruled group open by design"). This PR adds `refused` and `deferred` to `CLOSED_STAGES`, so `open_groups` drops those groups before `closeout_exempt` and `roster_blockers` see them. The host rule is now dead for `refused`, and a hosted `deferred` group no longer blocks either. Probe (`ev/probe_closeout.py`): fixture R(stage, host=H), H in-progress. At base 20e83746 `roster_blockers` returns `['H', 'R']` for refused, refuted and deferred. At the head it returns `['H']` for refused and deferred, and `['H', 'R']` only for refuted. closeout's self-test still passes, because its hosted row uses `refuted`. The body's seam list (`is_open|CLOSED_STAGES|DONE_STAGES` plus the tick's `open_groups|groups_of`) does not name `closeout.py`. The same `open_groups` path also reaches `plan_table.py` and `resume_doc.py`, which the body does not name either. They now drop deferred and refused groups from open counts and waves, which looks like the reading the body intends, but the body does not say so for them. Carry: R10-FLY-REPLAN-DEFECTS

merges.body:
R10-SAV-METER-FLOOR, with its two carries. Three changes to the savings row:

- **The meter floor (the group's brief).** `ledger.below_meter_floor` reads a row's *booked* `savings_baseline` kWh over its `savings_actual` kWh. Where that is under `METER_FLOOR` (0.5, `ledger.py`) on a row of the current reference basis with at least `MIN_CALIBRATION_KWH` metered, the row keeps both columns, its saving and percent read `None` as an old-basis row's do, and it carries `below_meter_floor: true`. It reads the booked lines, never the calibrated column, which cancels the meter. The card's table tags the row, and a note under the table and on the receipt says why (en and sv). The receipt event carries `saving_below_meter_floor`, and the notifications blueprint's monthly receipt quotes the card's note. There is no ceiling (binding of triage P387).
- **Carry 1 (owner ruling L5): the wood calibration.** `ExternalHeatState.heating()` answers "did wood heat this interval" (a fire active or fading, any displacement, any free heat). The coordinator's pending snapshot carries it as one key, `wood_heated`, and only on a wood-configured house (`None` elsewhere, so a no-wood ledger books exactly what it booked before). `add_savings_settlement` books a wood-free plan/meter pair (`SAVINGS_WOOD_FREE_LINES`) for intervals with `wood_heated` False. On a wood month, `ledger.applied_calibration` reads that pair, unfloored, once its plan kWh reaches `MIN_CALIBRATION_KWH`. With too few wood-free kWh, and on every month booked before the pair existed, the old floor `max(1.0, measured)` stays as the fallback. Each row states the basis it used as `calibration_basis`: `meter`, `wood_free` or `wood_floor`. No store migration: a month without the pair falls back.
- **Carry 0 (R10-RCA-SAV-ESTIMATE), applied here.**
  - `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-SAV-ESTIMATE.md`: part 2 is now the floor; "about zero" is corrected to the group's cost; the class is stated not fully barriered while the high side has no meter oracle.
  - `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_sav_estimate.py`: `METER_BAND` is removed, and the `ledger` arm calls production's `ledger.below_meter_floor`.
  - `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`: `parts_missing` says "the meter floor" and adds "an inflated reference on a wood house has no meter oracle (owner ruling)"; `countermeasure` and `detector_idea` are updated.
  - The class mint is kept: `fold_ledger.py sync` reports `audit-find.js` already carries it, so there is no code-owned hunk.
  - The 2026-11 ratio is not re-derived (see Forward-carry).

Alternatives considered, and why each lost:
- Carrying the flag as a `SETTLEMENT_KEYS` member was rejected: that tuple is the plan step's readings from `_current_action`, and the flag is the detector's.
- Booking the pair on every house was rejected: it would add two lines to every no-wood store and receipt for nothing.
- Re-deriving "wood heated" in the ledger from published fields was rejected: the carry names `ExternalHeatState` as the owner.

Roster carries, numbered from 1 as the review packet counts them: **Carry 1** is the brief's carry 0 (the R10-RCA-SAV-ESTIMATE rewrite), answered above and under Forward-carry. **Carry 2** is the brief's carry 1 (owner ruling L5, the wood calibration), answered above and in the mutation proof and figures.

merges.body:
R10-COP-GATE-E (#3106), the two measure-first carries routed from R10-COP-GATE-D. Carries are numbered as on the roster entry: Carry 1 is the dispatch brief's carry 0 (from R10-COP-GATE-D carry 3), Carry 2 its carry 1 (from R10-COP-GATE-D carry 8).

**Carry 1: the unsensed slab across a mode switch: measured, confirmed, fixed.** `_propagated_slab` (`coordinator.py`) advanced the slab by `draw_range.space_draw_kw` on the draw read at the close, split by `coord._commanded_split()` and gated on the live mode alone (`space_served=signals.space_heat or not signals.mode_observed`). Over an interval whose mode dwell saw both duties, the close's mode decides the whole interval: a switch back from hot water to heating books the whole draw as space heat (over-advance = the draw x the dwell's hot-water share), and the reverse switch books 0 kW (under-advance by the draw x its space share). The second direction is the same seam read the other way; the carry named only the first.

The rule, chosen on the measurement: **prorate by the dwell's space hours.** `_propagated_slab` now splits the draw by `heat_energy.meter_of(coord).attribution(coord._commanded_split())`, the same owner `_interval_measured_heat_kw` beside it already reads: the dwell's (space, hot-water) hours where observed, else the plan's ask exactly as before. Observed, `space_share` of zero space hours is 0, so `space_served` is the live-mode rule only on an unobserved dwell (`a.observed or ...`). A dwell on one duty reads byte-for-byte as before (the all-space null below); an unobserved dwell passes the plan split unchanged.

Why not the plan-trajectory fall-back (`ran_hot_water` skip): on the harness's switch-back interval, against a reference of the same space energy spread over the interval (`truth`: an all-space interval drawing the draw x the space share), the prorate reads the reference's slab exactly, the base's rule is +0.665 K high, and the fall-back is +1.495 K high: worse than the defect it would replace, because the plan's trajectory is the commanded heat #2499 removed from this path. Prorating assumes the pump draws a constant kW while on space heat; on a switch out, the close's draw is the hot-water draw standing in for the space draw, which is the reading the interval has.

**Carry 2: set-point to drawn power between the duty gate and the ceiling: not measurable from the recorded fixtures; stays open on named owner data.** `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_cop_gate_band.py` pairs each flow set-point step strictly inside the band (`pump_arbiter.FLOW_GATE_C` + `draw_range.GATE_TOLERANCE_K` to `thermal_model.configured_flow_heat_c` less `draw_range.CEILING_TOLERANCE_K`, 25.25 to 54.5 degC on the owner fixture) with the last power reading inside that step, counting only steps the mode entity holds on space heat alone. The two recorded fixtures under `tests/replay/` yield one in-band step (`owner-2026-10-30-away.json`: 47 degC, 1.55 kW) and none; a gain and its linearity need at least three distinct set-points, so no fit exists. The 35 degC steps of the owner fixture are excluded because the mode read `Heating + DHW` throughout them (draw 0.0 kW). What closes it: a diagnostics download with the week of debug data on, from an install whose pump ran across the band, carrying the space set-point entity's history, the power entity's history and the mode entity's history, with at least three distinct space-only flow set-points between 25.25 and 54.5 degC each held long enough for one settled power reading. The flat-price null for a fit applies to none, since no fit was computed; the instrument's own null (`--synthetic`, a linear 0.1 kW/K series through the same pairing) reads the gain exactly, so `fit=none` is the data's, not the instrument's. Carry 2 stays open, and so does #3106 with it.

**Predecessor.** The roster sets this group `after` R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED (#3297), which is open and unmerged at origin/main ba6fd7e8b. This branch is cut from ba6fd7e8b, the base the dispatch named. #3297's diff touches neither `heat_energy.py` nor `draw_range.py` nor `_propagated_slab` (`git diff origin/main...origin/fix/r10-hotfix-cop-unmeasured -- custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/heat_energy.py custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/draw_range.py` prints nothing), and `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/fix/r10-hotfix-cop-unmeasured` exits 0.

## Head

`ce4cdb2271c3a3883c422e228f55d526d93827e2` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

## Mutation proof

Block command `BLOCK_CMD` (see `## Figures`), at 85acb2c184e685e2289af52ad39a8def1b3995dc. Unmutated: `ALL 17 FEATURES BLOCK PASSED`.
- M1: `(a.space, a.dhw),` -> `coord._commanded_split(),` in `_propagated_slab`: `2 of 17 FEATURES BLOCK FAILED`: "R10-COP-GATE-E: a switch back from hot water to heating advances the slab by the dwell's space share of the draw, not the whole draw as space heat" `[slab switch-back/half-draw/heating=24.1700/23.5050/24.1700]`, "R10-COP-GATE-E: a switch from heating to hot water books the dwell's space share of the draw, not 0 kW" `[24.1700/23.5050/22.8400]`.

- `BLOCK_CMD`: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/seat/features_block.py --prelude 'from datetime import datetime, timedelta, UTC' --prelude 'import asyncio as _r9f12_aio' --prelude 'from harness import FakeEntry as _r9f12_entry' --prelude 'from homeassistant.util import dt as _r9f12_dt' --prelude 'from types import SimpleNamespace as _r9f12_ns' 'R.section("R10-DEMAND-OVERBOOK' 'R.section("R9 P2: stamp owner, plausib'`.

At 85acb2c184e685e2289af52ad39a8def1b3995dc: `all_space` identical, `switch_back` and `switch_out` `booked_kw=2.0 over_kw=0.0 slab=23.5050`. The rule: `over_kw` = booked kW minus the draw x the dwell's space share (`heat_energy.ModeDwell.shares` over the meter's cycle). The orchestrator's earlier "about 2.25 kW" was a figure from another configuration; this rule gives draw x hot-water share, 2.0 kW for 4.0 kW over a half-and-half dwell.
- Rule comparison (switch_back, 4.0 kW, against `truth` 23.5050): base +0.665 K, plan fall-back (`plan=25.0000`) +1.495 K, prorate 0.000 K.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_cop_gate_band.py --synthetic` (sha1 02129ef0ca51334e432e34e50150ea29dd49e2a7), at the base and at 85acb2c184e685e2289af52ad39a8def1b3995dc alike: `owner-2026-10-30-away.json steps=1 distinct_c=1 fit=none`, `synthetic-dhw-only.json steps=0 distinct_c=0 fit=none`, `synthetic-linear steps=4 distinct_c=4 gain_kw_per_k=0.1 max_resid_kw=0.0`.

Within it: `ALL 4988 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, `ALL 2670 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`, `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`, `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 56 scenario(s) checked against ba6fd7e8b0b0502dfcce26df781810e474fc1d2f`, `NO STALE FIXTURE: 56 committed fixture(s)`, `card_drift.mjs` ok. The one failure is `tests/stress.py`, `1 of 113 STRESS CHECKS FAILED`: "the probed scenarios' memory peaks stay within their recorded budgets" (typical_slab/winter 5.3 MiB vs 3.4, typical_slab/shoulder 4.0 vs 1.8, and four more scenarios at 5.3). bus-nonce: 04b43806e2e3e6d45158d0e5f57f4d85

Measured head ce4cdb2271c3a3883c422e228f55d526d93827e2; the body's measurements were taken at 85acb2c184e685e2289af52ad39a8def1b3995dc, and `review_carry.py 85acb2c ce4cdb2` prints CARRY (only a main merge and the delivery row lie between them; no diff in custom_components, tests/features.py or the harnesses).

## Block

`merge_train.py classify ce4cdb2271c3a3883c422e228f55d526d93827e2 --pr 3371` exited 1: `RED ... pending: none red: gate`. Neither run at this head (42597670888, 42598782881) ran `tests`, `codeql`, `governance`, `hassfest`, `validate` or `kernel-points`. All were `skipped`, and the PR is `draft: true`. The `gate` job (`KIND: edit`) printed `FAIL tests: no run at this head judged base 'main'`, the same for codeql/governance/hassfest/validate, and `pr-contract / pr-contract: failure`. Both `pr-contract` runs failed closed: `FAIL closed: no run at this head owns a finished codeql unit for base 'main' after 600 s`. The red does not come from the authored code. But the heavy suite (full gate, goldens, stress memory probe, mutation lane) has never run at this head, and fix-review step 11 has me cite CI's heavy runs, not re-run them. Every check I could run myself passes (Evidence). Once a run at this head (or a carried head) runs `tests` and `codeql` and the gate is green, a re-review needs only CI and the step-11 answer for `pr-contract`'s red. Note the body's own local `tests/run.sh` read `1 TEST SCRIPT(S) FAILED` (`tests/stress.py` memory peaks). The body attributes that to the base's bimodal traced peak, and I did not re-derive it; CI's `tests` lane has to settle it. Also, `## Red checks` reads `none`, but `pr-contract` is now red at this head. The cause is outside the diff (no codeql run), but the body has to answer that red once the head's workflows conclude (defect-root-cause.md enforcement).

## Findings

- Follow-up: the finding's harnesses `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_cop_gate_slab.py` and `r10_cop_gate_band.py` were built by the fixer in this PR. The packet reads `Finder's harness: none named` (fix-review step 9). The body discloses them as this branch's files and runs them at both ends from an export; they land in the tree and are in the closure. I ran both myself at base and head. Carry: dismissed: harness disclosed as the fixer's own and committed by this PR (fixer.md 18), measured independently below
- Follow-up: Carry 2 (set-point-to-draw linearity) stays open, carried to #3106. Its control (≥3 distinct space-only flow set-points strictly inside 25.25–54.5 degC, the `--synthetic` null reading `gain_kw_per_k=0.1 max_resid_kw=0.0`) is stated in the committed harness docstring and the PR body, not in the #3106 issue body or the roster brief. When R10-COP-GATE-E goes `done` at merge, the carry needs a live destination, e.g. `dev/programme/carries/carry-3106.json`, holding that precondition. Carry: #3106

- Merge with main: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main ce4cdb2` exit 0 at origin/main 806e952ca (`LEDGER-MERGE: resolved tests/closures.json`, no conflict), in `ev/merge-tree.txt`.

- Mutation proof, all restored, `git status --short` empty after:

  - M2 drop `a.observed or`: `1 of 17`, switch-out `22.8400/23.5050/22.8400`. Matches the body.
  - M3 (mine) `space_served=True`: `2 of 17`, kills the #2499 dhw-only check and switch-out. The `space_served` gate is pinned on both arms.
- Finder-shape harness, my own RESULT lines (`ev/harness-both-ends.txt`, sha1 slab 746454bbf9a3e19b89c263ef7a98bb2f187f5d2d, band 02129ef0ca51334e432e34e50150ea29dd49e2a7, as in the body):
  - At base ba6fd7e8b, 4.0 kW: all_space `over_kw=0.0 slab=24.1700`; switch_back `booked_kw=4.0 over_kw=2.0 slab=24.1700`; switch_out `booked_kw=0.0 over_kw=-2.0 slab=22.8400`; truth `slab=23.5050`.
  - At head, 4.0 kW: all_space identical (the null holds at both ends); switch_back and switch_out `booked_kw=2.0 over_kw=0.0 slab=23.5050`, equal to truth.
  - Perturbation `--drawn 6.0`: base `over_kw` 3.0 / -3.0 (scales with the draw); head 0.0 / 0.0, slab 23.8375 vs truth 23.8475. That is the 0.01 K the body attributes to learner folds on truth's clean interval; I did not re-derive that attribution.
- Rule comparison re-derived from these lines: base 24.1700-23.5050 = +0.665 K; plan fall-back 25.0000-23.5050 = +1.495 K; prorate 0.000 K. Matches.

The body's `+3` at 214c0e22f was not re-derived at that commit.
- Arch score: CI `arch-score` success in both runs. The body reports `dS -0.0012 WORSENS (coord_footprint 2489->2491)` with no budget raised; `git diff --stat` of `*_budgets.json`, VERSION, the manifest, RELEASE_NOTES.md and both claim files over the merge base prints nothing. CI `pr-contract` printed `no version edit`.
- `tests/closure.py select --diff a5dce6b9e`: `MODE: SCOPED -- 27 script(s) run, 6 scoped out.` `tests/harness_headers.py`: `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`.

R10-HOTFIX-CODEQL-HEADROOM part 2 (topic r10-hotfix-codeql-headroom-p2)
Closes: none (triage ruling P463; design note design/r10-hotfix-codeql-headroom sections 3 and 7)
Cap change only: the module-scope-try wrap is not used, tests/features.py is untouched and no file is excluded from the scan.

Main's `codeql / Analyze (python)` job outgrew the job-level 45-minute cap. The cap moves into the matrix `include` entries of `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`: python 75, actions and javascript-typescript 45, with `timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.timeout }}`. The cap-paragraph comment is rewritten. The `tests/entities.py` pin (`_analyze_cap`) now reads the include entries: `timeout-minutes` is exactly the matrix expression, python an int at least 51 (the design's projected worst case), each other leg exactly 45. Check count unchanged. The brief's "do not edit tests/entities.py" binds that file's structure; "every check must still pass" forces this one pin's edit. Alternatives (blanket 75, three jobs, refuse) lost as in design section 4. A stopgap; the structural cure (split tests/features.py) awaits an owner ruling, design section 5.

## Head

`7b0575e7e9ea24b59279b77c21d7a0151302f125` merges main `79b7356` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`0eeb6bdb3663b598c8421cc47ff8992d99c65b64` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

Code head a325da3809246b9571938795021f9b7a03bba2ea (merge base 3fdaa9da9ab667042338fcf034147bde16b91fe4, origin/main at 2026-11-09T04:59Z).

## Mutation proof

Run: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` on the pin, mutating the workflow's predicate values; baseline restored after each.

- actions 45 to 75: FAIL (1 of 2668).
- drop python's timeout from the include entry: FAIL (1 of 2668).
- comment-only edit: ok, ALL 2668 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED (diff stat shows the file modified).

## Null control

The two legs left at 45 read 45 in the diff (`git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD -- .github/workflows/codeql.yml` shows actions and javascript-typescript at 45); the pin fails when actions is raised to 75 (mutant above). Runner-speed control for the PR's own python job: tests/closure.py extraction time in that job's log against the base job's, to be read from the PR's own run; this seat opens no PR and cannot report it, the reviewer reads it at the head.

- Python jobs of main's ci.yml push runs, newest 20, at merge base 3fdaa9da, taken 2026-11-09T04:59Z: 10 cancelled at 45.1 min and 10 other; capped (duration >= 44.9 min) also 10, equal to the cancelled count (null control: a cap that did not bind would show cancelled below capped). The newest of the 20 started 2026-11-09T03:06Z; window 2026-11-08T15:23Z to 2026-11-09T03:06Z.
- Fixture and claim files: none moved; `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD --stat` lists only codeql.yml and tests/entities.py.

merges.body:
Root cause fix for the roster drain's "stale-worktree trap" and its "HEAD ... is on no origin ref" cascade (round 10 root-cause seat, 2026-11-08). The sweep runner drain refused roster ops because the lint clone stayed at an older main; each refusal then stranded a local commit in wt-run and refused the next op for that op's fault.

Cause, in tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py `_run_op`: (1) the lint refresh (fetch, detach) ignored return codes and read the lint clone's own origin/main, a different ref from the edit checkout's origin/main that roster_edit.lint_gate compares; four attempts in a row stayed stale (main-lint's origin/main reflog: no update 11:40 to 14:34 +0100 while the edit checkout saw 4a9d2d5 and bb7dfb9). (2) A refusal other than "not origin/main" left its edit as a local commit in the worktree. Why the clone's fetch did not move is not established; the fix does not depend on it.

Process state (defect-root-cause.md): (c). The check existed (the lint gate, the retry on "not origin/main") but the refresh feeding it was unchecked and read another ref.

Fix: `refresh_lint` detaches the lint clone at the edit checkout's origin/main SHA after a fetch there, verifies HEAD equals it, and refuses by name ("lint clone not refreshed") otherwise; a final refusal removes the worktree.

Repair round 1 (fix review blocked `mutation-vacuous` at d0db3e30b8, ref verdict/3337): only the detach SHA was pinned; M4, M5 and M6 survived the harness and the self-test, M3 and M7 survived as minor. This round adds no production line; it adds checks that each mutant fails:
- the harness now runs three scenarios: `stale` (the finder's: the lint clone's fetch fails, both ops push), `cascade` (the reviewer's variant: the stub refuses op1 once for an unrelated reason and op2 must push, which needs the refused op's worktree removed: pins M4), `follow` (another clone pushes main, and `refresh_lint` alone must detach a clone with its own object store, no alternates, at origin's new main: pins M3, the edit checkout's fetch, and M7, the clone's fallback fetch).
- the self-test gains two checks on an empty lint clone (a directory with no objects and no origin): `refresh_lint` must refuse it naming the wanted SHA (pins M5), and `_run_op` must report "lint clone not refreshed" and never run the editor, read from the stub's calls file (pins M6).

Cost test: defect about 5 min hand-landing plus about 20 min pass delay per stale refusal, 172 of 1327 drain report lines (13%) were cascade refusals, 3+ instances on 2026-11-08; countermeasure a one-time diff of about 40 production lines and about 50 ms per op, no extra network call. cost(countermeasure) < cost(defect) x P(recurrence).

## Head

`805f5759c9f396a3fa7e88b2605cee0164685906` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

778782832170d403103adc051922f63303a7c412

Null control: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD | grep -c CONFLICT` prints 0. Re-run on the merged tree: `roster_queue.py --self-test` (62 checks, 0 failed), `roster_edit.py --self-test` (257, 0 failed), `dev/audit/harnesses/roster_queue_stale_lint.py` (stale, cascade, follow PASS), mutant M4 re-applied by hand (cascade FAIL, killed), `tools/pr/prepr.sh` rc=0.

Resolution delta (review only these): in `_run_op`, the refusal report line is `refusal_tail(out)` (main's P435) followed by the PR's `worktree remove --force` of the edit worktree; `refresh_lint` (PR) and `refusal_tail` (main) both sit between `run_batch` and `_run_op`, kept verbatim. Main's P417 batch changes merged without conflict. tests/closures.json resolved by its driver.

## Mutation proof

Mutants are the reviewer's seven (verdict/3337 evidence/mutants_src), re-applied as the same one-line edits to this head's roster_queue.py. Harness: `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/roster_queue_stale_lint.py <mutant>`; self-test: the mutant copied over tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py, `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py --self-test`, the file restored by copy (cmp-checked).

| mutant | edit | harness | self-test (56 checks) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | `return ""` at the top of refresh_lint | stale, cascade, follow FAIL | 3 failed: missing clone refused; checkout-fails clone refused; unrefreshed lint clone reported | killed |
| M2 | detach at `origin/main` (the clone's own ref) | stale, cascade, follow FAIL | 0 failed | killed (harness) |

| M5 | `if c.returncode != 0 or head != sha:` -> `if False:` | PASS | 2 failed: "refresh_lint: a clone whose checkout fails is refused, not passed"; "run: an unrefreshed lint clone is reported by name and the editor never runs" | killed (self-test) |
| M6 | `if err:` in _run_op -> `if False:` | PASS | 1 failed: "run: an unrefreshed lint clone is reported by name and the editor never runs" (got a pushed line) | killed (self-test) |
| M7 | drop the lint clone's fallback `fetch origin main` | follow FAIL | 0 failed | killed (harness) |

Harness at base (the merge base 8a4974d15's pre-fix roster_queue.py) and at head:

```

```

- The reviewer's null variant (verdict/3337 evidence/variants_src/null_fresh.py: the lint clone's fetch works and is fresh, no refusal) prints `RESULT: PASS` against the base roster_queue.py and against this head's: a healthy drain was never refused, so the checks read the defect, not the setup.

- In `cascade`, op1's refusal is still reported (`refused rc=4`) at head: the fix removes the stranded worktree, it does not hide the refusal.

- Mutation table, 7 of 7 killed (rule: a mutant is killed when the harness prints `RESULT: FAIL` or the self-test reports at least one failed check): the commands in `## Mutation proof`, mutants from verdict/3337 evidence/mutants_src.
