Null control against main: `git diff 17e621f08 HEAD -- tests/closures.json` is the one inert entry for the harness, which the previous round already recorded, and this round's commit (`git diff --stat d0db3e30b 516f48443`) touches only the harness and roster_queue.py, both already classified, so the skipped step has nothing new to read.
- 1327 report lines, 786 pushed, 172 no-origin-ref cascade, 2 stale-worktree, 30 lint TOTAL refusals: counted from the sweep runner's roster-rep.txt (outside the tree); `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/roster_queue_stale_lint.py` reproduces the two mechanisms, not the counts.

## Red checks

No defect in this diff; no cheaper detector is owed. R10-HOTFIX-AUTHOR-EMAIL (triage s6-batch133 P408, owner hotfix tier, 2026-11-07). Commits reached main under placeholder or unnumbered author and committer emails (`seat@`, `hpo-fixer@`, `noreply@users.noreply.github.com`, `t@t`, `fixer@invalid`), which GitHub credits to unrelated accounts. History is not rewritten; this refuses the bad shapes on every commit a push newly publishes. `ref_privacy.py`'s guard now refuses `unnumbered-email` for any author or committer email outside this grammar: `<digits>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com` (the seat identity `70032254+tvofi@...` included), `[<digits>+]<name>[bot]@users.noreply.github.com`, `noreply@github.com` as committer only, and an adopted outside contributor's own address named per adoption by `--adopt-email ADDR` (author only). The refusal prints the exact pin (`-c user.name=tvofi -c user.email=70032254+tvofi@...`, `--author`, or the per-worktree `git config --worktree user.email` form) so a refused seat can self-correct. The fixture identity in `tests/throwaway_git.{py,sh}` moves from `t@t` to `1+t@users.noreply.github.com` so guarded self-tests keep passing. Writers of `seat@` and `hpo-fixer@`: none are in the tree (cloud-setup.sh, cloud_dispatch.py, update_pr.sh, open_pr.sh and delivery_row.sh already pin the numbered seat identity); they are local seats' own launch identities, which the orchestrator pins outside the tree.

## Head

`91822074e315708caca295154f33babf20034bd1` merges main `ba6fd7e` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`8978e0437c46a10207dd682057665a214453e083` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

Code head: `84bd4fb40e87530ea6b27ba2ec0d97f4d235fb00`, on `45339147f9fbeffb50df4cbcf047ac248b94efb4`. Code from the first round is unchanged (`ref_privacy.py`, `tests/throwaway_git.*`).

The assertion now builds its expected prefix from `throwaway_git.IDENTITY`, the fixture's one definition (alternatives: a second literal `1+t@users...` in plan_audit, which recurs at the next identity change; or dropping the assertion, which loses the check that the harness identity beats the box's). `delivery_row.sh`'s stale comment now names `IDENTITY` and no address. ## Mutation proof

Three mutants of `tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py`, each run through `python3 tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py --self-test` (baseline 124 checks, 0 failed):
- `email_shape` returns `[]` (admits everything): 7 arms fail, among them "every placeholder or unnumbered form is refused" and both guard-CLI arms.

At the head: the seat identity, `476059+Bankaifan@users.noreply.github.com`, `41898282+github-actions[bot]@...`, `hpo-author[bot]@users.noreply.github.com` and `331381602+hpo-author[bot]@...` pass; `noreply@github.com` passes as committer only; a `Co-authored-by:` trailer naming `476059+Bankaifan@users.noreply.github.com` and one naming `seat@users.noreply.github.com` is not judged (messages are not email-judged); the numbered fixture identity passes the guard CLI end to end.

- `governance / instrument-self-tests` (job 128917294764, `plan_audit self-test: 27 checks, 1 failed`): red at 45339147f, answered here. Cheaper detector: the census `git grep -nIE '(^|[^[:alnum:]_.+-])t@t([^[:alnum:]]|$)' -- . merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-CI-SELFTEST-SCOPE (owner lever 3, tvofi 2026-11-07, #201 comment 6707834331, which also approves the policy widening). On a pull request, each gated step of governance.yml's `instrument-self-tests` now runs only when the diff reaches that step's MEASURED read set; every other event runs every step, and a push to main runs each under `strace` and refuses a table that misses what it read. Built on R10-HOTFIX-SELFTEST-TIMEOUT's sharded form (the five detached self-tests), not re-sharded.

What changed:

- `tools/ci/selftest_scope.py` (new): parses the job's steps without a YAML library, holds the selection rule, folds traces into the table, runs the drift check (`check`), the PR-side static check (`static`), the local recorder (`record [--step ID]`) and its own `--self-test`. The rule, every fail-closed arm and the blind spots are its docstring.
- `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json` (new, measured): per gated step its `files`, `probes`, `dirs`, `index`, `objects`, `git` and `run_sha`. A directory whose every tracked file a step read is written `D/**`. Recorded on Linux with strace: two full runs at this branch, then `verdict-bus` re-recorded alone (see Figures).
- `tools/ci/selftest_step.sh` (new): the job's `defaults.run.shell`. With `SELFTEST_TRACE` empty it runs `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}`, the runner's default; with it set it runs the step under `strace -f --seccomp-bpf -e trace=%file`, and `--as NAME` does the same for one detached self-test (the launcher's `bg_run`).
- `tools/ci/prelude.py`: a `selftests` output, `all` unless the event is `pull_request`, else `selftest_scope.selection(base sha, head sha)`. The prelude runs the BASE copy of `tools/ci/*.py`, so a pull request cannot choose its own scope. On THIS pull request the base prelude has no such output, the input arrives empty, and empty means every step.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: passes `selftests` from the prelude to the governance call.
- `.github/workflows/governance.yml`: the `selftests` input; a `scope` step that turns it into one `steps.scope.outputs.<id>` per chosen step; an `id:` and an `if:` reading its own output on each of the 102 gated steps (`!cancelled()` and `always()` kept where they were); the launcher starts a detached self-test only when its waiter step is chosen (`sel`); `bg_unread` passes with nothing started; on a push, `strace` is installed, every step is traced, `drift` refuses a table missing a read and uploads the run's measurement as the `selftest-closures` artifact; the push timeout is 60 minutes (30 otherwise).
- `dev/governance/rules/gate-scoping.md` (policy, + regenerated `.claude/rules/` and `.cursor/rules/` copies by `node tools/policy/rules_sync.mjs`): one line saying the self-test steps are scoped too and where the rule and re-record live. Here, a pull request that ADDS a file under tools/ that no step recorded by its exact path runs every step (FULL): a new file has no recorded closure, and a `D/**` entry is no record of a file D did not hold yet. Main's traced run then measures it. A file added anywhere else selects the steps that listed its directory, probed its path or read the git index.

How a step is chosen. A step runs when a changed path is in its `files` (or under one of its `D/**`), or when the step opened the git object store through a git subcommand other than the worktree readers in `WORKTREE_GIT`, because then it read committed content the trace cannot name. An added or deleted path also selects a step that probed it, that listed a directory above it, or that read the index. Gate files force FULL: governance.yml, ci.yml, prelude.py, the table, the scope module and the wrapper. So does an unreadable table, a stale one (its step set or a `run_sha` differs from the workflow's), an empty diff, and an unknown step id at the `scope` step.

merges.body:
R10-PARTLOAD-RESIDUE: the three measure-first items #3182 left. Each was measured at this group's merge base. Repair round 3 adds carry 2's fourth seam, the wood advisor's pump-heat price, which is measured and **fixed in production** (`wood_fuel.py`, plus the one `partload_at` line in `coordinator.py`). Repair round 4 re-cuts that fix's signature only: `build_wood_fuel_view` now takes the per-step COP series instead of an eleventh parameter, so `params_over_10` is back at main's 6 (`## Repair round 4`). The diff also lands the harness that re-derives the CPU figures and carry 2's stated-rate figures (`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_partload_residue.py`), plus its `INERT` classification. The linear-valuation bounds come from `r10_partload_pricing.py`, the finder's harness, which is already in the tree. Carries are numbered 1 to 3 in roster order, so the brief's carry 0, 1 and 2 are carries 1, 2 and 3 here.

- **Carry 1, the live buffer store's CPU.** A 750 L store costs about 1.9x per solve. One lever at a time: 1.87x on the seeded spread days, 1.93x on the flat null, and 1.15x for the price day alone. The worst solve is 1.83 s here, about 12 s scaled to Pi class. That is 2 % of the shortest optimisation interval the options flow accepts (10 min). The 272 s owner-box outlier did not reproduce in 80 seeded solves, and no harness in the tree re-derives it. **Refused:** no bound or warm start is earned at these numbers.
- **Carry 2, linear valuations under a convex cost.** The hot-water LP's secant error is at most 0.27 currency/day against a hot-water cost of about 7 to 8 per day (3.8 %).
  - This round states a refill rate for the terminal and deferred figures: the plan's own energy-weighted mean draw, `P_r`. At that rate their errors are at most 3.71 and 0.79 per horizon (flat day), against bounds of 4.37 and 2.14 at max power. The zero-derate null reads exactly 0 at both rates.
  - **Not immaterial at the stated rate**, so this measurement does not settle the carry. Whether to segment the hot-water LP and derate the terminal and deferred refill is a production decision on `_plan_dhw_min_cost`, `_terminal_cost` and `_deferred_energy_cost`.
  - The fourth seam, the wood advisor (`wood_fuel` `cheaper_steps` and `_scan_wood_night`), priced pump heat at `price / compute_cop(outdoor)` with no draw. At d = 0.112 that under-prices pump heat by up to 12.6 % (`d / (1 - d)`), and the advisor counted up to 19 (spread) and 58 (flat) fewer wood-cheaper steps than at the derated price. **Fixed here:** each step's COP is multiplied by `partload_factor` at the plan's own total draw (`## Repair round 3`). At the default derate 0 every factor is exactly 1.0, so the view is unchanged.
  - `_terminal_cost`'s docstring binds its refill pricing to the savings settle-up "exactly as `_deferred_energy_cost` prices it", so the decision cannot be taken in one of them alone. It is carried, with its control and these figures, to the live group that owns the savings settle-up's stored-heat term on `optimizer.py`: R10-SAV-COMFORT (`## Carry for the roster`).
- **Carry 3, Pi CPU of the relaxed start.** The worst clamped solve is 1.96 s and the relaxed pass inside it at most 0.32 s. At the derived Pi-class factor of 6.8x that is about 13.3 s and 2.2 s, against the 600 s budget. The null control holds: the unclamped cells start 0 relaxed runs and spend 0.000 s in the pass. **Refused:** a `maxiter` cap on the relaxed pass is not earned. It would become due only if a clamped solve ran 306x slower than here.


## Head

`f617930aab8052bdea7caa7b4dedc1382c75afee` merges main `c782949` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`6517b1f443af372887dbadd49919a2ab605b66fe` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`5e21a591e7728b8ba4f103dcbc30f6e373371b8b` is this PR's head, the round-5 repair. It is a merge of origin/main 51cd5ec8a42abde3c223f22e9f4a0d5f35f8844a into the prior head 5fca8c7042a0b1b11057b9694a55e9965a07bdf4 (parents in that order), made because origin/main had moved since 5fca8c70's base 16f3d9cc3. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 5fca8c70` reported no conflict; the ledger driver merged `tests/closures.json`'s `inert_reads` as a set. No other commit is added.

- The branch's own three-dot diff from merge base 51cd5ec8a has the same `git patch-id --stable` (f7727f66e6957271c8062dbbaf045e2f43453894) as 5fca8c70's own diff from 16f3d9cc3. A different patch would have printed a different id.
- `git diff --quiet 5fca8c70 HEAD` passes on `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/{coordinator,wood_fuel,thermal_model,optimizer}.py`, `tests/wood_advisor.py`, `tests/profiles.py` and the four `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_*` harnesses the figures read; the only `custom_components` paths main moved are `manifest.json` and the card JS (the stamp). So every figure below, taken at a3a54793c (tree-identical to 17e891bf0) or earlier as each states, holds at this head for the branch's own code; none was re-taken.
- `tools/pr/prepr.sh` was re-run at this head (`## Figures`, **Gate**).

## Repair round 5

The answer to the round-5 verdict at 5fca8c70 (`ci-red`). The verdict owes no code change: the head's units were all green and the two red `gate` jobs were deferrals to an edit run. Its one body finding was that `## Red checks` did not name 5fca8c70's reds; they are now named there. Carry: dismissed: fixed in this body
- origin/main had moved (16f3d9cc3 -> 51cd5ec8a), so the brief's merge-and-rerun applies, and the new head gets fresh code-run gates. Carry: dismissed: fixed in this diff

## Repair round 4

The answer to round 3's three reds at 0940e9aae (`## Red checks`), in one commit, a3a54793c.

- **`build_wood_fuel_view` had eleven parameters.** It took `outdoor`, `cop_at` and the new `partload` only to build one per-step COP series. It now takes that series, `cops`. `wood_fuel_from_parts` builds it as `_derated(_cops(outdoor, compute_cop), _plan_partload(...))`, and `_attach_night_advice` reads the same series. The view goes from 11 parameters to 8 keyword ones plus `config` (9), and `_attach_night_advice` from 10 to 8. No budget is raised and no `PARAMS_OVER_10_LEFT` row is added. Carry: dismissed: fixed in this diff
  - The night scan's flat-COP fallback now reads `cops` instead of `outdoor`. The two are empty together: `_derated` keeps the length of its COP list, which is the length of `outdoor`.
  - Callers updated: two in `tests/wood_advisor.py` and three in `tests/features.py`, each `outdoor=[x] * n, cop_at=lambda _t: c` becoming `cops=[c] * n`. Each fed a constant COP, so each test reads the same numbers as before. The `wood_fuel_from_parts` tests are unchanged.
  - `dev/audit/rounds/round9/D12/leads/l2_wood_currency.py` calls `build_wood_fuel_view` with `space_kw` and `dhw_kw`, which the function has not taken at main either. It is a round-9 lead record, so it is left as it was.
- **The pins `mutation-autofix` wrote at 9211bed5a are kept.** The two pinned lines (`_derated`'s return and `_plan_partload`'s `result is None or partload_at is None` guard) are unchanged in text, now at lines 541 and 660. Each mutant was applied by hand at a3a54793c and still fails `tests/wood_advisor.py` (`TypeError` from a `None` list and from a `None` callable). Carry: dismissed: fixed in this diff
- **Architecture score.** Before, at 9211bed5a: `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff 73365699a HEAD` printed `Architecture score: dS -0.1926 WORSENS (inadmissible: params_over_10 6 -> 7)`, and `tests/arch_score_head.py` printed `1 of 18 ARCHITECTURE SCORE HEAD CHECKS FAILED`. After, at a3a54793c: `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL` and `ALL 18 ARCHITECTURE SCORE HEAD CHECKS PASSED`. Carry: dismissed: fixed in this diff

Architecture score: dS +0.0000

## Repair round 3

The answer to the fix review's verdict at 8bef9bc86, one finding at a time.

- **Block: the wood advisor's pump-heat price was neither measured nor dispositioned.** Measured in 4555ba0c8, fixed in 26fcbc7eb (pins completed in 8594a61c5 and 2f25b3893).
  - Measured with `r10_partload_residue.py refill`'s new wood arm. It uses the same 16 installs x 2 price days x 2 derates and the same solves as the other three seams, and has the zero-derate null.
  - The production `cheaper_hour_count` and `_scan_wood_night` are each fed two COP lists. The first is the advisor's own `compute_cop`. The second is that COP derated at each running step's published draw.
  - Wood prices: 41 points spanning each cell's band, from its lowest linear to its highest derated pump-heat price.
  - At d = 0.112:
    - The pump-heat price error is up to 0.037629 (spread) and 0.061299 (flat) currency/kWh, relative 0.12613 = 0.112 / 0.888.
    - The cheaper-count shortfall is up to 19 steps (spread, on all 16 cells) and 58 (flat, 14 cells).
    - The night pick changes at 67 and 560 of 656 grid prices.
  - At d = 0 every wood figure reads 0.
  - This is not immaterial, and unlike the other three seams it binds no savings settle-up, so it is fixed rather than carried.
  - The fix: `wood_fuel_from_parts` builds the per-step factors with `_plan_partload`, `partload_factor` at space plus hot-water draw. `_derated` multiplies the COPs by them. Since round 4, `wood_fuel_from_parts` does this and passes the series to `build_wood_fuel_view` as `cops`.
  - `thermal_model` imports `wood_fuel`, so `partload_factor` is passed in by the coordinator (`partload_at`), as `compute_cop` is. A late import would add an import cycle, which `tests/structure.py` refuses.
  - After the fix, the harness's production comparison reads count residual 0 and night picks off 0 on every row. At the merge base the same harness reads 19/67 (spread) and 58/560 (flat) (`## Figures`). Carry: dismissed: fixed in this diff
- **Follow-up: `refill` had no positive control.** Added in 4555ba0c8. `refill` now exits 1 when a d > 0 price day's terminal, deferred or wood-price maximum is 0. Mutant `k_r = 0.0` now prints `positive (d>0) price days with a zero maximum 2` and exits 1 (`## Null control`). Carry: dismissed: fixed in this diff
- **Residual: carry 1's 272 s outlier.** Kept as stated. It is refused on non-reproduction in 80 seeded solves, on the synthetic owner shape alone, and it re-opens only from a diagnostics bundle (D15). Carry: dismissed: no in-tree input reproduces it; re-opens only from a diagnostics bundle (D15), which this group does not hold

## Mutation proof

Re-executed at a3a54793c, because round 4 changes where the derate is applied. Each fix line was mutated alone in the worktree, the pinning checks were run, and the line was restored. The checks: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests python3 tests/wood_advisor.py`, and the `tests/features.py` wood block through `python3 tools/audit/seat/features_block.py --prelude "from heatpump_optimizer.coordinator import HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator" --prelude "from harness import FakeEntry, FakeHass" --prelude "NOW = datetime(2026, 2, 1, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)" "from heatpump_optimizer.wood_fuel import (" "_wf_soc_kwargs = dict("`. Baseline: both exit 0 (25 and 31 checks).

| mutant | failing checks |
|---|---|
| M1 `coordinator.py` drops `partload_at=partload_factor` | features: "the published wood advisor prices a max-power step's pump heat at the derated COP (cheaper at d = 0.1, not at d = 0; R10-PARTLOAD-RESIDUE)" |
| M2 `_plan_partload`'s guard always returns the empty list | wood_advisor: "the wood advisor prices pump heat at the derated COP of the plan's own draw ...", "the derate reads only what the plan publishes ..." and "the night advice prices pump heat at the derated COP ..."; features: the check above |
| M3 `_derated` drops the factor (`c` for `c * f`) | the same four |
| M4 the night scan ignores `cops` and always reads the flat COP 3 | wood_advisor: "the night advice prices pump heat at the derated COP ..." |
| M5 `wood_fuel_from_parts` derates by an empty factor list | the three wood_advisor checks of M2, and the features check |
| M6 the hot-water draw is dropped from the total | the three wood_advisor checks of M2 |

The failing test came first in round 3. Its first version, run against the unfixed `wood_fuel.py`, read `[0, 0, 0]` where `[30, 0, 0]` was expected. The final checks pass `partload_at`, which the unfixed `wood_fuel_from_parts` does not accept, so at the merge base they raise `TypeError`.

Diff mutants (`prepr.sh` step 6d', owner ruling 2026-11-07): `MUTANT_CMD` was `bash <script>`, with `MUTANT_MAX=40`. The script, a short file in this seat's scratch directory, runs `tests/wood_advisor.py`, then the features wood block above, and exits non-zero on the first failure.
- Standalone at a3a54793c: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff 73365699a...HEAD --cmd "bash <script>" --max-mutants 40 --report-only` listed 7 mutants (`--list`), took 12 s wall, printed no `SURVIVED` line and exited 0. Survivor count: 0.
- `prepr.sh`'s own step: see `## Figures`, **Gate**.

## Unpinned sites

none: the two sites this diff added (`_derated`'s RETURN_DEL and `_plan_partload`'s GUARD_OFF, numbered 546 and 666 at 0940e9aae and 541 and 660 now) were pinned by `mutation-autofix` at 9211bed5a, killed by `tests/wood_advisor.py`. Those ledger files are kept, and both mutants still fail `tests/wood_advisor.py` at a3a54793c (`## Repair round 4`).

## Null control

- Carry 1: the flat price day, with no cheap window to store for. The 750 L store still costs 1.93x there, so its cost is per-solve model work, not arbitrage search. The no-buffer arm separates the price lever: 0.455 s flat against 0.522 s spread, p50.
- Carry 2: zero derate.
  - `r10_partload_pricing.py` prints `null rows not zero 0`.
  - `r10_partload_residue.py refill`, at 2f25b3893, at a3a54793c and at the merge base, prints `null rows not zero 0`. Its d = 0 rows read `0.000000` for the terminal, deferred and wood-price errors, a count shortfall of 0, 0 night picks changed, and production residual 0.
- Positive controls on `refill`, each on a mutated copy of the harness at 4555ba0c8 (outputs in this seat's evidence):
  - `k_r = 0.0`: `positive (d>0) price days with a zero maximum 2`, exit 1.
  - The wood derate dropped (`true = lin`): the same line, `2`, exit 1.
  - The null arm perturbed (factor - 1e-9): `null rows not zero 32`, exit 1.
- The production comparison is its own control. At the merge base it reads the defect (count residual 19 and 58, night picks off 67 and 560). At 2f25b3893 and at a3a54793c it reads 0 on all four rows. At d = 0 it reads 0 at both ends.
- The fix's own null is `tests/wood_advisor.py` and the features check at derate 0: 0 cheaper steps, and no night advice.
- Carry 3: the non-relaxed path, on the 32 unclamped cells. They show 0 relaxed runs and a maximum of 0.000 s inside the pass.

## Figures


All CPU times are `time.process_time` of one process pinned to one core (`taskset -c N`), with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1`.
- Host: x86_64, `Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.30GHz`, family 6, model 173 (Granite Rapids class), Python 3.14.7, numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1.
- The budget is `config_flow`'s `CONF_OPTIMIZATION_INTERVAL` slider minimum, 10 min = 600 s; the default interval is 30 min.

**Carry 3, relaxed pass.** Command: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests taskset -c 0 python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_partload_residue.py relaxed`.
- It prints `clamped solves 32: solve_s p50 0.466 max 1.961; relaxed_pass_s p50 0.105 max 0.318; worst solve share of budget 0.00327` and `null (unclamped) cells with a relaxed run 0`, exit 0.
- Rule: 16 installs (`r10_setpoint_boost.CELLS`) x 2 price days x 2 derates (0 and the central plant's 0.112), timing only the cells whose levels ship clamped.
- The per-cell delta figures (p50 +0.150 s and maximum +0.667 s clamped; -0.082 to +0.056 s unclamped) are the median, minimum and maximum of the `delta_s` field over the printed per-cell lines, grouped by `clamped`.

**Carry 1, buffer store.** Command: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests taskset -c 1 python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_partload_residue.py buffer 20`. Over 20 seeded solves per arm (seed 2500, `r10_buffer_store.solve`'s owner shape) it prints:

merges.body:
Owner ruling (tvofi, 2026-11-07): a red on a check outside the required set needs no `## Red checks` answer anywhere. The required set is the one the merge train judges: `merge_train.py`'s new `judged(gating_names(required(pr_head=True)))`, read live from `main-protect-checks` and printed by the new `merge_train.py owed-reds`. It is read through that one owner and never copied. A red on a required check still owes its answer, as before.

Where it applies:
- **pr-body red check** (`tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs` `checkPrBody`). When a red goes unnamed, it reads the set lazily: through `owed-reds`, or from `--required-file` when a caller already holds it. `redOwed` counts a red as owed when its name is in the set, when it is the job half of a set name (prepr's offline `--red budget-raise-gate` / `--red mutation` predictions), or when it is a code-scanning alert. If the set cannot be read, every red is owed under the rule as it stood, MAIN_STATE_REPORTERS' exemption included (fail closed). Earlier-head reds (the red-history walk) feed the same filter.
- **review packet** (`tools/audit/seat/review_packet.py` `unanswered_reds`). It delegates to policy_lint as before (P282) and gains an optional `required` argument, so the self-test reads no ruleset. This covers the red-unanswered arm, cancelled runs included, and the ancestry reds that policy_lint's `--base`/`--head` walk adds.
- **reviewer's rule text**. `defect-root-cause.md` Enforcement names the boundary once, and `fix-review.md` step 11 cites it. The generated `.claude/rules` and `.cursor/rules` copies are regenerated by `rules_sync.mjs`.
- `record_row.py`'s body-check self-test, and prepr.sh's self-test through `body_check`'s new `PREPR_REQUIRED_FILE`, pass an empty required file, so their reporter arms still drive the pre-ruling rule without a ruleset read. A third prepr arm gives a set and pins that `delivery-status` is then owed nothing.

The two policy files (`dev/governance/rules/defect-root-cause.md` and `dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md`) need the owner's approving review at merge.

Fix review round 1 (blocked at d7b25eca, `architecture-unsound`): the design now matches the PR's claim that the set is read through its owner and never copied. In CI the owner is now main's copy.
- **pr-contract runs no pull-request program, spawned ones included.** `.github/workflows/pr-contract.yml`'s base restore now also lists `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py`, the `gh_read.py` it imports and `tools/policy/fixtures/required-contexts.json` it reads. The pin is a new rule in `tests/entities.py` (`_pcr_unrestored`). For every `spawnSync('python3', [path.join(ROOT|root|HERE, ...)])` in `policy_lint.mjs`, it walks the spawned file's local closure: column-0 `import X` with X.py beside it, and column-0 `NAME = ROOT / "path"` reads. Each file in that closure must match a pr-contract restore pathspec.
- **The fail-closed rc check is driven on its live path.** `requiredFromTrain(root)` takes the tree whose `merge_train.py` answers, and the `--pr-body` thunk body is now `requiredSet(requiredFile, notes, root)`. policy_lint's acceptance runs the real chain (`checkPrBody` -> `requiredSet` -> `requiredFromTrain` -> `spawnSync`) against a stub tree whose `merge_train.py` exits 2 with `REFUSE proof: HTTP 403`, and asserts that every red is owed and that the skip note names the REFUSE line.

Code repair round 2. The body-push seat found two reds this diff causes. Both are repaired in code:
- **`tests / closures` UNDER-SCOPED** -> be2cfbef5. `tests/entities.py`'s `_pcr_unrestored` rule reads the source of every program policy_lint.mjs spawns, `tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py` among them, and no measured closure listed it. The closure was re-recorded with `derive_closures.sh --single tests/entities.py` on this Linux box, and the file moves from the `tools/policy/` INERT prefix to `INERT_EXCEPT`.
- **CodeQL alert 52, `js/insecure-temporary-file`** -> ef082a130 (`policy_lint.mjs`, the named-reds null control in the self-test). The body file had a pid-derived name in the shared tmpdir. It now sits inside a `fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'prbody-named-'))` directory, which a `finally` removes. A new self-test pin scans policy_lint.mjs's own source and refuses any `path.join(os.tmpdir(), ...)` outside `mkdtempSync`.

## Approval

Pending: this diff changes `dev/governance/rules/defect-root-cause.md` and `dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md` (policy) on the owner's ruling of 2026-11-07, quoted above; it merges only on tvofi's approving review at its head.

On merge (the orchestrator's): the brief says this subsumes R10-BODY-CONTRACT's carry from triage batch 133 (proposal P406, recorded at 0ef02f3cab9eccf6ed8823fa46039c2d561f9096), and that carry should then be marked moved here. Under a readable required set neither main-graded reporter is required, so the carry's per-reporter REPORTER_INPUTS split matters only on the fail-closed path. This seat writes no roster ref, so the roster op is left for the merge.

## Head

`69e12ea4107e51f93a896867bf5384522c0fa929` merges main `c782949` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

c391823f01f996bb4324815e31424657cd311a20, the PR head: a merge of the handoff tip be2cfbef52ecc71b9dcb5c0ca6f8da6f025151a0 into the branch's 6ef8ac12236f3ff258f19180334cbe216962dfd3. `git rev-parse c391823f0^{tree} be2cfbef5^{tree}` prints one tree (6438dcf0e4e7b1f5d353fc97282380a430145e71) twice, so every figure below that names be2cfbef5 was measured on the tree this head holds.

`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main c391823f0` exits 0 against origin/main 8a4cf2618 (2026-11-08 15:09 +01:00; it prints `LEDGER-MERGE: resolved tests/closures.json`, the merge driver's own resolution, no conflict), so main is not merged (owner ruling 2026-11-07). Figures from earlier rounds are stated at the heads they name. Round 2's figures are at be2cfbef52ecc71b9dcb5c0ca6f8da6f025151a0.

## Review findings answered

1. **The required set's owner is read from the change under check** -> fixed in b8141a7ce, with the rule's pattern corrected in 3b23a50da and 3b4dec95f.
   - pr-contract now restores the owner and its closure from the base.
   - `tests/entities.py` pins the class (`_pcr_unrestored`), with a null control: each of the three pathspecs removed in turn is refused on exactly that file.
   - The reviewer's drive was reproduced. Both drives use a tree whose `merge_train.py` alone is edited so `owed-reds` prints `bogus / name`; the body is silent on `tests / typing`, `tests / fast (3.14)` and `gate`. Results are under Figures, "Reviewer's drive".
2. **Fail-closed on an unreadable set was unpinned on its live path** -> fixed in d45cdb79f. The reviewer's mutant now fails policy_lint's acceptance (Mutation proof).
   - **How the `.mjs` lines are mutation-covered.** `mutant_run.py --diff` mutates added Python lines only, and its `--list` at this head names no `.mjs` and no `tests/` line. So every new `.mjs` line and every new `tests/entities.py` line is covered by the hand-applied mutants under Mutation proof, each run against its own check.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant was applied in the working tree at 3b23a50da (and the pathspec mutant again at 3b4dec95f), run, and then restored. Restoration was checked with `git status --short` (clean).

- **policy_lint.mjs, the reviewer's mutant.** `if (r.status !== 0 || !names.length)` became `if (!names.length)` in `requiredFromTrain`.
  - `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`: rc=1, `FIXTURE VACUOUS: an owed-reds that exits 2 with a REFUSE line owed [] (notes []), not every red; a refused read must leave every red owed`.
- **policy_lint.mjs, the root ignored.** `requiredSet`'s `else got = requiredFromTrain(root)` became `requiredFromTrain()`.
  - rc=1, `FIXTURE VACUOUS: an owed-reds that exits 2 with a REFUSE line owed ["tests / fast (3.14)"] ...`: the live owner answered instead of the stub.
- **pr-contract.yml, each new pathspec deleted in turn** (merge_train.py, gh_read.py, required-contexts.json). The check was the `_PCR` block run alone with entities.py's own `_twp_` helpers. That harness is a scratch exec of entities.py's source, shown under Figures.
  - All three: rc=1. `every python3 program policy_lint.mjs spawns ... is restored from the base by pr-contract` FAILs, naming the dropped file as not restored.
- **pr-contract.yml as it stood at the reviewed head d7b25eca** (the control): rc=1 on the same check.
- **entities.py, the closure following no import** (the import arm emptied): rc=1, gh_read.py missing from the closure.
- **entities.py, the closure following no ROOT read** (the read arm dropped): rc=1, required-contexts.json missing from the closure.
- **The earlier body's mutant** (`return true` first in `redOwed`) and its kills are unchanged from round 1, which the reviewer confirmed.

- **Round 2, policy_lint.mjs, the temp file in the shared tmpdir again.** At ef082a130, `fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'prbody-named-'))` became ``path.join(os.tmpdir(), `prbody-named-${process.pid}`); fs.mkdirSync(namedDir, { recursive: true })``.
  - `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --self-test`: rc=1, `FIXTURE VACUOUS: line(s) 4525 join a name onto the shared tmpdir outside mkdtempSync; a temporary file goes inside a private mkdtempSync directory`. Restored from a copy; the rerun gives rc=0.
- **Round 2, closures.** The control is the PR head's `tests/closures.json`: CI's `tests / closures` reported UNDER-SCOPED at 6ef8ac122 for `tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py`. At be2cfbef5, `python3 tests/closure.py check --in-dir <recording> --partial` gives rc=0, `committed closures cover every file this run touched`.

## Null control

- **The stub tree's other arm.** The same stub `merge_train.py`, exiting 0 and printing `tests / fast (3.14)`, owes exactly `tests / fast (3.14)` and adds no skip note. This proves the stub answered, not a fallback.
- **The entities rule's own null.** pr-contract with one pathspec removed is refused on that file and no other, and `tools/release/stamp.py`, which policy_lint only reads as text (`fs.readFileSync`), is not in the closure.
- **The pattern's non-vacuity term caught a real miss.** At d45cdb79f the pattern was ROOT-only and missed `path.join(root, ...)`. It read an empty closure and the check refused (entities run at d45cdb79f: `5 of 2665 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`, the two `_PCR` checks among them). 3b23a50da fixed the pattern. 3b4dec95f then split the path segments on commas, because agreement.mjs refused the quoted-token regex as a grammar duplicated with `tools/audit/merge_fastpath.py`.
- **The drive's control** is the reviewed head's pr-contract.yml (Figures).
- The round-1 null controls hold unchanged at this head: a body naming every red is owed nothing and never reads the set, and an unreadable set leaves every red owed.
- **Round 2, the scan's own null.** On the unmodified tree, the scan finds three `os.tmpdir()` joins, all inside `mkdtempSync` (the raise, stub and window-cache fixtures), and the pin is ok. If it finds no site at all, it refuses with `no os.tmpdir() site found`, so a scan that read nothing cannot pass.

## Figures

- **Reviewer's drive.** Instrument: `drive.sh <commit>`, a scratch script. For each run it:
  1. checks out a detached worktree at HEAD;
  2. edits only `merge_train.py`, so that `owed-reds` prints `bogus / name` and exits 0;
  3. extracts the `Restore the check source from the base commit` step's `run:` from `<commit>`'s pr-contract.yml, and runs it with `PINNED=HEAD`, standing in for the base;
  4. runs `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --pr-body tools/policy/fixtures/policy-rot/prepr/unnamed-red.md --head 0x40 --red 'tests / typing' --red 'tests / fast (3.14)' --red gate`.

  Results:
  - With pr-contract.yml at d7b25eca (control): `Updated 0 paths`, merge_train.py is still the PR copy, `PR-BODY: 0 error(s)`. The defect is reproduced.
  - With pr-contract.yml at the fix head: `Updated 1 path`, merge_train.py is the base copy, and `PR-BODY: 3 error(s)`, one per required red, naming `tests / typing`, `tests / fast (3.14)` and `gate`.
  - Before the restore, both trees give `PR-BODY: 0 error(s)`.
- **The entities rule at this head.** It enumerates `spawned=['tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py', 'tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py']`. The closure is gh_read.py, merge_train.py, tools/ci/gate.py, tools/ci/ghapi.py, tools/ci/prelude.py, tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py and tools/policy/fixtures/required-contexts.json. Not restored: `[]`. Each seat it returns has a disposition:
  - the three new pathspecs: closed in this diff;
  - `tools/ci/*.py` and `tools/policy/*.py`: already restored before this diff.
- **Mutant harness for the entities block.** It exec's entities.py's source from `import shlex as _twp_shlex` to `_TWP_TRACKED`, plus the `_PCR` block, with `_PRW_TEXTS` read as entities.py reads it. At this head it gives 2 ok, rc=0.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` at 3b4dec95f (and before it at 3b23a50da): `3 of 2665 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`, the same three as round 1: the coverage-cache reuse check, the release-ZIP build and the Pages-workflow probe. Round 1's run at the merge base failed the same three, and none of them reads a file this diff touches. Both new `_PCR` checks are `ok`.
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test`: 509 checks, 0 failed. The count is up from 475 because of the merged main.
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/review_packet.py --self-test`: 72 checks, 0 failed.
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/record_row.py --self-test`: all checks passed.
- `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`: rc=0, `FIXTURE ok: 93 error(s) hold 275 pins across 12 check classes`.
- `node tools/policy/rules_sync.mjs --check`: RULES-SYNC ok.
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED. No budget was touched.
- `node tools/policy/field_coverage.mjs`: `FIELD COVERAGE ok`, `blind=0 dead=0 refused=0`. The extra restored pathspecs leave codeowners_gap's PINNED registry whole.
- `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1 MUTANT_CMD=... MUTANT_MAX=24 bash tools/pr/prepr.sh <this body>` at 3b4dec95f: `PRE-PR: 3b4dec95f05704d3495e3e2d1f32f35667a1412f ... rc=0`, with `pr-body: PR-BODY: 0 error(s)` and `agreement lane` ok.
  - An earlier run at 3b23a50da was refused by the agreement lane: `UNREGISTERED "'([^']+)'" in tests/entities.py, tools/audit/merge_fastpath.py`. 3b4dec95f answers it.
- **Diff mutants.** The run was `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff 8aec35435...HEAD --in-place --report-only --max-mutants 0 --cmd "bash -c 'python3 tools/audit/seat/review_packet.py --self-test && python3 tools/audit/seat/record_row.py --self-test && python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test'"` at 3b4dec95f.
  - Result: rc=0, wall 1144 s, 0 SURVIVED. Diff mode prints only survivor lines, and its baseline passed (no `BASELINE FAILS`).
  - Mutants run: the 24 that `--list` names, 22 in merge_train.py and 2 in review_packet.py. None is in `.mjs` or `tests/`; those lines are covered by Mutation proof.
  - prepr.sh's own diff-mutant step, with the same MUTANT_CMD, prints `BASELINE FAILS`, as in round 1: its `git archive` copy has no `.git`, which these self-tests read. That is why the step's tool was run `--in-place`.

- **Round 2, at be2cfbef52ecc71b9dcb5c0ca6f8da6f025151a0:**
  - `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --self-test`: rc=0, `FIXTURE ok: 93 error(s) hold 276 pins across 12 check classes`. That is one pin more than round 1's 275: the tmpdir scan.
  - `bash tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/entities.py --record-only --out-dir D`, then `python3 tests/closure.py merge --in-dir D --partial --allow-failures`.
    - The recording reached entities.py's summary line, `3 of 2667 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`, the same three as round 1 (coverage-cache reuse, release ZIP, Pages probe), so the read set is the whole run's. The entry's recorded `rc` is therefore 1.
    - The merge added `tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py` to entities.py's closure.
    - It first refused the file as INERT-and-read, which is why the file moves to `INERT_EXCEPT` in `tests/closure.py`.
    - It kept `tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt`, which this run did not touch (over-scoped, safe).
  - `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff <merge-base>`: `MODE: FULL`, because `tests/closure.py changes the gate itself`. CI runs the full suite.
  - `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED. No budget was touched.
  - `MUTANT_CMD="node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --self-test" MUTANT_MAX=24 PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1 bash tools/pr/prepr.sh <this body>` at be2cfbef5: `PRE-PR: be2cfbef52ecc71b9dcb5c0ca6f8da6f025151a0 ... rc=0`, with `pr-body: PR-BODY: 0 error(s)`. Its diff-mutant step printed `BASELINE FAILS` without running a mutant, as in round 1 (the `git archive` copy has no `.git`). Survivors: 0. Wall time: no mutant ran.
  - `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff HEAD~2...HEAD --list` names no site: round 2 adds `.mjs` and closure-list lines only. The tmpdir scan's hand mutant (Mutation proof) covers them.

## Red checks

- `tests / closures` (UNDER-SCOPED at 6ef8ac122): caused by this diff. entities.py's new spawn-closure rule reads `tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py`, and no closure listed it. It is repaired in be2cfbef5 by a `--single` re-recording. The cheaper detector already exists and ran: `tests/closure.py`'s recording, which prepr.sh skips under `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1`. Round 1 ran prepr with that skip, so the detector never saw this diff before CI. No new countermeasure: the standing cost is one Linux recording (about 17 min for entities.py), and CI's closures job caught it within one push.
- `code-scanning alert 52 (js/insecure-temporary-file)`: caused by this diff's self-test fixture in policy_lint.mjs. It is repaired in ef082a130. The cheaper detector is the new self-test pin, which scans policy_lint.mjs for any `path.join(os.tmpdir(), ...)` outside `mkdtempSync`. It runs in every policy_lint self-test (about 30 s, already paid), and its mutant fails it (Mutation proof).

Read at c391823f01f996bb4324815e31424657cd311a20 across all pages of `commits/<sha>/check-runs?filter=all` for each of the 22 commits between origin/main and the head. Every concluded red follows, by check-run name. At the head itself `CodeQL`, `tests / closures` and `tests / closures-autofix` are `success` or `skipped`; only the three `gate` runs and `pr-contract / pr-contract` below are red there.

- `CodeQL` (check run 128665693227, `failure` at 6ef8ac122, 07:37Z, "1 new alert including 1 high severity"): this is code-scanning alert 52 above, `js/insecure-temporary-file`, reported on the PR as a check. It is caused by this diff and repaired in ef082a130; `CodeQL` is `success` at the head (13:11Z). It is not the codeql-bundle infrastructure failure: the three `codeql / Analyze` jobs all concluded `success` at the head, and no `Analyze` job concluded `failure` at any of the 22 commits (they were only `cancelled`, by the supersede below). The cheaper detector and its standing cost are the alert 52 bullet's: the policy_lint self-test pin, about 30 s on every run.
- `tests / closures-autofix` (job 128671575631, `failure` at 6ef8ac122, 08:06Z): caused by this diff, not by the autofix job. The job read the same UNDER-SCOPED recording as `tests / closures` and exited `AUTOFIX: skip-merge-failed -- THE REPAIR DID NOT HAPPEN`, because `closure.py` refused the merge: `files on the INERT list are actually read by tests: tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py`. That file sat under the `tools/policy/` INERT prefix and entities.py's new spawn rule reads it. A refusal of an INERT-and-read file is a human classification (`ci-autofix.md`), which the bot rightly does not guess. be2cfbef5 moves it to `INERT_EXCEPT` and re-records the closure; the job is `skipped` at the head because `tests / closures` is green. Cheaper detector: the same one as the `tests / closures` bullet (the closure recording `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1` skipped in round 1), and it would have refused the same file at prepr, before CI. Standing cost: that one Linux recording, about 17 min for entities.py.
- `gate` (the aggregate verdict, red whenever a required check is) has concluded `failure` four ways. None is a defect of this diff's code, and none has a detector of its own to build:
  - **Edit-run deferral, "still being judged", class R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER.** `gate` 128665715448 (6ef8ac122, 07:38Z, run 42459465906), 128741159031 (13:12Z, run 42483640239) and 128745196734 (13:28Z, run 42484970071) at the head, and 128574152117 and 128574974768 (00:19Z and 00:23Z) at d7b25eca4, each failed `FAIL run(s) [<id>] at this head are still being judged; their gate decides`, which is the gate deferring to a second run on the same head that has not concluded. The diff does not touch `tools/ci/`. The class is owned by the root-cause seat's `dev/audit/rca/r10-gate-busy-defer-2.md` and `R10-RCA-GATE-BUSY-DEFER-2` in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json` (status `proposed`: the stale-pin compare in refresh and the sweep); nothing in this PR is a countermeasure for it. Standing cost: the deferred run's own verdict lands later, so the cost is one wait or one re-run per push.
  - **The aggregate of a required red.** `gate` 128675003243 (6ef8ac122, 08:23Z) printed `tests / closures: failure (this run)` and `pr-contract / pr-contract: failure (this run)`; `gate` 128750588715 (c391823f, 13:51Z) printed `pr-contract / pr-contract: failure (this run)`. Each repeats a red answered by its own bullet, so it owes no second detector.
  - **A held run it could not read.** `gate` 128685147771 (6ef8ac122, 09:08Z) printed `FAIL run 42459569280: unreadable title 'R10-HOTFIX-NONREQUIRED-REDS: hotfix nonrequired reds'` beside `tests / closures: failure (run 42459465906)`. Run 42459569280 is the `CI` run for the `pull_request_review` event at 6ef8ac122, and its API conclusion is `action_required`, a run held for approval. That is not this diff's doing and no detector inside it applies; hpo-runs approves held runs (decision 0011), so the standing cost is one approval per held run. I found no existing check that names this arm, and I file nothing (`CLAUDE.md`, "Fix it; if you cannot, verify it independently; only then file it").
- `pr-contract / pr-contract`, red at 6ef8ac122 (job 128674622902, 08:21Z) and at the head (job 128750387573, 13:50Z): both refused the body, not the code. 1. **The required set's owner is read from the change under check (architecture-unsound).** `pr-contract.yml` restores its check source from the base commit, "so this job runs no pull-request program at all" (#1515, decision 0013). The restored pathspecs cover `tools/policy/*.mjs` but, under `tools/audit/seat/`, only `roster_lib.py`. After this merge, the base's `policy_lint.mjs --pr-body` spawns `python3 <ROOT>/tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py owed-reds` (`requiredFromTrain`, where ROOT is the checkout). That file, together with `gh_read.py` and `tests/fixtures/required-contexts.json` which it imports, is the **pull request's** copy. The step also has `GH_TOKEN` in its environment.
   - Drive (`ev/drive-unpinned-owner.txt`): I left `policy_lint.mjs` as shipped and edited only `merge_train.py` so that `owed-reds` prints one bogus name. A body silent on the reds `tests / typing`, `tests / fast (3.14)` and `gate` then gives `PR-BODY: 0 error(s)`. The required reds go unanswered, which is the opposite of what the ruling keeps.
   - This also contradicts the PR's own claim that the set is "read through that one owner and never copied". In CI the owner read is whatever the diff makes it.
   - Fixes that keep the architecture: pin `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py` and what it imports in pr-contract's restore list, or have the workflow compute the set in a pinned step and pass it as `--required-file`. Either way, add an entities or self-test pin that the program pr-contract runs is base-restored.
2. **Fail-closed on an unreadable set is unpinned on its live path (mutation-vacuous at the brief's FOCUS).**
   - Mutant: `if (r.status !== 0 || !names.length)` becomes `if (!names.length)` in `requiredFromTrain`.

   - Driven (`ev/drive-unreadable.txt`): with a `gh` that fails (403), `owed-reds` prints `REFUSE proof: ...` on stdout and exits non-zero. As shipped, that leaves every red owed (2 errors). Under the mutant, the REFUSE line becomes a one-name "set" and every red, required ones included, is owed nothing (`PR-BODY: 0 error(s)`).
   - Every fail-closed fixture drives a thunk or `--required-file`. None drives `requiredFromTrain` over a non-zero `owed-reds`.
   - The body's diff-mutant run (`mutant_run.py --cmd` over three Python self-tests only) cannot reach `.mjs` lines. So "24 mutants, 0 SURVIVED" does not cover policy_lint's new code. A fixture should run `requiredFromTrain` against a stub `merge_train.py` (or an injectable command) that exits 2 with a REFUSE line, and assert every red is owed.

merges.body:
This is the root-cause seat for R10-RCA-CLOUD-ENTITIES-ENV, run beside the work and never inside it (`dev/governance/roles/root-cause.md`). The analysis is `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-CLOUD-ENTITIES-ENV.md`, registered in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json` `_rca`.

**Defect.** On 2026-11-08 four cloud fixer handoffs stopped at `tools/pr/prepr.sh` step 6b with `failed while being recorded: tests/entities.py (exit 1)`. The diffs were not involved. Three checks failed, identically at main: coverage job reuse, the release ZIP, and the Pages probe.

**Cause.** The cloud environment's `BASH_ENV` sources `cloud-setup.sh`'s profile ahead of every nested bash, `--noprofile --norc` included. Since #3222 that profile has exported `RUNNER_TEMP` unconditionally, to a prefix directory that nothing creates. Each of the three harnesses hands its child bash its own `RUNNER_TEMP` and reads the result back from it. Under the profile the child wrote elsewhere, or failed to write at all.

**Reproduction.** The base profile as `BASH_ENV` gives `probe on workflow: rc=1 enabled=[]` and a ZIP build at rc 128. These match the seat's `BLOCKED.md`. The second shape (`ModuleNotFoundError: homeassistant`, then `paho`) was a diagnostic re-run without `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`.

**Process state.** (d), with an existing barrier whose unit was too narrow. The #2452 arm covered `PATH` only, and the #2835 `_stub_path_env` covered only the `PATH` stand-in helpers. The second shape is (c).

**Countermeasure.** `write_profile` now sets every variable except `PATH` with `${NAME:-default}`. A new `--self-test` arm takes every name the profile exports and requires each to keep a caller's value under `BASH_ENV`. This is the class barrier: the class has three or more instances in round 10. Not built: a prepr replay at the merge base, refused because it costs 868 s per failed recording and would have passed all four broken environments. Owner action: remove `BASH_ENV` from the environment's variables, and re-paste the setup script after merge (RCA section 7).

The two instrument docs are corrected: `cloud_dispatch.py.md` no longer lists `BASH_ENV` as a toolchain variable, and its `env -u BASH_ENV` workaround is conditional on the new profile. No policy, budget, claim file, `VERSION`, manifest or `RELEASE_NOTES.md` is touched. The new file is under `dev/audit/`, an INERT prefix.

## Head

`986e67b17b0c92befdcbaa4e55f84e338dea686e` merges main `c782949` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`9fdf05abf58983d6d36d6bbdead3d8155fea190c` merges the authored code head `1d4c7cda56dc8d4604977c621b0ccc9457818b21` and then merges origin/main `19865e5a86` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`1d4c7cda56dc8d4604977c621b0ccc9457818b21`, the conflict-resolution merge of origin/main `daf8b349fd30cc60786eeca333a426b693aa4c5f` into the verdicted head `2bb81f4215c17cd6640ef2c69d7a1458a7235587` (the PR was DIRTY; resolved by merge, not re-cut). Resolution delta, one conflicted file:

- `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`: both sides added a class entry at the same spot. Union: this branch's `R10-RCA-CLOUD-ENTITIES-ENV` and main's `R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED` are both present (read back as parsed JSON: both keys present), and the file ends with the trailing newline main carries (a second commit, `git diff origin/main -- <file>` is only the 16 added lines of this branch's entry). No other file was touched by the resolution.

`tools/pr/prepr.sh` (PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1) at this head: rc 0, on origin/main `daf8b349fd30` (stamped 2026-11-08, `date -u`).

## Mutation proof

The base `write_profile` is the mutant. The new arm was extracted verbatim and run against it and against the head's (macOS bash 3.2 has no `mapfile`, so the full `--self-test` runs in governance's cloud-setup step).

- On the base profile: `FAIL under BASH_ENV a nested bash keeps every variable its caller set`, with all seven names overwritten (`GIT_AUTHOR_*`, `GIT_COMMITTER_*`, `HPO_TYPING_PYTHON`, `OPENBLAS_CORETYPE`, `RUNNER_TEMP`).
- At head: `ok`.

## Null control

The arm has two controls:

- `control: a nested bash under BASH_ENV runs the profile` reads the profile's own `RUNNER_TEMP`, so the main arm cannot pass because the profile did not load.
- `the profile exports seven names besides PATH` is the never-empty guard.

Without `BASH_ENV` the Pages probe and ZIP harnesses are clean at base. Under the head profile they are clean too (RCA section 2 table).

merges.body:
R10-SAV-COMFORT part 4 (topic r10-sav-comfort-p4). Part of #201.

Behind a valve, the thermostat reference (`HeatPumpOptimizer._apportion_by_steady_demand`) spread the horizon's simulated energy by steady demand with no pump cap. On a 3 kW pump with a -25 C night and 400 W/m2 midday sun it booked 3.678 kW, which is 1.226x the pump. That is carries 10, 13, 15, 16 and 18 (items 0497bde5, e9ced5fc, 7f2fa39d and fc24128d).

Now a step the spread would put past `max_electrical_power` is held at the pump, and its excess goes to the uncapped steps in proportion to their steady demand. Each pass holds only steps not yet held (`~held & (spread > cap)`), so the loop ends within one pass per step whatever the comparison. The energy is kept. The reference is inside the solve's bounds at its source, so `_optimize_space_only` no longer needs to clamp its seed (`np.clip(seed_power, 0.0, p_max)` is removed). This also adds the two-zone comfort-shortfall check owed by carry 11 (item 435eb685).

Alternatives considered:
- Triage the `spread >= cap` mutant as a hang. Rejected: the hang came from the loop's progress resting on a held step re-reading at exactly the pump; holding only new steps removes that, and the mutant is then killable, so a triage would sit on a killable mutant.
- Clamp the booked reference after the spread. Rejected: it destroys energy, and the saving would then be booked against a thermostat that bought less than it needed.
- Keep the seed clip as a second guard. Rejected: once the reference is capped it is dead code, its mutant can only survive, and the concern would have two owners.
- Move the helper to module level, beside `_floor_demand_at_target`. Rejected: it orphans three mutation-ledger rows whose anchors carry the class qualname, and gains nothing over paying the class lines in place.

Carry dispositions, numbered 1 to 20 as the roster entry holds them (the dispatch brief rendered the same list 0 to 19; its index is in brackets). Each one was re-measured at merge base 5bc009bc8 and at the head:

- Carry 1 (brief 0), comfort-matched null and summer_dhw_only start bound: both settled at main.
  - Part 3 (e57dfbbe0) settled the comfort-matched null. `r10_sav_null_settled.py` reads the const arm, comfort-matched with stored heat settled at both ends, at +0.28 %. The varying arm reads +14.28 %, which is the timing term.
  - `r10_sav_baseline.py null` still prints DEFECT at 12.34 % (10.83 % at 92588d581). That arm reads the raw month saving, which publishes the comfort shortfall beside the saving rather than netting it out, by the part 3 ruling.
  - `golden.capture('summer_dhw_only')` reads +5.881915 %, and `away_setback` reads 29.627509 %. The committed fixture's -3.17 % is a canonical-environment recording that this seat cannot honestly re-record (rule 3).
  - All of these read the same at both ends.
- Carry 2 (brief 1), volume basis: implemented at main (34cd75bf1). `r10_sav_volume.py` reads flat 0.00 and vary timing +74.88 at both ends.
- Carry 3 (brief 2), card equals `ledger.savings_months`: implemented at main (34cd75bf1).
- Carry 4 (brief 3), owner's baseline definition: implemented at main (34cd75bf1, then part 3).
- Carry 5 (brief 4), actuation phase: implemented at main (5d4e0bcfb). `r10_sav_actuation_phase.py` prints `AGREE: yes` at both ends.
- Carry 6 (brief 5), the two accuracy biases on one sample window: not taken here. It stays open on this group's roster entry.
- Carry 7 (brief 6), the month row's comfort shortfall: implemented at main (e57dfbbe0), with the same figures as carry 1.
- Carry 8 (brief 7), the duty-ledger tail settle: implemented at main (eb0cf1893). `AGREE: yes` at both ends.
- Carry 9 (brief 8), the unattributed residual (item 476710bb): measured, not attributed, and it stays open on this group's roster entry.
  - `r10_sav_wood_reference.py` reads -3.90 % (valve-flat), -8.02 % (valve-vary), -3.22 % (wood-cold) and -3.42 % (wood-stale), identical at both ends.
  - A scratch probe on valve-flat, in kWh_th: the plan delivers 264.54, the reference 263.10, comfort 11.25, stored -9.68. The plan buys about 22 kWh_th more than the settled reference.
  - Buffer-tank standing loss is ruled out: 2.16 for the plan against 1.91 for the reference.
  - The next hypothesis is that the two-zone comfort term counts the lower floor only (`_floor_demand_terms`). That needs a two-zone control. The single-zone reading of the same arm, at -154 %, is a different regime and not a control.
- Carry 10 (brief 9), no pump cap in `_apportion_by_steady_demand` (item 0497bde5): closed in this diff.
- Carry 11 (brief 10), the two-zone comfort check, M2 (item 435eb685): closed in this diff.
- Carry 12 (brief 11), the residual (item c38cb7d9): the same as carry 9.
- Carry 13 (brief 12), the pump cap (item e9ced5fc): closed in this diff.
- Carry 14 (brief 13), the residual (item d7f65c3b): the same as carry 9.
- Carry 15 (brief 14), the pump cap (item 7f2fa39d): closed in this diff.
- Carry 16 (brief 15), the pump cap, 1.226x on a 3 kW pump (item fc24128d): closed in this diff. The check that pins it reads 3.678 kW on the 3.0 kW pump at main.
- Carry 17 (brief 16), the residual (item 7da8ff67): the same as carry 9.
- Carry 18 (brief 17), the pump cap: closed in this diff.
- Carry 19 (brief 18), the residual: the same as carry 9.
- Carry 20 (brief 19), part-load refill pricing (item 213e8a10): not taken here, and it stays open on this group's roster entry.
  - `r10_partload_pricing.py` prints `null rows not zero 0`. Flat d=0.112 reads lp_err 0.267290, terminal-at-max 4.368455 and deferred-at-max 2.139841, at both ends.
  - The refill-residue harness the carry cites is not in the tree at the merge base.

## Head

`a942da87b28a2ec60cf29717754c6a663c9f4efe` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

682edb35c57930b5ea4b1b589b85139d9952032b, the code head, measured against merge base 661d26a5d2e655f32391048605db5970d133db1d (origin/main's tip when fetched, 2026-11-08T22:17Z).

This repair pass starts from the pull request's head e329c7a437744b790a7562223e16d4c212ae3975: mutation-autofix's pin commit on `06a9e764c` (this PR's delivery row) on `59c5ece96` (the orchestrator's merge of main `996ded2a6`). It merges origin/main `51cd5ec8a` (`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reported no conflict), then adds two commits: the held-step pass with its check, and the ledger rows for the line it changed. main moved twice during clean `prepr.sh` runs: to `daf8b349f` (at e456d0fe; it brings `tests/card_browser.mjs` and a delivery row) and to `661d26a5d` (at e423a79d; it brings `tools/ci/` and `tools/audit/seat/` instruments and two delivery rows). Neither touches `optimizer.py`, `tests/features.py` or the mutation ledger, so the mutation proof and harness figures below, taken at e456d0fe, describe this head's production and test code. The unpinned-site count, gate scope and structure ratchet were re-taken at this head, and `prepr.sh` re-ran here.

After that clean run origin/main had moved again, to `7812357d5`; `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflict and its delta touches none of `optimizer.py`, `tests/features.py` or the mutation ledger. main moved three times in three prepr cycles, so this head is handed off unmerged with it rather than chasing the tip; the merge-main bot or the orchestrator merges it.

## Mutation proof

Run through `tools/audit/seat/features_block.py "# Item 1: the settlement books the plan's thermostat baseline" "# The start's settlement, at its limits"` with `--prelude 'from datetime import datetime as _SavDT' --prelude 'import types as _sw_types'`, `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`; each edit restored after:
- **Head as committed:** rc=0, 14 checks ok.
- **`~held & (spread > cap)` changed to `~held & (spread >= cap)`** (the CMP_BOUND site): rc=1; one check goes red, `behind a valve, a step spread exactly to the pump keeps the spread`, reading `[1.5, 1.5, 1.5, 1.5]` (the simulation handed back) against `[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 6.0]`.
- **The previous line `spread > cap` changed to `spread >= cap`** (the mutant CI left unpinned): the block runs to `timeout 90`, rc=124. A held step re-reads as over, the held set never grows, and the loop never ends. That is why `--pin-killed` could not kill it: a timeout is not a kill (`mutation_table.py` `SURVIVOR_LINE`).
- **The previous line `spread > cap` with the new check in place:** rc=0, 14 checks ok. The new check holds on the old code too; the behaviour at the boundary is unchanged.
- `python3 tests/mutation_table.py --pin-killed --base origin/main --jobs 3`: `PIN KILLED: 2 pinned, 0 left unpinned`; `optimizer.py:5594 CMP_BOUND` killed by `tests/features.py` (rc=0 failed=0 to rc=1 failed=2), `optimizer.py:5594 GUARD_OFF` killed by `tests/typing_ruler.py` (rc=0 failed=0 to rc=1 failed=1). The null control `optimizer.py:552 NULL_COMMENT` survived every driver.

The earlier proofs (main's uncapped spread, `zone = lowers` to `rooms`, the `> 0.0` to `> 1.0` guard) concern lines this pass leaves alone.

## Null control

- **The new check against the old line:** it passes there (above), so its red under the mutant is the mutant's, not a check that fails on any tree.
- **Comfort-matched and savings harnesses:** re-run at this head, each reads the figure it read at 7da8a92 (below). The cap does not bind in them, and the change touches only which steps are re-tested once held.
- **Two-zone check:** passes at this head.

## Figures

- **Unpinned sites** (`python3 tests/mutation_table.py --pin-killed --base origin/main`, first line): 2757 against 2755 at base 51cd5ec8a before the pins; 2755 against 2755 at base 661d26a5d at this head, `PIN KILLED -- 0 new unpinned site(s)`. The CI run 42521434959 at e329c7a read 2756 against 2755, the one being `optimizer.py:5594 CMP_BOUND`.
- **Feature checks** (`PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py`, run with the new check over the previous line): `ALL 4984 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, 6m01s.
- **Comfort-matched null** (`PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_null_settled.py`, sha1 eca29a18ee19): const +0.28 %, vary +14.28 %, both SOUND, rc=0, at this head; the same at 7da8a92 and at main 5bc009bc8.
- **Raw month null** (`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_baseline.py null`, sha1 bc31f356191e): 12.336 % saved, DEFECT, rc=1, at this head; the same at 7da8a92 and at main.
- **Null-arm split** (`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_null_terms.py`, sha1 c981e7c840ed): power-weighted COP gain +17.29 %, at this head; the same at 7da8a92.
- **Unattributed residual** (`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_wood_reference.py valve-flat`, sha1 dfcdcc46269e): -3.90 %, SOUND, at this head; the same at 7da8a92 and at main.
- **Gate scope** (`tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`): `MODE: SCOPED -- 27 script(s) run, 6 scoped out`.
- **Structure** (`python3 tests/structure.py`): `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`; the pass is the same line count, no budget moved.

## Architecture score

`python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`: `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`.

## Unpinned sites

- `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py:5592 CMP_BOUND`: pinned by mutation-autofix (ledger row `CMP_BOUND.bcdccc59`).
- `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py:5594 CMP_BOUND`: pinned by `--pin-killed` at this head (row `CMP_BOUND.a0bdc820`, killed by `tests/features.py`).
- `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py:5594 GUARD_OFF`: pinned by `--pin-killed` at this head (row `GUARD_OFF.a0bdc820`, killed by `tests/typing_ruler.py`); it replaces row `GUARD_OFF.979967aa`, whose line text this pass changed.
- `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py:5597 RETURN_DEL`: pinned by mutation-autofix (row `RETURN_DEL.cb4dc380`).

## Red checks

- `tests / mutation` at e329c7a (run 42521434959): `MUTATION TABLE REFUSED -- 2756 unpinned site(s) against 2755`, the added `optimizer.py:5594 CMP_BOUND`. This branch's own: its `spread >= cap` mutant hung rather than failed, so mutation-autofix could not pin it. Repaired here: the pass now holds only new steps, the mutant is killed by a check, and both sites on the line are pinned. The cheaper detector: `prepr.sh` step 6d listed the site before the first handoff, and the previous body recorded it as killed on the diff-mutant run's count, not on the ratchet's verdict. `--pin-killed` at the head is the ratchet's own verdict and the cheaper detector; it ran at this head (above).

## Block

`merge_train.py classify a942da87b28a2ec60cf29717754c6a663c9f4efe --pr 3347` exits 1: `RED a942da87b28a2ec60cf29717754c6a663c9f4efe pending: none red: gate` (ev/ci-classify-final.txt). This head has two CI runs. In the edit run 42533670001, `gate` concluded failure at 23:14 with `FAIL run(s) [42533669919] at this head are still being judged; their gate decides`. Then the code run 42533669919 was cancelled at 23:21:03-05. No job in it failed. `tests / fast (3.14)`, `tests / mutation`, `tests / coverage`, `tests / closures`, `tests / replay`, `tests / browser`, `governance / instrument-self-tests` and `codeql / Analyze (python)` were all cancelled together, and so were its `gate`, `mutation-autofix`, `claims-autofix` and `closures-autofix`. The branch and `refs/pull/3347/head` both still read a942da87b, and no newer run exists on this head. So the gate's suite (features, golden, env_drift and the mutation ratchet are all in the closure) has no conclusion at this head, and a red CI never yields `merge`. Nothing in the authored work is defective, as far as this review can see (below). A re-run of the CI code run on this head, then a re-dispatch, is what is owed; the patch is unchanged, so the review below stands for it.

## Findings

- Out of scope: the space solve's seed is the thermostat reference, and it is capped only at `max_electrical_power`. Where `h.power_caps` bounds a step below the pump (space-blocked and off steps, `_build_space_power_caps`), `seed_power` still lies outside that step's bound. That holds at main too: `np.clip(seed_power, 0.0, p_max)` never read `power_caps`, so this diff neither causes nor changes it. Neither the new code comment ("inside the bounds: the reference never passes the pump") nor the check name ("the reference seeds the space solve only inside its bounds") says that it holds only where no power cap binds. Part 1 merged as #3278. Part of #201. This seat edits nothing in `tools/ci/` and no reader of the gate conclusion. The analysis is `dev/audit/rca/r10-gate-defer-read-final.md`, indexed in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json` as `_rca.R10-RCA-GATE-DEFER-READ-FINAL`.

- **Cause 1, the reader window.** #3287 made a red on the required `gate` check provisional: gate.py's `deferral()` red is published at once, and `settle` re-judges it later. No step enumerated that conclusion's readers. Five still take the red as final at origin/main `73365699a`, four in code and one in policy: `merge_train.py` `policy_refusal` (the BRANCH-POLICY park), `orchestrator_tick.py` `one_pr`/`main`, `review_packet.py` `gate_digest`, `merge_pr.sh` and `nudge.md` step 15. Process state (a): fixer step 8's `agreement.mjs` rule fires on a change to a reader, never to a writer. The countermeasure is P436's barrier on R10-HOTFIX-TRAIN-DEFER-WAIT, which has not landed.
- **Cause 2, the settle loop (finding, carried).** `sweep.py` `undecided()` counts the skipped jobs that a job re-run re-stamps. So `settle` re-runs two red gates at one head in turn, up to `ATTEMPT_CAP`, even on content reds. #3274's three runs reached attempt 44. Process state (c).
- **Carry 0:** covered by `5c1fa41fb`, with figures below.

## Carries

- Carry 0: covered by `5c1fa41fb`. The deciding gate's conclusion re-judges every deferring gate at the head without a human.
  - Census: `at_once_lag_min_max_decider_success=1.5` (every at-once deferral red whose deciders succeeded was green within 1.5 min), `residual_red_decider_success=0`, `at_once_green_by_human=6`.
  - Four of those six are hand re-runs at lag 0.0 racing the sweep. Two follow a cancelled or failed decider, which the sweep rightly leaves red.
  - The proving test in the tree is `tools/ci/sweep_selftest.py`'s settle census (#3287).
  - Measure asked for: 86 deferral reds on 43 heads, 2.0 per head that carries one. Decider-to-green: median 0.0 min under both programs; max 1.5 min (at-once) after a successful decider.
- Carry 1 (items 39f0a86e), and Carry 2, the same item written twice:
  - §1 of `dev/audit/rca/r10-gate-busy-defer-2.md` is corrected in this diff. "In #3261, the higher gate waits one poll" is bound to #3246's program, the one it replays, and #3287's at-once deferral is stated after it.
  - The document's `census` arm reads `gh api`, which this seat does not have. It was not run. The same question (gates judged by a program without the fix, after the fix merged) is measured with this PR's census instead: `stale_pin_reds_after_fix=6`, `stale_pin_reruns_after_fix=2` (#3291 d5f8f410, attempts 3 of two runs).
  - §5.2 stays needed. It is being built on `handoff-wip/r10-hotfix-gate-busy-defer-p5` (`a5ee73e39`, not merged), so it waits on that group.
- Carry 3: the addendum owed at the third instance is delivered.
  - Cause: RCA section 2.

  - Cost test with numbers: section 5.

## Head

`679cd0700d1188cce786296d9247315804684b9b` merges main `6457496` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`4b3af66de2b935ae66c986693bece3e85c9addef` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`aca864bce91258fb85d14ae7eba75075132e13b5`, branch `handoff/r10-rca-gate-busy-defer-p5`, cut from origin/main `73365699a`. origin/main was `73365699a` at the clean `tools/pr/prepr.sh` run (PRE-PR rc=0 at this head, 5 min 11 s) and at the re-read at 2026-11-08T08:00Z (`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD`: no conflict). By the owner ruling of 2026-11-07, no merge of a moved main is owed. The three-dot diff:
- adds the harness, its fixture and its mutant spec;
- adds the RCA document;
- edits #3278's document (§1 and its Carries);
- adds the `_rca` entry;
- adds the harness's `tests/closures.json` INERT READS entry.

## Mutation proof

This PR adds no production line. It adds two detectors, and each is proven against real program copies and its own perturbation.

- **`loop`.** It replays #3274's recorded loop through `sweep.undecided()`.
  - At `73365699a` (and at `5c1fa41fb`, and at `d23377e1d` on the sibling branch) it predicts 129 of 129 actual re-runs.
  - Perturbation: with every `skipped` job dropped, it predicts 38.
  - The arm cannot run at `5c1fa41fb^1`, which has no `undecided()`. The settle, and so the loop, arrived with #3287.
- **`census`.** It separates a deferral red from any other gate red. With every deferral line erased, the fixture scores 0 deferral reds (the `selftest` arm's first null control).
- **`selftest` under a mutant.** Widening the scored conclusion from `failure` to `failure` or `cancelled` prints `FAIL non_deferral_reds: want 276, got 331` and `SELFTEST FAIL`. The unmutated harness prints `SELFTEST ok: 18 expected result(s), 2 null controls`.
- **#3278's replay arm** exits 0 at `812bb8747` and 1 at `73365699a`. It reads `C3-AT-ONCE` on all three c3 scenes, #3287's design.
- **Diff mutants.** With MUTANT_CMD set to this harness's `selftest`, `prepr.sh`'s step reads `no survivor` over 0 mutants. `mutant_run.py --diff` skips `dev/` (`SKIP_PREFIXES`), and every added Python line here is under `dev/audit/harnesses/`. Its wall time: 0.065 s.
- **Spec mutants instead.** `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --spec dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_read_final_mutants.json --cmd "env GIT_DIR=<repo>/.git python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_read_final.py selftest"`.

  - Wall 5.5 s. NULL survived; 14 KILLED; 1 survivor: M3-green-after-red.
  - M3 (`t > done` to `t >= done`) is equivalent on the recorded data: no `gate` success completes in the same second as a deferral red at its head.
  - The first pass had 6 survivors (M3, M5, M6, M10, M11, M15). Pinning the figures they move in the header's EXPECTED RESULT block (18 results now) killed five of them. The commit subject `aca864bc`^ says six; five is the count.

- 276 gate failures that are not deferrals (`non_deferral_reds`) are never scored as deferral reds. A census keyed on `conclusion == failure` alone would count 362.
- Every residual deferral red (18) had a cancelled or failed decider (`residual_red_decider_success=0`). The sweep left no red standing behind a decider that succeeded.
- `loop` with the re-stamped skipped jobs dropped predicts 38, not 129. The 38 come from `undecided()`'s third arm (overlapping re-run gates), which only the loop produces.
- #3278's replay at `812bb8747` exits 0 on the same fixture where `73365699a` exits 1.

## Figures

- Census: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_read_final.py census`.

Policy change on two owner rulings (tvofi, 2026-11-08, chat to the orchestrator): the bar for a new process, tooling or instrument proposal and for the owner's exemption moves from over 10% to over 20% improvement (CI time, programme completion time, right-first-time, token usage); an already planned instrument or machinery group, or an existing non-production CI lane or seat, stays only on a measured improvement of at least 10% (was 5%, in no policy file; its only statement was `dev/programme/triage/s6-batch126.md`, a record left as written); a minor or low defect repair in instrument or machinery code takes the same bars. Owner correction of 2026-11-08: the issue bar applies only to instrument and machinery code. Approval: mandate 6715477401 (scope all) covers the owner's approving review.

Sites changed: `dev/governance/roles/proposal-triage.md` (exemption sentence, keep test, minor-defect rule), `dev/governance/rules/ratchet-budgets.md` plus its generated `.claude/rules/` and `.cursor/rules/` copies (`node tools/policy/rules_sync.mjs`), `tools/audit/machinery_ratchet.py` (docstring, `THRESHOLD`, self-test cases at exactly 20%), `tools/audit/seat/instruments/machinery_ratchet.py.md`. ## Repair of the blocked review (comment 6721196982)

Block, the rule conflict. The skip list at 2684306f named "a required countermeasure", and the opening defines a countermeasure policy requires as "(root cause, red-check carry, finding fix)", so a `low` or `normal` machinery repair that fixes a finding both met the bar and skipped it. At this head:

- the skip list reads "`medium`, `high`, `major`, `critical`, root-cause countermeasure, closeout, owner directive skip them": only a root-cause countermeasure skips, as the group brief keeps it;
- the opening reads "(root cause, red-check carry, finding fix; see below) keeps its route", pointing the finding-fix route at the Machinery paragraph, which is the one exception.

So a `low` or `normal` repair of instrument, machinery, CI-lane or seat code (outside `custom_components/`) meets both bars whether or not it fixes a finding; a product defect never takes the bar. The `low`/`normal` take, `medium`/`high`/`major`/`critical` skip mapping is unchanged from the orchestrator-approved one.

Findings, each restored:

- DEFER's "or the owning group" (base wording): "DEFER, what would change it or the owning group".
- "never assumed major" (group brief): "unset is classified first, never assumed major."
- "An even or marginal trade is REJECT" (base): "Even or marginal: REJECT".

Paid within the 489 ~token cap (bytes/4) without a raise, by prose trims that change no seat duty, each listed: "this cost/benefit gate before it is built" to "this gate before building" (the **Bar** paragraph defines the gate as cost against benefit); "the orchestrator's sweep" to "orchestrator sweep"; "outweighs its costs" to "outweighs cost"; "An ACCEPT on the exemption" to "An exemption ACCEPT"; "or an existing" to "or existing"; "A repair" to "Repair"; "a required countermeasure" to "root-cause countermeasure" (the repair itself); "closeout and an owner directive" to "closeout, owner directive"; "`Cost:` (the estimate," to "`Cost:` (estimate,"; "**A ruling** is a" to "**A ruling**: a"; "routes an ACCEPT" to "routes ACCEPTs"; "citing no ACCEPT ruling" to "citing no ACCEPT" (an ACCEPT is a ruling here). - `MUTANT_CMD="python3 tools/audit/machinery_ratchet.py --self-test" PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1 bash tools/pr/prepr.sh`: `PRE-PR: 42c0ebbb531244c8815968779d519f9680d0fef7 ... rc=0`, run on the committed merge head; closures skipped, diff mutants WARN (7 survivors, the same seven answered under Unpinned sites), every other step ok or skip.

All seven survivors sit on added lines inside `machinery_ratchet.py`'s own `self_test()`, the instrument's test assertions, not its production logic; this repair adds no code site:

- `:614`, `:615`, `:616`, `:633` CALL_DEL (the `ok(...)` call deleted): deleting a self-test assertion cannot fail the same self-test. Disposition: value check. The THRESHOLD mutant above turns `:614` and `:615` red, so they bite; `:616` (21% passes) and `:633` (`improvement()` exact) are the positive and exact-value controls. The seat's python3 is a shim that resolves its venv under $HOME; the arm plants a substitute HOME, so the shim exits 127 and body_privacy_line returns nonzero. The sibling "host home refused" arm only saw a nonzero rc and passed for the wrong reason.
