## Round

First round. This review is of part 3 of R10-HANDOFF-PATH, at head 4bfb5d134a0d5fe0c8bbc716b41ca981d24dbbe1. The head is unchanged at post time (ls-remote).

## Block

- Carry 12 is not delivered for the case it names. `tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh:619` classes a refusal as body-content when `grep -qiE 'REFUSE[: ]+(unpinned sites?|carry|pr-body|figures|brief)|unpinned site'` matches anywhere in the whole `update.out`. The second alternative, a bare `unpinned site`, has no `REFUSE` anchor. A full prepr run prints a step line for unpinned sites on every run that gets past its early exits. That line reads `skip unpinned sites ... the diff adds no unpinned mutation site`, `ok unpinned sites ...`, or `WARN unpinned sites`: `say` writes it to fd 3, which is app_push's inherited stdout and so lands in `update.out`. The `ci predict` step (prepr.sh:4453) does not exit; `step` only sets rc. So the run always reaches step 7d (prepr.sh:4603) and prints that line, and every `ci predict` refusal is recorded at once, never retried. The same holds for closures, mutants, policy_lint and every other late step. Carry 12 names `ci predict` explicitly as a retryable class. Only the early-exit `ancestry reds` (prepr.sh:4098) escapes, and that is the only class the fixture exercises: its `rt.sh` stub prints one REFUSE line, not prepr's real output. Reproduction, using the production regex read from line 619 at the head: `ev/regex_demo/RESULT.txt` gives `ci_predict_refusal.out content` and `early_ancestry.out retry`. Remedy: classify only on the step names of `REFUSE` step lines, and drop the unanchored alternative. Add a fixture arm whose stub prints a prepr-shaped `REFUSE ci predict` run that includes the unpinned-sites skip line, and show that arm red against today's line.
  Carry: R10-HANDOFF-PATH

## Findings

- Carry 6's third clause ("the sweep's disk floor names which checkouts it could collect") is left unbuilt. The body's reason for that is wrong: it says "no such floor instrument was found in the tree", but the instrument exists. It is `tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py:77`/`:490` (the beat's `disk` row with `disk_floor_gib`), which runs `tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh`, and it is documented at `tools/audit/seat/sweep_template.md:48,87`. The re-cut owes either that naming or a disposition that cites this instrument.
  Carry: R10-HANDOFF-PATH
- Follow-up: the relay key changes from `<topic> <hs>` to `<topic> <hs> <bs>` for non-body-only failures, so existing two-field entries in `cloud-handoff-failed` stop matching. Each such topic is rerun once on the first pass after deploy. Carry 8 wants that, because the reasons of the 28 measured entries were unrecoverable, but the body does not state it. Disclose it in the re-cut body.

merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-SWEEP-SETTLE-LOOP: stop sweep.settle re-running sibling gates on re-stamped skipped jobs
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
The gate sweep's `settle` branch re-runs red gates in a loop, and the loop uses up the CI concurrency every PR waits on. GitHub re-stamps every skipped job of a run each time that run's gate is re-run. `undecided()` arm 1 in `tools/ci/sweep.py` read those stamps as sources that finished after a sibling's gate started. So a sibling's sweep re-ran that gate, the re-run re-stamped its own skipped jobs, and the two runs kept re-running each other until `ATTEMPT_CAP`. #3308 at head 6016f9dd shows it: runs 42470642055, 42470643072 and 42471173865 were at attempts 39, 25 and 24 when this was recorded.

Fix, in `tools/ci/sweep.py` only (with doc corrections):
1. `undecided()` arm 1 reads `sources(jobs)`: jobs that are neither a gate nor `skipped`.
2. `settle` leaves a gate whose latest attempt the bot started (`SWEEP_ACTOR`, `github-actions[bot]`: the sweep's `github.token`, which ci.yml's `refresh` also posts as) unless a source finished after that attempt started (`settled()`). So it re-runs a gate at most once per source change, whichever arm reads the gate as undecided.
3. Unchanged: the `run()` branch (green gate that covers the newest event), `covers_newest`, and gate.py's own refresh and defer re-runs.
4. Corrected: the false no-loop claim in sweep.py's module doc ("the branch cannot loop"), the same claim in gate.py's DEFERRAL doc ("settle cannot loop"), and `undecided()`'s "nothing loops".

Root cause: release trigger, introduced by #3287 (52f9fc5b34, r10-gate-busy-defer-3) in v7.1.6, process state (c). The process was followed: the self-test's fixtures modelled skipped jobs as sources, and no fixture was recorded from a real re-run listing. The full analysis is owed by a separate RCA seat at `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-SWEEP-SETTLE-LOOP.md`, not part of this diff.

Topic r10-hotfix-sweep-settle-loop. VERSION, the manifest, the RELEASE_NOTES heading, the budgets and both claim files are untouched. Scope: `MODE: FULL`, because the gate.py doc correction "changes the gate itself". Locally I ran the self-tests of both changed programs, `tests/entities.py` (the one closure that reads sweep.py) and the `run_always` scripts. The FULL suite is left to CI (fixer.md step 5).

## Head

`a28cb436e06e6fdef9784fa9b0c0b39a75950474` merges main `51cd5ec` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`f6d7be0cd4ef22a353d72532ca18aae38089e5cc` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

6158186e11747e9f145eb761264b458453326f9d (base 4fe7d5934b0a4bc092c9398f29b579fbd2df8b50)

## Mutation proof

Each mutant was applied to `tools/ci/sweep.py` alone, then `python3 -I tools/ci/sweep.py --self-test` was run, then the file was restored from a copy:
- M1, a skipped job counts as a source again (drop `and j.get("conclusion") != "skipped"` in `sources`): 5 failed: `#3308: skipped jobs re-stamped by a sibling's gate re-run are no source; settle re-runs nothing` (swept from each of the three runs), `#3308 null: a non-skipped source (codeql python) ... re-runs that gate, once`, `#3308 null: that re-run ... is final; no sweep re-runs a gate`.
- M2, `settled()` returns False: 1 failed: `settle: an overlapping pair of re-run gates, re-run by github-actions[bot], with no source after them, is final`.
- M3, `settled()` drops its `not source_after(...)` clause: 1 failed: `#3308 null: a non-skipped source (codeql python) finishing after a sibling gate started re-runs that gate, once`.

## Null control

Those are the gates of 42470642055 and 42470643072, and the recorded listings show both re-run at 11:48:33Z (attempts 39 and 25).
- A real source still triggers a re-run. With codeql python of 42470642055 set to finish at 11:47:30Z, after 42470643072's gate started at 11:46:43Z, there is exactly one post (`jobs/128721143539/rerun`). Once that re-run starts after the source and re-stamps its own skips, a sweep from each of the three runs posts nothing.

- fixture source: `gh api repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/actions/runs/<id>/attempts/<n>/jobs` for 42470642055/38, 42470643072/24 and 42471173865/24. The edit runs are kept whole. 42470642055 is trimmed from 41 jobs to its gate, its 9 skipped jobs and 5 non-skipped sources.

Outside sweep.py it returns only gate.py lines 662, 664, 682, 739 and 740, all inside `self_test()` (the #3282 recording's `at_time`/`replay`). Disposition: test-only, no production reader. In production, the only reader of job stamps is sweep.py's `undecided()`/`settled()`, closed in this diff. gate.py's `busy()`/`judging()`/`started()` read job status, never stamps.

It does not touch VERSION, the manifest, RELEASE_NOTES.md or any *_budgets.json. No policy file is touched: cloud_dispatch.py is not in CLAUDE.md's policy set and CODEOWNERS does not own it. The body calls it "policy-adjacent", but no owner approval is required by path.
- RESULT self-test head: `cloud_dispatch.py --self-test` reports 129 checks, 0 failed (ev/selftest-head.txt). The two new arms (P398 frugal line; pack render per role) are ok.
- RESULT mutants (each restored afterwards): M1 dropping FRUGAL_LINE from the join is killed (1 FAIL), the body's own mutant reproduced. M2 emitting FRUGAL_LINE twice is killed. M3 removing the pack setup is killed. M4 giving the probe a pack is killed. M5, M6 and M7 survive (see Findings).

- RESULT merge: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 7e9b464acd5289660b0d5a4ef10c7d609dd50c45` gives rc 0, tree 0469adc20507, no conflict.
- RESULT CI: `merge_train.py classify 7e9b464acd5289660b0d5a4ef10c7d609dd50c45 --pr 3333` returns rc 0, `GREEN 7e9b464acd5289660b0d5a4ef10c7d609dd50c45 pending: none red: none` (ev/classify.txt). The packet digest lists no failure on any check run.

merges.subject: Merge pull request #3316 from tvofi/fix/r10-rca-cop-unmeasured
merges.title: R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED: rca cop unmeasured
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED: the root-cause seat for R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED (#3297).

- **Trigger:** 1. The defect reached v4.0.0 through v7.1.5.
- **Scope:** this seat ran beside the hotfix fixer. It edits nothing under
  `custom_components/` and does not touch #3297's branch.

The product is `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED.md`, cited from
`dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json` `_rca["R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED"]`. Its
reproduction and detector is `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_cop_unmeasured.py`.
The four parts follow.

- **Named cause.** One COP sample per interval serves both a learner (the
  COP scale) and two graders: the last measured COP and the COP health watch.
  The sample carries no provenance.
  - With no heat input, `flow_meter.cop_evidence` infers the COP as the model
    times ask over draw.
  - A vendor-estimated thermal power entity was read as metered heat.
  - Either way, the watch's bands and `machine_score` compared the model with
    itself.
  - By `git log`, the inference came first, named "measured" from
    `df7db8215` (PR #11, v2.8.0). The watch was built onto it in `a63b576cd`
    (PR #50, v4.0.0) and had no metered input until v7.0.5. The watch did not
    degrade: it was born on an inference.
- **Process state: (c).** Three processes read this seam and passed it.
  Each judged whether the sample was clean. None traced where its inputs came
  from.
  - `D1.md` hunts "fabricated data as measured" but has no method step that
    reaches it.
  - The round-10 P5 sweep (`dev/audit/rounds/round10/sweep-P5.md:37`) cleared
    `_cop_health_cusum` as "an empirical per-bucket, per-curve baseline ...
    not a model residual".
  - STUDY R10-IDENT Q2 (#2262) found "COP is not observable without a heat
    meter". The R10-COP-GATE group carried it as a draw-follows-plan state.
    Its null control was "an install whose draw does follow the plan still
    reaches a COP model": the learner only, never the graders.
  - Not (a), not (b) and not (d): the reasons are in the document's
    section 2.
- **Cost test.**
  - P = 0.1 per round, estimated from one release escape over ten rounds
    (78 days). No class frequency exists.
  - cost(defect) is at least 12 h of fix wall-clock, plus an RCA seat and 73
    days of exposure.
  - The expected cost is 1.2 to 1.5 h per round.
  - A D1 provenance step costs about 10 min a round, covering only the
    `measured` / `observed` names a round adds (23 today), so it **passes**.
  - A CI-wide provenance type on every reading **fails**: it would rewrite
    the readers, and #3297 already concentrates the decision in
    `InstallCapability.cop_measured`.
- **Countermeasure.**
  - **Built:** the harness's `--check` is the detector. It exits 1 on v7.1.5
    and on main, 0 at the fix head, 2 on a skip tree, and 1 on each of two
    single-door trees, whatever the shell's cwd: it changes into the named
    root before importing, and exits 3 if a module it grades loaded from
    outside that root. It is hand-run and wired into no gate: #3297's own
    `tests/features.py` section is the instance's CI barrier, and a second
    copy would pin the same line twice.
  - **Proposed to the owner, not landed:** the D1 step "Measured means
    measured". It is quoted in the document's section 5, with its planning
    counterpart. Both are policy, so both wait for the owner's approval.
  - **Refused, and recorded:** the static provenance check.
- **Class.** No class is minted. The shape has one instance on the register,
  closed through one function.
  - The class search is in the document's section 3. It traced 23 names and
    the sample's readers.
  - It found one more self-referential seam, `_fold_capacity_envelope`'s
    no-heat branch. That is a learner, off by default, and kept by the owner's
    ruling of 2026-11-07 that no learner is gated.
  - The nearest classes are N-unmetered-reference and P11.
- **No issue comment.** `defect-root-cause.md` asks for a Root cause section
  on the defect's issue. This hotfix has no issue, and this seat's brief
  forbids comments. If the orchestrator opens one, the section is state (c),
  the cost-test numbers above, and the document's path, all in the
  document's section 6.
- **Owner decision owed.** The D1 step and its planning counterpart are
  policy. The register's `_rca["R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED"].parts_missing`
  holds both, `status` `proposed`, until the owner rules. Neither is landed
  here.

## Head

`1623c5ade60f6b9023a7d613631b998f5cc39c4d` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

The head is `1b684dfbffdd6bbe3d864dc9d339c50c82739c9d`.

Repair of round 1's block, `countermeasure-unsound` at `b8fba2c8d`: the
detector measured the shell's cwd tree, not the checkout it was given.
`tests/harness.py` inserts the cwd-relative `tests` and `custom_components`
ahead of the root's own `sys.path` entries, so `heatpump_optimizer` loaded from
the cwd. Commits since `b8fba2c8d`:

- `142bbf919`: `main()` runs `os.chdir(root)` before its imports, then refuses
  with `REFUSED <module> loaded from <path>, outside <root>` and rc 3 if
  `harness`, `flow_meter` or the coordinator loaded from outside the root.
  The docstring states both.
- `8c1b6a017`: the document's section 5 states the cause and the re-taken
  rcs, two mutants join the set, the Reproduce recipe gains the two
  cross-cwd lines, and section 6 carries the class (below).
- `1b684dfbf`: a merge of origin/main `8a4cf2618`, no conflict
  (`LEDGER-MERGE: resolved tests/closures.json`).

The three commits were first written under another author identity and rebuilt
with `git commit-tree` on the same trees under the pinned one, before any push:
`git diff --quiet` between each rebuilt commit and its original exits 0, so
every figure below was taken on this tree.

The group's Carry 1 is this body's own Forward-carry item on the cwd capture
across `dev/audit/harnesses/` (body item 6d58568e), landed on
`handoff/audit-r10-roster` at `a62e0a80a2039fdf89953ac83ae06311f40beb4a`. It is
routed, not closed, by this pull request: only this seat's detector is repaired.

Alternatives considered for the fix:

- Anchor the two inserts in `tests/harness.py` to its own directory: lost,
  because a historical root such as v7.1.5 brings its own `tests/harness.py`
  with the cwd-relative inserts, so the detector would still read the cwd's
  tree when measuring any release before that change. It is carried as a
  class repair instead (Forward-carry).
- Import `harness` first, then re-put the root's entries ahead: works for the
  inserts known today, but any later cwd-relative read still follows the cwd.
  The change of directory makes cwd and root the same tree, and the
  provenance refusal catches whatever the change of directory misses.

## Mutation proof

`tools/pr/prepr.sh`'s diff-mutant step lists no mutants, because
`tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py` skips `dev/` (`SKIP_PREFIXES`) and every
added line is under `dev/audit/`. So the detector was mutated by hand. Each
mutant was applied alone to a copy of
`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_cop_unmeasured.py`; the tree's file was never
edited.

The scored command requires all of these together, each run with the shell's
cwd on a **different** tree from the target:

- rc 0 on the fix head `2d010b091`, cwd v7.1.5;
- rc 1 on v7.1.5, cwd the fix head;
- rc 2 on the skip tree, cwd v7.1.5;
- rc 1 on door N and on door T, cwd v7.1.5.

Unmutated it passes. Each mutant below fails it, so 8 of 8 are killed:

| mutant | the edit | first failing arm |
|---|---|---|
| M-a | the verdict line becomes `return 0` | v7.1.5 rc 0 |
| M-b | the skip guard becomes `if False:` | skip rc 0 |
| M-c | the null verdict is forced to `withheld` | door N rc 0 |
| M-d | the tuya verdict is forced to `withheld` | door T rc 0 |
| M-e | `null` is dropped from the verdict | door N rc 0 |
| M-f | the metered verdict is forced to `graded` | skip rc 0 |
| M-g | `os.chdir(root)` deleted | fix rc 3 (the refusal fires) |
| M-h | M-g, and the refusal's `return 3` made `pass` | fix rc 1 |

M-h is the head `b8fba2c8d` shipped. Run alone, with cwd the fix head and the
target v7.1.5, M-h prints `null=withheld tuya=withheld metered=graded` and
rc 0: the false clean the block named, reproduced on the mutant and absent at
this head.

## Null control

- **Cwd control (the block's).** The same detector, the same target, the
  shell's cwd moved between trees. At `b8fba2c8d` the verdict followed the cwd;
  at this head it follows the target. Both runs are in Figures.
- **Metered control.** The metered install (plain ids, 6.0 kW of heat over
  2.0 kW of power) grades on every tree, defective and fixed. So the detector
  can see a sample.
- **Skip control.** The fix head with `if measured:` turned to `if False:`
  withholds all three samples, and the detector exits 2, not 0.
- **No production change.** `git diff --stat $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD`
  lists `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`,
  `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_cop_unmeasured.py`,
  `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED.md`, `dev/programme/delivery/3316.md`
  and `tests/closures.json`, nothing under `custom_components/`.

## Figures

Trees: detached worktrees of v7.1.5 (`516ad1b6b`), the #3297 head
`2d010b091`, origin/main `bb7dfb9bd`, and three copies of `2d010b091` edited
as the skip tree, door N and door T (section 5 of the document).

- **The block, reproduced at `b8fba2c8d`.** That head's detector, copied out,
  `python3 -I <copy> --check <target>` from `cd <cwd>`:
  - cwd v7.1.5, target fix head: `null=graded tuya=graded metered=graded`, rc 1.
  - cwd fix head, target v7.1.5: `null=withheld tuya=withheld metered=graded`, rc 0.
  - cwd `/tmp`: fix head rc 0, v7.1.5 rc 1.
- **This head, the full cwd by target matrix.** cwd each of v7.1.5, fix head,
  origin/main `bb7dfb9bd` and `/tmp`; target each of fix head, v7.1.5 and
  origin/main. All 12 cells: the fix head prints
  `null=withheld tuya=withheld metered=graded`, rc 0; v7.1.5 and origin/main
  print `null=graded tuya=graded metered=graded`, rc 1. No cell printed
  `REFUSED`.
- **Section 5's rcs, re-taken from a different cwd.** fix head rc 0 (cwd
  v7.1.5); v7.1.5 rc 1 (cwd fix head); origin/main rc 1 (cwd v7.1.5); skip
  tree `null=withheld tuya=withheld metered=withheld`, rc 2; door N
  `null=graded tuya=withheld metered=graded`, rc 1; door T
  `null=withheld tuya=graded metered=graded`, rc 1 (each cwd v7.1.5).
- **The Reproduce recipe**, run from this worktree with the tree paths
  substituted: v7.1.5 rc 1; `.` rc 1 (origin/main as merged here, before
  #3297); fix head rc 0; cwd fix head to v7.1.5 rc 1; cwd v7.1.5 to fix head
  rc 0.
- **Release reach.** `git tag --contains a63b576cd -l 'v*' --no-contains v7.1.6`
  lists the tags v4.0.0 (2026-08-26) to v7.1.5: 134.
- **The name census**, at the merge base `8a4cf2618`:
  `grep -ohiE '"[a-z_]*(measured|observed)[a-z_]*"'` over
  `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py`, `sort -u | wc -l`: 23.
- **The register.** `python3 tools/audit/fold_ledger.py check`: `fold_ledger: 50 classes, 755 instances, 121 in-tree judge survivors (rounds [8, 10]), 138 rca entries`, `0 violation(s)`.
- **Scoped gate.** `tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`:
  `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out`, running
  `tests/entities.py`. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`: on this macOS host the run dies with a traceback before its summary line, `PermissionError: Cannot get task port` in `_hb_stdlib_reads` (the heartbeat lane's stdlib sampler needs the `com.apple.system-task-ports` entitlement). The same command at origin/main `8a4cf2618` dies with the same traceback, so the crash is the host's, not this diff's; CI's Linux runner is the verdict.
  `tests/harness_headers.py` (it reads the changed docstring): `12 of 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED`, every failing line `dev/audit/rounds/round4/D7/sysid_estimator_frontier.py` (`rc=124 ... wall limit 900s exceeded`, host load average about 121). This diff does not touch that harness; `grep FAIL | grep -v sysid_estimator_frontier` returns only the summary line. CI runs it unloaded.
  `tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- **prepr.** `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh BODY.md` at `1b684dfbf`, `MUTANT_CMD` unset (the diff-mutant step skips; `mutant_run.py` skips `dev/` regardless, and the hand proof is above): `PRE-PR: 1b684dfbffdd6bbe3d864dc9d339c50c82739c9d 000000000000000000000000000 rc=0`. Its `ci predict` step: `CI PREDICT: no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted against 8a4cf2618c53`.

## Red checks

No check has concluded at this head; CI runs once the handoff is published.

At `b8fba2c8d`, every red was a **cancellation** of one run, `CI code pr=3316`
(run 42463804677, concluded `cancelled`), plus `gate`'s derived failure over it:
`tests / fast (3.14)`, `tests / closures`, `tests / coverage`,
`tests / coverage-ratchet`, `tests / ci-ratchet`, `tests / graders-head-copy`,
`tests / lane-proofs`, `tests / claims-autofix`, `tests / closures-autofix`
and `governance / instrument-self-tests`. No job log showed an assertion or an
`UNDER-SCOPED` line. The latest edit gate on that head (128707623015) exited 3
on `RATE-LIMITED`: the API refused the gate's read, not a test.

- Cause: run cancellation and a secondary rate limit, neither caused by this
  diff, which touches only `dev/` and one inert `tests/closures.json` line.
- Cheaper detector: none. A cancellation or an API rate limit is not a defect
  a local check predicts. What a local check does predict (`ci predict`, the
  carry routing, the body) was run before this handoff (Figures, prepr).
- Owed: a code run at this head that concludes. A failure there is the finding.

## Forward-carry

- **Doc claims #3297 leaves stale.** These are for the user-docs
  verification pass, once #3297 merges:
  - `README.md:614`: Observed COP "Needs measured power".
  - `docs/how-it-works.md:1240`: the watch "compares each measured COP".
  - The `ObservedCOPSensor` docstring: "derived from measured electrical
    input".

  At the fix head, observed COP needs a heat reading over a power reading,
  neither of them an estimate. Carry: #3139
- **The cwd capture across `dev/audit/harnesses/`.** Any harness that takes a
  root and imports `tests/harness.py` measures the cwd's tree unless it changes
  into the root first, for the cause in Head. This seat's detector is
  repaired. The rest are enumerated, as a superset and not a per-file trace,
  by `git grep -l 'from harness import\|import harness' -- dev/audit/harnesses/ | xargs grep -l sys.path`,
  less those `git grep -l os.chdir -- dev/audit/harnesses/` also lists. The
  repair belongs to the stage owning those harnesses: a change of directory
  per harness, or anchoring `tests/harness.py`'s inserts (current trees only,
  see Head). Recorded in the document's section 6 for the orchestrator to
  route. Carry: R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED

## Friction

Fix review: blocked b8fba2c8d5ab03067539c7e8d06e369f85162c31 countermeasure-unsound: the built detector measures the shell's cwd tree, not the checkout it is given; the RCA's own Reproduce recipe returns rc 1 for the fix tree, and a defective v7.1.5 reads rc 0 from a fixed cwd

bus-nonce: 02fea4f6344a76b34285b6cbdbd280ad

Round 1 of the fix review for PR #3316 (R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED). Measured at head `b8fba2c8d5ab03067539c7e8d06e369f85162c31`, merge base `2a3c05644d85b7ee5c2c314fde5aca950e4aba91`. `refs/pull/3316/head` was re-read at 11:00Z and has not moved.

## Block

- The RCA's only built countermeasure, `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_cop_unmeasured.py --check <checkout>`, does not measure `<checkout>`. It prepends `<root>/tests/hastub`, `<root>/custom_components` and `<root>/tests` to `sys.path`, then imports `harness`. `tests/harness.py:22-23` (at this head and at every tree measured) then runs `sys.path.insert(0, "tests")` and `sys.path.insert(0, "custom_components")`. Those cwd-relative entries go ahead of the root's, so `heatpump_optimizer` loads from whatever checkout the shell is in. Shown in `ev/cwd_dependence.txt`:
  - The RCA's `## Reproduce` recipe, run verbatim from a repository checkout at this head (`python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_cop_unmeasured.py --check <fix tree 2d010b091>`), prints `RESULT null=graded tuya=graded metered=graded` with rc 1. The document says `# rc 0`.
  - Run from inside the fix tree with the root set to v7.1.5 (`516ad1b6b`), it prints `null=withheld tuya=withheld metered=graded` with rc 0. That is a defective release certified as fixed: a false clean from the detector.
  - My first measurement pass, run from the repository root, printed rc 1 for every tree including the fix head (`ev/harness_runs.txt`). That is how I found this.
  - The module docstring says it "builds the real coordinator ... from the checkout named on the command line". That is not true unless the cwd is neutral.
  - The fix is small and has to go in the PR: `os.chdir(root)` before the imports (or importing `harness` before the inserts and then re-putting the root first), plus a control that runs the detector from a cwd holding a different tree and shows the verdict follows `<checkout>`. The documented recipe and every rc in section 5 should then be re-taken under it.
  Carry: R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED

## Findings

- Follow-up: the same cwd capture reaches every harness that takes a root and imports `tests/harness.py`. Eleven files under `dev/audit/harnesses/` pair `from harness import` with a root-relative `sys.path` insert (`ev/class_sites.txt`, a pattern grep, not a per-file trace). Each one silently measures the cwd's tree when run from a checkout. The single sound repair is in `tests/harness.py`: anchor its two inserts to `os.path.dirname(__file__)` rather than the cwd. This seat's PR may land that repair with its own control, or record why not. Either way, the RCA's process section should name it, because a detector that reads the wrong tree is the same "never traced its inputs" unit this RCA indicts.
  Carry: R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED
- Follow-up: CI is not green at this head, independent of the block. The required `gate` is `failure` on every entry. The only code run (`CI code pr=3316`, run 42463804677, attempt 44) concluded `cancelled`, with `tests / fast (3.14)`, `tests / closures`, `coverage`, `coverage-ratchet`, `ci-ratchet`, `graders-head-copy`, `lane-proofs`, `claims-autofix`, `closures-autofix` and `governance / instrument-self-tests` cancelled. The code gate printed `FAIL tests / fast (3.14): cancelled (this run)`. The latest edit gate (128707623015) exited 3 on `RATE-LIMITED reset_epoch=1794135167`. So no run has shown this head's suite green. The body's `## Red checks` names the cancellations truthfully, but it was written before the 10:25Z, 10:45Z and 10:47Z gate entries and does not mention the RATE-LIMITED one. The next head needs a code run that concludes.
  Carry: R10-RCA-COP-UNMEASURED

merges.body:
Closes #3289

R10-MIN-POWER-FLOOR, built to the approved design (`design/r10-min-power-floor` 23fbff36b, `Design review: approve 23fbff36` at e3568092b). A non-modulating pump planned steps below `heat_pump_min_power`, because nothing could declare it on/off when its surface is not switch plus setpoint; and a clamped switch-plus-setpoint install with DHW shipped space plus DHW above `p_max` (5.30 kW on a 3.5 kW pump), because `optimizer._realize_draw` projected the two channels separately while one compressor serves both.

- `compressor_modulation` (auto / on_off / modulating) on the `thermal_model` options page. `thermal_model.declared_modulation` is the only reader of it and of the legacy `clamp_planned_levels` (true -> on/off, false -> modulating, read only under auto or absent). `probe_install` sets `InstallCapability.on_off`, and `can_duty_cycle` returns False first when it is set, so `levels_clamped`, `learner_unmetered` and `draw_range.planned_range` follow without changes of their own.
- `thermal_model.project_space_against`: space projected against the DHW the step already carries, clipped to `[0, p_max - d]`, with a running level below `p_min - d` raised to it. The total is 0 or in `[p_min, p_max]`, and DHW keeps what its planner booked. `_realize_draw` reaches it through `optimizer._realize_joint` when clamped with DHW, in `objective`, `objective_batch` and the publish.
- Departures from the design note, both behaviour-identical:
  - The publish calls `_realize_joint`, the typed DHW-present arm `_realize_draw` delegates to, and not `_realize_draw`. `_realize_draw`'s optional DHW failed mypy against the publish's non-optional `optimal_dhw`.
  - The note's floors at 0 (`max(0, p_max - d)`, `max(0, p_min - d)`, `min(lo, hi)`) are dropped. A cap below 0 already clips to 0 and a raise below 0 matches no running level, so they changed no output except under `p_min > p_max`, where `project_planned_levels` raises to `p_min`. Without them `d = 0` is that function exactly, and their CLAMP_DROP mutants, all equivalent, are gone.
- It shares `_onto_band` with `project_planned_levels`; a second copy would have raised `duplication_copies`. The space-only path is unchanged.
- Behaviour that changes, by install: a probed switch-plus-setpoint install with DHW (space capped at `p_max - d`), and a declared `on_off` on any surface (newly clamped). Clamped without DHW, and every unclamped install, are unchanged: the harness's clamp=False arm is byte-identical at both ends.
- Alternatives that lost (the design's): a shared scale on the total writes into the DHW plan the space solve treats as fixed and makes the batch's DHW a matrix; an integer on/off solve needs a second backend on a Pi-class target; flipping the probe default clamps modulating installs no finding names; a boolean UI key cannot store "absent".
- Space below `p_min` is counted only on space-only steps (DHW <= `MIN_RUNNING_DRAW_KW`): in a mixed step space is a diverter share of a compressor running at >= `p_min` (carry a1c0f3d2). The harness's older `space_steps_below_min` (from `channel_heating_steps`) reads 3, 1, 3 in the DHW cells at the head for exactly that reason, and `space_only_below_min` reads 0.
- Roster: the queued edits (files `config_flow.py`, `const.py`, strings x3, `draw_range.py`, `tests/features.py`, `tests/config_flow_steps.py`, `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt`; size L; `after` R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED, R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE) are still in the drain queue, so the roster row lists fewer files than this diff touches. Per the brief this group goes first (issue 3289 is outside); the `after` edges are textual, rebase at merge. `draw_range.py`, `plan_slots.py` and `tests/config_flow_steps.py` needed no edit. The diff also touches `tests/golden/config_flow.json` and `dev/audit/rounds/round3/D5/option_doc_coverage.py`, which design verdict e3568092b (i) asks the orchestrator to add.

## Head

merges.body:
Part 2 of R10-FLY-STANDING-CONTRACTS: the design's P3, the hooks (design/r10-fly-standing-contracts at 21210036, section 6; P1 merged as #3197). It makes carry 19 section (2), the hooks the orchestrator's sessions depend on, tracked, described and installable. The Bash guard of the orchestrator's checkout (gap 4) is the second arm of the project-level `.claude/hooks/pre-bash.sh`.

Fourth round (minimal re-cut, fixer.md's three-round rule): the second fix review blocked 7359a638 (PR comment 6718280627), class-open: the shared parser read a compound command's reserved word (`if then else elif do while until {`) as the command word, and the guard did not follow `pushd`. The cure, the verdict's first: `parse()` keeps those words at command position as it does WRAP words, and the guard treats `pushd` as `cd`. Pinned in `pre-bash.sh --self-test` (46 passed, 0 failed): guard `if true; then git -C <orch> pull; fi`, guard `pushd <orch> >/dev/null; git reset --hard`, kill arm `if true; then pkill x; fi`; null controls `echo then git pull`, `echo then pkill x` and the existing `git status` stay allowed. Mutants on a copy: dropping `w in RESERVED` fails the reserved-word guard and kill-arm cases; `("cd","pushd")` back to `== "cd"` fails the pushd case.

The earlier round repaired the blocked fix review at 131b1358 (verdict/3294), two blocks:

1. architecture-unsound, design [V4]: the guard arm split a command with its own `re.split` and `shlex`, so `bash -c`, `eval`, `( )` and `$( )` moves of the orchestrator checkout passed. The command-position parser is now its own block, `HPO_PRE_BASH_PARSE_PY`, and `decide` prepends it to each arm through one `arm` function, so neither arm splits a command itself. The parser now records each simple command's argv as well as its word (the kill arm reads the word, the guard reads the argv and follows `cd` in order), and an `eval`'s whole argument list is read as its body (before, only the first word after `eval` was). The guard's own `re.split`/`shlex` loop is deleted.
2. mutation-vacuous: `hooks_setup.py --self-test` gains a case whose `seat_venv.sh --check` refuses (the fixture state holds `orch-checkout` and no `venv-ci`) and asserts the `SEAT-INTERPRETER refused` line, and its in-tree mutant list gains S1 (`if r.returncode == 0:` becomes `if True:`).
3. Found while pinning S1, disclosed here: the in-tree mutant loop of `hooks_setup.py --self-test` was vacuous at 131b1358. It copied `tools/audit/seat` alone, and in that copy the un-mutated self-test was already red (3 cases: no `.claude/settings.json`, no `pre-bash.sh`; with S1, a fourth: no `tests/typing_budgets.json`), so every in-tree mutant counted as killed whatever it did, including the body's five that the review accepted. It now copies what `cases()` reads (`COPY_FOR_MUTANTS`), runs the un-mutated copy first as a null control that must pass, and searches the hook files before `hooks_setup.py`: the stale-digest anchor carries no newline, so it also matched its own literal in the `MUTANTS` list, and that literal took the mutation instead of liveness.py. With the copy repaired, that mutant survived until the search order was fixed.
4. The diff-mutant step (`mutant_run.py --diff`, owner's 2026-11-07 ruling) found unpinned branches in the hooks this PR adds. New cases cover them: liveness.py against a stub `beatd.py` (failed job, `DOWN`, `ALERT`, `STALE-CODE`, a short `JOB` line, exit 2), its alive and digest thresholds half a minute past their defaults, an unparseable `HPO_ALIVE_STALE_MIN`, a missing re-read stamp, a `policy_reread_check.py` that cannot run, an `orch-checkout` naming no directory; seat_interpreter.py against a stub `seat_venv.sh` (passing: silent; refusing: its last line); git_identity.py's `user.name` and a one-line identity file; each hook's bare `--state`; and `hooks_setup`'s check without a project guard, install under a missing directory, and its command line. `_run_hook` now appends `EXIT <rc>` when a hook exits non-zero, so a crash no longer reads as silence.

Alternatives weighed: keeping the guard's splitter and adding `bash -c`/`eval`/`$( )` cases to it lost because it is the duplicate parser [V4] rejects, and it would drift from the kill arm's rules. Making the guard a separate hook lost for the same reason (the design rejected it). Sourcing the parser as a separate `.py` file lost because the hook already carries its python as marked blocks that `extract` reads; one more block keeps the one mechanism.

Not in this part, by the part-scope carry: design P2 (the standing-*.md policy edits, standing.md, orchestrator.md, CLAUDE.md, pulse.py STANDING, sweep_template.md), because open PRs 3245, 3262 and 3267 edit those files and its gate (every P1 row ok from main for one cycle) is unmeasured; carry 25 (the loop-cwd row), because 3262 and 3267 edit beat_jobs.py and beatd.jobs.json (read here, not edited); carry 19 section (1); the P5 carries.

## Mutation proof

The fix review's five probes, each pinned in `bash .claude/hooks/pre-bash.sh --self-test`, each with a mutant applied to a copy of the hook (the real hook untouched) that turns its case red; a one-off driver in scratch, as the reviewer's was:

- P1, the `bash -c` body is never parsed (`if shellc:` becomes `if False:`): KILLED, FAIL `guard: a bash -c body is read`, `guard: a cd inside sh -c is followed`, and the kill arm's `pkill inside bash -c is refused`.
- P2, an `eval`'s words are never collected (`body = []` becomes `body = None`): KILLED, FAIL `guard: an eval body is read`.
- P3, `(` no longer reopens command position (`end(); at = True` becomes `end(); at = False` in the `(` branch): KILLED, FAIL `guard: a subshell's cd is followed`.
- P4, an unquoted `$( )` body is skipped, not parsed: KILLED, FAIL `guard: a $( ) substitution is read` and the kill arm's `kill fed by pgrep in a substitution is refused`.
- P5, the guard ignores `cd` (`cur = under(cur, to[0])` becomes `pass`): KILLED, FAIL `guard: cd then reset is refused`, `guard: a subshell's cd is followed`, `guard: a cd inside sh -c is followed`.
- N0, a comment-only change: SURVIVED, as a null control should.

`hooks_setup.py`'s in-tree mutants, each run in a faithful copy with `--self-test --no-mutants`, naming the case that kills it (a one-off driver in scratch; the in-tree loop runs the same set): null control, the copy un-mutated: rc=0, no FAIL. Install skips the backup: FAIL `install backs the file up first, holding the old bytes`. Install rewrites an unrelated entry: FAIL `install keeps unrelated entries`. Install is not idempotent: FAIL `a second install changes nothing`. Liveness reads no dead loop: FAIL `liveness: a planted dead loop prints DEAD`. Liveness reads no stale digest: FAIL `liveness: a planted stale digest and alive file print STALE` and the 30.5-minute case. S1, seat-interpreter never reports: FAIL `seat-interpreter: a refusing seat_venv.sh --check prints SEAT-INTERPRETER refused` and `the refusal quotes the check's last line`. The null control bites: with `.claude/settings.json` removed from `COPY_FOR_MUTANTS`, `--self-test` prints `FAIL mutant 'null control: the copy un-mutated' is red` and exits 1.

## Block

- class-open (fix-review.md step 6). The first block was gap 4's class: git moves of the orchestrator checkout that reach command position through a shell construct the guard did not read. This repair routes the guard through the shared parser and gives a seam census of 25 seams. That census's rule is the parser's own branches (SEP, the separators, the `(`, `$( )` and backtick recursions, the `-c` and `eval` bodies, the WRAP words, assignment prefixes, `cd`). A rule built from the instrument's own branches is the harness's parameters, not its population: it cannot return a construct the parser does not handle. Opening the class with ordinary bash compound commands, I found seven moves that pass at this head, each exit 0 with `HPO_STATE_DIR/orch-checkout` naming a throwaway repository and the cwd in another repository (ev/guard_probes_head.txt):
  - `if true; then git -C <orch> pull; fi`
  - `if false; then :; else git -C <orch> pull; fi`
  - `if false; then :; elif git -C <orch> pull; then :; fi`
  - `for x in 1; do git -C <orch> pull; done`
  - `while git -C <orch> pull; do :; done`, and the same with `until`
  - `{ git -C <orch> pull; }`
  - `pushd <orch> && git pull`, and `pushd <orch> >/dev/null; git reset --hard`

  In the same run, `case x in x) git -C <orch> pull;; esac` is refused, because `)` reopens command position.

  The cause is in `parse()`. A reserved word at command position is recorded as the command word, so `git` becomes its argument. The guard follows `cd` but not `pushd`, although the design's predicate is the cwd (design.md:194). The body dispositions `timeout 5`, the same kind of parser gap, as a carried finding, but it names none of these. The kill arm shares the parser gap, both at the merge base and at this head: `if true; then pkill x; fi`, `{ pkill x; }`, `for ...; do pkill x; done` and `while ...; do killall y; done` all exit 0 (ev/kill_arm_reserved_words.txt).

  Cure: in `parse()`, treat `if then else elif do while until {` at command position as still at command position, as WRAP words are, and have the guard treat `pushd` as it treats `cd`. Pin one guard case and one kill-arm case of the reserved-word form, and one pushd case, each with a mutant. My plant of the reserved-word half confirms the cure is cheap: one predicate turns every probe above to exit 2 (including the kill arm's `then pkill x`), keeps `git -C <orch> status` and `echo then git pull` at exit 0, and keeps `pre-bash.sh --self-test` at 41 passed, 0 failed (ev/cure_plant.txt). The other acceptable cure is a disposition: name each construct in the body as a carried parser finding, as `timeout` is. Given what the guard exists for, the first cure is the sound one.

So `git --git-dir=<orch>/.git --work-tree=<orch> reset --hard` (both spellings) and `GIT_DIR=<orch>/.git GIT_WORK_TREE=<orch> git reset --hard` pass (exit 0, ev/guard_probes_head.txt). merges.body:
R10-OUTSIDE-INTAKE. The owner's ruling (tvofi 2026-11-06), verbatim: "the plan html for an ongoing round should be made publically available from a suitable place in the developer documentation on the repo. During future audit rounds, issues, PRs or other posts from outside users should be regularly checked, triaged/designed and planned. Fold this shape into the repo machinery. When the plan html is done, and any outside submission is on the roster, the plan HTML should be linked in an answer to the outside submission."

**Policy and developer docs change: this merges only on tvofi's approving review** (`orchestrator.md` section 5, `standing-dispatch.md`, `dev/programme/HANDOVER.md`). The ruling approves the shape in principle. The review is the approval.

What lands, by the brief's three parts:

1. **Public plan page.** `tools/audit/seat/plan_public.py stage` takes `PLAN.html` from the newest `origin/handoff/audit-r<N>-plan` state ref (the layout `state_docs.state_of` owns) and writes `plan/index.html`. `.github/workflows/pages.yml` runs it from the dispatched ref's tree. It then checks out the newest `v*` tag for the docs and adds the page, served at `https://tvofi.github.io/heatpump_optimizer/plan/` (`plan_public.PLAN_URL`, the one spelling of the URL). The beat's `plan-beat` row dispatches `pages.yml` on `main` after each state push that landed. `dev/programme/HANDOVER.md` links the page from the head of its Round 10 section; no user doc links it. If `ref_privacy` reads a host path, account name, uid, scratch root or a tool's attribution in the page, it refuses the page (rc 1: the deploy goes red and nothing is published). With no state ref, or no `PLAN.html` at the newest one, it stages nothing (rc 2): the site deploys without a plan and warns. A closed round's state ref stays the newest until `closeout.py --apply` deletes it, so the closed round's page is served until then. `plan_public.py`'s docstring and the `pages.yml` header now say so (round 6).
2. **Intake as machinery.** `tools/audit/seat/outside_intake.py list` lists threads (issues, pull requests and discussions, which share one number space). It lists a thread when it has activity at or after a cursor by an author who is outside `OURS` and not a bot. It prints the `OUTSIDE #N owed=triage|answer|reply` lines owed this turn. Disposition is read from the roster (`issues`/`fixes`, wired by `roster_edit.py wire-issue`) and from marker comments by our accounts, never from memory. The new beat row `outside-intake` [1800 s] runs it with a cursor under the digest's `state/` and writes its lines to the digest. Sweep step (5b) in `sweep_template.md` names the action for each line. `orchestrator.md` section 5 and `standing-dispatch.md` each carry the short obligation.
3. **Answer step.** `outside_intake.py answer --issue N` posts the plan link through `tools/pr/gh_comment.py post`, whose read-back is the proof. It marks the comment. A marker is read only from a comment by an account in `OURS`, and only `saw()` moves a thread's outside activity, so a third-party bot's comment is neither ours nor outside activity. It refuses a thread already answered or refused, so none is answered twice. It also refuses a thread on no roster group, any thread while the plan page does not answer, and a discussion. `refuse --issue N --reason-file F` records a refusal the same way.

Alternatives, and why each lost (`fixer.md` step 17):

- **A committed path under `docs/`.** It needs a commit to `main` at every sweep, each a pull request through the gate, for a generated file.
- **Pages from a push to the state ref.** A workflow runs from the pushed commit's own tree. The orphan state ref carries no `.github/`, so a `push:` trigger there never fires.
- **A `schedule:` trigger.** It runs 48 deploys a day whether or not the plan moved. It would also change the trigger set `tests/entities.py` pins (release tags plus dispatch).

The dispatch keeps that pinned set. One existing behaviour changes: a dispatch now serves the newest release's docs rather than the dispatched ref's. That matches the workflow's stated design ("the served page is the release HACS installs"), and it keeps a plan refresh from publishing main's unreleased docs. The owner may prefer otherwise; this is the change to review.

## Re-cut note

Round 6. This is a minimal re-cut of the round-5 block (`verdict/3262`, ci-red). The block is cured by a fresh head, and this round also takes the four findings that verdict carried to R10-OUTSIDE-INTAKE. The plan_public.py lines the round-5 reviewer found cured are untouched: the CLI case, the `host_ident_dropped` and `main_rc0` mutants, and the runner.

- **A fresh head.** `10bd5426d`, `f6a7b52fe` and `8eac7a704` are clean merges of `origin/main`, the last at `364353e670f666be6c97a5942ffa0bea9132b5ce`, so the head's runs start anew.
- **The false sentence is corrected.** In both `plan_public.py`'s docstring and the `pages.yml` header, "between rounds there is no page" now reads like this:
  - A closed round's state ref stays the newest until `closeout.py --apply` deletes it, so its page is served until then.
  - The page is absent only when there is no state ref, or no `PLAN.html` at the newest one.
  - Source: `closeout.py`'s `refs` step (2) is the only step that deletes remote branches, and it runs only under `--apply`.
- **`main_url_rc1` is killed.** A new `plan_public.py` case, "url prints PLAN_URL alone, rc 0", runs `main(["url"])` and requires rc 0 and stdout of exactly `PLAN_URL` plus a newline. The mutant `main_url_rc1` is entered in `MUTANTS`.
- **`scan_disc_kind` is killed.** A new `outside_intake_selftest.py` case, "discussions: a discussion opened before the cursor, its new outside comment listed as a discussion", covers discussion #3262. It was opened before `SINCE`, and an outside comment came after it. The case requires the line `OUTSIDE #3262 owed=triage discussion by=asker since=2026-11-06T10:00:00Z`; the mutant prints `comment`.
- **`owed_reply_ge` is killed.** A new case, "reply: outside activity in our answer's own second owes nothing; one second later owes a reply", drives `owed()` on two threads. In the first, outside activity falls in the same second as our answer and owes `None`. In the second it falls one second later and owes `reply`.
  - **This case encodes a design choice** (`fixer.md` step 11). GitHub stamps to the second, so a same-second outside comment cannot be ordered against our answer.
  - The choice is that only activity strictly after our latest comment owes a reply. The alternative, `>=`, would owe a reply on that tie. Both directions are defensible. This one keeps the production predicate unchanged, and the case names the tie, so a later seat that reads the tie the other way is reversing a stated choice rather than fixing a bug.
- Both new entries go in `outside_intake_selftest.py`'s `MUTANTS`.
- **Carry 1 is not this PR's work.** It is the group's part 2, prototyped at `handoff-wip/r10-outside-intake-p2`, and the carry itself says it starts after #3262 merges. This round leaves it untouched.

No production line moved. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reported no conflict, so main was not merged; origin/main had not moved since the last prepr run (merge base `7c9c4c154cda514f938fd503cde2779716caf251`).

The previous head `0ac370fa2` was a conflict resolution by merge: one merge commit whose parents are the previous head `33c3dd998d2413452fa6aec5c331a0a7e9c0c579` and `origin/main` at `8a1358e8448e6734ed16982f25da6aae223ba8b9`. The merge conflicted in `tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py`, `tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs_selftest.py` and `tools/audit/seat/instruments/beat_jobs.py.md`; `tests/closures.json` and `sweep_template.md` merged without a conflict. Review only the resolution delta and the round 7 test commit: `git show --cc 0ac370fa2`, which prints just the hunks that differ from both parents.

- `beat_jobs.py` docstring: `plan-beat` keeps main's `PLAN MOVED` sentence, then this branch's `pages.yml` dispatch sentences. The `gantt` and `verdict-audit` docs are main's.

A state push that landed (`pushed ` on rc 0 or 1) dispatches `pages.yml`, and a refused dispatch adds `PAGES NOT DISPATCHED`. A single `write_job` call writes the list.

Carry 2 (self-test-reads file-key plant) and Carry 3 part (c) (BOOTSTRAP remedy) are included. Repair round 1 (verdict: mutation-vacuous, 9 of 20 reviewer mutants on added `ci_predict.py` lines survived the full self-test, plus S): `graders_self_test` gains a planted pr-contract-shaped workflow and `summary_line` is factored out of `main` so the closing line is pinned; no behaviour changes.

## Head

`987f88c7fac15ebd9a56466e531c7c3b36a405b1` merges main `7336569` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

Every figure below was re-taken at this head. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0 (no conflict) against origin/main d2e4d2d10cfe at 2026-11-08T02:58Z, so main is not merged again here; the merge train recarries.

## Mutation proof

`python3 -I dev/audit/rca/prepr-head-graders/mutants.py .` runs each mutant against `graders_self_test` from a copy of tools/pr/ and prints its failing checks. M1..M7 as before now read M1 11 FAIL, M2 1, M3 2, M4 1, M5 4, M6 6, M7 10. The reviewer's surviving mutants are added as R1-I, K, L, O, P, E, H, F, N, S; each is killed at this head: R1-I (run regex drops bash/.sh) 4 FAIL, R1-K (no-body skip off) 1, R1-L (event tokens unsubstituted) 1, R1-O ($INTENDED stood in empty) 1, R1-P (stdin redirect dropped) 1, R1-E (partial missing-input swallow deleted) 1, R1-H (stdout redirect kept as arguments) 1, R1-F (collision key always the bare job) 5, R1-N (codescan_wait exemption deleted) 1, R1-S (summary always owes a repair) 1. R1-P first hung (the planted `p/pre.sh` read an inherited stdin); the plant reads it through `timeout 5 cat`, and the mutant now fails in seconds. The new cases: a `bash p/pre.sh $INTENDED < /tmp/pr-body.md` run (args and stdin read back), a `--head "$PR_HEAD" --title "$PR_TITLE" --author "$(cat ...)" > out.txt` run, a partial run printing "reviews could not be read", a plain refusing run, two workflows sharing a job name, a run with no body, the pr-contract exemption, and the `.sh` run in `want`. Carry 2's mutant R1 is as in the prior body (1 FAIL), not re-run.

## Null control

Unmutated head: `python3 -I tools/pr/ci_predict.py --self-test` prints `ci_predict self-test: 0 failed`, and `graders_self_test` alone prints `bad 0`. The new cases carry their own nulls: the no-body tree still runs the plain program; the plain run's refusal is reported where the partial one's is not; `summary_line(2, 1, ...)` still owes a repair where `(2, 2, ...)` does not; the pr-contract preflight run is graded where codescan_wait is exempt. ## Figures

- `python3 -I dev/audit/rca/prepr-head-graders/mutants.py .` (counts above; the instrument is the mutant list in that file).
- `git grep -n -- "- name: Restore the check source from the base commit" HEAD -- .github/workflows/` returns six jobs; graders_self_test asserts the arm's job count equals that grep's count (the enumeration rule; M7 kills it).
- `MUTANT_CMD="bash <script that git-inits the archive copy and runs graders_self_test>" MUTANT_MAX=60 bash tools/pr/prepr.sh`: diff-mutant step, wall time of the whole prepr 36 m 8 s (`time`), 14 survivors (dispositions under `## Unpinned sites`). A first run with a MUTANT_CMD that did not git-init the copy printed BASELINE FAILS and ran no mutant.

- `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED.

The `ci predict` step is ok, "no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted".
- `tools/audit/seat/handoff_push.sh` refused with `app_push: REFUSE: App id file missing or empty (fail closed)`; the code head was pushed to refs/heads/handoff/r10-fly-cipredict-restoring directly, fast-forward, which moves the existing pull request; no row or retitle was written by this seat.

## Unpinned sites

14 survivors of the diff-mutant step (report only), all in the repair's own added lines: 1236 `sum(2 ...)` in `main` (the count of BOOTSTRAP reds fed to `summary_line`; the closing line itself is pinned by direct calls, the counting expression is not driven by a main-level case); 1459 `>=` for `>` (equivalent here, the count equality beside it is what pins the job set); 1559, 1566, 1639, 1640, 1688 (`pass`/`if False:` deletions of test-side bookkeeping calls: the mutant edits the self-test, not the predicate it grades); 1589, 1622, 1634-1636, 1709, 1710 (constants and comparison bounds inside the self-test's own assertions; each is a weaker assertion of a property whose strict form is separately asserted or killed by the production mutants above). None is a production predicate other than the 1236 counting expression, left as a stated gap.

Landed in this PR: Carry 2 and Carry 3 part (c). Still owed, each carried by this group's roster entry:

- Carry 1 (inline_scan arm for `parents[N]` harnesses). Carry: R10-FLY-CIPREDICT-RESTORING | dismissed: still owed, already stated in this group's own roster carries; re-homing at merge is the orchestrator's roster write (the review raised it).

- L `a = ctx.get(a, a)` -> `a = a`: `$PR_BASE`, `$PR_HEAD`, `$PR_TITLE` and the others go unsubstituted.

The surviving set is the pr-contract stand-in path: argument substitution, stdin, the body skip and the `.sh` population. It is the machinery that makes the issue's pr-contract case gradable at all, and nothing pins it. Part 2 of R10-TRAIN-MERGE-LOOP (#3242), repair round 2 after `Fix review: blocked 35fc2646` (class-open: `tools/pr/app_approve.sh` carry-path `git fetch` unretried). The round adds two commits on top of the reviewed head 35fc2646, which is unchanged beneath them; the head is 17b8194e, which merges origin/main 48af0864 (#3290) into 022a55fd to resolve one content conflict (see Resolution delta).

Carry N is the 1-based position in this group's carry list on the roster (handoff/audit-r10-roster); the parent's numbers are noted.
- Carry 15 (the hotfix): `wait_ci` treats a red `gate` as pending while another workflow run at the same head is unfinished (read from actions/runs?head_sha, not check-run presence), then allows one poll for gate.py's rerun cascade. Bounded by the polls. A held (`action_required`) sibling run is not unfinished: this round pins that.
- Carry 1, Carry 8 and Carry 16 (parent carry 3): a bot tip whose pull_request runs are all approved is no longer refused; held, absent or unreadable runs keep the BOT_HEAD refusal.
- Carry 2 and Carry 10 (parent carry 6): `merge_train.py add --wait-post-approval [--poll] [--budget-hours]`, one module-level predicate (gate runs started at or after the approval, head pin, red refusal rc 2, budget rc 3). This round pins the verdict-comment half of its predicate.
- Carry 3, Carry 7, Carry 9, Carry 11 and Carry 17 (parent carries 7 and 17): one git-transient rule for every git fetch/push the train reaches. This round moves the rule (`GIT_TRANSIENT`, `GIT_REFUSED`, `git_transient`) and its bounded loop (`run_git_retry`, `GIT_TRIES`) from merge_train.py into `tools/audit/seat/gh_read.py`, the module that already owns the train's GitHub-transport retry rule, and exposes it as `--classify-git` and `--git-retry` for the shell callers. The 18 merge_train.py fetch/push sites reach it through `Train._reads_retried`. `tools/pr/app_approve.sh`'s carry fetch (the blocked seam) now retries through its own read loop (`retry_with`, generalised from `read_with`), classified by `gh_read.py --classify-git`. `tools/audit/seat/remerge_main.sh`'s recarry fetch, a further seam the class census returned, runs under `gh_read.py --git-retry`. Before this, one 502 there printed `MERGE CONFLICT` and stopped the train.
- Carry 4 and Carry 12 (parent carry 8): `pages()` in r10_codescan_wait_race.py falls back to per_page=30 after ghapi.get's own 5xx retries.
- Carry 5 and Carry 13 (parent carry 9): undraft only a head recorded `draft: true` at add; a failed ready or a re-draft is a Stop. This round keys each arm's test on its own Stop text.
- Carry 6 and Carry 14 (parent carry 16): remerge_main.sh prints FAIL and `full log:` lines and keeps the push log when nothing was pushed.

Alternatives for the shared rule: (a) copy the regexes into app_approve.sh: rejected, because it would be a second copy of the classifier. (b) A new module: rejected, because gh_read.py already holds the train's transport rule and app_approve.sh already shells to it (`--classify`), and a new file would need its own closure classification. (c) app_approve.sh calling `--git-retry`: rejected, because its self-test stubs `sleep` on PATH and runs each case under a 10 s deadline, and a Python `time.sleep` would sleep for real. So app_approve.sh shares the classifier and keeps its read loop's 4-try 5/15/45 s schedule. merge_train.py and remerge_main.sh share both the classifier and the 3-try 5/15 s loop.

- Conflict: `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py`, two hunks, from #3290 (R10-HOTFIX-TRAIN-DEFER-WAIT, 48af0864). Hunk 1: #3288's `gate_deferred` against #3290's `_gate_busy` and `classify_at`. Hunk 2: #3288's `graced = False` against #3290's `held`/`settle` in `wait_ci`.

## Mutation proof

The gh_read.py CLI, `_run_captured` and `run_git_retry`'s log survived because MUTANT_CMD ran only merge_train.py's self-test. gh_read's self-test now drives them (7 new checks), and the rerun with gh_read's self-test in MUTANT_CMD kills every one of them.

## Null control

A rejected carry fetch (`couldn't find remote ref`) is one fetch, no settle, refused with git's text appended. A rejected recarry fetch is one fetch and still prints `MERGE CONFLICT 7`: a second fetch would have succeeded, so the arm shows it was not retried. A git rejection mixed with a 502 is not transient (merge_train's `_git_retry_self_test` table, now reading `gh_read.git_transient`). A red gate with no unfinished sibling run still returns red on the first poll. A review plus a `Fix review: merge <head>` comment with a green post-approval gate adds (rc 0). A re-drafted head stops as "is a draft again", not as a failed ready.

## Figures

- `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` prints `523 checks, 0 failed` at 022a55fd (35fc2646: 519). At 17b8194e it prints `564 checks, 0 failed` (main's #3290 arms merged in).

It returns app_approve.sh's carry fetch, closed in this diff. It returns remerge_main.sh's recarry fetch, closed in this diff. train.sh returns none. The census also reaches app_push.sh's pushes, which the train runs through remerge_main.sh. They are outside this group's files, and app_push.sh's read-back rule already confirms a push. ## Block

Round 1. Measured head `e3094246142cdfa6028f8c92bf9a42b0d548f2c7`, merge base `4b5d771bdf8feb1f83d7d9443e5117b771a0ab76`.

`R10-RCA-CI-RED.md` section 3 defines group A as "Run cancelled or gate deferral, no check failed on the diff: 8 entries, 8 PRs" and lists #3219 in it. The check runs at #3219's blocked head `aca500910` (read with `filter=all`, every page) show `tests / mutation` concluded `failure` at 2026-11-05T04:18:12Z (job 127045678304), before the `ci-red` verdict at 04:32:06Z. Its log, line 6869: `MUTATION TABLE REFUSED -- 3175 unpinned site(s) against 3174 at the ratchet base 78a2be77c..., 1 of them added by this diff.` That is a red on the diff, the same mechanism as #3195's third entry, which the record files under D. `tests / replay` also failed at 04:38:35Z, after the verdict.

So the 8 / 4 / 4 / 2 split, group A's 110 min mean (769 over 7), P_A = 8 / 93, and section 4's "A is state (d)" over all eight entries do not re-derive under the record's own rule. The cheap fix: move #3219 to D (or to C, if its body's Red checks omitted the mutation red, as its verdict suggests stale Red checks), then re-take the section 3 counts and the section 5 table. It changes no conclusion about B, which is the record's one built-later countermeasure.

## Findings

- #3219 (`aca500910`) is misclassified into group A; tests / mutation failed on an unpinned site its own diff added (job 127045678304, log line 6869) before the verdict, so group A's count, mean and P, and group D's (or C's) count, are wrong. Carry: R10-FRICTION-CI-RED

- `entries.py W.json ci-red` reproduces `entries_v7.1.2.tsv` byte for byte (`diff` empty, `ev/entries_review.tsv`). `ci-redd` gives `ENTRIES 0 PRS 0`. Null control: I rewrote #3189's `ci-red` verdict to `ci-redx` in a copy of the cache, and the output moved to `ENTRIES 17 PRS 13` (`ev/null_control.txt`).
- Check runs for all 18 heads, `filter=all`, every page fetched explicitly: `ev/checkruns_all/`, summary in `summary.txt`. The default `filter=latest` view, in `ev/checkruns/`, hides cancelled-then-rerun runs, e.g. #3181's and #3217's codeql cancellations. Apart from #3219, every row's named red appears there: the codeql cancellations at #3181, #3217 and #3244 first; the prelude/gate cancellations at #3167 second and #3204; nothing but gate at #3240; full cancellation at #3211; fast at #3180, #3189, #3208 and #3242; typing at #3195 first; CodeQL at #3244 second; instrument-self-tests and fast at #3227.

- Policy: the record changes neither the keying rule nor the gate. The vocabulary change (C) is stated as policy awaiting the owner, and nothing of it is applied. The cancellation and D refusals are recorded. All three forward-carries name #3156, which the body says is not to close on this record.
- Body: `Disposes #3156` with no closing keyword. The delivery row `dev/programme/delivery/3295.md` is in the diff. VERSION, manifest and RELEASE_NOTES.md are untouched (three-dot diff is the 5 listed files). `## Head` names `e3094246` with code head `809d97772`; the only later commit adds the delivery row.
- Merge: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0 (tree `a8268e493`).
- CI: `merge_train.py classify e3094246... --pr 3295` gives `GREEN e3094246142cdfa6028f8c92bf9a42b0d548f2c7 pending: none red: none`, rc 0 (`ev/classify1.txt`). The packet's `tests / nightly-status` failure is not this PR's: the diff does not reach what it reads. So `## Red checks: none` stands.

I re-derived the split from the tsv's 18 rows: A 7 entries / 7 PRs (#3167 second, #3181, #3204, #3211, #3217, #3240, #3244 first); B 4 / 4; C 4 entries / 3 PRs; D 3 / 3; 7+4+4+3 = 18. The two extra entries are #3265 and #3273, both merged after `4b5d771bd` (`87082a25a`, `53273de4d`). `entries.py` on that cache prints the record's 18 rows byte-identical as its first 18 lines, plus those two (`ev/entries_review.tsv`). - Rules 2 and 3 (root-cause.md, defect-root-cause.md): every group has a named cause. B, C and D have states (c), (b) and n/a; A has (d) with the deferral sub-cause stated as not established. The cost test carries numbers. B's countermeasure is owed later with the red/green demonstration named. C is stated as policy awaiting the owner, and nothing of it is applied. A (runner kills) and D carry recorded refusals. The record changes neither the keying rule nor the gate. The three-dot diff touches no file under `.claude/`, `tools/`, `tests/` or `.github/`.

The edit-kind `gate` job 128613059066 (run 42441205339) concluded failure at 03:28:36Z with the line `FAIL run(s) [42441204994] at this head are still being judged; their gate decides`. That is the edit/code deferral, superseded by the code run's gate, which classify reads green. merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-WHY-NOW-WIDGET (tvofi 2026-11-01, rulings card 2 option (c) part (b)): a live "Why now" block for the current slot, built to the approved note at design/R10-WHY-NOW-WIDGET 60d61fcf (verdict 043b31ad). The solver publishes five signed drivers per step (`price_rank`, `comfort_floor`, `mold_guard`, `away`, `forecast`). Each is a percent of that step's push, and the magnitudes sum to 100. `get_current_action` carries step i's drivers through `slot_drivers.why_now_at`, at the one index it already finds. The space-plan sensor publishes them as `why_now`, and the card renders them after the headline narrative, in en and sv, with the metric in plain words as every hover.

**Owning seam.** A new pure module, `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/slot_drivers.py` (numpy, no Home Assistant import). `_build_result` calls `slot_drivers.space_drivers` once. The away setback enters as a solver input, `SolveLimits.away_floor_drop_c`, from `away.floor_drop_c`, which shares `_setback_target` with `solve_bands`, so the setback's condition is written once. `_build_comfort_bounds` returns a fourth element, (the comfort floor before the mold guard, the padded mold floor), which `_Horizon` carries to the drivers.

**Coordinator growth (r3-b), the whole of it.**
- `_solve_record` passes one kwarg (`away_floor_drop_c=`).
- The module-level `_apply_result_payload` copies `why_now` when the action carries one.
- `HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator` gains no method body and no attribute, so there is no seam_map entry. The what-if solve is untouched.

**Departures from the note, each raised here.**
- `_Horizon` carries a third field, `away_floor_drops`, beside `comfort_floors` and `mold_floors`. `_build_result` sees only the horizon, and `_Horizon` is the per-solve carrier by its own docstring.
- `slot_drivers.step_reasons` owns step i's `space_reason` and `dhw_reason` reads as well as `why_now`.
- The attribute comes from a `SpaceHeatingPlanSensor.extra_state_attributes` override, not from inside `_PlanSensorBase`'s 150-line method.
- No `coord_*` claim: the coord captures never solve, so no why_now key can reach them.
- The card's tile and Plan-page figures under docs/img/card were re-taken after card_browser.mjs's P40 refused them.
- `knownCodes` is the one unknown-code filter shared by the score and the why-now block.
- The card shows each weight as a whole signed percent.

**Brief carries.**
- Carry 1, the group's spec from the owner's 2026-11-01 ruling, is implemented whole. Its strings are verbatim in en and sv, except the two sentences of the metric explanation round 5 rewords (finding 1).
- Carry 2 and Carry 3 (PR 3198 item 7c609975, the same P9 defect recorded twice) are the clip-walk fix: `unreachable()` in tests/card_browser.mjs starts its walk at `run.el`, so it reports a run clipped by its own box.

**This pass (repair round 6: the closures red at 4f8ab9654).**
- **The red.** The previous pass made tests/features.py import `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_demand_overbook.py` to drive `comfort_schedule`. That file sat on the `dev/audit/harnesses/` INERT prefix, so `tests / closures` (job 128558742815) read INERT READS UNDER-APPROXIMATED on features.py, and `tests / closures-autofix` (job 128558743106) ended skip-merge-failed. The recorder cannot file a file that a script imports in-process under `inert_reads` alone, and the merge refuses a file that is both INERT and recorded.
- **The fix (e51073c67).** The harness joins `INERT_EXCEPT` in tests/closure.py, with a comment naming the read and the job, the way `record_burst_replay.py` did. Then `./tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/features.py` adds it to features.py's closure. So an edit to the harness now selects tests/features.py, which pins it. Two alternatives lost. Filing the read under `inert_reads` would leave the harness INERT while features.py reads it, which is the pair the merge refuses. Dropping the import from features.py would undo the previous pass's class fix: a stale caller would again raise only in a lane nobody runs.
- **Its consequence (69f76c2b3).** With the harness off the prefix, `tests/harness_headers.py`'s read of it had to be in that closure too. prepr.sh step 6d predicted UNDER-SCOPED on `tests / closures`, and the prepr self-test's `pleftrec` null control failed on the same entry. `./tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/harness_headers.py` files it, beside the `inert_reads` entry that record_burst_replay.py also keeps.
- No production line changes in this pass.

**Round 5 (repair for fix review blocked 97786d25), carried unchanged.** The class fix: every caller of `_build_comfort_bounds` reads the 4-tuple, and the harness caller reads through `comfort_schedule`. Finding 1: the metric text is reworded, not gated. Finding 2: `why_now` is in `_PlanSensorBase._unrecorded_attributes`. Finding 3: mutants C, D and E each have a killing check. One new check kills four diff-mutant survivors. Its mutation proofs are below. Its figures were measured at 9cde30560 and 0765b49d9, and each is labelled with its SHA.

## Head

`178dc0feb4dc4fa6ca11e784290d41862cd0f272` merges main `d2e4d2d` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`dbf79f836ea9acf89f3a076a94fa5c45962e2e88` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

69f76c2b365cd3e2cc306bb1a18f99c306a64d89, merge base 8a1358e8448e6734ed16982f25da6aae223ba8b9.
- 4f8ab9654 is the relay's merge of origin/main into the round-5 tip 0765b49d9. This pass adds two commits above it, e51073c67 and 69f76c2b3. `git diff --name-only 4f8ab9654 69f76c2b3` is tests/closure.py and tests/closures.json.
- At 2026-11-08T00:10Z, origin/main was 17e1157925908bd69addb58ed824c1ac22bfa82f. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` returns rc 0 with no conflict. Per the owner ruling of 2026-11-07, main was not merged.
- Re-taken in this pass: the closure checks, tests/features.py under the recorder, tests/entities.py, the card checks, the harness `--dp` run, the diff-mutant run, structure.py, the archscore run and prepr.sh. The scoped gate is `MODE: FULL` at this head (see Figures), so the full suite is CI's to run.

## Mutation proof

- This pass's fix. Remove the `INERT_EXCEPT` entry, which is the tree at 4f8ab9654. `python3 tests/closure.py check --in-dir $REC --partial` then exits rc 1 ("1 closure(s) are stale. Re-derive the named script"). At 69f76c2b3 the same recording reads rc 0. `$REC` is `./tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/features.py --record-only --out-dir $REC`, recorded at e51073c67.
- Its consequence. At e51073c67, without 69f76c2b3's closure line, prepr.sh step 6d printed `PREDICT tests / closures UNDER-SCOPED tests/harness_headers.py: dev/audit/harnesses/r10_demand_overbook.py leaves INERT in this diff`. At 69f76c2b3, `tools/pr/ci_predict.py --base 8a1358e8448e` reads `no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted`.
- Round 5's proofs stand, because this pass changes no line they mutate:
  - The class: a 3-tuple unpack at the harness site or the production site raises `ValueError('too many values to unpack (expected 3, got 4)')`.
  - C: FAIL "at every step the rows run largest magnitude first, an idle push ahead of a smaller run push".
  - D: FAIL "_solve_record hands the solve away.floor_drop_c while away, None at home".
  - E: FAIL "the drivers' comfort floor is the margined floor, below the mold floor's raise".
  - slot_drivers.py :84, :96, :118 and :143: FAIL "the forecast window floors at one step and clips at -1; comfort clips at -1; step_reasons past the end is None".
  - Finding 1: the card checks FAIL "why-now: every en string has its sv twin, and every driver code has a label and an explanation".
  - Finding 2: `why_now` is absent from `_unrecorded_attributes` without the sensor line.
  - sensor.py:1637 RETURN_DEL: tests/entities.py exits rc 1 with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'`.
  - The earlier passes' M1–M14, C1–C9 and the 14 `--pin-killed` sites.

## Null control

- The closure check at 4f8ab9654 against the same recording exits rc 1, and at 69f76c2b3 rc 0. So the check reads the defect.
- `--single tests/features.py` reports `would drop 1 file(s) the committed closure listed; keeping them` (tests/replay/owner-2026-10-30-away.json). The `--partial` merge keeps it, so the closure only grew, by the one harness line.
- The harness `--dp` run prints the same `dp_learned.gap -0.0006` and `dp_true.gap -0.0012` at 69f76c2b3 as at 9cde30560 and 53273de4.
- tests/entities.py fails the same 3 workflow probes it fails at the round-5 base 53273de4: the coverage job's cache key, the release ZIP and the Pages workflow. The diff touches no file they read.

## Figures

- Gate scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir $D` at e51073c67 printed `MODE: FULL -- every test script runs, nothing is scoped out.` with the reason `tests/closure.py changes the gate itself, so every closure is suspect`. That is a gate-file diff, not CI to reproduce (fixer.md step 5).
- Closure check: `python3 tests/closure.py check --in-dir $REC --partial` at 69f76c2b3 printed `closure: committed closures cover every file this run touched`, rc 0.
- `./tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/features.py` at e51073c67: exit 0. The recorded run's output reads `ALL 4937 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`.
- `./tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/harness_headers.py` at 69f76c2b3: exit 0, `tests/harness_headers.py 404 files`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` at e51073c67: `3 of 2657 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`, the 3 workflow probes under Null control.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_demand_overbook.py --one owner_i01 dp` at 69f76c2b3: rc 0, `dp_learned.gap -0.0006`, `dp_true.gap -0.0012`.
- `node tests/card.mjs` (after `tests/plan_view.py`) at 69f76c2b3: ALL CARD CHECKS PASSED. `node tests/card_drift.mjs origin/main`: `card_drift: 1 state(s) moved and claimed, 44 identical`.
- Diff mutants: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff 8a1358e8448e...HEAD --cmd "<MUTANT_CMD>" --max-mutants 66 --report-only` at 69f76c2b3 ran all 66 mutants. The count is `--list`'s `MUTANT` lines. Wall time was 586 s. There were 3 survivors:
  - sensor.py:1637 RETURN_DEL: killed by tests/entities.py, which is outside the block (Mutation proof).
  - slot_drivers.py:23 GUARD_OFF: equivalent, because the guarded imports are type-only under `from __future__ import annotations`.
  - slot_drivers.py:136 CMP_BOUND: equivalent, triaged at `tests/mutation_ledger/survivor_triage/slot_drivers.py/_direction.CMP_BOUND.23463a3d.json`.
  - `MUTANT_CMD` is `env PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests python3 tools/audit/seat/features_block.py --prelude 'from types import SimpleNamespace' --prelude 'from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import ThermalModel, ThermalParameters, ThermalState' '# --- R10-WHY-NOW-WIDGET: per-slot drivers' '# R10-CLONE-2238 (#2238'`. prepr.sh step 6d' at e51073c67 printed the same 3 survivors.
- `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`: `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED.
- Claim files: three-dot `git diff 8a1358e8...HEAD -- tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` is empty. card_claimed_drift.txt carries only this branch's `score_open` entry, under `claims-for:` equal to VERSION. VERSION, the manifest version and RELEASE_NOTES.md are untouched.
- Round 5, at 9cde30560 / 0765b49d9 (carried):
  - The class census, `git grep -n '_build_comfort_bounds(' -- custom_components tools tests dev ':!*.tsv'`, returned 12 lines. Each is dispositioned in round 5's body: one def, one production caller, one harness caller, five older and four new features.py lines.
  - The harness rc census returned 65 scripts, each with the same rc at head and base.
  - The why-now block alone: ALL 25 FEATURES BLOCK PASSED.
- `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh <this body>` at 69f76c2b3, with MUTANT_CMD as above and MUTANT_MAX=66: `PRE-PR: 69f76c2b365cd3e2cc306bb1a18f99c306a64d89 … rc=0`. It printed `CI PREDICT: no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted against 8a1358e8448e` and `ancestry reds: the body answers every red this branch pushed`. The code-scanning alert read was skipped (`HTTP 403`), as the step prints. The run was clean at the first head where it ran clean. Per the owner ruling, main was neither merged nor re-run against.

## Unpinned sites

none. This pass adds no production line. The added lines are an `INERT_EXCEPT` tuple entry with its comment, and two closure-table lines. The round-5 diff-mutant survivors are dispositioned under Figures.

## Red checks

These are the concluded reds of 4f8ab9654, on the single check-run page, total_count 68:
- `tests / closures`, job 128558742815 (run 42419763628): `INERT READS UNDER-APPROXIMATED ... tests/features.py: dev/audit/harnesses/r10_demand_overbook.py`. Class: a real closure defect of this branch, repaired in e51073c67 and 69f76c2b3. Cheaper detector: one exists, and it is already in the tree. `./tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/features.py`, or `PREPR_RECORD_CLOSURES=1`, records the read in about 10 minutes, and its merge names the INERT pair.
