Claim: the shipped metric text says "The reasons behind this hour's decision ... the arrow shows whether it pushes the heat pump to run or to idle ... A high share means that reason mostly decides the hour". Harness: this is my own instrument, not the finder's (no finder harness exists; owner report). `ev/claim.py`, run at head, makes 12 production solves: 4 price profiles (flat_null, daily_curve, cheap_night, spiky) × room 20/21/22 °C, 24 h at 15 min, a sinusoidal outdoor temperature around −5 °C. At each step with `why_now_at` not None it compares the sign of the net push (Σ weights) and the top driver's direction with whether the solver actually ran (power_schedule > 0.05 kW). Metrics, per config:
  - Net-push agreement with run/idle: 37, 49, 59 (flat_null); 55, 57, 59 (daily_curve); 73, 67, 66 (cheap_night); 27, 34, 47 (spiky), each out of 96.
  - Top-driver agreement: 37–69 of 96.
  - The trivial "always idle" predictor scores 75–82 of 96 in every config, so the widget does worse than it in all 12.
  - Null control (flat prices, where price_rank is 0): 37 to 59 of 96, all non-neutral. The design's own all-neutral null needs flat weather, and a real forecast is never flat.
  - Top driver against the solver's own `space_reasons[i]`: frequent pairs are (comfort_floor, idle_coasting), (price_rank, idle_dearer) and (comfort_floor, cheap_price) (ev/claim_head.log).
  - Perturbation: negating every weight maps each agreement count a to n − a. For example, flat_null at 20 °C goes from 37 to 59. That figure is derived, not re-run.
  - Cause, as I read it: `comfort_floor` is computed from the solved room trajectory, and `price_rank` ranks a step against the whole horizon whatever the slab's state. Neither is the solver's marginal reason, so the dominant row often points away from what the pump does.
  - Status: the approved note never claimed agreement with the decision. The brief's point (2) asks for it, and the UI text asserts it. The fix is either to measure and gate an agreement figure against this baseline, or to reword the metric so it does not say the rows decide the hour. Either needs a design ruling. Carry: R10-WHY-NOW-WIDGET

- Surviving mutant E, optimizer.py `_build_comfort_bounds`: deleting `comfort_floors = temp_min_bounds` after the confidence margins are applied leaves tests/features.py at rc 0. merges.body:
Beat-only dispatch (P404) and one window for rules 4 and 5 (P403), from triage batch 132 (dev/programme/triage/s6-batch132.md), repaired for the blocked fix review at 01e9c612 (verdict/3296, class-open). The record flush dispatched nightly.yml with no input, so every nightly lane ran to reach the one-minute record-autofix job. Rule 5 read tag..origin/main while rule 4 read tag..HEAD, so a merge past HEAD after a flush timeout refused rows (v7.1.5 run 1, #3271).

Round 1 changes (unchanged): nightly.yml gains `workflow_dispatch.inputs.lanes` (choice all|beat, default all); mutation-nightly, mutation-ledger, mutation-ledger-push, slow and nightly-ha append `&& inputs.lanes != 'beat'`; record-autofix's `if` is unchanged. stamp.py `RECORD_BEAT_PAYLOAD` posts `lanes=beat`. `tests/delivery_status.py --head REV` (default origin/main) ends its window; `disposition_gate` passes the stamp head.

This round, the review's block: a lanes=beat dispatch skips every REQUIRED_LANES job, and `tests/nightly_status.py` graded it as the newest concluded main dispatch, reading ABSENT (EXIT_RED) after every stamp flush and hiding the last real nightly's jobs. The cure is the reviewer's, in the same files:
- nightly.yml gets `run-name: ${{ inputs.lanes == 'beat' && 'Nightly record beat' || 'Nightly' }}`.
- `nightly_status.BEAT_TITLE` / `is_beat(run)`: `_discover` drops a run whose `display_title` is the beat title before `pick_runs`, and `collect(--run-id)` refuses one as `Unreadable` (a beat verifies nothing).
- tests/entities.py evaluates nightly.yml's own `run-name:` against `BEAT_TITLE` (beat gives it; lanes=all and the schedule do not), and drives `collect` over a listing holding a newer dispatch and an older scheduled nightly. A beat dispatch is never graded, by discovery or by `--run-id`. The null control is a lanes=all dispatch, which still is.
- stamp.py: the `FLUSH_MAX_DISPATCHES` comment and the rule-"flush" docstring named the old every-lane dispatch; both now name the lanes=beat run. The stamp self-test's rows-gate and record-beat pins now also read the return values, which kills the three diff-mutant survivors (below).

merges.body:
R10-CI-OWN-DELIVERY-ROW (owner-approved CI-throughput lever 2, #201 comment 6707834331). R10-CI-SLIM's C7(a) stands the machinery lanes down only on an all-product pull request. Every pull request carries its own delivery row `dev/programme/delivery/<N>.md`, which is not product, so the idling could not fire on any of them.

**Step 1's recording changed the scope of this fix.** The brief said to exempt the row only for the lanes that read no row. `dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py` ran every `run:` step of each machinery lane under strace, in a fresh clone of the head (f020f31c). It counted each open, directory listing and exec that names a row of the clone, or of a copy of the tree. The result is `dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.recording.json`:

- `tests / arch-instrument` reads **no** row. No syscall in any of its three run steps names `dev/programme`, under any root. `arch_score.py` and `arch_score_head.py` ran to `ALL TEST SCRIPTS PASSED`.
- `tests / closures` reads rows in its re-record step: the `tests/entities.py` recording, `policy_lint.mjs --record`, and `policy_lint`'s tree-wide `git grep -I -l`.
- `governance / env-matrix` reads rows. It copies the pull request's tree into `$RUNNER_TEMP/envmatrix/{pr,push-main,no-remote,shallow,…}` and runs `policy_lint` in each copy, which opens and lists every row.
- `governance / instrument-self-tests` reads rows. Step 2 (`policy_lint_mutants.mjs`, which runs `policy_lint.mjs --record --since` and its `git grep`) opens and lists the clone's rows. This lane's trace was still running when the recording was summarized (49 of its 100 run steps closed). A partial lane can only add readers, never clear one, so the verdict stands.

So this pull request does **not** idle all four lanes on a package-plus-own-row diff. `prelude.outputs` now emits two outputs:
- `machinery`: unchanged, the strict C7(a) rule. It gates the three lanes that read rows.
- `machinery_rowblind`: the same rule with exactly this pull request's own row ignored. It gates `tests / arch-instrument` alone, through a new `tests.yml` input that `ci.yml` passes.

`LANE_GATE` records which output each lane gates on, and the self-test `lane_gates` check pins it against the workflow text. A lane that reads rows therefore cannot drift to the row-blind input unseen.

The brief estimated 1,380 runner-minutes a day for idling all four lanes. That estimate does not carry over: what remains is arch-instrument's share alone, and that share is not re-measured here. Taking the row out of the other three lanes needs their row reads either shown irrelevant or removed. That is a separate change, and its seams are the readers listed above.

Transition: `ci.yml`'s prelude job restores `tools/ci/*.py` from the base, so on this pull request the base prelude runs and emits no `machinery_rowblind`. arch-instrument's steps test `!= 'false'`, so an empty input runs them (fail closed).

**Repair round (the `tests / fast (3.14)` red).** `tests/harness_headers.py` failed on its own check `every inlined walk matches the canonical helper and no depth root remains`. It printed `FAIL depth seams: dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py:50: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]`. Main is green because that harness is new in this diff: `depth_root_seams()` scans every harness file, and a fixed `parents[N]` root is a depth seam it refuses. ef830f662 replaces that line with the canonical `repo_root(__file__)` walk, inlined byte-for-byte from `tools/audit/repo_root.py` as every sibling harness does it. No assertion or harness was changed.

## Head

`da510c74b86849dba15ec596457f1d880842a192` merges main `48af086` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`3dd5a3556fde58a9bc46961ef19e6724e2b6d567` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

ef830f662b648d3113dadae22e23f903e6ea03fe, a fast-forward of the PR head 2a7dcd6cf. The earlier step evidence below was measured at f8c052779. The repair commit touches only `dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py`'s root line. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflict, so main is not merged in, per the owner's 2026-11-07 ruling.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant applied to `tools/ci/prelude.py` (M5 to `.github/workflows/tests.yml`), checked with `python3 tools/ci/prelude.py --self-test`, then restored:
- M1, own-row exemption deleted (`and f != own` removed): 2 failed, `C7a-row: a package file plus its own delivery row idles them` and `C7a-row: the prelude passes the event's number: package + row 7 on pull request 7 idles the row-blind lanes`.
- M2, the brief's mutant (every file under `dev/programme/delivery/` exempted): 4 failed. These are `C7a-row: ANOTHER pull request's row still counts as machinery`, `C7a-row: ... and so does the row when the event names no number`, `C7a-row: ... and runs the lanes that read rows` and `C7a-row: ... and row 8 on pull request 7 runs them`.
- M3, `machinery_rowblind` not passed the PR number: 1 failed, `C7a-row: the prelude passes the event's number: ...`.
- M4, the strict `machinery` output also exempts the row: 1 failed, `C7a-row: ... and runs the lanes that read rows`.
- M5, `tests / closures` gated on `inputs.machinery_rowblind`: 1 failed, `C7a-row: each machinery lane's job names exactly its own machinery input`.

Failing test first: c35565f94 is the self-test against the unchanged production code, and it fails with `TypeError: machinery() takes from 1 to 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`.

## Null control

Repair: at the PR head 2a7dcd6cf, `cd tests && python3 -c "import harness_headers; raise SystemExit(harness_headers.inline_scan())"` prints the depth-seam FAIL above with rc=1. At ef830f662 it prints nothing, rc=0. Restoring `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]` makes it red again: that is the mutation proof for this repair.

At the base, `machinery` has no PR number, so a package file plus its own row runs every machinery lane (the c35565f94 red above). At the head:
- a row beside `tools/ci/gate.py` still runs the lanes;
- a row of ANOTHER pull request still counts as machinery;
- the row when the event names no number still counts;
- the own row alone runs them;
- an empty or unread changed list runs them;
- an unreadable script table runs them;
- a push runs them, for both outputs.

These are the `C7a-row:` checks in `python3 tools/ci/prelude.py --self-test` (76 checks, 0 failed).

The `--refresh-index` arm (`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py --refresh-index --lanes closures --out <dir>`) refreshes the clone's index before any step runs, which removes git's rehash of a fresh checkout. Under it the closures re-record step still prints `open=128508 list=18`, so its reads are the steps' own and not that rehash.

The recording's own controls are in the `control` lane: a planted reader of a row (`cat`, plus `git show HEAD:<row>`), a planted copy of the row directory read whole, and a one-row fixture. They print `RESULT control_hits=3 copy_reader=True fixture_reader=False` (`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py --lanes control --out <dir>`). So a tracer recording nothing would not read as clean, and a fixture repository is not counted as the clone. The fixture control caught two scan errors in the inherited harness, both fixed in 245cb2055. Copies of the tree went uncounted, which hid env-matrix's reads, and an absolute argv into a fixture was counted.

## Figures

- Lane read verdicts: `dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.recording.json` `verdict`, from `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py --lanes <lane> --out <dir>` per lane, then `--summarize`. The rule is in the file's `rule` field.
- Control: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.py --lanes control --out <dir>` prints `RESULT control_hits=3 copy_reader=True fixture_reader=False`.
- Self-test: `python3 tools/ci/prelude.py --self-test` prints `prelude self-test: 76 checks, 0 failed`.
- Diff mutants: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff <merge-base>...HEAD --cmd "python3 tools/ci/prelude.py --self-test" --max-mutants 0 --report-only` ran 19 mutants on the added lines of `tools/ci/prelude.py` in 5 s wall (at f8c052779). 5 SURVIVED, listed under `## Unpinned sites`; the other 14 were killed.
- Structure: `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- Gate scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff <merge-base> --workdir <dir>` prints `MODE: FULL` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` changes the gate itself), so the suite is left to CI.
- `tools/pr/prepr.sh` with `MUTANT_CMD="python3 tools/ci/prelude.py --self-test" MUTANT_MAX=0` and this body: rc=0 at ef830f662, 355 s wall. Its diff-mutant step ran the same 19 mutants (the harness lines are outside the driver's scope) and left the same 5 survivors, all answered under `## Unpinned sites`. Main has not been merged in. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflict, and the owner's 2026-11-07 ruling says to hand off at the first clean head.
- Repair: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests python3 tests/harness_headers.py` prints `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED` at ef830f662. `cd tests && python3 -c "import harness_headers; raise SystemExit(harness_headers.inline_scan())"` exits 0 in 0.7 s at ef830f662 and 1 at 2a7dcd6cf.

## Unpinned sites

- `tools/ci/prelude.py:553 CALL_DEL`: deletes the self-test check `an empty list still runs them`. Deleting an assertion cannot redden its own suite. The fail-closed `not files` arm it pins predates this diff (C7a's own empty-list check).
- `tools/ci/prelude.py:554 CALL_DEL`: deletes the self-test check `an unread changed list still runs them`. Equivalent by construction, as for 553.
- `tools/ci/prelude.py:561 CALL_DEL`: deletes the self-test check `... and runs the lanes that read rows`. It is the check that kills M2 and M4 above, so its work is shown there.
- `tools/ci/prelude.py:564 CALL_DEL`: deletes the self-test check `... and row 8 on pull request 7 runs them`. It kills M2 above.
- `tools/ci/prelude.py:567 CALL_DEL`: deletes the self-test check `a push with the row still runs them`. Equivalent by construction. The push arm (`ev != "pull_request"`) is also pinned by `C7a: a push always runs them (null control)`.

## Red checks

- `tests / fast (3.14)` (and the required `gate`, which reports it): class: own diff. `tests/harness_headers.py`'s depth-seam check refused the new harness's `parents[3]` root; repaired in ef830f662. Cheaper detector: `harness_headers.inline_scan()` alone takes 0.7 s and measures nothing about the machine. `tools/pr/prepr.sh` leaves all of `harness_headers.py` to CI, because the script holds the EXCLUSIVE gate lease (`gate_lock.py needs-lease` answers `lease`). So the structural check rides inside a lease-deferred run, and no seat-side step runs it. Countermeasure not built here: it changes `prepr.sh`, which is outside this group. Carried below.

## Forward-carry

- The row reads of `tests / closures`, `governance / env-matrix` and `governance / instrument-self-tests` are listed in `dev/audit/harnesses/lane_reads_delivery.recording.json`. They stop the own-row exemption from reaching those three lanes. Carry: dismissed: the brief's own rule (exempt only the lanes that read no row) decides them here; whether to remove those reads is a new lever for the owner to price
- `tools/pr/prepr.sh`: run `harness_headers.inline_scan()` (0.7 s, no lease) as its own step, so a depth seam is refused before the push instead of in `tests / fast`. Carry: dismissed: tooling outside this group's scope; recorded here for the root-cause seat

## Friction

- `fixer.md`: cost: the cloud seat's `BASH_ENV` (`/etc/profile.d/hpo-toolchain.sh`) re-exports `RUNNER_TEMP` into every non-interactive bash, so harness lanes run side by side shared one runner temp and env-matrix's step failed. The harness now clears it (f020f31c4). Carry: dismissed: repaired in this diff

merges.subject: Merge pull request #3290 from tvofi/fix/r10-hotfix-train-defer-wait
merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-TRAIN-DEFER-WAIT: hotfix train defer wait
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
The merge train treated a red `gate` as a final verdict while the head's code run was still running, and skipped pull requests that would have gone green. This is a hotfix-tier change because it blocks merges. It is CI-throughput lever 1, approved by the owner (tvofi, 2026-11-07, #201 comment 6707834331).

How it happens: an edit run's gate fails at once, deferring to the code run (tools/ci/gate.py `deferral`: "run(s) [..] at this head are still being judged; their gate decides"). The code run publishes no `gate` check run until every unit has finished. So `latest_runs` sees only the edit gate, and `classify` counts it red. Then `wait_ci` returns it, and `at_head` logs `ci red=['gate']` and SKIPs. The brief's s12 CI-throughput study (2026-11-05 13:26Z to 2026-11-07 13:26Z) counted 56 such SKIPs; in 32 the code run later concluded success. This seat did not re-take those figures; they come from the brief. #3293 at fefaa492 (2026-11-07 21:07:58Z, `SKIP #3293 ci: red at the head: gate` on main's tools at dee8b413) is a fresh instance, and this body replays it.

The fix (tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py, tools/audit/seat/proof_watch.py, tools/audit/seat/ci-watch.sh):
- `classify(latest, required, busy=())`: a red GATE is pending while `busy` is non-empty. Every other context, and every caller that passes no `busy`, behaves as before.
- `gate_busy(ci_runs, check_runs)`: tools/ci/gate.py's own `busy`, imported from its tree path and never copied. Each run's jobs come from its own check suite's check runs, so no read per run is needed.
- `Train._gate_busy`: one `actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?head_sha=` listing, made only on a red gate. An unreadable listing reads no run busy, logged, so the red stands. **Round 3:** it also returns `gate_rerunning` over the same listing. That covers a ci.yml run that is unfinished although its suite's latest `gate` is completed. `gate` is ci.yml's last job, so such a run is a re-run attempt (gate-sweep's attempt 2) whose gate has not been listed again, and gate.py's `busy` reads it as judging.

merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-SELFTEST-TIMEOUT. `governance / instrument-self-tests` ran its steps in line under `timeout-minutes: 30` and spent most of its wall time in five self-tests: prepr.sh's, beatd.py's, and pr_args.sh's alone and again through open_pr.sh and update_pr.sh, which each run it. Only prepr.sh's of the five keeps a core busy; the other four wait. They start detached in the job's first step, each to its own log and exit-status file. Five steps near the end of the job, under their old names, print each log, fail on its status and grep the same tally lines. The job lasts as long as the longer of its in-line steps and the detached work, instead of the sum of both. The timeout stays 30: no raise.

The three pr_args.sh callers run one after another in a single detached chain, and prepr.sh's self-test runs at `nice -n 10`. With all five at once, pr_args.sh's `mut:unlock` arm failed once in nine observations: it checks for a lock holder inside the 0.2 s poll the holder takes to notice that its parent has gone, and CPU contention shortens that window. Chained, they keep the order they had in line.

Alternatives, and why each lost:
- **Matrix shards** of the job would rename its check runs to `governance / instrument-self-tests (<shard>)`. That name is read in tools/pr/ci_predict.py's `JOB` table and by tools/audit/round4/D11/governance_cost.py's `bare()`, and each shard repeats checkout. Separate jobs fail tests/entities.py's census, which ties governance.yml job ids to governance_cost.py's `GOV`, until a file outside this group names them.
- **Dropping the standalone pr_args.sh step** would remove a step, and would leave pr_args.sh's tally to two callers outside this file.
- **Cutting prepr.sh's own cost** was not needed for the headroom: the detached run already takes it off the critical path.

Repair round 3 (review blocked a09ebaeb, mutation-vacuous, mutant W1). Deleting the waiter step `Show the pre-PR self-check refusing its own fixtures` survived every check: the launcher line still counted as wiring for selftest_wiring.py, and the harness read only the bg_* library. In CI, prepr.sh's self-test would have run detached with its exit status unread and the job green. The cure is the one the verdict names, in this group's own file:
- `bg_wait` writes a `<name>.read` marker when it reads a status.
- A new library function, `bg_unread`, lists every `<name>.pid` the launcher wrote with no `.read` beside it, prints `bg_unread: <started> started, <unread> unread`, and fails if any is unread.
- A new last step of the job, `Refuse a detached self-test whose status no step read`, runs `bg_unread` under `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`.

Deleting a waiter step, deleting its `bg_wait` line (the verdict's mutant A), or replacing a waiter with an echo of a fake tally (mutant D) now each leave a name unread, so the job itself goes red on main as well as at review. The harness gains the matching arms and mutants, and a shape check that the job's last step is that one.

## Head

`2ad71eb0e78f65a88f1f43bdcfb04e074e2ddf72` merges main `dee8b41` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`9c83f1ab03c674e6651a9afcca9c7e6acfdb8e93` merges main `53273de` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`763d98319f8a02bb0ef43eae1b22c0e7be7b77de` merges the authored code head `81ccb60da92ba016bd8f445ce43db368f2738d4c`.

Head 81ccb60da92ba016bd8f445ce43db368f2738d4c. It is the reviewed head a09ebaebd4f892729d96f24c7ec930ab6a12a37b, plus three commits:
- the cure commit 2a3a6998c1df6dd6692d7b54d956575c7c91624e;
- ec8c58a9446b68540d5fe2dc638f2461e5e8ce38, merging origin/main 1c1ae100b59e29564c7aec069b257dface6ef50f (fetched 2026-11-07 15:25:51 UTC). Main's commits there change nothing under tools/ or .github/ except tools/policy/agreement.mjs, which no figure below runs;
- 81ccb60da, merging origin/main 4b5d771bdf8feb1f83d7d9443e5117b771a0ab76 (fetched 2026-11-07 16:12:57 UTC), because main moved during the first prepr.sh run. That merge adds only dev/programme/delivery/3272.md and dev/programme/triage/s6-batch128.md.

Both merges were clean. The three-dot diff is unchanged by either: .github/workflows/governance.yml, dev/audit/harnesses/r10_selftest_timeout.py, dev/programme/delivery/3275.md and tests/closures.json. The harness, the replays, the gate and structure.py were taken at ec8c58a9. 81ccb60da differs from it only by those two record files, which none of them reads. prepr.sh and the body check were re-run at 81ccb60da.

## Mutation proof

`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_selftest_timeout.py` reads the bg_* library out of the launcher step as committed, drives it over planted commands, and checks the job's last step. At the head:
- M0, the library as committed: all 14 lines PASS. That is the 10 arms from earlier rounds, plus `refuse unread`, `names unread`, `control all read` and `shape last step reads bg_unread`. The three new arms start the job's five names, wait on four, refuse and name the fifth (`UNREAD prepr:`), then wait on it and pass.
- W2, the job's last step deleted: KILLED by `shape last step reads bg_unread`.
- M1, `bg_wait` returning 0 in place of the recorded status: KILLED by `refuse slow bad`, `refuse chained bad` and `refuse bad`.
- M2, `bg_wait` returning 0 for a launcher gone with no status: KILLED by `refuse chain killed` and `refuse killed`.
- X8, `bg_wait` returning 0 after its first poll finds the command still running: KILLED by `refuse slow bad` and `control all read`.
- M3, `bg_wait`'s read marker `: > "$d/$1.read"; ` deleted: KILLED by `control all read`.
- M4, `bg_unread`'s verdict `test "$u" -eq 0` replaced by `true`: KILLED by `refuse unread`.
- `RESULT survivors=0`, rc 0.

Failing first: the same harness run from a detached checkout of a09ebaeb (the workflow before the cure) prints `M0 FAIL names unread`, `M0 FAIL control all read`, `M0 FAIL shape last step reads bg_unread`, `M3 NOT APPLIED`, `M4 NOT APPLIED`, `RESULT survivors=2`, rc 1.

W1 in the job itself: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_selftest_timeout.py replay <W1 workflow> bg`. The W1 workflow is governance.yml with the prepr waiter step removed by a `yaml.safe_load`/`safe_dump` filter on its name. At the head the last step fails, printing `bg_unread: 5 started, 1 unread` and `UNREAD prepr: no step read its status`, then `RESULT replay_seconds=610 failed=1`. At a09ebaeb the same mutant gives `RESULT replay_seconds=605 failed=0`. That is the verdict's W1, reproduced at the old head and killed at the new one.

## Null control

- Each refusal arm has its passing control in the same run: `control ok`, `control tally`, `control chained tally`, `control slow ok` and, for the new arms, `control all read`. A library that refused everything would fail them.
- The unmutated head replay (`... replay .github/workflows/governance.yml bg`) passes every step, the new last step included: `RESULT replay_seconds=616 failed=0`. So `bg_unread` does not refuse a job whose five statuses were all read. Its refusal under W1 is the other end.
- Every job step still runs and greps its `checks, 0 failed` line. The five waiter steps keep their names, and their grep lines are byte-identical to the base's.
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/selftest_wiring.py --check` prints `118 self-testing, 118 wired, 0 unwired` and `0 index gap(s)`, rc 0.

Seams of the class, a detached self-test whose status nothing reads. The enumerating rule is the started names against the waited names in governance.yml:
- `{ grep -oE '^ +bg_start [a-z-]+ ' .github/workflows/governance.yml | awk '{print $2}'; grep -E '^ +bg_pid "\$!" [a-z]' .github/workflows/governance.yml | sed -E 's/^ +bg_pid "\$!" //' | tr ' ' '\n'; } | sort` gives `beatd open-pr pr-args prepr update-pr`.
- `grep -oE '^ +bg_wait [a-z-]+' .github/workflows/governance.yml | awk '{print $2}' | sort` gives the same five.

All five are closed in this diff: each is read by its waiter step, and `bg_unread` refuses any that is not. The rule's null control is W1, where the started set keeps `prepr` and the waited set loses it, and `bg_unread` names it. In CI, `bg_unread` is the same rule at run time, over the `.pid` files the launcher actually wrote.

## Figures

- Harness at the head: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_selftest_timeout.py` gives 14 of 14 M0 PASS and `RESULT survivors=0` over W2, M1, M2, X8, M3 and M4, rc 0 (Mutation proof). The same file run from a09ebaeb gives `RESULT survivors=2`, rc 1. The harness sha1 at the head is `0196700d5c0e348f72671cc07f8ec82686103285` (`sha1sum`).
- Job replay, head: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_selftest_timeout.py replay .github/workflows/governance.yml bg` gives `RESULT replay_seconds=616 failed=0`. Per step: prepr waiter 365.3 s, PR opener 0.0, PR argument builder 45.0, supervised beat 0.0, PR updater 205.1, the new last step 0.0. The total is the replay's own `replay_seconds` line. Earlier rounds' figures stand as cited there: a base replay of 1870 s, and CI at d6482b704 of 631 s of 1800 s.
- Job replay, W1: 610 s with `failed=1` at the head, and 605 s with `failed=0` at a09ebaeb (Mutation proof).
- CI at a09ebaeb, the reviewed head with the same five-step layout: code run 42380487764, `governance / instrument-self-tests` job 128427022752 ran 14:12:54Z to 14:23:30Z, which is 636 s of the 1800 s timeout. That is completedAt minus startedAt from the PR's check runs. The cure adds one step that reads files and sleeps nothing, timed at 0.0 s in both replays.
- `mut:unlock` chained, under the rule "each pr_args.sh caller's waiter passed its `pr_args self-test: [1-9][0-9]* checks, 0 failed` grep". 13 of 13 before this round, by the verdict's count. This round's three local replays (head, W1 at the head, W1 at a09ebaeb) each passed all three pr_args waiter steps, for 9 of 9. The total is 22 of 22, which bounds the failure rate only to below about 1 in 7 (95%, rule of three: 3/22). It is not a measured rate, and it is carried below.
- Scoped gate: `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) ./tests/run.sh` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 2 script(s) run, 31 scoped out.` and `5 TEST SCRIPT(S) PASSED; 30 SCOPED OUT AND NOT RUN`, rc 0, with `ALL 2645 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` and `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`. `tests/closure.py select` names `tests/entities.py` and `tests/harness_headers.py`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- prepr: `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh` prints `PRE-PR: 81ccb60da92ba016bd8f445ce43db368f2738d4c ... rc=0` at the head. Its `ci predict` line reads `no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted against 4b5d771bdf8f`. origin/main had not moved past 4b5d771bd when it finished, so that run stands. The body passes `tools/pr/prepr.sh --body-check`, and `carry_audit.py check` reads 4 routed, 0 unrouted.

## Red checks

At the new head ec8c58a9 no CI run exists at handoff: the head is on the handoff ref only.

At the reviewed head a09ebaeb, the PR's check runs are 81, all on one page (`pull_request_read get_check_runs`, perPage 100, total_count 81). That tool takes no `filter` argument, so attempts were read per run with `actions_list list_workflow_jobs` and `filter: all`. Concluded reds:
- `gate`, edit run 42380487589, attempt 1, job 128427176656, failure at 14:25:41Z. Class: edit-run gate deferral. Its `Judge this head` step printed `FAIL run(s) [42380487764] at this head are still being judged; their gate decides` while the code run was in flight. Attempt 2, job 128437108588, concluded success at 15:02:27Z. Gate jobs 128431169741 and 128433055053, which the verdict names, are the same deferral in the later edit runs 42381808661 and 42382449320. Their latest attempts, 128437112022 and 128437116063, concluded success. Answer: a deferral to the code run, which concluded green. No code answer is owed.
- `tests / nightly-status`, job 128427022838, failure. Class: not this PR's (fix-review.md step 11). The three-dot diff touches none of the files nightly-status reads (the governance workflow's self-test job, the harness, this PR's delivery row and the closure ledger). Answer: no code answer is owed by this diff.

The previous body called this diff's change "the self-test shards" under nightly-status. That was wrong: the diff has no shards (see Alternatives). That sentence is gone from this body.

## Forward-carry

- pr_args.sh's `mut:unlock` arm passes only while its checker runs `kill -0` within the lock holder's 0.2 s parent poll, so CPU load can turn it red. Measured: 1 in 9 with all five self-tests at once, and 22 of 22 chained (Figures). That bounds the rate only to below about 1 in 7. The deterministic cure belongs to pr_args.sh, which this group does not own, and the reviewer concurred with this route. Carry text: make pr_args.sh's `mut:unlock` arm deterministic under CPU load (wait for the holder's exit with a bound, not one `kill -0` inside the holder's 0.2 s parent poll), null-controlled by the unmutated holder still read alive; measured 1 FAIL in 9 with five self-tests concurrent, 22 of 22 chained. Carry: R10-HANDOFF-PATH

- Carry 1 (roster, orchestrator evidence 2026-11-07: #3262 and #3265 each cancelled at the 30-minute job timeout; the fixer re-measures the self-test wall time at its own base): re-measured at this head. The job replay is 616 s with `failed=0`, and CI at a09ebaeb, the same layout without the 0.0 s last step, was 636 s of 1800 s. #3262's and #3265's timeouts ran the base's in-line layout, which this PR replaces. Carry: dismissed: re-measured here, 616 s replay and 636 s CI under the 1800 s timeout

## Friction

- fixer.md-step-3: unenforced: a CI-time claim owes before and after on a probe run, but a fixer seat has no probe path. ci_probe.py takes only `ci-probe/*` refs, and this seat writes no other branch. This head's first code run is the probe for the last step's cost. Carry: dismissed: the pull request's own first run is the probe
- seat-output-refs: stale: refs/heads/handoff-wip/r10-hotfix-selftest-timeout still held round 2's BLOCKED.md commit cfb1d69f3, which the orchestrator's body push 931e696ce had resolved. The step push is fast-forward only, so this round's step pushes are merge commits over cfb1d69f3 that carry this head's tree. Deleting the ref first was refused in this environment. Carry: dismissed: one stale step ref, deleted after this body's push

Round: first-round fix review of PR #3275 (R10-HOTFIX-SELFTEST-TIMEOUT), measured at head d6482b704bb11831c12001ffc0b0210a47c35483 from a detached worktree. The head is unchanged at verdict time (`refs/pull/3275/head` = d6482b704).

## Block

- Mutant X8 inserts `return 0` after `bg_wait`'s `sleep 5`, so `bg_wait` returns 0 once its first poll finds the test still running. It survives every arm of `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_selftest_timeout.py`. Every arm's command has either finished or been killed before its `bg_wait` runs (the arms `sleep 2` first), so the loop's still-running path is never exercised. The mutant is the same shape as the fixer's M1 and M2: a return replaced by 0, on a line this PR adds.
- The defect it admits is a false green. "Show the pre-PR self-check refusing its own fixtures" is `bg_wait prepr` alone, with no tally grep (prepr.sh prints none). Under X8 that step passes while prepr.sh's self-test is still running, or after it fails late. I added a slow arm (`bg_start slowbad bash -c 'sleep 8; echo partial; exit 5'`, then `bg_wait slowbad` with no grep, as the prepr step does):
  - committed library: `PASS refuse slow bad`, `PASS control slow ok`
  - X8: `FAIL refuse slow bad (prepr-shaped step passes)`, `PASS control slow ok`

merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-NIGHTLY-PIN-THROUGHPUT: hotfix nightly pin throughput
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-NIGHTLY-PIN-THROUGHPUT: where the 06 Nov nightly's 320 drain draws went, and three changes that raise pins per night.

The owner asked: measure from scheduled nightly run 42139479636's mutation-ledger shard logs where the drawn mutants go, then make the sound changes that raise pins per night. The measurement (`## Figures`) splits the 320 draws into: 90 killed, 44 lives, 1 timed out, 185 not started for `--budget-minutes`. Of the 90 kills, only 20 landed as pins. The other 70 had already been pushed by workflow_dispatch run 42135552492. That run started 33 minutes earlier on the same UTC date, so it drew the same slice under the same date seed 20261106.

Three changes, each tied to one line of that breakdown:

1. **The seed is the run id** (`nightly.yml` mutation-ledger, `--seed "${{ github.run_id }}"`). This is aimed at the 70 duplicate kills. Every run draws from the unpinned stock as it stood at its own checkout. So two runs on one date, a dispatch beside the schedule, drew one slice twice and the later push landed 22% of its kills (20 of 90). A run's four shards share one id, so they stay disjoint. The seed is printed in each `DRAIN SHARD` header, so a night's draw still replays. mutation-nightly keeps its date seed: it records nothing, so a duplicate draw there costs no pin.
2. **Admission charges no reach-free pair** (`drive_pool` and `drive_pin_pool` take `free`; `main()` passes `reach_free`). This is aimed at the 185 unstarted sites. Each mutant was admitted only if the sum of all its shared drivers fit before the deadline, and that sum included pairs `reach_skip` drops without a run. On the same draw those pairs are 37% of the shared pairs and 13% of the charge (`drain_admission_probe.py`). The charge now counts only runs that happen. `drive()` keeps its own check for lazy drivers, whose trace exists only after their deferred baseline.
3. **`--budget-minutes 270`**, the owner-allowed time raise, also aimed at the 185 unstarted sites. At 240 the four shards closed admission 16-80 minutes before the budget deadline, and the longest job ended 225 minutes into its 330-minute timeout. 270 is mutation-nightly's own sizing under the same timeout, leaving the same 60 minutes for runs in flight.

Alternatives considered, and why each lost:
- **More shards or `--jobs`.** The runners have 4 cores (`nproc` 4) and `--jobs 4` already uses them. More shards adds runner-hours without any measured share of the loss that it would recover.
- **Dropping or reordering a costly driver.** `tests/features.py` kills 130 of the 194 kills across both runs' logs, so dropping it loses coverage.
- **Optimistic admission** (charging less than a survivor's full sweep). It would re-open R9-F10.12's overrun and bias the measured prefix toward cheap mutants.
- **Draw de-duplication against existing pins.** It is already in place: `unpinned_sites` excludes every disposed site before `drain_pool`. What was missing was de-duplication between concurrent runs, which change 1 provides.
- **Survivor triage.** It stays manual, per `ci-autofix.md`; nothing here touches it.

The pins-per-night after-figure is owed on a workflow_dispatch nightly from `main` after this merges. The `mutation-ledger` jobs run only on `refs/heads/main` (`if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`), so no dispatch on this branch measures them. No seat instrument requests a nightly dispatch either (`tools/audit/seat/INSTRUMENTS.md` lists none). The before-figure is run 42139479636, plus dispatch 42135552492 as the run it collided with. The after run, owed by the seat that lands this PR (`gh workflow run nightly.yml --ref main`, nightly.yml's own recipe), reads the same way, with `nightly_drain_breakdown.py` over its four shard logs, `--prior` naming any run that pushed during it. A dispatch on the same date as a scheduled run no longer duplicates its draw.

## Head

merges.body:
R10-BUFFER-OPENLOOP (R10-COMBI-TANK PR 0, S; design `a605014bff4478f470853109060f4ff7ef605d4c` §C0, approved by `design-verdict/r10-combi-tank` `56810263b`). Carry 0 (owner ruling tvofi 11-06): without a buffer probe, `_update_current_state` never advanced `buffer_tank_temperature` (class D12-s1-01). It kept the 40 °C `ThermalState` default, or its last value, and every solve started the buffer from it. Refs #3225 (PR B closes it); this PR closes no issue.

What changes (`custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py`):
- **`_seed_store(reading, result, trajectory_attr, now) -> float | None`** is a module-level function beside `_open_loop_plan_value`. It returns the reading if ok, otherwise the previous plan's trajectory at the covering step, otherwise `None`. On `None` the caller leaves the field as it is, so nothing is fabricated. It is one primitive, and PR B reuses it for `combi_tank_seed`.
- **`_update_current_state`**: the DHW seed is re-expressed through `_seed_store` with identical behaviour; the R9 D12-s1-01 checks are its control. The buffer is seeded the same way from `buffer_temp_trajectory`. Both writes land on the private `state` copy before `ctx.publish(self, state)`, which is R10-LIVESTATE's I1/I2. R10-LIVESTATE is on main (`f7567be02`), so this PR is not blocked on it.
- **The observation split (`_update_external_heat_detection`)**:
  - The rise inputs `dhw_temp` and `buffer_temp` take the measured value or `None`. Without this, a planned rise would be read as external-heat evidence.
  - The level input `hp_tank_temp` keeps its text and reads the best estimate, which is the seed. This keeps wood energy and displacement on for a wood install with no buffer probe.
  - Following the verdict's `observation-read-in-place` note, the rise inputs are read with the `reader` that method already builds, the way `outlet` and `wood_top` are. No coordinator attribute is carried between methods.
- **Which buffers.** The seed applies to every buffer whose last plan published a trajectory. The plan publishes one only under a throttling valve (`optimizer.py`, the `buffer_temp_trajectory=` ternary on `mixing_valve.is_throttling`). Without one the level stays where it was. The harness's `solve` arm shows this with the real solver.
- **Observable side effect, publish-only.** On an install with no DHW probe, the external-heat attribute `dhw_rise_c_per_h` (binary sensor attributes, `ExternalHeatState.as_dict`) now reads `None` instead of a rate taken from the constant or the seed. Every reader is publish-only (`grep -rn "dhw_rise_c_per_h\|buffer_rise_c_per_h" custom_components`). The goldens already read `null`.

**Note for PR B. It is not carried, because it is not a measured finding: combi is not reachable yet, so nothing can be measured.** In combi one buffer probe fills both store fields, but the DHW rise input here reads only `CONF_DHW_TEMP_ENTITY`. PR B's `combi_tank_seed` will have to decide whether the combi DHW rise input reads the buffer probe, since it is the same water.

Group carries (roster `R10-COMBI-TANK`, read at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster`), one disposition each:
- **Carry 1** (owner ruling 11-06, the no-probe buffer bug): **closed in this PR.** The unprobed buffer is seeded from the previous plan's `buffer_temp_trajectory` through the same seed helper the design adds, `_seed_store` over `_open_loop_plan_value`. PR B reuses that helper for `combi_tank_seed`. Its failing test and its controls are below.
- **Carry 2** (physically sound, general combi-tank types): not reached by PR 0. It adds no heat-transfer path, no tank type and no type branch. The seed is type-agnostic, because it reads whichever trajectory the plan published, so PR A and PR B build on it without a combi special case.
- **Carry 3** (judged on robustness, integration efficiency, architecture and maintainability): answered here as follows:
  - **Robustness.** No reading and no plan leaves the field as it is, never fabricated. The rise inputs are never fed a planned value.
  - **Integration efficiency.** It adds two `InputReader` reads in the same tick and no new coordinator attribute, following the verdict's `observation-read-in-place` note.
  - **Architecture.** One module-level primitive outside the coordinator class. `max_class_loc` and `class_excess_loc` each fall by 1.
  - **Maintainability.** The DHW and buffer seeds share one code path.
- **Carry 4** (web verification of the figures before PR B): binds PR B. PR 0 states no tank figure.
- **Carry 5** (the folded web-verification report): binds PR B, and PR A takes only item 1's UA. PR 0 touches no preset, UA, volume or help text.
- **Carry 6** (re-routed from R10-BUFFER-STORE carry 1, `dev/programme/triage/s6-batch127.md#P395`: seed the `dhw_temp_trajectory` tank seed from the measured tank temperature where one exists, failing test first): **already the behaviour, answered here, no code owed beyond the routing.** `_seed_store` reads an ok DHW probe first and falls to the plan's `dhw_temp_trajectory` only without one, so a measured tank temperature already wins wherever one exists. This PR moves the DHW seed onto that primitive with identical behaviour. Its control is `the open-loop DHW seed reaches the state but not the detector's rise input`, together with the R9 D12-s1-01 checks, and it is killed under the `GUARD_OFF` mutant of the DHW call listed under `## Unpinned sites`. Whether issue 2499 closes on this is the orchestrator's call, and this PR closes no issue.

## Head

`64fe84b24efb6e4f720e011b75b559b6a3bac7e9` merges main `dee8b41` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`75f0075571c14748c25674b2b846fc1cb734558f` merges main `4b5d771` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`9e903ce7974cc8a233cf3947f2d1fc9c24976072` merges main `a37c58e` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`2a85b504885f3407750b2c260259f40dab3bca33` merges main `28d46c4` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`8293b51a070f2124a39692639ea10cb4858e0d8c` merges main `516ad1b` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`88934198813b33a4562c3b58f2f1dde1dc82632f` merges main `08fd676` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`fc6af95eab538606f1cdf0481d911cd2cdd922ec` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`fc6af95eab538606f1cdf0481d911cd2cdd922ec` is the PR head; the Code line is the handoff head `0ec5d1852cf679730c04e2923a8bbc3a6fafecee`. The merge base is `80016a71f567d936450d8708abcbb79d9e8071d7`, which was origin/main's tip at 2026-11-06T23:29Z. Main moved from the design base `28482ece` during the first gate run. It was merged in, never rebased; that merge brought #3234 (replay-cost tooling, no `custom_components` change). The scoped gate, `ci_predict`, structure and the harness were then re-taken on the handoff head, and prepr.sh was run on it.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant was applied to the head's `coordinator.py`, the new `tests/features.py` block was run (`R10-BUFFER-OPENLOOP` section), and the file was restored:
- **Delete the fix line** (buffer call → `buffer_reading.value if buffer_reading.ok else None`). FAIL: `with no buffer probe the buffer level follows the previous plan's trajectory`; `(wood_seed): with no buffer probe the wood reference hp_tank_temp is the plan's seed`. I also ran this mutant through the whole closure script: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` printed `2 of 4885 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`. The two failures are exactly those checks.
- **Seed fed to the buffer rise input** (`buffer_temp=ctx._current_state.buffer_tank_temperature`). FAIL: `the observation's rise inputs carry no seed`.
- **DHW seed fed to the DHW rise input.** FAIL: `the observation's rise inputs carry no seed`; `the open-loop DHW seed reaches the state but not the detector's rise input`.
- **`None` to `hp_tank_temp`.** FAIL: all three `wood_seed` checks.
- **Predicate mutated** (`reading.ok` → `False` in `_seed_store`). FAIL: `a buffer probe reading ok wins over the plan (null control)`; `(wood_seed): a buffer probe wins`.

Failing first, at the design base `28482ece`: with the production diff reverted and the tests kept, 4 checks FAIL: the buffer level, the rise inputs, the DHW rise input, and `wood_seed` seed. The 5 controls are ok at both ends.

## Unpinned sites

`tools/pr/ci_predict.py` lists three sites the diff adds. Each one's lane mutant was run against the new `R10-BUFFER-OPENLOOP` block and is killed. Each is pinned by `mutation-autofix` (`ci: pin killed mutants`):
- `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py:2358 RETURN_DEL` (`_seed_store` returns `None`): 5 FAIL. Among them are the buffer level, the probe null control and the DHW seed.
- `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py:6581 GUARD_OFF` (the DHW `_seed_store` guard): 1 FAIL, `the open-loop DHW seed reaches the state but not the detector's rise input`.
- `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py:6583 GUARD_OFF` (the buffer `_seed_store` guard): 4 FAIL. Among them are the buffer level, the probe null control and `wood_seed`.

The stale pin `tests/mutation_ledger/killed_by/coordinator.py/HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._update_current_state.GUARD_OFF.12569471.json` is deleted by hand, per `ci_predict`'s STALE PIN repair. Its line `if buffer_reading.ok:` no longer exists.

## Null control

- **Probe present.** A buffer probe reading 36.5 °C gives levels 36.5, 36.5 and a buffer rise input of 36.5 at both ends. The install has no DHW probe, so its DHW rise input moves from 55.0, the never-advanced default, to None. That move is the fix, not a drift. With the wood furnace and a 38 °C probe, `hp_tank_temp` reads 38.0 and wood energy is 29.0000 kWh, displacement 0.5312, identical at base and head.
- **Empty trajectory**, which is the no-valve plan. At both ends the level stays 40.0, 40.0. Wood energy is 26.6800 kWh, displacement 0.5000, identical at base and head. `None` is never invented.
- **`solve` with valve `none`.** The solver's buffer seeds read 40.0 ×4 at both ends, because the previous plan published no buffer trajectory.

## Figures

Harness `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_combi_tank.py`, sha1 `7eb9b4b12c2fa83171e8d71fedf0d73b59f2b6eb`, run at base (`80016a71`, the file copied in, `cmp`-identical; the first pass at `28482ece` printed the same lines) and at the head:
`PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_combi_tank.py all`
- `no_probe seed`: base 40.0, 40.0 → head 41.0, 43.0, which is the plan at covering steps 1 and 3. Rise inputs: base (40.0, 55.0) → head (None, None).
- `wood_seed seed`: `hp_tank_temp` base 40.0, 40.0 → head 41.0, 43.0. Wood energy 26.6800 → 23.2000 kWh, displacement 0.5000 → 0.4444. These equal the hand formula against 43 °C, and the test computes and compares them.
- `solve valve=manual`: solver buffer seeds base 40.0, 40.0, 40.0, 40.0 → head 40.0, 42.5, 40.9, 40.3. The first solve has no prior plan.
- Controls, as under Null control: `no_probe probe`, `no_probe empty`, `wood_seed probe`, `wood_seed empty`, `solve valve=none`. Each is identical at both ends.

Scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 22 script(s) run, 11 scoped out.` `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub bash tests/run.sh`: `24 TEST SCRIPT(S) PASSED; 10 SCOPED OUT AND NOT RUN`, golden lane `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 56 scenario(s) checked against origin/main`.

Structure: `python3 tests/structure.py` prints STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED. `max_class_loc` and `class_excess_loc` each moved down by 1 and were re-recorded, with the reason in the commit message: the two seeds collapse into a function outside the coordinator class. Seam map: no coordinator method was added or renamed.

The census rule for the class (step 8): `git grep -n "_open_loop_plan_value(\|_seed_store(" -- custom_components` enumerates every open-loop seed site. Each returned seed site is dispositioned:
- `_seed_store`'s own body: the primitive;
- the DHW and buffer `_seed_store` calls in `_update_current_state`: closed here;
- the slab `_open_loop_plan_value` in the slab-estimate helper (R9, already guarded by the R9 D12-s1-01 slab checks).

The one other plant-state level that has a trajectory is the wood tank (`wood_temp_trajectory`). It is already guarded and is not a never-advanced constant: without a wood probe, `_update_current_state` sets `wood_tank_temperature = None` and falls back to the single-tank abstraction (issue #40).

For the rise-input class, `git grep -n "ExternalHeatObservation(" -- custom_components` names one construction. Its rise inputs are closed here.

## Red checks

Read from the check-runs of every commit of the PR (`7515282d`, `133fe9d1`, `219838cd`, `28b3933f`, `0ec5d185`, `d95f6b7a`, `129dc30d`, `fc6af95e`), `filter=all`, all pages. The commits `7515282d`, `133fe9d1`, `219838cd` and `28b3933f` have no concluded red.

- `tests / mutation`: red on the three unpinned sites the diff adds, listed under `## Unpinned sites`. Failure 128233877269 at `d95f6b7a` is that table. Cancelled 128233790198 at `0ec5d185` and cancelled 128320026602 at `fc6af95e` were superseded by a newer push, so they concluded no verdict. The table is now green at the final head `fc6af95e`: success runs 128325233303 and 128345411068. Cure: each site's lane mutant is killed by the new `R10-BUFFER-OPENLOOP` block, and `mutation-autofix` pins it by a `ci: pin killed mutants` commit (`ci-autofix.md`). The cheaper detector exists and ran before the handoff: `prepr.sh` step 6d / `tools/pr/ci_predict.py` predicted all three, at no standing cost beyond that step. No new detector is owed.
- `governance / instrument-self-tests`: cancelled 128233790595 (`0ec5d185`), 128233877434 (`d95f6b7a`), 128320026640 (`fc6af95e`). Class: the 30-minute job timeout, not a test failure, and no code in this PR touches the instruments. Owner: R10-HOTFIX-SELFTEST-TIMEOUT, with the cure R10-PROCESS-SLIM #3245. The cheaper detector is that cure. This PR adds none.

## Summary

Round 1 of the adversarial fix review of #3268 (R10-COMBI-TANK PR 0, R10-BUFFER-OPENLOOP), done from a detached worktree at `d95f6b7a88e6c2d960ee897b915d4c7941b45de9`. Merge base and origin/main are both `80016a71f567d936450d8708abcbb79d9e8071d7`, and `git diff <mb>...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty, so the role contract is current.

The production diff implements design `a605014b` §C0 and nothing more:
- `_seed_store(reading, result, trajectory_attr, now)` is one module-level primitive over `_open_loop_plan_value`.
- The DHW seed is re-expressed through it, and the buffer seed is added.
- In the observation split, the rise inputs take `reading.value if reading.ok else None` from the method's own `reader` (the `observation-read-in-place` note), and `hp_tank_temp` keeps its text and reads the seed.

Every quoted figure re-derives at both ends. Every mutant I planted is killed. The test fails first at base. The branch merges cleanly. CI at this head was never decided: the code run was cancelled when the bot's pin commit was pushed (see Evidence). That commit carries this verdict to `129dc30d`, whose own runs decide.

## Findings

- Follow-up: `## Red checks` spells the red as `mutation`, but the check is `tests / mutation`, and it does not name the concluded-red `gate` (edit run 42317532474, job 128234307691). `review_packet.py` refuses both as `red-unanswered`. The substance is answered: the three ADDED UNPINNED sites were predicted by `ci_predict` and are pinned by bot commit `129dc30d`. The fixer should spell the check names exactly, and should name the `gate` red as the edit-run deferral that run 42317532285 decided (later cancelled), so that `pr-contract` at the new head reads the body clean. The edit is body-only and does not move the head. Carry: R10-COMBI-TANK
- Follow-up: the `gate` red at this head is the edit-run gate deferring to the code run: `FAIL run(s) [42317532285] at this head are still being judged; their gate decides`. That run was cancelled at 01:16Z when `ci: pin killed mutants` was pushed, so this head has no deciding gate. `merge_train.py classify` printed `RED ... pending: none red: gate` on every poll from 00:29Z to 01:33Z (20 polls over 60 min). The run that decides is now the code run at `129dc30dfc100eac1ffb60f6047648b5607988ee`, which read `WAIT ... pending: gate red: none` at 01:37Z. This is the open gate-deferral class. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER
- Follow-up: design `a605014b` §T.3 owes the energy-balance invariant `combi_energy_balance`, `|C·ΔT − RHS| ≤ 1e-9 kWh` over a 48-step `combi_tank_step` day, and its UA = 0 null control, which conserves `Σ(in − out)·Δt` to 1e-12 relative. PR 0 adds no heat-transfer path, no `combi_tank_step` and no `buffer_store_volume`, so the invariant has no code here to hold or fail. There was nothing to hand-derive or mutate at this head, and I did not build a stand-in. PR A must land it as a precondition, together with the double-count mutant the design names (capacity read from `buffer_tank_volume` on one side and `buffer_store_volume` on the other). Carry: R10-COMBI-TANK
- Follow-up: in combi, one buffer probe is the DHW water, but the DHW rise input added here reads only `CONF_DHW_TEMP_ENTITY` (`coordinator.py` `_update_external_heat_detection`, `dhw = reader.read(CONF_DHW_TEMP_ENTITY)`). On a combi install with only a buffer probe, the DHW rise detector therefore gets `None`. The body records this as a note for PR B but carries it nowhere, because combi is not reachable at this head and nothing can be measured. PR B's `combi_tank_seed` must decide the combi DHW rise input as a stated precondition, with an arm. Carry: R10-COMBI-TANK

## Evidence

- RESULT head=d95f6b7a88e6c2d960ee897b915d4c7941b45de9 (ev/HEAD.txt); merge base 80016a71f567d936450d8708abcbb79d9e8071d7 = origin/main.

- Harness: `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_combi_tank.py`, sha1 7eb9b4b12c2fa83171e8d71fedf0d73b59f2b6eb. It is the fixer's own build, made to the design's spec: `a605014b` §Evidence plan names this file and the `no_probe` and `wood_seed` arms, and the design records that there is no finder harness, because the evidence is the owner report on #3225. I ran it at base (file copied in) and at head (ev/harness_base.txt, ev/harness_head.txt):
  - RESULT no_probe_seed: base 40.0,40.0, head 41.0,43.0.

merges.body:
Fold the 2026-11-06 out-of-tree sweep changes into the tracked sweep scripts the owner ruling names, so that one overlay renders the sweep and also feeds the beat rows. Repair round 5 for the `architecture-unsound` block on `verdict/3267` at `14a73c15`.

Owner ruling (tvofi 2026-11-06), verbatim: "There should already be tracked sweep templates/scripts for these, update them if needed".

Review accepted these parts and this round leaves them unchanged:
- `sweep_runner.sh`, `sweep_runner_selftest.py` and `roster_drain.py` are gone.
- `gantt` and `verdict-audit` are `beat_jobs.py` rows with `beatd.jobs.json` entries.
- `PLAN MOVED` is in `plan-beat`.
- (4b) is the single owner.

This round makes only the four named repairs:

1. **The block.** `tools/audit/seat/sweep_template.md`'s `## Placeholders` table now declares the five overlay keys the new rows read: `gantt_roster`, `gantt_acks`, `fire_ledger`, `train_glob` and `unheld_skip`. (4b) cites `{{gantt_roster}}`, `{{fire_ledger}}` and `{{gantt_acks}}`. (4c) cites `{{fire_ledger}}`, `{{train_glob}}` and `{{unheld_skip}}`. `sweep_render.py` refuses a declared name that is never used, so each one is used.
   - All five are declared as required placeholders, not as `OPTIONAL_FLAGS`. `sweep_render.py`'s optional flags render as `pulse.py` flag text inside a command. (4b) and (4c) cite these keys as files in prose, so flag text would be wrong there.
   - A session running the beat has all five files, so requiring them costs nothing. `beat_jobs.py`'s own tolerance of an absent optional key is unchanged.
   - A new census in `beat_jobs_selftest.py` keeps the defect from returning unseen. It parses `beat_jobs.py`, reads every overlay key the file reads, and compares them with `sweep_render.declared()` of the tracked template. It counts `ctx.need(...)`, `.get(k)` and `[k]` on the overlay, plus a key bound by a `for` loop over a literal tuple. `need`'s own body is skipped, because its callers are the reads. Any read whose key it cannot resolve fails the census rather than being skipped.
2. **The four surviving gantt mutants, plus the fetch rc.** M3 to M12 are the reviewer's mutant numbers.
   - The `gantt` row's `git fetch` rc is now checked. On a failed fetch the row writes `gantt: UNREADABLE fetch rc=<n>: <last stderr line>` and returns. Before, it went on to `git show` the stale `refs/gantt/roster` left by the last pass, and to its handoff tips.
   - Five failing-first cases cover each guard and input, and each carries its null:
     - the `gh pr list` rc (M3)
     - the roster `git show` rc (M4)
     - the new fetch rc, the stale-roster case M4 exposed
     - the `handoff-wip/*` refspec (M11), with a fake `git` that lists only the tip namespaces the fetch named
     - the copied fire ledger (M12)
   - Each case is registered as a `MUTANTS` entry.
3. **The body**, re-taken whole from `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`. `## Red checks` names every red from the reviewer's `filter=all` read.
4. **The gate checks** are re-run. Each is listed under `## Figures`.

## Head

comments.body:
Fix review: blocked 61f1ec71a428b43fc2965379ab08c6747d214e5b architecture-unsound: sweep_runner.sh is a second copy of six beat_jobs.py rows, not an update of the tracked sweep scripts the owner ruling names

bus-nonce: 96c989956d6388b5c07d3d4b99445a4f

## Block

Round: first review of #3267 (R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC), at head `61f1ec71a428b43fc2965379ab08c6747d214e5b`. Role checked: `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty, so the contract I read is current.

The owner ruling the brief quotes is "There should already be tracked sweep templates/scripts for these, update them if needed". The PR body says the opposite: "Tracked counterparts: only `sweep_render.py` and `sweep_template.md` existed". That is false at the merge base `f2a01514`. `tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py` (run by `beatd.py` from `beatd.jobs.json`) is the tracked script for the sweep's mechanical steps. Its `ROWS` are `tick-digest, owed-check, roster-drain, plan-beat, pulse, cancel-sweep, disk, opener, head-watch, audit-dispatch` (ev/base-beat_jobs-rows.txt, ev/base-beatd.jobs.json).

The new `tools/audit/seat/sweep_runner.sh` (ev/head-sweep_runner.sh) is a parallel loop. It re-implements six of those ten rows: the roster drain, `pulse.py`, `cancel_superseded.py sweep`, the disk floor with `worktree_gc.sh`, `replan.py` + `state_docs.py --push --mirror --plan` (plan-beat), and `owed_unactioned.py` (owed-check). The new `roster_drain.py` re-implements the `roster-drain` row's drain through `roster_queue.py run`, and its own page has to rule that "the two do not run together on one queue". Running both loops in one session runs `state_docs.py --push` twice against one state ref, with nothing to serialise them.

`sweep_template.md` now names both owners for the same step. (4b) says the beat's `plan-beat` row replans and pushes the state docs every 30 minutes. The new (4b+) says `sweep_runner.sh` re-renders and republishes them every second pass. Its consumer (`sweep_render.py` renders the template for the orchestrator) gets two contradictory instructions.

The sound shape is the one the ruling asks for. Make `sweep_gantt.py` and `verdict_audit.py` new rows of `beat_jobs.py`, with their lines going to the digest the orchestrator already reads. Add the `PLAN MOVED` compare to the `plan-beat` row. Fold the roster-drain differences (exact-line `#refused` + ROSTER-CASCADE/UNRUN) into the existing row or `roster_queue.py`. Do not ship a second loop, a second drain and a template step that duplicates (4b).

Harness: the base tree's `beat_jobs.py` ROWS against the runner's step list. Metric: the number of runner steps that already exist as a beat row, 6 of the runner's 9 steps. Perturbation: delete the runner's six duplicated steps. The template's (1b), (4b) and (4e) steps, run by beatd, still cover every one of them, so they are redundant, not new coverage.

## Findings

- Defect: `sweep_runner.sh` and `roster_drain.py` add a parallel sweep loop and drain beside `beat_jobs.py`/`beatd.py` instead of updating them (the owner's ruling), and `sweep_template.md` (4b+) contradicts (4b) on who replans and pushes the state docs. Claim, evidence, harness and metric are as in `## Block`. Repair: Gantt and verdict audit become `beat_jobs.py` rows, PLAN MOVED goes into `plan-beat`, and the runner and second drain are dropped. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC
- Defect: the body's "Tracked counterparts: only `sweep_render.py` and `sweep_template.md` existed" is false at the merge base (`beat_jobs.py`, `beatd.py`, `beatd.jobs.json`, `tick_loop.sh`), so the body's justification for adding files rather than updating them does not stand. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC
- Defect: alert 51's repair has no local check that reads the file mode. The 0o755 copy of `sweep_runner_selftest.py` (89f08728^) prints `sweep_runner self-test: 11 checks, 0 failed`, the same as the 0o700 head (ev/selftest-0o755.txt, ev/selftests-head.txt). The only detector that moves under the mutation is CodeQL `py/overly-permissive-file` on CI, as the body itself says. The repair is at the root (both `w(...)` callers pass 0o700, with no suppression), but the brief's "a named check goes red" holds only for CI's CodeQL. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC
- Defect: `.github/workflows/governance.yml`'s new step runs `sweep_runner_selftest.py` twice, because `sweep_runner.sh --self-test` already `exec`s it. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC

## Evidence

- HEAD reviewed: `61f1ec71a428b43fc2965379ab08c6747d214e5b` (ev/HEAD.txt); merge base `f2a015142714383722bf49d7ab20d8398ec9674c`; three-dot diff in ev/three-dot.diff (14 files, +813/-1).

## Block

Round: second review of #3267 (R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC), at head `14a73c15e5f060069f0fd4831eb46a436bd14f1d`, merge base `294a880dae608502b62055775e34a5db93217b98`. `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md` is empty.

The re-cut answers round 1's architecture finding. `sweep_runner.sh`, `sweep_runner_selftest.py` and `roster_drain.py` are gone. Gantt and verdict audit are now `beat_jobs.py` rows with `beatd.jobs.json` entries. `PLAN MOVED` is in `plan-beat`. (4b+) is gone, and (4b) has one owner. `git grep "sweep_runner|roster_drain.py" -- tools .github tests` finds only one history comment, in `beat_jobs_selftest.py`.

The re-cut does not keep the rows in sync with the tracked template, though. `Ctx` reads its overlay from `S/sweep-overlay.json`, which its own docstring calls "the same JSON `sweep_render.py` fills the sweep from" (`beat_jobs.py:34`, `:172`). `sweep_render.render` refuses any overlay key that is not in the template's `## Placeholders` table: `unknown: ... not in the placeholder table`. The new rows read `gantt_roster`, `gantt_acks`, `fire_ledger`, `train_glob` and `unheld_skip`. `sweep_template.md` declares none of them. That leaves the orchestrator two outcomes:
- If the overlay leaves the keys out, every gantt pass writes `gantt: UNREADABLE overlay lacks gantt_roster, gantt_acks` (`Ctx.need`), and the verdict audit runs without its ledger, train glob or skip file.
- If the overlay adds the keys, the sweep render is refused.

The owner ruling is to update the tracked templates and scripts, and this updates the script half without the template half.

Harness: `ev/keys.py` lists every overlay key `beat_jobs.py` reads (`ctx.need` and `overlay.get`/`[...]`) and subtracts `sweep_render.declared(sweep_template.md)`. The render probe in `ev/overlay-keys.txt` renders the head's template with only the declared keys, then adds one new key at a time. Metric: the number of undeclared beat keys. It is 0 at the merge base and 5 at the head (`ev/overlay-keys.txt`). Perturbation: add `gantt_roster`, `gantt_acks` or `fire_ledger` to the overlay. The control render with declared keys only prints `OK`. Each single addition prints `REFUSED: unknown: <key> not in the placeholder table`. The harness moves under its own perturbation.

Repair, in this PR: declare the five keys in the `## Placeholders` table and use them in (4b)/(4c). `sweep_render` refuses a declared but unused name, so the sweep text has to cite them. Add a check, in `beat_jobs_selftest.py` or `sweep_render`'s self-test, that every overlay key `beat_jobs.py` reads is a declared placeholder, so this cannot recur unseen.

## Findings

- Defect: `beat_jobs.py` reads five overlay keys (`gantt_roster`, `gantt_acks`, `fire_ledger`, `train_glob`, `unheld_skip`) that `sweep_template.md` does not declare, while `sweep_render.py` refuses an overlay that holds them. The new rows therefore cannot be fed and the sweep rendered from one overlay. The claim, harness, metric (0 at the base, 5 at the head) and perturbation are under `## Block`. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC
- Defect: four mutants on changed `gantt` lines survive `beat_jobs.py --self-test`, which prints 146 checks, 0 failed under each (`ev/mutants-mine.txt`, harness `ev/mut.py`):
  - M3 drops the `gh pr list` rc guard.
  - M4 drops `rc != 0` from the roster `git show` guard.
  - M11 drops the `handoff-wip/*` refspec from the fetch.
  - M12 replaces the copied fire ledger with `""`.
  No case drives a `gh` failure, a roster `git show` failure, a `handoff-wip` tip or a gantt ledger line. M3 and M4 are partly masked, because an empty file then fails `sweep_gantt` and that prints `UNREADABLE sweep_gantt`. M4 is not masked when the fetch fails but an earlier `refs/gantt/roster` exists: the stale roster is read silently. That failed fetch's rc is also unchecked. Repair: one case per guard and input, each with a null. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC
- Defect: `## Red checks` misstates the red history. It says `61f1ec71` had "68 runs (`total_count` 68), all on one page. None concluded `failure`, `cancelled` or `timed_out`". That reading used the API default `filter=latest`. With `filter=all`, `61f1ec71` has 147 runs on 2 pages and 5 reds:
  - `gate` failure 128279140047, 128285014276 and 128290983518
  - `gate` cancelled 128288757875
  - `pr-contract / pr-contract` cancelled 128288387497

  At the head, `gate` failure 128312324401 is unnamed. Its log reads `FAIL run(s) [42340579795] at this head are still being judged; their gate decides`, the edit-run deferral R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER, and gate 128324519569 later concluded success. `arch-score / arch-score` cancelled 128324556485 and 128307712802 are also unnamed: both sit in edit run 42340579009, which was cancelled. Also unnamed are the `pr-contract` failure 128231570697 at `0ae78ac1`, which round 1's body named and this body dropped, and the 6 `gate`/`refresh`/`prelude` cancellations at `aa680f8b` (`ev/red-history-filter-all.txt`). The head's `pr-contract` 128321564289 started at 06:06:36Z, after the last red concluded at 05:22:16Z, and passed. So `defect-root-cause.md`'s trigger is answered by that run, and this is not the block. The brief requires the section to name every red that a later push cleared. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC
- Defect: `review_packet.py render` refuses `red-unanswered: concluded red check arch-score / arch-score is not named in ## Red checks`. The body's "This head's own runs ... Any red there is the next round's to answer" does not answer it, because this head is the head under review. Carry: R10-SWEEP-TEMPLATE-SYNC

No added helper sets a file mode. I re-derived that by reading the diff: `atomic()` and `mkdir` use default modes.

  The body's ten in-tree `MUTANTS` are all killed inside the 146-check run.

The new tracked `sweep_gantt.py` and `verdict_audit.py` are in `tests/closures.json`. `dev/programme/delivery/3267.md` is in the diff. The scope is the sweep instruments plus their governance step, and no production code is touched.

R10-HANDOFF-PATH part 2 (r10-handoff-path-p2): pr_args.sh resolves its own directory once at source time; open_driver.py stem escape, guarded log read and a STUCK line after three tries. Part of #201.

## Head

`fefaa4926e36e9c571cc685e0b6aa2b391d14793` merges main `dee8b41` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`4b663581a88e96ce6b90223ae4b1a563de1e250f` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

Measured at the merge of origin/main a37c58e5f into the code commit 1e994e484 (head 2a8a3e338751cfd1cf10ae2305d9062591378fdf). origin/main moved after the first prepr run, so main was merged and prepr rerun on this head.

## Mutation proof

## Null control

The unmodified pr_args.sh refuses the relative-path arms (same self-test, mutant arm); the null arm "the same clone made stale refuses STALE CHECKOUT" stays red-on-stale. Two failed opens print OWED, not STUCK; `r10-plain` launches as before; a new sha for a stuck topic launches again.

Part of #201. #2238 is already closed, so this body closes nothing.

| # | the one fact | owner | callers routed through it |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | an interval's planned (space, dhw) kW, an absent channel read as 0 | `coordinator._planned_split` | `_accumulate_energy`, `_settle_interval_diag` |
| P2 | a fabric-loss residual too large to be a heat-loss error is refused and logged | `coordinator._loss_residual_rejected` | `_async_learn_house_heat_loss`, `_async_learn_lower_floor_loss` |
| P3 | the trajectory the indoor sensor reads (upper floor in two-zone mode when present, else the room) | `OptimizationResult.sensor_trajectory` | `_file_lead_predictions`, `_predicted_next_room_temp`, `_publish_breach_reports`, `_safety_release_steps` |
| P4 | window means at their billed-equivalent factor, a window past the factors billed at 1 | `tariff.billed_windows` (on `shape[-1]`) | `_peak_excess`, `peak_cost_batch`, optimizer `_grid_report` |
| P5 | how many metering windows a plan of `n_steps` spans | `HeatPumpOptimizer._n_peak_windows` | `_peak_window_factors`, `_peak_day_kwargs` |
| P6 | an evidence sensor's attributes: payload block, `waiting_for`, at most one insight report | `_WaitsForEvidenceMixin._evidence_attributes` | `PredictionAccuracySensor`, `ContractComparisonSensor`, and `FrequencyAdvisorSensor` (see below) |
| P7 | the tracker stores a ranked (kW, day) record as the parallel `peaks`/`peak_days` lists | `PeakTracker._keep_ranked` | `_close_window`, `from_dict` |
| P8 | the metering-window partition: steps per window, steps in the leading partial window | `tariff._window_partition` | `metering_windows`, `_window_means_batch` |
| P9 | each window's real local start, walked in UTC from the slot of `start_time` (#243, #777) | `tariff._window_starts` | `window_factors`, `plan_window_days` |

Re-measured at my own merge base (`git archive origin/main`, then `enumerate_p2.py --json`): the two pairs the brief lists that are no longer in F5 are gone and dropped (`_fold_internal_gains`/`_fold_solar_aperture`, `_buffer_charge_ceiling`/`hold_demand_kw`); the other nine are the nine above.

Departures from the note, raised here rather than made silently:
- **P6 has a third caller.** The P2 registry rule for this fact (below) returned `FrequencyAdvisorSensor.extra_state_attributes`, which builds the same payload block plus `waiting_for` with no report. That is the same fact, so it is closed here, not dispositioned: `report_key` is optional and that sensor calls the owner too. The other `insight` readers the note names (no `waiting_for`) are untouched.
- **P8's owner takes no `n`.** The note's signature is `_window_partition(n, window_minutes, dt_hours, offset_steps)`; neither output depends on `n` (the partition is the clocks' property, as `_window_means_batch`'s docstring says), so an unused parameter was left out.
- **Commit shape.** Nine pair commits (P1..P9, each with its owner, its callers, its sentinel check and its registry entry), then the probe repair, the budget re-record, three follow-up commits (a wrong `CapacityTariff` keyword and a missed owner binding in P4's check, strict typing of the P4/P6 owners, and an unbound name in P8's check) that the step ref's fast-forward-only rule kept as their own commits instead of folded in, and the merge of origin/main.

merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER: a deferring gate publishes at once and the sweep settles it, holding no runner
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER, third PR (topic r10-gate-busy-defer-3). A deferring gate no longer holds a runner. `gate.judge()` publishes the deferral at once. `gate-sweep.yml` (`tools/ci/sweep.py`) re-runs that gate without a human once the deciding run completes. The existing green, newest-covering branch handles most heads. A new `settle` branch handles a head that no green gate follows: two gates that deferred to each other, or a decider that ended red or cancelled.

**What the runs say about the brief's cause.** The brief says nothing re-judges the deferring gate when the deciding run concludes. Today's runs do not support that as stated. On #3282 the sweep did fire for code run 42367457479. That run concluded at 11:48:41Z, and tvofi re-ran edit gate 42367457809 at 11:48:45Z. The sweep's read at 11:48:53Z then found that gate already re-queued and left it (`SWEEP-DONE run=42367457479 reruns=0`). The replay below shows that, without the human re-run, main's sweep re-runs the gate and it passes. The defects the runs do show are the following:
1. **The wait held a runner and ended red anyway.** Since #3276 merged (08:36:40Z), every deferral FAIL held its runner for the full ~12 min before publishing (`held_ge_600` = `deferral_fails` in the census below).
2. **The sweep's SKIP branch had no exit when nothing green follows.** This is a mutual deferral, or a decider that ended red or cancelled. These reds stayed until a human acted. Examples: #3265's pair at 04:06–04:08Z, and #3255's pair, both re-run attempts. The RCA of #3278 shows those ran pre-fix programs. `settle` covers the shape for whichever program the gate runs.

**The fix and the alternatives considered.**
- **Keep the wait and fix only the sweep.** This would leave a runner held ~12 min per deferral, which the brief forbids. It also feeds the runner queue that delayed the sweep's own re-runs by 7–26 min today, for example sweep 42353870719, created 08:04:01Z and run at 08:18:20Z.
- **Mark a deferral with a `ci.yml` step, or with an annotation the sweep reads.** `tests/entities.py` pins the gate job's last step (rev3 R3-1) and the sweep job's permissions (`checks: read` is absent). Either would change a pin.
- **Have the sweep read gate logs.** That needs a raw-body mode in `ghapi`.

`settle` instead decides from data the sweep already reads, the `filter=latest` jobs listing. A red gate is re-run when it started before another run's job (its gate aside) finished, or when a higher-id run's gate started while it judged. In the second case only the lower id is re-run, because `busy()`'s tie-break makes the lower id the one that decides. The third case is that same pair seen from its higher side: a red gate whose lower-id peer's gate judged beside it and ended green deferred to that decider, so the higher is re-run. A red lower is re-run by the second arm and the higher is not, so the pair is never both re-run. A re-run judges after every source finished and after the peer gate concluded, so it is never re-run again, and the branch cannot loop. The new harness `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_busy_defer_3.py` (record, replay, census) lands with the fixture rows for #3282.

**Round 2 repair (verdict/3287 at 29ee7261, `settle-unjudged`).** At 520538cc, a higher-id gate that deferred by `busy()`'s tie-break to a lower run whose listing lagged stayed red whenever the lower's green gate did not cover the newest event, that is, the higher run was created after the lower's gate started. The sweep then took `settle`, where `undecided()` re-ran only the lower id of an overlapping pair, and the lower was green. At the base that gate waited one poll and passed, so the change introduced this.
