Round 1 (first-round adversarial review), head 520538ccfad01bee373382e9d56fc036c8c87ea0, merge base b4ec2f332fe3ab8dcf169bd3066276d3bb8848ab.

## Block

Brief focus (2) and (4). `undecided()` re-runs a red gate in two cases. The first is when another run's non-gate job finished after the gate started, using real timestamps. The second is when a HIGHER-id run's gate started while it judged, and then only the lower id is re-run. But `busy()`'s tie-break, in the gate self-test check "busy-defer: the higher deferring edit gate defers at once to the lower whose listing lags", makes the HIGHER run defer to the LOWER one. Neither arm catches that red. It is only re-run when the lower's green gate covers the newest event, through the green branch. If the higher run was created after the lower's gate started (for example, a body edit landing during the lower gate), `covers_newest` is false and the sweep goes to `settle`. There the lower's sources finished before the higher gate started, and the lower id is not higher. So no sweep re-runs the higher's red deferral. It stays red at a head where a later green gate exists, until a human re-runs it. At the base the same gate waited one poll and judged PASS (the removed check "the higher deferring edit gate waits on the lower whose listing lags, then judges, never a red deferral"), so this is a regression the change introduces.

Reproduction (the reviewer's own instrument, disclosed; ev/probe_settle.py over sweep_selftest's World): lower run 1 created 10, units done 40, gate 50-60 green; higher run 2 created 52, gate 55-56 red (the deferral). Swept from run 1: `posts=[] SWEEP-DONE run=1 reruns=0`; swept from run 2: `posts=[] SWEEP-DONE run=2 reruns=0`. Null control: the same with run 2 created at 45, before the lower gate started, so the green branch applies: `posts=['repos/o/r/actions/jobs/20/rerun']`.

To repair it, settle needs to catch the higher side of a lagging pair, or any red gate whose run overlapped another run's gate start in either order, without reintroducing a loop. The fixer and design own the shape. A gate or sweep self-test case for this ordering should fail first.

## Findings

- settle leaves the higher-id deferral to a lagging lower green gate unjudged when that green gate does not cover the newest event (the Block above); repair in this PR. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER

## Evidence

The #3282 replay matches the body. Note that the base also ends PASS by the sweep: the base defect the replay reproduces is the 720 s held runner, not a missing re-judge, which agrees with the body's own account of the brief's cause.
- Race harness r10_gate_defer_race.py, head against base: the four fixture rows read wait 0 s at head and 720 s at base for 42367457809 and 42338396358; 42307493684 and 42307798573 read PASS at both ends (ev/race_head.txt, ev/race_base.txt).
- Self-tests at head: gate 77 checks, 0 failed; sweep 33 checks, 0 failed (ev/selftests_head.txt). These match the body.
- Reviewer mutants (ev/mutants.txt): overlap arm removed: sweep 2 failed (matches the body's M4). Late-source arm removed: sweep 3 failed (matches M3). A null mutant (comment line only): 33 checks, 0 failed. A judge-wait mutant did not finish in ~4 min; it was stopped and is not counted. The body's M1 covers that line.

- Roles drift `git diff merge-base...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/`: empty.

## Verdict

PR #3287 (R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER, r10-gate-busy-defer-3) at head 16452e45300be5507d6f979e5033676052d0f4e8, merge base and origin/main 4b5d771bdf8feb1f83d7d9443e5117b771a0ab76. This is review round 2: an earlier verdict/3287 at 29ee7261 was `settle-unjudged`, and this head carries its repair. The review ran from a detached worktree at the head, by the three-dot diff. The finder's harnesses were run at both ends: `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_busy_defer_3.py replay` and `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_defer_race.py`, the latter also as main's unmodified copy. Every production line the PR adds or changes was mutated, with a null control. CI on this head is GREEN.

Answers to the brief's four focus questions:
1. The #3282 replay reproduces the defect at the base and passes at the head. Base: `RESULT replay wait_s=720 first=FAIL swept=yes final=PASS`. Head: `wait_s=0 first=FAIL swept=yes final=PASS`. `final` stays flat because the sweep did fire at the base too, as the body says. The metric the replay moves is `wait_s`, the runner hold. Mutant G1, which restores the wait, puts head back to `wait_s=720`. The null mutant leaves it at 0. CI showed the defect live at this head: edit gate 128458265063 ran on main's program (`programs restored from 4b5d771b`), held its runner 16:36:00–16:48:08Z, and then published `FAIL run(s) [42388999905] at this head are still being judged`.
2. `settle` leaves nothing unjudged and loops nowhere in the cases I checked. Mutual deferral, a red decider, a cancelled decider, a red lower or green lower in a lagging pair, and real reds all behave. My mutants S2–S7 each turn a named settle check red. Every re-run judges after every source and the peer gate concluded, so no `undecided()` arm fires again (S3 and S4 kill the no-loop nulls). One gap remains, and it is not a regression: a head with a completed `ci.yml` run that has no `gate` job (see Findings).
3. `gate.judge` has one bound left, `lag_bound(why)`, for the run's own listing lag. The deferral-specific `GATE_WAIT_MAX_S` branch is gone, and `deferral()` is the only producer of the text. There is no second copy of the busy/wait rule in `tools/ci`. Two stale descriptions and one copied text pattern live outside the diff; they are carried below.
4. A deferral red at a head that a later green code run covers is re-run by the green branch (unchanged) or by `settle`. Live at this head, both edit gates were re-run and green within about 30 s of code gate 128470411243 going green (17:11:32Z → 17:12:23Z and 17:12:34Z).

## Findings

- Follow-up: two new `settle` lines survive their deletion with every self-test and the replay green (ev/mutants.txt). S9 drops the poll on a gate that completed while its run is still open. S10 drops the `live()` head-moved stop inside settle's poll. Neither breaks liveness. Under S9, `judge()` leaves that run ("run still busy") and that run's own completion sweep settles it. Under S10, a sweep re-runs gates at a superseded head, which wastes runners but leaves no red at the live head. They are still untested branches on lines this PR adds, and the PR names neither in its mutation proof. Owed: a settle self-test that kills each one. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER

R10-RCA-GATE-BUSY-DEFER-2, the root-cause seat for R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER (topic r10-gate-busy-defer-2). It ran beside that fixer and did not edit `tools/ci/`. Part of #201. The analysis is `dev/audit/rca/r10-gate-busy-defer-2.md`, indexed in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json` as `_rca.R10-RCA-GATE-BUSY-DEFER-2`.

## Re-cut note

Repair round 2, after a blocked verdict (`rca-claim-false`): the first record called #3263's edit/code-run red "designed, not the race", and main's #3276 (`812bb8747`) had fixed it as a defect. This body is re-taken whole at the head below.

- **Stale pin (unchanged finding).** ci.yml restores `tools/ci/*.py` from the payload's `pull_request.base.sha`, and a job re-run replays that payload. So each re-run of a run created before #3246 merged (`355d9965`) ran the pre-fix `gate.py`. The six mutual-deferral gates (#3261, #3265, #3255 pairs, pinned `28482ece`, `f2a01514`, `80016a71`) all ran such a copy. Process state (c).
- **#3263 (corrected).** Run 42338396358's 2-second red is the edit/code-run deferral, a second defect with its own cause. `prelude.judging()` read a deferring edit run's skipped `pr-contract` caller (listed completed under its bare name) as owed, so that run looked busy to every gate at its head, and gate.py's at-once bound dodged the wait cycle that made. #3276 fixed `judging()` and deleted the bound. RCA section 1 gives the cause, section 3 the process state (c: the self-test and #3246's `prelude` scene pinned the at-once red as the specification, not the property "a deferring run is judging") and the cost; the countermeasure is landed by #3276 and scored here.
- **Instrument.** The replay arm's exit code ignored the single-gate class, so it read rc 0 for the at-once red at `294a880d`. `DEFECTS` now counts `C3-AT-ONCE`; a single gate that waited and then deferred is `DEFERRED`, the bounded wait, not a defect. The arm's remaining blindness (the wait cycle itself) is stated in its docstring and RCA section 1.
- **Countermeasure, proposed and not built.** A re-run of a gate whose pinned programs differ from the base tip becomes a ci.yml dispatch (`tools/ci`, the gate fixer's and the orchestrator's).

## Head

`71710c566283e302de7db598c8a6fc3045a41dbf` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`b38e5c08bddba4817e362c450e7369ddd1b819ae`, branch `fix/r10-rca-gate-busy-defer-2`: the reviewed head `d5c4a06b` plus origin/main (merged by the bot as `510b2a108`; origin/main `b4ec2f332` is an ancestor) plus one repair commit. origin/main was `b4ec2f332` at 2026-11-07 15:07Z, at the final `tools/pr/prepr.sh` run, so no further merge was owed. The three-dot diff adds the harness and its fixture, the RCA document, the `_rca` entry, the harness's `tests/closures.json` INERT READS entry and the delivery row.

## Mutation proof

This PR adds no production line. The detector it adds is the `replay` arm, proven against real program copies (`git archive <sha> tools/ci tools/pr`) and two mutants:

- Red on the defect: `replay --ci` at `28482ece`, `f2a01514` and `80016a71` gives rc 1, `DEADLOCK` on the three pairs. At `294a880d` it gives rc 1, `C3-AT-ONCE` on the three edit/code-run scenes.
- Green on the fixes: rc 0 at `812bb8747` and at this head's `tools/ci`, the pairs `DECIDED` (naps 0 and 0 in #3261) and the C3 scenes `DEFERRED` with naps 12.
- Scoring mutant: a copy of the harness with `DEFECTS = ("DEADLOCK", "HALF-DEFERRED")` gives rc 0 at `294a880d`; the unmutated copy, relocated the same way, gives rc 1.
- M17 (busy()'s later-started-gate tie-break deleted) on this head's `gate.py` **survives** the arm, rc 0: under #3276's `judging()` the pair no longer reads each other busy. `gate.py --self-test`'s M17 row pins it; the arm does not replace the self-test. M24 named code #3276 deleted and is not run.

## Null control

- Pre-#3246 programs give rc 1 and #3246's gives rc 0 on the same listings; the fixed program decides the pairs the stale program deadlocks.
- At `294a880d` the C3 scenes read `C3-AT-ONCE` with naps 0, at `812bb8747` and this head `DEFERRED` with naps 12, so the class separates the at-once publication from the bounded wait (`GATE_WAIT_MAX_S` 720 s at `POLL_S` 60 s, the recorded code run still unfinished at 29 minutes).
- The arm refuses, and does not go green, on a fixture whose pair gates did not overlap in time or whose gate never started.
- The compare the countermeasure would run, `git diff --quiet 28482ece 294a880d -- <restored paths>`, gives rc 1; the same sha on both sides gives rc 0.

## Figures

- Replay at each program: `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_gate_busy_defer_2.py replay --ci <export>/tools/ci`, with `<export>` from `git archive <sha> tools/ci tools/pr`. rc 1 at `28482ece`, `f2a01514`, `80016a71` and `294a880d`; rc 0 at `812bb8747`; `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_gate_busy_defer_2.py replay` at this head prints `RESULT replay ... defects=no`.
- Pins of the 9 recorded gates: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_gate_busy_defer_2.py pins` prints `RESULT pins gates=9 stale=6`.
- Fixture: `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_gate_busy_defer_2.json`, sha1 f926d6a67b5582c172f49cb436a09e7ff7b63b70 (`sha1sum`), unchanged by this repair.
- Census (the first handoff's figures, from `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_gate_busy_defer_2.py census --since 2026-11-07T03:45:14Z --until 2026-11-07T04:50:21Z`). **Re-derived in this repair** at 2026-11-07 after the review's run failed on proxy resets; the same command printed the same three rows: stale `gates=46 {'defer': 21, 'other-red': 1, 'pass': 24}`, 7 PRs, `reruns=36`; fixed `gates=3 {'defer': 3}`, all the at-once edit/code-run red, now #3276-class; unpinned `gates=5`.
- Recurrence, rule pinned at a time: `git log --first-parent --format=%h --since=2026-10-23T00:00:00Z origin/main -- 'tools/ci/*.py' tools/pr/codeql_scope.py tests/closure.py tools/pr/cancel_superseded.py | wc -l` gives 30 at origin/main `b4ec2f332` (15 with `--since=2026-10-31T00:00:00Z`). The same rule over `tools/ci/gate.py tools/ci/prelude.py` since `2026-10-31T00:00:00Z` lists 4 merges (#3276, #3246, #3230, #3205). The count moves with each merge to those paths; the rule is the record.
- Ledger: `python3 tools/audit/fold_ledger.py check` prints `0 violation(s)`, 137 rca entries.
- Scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out`, the script `tests/entities.py`. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` prints `ALL 2645 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`; `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- Seam enumeration (fixer step 8). Rule: the `git checkout "$PINNED" --` lines in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, each naming programs a run restores from its payload base. Each returned seam (prelude/gate: `tools/ci/*.py`, `tools/pr/codeql_scope.py`, `tests/closure.py`; cancel-superseded: `tools/pr/cancel_superseded.py`; refresh: `tools/ci/*.py`) is in the class, open, dispositioned in RCA section 3 and covered by the proposed countermeasure 5.2.
- Instrument blindness: the single-gate scenes judge one gate beside a code run listed as recorded, so the replay scores the at-once publication and not the wait cycle `judging()` made; #3276's fixture self-test in `gate.py` pins the cycle (RCA section 1).

## Red checks

Read with `pull_request_read get_check_runs` on PR 3278 at 15:07Z, all 86 check runs in one page, at head `510b2a108` (the bot merge this repair builds on). The repair commit `b38e5c08` had no check runs at the time of writing.

- `gate` cancelled (run 42383179334, job 128439401244, with `tests / coverage`, `tests / closures`, `tests / fast (3.14)`, `governance / instrument-self-tests` and the other cancelled lanes): the run was superseded at 15:05:24Z by run 42383590829, whose `gate` job 128439014625 is in progress. Cleared by the newer run, class: superseded run, not a failure of this diff. The earlier head `d5c4a06b` had the edit-gate deferral `gate` red (job 128409314146, run 42374407743, "FAIL run(s) [42372899314, 42373060299] ... still being judged"), cleared when the code runs classified GREEN at 13:25:08Z, and the same `tests / nightly-status` red (job 128405124320, run 42372899314).
- No open `code-scanning alert` at the read.

Until it lands, after any pinned-program merge, dispatch ci.yml (`pr=N base=main`) for each PR whose latest gate is a stale-pinned red (RCA 5.3). Carry: #201

merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-PLAN-LANES: plan page places instrument and CI groups in the core model lane
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
Owner ruling (tvofi 2026-11-06), verbatim: "The HTML plan seems to incorrectly place some instrument or CI fixes in the core model lane, fix that".

Where the lane is decided: `roster_lane` in `tools/plan/replan.py` writes each group's `lane` into the plan JSON, and `tools/audit/seat/plan_page.py` only draws that field. `roster_lane` placed a group by `kind` (`instrument`, `policy`), then by a list of name prefixes, and **every group neither rule placed fell through to Core model**. So a new CI hotfix, an RCA seat, a tooling chore or a doc group was drawn as core-model work, and the stamp cadence counted it as production.

The fix is at that source, not per group. The kind and name rules keep their precedence, so Learners, Product UX, Replay and Docs placements by name do not change. After them, `roster_lane` reads:
1. **The files the group owns** (`files` + `hot_files`). When every one is an instrument, CI or record path (`tools/`, `tests/`, `.github/`, `.claude/`, `dev/`, `docs/`, or a root record such as `CLAUDE.md`), the group is Instruments. It is Docs instead when it is a `doc` kind, or when it touches user docs (`docs/`, `README.md`) without landing a tool (`tools/`, `.github/`, `.claude/`). A single `custom_components/` file or a bare filename, in either list, keeps it core.
2. **Then a tool-landing kind or roster class**, for a group whose roster names no file: `kind` in `INSTRUMENT_KINDS` (`instrument`, `policy`, `rca`, `tooling`) or `class: instrument`. `work_class` already priced those kinds as instruments. It now reads the same tuple, so the lane and the duration class cannot disagree on which kinds land tools.

Alternatives considered:
- (a) Reading the roster's own `lane` code. It is not a lane in this sense: production groups owning only `custom_components/` files carry `lane: IN`. So it lost.
- (b) Adding the misplaced names to the prefix list. That is a per-group spelling list, and the next CI hotfix would fall out of it again (fixer.md step 17). So it lost too.

**Round 2 (this repair).** The review blocked at `8ff3432a` as mutation-vacuous. Dropping `hot_files` from `_owned_lane` (m8) survived the self-test, because every control put the bare filename or the `custom_components/` path in `files`. The production code is unchanged in this round. The self-test gains four `hot_files` cases on a group with `files: ["tools/x.py"]`:
- an integration hot file (`custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/x.py`) stays Core model;
- a bare `coordinator.py` hot file stays Core model;
- a bare tool basename (`merge_train.py`) in `hot_files` stays Core model, which is the conservatism the brief's rule (1) prescribes and the reviewer's follow-up asked to pin;
- an instrument-path hot file (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) keeps it Instruments.

m8 is now killed by three of them. I re-ran all twelve of the reviewer's mutants myself, and all are killed.

## Head

`c7c5cef52a49bed59ee4c8a42e495ef2dae30db5` is this PR's head, and every figure below was re-taken at it (worktree of the head, 2026-11-07). Its code is the handoff code head `aa5c0505b73c77d1ab5a650af2da58759b8b307a` (`8ff3432a965df930fb54e7aa6ffd52bf210e5f3f`, the reviewed head, plus a merge of origin/main at `f2a015142714383722bf49d7ab20d8398ec9674c` and one commit that adds the self-test cases): `git diff aa5c0505 c7c5cef5 -- tools dev tests` is empty and `replan.py` is byte-identical between them. The three-dot diff against the merge base `f2a015142` touches `tools/plan/replan.py` and `dev/programme/delivery/3265.md` only. `git diff 80016a71f f2a015142 -- tools/plan` is empty, so the main merge reaches nothing `replan.py` reads. origin/main is now `b4ec2f332fe3ab8dcf169bd3066276d3bb8848ab`; the head has not merged it, and the merge base is unchanged. `tools/pr/prepr.sh` ran clean (rc=0) at `aa5c0505`, whose tools are identical to the head's. This body re-take changed no code and pushed nothing to `fix/` or `handoff/`.

## Mutation proof

Method: for each mutant, take a `git archive` copy of the head, apply one exact string substitution to `tools/plan/replan.py` (it must match once), and run `python3 -I tools/plan/replan.py --self-test`. The unmutated copy (m0) exits rc=0 with no lane failure. The FAIL lines are the self-test's own check names.
- m1, delete `if owned := _owned_lane(group): return owned` → rc=1: `lane: a CI-only group is Instruments`, `lane: a tests-and-tools group is Instruments`, `lane: a docs-only doc group is Docs`, `lane: a user-docs group is Docs`, `lane null control: docs plus a tool is Instruments, not Docs`, `lane: user docs with a dev harness are Docs`, `lane: an instrument-path hot file keeps a tool group Instruments`
- m2, delete the `INSTRUMENT_KINDS`/`class` fallback → rc=1: `lane: an RCA group with no files is Instruments`, `lane: a tooling group with no files is Instruments`, `lane: a roster class instrument with no files is Instruments`
- m3, drop the `class == "instrument"` arm → rc=1: `lane: a roster class instrument with no files is Instruments`
- m4, `not all(` → `not any(` → rc=1: `lane null control: a mixed group stays Core model`, `lane null control: an integration hot file keeps a tool group Core model`, `lane null control: a bare hot filename keeps a tool group Core model`, `lane null control: a bare tool basename in hot_files stays Core model`
- m5, drop the `not files` guard → rc=1: `lane null control: a group with no files stays Core model`, `lane null control: a production group with no files stays Core model`
- m6, drop the tooling exclusion from `user_docs` → rc=1: `lane null control: docs plus a tool is Instruments, not Docs`
- m7, drop the `kind == "doc"` arm → rc=1: `lane: a docs-only doc group is Docs`
- **m8, drop `+ list(group.get("hot_files") or [])` → rc=1**: `lane null control: an integration hot file keeps a tool group Core model`, `lane null control: a bare hot filename keeps a tool group Core model`, `lane null control: a bare tool basename in hot_files stays Core model`. At the reviewed head `8ff3432a`, the same m8 substitution exits rc=0 with no lane failure. That is the block, reproduced, and it is the failing-test-first for this round.
- m9, remove `docs/` from `_NON_PRODUCT_PREFIXES` → rc=1: `lane: a user-docs group is Docs`, `lane null control: docs plus a tool is Instruments, not Docs`, `lane: user docs with a dev harness are Docs`
- m10, empty `_NON_PRODUCT_FILES` → rc=1: `lane: a docs-only doc group is Docs`, `lane: a user-docs group is Docs`, `lane: user docs with a dev harness are Docs`
- m11, remove `rca` from `INSTRUMENT_KINDS` → rc=1: `lane: an RCA group with no files is Instruments`
- m12, `user_docs = True or (...)` → rc=1: `lane: a CI-only group is Instruments`, `lane: a tests-and-tools group is Instruments`, `lane null control: docs plus a tool is Instruments, not Docs`, `lane: an instrument-path hot file keeps a tool group Instruments`

Result: 12 of 12 killed, and the unmutated copy exits rc=0. These runs were made at `aa5c0505`; `replan.py` is byte-identical at `c7c5cef5`, so they stand for the head. The unmutated self-test re-run at `c7c5cef5` prints `self-test: 0 failed`.

## Null control

- A real core-model group stays core. These controls all pass at the head:
  - a `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py` group;
  - a mixed tools + `custom_components/` group;
  - a file-less group;
  - a bare `coordinator.py` in `files`;
  - a file-less `kind: production, class: production` group;
  - and, new this round, a tool group whose `hot_files` holds an integration path, a bare `coordinator.py` or a bare `merge_train.py`.
- Name rules keep precedence: R10-COP-GATE with only a `tools/` file stays Learners, and R10-DEEPLINK-CENSUS with `kind: rca` stays Product UX.
- The new Instruments case is the positive control for the three new Core-model cases. It shows that `hot_files` is read both ways, not only as a veto.
- On the live plan, no group outside the core lane changes lane. Learners 8, Product UX 14 and Replay 9 are identical at both ends. Every moved group was Core model at main.
- m8 has no live effect today. Rule: `roster_lane(g) != roster_lane({**g, "hot_files": []})` over every live roster group (364 at roster blob `1477cf7acb05`). It returns 0 groups. Had m8's arm mattered live, that rule would list the group. So round 2 pins the arm, and it does not change the plan.

## Figures

All live figures below are from the roster at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster`: commit `087aab43b137e909333e01913fb1437383f0b6da`, roster blob `1477cf7acb05` (`wave-r10-groups.json`), re-read 2026-11-07. Each run used `--start 2026-11-06T22:00:00Z --roster-ref origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster`, with `tools/plan/replan.py` at main `b4ec2f332` (a worktree of it) and at the head `c7c5cef5` (a worktree of it). These figures are a function of the roster ref, not of main's tip; the roster has grown since the earlier body (351 groups, blob `e7207ea34c7f`).
- `python3 tools/plan/replan.py ... --out plan.json`, then `jq -r '[.groups[]|.lane]|group_by(.)|map("\(.[0]) \(length)")'`, over 364 groups at each end:
  - main: Core model 135, Instruments 196, Docs 2, Learners 8, Product UX 14, Replay 9;
  - head: Core model 65, Instruments 260, Docs 8, Learners 8, Product UX 14, Replay 9.
- The same count over open groups (`select(.done|not)`):
  - main: Core model 28, Instruments 29, Docs 1, Product UX 2, Replay 1;
  - head: Core model 12, Instruments 55, Docs 4, Product UX 2, Replay 1.
- Groups whose `lane` differs between the two plan files: 70. All moved from Core model: 64 to Instruments and 6 to Docs. 17 of them are open (`jq` over the two files, rule: `lane` in main's plan differs from `lane` in the head's). The table lists each one. Learners, Product UX and Replay are identical at both ends.
- The build's `summary` line: stamps 7 at main, 3 at the head; CI 7200.0 min at main, 7762.5 min at the head; batches 57 at main, 66 at the head. Not every count moves the way the stamp cadence alone suggests: the head's plan also reads each group's `done` flag from the same roster, and the two plans do not agree on how many groups are done (303 at main, 290 at the head), so I do not claim a direction for CI minutes or batches here. The wall-clock closure is the same at both ends (`2026-11-13T03:02:00Z`, 149.03 h). `python3 tools/plan/replan.py --check --plan plan.json` prints `PLAN OK` on the head's plan.
- `python3 -I tools/plan/replan.py --self-test` → `self-test: 0 failed` at the head.
- Scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff f2a015142714383722bf49d7ab20d8398ec9674c` at the head → `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out`, running `tests/entities.py`. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` exits 0 at the head. `python3 tests/structure.py`, `python3 tests/env_drift.py --claims-only f2a015142`, `python3 tests/closure.py selftest`, `python3 tests/layout.py` and `python3 tests/harness_headers.py` (the last with `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`) each exit 0 at the head.

The bare-basename seam (the reviewer's follow-up), enumerated by a rule and not by instance: Core-model groups at the head that own no `custom_components/` file (`roster_lane(g) == "Core model"` and no `files` or `hot_files` entry starts with `custom_components/`). There are 7. Each owns no file at all, so none is core because of a bare filename:
- open: R10-CATALOG-PR (`owner-step`, the owner's marketplace step) and R10-COMBI-TANK (`production`, the combi-tank design);
- done: R10-CARD-VOICE (`feature`), R10-STORE-RACES (`production`), R10-RCA-HEADMOVED (`kind: study`), R10-ROSTER-PUSH-RACE (`kind: defect`) and R10-NIGHTLY-SLOW-ROLLING (`kind: production`, `class: hotfix`).

The last three may be instrument work. The roster records neither a file nor a tool-landing kind for them, so the remedy is the roster's data, not another name rule. All three are done.

comments.body:
Fix review: blocked 8ff3432a965df930fb54e7aa6ffd52bf210e5f3f mutation-vacuous: dropping hot_files from _owned_lane survives the self-test and moves a custom_components group out of Core model

bus-nonce: c69f2b2f30f4a04a12cfa21cd9ef4474

Round 1. Reviewed from a detached worktree at 8ff3432a965df930fb54e7aa6ffd52bf210e5f3f, merge base 80016a71f567d936450d8708abcbb79d9e8071d7. The finder's harness: none is committed. This is an owner-reported hotfix, so the harness is the owner's ruling plus the live plan. I built the enumeration below myself and disclose it as mine.

Owner ruling (tvofi 2026-11-06), verbatim: "The HTML plan seems to incorrectly place some instrument or CI fixes in the core model lane, fix that".

## Block

- Claim: the PR's predicates in `_owned_lane`/`roster_lane` are each pinned by a named self-test check (brief item 3; body `## Mutation proof`).
- Evidence: mutant m8 replaces `list(group.get("files") or []) + list(group.get("hot_files") or [])` with `list(group.get("files") or [])` in `tools/plan/replan.py` `_owned_lane`. On a `git archive` copy of the head, `python3 tools/plan/replan.py --self-test` then exits rc=0 (`ev/mutants-all.txt`, line `MUTANT m8-hotfiles rc=0`).
- Metric: the probe group `{"kind": "fix", "files": ["tools/ci/gate.py"], "hot_files": ["custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py"]}` is drawn as `Core model` at the head and as `Instruments` under m8 (`ev/m8-probe.txt`). The same holds with a bare `hot_files: ["coordinator.py"]`, and `work_class` flips to `instrument` with it. So the arm that keeps a group touching the integration in the core lane, which is the brief's item-1 null control, is unpinned. The self-test's controls put the bare filename and the `custom_components/` path in `files` only. Yet on the live roster, bare names occur in `hot_files` (for example R10-FAHRENHEIT `hot_files: ["coordinator.py"]`).
- Perturbation: m8 itself; the harness (`--self-test`) does not move under it, which is the defect.
- Live effect today: none. All 11 roster groups whose `files` are all non-product but whose `hot_files` are not are `kind: instrument`, so the kind rule places them before `_owned_lane` (`ev/m8-live.txt`). The block concerns the pin, not the current plan.

merges.body:
stamp.py `record_flush` waited for a record merge while a live `refs/heads/train-hold` made every beat it dispatched exit `skip-train-hold`. Its three dispatches were spent under the hold, and the timeout named no hold. It now reads the hold itself and spends no dispatch under one. A second change, in `merge_train.py`, keeps the hold DELETE from being skipped by a second TERM or HUP during the unwind, and (repair round 2) delivers a first stop that lands in a batch's closing release instead of discarding it.

Repair round 2 (verdict/3280, blocked d65bcee9bdfb): `Train.batch` calls `unwind()` in the `finally` of every batch, and the round-1 `stop_ignored` set `SIG_IGN`, which discards a signal. A first TERM in batch k's release was lost and batch k+1 merged. `stop_ignored` now records the signal in a handler that does not raise, restores the handlers, and delivers the first recorded signal through the restored handler after the hold DELETE. Entered with a stop already unwinding (a `SystemExit` in flight), further signals are dropped, as the brief requires. The duplicate `import contextlib` is removed.

Alternatives: masking with `signal.pthread_sigmask` was not taken (it leaves the signal pending to the kernel, with no hook to say when the stop is already unwinding). No `train.sh` trap change. One `Train.unwind` method serves `train` and `batch`. The hold is an injected collaborator `held`, defaulting to `train_hold` (zero REST), the bound read from `nightly.yml`'s `HOLD_MAX_AGE_S=`, never a second literal. A hold never refuses the flush; an unreadable hold or bound reads as no hold.

`record_flush` gives a dispatch back (`count - 1`) whenever a hold appears after one, even if that beat had already run. A hold that flaps can therefore re-dispatch more than `FLUSH_MAX_DISPATCHES` beats in total; the 7200 s deadline bounds it, which is accepted.

Shared file: `tools/release/stamp.py` is also changed by the hotfix R10-FLY-STAMP-FLUSH-COST (topic r10-fly-stamp-flush-cost). This round changes no line of stamp.py; its stamp.py change is round 1's `record_flush`/hold reading. Whichever lands second merges `origin/main` and reruns `stamp.py --self-test`; no ordering is required by this PR.

Closes: triage batch 131 P402 (`dev/programme/triage/s6-batch131.md`, which exists only at triage ref `cd88cf6bd00d`, not at origin/main or this head).

Fix review: blocked d65bcee9bdfb2cc11302d1c96d4bf00659ec24db class-open: Train.batch runs unwind after every batch, so a first TERM or HUP landing in a between-batch release is discarded by SIG_IGN and the train goes on to merge the next batch

bus-nonce: 206cf0ae7035dcafbdd6b18a4ab76231

## Block

Round 1. `stop_ignored` sets `SIG_IGN` for TERM and HUP, which **discards** a signal and does not defer it. `Train.unwind` is documented as running "once a stop is already unwinding it", and in `train()` that holds. `Train.batch` (merge_train.py:3205-3208 at the head) is different: it calls `self.unwind()` in the `finally` of **every** batch, including one that completed normally. A first, and only, operator TERM or HUP that lands while batch k releases its worktrees and hold is therefore thrown away. The loop then goes on to `queue_take` and `_batch(k+1)`, and that batch merges.

I measured this with my own probe, not the finder's or the fixer's. It is `ev/probe/batch_swallow.py` and `ev/probe/run.sh`: two batches, stubbed `run` with a 2 s `git worktree remove`, and one TERM sent 0.3 s into batch 1's unwind.
- At the head (`ev/probe-batch-swallow-head.txt`): `BATCH T` … DELETE, then **`BATCH T-b2`** … DELETE, then `RETURNED rc=0`. The stop was lost and the second batch ran.
- Null control, with the base's unwind and the same driver (`ev/probe-batch-swallow-null.txt`): `SYSTEMEXIT 143` after batch 1, so the stop is honoured. That run shows the original hold-DELETE skip, which is the bug the PR fixes.

The fix trades the hold-ref leak for a lost stop request on the path that merges pull requests. That is the worse failure. The brief asked for the unwind to ignore further signals "once it starts", meaning once a stop is unwinding, and not on every batch boundary. The self-test `_unwind_self_test` drives only `train()`, so this seam is untested.

The cure is the fixer's to choose. One sound shape: keep the signal but defer it. Inside the block, record the signal number in a handler that does not raise, or mask it with `signal.pthread_sigmask(SIG_BLOCK, …)`. Re-raise or unmask it after the hold DELETE, so a pending stop is delivered then. Add a batch-path arm: one TERM during batch 1's unwind, assert there is no `BATCH T-b2` and a non-zero exit, with this probe's mutant as the control.

## Findings

- `import contextlib` is now imported twice, at merge_train.py:277 and :280. The diff adds a duplicate of an existing import. Carry: R10-FLY-STAMP-FLUSH-HOLD
- The body's `Closes: triage batch 131 P402 (dev/programme/triage/s6-batch131.md)` path resolves neither at origin/main nor at the head. It exists only at `cd88cf6bd00d`, the triage ref named in the roster brief. Name that ref beside the path. Carry: R10-FLY-STAMP-FLUSH-HOLD
- `record_flush` gives back a dispatch whenever a hold appears after one (`count - 1`). This happens even when that beat already ran before the hold appeared. A hold that flaps can therefore re-dispatch more than `FLUSH_MAX_DISPATCHES` beats in total within the 7200 s deadline. The deadline bounds it, so I judge this acceptable, but the body should say so. Carry: R10-FLY-STAMP-FLUSH-HOLD

merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-SAV-ESTIMATE part 2 (part 1 merged as #3220), topic r10-sav-wood-heat. This is repair round 5, after fix review round 4 blocked `8bc540e0` as ci-red on CodeQL code-scanning alert 50.

## Re-cut

This is past the third round, so this body replaces the earlier ones. Every figure below was re-taken in this pass, at the head named under `## Head`.

**Carry A (owner ruling, tvofi 2026-11-04).** The reference has no wood, and wood's heat counts in the saving. Wherever wood is configured, the saving the integration states says that it includes wood's heat and excludes firewood's cost.

**What the PR builds.**
- `wood_fuel.py` `saving_includes_wood(data)` is the one definition. It is `True` where wood is configured (`show_whatif`).
- The receipt event (`notifier.py` `_monthly_receipt`) and the `MonthlySavingsSensor` attribute `saving_includes_wood` both read that definition.
- The card's receipt (`receiptHtml`) and savings table (`_savingsPageHtml`) show `savings.wood_note` on a wood house.
- The "Monthly receipt" message in `blueprints/automation/notifications.yaml` appends the card's `savings.wood_note` text, guarded by `data.saving_sek is not none and data.saving_includes_wood`. There is one wording, the card's.
- `docs/automations.md`, `docs/dashboard-card.md`, `docs/how-it-works.md` and the README's sensor row say so.
- `tools/policy/agreement.mjs` `SHARED_GRAMMARS` registers the card-string extractor that the pin and the render harness share, as `identical:`.
- The five `coord_*` golden captures each gain the one boolean key. They are claimed in `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` and were not re-recorded.

**This round: the CodeQL red, fixed at the root.** `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_receipt_render.py` built `jinja2.Environment()`, whose autoescape is off, and CodeQL flagged that as alert 50, `py/jinja2/autoescape-false`. The harness now builds `jinja2.Environment(autoescape=True)`. The alert is not suppressed or dismissed.
- Why `autoescape=True` and not `select_autoescape()`: `select_autoescape()` keys on a template file's extension. This harness builds its template from a string, so the result would depend on that function's `default_for_string` argument. `autoescape=True` states the setting directly.
- The reviewer's warning, handled deliberately: autoescape escapes only an expression's output (`{{ … }}`), never a template's literal text. The note is literal text in the blueprint, outside any `{{ }}`, so its apostrophe is not escaped. The harness therefore counts the note as written, with no escaped form and no `Markup` wrapper. The expressions in the message render numbers and the currency code, which contain no escapable character. So the rendered text is the same as what Home Assistant's template engine (a sandboxed environment with autoescape off) sends.
- The perturbation that shows the warning was real but does not apply here: on a copy of the blueprint with the note moved inside a `{{ "…" }}` expression, the harness reads `RESULT wood notes=0 want=1 DEFECT`. The apostrophe becomes `'` there. So if a later edit moves the note into an expression, the wood arm goes red loudly rather than passing silently.
- Alternatives considered. Dismissing the alert with a reason: rejected, because the brief requires a root fix and a dismissal leaves the pattern in the tree. `select_autoescape(default_for_string=False)`: rejected, because it is still autoescape-off for this string template, and CodeQL's query reads it the same way.

**The pin and why it is a source pin.** `tests/entities.py` loads the blueprint and finds the "Monthly receipt" option. It requires three things: the card's `savings.wood_note` text occurs exactly once in the message; it sits inside `{% if data.saving_sek is not none and data.saving_includes_wood %}`; and the event declares `saving_includes_wood` (`notifier.EVENT_DATA`). It does not render the template, because CI's interpreter (`venv-ci`) has no jinja2. That is a design choice, stated here. The render harness measures the rendering under `venv-ha`.

**The class rule.** The question: where does the integration state the metered saving to a user?
- R1: `git grep -n -E 'savings_sek|saving_sek|savings_months|plan_monthly_savings|MonthlySavingsSensor|EVENT_MONTHLY_RECEIPT|monthly_receipt|saving_includes_wood' -- custom_components blueprints docs README.md ':!docs/design' ':!custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/www'`
- R2 (prose that states the saving without naming a key): `git grep -n -i -E 'monthly receipt|savings page|plan monthly savings|than a plain thermostat' -- docs README.md blueprints ':!docs/design'`
- R3 (the card's keys): `git grep -n -o -E '\b(savings|receipt|headline)\.[a-z_]+' -- custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/www/heatpump-optimizer-card.js`

`docs/design/2026-09-05-monthly-savings-history/` is excluded. It is a dated design record that recounts a past design (fixer step 10).

| seam | what it states | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `ledger.py` `savings_months` | the producer | built (#3220) |

R10-RCA-LIVEHEAD-CANCEL, the root-cause seat. The two whole-run cancels at live heads on #3241 (run 42332985078, attempt 1) and #3232 (run 42329221705, attempt 2) were not `concurrency:` cancels, runner loss or `cancel_superseded.py`. GitHub annotates every cancelled job `The run was canceled by @tvofi.`: a cancel POSTed under the owner's credential, from outside every in-tree canceller, and followed by a rerun under the same credential. The class is routine: 155 such cancels at live heads in 76 h.

This PR lands:
- `dev/audit/rca/r10-livehead-cancel.md`: cause, process state (a), class reach, cost test, countermeasure and refusals;
- `dev/audit/harnesses/livehead_cancels.py`: the detector, which attributes every cancelled `ci.yml` attempt to its canceller and tests it against the live head;
- the class `N-livehead-operator-cancel` and the `_rca` record `R10-RCA-LIVEHEAD-CANCEL` in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`;
- the class id registered in `finding.schema.json`'s `class_guess` enum, and in `.claude/workflows/audit-find.js`'s `CLASS_GUESS` and `FINDING_REPORT`, the readers the `agreement` lane pairs with the ledger;

The process that sent the cancels cannot be named from GitHub data. The orchestrator's seat transcripts can name it (RCA section 6).

## Round

First round. Reviewed from a detached worktree at 2a8b8f0ccdf5ce4f3ed2f8101e201de7caf7354a, merge base 567565eec1600208b637453ea08d7e8e4b8138f8, three-dot diff. No role-file drift: `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty.

## Findings

- Surviving mutant in the detector's selftest. The mutant: in `canceller()`, the `higher priority waiting request` branch is disabled and `"@concurrency"` is returned in its place, so a `concurrency:` cancel is attributed to an operator login. `--selftest` still prints `ok`, and over the cache the CLASS line stays 155, because the selftest has no concurrency-annotated attempt and the 76 h window holds no concurrency cancel at all (there is no `by=concurrency` row). The unmutated code does attribute correctly: perturbation P-concurrency, which rewrites every `@tvofi` annotation to the concurrency line, prints `CLASS ... 0` (ev/perturb.txt). But nothing in the tree pins it. A regression would go unseen as soon as a concurrency group becomes able to cancel a `ci.yml` run, and that is exactly when the reading after a countermeasure would be taken. Claim: the concurrency branch is unpinned. Evidence: ev/mutants.txt, mutant 4. Harness: `livehead_cancels.py --selftest`. Metric: selftest result and CLASS count. Perturbation: the mutant itself, under which both stay flat. Owed: one synthetic `Canceling since a higher priority waiting request` attempt in `selftest()`, expected `by=concurrency` and out of class. That is a precondition for reading the CLASS line after the bounded pause lands. Carry: R10-CI-PRIORITY-PAUSE
- `NULLCONTROL-HEAD` and `NULLCONTROL-BOT` force the classified rows (`dict(r, live=False)` and `dict(r, by="@github-actions[bot]")`) after `classify()` and `canceller()` have already run. So they pin only the two terms of `in_class`, and never the attribution or the live-head computation. Under every one of the five mutants (ev/mutants.txt), including `live: True` (CLASS 184) and `head_at` without its time bound (CLASS 23), `NULLCONTROL-HEAD` printed `live=0 class=0`. The body's "So the class count is not something the classifier produces whatever its input" (RCA section 4) therefore overstates what these lines show. The property itself holds under perturbations of the inputs, which I ran on copies of the cache: P-concurrency, P-bot and P-superseded (a newer-head run injected 1 s before each cancel) each print `CLASS ... 0` (ev/perturb.txt). So the class count stands, and the in-tree control is weaker than described. Owed: replace the two forced-row lines with perturbations of the inputs (rewrite the annotation, inject a newer head) inside the harness, so that every reading carries them. Carry: R10-CI-PRIORITY-PAUSE

## Evidence

- RESULT judge(1) root-cause record: named cause (a whole-run cancel POSTed under the `tvofi` credential, outside every in-tree canceller), process state (a), cost test with numbers (155 cancels, 2864.7 runner-min, restart median 906 s), countermeasure (detector, 0 s standing cost), refusals of candidates 1-4, and the parts missing (the sending process) all present in dev/audit/rca/r10-livehead-cancel.md and in the `_rca` record.
- RESULT the two events, re-read via `gh api` (ev/events.txt): 42332985078/1 cancelled, sha 96987ab3d722, updated 03:25:07Z, attempt 2 started 03:25:29Z (actor tvofi); 42329221705/2 cancelled, sha 28e4375441e6, updated 03:49:41Z, attempt 3 started 03:50:51Z (actor tvofi). All five cited jobs (128283882523, 128284504740, 128288382623, 128288382597, 128288382585) are annotated `The run was canceled by @tvofi.`
- RESULT detector at the head, my own fetch at 06:06-06:26Z (ev/harness-head.txt): `CLASS live-head external cancels: 155, minutes lost 2864.7`; CANCELLED rows identical to the body's (182/154/29/32/1/1/1/17/2); FOLLOW restarted 81 (1861.2), duplicate 5 (153.0), dropped 69 (850.5); restart gap min 22, median 906, max 7496, 18 within 120 s; NULLCONTROL lines 0. Both brief events are in `--list`. ## Block

The body's carry 3 says a `Fold (x): Carry:` answer "is checked against the roster in `check --body` and in `pr`", and names only the `pr` wiring as unpinned. The `check --body` wiring is unpinned as well, and `check --body` is the path pr-contract runs. Under each mutant the real CLI (`check --body` on `Closes #7` / `Fold (a): Carry: R10-INVENTED`, with an issue-folds file holding `Fold (a): x`) exits 0. Unmutated, it exits 1 with `FOLD-UNANSWERED fold (a) answer `Carry: R10-INVENTED` is refused: R10-INVENTED is not a group of the roster`. The body's mutant `for m in ():` kills `fold_problems`'s loop, but not the CLI line that feeds it. The self-test already has the harness the cure needs: `cli()` in `_self_test` drives `main(["check", "--body", ...])` with `--issue-folds-file` and a stubbed `load_dests`. The cure is one arm there: `Fold (a): Carry: R10-INVENTED` refused with rc 1, and `Fold (a): Carry: R10-CONS` accepted as the null control. Both mutants must then go red. Also correct the figure in Findings below.

## Findings

- Surviving mutants A and B on the `check --body` fold-destination wiring (`tools/audit/carry_audit.py:927`, `:929`), as given under Block. Metric: the failed-check count and the CLI's rc. Perturbation: each mutant moves the CLI's rc from 1 to 0 and leaves the self-test count at 0 failed. Carry: R10-BODY-CONTRACT
- The body's `## Figures` says the self-test "at the merge base ... printed 366 checks" and names that base as cb48d97e2. Re-measured, it prints `carry_audit self-test: 364 checks, 0 failed` at the actual merge base 57958d6a4, at cb48d97e2 and at 4b7e1770b (the base of code head 95a5cca4). The diff adds 24 arms (5 spellings x 2, 1 uppercase answer, 4 null spellings, 4 roster-destination arms, 2 owner-comment arms, 2 separator arms, 1 Round arm), and 364 + 24 = 388, which matches the head. The 366 is wrong, and the named base is not this PR's merge base. Following fixer.md step 3 ("name the instrument, never the number"), the body should state the instrument rather than a count. Carry: R10-BODY-CONTRACT
- The `pr` subcommand's fold wiring (`carry_audit.py:956`) is unpinned, as the body itself declares in carry 3. It is recorded here so that the cure for the Block also covers it, either with a stubbed `read_pr`/`gh_json` arm or with a recorded reason. Carry: R10-BODY-CONTRACT

merges.body:
ref_privacy read a cloud seat's own paths as a host identity. On uid 0 with HOME=/root, a line citing that home was refused as home-directory. With HOME=/nonexistent, it was refused as home-directory and account-name, where `nonexistent` is the name derived from the placeholder home's basename. `Identity.of_host` now drops homes that name no person before it derives names from them: the no-home placeholder, and a public account's own home (`_public_home`). `_HOST_PATH` is untouched, so a real `/Users/<name>` or `/home/<name>` path still refuses everywhere.

Repair (round 2): the drop also covers the CI runner's home and this seat's. Two self-test arms planted the real `$HOME` and expected a refusal, so both went red at the PR head and passed on main: heartbeat.sh's "a message carrying the host's home directory is refused and the reachable ref does not move", and gh_comment.py's `arm_privacy_post_dry_run_refuses_this_hosts_home`. Each arm now plants a private home outside `/home` and `/Users`, so only the home rule can refuse it. Each also gains a null control that passes another path under the same planted host. The alternative was to keep public homes in the identity and exempt them only in `--check`. It lost: two readers of one identity would disagree about the same host, and roster lines would still be refused under `guard`.

Carry 1 (the #3239 round-1 fix review, ref_privacy on a uid-0 cloud seat): closed here. The passwd name root was already in `PUBLIC_ACCOUNTS`.

Carry 2 (cloud seat identity, found 11-06): closed here, at the source. `cloud-setup.sh` already exported `GIT_AUTHOR_*` and `GIT_COMMITTER_*`, and its self-test already held the null control "control: without the exports the config identity authors the commit". The values were the wrong identity, `seat`. The seat identity is now `hpo-fixer` at the owner's noreply address, the one `dev/programme/HANDOVER.md`'s Identity bullet names. It is set in `cloud-setup.sh` (`SEAT_NAME`/`SEAT_EMAIL`) and in `cloud_dispatch.py` (`SEAT_NAME, SEAT_EMAIL`, which also feeds the fixer and probe setup line). A new `cloud_dispatch.py` check pins the value: the existing arms compare against the constant, so they read green for any identity, and that is how `seat` went unnoticed. This pin encodes a design choice.

## Head

`607572db38f781a9bfb475f38baf7e861d150a21` merges main `be813ec` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`986b33e0b58d9031b51c938e94030c465e6da3b5` merges main `294a880` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`a0720a3951016893fd6716d4b0461f83c6b50bd6` merges main `80016a7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`b4951a08c98c98c94d3050ca4c0bbb627c6f5401` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

bf4d200e37ec5bfd14ed7e03877f0bead48e54e2 is the repair bd0525cbe and the carry-2 commit 7d04f651b, merged with origin/main 57958d6a4 (`date -u` 2026-11-06T18:33Z). It descends from the PR head 66662fc28. Every figure below was re-taken at this head.

## Mutation proof

- The fix line `homes = {h for h in homes if not _public_home(h)}` in `Identity.of_host` replaced by `pass`: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py --self-test` reports 113 checks, 2 failed. The failures are "a uid-0 cloud seat (root) judges its own paths and names no leak" (['home-directory']) and "a uid-0 cloud seat (nonexistent) judges its own paths and names no leak" (['home-directory', 'account-name']). Restored: 0 failed.
- `of_host`'s `homes.update({h, os.path.realpath(h)})` replaced by `pass`: `bash tools/audit/seat/heartbeat.sh --self-test` fails "a message carrying the host's home directory is refused and the reachable ref does not move" (8 checks, 1 failed), and `python3 -I tools/pr/gh_comment.py self-test` fails `arm_privacy_post_dry_run_refuses_this_hosts_home (the wiring)`.
- `_public_home` made to return True: the same two arms fail. Restored: both self-tests pass.
- Carry 2: `SEAT_NAME`/`SEAT_EMAIL` reverted to `seat` in both `cloud_dispatch.py` and `cloud-setup.sh`. `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py --self-test` then reports 127 checks, 1 failed ("the seat identity is hpo-fixer at the owner's noreply address"). `bash tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh --self-test` stays at 19 checks, 0 failed, which is the gap the pin closes. Restored: 0 failed.

## Null control

- At origin/main 817c2b169, `leaks()` under `Identity.of_host()` on the line "on a cloud seat, where `$HOME` is `/root`, a nonexistent group" reads ['home-directory'] with HOME=/root and ['home-directory', 'account-name'] with HOME=/nonexistent. At the head it reads [] for both.
- The head's self-test keeps two arms that must still refuse: "a real host's /Users/<name> path still refuses through of_host" (home-directory, account-name, host-path) and "a /Users/<name> path refuses on a cloud seat too" (host-path). Both pass.
- The repaired arms each carry a null control: heartbeat's "null control: the same host's message naming another path is pushed", and gh_comment's `arm_privacy_post_dry_run_passes_another_path (null control)`. Both pass.
- Carry 2: the null control is cloud-setup's "control: without the exports the config identity authors the commit", which passes. Its "the profile exports the seat identity" arm passes, so the exports now carry hpo-fixer.
- Before the repair, at 66662fc28, both arms failed with HOME=/root and with HOME=/home/runner. At main both passed under the same two HOMEs.

## Figures

- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py --self-test`: 113 checks, 0 failed at the head.
- `bash tools/audit/seat/heartbeat.sh --self-test`: 8 checks, 0 failed at the head with HOME=/root, HOME=/home/runner and a private /home/<name>. At 66662fc28: 7 checks, 1 failed under HOME=/root and HOME=/home/runner.

- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py --self-test`: 127 checks, 0 failed. `bash tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh --self-test`: 19 checks, 0 failed.
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py --check`: 0 refused at the head with HOME=/root and with HOME=/nonexistent.
- `python3 tests/closure.py select`: MODE: SCOPED, which named tests/doc_claims.py and tests/entities.py. Both ran green at the head. `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED.
- Class instrument (seats that judge with the real host identity): a git grep over the tree for `of_host(`, `ref_privacy.py guard` and `ref_privacy` imports that pass no identity. Every self-test hit was checked for an expected refusal that depends on the real `$HOME`. Two depended on it, heartbeat.sh's arm and gh_comment.py's arm, and both are repaired in this diff. The rest have no dependency on the real `$HOME`: cloud_dispatch.py's `judged()` refuses an email class, ci_probe.py's log arm refuses nothing, stamp.py's arm uses the host-path grammar, ci_predict.py plants a home, and ref_privacy.py's own arms are mocked or planted. Its unmocked `of_host` arm tolerates a public home through `_public_home`.

## Red checks

- governance / instrument-self-tests (job 127924787550, run 42227485863): caused by this diff and repaired here. The red was heartbeat.sh's home arm. gh_comment.py's arm shares the same cause and was measured red locally at 66662fc28. The `BAD X`, `BAD X2` and `BAD B` lines in that log are not failures. They are `alert_list_mutants.sh` printing each mutant's refused arms. That step ends "ALERT-LIST MUTANTS: every mutant refused", and the real `alert_list.py --self-test` step in the same log ends "25 checks, 0 failed". ## Block

The round-1 defect "a blocked verdict carried" is not closed in production. The repair takes `review_owed`'s priors from the heads of `merge` verdicts **plus every dispatched head** (`tools/audit/seat/ledger.py`, `priors = [...] + sorted(h for k, h in dispatched if k == str(n))`). The tick builds `dispatched` from bus.sh's dispatch record (`orchestrator_tick.py` `_dispatched`). bus.sh appends every dispatch to that record and never prunes it (`bus.sh:624`), and it refuses a verdict whose head has no dispatch at that head (`bus.sh:195-198`). So every blocked verdict's head is always in `dispatched`. When such a PR's head then moves only by a clean merge of main, `git_recarry(blocked_head, new_head)` is True and the tick prints an unflagged `CARRY:`. It does not print `REVIEW OWED`. That is the case fix-review.md step 12 rules out: only a merge verdict carries, and a red CI never carries.

My own probe, `ev/blocked_dispatched.py`, run against the head's ledger.py (`ev/probe_blocked_dispatched.txt`):

    blocked verdict, head X not in dispatch record : ['REVIEW OWED: #9 cb8d7b749b6d']
    blocked verdict, head X in dispatch record     : ['CARRY: #9 cb8d7b749b6d']

The in-tree null controls do not catch this:
- ledger.py's "a blocked verdict's head is no prior, whatever its class" passes `dispatched=set()`;
- the tick's "same head after a blocked verdict is REVIEW OWED" runs with an empty `bus-ro` record.

Both model a state the bus cannot produce. The C9 plant is killed, but only inside that unreal state.

A concrete trigger: a PR is blocked on a red that main's own breakage caused, and the fixer merges the repaired main. The re-review is owed, and the board shows `CARRY`.

Repair direction, for the fixer to own:
- a dispatched head stops being a prior once any verdict names it, or once the newest verdict at it is blocked;
- add a fixture whose blocked head is also in `dispatched`, and a plant that drops that exclusion.

Under bus.sh's append-only dispatch record this re-opens the blocked-carry path that the body says round 2 closed. The brief allows no deferral, and a policy edit needs the owner's approval before merging, not before drafting (CLAUDE.md). merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER (reopened): an edit gate that defers to a sibling run no longer fails, and no two runs wait on each other
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER (reopened), topic r10-gate-busy-defer-2: an edit gate that defers to a sibling run at its head no longer publishes the deferral at once, and no two runs at a head wait on each other.

**Cause.** `prelude.judging()` read the units a run owes from its title's workset. A deferring edit run (C3, `prelude.defer_to`) never expands `pr-contract`: GitHub lists the caller under its bare name `pr-contract`, completed `skipped`, and never lists `pr-contract / pr-contract`. So judging() read every deferring run as busy, to every gate and prelude at its head, forever. #3246 dodged the resulting prelude/gate cycle with an at-once bound in `gate.judge` (the `deferring(...)` clause). That bound is #3263's red: edit run 42338396358 published `FAIL run(s) [42338396871] at this head are still being judged; their gate decides` 2 s into its judge step, beside code run 42338396871 still in progress.

**Fix.** `prelude.judging()` reads a unit whose caller job is listed completed under the unit's bare name as one the run never ran, so it adds no source. A deferring run is then judging once its gate is listed, and nothing waits on it. With the cycle gone, the at-once bound and `deferring()` are deleted, and a deferring edit gate waits on its sibling bounded by `GATE_WAIT_MAX_S`, like every other gate. The order is total:
- a code run's prelude waits on nothing;
- any other prelude waits only on an earlier run, or a code run, that is not judging;
- a gate waits only on runs that are not judging, past `busy()`'s id tie-break.

No judging run waits on a non-judging one, so no cycle closes. The tie-break stays, for a started gate whose listing lags a caller already resolved.

**#3261's pair is a different cause.** 42307493684 and 42307798573 were sweep re-runs at attempt 10. A re-run restores `tools/ci` from the original event's `pull_request.base.sha`, so both ran 28482ece's programs, which predate #3246 (each gate log: `programs restored from 28482eceeb6b9809e44b12d80fc994282cc21645`). The recorded replay reproduces both verdicts on 28482ece and reads PASS at origin/main and here. See Forward-carry for the re-run finding.

**Alternatives not taken.**
- (a) *An edit gate that exits non-failing (PASS) when it defers.* Unsafe. While code run 42338396871 ran, `commits/02e92e7c/check-runs?check_name=gate` listed only the edit run's `gate` check-run: a gate waiting on its `needs` has no check-run yet. A PASS would have read the head green with tests still running.
- (b) *"Only the lowest id decides."* Ids order nothing here: a same-second edit and code run are numbered out of order (sweep.py docstring).
- (c) *Keep the at-once red, add a second exemption.* That stacks a parallel rule on a misread; the misread is the cause.
- (d) *Raise the bound past a code run's span.* Needs `ci.yml`'s `timeout-minutes`, outside this group's files, and holds a runner throughout.

**Residual, stated plainly.** A code run longer than the bound still ends in the documented past-bound deferral red. #3263's code run was still in progress 20 min in, so the replay at this head waits 720 s and then publishes that red. gate-sweep.yml re-judges it once the code run's gate is green. The at-once red is gone for every sibling that finishes inside the bound. Whether to lengthen the bound (`ci.yml`'s gate `timeout-minutes`) is the orchestrator's call. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-BUSY-DEFER

**Departure from the owned files.** `tools/ci/prelude.py` (`judging`, 4 lines and its docstring) is outside the roster's list (gate.py and the two harnesses). It is the one owner of "can this run still add a source": `gate.busy` and `prelude.wait_sources` both read it. A gate-side copy would be a parallel mechanism and would leave the prelude edge of the cycle open. The new fixture `tools/ci/fixtures/gate_busy_defer_runs.json` is the jobs API's record of both heads, fetched via `gh api` at 2026-11-07T04:4xZ, not re-typed.

## Head

`4de88a038e0e0923300cce8a09ec58e93a6ab1c4` merges main `be813ec` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`cecca4391dab34349fe10eb41a6ccfb2c4d3600e` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

## Mutation proof

merges.title: R10-RCA-PROCESS-WORKER-HANG: root cause of the unbounded process-worker reply wait
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
Root cause for the v7.1.2 process-worker hang, group R10-RCA-PROCESS-WORKER-HANG (trigger 1, the defect reached a release). The fix is #3232; this branch touches none of #3232's code or test files. Both PRs change `tests/closures.json`, a shared generated ledger with a merge driver: `git merge-tree --write-tree bba5b4d4d HEAD` (#3232's head) exits 0.

- Analysis: `dev/audit/rca/r10-process-worker-hang.md`, cited by the `_rca` entry `R10-RCA-PROCESS-WORKER-HANG` in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json`. That entry is also on class `N-reap-lock`'s `rca` list, and the class now carries a `barrier_refusal`, which `fold_ledger.py check` requires once a class has an in-tree RCA.
- **Cause:** `_run_in_process` read the reply with `pickle.load(stdout)` and no deadline while holding `_PROCESS_LOCK`. The read has been unbounded since 8542e51cb (first tag v6.3.15). The worker was computing, not dead: one core stayed busy for about 55 minutes with memory flat. No tool can now say which job it ran, on which inputs, or why it did not finish; the document lists what is known.
- **Why the stop did not free the lock: not reproduced.** At v7.1.2 the kill-first stop path frees the read in 0.00 s, both for a silent job and for a CPU-spinning one.
- **Process state (c).** Round 9's D1 seat read this lock and this read (D1-s2-05), but it measured stop latency against a finite solve. The double in its check ends the read when the worker is killed. D1 step 5 injects exceptions, and a silent peer never raises one. The #511 checks drive only a worker that fails.
- **Countermeasure.** Step 5 of `dev/governance/dimensions/D1.md` becomes "Guards, waits": each peer wait (pipe, child, lock) is driven by a live, silent peer, with the instrument `dev/audit/harnesses/silent_peer_waits.py`, "unless the wait is its own idle state", which admits `run_worker`'s `pickle.load(stdin)` (the idle worker waits for its parent; the parent's close is EOF). The brief was at its line and token caps, so the change is paid for by tightening step 5 and step 6; no cap moved. **This is a policy change: it merges only on the owner's approving review**, and it addresses state (c) by changing the unit that missed the defect.
- **Code-side candidate, not carried.** `ThermalModel._stability_substeps` was raised by D1-s2 and closed by D1-s2-02 in round 9's `leads.json`, as covered by `_FORECAST_FIELD_RANGE`. merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-NIGHTLY-STATUS: `tests / nightly-status` read red on main and every PR ("slow failed in the last verification dispatch"). The nightly now takes ~3.5 h, and the check graded the newest *concluded* run, which a newer in-flight run had already answered.

The cause has two parts. (b) The grader named a stale run. (a) The `slow` lane really is intermittently red. Actions API: dispatch 42235215315 (created 14:35:02Z, head 33e60b5) failed `slow` and concluded at 18:06:31Z. Dispatch 42242870295 (15:25:13Z) passed `slow` and concluded green at 19:17:32Z, and so did 42247578523 (15:55:42Z). For about 71 minutes the newest concluded run was the failed one while a newer run had already passed `slow`.

The lane failures are in `cycle_cost` (`tests/replay.py`): "runner class unknown: ref_ms 41.5 lies in no band of COST_RUNNER_CLASSES" (job 127950940724; ref_ms 40.1 in schedule run 41943946464), plus budget overruns in 41555367389 and 41749544997. That is the R10-REPLAY-COST-BUDGET seam, which this PR does not touch; it fixes only the grading. The lane flake is still open on main, and the orchestrator should route it to a replay-cost group.

Repair round 1 answers the blocked review (verdict/3263 at a5641182). (1) New arms kill every surviving grading-line mutant: two failed lanes with one answered, a green on another lane only, a newer `skipped` job, a newer `neutral` job, and an equal `created_at`. (2) A new check drives `main` with a stubbed `collect` and `_jobs`, and asserts that the in-flight run's jobs reach `verdict` (kills M10). (3) The code comment now gives the measured window of about 71 minutes, not "for hours". (4) This body is retaken whole. The dead `superseded` list (assigned, never read) is replaced by `all(...)`, which removes two unmutatable lines.

## Head

`02e92e7cbcb95c32fbb2ad3a7a46a8d465a436d8` merges main `294a880` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`5cf07f77a1b7090a1d813e9747765c6807b98055` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

795e8aae20053c051a762242b28adcc5b93661a9. This is PR head b0ef8f54 with origin/main merged three times (merge-tree: no conflict each time): 80016a71f567, then 41aa9050fc87, then f2a015142714 (delivery rows only), because main moved twice during the `prepr.sh` passes. On top sit three commits: the checks and the grader edit, the harness, and `tests/closures.json`'s INERT read of the harness via `ci_predict.py --apply-inert`. Every figure below was re-taken after the last merge: harness, scope, structure, `tests/entities.py`, and `tools/pr/prepr.sh` rc=0. origin/main was re-read at 2026-11-07T01:41Z, at f2a015142714.

## Mutation proof

Mutants are applied one at a time to each changed grading line of `verdict` and of `main`'s in-flight fetch, 16 in total. M1 to M10 are the review's labels. Each mutant runs the `tests/entities.py` superseded-failure checks verbatim (sliced between their section markers) through `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_nightly_status_mutants.py`.

- At this head's check: 15 of 16 are KILLED, including the review's survivors M2 (`>` to `>=`), M4 (`== "success"` to `in OK_CONCLUSIONS`), M6 (all to any), M8 (any green name supersedes), M9 and M10 (`main` stops fetching). M11 (drop the `failing_jobs` guard) is killed by the new "concluded green fetches nothing" arm. M13 (drop the inner `except Unreadable`) is killed because the unreadable arm must read FAILED, exit 1, not UNREADABLE, exit 2. M14 (fetch the concluded run's jobs) and M15 (`verdict` not handed the jobs) are killed.
- M12 (drop the `concluded is not None` guard in `main`) SURVIVES and is equivalent. With no concluded run, `verdict` returns RUNNING before it reads `in_flight_jobs`, and `collect` returns no jobs to `failing_jobs` for a missing concluded run.
- The same 16 mutants against the old head b0ef8f54's check kill 4 (M1, M3, M5, M7) and leave 12 surviving. That reproduces the review's finding, and the reviewer's own harness (verdict/3263 `evidence/ns_check.py` arms A) gives the same split.
- Failing checks named under a killed mutant: "a failed lane is superseded only by a NEWER in-flight run that concluded the same job green; every other arm stays FAILED" (M1 to M9), and "main fetches the in-flight run's jobs and grades with them: ..." (M10, M11, M13 to M16).

## Null control

The unmutated slice reads rc=0 at this head. The same slice against the pre-fix grader at merge base 28482ece reads rc=1 (`TypeError: verdict() got an unexpected keyword argument 'in_flight_jobs'`), so the check cannot pass without the fix. A really failing lane still reads red. Ten arms must read FAILED: nothing newer; newer `slow` failed; newer `slow` pending; an in-flight run older than the concluded one; two failed with one superseded; green on another lane only; newer `skipped`; newer `neutral`; equal `created_at`. In `main`, a newer failed lane and an unreadable jobs listing both exit 1. The reviewer's harness `evidence/ns_check.py` gives PR-CHECK PASS and PROBES PASS at this head; at b0ef8f54 its probes also passed, because the production predicate was already right and only the check was vacuous.

## Figures

- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_nightly_status_mutants.py . .`: `RESULT unmutated rc=0`, `RESULT killed=15/16`. The rule is one mutant per changed grading line, and a mutant counts as killed when any sliced check fails.
- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_nightly_status_mutants.py <b0ef8f54 export> .`: `RESULT killed=4/16` (old check, same mutants: the null control for the kill count).
- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_nightly_status_mutants.py . <28482ece export>`: `RESULT unmutated rc=1` (pre-fix grader).
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"`: `MODE: SCOPED -- 2 script(s) run, 31 scoped out`. `scope.run` names `tests/entities.py` and `tests/harness_headers.py`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`: rc=0, "ALL 2642 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED" (count printed by the instrument). `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/harness_headers.py`: rc=0.
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED. No budget raised.
- The 71-minute window, read from the Actions API (`get_workflow_run`): 42235215315 `updated_at` 2026-11-06T18:06:31Z (failure); 42242870295 `updated_at` 2026-11-06T19:17:32Z (success). The difference is 71 min 1 s.
- Environment: `bash tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh --check` printed OK (venv-ci python3). The goldens are untouched; CI remains their authority.

## Red checks

Check runs for PR 3263 at the previous head b0ef8f54, read at about 00:40Z on 2026-11-07, every page (81 runs on one page of 100). The concluded reds are:

- `gate` (job 128239038648, run 42310451878, KIND edit, WORKSET arch-score budget-raise-gate): "FAIL run(s) [42309259823] at this head are still being judged; their gate decides".
- `gate` (job 128239026202, run 42309259823, KIND edit, same WORKSET): "FAIL run(s) [42310451878] at this head are still being judged; their gate decides".

Both are ordering reds between two edit runs, each deferring to the other's gate. This diff did not cause them; the code runs' gates (42309258015 job 128237638987, and 42318600453 job 128238186312) concluded success. Cheaper detector: none from this seat. The gate's ordering between sibling edit runs is the gate workflow's, outside this diff. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-NIGHTLY-STATUS.

`governance / instrument-self-tests` concluded success at b0ef8f54 (23:04:17Z to 23:31:05Z). It is the main-wide 30-minute timeout seam, so a timeout red at the new head would be that seam and not this diff. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-SELFTEST-TIMEOUT.

merges.body:
Bound the process worker's reply. Before this change `_run_in_process` wrote the job and blocked in `pickle.load(stdout)` inside `with _PROCESS_LOCK:` with no deadline. A worker that is alive but silent never raises, so the #511 fallback never fired; every later solve queued on the lock, a reload did not help, and Home Assistant's stop ran into the supervisor timeout. The branch adds the reply deadline (`PROCESS_REPLY_TIMEOUT_S`, 1800 s; the contributor's change), the off-loop route's re-raise and held warning, the frame deadline (`_REPLY_FRAME_TIMEOUT_S`, 60 s), the frame size cap (`_REPLY_FRAME_MAX_BYTES`, 256 MiB), the stop path's bounded lock (`_SHUTDOWN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S`, 5 s), and the diagnosis service's translated failure (`diagnose_interval_failed`). The worker checks live in `tests/worker_deadlines.py`, a module `tests/features.py` calls, so CodeQL extracts them as a separate small file (round 3).

This round (5) repairs the review block at `bba5b4d4` (verdict `mutation-vacuous: measure`). The mutant that deletes `left_bytes -= size` in `_frame_reader.read` (`coordinator.py`, the running count that makes `_REPLY_FRAME_MAX_BYTES` a bound on the whole frame rather than on each `read()`) survived every feature check, and the real reader then accepted a 1,200,044-byte frame over a 1,000,000-byte cap. The repair adds one check pair to `tests/worker_deadlines.py` and changes no production code.

**Trust boundary.** Unchanged by this round. The worker is the integration's own child process, launched by `_ensure_worker` from the installed package; its reply is unpickled in the parent as at base; `_frame_reader` feeds the same `pickle.load` under a time bound and a size bound. This round touches no file under `custom_components/`.

Thanks to @Bankaifan for the original change in #3226: the bounded reply deadline on the process worker, and the field report and shutdown traces that found the hang. This pull request is a seat re-author of that contribution: decision 0011 gives an outside contributor no way to author a pull request here.
