comments.body:
Fix review: blocked e80a319c21f7b652fa579bab63e8997532aef22c regression: select.select refuses a worker pipe fd >= 1024 (FD_SETSIZE) that main serves, and tests/entities.py fails the N-log-flood barrier on the new _await_optimize WARNING

bus-nonce: ab1ee6d5f52ad8399c2670c58f685963

Round 1 of review for #3232 (seat re-author of outside PR #3226, contributor Bankaifan). Measured head: e80a319c21f7b652fa579bab63e8997532aef22c, base 7d95405e384e1ebf8223f04657c85996af55f3d9 (origin/main, 0 behind). `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty, so the contract is current.

## Block

1. **Regression: `select.select` on the worker's pipe.** `_run_in_process` now calls `select.select([stdout], [], [], timeout)` (coordinator.py:1954). `select()` raises `ValueError: filedescriptor out of range in select()` for any descriptor >= FD_SETSIZE (1024). The generic `except Exception` translates that into a transport fault: the worker is killed and `ProcessWorkerUnavailable("exited rc=None: ...")` is raised, so every solve on such a host falls back in process. That repeats every cycle while the pipe's fd stays high (each respawn takes the lowest free fd), and the repair issue follows after WORKER_FALLBACK_CAP cycles. Main serves the same call.
   Home Assistant raises its own soft RLIMIT_NOFILE to 2048 (`homeassistant.util.resource.DEFAULT_SOFT_FILE_LIMIT = 2048`, read from /opt/hpo/venv-ha), because real installs exceed 1024 descriptors. This PR also adds a new respawn trigger (the timeout), and a respawn happens at runtime, when the fd table is fullest.
   Measured (ev/probe.out, ev/probe.py `fd` mode, 1100 fds held, RLIMIT 4096):
   - head: `RESULT fd FAIL ProcessWorkerUnavailable: process worker exited rc=None: filedescriptor out of range in select()`
   - origin/main (null control): `RESULT fd ok child=1430 stdout_fd=1106`
   The repair is one line, and the claim it rests on is shown in ev/poll.out: `selectors.DefaultSelector()` (epoll on Linux) or `select.poll()` reads the same fd. `RESULT select.select fd 1103 ValueError ...` against `RESULT selectors EpollSelector fd 1103 True`. Pin it with a check that holds >1024 fds before spawning the worker.
2. **tests/entities.py fails at the head: 1 of 2632 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED.** The failing check is `R10 N-log-flood barrier: every unlatched WARNING/ERROR is on the reasoned list with its exact count -- a persisting condition goes through log_held  [mismatch {('coordinator.py', '_await_optimize'): (1, 0)}; read 69 sites]`. The PR's new `_LOGGER.warning("%s; keeping the last plan, a fresh worker starts next cycle", err)` is an unlatched WARNING. It repeats every cycle while the worker keeps timing out, so it must go through `log_held` or be added to the reasoned list with a reason. The body's figures ran only features.py and structure.py, never entities.py. Run with `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` (ev/entities_head.summary.txt). Null control at origin/main: `ALL 2632 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`, with `ok   R10 N-log-flood barrier` (ev/entities_main.summary.txt).

## Findings

- Follow-up: `_await_off_loop` (sysid step, replay interval, recovery estimate, sensor advisor; coordinator.py:2007-2017) catches `ProcessWorkerUnavailable`, which now includes `ProcessWorkerTimeout`. It then reruns the timed-out job on HA's executor with no deadline. Measured (ev/probe.out `offloop`): with `PROCESS_REPLY_TIMEOUT_S = 0.5` and a 3 s job, head returned after 3.5 s (0.5 s deadline plus a full 3 s rerun on the executor); main returned after 3.0 s. So the contributor's open question resolves to yes: a genuinely hung model job, after 1800 s, moves to an executor thread and holds it unbounded. It does not hold `_PROCESS_LOCK`, so the wedge of every later solve does not return, but the thread and one core do. `_await_off_loop` should re-raise `ProcessWorkerTimeout` as `_await_optimize` does, unless a rerun is deliberately wanted. Owed in the same re-cut as the block. Carry: dismissed: owed by this PR's re-cut under the block above, not carried to another stage
- Residual: the bounded reap after a timeout (`worker.wait(timeout=_SHUTDOWN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S)`, coordinator.py:1961, commit 5088d3688) has no mutation proof; the body says so. No check drives a child that survives SIGKILL, so the mutant `wait(timeout=...)` -> `wait()` survives by construction (not run: no test reaches that branch). Carry: dismissed: the branch needs a child in uninterruptible sleep, which no portable test can produce; disclosed in the body
- Non-blocking: the body and contract are the seat's re-author template. The quoted counts are stale: the body says `ALL 4836 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, while this head measures 4864 against main's 4858. The unpinned-sites list and mutation disposition are the orchestrator's to refresh. Carry: dismissed: external author, orchestrator repairs the body
- Non-blocking: `select()` on a pipe is POSIX-only. On native Windows it raises, and the same transport fallback would fire every cycle. Home Assistant supports Linux (HA OS, container, supervised, core on Linux) and macOS core, where pipes select fine, so this matters only if the selectors fix is not taken. Carry: dismissed: no supported HA platform lacks pipe select

## Evidence

- Re-author claim verified. The patch-id of `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main refs/pull/3226/head) refs/pull/3226/head` is `374d81b62985683137ea82b99325c6988289a9aa`; the same diff against this head minus the delivery-row commit (`e80a319c2^`) gives the identical id. Per commit, b5eeedbb2/61cec72ac, 585be114b/010534bbc, 530457f6d/dd4416f1a and ba704972f/5088d3688 have identical patch-ids. Each commit message differs only by the removed `Co-Authored-By` and `Claude-Session` trailers. Author Bankaifan is kept on all four. The seat adds only dev/programme/delivery/3232.md (1 line) and a clean merge of origin/main (1284c8058).
- Three-dot diff: coordinator.py, strings.json, translations/en.json, translations/sv.json, tests/features.py, tests/harness.py, dev/programme/delivery/3232.md. VERSION, the manifest, RELEASE_NOTES.md and both claim files are untouched.
- Merges (ev/mergetree.out): `git merge-tree --write-tree` exits 0 against origin/main 7d95405e3, against PR 3220 e70dfd645 (the same tree as main) and against PR 3198 e99f1555f. No conflict on coordinator.py or tests/features.py.
- features.py (`PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py`): head `ALL 4864 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`; origin/main null control `ALL 4858 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`. The 6 new checks are the 6 R.check calls in the new section.
- Mutation proof, re-run by me on full features.py in copies (ev/mutant_m*.diff, ev/feat_m*.summary.txt):
  - m1, deadline -> None (`select.select([stdout], [], [], None)`): `3 of 4864 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED` (raises ProcessWorkerTimeout `raised None after 30.0 s`; fresh worker; `_await_optimize keeps the last plan`)
  - m2, the `except ProcessWorkerTimeout` clause in `_await_optimize` removed: `1 of 4864 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED` (the in-process rerun and the solve_worker_fallback issue appear)
  - m3, stop-path `acquire(timeout=...)` -> `acquire()`: `1 of 4864 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED` (`_shutdown_process_pool took 9.95 s with the lock held`)
  The new tests drive the real select path through a real child, not a stub.
- structure.py: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED` at head and main, with identical `ok` lines (ev/structure_*.log).
- Large-reply claim ("a readable pipe means the job is done"): holds for replies over the 64 KiB pipe buffer. Under a 2 s deadline, replies of 70 kB, 10 MB and 100 MB returned in 0.00 s, 0.02 s and 1.34 s (main 1.01 s). After select returns, `pickle.load` reads while the child's single `write(blob)` continues, so the load can block only on a writer stopped mid-write (e.g. SIGSTOP), which nothing produces (ev/probe.out `big`).
- Leaks after a timeout: 10 consecutive 0.3 s timeouts took 3.1 s in total (main, with no deadline, 50.1 s). The parent's fd count went 7 -> 5, with no zombie (`Z`) children (ev/probe.out `leak`). The reap is bounded at 5 s.
- `_PROCESS_LOCK` release: `_run_in_process` holds it only through `with`, so every exit path (the timeout raise, the transport raise, a BaseException) releases it. The stop path pairs acquire with `try/finally: release`, and skips the swap on timeout. That leaves `_PROCESS_WORKER` pointing at a killed child, and `_ensure_worker` replaces it because `poll()` is not None once the kill lands. All `_PROCESS_WORKER` writes are under the lock, except the stop path's read of the handle before the lock, which predates this PR.
- 1800 s deadline: the contributor's spread (median 18 s, p90 263 s, max 426 s, 168 values, one Pi 4 install) **cannot be re-derived**: it comes from their HA recorder, and the repo has no solver time limit or solve-time harness (no `time_limit`/timeout constant on the solve path). Taken as given, 1800 s is about 4.2x the reported max. Diagnosis (`async_diagnose_interval`, which calls `_await_process` directly) and sysid jobs share the same deadline, and no bound on their runtime exists in tree to check against.
- The UpdateFailed path reuses `_raise_update_failed` (the #1546 route that `process_worker_unusable` already takes), with the key `process_worker_timeout` in strings.json, en.json and sv.json and the placeholder `{minutes}`. The `_ET_KEYS` registration was added, and the features check asserts `translation_key == "process_worker_timeout"` and that no in-process job ran.
- No finder's harness applies (an outside contribution with no audit finding). The contributor's harness is the new features section, disclosed as theirs. The fd and offloop probes are mine (ev/probe.py).
- CI at this head: `merge_train.py classify` exited 1, `RED ... pending: none red: gate`. The red `gate` (run 42136508003) is `cancelled`, which is a superseded refresh run. In run 42135610131 at read time: `tests / replay` failed `4 of 194 replay checks FAILED`, all `cycle_cost ... runner class unknown: ref_ms 27.26 lies in no band of COST_RUNNER_CLASSES`. That is a runner-calibration gap in the instrument, not this diff. `tests / mutation` failed; per the body it is red by construction on 6 unpinned sites, but the log's tail I read held only the shard set-up, so I did not see its failure lines. `governance / delivery-status` failed on other PRs' OVERDUE rows and is not a required context. `tests / nightly-status` failed and is not this PR's. `tests / fast`, `coverage`, `closures`, `arch-instrument`, `mutation-pins (1,2)`, `instrument-self-tests` and `codeql / Analyze (python)` were still in_progress. CI is not GREEN at this head; the block stands on the code independently.

Fix review: blocked 6e048afc6d857f65b62108e0648543dd611bd433 mutation-vacuous: dropping the off-loop timeout warning or its recovery (log_held off_loop_timeout) leaves every check green

bus-nonce: e3ffee93bf03b42feca3f39531bbb0a2

Round 2 (re-check of the round-1 block 985c64df). Measured head 6e048afc6d857f65b62108e0648543dd611bd433 (tree c11ea7441, identical to c9614abb7's, which the body's figures name). Role file unchanged since the merge base (`git diff merge-base...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` empty).

## Block

Repair 3 of the body says `_await_off_loop` "holds a per-job warning (`log_held(hass, "off_loop_timeout:<qualname>", ...)`, cleared when that job next completes)". No check pins either half:
- m4, the `log_held(hass, key, True, ...)` line in the `except ProcessWorkerTimeout` clause deleted (the re-raise kept): `ALL 4888 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` (ev/features-m4.log, ev/mutant-m4.diff).
- m6, the clearing `log_held(hass, key, False)` before `return result` deleted: `ALL 4888 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` (ev/features-m6.log, ev/mutant-m6.diff).

Without that warning an off-loop timeout is invisible at default log level: the replay (`_replay_interval`) and the sensor advisor (`_with_sensor_advisor`) catch it with `except Exception` and log only at DEBUG, so a worker reaped after 30 minutes on those jobs leaves no WARNING at all. The mutation table draws no mutant for a bare call statement, so its "8 sites, 0 unpinned" is true by its own definition and does not cover these two lines; the R10 N-log-flood barrier counts unlatched WARNINGs, so it cannot see a deleted one either. This is the brief's item (b) ("the held message reaches the log through the route, mutant: drop it, red") failing for the off-loop route. The `_await_optimize` route passes it (m3, m7 below).
Repair: one check in the worker read timeout section. Run `_await_off_loop` past a short deadline twice, then once within it, with a sink on `log_held`'s logger. Require [WARNING, INFO "Resolved"] and the job name in the message. m4 and m6 must then each turn it red.

## Findings

merges.body:
Root-cause records for the recurring-friction keys R10-FRICTION-REGRESSION left owed, the policy-tooling countermeasures of R10-RCA-FRICTION-RESIDUE, and the `instrument-self-tests` countermeasure #2865 never got. One record per key under `dev/audit/rca/`; the four existing records are judged for sufficiency and left alone.

No closing keyword: the roster lists these issues in the group's `issues` with `fixes: []`, so `pr-contract`'s intended list refuses `Closes` on them (`prepr.sh` step 7); the orchestrator wires `fixes` and the delivery closes them. One line per issue so the wiring has each:

Disposes #2875
Disposes #2950
Disposes #2998
Disposes #2436
Disposes #2437
Disposes #2429
Disposes #2840
Disposes #2835
Disposes #2895
Disposes #2907
Disposes #2860

#3156 (`ci-red`) is in the roster `issues` and is **not disposed** by this group: no record for the key lands here; `R10-RCA-FRICTION-SWEEP.md` section 4b says so and asks the orchestrator to re-route it to its own group, so the delivery must not close it from this PR. #2942 is closed and not in `issues`; its carry is in the group and landed (`R10-RCA-MUTATION-VACUOUS.md` section 6).

## Approval

This diff touches `dev/governance/rules/ci-autofix.md` (with its generated `.claude/rules/` and `.cursor/rules/` copies) and `tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`'s family map, which decides what the cron files. **It merges only on tvofi's approving review at the head**; that review is the approval of record. The dispatch brief carries an earlier approval ("All of these are approved.", 2026-10-29) of the countermeasures `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-FRICTION-RESIDUE.md` drafted; it is carried from the brief, not a live approval.

Covered by that drafted text, landed verbatim:

- #2429, `ci-autofix.md`: "If `mutation-pins` has not concluded by `tests / mutation`'s conclusion, the pin is owed by the handoff and the body says `unmeasured`;" and "`pinned` only if `--pin-killed` ran on this head." This is the bound as the reviewer quoted it from the draft (record section 7 words it "the next `tests / mutation` conclusion"). "(kept until M-3)" and "; the reviewer re-checks it" are byte-identical to base.
- #2436, the derived `other (untaught)` verdict family, and #2437, the declared `root-cause` family over `root-cause-unanswered`, `-detectable` and `-unrecorded`, in `policy_lint.mjs`.

**Changed policy sentences the approval does not cover**, each for tvofi's review:

- **Removed from `ci-autofix.md`:** "A failed recording reads files a clean run never does (`linecache`): an UNDER-SCOPED beside one may be an artefact. Fix the script; a push re-records." Reason: the file had 3 tokens of headroom under its 1469 cap, and the two approved sentences need the paragraph's tokens; with them in, `--budgets` reads 1469 / 1469. The action half ("fix it first") stays in the bullet above; the warning that an UNDER-SCOPED beside a failed recording may be an artefact goes.
- **Three new `mutation` family members** in `policy_lint.mjs`: `mutation-unpinned`, `unpinned-site`, `mutation-survivors`. Reason: #2942 measured these spellings splitting the `mutation` family below threshold (`R10-RCA-MUTATION-VACUOUS.md` section 6, a stale member list).
- Not policy, disclosed for completeness: the `ci_predict.py` `mutants` arm (#2865).

The `fixer.md` sentence drafted in `R10-RCA-CLASS-OPEN.md` section 6 is not landed and waits on the owner.

## Head

`5ff5aa998eee5df40a77fbdd28a6b64dc0fb5706` merges main `294a880` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`2ad28ecb50906877b34a378cacd8085e6afca029` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

9ca25bb8dedb81fffc74b65c176e5a07aa9b01c7

Repair round 3 (the third review's block on `a8d19cf1950250e378b3cf0dfd4f8c5c29e01255`, `verdict/3255`): `origin/main` merged at `80016a71f567d936450d8708abcbb79d9e8071d7` (`git merge`, clean), then three commits. `origin/main` read `80016a71f567d936450d8708abcbb79d9e8071d7` at 2026-11-06T23:08Z, unmoved since the merge, so `tools/pr/prepr.sh` ran once on this head.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant applied with `sed`, run, and restored from a saved copy; the unmutated tree is the null control.

- `tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs` `statsFindings`: `kind === 'verdict family' ? derivedInput(blocks, passing) : null` -> `derivedInput(blocks, passing)` (the derived family also applied to friction rule ids). **KILLED**, rc 1: `FIXTURE VACUOUS: statsFindings did not file the families end to end (... 3 untaught friction ids -> 1 friction-family would-open(s), want none)`. Null control: rc 0, `FIXTURE ok: 93 error(s) hold 269 pins`. The pin is a new friction-id row in the wiring block: three untaught friction ids on three PRs, expecting no `friction family` would-open.
- `tools/pr/ci_predict.py` `mutant_preds`: `(quoted | {rel}) & changed` -> `quoted & changed` (a diff touching only a driver would not run that driver's self-test). **KILLED**, rc 1: `FAIL a diff touching only the driver runs it: the driver is its own target`. Null control: `python3 -I tools/pr/ci_predict.py --self-test` rc 0. The pin is a new row in `mutant_self_test`.

Each listed `pr-contract` skipped under the caller's bare name and never listed the `pr-contract / pr-contract` its title's workset owes. So `prelude.judging` read each as still adding a source, `gate.busy` named it, and `gate.deferring` set the wait bound to 0. Both published `FAIL run(s) [<the other>] ... their gate decides` within 9 s of starting (finder's logs: #3241 head 95c7e604, attempt 2 of runs 42192623509 and 42193153511).

The fix, in `tools/ci/gate.py`:
- `busy()`: a LATER run whose `gate` has started (`in_progress` or `completed`, the one predicate `started()`) is not waited on. Of two started gates, the lower id decides and the higher waits on it. A gate merely listed `waiting` is no proof (R3-2).
- `judge()`: a deferring gate waits only when ALL the runs it waits on have started their gate. Beside any other run (a code run, or an edit run in its prelude or units) it publishes the deferral at once, as main does, because such a run may sit in `prelude.wait_sources` waiting on this one. `busy()` leaves out later started gates, so every started run a deferring gate waits on is an earlier one, and the waits run down in id and cannot close a cycle.

This round adds no production line. It pins the `all` in that rule. The round-2 review's mutant M24 (`and not all(` to `and not any(` in `judge()`) re-opened the prelude/gate cycle and survived the self-test. This round adds the review's mixed scene as a self-test case and M24 to the mutant table.

Alternatives that lost:
- Make `prelude.judging` read a gate `in_progress` as judging (round 2's first fix, 3c66c9b3, reverted by b0bccab4, a disclosed self-correction). The approved design's replay reads DIFFERS on it: a gate `in_progress` while a unit re-runs must be waited on.
- Teach `judging()` to read the skipped bare `pr-contract` as finished. A skipped caller cannot be told apart in the listing from one the platform has not expanded yet.
- C3 at once only beside a code run (c0c60886, round 1). It re-opened the cycle with a later edit run in its prelude (M22 now pins this).

merges.body:
R10-POLICY-ROLE-PACK (#2717, owner ruling tvofi 2026-10-24, recommendation (b)). Adds a per-role policy pack, the SessionStart line that names it, and the `nudge.md` step 3 carry. It is a partial delivery of #2717, so this pull request does not close the issue: `cloud_dispatch.py` cannot set the role variable (see Departures), and that residual stays carried on #2717.

**This is a POLICY pull request: it merges only on the owner's approving review at its head** (see Approval).

**Repair of the red at 9478bca5.** `governance / instrument-self-tests` failed: `pr_args self-test: 174 checks, 1 failed`, on the check "the pusher census: the rule returns exactly the dispositioned paths, and every runner reaps" (`tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh`, function `pr_pushers`).

- Cause, measured: the census rule `PR_PUSHER_RULE='(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])(app_)?push\.sh'` returns `tools/policy/role_pack.py`, and `PR_PUSHERS` gives it no entry. At 9478bca5, `bash -c '. tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh; pr_pushers' | grep -v '^ok'` printed `OPEN tools/policy/role_pack.py: undispositioned -- it names a pusher; give it an entry in PR_PUSHERS`. The same census at `origin/main` printed no `OPEN` line.
- The matching lines are 46, 272 and 275 of `role_pack.py`: the docstring's "so `push.sh` does not match inside `app_push.sh`" and the `named_entries` self-test, which uses the two names as sample instrument names.
- `role_pack.py` is a non-pusher. It imports only `argparse`, `fnmatch`, `re`, `sys` and `pathlib`. `grep -nE 'subprocess|os\.system|Popen|exec' tools/policy/role_pack.py` exits 1 (no line matches). The positive control for the pattern is the same `grep -cE` on `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py`, the census's `runner-py`, which counts 27 matching lines.
- The fix gives it the census's existing disposition for a file that names a pusher and runs none: one `mention:` entry in `PR_PUSHERS`, beside the ten `mention` siblings (`head_note.py`, `gh_read.py` and others). The rule itself is unchanged, so the census still refuses every new file that names a pusher.
- Departure from the brief: the brief suggested "a rule that recognises a real push site rather than any mention". Not taken. A push site has no syntactic shape across `.sh`, `.py` and `.mjs` (an argv built from a variable), so a narrower rule would let a new runner pass undispositioned. That is the weakening the brief forbids. The census is deliberately over-inclusive, and every mention is dispositioned by hand.

What lands:

- `tools/policy/role_pack.py`: renders one role's pack (`fixer`, `fix-review`, `designer`, `design-review`, `root-cause`, `verifier`, `judge`, and `finder` for `COMMON.md`). A pack holds three things, each framed and byte-equal to its file:
  - the role's contract under `dev/governance/roles/`;
  - every rule under `dev/governance/rules/` whose `paths:` globs match the contract or `INSTRUMENTS.md`, derived at each render and never listed;
  - the `INSTRUMENTS.md` entry lines whose instrument the contract names as a whole token.
- `role_pack.py check`: refuses a paraphrased line, a block that is missing, outside the role's plan or required but absent, a line outside every frame, and a pack larger than the files it frames. `sizes` prints the figures below. `--self-test` runs every role plus one mutant per rule. Each mutant must be refused by its own rule's message, so a mutant that some other rule catches does not count.
- `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`: when `HPO_SEAT_ROLE` names a role, the hook writes the pack to `git rev-parse --git-path role-pack-<role>.md` and prints one `role pack:` line after the clone-fact lines. When the variable is unset, its output is byte-equal to the base hook's. Its `--self-test`, which `policy_lint.mjs --hooks` runs in CI, adds seven arms: unset equals `report()` exactly; set is that output plus exactly one line; the named file checks clean; an unknown role prints a REFUSE line and the session still starts; `role_pack.py --self-test` passes.
- The `INSTRUMENTS.md` entry with its `instruments/role_pack.py.md` page, and a line in `governance.yml`'s `instrument-self-tests`, which `selftest_wiring.py --check` requires.
- `tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh`: the `PR_PUSHERS` entry for `tools/policy/role_pack.py` (the repair above).
- `dev/governance/roles/nudge.md` steps 3 and 7 (Carry 4), covered under Forward-carry.

Brief carries, in the review packet's 1-based numbering (the payload's 0-based `Carry <i>` is `Carry <i+1>` here):

- Carry 1 (owner recommendation (b); after-edges): this group is the pack's home.
  - Both after-groups have merged: R10-POLICY-FIXER-MD as #2704; R10-FLOW-DESIGN-STAGES as #2994, #3012 and #3002 (`dev/programme/delivery/`).
  - So every pack renders `main`'s final `fixer.md` and `fix-review.md`, read at each render and never copied.
  - The role is not named at dispatch, because the cloud payload has no per-seat environment: departure 3, carried on #2717.
- Carry 2 (verbatim, never paraphrased; owner review read at the base):
  - Every byte between a pack's frames is a byte of the file the frame names.
  - `check` refuses a paraphrased line, and its mutant is in Mutation proof.
  - The owner question was read from `.github/CODEOWNERS` and `policy_lint.mjs`'s `POLICY_GLOBS`: see Approval.
- Carry 3 (classify the new module):
  - `tools/policy/role_pack.py` is on `tests/closure.py`'s INERT prefix `"tools/policy/"`, deliberately: no gate script opens it, and its self-test runs in `instrument-self-tests` and through the hook's self-test.
  - `tools/audit/seat/instruments/role_pack.py.md` is under the INERT prefix for `tools/audit/` prose.
  - `tests/entities.py` passes at the head, so neither file "forces the FULL suite when touched".
- Carry 4 (R10-FLOW-AUTOTRAIN item 1, `nudge.md` step 3): closed in this diff; see Forward-carry.

Departures from the brief, each measured, with the alternatives and why each lost (fixer step 17):

1. **The pack is a file, not the hook's stdout.** Claude Code 2.1.318's bundle (`hke`, threshold `1e4`) keeps at most 10,000 characters of hook stdout in context. Longer output is saved to disk, and the context gets a preview whose path is replaced by `<persisted>`.
   - Every pack is over that limit (`role_pack.py sizes`, column `pack`), so a printed pack would reach the seat as a preview it cannot follow.
   - Alternative: split the pack below the cap. Lost, because the cap applies to the hook's whole stdout and there is one hook.
   - Alternative: `additionalContext` JSON. Lost, because the cap is applied to raw stdout before any JSON parsing.
2. **CLAUDE.md is not in the pack.** The harness injects CLAUDE.md into every Claude Code session, and this hook is Claude Code's.
   - In the first fixer's transcript, CLAUDE.md arrived as a system-reminder before any hook output, and no tool result re-read it.
   - Carrying it would put the same text in context twice. The rendered header says it was left out and why.
3. **`cloud_dispatch.py` does not set the variable.** The cloud payload has no per-session environment field. `cloud_dispatch.py`'s own self-test pins `session_context` to exactly `{allowed_tools, model, sources}` (its check "the ccr carries environment_id, session_context and one user event").
   - Inventing a field risks a payload the runner rejects.
   - The cloud environment's variables are per environment, not per seat.
   - So cloud seats get no pack from this pull request; the residual is carried below.
   - Alternative: rewrite the Role lines in the cloud prompt to `role_pack.py render`. Not taken, because it is no saving for the cloud fixer, which reads through Bash: see Figures, `read_set(Bash)` against `pack`.
4. **Agent-tool subagents run no SessionStart hook**, measured at the base by the first fixer:

merges.body:
R10-ROSTER-WRITE-SWEEP, repair after fix-review round 1 (blocked at `21be201c`): the roster write path's residue in `tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py` and `tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py`, built carry by carry, each with a self-test arm and a plant. Part of #201.

What the repair changes, by review finding:

1. selftest-red. `roster_queue.py --self-test` crashed under `python3 -I` because `_run_batch` imported `roster_edit` from the edit checkout (absent from the self-test's throwaway clone) and ignored the `editor` it was passed. One resolution now serves both paths: `resolve_editor` is `--editor`, else the `roster_edit.py` beside the script; `load_editor` loads that same file for `run --batch` (refusing, unexecuted, a file that has no `batch_edit`), and the single-op path runs that same file as a subprocess. The edit checkout supplies the roster and the shims only.
2. Red checks: named below, with the cheaper detector.
3. Forward-carry: the deferred items are built where buildable (the marker guard, carry 15, is now built: the carry says "Owner-ordered: no", so nothing waited on an owner), dismissed with a reason, or routed with a `Carry:` and its control stated as a precondition.
4. Carry 8's read-only roster instrument is built: `roster_queue.py show [GROUP] [--ref R] [--stage S]` and `diff REF_A REF_B`, `git show` reads only, `diff` exits 1 when the refs differ, with arms and plants Q10-Q12.

Dispositions by the review packet's 1-based numbering of the 17 roster carries (the review's own labels above and below, "carry 4", "carry 8", "carry 9", "carry 13(2)", "carry 15", "carry 16", are the verdict's and the brief's order, not these): lettered proposal labels, built (Carry 1); the M4-M6 plants, answered by W1-W15 and Q1-Q13 (Carry 2); the stale note, built (Carry 3); closing-destination refusal, built (Carry 4); `pr` in set-resume, built, its data edits are under Forward-carry (Carry 5); the overlap refusal and phase branches, built (Carry 6); `append-group @file`, built (Carry 7); the host-path gate, built (Carry 8); ordering after the schema group, holds, R10-ORCH-ROSTER-SCHEMA being absorbed (Carry 9); the brief-route edit-briefs, data edits under Forward-carry (Carry 10); the trailing-comment grammar, built (Carry 11); the word-start comment rule, built (Carry 12); `--mark` and `all`, built, with the arm for a pass cut short (Carry 13); the s9 bulk defects, docstring, incremental marks, comment parse and `--batch`, built (Carry 14); the loop and its subcommands, plus the read-only `show` and `diff` of this repair, built (Carry 15); the marker guard, now built (Carry 16); `absorbed --into`, op built, data edits under Forward-carry (Carry 17).

Also: carry 13(2) (the drain's timeout loses marks) has its own arm now: a pass that dies mid-queue keeps the marks already written (`run --mark`). The lane marker (`HPO_ROSTER_LANE=queue-runner`) is set by the queue runner, `carry_fold.py` and the two harnesses that call structural ops directly (`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_roster_push_race.sh`, `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_tick_which_roster.py`); `set-stage`, `append-group`, `set-resume` and `mark-carry` stay directly callable, as the carry specifies. A caller that sets the variable by hand is out of scope. This changes what a seat may call directly (policy-adjacent): it needs the owner's approving review before merging.

Merged `origin/main` (30638cf0c, 2026-11-06 16:15 UTC) into the branch cleanly; `tools/pr/prepr.sh` is re-run at the head below.

## Head

`ce7ae991b55800a344d1f1bfeeb639654c0d433e` merges main `198b8f7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`d30513cdca74c3c6b768c38395d4fb5c3b19b56c` merges main `af56818` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`ecbba06860aa197bfa9a6fe5d982512f2c2b71d8` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

2b27bf482e33ab4fd7e1fdb867353a74b8da10a3

## Mutation proof

`python3 tools/audit/seat/r10_roster_ops_mutants.py` (all 105 plants, the driver restores each file byte for byte; it prints `plants: 105, without a FAIL line: ['C6']`). Every plant of this group is killed by at least one FAIL line, none by a crash: W1 12, W2 3, W3 2, W4 1, W5 1, W6 3, W7 1, W8 1, W9 2, W10 2, W11 4, W12 1, W13 1, W14 1, W15 1, Q1 2, Q2 3, Q3 1, Q4 2, Q5 3, Q6 1, Q7 1, S7 2, K8 4, K12 2, H2 1, and the plants this repair adds: Q8 2 (the batch path loads the edit checkout's editor), Q9 1 (the loader executes a file that is no roster_edit), Q10 1 (`diff` blind to removed groups), Q11 3 (`diff` compares a carry by count), Q12 1 (`show --stage` unfiltered), W16 8 (the lane guard dropped), W17 1 (`set-stage` made structural), Q13 1 (the runner does not set the marker).

Failing test first: at the head before the fix, `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py --self-test` exits 1 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'roster_edit'` at `_run_batch`; after it, 52 checks, 0 failed.

Inherited, not this diff's: plant C6 (roster_edit.py, from R10-ROSTER-OPS) is `rc=1` with no FAIL line, a crash (`KeyError: 'carry'` in `op_drop_carry` on the mutated tree); the same result at `origin/main` (30638cf0c, `r10_roster_ops_mutants.py C6` in a detached worktree of it). The plant is killed, by a crash in a later arm; two attempts to turn it into a FAIL line crashed in yet another arm and were reverted. Carry: R10-CARRY-RESIDUE-2 (item: C6 killed by crash, not by FAIL line).

## Null control

Each refusal has its passing twin in the same self-test. New here: a `run --batch` with no `--editor` resolves the roster_edit.py beside the script and never the edit checkout (`resolve_editor` arm); a stub editor passed with `--editor` is the file both the batch's fallback and the single-op path run; `diff` of the same ref twice is empty; `show` without `--stage` lists both groups; `show` and `diff` leave the working tree and index unchanged; `set-stage`, `append-group`, `set-resume` and `mark-carry` need no marker; a structural op with the marker is accepted; a marker with another value is not the lane. Earlier nulls hold: a numbered label and text naming no proposal land; a bare `append-group` path lands; overlap on the index file only lands; append-carry to an open group with no PR lands with no WARN; a queue run without `--mark` leaves the queue byte-identical; a batch of one is byte-identical to the single-op roster; a quoted `'a # b'`, `@/p/b#1.txt` and `s6-batch8.md#P70` keep their `#`; a held line whose batch file is absent stays held. The unmodified base (b36679ce) under `python3 -I`: `roster_queue.py --self-test` 17 checks, 0 failed (the base has no batch path).

## Figures

- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py --self-test`: 52 checks, 0 failed at the head (17 at the merge base b36679ce)
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py --self-test`: 242 checks, 0 failed (191 at the merge base)
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py --self-test`: 63 checks, 0 failed (60 at the merge base)
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/r10_roster_ops_mutants.py --self-test`: 321 checks, 0 failed (231 at the merge base)
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/carry_fold.py --self-test`: 6 checks, 0 failed
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`: ALL 2637 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED (run before the merge of `origin/main`; rerun by `prepr.sh` at the head)
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`: MODE: SCOPED, runs `tests/entities.py` only
- Absorbed groups with no `resume.absorbed_into`, python json over the r10 roster at the merge base: 13 of 13. This is why the write-time check is at the op and brief_lint is unchanged.

## Red checks

At PR head `21be201c`, across all 68 check runs (all pages, `ev/check-runs.tsv` of the review):

- `governance / instrument-self-tests` (concluded failure): the `roster_queue.py --self-test` crash under `python3 -I`, finding 1. Cheaper detector: the same command CI runs, `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py --self-test`, about 10 s locally; standing cost: one line in this handoff's figures. The driver `r10_roster_ops_mutants.py` now runs every target's self-test under `-I` too, so a plant is measured the way CI runs it.
- `pr-contract / pr-contract` (concluded failure): refused because `governance / instrument-self-tests` was red and `## Red checks` did not name it; it clears with the repair and this section.

No other check run concluded failure at `21be201c` (the first-pass `gate` run was superseded; the three later `gate` runs concluded success). No open `code-scanning alert` is known at that head.

## Forward-carry

- Carry 13(2), the drain's timeout: Carry: R10-ROSTER-WRITE-SWEEP | dismissed: the drain script is not in the tree and `run --mark` writes each mark as its op pushes, pinned by the arm "a pass that dies mid-queue keeps the marks already written".
- Roster DATA edits these ops enable, which write the roster branch this seat may not write. Each carries its control as a precondition. Carry: R10-CARRY-RESIDUE-2 (item: carry 4, `set-resume --field pr` for every done group lacking `resume.pr`, starting R10-FLOW-RECORD-PITCH = 2836; precondition: the count of done groups lacking `pr` is measured at the roster seat's own base, and a group's `pr` is read from `dev/programme/delivery/<N>.md`, never guessed).
- Carry: R10-CARRY-RESIDUE-2 (item: carry 9, one `edit-brief` per live group whose brief still names `the seat pushes refs only, through tools/audit/seat/handoff_push.sh`; precondition: a python count of that phrase over live groups' briefs is the control, and reads 0 afterwards; 64 groups carry it in total at the review's base, 1 live).
- Carry: R10-CARRY-RESIDUE-2 (item: carry 16 data, `set-stage <G> absorbed --into <host>` for the ten folded groups of the carry and for the 13 absorbed groups with no host; precondition: afterwards `carry_audit.py roster` reports each group's carries as REROUTED to its host, and the lint refusing an absorbed group with no `absorbed_into` is built only after those data edits land, because it would fail the roster as it stands: 13 of 13 lack the field today).
- Carry: R10-CARRY-RESIDUE-2 (item: plant C6 killed by a crash, not by a FAIL line, as above).

bus-nonce: 197402a58d6c485fbb21bb4a66c98009

Round 1. Measured head 21be201ce8cc097c87d95e81e42d036786a539dc (re-read at post time: refs/pull/3253/head still 21be201c). Merge base b36679ceaa65a08a67a84f0d934c93aa15f7c7f3. Roles diff merge-base...origin/main: empty (contract current). Roster read at origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster (ev/roster-ref.txt).

## Block

1. selftest-red. `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py --self-test`, which is how CI's `governance / instrument-self-tests` runs it, exits 1 at the head with a traceback. `_run_batch` (roster_queue.py:235-236) puts `<edit_checkout>/tools/audit/seat` on sys.path and imports `roster_edit`. The self-test's throwaway clone has no roster_edit.py, so the import resolves only when the script's own directory is already on sys.path, which `-I` removes. The body's figure "37 checks, 0 failed" holds only without `-I`. The batch path also imports the editor from the edit checkout and ignores the `editor` it is passed, so `run --batch` and single-op `run` can execute different roster_edit.py versions.
2. root-cause-detectable: `governance / instrument-self-tests` (job 127934936719) concluded failure at this head and `## Red checks` says "none". `pr-contract / pr-contract` (job 127949034888) is red for that reason: "check `governance / instrument-self-tests` is red and `## Red checks` does not name it". The cheaper detector exists: the same one-line command, run locally with `-I` before the handoff, takes about 10 s.
3. carry-missing: `## Forward-carry` is "none", yet the body defers six items and writes none of them to a destination: (a) roster carry 15, the marker guard, withheld pending the owner although the carry says "Owner-ordered: no"; (b) carry 4, `set-resume --field pr` data for done groups; (c) carry 9, edit-brief data; (d) carry 16, `absorbed --into` data for the ten folded groups, plus its control ("an absorbed group with no absorbed_into is refused by the lint"), which the body declines to build; (e) carry 13(2), the drain timeout, closed only by `run --mark`; (f) carry 8, the folded R10-ROSTER-QUEUE brief's "read-only roster show and diff instrument". Item (f) is neither built nor dispositioned: the body reads carry 8 as "ordering holds", and no add_parser in roster_queue.py names show or diff. Prose in a PR body is not propagation (finding-propagation.md).

## Findings

- roster_queue.py `--batch` imports roster_edit from the edit checkout rather than from its own tree, so its self-test crashes under `python3 -I`. Claim: the head's self-test is red the way CI runs it. Evidence: ev/rq-isolated-head.txt shows rc=1 and the traceback; ev/job-127934936719.log has the CI copy. Harness: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py --self-test`. Metric: rc and the checks/failed line. Perturbation: at base b36679ce, rc=0 with 17/0 (ev/rq-isolated-base.txt); at the head with `sys.path.append(Path(__file__).resolve().parent)` added after line 235, rc=0 with 37/0 (ev/rq-isolated-probe.txt). The harness moves under both. Carry: R10-ROSTER-WRITE-SWEEP
- `## Red checks` says "none" while `governance / instrument-self-tests` and `pr-contract / pr-contract` concluded failure at this head; the body owes the name and the cheaper detector. Evidence: ev/check-runs.tsv and ev/job-127949034888.log. Carry: R10-ROSTER-WRITE-SWEEP
- The deferred carries 15 (marker guard), 4, 9 and 16 (roster data edits, with carry 16's lint control) and 13(2) are stated in prose with `## Forward-carry: none`. Each needs a `Carry:` to a live roster destination, or to a carry file, with its control stated as a precondition, before merge. Carry: R10-ROSTER-WRITE-SWEEP
- Carry 8's "read-only roster show and diff instrument" is neither built nor dispositioned: no show or diff subcommand exists in roster_queue.py or roster_edit.py at the head. Build it, or route it with a destination. Carry: R10-ROSTER-WRITE-SWEEP

## Evidence

- RESULT mutation proof at the head: W1-W15, Q1-Q7, S7, K8, K12 and H2 each give rc=1 with at least one FAIL line and no traceback; the driver exits rc=0 and the tree is clean afterwards (ev/plants-head.txt). Counts match the body: W1 12, W2 3, W3 2, W4 1, W5 1, W6 3, W7 1, W8 1, W9 2, W10 2, W11 4, W12 1, W13 1, W14 1, W15 1, Q1 2, Q2 3, Q3 1, Q4 2, Q5 3, Q6 1, Q7 1. S7 2, K8 4, K12 2 and H2 1 are killed; the body states no count for them.
- RESULT null control: `r10_roster_ops_mutants.py --null` gives rc=0 at both the base and the head (ev/null-base.txt, ev/null-head.txt). The W and Q anchors do not exist at the base, so the base run is the null rather than a replant.
- RESULT self-tests without -I (ev/selftest-summary.txt): roster_edit 232/0 at the head, 191/0 at the base; roster_queue 37/0 and 17/0; roster_lib 63/0 and 60/0; r10_roster_ops_mutants 297/0 and 231/0. These match the body's figures, but see Block 1 for roster_queue under -I.

merges.body:
R10-TRAIN-MERGE-LOOP part 1, repair round 3 of the `Fix review: blocked e836876f3dadc368a414ccc2b19126e78507f7d0 ci-red` verdict. This round does what the verdict owes and nothing else. (1) `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_ci_layout_p1/critpath_fetch.sh` resolved its seat directory with a hand-written `../../../../` depth root, which `tests/harness_headers.py` refuses. It now inlines the canonical `repo_root()` from `tools/audit/repo_root.sh`. The Python callers this branch added, re-read against the same rule, are moved to the canonical walk too. (2) Carry 15 is wired at the stamp: `.claude/workflows/web-stamp.js` runs a records step, `merge_train.py sweep --stamp`, before its stamp agent, so the notes and the tag carry the records. A self-test launches that sweep over several held records. (3) This body is re-taken from `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, and `## Red checks` reads the PR head's own check runs. Carries 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 16 and 17 stay forwarded to R10-TRAIN-MERGE-LOOP-2 as before (`## Forward-carry`). Refs #2715 #3137; both stay open for part 2.

Carry status, 1-based (group R10-TRAIN-MERGE-LOOP on the roster, 19 carries; Carry N is the Nth element of its `carry` array). This round changes none of the dispositions.
- Carry 1 (review settle bounded by time, P331): on main (`git merge-base --is-ancestor d69619360 origin/main` succeeds). Nothing is built here.
- Carry 2 (one Actions job-log reader): built on this branch in round 2, `job_log` in merge_train.py. Killed by merge_train-45, 46, 54 and 55 (below). This round moves its outside callers' seat lookup onto the canonical `repo_root` walk (finding 1).
- Carry 3 (bot tip, run still action_required): forwarded to R10-TRAIN-MERGE-LOOP-2 (`## Forward-carry`).
- Carry 4 (a cured pre-flight park rejoins at the same verdict): built on this branch at 6e3a59b29. Killed by merge_train-44 and merge_train-48.
- Carry 5 (same-tree commit after the posted verdict): built on this branch at 6e3a59b29, `same_tree_posting`, with its fetch-failure arm. Killed by merge_train-43 and merge_train-47.
- Carry 6, Carry 7, Carry 8 and Carry 9 (the hand-written add scripts and the three stranded carries): forwarded to R10-TRAIN-MERGE-LOOP-2.
- Carry 10 (R10-FLOW-POSTMERGE after-merge bookkeeping): implemented by #3090, merge commit 38dcb6c5d, an ancestor of origin/main and of this head. Nothing is built twice.
- Carry 11 (P312's drain order): implemented by #3090, merge commit 38dcb6c5d (`Train.queue_take`). Nothing is built here.
- Carry 12 (`set-stage owed <GROUP> <merge sha>`): implemented by #3090, merge commit 38dcb6c5d (`roster_lib.group_for_branch`). Nothing is built here.
- Carry 13 (P312, `add --priority N` and the stable sort): implemented by #3090, merge commit 38dcb6c5d. merge_train-42 re-anchors on the drain order carry 14 adds.
- Carry 14 (batch by default): built on this branch in round 2 (`Train.ready_batch`). Killed by merge_train-49.
- Carry 15 (record PRs ride the stamp): built at the queue, `add` and `sweep` in round 2 (merge_train-50 to 53). This round wires it at the stamp launcher (design below).
- Carry 16 and Carry 17: forwarded to R10-TRAIN-MERGE-LOOP-2.
- Carry 18 (the instrument page states the train.sh default): built on this branch in round 2. merge_train.py.md names `RECOMMENDED`, and no hand-passed flag line is left under instruments/.
- Carry 19 (every arm): built on this branch in round 2: the cured and uncured `policy` and `findings` parks, the drain arm, and the new-verdict null. Killed by merge_train-44 and merge_train-48.
Tally: 1 on main; 10, 11, 12 and 13 by #3090; 2, 4, 5, 14, 15, 18 and 19 built here; 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 16 and 17 forwarded. That is 19.

Depth-root design (verdict finding 1). `critpath_fetch.sh` now carries the canonical shell `repo_root()` text, which `harness_headers.py`'s inline scan compares byte for byte with `tools/audit/repo_root.sh`. It sets `SEAT="$(repo_root "$0")/tools/audit/seat" || exit 2`. The verdict asked for the three Python callers to be re-read. `ci_script_seconds.py` (`parents[3]`) and `r10_gate_stale_jobs/scan.py` (`parents[4]`) counted parents the way the rule forbids. The scan did not flag them only because the expression sat inside `sys.path.insert(...)`, not on a `ROOT =` or `HERE.parents[` line. Both now inline the canonical Python `repo_root(start)`, which the same scan compares with `tools/audit/repo_root.py`. `r10_replay_loopnorm.py` already had `ROOT = repo_root(__file__)`, so its `parents[3]` now reads `ROOT`. One alternative lost: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. That command returns the checkout the caller stands in, not the tree that holds the script, and the canonical walk is the one form the scan checks.

Carry 15 at the stamp (verdict finding 3). There were two routes: wire the launcher, or carry the gap to the stamp stage's brief. Wiring won. The stamp stage's roster group, R10-STAMP, is at `resume.stage: done`, and `finding-propagation.md` says a done group is not a destination. A carry file would need a destination issue, which this brief rules out. Most of all, a carry would leave every record PR HELD-FOR-STAMP with nothing in the tree releasing it: the defect, stored. The wiring reuses the existing mechanism, `sweep --stamp`, which was already built in round 2: an `add` per admitted entry, the first starting one train over the whole ready queue (carry 14), so all the held records land in one batch. It adds no new subcommand and no second launcher. The step is a records agent in web-stamp.js's Stamp phase. It runs after the main-gate wait and before the stamp agent, and it is gated on the same deploy key. It returns `landed: false` on `SWEEP HELD`, `SWEEP REFUSED` or a non-zero record-train `rc`, and then the launcher does not stamp. The stamp agent then cuts its worktree from a fresh `origin/main`, so the notes and the tag carry the landed records. One alternative lost: the step inside the shared `stampPrompt` fragment (canonical in `.claude/workflows/web-fragments.md`, copied to web-decomp-stage.js, web-fix-wave.js and web-triage.js). That was tried in commit 2 of this round and reverted in commit 3, for three reasons. `web-fragments.md` is policy. At origin/main it measures 2417 of its 2427-word `policy_lint.mjs --budgets` cap, and the step put it about 195 over. And `tests/entities.py`'s template arm refused the policy diff (`1 of 2637 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`). The other three launchers stamp at a decomposition stage, a fix wave and a triage wave. The verdict and carry 15 name the stamp launcher, so wiring them, through policy, is outside this round's scope. The step returns `stamped: false` on `SWEEP HELD`, `SWEEP REFUSED` or a non-zero record-train `rc`. After the train closes it resets to `origin/main`, so the notes and the tag carry the records. `tools/release/stamp.py` stays untouched: it dispatches no merges, and giving it a merge-train dependency would put two concerns in one module. `orchestrator.md` section 13 is policy and is not edited. The launcher it names (`web-stamp`) is what changed. The two instrument pages (`merge_train.py.md`, `train.sh.md`) now name the launcher step instead of a hand-run `queue --stamp`. `node tools/policy/fragments_sync.mjs` reads `FRAGMENTS ok` at this head: the records step is a launcher-local `const`, not a copy of a canonical fragment.

## Head

`641b9d78e25f21961cd5f04b6a48bbdfbfc45ea0` merges main `9cbd7dd` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`2d58088f451e13e1735da7be2c09fa36995bf0b8` merges main `57958d6` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`f7e3ed1a8aefc03ccc49bf72cb326bea5f207767` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`83d33ad2ea4c4cf17dd69feae0f8a30d3ccab87d` is the code head handed off. It is `260f8d4038f20090365de6a1cf6bbc24ab57e835` with three further merges of origin/main, read 2026-11-06 after `git fetch origin main`: 30638cf0c (two delivery rows), cb48d97e2 (the v7.1.4 stamp: VERSION, the manifest, RELEASE_NOTES.md, the card's version string, both claim files and the D6 claims register), and 862affd07d2ce3430c200d4f09aa6e16934b5c4d (#3247: the D0 brief and its delivery row). None touches a file this diff's scripts read: `git diff --stat 260f8d40 83d33ad2ea4c` lists only those record, brief and stamp files. So the self-tests, harness_headers, entities and mutants were measured at 260f8d40, and `tools/pr/prepr.sh` was re-run at `83d33ad2ea4c`. 260f8d40 is this round's four commits on `0c99efec2`, plus the merge of origin/main 817c2b169. `0c99efec2` merged origin/main b36679cea into the PR head e836876f3dadc368a414ccc2b19126e78507f7d0. The merge base is 862affd07d2ce3430c200d4f09aa6e16934b5c4d. The earlier PR head's merge base was dc0a170b6.

## Mutation proof

Every row is a production-line mutant in `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py`, run as `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py merge_train-42 … merge_train-55` at this head (260f8d40, after the merge of origin/main 817c2b169; the same 14 rows read identically at f9033c42 before it). The harness first runs the same step on the unmutated file, which must pass (the null control). Then it plants the mutant and restores the file.

| mutant | what it breaks | at the mutant | null control (unmutated) |
|---|---|---|---|
| merge_train-42 | the started train's drain order | KILLED, `465 checks, 2 failed` | 0 failed |
| merge_train-43 | same-tree posting drops the tree comparison | KILLED, `465 checks, 1 failed` | 0 failed |

| merge_train-47 | same_tree_posting's fetch-failure check becomes `if False:` | KILLED, `465 checks, 1 failed` | 0 failed |
| merge_train-48 | PREFLIGHT_PARK dropped from READMIT_SAME_VERDICT | KILLED, `465 checks, 4 failed` | 0 failed |
| merge_train-49 | carry 14: a started train's `others = []` | KILLED, `465 checks, 6 failed` | 0 failed |

| merge_train-54 | gate_raise_only reads without job_log | KILLED, `465 checks, 1 failed` | 0 failed |
| merge_train-55 | culprit reads without job_log | KILLED, `465 checks, 1 failed` | 0 failed |

`RESULT survivors=0`. Against the previous head's table, three counts rose by one: merge_train-49 (5 to 6), merge_train-50 (1 to 2) and merge_train-52 (3 to 4). The 49 and 52 rises were re-run by hand, planting each harness mutant and running `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test`. In both, the one FAIL line not in the previous table is `FAIL carry 15 at the stamp: sweep --stamp over three held records ...`.

The new check this round is `carry 15 at the stamp: sweep --stamp over three held records ...`. merge_train-50 kills it (build_queue holds every record even under `--stamp`): the run reads `465 checks, 2 failed` against the previous head's 1. It was checked by hand before the harness run too. The same edit (`if not self.stamp and record_pr(` to `if record_pr(`) gave `merge_train self-test: 465 checks, 2 failed`, with `FAIL carry 15 at the stamp: ...` and `FAIL carry 15: a stamp's queue (--stamp) holds nothing ...`. The file was restored from a copy.

The depth-root repair is pinned by `tests/harness_headers.py` itself. The previous PR head e836876f3dadc368a414ccc2b19126e78507f7d0, with the hand-written root, is the mutant: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/harness_headers.py` there prints `1 of 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED`, rc 1. The failing check is `every inlined walk matches the canonical helper and no depth root remains`, with `FAIL depth seams: dev/audit/harnesses/r10_ci_layout_p1/critpath_fetch.sh:12: SEAT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../../t…`.

## Null control

- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/harness_headers.py` at e836876f3dadc368a414ccc2b19126e78507f7d0 (detached worktree): `1 of 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED`, rc 1. At this head: `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`, rc 0.
- The carry 15 stamp-launch check carries its own null arm: the same sweep without `--stamp`, over the same three record PRs, starts no train, and each record is logged `HELD-FOR-STAMP`.
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test`: `464 checks, 0 failed` at e836876f (the verdict's ev/selftest_head.txt). At this head: `465 checks, 0 failed`. The one added check is the stamp launch.

## Figures

- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/harness_headers.py`: `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED` at this head. At e836876f3dadc368a414ccc2b19126e78507f7d0: `1 of 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS FAILED`.
- Class seams for the depth root (fixer step 8). The instrument is `harness_headers.py`'s own `depth_root_seams()` over the RO-7 scope, which returns nothing at this head (the pass above). It keys on a root-named assignment, so it misses a `parents[N]` inside a call. A second enumerator covers that form: `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD -- dev/audit/harnesses tools/audit/seat | grep -E '^\+.*parents\['`. Run on e836876f's own diff (`git diff dc0a170b6...e836876f3dadc368a414ccc2b19126e78507f7d0`, its merge base), it returns the three Python callers (ci_script_seconds.py, scan.py, r10_replay_loopnorm.py), all closed in this diff. At this head it returns nothing. The other `parents[3]` near this work is in `tools/audit/seat/probe_bridge.py:52`. It is outside the RO-7 scope, and main had it before this branch, so it is not this diff's.
- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/ci_script_seconds.py --selftest`: `SELFTEST is_fast got=[True, True, False, False] want=[True, True, False, False] ok`. merges.title: R10-PLANTED-DEFECT-AUDIT: planted defect audit
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
Owner ruling (tvofi, 2026-11-01): a review-strength guardrail trip dispatches the planted-defect audit it names, and P0 = 0.28, ALPHA = 0.05 is adopted; the guardrail still sets no exit code and blocks nothing. Built as the beat job row `audit-dispatch` in `tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py` (job table `beatd.jobs.json`, interval 1800 s): it runs `review_strength.py --fetch --guardrail` and writes one `DISPATCH: planted-defect-audit arm=<arm> cut=<span>` line per sustained trip of an arm. Round 2 repairs the round-1 block: (1) the memory is keyed on the arm and the trip, not on the sliding cut, so a still-tripped arm dispatches once, and again only after it has read `ok` or `insufficient`; (2) a readable run rewrites the job file, so a failed run's `audit-dispatch: UNREADABLE` clears on the next good run, DISPATCH lines kept; plus the case for output whose only GUARDRAIL line is the unclassified one. `carry-201.json` records the ruling. Carry 1 (stranded 13, DISPATCH-REG), Carry 2 (stranded 48, BEATD) and Carry 3 (stranded 50, BEATD) are answered together by this one row. Alternative not taken: a standalone script; the row reuses the digest, fold and memory the other rows share.

## Head

`79cf40f4751210c7868d8178b87dc97a69fa28ae` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

71eca59832171f8940547f304a59289cd8f18404 (origin/main dc0a170b is an ancestor of this head, merged; prepr.sh run at this head, no second run owed).

## Mutation proof

Re-taken from scratch at this head: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py --self-test` plants each `MUTANTS` entry in a temp copy of `beat_jobs.py` and requires its named case to turn red; it prints `beat_jobs self-test: 124 checks, 0 failed`, i.e. every row below red at the mutant and the same case green on the unmutated null control.

| mutant | change | case red at the mutant |
|---|---|---|
| audit_trip_any_arm | the trip regex also matches `ok` | a would-trip arm gives one DISPATCH line; ok and insufficient give none |
| audit_no_memory | drop the `arm not in tripped` test | null: a repeat of the same arm line dispatches nothing and writes no byte |
| audit_key_by_span | re-key memory by the sliding span | a second arm dispatches; the still-tripped arm at a slid cut gives none |
| audit_trip_never_clears | an arm reading ok never leaves memory | null: a trip that clears and trips again dispatches again |
| audit_no_clearing_write | write the job only when `new` | a good run after a failed one clears UNREADABLE |
| audit_unclassified_kept | drop the `" unclassified "` filter | output whose only GUARDRAIL line is the unclassified one is UNREADABLE |
| audit_rc_ignored | `rc != 0` not read | a failed run is UNREADABLE, never a dispatch |

Unpinned sites: the new code is in `tools/`, which `mutation-autofix` does not mutate; the in-tree `MUTANTS` harness above is its pin.

## Null control

Cases `audit-dispatch null: a trip that clears and trips again dispatches again`, `...: a still-failing run stays UNREADABLE`, `...: a repeat of the same arm line dispatches nothing and writes no byte` and `...: only ok and insufficient arm lines write no job, no digest, no memory`. Finder's harness at both ends (the reviewer's hourly sweep of the real `audit_dispatch`, 2026-11-01T00:00Z to 2026-11-06T09:00Z, 60-day window, local bus, no `--fetch`, 130 cuts): at the baseline `f6a299d3` it emits 38 distinct DISPATCH lines; at this head 3, which are three distinct trip episodes (model:sonnet read `ok` at the 2026-11-01T04:00Z to 08:00Z cuts, so its second dispatch follows a clear, and `all` tripped once). Perturbation: that clear-and-retrip is the null control of the keying, not a slide. `stale_probe.py` (trip, fail, recover-same-cut, recover-ok, ok-again): at the baseline the digest reads `audit-dispatch: UNREADABLE review_strength boom` after all of the last three; at this head the UNREADABLE line is gone after recover-same-cut and the DISPATCH line is kept.

## Figures

- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py --self-test`: 124 checks, 0 failed (107 at the merge base).
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/review_strength.py --self-test`: 116 checks, 0 failed.

- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir $D`: `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run`, `tests/entities.py`.
- The sweep counts above: `python3 -I $EXPORT/sweep_row.py <seat dir> <repo> <cache dir>` (sha1 56bc3f1f688a; drives the row's real `audit_dispatch` once per hourly cut over cached `review_strength.py --guardrail` outputs, the reviewer's sweep adapted to count the row's DISPATCH lines), run with the `beat_jobs.py` of `f6a299d3` and of this head; the reviewer's own count was 37 keys over its cuts, mine is 38 lines over mine because my local bus snapshot differs.

comments.first: Fix review: blocked f6a299d30092bcc5e63a6d1b9e904a7df33459c4 over-fire: a sustained trip dispatches once per sliding cut (37 audits for model:sonnet in 5.4 days) and one failed run leaves UNREADABLE in the digest forever
comments.body:
Fix review: blocked f6a299d30092bcc5e63a6d1b9e904a7df33459c4 over-fire: a sustained trip dispatches once per sliding cut (37 audits for model:sonnet in 5.4 days) and one failed run leaves UNREADABLE in the digest forever

bus-nonce: bd1ba3ae797ee537a33db5779fb2cb39

Round 1 (first-round adversarial fix review), head f6a299d30092bcc5e63a6d1b9e904a7df33459c4, merge base 9315526f8dca6dcd07f9cf3f2685bd1dd633b4f6, three-dot diff.

## Block

1. **The cut key slides with every new verdict, so one sustained trip is many dispatches, and the body does not state it.** Claim (body, Figures): a cut is keyed by the arm line's printed first..last verdict span, and its only stated limit is the missing year. Evidence: the span is the first verdicts of the arm's last N PRs, so each new reviewed PR on a tripped arm moves it and the row emits a fresh `DISPATCH` line on the next 1800 s pass. Harness (mine, ev/sweep.sh): `review_strength.py --window X=2026-09-07T00:00Z..<T> --guardrail` at every hour T from 2026-11-01T00:00Z to 2026-11-06T09:00Z on the bus as fetched 2026-11-06 (2091 verdicts), counting distinct (arm, cut) keys among would-trip lines, which is exactly the row's memory key. RESULT: model:sonnet would-trip at 125/126 hourly cuts with **37 distinct keys**, all at 1/126 with 1; 38 dispatches in 5.4 days from one sustained trip, each auditing a last-20 window that overlaps the previous one in up to 19 of 20 PRs (ev/sweep-summary.txt, ev/sweep-raw.txt). Hourly sampling undercounts the row's 30-minute cadence. Perturbation: the same sweep's all arm, tripping at one cut, yields one dispatch, so the multiplicity is the slide, not the harness. The ruling's "one per tripped arm and cut" admits this reading, but the brief asks that the cut key's limit be stated and judged; the stated limit (year) is negligible and the real one is not stated. Fix either way: key a dispatch by trip episode (once per arm until it reads `ok`/`insufficient` again) or by a cut sharing no PR with the last dispatched cut for that arm, with a self-test case for a slid cut; or keep per-cut and state the measured rate in the body for the owner to confirm.

2. **One failed `review_strength` run leaves `audit-dispatch: UNREADABLE` in the digest until the next new trip.** Claim (instrument doc, docstring): only a failed run is UNREADABLE. Evidence: `audit_dispatch` writes the job file only on UNREADABLE or on a new dispatch (`if new:`), so a recovered pass with nothing new never clears the UNREADABLE line; roster_drain, the precedent the comment cites, clears its HOLD-STALE line on an idle pass. Harness: ev/stale_probe.py drives the real `audit_dispatch` with a fake runner through trip, fail, recover-same-cut, recover-ok, ok-again. RESULT: after the failure the digest reads `audit-dispatch: UNREADABLE review_strength boom` at every one of the three recovered passes (ev/stale-probe.txt). Perturbation: the first pass (trip) writes the DISPATCH line and no UNREADABLE, so the stuck line is the failure's. `--fetch` hits the network every 30 min, so a transient failure is expected, and a stale UNREADABLE is a false actionable line on the orchestrator's one wake. Fix: on a readable pass with nothing new, rewrite the job without the UNREADABLE line (keeping any DISPATCH lines), with a self-test case and a mutant for it.

## Findings

- Surviving mutant: dropping the `" unclassified " not in ln` filter from `arms` (ev/mutants.txt, `unclassified_kept`) leaves the self-test at 116/0: no case feeds output whose only GUARDRAIL line is the unclassified one, which the filter exists to report as UNREADABLE. Carry: R10-PLANTED-DEFECT-AUDIT

## Evidence

- Head measured: f6a299d30092bcc5e63a6d1b9e904a7df33459c4 (ev/HEAD.txt); still the PR head at verdict time per the PR read.
- CI: `merge_train.py classify f6a299d30092bcc5e63a6d1b9e904a7df33459c4 --pr 3240` -> `GREEN f6a299d30092bcc5e63a6d1b9e904a7df33459c4 pending: none red: none`, rc=0 (ev/classify.txt). Red checks on this head: none, matching the body.
- Merge: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` rc=0, tree d4472e1d (ev/merge-tree.txt).
- Self-tests at head: beat_jobs 116 checks 0 failed, review_strength 116/0, beatd 119/0; at origin/main (null control): beat_jobs 107/0, review_strength 116/0 (ev/selftests-head.txt, ev/selftests-main.txt). Body figures 116/107/116/119 re-derived.
- entities.py: ALL 2632 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED at head and at origin/main; structure.py: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED at both (ev/entities-structure.txt). prepr.sh not re-run (CI cited, fix-review step 11).
- Stated mutants planted by hand in a temp copy, each named case red with self-test rc=1 and green at the head: audit_trip_any_arm (trip case and ok/insufficient null case FAIL), audit_no_memory (repeat null FAIL), audit_key_arm_only (repeat null and second-arm case FAIL), audit_rc_ignored (failed-run case FAIL). Extra: dropping `ctx.remember` and forcing the write on an idle pass are both killed (ev/mutants.txt).
- Live guardrail (`review_strength.py --fetch --window X=2026-10-01T00:00Z..2026-11-06T12:00Z --guardrail`, rc=0): all, cloud, local, model:claude-opus-5-5, model:opus ok; model:claude-sonnet-5-5 insufficient (7 < 20); model:sonnet 0/20, P = 0.0014, would-trip. That matches the body's Null control (ev/guardrail-live.txt).
- (1) restart null, settled: two separate `beat_jobs.py audit-dispatch --state S` processes on the live bus; pass 1 wrote `DISPATCH: planted-defect-audit arm=model:sonnet cut=11-04T18:40Z..11-05T22:03Z`; pass 2 left every file under the digest byte-identical (sha256) with new.stamp's mtime unchanged (ev/live-restart.txt). The TRIP regex matches the real `model:sonnet` line.
- (2) cut key: the year limit needs identical first and last verdict minutes a year apart, so it is acceptable; the sliding limit is Block 1.

merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-STAMP-BASE: the stamp bumps from the highest release tag
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-STAMP-BASE (lane C, fix, size S), repair round 2. v7.1.2 was tagged by hand at b8e823699, on a tree whose VERSION, manifest version and notes still read 7.1.1. `tools/release/stamp.py` bumped from VERSION alone, so it proposed v7.1.2 again, and rule 3 refuses that as an existing tag. Rules "flush", 4 and 5 (`window_log_args`, `rule4_problem`, `disposition_gate`) also took their window from the newest v* tag, and no stamp had made that tag. v7.1.2 is kept. Nothing is deleted or retagged.

What changes:

- `stamp.py` gets two pure functions. `bump_base(current, tags)` returns the higher of VERSION and the highest `TAG_RE` tag. `last_stamped_tag(tags, version_at)` returns the newest release tag whose own tree's VERSION equals its name. The VERSION lookup is passed in, so the self-test needs no git. `tag_version` reads `git show <tag>:VERSION` through the module's `sh` seam. After Rule 1's `fetch --tags`, the Rule 3 block computes `base = bump_base(current, tags + remote)` and then `nxt = next_version(base, ...)`. `last_tag = last_stamped_tag(tags, tag_version)` feeds flush, rule 4 and rule 5. Rule 3's exists refusal and above-every-tag refusal stay as the backstop.
- `release.yml` gets a new step, `Refuse a tag whose tree does not carry its version`, which runs before `Create the GitHub release`. It refuses unless VERSION is the tag, the manifest version is the tag and RELEASE_NOTES.md has an exact `## $TAG` line, and it prints every problem it finds. The publish step reads the asset back `attempts=5` times, with a `sleep 10` between reads and none after the last, then fails. `RELEASE_READBACK_ATTEMPTS` names that bound in stamp.py, and the self-test pins the two to agree.
- The self-test cuts each step's own `run: |` block out of release.yml with `release_step_script`. It never runs a copy of the step's logic.

Round 2 builds the review's three findings at 66577738. None is carried.

1. The previous body's `## Head` figure was false. This body is re-taken whole from the template, and every figure below was re-derived at the final head by the command shown with it (see `## Head` for the corrected claim).
2. The pin `flush: main runs it after rule 3 and before rule 4` searched `main()` for `last_tag = "v"`, which this diff removed. `find` returned -1, so the after-rule-3 half held for any order. The pin is now anchored on `last_tag = last_stamped_tag(tags, tag_version)` and starts its chain with `-1 <`, so a missing anchor fails it.
3. The self-test ran the release.yml steps with no bound, so an endless read-back hung it instead of failing it. Both step seams now go through one runner, `_run_step`. It starts `bash -e -c <step>` in its own session, waits up to `RELEASE_STEP_TIMEOUT_S` (10 s) and kills the whole process group at that bound, returning `None`, which every caller's `== 0` / `== 1` check reads as FAIL. Two smaller fixes go with it: the publish stub's read count tolerates an empty file (`-1`), and the tree step uses the same runner (one more seam found by the census in Figures).

Alternatives considered for (3), and why each lost: (a) `subprocess.run(..., timeout=)`, which this branch took first (cb0909079). The kill reaches only bash, so the stub `gh` it started kept writing in the temporary directory. In 10 runs of the unbounded mutant at 60fb6879, 2 crashed with `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''`. With the read made tolerant, 1 run in 10 still crashed with `OSError: [Errno 39] Directory not empty` while the directory was being removed. Killing the process group removes the cause, and 20 runs out of 20 then fail cleanly (Figures). (b) `TemporaryDirectory(ignore_cleanup_errors=True)` hides the symptom and leaves a live stub behind. (c) Bounding only by the CI job's timeout is what the review found: a hang, not a FAIL. Alternatives for the base fix: (a) reading the base from the tag list alone, ignoring VERSION, loses the case where VERSION is ahead of every tag (a first stamp after a manual VERSION fix). (b) Hand tags listed by name would be a spelling list the next hand tag defeats. (c) Deleting or retagging v7.1.2 is excluded by the brief.

## Head

## Findings

It says `git diff --stat c679f4b69 8a39977cb -- tools/release/stamp.py .github/workflows/release.yml tests/entities.py tests/closures.json` prints nothing, but it prints `tests/closures.json | 26 ++++++++++++++++++++++++--`, which is R10-GRADE-DRIVERS adding `driving_grade.py` to seven closures (ev/figures.txt). So it does not block, but the figure is not verified as written. Carry: dismissed: substance re-derived at the head; the delta is an unrelated module's closure membership
- The pre-existing pin `flush: main runs it after rule 3 and before rule 4` (tools/release/stamp.py:1929) now searches main() for `last_tag = "v"`, which this diff removed, so `find` returns -1 and the "after rule 3" half of the pin is vacuous (ev/flush_pin.txt: origin/main 4741, head -1). Carry: dismissed: ordering still pinned by the new rule-3 slice check at stamp.py:1950; a one-token cleanup for the next stamp.py touch
- An unbounded read-back mutant of the publish step (`for ... seq` replaced by an endless while loop) does not fail the self-test. It hangs, because `_publish_step` runs the step with no subprocess timeout, so the bound is guarded only by the job's own timeout. The shipped step is bounded: I measured exit 1 after 5 reads. merges.body:
Triage batch 126 (R10-TRIAGE-S6) rules on the existing set under the owner's 5 % and 10 % rule: P391 DEFER on the non-production CI lanes, P392 DEFER on the triage seat. This is repair round 3 of the review block `owner-ruling-contradicted`.

**Round 2 block, answered.** P392 Binding item 1 ("a queue line with no measured figure gets a one-line DEFER... needs no decision") is removed from the Binding list. It changed the ruling form that `dev/governance/roles/proposal-triage.md` requires, which is policy. The record now holds it as a proposal for proposal-triage, adopted nowhere, with destination `dev/governance/roles/proposal-triage.md`. The remaining two bindings are renumbered 1 and 2; the first now refers to the proposed form. Nothing else in the file, the body or `dev/programme/delivery/3238.md` cited the removed item (grep).

**Follow-up, the `ci-fails` arm.** It now reads REST only: `gh api -X GET search/issues` for merged_at inside the window, and `pulls/<n>` for each head ref (the harness's `api()` now passes `-X GET`). The docstring and the ruling state the definition. Re-run at this head, cold cache, from this cloud seat: 423 failed pull-request runs, 55 failed push runs, 262 pull requests merged, 232 distinct head refs. Unchanged. The arm's definition is merged_at (262 by REST); the git arm's 263 first-parent merges by commit date differ at the window boundary. The 233 vs 232 distinct branches the reviewer counted came from that git count; the arm's own 232 is distinct head refs of the 262. `report` re-run on the ci-cost (221 runs, 309.7 runner h) and ci-fails outputs reproduces the per-lane table, for example arch-instrument 5.4 % / 779 s / 0 caught and instrument-self-tests 10.7 % / 1328 s / 9 caught. No ruling figure changed. Carry: dismissed: fixed in this PR, the arm in `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_triage_p391.py` is REST.

## Head

`21dbeb61c28f18aea98b45eebc290e30d991461a` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`86d1220327a31155f78423bf19e17aa05cbc7d5e`

## Mutation proof

This file's only consumer is the triage gate in `tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py`: `ruling_verdict` reads P391 and P392 DEFER and P393 None, and a carry citing either is refused as not an ACCEPT ruling. The harness change is evidence only; the arm was run, its output compared with the recorded figures.

## Null control

P393 reads None; with the file absent a carry citing it is refused as not on the roster branch or origin/main. For the REST switch the null control is the unchanged figures: 423, 55, 262, 232 against the recorded ones.

## Figures

- `git diff --stat $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD`: 4 files changed, 450 insertions(+) (harness, `tests/closures.json`, the ruling, the delivery row).
- origin/main was merged into the branch before the run; `tools/pr/prepr.sh` ran at `86d1220327a31155f78423bf19e17aa05cbc7d5e` and printed `rc=0`.
- The git, roster, ci-cost and nightly figures are untouched.

## Red checks

none concluded at this head yet; its checks run after the push.

## Forward-carry

- The proposal-triage proposal (a one-line DEFER for a queue line with no measured figure) is for the owner and proposal-triage, not this PR. Destination: `dev/governance/roles/proposal-triage.md`. Carry: dismissed: a policy change needs the owner's approval in its own policy pull request; the ruling records it as a proposal and no roster group follows R10-TRIAGE-S6.

## Friction

none
