## Block

First round. Reviewed from a detached worktree at 08d62371ac0d8170ab74042b254f3b961d26fdfc, under fix-review.md and proposal-triage.md. The role files match main: `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty.

proposal-triage.md requires `Instances:` with "each figure beside its command or log: cite, don't carry". Check 2 of the brief asks for the command at a pushed ref. `dev/programme/triage/s6-batch126.md` describes how the figures were taken: API endpoints, windows, and a definition of "PRs". It then says: "The two listing scripts and the raw JSON are kept in the seat's folder, outside the tree." So no figure in either ruling can be re-run from a pushed ref. That covers the 294 runner hours and 220-run sample, every lane share and mean, every "PRs" count, the 25 % total, the token table (5.27 M, 71.5 M, 1.92 G, 8.6/12.0/7.2 %), and the roster tallies (382 entries; 233/93/55/1; 247 carries; 56/58/5/57/71).

fix-review.md step 9: an instrument whose copy lived out of tree "is named, and lands". It has not landed.

Some figures can be re-derived from git alone. I counted them over `git log --since=2026-10-29` at merge base b88684a2 (ev/rederive.txt). My definition is my own, because the record gives none. None of them matches:
- `ci: pin killed`: record 18, re-derived 27. This changes the "nearest case": 27/228 is 11.8 %, not 7.9 %.
- `ci: record delivery`: record 46, re-derived 52.
- `ci: record nightly`: record 12, re-derived 14.
- `ci: re`: record 3. `ci: re-record closures` re-derives as 7, and the bare prefix `ci: re` also matches the record commits.
- PRs merged since 2026-10-29: record 228, re-derived 239 PR numbers on main's first parent. 228 is the denominator of every 5 % test ("5 % of 228 is 12").

The windows may differ, since the record's main and mine are not named. That is the point: without the command at a ref, the discrepancy cannot be settled either way. Both rulings are DEFERs that rest on these numbers ("under 12 pull requests at the upper bound"), so the ruling is not yet standing on measurement.

To clear the block, land the two listing scripts in the tree, either under `tools/audit/seat/` per decision 0013 or as a committed harness. Cite each figure as the command and ref that produce it, and correct the git-derivable counts. Token figures from local transcripts cannot be reproduced by another seat: say so beside each one, and give the command and window.

## Findings

- Figures carried, not cited: listing scripts and raw JSON are kept out of tree, and five git-derivable counts do not re-derive (18/27, 46/52, 12/14, 3/7, 228/239). The P391 `mutation-pins` "nearest case" moves from 7.9 % to 11.8 % under my count. Carry: R10-TRIAGE-S6
- The body's opening says "the diff is one markdown file under `dev/programme/triage/`". The three-dot diff is two files; it also adds `dev/programme/delivery/3238.md`. Red checks also reasons "A ref with no pull request has no checks", but this head has a PR and 68 check-runs. The conclusion `none` is correct; the stated reason is not. Carry: R10-TRIAGE-S6
- Two commits on the branch, 34ee0cc0 (merge of main) and 08d62371 (delivery row), are authored `tvofi`. The record itself lists "body commits under the owner's name" as a corrected slip, and CLAUDE.md (decision 0011) has the hpo-author App author. `pr-contract` passed at this head, so this is noted, not blocked. Carry: R10-TRIAGE-S6

- Check 1, cites: base b88684a2, dad3178d, c1dd4a51 and 15b2376f all resolve on origin. `tools/ci/prelude.py` `UNITS` agrees with the record's "req" column for all nine lanes in the first table (ev/prelude-units.txt). `dev/governance/config/machinery_budgets.json` `exemptions` is `[]` at the head, as the record says. The roster group R10-TRIAGE-S6 exists on origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster at 0a462125.
- Check 2: no figure carries a command at a pushed ref (see Block). I could not reproduce the CI-API figures, the token figures or the roster tallies. My own definitions for the git-derivable counts are in ev/rederive.txt.
- Check 3: both rulings are DEFER. Each records why ("unmeasured does not pass") and what would change it (an owner decision, or a measured benefit), as proposal-triage.md requires. There is no ACCEPT, so no destination is owed.
- Check 4: I found no contradiction with an owner ruling. Both DEFERs go to the owner through the orchestrator, not to round 11. P391 repeats the owner's 2026-11-01 ruling against routing as CI capacity, and the record cites 2026-11-04 for ci-ratchet.
- Check 5: `dev/programme/delivery/3238.md` is in the three-dot diff. Body `## Red checks`: `none`. I read all 68 check-runs of the head on one page of 100: 0 failure, 0 cancelled. The packet digest is green.
- Mutation proof (ev/mutation.txt): `roster_edit.ruling_verdict` reads DEFER, DEFER and None for P391, P392 and P393. Flipping P391's verdict line to ACCEPT makes it read ACCEPT, so the body's mutation claim holds.
- CI: `merge_train.py classify 08d62371ac0d8170ab74042b254f3b961d26fdfc --pr 3238` printed `GREEN 08d62371ac0d8170ab74042b254f3b961d26fdfc pending: none red: none` with rc=0 (ev/classify.txt).

The record states the opposite ("needs no decision"), and later triage seats read a merged record as authority. This fails brief Check 4. merges.subject: Merge pull request #3243 from tvofi/fix/r10-gate-lease-toctou
merges.title: R10-GATE-LEASE-TOCTOU: gate lease toctou
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
Closes the R10-GATE-LEASE-TOCTOU free-slot race carried from PR 3170 (item 42008ca4). `_free_slot` looked a second time (`is_file`) after a missing read, and its unparseable-slot branch unlinked a rival's fresh owner, so two takers held one slot. One `read_text` now decides absent (`FileNotFoundError`, return the index; `Owner.create`'s hard-link arbitrates) against broken, and a broken slot is reaped through `_steal(path, None)`. Repair round 2 (verdict/3243, blocked at 3cbcbd5d: mutation-vacuous) adds the acceptance cases that pin the reap and its put-back, and one production change: `_steal` removes a directory-valued grave (`shutil.rmtree`) instead of raising `IsADirectoryError` out of `take_slot`.

Alternatives that lost: a lock around `_free_slot` (the pool takes no flock by design); a retry loop on the test side (hides the race); an inode re-check before the rename (narrows, does not close, and adds a second look of the kind this PR removes).

Carry 0: the free-slot race left open by PR 3170 (item 42008ca4), closed by this diff.
Carry 1: the gate-lease `_free_slot` `is_file` time-of-check/time-of-use race, closed by this diff; its delay-only plant is the null control above, made exact in `delayed_read`.
Carry 2: the group's own roster carry (`Carry: R10-GATE-LEASE-TOCTOU`), discharged by this pull request.

## Head

`7baf10d6696534f62ea481182c2cdffd74216c2c` merges main `7e8939d` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`411270a40b14a235482fa37c2af55132cfc74760` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

That is the exact property the body claims for this line.
- M4 (delete the `_steal(path, None)` line): `ALL 42 ... PASSED`. Behaviourally a broken slot is never reclaimed: `_free_slot` returns the index, the following `create` fails (`then create wins: False`), and `take_slot` loops forever on one hand-written or corrupt slot file. No test anywhere pins unparseable-slot recovery (searched `tests/` and `tools/` for `_free_slot` callers and unparseable/garbage cases). That gap also exists at main, but this PR rewrites that line and claims its behaviour.
- M2 (restore the `is_file` second read but reap via `_steal`): passes. I judge this mutant near-equivalent, because `_steal` puts back the rival's file. Reported, not blocking. Carry: dismissed: near-equivalent mutant, the put-back makes the second look harmless

R10-CI-SLIM: two of the three slip-study cards the owner accepted on 2026-11-05 land here (C2, C3), and C7 lands as (a) and (b). (c) is dropped, because once its premise is checked its saving measures 0. This change does four things. Main's critical-path ratchet becomes report-only. Edit runs stop holding a runner while the code run works. Product pull requests stop paying for machinery lanes. Tools-only pull requests stop paying for PR CodeQL. No product file changes (`custom_components/` untouched).

**Repair round 3.** The review at 84a7c456f blocked C7(c). `prelude.pins_due` skipped `tests / mutation-pins` and `tests / mutation-autofix` on a non-product delta from `before`. The rule never checked that the previous head's pins had concluded. cancel-superseded cancels them, and in the PR's own sample that held in 3 of 3 skips.

The repair is in two commits:
- 2c51d07b5 adds the reviewer's sound rule. The delta counts only from a head whose code run concluded the measurement (`prelude.pins_measured`): `tests / mutation` success, or failure with every pins shard and the autofix succeeding. Anything else measures. Eleven self-tests were added. On round 2's rule, 7 of them fail: previous pins cancelled, autofix failed, pins still running, pins skipped on a failed mutation, one shard of several cancelled, an unreadable runs listing, and no run at the previous head.
- 4056a2c5e drops C7(c). With the premise checked, `c7_replay.py` reads (c) as 0 runs and a saving of 0. Even with the read moved to the latest moment it could happen (each run's prelude end), the saving is still 0. One reason is that the autofix's own pin commit lands while that autofix is still running, so the previous head is never concluded at the next prelude.

The card asked for a measurement guaranteed at review-ready, and a saving that is not real is not kept. So `prelude.pins_due`, the `pins` output, tests.yml's `pins` input and both `inputs.pins` job conditions are removed. The `mutation`, `mutation-pins` and `mutation-autofix` jobs are YAML-identical to main's again. `gate_satisfiable.py` now refuses any caller input in either pins job's `if:`, and it reads `GATE NOT SATISFIABLE` on round 2's workflows.

Alternatives not taken:
- Keeping 2c51d07b5's rule: it is sound, but it costs one runs read and one jobs read per synchronize for a measured saving of 0. Per fixer.md step 17, the simpler tree wins.
- Taking the delta from the last concluded head, the reviewer's equivalent form: it walks history for the same 0 saving.

**C2. `critical_path_minutes` is report-only.** `tests/ci_ratchet.py` adds a `REPORT_ONLY` set holding that one metric. `compare` prints it as `info critical_path_minutes: X (reference R; report-only, never graded)` and never counts it. Every other `ci_budgets.json` row is still graded at zero tolerance. The band row `critical_path_minutes_band` and `BAND_KEYS` are deleted. The recorded value stays as the reference that `orchestrator_tick.py`'s ETA reads. `tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py` types that reference `free`.

**C3 (option A). An edit run holds no runner.** `prelude.defer_to` finds an unfinished code run at the same head and PR whose `pr-contract / pr-contract` has not started. When it finds one, the edit run's workset is `arch-score budget-raise-gate` and the run does not wait. `pr-contract` reads the body off the API when it starts, after every unit, so the code run's gate judges the LATEST body. The edit run's gate takes the prelude's workset (`WORKSET`, `gate.deferring`), and a unit skipped in a deferring run is no source. If `pr-contract` has started, the code run is finished, or there is no code run, today's wait applies. A deferral read in a race is a false RED, which `gate-sweep.yml` re-judges. It is never a false green.

**C7.** (a) `prelude.machinery`: a pull request whose every changed file is product stands down three lanes at step level, each reporting success: `tests / arch-instrument`, the `tests / closures` recording and `governance / env-matrix`. `governance / instrument-self-tests`, which is not required, skips whole. Product means `custom_components/`, `docs/`, `README.md`, a script that `tests/closures.json` measures, `tests/golden/` or `tests/mutation_ledger/`. Any other file runs the lanes, and so does every push. (b) `codeql_scope.decide` skips every leg of a pull request with nothing under `custom_components/` or `.github/`. The stand-in reports success, and a push to main always analyzes.

**Owner constraint (tvofi, 2026-11-05), per change.** For each change: the check that still guards each production path, and why the risk to production quality and to future throughput is acceptable.
- C2: no production path. `tests / ci-ratchet` still grades every other CI metric at zero tolerance (a planted `script_runs_per_push` 54 -> 55 is GREW at the head). The accepted risk is that a slower critical path goes ungraded. It is still printed and still feeds the ETA. Throughput gain: no more re-record and band-widening PRs (#2839, #3045, #3180, #3189, #3201, #3228). Before: grew=1. After: grew=0 (`## Null control`).
- C3: no check is skipped. The code run's gate still judges every production unit, and its `pr-contract` reads the latest body. Opus review dispatch is not touched. A race gives a false red, never a false green. Before: 4438 edit-run job-minutes. After: 660.
- C7(a): the idled lanes measure machinery only. On a diff that touches `custom_components/`, these still run: `tests / fast`, `tests / mutation` with its pins and autofix, goldens, features, CodeQL and review. `gate_satisfiable.py`'s production-only case reads every CodeQL leg as `analyze`. Before: 4988 job-minutes. After: 4988 (0 runs idled in the sample, so it pays after C1, as the card says).
- C7(b): CodeQL still analyzes every pull request reaching `custom_components/` or `.github/`, and every push to main. It skips only tools/dev-only pull requests, which main's push analysis covers. Before: 2955 job-minutes. After: 1764.
- C7(c) dropped: mutation testing on production changes is main's again, byte for byte (YAML comparison, `## Figures`). Throughput risk removed: the skip that left `mutation` red with no pins table at a head the seat could not re-trigger is gone.

Toolchain: `bash tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh --check` read `OK python3 is /opt/hpo/venv-ci/bin/python3`. No golden ran: the scope is MODE: FULL, so the goldens are CI's.

## Block

**C7(c) skips measurements that never happened.** `prelude.pins_due` gates `tests / mutation-pins` and `tests / mutation-autofix` on the push's own delta (`before...head`). Its docstring states the premise: "the sites still unpinned were measured at the head before". The rule never checks that premise. Cancel-superseded cancels a previous head's run, and its pins shards with it. When the next push is non-product (a delivery row, a body fix-up, a tooling commit), those sites go unmeasured.

Measurement, on the PR's own recorded sample (`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_ci_slim/sample.json`, my script `ev/c7c_probe.py`, output `ev/c7c_probe.txt`, `ev/c7c_three_runs.txt`):
- C7(c) changes behaviour only where `pins_due` is False AND `tests / mutation` failed, because the pins job's `if:` already needs a failed `mutation`. That is 3 runs, which are the body's "3 runs" and its whole 479-minute saving (re-derived: `ev/c7_replay_head.txt`).
- In all 3, the previous head's survivors were never pinned:
  - PR 3219, run 41937668180: the previous run 41937637106 had `tests / mutation-pins` **cancelled**. Its own pins succeeded in reality, and that was the only completed measurement of those sites. C7(c) removes it.
  - PR 3220, run 41951544787: the previous run 41951503566 had pins **cancelled**. Its own 7 pin shards succeeded, the only completed measurement. C7(c) removes it.
  - PR 3219, run 41951472711: the previous run's pins succeeded, but its autofix **failed**, so nothing was pinned.
- Control: runs where `pins_due` is True keep today's behaviour by construction. The planted production defect below shows `pins_due` True on a product diff at the head.

Consequence: at such a head, `mutation` stays red with no pins table and no autofix. The seat cannot re-trigger the measurement. A dispatch never runs pins (`github.event_name == 'pull_request'`), and an empty commit or a close-and-reopen is forbidden. Only a later push touching the package does. This does not weaken production quality, because `mutation` still fails closed. It is a throughput risk: in this window every C7(c) skip hits it.

Card sentence it contradicts: C7 (c) "mutation-pins runs once when the PR is review-ready, not at every head", with the accepted risk "(c) A survivor is found at review-ready instead of per head". The implementation guarantees no single measurement. A survivor whose only measurement was superseded is not found at review-ready or at any later non-product head. That goes beyond the card.

Minimal sound repair (the fixer's call): `pins_due` is False only when the head the delta starts from actually concluded `mutation-pins` (success, or skipped because `mutation` passed). Otherwise, measure. Equivalently, take the delta from the last head whose pins concluded, not from `before`. Add a self-test whose previous head's pins were cancelled. Re-run `c7_replay.py`: on this sample (c)'s saving becomes 0, so report it honestly.

merges.title: feat(inputs): accept a water_heater entity as the DHW set-point (outside contribution, was #3224)
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
Accept a `water_heater` entity as the DHW set-point (`dhw_setpoint_entity`).

Some pumps expose their hot-water set-point only as a `water_heater` entity — Luxtronik's `water_heater.<id>_domestic_water` is one (state = operation mode, target in the `temperature` attribute, range `min_temp`/`max_temp`, step `target_temp_step`, all in the instance's unit). The selector offered only `number`, `input_number` and `climate`, so such an install could not configure the slot. A `water_heater` carries the climate shape, so this treats it as one: read, range, step and unit follow the climate path, and the write goes through `water_heater.set_temperature`.

Changes: `inputs.py` (`SETPOINT_SERVICES`, `_RANGE_KEYS`, `_STEP_KEYS`, and `setpoint_unit` now keys on `_ATTRIBUTE_TARGET_DOMAINS = ("climate", "water_heater")`), `config_flow.py` (selector domain list), the `dhw_setpoint_entity` help text in `strings.json` / `en.json` / `sv.json`, the #1526 service table and one new check in `tests/features.py`, and `tests/golden/config_flow.json` re-recorded (the two `dhw_setpoint_entity` filter lines move, nothing else).

**Contributor credit.** This change is by the outside contributor Bankaifan, first opened as PR #3224 (https://github.com/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/pull/3224, head `a1fc6edb0e7fb51015bb50cb66b4c9bbbecfe877`). It is re-authored here as a seat pull request because decision 0011 gives an outside contributor no way to author one: the contributor's three commits are cherry-picked unchanged, each keeping its author (Bankaifan), with no squash and no edit, and their three-dot diff is the same patch as the original (identical patch-id). The feature measurements below are the contributor's, from their own head.

**Repairs on top of the contributor's commits.** The contributor's three commits are untouched. Earlier rounds added the `config_flow` claim in `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` (the re-recorded fixture moves two leaves; without the claim `tests/env_drift.py --all <base>` reads `1 UNCLAIMED DRIFT(S)`) and the `setpoint_unit.GUARD_OFF.d9727610` pin. This round (the review of bd0ee867e49b blocked on mutant m4) adds one test-only commit: a degF leaf for the water_heater DHW slot in `tests/features.py` as its own check, plus a commit dropping the earlier round's stale `PR-BODY.md` from the tree (it failed the `tests/entities.py` classification check once merged in). No production, golden or claim-file change in this round.

## Head

`4c7df1c19fb37f0699000fe83889f4fe9648743c` merges main `0a7c84f` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`4dc59c5991d238ff2fcccd16d81b91d7a1ea25c6` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`b3bb708c05a3bfb54797cb62f0cedf6a48c8d763` (the previous PR head `bd0ee867e49bf6f0af414efcf2aa29ae775ac926` plus the test commit, the PR-BODY.md removal and two merges of origin/main, the last at `c679f4b692f483959769ec5b5147aa4d624c45f4`). The two earlier seat commits are authored as `seat` (disclosed in earlier rounds); this round's commits are authored as `hpo-fixer`.

## Mutation proof

The new check `a water_heater DHW set-point on a degF instance reads its range in degC and is clamped to it` pins `setpoint_range_c` == (30.0, 65.0) and the arbiter's DHW clamp (70 degC -> 65.0, 20 degC -> 30.0) for a degF water_heater with min_temp 86 and max_temp 149. Measured on tests/features.py, each mutant in a copy of the head:

- m4, `_ATTRIBUTE_TARGET_DOMAINS = ("climate",)`: `1 of 4860 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`, the new check, reading `range (86.0, 149.0)`. Before this commit the same mutant printed `ALL 4859 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` (the review's block).
- m1 (water_heater out of SETPOINT_SERVICES): 2 failed (the #1526 service-table check and the contributor's water_heater check).
- m2 (out of _RANGE_KEYS): 2 failed (the contributor's check and the new one).
- m3 (out of _STEP_KEYS): 1 failed (the contributor's check).
- m6 (`if False` at inputs.py:478): 4 failed (three climate checks and the new one), which now matches the pin reason's `failed=4`.

## Null control

Unmutated head: the new check passes (`ALL 4860 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, 4859 plus the one new check). On unmodified main the contributor's water_heater slot reads `range=(None, None)`, `step=1.0`, and `write_setpoint(..., 52.3)` makes no call (the contributor's null control, re-read by the reviewer).

## Figures

- `ALL 4860 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` at the test commit — `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py`
- `ALL 2632 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` — `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` (after the PR-BODY.md removal; the first run failed only on that file)
- `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED` — `python3 tests/structure.py`, also at the merged head inside prepr
- `PIN KILLED -- 0 new unpinned site(s) against 750a6001ae4d…; PIN KILLED: nothing to pin`; `3091 unpinned site(s) of 6799 candidate sites, 3091 at the ratchet base` — `python3 tests/mutation_table.py --pin-killed --base origin/main`
- `PRE-PR: … rc=0` on the merged head — `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh` (no body passed; the body check runs in body_push). Main had moved (750a6001 to c679f4b6), so it was merged and prepr run once more after.

## Red checks

The final head is not pushed to the pull request yet, so it has no check-runs. At the PR's current head `bd0ee867e49b` the only concluded red the review read was `tests / nightly-status` (`NIGHTLY FAILED`, main's scheduled nightly, not required, outside this diff). Everything else was green (`merge_train.py classify`: `GREEN … red: none`). CI's `mutation` lane stayed green while m4 survived because a tuple-literal edit is not a mutant its operators draw; this commit closes that gap with a check.

The reds of the earlier heads, carried (all cleared by the claim and pin commits of the previous round):

Every concluded red across all 56 check-runs of the previous head `6f3b23fd9c8984479046d6a4e88b857acff3ae3c` (and its two runs), causes read from the logs. The final head has no concluded check yet; the reviewer reads its check-runs.

- `tests / fast (3.14)` — `FAILED python3 tests/env_drift.py --all 203b4dfc…`, `DRIFT config_flow: 2 leaves moved`, `1 UNCLAIMED DRIFT(S)`. Cause: the re-recorded fixture with no claim. Cheaper detector: it existed — `tests/env_drift.py --all <base>` is in the scoped `scope.run` and `prepr.sh` and takes about 3 minutes (CI's was 174 s); the outside contributor had no 3.14.7 environment to run it in (their note said so). Standing cost of a countermeasure: none worth adding; the existing local check was not reachable from the contributor's box. Fixed by the claim commit.
- `tests / mutation` — `MUTATION TABLE REFUSED -- 3094 unpinned site(s) against 3093 … 1 of them added by this diff`, the site `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/inputs.py:478 GUARD_OFF`. Cause: the edit made the old pin stale and the new line had no pin. Cheaper detector: `mutation_table.py --pin-killed` (about 5 minutes) and the `mutation-autofix` job. Fixed by the pin commit.
- `tests / mutation-autofix` — `skip-measure-failed -- THE REPAIR DID NOT HAPPEN`. Cause: its baseline `tests/env_drift.py` run was red on the unclaimed `config_flow` drift above (reproduced here: the first `--pin-killed` run read `MUTATION TABLE INCONCLUSIVE`, baseline red in `tests/env_drift.py`; after the claim it pinned). A second symptom of the same cause, not a separate defect.
- `gate` (both runs) — the aggregate: `FAIL tests / fast (3.14)`, `tests / mutation`, `pr-contract`. Clears with them.
- `pr-contract / pr-contract` (both runs) — `check tests / fast (3.14) is red and ## Red checks does not name it` (and the same for `tests / mutation` and `tests / mutation-autofix`). Cause: the previous body said `none`. This body names them.
- `tests / nightly-status` — `NIGHTLY FAILED: slow failed last night` (scheduled run 41943946464, head 499162c). Main's, not required, outside this diff; the cause is not in this pull request and is the orchestrator's to dispatch.
- `governance / delivery-status` — overdue rows on main (#3189, #3204, #3203, #3202, #3174, …); not required, and this diff adds only its own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3231.md`. Main's, the orchestrator's to drain.
- `tests / replay` concluded `skipped` on that head, not red; if it reds on the final head, its `cycle_cost` runner-class band miss is main's, owned by R10-REPLAY-COST-BUDGET.

## Block

Round 1 of this re-author (PR #3231, the outside contribution #3224). Measured head `bd0ee867e49bf6f0af414efcf2aa29ae775ac926`, base `785c2b604ba4c01891737a5285f4f4f49394c18f` (= origin/main at review).

The product code is correct. I found no defect in `inputs.py`, `config_flow.py` or the strings. But one of the four production seams the diff adds is not pinned by any check. That seam is `setpoint_unit` keying on `_ATTRIBUTE_TARGET_DOMAINS = ("climate", "water_heater")` (inputs.py:467, :478).

- Mutant m4 (`ev/mutant-m4.diff`): `_ATTRIBUTE_TARGET_DOMAINS = ("climate",)`. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` at the mutant prints `ALL 4859 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, rc=0 (`ev/features-m4.log`). The new water_heater check still passes.
- Effect of the surviving mutant, measured with my own instrument (`tools/null_control.py`, mine, not the finder's: no finder harness exists). A `water_heater` in a degF instance with min_temp 86 and max_temp 149 gets `setpoint_range_c` → `(86.0, 149.0)` instead of `(30.0, 65.0)` (`ev/null-control-m4.txt` against `ev/null-control.txt`). The arbiter's DHW clamp ceiling becomes 149 °C, so a degF water_heater is no longer held to its own max_temp.
- Why nothing fails: the new check's degF case covers only the write (`setpoint_and_unit` falls back to the instance unit when the state is non-numeric, so the write survives the mutant). It never checks the range or the clamp on degF. The GUARD_OFF pin `setpoint_unit.GUARD_OFF.d9727610` is killed, but only through climate checks. m6 (`if False:` at inputs.py:478) fails exactly three checks, all climate (`ev/features-m6.log`). No water_heater check is among them.
- Repair (small, test-only): add a degF leaf to the new check, `setpoint_range_c` on the degF water_heater == `(30.0, 65.0)` and/or `_df_dhw_command(..., _DF, 70.0)` clamped to 149 °F. Then show m4 failing it.

## Findings

- Follow-up: the GUARD_OFF pin reason in `setpoint_unit.GUARD_OFF.d9727610.json` says "failed=4". At this head the same mutant fails 3 checks (`3 of 4859 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`, `ev/features-m6.log`). The kill verdict holds, but the count in the reason does not re-derive here. Carry: dismissed: kill verdict holds; count is the pin drive's own run, not a claim this PR depends on
- Non-blocking body gap: the body's feature figure `ALL 4831 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` is the contributor's, at their head, and is not re-derivable at this head. Here the head reads 4859 and main reads 4858 (+1, the new check). The body says this itself. Carry: dismissed: contributor figure, disclosed as such; re-derived count is in Evidence
- Non-blocking: the seat commits 180dc5934 and b9743dcdf are authored as `seat`, not `hpo-fixer`, and the body discloses this. Carry: dismissed: disclosed in body, author identity of seat commits, not product code
- Non-blocking: the brief's GOLDEN-CLAIM premise (a) calls config_flow value-bearing. It is not: `carries_floats()` is False and env_drift compares it exactly at level 1 (claimed_drift.txt notes, #547). Re-recording plus claiming is the established practice for this fixture, and both were needed (the re-record clears the level-1 staleness; the claim clears the branch-vs-base drift). Carry: dismissed: brief premise, the claim is correct under #547's practice

## Evidence

- Patch identity: `git diff $(merge-base origin/main refs/pull/3224/head) refs/pull/3224/head | git patch-id --stable` = `9f2a5297…` = the same over `d1153ae86~1..1fe34a84f` (the head's first three commits). Per-commit patch-ids match (b89289d1fc8f, 0a0c45ed6c70, 8b291fd54604). All three commits are authored by Bankaifan. The messages differ from #3224's only by the removed `Co-Authored-By` and `Claude-Session` trailers.
- Seat commits beyond the three: 9376cfbc5 (delete the stale pin 2c91312e), 6f3b23fd9 (delivery row 3231.md), 180dc5934 (config_flow claim), b9743dcdf (new pin d9727610), and three merges of main. The three-dot diff against origin/main touches exactly the 11 files in the packet; the merges add nothing beyond main.
- RESULT features head: `ALL 4859 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` rc=0 (`ev/features-head.log`); main: `ALL 4858 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` rc=0 (`ev/features-main.log`).
- RESULT mutants on tests/features.py:
  - m1 (drop `water_heater` from SETPOINT_SERVICES): `2 of 4859 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`. The #1526 service-table check (`water_heater.p6_dhw_setpoint_entity: the consumer issued no call`) and the new check both fail, as the body's mutation proof says.
  - m2 (drop it from _RANGE_KEYS): 1 failed, the new check.
  - m3 (drop it from _STEP_KEYS): 1 failed, the new check.
  - m4 (drop it from _ATTRIBUTE_TARGET_DOMAINS): 0 failed, which is the block.
  - m6 (GUARD_OFF at inputs.py:478): 3 failed, all climate.
  - m5 (drop `water_heater` from the config_flow selector): `GOLDEN_MODE=strict python3 tests/golden.py --only config_flow` reads `1 of 1 GOLDEN SCENARIOS CHANGED` rc=1 (`ev/golden-config_flow-m5.log`); the head reads `ALL 1 GOLDEN SCENARIOS UNCHANGED` rc=0.
- Null control (own instrument, `tools/null_control.py`, at main and head, degC and degF, states heat_pump/off/eco):
  - At main: `range=(None, None) step=1.0 write52.3=False calls=[]`. This matches the body.
  - At head: degC gives `range=(30.0, 65.0) step=0.5`, and a write of 52.3 calls `water_heater.set_temperature {'temperature': 52.5}`. degF gives `range=(30.0, 65.0)`, and 52.3 °C is written as 126 °F.
  - `unavailable` reads None.
  - The operation-mode state is never parsed as a number: `setpoint_and_unit` gets None from `temperature_c(state)` and falls back to the `temperature` attribute. The only consumers of the slot are pump_arbiter (`read_setpoint`, `write_setpoint_c`, `setpoint_range_c`, `quantise_setpoint_c`) and setpoint_check (`setpoint_and_unit`, `quantise_setpoint_c`, `read_setpoint`). None reads `state.state` as a number.
- HA schema, pinned venv-ha HA 2026.10.4, read from source:
  - `water_heater.set_temperature` requires `temperature` (ATTR_TEMPERATURE) and takes `operation_mode` as optional. This matches the SETPOINT_SERVICES row.
  - The registered services are exactly turn_on, turn_off, set_away_mode, set_temperature and set_operation_mode. This matches the `_P6_IMPLEMENTS` row.
  - The capability attributes are `min_temp`, `max_temp` and `target_temp_step` (the step is emitted only when truthy, and the default step of 1.0 then applies). The target attribute is `temperature`. All are converted with `display_temp` to the instance unit, and the state is `current_operation`.

merges.title: R10-GRADE-DRIVERS: grade drivers
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-GRADE-DRIVERS: the heat-pump and Driving grades publish drivers in the house grade's interface, every score hover carries its metric in plain words and its current reasons, and the P9 grid starts each state from empty storage, with the ink collision that exposed fixed.

What changed:

- **Heat-pump grade** (`coordinator.machine_score`): publishes `machine_drivers`, one driver `cop_shortfall` whose points are the grade minus 100 (the pump matching its own COP history). Ungraded, it publishes `machine_evidence` instead (`coordinator.machine_evidence`): COP samples per 3 °C outdoor band against `COP_BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES`, fullest first, and the intervals a learner freeze refused (`MeasuredCop.frozen_refusals`, counted where `_fold_measured_cop` returns `COP_REFUSED_FROZEN`; in memory, since start, not persisted).
- **Driving grade** (new `driving_grade.py`): the day's saving against the flat replay splits exactly into `cheap_hours` (energy bought below the day's running mean, as it was bought) and `dear_hours` (the rest), each weighed against the day's own mean and scaled onto the clipped sample, so they sum to it. They fold with the grade's own EMA and persist beside it in the ledger store (`operation_drivers`, declared in `store.py`); a grade stored before they were kept reads as `earlier_days`, decaying with the EMA. The grade's own arithmetic is unchanged expression for expression.
- **One interface**: `compose_scores` publishes `envelope_drivers`, `machine_drivers` and `operation_drivers` the same way: `{code, points}`, points rounded to one decimal, summing to the grade minus that part's `SCORE_REFERENCE` (house 50, heat pump 100, Driving 0), empty with no grade; `reasons` stays the absent-grade channel.
- **Card**: `scoreDrivers` renders every part's drivers with a signed weight, and the part's own "typical" line when none moves a point; `machineEvidence` renders what an ungraded heat pump waits on; each breakdown row now has a hover (`scoreRowTitle`) carrying its grade or reason, its drivers or evidence, and its metric in plain words, the same line the headline hover gives. `score.part_machine` and `score.part_operation` now say what is measured, the unit, what high and low mean and what no grade means. Every new string has en and sv.
- **P9 grid** (`tests/card_browser.mjs`): `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` are cleared after each `page.goto`. That exposed the carried collision: `wood_lane` at 375 px stacked four value-axis labels into each other. `valueAxis` now labels a tick only a line (one font size) clear of the last label drawn, keeping every tick mark, as `timeAxis` already does for time labels.
- **Structure and architecture**: the Driving grade's booking, daily fold and drivers moved out of the coordinator class into `driving_grade.py` (a per-coordinator side table, the `price_tiles` pattern; only `held()` is handed the coordinator, and `tally` returns a new book that the coordinator rebinds). The structure budgets are re-recorded as an improvement; nothing was raised.

## Head

`a96762c018226119e8ae21d8377195a4a27f8b33` merges main `c679f4b` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`3f188f896081284798c86cbaecc3cd3f2405e26d` merges main `785c2b6` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`966c51a1e4f490852d512392698fb080dd2eec4f` merges main `8bf45e5` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`91822840c47600724d9ec14b95f8c80ccfc364ae` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

8035c6c17acffa096001ae4c3e92b7e2ab7342b4. Repair round 5 over the reviewed head d0423d4f296a9b990a33cc8ce0065df02fa85ce3: one commit (`tests/card_browser.mjs` only) and merges of origin/main at 0ae75bf3146566bffca4490464dcc8d6d45c29ab (the head of origin/main when I fetched it, 2026-11-05 11:3xZ) and of the stale `handoff-wip` history (`-s ours`, no tree change). The card, the backend and the claim files are untouched by this round: `git diff d0423d4f HEAD -- tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt` is empty. The added P9 states exist only in `card_browser.mjs`, which `card_drift.mjs` does not read, so no fixture value moves and nothing is claimed. `origin/main` had not moved when `prepr.sh` ran (rc=0, below).

Dismissed review finding (no destination file): rounded drivers do not always sum to the rounded grade (up to 0.1). Carry: dismissed: per-item rounding of an exact sum is the house grade's existing convention (`envelope_drivers` since #2816), invisible at the card's whole-point display.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant was applied to one production site in a copy of the tree at 7649fad's code (the Python mutants; the later side-table rename and retyped `published` move none of the three sites) or b713c02's (the card mutants), then the closure script was run. Main's merged delta touches none of the mutated lines. In each Python copy, the extra `and the path that proceeds still stamps a resolvable recorded_at (#363)` red is the copy's own artefact (fixer.md step 2), and appears in every copy.

- M1 `driving_grade.tally`: the cheap-side `_add(book, "kwh_lo", ...)` and `_add(book, "sek_lo", ...)` replaced by `pass`. `tests/features.py` turns red on `R10-GRADE-DRIVERS: the Driving grade's drivers split it exactly -- energy bought under the day's mean pushes it up, energy bought over pulls it down -- and keep summing to it through the EMA`.
- M2 `coordinator.machine_score`: returns `[]` instead of the `cop_shortfall` driver. `tests/features.py` turns red on `R10-GRADE-DRIVERS: a graded heat pump drops its evidence and carries one driver, its distance below its own COP history: none at 100, and a Cusum a quarter of the way to its alarm takes 25 points`.
- M3 `coordinator._fold_measured_cop`: `self._measured_cop.frozen_refusals += 1` deleted. `tests/features.py` turns red on `R10-GRADE-DRIVERS: the heat pump's evidence lists each band's samples, most first, and counts only the intervals a freeze refused`.
- C1 card `scoreDrivers`: the per-part typical line replaced by the house's `score.driver_typical`. `tests/card.mjs` turns red on `R10-GRADE-DRIVERS null control: all-zero Driving drivers show the metric and no reason rows, House unchanged`.

With the thinning, the same grid run is green and the dumped overlap list is empty.

Failing test first: the head's `tests/card.mjs` run against the base's card turns red on all 7 new `R10-GRADE-DRIVERS` checks and on `each row carries its plain-language explanation`, which now pins the new metric wording. The new `tests/features.py` block imports `SCORE_REFERENCE` and `driving_grade`, neither of which exists at the base.

Repair round 4 mutants:

- E1 card `machineEvidence`: the unrepaired text (ASCII hyphen, bare count) is the mutant: with the card at the previous head and the new `tests/card.mjs`, `2 CARD CHECK(S) FAILED`, on `an ungraded heat pump shows samples per outdoor band against the requirement, and freeze refusals` and `a negative evidence band uses the card's minus sign and its count carries a unit, in sv as well`. With the repair: `ALL CARD CHECKS PASSED`.
- B1 `tests/card_browser.mjs`: the mutant `.sb-row { overflow: hidden; max-height: 2.2em; }` added to the card's CSS turns `P9 grid: no text is clipped where its ancestor cannot scroll to it` red, naming the three `sb-drivers` lines (the House, Heat pump and Driving drivers) with 8.8, 51.8 and 8.8 px clipped. Null control: the unmutated head reads `ALL BROWSER CHECKS PASSED`. Two weaker mutants stayed green and are recorded as non-findings: a 263-character unbroken driver label (the card wraps it) and `.sb-drivers { overflow:hidden; white-space:nowrap; width:6em }` (the grid's clip check starts at the run element's parent, so a clip on the text's own element is outside its reach).

Repair round 5 (the P9 design trace), the same method as the verdict's: each added en/sv `score.*` STRINGS key in the three-dot card diff (11 added keys) plus the two rewritten metric texts (`score.part_machine`, `score.part_operation`) is a regex, placeholders as wildcards, matched against the rendered `.score-breakdown` text of every `score_open*` cell at 375 px (a scratch copy of `card_browser.mjs`, not in the tree, dumps it after the grid's measurement of each cell):

- At the head: all 13 labels match in en and sv-SE. Cells reached: `driver_earlier_days` and `driver_dear_hours` in `score_open`; `driver_typical_machine` and `driver_typical_operation` in the new `score_open_typical`; `evidence_empty` in the new `score_open_no_evidence`; `driver_cop_shortfall` in `score_open_graded_pump`; the rest in `score_open`.
- Null control, the same method on the previous head's `card_browser.mjs` (d0423d4f) against the same card: exactly 4 misses, in both languages: `driver_earlier_days`, `driver_typical_machine`, `driver_typical_operation`, `evidence_empty`. The other 9 match.
- Fixture changes: `earlier_days` in `score_open` has `points: 2.4` (was 0, which the renderer drops); `score_open_typical` is a graded pump (`machine_drivers: []`) and a graded Driving row whose only driver is `cheap_hours` at 0 points, so both read their "typical" line; `score_open_no_evidence` is an ungraded pump with `machine_evidence.bands: []`. I added two states, not three: one state reaches both graded-typical lines. 351 cells = 333 + 2 x 9.
- Mutant (P9 check red): the verdict's discriminating clip mutant (`.sb-row` with `overflow: hidden`, `.sb-text.sb-drivers` with `white-space: nowrap`) applied to the card with the unmodified `tests/card_browser.mjs`: `FAIL P9 grid: no text is clipped where its ancestor cannot scroll to it`, 351 cells, every entry a `div.sb-text.sb-drivers` line (en and sv). Null control: the unmutated head reads `ALL BROWSER CHECKS PASSED` at 351 cells. The verdict's other control (the mutant with the pre-round-4 fixture, 324 cells, green) is not reproducible on this tree: d0423d4f's fixture already carries the driver lines, and the mutant is red there too (333 cells, 17 `sb-drivers` entries), as the verdict itself reads at head. So the control that stands is the unmutated head.

## Null control

- `tests/features.py`: buying flat all day scores 0, and no Driving driver moves the grade a point (`R10-GRADE-DRIVERS null control`).
- `tests/card.mjs`: a payload whose Driving drivers are all zero renders the metric and the "bought at the day's flat mean price" line, with no reason row, and the House row's hover is byte-equal to the same payload without `operation_drivers`. Perturbation: flipping the sign of `dear_hours` flips its mark from − to + (`R10-GRADE-DRIVERS perturbation`).
- House grade unchanged (Carry 3's precondition, re-measured at the merge base and at the head): `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_scores_envelope.py` prints 40 `tree_grade=` rows and none off 50.0 at both ends; `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_house_grade.py` prints `owner_min=35.2`, `monotone=True` and `drivers_max_gap=0.0` at the head.

## Figures

- `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub bash tests/run.sh` at d113fe6 (the earlier head; the delta since is the merge of main, the bot's re-record, the pins and one check in `tests/features.py`, re-run directly below): `MODE: SCOPED -- 28 script(s) run, 5 scoped out.`, rc=0, with `tests/features.py` and `tests/card.mjs` among them; `env_drift.py --all origin/main` reads no unclaimed drift, and `card_drift.mjs origin/main` one moved state, claimed.

R10-RAISE-GATE-SHIM (issue 3128), repair round 4: the round-3 fix review blocked on `body-stale` (the body described code head `289fe24b`, not the deny-by-default shim). This body is retaken whole for the head below, and the three cheap findings the review measured are closed in the code.

## Head

`b1abbac61034cbdbec79c765db94ed3a132e5876` merges main `7d95405` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`81ee61752cff8ba51d41546f540e50ff1c950fac` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

Code head `88d809f841a1fadc7ccdb34badc142dc65ef522e` (`handoff/r10-raise-gate-shim`): the PR head `6b416a18fc8752eaa3c10404cec43f896df3ed60` plus three commits of this repair, merged with `725410a6b` (the round-3 seat's commit already on `handoff/r10-raise-gate-shim`: `queue_pre_flight.py`'s self-test answers the train's measured score, three added lines; kept so the handoff ref stays a fast-forward). `6b416a18` merges the authored code head `6027fe3e`, which carries `1d4ed28e4`. The merge base with origin/main is `8b49d50b0a4c3eebee0edeb6ec98aa365e3d004f` (`git merge-base origin/main HEAD` at `81ee61752`). The PR head `81ee61752` has first parent `4404f5e74`, a merge of `origin/main` at `8b49d50b0` (4 commits past `8bf45e5dc`, the base the round-3 and round-4 text named); the resolution delta of that merge (`git diff 88d809f84 81ee61752`) is main's own three files, `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, `tests/ci_budgets.json` and `dev/programme/delivery/3228.md`, none of them this PR's.

The shim under review is `1d4ed28e4`: `tools/audit/seat/shims/seat-gh` carries a deny-by-default `gate()` over `api_gate`, `issue_gate` and `pr_gate` (there is no `api_hits`). A call that could write a comment on the tracking issue (#201) is refused unless the caller is python running the tree's own `tools/pr/gh_comment.py` by real path, or the call is on gh's own explicit table of calls that cannot write one: reads, `issue view/list/status/create`, `issue comment/close/...` on one plain number other than 201, `pr` with no word reading 201, `api` reads, `api` writes at paths that are neither `issues/201/comments`, `issues/comments/<id>`, an unreadable path nor a graphql mutation, and the command groups with no issue-comment surface. Everything else (an unknown subcommand, an alias, an extension, an unknown flag) is refused.

This repair changes three things on top of `1d4ed28e4`:
1. `norm()` lower-cases the api path before matching, so `repos/o/r/ISSUES/201/COMMENTS` is the tracker's (review finding: the case gap).
2. The kill word is built from fragments at runtime in `gh_calls.py` (the `planted` argv and the `gh issue comment 201` refused row) and the id is the fixture id `fixture-mandate-0000`, replacing the fake numeric id.
3. `seat_venv.sh --self-test` has a row for the installer's `gcpy=` bake (review finding: the surviving installer mutant).

No budget file, claim file, `VERSION`, manifest version or `RELEASE_NOTES.md` is touched.

The brief's four carries and where each stands:
- Carry 1 (the mandate-revoke fixer's gaps): (a) a raw `gh api` or `gh issue comment` post to #201 is refused by the shim (`1d4ed28e4`, this PR); (b) merge_train and `--check-body` check the dS value (landed in round 1; mutants M2 to M4 of the review kill it); (c) is Carry 3.
- Carry 2 (the value check re-routed from #3045): built as (b) above and unchanged by this repair.
- Carry 3 (item 870f6b21, `(c)` measured, no change needed): the `budget-raise-gate / budget-raise-gate` job against its 5-minute timeout. The round-3 seat's measurement over 31 jobs (min 19 s, median 28 s, max 48 s) is carried as it stands; this repair adds two more runs read at `6b416a18` (jobs 127348404149 and 127322514552, 29 s and 25 s). The scorer's cost on a raise diff stays unmeasured (no raise diff runs it).
- Carry 4 (item aae60647, `exec -a` argv0 spoofing): the declared residual, under Forward-carry.

## Mutation proof

All counts are `python3 tools/audit/seat/gh_calls.py --self-test` at the head, `195 checks, 0 failed`.
- Predicate `[ -n "$ok" ] || {` changed to `true || {` in the shim (the refusal never fires): `gh_calls self-test: 195 checks, 67 failed`; restored, 0 failed. (The reviewer measured 190 checks, 65 failed at `6b416a18`; the difference is this repair's own rows.)

merges.body:
The owner's month row read nonsense on a valved house with a wood tank (tvofi, 2026-11-04): November's reference far below the meter, a percent clipped at -100. The settlement booked the thermostat's first step of a plan re-made every interval, and behind a valve that step read the stores' transient. This pull request books the reference with no wood on any house (owner ruling, 2026-11-04), holds its tank behind a valve at the temperature that delivers the need and spreads its horizon by the steady demand, unclips the month percent, floors the calibration at 1.0 on a wood-configured house, and stamps each month with the reference basis it was booked on, so a month booked against the retired reference keeps both columns and states no saving.

**The owner's September, October and November rows show a dash, and the first saving figure arrives with the next new month.** Totals are never rewritten.

Carry 1, the owner's no-wood ruling (2026-11-04): done. The reference has no wood tank, no fire and no refill coil on any house; wood-configured houses show a figure with the disclaimer that the saving includes wood's heat and firewood's cost is not counted, and old-basis rows keep the dash. Pinned by `the reference has no wood: a wood tank, cold or warm, reads the plain valved house's kW` and `the reference's hot water has no refill coil: a known wood tank moves nothing (owner ruling, 2026-11-04)`, both passing in this pass's `tests/features.py` run at ca0d33c12.

Carry 2, triage P387 (`dev/programme/triage/s6-batch122.md#P387`, metered kWh cancels in the calibrated percent): answered by the calibration floor. On a wood-configured house calibration may only raise the reference, so a meter under the plan is never scaled down (option A, relayed by the orchestrator under the mandate, pending the owner's override); with no wood the 2026-10-24 calibration stands as specified. Pinned by `with wood configured a meter under the plan earns its saving: the calibration does not cancel it`, passing in the same run.

## Findings

- The zero floor placed at the wrong spot survives `tests/features.py`. Mutant `floorlate`: `required_thermal = (_thermostat_demand(...))` with no floor in the loop, plus `return np.maximum(baseline_power, 0.0), state` at the return. It reads 2 of 4814 failed, the same two as the null control (`recorded_at` from the archive copy, and R9-F2.1 P3 below). Its numbers are wrong, though. On a plain 1-zone house on a swinging day the reference books 3.4584 kWh against the head's 0.3165 (ev/floor_probe-*.txt). On a warm day it books 0 kWh but simulates negative power, so the horizon ends at a room of 21.447 C against the head's 22.721 C, and that end state is what `_settle_horizon` settles. The pin `a thermostat on a warm plain house buys no heat and sells none: not one reference step is negative` reads only the output's sign. It needs a companion on the reference's end state, or its energy against the floored simulation. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-SAV-ESTIMATE
- R9-F2.1 P3 (`the half-price continuation buys a strictly better storage plan than the same solve without it`, tests/features.py:62706) is now host-dependent because of this diff. This host is Linux x86_64, Python 3.14.7, numpy 2.5.4 with scipy-openblas 0.3.34, and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 makes no difference. Here the base passes (j_plain 109.578998 against 109.589887, gain +0.010889) and so does origin/main 499162c89 (the same figures). The code head a9f8cb2b5 and the PR head both fail: 108.992821 against 108.992821, gain +0.000000. CI's `tests / fast (3.14)` passes it with j_plain 108.958453 against 108.992821, gain +0.034369. The new valved reference seeds the starts so that the continuation's basin is reached on one kernel class and not on another. The plan's objective improved at both ends (about 108.99 against 109.58), so this is a pin that lost its margin, not a worse plan. The body's `## Figures` host-reds list does not include it. Re-pin the continuation on a case where its gain is not a cliff for the new seeds, or record it as a may-drift with the owner. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-SAV-ESTIMATE
- `migrate_ledger_v1` stamps every month a v1 store holds as the old basis, including a month that has no `savings_baseline` yet. If that month books its first savings after the upgrade, `add_savings_settlement`'s `setdefault` keeps the old stamp, and the month shows a dash although it was booked entirely on the new reference. It fails safe, since it states no saving rather than a wrong one, and it only reaches a month that holds lines but no savings at upgrade time. Stamp only months holding `savings_baseline`. merges.body:
`bus.sh train_add` posted every merge verdict to `merge_train.py add` without reading the orchestrator's `cloud-handoff-hold` file, so a held PR (#3198, #3222 on 2026-11-05) was queued for the train anyway. `train_add` now asks `cloud_relay.sh held <pr>`, the relay's one reader of that file, and skips a PR it lists. Nothing is copied: the hold grammar stays in `hold_list`/`held`. A malformed hold file (rc 2) also skips the add, matching the relay's rule of never hold-none; `merge_train.py sweep` remains the backstop for a head the event add missed. No new file, seat or lane; claim files, VERSION and release notes are untouched.

## Head

`189fdb8893334dba36f5841ee62ddbb160e43659` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

58d7d839e7c900479b07fa5df22195de1b732f30 (one commit on origin/main 2dc960f4a92b1ebf56ed5aa33f55400d8e269a10). main had not moved since the `tools/pr/prepr.sh` run, so no second run was made.

## Mutation proof

The predicate line (`[ $rc = 1 ] || { printf 'BUS train-add ... held ...'; return 0; }`, marked `# mut:trainhold`) was replaced by `true`, then `bash tools/audit/seat/bus.sh --self-test` run. Red: `a PR listed in the hold file is not added to the train` and `a malformed hold file adds nothing (never hold-none)`; `bus self-test: 132 checks, 2 failed`. Restored; the same command reads `132 checks, 0 failed`.

R10-BODY-CONTRACT: the body contract at the head (V115), roster ref, review trailers, fold grammar, closed-destination refusal with its consumers, dismissal pointer, refused-body keep, carry control lint, and the orchestrator's pre-merge carry fold. Card 7 (generated figure block) is stopped on measured missing preconditions and stays a Forward-carry item.

## Head

`a2098902e0f212b70963295401b2d2b07fb28c86` merges main `d1cab99` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`ece7cbabb8bd012617692eaeb8ef585f13ee1f4e` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

Repair round 2 of #3227 after a blocking review at `a52354e6`.

Carry 11 to Carry 16 are the roster's carries of this group from the previous body (the Forward-carry items of that body); the new items under Forward-carry are the review findings this round did not fix.

## Mutation proof

Each arm was red first where it can be red on the unchanged code, and each has a mutant that turns it red:
- V115 tree revision: dropping `BRIEF_LINT_TREE_REV=$head` (the `# mut:contract` line) fails the `treerev` assertion in `body_patch.sh --self-test`.
- Roster ref: removing the argument (`# mut:rosterref`) fails the roster-ref arm.
- Trailers: deleting the new alternation fails `TRAILER reads 'Round: 3'` and `'bus-nonce: abc123'`.
- Dismissal pointer: forcing the pointer branch off fails `Carry: <done group> | dismissed: <reason> routes`.
- Closed destination: testing against `DONE_STAGES` instead of `roster_lib.CARRY_CLOSED`, or listing every live group, turns the closed-group arms red.
- Fold grammar: disabling the unanswered-fold test fails the "(a)-(d) answered, (e) named" arm.
- Keep ref: replacing the `# mut:keep` calls fails all four refusal arms.
- Repair 1 (bare array): the merged marker comment is above `policy_lint`; `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/bare_array.py --check` was red at `a52354e6` (names `body_patch.sh:146`, rc 1) and is rc 0 now. The pre-existing `bare_array.py` self-test already holds the mutant of the same shape (a comment between the marker and the line).
- Repair 2 (closing keywords): thirteen new arms in the carry_audit self-test, one per form (the nine keywords close/closes/closed, fix/fixes/fixed, resolve/resolves/resolved; the colon spelling; the issue-URL, owner/repo and GH- reference shapes), were ten red on the old two-keyword `CLOSES` before the regex change (failing test first). Mutants, each run: back to the two keywords (10 failed); dropping fix (5), resolve (4), closed (1), the URL shape (1), the owner/repo shape (1), the GH- shape (1).
- Pins for the review's surviving mutants, each run red against its mutant: `fold_rc = 0` in `check` (2 failed), dropping `| fold_rc` on the roster path (1) and on the empty path (1) through three end-to-end `check --body` arms; `dests.pr_group = pr_group_of(...)  # mut:branch` replaced by `pass` (1 failed, an end-to-end `check --branch` arm); `carry_fold.py` `if bad:` to `if False:` (1 failed, a body with one good and one done destination writes nothing); `treeListing(process.env.BRIEF_LINT_TREE_REV, cwd)` to `treeListing(undefined, cwd)` (`TREEREV VACUOUS`, through `trackedFiles(dir)` with the variable set and unset); stripping `<!--.*?-->` from `fold_problems` (1 failed).
- Carry 6 (`--branch`): making `pr_group_of` return None fails `branch fix/r10-pr resolves to the PR group R10-PR` and the `-pr` suffix arm (2 failed, run this pass).
- Carry 9 (control lint): changing `if (!names) {` to `if (false) {` makes `assertCarryControl` print `CONTROL VACUOUS` for both `the FUTURE-STATE section 2 figures` and the bare statistic (run this pass).
- Carry 8 A2 (`carry_fold.py`): replacing the post-fold `landed` call (`# mut:postfold`) with `[]` fails `an op that returned 0 but wrote nothing fails after the fold, naming the id` (1 failed, run this pass).

## Null control

- V115: a path the head deletes refuses with the revision set; the checkout listing differs from the head listing.
- Folds: all five answered is accepted; no `Fold (x):` line is accepted unchanged; `Fold (e): dismissed:` with no reason is refused.
- Dismissal: `Carry: <done group>` alone is still refused; an unknown token with `| dismissed:` is refused.
- Closed destination: a live after-edged group and a not-yet-started group are accepted as before; branch `fix/r10-nothing` resolves to no group (the refusal then says so).

- carry_fold: the same body folded twice writes nothing the second time; a done destination is refused before any write.

- Closing keywords: `Mentions #7`, `Fixing #7` and `unfixes #7` close nothing and owe no fold answer; `check --body` with the fold answered is accepted; `check` without `--branch` still prints `valid targets: unknown`.

## Figures

- `python3 -I tools/audit/carry_audit.py --self-test | tail -1` (carry_audit self-test; the count is its own line)
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/carry_fold.py --self-test | tail -1`

## Red checks

Read against the check runs of the PR head `a52354e6e441236ec0b63fa49fd303900c64f6cf`, the last head CI graded (the final head below has no run until it is pushed; CI is the authority for it). Merge base: `b707d89329c746c870d07e0b1725e644874078dc` (`git merge-base origin/main HEAD`). Every concluded red, all pages:

- `governance / instrument-self-tests` (job 127227661299), step 27 `Refuse a bare array expansion in a set -u script`: this diff. `body_patch.sh:146` carried a comment between the `# never-empty:` marker and the `policy_lint` line, which `bare_array.py` does not accept. - `pr-contract / pr-contract` (jobs 127240182833, 127241211745, 127242351411), step 10 `Check the body against the contract`: this body, which said `none` and answered neither red above. Answered here.
- `gate` (jobs 127240629116, 127241637011, 127242766124): the aggregate of the two required reds above; it follows them.
- `governance / delivery-status` (job 127227661367): inherited. It grades main's ledger, red on the base ancestry (merge base `b707d89329c746c870d07e0b1725e644874078dc`): overdue delivery rows of other merged PRs, not this diff's. This diff touches `.github/workflows/governance.yml` for self-test steps only.
- `tests / nightly-status` (job 127227661278): inherited. It reads last night's run of main (merge base `b707d89329c746c870d07e0b1725e644874078dc`): the nightly slow-job replay cost-band failure, carried by R10-REPLAY-COST-BUDGET. This diff does not touch that lane.

Root cause of the two own reds (`defect-root-cause.md`, red-check trigger): the last edit to `body_patch.sh` (the inserted comment line) was made after the prepr run that the previous body cited, and `tools/pr/prepr.sh` did not run `bare_array.py --check` at all. The cheaper detector was `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/bare_array.py --check` (seconds). Countermeasure built: `privacy_line` in `prepr.sh`, step 3f7, now runs it first (one added command in an existing step) and refuses with its last line.

## Forward-carry

Not built here; each is stated once, and the dispatch seat lands them in the roster:
- Card 7, every body figure from a generated block: the carry's own preconditions are missing, measured above. No workflow edits a body on synchronize; `features_block.py` renders no figure block (it runs test blocks); `figure_lint.mjs` refuses by design to execute body commands, so a renderer would need an owner ruling on running PR-authored commands in `pr-contract`, and a new block format and marker. The carry also touches the PR template and `checkPrBody` (owner review at merge). Carry: R10-BODY-CONTRACT (Carry 11)

The set is closed and shrinks as those carries are re-measured. Carry: R10-BODY-CONTRACT (Carry 15)
- Issue-side fold spellings: `FOLD_LINE` reads `Fold (x):` with a lowercase letter and the colon straight after the parenthesis, so an owner's `**Fold (a)**:` or `Fold (A):` gets no fold read; the live spelling could not be confirmed. Carry: R10-BODY-CONTRACT

- The `Round:\s*\d` trailer reads any item line opening `Round: <digit>`, so a finding written that way is read as a trailer; the null control covers only `Round:` with no number. Carry: R10-BODY-CONTRACT
- Dropping `--branch "$HEAD_REF"` from `pr-contract.yml` is unpinned: nothing tests the workflow text, and the effect is only the refusal printing `valid targets: unknown`. Carry: R10-BODY-CONTRACT
- Policy files drafted here, merging on the owner's approval: the one sentence in `dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md` and `judge.md` (#2438 (ii)), and the template and contract are untouched. Carry: dismissed: nothing owed beyond the owner's review at merge

## Approval

Not yet given. This diff touches two policy files; the owner's approving GitHub review at merge is the approval, and it waits for that review. The three-dot diff changes three places in `dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md` and five in `dev/governance/roles/judge.md` (#2438 (ii)); each, old to new:

## Block

- The head is RED, and this diff causes it. `merge_train.py classify` exits 1 (`RED a52354e6... pending: none red: gate`). Two required checks fail on one defect the diff introduced:
  - `governance / instrument-self-tests` (job 127227661299), step 27, "Refuse a bare array expansion in a set -u script". Reproduced locally: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/bare_array.py --check` names `tools/audit/seat/body_patch.sh:146: BRIEF_LINT_TREE_REV=$head node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs "${args[@]}" || rc=1 # mut:contract` and exits 1 at the head. It exits 0 at the base.
  - `tests / fast (3.14)` (job 127227966145), "1 TEST SCRIPT(S) FAILED". Reproduced locally with `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`, which reports `1 of 2631 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`. The one top-level FAIL is `no tracked tools/**/*.sh script expands a bare "${array[@]}"`, naming the same `body_patch.sh:146`.
  - Cause: at the base, the `# never-empty: args starts with the literal --pr-body list` marker sat directly above the `policy_lint` line (`ev/body_patch-base-117-121.txt`). The diff inserted `# the body cites paths of the head under review, not of this checkout` between the marker and the line (`ev/body_patch-head-143-147.txt`). The exemption is lost because `bare_array.py` accepts the marker only on the line itself, or on the comment line directly above a line ending in `# mut:<name>`. Repair: move the new comment above the `# never-empty:` line, or merge the two comments.
  - `pr-contract / pr-contract` (job 127242351411) is red at step 10, "Check the body against the contract", in its run at 12:23, after both reds concluded. The body's `## Red checks` says `none` and answers only `delivery-status` and `nightly-status`, so these two reds are unanswered.
  - Cheaper detector: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/bare_array.py --check` takes seconds and shows the red before the handoff. The body states that `prepr.sh` ran clean on this head, which does not square with that check. Either prepr does not run `bare_array.py --check`, or the last edit to `body_patch.sh` came after the prepr run. The re-cut should say which, under `defect-root-cause.md`'s red-check trigger. This is `root-cause-detectable: governance / instrument-self-tests` if the body is not amended.
- Second blocking point, found by the brief's spelling attack. The new fold refusal can be bypassed through a closing keyword other than `Closes`. `CLOSES = re.compile(r"\bcloses?\s*:?\s+#(\d+)", re.I)` reads only `close`/`closes`. GitHub closes an issue on `Fixes #N`, `Fixed`, `Resolves`, `Resolved` and `Closed` too.
