merges.body:
Part 1 of R10-SUITE-HOST-DETERMINISM (issues #2726, #2730): the suite's host-zone, gate-lease-timing and coverage-descendant nondeterminism. This round closes the host-zone class across every script `tests/run.sh` invokes, not only `tests/features.py` and `tests/finite_boundary.py`. The parts named under Forward-carry are not built here.

## Re-cut note

This is the final body-only round for verdict/3170 (round 4, blocked at 5ee2be2d). The orchestrator ruled, under the owner mandate, that the host-zone class is closed and the PR merges as is; no production or test file changed in this round, only origin/main was merged in. Earlier: round 3's answer to verdict/3170 (round 2, blocked at 0a459e60). The finding was: "class-open: tests/finite_boundary.py still fails host-zone checks at the head under America/New_York (1 of 108) and Asia/Kolkata (2 of 108), and passes under UTC". The body is retaken whole from the template headings, and round history is deleted. Every figure below was re-taken in this pass.

The class is a suite check whose result moves with the host zone (`TZ`) or Home Assistant's configured zone (`HASTUB_TZ`), when it should not. The rule that enumerates the class is `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/host_zone_features.py --suite`. It runs every script `tests/run.sh` invokes (its `run` and `run_always` lines, 38 commands) under seven rows:
- `gate`: `TZ=UTC`, `HASTUB_TZ` unset. This is the null row.
- UTC.
- America/New_York, Asia/Tokyo, Europe/Stockholm and Asia/Kolkata (half-hour).
- Europe/London, a DST zone whose 2026 transitions fall on the EU dates the suite's own instants read (2026-03-29, 2026-10-25). Its winter offset is zero, so a leak there shows only across a transition.

Each zone row sets `TZ` and `HASTUB_TZ` together. Every red row is a seam. The seams the sweep returned at the round-3 tip and at the merge base are below, each with its disposition.

What this round changes on top of the round-3 commits (the finite_boundary instant arm, card.mjs's seam clock, guard_pins' idle-cooling clock):
- **`tests/ha_contract.py`**: four default-case `util.dt` contracts asserted `HASTUB_TZ` unset. So the script read `4 of 96 contracts FAILED` under every configured zone, UTC included. Each contract now evaluates in the zone that a fresh copy of the provider's own `util/dt` module sets with `HASTUB_TZ` absent (`_unconfigured_zone`, `_in_default_case`). The default case is constructed rather than read off the host. The nightly lane copies upstream's module in the same way.
- **`tests/golden.py`**: the `coord_*` payloads move with Home Assistant's configured zone, as a time-of-use grid fee's peak hours and the energy totals' local day rightly do. Under America/New_York, 5 of 56 golden payloads differed from the gate capture (`coord_grid_fee`'s forecast prices took the peak fee five hours early). The configured zone is an input of the installation the scenario describes, so `capture_coordinator` now sets `DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE` to `SCENARIO_ZONE` (UTC, the zone the fixtures were recorded in) at the capture boundary, and restores it after. In that zone the naive `START` freeze is the instant it names, so round 3's aware-freeze workaround is dropped, and one mechanism covers both leaks.
- **`dev/audit/harnesses/host_zone_features.py`**:
  - `--golden-zones` compares every golden payload (`env_drift.py --all`'s 56) per zone with the gate row. golden.py's own drift check compares against a baseline captured in the same zone, so it cannot see a payload that moves with the zone on both sides.
  - Mutants: `golden_scenario_zone` and `ha_contract_default_zone` replace the retired `golden_clock`.
  - A further commit on this topic (3181c947, the faketime `Zone@<wall time>` option) adds an opt-in sweep mode. Nothing below uses it.
- **`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`** (commit 9f5a45ba): a slow-job step runs `tests/features.py` and `tests/finite_boundary.py` under `HASTUB_TZ=TZ=Asia/Kolkata`. This is the cheap one-zone lane that the verdict's second finding asked for, so a reintroduced UTC-literal instant reads red nightly.

No `TZ` or `HASTUB_TZ` is pinned in the suite, the runner or the environment. The only assignments are the harness's own subprocess environment and the nightly step above, which sets a non-UTC zone on purpose. No allowlist entry is added, and `tests/harness_headers.py` is untouched.

Disclosure: a second fixer session ran this topic beside this one. Its commits 9f5a45ba (nightly lane) and 3181c947 (faketime option) and its main merges b68368e2, e581b01c and ab57cc05 are in this head as fast-forwards. No work of either session is dropped.

Carries, each named as built, discharged or next part:

- Carry 1 and Carry 4 (0-based 0, 3; features under a non-UTC zone): BUILT. The class is now the whole suite under every zone the sweep runs (Figures), not only `tests/features.py`.
- Carry 2 (0-based 1; gate-lease one-winner flake): the test-side change is BUILT (a condition wait replaces the 0.15 s hold). The `_free_slot` is_file TOCTOU in `tests/gate_lock.py` is not built here; it is carried to R10-GATE-LEASE-TOCTOU (Forward-carry).
- Carry 3 (0-based 2; coverage_tree.sh descendants): BUILT. `measure()` waits for processes still carrying the script's own `COVERAGE_PROCESS_START` rcfile path, and refuses, naming the script, after `W5P_DESCENDANT_WAIT`.
- Carry 5 (0-based 4; base-red entities U0c / delivery_status): NEXT PART.
- Carry 6 (0-based 5; scan("HEAD") vs working tree): NEXT PART.
- Carry 7 and Carry 8 (0-based 6, 7; stdlib sampler macOS platform rule, six wrappers): NEXT PART.
- Carry 9 (0-based 8; nightly respawn): NEXT PART.

The open parts above are this group's own carries, already in its brief. The one finding carried to another group is the gate-lease TOCTOU (Forward-carry). The verdict's second finding (no CI lane runs a non-UTC zone) is built here as the nightly Kolkata step.

## Head

`b1e18bf3ee9ee67cf5f45e05b6f87a2f951efe80` merges main `b707d89` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`10805aa975d9c6ba62f9fe669f8d288c431a6468` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`0cac0fe21b10e28d0a6e99aafd7af0ac84625c09` is the final head. It merges origin/main `cd0dd16910898553bb85a95bf718840b131b1a82` into the PR head `5ee2be2db0abefd7988a4465b4f431334925895e` (which merges `04dc60576c344f702b11084d43e9a653d2fe198c`). The merge was clean and touched no suite script, so no figure below moved. The merge brings in `dev/governance/config/machinery_budgets.json` (#3208), which the earlier head lacked. The claim files, `VERSION`, the manifest and `RELEASE_NOTES.md` are byte-identical to origin/main, and the three-dot diff holds no `*_budgets.json`. `tools/pr/prepr.sh` was run once on this head: `PRE-PR: 0cac0fe21b10e28d0a6e99aafd7af0ac84625c09 ... rc=0` (its `closures` step printed its own skip, `diff mutants` skipped, `body` skipped for no body passed; `ci predict` read no predicted red against cd0dd1691089). origin/main had not moved since that merge.

Where each figure was taken:
- **The full sweep, the mutants, the golden null and the scratch-baseline drift**: at `e581b01c5371bfc0324e65fd6d6b2cc55f29930d`, whose main parent is `c0b082bc48777199cb9b4998514b20b88ec805a1`.
- **The before sweep**: at `1a148834384e3f81bbaed41809853a06ac902bda`, the round-3 tip.
- **Merge-base controls**: at `d7582ed404a87603bd02fefda610d7ebbe4181e1`.

The branch's own delta from e581b01c to the head is the faketime option in the harness (3181c947, opt-in, unused by the default sweep). The rest is origin/main's. So the PR's touched scripts and the golden null were re-run at the head (Figures).

## Mutation proof

Run by `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/host_zone_features.py --mutant all --zones UTC,America/New_York,Asia/Tokyo,Europe/Stockholm,Asia/Kolkata,Europe/London` at e581b01c. Each mutant is a detached worktree with one fixed site restored to its host-zone read, and it is KILLED when at least one zone reads red. All nine were KILLED, and the command exited 0. Every mutant passes in its UTC row.

- `finite_boundary_leaf_zone` (naive leaves read as UTC): New_York 2 of 108 ("an honest payload comes back byte-identical (null control)", "an instant inside its store's lead survives the load"). Tokyo, Stockholm, Kolkata and London 1 of 108 each ("no stored instant reaches a loader beyond the clock plus its store's lead"). UTC all 108 passed. **KILLED.**
- `golden_scenario_zone` (the capture inherits `HASTUB_TZ` again): `--golden-zones` reads `fail:5/56 coord_all_features,coord_dhw,coord_grid_fee,coord_minimal,coord_two_zone` under New_York, Tokyo, Stockholm and Kolkata. UTC and London (winter instant, offset 0) read 56 equal. **KILLED.**
- `ha_contract_default_zone` (`_dt_default_zone` reads its precondition off the environment again): 1 of 96 contracts failed in every row that sets `HASTUB_TZ`, UTC included. Control: the same mutant in the `gate` row (`--zones gate`) reads `ALL 96`, and the harness prints `SURVIVED`. So the mutant is red only where a zone is configured. **KILLED.**
- `card_seam_clock`: New_York and Tokyo 1 card check failed. **KILLED.**
- `guard_idle_cooling`: Tokyo, Stockholm and Kolkata 1 of 61 failed. **KILLED.**
- `nometer_month`: New_York, Tokyo and Kolkata 1 of 4784 failed. **KILLED.**
- `sysid_night_t0`: Tokyo and Kolkata 1 of 4784 failed. **KILLED.**
- `outage_naive_tick`: New_York 1 of 4784 failed. **KILLED.**
- `humidity_now`: New_York, Tokyo and Kolkata 1 of 4784 failed. **KILLED.**

## Null control

- **The unmutated suite at e581b01c**: `--suite` reads the per-zone counts in Figures. Every script passes in the gate, UTC and London rows. In the four offset zones every script passes except `golden.py` and `env_drift.py --all origin/main`.
- **Those two reds are origin/main's capture, not this tree's.** Both compare this tree's capture with a baseline captured from origin/main's own `tests/golden.py` in the same zone, and origin/main still lets the coordinator scenarios inherit `HASTUB_TZ`. Against a local scratch baseline, `8814fa88dfdb` (c0b082bc with only this diff's `tests/golden.py`, never pushed), `HASTUB_TZ=TZ=<zone> PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub GOLDEN_MODE=drift python3 tests/env_drift.py --all 8814fa88dfdb` read `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 56 scenario(s)` and `NO STALE FIXTURE` under New_York, Tokyo, Stockholm and Kolkata, rc=0 each.
- **Zone invariance itself**: `--golden-zones` at e581b01c reads `pass:56 payloads equal to gate` in all six zones. At the merge base d7582ed4 the same comparison read `fail:5/56` (the five `coord_*` payloads) under New_York, Tokyo, Stockholm and Kolkata. So once this merges, origin/main's baseline carries the fix and those two rows go green.

## Unpinned sites

none: the diff adds no production line. The only `custom_components/` change is the `_comparable_ts` docstring in `coordinator.py`; its AST is identical at base and head with docstrings blanked (verdict/3170 evidence/coordinator_ast.txt). `prepr.sh` step 6d is re-read at the head.

## Figures

Class rule: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/host_zone_features.py --suite` (every `tests/run.sh` `run`/`run_always` command, under the seven rows above, both `TZ` and `HASTUB_TZ` set per zone). Its `RESULT zone.<zone>=<passed>/<total>` lines:

| row | before, 1a148834 | after, e581b01c |
|---|---|---|
| gate | 38/38 | 38/38 |
| UTC | 37/38 | 38/38 |
| America/New_York | 35/38 | 36/38 |
| Asia/Tokyo | 35/38 | 36/38 |
| Europe/Stockholm | 35/38 | 36/38 |
| Asia/Kolkata | 35/38 | 36/38 |
| Europe/London (DST) | 37/38 | 38/38 |

Every seam the rule returned, with its disposition:
- `tests/ha_contract.py`, red in every configured row before, 4 of 96 each: **closed in this diff** (`_unconfigured_zone`). Green in every row after.
- `tests/golden.py` and `tests/env_drift.py --all origin/main`, red in the four offset rows before and after: **closed in this diff** for this tree (`SCENARIO_ZONE`; `--golden-zones` 56 equal in every zone). The residual red is origin/main's baseline capture (Null control: NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT against the scratch baseline in all four zones). It clears when this merges.
- `tests/finite_boundary.py`: green in every row at 1a148834 and e581b01c. At the merge base d7582ed4, `HASTUB_TZ=TZ=<zone> PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/finite_boundary.py` read UTC `ALL 108`, New_York `1 of 108`, Tokyo `2 of 108`, Stockholm `2 of 108`, Kolkata `2 of 108` and London `1 of 108`: **closed in this diff** (round 3's instant arm, the verdict's block).
- `tests/features.py`, `tests/card.mjs` and `tests/guard_pins.py`: green in every row: **closed in this diff** (rounds 1-3, each pinned by its mutant above).
- No other script was red in any row.

Other figures:
- `HASTUB_TZ=TZ=<zone> PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/ha_contract.py` at d7582ed4: `4 of 96 contracts FAILED` in each of UTC, New_York, Tokyo, Stockholm, Kolkata and London.
- `--golden-zones` at the base (the harness's `golden_zones` driven on a d7582ed4 worktree): UTC and London 56 equal; the four offset zones `fail:5/56`.
- At the head dc32ec6f, `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/host_zone_features.py --script <s> --zones gate,UTC,America/New_York,Asia/Tokyo,Europe/Stockholm,Asia/Kolkata,Europe/London` for `tests/finite_boundary.py`, `tests/ha_contract.py`, `tests/guard_pins.py`, `tests/card.mjs` and `tests/features.py`, and `--golden-zones`: every script passed in every row (finite_boundary `ALL 108`, ha_contract `ALL 96 contracts`, guard_pins `ALL 61`, card `ALL CARD CHECKS PASSED`, features `pass:4800` per zone and `pass:4807` in the gate row, which also runs the checks that need `HASTUB_TZ` unset). Golden read `pass:56 payloads equal to gate` in all six zones. Each exited 0.
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`: `MODE: FULL -- every test script runs, nothing is scoped out` (the diff touches `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`). The full gate's script set is the sweep's `gate` row, 38/38 at e581b01c.
- `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh` with this body, on the committed head dc32ec6f: `PRE-PR: dc32ec6feb503e4236d8fd351ee7298f8176bcfa ... rc=0` (its `closures` step printed its own skip, "the diff cannot be scoped, so CI re-records every closure"; `carry` read `0 bad destination(s)`). origin/main then moved to 6125b263, so it was merged and `prepr.sh` re-run on cb323c1f: `PRE-PR: cb323c1f8635ec5cd94e80ddfdf3c0ae5adea741 ... rc=0`. origin/main then moved to 6777ec33 (it changes `tools/pr/ci_predict.py`, a prepr step), so it was merged and `prepr.sh` re-run on 04dc6057: `PRE-PR: 04dc60576c344f702b11084d43e9a653d2fe198c ... rc=0`, with the same `closures` self-skip and `carry` `0 bad destination(s)`.

## Red checks

The check runs of the previous head 5ee2be2d, all 69 over both pages, hold nine non-green runs: `gate` x3, `pr-contract / pr-contract` x3, `governance / delivery-status`, `tests / nightly-status` and `governance / policy-docs`. `gate` and `pr-contract / pr-contract` are the graders: `pr-contract` refuses while the three named reds below stand, and `gate` reads red on the same set. The merged head 10805aa9 now has CI: its reds are the four below, read across all 41 check runs of one page, and each answer is re-derived at the merged tree and at main.

- `governance / policy-docs` (127109349298): `machinery_ratchet: dev/governance/config/machinery_budgets.json is absent` (exit 2). **Inherited, cured by the merge.** The file is absent at the merge base 6777ec33 and at 5ee2be2d (a head cut before #3208), and present on origin/main cd0dd169. The diff does not touch that check's closure (no `dev/governance/config/`, no `tools/audit/machinery_ratchet.py`). On the merged tree the file exists, and `prepr.sh` reads the `machinery ratchet` step `ok` (`nonproduction_merges 515 <= 521 + band 5`).
- `governance / delivery-status` (127109349630): `DELIVERY STATUS OVERDUE — 10 rowed, 10 pending, 10 overdue`. The diff touches `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`, which that check reads, so I re-ran `python3 tests/delivery_status.py` on the merged tree: `DELIVERY STATUS OVERDUE — 10 rowed, 11 pending, 12 overdue (overdue at 12 commits)`. **The overdue flags fall on other merges' rows, not on this PR.** Every overdue line is an already-merged PR rowless in the ledger (#3181, #3191, #3201, #3206, #3189, #3204, #3203, #3202, #3174, #3091, #3089, #3192); #3170 is open and is not listed at all. The count grows with each main commit, not with this diff. The tool prints that this check is not a required context. Inherited from main's ledger; this PR's row is `dev/programme/delivery/3170.md`, open.
- `tests / nightly-status` (127109349506): `NIGHTLY FAILED: slow failed last night`. **Not this PR's own.** The failing night is scheduled Nightly run 41943946464 (run_number 547, event schedule, 2026-11-05 00:47 UTC), at main commit `499162c89d0f4f8369e16e6e41fb3a620bc1ecb0`. Its `slow` job (126971378040) failed at step 8, "Replay recorded days through the real coordinator"; the steps before it (the golden drift report, the closed-loop simulation) succeeded. The step this PR adds is named "Zone-sensitive scripts under Asia/Kolkata", added by commit `9f5a45ba7d3c337aa3c794f1368fa58f776f6383`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 9f5a45ba7d3c337aa3c794f1368fa58f776f6383 499162c89d0f4f8369e16e6e41fb3a620bc1ecb0` returns 1, and `git grep "Zone-sensitive scripts" 499162c8 -- .github` finds nothing, so the failing run executed without this PR's step. 499162c8 is an ancestor of origin/main (`--is-ancestor` returns 0). The preceding scheduled nights, runs 41749544997 (c3a279e3) and 41555367389 (b8e82369), also concluded failure, so the red predates this PR's branch. This diff writes no runtime code and its nightly step runs after, and independently of, the replay step. I did not read the replay step's log text to name its cause. I read the failing step's name from the job's step list, not from its log text.
- `tests / replay` (job 127191893386, run 42011494510, concluded failure 10:41:12Z) at this head 10805aa9: `4 of 194 replay checks FAILED`, all four `cycle_cost` arms on `synthetic-dhw-only.json`, each `runner class unknown: ref_ms 21.58 to 22.10 lies in no band of COST_RUNNER_CLASSES [(22.64, 25.53), (28.72, 32.69), (42.99, 49.51), (49.6, 56.78)]; no budget is assumed` (the memory-doubled arm reads ref_ms 21.91). **Inherited; not this PR's.** The runner measured a reference time below the lowest band (22.64), so `cycle_cost` assumes no budget and refuses. It is the same cause as main's scheduled nightly `slow` job 126971378040 (run 41943946464, main commit 499162c8, ref_ms 40.1, also in no band). The diff touches no replay or cost code: the only workflow it changes is `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` and it changes no `tests/replay*`, no cost-band table and no coordinator code, so the diff does not touch that check's closure. The earlier head 0a459e60's replay red (job 125268597357, `cpu_ratio 2.385 over its budget 2.173`) was a different arm of the same runner-class cost lane. The cost bands are carried under Forward-carry below.

Cheaper detector: for policy-docs, `ci predict` reads no predicted red once main is merged (it reads against the base); for delivery-status and nightly-status, none: they read main's ledger and last night's run.

## Forward-carry

- The gate-lease `_free_slot` `is_file` time-of-check/time-of-use race in `tests/gate_lock.py`, unchanged by this PR. With a delay-only plant (a 30 ms sleep after `_read_at` returns None for a slot path, no logic changed), `one_winner` reads red 8 of 10 (the verdict's delay-only plant and its run log, on the `verdict/3170` ref). This PR's test-side condition wait makes the check see the overlap more reliably; it does not remove the production race. It is carried to group R10-GATE-LEASE-TOCTOU, roster commit `7f6468d1ce071e988cdb1a401da183e4e2035bc9` on `handoff/audit-r10-roster` (`dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json`, line 16813, `"group": "R10-GATE-LEASE-TOCTOU"`, confirmed by `git show 7f6468d1...:dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json | grep R10-GATE-LEASE-TOCTOU`), with that delay-only plant as its precondition control. Carry: R10-GATE-LEASE-TOCTOU
- The replay lane's `COST_RUNNER_CLASSES` bands miss the runners CI assigns (ref_ms 21.58 to 22.10 on this head's replay, 40.1 on main's 2026-11-05 nightly), so `cycle_cost` refuses with no budget on main and on any head, whatever the diff. This PR neither causes nor fixes it. Carry: R10-REPLAY-COST-BUDGET

Fix review: blocked b307f3599921ff345f677f34583958fa930a935a class-open: features.py still fails 3 zone checks at the head under America/New_York and Asia/Tokyo; only Europe/Stockholm was measured

bus-nonce: 63a83911d29f177af308c181cff4727f

## Head

b307f3599921ff345f677f34583958fa930a935a, the head named in the dispatch and in the PR body; `git ls-remote` re-read it unchanged at the end of the review. Round 1, full review. Merge base dfb4ce2b52fafb340e0320bc2efb870099a53884. `git diff <mb>...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty, so the contract is current.

## Block

1. **class-open (carries 0 and 3, 0-based).** The group brief's class is "the features checks that fail under a non-UTC `HASTUB_TZ`". 1. roster-drain ran a half-written queue line. It now runs only newline-terminated lines; an unterminated tail waits for its newline and then runs once, whole.
2. The done-marker lost a re-queued op after the queue was cleared. The queue is now stated append-only: roster-drain remembers how many terminated lines it has drained (`roster-queue-lines.json`) and, on a queue with fewer, reports `roster: QUEUE-SHRANK ...`, runs nothing and stays refused (`roster-shrank.json`) until the operator deletes the four roster memories, which the line names.
3. The nine surviving reviewer mutants each have a planted case, and an argv assertion where the arm is wiring (tick-digest provenance line, owed-check `--tick`/`--acks`/`--state`, roster-drain no-op-attempted retried, plan-beat rc 2 REFUSED and replan `--out/--slots/--seats`, pulse rc outside 0-2 UNREADABLE and `--seat-alive`, cancel-sweep rc != 0 and `--repo`, opener rc != 0 and `--board`).

Both Follow-ups were free in the same lines and are taken: head-watch's HEAD-MOVED dedupes only against that PR's last move (A->B->A->B is three events; STUCK lines keep the whole-file dedupe), and tick-digest forgets its remembered pass on UNREADABLE, so the same board returning clears the line.

What lands overall:
- `tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py`, the one owner of the beat's job predicates and the only writer of `$HPO_STATE_DIR/digest/`. Nine rows: tick-digest, owed-check, roster-drain, plan-beat, pulse, cancel-sweep, disk, opener, head-watch. Each writes only actionable lines to `digest/jobs/<row>`; `fold()` under `flock digest/.lock` builds `digest.txt`, `new.txt`, `gone.txt` and touches `new.stamp` only on a new line. A null pass changes no byte. head-watch and the opener's STUCK lines go to `digest/events.txt`; `events.tsv` stays ledger.py's.
- `tools/audit/seat/beatd.jobs.json`, beatd's default table, one row per job.
- `tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs_selftest.py` (cases and mutants), `tools/audit/seat/fixtures/beat_jobs/`, `instruments/beat_jobs.py.md` and its `INSTRUMENTS.md` row, the governance workflow step that runs the self-test.

Design choices, stated:
- Session paths come from the sweep overlay; a row whose key the overlay lacks writes `<row>: UNREADABLE overlay lacks <key>`, never nothing.
- roster-drain marks done in its own memory (`digest/state/roster-done.json`, keyed by occurrence and exact text) rather than rewriting the orchestrator's unlocked queue. Alternative considered for item 2: key on something that survives truncation (lost: no such key exists in an append-only line list, and silently re-running a cleared queue could apply an op twice); refusing a shrink visibly was taken. The refusal is sticky because a re-queued op appended past the old length would otherwise run while its predecessors are skipped.
- The pulse row writes pulse.py's stdout to `S/beatd/pulse.txt` (pulse.py has no `--out`), the one write outside `digest/`.

Opener STUCK arm: the opener row's STUCK arm has no producer at this head; `open_driver.py` prints no `STUCK ` line, and the design lands STUCK as an `open_driver.py` edit owned by R10-HANDOFF-PATH. The arm is forward-wired as designed; the stage that lands STUCK must keep the `STUCK ` prefix the OPENER regex reads.

comments.body:
Fix review: blocked fe2077441519c34d8000e5107e71b351807cb586 defect: roster-drain applies an unterminated queue line read mid-append, and nine own mutants on the rows' failure and argument arms survive the self-test

bus-nonce: 6dfac2bc6ae554806c2c3ab3040455d8

## Block

Round 1 of the fix review of #3197 (R10-FLY-STANDING-CONTRACTS P1), measured at head fe2077441519c34d8000e5107e71b351807cb586 (unmoved at the time of writing: `refs/pull/3197/head` and the branch both resolve to it).

1. **roster-drain runs a half-written queue line (the append race the brief asked about).** `roster_drain` reads `S/roster-drain.queue` with `read(...).split("\n")` and treats the last, unterminated segment as a complete op. The orchestrator appends to that file without a lock, so a pass that lands mid-append runs the truncated op through `roster_queue.py run`, then marks it done under its own text. When the append finishes, the full line has a different key and runs as well. Reproduced in `ev/probes.py` (P1). The queue holds `append-carry G2 note text that is lo` with no newline, then `append-carry G2 note text that is long\n`. The ops run are `['append-carry G2 note text that is lo', 'append-carry G2 note text that is long']`. A truncated carry or note text can pass the roster lint, so the roster would be written twice, once wrongly. The fix is a one-line repair plus a case: ignore a final segment that has no trailing `\n`, and add a self-test case and a mutant for it.
2. **The done-marker loses an op after the queue is cleared.** Done keys are `<occurrence>\t<text>`. When the orchestrator truncates or rotates the queue and later queues the same op again, the new op is occurrence 1 again. It is already in `roster-done.json`, so it is skipped silently and no digest line appears. Reproduced in `ev/probes.py` (P2): `set-stage G1 done` runs, the queue is emptied, `set-stage G1 done` is queued again, and the runs are `['set-stage G1 done']`, one run. Either state a contract that the queue is append-only and never cleared, and refuse a shrink (for example, store the drained byte offset or line count and report `roster: QUEUE-SHRANK`), or key on something that survives a rotation.
3. **Nine of my own mutants survive the self-test.** I planted one or more per row (`ev/own_mutants.py`, output in `ev/own_mutants.txt`). All 16 claimed mutants are killed. These nine survive. Most sit on the "never nothing / UNREADABLE is never clean" arms that are the design's point:
   - tick-digest: a board present but missing its provenance line passes as readable (`if not PROVENANCE.match(first)` changed to `if not text`). Only the absent-board case is tested.
   - owed-check: `--tick` pointed at the state dir instead of the board. The Fake ignores argv, so the argument wiring is untested.
   - roster-drain: an op that roster_queue reports as `no op attempted` (lint clone not provisioned, roster_queue.py:115) is marked done instead of retried (`if True:`). The body depends on this retry ("roster_queue.py refuses it by name until then"), so a regression would silently drop every op queued before the lint clone exists.
   - plan-beat: state_docs rc 2 reported as `PLAN UNAVAILABLE` instead of `REFUSED`. The REFUSED arm is untested. Separately, replan's `--slots`/`--seats` can be dropped.
   - pulse: the `pulse: UNREADABLE` arm (`rc not in (0,1,2)`) is untested. Separately, `--seat-alive` args can be dropped.
   - cancel-sweep: `cancel_superseded.py` rc != 0 can be dropped, leaving the digest silent.
   - opener: `open_driver.py` rc != 0 can be dropped, leaving the digest silent.

   Each needs a planted case, plus an argv assertion where the arm is argument wiring. The mutant rule here is the fixer's own: one per row. For tick-digest, owed-check, roster-drain, plan-beat, pulse, cancel-sweep and opener, the row's failure arm has no killing case.

## Findings

- Follow-up: head-watch's HEAD-MOVED events are deduplicated by line text over the whole of `events.txt`. A PR whose head goes A→B→A→B records only the first two moves, so the third, a real move to a head that may need a reviewer, writes no event (`ev/probes.txt` P3: two events for three moves). STUCK lines want the dedupe; HEAD-MOVED does not, or should dedupe only against the last event for that PR. Carry: R10-FLY-STANDING-CONTRACTS
- Follow-up: tick-digest's UNREADABLE line can stick. If the board is absent or empty for one pass and then returns at the same provenance line as the remembered pass, the `seen["pass"] == first` early return keeps `tick-digest: UNREADABLE board ... absent` in the digest until the next board stamp (`ev/probes.txt` P4). tick_loop.sh writes the board atomically (temp then `mv`), so the only way in is a deleted-and-restored board. That makes this low severity, but it is a false wake: new.stamp is touched. Carry: R10-FLY-STANDING-CONTRACTS

## Evidence

merges.body:
R10-FLY-ARCHSCORE-STMT-PACKING, repair round 3. `coord_footprint` (counter C25) reads a packed statement as the plain statements it spells. This round closes the conditional chain nested in the body arm (round 2 block, attempt 54), removes the starred-target over-count, answers `## Red checks`, and disposes the remaining over-count and unclosed shapes in `tools/audit/archscore/ABOUT.md`.

What changed:
- `footprint._chain` counts the branches of a conditional-expression TREE: every `IfExp` reachable through `body` as well as `orelse` (`(a if q else b) if p else c` is three branches, as its nested if/else spells). `_extras` skips every `IfExp` nested directly under another, so the tree is charged once at its root.
- `footprint._bound`: a tuple target holding a starred element against a display value reads the names it binds. `a, *b = e1, e2, e3` reads 2, as `a = e1; b = [e2, e3]` does (it read 3).
- Plant 54 (`planted/redteam/54_footprint_ifexp_body_chain.py`), the reviewer's `x = ((A) if (p) else (B)) if (p) or (q) else (C)` respelling of each if/elif/else of the coordinator: recorded GAME, NULL, admissible.
- Plant 55 (`planted/redteam/55_footprint_boolop_control.py`), `if p: x = A / else: x = B` respelled `x = (p) and (A) or (B)`: it reads IMPROVES (admissible), so it is recorded KNOWN-OPEN through `planted/cases.py` `KNOWN_OPEN`, not closed. The disposition is in ABOUT.md (design choice, below).
- `tests/arch_score.py`: four new rows of the packed/plain table (the body-arm tree, a tree in both arms, `a, *b` and `*a, b`).
- ABOUT.md dispositions, each with the reason: `for` over a literal of tuples and its `async for` twin (over-count, safe direction; the loop body is written once); `p and A or B` (attempt 55, KNOWN-OPEN); a comprehension used as a loop over a literal (open by design, not planted: a comprehension is also a mapping).

Design choice, said where it is made: counting a `BoolOp` as control flow was not built. `a or b` and `a and b` are idioms and no structural test separates control flow from them, so a counter would charge ordinary code; the respelling is the same bounded 3-to-1 as the lone `a if p else y` already disposed in ABOUT.md. The alternative (count `A and B or C` as a two-branch tree) was rejected for that reason; a class fix flips attempt 55 and `tests/arch_score.py` then refuses until it is re-recorded.

Closes the round 2 block of #3218. No issue is closed by this repair.

merges.subject: Merge pull request #3221 from tvofi/fix/r10-handoff-path-p1
merges.title: R10-HANDOFF-PATH part 1: reuse the fixer's prepr receipt at open and update
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-HANDOFF-PATH part 1 (triage `dev/programme/triage/s6-batch121.md#P386`, the owner's directive of 2026-11-04): a fixer's prepr is not repeated at open or update. Part 1 is P386's carry with roster carries 3 and 4 and no other; one checkout per pull request, exit 75, the retry and the `open_driver` repairs are part 2. Carry 9 is answered by #3089's merge.

- **The receipt.** `tools/pr/prepr.sh`'s `receipt_write`: a run with a body that ends rc=0 writes `<HEAD sha> <tree sha>` to `hpo-prepr-receipt` in the checkout's git dir. The main flow removes an earlier receipt first, so a failing run leaves none. `--body-check` and `--fill-red` exit before the main flow and write none. A run that sets any `PREPR_SKIP_*` except `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES` writes none, and neither does a run over a dirty tree.
- **The trailer.** In `tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh`, `prepr_trailer` adds `Prepr: <sha> <tree>` to the `handoff-body/<topic>` commit, under `Code:`. It does so only when the receipt's sha is the handoff's code head and its tree is that head's tree. Otherwise one line says that no trailer was written.
- **The verdict.** `tools/pr/app_push.sh --reuse`'s `reuse_verdict` sits beside `recarry_verdict` and `row_only_verdict` and fails closed. Every one of these must hold:
  - (a) the tip of `handoff-body/<topic>` carries exactly one `Prepr: C T` trailer;
  - (b) C's tree is T;
  - (c) C is in HEAD, and C merges cleanly with the live head and then with the origin/main commit HEAD holds, which is on main's first-parent chain;
  - (d) HEAD's tree is that merge's tree, or that tree plus this pull request's own row;
  - (e) HEAD carries no commit beyond C, the live head and main except that one row commit.

  When the verdict holds, prepr runs under `PREPR_SKIP_CODE=C`, and then `row_only_checks` runs. Otherwise the full prepr runs, exactly as today. One `app_push: REUSE:` line names which path ran and why. `open_pr.sh` p1 asks for `--reuse`. `update_pr.sh` asks for `--reuse` on every head that is not a row-only push.
- **What still runs, with no heavy slot.** Under `PREPR_SKIP_CODE`, prepr takes no slot. It still runs transport, ancestry reds, ref privacy, temp paths, no version edit, claim files, claims hygiene, layout guard, preflight, pr-body, figures, carry, unpinned sites and push order. `merged_steps` adds two checks on HEAD merged with origin/main: `tests/structure.py` (carry 4, in every run) and ci predict (in this mode only). The merged tree is HEAD itself when HEAD already holds main; otherwise it is the `merge-tree` result. The skip is not keyed to main standing still under a closure (`s6-batch95.md#P346`).

**Each step's input, checked before dropping it** (read from `tools/pr/prepr.sh`'s main flow). The triage's split was a reading, and the input check differs from it in four places:
- **transport: kept.** Not listed by the triage, but it reads the commits since the merge base, which the merge and the row add, and it costs 0.0 s.
- **push order: kept.** Not listed either; it reads the remote head ref.
- **claims register: dropped.** Not listed either. It reads `BASE...HEAD` paths against `CLAIMS_READS`, and that is the code's diff alone.
- **gate mode and diff mutants: dropped.** The first prints the scope of the code's diff. The second is report-only, and `MUTANT_CMD` is code-keyed.

The other drops read the code alone:
- `policy_lint`, `rules_sync`, `fragments`, `hooks`, `codeowners_gap`, `brief_lint`, `field coverage`, `register check`, `pinned graders`, `self-test`, `wave-script`, `no-copies` and `throwaway git` read the tree's corpus and its own scripts. Main's half of that corpus passed on main.
- `agreement lane` reads the first-parent subjects since the tag. The only new ones are the open's or update's automatic merge and the row, both shapes the full prepr already passes at every open today.
- `closures` is already `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES` at every open.

**Merge resolution.** The open refused this head (`91a75ed8`): `merging origin/main into 91a75ed8 conflicts` in `tools/pr/prepr.sh`, because main had moved by 23 commits. Main's three commits to `prepr.sh` since `af941ad4` are `8f6f0ea2f`, `18481fd52` and `1584530f3`. They add the lazy `take_slot`, `closures_owes_slot` and the early `## Head` arm, step 1a3 (P208). The change over the reviewed content is a merge of origin/main, `c0b082bc`, with one conflict, in `tools/pr/prepr.sh`. It is resolved with both sides kept. Main's step 1a3 runs first, right after the ancestry-reds arm 1a2: it is keyed to the body, so it also runs under `PREPR_SKIP_CODE`. Next come this branch's recorder cache and its `PREPR_SKIP_CODE` gate. Main's five lazy `take_slot` calls are in these steps: mutants, field coverage, self-test, closures and diff mutants. Mutants and field coverage are in the first code-keyed group, self-test in the second and diff mutants in the third. Closures is behind `elif [ -n "${REUSE:-}" ]`. So a reuse run still defines and takes no slot. No other file of this diff changed on main since `af941ad4`: `git diff af941ad4a origin/main -- tools/pr/app_push.sh tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh tools/audit/seat/update_pr.sh` is empty.

Alternatives:
- A separate check list in `app_push.sh` would have duplicated prepr's steps beside their owner. It lost to one mode of prepr's own flow.
- Reading the receipt from the body's prose is what the ruling had to do, and prose cannot be verified. A trailer on the body commit carries a sha and a tree that can be checked.

**Repair round 2** (the first fix review blocked `794fe6a7` on two defects, each letting a receipt skip a check the body says still runs):
- **The main flow's `merged_steps` call is pinned.** The `(a)` arm's real `PREPR_SKIP_CODE` prepr now runs with a body and asserts that one `merged structure` line and one `ci predict` line appear. Under `PREPR_SKIP_CODE` that call is the only ci predict and the only `tests/structure.py` on HEAD merged with main, and the function-level arms (d) and (e) could not see it deleted.
- **The receipt names the HEAD the run started on.** `receipt_line` reads `<HEAD sha> <tree sha>` once, where the main flow starts (`RUN_START`, right after the early receipt removal). `receipt_write` gets it as a third argument and writes that line, never a fresh read. When HEAD or its tree differ at the end, it refuses through `step "receipt" 1`, so the run ends rc=1 and writes no receipt. When no start was read, it writes none. A commit landing mid-run is therefore code the receipt never claims.
- **The five follow-ups, one row each, in the self-tests already touched:** reuse_verdict's first-parent arm of (c) (real git: HEAD holding a side commit main merged); two `Prepr:` trailers; `row_only_checks` after the reduced prepr under `--reuse` (a copy whose `reuse_verdict` is a stub that reuses, so the wiring past a reusing verdict runs: prepr under `PREPR_SKIP_CODE`, then the body contract and the carry check, and a contract refusal stops the push); the early receipt removal (the `(a)` run plants a stale receipt and asserts it is gone); and body_push.sh's sha comparison (a receipt whose tree is the head's but whose sha is not).
- The unsigned-receipt finding stays as it is: P386 dismissed it.

Alternatives for the starting HEAD:
- Re-reading HEAD at the end and comparing it to `## Head` alone was rejected. A seat that moves both the code and the body mid-run, which is the reviewer's real run 2, passes that check.
- Taking a lock on HEAD for the length of the run was rejected. It is heavier, and it would still need the same comparison at the end.
- Writing the start line, after checking that it is unchanged, makes the receipt the measured HEAD by construction.

**Repair round 3.** The second fix review blocked `20d5aab0` on two defects:
- **`governance / instrument-self-tests` was red: pr_args.sh's fixtures had not been updated for the `--reuse` code push.** `bash tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh --self-test` gave `172 checks, 19 failed` at `20d5aab0`, and `0 failed` at base `8364e624`. There were three causes:
  - The stubs shifted only `--row-only`. Under `--reuse` their `$2` was the repository, not the worktree, so the stub pushes failed. That accounts for the race, row-close, kept-worktree and lock rows.
  - The open row and the two update null controls still expected no flag on the code push.
  - The pusher census found two new files naming `app_push.sh` with no disposition: comments in `body_push.sh` and `prepr.sh`.

  The repair:
  - Every stub drops either mode flag.
  - The open row now asserts `--reuse` on the code push and `--row-only` on the row push. Both update null controls assert `--reuse`, never `--row-only`. They stay meaningful: each still separates a new-code head from a row-only head, which `mut:rowonly` crosses.
  - Each runner now carries `--reuse` on a line of its own, so a mutant can delete it without deleting the push. In `open_pr.sh` that is `RU=--reuse  # mut:opreuse`, and the push takes `${RU-}`. Before, the marker sat on the whole p1 push line. In `update_pr.sh` it is `[ -n "$RO" ] || RO=--reuse  # mut:updreuse`, placed after the restored `RO=""; … || RO=--row-only  # mut:rowonly`. Each mutant has a row that kills it.
  - The census gives both files `mention` entries.
- **The mutation-vacuous condition (e).** One real-git row in app_push.sh's reuse block has the shape of the reviewer's F9: the clean merge of C and main plus two commits that net to no tree change. It asserts (e)'s refusal, `HEAD carries 2 commit(s) beyond code …`. The same head reset under those two commits reuses again, which is its null control.

Alternatives for (1):
- Reverting the code push to no flag would have restored the old fixtures and dropped P386's reuse at open and update. That is the feature this PR exists for.
- Keeping the marker on the whole push line would leave a mutant that deletes the push itself. The run would then stop at `pr_wait` for a reason other than the missing flag, which is a vacuous pin.

## Head

`0f6771a7a4b8ca1146d74b81e66bc5b357e45f9b` merges main `0ae75bf` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`fd0d130a7e040c64da4fcd93c1ca2aa2a2fc9f56` is this PR's head, unchanged: its code was already in it and main merged cleanly, so the orchestrator's script set this body without a push.

`533b00b37c7f02896c7d5a14926aa97b947d1b2a`. It is the reviewed head `20d5aab0` with these commits added:

Two defects. Each lets a receipt skip a check that the body says still runs.

1. **mutation-vacuous: the call that runs the merged-tree checks is unpinned.** Delete the one main-flow line `merged_steps "${1:-}" "$UNPINNED_SITES"` in tools/pr/prepr.sh. `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh --self-test` still reads `504 passed, 0 failed` (ev/mutants-prepr.part1.txt, P1). Under `PREPR_SKIP_CODE` that line is the only ci predict and the only `tests/structure.py` on HEAD merged with main: step 6d's predict is behind `if [ -z "$REUSE" ]`. Without it, a reuse run checks neither, and no test notices. The self-test drives the `merged_steps` function directly (arms (d) and (e)). The `(a)` arm runs a real `PREPR_SKIP_CODE` prepr but asserts only that the code-keyed steps are absent, never that `merged structure` and `ci predict` are present. The body's own mutant edits inside the function, which is why it was killed. Repair: in the `(a)` arm's real run, assert that both `merged structure` and `ci predict` lines appear. Then the deleted call fails a check.
2. **A receipt names the HEAD at the run's end, not the HEAD it measured.** `receipt_write` writes `git rev-parse HEAD` after the run, and nothing in the main flow pins the HEAD the run started on. Demonstrated end to end (ev/realrun2-summary.txt, ev/realrun2.sh):
   - A real `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1 bash tools/pr/prepr.sh <body>` started at `1acf58eb7c1f` (02:32:46), with this PR's own handoff body.

   - The run ended `rc=0` and wrote `receipt fba41aea801e written`.
   - `body_push.sh` would carry that receipt as `Prepr: fba41aea… <its tree>`, and `app_push.sh --reuse` would then drop the code-keyed steps for code that the steps run before 02:36 never saw.
   
   This is the brief's "head that moved after the receipt", moved during the run instead. The function-level form is ev/midrun-receipt.txt (ev/midrun.sh). Without the body edit, step 7's `## Head` check refuses, and so does the early `## Head` arm (ev/realrun-summary.txt). So the hole needs code and body to change mid-run, which is a seat working while its prepr runs. Repair: capture `HEAD` (and its tree) where the main flow starts, and have `receipt_write` refuse when either differs at the end. Add a self-test row for it.

## Findings

- Follow-up: surviving mutant: in `reuse_verdict`, remove the first-parent-chain check of (c) (`rev-list --first-parent … | grep -x "$mb"` replaced by `true`). `app_push.sh --self-test` stays at `219 checks, 0 failed`; only this reviewer's planted R6 (HEAD holds a main commit off main's first-parent chain) kills it (ev/mutants-app_push.txt, M2b). - Follow-up: surviving mutant: the trailer-count test `= 1` relaxed to `-ge 1`. The self-test stays at 219/0; only planted R7 (two `Prepr:` trailers) kills it (M5). Carry: R10-HANDOFF-PATH
- Follow-up: surviving mutant: under `--reuse`, `row_only_checks` after prepr removed (`[ "$reused" = 0 ] || row_only_checks` replaced by `true || …`). The self-test stays at 219/0 (M6). The live-title body contract and carry check the header promises under reuse are unpinned. Carry: R10-HANDOFF-PATH
- Follow-up: surviving mutant: the main flow's early `rm -f "$(receipt_file)"` removed. The self-test stays at 504/0 (P3). The body's claim that "a failing run leaves none" is unpinned; the `--body-check` row deletes the receipt itself before it runs. Carry: R10-HANDOFF-PATH
- Follow-up: surviving mutant: in body_push.sh `prepr_trailer`, the sha comparison `[ "$s" = "$2" ]` weakened to `[ -n "$s" ]`. The self-test stays at 504/0 (P6), because the tree comparison masks it in the only row. Downstream, `reuse_verdict`'s is-ancestor and tree-diff arms would still refuse a mismatched sha, so this is a test gap, not a hole. Carry: R10-HANDOFF-PATH
- Out of scope: the receipt is an unsigned self-attestation. A hand-written `Prepr: <C> <tree(C)>` trailer on handoff-body/<topic>, with no prepr run behind it, is accepted (planted R8 → REUSE). Likewise a seat may set `PREPR_SKIP_CODE` by hand. Carry: dismissed: P386 rules that the fixer's prepr is trusted; the body says so under Alternatives; CI gates the merged head, and PREPR_SKIP_* knobs were already seat-settable

Read as subsumed: when C is not in HEAD, or HEAD carries extra commits, either the tree diff (d) differs, or the trees are identical and reuse is sound.

The mask now takes roles from the same entry keys and items that `sanitise` keeps, through the one predicate `_entry_shape`. Round 3 of the repair: round 2's `prepr` step 6d refused the body for omitting two unpinned `replay_doc.py` sites.

`2ecd546699d8c7f748316660c9b5d2164dc70a9e` merges main `cd0dd16` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

Alternatives: (a) delete the list filter only: leaves `_entities` lists with non-id items refused; (b) a second hand-copied `endswith("_entities")` predicate: duplicates the concept and can drift; both lost to the shared function.
- Round 3: the `if value is _DROP: continue` that followed the `_entry_shape` call is deleted. Its mutant (`if False:`) survived `replay.mask_checks()`, and no check can kill it: the only consumer of `_role_claims` is `entity_roles.claim`, which ignores any value that is not a `str` matching `ENTITY_ID`, and a `_DROP` is a bare `object()`. The branch was an equivalent mutant, so I took the deletion over a check that cannot fail (owner-directed alternative was a new check reaching the skip; it cannot exist for this reason, shown by the mutant below). Design choice: `_role_claims` yields the sentinel and the consumer's id test passes it over; the comment at the call says so.

merges.body:
R10-SAV-COMFORT part 3: the month row settles the plan's stored heat and publishes the comfort shortfall beside the saving (carries 0 and 6, under the owner's ruling on carry 7).

Part of #2492. Part of #201. Critical path: R10-SAV-COMFORT. #2492 stays open: the summer start-bound limit and carry 5 are routed back to it.

## Re-cut

Fourth round (`fixer.md`, "Past three rounds"): this body replaces the earlier ones. Round history is deleted. Only figures re-taken in this pass remain; the production-call table of the earlier bodies is dropped, and `tests / fast (3.14)` is the authority for it at the final head.

**The ruling applied.** tvofi's mandated orchestrator ruling of 2026-11-04 on carry 7: the month row settles stored heat, the thermostat stays start-independent, and the comfort-matched null is reported beside the saving. Each plan step carries four settlement readings, `ledger.SETTLEMENT_KEYS` (`baseline_kw`, `stored_kw_th`, `comfort_kw`, `steady_cop`), from `optimizer._settlement_schedule` through `get_current_action` (`_settlement_at`) into the coordinator's pending snapshot, which `MonthlyLedger.observe_spot_and_settle_savings` books:

- `stored_kw_th`: the house store's change over the step (`_stored_thermal_energy` at the plan's boundary states), booked as kWh_th on `savings_stored`. `savings_months` converts the month's total once, at the month's mean steady COP, and prices it once, at the row's metered kWh price (`stored_heat_sek`).
- `comfort_kw`: the steady thermostat's heat demand at the step's comfort target less at the room the plan delivered (the slab-fed zone, at the step's midpoint), each floored at zero, at the step's steady COP. Published as `comfort_sek` beside `savings_sek`, not netted out of it.

**Three shapes tried** (figures from `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_null_settled.py`): stored heat at the settlement caps and each step's COP lost because a cap that moves between re-plans breaks the telescope (varying arm -4.50 %); uncapped at each step's COP lost because it cancels the COP-timing saving (varying arm +0.01 %); uncapped at one COP and one price per row won (below).

**Payments (no budget raised).** The schedule is a module-level pure function; `ledger.settle_interval_savings` is folded into its one caller; the pending snapshot copies `SETTLEMENT_KEYS` in one spread; `_settlement_at` replaces `get_current_action`'s baseline branch. `tests/structure_budgets.json` is byte-identical to main's.

**This repair (blocked head `c383169a5`, `ci-red`).** `prelude` outlived its 8700 s cap because `tests / mutation-pins` shards ran the whole closure once per surviving site. The sites are killed by checks, not triaged:
- `tests/features.py` drives `_settlement_schedule` directly on controlled trajectories with a stored-heat function weighting every state field differently, for two-zone and single-zone houses and buffer lengths absent, valid, exactly `n_steps` and shorter. A mutant that crashes fails a named check (the call is wrapped).
- The COP floor `if cop < 1e-3: cop = 1e-3` and the comfort clamps `d if d > 0.0 else 0.0` become `max(...)`: the `<`/`>` to `<=`/`>=` mutants on those lines were equivalent (at equality the assignment is a no-op), so no check could kill them and a triage verdict would have papered over a killable shape.
- The ledger's `max(float(steady_cop), 1e-3)` is pinned by a zero-COP step.
- Carried defects of `verdict/3195` taken in lines already touched: the dead duplicate `before = after` is deleted; the `_settlement_schedule` docstring cites `_floor_demand_terms`, the function it calls; `payload.py`'s comment cites `OptimizationResult.settlement_schedule`, the field that exists.

## Head

`33e5d882748605da815affa2fc0ef11326d7f7e3` merges main `79f765e` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`8050a943c21757575afb59fd2b5d7125714fff9b` is this PR's head. It is the bot commit `ci: pin killed mutants` on top of the reviewed code head `611e1aa6fc004d5f5666ca99efc402a1003c0849`; it adds the 11 killed_by anchors and no other change, and `review_carry.py` reads CARRY for it. No code moved.

`e0018143649336998518d267f49d66ea9a073b0a`: the handoff of `c383169a5` with the repair commit, merged with `origin/main` `499162c89d0f4f8369e16e6e41fb3a620bc1ecb0` (2026-11-05T01:48Z; merge, not a re-cut, no conflict). `tests/structure_budgets.json` and both claim files are byte-identical to `origin/main`: `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD --stat -- tests/structure_budgets.json tests/golden` prints nothing.

## Mutation proof

Mutant: in `MonthlyLedger.savings_months`, `baseline_sek = self.line(key, "savings_baseline")["sek"] * scale + stored_sek` becomes `... * scale`, at the head above.
- `python3 tests/features.py` prints `1 of 4810 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`; the FAIL is `R10-SAV-COMFORT: the month row settles the plan's stored-heat change at the row's metered kWh price`.

- Restored: `ALL 4810 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`.

Mutants of the 11 sites `ci_predict.py` lists for this diff, each applied by `sed` to `optimizer.py` or `ledger.py` and run against the new checks' statements (extracted unchanged from `tests/features.py`; the mutant column is the number of FAIL lines printed; the unmutated tree prints 0):

## Null control

## Figures

Rule: const `|pct| < 3.0`, vary `pct >= 3.0`.
- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_baseline.py transient` (sha1 `bc31f356191ededbfb0b15f768b258249867b134`): spread 0.00 kW, SOUND.
- Gate scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir <dir>` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 27 script(s) run, 6 scoped out.` Every script `scope.run` names except `tests/stress.py` and the `.mjs` ones ran with `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`, rc=0 each: `arch_score_head`, `backtest`, `block_duty`, `boost_drift_replay`, `config_flow_steps`, `debug_collect`, `deployment_shape`, `doc_claims`, `edge`, `entities`, `env_drift`, `features`, `finite_boundary`, `golden`, `guard_pins`, `harness_headers`, `manual_plan`, `optimality`, `plan_view`, `solar_alignment`, `structure`, `typing_ruler`, `validate`, `wood_advisor`. `python3 tests/stress.py` printed `ALL 113 STRESS CHECKS PASSED`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- Class seams: `git grep -n "_settlement_schedule" -- custom_components` returns the definition and its one caller; `git grep -n SETTLEMENT_KEYS -- custom_components` returns the coordinator's pending snapshot and the ledger.

## Unpinned sites

`python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py` at the head lists 11 sites, all under `custom_components/`, the directory `mutation-autofix` mutates. Each is killed by the check named in `## Mutation proof`, so each is pinned by `mutation-autofix` when its lane drives it, and none is claimed pinned by this seat before the lane has run. No site is waiting on a triage verdict.

- `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/ledger.py:309 CLAMP_DROP` (`max(float(steady_cop), 1e-3)`): killing check in `tests/features.py` (see `## Mutation proof`); pinned by `mutation-autofix`

## Red checks

Concluded reds of the blocked head `c383169a5` (the check-run set of `tests`, `governance` and `prelude`, read in full by the reviewer in `probe/rev-3195-50e00e14` `ev/check_runs_final.tsv`, 54 rows). The final head above has had no CI yet: moving the head is what starts it, so none of these is claimed cured by a run.

The runner's speed fell between the bands, so it is not branch-caused: this diff touches neither `tools/replay/` nor the cost budget, and the baseline tree reads the same on that runner. `gate` does not list it. comments.body:
Fix review: blocked 6f742a33e5216932d4fb0f4583e09b137432ea9f ci-red: tests / typing is red on this branch's code (9 no-untyped-call from _settlement_schedule's untyped _l lambda) and the body's Red checks does not name it

bus-nonce: a50715cc35d8e7d0271b7ed10cc9392a

Round: first fix review of #3195 R10-SAV-COMFORT part 3 (the repair head). Measured head: `6f742a33e5216932d4fb0f4583e09b137432ea9f`, still the PR head when this verdict was written (`git ls-remote`). Roles diff `merge-base...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty, so the contract is current.

## Block

- `tests / typing` (check run 126700212941) concluded `failure` at this head. It is in the gate's required set (`tools/policy/fixtures/required-contexts.json` `gate_required`). Its log says `optimizer.py 9`, `FAIL errors did not grow [recorded 0, measured 9 (+9)]`, `FAIL by_code[no-untyped-call] did not grow [recorded 0, measured 9 (+9)]`. The red comes from this branch. `_settlement_schedule` binds `_l = lambda x: np.asarray(x, dtype=float).tolist()` and calls it exactly 9 times (rooms, slabs, uppers, lowers, bufs, outs, winds, precs, suns). Under mypy 2.4.1, the CI pin, every call of an untyped lambda in typed code is `[no-untyped-call]` (reproduced: `ev/mypy_lambda_snip.py`). This is the repair's step (a). The figure is not the instrument's: main records 0.
- The body's `## Red checks` names `fast (3.14)`, `mutation`, `replay` and `nightly-status` at the previous head, but not `typing` at this head. `review_packet.py` refused on exactly this: `red-unanswered: concluded red check tests / typing is not named in ## Red checks`. The body also says "the census in `tests/typing_ruler.py` went red locally during the earlier work … passes at this head". CI says it does not pass. `tests/typing_ruler.py --mypy` is the cheaper detector, about 12 s of mypy plus the typing venv. A root-cause class is not posted here: the head's workflows did not all conclude normally (the mutation-pins shards and `mutation-autofix` were cancelled, `gate` cancelled), and no `pr-contract` run followed the last red.
- Owed: give the conversion a typed helper (e.g. a `def _floats(x: ArrayLike) -> list[float]`), or annotate it so mypy reads it as typed, with the same per-step cost, so `tests/stress.py` stays under its 1.05x. Re-run `tests/typing_ruler.py --mypy` and the stress meter. Answer `typing` under `## Red checks`.

## Findings

- M13 survives features.py and entities.py (`ALL 2602 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`, `ev/M13_entities_tail.txt`): `step["baseline_kw"] = baseline[i]` in `_settlement_schedule` replaced by `pass` leaves `ALL 4783 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`. Yet with it, the current action carries no `baseline_kw` and the month row books nothing: my probe's ledger has no savings row at all (`IndexError` on `savings_months(...)[0]`). Since this PR, the action's `baseline_kw` comes only through the schedule (`_settlement_at`), so this line now carries the whole savings settlement and no check pins it end to end through `get_current_action`. The mutation lane did not evaluate it: `mutation-pins (1..5)` were cancelled. Owed: a features check that `get_current_action(plan, t0)["baseline_kw"] == plan.baseline_power_schedule[0]` on a solved plan. Carry: R10-SAV-COMFORT
- M2 survives features.py: in `_settlement_schedule`, `zone = lowers` replaced by `zone = rooms` (the two-zone comfort shortfall reads the whole-house room instead of the slab-fed lower floor). It moves the figure: on a two-zone winter_cold 24 h flat plan, comfort kWh is 1.7704 at the head and 2.0018 mutated (step 0: 0.0460 against 0.0110). The two-zone comfort path the docstring states is untested. The only comfort check is single-zone and asserts `> 0` (`tests/features.py`). Owed: a two-zone comfort check against the lower-floor trajectory. Carry: R10-SAV-COMFORT
- M3 survives features.py: `delivered = 0.5 * (zone[i] + zone[j])` replaced by `delivered = zone[i]`. It moves the vary arm's `comfort_sek` from 8.28 to 8.24. The midpoint rule is unpinned. Carry: R10-SAV-COMFORT
- M9 and M10 survive features.py: in `savings_months`, the meter-calibration `scale` dropped from `stored_sek` (M9) or from `comfort_sek` (M10). The docstring says both are "scaled as the thermostat is", and no check exercises a calibrated month with stored or comfort lines. Owed: one calibrated-month check over both. Carry: R10-SAV-COMFORT

merges.body:
R10-LEARNED-STORE-LOAD: two latent learned-store lifecycle defects, found by the R10-FACTORY-RESET fixer, each reproduced through the production coordinator and fixed in `coordinator.py`'s learning seam.

1. **A save during the thermal load wrote the COP and T4b learners' defaults.** `_async_load_thermal_learning` awaited its gated re-anchor save halfway through applying the read. That was before `_COP_STORE_KEY`/`cop_samples`, `measured_cop`, the cusums, the COP baselines and every `_load_t4b_learners` key had loaded. So the saved payload (the loader's own, and any save scheduled behind the read) carried those learners as defaults. A restart in that window lost them on disk. Fix: the gated save is now the loader's last step.
2. **A restore right after setup found the snapshot ring empty, and no restore ever rolled back sample counts.** `async_restore_learned_snapshot` waited for the reads of the stores it rewrites but not for the snapshot store it restores from, so it read the empty constructor ring and returned False. `_apply_learner_payloads` set the four scalar learners through their setters and left each sample count at its live, drifted value. Fix: the restore also waits for `_snapshot_store`'s read. The four scalar learners now load through one parser, `_load_scalar_learners`, shared by the store loader and the snapshot restore, so a count rolls back with its learner.

**The load barrier.** The brief asks for "one load barrier that every save and restore awaits". That barrier is the store's existing read fence (`QuarantiningStore.async_wait_for_read`), not a new mechanism. Every `QuarantiningStore.async_save` already awaits it, and so does each restore and reset (ls-r1). It is a load barrier, and not merely a read barrier, exactly when the loader applies its read with no await in between. Defect 1 was the one learned loader that broke that rule. With the save moved to the end, it holds again, and the coordinator comment at the save names the invariant.

Alternatives considered:
- I wrote and measured a separate `LoadFence` (an in-flight-loads set in `store.py`, held by the thermal and snapshot loaders and awaited by both saves, the restore and the factory reset). It was rejected. Once the save moved, no mutant of its save-side waits could fail any check, so it was a parallel mechanism that nothing pins (fixer step 17: the existing mechanism, never a parallel one). It also cost a new class and the reindent of a 70-line method.
- Making the thermal loader spawn its save instead of awaiting it was rejected too: direct-call loaders in tests would lose the re-anchor write.

**Carry 1, STRANDED CARRY 55 (#2674, seven unprobed store-load leads),** is already answered, and was re-run here. #2674 is closed by probe (owner comment, 2026-11-01). Its harness `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_store_load_leads.py` (sha1 `9b69a689bda785ea14769dc8d42858a493cacbde`) prints identical `_lost=`/`fresh_call_writes` lines at base and head (`diff` of the two greps, empty). That is `price_shape_lost=0 null=0` and `extra_legionella_observer_lost=0 null=0`, every other lead `fresh_call_writes=0` with its gate-open arm `lost=1 null=0`. The census reads `0 of 12` at both. `dev/programme/carries/carry-2674.json` is owed deletion in a record PR, per that comment.

`coordinator.py` edits stay inside the learning seam (loader, restore, the new `_load_scalar_learners`, a `tests/features.py` disposition for the learner-feeder class check, mapped `learning` in `tests/seam_map.json`). Nothing outside this group's seam changed.

## Head

`16f006264e53efcc09ca3175b1bfb2d988436080` merges main `dad3178` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`785d43a97fe5ca765b97090a0e735c2d5690f11e` merges the authored code head `c6444f38f775cb9859e80a0dfcb0fd420b6e390b` and then merges origin/main `8e90d8144` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`c6444f38f775cb9859e80a0dfcb0fd420b6e390b`. Branched from PR head `876c1c4e38d2d768580f804c3135236678485a76`, with `origin/main` `8e90d81443317f76f22602a89651f7ca17c633f9` merged in (the #3180 hotfix included; tip read 2026-11-04, `prepr.sh` rerun after that merge). The fix is `69dcabb8e`. The repair commits on top change the parser's spelling only (below), drop the one ledger pin that spelling made stale, and add one `tests/features.py` disposition. The mutation proofs were taken at `69dcabb8e`, where the three predicates they break (the save's position, the ring's read wait, the shared parser) are the ones this head still carries; the checks they killed pass at this head (`ALL 4779 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`). Toolchain: `bash tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh` then `--check` read OK, numpy 2.5.4 / scipy 1.18.1 match `tests/requirements-ci.txt`.

## Mutation proof

Three mutants, one per gate, run by `tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --spec mutants.json --cmd 'bash partial.sh'` (archive copy; `partial.sh` runs `tests/features.py` through the new checks and exits with their status). The NULL mutant survived. Each mutant's failing checks, from re-applying it to a `git archive HEAD` copy:

- **M1, the loader saves mid-load** (the gated save re-inserted before `self._measured_cop = …`, so it runs before the T4b learners load): killed. Failing checks:
  - `a thermal save issued mid-load keeps the stored COP and T4b learners in every payload` [raced `[(30, []), (30, ['-5']), (30, ['-5'])]`]
  - `a re-anchor persists exactly once`
  - `adding a power meter re-anchors both learners at zero confidence`
  - `a lower-floor sensor swap voids the ratio and leaves the scale intact`
  - `an indoor sensor swap voids the scale and leaves the ratio intact`
  - `a store without recorded zone sensors keeps both learners and adopts the ids`
- **M2, the restore skips the ring's read** (`for store in _restored_stores(self):`): killed. Failing check: `a restore issued right after setup applies the newest snapshot, sample counts included` [raced `(False, (1.0, 0, 1.0, 0))`].
- **M3, the restore drops sample counts** (the base setter loop back in place of `_load_scalar_learners(thermal)`): killed. Failing checks:
  - `a restore issued right after setup applies the newest snapshot, sample counts included` [`(True, (1.4, 0, 1.1, 0))`]
  - `a snapshot restore re-anchors a pre-edit scale, not restores it`

## Null control

Each new check carries its own null control: the same command run after the load landed (`_store_race(..., after=True)`).

- **At the base**, the save check's null fails too: `[(0, []), (30, ['-5'])]`. That is defect 1 itself, because the loader's own save carries the defaults whenever the load runs, raced or not. The restore check's null reads `(True, (1.4, 0, 1.1, 0))`: the snapshot applies, but its counts do not.
- **At the head**, both the raced and the null arms read the stored state: every saved payload is `(30, ['-5'])`, and the restore reads `(True, (1.4, 33, 1.1, 21))`.
- **A fully loaded entry still behaves as it does today:** every other check in `tests/features.py` up to the new block is unchanged (`1089` run, same set, at base and head), and the scoped gate is green (Figures).
- **The changed test is `a snapshot restore re-anchors a pre-edit scale, not restores it`.** Its snapshot now carries `house_heat_loss_samples: 300` instead of leaving 300 on the live learner. The re-anchor law weighs the snapshot's count, as the loader weighs the store's (`a converged scale is re-anchored onto the new nameplate`, same 300, same expected value).

## Figures

- New checks at base vs head (`bash partial.sh` in a base worktree and at the head; base output kept from a partial copy of `tests/features.py`):
  - base: `2 of 1089 PARTIAL FAILED`, the two new checks.
  - head: `ALL 1089 PARTIAL PASSED`.
- Mutants: `python3 tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --spec mutants.json --cmd "bash partial.sh" --timeout 900` printed `SURVIVED NULL`, `KILLED M1-loader-saves-mid-load`, `KILLED M2-restore-skips-ring-read` and `KILLED M3-restore-drops-sample-counts`. A first run printed `SURVIVED` for all four because the wrapper piped the runner through `grep` and lost its exit status. That was a vacuous harness, repaired before this run (Friction).
- Both ends of the restored counts' range: `ends_probe.py` (scratch, not landed) snapshots a coordinator, perturbs a second one to scale 1.6 with 77 samples, and restores into it.
  - Zero evidence: head `(True, 1.0, 0)`, base `(True, 1.0, 77)`.
  - On the clamp (`HOUSE_HEAT_LOSS_SCALE_MAX`, 500 samples): head `(True, 3.0, 500)`, base `(True, 3.0, 77)`.
- Scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"` printed `MODE: SCOPED`. The gate ran `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub bash tests/run.sh`; result: `ALL 4779 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, `tests/golden.py` and `tests/guard_pins.py` rc=0, `tests/entities.py` `ALL 2602 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`.
- Structure: `python3 tests/structure.py` printed `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED` at the head. A first spelling of the parser put `class_excess_loc` and `max_class_loc` 3 lines over budget (`FAIL class_excess_loc 17642 > 17639`); the compacted spelling clears it with no raise.
- Architecture score: `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff origin/main` printed `Architecture score: dS +0.0042 IMPROVES` with `coord_footprint 2381 -> 2374`; no reflective write or computed attribute access is added (see Red checks).
- Class census (fixer step 8): the instrument is the setup census already in the tree. Its harness form is `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_store_races_census.py` (sha1 `dfaa8ff388283bd364f29ebb7c491f5ac33805ae`), and its in-suite form is `no write in the setup refresh is lost to a store read still in flight`. It enumerates every store the constructor builds and reads, from the constructor itself.
  - Base and head both print `census_lost_total=0 of 12` and `census_unfenced_differs=_ctx,_price_learner`, so the census is live.
  - It cannot see defect 1, because the loser there is the disk payload, not the in-memory state the census diffs. The new save check covers that seam.
  - The other learned loaders under the same rule (apply the read without an await) are `async_load_profile`, `async_load_draws`, `_async_load_price_model`, `_async_load_accuracy` and `_async_load_snapshots`. The census reads them clean at both ends.

## Architecture score

The first spelling of `_load_scalar_learners` wrote the sample counts through `setattr(self, f"_{samples}", n)`, which the gate measured as `reflective_writes 11->12` and `computed_attr_access 28->29` (arch-score run 126496102862). Paid by improving the code, not by explaining it: the parser now assigns the four sample counts by name from one generator, with no computed attribute. `score.py --diff origin/main` now reads `dS +0.0042 IMPROVES` (`coord_footprint 2381 -> 2374`), so no metric rises and no explanation line is owed.

## Red checks

Every concluded red check at PR head `876c1c4e38d2d768580f804c3135236678485a76`, from the whole check-run set (`get_check_runs`, 81 runs, read in one page):

- `arch-score / arch-score` (BRANCH-OWNED): `dS +0.0042 WORSENS (reflective_writes 11->12; computed_attr_access 28->29)`. Paid, see `## Architecture score`. No cheaper detector is owed: `archscore/score.py --diff origin/main` is the check's own instrument and runs offline in seconds; this seat did not run it before the first push.
- `tests / replay` (MAIN-OWNED): `synthetic-dhw-only.json cycle_cost cpu_ratio 2.851 over budget 2.173`, the host-class cost-budget flake that #3174 R10-REPLAY-COST-BUDGET addresses (#3167 hit the same). Main's own slow lane failed the same check at run 41749544997, job 126403921052: `FAIL synthetic-dhw-only.json: cycle_cost [1 offender(s): cpu_ratio 3.382 over its budget 2.173]`, `1 of 176 replay checks FAILED`. The branch does not touch the replay path: `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD --stat` names `coordinator.py`'s learned-store loader and restore (load and restore time, not the per-cycle path the replay times), `tests/features.py`, the delivery row, `tests/seam_map.json`, `tests/structure_budgets.json` and golden ledger pins. The budget is not changed here.
- `tests / mutation` (BRANCH-OWNED, red at earlier commits of this branch, green at the PR head `876c1c4e38d2d768580f804c3135236678485a76`, runs 126496102859 and 126496066770): red by construction on the two new unpinned GUARD_OFF sites the diff added, which `prepr.sh` step 6d predicted; cleared by mutation-autofix's `ci: pin killed mutants` commit. No cheaper detector is owed: step 6d already names each site before the handoff, and the standing cost is one autofix commit per diff that adds a guard.
- `tests / nightly-status` (MAIN-OWNED, unrequired): grades main's slow lane; it is red because the lane above (job 126403921052) failed on the same replay `cycle_cost`. Nothing in this diff feeds it.
- `pr-contract / pr-contract` and `gate`: red on the unanswered reds above plus an HTTP 502 reading the check-runs (transient); they aggregate the others and are answered by this section.

## Unpinned sites

- none: the diff adds no unpinned mutation site (`prepr.sh` step 6d: `the diff adds no unpinned mutation site`). The parser's respelling removed the guard line the ledger pin `GUARD_OFF.3986447e` named, so that pin was deleted as the `ledger` arm's repair directs; the save guard's pin (`GUARD_OFF` on `if save:`) stays.

## Forward-carry

- n/a: STRANDED CARRY 55 (#2674) is answered by #2674's own probe reading, re-run at this branch (description). The invariant (a learned loader applies its read with no await before its last assignment) is stated at the code site and pinned by the new save check; no later stage's brief changes.

## Friction

- `fixer.md#2`: unenforced: the mutation wrapper first piped the check runner through `grep`, so every mutant, NULL included, read `SURVIVED`. Nothing refuses a wrapper whose NULL and real mutants all survive; reading the uniform result caught it. Carry: dismissed: caught by reading

Failing check: `a thermal save issued mid-load keeps the stored COP and T4b learners in every payload`, raced `[(30, []), (30, ['-5'])]`. The re-anchor checks the body also lists lie past the cut.
  - RESULT M2 (the restore skips `_snapshot_store`'s read): KILLED, `1 of 1089`. Failing check: `a restore issued right after setup applies...`, raced `(False, (1.0, 0, 1.0, 0))`, null `(True, (1.4, 33, 1.1, 21))`.

The change stays sound and improving under either spelling, and no budget raise rests on the score, so this is an instrument finding (Findings), not `metric-gamed`.
