merges.body:
R10-TWO-ZONE-HHL: the two carries on the whole-house heat-loss coefficient (`house_heat_loss_coefficient`) in two-zone mode, in the order Carry 2 sets: the sysid precondition first, then the options-flow hide.

- Carry 1 (plan-energy probe: hide or label the field on two zones): built as a hide, section (2) below; its control and null control are the `opt_thermal_model` checks under `## Figures` and `## Null control`.
- Carry 2 (R10-UX-HEALTH part 3: the sysid step sizer first, then the hide): (1) built in `HousePlant.of_params`, section (1) below; (2) is Carry 1's hide, built after it in this diff. Its control is the harness's `two_zone_sysid_steps` line, re-measured below.

**(1) The sysid sizer, re-measured at the merge base.** The carry's figure (1.738 kW at 0.1, 3.386 kW at 0.4, none at 1.0 "identical to single zone") was the harness, not production: it built a bare `SystemIdentification()` and never called `arm`, so `_two_zone_plant` stayed `None` and it measured the single-zone sizing path in two-zone mode. Production arms first (`sysid.arm_from_config` -> `SystemIdentification.arm`, which keeps a two-zone plant in `_two_zone_plant`), and the armed sizer already rolls the step out on `ThermalModel(two_zone_plant)` (#1524), whose loss is the zones'. At the merge base, the armed sizer's step does not move with the coefficient (figures below). What still carried the whole-house figure on two zones was the plant record itself: `HousePlant.of_params` built `ua` from `heat_loss_coefficient` and `capacity` from `room_thermal_mass` with no two-zone branch, read by the sizer's `ua > 1e-6` gate in `_begin_step_phase`, the degenerate-house guard in `_predict_step_excursion_plant` and the one-state comparison `_size_step_power` logs. The fix gives `of_params` its two-zone branch: `ua` is `house_heat_loss_base * house_heat_loss_scale` (the zones' loss with the learned split, the one owner of "the loss the dynamics use"; single zone it is `heat_loss_coefficient`, unchanged) and `capacity` the two zones' mass, as `arm` already seeds the fit's prior. Sysid now computes from the zone model it is given, with no reader of the whole-house figure left on two zones.

**(2) The hide.** The thermal-model page's `house_heat_loss_coefficient` row carries `when=_single_zone`, the registry's existing reveal mechanism (as the wood block uses `wood_furnace_on`); `_single_zone` is `not ThermalParameters.from_config(config).two_zone_enabled`, the model's own resolution of the mode, so an `auto` entry follows the zone keys as the solve does (the same call `config_flow` already makes for the flow write target, D12-01). Hidden, not cleared: `_clear_absent` walks only rendered rows, and the row is `_SUGGESTED`, never cleared, so the stored value survives a two-zone save and reappears if the entry goes back to one zone (pinned below). Hide over relabel: a relabel would still render an input that changes nothing, which is what Carry 1 asks to stop.

Alternatives: (a) hide alone, refused by Carry 2 and unnecessary now that the record is two-zone; (b) a two-zone branch inside `_size_step_power` instead of `of_params`, which would leave the record the coordinator builds still describing a house the model does not run, and duplicate the zone sum `arm` already owns; (c) relabel, rejected above.

Reader census (step 8): the rule `grep -rn --include=*.py "\bheat_loss_coefficient\b" custom_components/ | grep -v "house_heat_loss_coefficient\|effective_heat_loss_coefficient\|tank_heat_loss_coefficient"` returns every attribute reader. Disposition of each one reached from a two-zone configuration: `sysid.HousePlant.of_params`: closed in this diff. Already branched on `two_zone_enabled` (zones read instead): `coordinator._house_loss_terms`, `_space_demand_kw`, `_house_heat_loss_anchor`, `optimizer._floor_demand_at_target`, `_house_ua_kw_per_c`, `slab_settlement_cap`, `thermal_model.house_heat_loss_base`, `_valve_draw_circuits`, `_simulate_step_single` (single-zone step only), `_substeps_and_loss`, `battery` storage build, `sysid._held_state`, `sysid.arm` prior, `sysid.adoption_decision`. Inert by form: `optimizer.optimize`'s `forecast_heat_loss_factors` is `effective(base)/base`, and `effective_heat_loss_coefficient` is multiplicative in its base, so the ratio does not depend on it. Constructions, not readers: `sysid._sizing_model`, `_candidate_model`, `optimizer` line building `heat_loss_coefficient=u_up + u_lo`, `thermal_model` builders, `mixing_valve` parameter. The service `set_thermal_params` still accepts the key (it writes the parameter, which on two zones nothing reads); not a UI offer, left alone.

Carry 1's control and null control, and Carry 2's control, are figures below. No carry here waits on an owner or orchestrator ruling.

R10-MACHINERY-RATCHETS part 2 (the orchestrator opens this under group R10-MACHINERY-RATCHETS). Part 1b is on main, and so is part 1, the `policy_lint.mjs` config exclusion.

This part adds the machinery ratchet, `tools/audit/machinery_ratchet.py`. It applies a counting rule that classes each merge in a sliding window as production, machinery or record. It has two capped metrics, `nonproduction_merges` and `churn_per_kilo_product_lines`, each with a band, recorded in `dev/governance/config/machinery_budgets.json`. It also takes a right-first-time exemption, which requires evidence. The rest of the part:
- `budget_raise_gate.py` gains the file's SCHEMA entry.
- `governance.yml` and `policy-docs` gain one run line (`--check-event`), and `tests.yml` graders-head-copy gains the pathspec line.
- `prepr.sh` runs the ratchet locally.
- The instrument doc and the `ratchet-budgets.md` and `proposal-triage.md` policy text are updated.
- The script is classified in `closure.py`, `closures.json`, `entities.py` and `layout.json`.
- The in-tree mutant harness is `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_machinery_ratchet_mutants.py`.
- `field_coverage.mjs`'s entry for the script was registered by part 1b; this part drops its `pending` key, so it is strict here.

This repair (after the blocking review of 10bc3fe8) fixes two CI reds and pins the exemption-entry guards: the harness's inlined `repo_root` is now byte-identical to `tools/audit/repo_root.py`, and the self-test gains rows for a `bool` `before` and for each missing entry key.

## Head

`03e55806a5bf9f4dd33c20d192a53f0b84982e86` merges main `6777ec3` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`4fa863b557a51614acb55fac72d3e914f79ec70d` merges the authored code head `1e9c43f0d01842bb02486abbefd764da11fba273` and then merges origin/main `499162c89` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`1e9c43f0d01842bb02486abbefd764da11fba273` is the final head. It merges origin/main `c0b082bc4877` (main had moved since the previous head) and adds the repair commit. The `prepr.sh` run below was on this head against that main tip.

## Mutation proof

`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_machinery_ratchet_mutants.py`: the control is `unmutated: rc=0`, and the run ends with `RESULT 18 mutants: 18 killed, 0 survived, 0 stale`. Killing checks per mutant:
- `product-prefix`: a path under blueprints/ is product.
- `production-gt-0`: 2 production merges in 6 give 4 nonproduction.
- `record-all-paths`: a merge touching a record path and a tools path is machinery.
- `cap-plus-band-ge` and `cap-without-band`: over() refuses only past cap+band.
- `pr-mode-no-drop-oldest`: the candidate takes the newest slot and the oldest merge drops out.
- `pr-mode-candidate-ignored`: a candidate machinery merge past cap+band exits 1.
- `threshold-ge`: exemption: exactly 10% refuses.
- `evidence-not-checked`: exemption: 11% with a missing evidence path refuses.
- `absent-at-p-not-checked`: an entry added before its PR merged exempts nothing when that PR merges.
- `subject-number-not-matched`: exemption: an entry naming another pull request refuses.
- `subject-number-not-parsed`: positive control: an entry its own merge added takes that merge out of the window.
- `no-rename-detection`: null control: a pure move across the boundary leaves M1 and M2 identical.
- `no-whitespace-ignore`: a whitespace-only reformat of product code costs 0 product lines.
- `rename-charged-to-source`: a rename's lines are charged to its destination.
- `bool-before-accepted` (new): exemption: a bool `before` is not a number and refuses.
- `entry-key-missing-ok` (new): killed by the missing-key rows. With `if missing:` replaced by `if False:`, the next line raises KeyError `'pr'`, so the self-test fails.

## Null control

- The harness's unmutated copy passes its self-test (rc=0) before any kill is counted.

## Figures

- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/harness_headers.py`: ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED.

- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir $D`: the diff touches gate files, so the gate cannot scope it; CI runs the full suite.
- `python3 tools/audit/machinery_ratchet.py --check`: both metrics within cap + band. The window slides, so the instrument prints the figure and it is not quoted here.

## Unpinned sites

The ratchet's predicates are `tools/` sites. Mutation-autofix's lane does not mutate them, so they are pinned by the in-tree mutant harness above.

## Red checks

- `budget-raise-gate / budget-raise-gate`: red until the owner approves at the head. The gate reads `dev/governance/config/machinery_budgets.json`, a new file, as raises from None (`window_merges` and both caps with their bands), and cannot sign a new pinned value as routine. So the red is the owner's approval being owed, per `ratchet-budgets.md` and `fixer.md`'s rule that a raise needs the owner's explicit confirmation. These are the only new caps this PR records, and no other budget is raised. No cheaper detector exists: the gate exists to hold a new cap for the owner, and prepr's body check names it before the handoff.

Repaired in this head by copying the helper verbatim; the check is green locally. The cheaper detector is that check itself, which `tests/README.md` lists in the fast tier and which was not part of the scoped run last time, as the diff was FULL.
- `tests / nightly-status`: main-owned. The contract names this diff as touching what it reads (`.github/workflows/governance.yml` and `tests.yml`). The red is not caused by this diff's content; it reports the nightly lane's state on main. The cheaper detector is `ci_predict.py`, which prepr runs and which predicts none; no further detector is worth building, as `nightly-status` reads the nightly run's conclusion and nothing in a PR diff changes that.

It prints `DELIVERY STATUS OVERDUE -- 10 rowed, 10 pending, 2 overdue (overdue at 12 commits)`, naming the rows of #3181 and #3191, which this diff neither adds nor touches (this PR adds only its own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3208.md`). It grades the count of main commits since a pending row, so it reddens every PR head until those rows are cleared. No cheaper detector exists for this PR: it is a time-based staleness count on other PRs' rows, which `delivery-status-tracking.md` already governs, and nothing in this diff can clear it.
- `governance / policy-docs` went green when part 1b reached main. It is not expected red at this head.

## Forward-carry

none

## Friction

none

## Raise justification

This is not a raise of an existing cap. The file is new, and the gate reads each of its values as a raise from None. The caps sit at the window's measurement, recorded by the previous seat and re-recorded after each merge of main. Each cap is graded against cap + band, and `--check` reads both metrics within cap + band at this head.
- Payments tried: none apply. There is no existing cap to stay under, and nothing in the diff can be moved, shared or deleted to lower a cap that does not yet exist on main. The approval sought is the owner's.
- Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL

## Approval

Awaiting the owner's approving review. This diff touches policy (`dev/governance/rules/ratchet-budgets.md`, its generated `.claude/rules/` and `.cursor/rules/` copies, and `dev/governance/roles/proposal-triage.md`), and it adds new caps in `machinery_budgets.json`.

merges.body:
Part 1 of R10-TICK-LEVELS (carries 0-6, 8; carry 7, the topic-family barrier, and carries 9-12 are later parts), repair round 2 after the fix review's `blocked` verdict at d7e67e0d786c73315e769345cb6fbefba1c5434d. The tick's PR levels in one seam, `tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py`. Part of #201.

Carry 0 is the umbrella for 1-5 and 8 and needed no code of its own. APPROVAL-OWED (8922cbf97) and REVIEW STALLED (3a15e84a4) were already delivered and are not rebuilt.

What changed since the first round: `REVIEW OWED` skips the record branch (carry 1). A new `owed_levels` pass puts every open PR the pass can read in exactly one bucket (train, verdict-pending, fixer-round, waiting-on #M, verdicted, review-owed, owed, unreadable) from data the pass already reads, plus one `ls-remote` over the handoff refs and no new GitHub call, and prints one `OWED <kind> #N <head12> <reason>` line per owed PR (carries 2-6). Carry-8 defects are fixed (P82 gate-race line, a reviewer's `merge_train.py --self-test` no longer a second train, a null `started_at` is stuck). Repairs this round, by the review's findings:
- Block 1: the T3 seat mutant's anchor in `tools/audit/seat/r10_ledger_mutants.py` followed the `lg.review_owed(...)` call's new tail (the `getattr(rr, "RECORD_BRANCH", None)):` line and the `self.line` under it), so it plants exactly once and is killed.
- Block 2: fixtures pin the null controls and the survivors the review listed (below).
- O3: a failed git read in the blocked arm (`_handoff_newer` returning None) is now bucket `unreadable`, printed as `UNREADABLE: owed buckets (#N: ...)`, never `OWED fixer-round`.
- O4: the claim is narrowed. Every open PR the pass can read is in exactly one bucket; a draft, a PR with no head, the record branch and a PR whose comments were not read are counted on the count line's `; not bucketed: ...` tail instead, and a test pins the line.
- Class-open (ci_predict `self_test_hosts`): a host is a script whose source runs the self-test near the file by the `--self-test` flag or by a quoted `"self-test"` argv element (the subcommand spelling tests/entities.py uses for tests/lane_skip.py); comments and `self_test` table keys are not hosts. Each pair the rule still drops is classified below.

## Head

`eaef0f10742b15d3a8b2e99f754f8d7f9b6ff44e` merges main `6125b26` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`c46a9c6abe46e17a30fcfd9add85390dc9c603ac` merges the authored code head `36924c5c7a9aa58c53977623f146c6b4924047ac` and then merges origin/main `d7582ed40` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

36924c5c7a9aa58c53977623f146c6b4924047ac (code head, `origin/main` merged in at d7582ed404a87603bd02fefda610d7ebbe4181e1; `tools/pr/prepr.sh` ran once at this head, after that merge). The first-round head c9993ab55cbbac35cc440713d61ad9cc30b2cfa6 is its ancestor, so `handoff/r10-tick-levels-p1` moves by fast-forward.

## Approval

`dev/governance/roles/standing-dispatch.md` is unchanged this round: still one added sentence (a `record/autofix` PR is never dispatched a reviewer), 38 lines against a 39 cap and 505 tokens against 509 (`node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --budgets`). Policy: it merges on tvofi's approving review or under mandate 6329234399. No budget is raised.

## Mutation proof

Driver `ev/mutants_driver.py` of the review (extended with M33-M36 below), each mutant applied to one predicate, `python3 tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py --self-test` (or `tools/pr/ci_predict.py --self-test`) run, then restored. At the head, with the new fixtures, each of the review's survivors is red:
- M06 `return "train"` deleted: `null: a DIRTY, red PR in train ...`
- M10 blocked arm's newer-handoff exemption: `blocked arm: a handoff tip newer than the verdict ...`
- M11 `verdicted`: `null: a DIRTY, red PR with a merge verdict at its head ...`

- M24 FIRE-OWED's `FIRE_GRACE_MIN` grace: `carry 5 FIRE-OWED ...` (a payload younger than the grace prints nothing)
- M27 `self.owed_levels(S, prs)` deleted from the PRS pass: `a tick's PRS pass runs the level ...` (drives `prs()`, not `owed_levels`)
- M29 the record-branch skip in `owed_levels`: `O4: the count line names what it leaves out ...`
- M30 critical-path ordering: `the critical-path group's OWED line prints before ...`
- M33 (new) the O3 `newer is None` arm deleted: `O3: an unreadable handoff ref is UNREADABLE ...`
- M34 (new) the `not bucketed` tail deleted: the O4 check
- M35 (new) the quoted-`"self-test"` alternative dropped from the host rule: `ci_predict self-test: 1 failed` (the lane_skip-shape case)
- M36 (new) the old `self[-_]test` word restored: `ci_predict self-test: 3 failed`
- T3 itself: `python3 tools/audit/seat/r10_ledger_mutants.py --self-test` is `135 checks, 0 failed` (it was 1 failed); the other `r10_*_mutants.py --self-test` whose plant target this diff changes: none (only the ledger one plants in orchestrator_tick.py or ledger.py; the roster_ops, mandate_guard and stamp_round ones run 0 failed unchanged; deeplink and roster_sync take no `--self-test` flag and plant elsewhere).
The review's other mutants (M01-M05, M07-M09, M16-M20, M22, M23, M25, M26, M28, M31) stay red as before (review `ev/mutants.txt`).

## Null control

Unmutated tree: `orchestrator_tick self-test: 272 checks, 0 failed` (261 at the reviewed head; 244 at the base). New nulls: a DIRTY, red PR with a queue verdict at its head and no merge verdict prints no OWED and counts `train 1`; with a merge verdict, `verdicted 1`; on the dispatch record, `verdict-pending 1` (off it, one `OWED dirty` line); sharing a file with a lower open PR, or in a group after an open group, `waiting-on 1` (disjoint files, or no open PR in that group, one `OWED dirty` line); a blocked verdict 9 h old beside a handoff tip 30 min old is `fixer-round 1`, beside one 600 min old, one `OWED fixer-round` line; a failed handoff `ls-remote` is `unreadable 1` and an UNREADABLE line naming the PR. A mixed board of a clean PR, the record PR, a draft and a PR with unread comments prints `buckets: review-owed 1; not bucketed: comments unread 1, draft 1, record branch 1` and no OWED line. `ci_predict self-test`: a host that runs the file by `--self-test` or by a quoted `"self-test"` element is predicted; a comment saying "self-test" and a `('<file>', 'self_test')` table key are not.

## Figures

- `python3 tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py --self-test`: 272 checks, 0 failed (rule: the count of `check(...)` arms plus the file's other sections the instrument prints).
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/r10_ledger_mutants.py --self-test`: 135 checks, 0 failed.
- `python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --self-test`: 0 failed.
- `python3 /tmp/ev/hosts_diff2.py .` (the review's harness, extended to print each dropped pair's nearest self-test line and whether the head kept it): old rule 24 host pairs, the head's rule 14; `tests/lane_skip.py <- tests/entities.py` is KEPT. The 10 pairs lost are all prose or a table: dev/audit/rounds/round3/D6/claims.py and round4/D6/claims.py <- tests/harness_headers.py (comments naming claims.py, an instrument-self-tests remark), tests/hastub/homeassistant/const.py <- tests/entities.py (a comment naming homeassistant/const.py), tests/nightly_status.py, tools/audit/archscore/gate.py and tools/ci/gate.py <- tests/entities.py (a string at 29525-29529 and CI-job text; entities.py only checks the CI invocation string `python -I -S tests/nightly_status.py`), tests/throwaway_git.py, tools/audit/judge_batch.py and tools/coverage/coverage_tree.sh <- tests/entities.py (the `_SHELL_NOT_A_STEP` table at 29036-29040, whose `("tests/throwaway_git.py", "self_test")` key names a function; entities.py imports `throwaway_git_env` and `judge_batch.run`, never a self-test), tools/audit/seat/ledger.py <- tests/entities.py (the `ledger.py landed` string fixture, the first-round false host).
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED; `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`: 0 errors; `--budgets`: standing-dispatch.md within its caps.
- `D=$(mktemp -d); python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"`: MODE: SCOPED -- 2 script(s) run.
- Toolchain: numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1 against tests/requirements-ci.txt (cloud-setup --check OK); no golden is touched, CI stays the authority.

## Red checks

At the reviewed head d7e67e0d786c73315e769345cb6fbefba1c5434d, the whole check-run set (55 runs, one page):
- governance / instrument-self-tests (job 126655674435): this diff's own. Cause: the first-round diff rewrote the `lg.review_owed(...)` call site that the T3 seat mutant in r10_ledger_mutants.py anchored on (`FAIL T3_review_owed_silent: anchor occurs once in tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py`, then `r10_ledger_mutants self-test: 135 checks, 1 failed`), repaired in this round. The cheaper detector exists: `python3 tools/audit/seat/r10_ledger_mutants.py --self-test`, about 2 s, which `tools/pr/prepr.sh` and `ci_predict` do not run for a changed plant target; its standing cost is that 2 s per diff touching a plant target. A second instance (#2865, #3200) is routed to R10-FRICTION-RECORDS, not built here.
- gate (runs 126678757606 and 126677715719) and pr-contract / pr-contract (126678318527 and 126677286569): downstream of the one red above (the aggregate gate, and the contract's own refusal naming it); no cause of their own.
- tests / nightly-status (job 126655674359): main's, not this diff's (this diff reaches nothing nightly_status reads; the review reached the same conclusion).
Every other concluded run at that head is success or skipped. The check-runs at this round's head do not exist yet; the next run's set is the proof.

Round 1 (no earlier verdict on #3200). Measured at d7e67e0d786c73315e769345cb6fbefba1c5434d (code head c9993ab55cbbac35cc440713d61ad9cc30b2cfa6; the only difference is `dev/programme/delivery/3200.md`). `git diff $(merge-base)...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty, so the contract is current.

## Block

1. **The head is RED and the red is this PR's.** `merge_train.py classify` at this head exited 1: `RED d7e67e0d786c73315e769345cb6fbefba1c5434d pending: none red: gate` (`ev/classify.txt`). The gate is red because `governance / instrument-self-tests` (job 126655674435) fails with `FAIL T3_review_owed_silent: anchor occurs once in tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py` and then `r10_ledger_mutants self-test: 135 checks, 1 failed` (`ev/instrument-self-tests.log` lines 1758-1775). The PR rewrote the `lg.review_owed(...)` call site in `orchestrator_tick.py`, and that line is the T3 seat mutant's anchor (`tools/audit/seat/r10_ledger_mutants.py:91`). I reproduced it locally: `r10_ledger_mutants.py --self-test` gives 1 failed at this head and 0 failed at base 8e90d81 (`ev/r10_ledger_mutants_head.txt`, `ev/r10_ledger_mutants_base.txt`). This is the same failure #2865 had. The body says `## Red checks: none`, and the `pr-contract` run that started after every workflow had concluded (job 126678318527, started 15:38:33) refused it: `check governance / instrument-self-tests is red and ## Red checks does not name it`. A cheaper detector exists and costs about 2 s: `python3 tools/audit/seat/r10_ledger_mutants.py --self-test`, the one #2865's body named. Hence `root-cause-detectable`. Repair: move T3's anchor and plant in `r10_ledger_mutants.py` to the new call shape, keeping its teeth (the plant must still silence REVIEW OWED). Then answer the red in `## Red checks`.

2. **The PR's own tests do not pin the null controls the brief asks about.** The brief asks one question first: whether a PR in train, verdict-pending or waiting-on prints no OWED line. The code does the right thing today: my own harness (`ev/owed_null.py`, 9/9 ok) shows a DIRTY+red PR in each of those three buckets prints none. But the PR's self-test does not pin any of these arms. I deleted each one in turn and `orchestrator_tick.py --self-test` still printed `261 checks, 0 failed` (`ev/mutants.txt`):

- M06: `return "train"` deleted. 0 failed. The P279 fixture `o_pk0` checks only `== []`, and a merge verdict at the head falls through to `verdicted`. So the body's "a PARK before the last STARTED stays in `train`" is not what the check checks.
- M12: `return "verdict-pending"` deleted. 0 failed. A dispatched PR that is DIRTY would then print `OWED dirty`, a false positive that nothing catches.
- M13 / M14: the waiting-on file-overlap arm and the waiting-on after-edge arm deleted. 0 failed each. The same false-positive path is open.
- M27: `self.owed_levels(S, prs)` deleted from the PRS pass. 0 failed. The fixtures call `owed_levels` directly, so nothing checks that the feature runs in a real tick.

All four are production lines this PR adds and its "What changed" names: the bucket set and "every open PR in exactly one bucket". Repair: add fixtures that put a DIRTY or red PR into train (with no merge verdict), verdict-pending and waiting-on (both edges) and assert no OWED line plus the named bucket. Add one `run()`/PRS-level check that an OWED line appears.

A third item (step 6, class-open) is listed under Findings: the ci_predict regex also drops a real host that runs a self-test without the flag spelling.

## Findings

- Recurrence: this is the second time a seat mutant's anchor has gone red in `instrument-self-tests` (#2865, now #3200), and `tools/pr/prepr.sh` and `ci_predict.py` still do not run the `r10_*_mutants --self-test` whose plant targets a changed file. R10-FRICTION-RECORDS already holds the owed root-cause record and its candidate ci_predict instrument arm. This second instance strengthens that group's cost test (P(recurrence) is now measured at two) and belongs in its brief. Carry: R10-FRICTION-RECORDS | #201 | O1 | dismissed: none, the group's own carry
- Class-open on `tools/pr/ci_predict.py` `self_test_hosts`. Requiring `--self-test` drops `tests/entities.py` as host of `tests/lane_skip.py`. Yet entities.py really runs that self-test as a subcommand: `entities.py:20327-20330` runs `subprocess.run([sys.executable, …/lane_skip.py, "self-test"])`, and `lane_skip.py:525` parses `self-test` as a subparser. Over every tracked tools/tests/dev/audit script, the old rule gave 24 host pairs and the new rule gives 13 (`ev/hosts_diff.py`, `ev/hosts_diff.txt`). Of the 11 lost, `lane_skip.py <- tests/entities.py` is a real run. The others look like prose or table matches (`throwaway_git.py`, `judge_batch.py`, `nightly_status.py`, `ledger.py` at 28492, the two round-3/4 `claims.py` via harness_headers); I did not open each one. The body's null control ("hosts that really name `--self-test` are still predicted") does not cover a host that runs the self-test under another spelling. Repair: match the invocation forms that really run it (`--self-test`, a `"self-test"` argv element, an in-process `self_test()` call) and add the lane_skip shape as a fixture. Carry: R10-TICK-LEVELS | #3200 | O1 | dismissed: none, owed in this PR's next round
- The rest of the mutants this PR leaves unpinned: M10 (the blocked arm's `newer` handoff exemption), M11 (`verdicted`), M21 (BODY-AHEAD's `in_head` conjunct), M24 (FIRE-OWED's `FIRE_GRACE_MIN` grace), M29 (`owed_levels`' own record-branch skip) and M30 (critical-path ordering of OWED lines). Each survives deletion with 0 failed. Carry: R10-TICK-LEVELS | #3200 | O2 | dismissed: none, owed in this PR's next round
- `_bucket`'s blocked arm treats `_handoff_newer` returning None (a failed git read) as "no newer handoff". It then falls through to the age test, so an unreadable read can print `OWED fixer-round` instead of an UNREADABLE line. That breaks the tick's own convention (`unreadable` everywhere else). Carry: R10-TICK-LEVELS | #3200 | O3 | dismissed: none, owed in this PR's next round
- The body says "every open PR in exactly one bucket", but drafts, the record branch, and PRs whose comments were not read land in no bucket, and the count line sums only the PRs that do. My mixed board of 8 open PRs (1 record) summed to 7. The code is consistent; the claim needs its exclusions stated, or the count line should name them. Carry: R10-TICK-LEVELS | #3200 | O4 | dismissed: none, owed in this PR's next round

## Evidence

- RESULT head d7e67e0d786c73315e769345cb6fbefba1c5434d: `orchestrator_tick self-test: 261 checks, 0 failed`; `ci_predict self-test: 0 failed` (body figures re-derived; `ev/head_checks.txt`).
- RESULT mutation: of 31 applied orchestrator_tick/ledger/ci_predict mutants, 20 turn a named check red. R10-CLOSEOUT-CLEANUP, instrument half (Part of #201; issues #2505, #2727, #2728). Lands the closeout instrument and folds in the two fly-ins: `prune_refs.py` (batched push arm, keep guards, `--topic`) and `worktree_gc.sh` (unpushed keep, `on-remote` class, a leased class A branch delete, a leased worktree removal for classes A and B, and now a leased orphaned-seat removal for class C). `closeout.py` step 3 uses the same lease. The `--apply` run is the orchestrator's final act and was not run here. Merging this sets the group carries-open, not done.

Carry dispositions, for every carry of the group's roster entry (`dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json`, numbered from 1 in roster order). origin/main's copy holds 7 carries, and the round roster ref handoff/audit-r10-roster, which the review packet reads, holds 9 (`carry` length 9 at 386f291d8). All 9 are named:
- Carry 1 (delete the probe refs for #2654 #2656 #2657): residue-no-pr in `prune_refs.py`'s plan, deleted by the final run. No new rule.
- Carry 2 (the `--apply` run is a separate, last step, the orchestrator's, roster-gated): `closeout.py` refuses while any other group is open, naming each one. Arms and mutants `closeout-1` and `closeout-2`.
- Carry 3 (folded R10-FLY-PRUNE-REFS, issue 2727): the batched push arm (0 gh calls, tags before deletes, every delete leased at the planned sha and atomic per chunk, null control 2N), and the `claude/*`, open-group `design/` and age keeps. Its inner carries (dispatch/`brief/` residue, stranded handoff refs) fall to the same plan as archive-delete residue.
- Carry 4 (folded R10-FLY-WORKTREE-GC, issue 2505): the `unpushed` keep on both the classify and apply paths, and the `on-remote` class with its cwd, fetch and lsof controls. Class A's branch delete is leased at the head the porcelain read. Every worktree removal, class A and class B, is leased at that head too. The class C orphaned-seat removal is leased at the HEAD read in the orphan's own `wt/` (this round).
- Carry 5 (s9 script census, `prune_refs.py --topic <t>`): archive-then-delete, refused on a `+` cherry line or an open PR. Mutants `prune_refs-5` and `prune_refs-6`.
- Carry 6 (plan-regain study, build the tooling now, run last): the instrument lands here. The `--apply` run is not made.
- Carry 7 (s9 local cleanup: worktree_gc "eligible 0, kept 131" at 7.8 GiB free): not built here. It needs a seat-branch to PR-topic mapping read from the live PR list, a configurable seats root and a class for plain repo copies with no `.git`. Its text, failing test and null control already sit as this group's `carry[6]` in the roster, which is where it is routed. It stays pending there, so the group cannot be set done while it is neither built nor re-carried (`carry_audit.py roster` reads a pending carry on a done group as STRANDED).
- Carry 8 (closure check, s11 replan: give every entry of the carry files under `dev/programme/carries/` its destination or answering commit before the closure stamp): not built here, and out of scope. It is a pre-stamp act over files this diff does not touch, and it sits as `carry[7]` of this group on handoff/audit-r10-roster, where it stays pending.
- Carry 9 (`worktree_gc.sh` keeps any worktree a live process has its cwd in, on every removal arm: call `cwd_inside` on classes A and B as well as `on-remote`): not built here. It adds a keep to two removal arms, which is new behaviour outside this round's brief ("one site, one self-test case, one mutant"; "do not widen scope"). This round's class C lease does not touch it: a lease keeps a worktree whose HEAD moved, and a cwd holder that has not committed moves no HEAD. It sits as `carry[8]` of this group on handoff/audit-r10-roster, where it stays pending, with its fixture arms and mutant as written. Like carries 7 and 8, the group cannot be set done while it is neither built nor re-carried.

Design notes: `--topic`'s `git cherry` refusal covers `handoff/` code refs only, since body and dispatch refs are orphan commits that always carry a `+`. Local branches holding commits no remote or tag has are never deleted.

The class this PR closes is "a delete with no lease removes something that moved after the read, so a commit or tip made after the read is lost". Earlier rounds closed it in `prune_refs.py`, closeout's local branches and worktrees, worktree_gc's class A branch delete and `remove_worktree` (classes A and B). The fix review at 5aae1e12 (`Fix review: blocked 5aae1e12ea1dea099edc87f94a914a33eabd1baf class-open`) found it open at class C, the orphaned-seat `rm -rf`. This round closes it there:
- `worktree_gc.sh` class C now reads the orphan's own HEAD once, right after the branch read, for both the attached and the detached arm (`ohead`). A wt that git reads as a checkout but whose HEAD does not resolve is kept as `unreadable-head`. Before the `rm -rf`, the removal deletes that HEAD with the value read: `git -C <wt> update-ref --no-deref -d HEAD "$ohead"`. That is the same atomic local lease `remove_worktree` uses. If a seat committed after the read, the lease refuses, `worktree_gc: FAILED to remove <seat>: its HEAD is no longer <sha>, kept` is reported, and the seat stays with its commit. On an attached HEAD, git compares the old value with the resolved branch tip, and deleting the symbolic HEAD leaves the branch ref itself in place (measured on git 2.43: stale old value refused, fresh one deletes `.git/HEAD`, `refs/heads/main` file untouched). For an orphan that is a worktree of another checkout, the branch therefore survives in that checkout. A wt that git cannot read as a checkout (the pruned class, `seat-orph-old` in the self-test) has no HEAD to hold a commit and goes unleased, as before.
- Alternatives: keeping every orphan whose wt is a git checkout would also close the race, but it re-opens the 9.5 GB class the instrument exists for, since every merged orphan is a git checkout. Re-reading HEAD just before `rm -rf` narrows the race and does not close it. The lease is the existing mechanism (`remove_worktree`), applied in the one place it was missing.

## Head

`5a8fd981f53c00dc69836d23ab7273493c37f8fc`. ## Re-cut

The scope is only what the 5aae1e12 verdict names: the unleased class C orphaned-seat `rm -rf` in `worktree_gc.sh` (one site, one self-test case, one mutant), the corrected class C disposition, and `## Red checks` read at the PR head. Nothing else was widened. The verdict recommended a split or a re-cut, and the brief took the re-cut.

## Mutation proof

`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py M0 closeout-1 closeout-2 closeout-3 closeout-4 prune_refs-1 prune_refs-2 prune_refs-3 prune_refs-4 prune_refs-5 prune_refs-6 prune_refs-7 prune_refs-8 prune_refs-9 prune_refs-10 worktree_gc-1 worktree_gc-2 worktree_gc-3 worktree_gc-4 worktree_gc-5 worktree_gc-6 cloud_relay-50 cloud_relay-51 cloud_relay-52 cloud_relay-53 cloud_relay-54 cloud_relay-55 cloud_relay-56 cloud_relay-57`, run at b1320783, printed M0 `0 seat step(s) red`, all 28 mutants KILLED, `RESULT survivors=0`, rc 0. Between b1320783 and the head, `worktree_gc.sh` gained only comment lines (`git diff b1320783 7f80e2dc -- tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh`, every changed line an added `#` line), and the merge leaves the four instrument and harness files byte-identical. Main's three changed `governance.yml` lines each add `--no-renames` to an `echo` that prints a restored-file count, and none is a `tools/audit/seat` step that M0 runs. The 27 earlier ids stay KILLED (`worktree_gc-1..5`: 105 checks, 5, 2, 2, 3 and 17 failed; `closeout-1..4`: 28 checks, 6, 5, 1 and 2 failed; `prune_refs-1..10`; `cloud_relay-50..57`).

The property itself is shown on real git: the reviewer's harness run against the mutated file gives race `RESULT race=1 orphan-detached-moved-head-lost=1` and null `=0`.

## Figures

Its git stub makes the seat commit right after the first `-C <wt> rev-parse HEAD` read, which is the class C `ohead` read in both trees. Results:
  - at the head 5a8fd981: race `RESULT race=1 orphan-detached-moved-head-lost=0`, with `worktree_gc: FAILED to remove $T/seats/seat-a: its HEAD is no longer <read sha>, kept` and `seat wt now: present`; null `RESULT race=0 orphan-detached-moved-head-lost=0`, `seat wt now: removed`.
  - at the PR head 5aae1e12 (`git show 5aae1e12:tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh`): race `=1`, null `=0`. At the previous merge base a45cf7f5: race `=1`, null `=0`. That is the verdict's result.
  - with mutant `worktree_gc-6` applied to the head: race `=1`, null `=0`.
- `bash tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh --self-test` -> `worktree_gc self-test: 105 checks, 0 failed` at 5a8fd981. - `classify()` class B (detached worktrees: the merged-ancestor path and the new `on-remote` path) calls `remove_worktree` -> `git worktree remove --force "$1"` after the read of `$head`, with no lease. A detached worktree's HEAD is the only ref holding a commit made on it. A seat that commits there between the read and the remove loses that commit, because nothing references it any more.
- The body's class enumeration covers this site wrongly. It says `worktree_gc.sh remove_worktree's worktree remove --force: no ref is deleted. The branch ref and its commits survive the removal`. That holds for class A only. Class B has no branch ref, and the worktree's own HEAD is deleted with it.

merges.subject: Merge pull request #3205 from tvofi/fix/r10-hotfix-gate-stale-jobs
merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-STALE-JOBS: gate re-reads this run's lagging job list
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-GATE-STALE-JOBS, repair round 3 of #3205 (body re-taken). `tools/ci/gate.py` published red verdicts for jobs that had already finished, because it read them from a stale Actions jobs listing.

**Cause.** The jobs listing lags the run graph. The ordering is sound: `gate` needs `prelude` and `pr-contract`, and `pr-contract` needs every unit. So by the time `gate` starts, every job it reads as unfinished (or does not see at all) has finished. The independent RCA seat measured this on handoff-wip/r10-rca-gate-stale (`dev/audit/rca/r10-gate-stale-jobs.md` at `9b0df6105`): 14 false reds over 8 days. Round 1's re-read matched only own `PENDING`, which covered 3 of the 14. The other 11 were `FAIL prelude: None` (10, from the prelude check in `gate()`) and own `ABSENT` (1).

**Fix (round 2).** Round 1's `lagging()` becomes `lag_bound(why)`. It returns the number of seconds `judge()` may keep re-reading, and 0 unless **every** reason is this run's own listing-lag reason:
- own `PENDING (this run)`: up to `GATE_WAIT_MAX_S` (720 s), as in round 1;
- **a prelude listed but unfinished**. `read_api` now passes the prelude job's `status` along with its `conclusion`, and `gate()` writes `prelude: PENDING (this run)` only when the prelude is listed with a status other than `completed`. That reason shares the 720 s bound. A prelude that is not listed at all still reads `prelude: None` and gets no wait;
- **own `ABSENT (this run)`**: up to the shorter `GATE_ABSENT_MAX_S` = 2 x `POLL_S` (120 s). Its one measured lag is 20 s. A structural absence, such as a renamed job, is absent on every run, so its wait is kept short.

What round 1 built is kept: a lagging job never reads as success, so an exhausted bound still FAILs; any other reason beside a lag reason (a real failure, a skip, a deferral mix) is published at once, with no wait. One addition: a cleared lag leaves a step-summary note, `listing lag: <first reason> re-read for <n> s`. This is the RCA's countermeasure 4, so the next incident cluster leaves a record. The 10-30 cluster left none.

**The bound.** I kept `GATE_WAIT_MAX_S` at 720. With 60 s polls the last read lands at exactly 720 s, so the measured 704 s prelude lag (41876634563, a lower bound) clears at that read: harness shape 3 passes, having waited 720 s. A longer bound does not fit the job. `ci.yml`'s `gate` has `timeout-minutes: 15`, and the self-test pins `GATE_WAIT_MAX_S + POLL_S + 120 <= 900`. Raising the timeout would change the pinned `ci.yml` graph to cover lags longer than any measured. A lag past 720 s stays a FAIL, which is safe: gate-sweep re-judges it. The RCA also advises against widening the bound on these numbers.

**ABSENT null (workset).** Own `ABSENT` is written only when a unit is in this run's own workset and its job is missing from the listing. A unit outside the workset never reaches that line: `gate()` skips the run as a source and writes `<unit>: no run at this head judged base ...`, which is not a lag reason. Self-test `null (workset): an edit run lists no code unit; that is no ABSENT and no wait` drives that case through `judge()`: an `edited` event, a body-only listing, no other run. It asserts no `ABSENT` reason and `naps == []`.

**Prelude disposition (root-cause constraint 3).** A prelude listed unfinished waits: `prelude: PENDING (this run)` shares the 720 s bound, and a prelude that really failed reads `FAIL prelude: failure` after the re-read (41094975103 shape). An unlisted prelude stays `FAIL prelude: None` with no wait, since it is not a lag reason; the self-test null `prelude not listed at all is no lag, no wait` pins it.

Alternatives, and why each lost:
- Treat an own unfinished or unlisted job as passed, since its needs ran it. Unsound: 3 of the 6 PENDING-only attempts hid a real failure (RCA section 3), and the 41094975103 shape (prelude really failed) would pass.
- Wait on an unlisted prelude too. The brief rules this out: an unlisted prelude is not "listed unfinished". Keeping `prelude: None` for it leaves the cross-check's meaning unchanged.
- One bound for ABSENT and PENDING (round 1 rejected a separate shorter bound; the head now adds one, `GATE_ABSENT_MAX_S = 2 * POLL_S`, for own-ABSENT only, because the RCA measured a 20 s ABSENT lag against a structural ABSENT, such as a renamed job, that is absent on every run and would otherwise cost 12 min on every run; RCA countermeasure 3). The self-test now pins the split: the mutant `ABSENT bound = WAIT bound` is killed (Mutation proof).
- Another endpoint (`GET /actions/jobs/<id>`, check-runs). The RCA could not measure that either is fresher, so it would be an unverified assumption.

Roster carries on this group, each answered:
- Carry 1 (e67341cc, prelude None and own ABSENT not re-read): closed in this diff. `lag_bound` covers a prelude listed unfinished and own ABSENT; finder's harness 0 of 9 mismatches at the head (Null control).
- Carry 2 (e350d851, `codescan_wait.py` own-run path): read here, not measured; carried on in `## Forward-carry`, first item.
- Carry 3 (d0916ca4, `pr-contract.yml` red list): read here, not measured; carried on in `## Forward-carry`, second item.

merges.body:
R10-COP-GATE part D: the ceiling probe's learned top now reaches the plan, as the approved round-2 design rules (`design/R10-COP-GATE` 72902290879c, `dev/programme/designs/R10-COP-GATE-D.md`, fix (a): the plan carries the band it was solved on). Before this change the store's median was published and read by no solve. A pump metered at 3.0 kW behind a configured 5.0 kW still had every plan book 5.0 kW steps, and the arbiter mapped them on the 5.0 kW band.

What changed:

- `draw_range.solve_band(draw, params, cap, now_s)` is the one ruling on the range a solve books. It returns the design's rule table as a frozen `SolveBand` with `source`, `reason` and the evidence. The 15 % rule lives only here (`AGREE_TOLERANCE`); the accessor `learned_max_kw` stays raw (item D1). `planned_range`'s and the module's docstrings now say the window's range is diagnostics only (item D2).
- `coordinator._solve_record` computes the ruling once per solve and hands it to `_solve_hubs(band=...)`, which applies it to the **solve copy only**. A configured row adds no field, so the copy is the hub's figures byte for byte. The what-if caller gets its own ruling there. `SolveRecord.band` carries it, and the plan's one writer stamps it: `replace(result, solve_band=record.band.as_dict())`. `_learning_view` publishes the live plan's stamp as `pump_max_power`.
- `optimizer.OptimizationResult.solve_band` is the new field (empty means the hub's band). `_warm_start_starts` clips the previous plan to the solve's top (item D6).
- `pump_arbiter._band_kw` maps a plan step by the plan's stamp, and an experiment's step (`system_identification`) by the hub's band (invariant 1, item D5).
- `sensor.ModelStatusSensor` publishes `pump_max_power` (configured, planned and learned tops, sample count, newest-sample epoch). It also publishes `pump_max_power_source` and `pump_max_power_reason` as top-level codes. Each code has its user string under the entity's `state_attributes` in `strings.json`, `en.json` and `sv.json` (carry 6). This departs from the note in one way: the note names one `pump_max_power` row. Home Assistant translates only top-level attribute values, so the two codes ride beside the row, and the evidence stays in it.
- Carry 0: `translations/en.json`'s `options.step.entities_pump.data_description.pump_duty_mode` now equals `strings.json`'s. Why the parity check missed it: `tests/entities.py`'s "en.json matches strings.json exactly" compared **keys only** (`all_keys`). It is renamed to what it checks, and a new check pins en.json to strings.json leaf for leaf, with its null controls in the check.
- Payment: `_record_manual_release`, a 17-line method that never read `self`, moves out of `HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator` to module level. That pays for the three class lines the wiring adds. The budgets are re-recorded downward in their own commit, with the reason in the commit message.

Invariant 1 (the hub never carries the learned top) holds by construction and is pinned: the configured figures still key the fold, the COP gates, sysid's commanded power and the other hub readers below.

Roster carries, 1-based as the roster holds them; the brief numbers them from 0:

- Carry [1] (brief 0, strings/en parity): fixed, and its check added (above). Red at the base, green at the head.
- Carry [2] (brief 1, COP refusal codes rendered): pinned by "carry 1: a counter install with no electric counter publishes unaligned_meters" with its aligned-span null. It already held at the base; see Null control.
- Carry [3] (brief 2, the learned top's consumer): this change. Asserted at eleven and twelve samples through the rule table, the live cycle and the harness. The synthetic known-maximum pump and the gate-held draw above idle are the producer's checks, green at the head.
- Carry [4] (brief 3, `_propagated_slab`): measured first, and the defect is confirmed. `draw_range.space_draw_kw` takes no dwell input, so an interval that ran 0.75 h of hot water and switched back to space before the read books the whole running draw as space heat. The probe gives +2.250 kW on a 3.0 kW interval, against +0.000 for the all-space null (`## Figures`). The rule is the design choice the carry names: prorate by the dwell's space hours through `heat_energy.meter_of(coord).attribution(...)` (`ran_hot_water`), or fall back to the plan's trajectory. The approved part D note keeps it out of part D ("The `_propagated_slab` lead: not absorbed": part 6's seam, a part E), so this change leaves `_propagated_slab` as it is. The measurement answers the carry. The build waits for the orchestrator's part E group, and nothing new is raised here.
- Carry [5] (brief 4, the orchestrator's s9 rulings): (1) the plan books the learned top only when it is measured below the configured nameplate; the configured value stays the hub's, and the published reason names the top the plan used. (2) It runs after R10-CEILING-PROBE (merged at the base), with `draw_range.py` in the files. (3) It takes the round-2 note's fix (a). Item D4's classification is below, and the probe step at the configured maximum still writes the heat level ("item D5").
- Carry [6] (brief 5, the `optimizer.py` field and the `pump_arbiter.py` band read): both edited exactly as the note states.
- Carry [7] (brief 6, the user strings): each `source` and `reason` code is translated in `strings.json`, en and sv, and "carry 6" pins every code. No card file changed. R10-UX-HEALTH also edits `strings.json` and the translations: whichever merges second re-runs steps 2-8.
- Carry [8] (brief 7, the producer's interface): built against `DrawRange.learned_max_kw(now_s)`, `ceiling_since()` and `CEILING_MIN_SAMPLES` (`CEILING_LAPSE_DAYS` through `learned_max_kw`). The probe's commanded power stays `params.max_electrical_power` on the hub.
- Carry [9] (brief 8, set-point-to-draw linearity): not measurable in this seat. The ceiling store holds only ceiling-commanded draws, so it cannot speak to intermediate set-points. The window's `(drawn, asked)` samples from ordinary operation exist only on a live install, and no diagnostics bundle or live store is available to a cloud seat. No correction is built and no refusal number is recorded. The carry stays this group's, open, until a live bundle (D15's route) can be measured.

The claim files are as the PR head had them: `claimed_drift.txt` claims the five coord fixtures (`claims-for: 7.1.1`), `card_claimed_drift.txt` is untouched.

Roster carries 7, 12, 15, 16, 19 and 20 of this part are not built here and stay open on the roster. Round 2 repair of verdict/3191 round 1 (blocked: step 3f3 unleased, `closures_owes_slot` undriven). Closes #2267.

## Mutation proof

- B, `[ "$k" = scoped ]` changed to `[ "$k" = full ]` in `closures_owes_slot`: red the same row and `and a full diff owes none (CI re-records every closure)`.

## Null control

- `closures_owes_slot` rows drive the production function over a throwaway repository whose `tests/closure.py` stub writes the case and scripts it is told: scoped with scripts and records-here gives 0; skip, full, records-here false, and scoped with empty `affected.scripts` each give 1 (the last is the null control for the scoped arm).

- 3f5 (register check, `fold_ledger.py`) stays unleased on purpose, stated in the code beside the step: it is light (about 0.5 s per call, the reviewer's own figure), so a queue wait would cost more than the work. 3f3 measured 234 s idle by the reviewer (`ev/step-timings.txt`, not re-measured here).

- Call-site rule: `grep -cE '^ *take_slot( |$)|&& take_slot$'` over the main flow equals 5 (mutants, field coverage, self-test, closures, diff mutants); the self-test row computes it.
- Heavy_skip-gated steps enumerated by `grep -n 'heavy_skip "' tools/pr/prepr.sh`: mutants (leased), field coverage (leased in this diff), register check (light, unleased by decision above).

## Block

1. **class-open: step 3f3 `field coverage`.** Carry 26, as the PR body's own index counts it, asks for the slot to be taken "just before the first heavy step that heavy_skip/selftest_owed/the scoped gate does not skip". `heavy_skip` gates three steps: 3a `mutants`, 3f3 `field coverage` and 3f5 `register check`. The diff calls `take_slot` before 3a, 3h, 6b and 6d', but not before 3f3 or 3f5. 3f5 measures about 0.5 s per call, so leaving it unleased is defensible, but the body does not say so. 3f3 is the most expensive step that is now unleased:
   - `node tools/policy/field_coverage.mjs` takes **234 s on an idle machine**, against 184 s for the mutants drive that the PR does lease (measured under load; `ev/step-timings.txt`, `ev/fieldcov-seam.txt`).
   - Plant: a one-line change to `.github/workflows/arch-score.yml` on this head. `heavy_skip mutants` returns skip (rc 0) and `heavy_skip "field coverage"` returns run (rc 1), with the reason "field coverage reads .github/workflows/arch-score.yml". The plan's case is `scoped` with 0 scripts (`ev/fieldcov-seam.txt`).
   - So a workflow-only diff, or any diff reaching `tests/structure.py`'s closure but not the mutants read-set, runs a ~4-minute step outside the four-slot cap. That reverses the old behaviour, where 1b leased the whole run. The body neither leases 3f3 nor rules it light, and the self-test pins exactly four call sites, so it holds that omission in place.
   - Repair: call `take_slot` in the else-arm of 3f3 (and of 3f5, or state why 3f5 is light). Update the four-call-site count row, and add a driven row: a plan where mutants skip and field coverage runs takes the slot before 3f3.

2. **mutation-vacuous: `closures_owes_slot`** (prepr.sh:773-783, new in this diff). This predicate alone decides whether the scoped recorder (`derive_closures.sh`, the step that P208 measured at 40 minutes) runs inside a slot. No self-test row drives it; `grep -n closures_owes_slot` shows only the definition and the one call site.
   - Mutant A: `return 1` as the first body line, so the recorder never takes a slot. Result: **477 passed, 0 failed** (`ev/mutant-A.diff`, `ev/mutant-A.summary`).
   - Mutant B: `[ "$k" = scoped ]` changed to `[ "$k" = full ]`. Result: **477 passed, 0 failed** (`ev/mutant-B.*`).
   - The "calls take_slot at ... (4)" row counts text only, so it stays green with the predicate gutted.
   - Repair: drive `closures_owes_slot` the way the 6b rows drive `closures_line` (a stubbed `closure.py affected` workdir). Cover scoped with scripts → 0, skip → 1, full → 1, `closures_records_here` false → 1, and a scoped but empty `affected.scripts` → 1 as the null control.

## Findings

- Follow-up: carry 26's "Measure before and after: slot-wait minutes per prepr over a day" is not measured. The body discloses this under `## Figures` ("Not measured"), and the "after" half can only be taken once the change is live. It is owed after the merge: count slot waits over one day of prepr logs with fixer logs included (carry 25's caveat), and compare them with the 29-of-35 baseline. Carry: R10-PREPR-CAP
- Follow-up: in `take_slot`, deleting `SLOT_TAKEN=1` survives (mutant C, 477 passed, 0 failed, `ev/mutant-C.*`). The idempotence row only drives a successful take, where the exported `HPO_SLOT_LABEL` makes the second call join anyway. On the WARN path (failed take), each later heavy step would retry `slot-take` and queue again, and append another `slot-unleased` marker. merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-CI-CRITPATH-4: price CI jobs by a per-runner speed probe
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-CI-CRITPATH-4: main went red at 8e90d8144 on `tests / ci-ratchet`, which read GREW critical_path_minutes 29.067 against 21.983 + 1.3 (CI run 41818271680), hours after #3180 re-based the grade. No work grew and no queue moved. The window lost its one fast-host draw of `tests / fast (3.14)`. #3180 priced each job at its fastest run in the 16-run window. Run 41491607650 (d40e377e5, `tests / fast (3.14)` 1223 s) aged out between the two newest windows, so the job repriced at its next-fastest draw, 1640 s, on the same work. The lane's 13 heaviest scripts, timed in the same runner, show its work flat across all 60 push runs: wall divided by its own scripts' speed has sd 2.9 %, against 17.5 % for raw wall. The fleet's mix moved: the fast class (factors 0.50-0.61) was drawn in 10 of 60 runs and in 1 of the newest 26.

**This PR does not turn main green, and merging it makes main red.** Under the probed pricing the pushes after the merge read GREW at 25.644 and 25.993 against 23.283 (replay.py section 6). They stay red until the owner decides under CLAUDE.md rule 2: re-record `critical_path_minutes` in the probed unit, with the reason in the commit message, or pay for it with work cut on the `tests / closures` path. Main is green today only by draw. Run 41870522291 (d7582ed40) read GREW 29.067 at 17:42:04Z and passed at 17:57:17Z on a rerun, at 21.883 (Red checks). Merging therefore trades a red that depends on the runner draw for a red that does not, until that decision. Round 2's body said this. The body posted on the PR still carried round 1's "the next push clears it without a re-record", and that is the text the round-2 review blocked on. This body replaces it.

The fix changes what the grade measures, so the runner draw cannot redden main:

- **A host probe in every heavy job.** `tests/host_probe.py` is fixed pure-Python work that refuses on its own checksum. It runs as its own step, `Probe the runner's speed (python X.Y)`, in `fast`, `arch-instrument`, `coverage` and `closures`, after setup-python under the job's matrix interpreter. The jobs API already carries step timestamps into `runs.json`.
- **Probed pricing (`job_price`).** A probed job's work in reference-host seconds is its wall × `PROBE_REFERENCE_S[python]` / its probe's seconds. It is priced at the median over the window. A job with no probe step is priced as before.
- **Pricing over the window's observed needs**, not each run's last-ending chain.
- **The reference is measured on the fleet, and pinned.** `PROBE_REFERENCE_S` is `{"3.13": 22.12, "3.14": 22.40}`. `tools/audit/seat/probe_bridge.py`'s stated rule derives it from this PR's own probed CI runs, which are committed as `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_hotfix_ci_critpath_4/fleet.json`. `probe_bridge.py --self-test` runs in governance's `instrument-self-tests` on every pull request. It re-derives the constant from the committed record and refuses any tree value that differs by more than the rounding. `tests/ci_ratchet.py`, `probe_bridge.py` and `fleet.json` are CODEOWNERS-owned, beside `tests/host_probe.py`.

**Why the probed grade reads higher: the unit changed, not the work.** The budget's 21.983 was recorded in fastest-draw minutes, each lane at its fastest run in the window. The probed grade prices each lane at the median of its reference-host seconds. `tests / closures` sets the probed path. Its "Re-record the closures" step took 1339 s at abf21ae34 on a probed 22 s host (job 126687075721, CI run 41862133797). The fastest draw in the budget's window, run 41506687984 at 871a20da1 (job 125487992256), took 1060 s in the same step. Its job wall was 1117 s, which is the lane's fastest draw that the replay prices at main. The work the two runs re-record differs by little. `tests/closures.json` holds the same 33 scripts at the budget's commit e1637032a, at 871a20da1 and at this head, and their recorded seconds rose 2.5 % (3974.9 -> 4073.0). The gap, 1339 / 1060 = 1.26, is the host that the fastest draw happened to be. On the fleet's three probed runs, `tests / closures` walls ran 1386..2360 s against reference 1339..1407 s (the review's figure). So the probe divides that host out, and the lane prices at about 23.3 min. Most of the 21.983-minute budget would go on that one job. That 1.26 ratio is a single pair of runs and not a measured host factor, because `tests / closures` has no host history before this PR: it is evidence, not a constant. The re-record that clears the red can only be taken in the probed unit once probed push runs exist. On the reviewer's harness, 16 copies of each probed run read 24.327 and 24.193, and a mixed window reads 25.6-26.0.

What clears the red, from the numbers:
- **A re-record of `critical_path_minutes` in the probed unit** (a raise of the number, not of the work). It needs the owner's confirmation, or a mandate scoped `budget-raise`, under CLAUDE.md rule 2 and `budget-raise-gate`. Its value is a measurement of probed push runs, so it cannot be recorded in this PR: no probed push run exists until this merges. Between the merge and that re-record, main reads GREW on every push (25.6-26.0 predicted while the window is mixed).
- **A payment on the closures path.** `tests / closures` alone prices at about 23.3 min probed, above the 23.283 limit with nothing ahead of it. The paths the review decomposed read 24.327 (prelude and `closure-scope` ahead of it) to 26.102 (with `refresh`, `validate-hacs` ahead and `ci-ratchet` after) against 23.283 (`review/3201` `evidence/decomp_out.txt`). A payment would have to cut 1.0-2.8 min of reference-host work from the closures re-record, out of about 22.3 min (1339 s). That is a closures-lane change, outside this group's scope.
- **Not** moving `PROBE_REFERENCE_S`, not pricing `tests / closures` on its fastest draw because it has no host history, and not a longer window. Each of these moves the statistic without changing the work. Round 1 was blocked as metric-gamed for exactly this on `PROBE_REFERENCE_S`.

Alternatives considered and why each lost:
- Re-record the budget at 29.x unprobed, or move the constant until main is green: both re-record merely to pass.
- Ship the probe steps but leave the grade unprobed until the budget records the probed unit, keyed by a unit field in `tests/ci_budgets.json`. That keeps main's draw-dependent red, which is what this hotfix answers, and it needs a budget-file change that a hotfix group should not make. It is offered to the owner as the conservative path in Forward-carry, not built.
- A local bridge, re-measured: it does not transfer. The probe is pure Python while the scripts are solver-heavy, so the ratio is per machine: 17.50 here, 18.29 on the reviewer's machine, 22.4 on the fleet.
- Computing `PROBE_REFERENCE_S` at import from `fleet.json`: this puts a harness data file in the grader's runtime path. A literal constant, pinned by a gate that re-derives it, keeps the grader's inputs explicit and its change reviewable.

Method of the reference (`probe_bridge.py`'s docstring):
- **3.14**: each probed `tests / fast (3.14)` job's host factor is the median, over its scripts of >= 20 s, of seconds / that script's 60-run median (`fast_scripts.json`). The job implies reference = probe × UNIT / factor, where UNIT 0.5645 is the fast class's median factor. The tree's value is the median over the three jobs (22.40, 22.43 and 20.72), which gives 22.40.
- **3.13**: 3.14's value times the interpreters' probe ratio on the fleet. That ratio is the median ratio of the 3.13 and 3.14 heavy jobs' probe seconds, paired by rank: 0.9875, which gives 22.12. The ratio of medians (1.070, giving 23.98) lost, because the fleet's two probe classes put its median in the gap. The self-test pins both readings.

## Head

`a74ae96ae4575dccc387d95a30755485c9d9b466` merges main `783d8dc` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`722037e783eff1d55d04ca575ae39bb8366c98c2`, the PR's head and this round's measured head. It is the orchestrator's merge of the code head `ae7fa1331e5dec7c022909199f5b241e8df2addc` (round 2's code, merged with origin/main d7582ed40) into the PR branch. Repair round 3 changes no code. The block was a body claim, and the head is the tree the round-2 review measured and passed on every instrument. origin/main is d7582ed40, unmoved since the head, so `tools/pr/prepr.sh` was run once, at this head. Figures were taken at this head, stamped `2026-11-04T18:50Z`. The body posted on the PR stayed at round 1's text through round 2: the update added the new head lines but not round 2's body at `handoff-body/r10-hotfix-ci-critpath-4` (d77767f1e).

## Mutation proof

No code moved this round, so the round-2 proof stands at this head. The reviewer re-ran the `tests/ci_ratchet.py` mutants on it and got the same counts. Each mutant was applied in place on the committed tree and restored with `git checkout`.
- `tools/audit/seat/probe_bridge.py --self-test` (8 checks; baseline 0 failed). `PROBE_REFERENCE_S["3.14"]` 22.40 -> 17.70: 1 failed (`-- 3.14: tree 17.7 derived 22.4`). 22.40 -> 27.10: 1 failed. `["3.13"]` 22.12 -> 17.48: 1 failed. 22.40 -> 22.42, one rounding step past: 1 failed. Rank pairing -> ratio of medians: 2 failed (`-- 3.13: tree 22.12 derived 23.98`). Wall-clock table row never read: 1 failed. Host factor not divided out: 2 failed.
- `tests/ci_ratchet.py --self-test` (65 checks). `seen = reference or walls` -> `walls`: 3 failed. Median -> min: 1 failed. Need edge -> `pass`: 15 failed. `reference_work` -> None: 5 failed (re-run by the reviewer, `review/3201` `evidence/mut.txt`).
- The `tests/entities.py` probe pins. `arch-instrument`'s step renamed `(python 3.15)`: `FAIL arch-instrument: probe steps ['3.15'], python ['3.14']`. `coverage`'s probe step deleted: `FAIL coverage: probe steps [], python ['3.13']`. The probe's work changed: the checksum pin `FAIL got 4289037`.

Failing test first: the fleet pin was written before the constant moved, with round 1's 17.50 / 18.92 still in place. It read `FAIL ... -- 3.13: tree 18.92 derived 22.12; 3.14: tree 17.5 derived 22.4`.

## Null control

- Unprobed, the change moves nothing. Across all 45 sliding windows of the 60 push runs, this head's grader minus main's reads 0.0 (review evidence). replay.py section 3 shows the same: `at main 29.067, this tree unprobed 29.067`.
- The post-merge GREW is not an artifact of the constant's rounding. In section 6, every probed job 1.9x slower (wall and probe) moves the grade by +0.456 and +0.949, inside the probe's rounding bounds of 1.166 and 1.181. 300 s more `tests / closures` work moves it by +5.027 and +5.144, all of it. Under the refuted one-machine 17.50 / 18.92 the same windows read 22.252 and 22.633. That is the control showing the constant is load-bearing, and why it is pinned rather than chosen.
- The closures-work figure has a control: the 33-script set compares with `diff`, which prints any difference and prints `SAME_SCRIPT_SET` only on equality.

## Figures

All taken at `722037e78`, stamped `2026-11-04T18:50Z`, with origin/main at d7582ed40.

- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_hotfix_ci_critpath_4/replay.py` -> `RESULT holds=1`. Its output is byte-identical to the reviewer's `review/3201` `evidence/replay_head.txt` (`diff` exit 0):
  - 1: at main, the newest window reads 29.067 and the window one run earlier 22.117. Run 41491607650 (1223 s) ages out between them.
  - 2: 60 runs, 13 scripts of >= 20 s. Fast class in 10 runs, 1 of the newest 26. UNIT 0.565. Wall sd 17.5 %, wall over factor sd 2.9 %.
  - 3: 45 windows. At main 19.967..29.783, unprobed 19.967..29.783, fast (3.14) probed 18.933..29.783. Newest window probed 20.35, with the other lanes at their fastest draw.
  - 4: newest window, every job probed (grade 19.118). Slow fleet 1.9x: +0.026 (1 s rounding bound 0.624). One hung run: +0.000. +300 s on fast (3.14) in the newest k runs, probed / at main: k=1 +0.00/+0.00, k=4 +0.18/+0.00, k=8 +1.93/+0.00, k=9 +2.30/+0.00, k=12 +2.46/+0.00, k=16 +2.70/+5.00.
  - 5: `fleet.json`, 3 probed fast (3.14) jobs imply 3.14 [22.4, 22.43, 20.72] -> 22.4. The 3.13/3.14 rank ratio 0.9875 gives 3.13 22.12, which agrees with the tree. The one-machine bridge reads 17.50, 22 % under.
  - 6: the merge push grades the newest 16 push runs, none probed: 29.067 against 23.283. Fleet run 41854976917 is not a stand-in (`tests / closures` did not succeed). As the merge run, 41862133797 reads 25.644 (GREW): 22.252 under 17.50 / 18.92, 1.9x slower +0.456 (rounding 1.166), +300 s closures +5.027. 41862145105 reads 25.993 (GREW): 22.633, +0.949 (rounding 1.181), +5.144.
- Closures work. Command: `for r in e1637032a 871a20da1 722037e78; do git show $r:tests/closures.json | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);k=set(d['closures']);print('$r',len(k),round(sum(v['seconds'] for s,v in d['recorded'].items() if s in k),1))"; done`. It prints `e1637032a 33 3974.9`, `871a20da1 33 3974.9`, `722037e78 33 4073.0`. The key sets compared by `diff` print `SAME_SCRIPT_SET`.
- Closures step seconds come from the jobs API (`list_workflow_jobs`, step timestamps). "Re-record the closures" took 1060 s in run 41506687984 (job 125487992256, job wall 1117 s, `PROOF_CONSUMED: false`) and 1339 s in run 41862133797 (job 126687075721, job wall 1399 s, probe step 22 s).
- Main run 41870522291 (d7582ed40). `tests / ci-ratchet` attempt 1 (job 126746954095) printed `GREW  critical_path_minutes: 29.067 (budget 21.983, band 1.3)` at 17:42:01Z. Attempt 2 (job 126755660076) printed `ok    critical_path_minutes: 21.883` at 17:57:17Z. Both gathered `push runs: 16 (16 CI)`.

merges.body:
Root-cause record for the `gate` reds that read a finished job as unfinished, beside R10-HOTFIX-GATE-STALE-JOBS. It changes no production code. It adds `dev/audit/rca/r10-gate-stale-jobs.md` and the finder's harness, under `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_stale_jobs/`. The five `.py` files there are measured closure members, recorded in `tests/closures.json` by the ci-autofix commit `79ac5afb`; `dev/audit/` is on `tests/closure.py`'s INERT list, but these files are not inert. This revision merges origin/main `d4e584ec6fe3bf017b91f69e3aaaf505c1a5365f` into the reviewed branch and changes no code.

**Cause.** The Actions jobs listing lags the run graph, and `gate` reads it once and treats not-completed as a verdict. The ordering is sound and no upstream wait lags.

**Process state (d).** The premise that the listing shows what `needs` saw is unstated and fails with the platform: 19 of 21 attempts sit inside or within 66 min of a declared GitHub Actions incident. Nothing noticed the 10-30 cluster.

**Cost test: build.** About 47 min of waiting (the doc sums each attempt-1 lag rounded up to the 60 s poll; the reviewer re-derives 45 min under that rounding and 39.7 min unrounded, the same verdict) against at least 224 min lost, over 8 days. **Countermeasure:** a bounded re-read over every listing-lag reason, plus a printed lag line. **Refused:** a status-page read or health lane, another endpoint, a train re-run, a new bug class.

## Head

`9f6d90798e73c858619bf01d78bc2f1a626b92a3` merges the authored code head `cf0a4a8a90ef3434693b41bd1c03885aa92d4610`.

cf0a4a8a90ef3434693b41bd1c03885aa92d4610

The branch head `79ac5afb80a921f3b4b13be6800dadf77ec7bec9` merged with origin/main `d4e584ec6fe3`. The figures below were measured at origin/main `d7582ed404a8` and read from files this merge did not touch.

## Mutation proof

The harness is the only code here. Both mutants are of a scratch copy, and both were restored by discarding the copy.

- The fix's predicate: with `lagging()` at handoff `a6305aa29` returning False, `harness.py` printed `mismatches 4 of 9` against 3 of 9 unmutated. The new BAD line is `41870314676 proof`.
- The harness's own predicate: with the listing never stale (`if clock[0] < stale.get(n, 0):` to `if False:`) over origin/main, it printed `mismatches 2 of 9` against 4 of 9. The `past the bound` shape turned BAD with `got PASS`.

## Null control

`harness.py`'s two null shapes, a fresh listing and a real red over a fresh listing, wait 0 s and answer PASS and FAIL `failure` on origin/main and on the handoff alike. The live probe (`probe.py`) made 143 listings over 18 polls and found 0 stale, so it detected nothing and settles nothing about other endpoints.

## Figures

Measured at origin/main `d7582ed404a87603bd02fefda610d7ebbe4181e1`, read 2026-11-04.

- Harness: `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_stale_jobs/harness.py` printed `mismatches 4 of 9` on this tree (rc 1, the defect present). Given an export of handoff `a6305aa29` as its argument it printed `mismatches 3 of 9`.
- Class count: `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_stale_jobs/tally.py dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_stale_jobs/reasons.jsonl` printed `scanned runs 1000 red gate attempts 383`, with `only-PENDING-this-run` 6, `only-prelude-None` 12, `ABSENT-this-run` 1 and `PENDING-plus-other` 2. The rule: `scan.py` over runs whose latest conclusion is `failure` or whose `run_attempt` exceeds 1, 2026-10-28 to 2026-11-04, every red `gate` attempt's Judge-step stdout. 37 of 1037 candidates stayed unread and first-attempt cancelled runs were not read, so these are floors.
- False reds, 14, and recovery, 170 min 4 s over 10 of them: `python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_stale_jobs/recover.py dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_stale_jobs/reasons.jsonl`. A false red is an attempt with every stale job's true conclusion `success`.
- Scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff origin/main` at this head printed `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out.` The harness files are measured closure members, so the gate runs the scripts that reach them; an earlier "0 script(s) run" read in this body was wrong.

## Red checks

Concluded reds over the whole check-run set (81 runs, every page) at `79ac5afb`, and one earlier red:

- `tests / closures`: red at `a615a76f` as UNDER-SCOPED, because the five new `.py` files under `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_gate_stale_jobs/` were in no measured closure. Answered by the ci-autofix repair `79ac5afb` ("ci: re-record closures"), which added them to `tests/closures.json`; the check reads success at that head. The cheaper detector exists: `tests/closure.py` and `prepr.sh` predict it before the handoff, so a repair was owed before the handoff and this body had wrongly said none.
- `pr-contract / pr-contract`: failure at `79ac5afb`, for exactly that reason (`check tests / closures is red and ## Red checks does not name it`). Answered by naming it here; the detector is `prepr.sh`'s body check, which `body_push.sh` runs.
- `gate`: failure at `79ac5afb`, on `pr-contract / pr-contract` alone, so it clears when that does. Same answer.
- `tests / nightly-status`: failure at `79ac5afb`, inherited from main; this diff reaches nothing it reads. Carry: none, outside this change.

## Forward-carry

- Handoff `a6305aa29` re-reads own PENDING only; `FAIL prelude: None` (10 false reds) and own ABSENT (1) still go red with no re-read. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-GATE-STALE-JOBS
