merges.body:
Keys the synthetic fixture's replay cost budget by runner class. The class signal is the run's own BLAS ruler: the median reference-solve `ref_ms` that each `cost` line prints. This round admits a fourth class, ref24, on its own CI readings. The class also keys `loop_cpu_ratio`, because ref24 reads 0.1282, over the shared 0.1278. A ruler in no band is still refused by name, and no default budget is assumed. The refusal is now probed in every gap between bands and at the two rulers CI read that no band admits. Closes #3129.

## Re-cut note

This is repair round 4 of #3174. Under the past-three rule this body is retaken whole, and round history is deleted. The finding: CI replay job 125461180429 (run 41498701363, at `acec536b`) ran on a runner whose ruler reads `ref_ms` 23.77-24.31. That is in no band of `COST_RUNNER_CLASSES`. So `cycle_cost` and its three doubled-arm checks failed on `runner class unknown`, and `pr-contract` failed because the body did not name `tests / replay`. The ruling for the later review: "CI exposed a runner class the r3 harness never ran; repair of the named band seam only".

What changed against `acec536b` is `tests/replay.py` only, in the band seam:
- `COST_RUNNER_CLASSES` gains `ref24` (22.64, 25.53).
- `COST_CLASS_BUDGETS` gains `ref24` `cpu_ratio` 3.630 and `loop_cpu_ratio` 0.1813.
- `COST_CLASS_READINGS` rows now name their metric and gain that job's two readings.
- New `COST_RULERS_REFUSED` (28.01, 34.35).
- `control:cycle_cost:runner_class_unknown` probes every gap between bands, a ruler under the lowest band, `COST_RULERS_REFUSED`, and NaN.
- The comments state the rule and the census.

No band is widened. No `*_budgets.json` is touched, nothing is refactored, and no existing budget moves.

**Why a band of its own, and not a wider band or a fallback.** The data says the per-class cost ratio is not a function of the ruler. ref24, the fastest ruler, reads synthetic `cpu_ratio` 2.5671, which falls between ref46 (2.27-2.42) and ref30 (2.61-2.81). The 28.0 runner (job 125000687320) sits 2.5 % under the ref30 floor, yet reads 1.8924, 0.67-0.72x of ref30's ratios. Grade that runner on ref30's 3.934 and its doubled arm, 3.8922, is not over budget. A widened band would therefore hide exactly the 2x regression the lane exists to see. Interpolating or borrowing a neighbour fails the same way. So the sound rule keeps r3's refusal: a class is admitted only on its own cited readings, and anything else fails closed by name. The standing cost is one red lane per new runner SKU. Its own `cost` lines are the readings that admit it.

## Head

`d52dc26f20770bed8fbf1b8fb0b154c42cc773d6` is the orchestrator's recarry of main into the previous head. It is not a clean merge of the live head and main (parent 1 372c21ac is not the live pull-request head 558c54a0), so prepr checked this head.

`372c21ac6cf2cc8b230a8ab8ec1d5b47de52bd6b` merges main `fad43b0` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`558c54a0f0f0617678caa9acc87a426a8ddb19bc` merges the authored code head `4de0f6565221868a0da1b5c88626f052e88d0eda` and then merges origin/main `b8e823699` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`4de0f6565221868a0da1b5c88626f052e88d0eda` fast-forwards `acec536b4ba1dc000126671f1f727defd21f1925` by three commits. Every local figure below was taken on that head. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflict against origin/main `871a20da138592ac892f4652a4f82992a6626783`, nor against `b8e823699981866383f1afa54ce708ded3419316` (read 2026-11-02T20:16:14Z), so main was not merged, as the brief allows a merge only on a conflict. Main's delta `871a20da..b8e82369` is 17 files of triage batches and delivery rows. It touches no `custom_components/` file and no replay file, so nothing the figures measure moved. Merge base: `38dcb6c5dbade5206f2fae885334483082f36d10`.

## Red checks

I read the whole check-run set at `acec536b` through the PR's `get_check_runs`: total_count 55, one page. Three concluded failure.
- `tests / replay` (job 125461180429). Four checks failed: `cycle_cost` and `sees a doubled cycle` cpu, memory and loop, each with `runner class unknown: ref_ms 23.83 lies in no band of COST_RUNNER_CLASSES`. Cause: a runner SKU that the r3 readings never sampled. Process state: the refusal worked as designed, failing closed at first sight and by name. Cheaper detector: none exists. A runner's SKU is assigned at job start and is unknowable before CI runs, and the 22-job census found no earlier ref24 reading at current code. The refusal is the detector, and its standing cost is one red per new class. Answered here by admitting the class on that job's readings.
- `pr-contract / pr-contract` (job 125483440211): `check tests / replay is red and ## Red checks does not name it`. Answered by this section.
- `gate` (jobs 125483784051, 125484217523): `FAIL pr-contract / pr-contract`. It follows pr-contract and has no cause of its own.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant is a `sed` edit to `tests/replay.py`, made at the head. The probe is `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 -B -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tests'); import replay; [print(n, ok, d[:120]) for n, ok, d in replay.controls() if 'class' in n]"`. After each run the file was restored and compared with `cmp` against the head copy, and a `cmp` hit on the mutant itself was checked so that no edit is vacuous.

**Per class: a budget that cannot see its own planted 2x.** The planted 2x is each class's `cpu doubled` arm from CI, held in `COST_CLASS_READINGS`. Each mutant loosens one class's budget past its own doubled arm:
- K24, `s/"ref24": {"cpu_ratio": 3.630,/"ref24": {"cpu_ratio": 5.3,/`: `FAIL control:cycle_cost:class_budgets [(23.83, ['cpu_ratio 2.567: budget 5.3 cannot see a 2x cycle; re-record 3.63'], [])]`. **Killed.**
- K24L, which drops ref24's loop key so it falls back to the shared 0.1278 (`s/, "loop_cpu_ratio": 0.1813}/}/`): `FAIL ... [(23.83, ['loop_cpu_ratio 0.1282 over its budget 0.1278'], ...)]`. **Killed.**
- K24B, which deletes the ref24 band: `FAIL control:cycle_cost:class_budgets [(23.83, ['no recorded budget: ...'])...]` and `FAIL control:cycle_cost:runner_class_unknown`. **Killed.**
- K30, ref30 3.934 to 5.76: `FAIL ... [(30.32, ['cpu_ratio 2.81: budget 5.76 cannot see a 2x cycle; re-record 3.974'], [])...]`. **Killed.**
- K46, ref46 3.357 to 4.83: `FAIL ... [(45.65, ['cpu_ratio 2.325: budget 4.83 cannot see a 2x cycle; re-record 3.287'], [])...]`. **Killed.**
- K53, ref53 2.081 to 2.96: `FAIL ... [(52.76, ['cpu_ratio 1.456: budget 2.96 cannot see a 2x cycle; re-record 2.06'], [])...]`. **Killed.**
- M1, one budget 3.614 for every class: `FAIL ... [(52.76, ['cpu_ratio 1.456: budget 3.614 cannot see a 2x cycle; ...'])...]`. **Killed.**

**Unknown class.**
- M4, an unknown class falls back to ref46 (`s/... and c in keyed), None)/... and c in keyed), "ref46")/`): `FAIL control:cycle_cost:runner_class_unknown bad=[] good=[]`. **Killed.**
- W30, ref30 widened down over the 28.0 runner (`s/"ref30": (28.72, 32.69)/"ref30": (26.0, 32.69)/`). At `834d0074` this **survived** (33 of 33 ok), because no control pinned a known foreign ruler. `4de0f656` adds `COST_RULERS_REFUSED`, and it now reads `FAIL control:cycle_cost:runner_class_unknown bad=[] good=[]`. **Killed.** This is a disclosed self-correction within this round.
- W46, ref46 widened down to 33.0, and W30u, ref30 widened up to 35.0, over the 34.35 ruler: both read `FAIL control:cycle_cost:runner_class_unknown`. **Killed.**

## Null control

- **Head unmutated:** `33 of 33 controls ok` (the probe above, counting every control).
- **The failing job, base against head.** I put the four `cost` lines of job 125461180429 through the production `class_budget` + `cost_offenders`:
  - At `acec536b`, all four read `runner class unknown`. That is the CI red, reproduced.
  - At the head, the clean run reads `[]`. `cpu doubled` reads `cpu_ratio 5.209 over its budget 3.63`, `memory doubled` reads `peak_kib 3861 over its budget 2686`, and `loop doubled` reads `loop_cpu_ratio 0.2603 over its budget 0.1813`.
  - The owner fixture's clean 269.8155 at `ref_ms` 24.06 reads `[]` at both (unkeyed, 337.8).
- **The census, every reading.** I graded all 22 jobs at the head (Figures).
  - The 19 jobs whose rulers lie in a band read `within`, and each `cpu doubled` arm reads `seen` (over its class budget).
  - The three outside every band read `REFUSED`, both clean and doubled: 28.01 (job 125000687320), 34.35 (nightly job 123225871060) and 22.16 (nightly job 121370544228, 10-26, older cycle code, not admitted).
  - Had a band been widened to fit these, at least one of them would read `NOT SEEN`. 28.01 graded on ref30's 3.934 gives 3.8922 < 3.934.
- **ref24 budget placement.** 2.5671 / 3.630 and 0.1282 / 0.1813 are each 70.7 %, inside (budget / 2, budget]. The class's `ref_ms` spread within the job is 2.3 %. The band is the extremes widened 5 % each way, and it is disjoint from ref30 (28.72).

## Figures

- **Readings source.** Each reading is the `cost {...}` line of a job log. Re-take one with `gh api repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/actions/jobs/125461180429/logs`, keeping lines holding `cycles over` and `doubled:`. Job 125461180429 read:
  - clean `cpu_ratio` 2.5671 and `loop_cpu_ratio` 0.1282 at `ref_ms` 23.83;
  - `cpu doubled` 5.2086 at 23.99;
  - `memory doubled` `peak_kib` 3860.7 at 24.31;
  - `loop doubled` 0.2603 at 23.77;
  - owner fixture 269.8155 at 24.06.
- **Band rule.** min / 1.05 floored and max x 1.05 ceiled to 0.01, over every clean and doubled `ref_ms` of the cited job: 23.77 and 24.31 give 22.64-25.53.
- **Budget rule.** sqrt(2) x the geometric midpoint of the class's clean extremes, the rule every budget in the file uses. One job gives sqrt(2) x 2.5671 = 3.630 and sqrt(2) x 0.1282 = 0.1813. The lane's own `record:` line printed `cpu_ratio=3.63 ... loop_cpu_ratio=0.1813`.
- **Census of 22 jobs.** These are every `tests / replay` job that ran in the 60 most recent `ci.yml` runs (4) plus earlier replay-branch runs (7, from PRs #3174, #3170, #3167 and #3078), and all 11 scheduled nightly `slow` jobs. Each was graded with `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 -B -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tests'); import replay as r; s='synthetic-dhw-only.json'; [print(x, r.class_budget(s, x)[1][:1] or r.cost_offenders({'cpu_ratio': c}, r.class_budget(s, x)[0])) for x, c in ((23.83, 2.5671), (28.01, 1.8924), (34.35, 1.8747), (22.16, 1.9455), (47.73, 2.2746), (54.55, 1.4448))]"`, the same call over each job's clean and doubled pair. Result: 19 in band read `within` and `seen`, and three read `REFUSED`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED` at the head.
- Scoped gate, re-run at `4de0f656`, `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`: `MODE: SCOPED -- 3 script(s) run, 30 scoped out` (`debug_collect`, `entities`, `features`). Every script it names, plus the run_always `env_drift.py --claims-only`, `closure.py selftest`, `layout.py` and `harness_headers.py`, exited 0 under `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub GOLDEN_MODE=drift`.
- `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh <body>` on the committed clean tree, closures step not skipped: `PRE-PR: 4de0f6565221868a0da1b5c88626f052e88d0eda 00000000000000000000000000 rc=0`. That run was against origin/main `871a20da`. Main has since moved to `b8e82369` with no conflict and nothing this diff reads (Head), and under the brief's merge-only-on-conflict rule there was no merge, so there was no second run.

## Carries

- Carry 1: the owner fixture's budget entry is unchanged at 337.8. Its clean reading on the new ref24 runner, 269.8155 (job 125461180429), reads inside it (Null control).

Their cycle code differs from this base only in learner_progress.py, replay_doc.py and snapshots.py, so the coordinator cycle is the same. Their readings (ev/nightly_slow_*.txt):
- `ref_ms` is 52.4-53.3 and `loop_ref_ms` is 156-166.
- Synthetic `cpu_ratio` reads 1.4563, 1.451 and 1.4926.

So merging this head turns the next scheduled nightly red on the synthetic fixture. On that class the budget no longer catches a real 2x cpu regression, which fails ASK (2) there. These are the "timed slow lanes" that the head's own comment above `COST_BUDGETS` says the base's 2.173 was centred on (its 1.391 low edge, `tests/replay.py:457-458`). The re-centring dropped them without saying so.

The class does not fit one 2x band as recorded:
- sqrt(2) x the geometric midpoint of 1.451 and 2.81 is 2.856.
- The nightly cpu-doubled arm at 2.841 then reads under it.
- So a re-cut needs a decision, not a re-derivation: per-class budgets, a paired reference, or tvofi's call on which classes the lane grades.

merges.body:
Part of #201. R10-FLOW-BODY-ONLY parts (a) to (c), the Lean flow pre-study's K12: ruling R4 made true in the tool, so a body fix no longer moves a clean head. Built on #3037 (V147, the `Code:` trailer).

The group's carries, numbered as the roster's `carry` list numbers them (from 1):

- Carry 1 (the Lean flow pre-study, K12): built here, parts (a) to (c) below.
- Carry 2 (`app_approve.sh --carry` until this lands): released once this merges; a body-only move no longer needs a carry.
- Carry 3 (self-test hygiene): (a) this PR's mutants take per-file ids inside their instrument's block (`cloud_relay-50` to `-58`, `update_pr-1` to `-7`); (b) the new rows reuse the fixtures' existing throwaway origins, and `tests/throwaway_git.py --check` refuses 0 sites; (c) no new git push site: body-only PATCHes through `body_patch.sh`; (d) `## Red checks` below.
- Carry 4 (V147, the `Code:` trailer and the stale-body refusal): landed in #3037; part (c) reads that trailer.
- Carry 5 (P321): landed with carry 4 in #3037.

As built:

- Part (a), `tools/audit/seat/update_pr.sh`: origin/main is merged only when `gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus` says `DIRTY` or `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` fails. An unread merge state counts as not DIRTY, because merge-tree is the local proof either way.
- Part (b), the same script: when the merges and the row leave the head exactly where origin had it, nothing is pushed; `body_patch.sh` runs the body contract at that head, from the run's worktree, and PATCHes the body (`update_pr: BODY-ONLY:`). With code `-`, a `handoff/<topic>` tip the head lacks refuses. A head that is the live head plus one commit asks `--row-only`.
- Part (c), `tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh` `handoff_arm`: a PR whose head holds its handoff tip, and whose `handoff-body/<topic>` tip this relay has not applied and names that tip in `Code:`, gets `HPO_UPDATE_BODY_ONLY=1 update_pr.sh <branch> - <body>` once per body move, recorded in `cloud-handoff-bodied`. The hold applies; the review freeze does not, and `update_pr.sh` now guarantees the reason it does not: under `HPO_UPDATE_BODY_ONLY` a run whose merges or row would leave the head other than the live head refuses (`update_pr: REFUSE: body-only update would move the head ...`) and pushes nothing, and the relay records that refusal as owed `handoff-update`.

Alternatives not taken:

- A commit-time rule for "this body is new": runner and host clocks skew, and a re-body of an unchanged head is legitimately newer. The applied-body record needs no clock.
- Body-only only for code `-`: a code sha the head already holds leaves the same unmoved head, and refusing it keeps the prepr re-run cost.
- Running `body_patch.sh` from the main checkout: its lint resolves cited paths in the caller's tree, so a body citing a file the PR adds is refused.
- Round 7's guard in the relay (apply the freeze unless the move is guaranteed body-only): the relay cannot know DIRTY or a missing row without re-deriving what `update_pr.sh` computes after its merges, so it would duplicate that logic. The flag puts the check where `H` and `LIVE` already are: one guard line in `update_pr.sh` plus one env assignment on the relay's launch line.

## Re-cut

Round 7 of R10-FLOW-BODY-ONLY, a minimal re-cut answering `verdict/3089` round 2 (blocked at `2fd46f26`, class-open): `handoff_arm` skipped the review freeze on a body-only move, but `update_pr.sh <branch> - <body>` still moved the head when (a) the PR was `DIRTY` and the local merge of main was clean, or (b) a contained head lacked its delivery row (`ensure_row`, `--row-only` push), so a head holding a merge verdict or a dispatched review could move with no `cloud-handoff-release` entry and no `HELD-*` line. Closed at one seam, `update_pr.sh`'s head check, driven by the relay's `HPO_UPDATE_BODY_ONLY=$bonly` (commit `62673524`); `9da59904` documents the refusal in both instrument guides. The verdict's second finding: `## Red checks` below is retaken from the whole check-run set and names `tests / nightly-status` as main's inherited red. Every figure below was re-taken in this body-only retake by running its command, at the handoff tip that holds `9da59904`.

## Head

`ecf4ef3fe30087e5a47ddbddcedcb6d2584f5c1d` merges main `3583448` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`98beb50fd6e7de0142a2e2ec96c55a43475eb00b` is the PR head: it merges the authored handoff tip `39e9abd5009448270215222943aa0fd0ac76b1e1` (which holds the code head named below, `9da59904cc9a3ea2d7a941ea3e24dab5f6d52017`, plus origin/main `8e90d8144`) into the previous PR head `2fd46f26`, by the orchestrator's script; no code was resolved by hand.

Code head `9da59904cc9a3ea2d7a941ea3e24dab5f6d52017` (the r7 repair: a fast-forward over the PR head `2fd46f26`, merging origin/main `fad43b04`, adding fix commit `62673524` and the instrument-guide commit `9da59904`). The PR head stays `2fd46f26` until the relay's update runs. The handoff ref's tip, `39e9abd5009448270215222943aa0fd0ac76b1e1`, is `9da59904` plus two clean merges of origin/main (`616868bd`, `8e90d814`); those moves touch the card, archscore, `thermal_model.py`, budgets and their tests, none of the seat files, so every figure below was re-taken in this pass by running its command, in a worktree at that tip, and describes `9da59904`'s seat tools. No code is pushed by this body retake and no file of the handoff changed.

## Mutation proof

Finder's own mutants (`verdict/3089:evidence/own-mutants.diff`): at the head, harness ids `cloud_relay-57` (mutant B) and `update_pr-6` (mutant A) are byte-identical to them and are KILLED (Figures).

The guard this round adds, killed at both seams:

- `update_pr.sh`'s guard line deleted (self-test mutant `mut:bodyonly`, harness `update_pr-7`): red on "update_pr: a relay body-only run on a head lacking its row refuses, the head unmoved and nothing pushed" and "update_pr: a relay body-only run on a DIRTY head whose merge of main is clean refuses, the head unmoved and nothing pushed"; the in-test mutant rows show the head moved (row pushed; main merged into the DIRTY head and pushed).
- The relay's `HPO_UPDATE_BODY_ONLY=$bonly` dropped (harness `cloud_relay-58`): `cloud_relay self-test: 332 checks, 4 failed`, the body-only rows, including "a new body at a contained head holding a merge verdict runs update_pr once, body-only" and "a new body at a contained head with a reviewer dispatched runs update_pr once, body-only", whose stub now records the flag.

## Null control

- The unmutated head: `bash tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh --self-test` reports `332 checks, 0 failed`; `bash tools/audit/seat/update_pr.sh --self-test` reports `delivery_row self-test: 6 checks, 0 failed` and `pr_args self-test: 172 checks, 0 failed` (168 before, plus the two guard rows and their two mutant rows).
- Without the flag the same shapes still move the head: "null control: without HPO_UPDATE_BODY_ONLY a DIRTY pull request still absorbs main, through the full prepr" and "update_pr: a head that only gains its row pushes once, asking for --row-only" pass.
- The relay's non-body-only updates record no flag: the anchored rows matching `^fix/topic-a-pr <sha>$` pass, so the flag does not leak to a code move, which the freeze still holds ("a handoff tip the verdicted head does not hold is still HELD-VERDICT (null control)" passes).

## Figures

- `bash tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh --self-test`: its last line reports 0 failed.

R10-LIVE-BUNDLE-READS (issue #3120), repair round 2. Closes #3120.

The fix (round 1, unchanged): `tools/replay/debug_ingest.py` `load_bundle` unwraps `data.debug` when the top level is a Home Assistant "Download diagnostics" file (`unwrap_download`), and stage 4 compares the store window and the rows over the samples both hold, each stamp once (D15-s1-03, D15-s1-01). Design choice, said so a reader does not take it for a bug: the comparison is over the intersection, and it still fails (not vacuous) when the intersection is empty.

This round settles the block of verdict/3186 (class-open: `dev/audit/rounds/round10/D15/s1/intake.py`). With `load_bundle` unwrapping, the finder's harness lost its wrapper: `bundle_unwrapped` read 0 on every download and `--perturb unwrap` did nothing. The repair:
- `debug_ingest.read_download(path)`: the file as handed, gunzipped and parsed, wrapper intact. `load_bundle` is now `unwrap_download(read_download(path))`, so there is still one loader and no second gzip/json path.
- `intake.py` reads the download through `read_download` (on a tree before it exists, `load_bundle` is that reader, so the harness still runs at the base); `bundle_unwrapped` is measured on the file as handed again. Its wrapped M3 arm is now what `load_bundle` hands `ingest` (the tool's own path), and `--perturb unwrap` flips that unwrap, so the arm moves at both ends. Header updated to say so.
- The verdict's finding: `intake.py` M4 called `store._store_name`, which the tree names `store_name`; it crashed at base and head, so the store metrics never printed. Fixed; they print at both ends.

Alternatives, and why each lost: reading the raw file inside `intake.py` (a second gzip/json loader beside `load_bundle`, duplicated concept); dispositioning the seam in the body and leaving the harness blind (its M1 and M3 wrapper arm would stay meaningless for the next live bundle); keeping the old "unwrap" perturbation semantics (at the head it is a no-op by construction).

LOCAL-SAFE: this round read no live bundle. Every figure below is from the synthetic download `debug_ingest._download(debug_ingest._tail_repeat_bundle())` the reviewer used, or the bare `_tail_repeat_bundle()` as the null control, written to a scratch file outside the tree. merges.body:
R10-OVERBOOK-RESIDUAL refutes the #2499 residual. The over-booking was in the reference, not in the plan. The harness's DP reference (`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_demand_overbook.py`, `_dp_reference`) priced comfort against one flat band, `target_temp` 21 with floor `min_temp` 20, at every step. The solve prices the day/night schedule that `OptimizationConfig.get_comfort_temp` / `get_temp_bounds` return: target 19.5 and floor 19.5 outside 07:00-22:00. So the reference read the night setback the solve is allowed as a breach and a pull deficit, and it priced the plan's pre-heating ahead of 07:00 as waste. With the reference reading the solve's own per-step schedule from `HeatPumpOptimizer._build_comfort_bounds`, the one site that builds it, the flat-price arm's plan reads plan_kwh at the DP's and the plan's cost equals the DP optimum. The owner arm's plan costs less than the relaxed DP on the same objective.

No production code changes. The diff corrects the instrument and adds the cross-check that would have caught it: `_production_cost` scores the plan on the optimizer's own full objective (`_solve_objectives`, captured from a real `optimize`), and the row prints it as `prod_cost` beside the reconstruction's `plan_cost`. When the two disagree, the reference measures a different problem.

Refs #2499. The group's roster entry (`R10-OVERBOOK-RESIDUAL` on `handoff/audit-r10-roster`) lists #2499 in `fixes`, but main's in-tree roster does not carry that entry yet. Until it lands, `tools/pr/prepr.sh` step 7's preflight, which derives its intended list from `dev/programme/rosters`, refuses a closing keyword on that issue because no group there names #2499 in `fixes`. The closing keyword is the orchestrator's to restore once the roster merges.

Carry 1 is answered by refutation. That is the brief's carry from R10-STORE-RACES / #2887, null 11.78 against 9.88 and owner_i01 5.37 against 3.88. Both arms were re-run at this merge base before any figure here was quoted, and `## Figures` shows them at both ends. The flat-price arm now reads plan_kwh within the DP's. The owner arm's remaining kWh difference costs no more on the same objective, so it is not price-side either. The precondition on `valve_charge_demand` does not bind here, because both arms are unvalved and this diff quotes no savings figure.

## Head

`02d6df06cbf8fd7d0387a3dca40161c219b51d8c` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3183.md`. The authored code head is `91a7c9c2e727c59e523af81faae212dd3aa17b50`.

Code head `91a7c9c2e727c59e523af81faae212dd3aa17b50`, cut from origin/main `c3a279e3252a8b57bb00b5a677318cd4fe20387f`, which is also the merge base. Every figure below was measured at this head or at that base, on numpy 2.5.4 / scipy 1.18.1: the `tests/requirements-ci.txt` pins, after `tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh` refreshed the environment's venvs, which had been behind them (numpy 2.4.6 / scipy 1.17.1 before the refresh). origin/main had not moved at the handoff, so `prepr.sh` was not re-run after a merge.

## Mutation proof

The fix is the harness's comfort schedule. Mutant: the per-step `targets, floors, ceilings, bands` in `_dp_reference` replaced by the flat `cfg.target_temp` / `cfg.min_temp` / `cfg.max_temp` band they replaced, from a scratch copy, run as `--one null --dp`. The mutant reproduces the base reading exactly: `dp_learned` gap 0.2601, dp_kwh 8.62 against plan_kwh 10.74. Its own cross-check flags it: `plan_cost` 20.384 against `prod_cost` 17.801. Restored, the head reads gap 0.0 with `plan_cost` = `prod_cost` = 17.801. No `custom_components/` line changes, so there are no production mutants and no golden claims.

## Null control

The unmodified tree (origin/main's harness, sha1 `f0575c58b587d9a41e922fb5393e1a30a7ddba0b`) at the merge base: the null arm reads `dp_learned` dp_kwh 8.62 against plan_kwh 10.74 (gap 0.2601) and `dp_true` dp_kwh 9.00 (gap 0.2928). The owner_i01 arm reads dp_kwh 3.75 against plan_kwh 5.27 (gap 0.158; `dp_true` gap 0.1598). The plan is the control for the reference: plan_kwh, plan/deliv, the learned scale and the per-day series are identical at both ends (null 10.74, 1.165, 0.98; owner 5.27, 0.854, 0.616), because only the reference changed. The perturbation that shows the corrected reference still detects a worse plan is the base reference's own DP schedule. Scored on the production objective it costs 19.744 against the plan's 17.801. So the plan beats it, and the flat-band "optimum" was not optimal on the solve's objective. That figure comes from a scratch probe and not from an in-tree instrument. The in-tree equivalent is the `prod_cost` cross-check above.

## Figures

All rows: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_demand_overbook.py --one <arm> --dp`. Head harness sha1 `edc0b3c076a8fd4ad62db1defcb5a8a79ddc0281`; base sha1 `f0575c58b587d9a41e922fb5393e1a30a7ddba0b`. A field name below is the name the harness prints. gap = (plan_cost - dp_cost) / dp_cost on the DP's relaxed objective, and is >= 0 up to the (room, slab) grid's interpolation error.

- null (flat prices, unvalved), base: dp_learned dp_kwh 8.62, plan_kwh 10.74, gap 0.2601; dp_true dp_kwh 9.00, gap 0.2928.
- null, head: dp_learned dp_kwh 10.75, plan_kwh 10.74, gap 0.0, plan_cost 17.801 = prod_cost 17.801; dp_true dp_kwh 11.00, plan_kwh 10.74, gap 0.0. This is the brief's close condition: the flat-price arm's plan_kwh is within the DP's.
- owner_i01 (flat prices, owner pump shape, idle 0.1 kW), base: dp_learned dp_kwh 3.75, plan_kwh 5.27, gap 0.158.
- owner_i01, head: dp_learned dp_kwh 4.50, plan_kwh 5.27, gap -0.0006, plan_cost 10.087 = prod_cost 10.087; dp_true dp_kwh 4.12, gap -0.0012. The plan books more kWh than the DP's rollout at a lower cost on the same objective. The extra energy buys pull and terminal value that the objective prices, so it is not over-booking against the reference. A negative gap is the DP grid's interpolation error, which is the bound the docstring states.
- plan/deliv, the closed-loop ratio the carry quoted, reads 1.165 (null) and 0.854 (owner) at both ends. It compares two 12-hour plans with the energy one day delivered under receding-horizon replanning. It is not measured against any optimum, and its sign differs between two flat-price arms, so it is not an over-booking measure. It is left as printed.
- The carry's figures (null 11.78 against 9.88; owner 5.37 against 3.88) were snapshots at #2887's head on the stale toolchain. Re-taken at this merge base, they are the base rows above.
- Gate scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run, 33 scoped out`. The four `tests/run.sh` `run_always` lines were run by hand and passed: `tests/env_drift.py --claims-only origin/main`, `tests/closure.py selftest`, `tests/layout.py`, `tests/harness_headers.py`. `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED.
- Class census (fixer step 8). Rule: `git grep -nE "target_temp ?- ?[a-z_.]*min_temp" -- dev/ tools/ tests/*.py` (a flat comfort band rebuilt outside the solve) and `git grep -n "_COMFORT_PULL_SINGLE_ZONE\|_COMFORT_PULL_TWO_ZONE" -- ':!custom_components'` (the pull rebuilt outside the solve). At the base, the first returns this harness's `band = max(cfg.target_temp - cfg.min_temp, 1.0)`. At the head it returns nothing. The second returns: this harness, closed in this diff; `dev/audit/rounds/round9/D9/s1/comfort_rowloop.py`, already guarded because it takes `comfort_band` as the solve's per-step array and builds none; and `dev/audit/rounds/round3/D0/reports/verify-2.md` and `dev/audit/rounds/round5/D0/seat-a/patch_f1b.diff`, which are records, not instruments.

## Architecture score

n/a: no production file changes. The diff is one audit harness.

## Unpinned sites

n/a: no `custom_components/` or `tools/` site added. The harness's `_production_cost` is its own cross-check and is exercised by every `--dp` run above.

## Red checks

none

## Forward-carry

n/a: the finding is the harness's own correction and lands in this diff, in the `_dp_reference` and `_production_cost` docstrings, which every later seat that re-runs or copies the reference reads. The census in `## Figures` returns no other reference that needs it, so no later stage's brief changes.

## Friction

none

## Head

`9a2b6ba8fe6b0040b87680ef5f79388f45686884` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3199.md`. The authored code head is `316f0a2ee5e80f5354fc1fef18186cd7a6b92b12`.

316f0a2ee5e80f5354fc1fef18186cd7a6b92b12

## Mutation proof

Each mutant is a copy of this head, full `tests/features.py` run.
- #2365: `pump_arbiter.py` restored to origin/main (literal `15.0`, `LOG_STEPS = 96`): 1 of 4781 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED, `R10-PROD-RESIDUE-PINS #2365: a 40 % hot-water share splits at minute 12 ...  [('space', 'space', 96)]`.
- #2351: the `forget_held(self.hass)` line deleted from `async_shutdown`: 1 of 4781 FAILED, `R10-PROD-RESIDUE-PINS #2351: async_shutdown re-arms a hass-owned latch ...  [[30, 10]]` (second call stays at DEBUG).
- Strict-`<` bound of `_share`'s short-remainder guard (a `<=` mutant survived the first pin drive): added check `a remainder of exactly SPLIT_MIN_MINUTES is still a heating share`; the `<=` mutant fails 1 of 4782 (`[('dhw', 'dhw')]`), this head passes ALL 4782 FEATURE CHECKS.
- The earlier counts above (4781) were taken before that one check was added.

## Null control

At the real 15-minute width the split is minute 6 and the log holds 96 steps (check `#2365 null control`, green at this head and on the #2365 mutant). Without the shutdown between the two `log_held` calls the second stays DEBUG (check `#2351 null control`, green on all three trees).

## Figures

- Full features run per tree: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` (this head, the #2365 mutant, the #2351 mutant).
- Scoped gate: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` printed MODE: SCOPED; every python script in `scope.run` run with `GOLDEN_MODE=drift` and passed, including `tests/golden.py`, `tests/env_drift.py` and `tests/finite_boundary.py`; `tests/card.mjs` and `tests/card_drift.mjs` were not run locally (no JS or card surface touched).

- origin/main moved twice while the gate ran (c3a279e32 -> a9c2f90fc -> 8e90d8144); both merged cleanly. The second delta touched thermal_model.py, the card, audit harnesses and ledger records, none of the files this diff or its closure edits (`git diff --name-only` against pump_arbiter, coordinator, plan_step, log_latch, features, golden returns nothing); the scoped scripts and a full `tests/features.py` were rerun at this head. `tools/pr/prepr.sh` rerun at this head.

`mutation` (predicted by `prepr.sh` step 6d, never red on the remote): the diff removed two pinned arbiter sites (`LOG_STEPS = 96`, the `15.0 -` guard) and added three unpinned ones, and one of them (the `<` bound) survived the pin drive. Cheaper detector: `tools/pr/prepr.sh` step 6d / `ci_predict`, already standing, which named all of it before the handoff; the survivor got a killing check rather than a triage.

- `pump_arbiter.py:1165 CMP_BOUND` (`_share`): survived the first drive; killed by the new boundary check, then pinned by a second `--pin-killed` (`_share.CMP_BOUND.4f254e46.json`).

merges.body:
R10-ARCH-SHAPES-CLASSIFIER: land the reason-classifier arm of D8-s1-01 that #2819 parked, the folded R10-HOTFIX-PREHEAT-LABEL fix, and the four #2238 sweep-P2 seams routed here, with the classifier drift claimed by shape.

- **Classifier arm (Carry 4).** `classify_space_steps` / `classify_dhw_steps` read each channel's draw through `_heating_draws`, which calls `thermal_model.channel_heating_draw`: the draw on the steps `channel_heating_steps` says the channel heats, 0 elsewhere. A share on a step the plan runs no pump at is now idle to the classifiers, as it already is to the plan views, pump schedule and wood advisor. Starting point: the parked `996b54cf1`. Main had since moved `channel_heating_steps` into `thermal_model.py`, so `channel_heating_draw` moved there beside it. The two `tests/entities.py` dispositions go back to the owner-module reading.
- **Pre-heat label (Carry 8, 9).** The four commits from `handoff-wip/r10-hotfix-preheat-label` (`9bfbe3866`) were cherry-picked unchanged. `_weather_loss_factors` divides each step's loss by the same house's calm, dry loss. The learned `house_heat_loss_scale` therefore no longer reads as weather in `preheat_weather` or in the warm start. At scale 1.0 the output is bit-identical to before.
- **Four P2 seams (Carry 6, 7).** `FrequencyMap.recommend`, `FrequencyMap.evidence_exhausted`, `_async_learn_buffer_cooling`'s `heating` and `_observe_frequency`'s `watch_active` each call `thermal_model.planned_draw_runs` in place of their own 0.05 kW copy.
  - Having `freq_control` read `thermal_model` would close an import cycle (entry_config → freq_control → thermal_model → entry_config). The two `FREQ_MODE_*` strings, which several modules share and `entry_config` parses, therefore move to `const.py`, and `freq_control` re-exports them explicitly.
  - Alternatives that lost: a function-level lazy import hides the cycle instead of removing it. Passing a `runs` flag into `FrequencyMap` would leave the decision with every caller. A new leaf module for the running rule would be a new tracked file outside every measured closure, for a two-constant problem.
- **Stress invariant.** `tests/stress.py`'s "heating steps have no reason code" counted a raw space draw over 0.05 kW as heating, which is a copy of the line this group retires. `winter_extreme/2z/space` puts a share on a step the plan calls off, and the classifier now rightly calls that step idle, so the invariant failed. It now asks `channel_heating_steps`.
- **Claim (Carry 0, 1, 5).** `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` restates its header with the SHAPE category and claims `shape: space_reasons[*]|dhw_reasons[*] * -> 'idle_coasting'|'idle'`. There is no fixed fixture list.


**Roster carries.** The review packet numbers carries 1-based, while the brief's "Carry N" labels are the roster's 0-based indexes. Each is named here in the packet's numbering, with the brief's label in brackets:
- Carry 1 [brief 0]: done. The claim-file header now names the SHAPE line, restated with this branch's claim.
- Carry 2 [brief 1]: done. The claim is `shape: space_reasons[*]|dhw_reasons[*] * -> 'idle_coasting'|'idle'`, and `r10_shape_claim_controls.sh` was re-run (`## Figures`).
- Carry 3 [roster 2, from #2843]: the same header carry as Carry 1, done by the same change.
- Carry 4 [roster 3, from #2843]: the same claim carry as Carry 2, done by the same change.
- Carry 5 [brief 4]: done. The parked arm (`996b54cf1`) landed, with `channel_heating_draw` beside `channel_heating_steps` in `thermal_model.py`.
- Carry 6 [brief 5]: done. The claim is by shape, not a fixture list. The census was not re-run (`## Figures` says why).
- Carry 7 [brief 6]: done. The four seams call `planned_draw_runs`, and the precondition and null were re-measured with the rebuilt probe harness.
- Carry 8 [brief 7]: the routing record for Carry 7's four seams. It is discharged by the same change.
- Carry 9 [brief 8]: done. The pre-heat label fix landed, with all three controls and the mutant.
- Carry 10 [brief 9]: done. The four WIP commits were taken from `9bfbe3866`. The scoped gate and `features.py` ran at the head, prepr ran with `## Unpinned sites` (both CLAMP_DROP floors included), and the body is this one.

## Head

`87319cb1c2218489d112548e05512100221660a5` merges the authored code head `825f8ecd0506076463683a766863a23793521386` and then merges origin/main `8e90d8144` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

825f8ecd0506076463683a766863a23793521386 (code head pushed to `handoff/r10-arch-shapes-classifier`). It is PR head c34999c1dd512e45fea3027bc49da31a78050d8a (the handoff 913e74e87 plus the bot commit `ci: pin killed mutants`) plus two commits of repair round 2, 2026-11-04: the new features check, then the pin json for the one site it kills. Merge base c3a279e3252a8b57bb00b5a677318cd4fe20387f. `origin/main` moved during the repair (a9c2f90f to 8e90d81443317f76f22602a89651f7ca17c633f9, fetched 2026-11-04 after the first `prepr.sh` run predicted `governance / wave-script AGREEMENT UNMERGED` and `GRADER UNMERGED`), so the head is a merge commit (`git merge origin/main`, no conflict; the ledger driver resolved `tests/structure_budgets.json` and `tests/closures.json`). Steps 2-8 were re-executed on the merged tree: `tests/features.py` printed `ALL 4786 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, `tests/entities.py` `ALL 2602 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`, `tests/structure.py` `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`, and `tools/pr/prepr.sh` ended `PRE-PR: <head> rc=0` with `ci predict` reading no predicted red against 8e90d8144331. `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` differs from origin/main by the ten lines of this PR's own shape claim (`## Figures`, unchanged since the first handoff); `card_claimed_drift.txt` is identical to origin/main, and VERSION, the manifest version and the `RELEASE_NOTES.md` heading are untouched.

## Mutation proof

One combined mutant, in a worktree at head b03b76d5d, ran `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` and reported `7 of 4785 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`. The reverted lines were:
- the two `_heating_draws` lines;
- `_weather_loss_factors`'s `calm_loss`, set back to the raw nameplate (`calm_loss = base_loss`);
- both `freq_control` gates, back to `target_kw <= 0.05`;
- both coordinator predicates, back to `> 0.05`.

Each failing check exercises a single seam:
- FAIL a target the plan calls off asks the map for nothing (D8-s1-01). Killed by the freq_control gates.
- FAIL a learned heat-loss scale of 1.24 under a flat forecast labels no step weather pre-heating, and the plan does heat. Killed by `calm_loss`.
- FAIL a forecast wind spell still labels weather pre-heating, at scale 1.0 and 1.24, and only on the spell's steps. Killed by `calm_loss`.
- FAIL a step the plan runs no pump at is idle to the reason classifiers (D8-s1-01). Killed by `_heating_draws`.
- FAIL the buffer learner reads heating from the plan's running rule. Killed by `heating`.
- FAIL the watchdog's two bounds: the floor is exclusive, the minimum inclusive. Killed by `watch_active` at `MIN_RUNNING_DRAW_KW`.
- FAIL a step the plan calls off is not watched (D8-s1-01, #2238 sweep P2). Killed by `watch_active`.

With the code restored, the gate's features run read `ALL 4785 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`.

**Repair round 2: the evidence_exhausted gate in isolation.** The review of 913e74e8 found that "a target the plan calls off asks the map for nothing (D8-s1-01)" does not kill `freq_control.py:228 GUARD_OFF`: its map holds buckets at 2.0 to 6.0 kW, so `evidence_exhausted(0.07)` reads False with or without the gate. The new check "evidence below a target the plan calls off is not exhaustion (D8-s1-01)" builds a map whose one bucket predicts 0.06 kW (`observe(25.0, 0.06, 20.0, 120.0)` repeated `FREQ_MIN_SAMPLES + 1` times) and requires `evidence_exhausted(0.07)` False and, as its null control on the same map, `evidence_exhausted(0.11)` True.
- With the gate replaced by `if False:` (the one mutated line, nothing else), `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` printed `FAIL evidence below a target the plan calls off is not exhaustion (D8-s1-01)`, `1 of 4786 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED` and `rc=1`.
- With the file restored by `git checkout`, the same command printed `ALL 4786 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`.
- `python3 tests/mutation_table.py --pin-killed --base origin/main --jobs 3` printed `pinned   custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/freq_control.py:228 GUARD_OFF -- killed by tests/features.py` and `PIN KILLED: 1 pinned, 0 left unpinned`. The null control `freq_control.py:33 NULL_COMMENT` survived every driver, as it must. The pin json is `tests/mutation_ledger/killed_by/freq_control.py/FrequencyMap.evidence_exhausted.GUARD_OFF.39c9b8d5.json`, committed.

The combined run does not show that each check kills its own mutant in isolation. Each check drives only its own seam, but a reviewer wanting per-mutant runs needs to rerun them. The preheat fixer's commit 589f65e2d recorded "Main's code fails exactly the first two" of its tests.

## Null control

- **Probes.** `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_run_owner_probes.py --perturb` at the merge base swaps each 0.05 kW copy (and the classifiers' `CHANNEL_ACTIVE_KW` default) for the owner's value on a temp copy, and reads `probes_failed=0`. Unperturbed, the base reads 6. The 0 at head is therefore the owner's rule and not a probe that cannot fail.
- **Pre-heat.** Scale 1.0 under a flat forecast is unchanged: it is a features check. The finder's arm 4 (configured, no learned scale) reads 0 of 96 at both ends.
- **Claim controls.** `r10_shape_claim_controls.sh` at BASE plus a comment-only production line reads rc=1, with the claim STALE. The narrow claim without `dhw_reasons[*]` reads rc=1, UNCLAIMED.
- **Freq map.** At 0.11 kW, a step the plan runs, the map still recommends.
- **Buffer learner.** At 0.5 kW the learner still reads heating.
- **Watchdog.** At 2.0 kW and 45 Hz, a running plan is still watched.

## Figures

Repair round 2 additions: `python3 tests/entities.py` printed `ALL 2602 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`; `python3 tests/structure.py` printed `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED` (`seam_cut_total 423 <= 423`); `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir $D` printed `MODE: SCOPED -- 29 script(s) run, 4 scoped out`. The commands for the first block of figures below are unchanged and were taken as stated there.

All figures below were taken at head 2bf3bed46 unless marked otherwise. The head c4d45522c669 adds only the tests/closures.json INERT entry. Toolchain: `bash tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh` refreshed the venvs, and `cloud-setup.sh --check` printed OK. Afterwards, `python3 -c 'import numpy,scipy;print(numpy.__version__,scipy.__version__)'` printed `2.5.4 1.18.1`, which matches tests/requirements-ci.txt. CI stays the authority for goldens.

**Scoped gate and per-script checks**
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir $D` printed `MODE: SCOPED -- 29 script(s) run, 4 scoped out` at b03b76d5d. That diff later added tests/stress.py, which the scope already ran. At head c4d45522c669 the diff also touches tests/closures.json (the INERT entry), which the gate cannot scope, so prepr skipped its closures step and CI runs the full suite.
- `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift ./tests/run.sh` at b03b76d5d went red on three scripts: typing_ruler, stress and harness_headers. All three are answered under `## Red checks` and were fixed in 2bf3bed46 (head c4d45522c669 adds only the closures INERT entry). Every other script in scope passed, including `ALL 4785 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, `ALL 2602 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` and `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 56 scenario(s) checked against origin/main`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/harness_headers.py` printed `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/typing_ruler.py` with HPO_TYPING_PYTHON=/opt/hpo/venv-ha/bin/python printed `ALL 9 typing-ruler checks PASSED` and `ALL 12 typing-ruler source checks PASSED`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/stress.py` printed `ALL 113 STRESS CHECKS PASSED`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py` printed `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`. `class_excess_loc` went 17640 → 17633, recorded in e3daad4d2. That commit's message says 17655 → 17648 because it was written at the preheat branch's older base. The row moves by the same -7: `_weather_loss_factors` left `HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize`. No other row moved.

**Goldens and the shape claim**
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/env_drift.py --all c3a279e32` without the claim (at e8c8de8e2) printed `4 UNCLAIMED DRIFT(S)`. The four were away_setback, valve_storage_flat_prices, valve_storage_low_target and valve_storage_small_tank. Every moved leaf on this host, may-drift fixtures included, was a `space_reasons[i]`/`dhw_reasons[i]` leaf moving to `'idle_coasting'`. Rule: the drift log's leaf lines, read by eye.
- The same command with the claim (at 5fb4f381a) printed `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 56 scenario(s)` and `NO STALE FIXTURE`, with four `SHAPED` lines.
- `bash dev/audit/harnesses/r10_shape_claim_controls.sh e8c8de8e2 c3a279e32 $OUT` printed `RESULT after_rc=0`, `RESULT narrow_rc=1` and `RESULT null_rc=1`. ARM is the last production commit before the claim, because the harness appends its own claim line.
- The census `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_band_census.py` was not re-run here, because it costs about 25 minutes per host. This host's movers are the env_drift run above, and the claim is by shape, so the census's susceptible set is not an input to it.

**P2 probes (Carry 6 precondition and control)**
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_run_owner_probes.py` printed `RESULT probes_failed=0 count` of 6 at head, `probes_failed=6` at the merge base, and `probes_failed=0` at the merge base with `--perturb`.
- The committed `dev/audit/rounds/round10/D14/sweep-P2/probes_p2.py` at the merge base was run with `defrost_interval` bound in the sixth probe's namespace, on a scratch copy. It printed `RESULT probes_failed=6 count` of 6. The new harness is that probe rebuilt: expressions are found by the local they are assigned to, and the null is rebuilt for this tree.

**Class enumeration (step 8)**
`python3 dev/audit/rounds/round10/D14/sweep-P2/enumerate_p2.py` printed `RESULT F1_run_threshold=13 count` at the merge base and `=9` at head. The four seams that left are exactly the four fixed here. The remaining nine are dispositioned as follows:
- accuracy `delivered_ratio` ×2: a ratio-denominator floor. Registry disposition `accuracy.py::delivered_ratio`.
- climate `hvac_action`: ORed with `heat_pump_on`. Registry disposition `climate.py::HeatPumpOptimizerClimate.hvac_action`.
- coordinator `_detect_immersion`: registry disposition.
- coordinator `_capacity_caps` and `_fold_capacity_envelope` (`p_max <= 0.1`): a capacity bound on the plant's maximum power, not "the plan runs this step". The P2 matcher does not return them.
- dhw_learning `async_learn_usage`: registry disposition.
- freq_control `observe`: a floor on a METERED draw. Registry disposition `freq_control.py::FrequencyMap.observe`.
- optimizer `get_current_action`: registry disposition.

merges.body:
R10-PARTLOAD-PRICING: the residue of R10-COP-PARTLOAD (#2872, #3006). The brief says to measure first and to change a cost law only where the error is material. This pull request does three things:

- It closes the last inline small-buffer fallback (carry 1).
- It lands the instrument that measures carries 2 and 3, `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_partload_pricing.py`, with a zero-derate null on every arm.
- It re-measures carry 0 at this merge base.

It changes no cost law. Carry 6 and the decision on carry 2 wait, as stated under each carry below.

**Carry 1, built.** `ThermalModel._substeps_and_loss`'s two-zone throttled branch had its own copy of the `c_buf < 1e-6 -> 0.04` fallback. Its comment says it mirrors `_simulate_step_two_zone`, and that function has called `_buffer_capacity` since #3006. Now this branch calls `_buffer_capacity(p)` too. The predicate and the value are the same, and the substep counts are identical bit for bit (Null control). This was the last copy (Figures, Class enumeration). The carry names `optimizer.py`, but the copy was in `thermal_model.py`.

**Carry 2: linear valuations under a convex cost. Measured, not segmented.** The scenarios are #3006 round 2's: `r10_cop_partload.py`'s 16 installs on its spread and flat days, at d=0 and at the central plant's derate d=0.112.

- The hot-water LP's objective `price * E / cop`, evaluated on the plan it published, under-prices the derated per-step cost by at most 0.173/day (spread) and 0.267/day (flat). The hot-water cost those plans pay is up to 8.07 and 7.01/day, so the error is at most about 3.8 % of the figure it prices. That is below what I would call material for a planner whose COP law itself carries larger errors. I did not segment the LP.
- `_terminal_cost` and `_deferred_energy_cost` state no refill rate, so their error is a range, not a number:
  - At a modulation-floor refill it is 0.
  - At a max-power refill it is the figure times `d / (1 - d)` (12.6 % at d=0.112): up to 4.37/day for the terminal and 2.13/day for the deferred figure.
  - Which end is true depends on a refill rate the tree does not state. Choosing one is the D0 decision the carry reserves for "a later D0 pass on `_plan_dhw_min_cost` and `_terminal_cost`". I made no change, and the measurement goes forward to that pass (Forward-carry).
- The wood advisor's pump-heat price (`wood_fuel.cheaper_hour_count`, `_scan_wood_night`) has the same secant factor, `P_r / heat_per_cop_kw(P_r) - 1`, at whatever rate the pump would run. It was not measured separately. It goes to the same destination.

**Carry 3: mean-draw pricing. Measured; no change.** Each production cost law was re-run with its module's `power_for_heat_per_cop_kw` swapped, for that call only, for run-power pricing `E * P_run / heat_per_cop_kw(P_run)`. `P_run` is the published hot-water plan's own peak draw (4.0 kW on every hot-water cell).

- **The setpoint sweep's chosen setpoint moved in 0 of 16 cells** at d=0.112 (8 hot-water cells, each on 2 price days). This holds by construction: `P_run` does not depend on the candidate, so run-power pricing scales every candidate's cost by the same factor and cannot reorder them. Only the displayed `cost_per_day` would change.
- **The always-hot baseline's cost rises by up to +0.673/day** against a baseline of about 23/day (+2.9 %). It rises in the same direction on every derated cell, and never falls. The baseline today is the cheaper of the two laws, so `predicted_savings` errs low, which is the conservative direction the baseline's own docstring states for the wood coil.
- Neither change is material to a decision, so neither cost law changes. The carry calls this a design change. Without a decision that moves, I judged it not worth making.

**Carry 0: live buffer store CPU. Re-measured; no fix built.** `r10_buffer_store.py bench 3` at this head (production code identical to the merge base except carry 1's bitwise-identical line) gives:

- owner shape: median 1.57 s, max 2.853 s;
- null: median 0.797 s;
- ratio 1.97x. #3006 measured 2.44x at `507a9ec26`.

The null differs from the owner shape in two levers, flat prices and no buffer, so the ratio is not a one-lever figure. The 272 s owner-box outlier does not reproduce here: max 2.85 s on a 4-core x86_64 container. A bound or warm start has nothing measured here to earn it, so none is built and the carry stays open (Forward-carry).

**Carry 6: the relaxed start's CPU on the owner's Pi. Waits on the owner.** It is owed as a measured `process_time` on the owner's Pi install. A cloud seat cannot take it, and an x86 figure would be the estimate the carry already rejects. It waits for the owner's run.

**Carry 7.** No `coordinator.py` edit. The harness calls `_dhw_setpoint_sweep` on a stub, read-only.

Alternatives considered:

- Segmenting the hot-water LP per step: refused on the measured magnitude, at most 3.8 % of hot-water cost.
- Choosing a terminal refill rate here: refused, because the carry reserves that choice for D0.
- Run-power pricing of the sweep: refused, because it cannot move the recommendation.

**Roster carries, by the checker's numbering.** The brief numbers carries by 0-based roster index. `review_packet.py`'s `brief-carries` count numbers them 1..8. Each roster entry is answered under both numbers:

- Carry 1 (roster index 0, live buffer store CPU): re-measured, not built. See "Carry 0" above. Carry: dismissed: already held open on this group's roster entry at index 0
- Carry 2 (roster index 1, inline 35 L fallback): built. See "Carry 1" above.
- Carry 3 (roster index 2, linear valuations): measured, routed to D0. See "Carry 2" above. Carry: dismissed: already held open on this group's roster entry at index 2
- Carry 4 (roster index 3, mean-draw pricing): measured, no change. See "Carry 3" above.
- Carry 5 (roster index 4): dismissed on the roster as a duplicate of index 2. It is answered by the measurement of index 2, and its flat-price null is in the harness's `flat` arm.
- Carry 6 (roster index 5): dismissed on the roster as a duplicate of index 3. It is answered by the measurement of index 3, flat-price arm included.
- Carry 7 (roster index 6, the relaxed start's Pi CPU): waits on the owner's Pi install. See "Carry 6" above. Carry: dismissed: already held open on this group's roster entry at index 6
- Carry 8 (roster index 7, coordinator lane): no `coordinator.py` edit. See "Carry 7" above.

## Head

Closes #2259

Part 2 of R10-ARCHSCORE-SPELLINGS, the rest of the split ruling. Part 1 (#3169, merged as 871a20da) added `card_rule_copies` (counter C24) for `&&`/`||` rules. Part 2 does two things:

- It makes C24 read a rule spelled as a **template literal**.
- It pays for what the new census reads by deduplicating the real copies in the card.

No budget is raised. `archscore.card_rule_copies` stays capped at 72, and the tree now reads 70.

- **The census** (`tools/audit/archscore/metrics/card.py`). With `strings=True`, `tokenize` keeps each template text segment as one token: a backtick, its place (`W`, `H`, `M`, `T`) and its text. `_templates` lists every template that has a `${..}`, nested templates included. In `rule_copies`, each run of two or more of a template's `${..}` is keyed by `_rule_key`, with the text between them as joints and `roots=True`. Under `roots=True` a value is its root name, numbered, and its members stay as spelled. A run is a rule when some value is read twice, it is `RULE_TOKENS` long, and it carries content. A site is one template. The chain census still reads a template's text as `S`, so its keys are unchanged.
- **The generic exclusion.** A MARKUP template is left out: one whose own text opens or closes a tag (`_MARKUP = <[A-Za-z/!]`). Its `${..}` fill different slots of what it draws, so it is not a rule, and markup belongs to `card_clone_copies`. This criterion excludes the SVG coordinate markup (shared bands, value axis and grid, chart rects, series paths, setup pipe paths) and the quiet-window form. It does not exclude a path string written without a tag, such as `pathPoint`.
- **The payment** (`heatpump-optimizer-card.js`). Every real copy the census reads is now shared:
  - `edgeKey`: `setupSvgHtml`, two sites in `evaluate`, and `removeEdge`.
  - `windowRange`: `formatWindows`, `draftSignature` (through a local `windowSig`), and both clash messages.
  - The overlap `span` in `quietOverlapProblem`, now one loop over the hot-water windows and then the silent ones, in the same order.
  - `storageKey`, built on `storageKeyLegacy`, which is its prefix.
  - `pathPoint`: `steppedLine` and `smoothLine`.
  - One `dropText` in the what-if `summary`.

  Every string the card writes is unchanged (Null control). The brief named four of these. `windowRange` and `dropText` are the two further real copies the census reads; without them the count would have been 77, over the cap.

## Head

`f5f56576b13dbcd8687dfabdbfbef587dcfaf3b9` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3179.md`. The authored code head is `79420455c0717f1fb4f8161787e1603a60304f60`.

Each mutant was run in a detached copy of the fix commit `d85ff06ac` and then restored; `git status --porcelain` was empty afterwards. The C24 checks were driven through `tests/arch_score.py`'s `card_rule_spellings` and `card_template_spellings` with `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`.

merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-CI-CRITPATH-3. main's required `gate` has been red on every push from 8f286293b on `tests / ci-ratchet`: `GREW critical_path_minutes: 40.817 (budget 34.267, band 1.3)`. 8f286293b is a diff of seven `dev/programme/delivery/*.md` rows, which cannot move CI work.

**What was measured.** Runner queueing is not the cause: `run_minutes` already removes each job's queue. No job's work grew either. Each heavy lane draws hosted runners of different speed on the same work. On a slow/quick pair of `fast` logs (c3a279e32 against c7aa12165), both running the same 31 scripts on 3 lanes, the per-script ratio had a median of 1.85 (range 1.6–2.9), and the CPU-bound reference solve read 45.0 ms against 18.8 ms. The fleet is **not two-speed**: over the 40 runs this PR carries, `tests / closures` reads 1117–1613 s, 2040–2401 s, and values in between. The critical path is a max over three ~18-minute lanes, so the median of per-run paths sat on slow draws.

**Fix: change the statistic, not raise the budget.** `critical_path_minutes` is now `window_work_minutes` over the newest `PUSH_WINDOW` (16) push runs:

## Block

The body and the new `window_work_minutes` docstring claim the grade reads work, not host speed: "a job that drew a slow host does not move it unless it drew one in every run of the window" / "A slow host draw moves it only if every one of 16 runs drew slow". Planted on the real 16-run window (the 40 newest ci.yml push runs on main, gathered at this review, `ev/runs40.json`), that is false:

The cause is `floor = max(seen) * OTHER_WORK_FRACTION`: the floor keys on the window **maximum**, the least robust order statistic, so a single slow run past 3x the fastest re-classifies every genuine fast run as "other work" and prices the job on a slow draw. The same shape is already in the data on a lane off the critical chain: `tests / coverage` max 3070 s (a failed run, a9c149289) puts its floor at 1023 s and excludes completed runs of 690-901 s.
- 15 of 16 slow. Each fast draw of `tests / closures` in the newest 15 runs made slow (x1.9, slow draws untouched): 21.717 -> 28.133 (+6.4); `fast` -> 28.667; `arch-instrument` -> 25.933. The fleet is not two-speed (closures reads 1117, 1234, 1245, 1306, 1449, 1608, 1613 s ... 2401 s), so losing the single fastest run reprices on a mid host; "every one of 16 runs drew slow" assumes a two-speed draw the data do not show.
- With the floor taken off the window median instead of the maximum, and only `success` job conclusions pricing, the same single 3.2x outlier moves nothing on any of the three lanes (20.75 -> 20.75) while +300 s on every closures run still moves it +3.23 (ev/perturb_oldmedian_variant.txt; my variant, not a prescription). The repair is local to `window_work_minutes`.

This is the false-red class this PR exists to remove (host draw read as growth), reintroduced through one outlier rather than a median. The self-test pins the floor only against a low "other work" run; it has no high-outlier case, which is the cheap detector the body's own Red-checks section prescribes (feed the statistic the same work with one host far slower; require the grade not to move).

## Findings

- Detection lag, undisclosed: real growth moves a window-minimum only once every pre-growth fast run has aged out. +300 s on `tests / closures` in only the newest k runs reads 21.717 at k = 1, 4, 8; 23.1 at k = 12; 24.95 at k = 15-16 (`fast`: no move until k = 15). The figures here come from my own instrument (ev/gather.py, an*.py, pert*.py), disclosed as mine. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-CI-CRITPATH-3

Both batch-building seams now call the one helper, so there is no second ordering copy. A fronted entry is placed first in the list it sorts and carries `front`, so the stable sort keeps it first in the top tier, as before.

Carries of the brief, each answered in this diff:
Carry 1 (part 2 and P312): the after-merge bookkeeping is `postmerge.py`/`record_beat.py`, run by `merge_pr.sh` and the train's landing; the spool drains `--priority`/`--front`, then critical-path, then arrival, on the live drain (`queue_take`) and on the start path (`train_add`), both through `Train.drain_order`.

## Round

Round 1. Reviewed from a detached worktree at 41790e2b8944e4529a921b27be4b61398e86bef2, which was still the PR head when this verdict was written.

## Block

1. **The merge resolution breaks main's `add --front` (P112).** The textual resolution in `ae3cae823` is correct: main's `--front`/`--remove` block is intact and the item carries `priority`. The semantic resolution is not. Main promises that `--front` puts the entry "FIRST in the next batch" and prints the spool order it read back. This PR's `Train.drain_order` (merge_train.py:3023-3034) re-sorts the whole spool at `queue_take` by `(not priority, not critical)`. A `--front` entry that is not critical therefore drains behind any critical-path entry. My harness `ev/front_vs_drain.py` builds a spool `[#3 critical, #1, #2]` and runs `spool_edit_locked(#1, "front")`. It logs `FRONT #1: spool read back: #1 #3 #2` but drains `[3, 1, 2]`. The null control, with nothing critical, drains `[1, 3, 2]`. So the read-back that `--front` prints does not describe what the train actually runs. Neither the body nor the self-test says how `--front` should rank against `--priority` and the critical path. The fix has two parts. First, decide the rule, for example that a fronted entry keeps first place, or that `--front` sets the same key `--priority` does. Second, pin it with a self-test arm that drives `--front` through `drain_order`.
2. **The `--priority` path is not covered by tests (mutation-vacuous) from the CLI into the spool.** Only `drain_order` is tested, and only on hand-built dicts. The following mutants each leave `merge_train.py --self-test` at 415 checks, 0 failed:
   - R1: drop `**({"priority": True} if a.priority else {})` from the `add` item. SURVIVED.
   - R6: change that line to `if False`. SURVIVED.
   - R4: drop `"priority"` from the spool-entry key list in `train_add` (merge_train.py:1054, added by this PR). SURVIVED.

   R4 matters most. It leaves P312's HOTFIX ordering dead in production: the spool never stores the key, so `drain_order` never sees it, and the suite stays green.

## Findings

- Main's `add --front` ranks below a critical-path entry once this PR's drain sorts the spool, and the read-back it prints no longer matches the drain order (Block 1). Carry: R10-FLY-TRAIN-DEFAULTS
- Surviving mutants R1, R4 and R6 on the `--priority` wiring (Block 2); the fixer owes an arm that drives `add --priority` through `train_add` and the spool into `drain_order`. Carry: R10-FLY-TRAIN-DEFAULTS
- Surviving mutant R2: `front=a.front` changed to `front=False` in `main()`'s add call. This passthrough is main's code (P112), not this diff. Its self-test calls `train_add(front=True)` directly and runs the CLI `--front` only on an already-spooled entry, so the CLI path for a new `--front` entry is untested. The fixer is editing these exact lines for Block 1 and can pin it in the same arm. Carry: R10-FLY-TRAIN-DEFAULTS

- Merge resolution, diffed against both parents. Against main (`fb0a6d5a3`), the conflict hunk differs only by the added `--priority` argument and the `priority` item key. Against `17b38f7d9`, it differs only by main's `--front`/`--remove` block and `front=a.front`. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 41790e2b8944e4529a921b27be4b61398e86bef2` (origin/main `e4c9e2016`) exits 0 with tree `d5a65434a` (`ev/standing.txt`).

## Block

**class-open: the P312 rule ("the train drains its spool into the next batch priority entries first, then critical-path entries, then arrival order"; train.sh's header and `--priority`'s help) is enforced at one of the two places that turn the spool into a batch.**

The spool is read into a batch at two sites (`grep -n "spool_read(" merge_train.py`, production lines only):

- `Train.queue_take` (merge_train.py:3048). It drains a live train's spool through `drain_order`. Round 2 fixed it, and it is pinned.
- `train_add`'s start path (merge_train.py:1044 → 1076). With no live train, `queue = [entry] + spooled if front else spooled + [entry]` builds the new train's first batch from whatever a stopped train left spooled ("spooled entries stay for the next train", `queue_close`) plus the new entry. It never calls `drain_order`.

My harness `ev/start_path.py` covers the start path. A stopped train left `[#3 critical, #1]` in the spool, there is no live train, and the harness adds #4. The train would be launched over these queues:

- `--priority`: `start_queue=[3, 1, 4]`. `drain_order` of the same entries gives `[4, 3, 1]`. The HOTFIX runs **last**, behind the entries a stopped train left, which are exactly the ones whose train stopped.
- `--front`: `[4, 3, 1]`, the same as `drain_order`. This path is correct at this head.
- Null control, a plain add: `[3, 1, 4]`, the same as `drain_order`.

The body does not name this seam, the diff does not change it, and no self-test arm covers it. The repair is one line on the seam the fixer already owns: order the start queue with `t.drain_order(...)`. A fronted entry carries `front` and stays first. The fix also needs a self-test arm on the start path with a leftover spool and `--priority`.

- The start path of `train_add` builds the new train's queue from leftover spool entries plus the new entry without `drain_order`. As a result, `add --priority` runs a HOTFIX last whenever a stopped train left entries spooled, and critical-path leftovers keep arrival order (Block). Carry: R10-FLY-TRAIN-DEFAULTS

`tools/audit/seat/bus.sh orphans` died on macOS bash 3.2 under `set -u` (`arms[@]: unbound variable`) whenever neither `--no-ancestry` nor `--no-content` was given, so `pulse.py`'s opener arm read UNREADABLE and orphaned handoffs were invisible (triage P303). Fix: the ledger.py call uses `${arms[@]+"${arms[@]}"}`. Class barrier: `tools/audit/seat/bare_array.py`, a static rule over every tracked `tools/**/*.sh` file, with or without `set -u` of its own (a sourced library runs under its caller's `-u`, and nounset has spellings a textual test misses): a bare `"${a[@]}"` is refused unless guarded, or unless `# never-empty: <reason>` sits on the line or on a comment-only line directly above it. It is pinned in `tests/entities.py`, run as a governance step and listed in `tools/audit/seat/INSTRUMENTS.md`. CI's bash 5 expands an empty array cleanly, so a run-time row would pass on the defect; the rule is therefore static. A never-empty reason placed after a `# mut:<name>` marker is refused in every file, because the self-tests find their mutant line by that marker at the line's end. Alternative rejected: plain variables in bus.sh lose the two-flag list the call forwards; the guard is the smaller change.

Departure from the group brief, stated: the roster brief asks for the check over files "running under `set -u`" with the null control "a file without `set -u` is not judged". Commit 07f79c3cf inverts that control: every tracked tools script is judged. Reason: the sourced `pr_args.sh` has no `set -u` of its own yet runs under its callers', and five of its sites would otherwise stay invisible to the rule. The control is now the twin pair "a file without set -u is judged too" and "the guarded form passes in a file without set -u (null)".

Carry 1 (the roster's carry from the R10-FLY-RAISE-REVIEWABLE round-2 fixer: `bus.sh orphans` fails on a macOS seat with `arms[@]: unbound variable`, bash-3.2 self-test row and a non-empty-array null control asked for): the empty-array expansion is guarded in `bus.sh orphans`. The reviewer decides whether that departure discharges the carry.

## Head

merges.body:
Part 1 of R10-AGREEMENT-BOOTSTRAP (#3100, stranded carry 35): the grader learns to accept a SHARED_GRAMMARS entry that lands before its grammar's second reader. Closes #3100. This replaces #3166's `bootstrap:` marker, which the round-1 review blocked (verdict/3166): its stale refusal reddened the second reader's pull request under the base-copy grader. Same split as R10-MACHINERY-RATCHETS part 1 (#3165) and R10-BASH-KILL-HOOK part 1 (#3168): graders first, here alone.

The rule. An ordinary disposition (`pair:`, `module:`, `identical:`, `not-a-concept:`) may end ` (awaits <path>)`. At one file such an entry is not DEAD while all of these hold: exactly one file reads the grammar; `<path>` is governance code, absent from the tree, and never on HEAD's history; and the clause landed at most 7 days before HEAD, by committer date on HEAD's first-parent line. Every failed condition reads DEAD with its own reason. Once a second file reads the grammar the entry is an ordinary two-file entry, which main's copy, the one CI pins, accepts unchanged. So the reader's pull request needs no edit to the pinned file. The spent clause is a note, never a refusal. The age bound is fatal only where the registry graded is the one HEAD commits (main's push run, a local run). A pull request that drops an expired entry is graded by the base's copy, which still holds the entry, and reads a note there. Entries without the clause read exactly as before.

Why this rule and not another:
- #3166's `bootstrap:` marker, with a stale refusal at two files. Rejected: a refusal keyed on registry content can only be cured by editing the registry, which CI restores from the base, so the reader's pull request is red (measured below).
- Accept any one-file entry. Rejected: a reader that left would no longer read DEAD, which is a steady-state bypass.
- Accept a one-file entry only in the commit that adds it (a diff against HEAD^1). Rejected: the entry would read DEAD at the next unrelated merge and on every pull request after it, until the reader lands.
- The clause as chosen keys acceptance on facts the grader measures, not on free text: whether the path is in the tree, whether it is in history, and the clause's age. It has no free-text reason to bound. A path that never arrives expires after 7 days. A path that once existed, whether copied from another entry or left behind by a reader, never qualifies.

There is no concrete entry yet. The carry is the grader capability alone: carry 35 records that "Route B avoided it" at 98b532ab1, so no grammar waits on this today. merges.body:
R10-FLY-RELAY-REVIEW-FF, carries round: the relay, tick loop, bus and carry_audit carries still owed after #2664, with CARRY-DISPOSITION's and RELAY-TOOLS-LEVEL's carries folded in. Part of #201.

**Already on main, not rebuilt.** P15 (`relay_start` passes `--confirm`, `tick_loop-3`), P-O (the confirm arm), and Carry 2's transient retry with `REFUSED <ref> <sha> <reason>`: `cloud_relay.sh` already holds `confirm_arm`, `HPO_RELAY_TRIES` and the `probe-refused` level. `--confirm` replaces the orchestrator's read of the reviewer thread with the relay's nonce, head and dispatch-record checks (decided 2026-10-18).

**Built here, one commit each:**
- `tick_loop.sh` (P14, as Carry 8 reconciles it). Each pass fetches `origin main` and counts `HEAD..origin/main -- tools/audit/seat tools/pr tools/audit/carry_audit.py`.
  - `code=<sha7> behind=<n>` goes on the `TICK-PASS` banner and in the heartbeat message.
  - Past `HPO_TICK_STALE_BOUND` (25), or on any commit touching `tick_loop.sh` or `cloud_relay.sh`, the loop restarts between passes, at most once a pass. It needs the relay lock free and a clean detached tree, and `bash -n` must pass on origin/main's copy. It then checks out origin/main detached and `exec`s it with the same args.
  - Otherwise `TICK-STALE ...: <why>`, the relay and sweep arms are skipped (`relay=stale`), and the board is still written.
  - Never a fast-forward in place, never an exit.
- `cloud_relay.sh`:
  - review_freeze holds only on a dispatch record of the PR at its head, and HELD-REVIEW names `dispatch=<nonce8> at=<utc>` (P288). The detached-worktree arm is removed.
  - `update_pr.sh` runs from `<state>/relay-tools`, a tools tree the relay levels to origin/main when clean. A dirty tree is refused by name and owed; a busy one (a live pid's `relay-tools.lock`) waits (P283).
  - The no-return line `SEAT ENDED NO RETURN <topic>` is `seat-no-return` on the level (P-E, below).
  - The confirm arm skips a relayed review whose PR is not in the pass's open-PR listing, once, owing nothing; a failed listing skips nothing (P332, Carry 18, landed on the roster after the dispatch).
- `bus.sh`:
  - push-verdict refuses before `review/<pr>` moves:
    - a line its post would refuse (`ref_privacy.py body-lines`, naming the line, P76);
    - a finding item with no valid `Carry:` (`carry_audit.py check`, P40/P207).
  - Its push carries `-c http.postBuffer=524288000` (#2563's HTTP 400).
  - dispatch reads a dependabot-only head's row at origin/main (P100), and refuses a body carry its group does not hold, printing the `roster_edit.py append-carry` op (CARRY 0, P310). `watch` holds a single-instance lock (P102).

## Findings

- The hook does not treat compound-command keywords as command position: `if true; then pkill x; fi`, `for i in 1; do pkill x; done`, `{ pkill x; }`, `if pkill x; then :; fi` and `pgrep x | while read p; do kill $p; done` all exit 0 (allowed). `then`/`do`/`else`/`{` are consumed as the command word, so the real command becomes an argument. The header's KNOWN GAPS list does not name this one, and it is the most plausible shape in a seat's script. Fix is adding those keywords to the pass-through set. Not blocking: the hook documents that it fails open and the other gaps are named by design. Carry: R10-BASH-KILL-HOOK | #2732 | O1 | dismissed: not dismissed; routed to the group's issue as a follow-up hardening
- False positive: `command -v pkill` / `command -v killall` exit 2 (refused) although nothing is killed, because `command` is in WRAP and `-v` is skipped as its flag. `which pkill`, `type -a pkill`, `man pkill` are allowed. Low impact (a seat is told not to use pkill) but it breaches "never blocks a legitimate non-kill command". Carry: R10-BASH-KILL-HOOK | #2732 | O2 | dismissed: not dismissed; routed to the group's issue as a follow-up
- Other surviving bypasses beyond the documented gaps: `timeout 5 pkill x` (wrapper with a value argument; same family as the documented `sudo -u`), `busybox pkill x`, `ssh host pkill x`, `echo pkill x | sh`, `bash <<< 'pkill x'`, `python3 -c 'os.system("pkill x")'`, `pgrep x > f; kill $(cat f)`, and `pkill\<newline> x` (line continuation). They are all outside "command position" for this hook or inside a different interpreter; I judge them not worth a name-matching rule. Carry: R10-BASH-KILL-HOOK | #2732 | O3 | dismissed: accepted residue of a name-matching guard; bypassing needs deliberate evasion and the hook is a guard against accidents, not an adversary

## Evidence

- Drove the REAL `.claude/settings.json` Bash PreToolUse command with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR at the head, 94 cases of my own (`ev/cases.txt`): 74 as expected; the 18 differences are the items under Findings. The origin/main `policy_lint.mjs` run against the head's settings.json accepts it (rc 0), so part 1's graders accept this change unmodified. Fixtures: bash-matcher.json (null control) passes, bash-under-edit-matcher.json is refused (rc 1) with `MATCHER BLIND ... pre-bash.sh`, the reason it exists; empty/no/star-matcher gain only the Bash entry (needed because REQUIRED now demands it) plus pretty-print reflow, and still pass with their original pre-edit matcher; removing the Bash entry from settings makes `--hooks` rc 1. prepr.sh: the two loops gain the new fixture names and one label is reworded; nothing skipped.
