merges.body:
R10-OPENER-REUSE part 1 (issue #3123, instrument): `tools/audit/seat/open_driver.py`, the open arm of the session-local opener as a tracked instrument. It resolves part topics to their roster group (P363), orders them by default class with a critical-path floor, and prints STARVED (P350). It marks a (topic, sha) seen only on rc=0, and otherwise retries with backoff and prints OWED. This re-cut adds a pin and nothing else: the self-test now reaps a slash topic's result, so the reap side of the slash-topic fix (`run_pass` reading `stem(t)`) can no longer be reverted with the self-test green.

Refs #3123: the group stays open until its next part lands.

## Re-cut

Round 3, a minimal re-cut that the orchestrator ruled past the three-round limit. It answers one finding, verdict/3164's block "mutation-vacuous: the reap side of the slash-topic fix (run_pass reads stem(t).rc) survives reversion with the self-test green". The diff since the previous code head is one self-test row pair in `tools/audit/seat/open_driver_selftest.py` and three mutants in `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_open_driver_mutants.py`. Production code is unchanged. The round history is deleted.

## Head

`051c1cd41f0237595e40e0d235797dce0bbd4249` merges main `279cb49` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`a9541f2f83649630ffbe20405d4334db693bcbef` merges the authored code head `3de2926c6e407a05539b15081c4fb655580353b6` and then merges origin/main `8fcaf47e1` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

The code head is `3de2926c6e407a05539b15081c4fb655580353b6`, measured with `git rev-parse HEAD`. Its one parent is the PR head `cee9f6f446c86e8c27b0e88d3193f8030c4c1726`, and `handoff/r10-opener-reuse` (0321068b2) is an ancestor, so the handoff push is a fast-forward. origin/main is at `8fcaf47e1d6989b6c5f2a053aaa0f2b79c24067a`, and `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0 with no conflict, so main is not merged in, as the brief rules. main did not move between my `tools/pr/prepr.sh` run and the handoff, so no second run was needed. The new handoff head is this code head.

## Mutation proof

Two harnesses, both run at the head with nothing mutated (the null control) and with each mutant applied.

1. `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_open_driver_mutants.py` applies one exact replacement per mutant to a copy of `tools/audit/seat/` and runs the copy's `--self-test`. M0 prints `failed=0`. All 19 mutants are killed (`RESULT survived=0`). The three new ones:

| side | mutant | the line reverted | self-test checks that go red |
|---|---|---|---|
| open | M-open-stem | `rc = d / f"{stem(topic)}.rc"` -> `f"{topic}.rc"` in `World.launch` | `launch 'a/b': rc file written with 0`, `slash topic reaped: RESULT a/b rc=0 with its log's reason`, `slash topic reaped: seen, not reopened` (3) |
| reap | M-reap-stem | `rcf = d / f"{stem(t)}.rc"` -> `f"{t}.rc"` in `run_pass` | `slash topic reaped: RESULT a/b rc=0 with its log's reason`, `slash topic reaped: seen, not reopened` (2) |
| reap (log) | M-reap-log | `reason(d / (stem(t) + '.log'))` -> `(t + '.log')` | `slash topic reaped: RESULT a/b rc=0 with its log's reason` (1) |

At the previous head cee9f6f44 the same three mutants give these results: M-open-stem fails 1 check (`launch 'a/b': rc file written with 0`), while M-reap-stem and M-reap-log stay green at `66 checks, 0 failed`. That is the vacuity the block names.

The other 16 mutants are unchanged from the previous round and all are killed. M-launch puts the old `bash -c` interpolation back. It fails `launch 'r10-a;touch INJECTED': rc file written with 0` and `... topic arrives as one argument`, and then the self-test crashes with FileNotFoundError at that topic's `log written` read. The mutant dies with rc=1, but the rows after that point are not evaluated under it.

2. The finder's harness. I ran verdict/3164's `evidence/reap_probe.py` (git blob 56aca252a7976352174c0a839f2e74e1a8acd12b) and `evidence/launch_probe.py` (blob a0baa3cc569719d90ad09bad1d223b7a29ce98a3) against a copy of `tools/audit/seat/` at each end:

| tree | self-test | reap_probe | launch_probe |
|---|---|---|---|
| cee9f6f44, M0 | 66 checks, 0 failed | failed=0 | checks=30 failed=0 |
| cee9f6f44, M-reap-stem | 66 checks, 0 failed (survives) | failed=1 (`FAIL a/b SKIP a/b 44444444 live`) | failed=0 |
| head, M0 | 68 checks, 0 failed | failed=0 | checks=30 failed=0 |
| head, M-reap-stem | 2 failed, rc=1 (killed) | failed=1 | failed=0 |
| head, M-open-stem | 3 failed, rc=1 (killed) | failed=1 | failed=3 (`topic='a/b' rc_file_0=False` per state dir) |
| head, M-reap-log | 1 failed, rc=1 (killed) | failed=0 | failed=0 |

At every row the self-test and the finder's probes agree on the slash-topic mutants, with one exception. The reap_probe checks only `RESULT a/b 44444444 rc=0` and `seen`, not the reason text, so it does not see M-reap-log. The new self-test row also asserts the reason (`opened`, read from the topic's stemmed log), and that is what kills M-reap-log.

## Null control

The unmodified head passes every row: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/open_driver.py --self-test` prints `open_driver self-test: 68 checks, 0 failed`. The new rows run a slash topic `a/b` through `run_pass` with a world whose `launch` is the real `World.launch` (a dummy `open_pr.sh` that prints `opened`, and a state directory containing a space) and whose `alive` is the real `World.alive`. Each pass checks something different:
- Pass 1 launches the topic.
- Pass 2 must log `RESULT a/b 44444444 rc=0 opened`, so the reap reads the stemmed `.rc` and the stemmed log.
- Pass 3 must print exactly `SKIP a/b 44444444 seen` and launch nothing more.

The finder's reap_probe at the head prints `ok   a/b RESULT a/b 44444444 rc=0 opened | SKIP a/b 44444444 seen | SKIP a/b 44444444 seen` and `RESULT reap_probe failed=0`, so a slash topic's result is reaped.

## Unpinned sites

`tools/pr/prepr.sh` step 6d lists none for this diff. The `tools/` sites the open driver adds are pinned by the in-tree mutant harness `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_open_driver_mutants.py` (19 mutants, 0 survived), because `mutation-autofix` mutates `custom_components/` only.

## Figures

- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/open_driver.py --self-test` prints `open_driver self-test: N checks, 0 failed`.
- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_open_driver_mutants.py` prints `RESULT mutants=19` and `RESULT survived=0`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py` prints STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED. No budget file is touched, and no figure moved beyond the self-test's check count and the harness's mutant count.
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 2 script(s) run, 31 scoped out` (tests/entities.py, tests/harness_headers.py), and `tests/run.sh` with `GATE_SCOPE=auto` is green.
- Instrument scope: the self-test drives the git layer against a throwaway bare origin, and `World.launch` and `World.alive` against a scratch directory with a dummy opener. It does not drive `roster_lib.show_roster` on the live roster or the real `open_pr.sh`.

## Red checks

none. `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py classify cee9f6f446c86e8c27b0e88d3193f8030c4c1726 --pr 3164` reads the whole paginated check-run set at the PR head and prints `GREEN ... pending: none red: none`. The new code head has no check runs until it becomes the PR head.

## Forward-carry

The roster `dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json` holds the group's carries, numbered 1 to 10:
- Carry 5 (seen only on rc=0, backoff, OWED line): built in the driver. The tick that prints the OWED lines is the next part. Carry: R10-OPENER-REUSE part 2.
- Carry 8 (P337 open driver, open arm), Carry 9 (P350), Carry 10 (P363): built here. Carry: R10-OPENER-REUSE part 2 (the opener session and tick adopt the driver).
- Carry 1, Carry 2 (card 4: hold lifted by the no-merge-queue ruling; body-only parts): not built. Carry: R10-OPENER-REUSE part 2.
- Carry 3, Carry 4 (prepr reuse in update_pr/open_pr with row_only_checks including tests/structure.py): not built, size. Carry: R10-OPENER-REUSE part 2.
- Carry 6 (opener checkout collected, one per-PR checkout in update_pr.sh): not built. Carry: R10-OPENER-REUSE part 2.
- Carry 7 (pr_args.sh records its absolute directory at source time, P362): not built. Carry: R10-OPENER-REUSE part 2.
- verdict/3164 finding: `stem()` maps `/` to `%2F` without escaping `%` first, so `a/b` and `a%2Fb` share one `.rc`. A topic named `open-driver` would also overwrite the driver's own log. Not touched in this minimal re-cut, and not yet in the roster entry: the brief allows no other change, so the roster op (`dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json`) is the orchestrator's. Carry: R10-OPENER-REUSE part 2.
- verdict/3164 finding: the hostile-topic `log written` read is unguarded, so M-launch crashes the self-test instead of reporting each row. The mutant is still killed, and its figure is corrected above. Like the finding above, it is not yet in the roster entry (`dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json`). Carry: R10-OPENER-REUSE part 2.

## Block

1. **mutation-vacuous: `elif topic in runs: skip("live")`** (tools/audit/seat/open_driver.py, run_pass). The docstring and the instrument note list `live` as a skip rule. If you replace it with `elif False:`, `open_driver.py --self-test` still prints 45 checks, 0 failed. Under that mutant, two passes over the same board with the first run still alive launch `open_pr.sh` twice for one (topic, sha): `launches 2`, pid=101 then pid=102 (ev/live_probe_mutant.txt). The unmutated code launches once and logs `SKIP r10-x 44444444 live` (ev/live_probe.txt). That second launch is a duplicate concurrent open of one PR, and the second write to `runs[topic]` loses track of the first PID. Owed: a self-test row covering it, and an M-live row in r10_open_driver_mutants.py.
2. **Shell injection and slash-topic breakage in `World.launch`**. The topic and the state directory are pasted unquoted into the `bash -c` string (`> {d}/{topic}.log ... echo $? > {rc}`), not passed as arguments. Both `refs/heads/handoff/z$(touch${IFS}INJECTED)` and `refs/heads/handoff/a/b` pass `git check-ref-format`. With a dummy open_pr.sh in a scratch copy, the first topic created the file `INJECTED`, so it runs code on the orchestrator's machine. Neither topic leaves its `.rc` file, so the next pass reaps the run as rc=-1 and backs it off forever (ev/launch_probe.txt). A `$HPO_STATE_DIR` containing a space breaks the same way. Fix: pass the log and rc paths as positional arguments, quoted (`> "$1"`), or redirect from Popen. Add a self-test row that drives `World.launch` with a metacharacter topic.

## Findings

- The quantified backoff schedule, "5 min doubling to 2 h" (docstring and instrument note), is not pinned. Mutants `BACKOFF_S 300->600` and `BACKOFF_MAX_S 7200->14400` both leave the self-test green, because `backoff doubles` compares against the constants themselves. Add a row asserting `backoff(1)==300` and `backoff(6)==7200`. Carry: R10-OPENER-REUSE
- The quantified "first three lines of the handoff body" rule (`World.body_head`, `splitlines()[:3]`) is not driven. Mutants `[:4]` and the whole body both survive, and the body says the self-test drives only `World.tips` and `World.landed` on the git layer. Drive `body_head` against the throwaway origin that already exists. Carry: R10-OPENER-REUSE
- Two smaller rules survive: "one per topic (the first line wins)" in parse_board (mutant `if m:`), and the `R10-TRIAGE-B<M>` fallback (mutant that drops it). Carry: R10-OPENER-REUSE
- The instrument note, tools/audit/seat/instruments/open_driver.py.md, says `triage-s<N>-batch<M>` maps to `R10-TRIAGE-S<N>`. It omits the `R10-TRIAGE-B<M>` fallback that the code and the module docstring both have. Carry: R10-OPENER-REUSE
- The body's `## Head` section contradicts itself. It says 91e4f39ff merges origin/main 8f286293b into 03f6ebbe8, and then says "no merge was needed ... so per the brief it was not merged". The commit list (`git log 8f286293b..709f438c04388cd8e0ec32d9f27d9881e8d91ba7`) shows the merge commit, so the second paragraph is stale. Carry: R10-OPENER-REUSE

## Evidence

- RESULT selftest: `open_driver self-test: 45 checks, 0 failed`, rc=0 (ev/selftest.txt).

- RESULT reviewer mutants, 22 planted, none of them the fixer's (ev/reviewer_mutants.txt). Killed: STARVE 2 h->3 h, DEFAULT_CAP 2->3, the whole-name lookarounds, the fix-branch and `-pr` skips, the moved and no-body skips, killed-PID-as-success, `live = 0`, each strip rule alone, the hotfix class, the part title, the OWED line, landed f[1]. Survived: `live` skip, backoff base, backoff max, body head [:4], body head whole, parse_board first-wins, triage B fallback.
- Suffix strip (brief item 3): the four split-part shapes the opener missed are self-test rows: r10-sav-comfort-p2, r10-prepr-cap-2, r10-fly-train-defaults-p2 and r10-ux-health-p3, plus r10-roster-ops-2-p1. **What the pull request does (unchanged since verdict `9070029ac258bc819e486d57b00b84a89e559936`).** One predicate, `roster_lib.pending_carries(group, legacy)`, says which carries a group still owes. A carry is discharged by a mark at its end (`[implemented: <sha>]`, `[moved: <GROUP>]` or `[dismissed: <reason>]`, `roster_lib.carry_mark`), or it is legacy, meaning a closed group held it at the cut-over (`roster_lib.CARRY_CUTOVER`). `closing_stage` writes `done` over a pending carry as `carries-open`. Its readers are `roster_edit.py set-stage`/`set-resume --field stage`, `roster_sync.py`'s merge transition (`derive()` and `apply_plan()`, both given the cut-over set), and `carry_audit.py roster` (STRANDED, ISSUE-STRANDED, ISSUE-UNLISTED). It adds `roster_edit.py mark-carry`, and a brief_lint warning on a live group with no issue.

**This head is a merge resolution, and nothing else.** It adds no finding, so `## Forward-carry` is the reviewed body's, unchanged. merges.body:
R10-996-RUNNER-CLAIMS, third PR: carry 3 (P214, ruling `dev/programme/triage/s6-batch41.md#P214`, ACCEPT, V127) only. Closes nothing: the group has no issue wired (#3099 tracks the part).

When main's claim driver refuses a merge, the merge-main bot answered only `skip-driver-refused tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt`, as it did on #2872 at `fe964895e`. The driver's decision text was already on the merge's stderr: `tests/env_drift.py`'s `merge_claim_refusal`, printed by `run_merge_driver` after its `MERGE-CLAIM: refused <path>` line. `merge_tree` captured that stderr, and `decide` dropped it.

The fix is `claim_refusal(driver_err)` in `tools/pr/merge_main_bot.py`. When the stderr holds the claim driver's `MERGE-CLAIM: refused ` line, `decide` appends that stderr under today's status line, verbatim and indented four spaces. Otherwise it appends nothing.
- The bot writes no summary of its own, so the driver's message stays the one source and its wording lives in `env_drift.py` only.
- The one string the bot keys on is the driver's refusal-line prefix, `CLAIM_REFUSED`. The self-test arm drives the real `tests/env_drift.py --merge-claim-file`, so a change to that prefix turns the arm red rather than silently dropping the relay.

**File ownership.** `tools/pr/merge_main_bot.py` belongs to this group by the P214 ruling's `edit-brief`, which the orchestrator has queued as the roster's `edit-brief`/`set-files`. The roster's `files` at this base still lists only `tests/env_drift.py` and `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt`.

**Code owners and policy.** `tools/pr/merge_main_bot.py` is not code-owned. `python3 dev/audit/rounds/round6/D11/fix/codeowners_gap.py` lists it as `NO-PR-JOB tools/pr/merge_main_bot.py` (on the enforcement surface, run by `merge-main.yml` on a push to `main`, with no owner pattern), and it is not a policy file named in `CLAUDE.md`. No claim file is touched and no claim is decided.

**One design choice, and the alternative that lost.** The relay carries the drivers' whole stderr for that merge, not only the claim driver's block. When a ledger driver resolved a file in the same merge, its `LEDGER-MERGE: resolved` lines appear too (see the #2872 replay under `## Figures`). The alternative was to cut out the claim block alone. That would mean parsing where the claim driver's text ends, keyed on wording of both drivers (the claim message's own lines also open with an uppercase `WORD:` prefix). That parsing is the second reader the ruling forbids. The extra lines are the drivers' own accurate output.

## Head

`92e5ca96207511a480bc655ebecf39972fed875e` merges main `94d8b47` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`36143360cea1d1076d917daa23898e0590a73872` merges the authored code head `ebb90ba992cff355674d5cf24d844722eee93914` and then merges origin/main `78dd34354` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

Handoff head `ebb90ba992cff355674d5cf24d844722eee93914`; the round-1 code head was `1e1d346b206bdad37f63e38c83ea268f6c48e9c3`, and this round adds one test-only commit on top of it, in `tools/pr/merge_main_bot.py`'s self-test alone (9 inserted lines; `claim_refusal` and `decide` are unchanged). `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`: `tools/pr/merge_main_bot.py | 91 +++++-` , 1 file changed, 89 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-). `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` is `7f849a24911e9d52336bd79ea9ce63c67416a6ae`. `origin/main` has moved since round 1 (to `0166aefd7`); `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` reports no conflict, so I merged nothing, as the brief permits a merge only on a conflict. The claim-relay arm also asserts `relayed.startswith(f"{CLAIM_REFUSED}{cf}")`: the relayed text opens with `MERGE-CLAIM: refused tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt`. - **append-on-other-conflict** (`decide` appends `claim_refusal(driver_err)` to `skip-other-conflict`). A decide loop with `text_conflicts=["led.json","a.py"]` asserts exactly `skip-other-conflict a.py`, once with a claim-refusal `driver_err` and once with an empty one. Both mutants were rebuilt from `evidence/mut.py` and `evidence/mut2.py` on `verdict/3153`, run against `python3 tools/pr/merge_main_bot.py --self-test`, and restored (`git diff --stat` shows only the 9 added lines):

## Mutation proof

- **append-on-other-conflict**: `decide` returns `"skip-other-conflict " + ",".join(other) + claim_refusal(driver_err)`. `plan_one` computes `driver_err` whenever git's text merge conflicts, so on a real merge that also conflicts on a non-driver file, this status would change while every arm stays green. The body's class enumeration says "no other status relays it", but no test pins that. Repair: a decide-table row (or plan_one arm) with `text_conflicts=["led.json","a.py"]` and a claim-refusal `driver_err`, asserting exactly `skip-other-conflict a.py`.

A driver writing non-UTF-8 bytes to stderr would raise UnicodeDecodeError in `merge_tree`, which `run`'s `except (RuntimeError, KeyError)` does not catch, and that would fail merge-main.yml. The same line is in the base (`git show 25c46e76e:tools/pr/merge_main_bot.py`), and `claim_refusal` itself can raise nothing (str operations only). Both in-tree drivers print str built from repo text. Carry: dismissed: predates this PR, not reachable from the in-tree drivers, which print decoded text
- The relay has no size cap: a 100,001-line stderr is relayed in full (1,388,917 chars) to stdout and `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. A summary over GitHub's 1 MiB limit is dropped with an annotation and does not fail the step, and realistic refusals run about 15 lines (the #2872 replay). - **Lever L6, the patch rule** (tvofi 2026-10-30). A commit of the branch's own no longer refuses on sight. It carries where the head's tree is git's automatic merge of the reviewed head onto the main it now sits on, outside the files the comparison leaves out, and the branch's own diff still compares equal. That covers a revert and its re-apply, an empty commit, and a side merge that changes nothing. `review_carry.py` drops its own non-merge pre-filter and asks `carry()` alone, so `bus.sh dispatch` stops minting those re-reviews.
- **P264, `app_comment.sh`.** When a merge verdict's head is not the live head, `check_pr` fetches main and the PR head and runs `app_approve.sh --carry`. It posts on `CARRY: yes` with the last body line `carry: <verdict> -> <live>, app_approve.sh --carry: yes`, and prints that line. Otherwise it refuses `head moved` with the carry's reason, as before. Blocked verdicts are unchanged.
- **The driver files' end state** (round 2, the round-1 block). Every comparison in `carry()` leaves main's merge-driver files out (`.gitattributes` `merge=`: the three ledgers, `bugclasses.json` and the two claim files). What each holds at the head is now read on its own. It must be one of:
  - git's automatic merge of the reviewed head onto H's merge base with main;
  - main's own driver output on the two (`driver_wrote`, which generalises `claim_driver_wrote` to `ledgermerge`), for a clone with no drivers configured;
  - for a claim file, the union of both sides;
  - the file as the newest carried, author-checked bot commit left it, and only where the file is one of that subject's own `bot_paths`.

  So a budget, closure or claim line written by a commit of the branch's own, by a bare `ci:` subject, by a merge's hand resolution, or by a bot subject outside its own paths keeps the re-review.

## Block

Under L6 a commit of the branch's own now carries when (a) the head's tree equals git's automatic merge of the reviewed head onto main and (b) the branch's own diff compares equal. Both checks pass `:(exclude)` for every file main's `.gitattributes` gives a merge driver: tests/structure_budgets.json, tests/mutation_budgets.json, tests/closures.json, dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json, and the two claim files. Before L6 a non-bot commit refused on sight, so that exclusion only ever applied to bot commits confined to their subject's paths. After L6 an ordinary `fix: ...` commit can change those files freely and still carry.

Reproduced at this head (ev/replay-budget-raise.txt, ev/replay-claimfile.txt): a commit `fix: tidy wording` that appends a digit to the first value in tests/structure_budgets.json gives `CARRY: yes d84340362 -> 4e3d100be`. A second commit appending a line to tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt also gives CARRY: yes. Neither the new budget nor the claim line was ever reviewed. The budget-raise-gate and env_drift run on the new head, but the reviewer's merge verdict, which the owner's gate treats as a review of the head, now stands over exactly those edits.

Fix: in the own-commit case, do not apply the driver-file exclusion (or exclude only the files a bot commit in the range wrote), so the tree check and the comparison cover the driver files too. A self-test needs both a budget-edit and a claim-file-edit twin that refuse.

## Findings

- The own-commit path above is the block. Carry: R10-FLY-CARRY-DOC-CONTEXT | #3077 | O1 | dismissed: blocked in this verdict, to be fixed in the PR.
- P123's residual (a tvofi-authored row commit naming another PR's number) is only exploitable for a file under dev/programme/delivery/. The path is bound to the subject's number, and the commit is confined to that one file and to tvofi's identity. I found no use beyond a row. Carry: R10-FLY-CARRY-DOC-CONTEXT | #3077 | O2 | dismissed: data file, one path, owner identity only.
- The .md context mask also covers CLAUDE.md, dev/governance/** and .claude/**, which seats load as instruction. A context-only rewrite by main beside the branch's lines can change a rule's meaning while the carry stays yes. That matches how code merges are already treated (main's content is main's reviewed content), but the head's own tree is never re-read for it. Not blocking, raised for the owner together with the beyond-brief "or keep its patch (L6)" clause in orchestrator.md section 11, which I note and do not decide. Carry: R10-FLY-CARRY-DOC-CONTEXT | #3077 | O3 | dismissed: owner decision, flagged here.

merges.body:
deps(tests): the pip group's bumps from Dependabot #3088, re-applied by the fixer, with homeassistant-stubs held at 2026.9.3

Supersedes #3088

The owner asked for this on 2026-11-01. Dependabot's branch cannot be edited, so this branch re-applies the version changes from #3088 (head bffd45a03, base d052f80f7) to the four test requirement files, cut from main. The four files are byte-identical between d052f80f7 and main. The bumps are #3088's, except one pin held back (below). The reds at #3088's head were bisected to four causes:

1. **Stale hashes on three pins.** Dependabot changed the version of coverage 7.17.0, cryptography 50.0.2 and uv 0.13.6 and kept the previous version's `--hash` lines, so pip's hash-checking mode refused each install. That turned `tests / coverage` red (`coverage-ratchet` then had no `coverage-json` artifact) and `tests / typing` red. Each block now holds every sha256 PyPI publishes for that version. The coverage block is its header's compile; the typing lock body reproduces byte-identically from its header's compile (below).
2. **The ruler's pinned pair.** `tests/typing_ruler.py`'s source-only check in `fast` refuses a lock whose mypy or homeassistant-stubs pin disagrees with `tests/typing_budgets.json`'s `ruler`. That was the one failed script in `tests / fast (3.14)`. `ruler.mypy` moves 2.3.1 -> 2.4.1. **The budget-raise gate reads that key as frozen, so this needs tvofi's approving review** (`## Raise justification`).
3. **homeassistant-stubs 2026.10.0 is held back at 2026.9.3** (Carry below). 2026.10.0 is an empty release that deprecates the package; its PyPI summary is "Deprecated: Home Assistant Core ships its own type information". Under it mypy reads Home Assistant's own py.typed annotations, and the ruler's census goes from 0 to 70 errors. CI never reached that, because the typing install failed first. Moving the ruler off the stubs changes what the census measures, so it is a design change, not a version bump. homeassistant 2026.10.4 still lands, as a lock override, because stubs 2026.9.3 pin homeassistant==2026.9.3.
4. **mypy 2.4.1's `reversed()`.** Its overload returns `Any` for a sequence whose element type holds `Any`. `SnapshotRing.best_restore` returned the loop variable, which made one `no-any-return` error. `learner_progress.snapshot_rates` lost its loop type with no error. Both loop variables are now declared before the loop.

Until a seat's venv-ha is rebuilt from this lock, that seat's `python3 tests/typing_ruler.py` refuses `mypy is pinned at 2.4.1  [found 2.3.1]` (guard 2, measured on this seat's `/opt/hpo/venv-ha`). That is the guard working; `HPO_TYPING_PYTHON` pointed at a venv built from this lock reads `ALL 12 typing-ruler source checks PASSED`.

One break that no CI check covers: `tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh` and `tools/audit/seat/seat_venv.sh` asserted `homeassistant == "2026.9.3"` in the venv-ha they build from the typing lock. Under `set -euo pipefail`, the cloud setup script would exit 1 once the lock moved. Both now read the version from the lock's `homeassistant==` line. **The environment's pasted setup script still holds the literal**, so tvofi re-pastes `tools/audit/seat/cloud-setup.sh` once this merges (Forward-carry).

Header text the bumps made false is corrected. PyYAML 6.0.3 installs from a wheel, so nothing in the ci lock builds from an sdist, and Cython's `<3.0` bound belonged to 6.0.1. The typing overrides are now the set `pip check` lists, and the pyjwt, aiohttp and yarl overrides are gone because homeassistant 2026.10.4 pins those itself. Every other bump in #3088 (numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1, threadpoolctl 3.7.0, multidict 7.2.1, pyyaml 6.0.3, cython 3.3.0, setuptools 84.2.1 and the rest of the typing lock) needed no change: at #3088's head `tests / fast (3.14)` passed every script but `typing_ruler.py`, `env_drift.py --all` included, with this branch's ci lock byte-for-byte.

## Head

`61a58246decdf63ce5a0c1a9d342856f62e4d03d` merges main `94d8b47` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`dba968f8d579890b70db289f0b5bd0400d0b921b` merges main `0166aef` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`5bb7710c1c347a7969b2319d97575eb4f15f8151` merges origin/main `56630e7e6` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`b3f22192f861d7705911fceb7da8a113b2788f33` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3147.md`. The authored code head is `7d56a8934d40b3969eb61e097c4003d445e3ec14`.

Main moved twice during the work, both times with no conflict: from ca6333333 to 407eb0cb3 (#3049, `tools/audit/seat/` only), then to c88d552c7 (#3051, #3074: the gate lease, prepr, carry_audit, the handover and their tests; none of the files this diff changes or the figures below read). merges.body:
R10-AUDIT-COVERAGE-ENDGAME (design `design/r10-audit-coverage` at `ae3d86dc0`, approved by `design-verdict/r10-audit-coverage` `5b77e98dd`). The owner asked that the audit dimensions, finder scopes, bug classes and harnesses cover production, the instruments and the repository machinery as they stand at v10.0.0. Every gap was re-measured at this branch's merge base, `c88d552c7`. No count is carried from the note.

**What changes**

- **G4 and Carry 1 (design-review C1): coverage is part of the default run.** `tools/audit/check_scopes.py`'s existing invocation (`--repo R --ref B`) now also refuses three things, so `.claude/workflows/audit-find.js` Prepare step 7 and the `check-wave-script.mjs` pins need no edit:
  - a tracked path that is in no dimension's universe and not on the new `_coverage_excluded` map in `scopes.json` (glob → reason);
  - an exclusion that also names a covered path, names nothing, or carries no reason;
  - a harness under `dev/audit/harnesses/` whose header names a brief (`D<k>.md`) that does not cite it (Carry 8).

  The exit code goes through one function, `verdict()`. `--self-test` drives it on the live scopes, with D10's universe dropped, and with an uncited harness planted. Since round 2 it also runs the default invocation whole, as a subprocess of the file with `--repo`/`--ref`: the live scopes must exit 0 and the scopes with D4's and D6's `blueprints/**` globs dropped must exit 1 naming a blueprint, both printing `verdict()`'s citation line. It also drives `coverage()` arms that must name `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/py.typed` (Carry 5), and `tests/closure.py` and `blueprints/automation/notifications.yaml` when every `tests/`/`blueprints/` glob is stripped.
- **G1, G2, G3: the universes.**
  - D3 gains `tests/*.{py,mjs,sh}`, `tests/README.md`, `tests/fixtures/**`, `tests/replay/**` and `tests/pwlane/*.json`.
  - D11 gains the gate machinery: `closure`, `entities`, `structure`, `env_drift`, `gate_lock`, `layout` and the ratchets; `tests/*.json` (closures, every budget file, `seam_map.json`); `tests/requirements-*.txt` and `tests/hastub/**`. It also gains the release and repo files (`.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`, `SECURITY.md`, `VERSION`, `RELEASE_NOTES.md`) and `dev/README.md`. From `dev/programme/` it gains `HANDOVER.md`, `plan-*.md`, `carries/**` and `rosters/**`.
  - D11's `dev/audit/**` becomes `dev/audit/{README.md,config/**,harnesses/**,rca/**,waves/**}`, so `dev/audit/rounds/**` is out of every universe.
  - D4 and D6 gain `blueprints/**`, and D6 gains `docs/img/**` (the figures and their generators).
  - The other unmeasured paths are excluded, each with its reason in the file: `dev/audit/rounds/**`, `dev/archive/**`, the record subtrees of `dev/programme/`, `docs/design/**`, `docs/site/fonts/**`, `tests/golden/**`, `tests/mutation_ledger/**`, `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`.
- **G5 and Carry 3 (design-review C3): barrier paths resolve.**
  - `tools/audit/fold_ledger.py check` refuses `MISSING-PATH`: a token in a class's `barrier` **or `detector`** that is path-shaped and absent at the root. A token is path-shaped only when its first segment is a tracked top-level directory, with any `:line`, `::symbol` or `@sha` suffix dropped.
  - The self-test's passing arm holds `F3.1/F3.2` and `handoff/r9-rca-p1@0ade2456`.
  - P5's and P9's barriers are repointed to `dev/archive/carries/carry-1655.json` and `carry-1757.json`.
  - P1's `enumerate.sh` has no live copy. Round 10's `sweep-P1` enumerates timestamp seams, not the live-input plausibility rule, so it does not supersede the script. The token is dropped and the sentence now says why. The blind-spot warning stays.
  - The rule also read `detector`, which found three more stale tokens. I3's and N-silent-zero's detectors now point to `tools/policy/field_coverage.mjs`, and I4's to `tools/policy/agreement.mjs`.
- **Carry 7: shipped barriers on the ledger.**

  - It returned eight classes at the base. Each is dispositioned in `## Figures`.
- **G6 and Carry 4 (design-review C4): harnesses.**

  - `dev/audit/README.md` states the retirement rule and gives its command. It does not name the repaired harnesses, because naming one there makes it live-cited, and then `tests/entities.py`'s N-move-stale-path arm requires it to resolve every path it opens at any ref. That arm turned red when an earlier draft of this branch named them.
  - The README cites `tools/audit/seat/moved_paths.py` as the instrument to run, so `tests/entities.py` now reads it. `tests/closures.json` records that read; `tools/pr/ci_predict.py --apply-inert` wrote the entry.

  Each file stays within its `policy_budgets.json` cap, paid by cutting prose the edit made redundant or that was false (see Figures). No cap is raised.

**Roster carries.** Carry 1 (C1) is coverage in the default invocation. Carry 2 (C2) is the per-dimension `--seat` proof under `## Null control`. Carry 3 (C3) is the barrier-path rule and the P1, P5 and P9 repoints. Carry 4 (C4) is the G6 cited set and its command under `## Figures`. Carry 5 (C5) is the D10 arm naming `py.typed`. Carry 6 is the approved design `ae3d86dc0`, followed as written: no departure is raised. Carry 7 is the shipped barriers and `UNRECORDED-BARRIER`. Carry 8 is the D15 harness citation and the harness-citation arm.

merges.body:
R10-MUTANT-RUN-DRIVER (size S, issue #3122; owner tvofi approved card 4 on 2026-11-01): the tracked mutant driver every seat-local `mut.py` was re-implementing, plus the `--diff` arm that mutates a diff's added lines. Fixer seat, topic r10-mutant-run-driver.

## Head

`77a09f42b8e4125e2f094c1dc719f6a21db88501` merges main `7680149` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`2322ae8c9d8456065e840a02be5fb31d0a533f53` merges main `9644fb7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`94f178421e227763eb7458817d0a034c85955977` merges main `0166aef` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

Pull-request head `1a6a7e6a8bf1cbe04f37989aaedbab66165df624` (the code head plus a merge of origin/main and the delivery row; no code differs from the authored head). Code head `7af8c887a2439357432ce6fb14efc27429773f16`, a merge of origin/main `56630e7e6d229d960cf1b4db304d488ee20873e6` into the branch; origin/main had moved since the last full `tools/pr/prepr.sh` run and the run was repeated after the merge (see Figures).

## Mutation proof

Instrument: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --self-test` (40 checks). Each production line below was broken in a scratch copy, the self-test run, and the line restored:

- drop GUARD_OFF, RETURN_DEL, CMP_BOUND, CALL_DEL or CONST_SWAP (the `yield` replaced by `pass`, one at a time): `diff: the added lines yield all five operators` and `diff: a self-test that does not pin them leaves survivors` go red, 2 failed each.
- skip the restore (`target.write_bytes(orig)` to `pass`): `spec: the file is restored between mutants` red.
- NULL reported as KILLED instead of SURVIVED: 3 spec checks red. `old` count check `n != 1` loosened to `n < 1`: `an old text occurring twice is refused` red.
- `start_new_session=True` to False, `_child.append(p)` deleted, or the handler's kill loop emptied: `SIGTERM mid-mutant ... the running command was killed with the driver` red in both modes.
- the timeout `_killpg(p)` deleted: `a mutant that hangs past --timeout is KILLED ... rather than waited out` red; the `--in-place` guard on a non-HEAD diff end set to `if False`: `--in-place with a diff end that is not HEAD` red.

Failing test first: before the arm existed the fixture check was red by absence (`mutant_run.py` not in the tree); the fixture adds `norm` (a guarded return, a bound, a call, a constant) and the self-test pins every operator's line with `check_norm.py` (no survivor) and none with `check_loose.py` (survivors for all five operators).

## Null control

- NULL mutant: `spec: the NULL mutant reports SURVIVED and a pinned mutant KILLED`; a command failing on the unedited tree prints `KILLED NULL`, rc 3, and no mutant runs.
- Empty diff (`HEAD...HEAD`): prints nothing, rc 0. `--report-only` over survivors: rc 0.
- A mutant whose `old` occurs twice is refused, rc 2, nothing run. Malformed spec, repeated name, NULL name, absent file, old==new, a dirty target (copy and `--in-place`): each rc 2.
- SIGTERM mid-mutant, both modes: rc 143, `git status --porcelain` empty for the target, byte-identical, no temp copy left under TMPDIR, and the running command's pid gone.
- Comment/import/def lines and lines inside multi-line strings yield no mutant; `"a < b"  # c > d` yields none; a log call yields no CALL_DEL.

## Carries answered

- Carry 1 (from R10-FLY-MUTANT-RESTORE): built here. `tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --spec mutants.json --cmd '<argv>' [--copy-tree|--in-place]`: automatic NULL, one `KILLED|SURVIVED name` per mutant, rc 2 on a dirty target or an `old` not occurring once, git-archive copy by default (`--copy-tree` names it), SIGTERM/SIGINT restore. The group's helper is already on main (#3060, `dev/audit/harnesses/mutant_guard.py`); `--in-place` reuses it rather than duplicating it. `features_block.py` gained `--through MARKER` and `--prelude 'import line'`, with 4 self-test checks plus 3 driving `_main`.
- Carry 2 (card 4): built here. `--diff <base>...HEAD` with the five operators, `--path`, `--max-mutants`, `--list`, `--report-only`; `tools/pr/prepr.sh` runs it report-only as step `diff mutants` when `MUTANT_CMD` is set (skips otherwise; cap `MUTANT_MAX`, default 40). Not built: replacing the seven seat-local block runners beyond `--through`/`--prelude`; the other seat-local drivers are not migrated (their seats own them).

## Figures

- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --self-test`: 40 checks, 0 failed. `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/features_block.py --self-test`: 9 checks, 0 failed.
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/selftest_wiring.py --check`: 107 self-testing, 107 wired, 0 unwired (the new governance.yml step wires mutant_run). `python3 tests/structure.py`: PASSED. Scoped gate: MODE: SCOPED, tests/entities.py and tests/harness_headers.py both pass.
- Heavy pass on this fix's own added lines: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --diff origin/main...HEAD --path tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --cmd 'python3 -I tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py --self-test' --report-only`, at head 980c898f9 (the code differs from this head only by two added self-test checks): 81 survivors. A first pass found 93, and each real gap in it got a check (SIGTERM kills the child, timeout, spec and main refusals, string masking, in-place diff, cap).

## Survivor answers

The heavy pass is the instrument above; the driver's own mutation ledger does not apply (survivor_triage covers custom_components only, and the `mutation` lane mutates nothing under tools/).

- Self-test scaffolding, lines of `_self_test` and `_gone` (about 60 of 81): CALL_DEL on a `check(...)` call, CONST_SWAP on a poll count/sleep/timeout, `flag.unlink`, `shutil.rmtree` flag, `checks += 2`, `sys.path.insert` index, `return 2 if fails else 0`, and `GUARD_OFF` in the wait loops. Disposition: a self-test cannot observe its own deleted check; CI's grep requires a non-zero check count and 0 failed, and removing a check is a review matter. Not pinned.
- Equivalent: the `compile` skip and `text == src` skip in `diff_mutants` (a skipped invalid mutant would be killed, not survive: same output, slower); `if not files` and `if not mutants` early returns (the later path returns 0 too); `ln = 1` for `cur, ln = None, 0` (the hunk header sets it before use); `range(...)+2` and `>=` bounds in `string_lines` and the `n >= len(lines)` guard (one extra line, never an added line); `description=__doc__.split("\n")[1]`, a help string; `flush=False` on prints (same bytes).
- Defensive, not reachable from a fixture: the `git archive`/`tar` failure branch (`arc.wait() or tar.returncode` and its cleanup), `capture_output=False` on tar, `rmtree(..., ignore_errors=False)`, `_killpg` swallowing ProcessLookupError, a mask of `group(1)` length. Left unpinned; triage would be the same.
- Operator-table survivors on the arithmetic of the mutation itself (`+ 2` for the constant swap, `float * 2` for `1.0`): the swapped value only has to differ; the fixture checks that a constant mutant exists, not its value.
- features_block.py: 15 survivors in the diff arm at this fix's first head, all in `_self_test` scaffolding (`check` calls, `rmtree`, return codes), `_expect_error`'s `return False`, the `sys.exit(_main(...))` entry line, and `rindex("\n", 1, ...)` in `through` (equivalent: the header always precedes the marker). The parsing arms (`--prelude`, `--through`, usage rc 2) were survivors before `_main` took its path and the self-test drove it; those are now killed.

## Red checks

The check-run set was re-read in full (check-runs API, all pages, 55 runs) at head `1a6a7e6a8bf1cbe04f37989aaedbab66165df624`. Concluded red, by name: `governance / delivery-status`, and `pr-contract / pr-contract` (two runs) with the aggregate `gate` (two runs), which are red only because they refuse this body for leaving `governance / delivery-status` unnamed. Every other concluded check is success or skipped.

`governance / delivery-status`: the red is the OVERDUE row for #3096 ("triage: s9 batch 102", 12 commits since), not this pull request's row (#3151 is not in the log's list). The check grades main at its pinned SHA (`PINNED: 7f849a24911e9d52336bd79ea9ce63c67416a6ae`) and its log says it is not a required context and a red blocks no merge. This diff does not cause it: the only change to `.github/workflows/governance.yml` is one added step in the `instrument-self-tests` job (it runs `mutant_run.py --self-test`), and the `delivery-status` job and the tool it runs are untouched (`git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD -- .github/workflows/governance.yml` shows one 7-line hunk at the self-test steps); the row set it reads does not change with this branch, and it would be red identically on main. Cheaper detector: none; the check already is the detector, runs in about 20 s, and its red clears when the #3096 batch is dispositioned. State (d), a precondition that changed underneath a sound process: the batch drain fell behind. Nothing to build here; recorded, no countermeasure.

`pr-contract / pr-contract` and `gate`: red only on `[pr-body] check governance / delivery-status is red and ## Red checks does not name it`; this section repairs that. Nothing else in the code is red.

## Forward-carry

none.

merges.body:
Part 3 of R10-UX-HEALTH: the carries neither #2976 nor #2997 answered. Part of #2253, Part of #2260, Part of #2263, Part of #2499, Part of #2809, Part of #2815 (the group's `fixes` is empty, so no closing keyword is used. Carry 20 assigns #2499's last residual, its Health line, to this group, and whether the issue is then done is the orchestrator's call after the merge).

What lands:

- **#2499's Health residual (carries 11, 20).** #2976 (559134e96) made the heat-loss row read "Not observable without a power meter." with no power meter. It still drew the row's learned bar, so the row still looked like a trusted learned scale. With no power meter the bar is now empty at every learner phase (`healthModelHtml`, one condition on the share the row already computes): a converged learner drew 100 % before and draws 0 %, and a learner still settling drew its progress (40 % in the check) and draws 0 %. Both are intended: without a meter the house's scale is not observable at any phase, so no phase may draw progress toward a learned scale. A metered install keeps its bar at both phases (100 % converged, 40 % settling).
- **udf-strings-history (carry 21).** UI text describes current behaviour only. `price_prior_enabled` ("used to be a flat repeat") now says what the option does and what switching it off does. `price_risk_lambda` drops ", as before". `heat_pump_mode_entity` drops "exactly as before", in three places per file (the setup page, its plant section, and the options pump page). `peak_tariff_offpeak_factor` drops "which is how it worked before". `two_zone_mode`'s Automatic states its rule instead of "keeps the old rule". The Swedish text is rewritten in step: "som tidigare", "precis som förut", "Dessförinnan var resten av horisonten ...", "som det fungerade tidigare" and "behåller den gamla regeln".
- **A check that keeps it so.** `tests/entities.py` refuses any leaf in strings.json, en.json or sv.json that carries a change-history phrase (`_HISTORY_MARKERS`).
- **The control for carry 22, which stays open**: `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_two_zone_hhl_inert.py`. See below.

Review round 1 (verdict/3062 at 822946aae, blocked `class-open`), answered:

- **The block**: `peak_tariff_offpeak_factor`'s "which is how it worked before" / "som det fungerade tidigare", in all three catalogues. Rewritten ("1.0 treats every hour the same." / "1,0 behandlar varje timme lika."). The marker list now holds `worked before` and `fungerade tidigare`. The wider census this round ran (Figures) found one more leaf of the same kind, which the reviewer's net did not name: `two_zone_mode`'s "Automatic keeps the old rule" / "Automatiskt behåller den gamla regeln", in all three catalogues. Rewritten too, and the markers hold `the old rule` and `den gamla regeln`. Both leaves failed the widened check before the rewrite (Mutation proof).
- **Finding 1, the unmetered unconverged bar.** Stated above, and pinned: `card.mjs` adds `with no power meter a still-learning heat loss draws no learned bar either (#2499)` and its metered null `a metered still-learning heat loss draws its progress as the bar`. The reviewer's narrower mutant now fails (Mutation proof).
- **Finding 2, carry 22's forward-carry is pending, not a control.** Agreed. It stays on R10-UX-HEALTH's carry list (Carries, Forward-carry). This part does not claim it.
- **Finding 3, the docs copy.** The `peak_tariff_offpeak_factor` and `two_zone_mode` rows of `docs/configuration.md` already state current behaviour. The other history phrasings under `docs/` are added to the R10-USER-DOCS-VERIFY forward-carry (Forward-carry).

What does not land, and why:

- **Carry 22 (two-zone `house_heat_loss_coefficient`), not built.** The carry rests on the live probe's finding that the field is inert in two-zone mode. That holds for the solve but not for system identification. `sysid.HousePlant.of_params` builds the step sizer's plant from `heat_loss_coefficient` with no two-zone branch, and the coordinator's sysid tick passes it whenever an experiment runs, on single- and two-zone plants alike. On the probe's two-zone config, the sized step is 1.738 kW at 0.1 kW/K, 3.386 kW at 0.4, and no step at 1.0 (Figures). Hiding the field would hide a setting that still changes what the integration does, and labelling it "unused" would be false. A first cut hid the field through the registry's `when=` with a shared `two_zone_from_config` predicate. That cut was withdrawn before the handoff once the sizer arm read non-zero. The sound order is to make the sizer read the zone loss first: `_slab_prior` in the same class already does, through `_zone_heat_loss`. The hide is then one `when=` row. That is a sysid change outside this group's seam (architect note: the Health tab renderer), so it is routed rather than made. No group owns it yet, so the carry stays open on this group's list. Carry: R10-UX-HEALTH
- **Carry 14 (the "driving scale") and carry 17 (the P9 storage reset)** stay where #2997 left them: each waits on an orchestrator decision (the widget's confirmation; an after-edge for the chart ink at 375 px). Nothing here changes either. Carry: R10-UX-HEALTH

Design choices:

- **The history check is a phrase list, and says so.** Tense has no syntactic shape. The markers are the change-history phrasings the catalogues held, plus words that held no current-behaviour leaf when added: en `as before`, `used to be`, `worked before`, `behaved before`, `did before`, `the old rule`, `the old behaviour`, `the old way`, `previously`, `formerly`; sv `som tidigare`, `som förut`, `dessförinnan var`, `fungerade tidigare`, `tidigare fungerade`, `den gamla regeln` (and `det gamla beteendet`, `det gamla sättet`), `förut`, `numera`. Bare `before`, `old` and `tidigare` are not markers: the census returns 28, 2 and 2 current-behaviour leaves for them (`before each deadline`, `an old value is treated as missing`, `något tidigare`). "Used to <verb>" as an instrument ("Used to read your hourly electricity prices") is current behaviour and is not matched. So is a repair's runtime history ("until now the plan was still being held ...", "no longer measured"). The census in Figures lists every remaining hit of the wider net and its kind.
- **The bar, not the value.** The W/K figure stays. It is the value the model plans with, and the row says it is not observable. The bar is the row's "how far learned" signal, so only the bar changes.

## Head

`6d577ce8a18d19f30240843ead1d71ae03bb7011` merges main `0166aef` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`b46f8832d5ea31651ef66294f8d0263c6c3b8732` is the orchestrator's recarry of main into the previous head. It is not a clean merge of the live head and main (the body file is not the live pull-request body), so prepr checked this head.

`8ad138bb59548a01b8d38c609c970c1e495c8a68` merges the authored code head `415a27e1bc5984d5fd7f6ce8e5ee474b6b9faaa4` and then merges origin/main `92588d581` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

415a27e1bc5984d5fd7f6ce8e5ee474b6b9faaa4, on merge base f3c9144b80883ae510f0207c30855b8c93c51a0a. origin/main was at 92588d581fde4ce287af3db5e8bb61461dc28015 at 2026-11-01T08:05Z, and `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0 (no conflict; `LEDGER-MERGE: resolved tests/closures.json`), so main is not merged in (`fixer.md` step 6).

Commits since the round-1 head 822946aae: ea1cb7a80be6afa4d78629773a0ae9fd28591140 (the failing checks), 415a27e1bc5984d5fd7f6ce8e5ee474b6b9faaa4 (the fix). Round 1's: 22626a277f5bb957d4f22357c242758b1d984f8f (the failing checks), 03fec96c13b50e83484413f55177bf0af4242e6b (the fix), fe5cdef51921638028f7a4b1c0776c6a561f6911 (the harness), bbbce602dc4b3374cbb079f3b067ac82365a1ca7 (its INERT READS entry), 4502c5ab3 (origin/main merged in), 822946aae49ec0cec8e9a9d1812334dae14aee04 (the delivery row).

Host note: macOS, load average 38 to 57 during these runs. `tests/entities.py`'s heartbeat arm cannot get a task port for its own child here (`PermissionError: Cannot get task port`). Each local `entities.py` run below therefore hid `_remote_debugging` from `importlib.util.find_spec` through a scratch wrapper (`importlib.util.find_spec` returns None for that one name, then `runpy` runs `tests/entities.py`), so that arm skips exactly as it does on an interpreter without the module. No tree file changes. No tree file changes. CI runs the card at its own default.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant is one production edit in a detached worktree at ea1cb7a80 (`git worktree add --detach`), run through the closure that owns the check, then discarded. The card runs used the head's plan payload (`HPO_PLANDATA`, written by `tests/plan_view.py` in this worktree; this diff changes no Python).

- Card, the reviewer's narrower mutant: `!observable ? 0 : hl.learned ? 1 : house ? house.share : 0` to `hl.learned ? (observable ? 1 : 0) : house ? house.share : 0`. `node tests/card.mjs` prints `FAIL UX-HEALTH D: with no power meter a still-learning heat loss draws no learned bar either (#2499)`, detail `bar 40%`. The converged check and both metered nulls stay ok.
- Card, the whole fix removed (the merge base's `heatpump-optimizer-card.js` under the new tests): `FAIL UX-HEALTH D: with no power meter the learned heat loss draws no learned bar (#2499)` (`bar 100%`) and `FAIL ... a still-learning heat loss draws no learned bar either (#2499)` (`bar 40%`). Both metered nulls stay ok (`bar 100`, `bar 40`). This is also the test-first run for both bar checks.
- Strings, the round-2 fix removed (the tree at ea1cb7a80, whose catalogues are 415a27e1b's minus its six edits): `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 <wrapper>` prints `FAIL strings.json: no UI text describes how the integration used to behave [2: options.step.grid.data_description.peak_tariff_offpeak_factor, options.step.thermal_model_zones.sections.mode.data_description.two_zone_mode]`, and the same two leaves for `en.json` and `sv.json`. That run's summary is `4 of 2496 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`; the fourth is `hb:positive_control survives one hung py-spy sample` (`gaps=[1.102, 0.804, 0.607]`), a timing arm under load 45 that reads no catalogue and that this diff does not touch; CI (Linux) runs it.
- Strings, round 1's mutant (unchanged by this round, kept): ", as before" restored in strings.json's `price_risk_lambda`, and ", som tidigare" restored in sv.json's, printed `2 of 2496 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`, one per mutated catalogue, `en.json`'s check ok.

## Null control

- The widened markers' own null: run over the head's three catalogues they return no leaf (`_HISTORY_MARKERS` extracted from `tests/entities.py` by a scratch probe; CI's `entities.py` at the head runs the check itself), while the census's wider net returns 79, 79 and 28 hits there, each disposed as current behaviour. So the new words (`previously`, `formerly`, `the old rule`, `förut`, `numera`, ...) refuse no current-behaviour text that exists today. Against the tree at ea1cb7a80 they return exactly the two leaves per catalogue above and no third.
- The unmodified merge base fails all three history checks (round 1's figure: 5 leaves per catalogue under the round-1 markers) and both no-meter bar checks. The metered nulls (`bar 100` converged, `bar 40` settling) pass at the merge base, at the narrower mutant and at the head.
- `node tests/card_drift.mjs origin/main`: not re-run locally this round. Round 1 at bbbce602d printed "card_drift: identical in all 45 states", and this round changes no card file (`git diff --name-only 822946aae HEAD -- custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/www` prints nothing); CI's scoped `card_drift.mjs` at the head decides. No committed card state has an unmetered heat-loss row, so nothing is claimed, and both claim files are byte-identical to the merge base.
- Carry 22's harness at the head: the solve sweep reads `two_zone_max_dkw=0.000000` and `two_zone_max_dcost=0.000000` against `single_zone_max_dkw=4.999993` (macOS; the reviewer's Linux run read 4.921374, and only non-zero matters). So the solve ignores the field in two zones, and the harness is not blind. The sizer reads `two_zone_sysid_steps=1.738,3.386,None`, identical to `single_zone_sysid_steps=1.738,3.386,None`. So sysid uses the field in two-zone mode exactly as it does in single-zone mode, and the carry's premise is false there.

## Figures

Measured at the head named under `## Head`, against the merge base f3c9144b8.

- Structure: `python3 tests/structure.py` prints STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED.
- Architecture score: `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff f3c9144b80883ae510f0207c30855b8c93c51a0a` prints `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`.
- Scoped gate: `D=$(mktemp -d); python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 12 script(s) run, 21 scoped out`. `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144 bash tests/run.sh` printed the same mode line, `claims hygiene: origin/main ok`, `ALL 117 closure shrink pins PASSED` and `ALL 4674 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, then queued `tests/entities.py` for a heavy slot (`tests/gate_lock.py slot-status`: 4/4 slots held by other seats' preprs, run.sh eighth in the queue, load average above 50). It had waited over two hours in total for slots, so it was stopped there, by PID, and the other ten scoped scripts were not run locally this round. What stands for them: `tests/entities.py` ran on this host through the wrapper at ea1cb7a80 (Mutation proof: the three history checks FAIL on exactly the two leaves, every other catalogue check ok); at the head its `_HISTORY_MARKERS`, extracted from `tests/entities.py` by a scratch probe and run over the head's three catalogues, return 0 leaves in each. `node tests/card.mjs` ran at ea1cb7a80 (a tree whose card files are the head's) and printed all four bar checks ok before this host's heap limit (Head's host note). The scoped gate in CI (`gate`, `tests / closure-scope`) at the head is the authority for the rest; round 1's local run of all twelve at bbbce602d passed but for the host's entities heartbeat arm.
- Browser: `NODE_PATH=<a playwright 1.64.1 install> node tests/card_browser.mjs` (macOS) at the head prints `2 BROWSER CHECK(S) FAILED`: `P9 grid: no two text runs share ink` (`20: text "2" x text "3" 2 px of shared ink`) and `P40 every committed card page figure has the size and structure of the page this card draws` (`setup-dark.png: height 714 committed, 720 drawn; setup-light.png: ...`). This is the same kind of text as the removed `heat_pump_mode_entity` "exactly as before". The body's census pattern missed it because "worked before" is not "as before". Its sv pattern lists `som tidigare` but not `tidigare` alone. Adds the roster's two missing field-writing ops, `set-size` and `set-files`, to `tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py` (R10-ROSTER-OPS-2 part 1, issue #3131; owner tvofi approved plan-slip card 1, cap gate passed with `--over-cap "tvofi 2026-11-01 plan-slip card 1"`). **One design per op, reconciling carries 5, 9, 10 and 11** (1-based, as the group row lists them):

- `set-size <group> <size> [--cite <ref>@<sha>]` (carries 5 and 9). The size must be keyed by `tools/plan/durations.json`, by the same `_size_why` check `append-group` runs. `--cite` is optional; where given it must be `<ref>@<sha>` and the ref must hold the sha. The old size (or `unset`) and the cite go to `resume.note`.
- `set-files <group> [--add <path>...] [--set-files <p,p|->] [--set-hot <p,p|->] [--cite <ref>@<sha>]` (carries 5, 10 and 11). `--add` appends; `--set-files` replaces `files` whole; `--set-hot` replaces `hot_files` whole (`-` for none, key kept). A path new to `files` must be in the tree at origin/main or at the cited sha. A hot token must be a basename of the group's resulting files or a token some group already holds. An unknown group refuses; every other field stays byte-identical; the lint gate, triage gate and push race are the shared `write_roster` path.
- A value already held writes nothing (no note, no commit), which is each op's null control.

**Round 2 repair (one finding, the fix review's unpinned-site block).** `cite_why`'s `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <ref>` clause survived deletion (reviewer mutant R11, `rc=0 fails=0`) because no arm cited a sha that exists but that the named ref does not hold. Nothing else changed.

R10-SAV-COMFORT part 2: the duty ledger's run fold settles one tick into each step (carry 8); the other seven carries answered.

Part of #2492. Part of #201. Critical path: R10-SAV-COMFORT. #2492 stays open: carries 6 and 7 are routed back to it.

Status: carry 8 built here; carries 2, 3 and 5 already on main; carries 1, 4, 6 and 7 deferred, each routed to #2492 (`Carry: #2492`), carry 7 pending the owner's ruling below.

**Carry 8 (#2968's residue), measured first.** `pump_arbiter._observe` folded a run at any tick reading at or above `on_threshold_kw`. The supply tick writes the switch on the step's first tick, and the arbiter's tick in that same minute reads the meter before the write shows, so the first reading of a planned-idle step after a planned-on step is the on step's tail. The probe is the step-boundary install `tests/features.py` already drives (section "supply switch at step boundaries"): its meter follows the switch one minute late. At the merge base every planned-idle step after a planned-on step books `space-instead` (5 of the install's 16 steps); with the tail removed (`tail=False`, the meter set to the step's own command before the step's first pass) the same steps book `delivered`. The verdict changes with the tail, so the carry's fix applies: `RUN_SETTLE` (one arbiter tick, `_TICK`) in `pump_arbiter`, and `_observe` folds a reading into neither `measured` nor `ran` until the step is that old. One owner, no per-call flag.

The window is one tick, not two. The mechanism measured is the two ticks firing in the same minute. A two-tick window was tried first: it also drops the reading one minute into a step, which `tests/features.py`'s existing duty-ledger checks take as a real in-step reading (`_pa_led`, `_pa_edge`, `_pa_lg` read the meter at minute 1 of each step). A longer meter lag than one tick is not measured anywhere in the tree and is not claimed here.

**Carry 7, measured, and the ruling it needs.** The carry asks for a priced comfort shortfall. `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_null_terms.py` (sha1 `c981e7c840ede1a5fef95aa903e00e5809c92aa7`) already prices exactly that: a steady thermostat at the comfort target against one at the room the plan delivered, through the production `_floor_demand_at_target` and `compute_cop`. Netting that comfort term out of the gap leaves the varying-outdoor arm at +6.93 % of the steady-at-target kWh and the `const` arm at +7.44 %, both above the owner's 3.0 bar. So a priced comfort shortfall alone cannot meet the owner's flat-price null, and no change was made to the month row. In the `const` arm the remainder (9.3 kWh) equals the stored-heat drawdown at the steady COP (9.3 kWh_e), so comfort priced plus stored heat settled at both ends reads about 0 there, which is carry 1's acceptance. Meeting it in the month row means settling stored heat in the ledger row, a seam #2745 did not open and that carry 4's baseline definition owns. The carry's fallback is the owner's ruling, which this seat cannot obtain: which of start-independence (#2255) or comfort matching the month row keeps, and whether the row settles stored heat. Routed to #2492.

**The carries, one by one.**

- Carry 1 (the three-term separation): on main through #2745 (`34cd75bf1`), which reports the terms and keeps the timing term. The null's residual is carry 7's, routed with it. Carry: #2492
- Carry 2 (volume against timing): on main, `34cd75bf1` (#2745: `MonthlyLedger.meter_calibration`). `r10_sav_volume.py` at this head: flat volume +0.00 and timing +0.00, vary timing +74.88. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 34cd75bf1 origin/main` exits 0.

- Carry 4 (the owner's baseline specification): the meter-calibrated basis is on main, `34cd75bf1`; flat-price timing reads 0 (carry 2's arms). The finder's `|pct| < 3.0` null is not met (12.34 % at this head) and is carry 7's question. Carry: #2492
- Carry 5 (the duty ledger's seams): on main. Seam 1, the re-freeze of `planned` at each plan adoption, is `34cd75bf1` (#2745); seam 2, the switch written at step boundaries, is `5d4e0bcfb` (#2968). `git merge-base --is-ancestor 5d4e0bcfb origin/main` exits 0.
- Carry 6 (power ratio against the planner's over-booking on one sample window): not measured here; it needs a sample window the tree does not hold and is outside carry 8's fold. Carry: #2492
- Carry 7 (the flat-price null books the comfort shortfall as a saving): measured above, needs the owner's ruling. Carry: #2492

## Summary

Round 1 review of PR #3145 (R10-SAV-COMFORT part 2, carry 8 of #2492), measured at head `d8b51ad10431b5838fab854ef35f608bbe1a6101` from detached worktrees at that head and at the merge base `c88d552c76f1ae11a879ce7ccb8d8dc29adabf50`. fix-review.md is unchanged between the merge base and origin/main (only orchestrator.md moved). The defect reproduces at the base with the finder's harness and is gone at the head. Every mutant planted on `RUN_SETTLE` is killed. Every figure in the body that I re-ran reproduces. CI is GREEN at this head. The head merges cleanly with origin/main `7f849a249`.

## Findings

- A meter that lags the switch by more than one arbiter tick still books the previous step's tail as a run. Examples are a power sensor reporting every 2 to 5 minutes, or a compressor run-down longer than a minute. `RUN_SETTLE` is fixed at one tick (`_TICK`), so a reading at minute 1 or later that still shows the on-step's draw sets `row["ran"]` in a planned-idle step. I derived this by reading `_observe` and `live_power_kw` and did not run it: no harness in the tree models a lag longer than one tick (`cop_duty_floor.py` models one tick; `_sa_install` models one minute). The body says this case is "not measured anywhere in the tree and is not claimed here", and that is accurate. A wider window is not the fix: my two-tick mutant broke three duty-ledger checks that read real in-step meter values at minute 1. A sound answer would key on the meter's own `last_updated` against the switch write, or on a real-install lag measurement. That is the later stage's work, so it goes back to the issue that owns carry 8's residue. Carry: #2492
- Carries 1, 4, 6 and 7 are deferred by this PR, and each names `Carry: #2492` in the body, as does the Forward-carry section for carries 6 and 7. #2492 stays open. Carry 7 waits on the owner's ruling (start-independence against comfort matching, and whether the month row settles stored heat). I re-derived its figures from the committed harness at both ends (Evidence). Carry: #2492

- Finder's harness, `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_actuation_phase.py` (sha1 d8871c1b96466f7d0d16df9ecc15454512d6adc5), at the merge base: phase 0 books `space-instead` at steps 1, 4, 7, 9 and 14 (5 of 16 steps), and phase 14 books the same plus `idle-instead` at step 0; AGREE: yes, rc=0. Files: ev/actuation_base.txt and ev/actuation_head.txt.
- RESULT features head: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` prints ALL 4682 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED, rc=0 (ev/features_head.txt).
- RESULT features base-components: the head's tests run against the merge base's `custom_components/`. It prints 1 of 4682 FAILED, the one FAIL being "a planned-idle step books no run from the previous step's tail power (#2492 carry 8)". The null-control check passes there, so the test fails first at the base (ev/features_basecc.txt).
- RESULT mutant nopred (the PR's own mutation proof): `if power is not None:` restored gives 1 of 4682 FAILED, exactly the named carry-8 check (ev/features_nopred.txt).
- RESULT mutant eq (`>=` changed to `==`): 1 of 4682 FAILED, "#2492: a plan adopted mid-step re-freezes the step's planned duty..." Killed (ev/features_eq.txt).
- RESULT mutant two (`RUN_SETTLE = 2 * _TICK`): 3 of 4682 FAILED: the `_pa_led` per-step ledger check, the at-threshold check and the DHW-only ledger check. Killed. This confirms the body's claim that a two-tick window drops the minute-1 readings these checks rely on: `_pa_led` reads at minutes 1, 16, 31, 46, 61 and 76 (tests/features.py:58125). File: ev/features_two.txt.
- RESULT mutant zero (`RUN_SETTLE = timedelta(0)`, the window unset): 1 of 4682 FAILED, the named carry-8 check. Killed (ev/features_zero.txt). I read the brief's "start unset" mutant as this zero window. A `start` that never binds makes the predicate always true, which is the nopred mutant above, so it is killed too.

BOOLOP fails `tests/guard_pins.py` with a TypeError on `float(None)` (ev/pin_boolop_guardpins.txt). I did not re-run the mutation table, which is CI's heavy run. Its lane log at this head (job 124958959174) evaluated the three mutants at line 1051, killed all three, ran the null control at line 186 and survived it, and prints MUTATION TABLE PASSED, not INCONCLUSIVE (ev/mutation_lane.txt).
- Null control (tail=False install): pinned in features.py as "null control: without the meter tail every step is delivered". It passes at the head and with the base's components, and its switch writes equal the tailed install's.
- Flat-price null for savings figures: `r10_sav_volume.py` gives flat volume +0.00 and timing +0.00 (SOUND), and vary timing +74.88 (SOUND), identical at base and head (ev/sav_base.txt, ev/sav_head.txt). `r10_sav_baseline.py` gives transient SOUND, coverage SOUND, cost DEFECT, and null DEFECT at 12.336145360155744 %, identical at both ends, so this diff does not move it. The check-runs API, all pages, returns 55 runs at this head, none failed, cancelled or timed out (ev/check_runs.tsv). The body's `## Red checks: none` matches. pr-contract is green at this head.
