merges.body:
## Re-cut

This is the re-cut after round 3 of the fix review (`verdict/3050`, blocked at `2be13c572cf34a475d18e3f5e2dbde4f9ff8482a`, class `metric-gamed`). The body is replaced as a whole. Every figure in it was re-taken in this pass, at the head named under `## Head`. The exception is the red-history entries under `## Red checks`, which `pr-contract` requires and which cite their own jobs.

The block had three items:

1. The arm call in `async_arm_system_identification` put six arguments on one 125-column line. The `hold_reason` call in `_run_system_identification` kept its closing parenthesis on its last argument's line. Together these hid 5 layout lines from `tests/structure.py`, so the budgets read 8049 / 17642 where the honest figures are 8054 / 17647.
2. The #1523 null-control marker in `tests/features.py` (`_P5_CONSULT`) matched only the hugging layout.
3. No check separated the ceiling store's median from an upper quantile.

This re-cut changes only what those three items need, in three files:

- `coordinator.py`: the two calls are laid out normally, using the review's null re-wrap verbatim. No production logic changed.
- `tests/structure_budgets.json`: re-recorded at the honest 8054 / 17647. The reason is in commit `e81bf9dbf`'s message. The merge with origin/main composed main's own deltas onto them, to 8051 / 17645.
- `tests/features.py`: the marker is keyed on the consult expression alone, and one item-29 check is added.

Nothing outside the block changed. `git diff 2be13c572 e81bf9dbf --stat` lists exactly those three files (18 insertions, 9 deletions).

**The merge (repair of the refused handoff).** The re-cut tip `e81bf9dbf` was refused by `prepr.sh`: two predicted reds on `governance / wave-script` (the `AGREEMENT UNMERGED` and `GRADER UNMERGED` arms), because origin/main had moved and `tests/features.py` no longer merged. The head is now `deceb3de7`, a merge of origin/main `d052f80f7` into `e81bf9dbf` (merge, not rebase). The resolution:
- `tests/features.py`: both sides appended a tail block. The resolution keeps this PR's R10-CEILING-PROBE block, then main's R10-HOTFIX-AWAY-PRESENCE block. `diff <(git diff 1a8051350 e81bf9dbf -- tests/features.py | grep '^[-+][^-+]' | sort) <(git diff origin/main HEAD -- tests/features.py | grep '^[-+][^-+]' | sort) && echo PR_DELTA_PRESERVED` prints `PR_DELTA_PRESERVED`.
- `tests/structure_budgets.json` and `tests/closures.json` were resolved by the repository's ledger merge driver: `class_excess_loc` 17653 + both deltas = 17645, `max_class_loc` 8059 + both deltas = 8051, and `inert_reads.tests/harness_headers.py` merged as a set.

No other file changed in the merge beyond main's own commits. Every figure below was re-taken at `deceb3de7`.

R10-CEILING-PROBE: the cheap-night ceiling probe, and the system-identification experiment's step reaching a flow set-point install.

Issues #2498 and #2808. The roster lists neither under its `fixes`, so this body names them without a closing keyword. Closing them is the orchestrator's call.

A set-point-driven install's plan rarely writes the flow ceiling. The metered draw window is therefore censored at the top, and the plugin cannot learn the pump's real maximum (the owner's case: configured 5 kW, believed near 3 kW). This adds a second experiment kind, the ceiling probe, inside the existing cheap-night system-identification gates:

- It commands the configured maximum, and the arbiter writes the ceiling for it.
- The metered draws of those intervals go to a separate store on `DrawRange`.
- The store's raw median is the learned top. It is published in the diagnostics, and R10-COP-GATE part D consumes it.

The design is the approved architect note `dev/programme/designs/R10-CEILING-PROBE.md` at `design/r10-ceiling-probe` 2212054e93c344d62762ac52e3b891bcce93d31d, as amended by its review `design-verdict/r10-ceiling-probe` 621e26313113ce925f7442cb935d0660a2505179. Where the two differ, carries 29-34 supersede the note. Items 7-28 come from the note and from `design-verdict/R10-CEILING-PROBE` e8da829f15771f047ba63b392b15af4d0fe99224. The orchestrator's s9 ruling (roster carry 6) makes that shape final.

**What changes, by owner.**

- `sysid.py` owns when the experiment runs and what it commands.
  - `armable(...) -> (kind, why)` picks the kind:
    - The fit runs while the house learner is unconverged and its own `min_days_between_runs` clock allows.
    - Otherwise the probe runs where the install can run one and the probe's clock allows: 7 days while unlearned, 30 once the store has a learned top.
    - A refusal is published in `result.reason`.
  - The probe's clock is the newer of two times: the store's newest sample, which persists in the accuracy store, and this process's last probe step (`probe_run`). A restart therefore cannot reset it (item 7). The converged denial in `conditions_met` applies to the fit only.
  - A flat price horizon refuses the probe. The fit's price gate is unchanged.
  - `probe_step_hours(...)` is the duration search:
    - It tries whole cycles at the configured maximum's heat, longest first. It returns the first whose predicted peak fits the comfort bound: `max_excursion_c` less the two-zone headroom only (item 14).
    - Below `PROBE_MIN_CYCLES` the arm aborts.
    - The duration found is stored in `_step_hours`, and that is what `step()` compares against (item 15).
  - A probe ends with its last step interval and hands back to the plan without relaxing. It completes uncompleted, with its outcome in `reason`, so `_adopt_system_identification` adopts nothing.
  - `stand_down(reason)` holds an armed experiment that has not started, with the reason published as `held`. A started one still aborts (#2808).
  - `hold_reason(...)` makes the stand-down decision for the coordinator: mode, the learners' freeze, an unread room, and `quiet_windows.quiet_reason`.
  - `arm_from_config(...)` is the arm. It is a module function, not a method, because `SystemIdentification` is over the 300-line limit.
  - The view gains `kind`, `held` and `last_attempt`.
- `pump_arbiter.py` owns how an action becomes a set-point.
  - `_experiment_kw(inp)` reads the experiment's commanded power before the plan's `power_schedule` (item 19).
  - `_planned_duty` returns `space` where `planned_draw_runs(power)` holds (item 32), and `idle` otherwise.
  - `_flow_target` maps that power through `flow_setpoint_for_level`. The install reads in `_flow_command` moved into `thermal_model.flow_setpoint_driven`, which the probe's eligibility shares (item 21).
- `draw_range.py` owns what a sample teaches.
  - `DrawRange.ceiling` is a deque of `(drawn_kw, epoch_s)`.
  - `fold(..., experiment_s=)` routes an experiment interval that `takes_ceiling` to the store and not to the window.
  - `learned_max_kw(now_s)` is the store's median. It is `None` below `CEILING_MIN_SAMPLES`, past `CEILING_LAPSE_DAYS` after the newest sample, or when the newest sample is ahead of the clock. It applies no agreement test (item 29).
  - Two ordinary intervals written at the ceiling that draw more than `AGREE_TOLERANCE` above the learned top drop the store (item 8).
  - The store and the overdraw count persist in the accuracy document.
- `coordinator.py` is wiring only.
  - `_pending_prediction` gains `"mode"`, and the fold routes on it (item 30).
  - The arm is one call, `sysid.arm_from_config`.
  - `_run_system_identification` asks `sysid.hold_reason` and calls `stand_down`.
- `quiet_windows.py`: `quiet_reason(config, now)` names a step inside a configured quiet off or silent window. The experiment stands down inside one: held while armed, aborted once started.
- `thermal_model.py`: `flow_setpoint_driven(config)` and `ceiling_probe_install(config)` sit beside `probe_install`.
- `sensor.py`: `ModelStatusSensor` publishes a recorded `system_identification_outcome` row. The view stays unrecorded (item 17).
- `store.py`, `accuracy.py`, `diagnostics.py` and `payload.py` declare, persist, pass the clock to, and type the new cells.

**Roster carries, answered.**

- Carry 1 (#2465's three):
  - (a) The set-point-to-draw gain is measured here at the one level the probe commands, the ceiling, and that draw is stored as the learned top. The levels between gate and ceiling stay uncalibrated, as the approved note scopes the probe to the top. That residual is forward-carried to R10-COP-GATE-D (`## Forward-carry`).
  - (b) The real maximum is reached by the ceiling probe, folded into the system-identification experiment.
  - (c) A gate-held draw above idle is refused by `takes_ceiling` and stays out of the store.
- Carry 2 (#2808): a converged house arms the probe instead of an experiment that cannot run (`armable`). The pump mode, a learning freeze or an unread room holds an armed experiment that has not started, and aborts one that has (`stand_down`, decided by `sysid.hold_reason`). The outcome is the recorded `system_identification_outcome` attribute (item 17).
- Carry 3 (the three blockers):
  - (1) Actuation: `_experiment_kw` feeds `_planned_duty` and `_flow_target` (items 19, 32). The harness's level arm writes the ceiling at 5.0 kW (Figures).
  - (2) The probe-only run on converged houses, with its 7- and 30-day clocks (items 7, 16).
  - (3) The top is learned from a ceiling store separate from the window, with the lapse and the overdraw drop as its re-test (items 8, 12, 29).
- Carry 4 (the approved r2 ruling): items 7 and 8, as described under `draw_range.py` and `sysid.py` above.
- Carry 5 (R10-COP-GATE part D): the raw accessor of item 29, now pinned against the median's mean, extreme and upper-quantile alternatives. Its interface goes forward under `## Forward-carry`.
- Carry 6 (the s9 ruling): items 29 to 34 bind as written.

**Departures from the note.**

- `button.py` is unchanged. Its availability at main is already `not system_identification_active`, which admits every armable kind. The refusal is published through the recorded outcome row.
- The accessor takes the clock, as `learned_max_kw(now_s)`. `draw_range` reads no clock, and the lapse is a clock. This is forward-carried to R10-COP-GATE-D.
- `stand_down` holds an armed experiment for every reason the coordinator's gate names: the pump mode, the learners' freeze and the unread room.
- Files beyond the note's seven: `thermal_model.py`, `quiet_windows.py`, `store.py`, `accuracy.py` and `diagnostics.py`. Each carries one predicate, one declaration or one argument. The quiet-window stand-down is a seam the step-8 enumeration returned (Figures).
- `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` claims the five `coord_*` fixtures for the new view keys and the outcome row. This re-cut does not touch it.

**Alternatives.**

- Probe samples in the rolling window, with `MIN_SAMPLES` lowered: rejected, because it moves the clamp for every install.
- Routing on `_current_action` at the fold: rejected, because it reads the next interval's mode.
- A second capture for the pair: rejected, because `_pending_prediction` already carries the interval's own split and command (#2262).
- The 15 % rule in the accessor: rejected, because part D owns it (item 29).
- Paying the ratchet by moving a `SystemIdentification` method to module level verbatim: not taken, because that is a mechanical split. The arm and the stand-down decision moved as module functions instead.
- Paying the re-cut's 5 lines: no payment that improves code was found inside the block's scope. Any further line removal in the coordinator class would be new scope, which a minimal re-cut excludes. So the budgets are re-recorded at the honest layout. Both still move down against origin/main.

## Head

`6d3958b70f1c43251615354aeb94499dad32680e` merges main `25c46e7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`f47e8ba434078083b9210e1b3acf213c95bd0a25` merges main `56630e7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`f5c4a8c75b4d796b3d0001e5a37ee08408cc590a` merges the authored code head `deceb3de7ee1f01a1e0f6ddd3d93acede6c68e41` and then merges origin/main `d052f80f7` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`deceb3de7ee1f01a1e0f6ddd3d93acede6c68e41`. It is the merge of origin/main `d052f80f7f81d42db5c57a55ebaef7056c7ce01a` into the re-cut tip `e81bf9dbf0beec990324b61335b62d4267b87e54`. That commit's parent is `fcfc221ff`, whose parent is the reviewed PR head `2be13c572cf34a475d18e3f5e2dbde4f9ff8482a`. The merge base is origin/main `d052f80f7f81d42db5c57a55ebaef7056c7ce01a`.

- `fcfc221ff`: the re-wrap of the two calls, the marker re-key, and the median-versus-p90 check.
- `e81bf9dbf`: `python3 tests/structure.py --record --allow-regression=...`, with the reason in its commit message.
- `deceb3de7`: the merge of origin/main described under `## Re-cut`.

## Mutation proof

The block in `tests/features.py` starts at `# --- R10-CEILING-PROBE (#2498, #2808)` and now holds 62 checks. `python3 tools/audit/seat/features_block.py "# --- R10-CEILING-PROBE (#2498, #2808)" "# R10-HOTFIX-AWAY-PRESENCE (tvofi, 2026-10-30"` at the head prints `ALL 62 FEATURES BLOCK PASSED`. The END argument is needed since the merge, because main's block now follows this one and the block runner otherwise runs to the file's close.

merges.title: R10-FACTORY-RESET: factory reset
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-FACTORY-RESET (owner request, tvofi 2026-10-30): "There should also be an option to reset all parameters to factory integration defaults if there currently is none". There was none: `restore_learned_snapshot` restores a snapshot or a refit, and the comfort-weight and heat-loss buttons reset one learner each. This adds a reset with three scopes the user picks -- `settings`, `learners`, `both` -- as an options-flow page behind an explicit confirmation (Advanced settings -> Reset to factory defaults) and as a `factory_reset` service taking a required `entry_id` and `scope`. An undo point is taken first, and `restore_learned_snapshot` undoes the reset while that point is the newest snapshot; the confirmation text says so. The entry is then set up again, and its first cycle re-plans.

Where each part lives (fixer.md step 17): the settings rule in `entry_config.py` (the module that owns the entry's settings, Home Assistant-free): `FACTORY_KEPT`, `factory_settings`, `undo_point`, `undone_settings`. The learned stores in `coordinator.py`, which owns them: `_FACTORY_VOID` over `_restored_stores`, `async_factory_reset`, `_async_rewrite_entry`, `_async_undo_factory_reset`. The undo point in `snapshots.py` (`SnapshotRing.take(before_reset=)`, `undo_target`). The options step and the service only orchestrate (`config_flow.HeatPumpOptimizerOptionsFlow.async_step_factory_reset`, `services.handle_factory_reset`). No Home Assistant import is added below the glue.

**Settings.** Every stored key outside `FACTORY_KEPT` is dropped from both `entry.data` and `entry.options`, so it reads as the default the parse of an absent key gives: one home for the defaults, never a second table. Kept, each with its reason (printed by the first command under `## Figures`):

- every entity assignment: each `CONF_` key ending `_entity`, plus `compressor_freq_sensor` (46 keys, listed by that command) -- resetting one disconnects a sensor or actuator;
- `name` -- the entry's name, not a setting;
- `price_source`, `tibber_token` -- the price source and its credential;
- `solar_forecast_source` -- the solar feed, the price source's sibling: its default would leave an assigned radiation sensor unread;
- `two_zone_mode`, `dhw_enabled`, `wood_furnace_enabled` -- zone, tank and furnace topology, **written** as the settings in force derive them: an auto-mode house is two-zone by its zone masses, which the reset drops, so the mode is pinned `on`/`off` first;
- `upper_floor_emitter`, `lower_floor_emitter` -- emitter topology;
- `dhw_wood_coil_enabled` -- tank plumbing;
- `mixing_valve_mode`, `mixing_valve_write_target_kind` -- valve topology and what its write entity is;
- `space_setpoint_unit` -- what the setpoint entity's number means;
- `topology_layout`, `topology_positions` -- the plant layout and its diagram;
- `ecl110_command_topic`, `ecl110_displace_set_topic`, `ecl110_state_topic`, `ecl110_mqtt_qos`, `ecl110_mqtt_retain` -- the controller's MQTT wiring;
- `modbus_prefill_prefix` -- the heat pump device the entities came from;
- `main_fuse_amperes`, `main_fuse_phases` -- the house's main fuse: a default arms the fuse guard against a fuse the house does not have.

**Learners.** Every learned store, enumerated as `_restored_stores` (the set the snapshot restore already writes), is voided: with the entry **unloaded** first, so no save in flight writes the old state back: the two heat-loss learners through the one void path #3022 built (`async_reset_heat_loss_learners`, after the undo point), then `voided_documents` drops each store's `_FACTORY_VOID` keys or removes the store: `thermal_learning` (buffer cooling, COP scale, COP baseline and health, open-window detector, immersion events, capacity envelope, solar aperture, internal gains, heat curve, frequency map, flow bias), `dhw_profile` and `dhw_draws` (DHW cooling, profile, draws), `price_model`, `accuracy` (accuracy history, DHW accuracy, defrost, comfort weight). Each then loads absent: its initial state. Kept, as facts: the heat-loss anchors, the meter's last COP, snow memory, the frequency watchdog's stand-down latch, the billed peaks, the operating mode.

**Undo.** Before anything changes, the reset flushes every learner to its store and takes a snapshot whose `before_reset` holds every learned store's document, the settings it drops, and, per (data, options), the three topology keys the reset pins (`entry_config.FACTORY_PINNED`: `two_zone_mode`, `dhw_enabled`, `wood_furnace_enabled`) as they were stored. `restore_learned_snapshot` (`SnapshotRing.undo_target`: the undo point while it is the newest snapshot, else `best_restore`) unloads, writes the documents back, restores the dropped settings and the pinned keys as stored over the wiring in force, and sets the entry up again: every learner, the accuracy history and the settings come back exactly, an auto-mode house auto again. The drift rollback never takes it (`best_restore` skips it); spent, it stays as an ordinary snapshot.

**Refused unload.** Where Home Assistant refuses to unload the entry, nothing is written but the undo point: the heat-loss void runs only after a successful unload. `async_factory_reset` returns False and logs "not applied"; the options step aborts `factory_reset_not_applied` and the service raises `HomeAssistantError` (`factory_reset_not_applied`, placeholder `entry_id`). An undo over a refused unload keeps its undo point and returns False.

## Head

`ace2e21a6f22cc3e9af22b5b1eed6a92b55105d9` merges the authored code head `3f9f152e2ac87cee1a1ab3ac0018d64bd023f13d` and then merges origin/main `407eb0cb3` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`3f9f152e2ac87cee1a1ab3ac0018d64bd023f13d`. It merges the PR head `2df0b81ed2fb9726a4b8d52de072fdb64520ded1` (github-actions[bot]'s `ci: pin killed mutants` on `7f6d7e72`, 13 `tests/mutation_ledger/killed_by/` records and nothing else) into `895f03158b222d8a8bd11cf697c3f3baeb01674e`, which merges origin/main `ca6333333afc1ec7937b9792880458d190f4d4d2` into the PR head `7f6d7e72260ca64e98ec13c3b7c46c5e01af62a6` (the orchestrator's merge of origin/main `d052f80f7f81d42db5c57a55ebaef7056c7ce01a` over `116233658`, which merged this round's handoff `fcbf8ec952187bac1adfc46691f1ad43cffa6984` into the previous PR head `78c0e8d0864d880f36cc5f5f09c2c53ae802ea73`). Main's delta `d052f80f..ca633333` touches no production file and not `tests/features.py`; among scripts it touches `tests/entities.py` and `tests/env_drift.py`, both re-run at `895f0315` below; the bot's records are the only delta from there to this head. `tools/pr/prepr.sh` with this body at this head: `PRE-PR: 3f9f152e2ac87cee1a1ab3ac0018d64bd023f13d ... rc=0`. origin/main then moved once more, to `407eb0cb38f3cd43e71f4ed7be1c23f80dc32cc1` (#3049, 2026-11-01 18:21 UTC, during that run): `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0, and its delta (`tests/closures.json`, `.github/workflows/governance.yml`, `tools/audit/seat/` gh-call instruments, a delivery row) shares no file with this diff, so it is not merged (fixer.md step 6: merge only on a conflict); the figures below are against `ca633333`.

`fcbf8ec9` is this round's one authored commit. It changes tests and the mutation ledger only, no production line: `tests/features.py` (two checks and their controls), `tests/entities.py` (the service stub), and two `survivor_triage` records; it answers the fix review's round-2 block at `d1662cf7b100fe99cc9938c2a536dbced55823f3` (verdict/3047, mutation-vacuous) item by item. ## Block

Round 1: this PR's first fix review. I measured head `96211117d1341cb71925086fc44182f68b67139d` from a detached worktree.

The brief asks me to verify that "after a learners reset every learner reads its initial state" and that the undo "restores the pre-reset learned state and settings exactly". The checks that claim both ("after a learners reset every learner reads what one that never learned reads", "a reset of both ...", "restore_learned_snapshot undoes the reset ...") compare whole learner payloads against a coordinator that never learned. `_fr_learn` moves only some learners, so for every other learner both sides read the initial state and the comparison passes without exercising the reset. The body describes its control as "learner by learner", but it runs per store category: `thermal_learning` is one category and covers 14 keys.

Measured (ev/mutants-void-entries.txt): I deleted each entry of `coordinator._FACTORY_VOID` in turn and ran the R10-FACTORY-RESET section of tests/features.py, extracted verbatim (ev/fr_section_extract.py, 19 checks).
- Killed (9): `buffer_cooling_rate`, `_COP_STORE_KEY`, `curve_learner`, accuracy `accuracy`, `defrost`, `comfort`, and the stores `dhw_profile` and `price_model` (each made "kept" by turning `None` into `()`).
- Survived (13): thermal `buffer_cooling_samples`, `cop_samples`, `vent_cusum`, `cop_baseline`, `cop_health_cusum`, `immersion_events`, `capacity_envelope`, `solar_aperture`, `internal_gains_profile`, `freq_map`, `flow_bias`; accuracy `dhw_accuracy`; the store `dhw_draws`. The test never writes `dhw_draws` to disk at all.

Each survivor is a learner the reset could stop voiding (a renamed store key, say) with the suite still green. Today the code is right: every void key is a key the stores write (ev/keys.py output under Evidence). The defect is that the claim is not pinned. The mutation-pins shards add five live sites in this diff's own code (Findings). One of them, `entry_config.py:350 GUARD_OFF`, shows that no test undoes a learners-only reset.

To repair: make `_fr_learn` move every learner the void list names (or assert per key that the before state differs from the initial one), save `dhw_draws`, add an undo of a `learners` reset, and kill or triage the five shard survivors.

In the test house `two_zone_mode` is absent (auto) before the reset and `on` after the undo; the test asserts that pinned state. ## Block

Round 2 (fresh review, range 96211117..d1662cf7), measured at head `d1662cf7b100fe99cc9938c2a536dbced55823f3` from detached worktrees. This round closes every round-1 finding (see Evidence). One mutant from the finder's own harness was killed at round 1 and now survives.

The finder's mutant U6 (ev/list3.py at probe/rev-3047-30905b88; here as list4.py `U6-no-flush-before-documents`) deletes `await _async_save_restored(coord)` from `coordinator._async_store_documents`. That is the mechanism the body names in "Before anything changes, the reset flushes every learner to its store". Round 1 killed U6 only incidentally, through the old refused-unload check, which saw an extra save (finder's ev/mutants-undo-order.txt). Round 2 rewrote that check to compare documents with the stamp removed, so the kill went with it. At this head U6 survives:
- the R10-FACTORY-RESET section, 28 checks: `ALL 28 FR CHECKS PASSED` (ev/mutants-targeted.txt);
- the whole of `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py`: `ALL 4704 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, rc 0 (ev/mutants-full-features.txt).

No other script in the closure drives the reset: `config_flow_steps.py` checks the page schema, `entities.py` runs the log barrier, and `nightly_ha.py` posts the unconfirmed `{}`.

The deletion is observable, and the claim it breaks is the body's own: "every learner, the accuracy history and the settings come back exactly". My probe (ev/u6_probe.py, a reviewer instrument appended to the extracted section, not the PR's) runs `_fr_learn`, then learns a COP scale of 1.21 in memory after the last save, resets `both`, and restores. At the head the undo brings back 1.21 (ok). With U6, `FAIL the undo brings back a learner learned since the last save (COP scale 1.21) [cop 1.13]` (ev/u6-probe.txt). Every check in the PR learns through `_fr_learn`, which saves each store explicitly before the reset. So no check ever holds unsaved state, and the flush is pinned by nothing.

To repair: add a check that learns at least one learner after the last save, without saving, then asserts that the undo point holds it and that the undo restores it. Run U6 against that check and require red.

A second defect in this diff turns `tests / fast (3.14)` red at this head. In `tests/entities.py` (line 15433), the service-test stub `_svc_fr_record` returns None. Since this round, `services.handle_factory_reset` raises `HomeAssistantError(factory_reset_not_applied)` when `async_factory_reset` returns a falsy value. So `_svc_call(SERVICE_FACTORY_RESET, ...)` at line 15439 raises, and the script dies (CI job 124865808454: `>>> FAILED: python3 tests/entities.py`, `HomeAssistantError: The factory reset of test_entry was not applied`). Reproduced here on Linux: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` gives rc 1 with the same traceback. With the stub returning True, "factory_reset hands that entry's coordinator its scope and reports both" reads `ok`.

The same red baseline made every `tests / mutation-pins` shard `MUTATION TABLE INCONCLUSIVE` ("the baseline is already red in tests/entities.py"). So `tests / mutation-autofix` failed on six "lives" sites that were never measured. The body's `## Red checks` does not answer `tests / fast (3.14)`. A cheaper detector existed: `tests/entities.py` takes about 25 s on CI's Linux, and here in this cloud container. The body records that it stops early on the fixer's host (`PermissionError: Cannot get task port`), so the script was never run past the barrier slice before handoff.

## Findings

- The learner flush before the undo point (`coordinator._async_store_documents`: `await _async_save_restored(coord)`) survives deletion through all of `tests/features.py`. Removing it makes the undo restore only what was saved: COP scale 1.13 instead of the in-memory 1.21 in my probe. The Block gives the repair. Carry: R10-FACTORY-RESET
- `tests/entities.py:15433`'s `_svc_fr_record` stub returns None, so the service raises `factory_reset_not_applied` and `tests / fast (3.14)` is red at this head. The red baseline also made the four mutation-pins shards inconclusive and `tests / mutation-autofix` red. The stub must return True, and the red check must be answered in `## Red checks` (the Block). Carry: R10-FACTORY-RESET
- Two of the six sites `tests / mutation-autofix` left alive are equivalent mutants. `entry_config.py:360 RETURN_DEL` and `coordinator.py:9957 RETURN_DEL` each delete a function's trailing `return None`, and the implicit return is also None. Both survive the section, I measured no difference, and each needs a `survivor_triage` record, which no tool writes. My hand runs kill the other four with the lane's exact operator once the baseline is green: 358 GUARD_OFF, 369 GUARD_OFF and 373 RETURN_DEL in the section; 9955 GUARD_OFF in the whole of tests/features.py ("a configured, healthy tank probe fills the hot-water accuracy record") (ev/mutants-lane-sites-section.txt, ev/mutants-full-features.txt). Carry: R10-FACTORY-RESET
- `SnapshotRing.undo_target`'s "while it is the newest" is pinned only for a newer snapshot that is healthy. My mutant U7 (`"before_reset" in self.snapshots[-1]` -> `any("before_reset" in s for s in self.snapshots)`) survives the section and all of `tests/features.py` (ev/mutants-full-features.txt). Under U7, once a newer weekly snapshot follows the undo point, the restore takes that newest snapshot with no health or alarm gate, bypassing `best_restore`. The check "a weekly snapshot newer than the undo point takes the restore back from it" plants a healthy one, so either path passes. Planting an unhealthy or alarmed newer snapshot would pin it. This is a reviewer-built mutant, not a lane operator. Carry: R10-FACTORY-RESET

## Evidence

merges.body:
This lands the measured size model for the round-10 plan: `tools/plan/size_durations.py` re-derives `replan.py`'s duration model (`tools/plan/durations.json`) from the merged pull requests of every done round-10 group (p75 of round-adjusted active hours per size and class, review rounds added back at a Theil-Sen cost, a per-carry slope, a held group priced by its open carries). `replan.py` now starts a started group at the replan instant past the slot cap, records why each group starts when it does, orders ready work by the owner's 2026-10-30 tiers, and draws at the owner's 16 slots and 16 seats unless told otherwise. The plan page (`tools/audit/seat/plan_page.py`) lists every open issue but the tracking issue; one on no open group is listed as unplanned with the groups it was wired to. A mutant harness, self-test arms, a CI step and a closures classification pin the model.

Owning roster group: `R10-PLAN-REAL-DURATIONS` (size M, wave 1, fixer sonnet / reviewer opus, after `R10-PLAN-ARTIFACT` and `R10-ORCH-PLANPAGE`, files `tools/plan/size_durations.py`, `tools/plan/replan.py`, `tools/plan/durations.json`, `tools/audit/seat/plan_page.py`) in `dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json` at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster` 5229384ba5337f577728377b76bc1f2be21c0bfd (`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/handoff/audit-r10-roster`). Its resume branch is `handoff/r10-plan-real-durations`. The owner is tvofi.

Round 2 repair of the r1 block `mutation-survivor: theil-sen-ordered-pairs`: `round_slope`'s pair rule `if k2 != k1` could be replaced by `if k2 > k1` with no check failing, because every Theil-Sen fixture listed its rows in ascending x. `size_durations.py --self-test` now holds a row-order arm (the 5.5 h fixture ascending, reversed and shuffled must all give 5.5), and the mutant `theil-sen-ordered-pairs` is in the harness. Each r1 finding is answered: the survivor is killed (Mutation proof); Red checks is re-taken from the PR head branch; the mutant count reads nineteen plus the new one; the ownership paragraph names the roster group.

## Head

`8f2ecc647cfd6b4b51a7e5dd8b931168810a553f` merges main `239e5e4` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`b8ecad2dc4c5cd112a80eb3d4d5532f3e801d511` merges the authored code head `4d624465940b5a4916b7ff3fd3e44b644cd668d1` and then merges origin/main `d052f80f7` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

Code head measured: 4d624465940b5a4916b7ff3fd3e44b644cd668d1, the PR head 3fd85299d9c2314a3316c1956a97d37a9d95de77 plus one commit (the row-order arm and the mutant). `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0 (no conflict), so `origin/main` is not merged; `tools/pr/prepr.sh` was run at this head.

## Mutation proof

`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_plan_durations_mutants.py` (twenty one-occurrence replacements in `size_durations.py` plus the M0 null, each run against `--self-test`): M0 prints `rc=0 fails=0 verdict=null`; every named mutant (shared-branch-maps, roster-pointer, merge-commit-pointer, verdict-dedupe, dispatch-stamp-start, active-not-span, not-answered, forward-needs-done, percentile-linear, theil-sen, theil-sen-ordered-pairs, rounds-priced-out, min-cell, monotone-lift, part-capacity-p90, held-open-index, future-groups-only, boilerplate, pnums-subset, forward-overlap) prints `verdict=killed` with `rc=1`, and the last line is `RESULT survived=0`. The count is the `RESULT mutant=` lines less M0: nineteen replacements at the r1 head plus `theil-sen-ordered-pairs` (`k2 != k1` to `k2 > k1`), killed by the row-order arm (reversed rows keep no pair, slope 0 instead of 5.5; shuffled rows give 10). `replan.py --self-test` runs its own mutation table, each `ok self-test fails when ... is deleted`.

## Null control

The unmodified `size_durations.py` (mutant M0) passes with `fails=0`, and the new arm passes on it; `replan.py --self-test`, `size_durations.py --self-test` and `plan_page.py --self-test` all end `0 failed` at this head. At the merge base `tools/plan/size_durations.py` does not exist (`git cat-file -e origin/main:tools/plan/size_durations.py` fails), so the model had no instrument to fail.

n/a: `tools/` sites are pinned by the in-tree mutant harness `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_plan_durations_mutants.py` (above) and `replan.py`'s self-test mutation table.

merges.title: R10-FLY-RAISE-REVIEWABLE: a budget-raise PR is reviewable before its approval; review-carry refuses only a merge verdict
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-FLY-RAISE-REVIEWABLE (S, instrument; triage P345 and its carry P348, batch 95). Every budget raise is red at `budget-raise-gate` until the owner's approval (or a mandated one) names its head, and that approval comes after the verdict. So the reviewer-dispatch readers refused the review that the approval needs (#3045 at 9ef51b82, hand override; #3006's pre-approval reds). This adds `merge_train.approval_owed(train, pr, head, red)` as the single owner of that state, built on `Train.raise_hold` and so on budget_raise_gate's own `raises_between` and `approval`. Every reviewer-dispatch reader now asks it. `classify` itself, the train and the merge state do not change.

- `merge_train.py classify --pr N`: when the head is RED and `approval_owed` returns a reason, it prints `APPROVAL-OWED <sha> <why>` and exits 4. Without `--pr`, the result is the same as before.
- `bus.sh dispatch` passes `--pr "$pr"`, dispatches on rc 4 the same way as on 0 and 3, and prints the line.
- `orchestrator_tick.one_pr` prints `#N: RAISE APPROVAL OWED at <head8>: review it, then approve under the owner or the mandate (0013) -- not its fixer (K15 (d))` in place of NOT REVIEWABLE.
- `review_packet.py render`: when classify `--pr` answers APPROVAL-OWED for a required red, the red becomes the `approval-owed` advisory and is not the `required-red` refusal (that refusal is what made `bus.sh dispatch` die). This reader is the third layer the dispatch measured.
- `cloud_dispatch.py`'s reviewer prompt waits on `classify <head> --pr <pr>` and treats 4 as reviewable. Without that change the reviewer would get a 1 and block.
- Instrument pages updated: merge_train, orchestrator_tick, bus.sh, review_packet.
- `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_fly_raise_reviewable.py` is the real-head control (fixer step 18). It is INERT through `ci_predict.py --apply-inert`.

**One departure from the triage text, and the reason.** P345 says `approval_owed` should get "the red set" in which `classify` "reports `gate` and `budget-raise-gate / budget-raise-gate` red". The `classify` red set is taken over the ruleset's contexts, and the only one is `gate` (`tools/policy/fixtures/required-contexts.json` `contexts`). At #3045, `classify` prints `red: gate` and never names the unit (see Figures F1). If the predicate were fed that set, it would never fire. Every caller therefore passes the red set over `merge_train.gating_names(required)`: the ruleset contexts plus every unit gate.py can owe. That is the same expansion `gating_names` already provides for exactly this purpose. Mutation M5 pins this. The names come from `git diff --no-renames --name-only <merge-base> <head>`: P345's command, with `--no-renames` added because `closure.py selftest`'s RENAME_SITES pin requires it.

**Round 2: P348, in the same function (Carry 1, the group's one roster carry, answered here: `verdict_at` beside `blocked_rounds`, the three rows and the mutant it names, and the orchestrator.md clause).** `bus.sh dispatch --reviewed-head <rh>` refused to mint whenever `review_carry.py` answered CARRY, but `review_carry` reads only the commit range and never what the review at `rh` decided. A blocked review carried leaves nothing to merge, so the refusal blocked the fresh review the block asked for. #3045 round 3 at 9ef51b82 went out only by dropping `--reviewed-head`, which also drops the check for the case it exists for. `verdict_at <pr> <rh>` now prints the latest verdict word naming `rh` on `verdict/<pr>`. It shares the ref read with `blocked_rounds` through one new reader, `verdict_log`, which took the fetch and log that `blocked_rounds` held, so the ref is read the same way in both places and the read is not copied.
- On CARRY, a `merge` verdict still refuses with the existing message (the ruling's case, tvofi 2026-10-27).
- A `blocked` verdict mints and prints `review-carry: <rh> was blocked, so a fresh review is owed`. No verdict at all mints and prints `review-carry: <rh> has no verdict, so a fresh review is owed`.
- An unreadable `verdict/<pr>` refuses (`cannot read verdict/<pr> to learn what the review at <rh> decided`), as `blocked_rounds`' caller does.
- `dev/governance/roles/orchestrator.md` (the carry sentence beside `--reviewed-head`) now reads "over a range clean against a reviewed head whose verdict was merge", P348's clause. **This is a policy change and waits for the owner's approving review, or the mandate, at merge.** `policy_lint.mjs --budgets` passes with the clause in (F7).
- Instrument pages `bus.sh.md` and `review_carry.py.md` state the condition. `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_fly_raise_reviewable_carry.sh` is the real-ref control, INERT through `ci_predict.py --apply-inert`.

Alternatives considered for P348:
- Teach `review_carry.py` to read verdicts. Rejected: its contract is "THE TEST IS A COMMIT RANGE", and `app_approve.sh --carry` asks it the same question; a verdict read there would answer for callers that already hold a merge verdict.
- A second, independent `verdict/<pr>` reader beside `blocked_rounds`. Rejected: two copies of one ref read can drift. `verdict_log` is the one reader.

**Round 3: the #3073 review's class-open block.** `approval_owed` read only the red SET, `classify(latest_runs(runs), gating_names(req))[2]`. gate.py also fails a SKIPPED, ABSENT or PENDING unit, and it fails for reasons naming no unit at all (the deferral bound, the prelude cross-check, a fork head, the attempt cap). None of those puts a unit into that set, so each read as APPROVAL-OWED (the reviewer's probe, `verdict/3073` evidence/overfire.py). The repair reads why `gate` is red, from the gate itself.
- `merge_train.gate_raise_only(train, runs)` reads every red gate suite's own job log and owes only when each reason is `budget-raise-gate / budget-raise-gate: failure (this run|run N)` (`RAISE_REASON`). It reads the latest gate run of each check suite (`gate_suites`, the per-suite map `latest_runs` already kept, now shared), because the ruleset refuses on any suite's red. It parses the log with `gate_outcome`, V142's existing reader of gate.py's `FAIL` lines, so no second parser was written. It returns False when a gate suite is still running, when there is no red suite, when a log cannot be read, when the gate.py step never ran, or when the gate is RATE-LIMITED. A check run's id is its Actions job's id, and `--allow-escape-sequences` is passed because gh refuses every Actions log without it.
- `approval_owed(train, pr, head, runs, required)` now takes the runs and the required list and builds the red set itself. Its two callers (the `classify --pr` CLI and `orchestrator_tick._approval_owed`) each rebuilt the same expression before. The other readers the reviewer names (`bus.sh dispatch`, `review_packet` required-red, the `cloud_dispatch` reviewer prompt) ask `classify --pr`, so all of them inherit the repair (F12).
- Review finding O2 (surviving mutant R5): a row now drives the three-dot diff read at rc 128, and R5 is killed (M-R5 below).
- The merge state is untouched. `classify` without `--pr`, `wait_ci`, `main_green` and the train do not call `gate_raise_only`.

Alternatives considered for round 3:
- The reviewer's second route: require every unit gate.py owes at this head's kind, other than the raise unit, to have concluded `success` exactly. Rejected. It needs this head's kind and workset, which only gate.py and the prelude derive, so it would restate gate.py. It also cannot see the reasons that name no unit (deferral, prelude, fork, cap).
- Re-running `tools/ci/gate.py`'s `gate()` offline over the runs. Rejected: it needs the Actions jobs, the PR and the prelude claim the gate itself read, which is a second copy of the gate's inputs.
- Making gate.py emit its reasons as check-run annotations. Rejected for this group: it edits the required gate, which is a FULL-scope change. The log already carries the reasons, and V142 already reads them there.

## Head

`a21f82ea4fff70dcda6607910d555b242530a87c` merges main `239e5e4` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`828b6e8ce5b5b646d0c291ee3998b8e284e26f4b` merges the authored code head `03ef99f28f68f1b8ce9a207562e9134178723caf` and then merges origin/main `e4c9e2016` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

The only conflict was `tools/audit/seat/review_packet.py`'s `gather()` dict line, a semantic one: this PR adds `"approval_owed": owed`, main adds `"branch": branch, "unlanded": unlanded`. Both are kept (`git diff 27ae023c..HEAD -- tools/audit/seat/review_packet.py` shows main's change and nothing else). The merge brings #3086 (the uutils `sleep` fix). The merge base with origin/main is c3b7c964f6de, and `tools/pr/prepr.sh` was run on this committed tree against it: `PRE-PR: 03ef99f28f68f1b8ce9a207562e9134178723caf ... rc=0`, with step 7 (the body check) re-run by `body_push.sh` at the push. Code since round 3's c8fdf1492 is main's only. Round 3's figures F9-F13 were taken at c8fdf1492, and no code of this PR changed since; the delta is the merge, whose self-tests are in F14.

## Mutation proof

Round 3 (#3073), each applied to merge_train.py at this head. Both `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` and `python3 tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py --self-test` were run, then the file was restored:
- MA: `gate_raise_only` returns True. Fails the five `#3073: a raise whose gate is also red for ...` rows (SKIPPED unit, ABSENT unit, PENDING unit, the deferral bound, the prelude cross-check), plus `#3073: a gate log that cannot be read, or whose gate.py step never ran, stays RED, rc 1`, `#3073: every red gate suite is read ...` and `#3073: gate_raise_only is False for a gate suite still running ...`. In the tick it fails `P345 PRS null (#3073): the gate also failed a SKIPPED unit` (both arms).
- MB: `all(RAISE_REASON.match ...)` becomes `any(...)`. Fails the SKIPPED, ABSENT and PENDING rows, and the tick's #3073 null.
- MC: the running-suite test is dropped. Fails `#3073: gate_raise_only is False for a gate suite still running ...`.

## Block

The brief's step (2) asks for proof that approval_owed fires only when EVERY reason the aggregate `gate` is red is a raise's owed approval. It does not. `approval_owed` (tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py, after `RAISE_GATE`) tests only the *red set*, `classify(latest_runs(runs), gating_names(req))[2]`, and needs that set to be `{gate, budget-raise-gate / budget-raise-gate}`. But `gate` (tools/ci/gate.py, `gate()`) fails for reasons that never put any unit into that red set:
- `<unit> / <job>: SKIPPED`. gate.py fails any conclusion other than `success` (`elif st[1] != "success"`), but merge_train's `GREEN = ("success", "skipped", "neutral")` reads a skipped unit as green.
- `<unit> / <job>: ABSENT`. No check run, so classify lists it as pending, never red.
- `<unit> / <job>: PENDING`, the deferral bound (`FAIL run(s) [...] still being judged`), the prelude cross-check, a fork head, and the attempt cap. Each of these fails `gate` with no unit red.

Reviewer's own probe (ev/overfire.py, run with `classify --pr 3045` against the head's merge_train and stubbed in the same way as the self-test's `owed_cli`; it is not the fixer's harness). It plants #3045's shape (gate and budget-raise-gate failed, one unheld raise, the owner's approval on an older head) plus one extra unit:
- `tests / browser` concluded `skipped`: rc=4 APPROVAL-OWED (base: rc 1 RED)
- a gate unit with no check run (ABSENT): rc=4 APPROVAL-OWED (base: rc 1 RED)
- `tests / browser` `in_progress` under a concluded red gate: rc=4 APPROVAL-OWED (base: rc 1 RED)
- `tests / browser` concluded `failure`: rc=1 RED, which is correct.

Every reader inherits this, because each one asks the same function. `bus.sh dispatch` mints a reviewer. `orchestrator_tick` prints "RAISE APPROVAL OWED ... review it, then approve" in place of NOT REVIEWABLE. `review_packet` drops the required-red refusal. `cloud_dispatch`'s prompt tells the reviewer to "judge the head as GREEN". The merge itself stays safe, because the train and the ruleset still need a green `gate`. But the head is dispatched and the orchestrator is told to approve while it is red for a reason that is not the raise. That is the over-fire this change was required to exclude. The body's claim that the red is "only budget-raise-gate" is therefore not true over this domain.

To close it, something must read why `gate` is red, not just which units are red. One way is to read the `gate` check run's own output (its first token is `FAIL <reason>`; read every listed reason) and require each reason to name `budget-raise-gate / budget-raise-gate`. Another is to require every unit gate.py owes at this head's kind, other than RAISE_GATE, to have a latest run that completed with `success` exactly. Fix review: blocked eeb947e513fb1b43bd81946e3818f51195e33c48 defect: a bounded give-up in flock-wrap's renew-refused re-queue deletes the held- witness, so the seat's next leased script FAILS instead of the named-unrun SKIP

bus-nonce: a15392239e81a14d0ef49efafb1845ab

## Round

Round 1. Measured at head eeb947e513fb1b43bd81946e3818f51195e33c48 (code head 2327669181a6b5efdd25d8b8cfd5e00d949f4100, plus the delivery-row commit), merge base 7539d1675d7fc8b5020f90b395f4bb0c3485d5b3, from detached worktrees at both SHAs. `git diff $(merge-base)...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty, so the contract in force is the one I read.

## Block

The PR's two lease carries (P206, the wait bound; P211, the lapsed own lease) combine into a new failure, against P211's own constraint (a lease artifact must not fail a command for a label that held the lease).

- `tests/gate_lock.py` `flock_wrap`, the `except RenewRefused` arm: it calls `release(label)`, and `release` now also removes `held-<label>`. It then calls `take(..., wait_bound=wait_bound)`. If that bounded wait runs out, `WaitBoundExceeded` escapes and `_bounded` exits 76, but the witness is not re-marked. The lapse arm two lines below re-marks it (`release(...); _mark_held(...)`); this arm does not.
- What happens: a seat holds the lease under `HPO_GATE_LOCK_LABEL`, another label's ticket waits, and that label then holds the lease past the awaited script's bound. `run.sh` gets `SKIP: tests/stress.py (waited past its bound ...)`, which is right. The next leased script, `tests/harness_headers.py`, then goes to `flock-wrap`. `renew` raises `lease held by w, not seat`, and with no witness the lapse arm re-raises. The result is `gate_lock: flock-wrap refused, seat holds no lease`, rc 1, and `>>> FAILED: ... tests/harness_headers.py`. The manifest has `main-002 1 ... harness_headers.py`: a red gate from a lease artifact, not the sanctioned named unrun. Evidence: `ev/runsh-requeue-edge.txt` (the real `leased`/`run_always`/`scope_script` taken from this head's `tests/run.sh`, a scratch lock dir, and both recordings set to 3 s in a scratch `closures.json` so the bound is short). The same at module level: `ev/requeue-bound-edge.txt`.
- Control: the same scenario with one added line, `_mark_held(lock_dir, label)` after the `release` in the `RenewRefused` arm, gives `#skip tests/stress.py` and `#skip tests/harness_headers.py`, both named unrun (`ev/runsh-requeue-edge-control.txt`). The unbounded path (`wait_bound=None`, every caller before this PR) never reaches this state, because its `take` eventually succeeds and re-marks. So the defect is new with this diff.
- A repair owes a `_wait_cases` row for this sequence (re-queue, bounded give-up, next `flock_wrap` for the same label goes back into the bounded queue, not rc 1), and a mutant that drops the re-mark. That row would also be the first pin on the cross-call witness contract.

## Findings

- `tests/run.sh` `leased()`/`run_always()`: no test pins the new P206 mapping. Deleting the whole `if [ -e "$one.waited" ]` block survives every committed check, and then the run records `main-001 76 ... stress.py` as a failure, not a skip (`ev/runsh-mutant-nomap.txt`). The behaviour at the head is correct (`ev/runsh-skip-demo.txt`: `SKIP: tests/stress.py (...left to CI, named unrun)`, manifest `#skip tests/stress.py`). But the carry's "never a silent pass" constraint is only pinned in `gate_lock.py`, not where the lane decides pass or skip. The repair round the Block opens should add a run.sh-level row, or an entities/self-test arm, that drives `leased` with the marker present and absent. Carry: dismissed: owed by this same pull request's repair round, which the Block above already forces; R10-PREPR-CAP's roster entry reads `resume.stage done`, so it is not a live destination for carry_audit
- `tests/run.sh` lane mode (`JOBS>1`): a script that waited past its bound prints `[hh:mm:ss] ok <script> (5s)` on the console before `run_always` rewrites its log to the SKIP note (`ev/runsh-skip-demo-jobs2.txt`). The manifest is right (`#skip`), but the progress line reads as a pass. It is cosmetic, and the fix is to compute the status word after the marker test. Carry: dismissed: cosmetic, the manifest and accounting are correct; it belongs in the Block's repair round of this pull request, whose group's roster entry reads done
- `held-<label>` witnesses are never cleared for a label that is abandoned without `release` (its lease is stolen as expired or orphaned by another label). A later reuse of the same label is then treated as "held once", and `flock-wrap` takes the lease and leaves it held after the run. Carry: dismissed: the lease it leaves still expires at LEASE_SECONDS and is orphan-stealable, labels are per-topic, and the files are zero-byte; recorded so the next seat touching the witness knows its lifetime is unbounded.

## Evidence

Requirement by requirement, at the head:

- (1) Slot pool (already on main at the base, as the body says; `take_slot`, `HPO_HEAVY_SLOTS`, `holding_slot`, and the `export HPO_SLOT_LABEL` in prepr step 1b are all present at 7539d1675). I re-ran the measure-first evidence on a scratch lock dir (`ev/slot-measure-first.txt`):
  - p1..p4 print `taken slot=0..3`;
  - `p5 --no-wait` prints `BlockingIOError: all 4 heavy slots held`;
  - a blocking p5 queues (`waiting for a heavy slot`), and after `slot-release --label p1` it prints `taken slot=0`;
  - `HPO_HEAVY_SLOTS=9` gives `heavy_slots()` 4 (clamped);
  - `HPO_SLOT_LABEL=prepr-1` gives `holding_slot() True`;
  - `needs-lease` answers `lease` (stress.py), `none` (structure.py) and `slot` (features.py).
- (2) P206: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/gate_lock.py --accept` prints `ALL 40 gate lock acceptance checks PASSED`, 7 of them new (`ev/gate_lock-accept.txt`).
  - Mutants (`ev/mutants-own.txt`), all killed: bound test -> `if False` (the run fails rc 1; the body said it hangs, rc 143 under `timeout 60`, and here the 60 s holder lease expired first, which is still killed); marker touch removed; `return WAIT_BOUND_RC` -> `return 0`.
  - The uncontended null holds: `ev/runsh-uncontended.txt` gives `STRESS RAN`, manifest rc 0, no lease left.

merges.body:
## Re-cut note

Round 5 of #3049, a minimal re-cut (fixer.md, "Past three rounds, re-cut rather than repair"). The round-4 block: the shim split the caller's `ps -o args=` line on spaces, and a value-taking option (python `-W`/`-X`) skipped exactly one word as its value, so a value that is one argv word containing a space was only partly skipped (`python3 -X "importtime LEAKVAL" c.py` logged `python3 LEAKVAL`). The header, the instrument page and the old body claimed more than the code did. Nothing outside that block changed: two commits touch only the parent-field rule of the shim, its arms in `gh_calls.py` and the two texts that state it.

Why: P284, the shared token's core bucket was spent twice with no host log naming the caller. `tools/audit/seat/shims/seat-gh`, installed as `gh` by `seat_venv.sh --install-shims`, appends `<utc> <ppid> <parent, 80 chars> <subcommand> <api path or verb>` to `$HPO_STATE_DIR/gh-calls.log` (directory 0700, log 0600) and execs the first real gh past itself; `tools/audit/seat/gh_calls.py` reads it and self-tests the shim.

The fix: a value-taking letter (python `-W`/`-X`, shell `-o`/`-O`) now ends the parent field unlogged, its value never read, instead of skipping its value. Cost: a script after such an option is not named (`python3 -W error c.py` logs `python3`). The field is otherwise as before: argv[0]'s basename plus at most one more word; a no-value letter is passed over; `c`/`e`/`s` log the option up to that letter and end the field; `--eval/--print/--command` log the name only; any other letter or long option ends it unlogged; `-m <module>` and the first non-option word are logged. Cleaned to `[A-Za-z0-9_./: -]`, cut to 80. Stated residual, by design: argv[0] and the script path are logged as given (`sh ./GH_TOKEN=abcLEAKVAL/script` logs `sh ./GH_TOKEN?abcLEAKVAL/script`; a `bashLEAKVAL` argv[0] symlink logs `bashLEAKVAL`), and `ps` joins argv with spaces, so a script path containing a space is cut at it. The shim header and `instruments/shims_seat-gh.md` state exactly this.

## Head

`a38d4fae44a742ceb1087f8e8c8d1188490265d1` merges main `6a09b4d` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`3602d1b64c88a947c7f5e815fff15b46a6c4c496` merges the authored code head `2f97d5701e0ae1e189dfe919dd6d5d08a0189202` and then merges origin/main `e4c9e2016` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`2f97d5701e0ae1e189dfe919dd6d5d08a0189202` (code and handoff head), measured on a root host. Branched from PR head `50694d12d3d488bf96b49b0cf44b3bb0eb6a6fce`; origin/main is `e4c9e2016a455d787d3a7604ef88c803c3ba5c70` and `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0 (no conflict), so main was not merged. `tools/pr/prepr.sh` was run at this head with main unmoved since.

## Mutation proof

Failing test first: commit one adds the exact-field arms `python3 -X 'a LEAKVAL' caller.py` and `python3 -W "ignore LEAKVAL" caller.py` (field must be `python3`), moves the other value-letter arms to the new expectation, and adds the mutant arm; against the previous shim: `gh_calls self-test: 84 checks, 8 failed`. Commit two (the shim) makes it `84 checks, 0 failed`. The new `fmutant` arm "a value-taking letter skips one word as its value, not ending the field" restores the old skip in the shim text and requires `python3 -X 'a LEAKVAL' caller.py` to change: `ok mutant killed`. The nine mutants of the previous round and the four older ones are unchanged and read killed.

## Null control

The field is not cut to nothing: through the real `ps`, `python3 -I W/caller.py --body LEAKVAL` logs `python3 W/caller.py` and `python3 -m caller_mod` for `-m`; through the fake `ps`, `python3 -I caller.py --body LEAKVAL` logs `python3 caller.py` (self-test arms, unchanged). The unfixed shim logs `python3 LEAKVAL` for the new arms, which is the 8 FAIL lines above.

## Figures

- `python3 tools/audit/seat/gh_calls.py --self-test`: `84 checks, 0 failed` (rule: every `ok`/`FAIL` line; one arm self-skips as root).
- `env -u BASH_ENV bash tools/audit/seat/seat_venv.sh --self-test`: `21 checks, 0 failed`.
- Finder's harness at both ends: the drivers live in the review evidence ref and not in the tree, exported with `git show origin/verdict/3049:evidence/finder-probe.sh`, the same for `finder-probe2.sh` and the reviewer's `probe3.sh`, each run against the shim exported from 50694d12 and from this head under `env -u BASH_ENV` (count rule: lines starting LEAK). Old head: probe 2, probe2 0, probe3 2 (the two spaced values). This head: probe 2, probe2 0, probe3 0. The two left in probe are exactly the disclosed residual above. Each file has one NOLINE (a bash --command= and a node --print= shape that never call gh); probe3 has 4 NOLINE at both ends.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`: `ALL 2497 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`. `python3 tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`. `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`: `MODE: SCOPED -- 2 script(s) run, 31 scoped out.`
- Claim files, `VERSION`, `RELEASE_NOTES.md` and the manifest: untouched by this pass.

## Red checks

- `governance / instrument-self-tests`: red on main itself (the uutils failure), fixed by #3086; this branch's `gh_calls.py` and `seat_venv.sh` self-tests pass above, and the PR head 50694d12 read GREEN in `merge_train.py classify`. No cheaper detector exists for a red on main before its fix lands; the standing cost is nil here.
- `CodeQL` and open `code-scanning alert 46 (py/overly-permissive-file)`: at this head no check has run yet (the head is not pushed to the PR), and `prepr.sh` reports `CodeQL` red from the branch's existing alert. This seat cannot read code-scanning alerts (no gh REST, no MCP code-scanning tool). At the PR head 50694d12, `merge_train.py classify` read GREEN, 53 check-runs, none failed, `codeql / Analyze (python)` success. The alert concerns the self-test setting two test logs to `0o600 | 0o044` to pin that an existing 0644 log is made 0600; the logs live in a private `TemporaryDirectory`, and the mode is the arm's input. No cheaper detector exists for a mode that is the test's deliberate input; this pass does not touch those lines.

## Forward-carry

none

  For instrument-self-tests a cheaper detector existed before the handoff (below), so the class is `root-cause-detectable`. The CodeQL alert body is unreadable from this seat (HTTP 403, ev/codeql-46.txt), so I did not re-derive which line it flags. The likely sites are the self-test's `chmod(0o755)` calls, which is an inference. The body must name and answer both.
- **The PR's own self-test is red in CI.** `governance / instrument-self-tests` (job 124609326791) concluded `failure` on this head at the step this PR adds:
  - The arm `FAIL no real gh: one line, rc 127, no self-exec` fails, and the run ends `gh_calls self-test: 19 checks, 1 failed` (ev/ci-instrument-self-tests-gh_calls.txt).
  - Cause: the self-test sets `PATH=<own>:<real>:/usr/bin:/bin` (gh_calls.py:171). The arm deletes only the stub. GitHub's runner image ships `/usr/bin/gh`, so the shim finds and execs that one instead of refusing with rc 127.
  - I reproduced it here by planting a temporary `/usr/bin/gh`, which gave `18 checks, 1 failed` (ev/repro-usr-bin-gh.txt), then removed the file.
  - The body's 18/0 figure was taken on a host with no gh in /usr/bin. The `## Red checks` section does not name this check.
  - A cheaper detector existed before the handoff: running the self-test on any host with gh in /usr/bin, or with `PATH` reduced to the stub dirs plus a dir that has `sh`/`ps`/`date`/`tr`/`cut`/`wc`/`mv` symlinked in.
  - Fix: make the test PATH hermetic.
- **class-open: the shim's own parent-command field.** Requirement (1) says the log never holds field values or bodies. The argv parser does drop them. But the third field is `ps -o args= -p $PPID` cut to 80 chars, and that field is not guarded. Any wrapper parent puts the full gh command line into the log, values included. Reproduced at this head (ev/leak-parent-field.txt):
  - `timeout 10 gh api repos/o/r -f body=VIA_TIMEOUT` logs `timeout 10 gh api repos/o/r -f body=VIA_TIMEOUT  api repos/o/r`.
  - `sh -c 'gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments -f body=SECRET_VALUE; :'` logs `body=SECRET_VALUE`.
  - `bash -c 'gh issue comment 1 --body TOPSECRET ...; :'` logs `TOPSECRET`.

  The self-test's only parent is the Python test runner, whose command line holds no gh arguments, so no arm reaches this case. The body does not name this field as a site. Fix direction, for the fixer to choose: log only the parent's executable and script name (argv[0], plus argv[1] when argv[0] is an interpreter), never its later args. Or apply the same value-stripping to the parent line, and when the parent is itself a gh-carrying wrapper, log its grandparent. Add a self-test arm where the parent is `sh -c '... -f body=secret'` and `timeout N gh ... -f body=secret`.
- **harness: design-trace-missing latency.** The brief requires the shim's per-call cost to be measured and stated as a number. The body states none. I measured it myself: about 20.9 ms per call over a `exit 0` stub (2.149 ms direct, 23.041 ms through the shim, 200 calls each, this container; ev/latency.txt). The cost comes from the ps/date/wc/tr/cut forks. The body owes the number, and the fixer's own figure on the host.

## Findings

- Surviving mutant: removing `--input` from the value-flag list leaves the self-test at 18/0. The arm "-X value, --input value and query string are dropped" puts `--input tokfile` after the path, where the parser has already stopped (`break`), so the arm cannot see the skip. `gh api --input FILE repos/o/r` is the case it misses: with the mutant, FILE is logged as the target. Add an arm that puts `--input` before the path. Carry: R10-FLY-GH-CALL-LOG
- Surviving mutant: replacing `clean()`'s `tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9_./:-' '?'` with `cat` leaves the self-test at 18/0. No arm feeds a token outside the allowed set, so the `?` claim in the body and the instrument doc is untested. Carry: R10-FLY-GH-CALL-LOG

- No logging when the state directory is missing: the shim never runs `mkdir -p "$state"`, so on a host where `$HOME/.local/state/hpo` does not exist yet it logs nothing, silently. The null control depends on that, so a fix would make the null control use a read-only path instead. Carry: R10-FLY-GH-CALL-LOG

## Block

The fix claims the parent field is built by construction: argv[0], then for an interpreter one word (the script, `-m <module>`, or the `-c`/`-e`/`--eval`/`--print`/`--command` option that ends the field), and that "no later word of the caller's command line is read". The PR body, `instruments/shims_seat-gh.md` and the shim's header comment all say this. The code does not do it. The round-2 shapes are closed. But the same class (a caller's argument value reaching `gh-calls.log`) is still open through seams the rule admits. Every probe below uses a LEAKVAL marker, and the logged line holds the marker at the evidence location given:

- **Glued code option.** The `-*[ce]*)` and `--eval*|--print*|--command*)` cases append the whole token `$a`. When the code is attached to the flag, the token is the code. `python3 -c<code>` and `python3 -Bc<code>` with no space in the code log the code up to the 80-char cut, flag values included (ev/probes2-head.txt lines 1-4). The same holds for `perl -e<code>` (ev/probes-head.txt "perl -eCODE glued"), `ruby -e<code>` (ev/probes2-head.txt line 7) and `node --eval=<code>` (ev/probes2-head.txt line 11). The `?` cleaning only replaces quotes, parentheses and `=`; the value itself survives.
- **Stdin script (`sh -s`/`bash -s`).** `-s` is skipped as an option, so the first positional argument is logged as if it were the script. `sh -s LEAKVAL < s.sh`, `sh -s -- LEAKVAL`, `bash -s LEAKVAL` and the common install shape `... | bash -s -- --token LEAKVAL` all log `sh LEAKVAL` or `bash LEAKVAL` (ev/probes-head.txt "sh -s" lines; ev/probes2-head.txt last line).
- **Value-taking interpreter options.** `python3 -W <v> script` and `python3 -X <v> script` log `<v>` as the script (ev/probes-head.txt "-W"/"-X" lines). `python3 -W error -m mod` logs `python3 error`, which also loses the module.

These are the same class round 2 blocked (a value from the caller's command line reaching the log), now reached through the interpreter rule rather than gh's flags. The enumeration the body names ("no word past the one it keeps") does not hold on the code: the kept word is chosen by a predicate whose domain includes option values, positional arguments of a stdin script, and option tokens that carry their own argument. A direction, not a requirement: for any `-c`/`-e`/`--eval`/`--print`/`--command` match, log only the flag name, cut at the first character after the flag letter (or `=`). Treat `-s` as ending the field. Treat any option the field rule does not know as ending the field, rather than skipping it and taking the next word. Pin each with an exact-field arm.

## Block

The re-cut closes every round-3 shape. The finder's harness reads 9/5 LEAK at 16cb22f6 and 2/0 LEAK at this head, and the two left are the disclosed argv[0]/script-path residual. All nine of the body's field mutants and seven planted mutants of my own are killed. One seam of the same class is still open and is not dispositioned. The shim reads the caller's command line from `ps -o args=`, which joins argv with spaces. It then splits that line back into words on spaces (`read -r -a pw`). A value-taking option (python `-W`/`-X`) skips exactly one word as its value. So a value that is one argv word containing a space is only partly skipped, and the rest is logged as the script:

- `python3 -X "importtime LEAKVAL" c.py` logs `python3 LEAKVAL` (ev/probe3-head.txt).
- `python3 -W "ignore LEAKVAL" c.py` logs `python3 LEAKVAL` (ev/probe3-head.txt).

The shim header claims "So no option value, code, stdin-script argument or later word reaches the log (P284)". The body says a value-taking letter "passes over its value, glued or the next word, unlogged". instruments/shims_seat-gh.md says the value of a known value-taking letter is passed over. All three are stronger than the code. The header's "Words split on spaces only" names the splitting but not this consequence. The body's class rule lists the field's case table as its seams and does not list the word-splitting seam. The shell value letters `-o`/`-O` take the same path, but bash rejects a spaced value before any gh call (NOLINE in ev/probe3-head.txt), so only python is reachable here. A direction, not a requirement: read `/proc/$PPID/cmdline` NUL-split where it exists, keeping `ps` as the fallback. Or end the field unlogged at a value-taking letter instead of skipping its value. Either way, pin it with an exact-field arm such as `python3 -X 'a LEAKVAL' caller.py`. Or disclose the residual in the header, the body and the instrument page.

The new `claim-files.md` text says: "a side's change or deletion (a `may-drift` line too) wins over the other's silence". Plant this merge: this branch deletes `# may-drift: flat_prices -- polish` (the R8-P3 suspension), and main leaves that line alone but rewords the adjacent `# may-drift: wood_coil` line. `_union_comments` runs `git merge-file --union`, which keeps both sides of the overlapping hunk. The result therefore reinstates the deleted `flat_prices` may-drift line, and keeps main's reworded `wood_coil` line next to the old wording. `merge_claim_defect` checks only for may-drift lines that were **lost**, never for ones reinstated, so the driver prints `resolved` (ev/adversarial.txt row `D2`).

2. **A surviving mutant on the deletion rule, theirs-deleted direction** (fix-review.md step 1). Mutant: `if mine == main or mine == was: lines = our_blocks.get(name) or their_blocks.get(name)`. On the probe (main deletes scenario `alpha`, the branch leaves it alone), it brings `alpha` back: `['alpha','beta','gamma']` against the head's `['beta','gamma']` (ev/m3-survivor.txt). That reinstatement is the very hazard the driver exists to prevent. `_CM_BASE_HELD` pins only the direction where this branch deletes. The body's M3 is killed; this variant on the other branch is not. It needs a fixture where main deletes a claim that the branch left alone. The `tests / mutation` lane is green, but it did not draw this mutant.

Root-cause seat for the eight issues a done transition orphaned (#2248, #2249, #2674, #2731, #2492, #2257, #2942, #2998), with its countermeasure. The analysis is `dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-ROSTER-SYNC-ORPHANS.md`; the issue-facing **Root cause** section is below, for the orchestrator to post (this seat makes no GitHub write).

**Cause.** Ownership of an issue is derived from its group being open (`carry_audit.Dests`, via `roster_lib.is_open`), so the write that closes a group also drops it as owner of every issue it lists. Neither writer of a closed stage reads ownership: `roster_sync.py`'s `derive` MERGED arm writes `done` from the merge alone, and `roster_edit.py`'s `op_set_stage` / `op_set_resume --field stage` write any classified stage. The one detector, `carry_audit.py sweep --issues`, runs later and by hand, and with no `--roster-ref` it reads main's roster copy, not the live ref `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster` (`git ls-remote` at `806d2db83aa0`) where both writers write.

**Process state: (c).** The sweep (`finding-propagation.md`'s enforcement) existed and was run; its unit, main's copy, did not reach the live record, so it missed 3 of 8, and even its 5 were found tens of hours late. The countermeasure changes the unit and moves the same test to the transition.

**The eight**, through `carry_audit.load_dests(<ref>).owned` at origin/main and at the live tip before the 2026-11-01T09:10Z closes (`84571a150c06`):

| issue | main's copy (the sweep) | live ref | dropped by |
|---|---|---|---|
| #2248, #2249 | UNOWNED: caught | UNOWNED | `roster_sync` R10-STORE-RACES done |
| #2257 | UNOWNED: caught | UNOWNED | `roster_sync` R10-ADVISOR-WHATIF done |
| #2942 | UNOWNED: caught | UNOWNED | `roster_sync` R10-FRICTION-MUTATION-SURVIVOR done |
| #2998 | UNOWNED: caught | UNOWNED | none: no group listed it before `e74e0870a` |
| #2492 | R10-SAV-ACTUATION, `in-progress` on main: missed | UNOWNED | `roster_sync`, then `set-stage` |
| #2731 | R10-FLY-GH-READ-RETRY, `carries-open` on main: missed | UNOWNED | `roster_sync` R10-FLY-GH-READ-RETRY done |
| #2674 | `carry-2674.json`: missed | `carry-2674.json` | none under the rule: a carry file is a destination |

The live ref catches 7 of 8; the transition test reaches 6 of 8 at write time (not #2998, never owned; not #2674, owned by its carry file).

**Countermeasure.** One owned-issue test, `carry_audit.Dests.owns`, now used by `check`, `sweep --issues` and the new `carry_audit.orphaned(dests, group)` (the `--issues` test asked of a closing group on the roster the write leaves; an unreadable state counts as open). `roster_sync.hold_open` writes `carries-open` at the merge commit instead of `done`, printing `HELD: owns open #n`, on the dry run and on the write path's re-derive; groups closing in one pass are judged together. `roster_edit.hold_done` does the same for `set-stage` and `set-resume --field stage`. `carry_audit.py sweep` with no `--roster-ref` reads `roster_lib.reader_ref` (`sweep_ref`). Offline, both writers take `--issue-state FILE`. No roster data file is edited.

## Head

`77524a704af85e3a402b95b8b8c66a25332a08a3` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3092.md`. The authored code head is `630b15e45e80126c5546385b2d603cde26fa19c2`.

`3afd1e0808e1331a24535fb4be18065cc3147b89` merges origin/main `fb0a6d5a3` into the authored code head `630b15e45e80126c5546385b2d603cde26fa19c2` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below).

`630b15e45`, which merges origin/main `6421fe135` (it moved from the dispatched base `92588d581fde4ce287af3db5e8bb61461dc28015` by #3075, touching none of this diff's files); every self-test and the scoped gate below were re-run at it.

## Mutation proof

In-tree harnesses, each plant applied alone and the file restored:

- `python3 tools/audit/seat/r10_roster_sync_mutants.py M25_hold_dropped M26_apply_unheld M27_owners_before_close M28_issue_state_ignored`: M25 rc=1 fails=4 (`a merged group owning an open issue nothing else owns is held carries-open ...`, `two groups closing together are not each other's owner: both are held`, `the dry run holds a merged group ...`, `the hold is written: carries-open at the merge commit`); M26 rc=1 fails=1 (`the hold is written ...`); M27 rc=1 fails=4 (the same four as M25); M28 rc=1 fails=3 (`... one whose issue is closed is done (null control)`, `... and closes one whose issue is closed (null control)`, `... and the closed issue's group is done (null control)`).

## Unpinned sites

The `carry_audit.py` sites `orphaned`, `sweep_ref` and `Dests.owns`: M28 pins `orphaned`'s state arm through roster_sync's self-test in `r10_roster_sync_mutants.py`; the other three were killed by the scratch driver above, which is not in the tree (`r10_carry_parser_mutants.py` censuses the parser only). - `python3 tools/audit/seat/r10_roster_sync_mutants.py --null`: rc=0 fails=0. `python3 tools/audit/seat/r10_roster_ops_mutants.py --null`: rc=0 fails=0. The scratch driver's unplanted run: rc=0 fails=0.

## Figures

- Self-tests at the head: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_sync.py --self-test` 83 checks, 0 failed (base 75); `python3 -I tools/audit/carry_audit.py --self-test` 214 checks, 0 failed (base 206); `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py --self-test` 135 checks, 0 failed (base 131); `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/r10_roster_ops_mutants.py --self-test` 105 checks, 0 failed.
- The defect, replayed on its own instances: the base's and the head's `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/roster_sync.py --checkout $DEMO/co --pr-state $DEMO/prs1.json` dry run, `$DEMO/co` a clone whose origin holds the live roster at `c47931afa` (the parent of R10-FRICTION-MUTATION-SURVIVOR's done, PR #2961): base `stage in-progress -> done at 13871b7aa4a1`; head (`--issue-state` #2840 and #2942 open) `-> carries-open at 13871b7aa4a1 (PR #2961 MERGED) HELD: owns open #2942`; head with #2942 recorded closed: `-> done` (null control). The same at `22622ddf6` with PR #2639, issue state read live from `gh`: base `-> done at 57b7b4994ac7`; head `-> carries-open ... HELD: owns open #2731`.
- The class over round 10: `python3 $SCRATCH/replay3.py $WT origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster $SCRATCH/issues.tsv` (replay3.py sha1 064d1f09be558cad9c570f9639a81d72a10c9a09; issues.tsv sha1 cff944d284d69bc3a92bfed0dbaaf21860839194, the REST `issues?state=all` number, created_at, closed_at, state, read 2026-11-01). Null control: an independent replay with its own owner logic (`$SCRATCH/replay.py`, sha1 2ac7792379625fb6b3c5bd3d09691fc7e83c6b65) prints the identical 86 event lines (`diff` of the two `ORPHAN` line sets, empty, then `IDENTICAL-EVENTS`).
- Cost test inputs, measured here: one `gh api repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/issues/2731` 0.35-0.37 s; one `roster_edit.py set-stage` op to its lint gate, no push, 10.3 s; `roster_sync.py` dry-run pass 9.27-9.73 s base, 9.55-10.40 s head with one hold read; `roster_lib.reader_ref` 0.06-0.07 s; `carry_audit.py sweep --issues` 0.88-0.93 s. The replay's state reads: 145 of 227 owned-issue references (`replay3.py`'s `issue-state reads` line).

## Cost test

Wall-clock over round 10 (2026-10-17 to 2026-11-01). Standing cost: 145 reads x 0.36 s = 52 s; disposal ops, +1 for a held group a person then disposes otherwise, -1 for one a person re-staged `carries-open` by hand (per transition: `roster_sync` 21 and 18, `set-stage` 17 and 2): +18 ops x 10.3 s = 185 s; the sweep's ref read 0.06 s each. About 237 s a round, 4.1 s per tool-written orphaning transition (58). P(recurrence), measured: 67 of 264 transitions orphaned an issue (58 tool-written), 67 of the 161 that owned one. Cost of the defect: finding and tracing each orphan, and its window (a carry to it refused `#n has no owner`, nothing dispatching it); the disposal decision is owed either way and cancels. Tracing time was not measured; the sweep alone is 0.9 s and missed 3 of 8. Verdict: pays if finding and tracing one orphan costs a seat more than 4.1 s; and the class meets `defect-root-cause.md`'s audit-class count (3+ in one round), so a barrier is owed whatever the test says and the test picks its form. The hold is the cheapest form found: a refusal at `roster_edit` costs the same op (refused, dispose, re-run) and one more where the owner wanted `carries-open`, and at `roster_sync` it leaves a merged group at its pre-merge stage; a warning is (b)'s treatment for a (c) cause; a self-releasing hold would save 36 ops (371 s) but needs a marker telling a sync-held `carries-open` from a person's and a re-read of every held group each beat pass, whose cadence this seat did not measure: not built.

## Forward-carry

## Friction

- payload-identity: contradiction: the payload says to pin commit identity `seat <seat@users.noreply.github.com>`; the brief snapshot says `hpo-fixer <70032254+tvofi@users.noreply.github.com>`; the commits carry the brief's, the task-specific one. State **(c)**: `carry_audit.py sweep --issues` existed and ran, but read main's roster copy, not the live ref, and ran after the fact; neither done writer (`roster_sync` MERGED arm, `roster_edit set-stage`) read ownership.
