merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-AWAY-PRESENCE: re-plan on presence and holiday-calendar changes
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-HOTFIX-AWAY-PRESENCE (live user defect, tvofi 2026-10-30; probe report `handoff-body/r10-live-away-heating` aa6e5db30, code chain steps 2 and 3).

**The defect.** `coordinator.py` subscribed state changes for the defrost flag and the peak guard only. An away flag from `away_presence_entity` (a person, a calendar, an `input_boolean`, a presence `binary_sensor`) therefore reached the plan only at the next scheduled update, one `optimization_interval` later (default 30 min). The holiday calendar (`holiday_calendar_entity`) is the other entity whose state switches a comfort band (`away.holiday_dates`, read in `_solve_hubs`), and it had the same gap; the class census below found it.

**The fix.** `away.watch_away_inputs`, called once from the coordinator's construction, registers one `async_track_state_change_event` listener per configured slot and hands each unsubscribe to the entry's `async_on_unload`. A listener requests the coordinator's `async_request_refresh`, the debounced path the away switch already uses, only when the reading the plan uses changes: `interpret_presence(...) is True` for presence (unknown or unavailable reads as home, as `away.resolve` reads it), and the covered dates for the holiday calendar (`_holiday_days`, now shared with `holiday_dates`). A change that leaves that reading where it was asks for nothing. An unconfigured slot registers nothing. An entry with no unload list registers nothing, so no listener is left that nothing could drop.

**The reload window (the brief's second item).** After a set-point change the entry reloads. The first publish is the pre-reload plan (`_reload_handover`) until the background solve lands. The window was already bounded at both ends, by two existing pins:
- A handover stamped more than one update interval ago is dropped (`__init__._take_fresh_handover`; `tests/manual_plan.py` #774).
- Setup requests the replacing solve at once, as the entry background task `heatpump_optimizer_first_solve` (`tests/entities.py`, "an entry's setup defers the first solve to one entry background task"). If that solve fails, the next scheduled update replaces the plan one interval later.

What the card did not show was the window itself. The handover republished the pre-reload cycle's `next_optimization` (that solve plus one interval), so the card's plan health read "Next solve in N min" while the replacing solve was already due. `_republish_handover_ages` now stamps `next_optimization` with the current time, so the card reads "Next solve due now" (`health.next_due`) beside the plan's true age ("solved N min ago", already recomputed). No card change is needed: `healthPlanHtml` already reads `_next_optimization`.

**Scope against the roster's `files`.** The roster names `coordinator.py` and `tests/features.py`. The listener lives in `away.py`, the module that owns presence and holiday interpretation. `pump_arbiter.py` and `early_cutoff.py` register their listeners at module level in the same way. Putting it in the coordinator class would have grown a class with zero headroom on `max_class_loc` and `class_excess_loc`. The coordinator gains one line, the registration. The ratchet is paid by deleting the dead `_unsub_timer` attribute, which has been assigned only `None` since v1.0.0 (ec45dc4d5), so its shutdown branch never ran. A new dev harness, `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_away_presence_listener.py`, is classified by `ci_predict --apply-inert`.

## Head

That commit merged main `92588d581fde4ce287af3db5e8bb61461dc28015` into the previous head `b8353012f530fe3d5f30606b60283d9b399c7712`. Both merges are clean, with no resolution, and neither changes a file of this PR's own diff. merges.body:
# HOTFIX R10-HOTFIX-CI-CRITPATH-2: a measured tolerance band on critical_path_minutes only

Main is red on `tests / ci-ratchet` from 05c0d6d5d (the #3040 merge) through 0cae227c3: `GREW critical_path_minutes: 34.467 (budget 34.267)` (run 41201096004). 0d33c9348 is green. `git diff --stat 0d33c9348 05c0d6d5d` is seven `dev/programme/delivery/*.md` rows, which cannot move CI work.

Since then main has drifted back to green, which is the flap itself, not a repair. Push runs 41244562778 (f3c9144b8) and 41254631180 (8fec54ee2) graded `ok critical_path_minutes: 34.233 (budget 34.267)`: 0.034 min of headroom, so one slow host draw turns main red again.

The metric is not a function of the tree. It is the median of the newest 8 completed ci.yml push runs' work, read live from the Actions API (`tests/ci_ratchet.py --gather-runs`, `PUSH_WINDOW = 8`). Whether the gate passes depends on which 8 host draws the window holds when the job runs: state (b), runner variance.

Measured with `ci_ratchet.run_minutes` over the runs and jobs that `--gather-runs` writes:
- 59 completed ci.yml push runs, 2026-10-30..31: median 33.767, sigma 1.638. The first-20 median is 33.884 and the last-20 is 33.867, so the work is flat. Every sliding 8-run median falls between 32.916 and 34.575, and the largest |median8 - window median| is 0.851.
- 86 runs of 2026-10-25, the recording window: median 32.55, p90 34.267. That p90 is the budget, reproduced exactly. Sliding 8-run medians run 31.709..33.850, and the largest |dev| is 1.300.
- The red window's record-only merges ran 35.150 (05c0d6d5d), 33.917 (3759d49a5), 33.967 (4c3645406), 34.917 (2fc0e95b2) and 33.500 (0cae227c3). The live 8-run median at fetch is 34.467, the logged value.

Cause: the 8-run median's sampling spread (up to 1.3 min) is larger than the headroom left between the work's center and the budget (34.267 - 33.767 = 0.5), so the gate flaps on host variance. Caveat, stated plainly: the center did rise from 32.55 to 33.77 since the 2026-10-25 recording. `tests / fast (3.14)` median work went from 29.47 to 31.83 and `arch-instrument` from 31.43 to 31.92. That is real growth across many merges, and it spent the headroom. The center is still under the budget, and the band does not raise the budget.

Fix (owner ruling 2026-10-31, under mandate 6329234399):
- `tests/ci_budgets.json` gains `critical_path_minutes_band: 1.3`, the largest measured |8-run median - window median| over every sliding window of 145 runs, unpadded.
- `compare()` reports `critical_path_minutes` as GREW only past budget + band. Every other row, the integer counters included, stays at zero tolerance. `--record` carries the band over, through `record_table()`, a pure function `main()` calls and the self-test drives.
- `tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py` types the band MAX0: absent means zero tolerance, so adding or widening the band is a raise and narrowing it is routine.
- `critical_path_minutes` stays at 34.267.

## Head

`f48fb142c4ac76f11907c2619d4abb021fc07bca` merges main `c3b7c96` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

9ef51b8215dd7216950f177386fb2f5a8f010a47

This head merges the authored code head 536da691c7c77d0275e72235bc0b95991ce7f722 and origin/main a7dd7f50d67e0c3819956b15ef95d77f4f6ebfc0, which is also the merge base. The branch-side change since fix review round 1 (head b02ffd170) is the `record_table()` refactor in tests/ci_ratchet.py and its pin. Fix review round 3 (verdict/3045 at ebc4a779f) blocked on `## Raise justification` alone. This round changes the body only; the head is unmoved.

## Mutation proof

- Before the code (test commit 765a0d19692ca5ed4b79b89192dcb1973bbac8b4), `python3 -I tests/ci_ratchet.py --self-test` failed 3 of its 44 checks: "the observed noise (34.467 on a 34.267 budget) passes inside the 1.3 band", "a median at budget + band exactly passes", and "a band row is a known, non-negative bound and not a graded metric". After the code (b8a027974): 44 checks, 0 failed. At this head, with the record-table pin: 45 checks, 0 failed.
- The checks that already pass on the unfixed code bound the fix from the other side: "a median one thousandth past budget + band is growth" (35.568), "the band never applies to a counter (54 -> 55 is growth with a band present)", and "no band row is zero tolerance".
- The `--record` carry-over (fix review round 1, surviving mutant M6). At b8a027974, deleting `**{k: budgets[k] for k in BAND_KEYS if k in budgets},` from `main()` left `ci-ratchet self-test: 44 checks, 0 failed`: no check pinned it. At this head that line is in `record_table()`, and the new check "--record carries the band over unchanged and re-records every derived metric" compares the whole table. Deleting the line now gives 45 checks, 1 failed.
- Every mutant, each applied to this head and restored, run with `env -u BASH_ENV python3 -I <script> --self-test` (summary lines):
  - Baseline: `ci-ratchet self-test: 45 checks, 0 failed`; `budget_raise_gate self-test: 240 checks, 0 failed`.
  - M1, band ignored in compare (`band = 0`): 45 checks, 2 failed.
  - M2, band applied to every row: 45 checks, 1 failed.
  - M3, gate row MAX instead of MAX0: 240 checks, 1 failed.
  - M3b, gate row deleted: 240 checks, 1 failed.
  - M4, band bounds check dropped: 45 checks, 1 failed.
  - M5, `>=` for `>`: 45 checks, 4 failed.
  - M6, record carry-over deleted: 45 checks, 1 failed. Killed.
  - M7, band key not excluded from the grading loop: 45 checks, 0 failed. This mutant is equivalent: the band key is never derived, so `compare()` prints `? not derived; not graded` for it and never grades it as growth.
- Deleting the `critical_path_minutes_band` MAX0 row from `budget_raise_gate.py` SCHEMA reds "ci: a critical-path band narrowed is routine" (240 checks, 1 failed). With the row: 240 checks, 0 failed.

## Null control

On the live window, `compare()` against the budget table without the band row reports `GREW critical_path_minutes: 34.467 (budget 34.267)`, which is main's red reproduced. With the band it reports `ok critical_path_minutes: 34.467 (budget 34.267, band 1.3)`. A copy of the window shifted by +1.31 min reads 35.777 and is GREW with the band. `script_runs_per_push` 55 on a budget of 54 is GREW with the band present.

## Figures

- `gh run view 41201096004 -R tvofi/heatpump_optimizer --log-failed`: GREW critical_path_minutes 34.467 (budget 34.267)
- `git diff --stat 0d33c9348 05c0d6d5d`: 7 files, all dev/programme/delivery/*.md
- `python3 -I tests/ci_ratchet.py --gather-runs FILE --window 60` (GITHUB_REPOSITORY=tvofi/heatpump_optimizer), then `ci_ratchet.critical_path_minutes` and `run_minutes` per run: the 59-run and 8-run figures above
- `gh api repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?event=push&branch=main&created=2026-10-25..2026-10-26` plus each run's jobs, through `run_minutes`: the 86-run figures above
- `gh run view 41254631180 --log --job 124702451375` and `gh run view 41244562778 --log --job 124672093606`: `ok critical_path_minutes: 34.233 (budget 34.267)`
- 2026-11-01: `GITHUB_REPOSITORY=tvofi/heatpump_optimizer python3 tests/ci_ratchet.py --gather-runs runs60.json --window 60` gave `push runs: 60 (60 CI)`. Over it:
  - `critjob.py` (sha1 9fa09d25fab72040a9fadbd979c24b6df5bcfb45) gives the per-run ending chain and the 8-run median range 32.9165..34.575.
  - `sim.py` (sha1 aed8cb5177ff3c48f7c276426c037fc35f51dc1d) gives the ci-ratchet cut simulation.
  - Both import `tests/ci_ratchet.py` and drive `run_minutes` unmodified. Both are published as RESUME.md on this body's ref.
  - The per-job and per-step medians come from the same file's `jobs[].steps[]` timestamps.
- `env -u BASH_ENV python3 -I tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py --self-test`: 240 checks, 0 failed
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED
- `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff a7dd7f50d67e0c3819956b15ef95d77f4f6ebfc0 9ef51b8215dd7216950f177386fb2f5a8f010a47`, three-dot (a7dd7f50d is the merge base of origin/main and this head), re-taken at this head: `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`. Round 1 and round 2 bodies stated dS +0.0012 IMPROVES (coord_footprint 2390 -> 2388); that figure is withdrawn.

## Architecture score

dS +0.0000 NULL, measured three-dot at head 9ef51b8215dd against the merge base a7dd7f50d (command in `## Figures`). The diff touches tests/ci_ratchet.py, tests/ci_budgets.json, tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py and a delivery row, none of which is coordinator code, so no architecture metric moves and this fix claims no improvement. The earlier +0.0012 IMPROVES (coord_footprint 2390 -> 2388) was main's own drift read two-dot, not this diff's, and is withdrawn. CI's arch-score job on this head concluded success, consistent with NULL.

## Raise justification

The raise is `tests/ci_budgets.json: critical_path_minutes_band: new at 1.3` (absent counts as zero). Mandate 6329234399, and the owner's ruling of 2026-10-31 in chat: "I suspect the ci-critical path minutes is runner variance, increase the variance band in that case under the mandate".
Payments tried: (1) a budget re-record, (2) a critical-path pay-down, (3) a wider grading window.

(1) Re-record critical_path_minutes by its documented rule, the p90 of a 40-run window: 34.267 -> 35.317. Rejected by the owner's ruling, which names the band and not a budget re-record. That ruling is the whole reason. On the graded statistic the band is the looser of the two: it passes an 8-run median up to 34.267 + 1.3 = 35.567, which is 0.25 min more than the 35.317 the re-record would pass. The round-3 body said the re-record "would hide the center growth". That reason inverted the comparison and is withdrawn.

(2) Pay down the critical-path work. The red is spread larger than the headroom (budget - center), not spread alone, so cutting work does help: it moves the center down and widens the headroom. At zero band the cut needed is center + max|dev| - budget:
- 33.767 + 1.300 - 34.267 = 0.800 min against the recording window's worst spread.
- 33.867 + 0.951 - 34.267 = 0.551 min on the live 60-run window gathered 2026-11-01 (below).

I looked for that cut on the 60-run window, using the production `ci_ratchet.run_minutes` walk (sha1-cited scripts below):
- The ending lane rotates. Shortening each job by 0.5 min and asking `run_minutes` whether the run's figure moves gives `fast (3.14)` in 20 runs, `closures` in 19, `arch-instrument` in 9, and the rest elsewhere. So a cut to one lane leaves the others setting the path. Their work spans 17.07..34.40 (fast), 0.83..34.42 (closures) and 17.62..33.45 (arch-instrument) min.
- Two jobs sit on nearly every path whichever lane wins: `prelude` (60 of 60, median 0.37 min, of which 18.5 s is the `fetch-depth: 0` checkout its merge-base derivation needs) and `tests / ci-ratchet` (47 of 60, median 1.15 min).
- In ci-ratchet, `Grade the ratchet` (median 28.5 s) is almost all `archscore_metrics()`. That measurement depends on none of the job's `needs`, yet it runs after two serial network steps: `Gather ... metrics` (26 s) and `Fetch the recent push runs' durations` (10 s).

The payment found: overlap that measurement with the fetches, or measure it off the needs chain. Simulated by shortening ci-ratchet's work in every run of the window and re-running `run_minutes`:
- cut 0 s (null control): median 33.867, 8-run medians 32.916..34.575. This reproduces the window as measured.
- cut 28 s: median 33.416, 8-run medians 32.683..34.108, headroom 0.851.
- cut 36 s: median 33.341, headroom 0.926.

So a cut of 0.45 to 0.53 min exists. It would have kept the live window green at zero band, but it is short of the 0.800 the recording window's worst spread needs.

Not taken in this hotfix, for three reasons:
- the owner ruled the band;
- the change is to the gate workflow `.github/workflows/tests.yml` plus a precompute path in `tests/ci_ratchet.py`, which forces a FULL gate and new self-tests;
- its effect cannot be measured until 8 main push runs carry it.

It does not substitute for the band; it complements it. The band covers the spread, and the cut covers the center the round-3 body recorded as grown (`fast (3.14)` 29.47 -> 31.83). It goes to the orchestrator as a proposal for triage (it is not filed as an issue).

(3) Grade on a wider window (median of 40). That cuts the noise, but it changes how the instrument grades and was not the ruled fix. It goes to the orchestrator as a proposal for triage.

No payment found clears the recording window's measured spread at zero band, and the owner ruled the band. The raise is justified with a null score movement, not an improvement.
Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL

## Red checks

`tests / ci-ratchet` on main pushes 05c0d6d5d..0cae227c3: GREW critical_path_minutes 34.467 (budget 34.267). It is green again on later pushes at 34.233, inside 0.034 of the budget: the same flap, not a repair. Root cause (defect-root-cause.md, red-check trigger): the graded statistic is an 8-sample median of live runner timings, and its noise exceeded the headroom. No cheaper detector exists. The metric reads only main's push-run history at the moment the job runs. A pull request's own run, prepr.sh and ci_predict.py cannot see it, because none of their inputs come from the tree. The countermeasure is this band, sized from measured spread and typed as a raise when widened.

`budget-raise-gate / budget-raise-gate`: red by design until a decisive approval at this head. The diff adds `tests/ci_budgets.json: critical_path_minutes_band` at 1.3. The base's schema reads it as a pinned value, and the head's schema types it MAX0, so either way it is a raise. This is the deliberate, mandated raise justified under `## Raise justification` (mandate 6329234399, the owner's ruling of 2026-10-31), not a defect, so the root-cause rule owes nothing: no cheaper detector applies to a gate that exists to hold a raise for approval.

## Forward-carry

- The fix review's instrument finding (rounds 1 and 2): budget_raise_gate checks only the shape of the `Architecture score:` line, never its value against the arch-score job; that is how an unearned improvement figure passed the gate twice. Destination: the group's brief in dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json, landed on `handoff/audit-r10-roster` at 697a0154f74b8873e681479a8e742eade69d06bf (group R10-FLY-MANDATE-REVOKE-GUARD, carry beginning "From the #3045 round-1 fix review"). Carry: R10-FLY-MANDATE-REVOKE-GUARD (the budget_raise_gate dS value check)
- The fix review's MAX0 finding: budget_raise_gate calls a removed band a raise. Carry: dismissed: a fail-closed false positive that opens no gate weakness, and only the owner can decide that removal should be routine
- The fix review's wording finding: the "86 runs of 2026-10-25" label spans 2026-10-25T00:42Z..2026-10-26T20:55Z. Carry: dismissed: only the label is loose, and every figure re-derives exactly
- The round-2 review evidence line recording that classify exited 1 at this head states the known stale-approval red the body already answers, not a defect. Carry: dismissed: a status record of the by-design budget-raise-gate red, answered under Red checks (item da8d5ab4)

## Friction

none

comments.body:
Fix review: blocked b02ffd170d5049d8869689cbc889a5cf46097a1e metric-gamed: archscore: the body's dS +0.0012 IMPROVES is not this diff's, which scores dS +0.0000 NULL three-dot and in CI

bus-nonce: 83ea6356a16366c48fbb3ccd206a96e0

Round 1 of this fix review. Measured head: b02ffd170d5049d8869689cbc889a5cf46097a1e. At the post time it is still the PR head (`git fetch origin fix/r10-hotfix-ci-critpath-2` resolves to it), and origin/main is 7539d1675, the merge base.

## Block

The body states `Architecture score: dS +0.0012 IMPROVES (coord_footprint 2390 -> 2388)` three times: in `## Figures`, in `## Architecture score`, and as the `Architecture score:` line of `## Raise justification`. The owner's mandated approval quotes the same figure. The diff touches only tests/ci_ratchet.py, tests/ci_budgets.json, tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py and a delivery row. None of those is coordinator code, so the diff cannot move coord_footprint.

- `score.py --diff origin/main HEAD` at this head, where origin/main is the merge base 7539d1675, prints `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL` (ev/archscore-diff.txt).
- `score.py --diff 0cae227c3 b8a027974` scores the authored code head against its own merge base and also prints `dS +0.0000 NULL` (ev/archscore-codehead.txt).
- CI's own arch-score job 124591643014 on this head prints `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL` and `PASS: dS +0.0000 NULL, no gate metric rose` (ev/ci-arch-score-log.txt).

So the +0.0012 movement survives with the mechanism removed. It is main's own drift, read two-dot against an origin/main that was not the branch's base, which CLAUDE.md rule 3 forbids for any branch-vs-main comparison. This is a misreport, not gaming of the instrument. The honest value, NULL, still meets rule 2's requirement that the score not read worse. But the brief makes an honest Raise justification a condition, and fix-review step 14 makes every figure the body quotes owed to the change. The repair is a body-only edit and does not move the head: replace the three occurrences with `dS +0.0000 NULL` measured three-dot, and drop the coord_footprint clause. All other checks below pass at this head, so a re-verdict should only need to re-read the body and the post-edit `budget-raise-gate` and `pr-contract` runs.

## Findings

- Surviving mutant M6: deleting the `--record` carry-over line `**{k: budgets[k] for k in BAND_KEYS if k in budgets},` in tests/ci_ratchet.py main() leaves `ci-ratchet self-test: 44 checks, 0 failed`. The body states "`--record` carries the band over" as part of the fix, and no check pins it. If the line is lost, the outcome fails closed: a re-record drops the band, and budget_raise_gate reads the removal as a raise (ev/gate-band-removal.txt). A one-check self-test pin on the record table is still owed. The fixer adds the pin with the body repair. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-CI-CRITPATH-2
- budget_raise_gate types the band MAX0, but MAX0 calls `critical_path_minutes_band` removed (1.3 -> absent) a raise, "a removed cap is no cap". Narrowing to 0 is routine, and adding it at 0 is routine. So removing the band, which tightens the gate to zero tolerance, would wrongly need owner approval. The PR's own docstring says "absent is a band of zero". This false positive fails closed, so it is not blocking. Carry: dismissed: a fail-closed false positive that opens no gate weakness, and only the owner can decide that removal should be routine
- Instrument finding: budget_raise_gate checks only the shape of the `Architecture score: dS <n> <verdict>` line (regex at tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py:145). It never checks the value against the arch-score job, which is how an unearned IMPROVES got through the gate and into the owner's approval. The orchestrator propagates it to the budget-raise-gate brief by finding-propagation.md. Carry: R10-HOTFIX-CI-CRITPATH-2
- Wording: "86 runs of 2026-10-25" comes from the query `created=2026-10-25..2026-10-26`, whose runs span 2026-10-25T00:42Z..2026-10-26T20:55Z. The figures reproduce exactly, so only the label is loose. Carry: dismissed: only the label is loose, and every figure re-derives exactly

## Evidence

- Band measured, not padded. I fetched the 86 ci.yml push runs with the body's own query and scored them with `ci_ratchet.run_minutes` (ev/band.py, ev/band-1025.txt): `RESULT n=86 median=32.550 p90=34.267 sliding8 min=31.709 max=33.850 max|dev|=1.300`. That is the head's 1.3, unpadded, and the p90 equals the 34.267 budget exactly.
- I fetched the 59-run set again with `ci_ratchet.py --gather-runs ... --window 90` (ev/band-59-search.txt). The set ending at 0cae227c3 reproduces the body: median 33.767, sliding8 32.916..34.575, max|dev| 0.851, first20 33.883, last20 33.867. The body's sigma 1.638 is the population SD; the sample SD is 1.652. On the newest 59 runs at review time, max|dev| is 0.875..0.925, still under 1.3.

Judged on the body's own figures, two of its three payment judgements do not hold:

- **Payment (1) is rejected on a false comparison.** The body rejects the re-record of critical_path_minutes 34.267 -> 35.317 because it "would hide the 1.2-min center growth inside the cap". The band it chose instead lets the graded 8-run median pass up to 34.267 + 1.3 = **35.567**. That is 0.25 min looser than the 35.317 it rejected, on the same statistic.
  - Under the band, the center stays flap-free up to 34.267, the budget itself. Under the re-record with no band, it stays flap-free only up to 35.317 - 1.3 = 34.017.
  - Viewed either way, the rejected payment is the tighter instrument, so "hides growth" cannot be the reason to prefer the band.
  - The owner's ruling ("increase the variance band") is a sufficient reason on its own. The body may rest on it, but it may not add a technical reason that inverts the comparison.
- **Payment (2) is dismissed by mistaking spread for headroom.** The body says "no reduction makes an 8-sample median ... stay within 0.5 min of its center, so that payment cannot fix a variance red". The 0.5 is headroom (budget - center = 34.267 - 33.767), not a property of the spread. Reducing the work moves the center down and widens the headroom. The body's own `Cause` paragraph says the red is "spread larger than the headroom", not spread alone.
  - On the body's figures, a critical-path reduction of 33.767 + 1.300 - 34.267 = **0.800 min** fits the worst measured |dev| under a zero band.

So this block does not claim a payment exists. It blocks on the justification's reasoning, which the mandated approval rests on.

Fix review: merge ae927c850c686e1680643fab442a58fe11e66329

bus-nonce: 8b45542d53747a5b82add12aa2c4772e

Round 1, a triage RECORD PR (one ruling file plus its delivery row; no production code, no policy file). Measured at head ae927c850c686e1680643fab442a58fe11e66329, merge base b5df066e7, origin/main 6421fe135.

## Findings

- The ruling says the class copies are "harmless to the train" under (a) alone, but they are not harmless to the round count: bus.sh blocked_rounds counts commits whose subject starts "verdict: #<pr> Fix review: blocked", so a same-tree copy of a blocked verdict counts as a second round. verdict/3062 holds two commits for one blocked round (68c79cae3, 88d613281, 7 s apart, one tree) and would count 2 toward the three-round rule. Carry (b) removes new copies; neither carry nor the ruling addresses existing copies or counts one round per tree. Carry: R10-FLY-RELAY-REVIEW-FF
- R10-FLY-TRAIN-DEFAULTS is at stage "done" (resume.pr 3010, merged), with its five earlier carries routed to other groups, so carry (a) lands on a group whose stage no fixer dispatch reads. roster_edit.py append-carry does not refuse a done group and does not reopen it. The ruling's "no PR in flight" holds, but the group needs a set-stage back to an open stage when the carry is appended or (a) is never dispatched. Carry: R10-FLY-TRAIN-DEFAULTS
- Minor, not blocking: the ruling says #3065's diff "does not touch confirm or append_commit". It does change one line of append_commit (the git push line, http.postBuffer). It leaves confirm alone, so (b) has no textual conflict; the hold on #3065 stays a valid ordering but its stated reason is slightly off. Carry: dismissed: the carry text itself edits confirm only, and the hold costs nothing.

## Evidence

- Class figures, re-derived from git (ev/figures.txt, ev/scan.py, ev/scan2.py), counted 2026-11-01 about 10:25Z: 519 verdict refs, 169 same-tree parent/child pairs on 78 refs, 53 pairs at most 60 s apart, 51 refs whose tip is a same-tree copy, 12 pairs from 2026-10-30. The ruling's 515, 170, 79, 54, 53, 13 are each 1 or 2 higher; none reproduce exactly. The difference is explained: verdict/3068 was rewound to 3c0b62eaa after the ruling was written (ls-remote now shows 3c0b62eaa), which removes one pair, one ref, one at-most-60-s pair and one tip copy, and #3052 has since taken a new round (tip 7420ddfb8, a different tree), which removes the other tip copy; four refs are new. Both sets agree on the order of magnitude and on the 4-commit verdict/3052.
- Mechanism (a): merge_train.py posted_verdict (line 2381) accepts a comment only if the body contains "bus: verdict/<n> at <tip>," for the exact tip, so a later same-tree copy fails today. Real heads: 3c0b62eaa and 948d1ee60 both have tree 03483ecd586e; 3c0b62eaa is the sole parent of 948d1ee60 (is-ancestor true); the two commit objects differ only in the parent line and the author/committer date (git cat-file diff). The rule "ancestor and equal tree" accepts them. It still refuses a different tree, a non-ancestor commit, and by construction a tip with a changed message or signature is not distinguished: bus.sh post_verdict keys on "<pr> <tree>" (posted-signed), so message and signature need not match; the signature is over the tree, so an equal-tree descendant carries the same signed verdict. Verdict-at-head is unaffected: the comment's first line still names the PR head, and the returned head and comment id are unchanged under the carry. 948d1ee60 is no longer on a ref; I fetched it by sha.
- Mechanism (b): bus.sh confirm (line 536 at origin/main) pre-checks posted-signed, then append_commit, then post_verdict; post_verdict writes posted-signed before the post (lines 354-366), after append_commit. There is no mkdir lock, flock or tip-tree check in confirm. The race window exists as the ruling says.
- Interim: no ruleset covers verdict/* (main-protect and main-protect-checks both include only ~DEFAULT_BRANCH, read from gh api). The rewind has already been done: verdict/3068 is 3c0b62eaa, a merge verdict. blocked_rounds counts by commit subject, so the rewind changes no count for 3068 (merge verdict, one commit). I did not check relay-ledger readers of verdict history beyond review_strength.py, which reads refs and tags and counts by confirmed id.
- Waiver: merge_train.py has no waiver path; a hand merge leaves no check record. The rewind is a cheaper, recorded fix. merges.subject: Merge pull request #3086 from tvofi/fix/r10-hotfix-uutils-sleep
merges.title: R10-HOTFIX-UUTILS-SLEEP: hotfix uutils sleep
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
Hotfix, main red: `governance / instrument-self-tests` fails `pr_args self-test: 158 checks, 2 failed` when `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` lands on ubuntu-26.04 (red at 6421fe135, job 124813746788; green at 92588d581, job 124783717352 on 24.04). There `/bin/sleep` is the uutils multicall binary, which refuses a renamed argv[0] ("Security violation: Requested utility `unrelated-sleep` does not match executable name"). `pr_args.sh`'s reap fixture started its bystander as `ln -s /bin/sleep "$REAP_DIR/unrelated-sleep"`, so the bystander died at once and both null controls that require it alive failed.

The fix makes the bystander a two-line wrapper, `exec sleep "$1"`: the exec keeps `$UNREL` the sleeper's own pid, and the sleep is invoked under its own name on either coreutils. Alternatives: pinning the workflow to `ubuntu-24.04` (rejected by the brief: it hides the class); `exec -a` (bash-only and still a renamed argv[0], which uutils refuses); dropping the bystander's distinct name (it is a path name only; the comm is `sleep` either way, so nothing keys on it).

`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_uutils_sleep.sh` lands the reproducer (fixer step 18): it binds an argv[0]-checking `sleep` over `/usr/bin/sleep` in a private mount namespace and runs the self-test in a detached worktree at `<rev>`, with a `gnu` null control and a `symlink` mutant. Classified inert for `tests/harness_headers.py` by `tools/pr/ci_predict.py --apply-inert` (the `tests/closures.json` line).

Carry 1 (the roster's brief for this group) is discharged as written, with one departure: the failing test is not a fake `sleep` earlier on PATH, because the fixture named `/bin/sleep` by absolute path, so a PATH entry never reaches the line that broke. The harness binds the emulation over `/usr/bin/sleep` in a private mount namespace instead; PATH lookups of `sleep` (the fixed wrapper's, and every other `sleep` in the self-test) reach it too. The class grep, the mutation proof and the null control the carry names are below.

## Head

`f4f7daf6ce71185391f69f09d4bd26e4932fe233` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3086.md`. The authored code head is `783e189f312a1eb574882123732cfdd8f5c15e91`.

## Mutation proof

The fix's production line restored to the symlink form, at the head, under the uutils emulation:

`bash dev/audit/harnesses/r10_uutils_sleep.sh 783e189f3 emu symlink` printed

    FAIL open_pr: the null control -- an unrelated sleeper survives
    FAIL null control: a normal successful update_pr leaves nothing behind and stops nothing it did not start
    pr_args self-test: 158 checks, 2 failed

the same two arms, and the same tally, that job 124813746788 printed.

## Null control

- The unmodified tree under the emulation reproduces CI's red: `bash dev/audit/harnesses/r10_uutils_sleep.sh 6421fe135 emu` printed the two FAIL lines above and `pr_args self-test: 158 checks, 2 failed`.
- The fixed tree on the host's GNU sleep stays green: `bash dev/audit/harnesses/r10_uutils_sleep.sh 783e189f3 gnu` printed `pr_args self-test: 158 checks, 0 failed`.
- The fixed fixture still kills nothing it did not start: the two bystander arms (`open_pr: the null control -- an unrelated sleeper survives` and `null control: a normal successful update_pr ... stops nothing it did not start`) pass under the emulation, and `$UNREL` is the sleeper itself: under the emulation `ps -o pid=,args= -p $UNREL` on a wrapper started the fixture's way printed the real sleep binary's argv at that pid, not `sh`.
- The emulation itself refuses as uutils does: invoked through a link named `unrelated-sleep` it printed "Security violation: Requested utility `unrelated-sleep` does not match executable name `sleep`" and exited 1, and as `/bin/sleep` it exited 0.

## Figures

- `bash dev/audit/harnesses/r10_uutils_sleep.sh 6421fe135 emu`: `pr_args self-test: 158 checks, 2 failed` (baseline under uutils emulation).
- `bash dev/audit/harnesses/r10_uutils_sleep.sh 783e189f3 emu`: `pr_args self-test: 158 checks, 0 failed` (head under uutils emulation).
- `bash dev/audit/harnesses/r10_uutils_sleep.sh 783e189f3 emu symlink`: `pr_args self-test: 158 checks, 2 failed` (mutant).
- `bash dev/audit/harnesses/r10_uutils_sleep.sh 783e189f3 gnu`: `pr_args self-test: 158 checks, 0 failed` (null control, host GNU coreutils 9.4).
- Gate scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"` printed `MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run`; `python3 tests/structure.py` printed `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- Class sweep (fixer step 8), rule: `git grep -nE '\bln +-[a-zA-Z]*s' -- ':!*.md' ':!*.mdc'` and `git grep -nE 'os\.symlink\(|symlink_to\(|hardlink_to\(|os\.link\(' -- '*.py' '*.mjs' '*.js'` and `git grep -nE 'exec -a' -- '*.sh' '*.py'`, at the merge base. Every seam returned, against its disposition:
  - `tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh` bystander `ln -s /bin/sleep .../unrelated-sleep`: closed in this diff.
  - `tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh` `nops` PATH (`ln -s "$k" "$t/nops/${k##*/}"`): keeps each basename, so a multicall binary dispatches correctly; not the class.
  - `tools/audit/seat/train.sh` `ln -s "$(command -v python3)" .../venv-ci/bin/python3` (two sites): same basename, and CPython does not dispatch on argv[0]; not the class.
  - `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py` and `tools/audit/seat/offline_spy.py` (`python3`/`python` to `sys.executable`), `tests/entities.py` (`python` to `sys.executable`): CPython is not multicall; not the class.
  - `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_fly_nightly_hb.py` `py-spy` link: same basename; not the class.
  - `tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh` (a venv directory), `tools/pr/prepr.sh` (markdown files, the `tests` directory), `tools/pr/gh_comment.py` (markdown files), `tests/arch_score.py` (a text file), `tests/gate_lock.py` (`os.link` of lock files): links to data, not executables; not the class.
  - `exec -a`: no site.

## Red checks

- `governance / instrument-self-tests` (on main at 6421fe135, job 124813746788): the cause is the runner-image change, `ubuntu-latest` moving to ubuntu-26.04 whose `/bin/sleep` is uutils' multicall binary refusing a renamed argv[0]. Cheaper detector: none exists; a seat's macOS or Ubuntu 24.04 host runs GNU coreutils, and macOS cannot run uutils' check at all, so no earlier check could have seen it. `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_uutils_sleep.sh` now reproduces it on any Linux seat.

plan: the closure stamp is the round's major, vN.0.0 (R10-FLY-CLOSURE-MAJOR)

Fly-in split from the R10-FLOW-TOOLKIT-MODEL carry "Round closure is v10.0.0".
`tools/plan/replan.py` modelled the programme-closing stamp as a minor bump
(`bump(version, patch, minor=True)`, kind `minor`), so `plan.json` and the plan
page printed v7.2.0 where decision 0016 (tvofi, 2026-10-29, restated 2026-10-31)
owes round 10's major, v10.0.0 -- the version `tools/release/stamp.py
--round-close 10` assigns. Landing this discharges that carry item; its roster
disposition is the roster seat's op.

Carry 1: closed in this diff -- the round-close stamp is vN.0.0, N the roster's round, as
`stamp.py --round-close N` assigns it; `check_plan` validates it and `plan_page` renders it.

The fix gives the version rule one owner. `replan.closure_version` calls
`stamp.next_version(version, None, N, N)`, the function `--round-close N` runs,
so the plan states exactly what the stamp will assign and refuses where the
stamp would (a round not above the current major). N is
`roster_lib.roster_round` of the roster's path, the reader `stamp.py`'s
`roster_round_at` uses; `main` derives it at the edge and `build_plan` takes it
as the required keyword `round_n`, so the model stays pure and no caller can
omit it. A roster naming no round refuses (exit 2), never defaults -- the same
stance `next_version` takes on an unreadable roster. The plan records
`generated.round`; the closure stamp's kind is `round-close` (`ROUND_CLOSE`);
`check_plan` refuses a closure stamp that is not the single last stamp, a
version that disagrees with `closure_version(generated.version,
generated.round)`, a plan recording no round, and any stamp kind other than
`patch` and `round-close`. Interim stamps stay patch bumps (`bump` lost only its
minor arm). `plan_page.py` renders the row unchanged in shape; its caption and
cadence note now name the round-close major, and its self-test pins the
rendered `v9.0.0` / `round-close` row.

Alternatives: hard-coding the major from the roster round inside replan (a
second copy of decision 0016's rule, which `stamp.py` already owns and refuses
on), and reading the round from `VERSION` (wrong source -- the major is the round
being closed, not the current one). Both lost to delegating to `next_version`.

## Head

`fe4af42579764bb8010e875ac5adb56ac542b3a0` merges the authored code head `8d176a6f714c84ffb6f5e29e8d0b6c4a73a3c1aa` and then merges origin/main `b5df066e7` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`8d176a6f714c84ffb6f5e29e8d0b6c4a73a3c1aa`, measured against merge base
`8fec54ee2afb5e37687f34bc5fd3aa7280f64e1f` (origin/main at 2026-11-01T04:25Z
is `61b0076f`, merge-tree clean). The round-1 review head was `815039200`
(the delivery row plus a merge of main over `6b38d24`); this head adds one
commit to `tools/plan/replan.py`'s self-test only. The plan files
(`tools/plan`, `plan_page.py`, `state_docs.py`, `stamp.py`, `roster_lib.py`)
are byte-identical at the two bases, so the before/after replan figures below,
taken against `2b6bef745`, describe this base too.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant is a copy of `tools/plan/replan.py` with one production line
replaced, run with `--self-test` (`REPLAN_MUTATION_CHILD=1`); every one also
sits in the self-test's own mutation table, which reports each `rc=1`.

Round 1 review (blocked at `815039200`, mutation-vacuous): the three survivors
it named, each now killed by a row planting exactly that input:
- P3 `round-close-last`: ` or plan["stamps"][-1] is not closes[0]:` -> `:`:
  rc=1; FAIL --check refuses a round-close stamp that is not the last stamp
  (planted: a correct round-close stamp followed by another stamp).
- P4 `round-close-stray-kind`: `("patch", ROUND_CLOSE)` -> `("patch", "minor",
  ROUND_CLOSE)`: rc=1; FAIL --check refuses a minor stamp beside a correct round
  close (planted: an extra `minor` stamp before a correct closure; the row also
  requires no `round close` refusal, so only the stray-kind arm can answer it).
- P5 `round-n-required`: `*, round_n: int)` -> `*, round_n: int = 10)`: rc=1;
  FAIL build_plan without round_n refuses (a call omitting `round_n` must raise
  TypeError naming it).

Null control for these rows: the same three mutants applied to
`815039200:tools/plan/replan.py` each print `self-test: 0 failed`, rc=0 -- the
reviewer's result, reproduced; at this head each is rc=1.

Unchanged from round 1, still killed:
- `round-close-version` (`"version": closing` -> `bump(version, patch)`): FAIL
  the clean plan passes --check; FAIL the closure stamp is the round-close major
  of the plan's round; FAIL the closure major follows the round, not a constant;
  and three --check passes rows.
- `round-close-check` (`elif closes[0]["version"] != want:` -> `elif False:`):
  FAIL --check refuses a round-close closure stamp v1.1.0 / v3.0.0 in round 2.
- `round-from-roster` (`round_n = roster_lib.roster_round(src)` -> `99`): FAIL a
  roster naming no round refuses, never defaults (exit 2).

Failing test first (round 1): at the baseline production code with the new arms
added, the self-test printed FAIL the closure stamp is the round-close major of
the plan's round (`kind 'minor'`, `v1.1.0`) and FAIL a roster naming no round
refuses, never defaults (exit 2).

The unmutated copy's self-test exits 0 (the table's own null control, printed
`null control: unmutated copy rc=0`). A real replan at the merge base and at
the head, both pinned to roster commit
`e71a089ea915a04960643dac50519aefdf3befa3` and `--start 2026-10-31T12:00:00Z`,
differ only in the closure stamp: with `stamps[-1]`, `summary.closure_stamp`,

and `waves[].stamp`, `diff` of the two `jq -S` renderings exits 0 (had any
group, wave, batch, patch stamp, CI price or closure time moved, it would print
the line). Both interim patch stamps are byte-identical (v7.1.1, v7.1.2).

Before (merge base): `v7.1.1 patch 5 | v7.1.2 patch 5 | v7.2.0 minor 4`.
After (head): `v7.1.1 patch 5 | v7.1.2 patch 5 | v10.0.0 round-close 4`;
`summary.closure_stamp` `v10.0.0`, `generated.round` 10, `--check` prints

## Figures

- self-test: `python3 -I tools/plan/replan.py --self-test` -> `self-test: 0 failed`, every row of the mutation table `rc=1`.
- plan page: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/plan_page.py --self-test` -> 0 failed.

- real replan: `python3 -I tools/plan/replan.py --roster-ref e71a089ea915a04960643dac50519aefdf3befa3 --start 2026-10-31T12:00:00Z --out plan.json` -> stamps as in `## Null control`.
- seam enumeration (rule: every tools/ or tests/ line modelling a closure as minor): `git grep -n -i -e 'minor=True' -e '"minor"' -e 'minor stamp' -e 'the minor at' -e 'closure_stamp' -- tools tests`, excluding `tools/release/stamp.py`. Base: 14 lines; head: 7. Dispositions at head: `tests/finite_boundary.py` (a store key, unrelated), `tools/audit/carry_audit.py` x2 (a word list, unrelated), `tools/audit/seat/r10_stamp_round_mutants.py` (stamp.py's legitimate interim minor bump), `replan.py` `closure_stamp` (now the round-close version), and two self-test lines (the planted refusal and its assertion). Closed in this diff: `bump(minor=True)`, kind `minor`, the `check_plan` minor arm, and the three plan-page texts.
- structure: `python3 tests/structure.py` -> STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED.

Design: `dev/programme/designs/R10-USER-DOCS-FINAL.md` on design/R10-USER-DOCS-FINAL 576654cce6e4fc0c643a2184e65d030a7fe0decf, approved by design-verdict/R10-USER-DOCS-FINAL 5b54eb18c1dc93418b881ce9f3e256553ccd8fd9. Brief and carries read at handoff/audit-r10-roster 315cd0441dd89059a1714c4f2e20ad9055063b3b. Carry 1 (the re-scope, tvofi 2026-10-31, "split USER-DOCS-FINAL"): answered by this diff. Brief items (1)-(6) are done against origin/main at the fork, not the true merge base: the enumeration (`--surfaces`), the pages, the correctness pass (claim table below), the removals (no feature the pages describe is absent from the tree: every `--surfaces` row homed, and the history text that described older forms is rewritten), and both arms, coverage with its reasoned exemption list and stateless, each red on its fixture and green on its null control. The check at the true merge base is R10-USER-DOCS-VERIFY's, which reuses these arms. Contract step 9: `git log --first-parent 14ed13551..origin/main` at the fork lists only #3037 (tools/audit/seat, tools/pr), so no in-flight group from the note's list landed since the note's base and there was no merged diff to re-read.

What it adds, all in `tests/doc_claims.py`:
- `surface_sources()` / `surface_rows()`: every user-facing surface in eleven classes, each from the tree (`PLATFORM_LIST` through `entity_census`, `services.yaml`, `config.step` in `translations/en.json` with the defaults each config-flow step renders, `_OPTION_PAGES`, `_OPTION_FIELDS`, `blueprints/automation/*.yaml`, `notifier.py` `EVENT_*`, the card's `tab("<id>"` calls plus the compact card, the card's `DEFAULTS` and `config.<key>` reads, `issues` in `strings.json`), and its home: the page, section and shape of the design's page map. `home-found` is the home shape present and, for `option`, `setup_field` and `card_option`, its Default cell agreeing with the shipped default (`default_agrees`); an option's row must sit under its own page's heading, a setup field's under a heading naming its screen.
- `python3 tests/doc_claims.py --surfaces` (one sorted tab-separated line per surface, `class id label home-page home-found default`; exit 1 while a non-exempt surface has no home) and `--surfaces --against FILE` (the keyed `LANDED` / `REMOVED` / `CHANGED` delta, `surface_delta`; exit 1 while a section is non-empty). `check_surface_coverage` calls the same `surface_rows()`, so the CLI and the gate cannot differ. `SURFACE_EXEMPT` holds one entry, the blank `_OPTION_FIELDS` key on `building_preset` (carry udf-blank-option-key), keyed `building_preset[questionnaire]`.
- `check_stateless`: the history lexicon over the seven pages after fences, code spans, HTML comments, tags and link targets are blanked; every phrase word-bounded (carry udf-used-to-boundary); a purpose-sense `used to` (sentence or table-cell start, after `,`, `is`, `are`, `only`, `also`) passes. Round 2 widened `_HISTORY` (see Round 2 below); `STATELESS_EXEMPT` holds five README literals, each matching exactly once.
- The marker census tag: `_in_comment` sets `scope` (`user` inside `<!-- -->`, else `wiring`); `marker_census` reads `marker_docs()`, the wiring documents and the user pages in one dict keyed by path (README.md read once); `doc_wiring_findings`' due note and the default `--markers` skip user rows; `--markers --user` prints `N user-doc marker(s), M due`, exit 1 while N > 0; `marker_placement_findings` refuses a bare marker on a user-only page, a wrapped one on `docs/architecture.md` or `dev/README.md`, and a user marker naming no roster group. Verdict note udf-user-marker-path-mask: path check (a) and `_groups` now count only wiring markers (`_wiring`), so a user marker excuses no missing path.
- `entity_census` read `getattr(e, "entity_registry_enabled_default", True)`; the stub has no such property, so the eleven entities declaring only `_attr_entity_registry_enabled_default = False` read as enabled (stub vacuity, fixer.md step 13). It now reads that attribute second, the rule `tests/entities.py` `registry_default` already uses. Measured: 9 disabled before, 20 after, which is the README's "Twenty entities".

The pages: every surface now has its home, and the change history is gone from all seven (round 1 by the round-1 lexicon; round 2 by the widened one, below). Main rewrites: `docs/configuration.md` `## Initial setup` headings carry the screen titles the user sees, with new sections for the Quick setup screen, the pre-fill screen, the review screen and Reauthenticate Tibber, and rows for every field; the options pages tabulate the fields they previously deferred to setup ("See setup step 1") under their own headings; README `## Entities` gains a switch, climate and datetime table, `## Troubleshooting` a `### Repair notices` list of all 26 repair titles; `docs/how-it-works.md` `### The house heat loss coefficient` states the learner's inputs, what an estimated power reading does to it, and the reset (brief item: the heat-loss learner's inputs, from R10-HOTFIX-LEARNER-INPUTS' merged diff 0cae227c3 and its harness, whose basis row reads `power = the pump's own estimate  metered`). User-doc markers, comment-wrapped, own line above the heading: R10-COP-GATE and R10-COP-PARTLOAD (`### COP, and the tracking-error gate`), R10-CEILING-PROBE (`### Active system identification`), R10-UX-HEALTH (`## The health page`), R10-ARCH-SHAPES-CLASSIFIER (`### Why a step is idle`).

Departure from the note (round 1), now answered: no R10-WOOD-NOTIFY marker on the Wood Cheaper Than Heat Pump row, because main's roster (`dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json`) holds no R10-WOOD-NOTIFY entry and the marker would be red under `marker_placement_findings` ("names no group in the roster"). R10-WOOD-NOTIFY (#3016) has since merged at a7dd7f50d67e0c3819956b15ef95d77f4f6ebfc0, and round 2 merges it and documents its window attributes in that row instead (Round 2 below). Still no marker: main's roster still has no R10-WOOD-NOTIFY entry.

The strings.json history wording (design carry udf-strings-history) stays out of this diff: the stateless item covers the docs only, and the rewrite is already on R10-UX-HEALTH's carries.

## Round 2 (answering the fix review at e5cbb1a9aa2099efd7d9237ef1069d2f81996047, hpo-approver 18:14Z, class-open)

The block: the stateless lexicon passed four change-history passages. Answered in three commits on 191ed6b74:

- 09af996ba6a32c9579adbe0b44f90767335e8638 (failing test first): `_HISTORY` gains `earlier|older versions/releases`, `versions/releases older|newer than`, `upgraded from`, `the upgrade`, `breaking change`, `is|are now ... rather than` (the `is/are` is required, so "snaps the window back to now rather than show a past" stays a statement; the gap admits a decimal point and a wrapped line, never a sentence end), and a bare three-part version number `(?<![\w.])\d+\.\d+\.\d+\b`. Multi-word terms take `\s+`, so a wrapped line does not hide one. One red fixture per new term (eight), each asserting exactly one finding with the exemptions out of play (`exempt=()`); one null control of the new terms' current-behaviour neighbours: "back to now rather than", "the older hourly clock", "an upgrade seems", a calendar release "2026.11", a decimal "0.55", a version in a code span. The probe calls now pass `exempt=()`, because a non-empty `STATELESS_EXEMPT` would otherwise report its own five mismatches on every probe and make each red fixture red for the wrong reason. `STATELESS_EXEMPT`, five entries keyed (page, fragment), each matching once: `Home Assistant: 2025.2.0+` (badge), `Home Assistant 2025.2.0 or newer` (requirements), `Home Assistant 2025.2.0 and Python` (installation), `at version 2.2.0` and `Versions 2.3.0 onward` (the fork's attribution, as NOTICE gives it). Key (fixer.md step 14): an entry silences only a hit that starts inside its own fragment's one span, so a history phrase anywhere else on README.md, or a second version number in the same sentence outside the fragment, is still a finding.
- 69d4d3bd4c422e1ceb72d6d6d22a9f31d0759afb (the pages, class census): the four listed passages and every other hit, rewritten as current behaviour.
  - `docs/how-it-works.md` `### Weather anticipation is emergent, not a bonus`, "Earlier versions added explicit anticipation terms ...": now "The objective carries no separate anticipation term on top of this ..."; the 4–6% figure, a measurement of a change, is dropped.

A stored derate that loads with a bucket outside 0.55–1.0 keeps that bucket, clamped into the range" (`DefrostDerate.from_dict` clamps each loaded factor to `[DERATE_MIN, DERATE_MAX]` = [0.55, 1.0]).

(for installs upgraded from before the ids moved, and for integration versions older than 2.6.1)": now "or in the other suffix order, `space_heating_plan` / `dhw_heating_plan`". I first wrote that the first form leads; `resolveEntity` takes the first sorted id ending in either suffix (`suffixes.some`), so the order decides nothing, and the sentence is not in the diff.
  - Beyond the four, same rule: README `## Installation` "and that was a breaking change", now "are the minimum"; `docs/dashboard-card.md` `### If an upgrade seems to change nothing` "from an earlier version", dropped (the sentence states the stale `/local/` copy without it); `docs/dashboard-card.md` `### Entity discovery` "An install upgraded from before the ids moved ...", now "Home Assistant keeps an entity's registry id once it is assigned, so an entry registered with the other suffix order ... keeps those ids".

## Mutation proof

Each production line in `tests/doc_claims.py` mutated in place, `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components python3 tests/doc_claims.py`, restored from the committed file after each (driver: scratch, not in the tree), run from a `git archive` export of the branch with the head's `tests/doc_claims.py` (191ed6b74) in it: the unmutated export reads `2 of 277 checks FAILED`, both export artifacts (`every path resolves or is marked, ...` and `every named element resolves ...`, on `dev/governance/config/policy_budgets.json`, which the archive's export-ignore drops); every mutant below is red beyond those two, on the checks named.
- home-found predicate (`surface_rows`, `"home": int(found)` to `1`): 4 of 277, FAIL `red fixture: a service planted in services.yaml with no home is the one finding`, `red fixture: a Default cell that disagrees with the shipped default (away_dhw_min_temperature) is a finding`.
- default comparison (`default_agrees`, numeric arm reduced to `return m is not None`): 3 of 277, FAIL `red fixture: a Default cell that disagrees with the shipped default (away_dhw_min_temperature) is a finding`.
- `used to` purpose guard (`stateless_findings`, every `used to` skipped): 3 of 277, FAIL `red fixture: a history-sense "used to" is a finding`.
- stale exemption check (`surface_findings`, `if k not in set(keys)` to `if False`): 3 of 277, FAIL `red fixture: an exemption naming a surface no longer enumerated is a finding`.

This batch has five entries (four rulings and one owner order) and one new group, which carries one carry. It is cut separately from batch 94, whose refs were pushed while its opener was in flight, so that head was not moved.

- **P345: ACCEPT, as a new S fly-in, R10-FLY-RAISE-REVIEWABLE.**
  - The mechanism: `budget_raise_gate.approval` refuses until an approval names the head, and `tools/ci/gate.py` line 76 makes `budget-raise-gate` a required unit of `gate`. As a result, `merge_train.classify` reads RED. `orchestrator_tick.one_pr` then prints NOT REVIEWABLE (back to its fixer), and `bus.sh dispatch` refuses the reviewer on rc 1, a refusal live since `9c53c107b` (2026-10-29).
  - Instances: #3045 at `9ef51b82` (OWED-ACK ttl=3, hand override) and the critical-path #3006 at `979797ad` (pre-approval budget-raise-gate reds at 17:01, 18:32 and 18:34Z).
  - The build: one `merge_train.approval_owed` that reuses `Train.raise_hold`, and with it the gate's own `raises_between` and `approval`. A `classify --pr N` arm exits 4, APPROVAL-OWED, and is reviewable. `bus.sh` dispatches on rc 4, and the tick prints RAISE APPROVAL OWED instead of NOT REVIEWABLE. `classify` itself, and so the merge state, is unchanged.
  - REJECTED in part: the proposal's alternative of rolling the gate up as "approval owed, not red". `gate` must stay non-green to hold an unapproved raise off `main`.
  - Ask: dispatch it ahead of other instrument fly-ins.

- **P346: OWNER-ORDERED (not ruled).** A fixer-recorded prepr receipt lets `open_pr.sh` skip its prepr. The owner ordered it directly (tvofi, 2026-10-31), and the orchestrator withdrew the queue line before this seat ruled. `proposal-triage.md` gates proposals, and an owner order is not one, so the entry records no verdict. An earlier draft's REJECT does not stand. The group is R10-FLY-OPEN-PREPR-REUSE.
  - The entry keeps the evidence, which the orchestrator carries to that group's fixer as constraints:
    - `open_pr.sh` always gates a merge of origin/main into the code head (lines 103-105).

Carries (roster group R10-FLY-ROW-HEAD-CARRY at `origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster` `7d1e05e0251d76d9cd77dc8f9b9ff8acbf850de8`, numbered as `review_packet.py` numbers them):
- Carry 1 (tvofi card 4: hold behind R10-FLOW-MQ-PROBE; close the group if the merge queue is adopted): resolved by carry 2.
- Carry 2 (the merge queue is not adopted in round 10): the train-path branch was taken, so the hold is lifted. That branch is what this PR measured.
- Carry 3 (the `tests.yml` comment above "Fetch the recent push runs' durations"): closed in this diff. The comment now says the critical path is "a run's work to its last `tests / *` job with runner queue removed (see tests/ci_ratchet.py run_minutes; U9a)", which is what `run_minutes` computes (its docstring: "its critical path with every runner wait removed").
- Carry 4 (no instrument corrects a PR title without moving the head; the row planner derives row titles from the PR title): closed in this diff. `tools/audit/seat/body_patch.sh --title <pr> <expected-head> <title>` PATCHes `{"title"}` alone and reads the title back exactly. It works on an open or a closed pull request. On an open one, the live body is judged by the contract under the new title. The two rows are regenerated by `record_row.row_line` from the corrected titles: `dev/programme/delivery/2846.md` now says "triage: batch 32, P184-P191 (V104-V111)" and `dev/programme/delivery/2844.md` says "roster: round-10 batch 16 (9 ops)". The live PR titles still read the old text. Before this PR merges, the orchestrator runs these two GitHub writes, which a seat may not make, each first with `--dry-run`. The heads are each merged PR's final head as `/pulls/<n>` reports it:
  - `bash tools/audit/seat/body_patch.sh --title 2846 569849cf18f65ef58a45e85036d4e0544d79f1bc 'triage: batch 32, P184-P191 (V104-V111)'`
  - `bash tools/audit/seat/body_patch.sh --title 2844 9dc2d96330e520e08b2918dd01f58e7d4ffa8a7e 'roster: round-10 batch 16 (9 ops)'`
- Carry 5 (re-measure the CI-result side before building): done, and it decides arm (a) below.

## Arm (a): the carry, closed as not needed

Ruling: orchestrator s9, under mandate 6329234399, on this measurement. The brief's carry kept the run at the row head's parent P, and the row head R skipped tests, codeql, hassfest and validate and reused P's results. GitHub cancels a whole run, never part of one, so keeping P's run also keeps P's prelude, governance, body units and gate. `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_row_head_carry.py` (rules in its header) measured the 40 newest row-only pairs among the PRs merged since 2026-10-28 (#3008..#3043). Over those 40 pairs the carry gains 13631 job-s (what P's cancelled runs had already spent in the four units) and loses 74900 job-s (what P's kept run would also spend outside them). The net is -61269 job-s, median -1870 per open, and 3 of 40 pairs come out positive. Every P code run was cancelled (40 of 40), and the gap between the two heads' first code runs is a median of 15 s (max 37 s), so a carry saves no lead time either. Since #2858 the row push lands seconds after the PR, so the class the brief priced at an 8-minute median gap no longer exists. It would also make `tools/ci/gate.py`, the one required check, read results from another head.

Arm (b), refused, measured: cancelling P's runs from `open_pr.sh` or marking P `[skip ci]` can recover at most P's whole spend, 34376 job-s or 8.6% of R's 398267 over the same 40 pairs, and `[skip ci]` on a commit that reaches a push to main risks rule 1.

## Head

`aab7289a69ed51d8d646ac2623e0d8cd5a0c7495` merges main `c89de2f` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

Three new `# mut:` arms in `body_patch.sh`, each deleted (or made a no-op) in the real file. `bash tools/audit/seat/body_patch.sh --self-test` was then run with `env -u BASH_ENV`, and the file was restored afterwards (`cmp` identical):
- `mut:titlereadback` (`same = True`): rc=1, `body_patch self-test: 91 checks, 6 failed`, including `REFUSE: the title read back is not the title sent` and `REFUSE: the body read back is not the body sent`.
- `mut:titleshape` (`:`): rc=1, `91 checks, 5 failed`, including `REFUSE: bad title 1 of 4 (empty, leading space, trailing space, two lines)` and the same for 2, 3 and 4.
- `mut:titlecontract` (`:`): rc=1, `91 checks, 2 failed`: `REFUSE: the contract refuses the new title on an open pull request` and `never sent, never minted`.

The self-test also carries each of the three as an in-test mutant arm (`trb`, `tshp`, `tctr`): `MUTANT title read-back deleted`, `MUTANT title shape check deleted` and `MUTANT open-PR title contract deleted`. Each prints `ok` at the head.

Failing test first: the self-test arms were written before the implementation. Against the merge base's `body_patch.sh` they gave rc=1 and `body_patch self-test: 91 checks, 12 failed` (among them `--title on a MERGED pull request: patched` and `round trip: record_row accepts the row regenerated from the patched title, refuses the old one (null control)`). At the head: rc=0, `91 checks, 0 failed`.

merges.body:
R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE part 4 (#2725), in `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py`. It covers carry 8 (P112: `add --front` and `add --remove`), carry 19 (#2992's forward-carry: the batch admission's required set, plus the review survivors R3, R5, R8 and R9), and carry 21's check. Carry 11 (P164) is forward-carried; see `## Forward-carry`.

What the train does differently:

- **Batch admission reads the PR-head set (carry 19; P34's sibling seam).** `Train._batch` reads `head_req = self.required(pr_head=True)` once per batch and passes it to `Train.admit`, whose parameter is now `head_req`. `admit`'s head wait judges that set. main's set (`req`, which leaves out PR_ONLY) still grades main (`main_green`) and the proof (`settle`), and neither of those carries a pull-request-only context. The bug stayed hidden because `PR_ONLY` is `()` at the fork. With a non-empty one, a head whose pr-contract was red would have been admitted.
- **`add --front <pr> [<verdict>]` and `add --remove <pr>` (carry 8, P112).** Both run under QUEUE_LOCK, through `spool_edit` / `spool_edit_locked`. Each prints the spool order read back from the file (`FRONT #13: spool read back: #13 #11 #12`, `REMOVED #12: spool read back: #11 #13`).
  - `--front` on a spooled PR moves its line first. On a new PR it runs `add`'s own admission, then spools the entry first in a live train, or with no live train queues it first in the train it starts.
  - `--remove` drops only that PR's line(s).
  - Every other line stays byte-identical and in order, unreadable lines included. The spool is rewritten aside and renamed (`spool_rewrite`).
  - An absent PR is refused with rc 1 and nothing is written. `--front --remove` together, or a plain `add` with no verdict, is refused with rc 2.
  - There is no priority drain. `Train.queue_take` is untouched (carries 20-22).
- **Four #2992 review survivors pinned (carry 19).** Each gets a self-test arm. Production code is unchanged:
  - R3: a critical-path entry that stops at ci under `--bot-prs` still lets the record PR merge, through `serial`'s `except Stop:` sweep.
  - R5: `CHANGES_REQUESTED` parks after one attempt, and no approval carry is tried.
  - R9: BLOCKED + APPROVED + every required context green is carried under `--approval-carry` and merges on the next attempt. Without the flag it parks naming the review.
  - R8: `Train._critical`'s live read runs against a stub `roster_lib`. It maps a critical group True and a non-critical or unmapped branch False, and reads the roster once for three entries. A read that raises gives False for every entry and is not retried.

Each roster carry (1-based, as `review_packet.py` numbers them on `handoff/audit-r10-roster`):

Carry 1: the overlap grade (#2595's countermeasure). Built in part 1, #2882, merged at 4db1d3e.
Carry 2: park instead of 8 retries on a missing approval at the live head (#2577). Built in part 3, #2992, merged at e035c66.
Carry 3: P4, park with the read reason and widen `_carry_owner_approval` under --approval-carry. Built in #2992. Its last sentence, --approval-carry in the live launch, is met on main: `RECOMMENDED` holds `--approval-carry`, and train.sh and the sweep launch it by default (0b79e8de9).
Carry 4: P34, the head wait reads `required(pr_head=True)`. Built in #2992 for `serial`. Its batch-admission sibling is closed here (carry 19).
Carry 5: the hold behind R10-FLOW-MQ-PROBE. Resolved by carry 10; no code owed.
Carry 6: the orchestrator ruling that releases the group. A resolution; no code owed.
Carry 7: #2595's root cause, item 6fb50ac5. The countermeasure is the overlap grade from #2882 (carry 1). Item 98904e32 concerns #2595's own merged body, so nothing is owed in this tree.
Carry 8: P112, `add --front` and `add --remove`. Built here.
Carry 9: P129, one admission rule. Built in part 2, #2978, merged at 89ccf73.
Carry 10: the merge queue is not adopted. A resolution: the train path was taken.
Carry 11: P164, `stats` and `--cap auto`. Not built; forward-carried (`## Forward-carry`).
Carry 12: P184. (a) remerge_main.sh aborts its failed merge: 332661e99 (R10-FLY-ABORT-OWN-MERGE, P276). (b) `freeable` frees an ancestor holder: #2992.
Carry 13: P189, the skip leaves pending, plus the HOLDER exception. Built in #2978.
Carry 14: P191, a record PR merged on refusal recovers through MAIN-MOVED. Built in #2992.
Carry 15: the HOLDER exception in the one shared predicate. Built in #2978.
Carry 16: P231, gh's refusal text in the BOT line. Built in #2992.
Carry 17: P289, critical-path entries jump the record sweep. Built in #2992.
Carry 18: P291, a BRANCH-POLICY skip is re-admitted at the same verdict. Built in #2978 (`READMIT_SAME_VERDICT`).
Carry 19: #2992's forward-carry (batch admission's required set, plus survivors R3, R5, R8 and R9). Built here.
Carry 20: P312, the priority drain. Not built here, per carry 21.
Carry 21: checked. At the fork 7539d167, and at the merge base c3a47e56 (whose `merge_train.py` is the same file), there is no priority drain: `grep -n priority tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py` prints only a comment, line 2734 at this head. R10-FLY-TRAIN-DEFAULTS has not landed P312, so there is no SHA to cite.
Carry 22: `add --front` and `add --remove` are built as written. `Train.queue_take` is untouched, so P312's sort, when it lands, keeps both verbs: they reorder only the spool file.

Alternatives not taken:
- Reading `required(pr_head=True)` inside `admit`, per entry, as part 3 did in `serial`. It lost because it costs two ruleset API reads per entry instead of two per batch, and `_batch` is `admit`'s only caller (`grep -n '\.admit(' tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py` prints its two call sites, both in `_batch`).
- A separate reorder verb. Carry 8 names flags on `add`, and a second verb would be a second writer of the spool.

Closes nothing: #2725 stays open for carry 11.

## Head

`e8a1a3b0d5712b4bfbcb1a1f7ba558191d641211` merges main `c89de2f` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`8e828d854e06e5ec9458e1831c27f4c293912c8c` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3063.md`. The authored code head is `34660f5c594b731d3099bedb13b17c888a304b43`.

`5b224e950d2ee6c1f99a46f9131ad68ded42a962` merges origin/main `2b6bef745` into the authored code head `34660f5c594b731d3099bedb13b17c888a304b43` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below).

Measured at 34660f5c594b731d3099bedb13b17c888a304b43, pushed to `handoff/r10-train-overlap-grade`. It is three commits on the fork 7539d1675d7fc8b5020f90b395f4bb0c3485d5b3 (5126ec445fd6fb24279cb259e05d49fbc22b7de2), plus a merge of origin/main c3a47e5656ef858674a1fd011c0e2f039c4ed838 (read at 2026-10-31, before the final prepr run). main moved during the first prepr run, so it was merged and every check re-run. The merged delta touches `tools/pr/ci_predict.py` and triage records only. `git diff --quiet 5126ec44 34660f5c -- tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py dev/audit/harnesses/r10_train_overlap_grade_p4_mutants.py tests/closures.json && echo MERGE_TRAIN_HARNESS_CLOSURES_IDENTICAL` prints the word, so the mutant run at 5126ec44, which reads only those two files, describes this head's `merge_train.py`. The merge base is c3a47e5656ef858674a1fd011c0e2f039c4ed838.

## Mutation proof

Instrument: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_train_overlap_grade_p4_mutants.py`, landed in this PR. It makes one exact single-occurrence replacement per mutant (a span not found once is reported STALE), runs `--self-test` on a sibling copy, and prints the FAIL lines. It was run at 5126ec44 and printed `MUTANTS: 13 run, 0 not as required`. M0, the unmutated head, prints PASS. Each mutant mutates the predicate:

- M1, batch admission reads main's set (`head_req = self.required(pr_head=True)` -> `self.required()`): fails `P34 batch: a PR-only context red at the head refuses admission, naming it; nothing merges`.
- M2, `--front` appends instead (`mine + rest` -> `rest + mine`): fails the `P112 --front` arm, its null arm, the new-entry arm and `P112 --front under the lock`.
- M3, `--remove` keeps the line (`else rest` -> `else raw`): fails `P112 --remove: drops only #12's line ...` and `P112 --remove under the lock`.
- M4, absent-PR refusal dropped (`if not mine:` -> `if False:`): fails `P112 --remove null: an absent PR exits nonzero and the spool is byte-identical`.
- M5, the lock dropped (`with queue_lock(t.state):` -> `if True:` in `spool_edit`): fails `P112 --front under the lock` and `P112 --remove under the lock`.
- M6, a new `--front` entry in a live train not moved first: fails `P112 --front on a new entry: admitted, spooled first ...`.
- M7, `--front` with no live train queued last: fails `P112 --front with no live train: the train it starts runs the entry FIRST ...`.
- M8 (R3), `serial`'s stop-path sweep -> `pass`: fails `P289 serial, a critical-path entry that stops at ci: the record PR still merges, the entry does not`.
- M9 (R5), `rd != "CHANGES_REQUESTED"` -> `True`: fails `carry 2 null (CHANGES_REQUESTED): ...`.
- M10 (R9), `or ms == "BLOCKED"` dropped: fails both `carry 2 (BLOCKED, APPROVED, all green)` arms.
- M11 (R8), `_critical` -> `return False`: fails `R8 _critical: the live read maps fix/a (critical group) True ...`.
- M12 (R8), the first-read sentinel `self.cp_read = ({}, set())` -> `pass`: fails `R8 _critical null: a roster read that raises is nothing critical for every entry, and is not retried per entry`.

Failing test first: the two `P34 batch` arms and the R-arms were written before or against the unmutated production line. M1 restores the fork's line and fails the new arm.

## Null control

- P34 batch: the same world with pr-contract green at both heads admits both and merges them on one proof (`P34 batch null: ...`).
- P112: a plain `add` into the live train appends last (`P112 null: a plain add appends last`). `--remove` of an absent PR leaves the spool byte-identical (`read_bytes()` compared). The lock arm's own null control runs the same edit without the lock (`spool_edit_locked` called directly, which is the M5 shape), and the concurrent add's line is lost (`P112 --front null (no lock, the mutant) ...` and `P112 --remove null ...`). So the locked arm measures the lock, not the timing.
- R8: a raising roster read gives "nothing critical", today's order.
- Every self-test arm that existed at the fork still passes: 381 checks there, all of them in the 400 here.

## Figures

- Self-test: `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` prints `merge_train self-test: 400 checks, 0 failed` at 34660f5c (and at 5126ec44). In a detached worktree at the fork 7539d167 (whose `merge_train.py` is the merge base's: the merged delta does not touch it) it prints `merge_train self-test: 381 checks, 0 failed`. The count is checks executed (some arms loop), not call sites.
- Mutants: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_train_overlap_grade_p4_mutants.py` prints `MUTANTS: 13 run, 0 not as required` at 5126ec44. M0 PASS and M1-M12 KILLED, each with the FAIL lines above.
- Gate scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff c3a47e5656ef858674a1fd011c0e2f039c4ed838 --workdir "$D"` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out` and names `tests/entities.py`. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` prints `ALL 2493 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`.
- `run_always` lines: `python3 tests/env_drift.py --claims-only c3a47e56...` exits 0, `python3 tests/closure.py selftest` exits 0 and `python3 tests/layout.py` exits 0. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/harness_headers.py` prints `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`.
- `python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --apply-inert` applied one entry (the new harness as an inert read of `tests/harness_headers.py`, in `tests/closures.json`), then printed `CI PREDICT: no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted against 7539d1675d7f`. Re-run after the merge, `python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py` prints the same line against c3a47e5656ef.
- `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`. No metric was re-recorded and no budget was touched.
- `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff c3a47e5656ef858674a1fd011c0e2f039c4ed838` prints `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`. No gain is claimed.
- Class rule, step 8. Let E be the line of `def _self_test` in merge_train.py (3343 at this head).
  - Required-set reads: `awk -v E=$E 'NR<E && /self\.required\(/' tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py` returns 4 sites. `serial`'s head wait (`pr_head=True`) was closed by #2992. `policy_refusal` (`pr_head=True`) was closed by #2992. `_batch`'s `req = self.required()` grades main and the proof, which carry no PR-only context, so it is correct as main's set. `_batch`'s `head_req = self.required(pr_head=True)` feeds `admit` and is closed in this diff. Null control: the same rule at the fork 7539d167 returns 3 sites, with `admit` fed main's set, which is the open seam.
  - Spool writers: `awk -v E=$E 'NR<E && /QUEUE_SPOOL/ && !/^QUEUE_SPOOL/' tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py` returns 10 lines. Every write goes through `spool_append` (append), `spool_rewrite` (`--front` / `--remove`), `train_add`'s unlink after it moves the spool into a started train's queue, and `queue_take`'s unlink after the drain. All of them run under `queue_lock`. The rest are reads and log text. `git grep -n "queue-add" -- . ':!tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py' ':!dev/programme/triage'` returns only the roster's carry text, so no other tool or doc tells anyone to hand-edit the spool.

## Unpinned sites

n/a: every production line this diff adds is pinned by a mutant in `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_train_overlap_grade_p4_mutants.py` (M1-M7). The `tools/` lane is outside mutation-autofix, so this is the in-tree harness fixer.md step 2 names.

## Red checks

none: no check has run on this head yet. `ci_predict.py` predicts no red.

## Forward-carry

- Carry 11 (P164: `merge_train.py stats` and, only past 0.5 h/day lost, `--cap auto`) is not built here. It needs "wall time lost to drop-and-retry, over a window", and the train's log lines carry no timestamps. `Train.log` is `print` into `train.log` through train.sh, and only the batch tag (`BATCH <yyyymmdd-hhmmss>`) holds a time. So the figure the cap decision keys on cannot be derived from the log, and no train log is in the tree or reachable from this container. The next stage must first give each train log line a UTC stamp, or define lost time from batch tags, before `stats` can measure it. Carry: R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE
