The orchestrator owes the wiring: add 2262 to R10-COP-GATE's `fixes` (the body then carries the keyword), or shut the issue by hand after the merge.

Round 2 answers the round-1 review (review/3005, blocked on a head move at 738791c0): the two surviving `CMP_BOUND` mutants at the flow-lift gate now have fixtures at both equality edges and are pinned in the ledger, the two class-enumeration leads have destinations under `## Forward-carry`, and every carry is cited by its 1-indexed position in R10-COP-GATE's `carry` list on origin/main 4d2f32b2e517c45c44eb0738dc5cb1e3c72287ad, which holds 18 entries.

**A. Model status copy (carry 18: the R10-UX-HEALTH design review's point A).** `ModelStatusSensor`'s `cop` attribute now also carries `cop_observability`, `cop_refusal` and `measured_cop_at`. Each is copied under its own name from the learning view (`data.get(...)`), with no boolean and no second derivation. The observed-COP sensor is unavailable exactly when the install is `not_measurable`, and Home Assistant hides an unavailable entity's attributes. The card's `copState` (heatpump-optimizer-card.js) already reads these three keys from this row, so its not-measurable branch can now fire in production.

**C. Flow-bias duty gate (carries 13 and 16: `_fold_flow_lift` reads the commanded split).** `_fold_flow_lift` read the commanded split. Its duty gate now reads `heat_energy.meter_of(coord).attribution(coord._commanded_split())`, which is the mode dwell where observed and otherwise the commanded split, through `heat_energy.dhw_share`, at the same `_COP_CURVE_SHARE`. This is the existing owner of the choice, so no parallel rule is added. `_cop_reference_curve` already reads the same attribution, so the two gates now agree.

**Not in this pull request, reported as the remainder:**
- **D (the learned top reaching the plan; carry 12, the orchestrator's 2026-10-26 ruling that the learned top's consumer is this group's).** `DrawRange.planned` returns `None` unless `engaged`, by design. The module docstring of `draw_range.py` says "a pump that realizes what it is asked must plan exactly as before", and the latch is what keeps the clamp from re-booking. Letting a learned top reach the plan while the latch is off changes what the plan books on every install with `draw_range.MIN_SAMPLES` (48) or more full-command samples. That is a threshold and behaviour change, but the group's architect note fixes the shape as "a published reason, no threshold change". So D needs a design ruling on which surfaces may read the learned top, and on whether the plan's clamp may engage without the latch, before any fixer. It already stands in the group's brief as carry 12. Carry: R10-COP-GATE
- **B (heat-pump grade drivers; carries 6 and 7, the hover reason codes and plain-words text, and 14 and 17, the `envelope_drivers` interface to mirror).** Not started. It mirrors `presets.house_grade`'s driver interface, publishes `machine_drivers`, extends the card renderer and adds hover strings: the largest item, and the brief names it as the remainder if the diff would exceed an L. It already stands in the group's brief as those four carries. Carry: R10-COP-GATE

merges.subject: Merge pull request #3024 from tvofi/fix/r10-fly-beat-fetch-race
merges.title: R10-FLY-BEAT-FETCH-RACE: fetch_origin retries a ref-lock race; roster_queue writes a FAILED line per failed op
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-FLY-BEAT-FETCH-RACE (size S). The detached `state_docs.py beat --apply` died three times on `roster_edit.Refuse` from `fetch_origin` ("cannot lock ref refs/remotes/origin/...: is at X but expected Y": another process sharing the repository moved a remote-tracking ref between the fetch's read and its write). The same race refused a roster op. Two defects, one seam:

1. `fetch_origin` (tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py) treated that transient race as fatal. It now retries, at most `FETCH_ATTEMPTS`=4 attempts with 0.25/0.5/1.0 s sleeps, and only when git failed and every line it printed is exactly the lock-race line. Any other failure refuses at once; a race past the bound refuses with git's message. Chosen over a loop-survives-a-pass fix because every caller (beat, roster_sync, every roster op) shares this function, and a retry costs milliseconds where a skipped pass costs an interval.
2. The beat's loop did not survive a refusal even where it was meant to: `roster_sync.main` catches `roster_sync.Refuse`, but `fetch_origin` raises `roster_edit.Refuse`, a different class, which escaped as a traceback (the three tracebacks in the beat log). `roster_sync.main` now converts it, so a race outlasting the bound is a refused pass (rc 2), retried at the next interval.

Folded in, same file family: P315 / #3020 (triage batch 78). `roster_queue.py run_queue`: a deleted `--lint-clone` raised FileNotFoundError before any report line was written, so callers read the previous op's line as this op's result (12 roster ops falsely marked done on 2026-10-30/31). Now every op attempted writes exactly one report line; an exception becomes `roster: <op> <group> FAILED <ExceptionType>: <message>` and the run stops rc 1; a missing `--lint-clone` (or `--edit-checkout`) is refused by name before the first op, rc 2, with a report line. No re-clone (rejected in P315). Overlap only: P300's `--mark` (R10-ORCH-ROSTER-SCHEMA) touches `run_queue` too; the per-op body is now `_run_op`, the seams are distinct, and whichever lands second merges main.

Carry: R10-FLY-BEAT-FETCH-RACE

## Head

`5f01496e4f65f2ef3623a7e8f625c41c929ec2de` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3024.md`. The authored code head is `b7ac768450038eac0afb83ac841187bd8b408e1a`.

`236611b5d1dea78fd968bf3045a50dca6a6a939d` merges origin/main `18b788ac2` into the authored code head `b7ac768450038eac0afb83ac841187bd8b408e1a` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below).

b7ac768450038eac0afb83ac841187bd8b408e1a

## Mutation proof

Each mutant applied to the committed head, the named self-test run, then restored (cmp against a backup); every mutant red:
- `FETCH_ATTEMPTS = 1`: `roster_edit.py --self-test` 2 failed ("fetch_origin: one lock race is retried and succeeds", "several raced refs in one fetch are one race"); `state_docs.py --self-test` fails "sync arm 4: the beat outlives one injected lock race" and "sync arm 4: the race was retried once, not skipped".
- race predicate `return rc != 0 and bool(lines) and all(...)` -> `return rc != 0`: `roster_edit.py --self-test` 2 failed ("a non-race failure refuses at once, unretried", "a race line beside another failure is not a race").
- `roster_sync.py` conversion `raise Refuse(str(e))` -> `raise`: `state_docs.py --self-test` fails "sync arm 4: a persistent race is a refused pass (rc 2), no crash" (got: raised Refuse).
- `roster_queue.py` `except Exception` -> `except ZeroDivisionError`: the self-test dies with the injected FileNotFoundError (no FAILED line).
- `roster_queue.py` clone guard `if not Path(d).is_dir()` -> `if False`: "a missing --lint-clone is refused by name, rc 2, before any op" fails.

## Null control

At the merge base the beat has no retry and no conversion: the same injected single race ends the beat with an uncaught `roster_edit.Refuse` (the sync arm 4 mutants above reproduce exactly that), and a run with a deleted lint clone writes no report line. Null controls in the self-tests: a clean fetch is one attempt with no sleep; a clean `roster_queue` queue writes `roster: set-stage <g> pushed <sha9>` for each op; a non-race failure is never retried.

## Figures

- Collision rate, rule: lines starting `roster_edit.Refuse:` containing `cannot lock ref` over lines starting `roster_sync: pull requests` (one per pass) in the beat log; at 2026-10-31 00:4xZ 11 over 1154 (about 0.95 per cent per pass; the log grows, so re-take it). Command: `grep -c "^roster_edit.Refuse: .*cannot lock ref" <the orchestrator state dir>/state-beat.log` and `grep -c "^roster_sync: pull requests" <the orchestrator state dir>/state-beat.log`. Null control: the same grep for a string absent from the log prints 0. One further `roster_edit.Refuse` line in the log is not a lock race and is not counted. At that rate and independent attempts, four attempts leave about 1e-8 per pass; the first sleep already exceeds the millisecond window of a race. Independence is an assumption; the bound caps the damage to a refused pass (item 2) if it fails.

R10-UX-HEALTH part 2: the residual after #2976. Part of #2809, Part of #2499.

What lands:

- **Hover spec (carry 14), the Health model rows.** Each model row's hover
  (`healthModelTitle` in the card) is now the metric in plain words, then the
  row's current reason: its learner phase, its evidence, or its COP reason.
  The rows were the metric title alone. `health.metric_lower`, `_tank` and
  `_gains` (en, sv) now also say what no data means. The other three already
  did.
- **#2809.** `DebugFinalizeButton.extra_state_attributes` names
  `debug_collect_start` for a finished collection. That is the action's
  `start`, the way out. The option-off case keeps `debug_collect`. Home
  Assistant drops attributes while the button is unavailable, so the card's
  Health debug row (`health.debug_final`, from #2976) stays the visible
  surface.
- **Card test gaps (carry 5).** `tests/card.mjs` pins the render that
  `openSetupSlot` must follow its state change with. It also drives the Configure
  chip's place-name fallback through a real Setup render.

- **The mutation null control, round 3 (orchestrator ruling, mandate
  6329234399).** `null_control` in `tests/mutation_table.py` now takes the
  first whole-line comment of any width and indent. It took only one whose
  full line, indentation included, was under 60 characters. That cap has no
  recorded reason (2fe38a487's message, #1521, is silent on it), and nothing
  reads a line's width: no driver, and no linter in CI (Figures). It refused
  every pool whose comments ran past it: `button.py`'s do, so `tests /
  mutation` and `--pin-killed` refused this PR whatever it pinned. The null
  arm is unchanged: a file with no whole-line comment still yields none, and
  a pool of only such files still refuses. `tests/mutation_table.py` is
  code-owned (`.github/CODEOWNERS`, the `mutation_table.py` and
  `typing_ruler.py` note: the mutation jobs install the pull request's
  requirement locks before the grader, and it runs the pull request's
  tests), so the change is kept to the predicate and its docstring: one
  condition dropped, four docstring lines.
- **The three `button.py` pins, re-recorded by the tool.** The round-2 rows
  came from an out-of-tree scratch script (`hand_pin.py`). They are
  re-pinned by `mutation_table.py --pin-killed` itself, now that the pool has
  a null control; only each row's `reason` changes.

What does not land, and why:

- **Carry 17, the P9 storage reset, is withheld.** It is measured, and the
  result needs an after-edge outside this group's seam. Routed in
  Forward-carry. Carry: R10-UX-HEALTH
- **The "driving scale" (carry 14), not built.** My reading is the headline
  score's third sub-score, `score.label_operation` = "Driving" (en) /
  "Körningen" (sv). It sits in the same hover as the House and Heat pump grades
  the owner names (`scoreParts`, `scoreDrivers` in the card). The card's own
  comment on `score.part_operation` reads "Driving: whether the plan buys at
  the cheap hours". Evidence that it lacks the owner's factor list: `scoreDrivers` reads
  `attrs["<key>_drivers"]`, and the backend publishes only `envelope_drivers`
  (`coordinator.py`, the `envelope_drivers` payload key, #2816).
  `grep -n operation_drivers custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py`
  returns nothing. So the Driving part never shows "each factor pushing it,
  its direction and rough weight", and neither does Heat pump. Building that is a
  backend driver list plus card copy, outside this seam. The carry requires
  the orchestrator to confirm the widget first, so it is not built here.
  Routed in Forward-carry. Carry: R10-UX-HEALTH
- **#2499 stays open.** See Figures: the no-meter arm still books about 1.9x
  what it delivers. The Health line "Not observable without a power meter"
  (`health.model_unobservable`) landed in #2976. The over-booking figure is
  not met, so this body closes nothing. Routed in Forward-carry. Carry: #2499

Design choices:

- **The fallback case withdraws a map entry.** The Setup boxes are a literal
  list in `setupSvgHtml`: outdoor, heat_pump, wood_tank, mixing_valve,
  buffer_tank, dhw_tank, upper_zone, lower_zone. All eight are keys of
  `SETUP_CONFIGURE_PAGE`. A slot whose place is not in that list is dropped
  by `slotsAt`, so no topology reaches the fallback; the brief's "topology
  whose place is outside" cannot be built. The case instead deletes
  `wood_tank` from the live map for one render and restores it. That is the
  case the fallback guards: a box added without its page.
- **One owner for the hover.** `healthModelTitle` is used by both
  `healthModelRow` and `healthGainsRow`, so the gains row cannot drift from
  the others. Alternative considered: append the reason at each of the six
  call sites. It lost because it spells the rule six times.

## Head

`d9f07e88c2e92d16aa228e04158efa3e3cb1bc0b` merges main `18b788a` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`5832ceb58e6f1e79aba0f6273f50d1b4a928819a` merges the authored code head `525e206910e181e8839d3efb979d6f4c8d6861f9` and then merges origin/main `a6e4a5afe` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

525e206910e181e8839d3efb979d6f4c8d6861f9, two commits on the reviewed head
feacede17c5e1eb6b7e399bf87a2efea3ea79cc7:
baf2c4c00c3d9f0d921ccfd03179bd1ee4e0b9fc (the `null_control` predicate and
its entities.py check) and 525e206910e181e8839d3efb979d6f4c8d6861f9 (the
three `button.py` rows re-recorded by `mutation_table.py --pin-killed`).
They replace the cloud seat's 700f21c18 and 077a87b02, which were committed
under another author identity; the tree differs from 077a87b02 only in the
`null_control` docstring's wording. Merge base
d99cadb1235a5e40e250466e656c41c7ce88e641. origin/main was at
7d6a95e5edb9564f8ab632bac2a0317c820bb29e at 2026-10-30T19:07Z, and
`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0 (no conflict), so main
was not merged in (`fixer.md` step 6). The round-3 tests, mutants and gate
ran at this head, or at baf2c4c00 where a line says so. The card, P9 and
#2499 figures are from earlier rounds, and no card, browser-test or learner
line has moved since.

Host note: this seat ran on macOS, whose kernel refuses
`entities.py`'s heartbeat arm a task port for its own child
(`PermissionError: Cannot get task port`, in `_hb_stdlib_reads`), at this
head and at feacede17 alike. Each local `entities.py` run below therefore
hid `_remote_debugging` from `importlib.util.find_spec` through a scratch
wrapper, so that arm skips exactly as on an interpreter without the module;
no tree file changes. CI (Linux) runs the arm.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant is one line in a worktree. `node tests/card.mjs`,
`python3 tests/debug_collect.py` or `python3 tests/entities.py` was run,
then the line was restored.

- Drop `host._render();` from `openSetupSlot` → FAIL `openSetupSlot renders
  the page it opens`. The existing `Assign redraws the dialog on the Setup page`
  also goes red, so this mutant was already killed at base. The carry's
  "unpinned at base" does not hold at this base. The new case pins it at the
  function rather than through the Advisor press.
- `b.cfgPage = page ? L(page) : placeLabel(b.place);` → `b.cfgPage =
  L(page);` → FAIL `P08/P41: the Configure chip of a place with no options
  page names the place, never undefined`.
- `healthModelTitle` returns `L(\`health.metric_${id}\`)` alone → FAIL
  `hover spec (en)…` and `hover spec (sv)…`.
- `button.py`: the final branch returns `{"waiting_for": "debug_collect"}` →
  FAIL `the finalize button on a finished collection names the action's
  start, not the option that is already on`. Output: `1 of 159 DEBUG COLLECT
  CHECKS FAILED`.
- `tests/mutation_table.py` (round 3), all in worktrees, each run
  `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`:
  - Test first: the new entities.py check at feacede17, before the
    predicate changed → `1 of 2489 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`, the failing check
    being `a comment line past sixty characters, by indent or by its own
    text, is still the null control; a pool with no comment line still
    refuses` (`long=None none=None pool-none=None`).
  - Mutant A, restoring the old predicate (`and len(lines[ln - 1]) < 60`
    back into `null_control`'s condition) at baf2c4c00 → `1 of 2489 ENTITY
    CHECKS FAILED`, the same check, the same detail.
  - Mutant B, the over-wide predicate (`if tok.type == tokenize.COMMENT:`,
    any comment, trailing ones included) at baf2c4c00 → `3 of 2489 ENTITY
    CHECKS FAILED`: the new check's null arm (`none=` picks `Y = 1  #
    trailing`), the #1521 check `the null control edits a whole-line comment
    and nothing else`, and the shard check `a shard whose files hold no
    whole-line comment inherits the whole pool's null control`.
  - Unmutated baf2c4c00 → `ALL 2489 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`.

## Null control

Unmodified tree: origin/main at the merge base, with this head's
`tests/card.mjs` copied in.

- `node tests/card.mjs` fails exactly `hover spec (en)` and `hover spec (sv)`,
  which is the defect. The openSetupSlot and fallback cases pass at base,
  because they pin behaviour the base already has.
- The #2809 check fails at base by construction, because the base is the
  mutant above.
- The hover case enumerates every `data-model-row` the page draws. It asserts
  the count is 6, so a seventh row without the two parts fails it, and so does
  a row dropped from the fixture.
- The null-control check has its own null arm. It asserts that a file
  holding only a string that looks like a comment, plus a trailing comment,
  yields no null control, and that `null_for` over a pool of that file
  returns None. Mutant B, a fix that took any comment at all, fails it. The
  check also asserts its preconditions: both fixture comment lines are longer
  than 60 characters in full, so the old cap admitted neither.
- The mutation run's own null control: button.py:37 plus ` (null control)`
  survived every driver that read it in both round-3 runs (Figures).

## Figures

- **Null-control census (round 3).** The rule: take every `*.py` under
  `custom_components/` (`Path("custom_components").rglob("*.py")`). Run each
  through `mutation_table.null_control` at the head, and through the old
  predicate and an indent-stripped one (the same tokenize loop with
  `len(line) < 60`, and with `len(line.strip()) < 60`). Count the files
  that get no null control. Run at baf2c4c00 (scratch one-off probe,
  `fixer.md` step 18; the standing pin is the entities.py check).
  - 84 files. The old predicate leaves 13 without a null control, the
    indent-stripped cap of 60 (the alternative the brief named) leaves 11,
    and the head leaves 3.
  - The 13: batchmath, button, currency, datetime, flow_meter, issues,
    plan_slots, plan_step, prefill_offer, repairs, silent_mode, switch and
    wood_fuel. The 11 are the same less button and plan_slots.
  - The 3 left are `flow_meter.py`, `silent_mode.py` and `wood_fuel.py`.
    `grep -cE '^\s*#'` reads 0 in each, so no whole-line comment exists in
    them: that is the null arm working.
- **Seams of the class** (a pool refused for want of a null control), by the
  census rule above:
  - The 10 files only the cap excluded, `button.py` among them: closed in
    this diff.
  - `flow_meter.py`, `silent_mode.py` and `wood_fuel.py`: still refused when
    the pool holds only these files, because no comment-only edit exists in
    them. Named under Forward-carry (the `null_for` pre-check), not closed.
  - A pool's non-Python files: outside this census. The null control is
    tokenized as Python, and this diff does not change that.
- **Why no cap remains.** The cap's only plausible purpose is the edited
  line's width: 60 plus the 15-character ` (null control)` suffix stays
  under PEP 8's 79. Nothing reads that width:
  - `grep -rlnE "ruff|flake8|pylint|pycodestyle|black " .github/` returns
    nothing, and the tree holds no `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg` or ruff
    config, so no linter runs in CI.
  - `grep -rnE "len\((line|l|ln|_l|row|lines\[[^]]*\])\) *(>|>=|<|<=)
    *[0-9]{2,3}" tests/*.py tools/` returns only the cap itself
    (`tests/mutation_table.py:2157` at feacede17). This search is a
    heuristic.
  - The run itself: the edited null-control line at button.py:37 is 91
    characters, and it survived every driver that read it (below).

merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
away: set back the weekend and holiday comfort pairs too (r10-hotfix-away-setback)

Hotfix from tvofi's live finding (#201 comment 6528614583, 2026-10-30), using the latent (b) the probe `r10-live-away-heating` measured (report: `handoff-body/r10-live-away-heating` at aa6e5db30ba6fe7cb4a2f1016c271ae9bf260af2). While away and not recovering, `away.solve_bands` set back `target_temp`, `min_temp` and `comfort_temp_day/night`, but it left `comfort_temp_{day,night}_weekend` and `holiday_comfort_{day,night}` as configured. `OptimizationConfig._comfort_pair` substitutes those fields per step on Saturdays, Sundays and holiday dates, so with away on, Saturday's comfort target read 21.0 where the away target was 16.0.

**Fix.** The four schedule fields join `away._OPT_FIELDS` and the `_SetbackConfig` protocol (typed `float | None`). `solve_bands` now reads only the configured (non-None) fields, and while away and not recovering it sets every comfort number it read to the away target, keeping `target_temp` and `min_temp` as `min(configured, target)`. An unconfigured field returns no band and keeps None through `replace`. The coordinator caller (`_solve_hubs`) is unchanged, because it already spreads `**config_bands` into `replace`.

**Alternatives considered.**
- (a) Bypass the weekend and holiday branches in `_comfort_pair` while away. This would put away state into the optimizer config, a second owner of the setback concept. Rejected (fixer step 17: one owner per concern; `away.py` owns the setback).
- (b) Always return all eight keys, including None. This would widen the return type to `dict[str, float | None]` and touch the coordinator's annotation for no behavioural gain. Rejected.

No issue is closed: the finding came from a #201 comment, not an issue. The presence-entity state listener (the probe's (c)) was routed to R10-LIVESTATE's coordinator move by the dispatch brief before this seat ran, so this body carries nothing forward.

## Head

`7e8c2248e6892e3484d5724fdb0a92155aae5b4f` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/3013.md`. The authored code head is `3ec79824c44eb346f6da62af678eae08ec742f2b`.

`8c009d866ddcffe5265f0610aa9851b8fb3947a7` merges origin/main `a9ba3022e` into the authored code head `3ec79824c44eb346f6da62af678eae08ec742f2b` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below).

Measured at `3ec79824c44eb346f6da62af678eae08ec742f2b` (branch `handoff/r10-hotfix-away-setback`), cut from `origin/main` = `cc930cdd1a3cfb005ba7ec557f4451ff5e53e364` (merge base, behind main by 0), measured 2026-10-30 UTC.

Commits:
- `82c6913c2`: the fix, the test and the harness.
- `3ec79824c`: `tests/closures.json`, the harness's INERT READS entry written by `tools/pr/ci_predict.py --apply-inert`.

## Mutation proof

The failing test came first. The new checks are in `tests/features.py`, in the `away.solve_bands` block after the economy-widening check, and they run through the production `OptimizationConfig`, then `away.solve_bands`, then `replace`, then `HeatPumpOptimizer._build_comfort_bounds`, with step times Sat 2026-10-31 14:00 and 03:00. No formula is re-implemented.

- **Before the fix** (test added, `away.py` at the base), `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` gave `1 of 4607 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`: `FAIL away sets back the weekend and holiday comfort pairs too: Saturday day and night read the away target [... ('weekend', 'away'): [21.0, 19.5] ... ('holiday', 'away'): [21.0, 19.5] ...]`.
- **After the fix**, the same command gave `ALL 4607 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`.

**Mutants: one per added field.** Each mutant deletes that one name from `_OPT_FIELDS`. Each ran in a copy of `custom_components/` and `tests/` outside git. All four were killed by the new check, and each mutant reverts exactly its own slot:

| mutant (field removed) | killing check | weekend away [Sat 14:00, 03:00] | holiday away [Sat 14:00, 03:00] |
|---|---|---|---|
| `comfort_temp_day_weekend` | away sets back the weekend and holiday comfort pairs too | [21.0, 16.0] | [16.0, 16.0] |
| `comfort_temp_night_weekend` | the same | [16.0, 19.5] | [16.0, 16.0] |
| `holiday_comfort_day` | the same | [16.0, 16.0] | [21.0, 16.0] |
| `holiday_comfort_night` | the same | [16.0, 16.0] | [16.0, 19.5] |

Each mutant run also printed `FAIL and the path that proceeds still stamps a resolvable recorded_at (#363)`. That is the runner's own failure for an out-of-git copy, which fixer step 2 names (#1713, #1723), and not the mutant's.

Disclosed: those copies did not include `tools/`, so each run stopped later at `ModuleNotFoundError: gen_device_fixtures`. That happened after the killing check had printed FAIL, so the kills stand, but no mutant run reached the end of the suite. CI's required mutation check is the complete run.

## Unpinned sites

The added production lines are the four `_OPT_FIELDS` names, the `if (v := getattr(...)) is not None` filter and the `dict.fromkeys(config, target)` setback.
- The four names are pinned by the value check above (the mutants).
- The setback line is pinned by the same check: without it, every arm reads [21.0, 19.5].
- The None filter is pinned by the existing `_G8Opt` checks, now with the four fields set to None. "And RECOVERY ends it" compares the exact four-key dict returned when away is off or recovering, so a filter that let None through would add four keys and fail it (reasoned from the exact-dict comparison; this one was not mutant-run).

## Null control

- **Away off** ("home" rows) and **recovery_active** ("recovering" rows) keep the configured pairs, [21.0, 19.5], in both the weekend and holiday arms. Check: `and away off, or recovering, keeps the configured weekend and holiday pairs (the null control)`. It passes at both the base and the head; under a fix that ignored the away state it would read [16.0, 16.0].
- Recovery deliberately keeps today's behaviour, which drops the setback wholesale. Whether it should is a design question for tvofi, not this fix.
- The harness's `weekend_away_off` row is unchanged between the base and the head (Sat 21.0).

## Figures

**Harness** `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_live_away_heating.py` (sha1 `822ccca27a2189754ee77e334e1e0544f8901191`; the probe's harness verbatim, committed here). Command: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_live_away_heating.py`. The rule is `diff` of the full output, base against head:
- Before (`cc930cdd1`): `arm=weekend ... comfort_sat=21.0`, `arm=weekend_flat ... comfort_sat=21.0`, `arm=holiday ... comfort_sat=21.0`, and `VERDICT weekend/holiday comfort REPLACES the away target (Sat 21.0 / 21.0 vs 16.0)`.
- After (`3ec79824c`): the same three rows read `comfort_sat=16.0`, and the verdict reads `keeps the away target (Sat 16.0 / 16.0 vs 16.0)`.
- `diff` returned exactly lines 6, 7, 9 and 13: those three rows and the verdict. Every other RESULT row (away, null_away_off, away_off_setpoint21, null_flat, indoor18, weekend_away_off, recovery) is byte-identical, including space slots, kWh and DHW. The null for this is the diff itself: a change touching any other row would have listed it.
- Space slots are 0 in the weekend and holiday arms at both ends. In this house the defect raised the comfort target and not the slot count (the probe's "extra space slots: none").

**Scoped gate.** `GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=cc930cdd1… PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub bash tests/run.sh` printed `MODE: SCOPED -- 22 script(s) run, 11 scoped out` and `24 TEST SCRIPT(S) PASSED; 10 SCOPED OUT AND NOT RUN`, exit 0. The scope comes from `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`.

**Goldens.** `tests/env_drift.py --all cc930cdd1…` reported `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 56 scenario(s) checked` and `NO STALE FIXTURE`.
- Rule: per-scenario lines in the env_drift section of the gate log.
- Of the 56, 37 printed `is byte-identical`, and every remaining one is a may-drift fixture printing `did not move here`.
- Neither claim file was touched, so no golden moved.

**Ratchet and architecture.**
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff cc930cdd1…`: `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`.

**ci_predict.** `python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --apply-inert` wrote `APPLIED inert_reads tests/harness_headers.py: dev/audit/harnesses/r10_live_away_heating.py` (commit `3ec79824c`), then `CI PREDICT: no closures, fast, governance or instrument red predicted`. The harness path is otherwise INERT by the `dev/audit/` prefix in `tests/closure.py`'s `INERT`.

**Class seams (fixer step 8).** The rule is an AST pass over `OptimizationConfig`, listing every `self.<attr>` read by `_comfort_pair`, `get_comfort_temp` and `get_temp_bounds`, the readers `_build_comfort_bounds` calls per step. It returned 15 fields:

| seam | disposition |
|---|---|
| `comfort_temp_day_weekend`, `comfort_temp_night_weekend`, `holiday_comfort_day`, `holiday_comfort_night` | closed in this diff |
| `comfort_temp_day`, `comfort_temp_night`, `min_temp` | already set back (unchanged) |
| `max_temp` | the ceiling. A setback lowers the target and the floor, and a ceiling above them buys no heat. Not part of the class. |
| `day_start_hour`, `day_end_hour`, `day_start_hour_weekend`, `day_end_hour_weekend`, `holiday_day_start_hour`, `holiday_day_end_hour`, `holiday_dates` | these only choose between the day and night value, and both are now the away target while away. Inert. |

Outside this class and not touched here: `coordinator._resolve_away` calls `get_comfort_temp(now.hour)` without `when` for the recovery target (probe report, code-chain step 4). That is the recovery design question below, not a setback seam.

## Red checks

None turned red on this branch. The predicted closures red for a new harness (`tests/harness_headers.py`) was repaired before the handoff with `ci_predict.py --apply-inert` (`ci-autofix.md`).

## Summary

Round 1 of PR #3013 (HOTFIX R10-HOTFIX-AWAY-SETBACK), reviewed at head `7e8c2248e6892e3484d5724fdb0a92155aae5b4f` from a detached worktree, against merge base `a9ba3022e32178c5fb4376b4f333be88544ce94d`. The role contract has no diff between the merge base and origin/main. The fix makes `away.solve_bands` set back the weekend and holiday comfort pairs when they are configured. The finder's harness is red at the base and green at the head. Every mutant I planted is killed, the null controls hold, and the per-step comfort class is closed.

`away.py` is code-owned, so `main-protect-checks` requires tvofi's approving review at merge. This verdict flags that and does not block on it.

merges.body:
R10-ARCH-DOCS-WIRING, arm A of triage P261 (dev/programme/triage/s6-batch52.md#P261). Refers to #2395, which stays open for arm B (R10-ARCH-DOCS). Part of #201.

What each brief item landed, and the design choice it encodes:

1. **Wiring test.** `tests/doc_claims.py` `named_element_findings` resolves what `docs/architecture.md` and `dev/README.md` name beyond a path. Each element is read in the artifact that defines it, never from a list kept in the test (fixer.md step 11):
   - a command's arguments: each one is a word of the script, e.g. `bus.sh push-verdict` or `heartbeat.sh --once`;
   - a `module.Symbol`, and a CamelCase class or `Class.method` in a diagram label naming a `.py` file: read through `ast`;
   - a check name `<stem> / <job> (<matrix>)` and the CI figure's job nodes: the job ids of the `.yml` that figure names, plus the job's `strategy.matrix` scalars;
   - a ledger kind, in the list under the ledger item or in a sequence-diagram note: the keys of `tools/audit/seat/ledger.py`'s `KINDS`;
   - a module list `a · b` in a diagram label: the package's modules;
   - a `services:` edge label: `services.yaml`'s keys.

   Arm W's paths, markers and mermaid predicates are unchanged. An element a `[target:]` marker covers (its unit, a heading, its diagram label, or the marked line listing a kind) is *pending*, not a finding. Under `[retired-by:]`, an absent element is what the marker states.

   Design choices:
   - A bare config-format name in prose (`pyproject.toml`) is not resolved, because the page also names Home Assistant's own files.
   - README.md is not read: it names the user's `configuration.yaml`.
   - An argument resolves as a word of the script. A renamed subcommand or flag is caught; a reworded help text is not.

2. **Target-marker resolver.** `marker_census` lists every marker with each named group's roster stage. It is due when every group it names is `done`.
   - `python3 tests/doc_claims.py --markers [--roster FILE]` prints the census, plus every pending element whose groups have all landed. It exits 1 while any marker is due.
   - The gate runs only its fixtures. Arm B makes the census hard.
   - Arm W's report-only note (c) now reads the census, so a marker naming one done and one not-started group is no longer reported as resolvable.

3. **P40.** `tests/card_browser.mjs` page mode records each page figure's PNG size and a digest of the page's visible element structure in `docs/img/card/pages.json` (HPO_PAGES_OUT). Every browser run then compares the live card to that record. `doc_claims.py` `check_card_figures` ties the record to the committed PNG headers and requires each light/dark pair to be one page.
   - Pixels are not compared. The committed plan figures (rendered on another machine) differ from this machine's render in 30-31% of pixels at identical size, so a pixel check would be a cross-machine check.
   - The 14 page figures are regenerated from one run. The advisor, savings and setup figures had changed height. `docs/index.html`'s declared advisor height follows (`check_image_dimensions`). The advisor alt text was checked against the new picture and still holds.
   - Not covered: the README hero (`card-plan-chart.png`, HPO_HERO_OUT) and the two generated SVGs (`make_card_figures.mjs`) are outside this record.

Carries moved here:
- Carry 1 (coffee button): already pinned by `check_coffee_button`, which R10-ARCH-DOCS-FIRST landed with a red case per placement and the light/dark token comparison. It is green at this head, so nothing was rebuilt.
- Carry 2: `resolveCited`'s canon lookup has not landed, so the `dev/README.md` entry stays and `corpus_excluded.json`'s `_comment` now carries its reason.

4. **Handoff repair: one kebab-word grammar.** `tools/pr/prepr.sh`'s agreement lane refused the earlier head 2352b3d28 with `UNREGISTERED "[a-z][a-z0-9-]*" in .claude/workflows/figure_lint.mjs, tests/doc_claims.py`. In doc_claims that shape was the diagram selector that sends a label's first segment to the job resolver. That was a second spelling of a grammar doc_claims already carries: `_ARG`'s bare-word arm, the lower-case kebab word. It is now named once, as `_WORD`, and both `_ARG` and the selector read it. figure_lint's copy is a different concept: a `gh` subcommand word passed to `gh <word...> --help`. Only the doc_claims copy was a duplicate, so nothing was registered in `agreement.mjs`.
   - Design choice: the selector stays lower-case kebab, not the workflow job-id grammar `[A-Za-z][\w-]*` that `agreement.mjs` registers for the jobs-block scan. Under the job-id grammar, `dev/README.md`'s sequence-diagram node `PUT` reaches the job resolver and is a false finding (mutant M8). The selector decides only which label is a job node; `job()` decides whether that job exists.
   - The clean fixture gains a `PUT` node, so the selector's case rule is pinned in the gate and not only by the live page.

5. **Handoff repair: doc_claims.py's closure.** The same prepr run refused `closures` as UNDER-SCOPED once agreement was clean. The doc-wiring arm opens each script the pages pass an argument to, and the workflows. The card-figure arm opens `docs/img/card/pages.json` and every page PNG. `./tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/doc_claims.py` printed 16 such files as `INERT ... actually read by tests` and exited 1: 13 under `docs/img/card/`, plus `bus.sh`, `cloud_relay.sh` and `heartbeat.sh` under `tools/audit/seat/`. They move to `tests/closure.py`'s `INERT_EXCEPT`, the route #2298 and R10-ARCH-DOCS-FIRST took. The re-record then exited 0 and added 21 paths to `tests/closures.json`: those 16, and 5 that were never INERT (`ledger.py`, `tests/gate_lock.py`, `tools/policy/rules_sync.mjs`, `ci.yml`, `tests.yml`).

Alternatives not taken:
- A new `tests/doc_wiring.py` script would split arm W from the predicates it shares (`_units`, `_MARKER`, `_FENCE`) and add a gate script to classify.
- Extending `brief_lint.mjs` lost too: it lints roster briefs and reads neither page.
- For the handoff repair, registering `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*` as `not-a-concept` would have cleared the lane but left doc_claims spelling its kebab word twice. Reusing `_CHECK_NAME`'s `[\w-]+` job atom, or the job-id grammar, lost to M8: either one turns `PUT` into a false finding.

## Head

`079fb16467219f6a46a8981ecf28c477c6d52ba3` merges the authored code head `fc907699e24dfbb28ae390fa26443c74303eb39e` and then merges origin/main `437f1ba9b` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

fc907699e24dfbb28ae390fa26443c74303eb39e (base cc930cdd1a3cfb005ba7ec557f4451ff5e53e364, origin/main at 2026-10-30T18:26Z). Main was merged into 2352b3d28, then two handoff-repair commits were added: the grammar (389c3baee), the closure record (75b30a4e28e8e5ee8573720043c31f570f1e345f) and the carry-1645 re-anchor (this head, fc907699e24dfbb28ae390fa26443c74303eb39e).

## Mutation proof

Each mutant was applied in turn to `tests/doc_claims.py` at the head, and `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components python3 tests/doc_claims.py` was run (rc=1 for each), then the file was restored byte-identical. The driver is a scratch probe; the replacements are quoted here.
- M1, argument predicate `None if any(word.search(read(h) or "") for h in hits) else` -> `None if True else`: FAIL `red fixture: a renamed subcommand is a finding`, FAIL `red fixture: a removed flag in a diagram node is a finding`
- M2, prose ledger-kind predicate `None if k in kinds else` -> `None if True else`: FAIL `the clean fixture resolves every class and leaves only the marked kind pending (null control)`, FAIL `red fixture: a removed ledger kind in a list is a finding`
- M3, `"due": all(v == "done" for v in st.values())` -> `"due": False`: FAIL `state tolerance: a marker naming a done group, and an absent retired-by path, yield only notes`, FAIL `red fixture: a marker naming a done group is due`
- M4, `if sizes[n] != want:` -> `if False:`: FAIL `red fixture: a figure regenerated without its record is a finding`
- M5, job predicate `if not block` -> `if False`: FAIL `red fixture: a removed workflow job in a diagram node is a finding`
- M6, `None if ms.group(2) in syms(` -> `None if True or ms.group(2) in syms(`: FAIL `red fixture: a removed class is a finding`
- M7, the diagram job selector `if flows and _WORD.fullmatch(segs[0]):` -> `if flows and False:`: FAIL `red fixture: a removed workflow job in a diagram node is a finding`
- M8, the same selector widened to the job atom: `if flows and re.fullmatch(r"[\w-]+", segs[0]):`. This FAILs three checks:
  - `every named element resolves in the artifact that defines it, or a marker covers it`: ``dev/README.md: job `ci / PUT` names no job of .github/workflows/ci.yml``
  - `the clean fixture resolves every class and leaves only the marked kind pending (null control)`
  - `a marked element that does not resolve is pending, not a finding (null control)`
- M1-M6 were taken at 2352b3d28. The merged delta touches none of their lines, since main's delta changes no path under `tests/doc_claims.py`, `tests/card_browser.mjs`, `docs/img` or the card frontend (`git diff --quiet 2352b3d28 HEAD~1 -- tests/doc_claims.py tests/card_browser.mjs docs/img custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/frontend && echo UNCHANGED` prints UNCHANGED). M7-M8 were run at this head.
- card_browser.mjs P40 is pinned in-run by `P40 red case: a figure one pixel taller than the page is stale; the run's own figures are not (null control)`, which calls the same `figureDrift`.

## Null control

- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components python3 tests/doc_claims.py` at the head: every check passes. `named_element_findings` returns no finding over the two pages, with every element class read (the anchor check names each class's count).
- The clean fixtures yield no finding. A marked unresolved element is pending, not a finding. A marker naming a not-started group is not due. A record matching its files is clean.
- `node tests/card_browser.mjs` (no HPO_PAGES_OUT), a second run after the writing run: `P40 every committed card page figure has the size and structure of the page this card draws` is ok, so the record reproduces on this machine. Cross-machine stability is CI's browser job's to show. Before regeneration, 8 of 14 committed figures from another machine had this machine's exact size.

## Figures

Each count is printed by `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components python3 tests/doc_claims.py` at the head unless the line names another command. The class counts and the marker census were re-taken at this head. The perturbation rows and the card-figure rows were taken at 2352b3d28 with the previous seat's scratch drivers, and are carried, not re-taken: main's delta touches none of their inputs (the UNCHANGED command under `## Mutation proof`). The handoff repair leaves the selector's verdict on both pages unchanged: `doc_claims.py`'s full output before and after the repair, at the merged tree, compared by `diff before.txt after.txt && echo IDENTICAL`, printed IDENTICAL.
- Agreement: `node tools/policy/agreement.mjs --only discovery` at 2352b3d28 merged with main and without the repair printed `UNREGISTERED "[a-z][a-z0-9-]*" in .claude/workflows/figure_lint.mjs, tests/doc_claims.py` (the null control). At this head it prints `RESULT divergent=0 unregistered=0 dead=0 refused=0` and `AGREEMENT ok`.
- Named elements checked, by class: the anchor line `every class of named element is read on these pages`. Rule: one count per `judge` call in `named_element_findings`, over the two pages. At this head: file 132, module 19, ledger kind 19, job 11, symbol 9, argument 6, service 3; findings 0, pending 5.
- Markers: the anchor line `the resolver reads every marker arm W reads`, plus `python3 tests/doc_claims.py --markers`. At this head, against the tree's roster copy: 25 of 28 due. Every due marker names a group whose roster stage is `done`. The 3 not due name R10-COP-GATE (in-progress) and R10-FLOW-TOOLKIT-MODEL (not-started).
- Perturbations of the real pages and artifacts, applied in memory, through `named_element_findings` (scratch driver). Null (head): 0 findings.
  - doc edits, each 1 finding:
    - `bus.sh push-verdict`->`push-verdicts`
    - `orchestrator_tick.py`->`orch_tick.py`
    - `heartbeat.sh --once`->`--one`
    - `tests / fast (3.14)`->`(3.13)`
    - CI node `gate`->`gates`
    - note `handoff-no-pr`->`handoff-no-prs`
    - `DhwPlanner`->`DhwPlaner`
    - module `sysid`->`sys_id`
    - service `simulate_plan`->`simulate_plans`
  - artifact edits:
    - ci.yml job `prelude`->`preamble`: 1 finding
    - `class InputReader`->`InputReading`: 2 findings, prose and diagram
    - gate_lock.py `needs-lease`->`needs_lease`: 1 finding
  - Removing `reviewer-fire` from `KINDS` yields 0 findings and moves it to pending, because the kind list is under `[target: R10-ORCH-MACHINERY]`. That is the case arm B makes hard.
- Card figures: a scratch canvas pixel diff, not in the tree, against the base's committed PNGs, after `HPO_PAGES_OUT=<scratch> node tests/card_browser.mjs`. Size mismatched: advisor 1056x616 -> 708, savings 158 -> 164, setup 552 -> 714, each in both themes. Size equal: tile, plan, plan-why, health. Pixels differing at equal size: plan 30-31%, plan-why 30%, tile 10-13%, health 80%.
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED. `python3 tests/entities.py`: ALL ENTITY CHECKS PASSED. `node tests/card_browser.mjs` at 2352b3d28: ALL BROWSER CHECKS PASSED, with both P40 lines ok. Its inputs are UNCHANGED since, by the command under `## Mutation proof`.
- Scope (at this head): `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` prints `MODE: FULL`, `reason: tests/closure.py changes the gate itself`. Run here: `tests/run.sh`'s four `run_always` lines (`env_drift.py --claims-only <merge base>`, `closure.py selftest`, `layout.py`, `harness_headers.py`), plus tests/doc_claims.py and tests/entities.py, which the diff edits or which pin it. Each exited 0. The rest is CI's. At 389c3baee, before the closure commit, the mode was `MODE: SCOPED -- 2 script(s) run`. `tools/pr/ci_predict.py --base origin/main`, at this head against cc930cdd1a3c: no closures, fast, wave-script or instrument red predicted. It says itself that it does not see a data-file read: doc_claims now reads docs/img/card/pages.json, the card PNGs, ledger.py, the workflows and services.yaml, so prepr.sh's `closures` step measured what ci_predict could not, and item 5 repaired it before the handoff.

## Red checks

`tests / briefs` was red at the previous head (75b30a4e28e8e5ee8573720043c31f570f1e345f): `dev/programme/carries/carry-1645.json` cited `tests/doc_claims.py:476` for `check_initial_setup_menu` and `tests/doc_claims.py:565` for `check_simulate_plan_fields`; this PR's two added imports (`collections`, `itertools`) shifted both, and `brief_lint` refused with "'check_simulate_plan_fields' not found near tests/doc_claims.py:476; found at line 570 instead".

Root-cause trigger (red-check, `defect-root-cause.md`): answered.
- Cause: a diff that moves lines in a file a carry cites by line number. A carry's `path:line` is data the code does not know it is.
- Process state: a check exists (`brief_lint`, CI job `briefs`) but prepr step 3f runs it only when a pinned path changed (`pinned_touched`), and `tests/doc_claims.py` is not pinned, so prepr skipped it ("no pinned path changed, so CI's briefs job reads this head's copy") and the first run reached CI to find it.
- Cheaper detector: a local `node tools/policy/brief_lint.mjs` before handoff (this round's step 2), or prepr step 3f extended to run when the diff touches any file a carry or roster `path:line` cites. Standing cost: one `brief_lint` run, about 2.5 minutes of one core on this machine, per handoff whose diff touches a cited file; the extension would add a carry-and-roster citation scan (seconds) to every prepr.
- Countermeasure decision: not built in this PR. It is a prepr change in a code-owned instrument, outside this group's seam; recorded here for the orchestrator to triage as a proposal (one occurrence so far; not yet a recurring class).
- Fix at this head: both citations re-anchored (476 to 479, 565 to 570); `node tools/policy/brief_lint.mjs` exits 0 and prints `carry-1645.json: 0 error(s), 0 warning(s)`. The ten remaining `ERROR` lines in its output are in wave-1 rosters and fixtures, cite wave-1 groups, not a file this diff touches, and do not fail the run (exit 0). The roster has no `tests/doc_claims.py:<line>` citation (grep of `handoff/audit-r10-roster` and this head's `wave-r10-groups.json`), so no edit-brief is owed.

## Forward-carry

- R10-ARCH-DOCS (arm B): the resolver at this head lists `stage-mismatch`, `absorb-edge-missing` and `record-owed` as pending under `[target: R10-ORCH-MACHINERY]`, which is `done`. None is a key of `tools/audit/seat/ledger.py`'s `KINDS`. They are a departure arm B resolves (redraw, or name the landed kinds). Re-measure with `python3 tests/doc_claims.py --markers --roster <the roster branch's wave-r10-groups.json>` at arm B's merge base. Carry: R10-ARCH-DOCS
- R10-ARCH-DOCS (arm B): `docs/img/card/health-light.png` and `health-dark.png` are now regenerated from the card. What remains of the carry naming them is the text: `docs/dashboard-card.md`'s Health alt text and the section's layout, COP, heat-loss and checklist sentences describe the old page. The regenerated picture also crops the checklist after its first item at the 860 px viewport. Carry: R10-ARCH-DOCS

merges.body:
R10-SAV-ACTUATION (#2492 carry 5, seam 2). The cycle wrote the pump's power switch once per optimization interval (30 min by default). A plan step's change therefore reached the pump only at the next cycle, as late as one interval past the step boundary, and a step's duty verdict in the arbiter's ledger depended on where the cycle fell against the 15-minute step grid. This PR writes the switch at the step boundary from a one-minute tick, and the ledger now reads the meter at each tick instead of the cycle's sample.

Refs #2492. Not closed here: one residue of the duty ledger is routed under Forward-carry to #2492.

## Re-cut

Round 4 under the three-round rule. The body is replaced. It carries the template's headings, the arms that fire, and only the figures re-taken in this pass. The block it answers is the fix review's `blocked` at `9fe3c4cf8`, `mutation-vacuous`. The reviewer's mutant R3 wires the step tick around `_write_supply`, the gate the cycle uses. It survived all 4617 checks of `tests/features.py`. This pass adds one case per gate arm. No production line changed: `git diff 9fe3c4cf81465123f5dc6b360a30df7631f75974 HEAD --stat` prints `tests/features.py | 74 +` and nothing else.

**Design (unchanged by this pass).**
- **Owning seam.** The switch's one writer stays `pump_arbiter.switch_supply`.
- **The gated write.** The coordinator's `_write_supply`, which both the cycle and the tick call, holds the gate. The gate has two arms: the early cut-off's `MIN_OFF` hold (`early_cutoff.allow_on`) and the blocked-mode OFF skip. The pure skip decision is `pump_arbiter.supply_write`.
- **The tick.** The tick is `pump_arbiter.supply_tick`. `pump_arbiter.note_supply` arms it once, from the cycle's write. It takes plain values, never the coordinator. `SupplyWiring` carries them: the `arbiter_inputs` builder, the boost record, and the gated write.
- **When the tick writes.** At a new step, the tick writes the step's command (`step_supply`) only where it differs from the last command.
- **The plan's switch rule.** `thermal_model.plan_step_runs` is its one owner.
- **The ledger's reading.** The ledger reads `pump_arbiter.live_power_kw` at each pass.

**The two cases this pass adds** are in `tests/features.py`, section "supply switch at step boundaries", in `_sa_gate_tick`. Each drives the REAL coordinator:
- 05:45: one `_apply_action` writes ON and arms the tick.
- 06:00: the armed tick fires at a step the plan turns off.
- 06:15: the armed tick fires at a step the plan turns on.
- Arm 1, the `MIN_OFF` hold. `early_cutoff.state_for(coord).cut_at` is set to 06:10, as `early_cutoff.on_room_event` records a cut. The check asserts the 06:15 tick writes no `turn_on`. Its null control is the same run with no cut on record, where the 06:15 tick writes `['turn_on']`.
- Arm 2, the blocked-mode OFF skip. `_pump_signals` is set to an observed mode with `space_heat=False, dhw=False`, so it blocks both channels. The check asserts the 06:00 tick writes nothing. Its null control is the same run in the default mode, which blocks nothing; there the 06:00 tick writes `['turn_off']`.

## Head

`efc415dc0832ca86e5c3b3065e189f3460c2cac1` merges main `a6e4a5a` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`343f2abcf7f5a4b0fc306591436496b4d04010fc`: the review's head `9fe3c4cf81465123f5dc6b360a30df7631f75974` plus one commit, which changes only `tests/features.py`. Merge base `89ccf73266a8dcfc0e8d4f45ad6583b0cb622db6`. `origin/main` was at `507a9ec264eb373b132248d752259254d8a9fa4d` (`date -u`: Fri Oct 30 13:00:29 UTC 2026). No merge was made: the handoff freezes the branch, and this pass is test-only.

## Mutation proof

Mutant R3 is the reviewer's own. I took the driver from `ev/mutant_driver.py` on `probe/rev-2968-5f6e06db` and changed only `HEAD` (to `343f2abcf`) and the scratch output directory. In `coordinator.py`'s `_apply_action`, the tick's `SupplyWiring(..., boost.held_for(self), self._write_supply)` becomes `lambda on: pump_arbiter.switch_supply(self.hass, getattr(self, "_ctx", self)._config.heat_pump_switch_entity, on)`. The driver asserts that the `str.replace` matches exactly once and applies it in a fresh detached worktree. It then runs the whole of `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` and removes the worktree.

- `python3 mutant_driver.py R3` prints `RESULT R3 rc=1 ['2 of 4621 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED']`:
  - `FAIL the step tick inside MIN_OFF of an early cut-off writes no turn_on at a step the plan turns on  [{'06:00': ['turn_off'], '06:15': ['turn_on']}]`

## Figures

- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` at `343f2abcf`: `ALL 4621 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` (rc=0), including the four new checks. The count rule is `R.check` calls run: `grep -c 'R.check(' tests/features.py` reads 4197 at `9fe3c4cf8` and 4201 at the head.

  - Every script in its three parallel lanes and `arch_score_head.py` printed `ok`: env_drift `--claims-only` and `--all`, validate, closure selftest, features, edge, backtest, boost_drift_replay, arch_score, optimality, plan_view, card.mjs, card_drift.mjs, entities, block_duty, doc_claims, wood_advisor, config_flow_steps, structure, typing_ruler, manual_plan, solar_alignment, guard_pins, debug_collect, finite_boundary, layout, deployment_shape.

Round 1 of review. The new step tick is a second actuator of the supply switch, firing between cycles. Its guards exist so that it does not override a command the plan did not give. Deleting any one of them leaves every check green. This head's checks pin the tick only in auto mode, with no boost, no experiment and a fresh plan.

Each mutant below also leaves `tests/features.py` fully green: its single red was `recorded_at = 'unknown'`, from a non-git copy in the first drive, and the null in a real worktree is clean. Each also leaves green `block_duty.py`, `boost_drift_replay.py`, `guard_pins.py`, `manual_plan.py`, `debug_collect.py`, `deployment_shape.py` and `finite_boundary.py` (`ev/closure_*.txt`, `ev/full_X*.txt`):

- X1 `pump_arbiter.py:1192` (step_supply: a live boost is on), with the branch body deleted. Path: the user presses boost on a step the plan keeps off, and at the next boundary whose plan command is off the tick writes OFF under a live boost.
- X2 `pump_arbiter.py:1190` (step_supply: a `system_identification` action returns None), deleted. Path: a step-response experiment's switch command is overwritten by the plan's at the first boundary where they differ.
- X3 `pump_arbiter.py:1188` (non-plan mode or stale plan returns None), narrowed to `inp.plan is None`. Path: comfort/boost/off modes, or a plan `_apply_action` refuses to actuate as stale, get the plan's switch written by the tick.
- X4 `pump_arbiter.py:1246` (`supply_tick`: `if inp.entry_released: return`), deleted. Path: a write after unload (#237 class).
- X5 `pump_arbiter.py:1279` (`release`: `release_supply(held)`), deleted. Path: the tick's interval listener outlives unload.

`grep -n 'supply_tick|step_supply|note_supply|release_supply|SupplyWiring|supply_write' tests/` finds no test reaching them, apart from one barrier reason string in `tests/entities.py`. The body's `## Unpinned sites` lists 1188/1190/1192/1246 GUARD_OFF (and others) as "pinned by `mutation-autofix`". That lane pins only killed mutants, and these survive, so the claim does not hold. They will surface as survivors, which `ci-autofix.md` forbids triaging automatically.

What would clear it: checks in the "supply switch at step boundaries" section, each a red under its mutant above:
- a live boost across a boundary whose plan step is off writes no OFF;
- a `system_identification` action is not overwritten at a boundary;
- a fixed mode, and a stale plan, write nothing between cycles;
- a released entry writes nothing;
- unload drops the tick.

Then re-run M1–M6 and these mutants.

## Findings

- No committed finder harness for carry 5 seam 2. The roster's carry (main `dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json`, group R10-SAV-ACTUATION) states the control in words: phase 0 vs 14 min with identical duty verdicts, plus one mutant per seam, and names no instrument. `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_sav_actuation_phase.py` is the fixer's own, and the body calls it "the owner's instrument for this carry" rather than disclosing it as the fixer's build (fix-review step 9). - The ledger residue the body forward-carries is real and is the larger part of the remaining misbooking. At the head the harness books every idle step that follows an ON step `space-instead`, at both phases: steps 1, 4, 7, 9 and 14 of `s-ss--s-s---ss-s`, so 5 of 16 verdicts are wrong. The base books 10 of 16 wrong at phase 0. The fix improves this but does not close it; the residue is phase-independent, so carry 5's control holds. Carry: #2492
- `coordinator.py` `_write_supply`'s `elif switch_entity:` GUARD_OFF survivor only logs. I agree it is equivalent in behaviour, but the body leaves the `survivor_triage` disposition to the reviewer, and it needs a recorded verdict rather than an implicit one. Carry: R10-SAV-ACTUATION

## Block

Review round 3 of PR #2968 (earlier blocks: `d26a00aa2` mutation-vacuous, `c4e9f6a3`/`ddf75aaf` ci-red). This review measured head `9fe3c4cf81465123f5dc6b360a30df7631f75974` from a detached worktree.

The PR says the tick goes through the same gate as the cycle. The design note says the gated write is `_write_supply`, "which both the cycle and the tick call". The `note_supply` docstring says "the tick passes the same cut-off hold and blocked-mode skip". The new `early_cutoff.py` module docstring says "a step the plan turns on passes :func:`allow_on` like the cycle's". No check holds that claim.

- Mutant R3 (mine): `coordinator.py`, in `_apply_action`'s `pump_arbiter.SupplyWiring(self.arbiter_inputs, boost.held_for(self), self._write_supply)`, replaces `self._write_supply` with `lambda on: pump_arbiter.switch_supply(self.hass, getattr(self, "_ctx", self)._config.heat_pump_switch_entity, on)`. The tick still writes at every boundary, but it no longer goes through `early_cutoff.allow_on` or `pump_arbiter.supply_write`.
  - The whole `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` prints `ALL 4617 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` (rc=0).
  - The mutation is one `str.replace`, asserted to match exactly once, in a fresh worktree (`ev/mutant_driver.py`, `ev/mutant_R3.res`, `ev/features_R3.log`).
- Why nothing fails: the only cut-off case, `an early cut-off holds across a step boundary the plan keeps on`, writes its cut with a direct `_sa_pa.switch_supply(hass, "switch.hp", False)` call. It never records an `early_cutoff` cut, so `allow_on` has nothing to hold. That check covers the tick's change-only rule (M3), not the gate.
  - No case drives the tick while the pump's signals block both channels or report cooling.
  - R1 (the gate removed inside `_write_supply`) is killed only by the cycle's check, `the coordinator's cycle inside MIN_OFF of a cut does not turn the switch on`.
- Consequence: the tick runs at every step boundary between cycles. If a later change wires it around the gate, the tick can turn the compressor back on inside `MIN_OFF` (10 min) of an early cut, or write OFF in a mode where the cycle skips OFF. No check would go red.
- What clears it: one `_sa_guarded`-style case per gate arm, driven through the real coordinator. Its null control is the same run with the gate inactive.
  - Arm 1: an `early_cutoff` cut recorded at 06:10, and a plan step turning ON at 06:15, inside `MIN_OFF`. Assert the tick writes no `turn_on`.
  - Arm 2: `_pump_signals` with both channels blocked (or cooling), and a step turning OFF. Assert the tick writes nothing.
  - Show R3 red on both.

## Findings

- The step tick's gate has no check of its own: mutant R3 (the tick wired around `_write_supply`) survives all of `tests/features.py`. This is the block above, owed by the fixer before the next handoff. Carry: R10-SAV-ACTUATION
- The duty ledger books the first reading of an OFF step after an ON step from the previous step's tail. Both phases book such a step `space-instead` at the head (`ev/harness_head.txt`). The control is phase independence, and it holds. A settle window on the ledger's run fold is still owed. The body routes it to #2492, which the PR leaves open (`Refs`). I confirmed the residue in the harness output. Carry: #2492

  - The unmutated head prints `ALL 4617 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`. The body says 4598; main's merge added checks.

  - Y2 (`note_supply`'s no-switch guard -> `if False:`): `1 of 4617`, on `an install with no supply switch arms no step tick ...`, as the body says.
  - M3 (`if on != last:` -> `if True:`): `3 of 4617`. It fails the two checks the body names plus the round-2 live-boost check, which was added after M3 was first measured.
  - M4 (the ledger reads `self._measured_power`): `1 of 4617`, on the phase-0/14 check, as the body says.
  - R1 (mine, `allow_on` dropped in `_write_supply`): `1 of 4617`, on the cycle's MIN_OFF check.
  - R2 (mine, `plan_step_runs` fallback ignores the hot-water draw): `1 of 4617`, on R9-F2.4 P2.

## Block

This is review round 4 of PR #2968. The earlier blocks were `d26a00aa2` (mutation-vacuous), `ddf75aaf8` (ci-red) and `9fe3c4cf8` (mutation-vacuous, R3). From this round, `fixer.md` ("Past three rounds, re-cut rather than repair") owes a re-cut under a `## Re-cut` note, not another repair. `bus.sh` refuses a later dispatch at 4 blocked rounds unless the orchestrator splits the PR, closes it, or passes `--past-three <reason>`.

What this round was asked to clear is cleared. Commit `343f2abcf` adds two gate cases and their null controls. Mutant R3 is the tick wired around `_write_supply`. At this head it goes red on both new checks: `2 of 4622`, on `the step tick inside MIN_OFF of an early cut-off writes no turn_on ...` and `the step tick writes nothing at a step the plan turns off while the pump's mode blocks both channels`.

The lane is green only because the survivor is under the cap, not because the site is killed.

What clears it is one of two things:

- a check, through the real coordinator, that this mutant turns red, such as a tick inside the same step that writes nothing and does not rebuild the inputs, or a boost ending mid-step that writes nothing before the boundary; or

After a payload-only re-dispatch (same prompt, other model), the next identical re-dispatch adds two commits and mints a new pin (ev/pin_attack.txt: "identical re-dispatch after model change pin: False"). merges.subject: Merge pull request #2989 from tvofi/fix/r10-fly-openpr-atomic-pr
merges.title: R10-FLY-OPENPR-ATOMIC: close a PR whose row push is refused, with a read-back comment saying why
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-FLY-OPENPR-ATOMIC (#2719, fly-in, lane F). `open_pr.sh` creates the PR on its first push (p1) and pushes the PR's own delivery row on its second (p2). When any step after p1 failed, the PR stayed open with no row. Now, once `N` is known, the EXIT trap runs `op_close_unrowed` first. This covers every exit before `PR_ATTEMPT=opened`: a refused row push, a step errexit stops (the title edit, `commit_row`, the head note), or a stop signal. That single path reaps the row push, returns the opener's worktree to the pushed head, and closes the draft. Only after the close succeeds does it post a comment, read back by `tools/pr/gh_comment.py`, that quotes the refusal or the `STOPPED` line (`open_pr: CLOSED: #N`). A close that fails prints `ROWLESS` and posts no comment, so `update_pr.sh`'s `ensure_row` can add the row later. The refused-row-push branch now only sets `OP_WHY` and exits; the old inline close is gone, so there is no second copy. `pr_args.sh`'s `pr_stopped` keeps its report in `PR_STOPPED_AT`, and the close quotes it. A conflicted `origin/main` merge is aborted and refused, so `pr_release_wt` removes the clean worktree.

Carries (roster group R10-FLY-OPENPR-ATOMIC, numbered as `review_packet.py` numbers them):
- Carry 1 (#2625/#2629, the rowless PR): closed in this diff, for every exit after the PR exists rather than only a refused row push. The self-test replays a refused row push, a failing title edit, and a row push that lands and then fails.
- Carry 2 (P-D, the exit-trap release): already on main (`pr_exit_trap` with `PR_TIDY` = `pr_release_wt`) and unchanged. `op_close_unrowed` runs before it in the same trap.
- Carry 3 (detach as the opener's last step): already on main. `pr_release_wt` runs in the EXIT trap after the last push, and this diff adds no push after it.
- Carry 4 (P71, default the Closes list from roster `fixes`): not in this diff. It needs `roster_lib` at the default ref inside the opener and can be done separately, so it stays on the roster.
- Carry 5 (P72, remove a clean worktree origin never had on REFUSE/STOPPED): already on main (`pr_release_wt`'s remove arm). This diff's merge-conflict arm exercises it.
- Carry 6 (V64, auto-open in `cloud_relay.sh`): not in this diff. It edits `cloud_relay.sh`, which is outside this group's files, and stays on the roster.
- Carry 7 (V141, delete a merged leftover branch): not in this diff. It touches `pr_args.sh`'s helper and `handoff_push.sh`, and stays on the roster. Until it lands, a re-run after a close opens from `fix/<topic>-pr`.
- Carry 8 (a conflicted main merge kept as dirty work): closed for `open_pr.sh`. The opener aborts its own conflicted merge and refuses. The `handoff_push.sh` seams are outside the group and stay on the roster.

## Re-cut

The row push can fail after its own `git push` has landed. `app_push.sh`'s `push_and_open` refuses a body PATCH or a read-back only after it has pushed, and a stop signal can arrive past the push. So, when `H` (the row commit) is set, `op_close_unrowed` first reads origin's branch tip with `git ls-remote`. It closes `#N` only when that tip is readable and is not `H`. When origin's tip is `H`, `#N` keeps its row and stays open. The run then exits non-zero and prints `open_pr: ROW LANDED: #N has its row on origin at <H>, but the row push then failed (exit status <rc>); #N is left open: <why>` (`op_row_landed`). A tip that cannot be read does not count as absent either, so `#N` is left open there too, with a `ROWLESS` line saying origin was not read.

## Re-cut

The body was replaced at round four (fixer.md, "Past three rounds"). The round-five review at `a11db7fe` was blocked: a row push that landed on origin and then failed closed a PR that had its row, with a comment saying the row was never pushed. That is closed here. Every figure below was re-taken in this pass.

## Re-cut

Round six repairs the red that round four's change caused. That change replaced the literal `pr_exit_trap 'python3 -I "$SEAT/ledger.py" attempt ...'` line with an `OP_LEDGER` variable. `ledger.py --self-test` builds its TERM fixture from the `open_pr.sh` lines that start with that literal, so it found only the `started` line. `r10_ledger_mutants.py`'s plant `O1_no_attempt_on_exit` anchors on the same literal, which then occurred zero times. The line is literal again. `pr_exit_trap` (`pr_args.sh`) now keeps its command in `PR_EXIT_FIRST`, and the second registration, made once `N` is known, is `pr_exit_trap "op_close_unrowed; $PR_EXIT_FIRST"`. So the opener has one attempt line on each exit path, and the O1 anchor occurs once. No ledger test was changed.

## Head

Issue #2719 sets the class: open_pr.sh must "close the draft with a comment saying why when a later step still fails". The body says "Closing is the smallest change that keeps every open PR with its row". The diff closes on only one later step: a refused row push (p2). The steps between creating the PR (p1) and p2 run under `set -Eeo pipefail` (`pr_trap`). These are `gh pr edit $N --title` (line 80), `commit_row` (81) and the head_note prefix (83-87). When one of them fails, the ERR trap stops the script, and the EXIT trap only writes the ledger, reaps the tree and releases the worktree. Nothing closes the PR. A stop signal at that point has the same effect. The body neither dispositions these sites nor names an enumeration rule.

Demonstrated at this head with the PR's own harness (patch in ev/demo-patch.txt). In the `rowless -` arm, the stub's `gh pr edit` exits 1 and p2 is allowed to succeed. The arm's later update_pr.sh is the only reason rowpushed=1 (ev/demo-edit-fails-state.txt, ev/demo-edit-fails-outo.txt). Fix: run the close-with-comment path for any non-zero exit after N is known, for example from the EXIT trap while PR_ATTEMPT is unset and N is set. Alternatively, disposition each site in the body.

## Block

`op_close_unrowed` (`tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh`) treats any non-zero exit of the `--row-only` push as "the row was not pushed". It closes the PR and comments `open_pr: CLOSED: #N ... before its row was pushed`. But `tools/pr/app_push.sh`'s `push_and_open` can exit 1 **after** `git push` has succeeded:

- `die "the body PATCH on #$num was refused; the branch IS pushed as the App ..."`
- `confirm_readback`'s `body`, `bad state=` and exhausted-budget refusals.

In each of those cases the row is on origin, so the PR is not rowless. The diff now closes a correct PR and posts a false reason. Before this diff the same seam only printed a false `ROWLESS` line and left the PR open with its row. So the diff turns a cosmetic error into closing a valid PR.

The body's class description ("a refused second (row) push, a step errexit stops between the two pushes, a stop signal") neither names nor dispositions this seam, and no enumeration rule is given. A stop signal that arrives after the push's `git push` has completed falls in the same seam.

The probe's own trailing rc=1 comes from a syntax error in my instrumentation line, not from the code under review.
