merges.body:
R10-ORCH-PLANPAGE, concern C of the R10-ORCH-MACHINERY re-cut. The plan page (`tools/audit/seat/plan_page.py`, landed by R10-PLAN-ARTIFACT #2558) gets three changes. `state_docs.py` now drives and publishes it. It fails to an explicit UNAVAILABLE page instead of writing nothing. And it carries the scratch generator's five defects as mutation-pinned self-test fixtures. Refs #2505. It does not close it: three of the group's carries remain residual and are listed under `## Forward-carry`. What changed: - **UNAVAILABLE page** (`plan_page.py`, `unavailable_page`, `_refuse`). Each refusal used to exit 1 and write nothing. A refusal is a stale plan, a plan `check_plan` refuses, a plan with no duration model, or an `origin/` roster ref that cannot be fetched. Each one now writes `

PLAN UNAVAILABLE —

` to `--html`, with every figure a dash and no table, and still exits 1. This is design 6.7 "How it fails", and carry 15 item 3 ("an UNAVAILABLE page in place of no page"). - **Driven by `state_docs.py`** (`--plan PLAN_JSON [--github-snapshot FILE]`, `draw_plan_page`). The page becomes `PLAN.html` in the same commit as `PLAN-TABLE.md` at `handoff/audit-r-plan`, and is mirrored with the other docs. When the page refuses: - if the state ref already holds a `PLAN.html`, that last good page is kept (it carries its own snapshot time); - if it holds none, the UNAVAILABLE page is published. Either way the other docs are pushed and the call exits 1. Without `--plan` the write set is unchanged. The beat runs no replan, so it never passes `--plan`. The sweep's record beat (`sweep_template.md` (4b)) now runs the replan and then `state_docs.py ... --plan`, instead of running `plan_page.py` by hand. Its pinned fragment is in `sweep_render.py` `DEFAULTS`. - **Five defect fixtures** (orch-machinery DESIGN.md S8 and 6.7, read at the approved design 09174d94e). The `.bak` files are out of tree. The pre-fix shapes are taken from the design's quotations of them (`gen.py.bak:4,148,89`) and from the live override shape it records. Each defect is one named self-test arm, plus one mutant in `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_plan_page_mutants.py` that restores the shape: 1. hardcoded override: every row's status is the roster's own stage; 2. scratch graph: the blockers are the roster's `after`, and the fixture scratch graph differs from it; 3. count from the wrong set: the open-issue count is the open set less #201, where `len(ISS) - 1` reads 3 on the fixture; 4. commit prefix as PR: no cell renders `#`; 5. two statuses: an `absorbed` group is not rendered done or delivered. - **Defect 5 needed a production change.** A group whose stage is in `roster_lib.DISPOSITION` used to fall through to `ready` or `blocked`. It is now its own class, `held`, in the label, pill, bar, strip, legend and filter. An absorbed group's label names its `absorbed_into` group, read at group level (the field R10-ROSTER-OPS owns; no roster carries it yet). Status is display state read from the roster, as `done` already is. The bars stay the plan's. - **Self-test robustness.** The fixture arms run inside one `try`. A mutant that crashes the renderer mid-arm now reports `the fixture arms ran to the end` along with the checks that failed before the crash. Without this, the defect-1 mutant was scored `CRASHED`, not killed. The diff stat (487+/203-) is inflated: the `try` re-indents the self-test body, about 190 lines, without changing it. Alternatives considered: - Leave a refused page as "nothing written" and let `state_docs.py` keep the old file. It lost because the first run would publish no page at all, which is the case 6.7 forbids, and a direct caller would see nothing at `--html`. - Map disposition stages to `ready` with a label. It lost because that is defect 5 in a new form: the text says one status and the class says another. - Have `state_docs.py` run `replan.py` itself. It lost because replan takes owner-set `--slots`/`--seats` from the sweep. The plan stays the caller's input, and the page refuses one that is stale. Each of the roster row's nine carries, by its index in the row (the brief's numbers 13, 15, 39 and 40 are the old R10-ORCH-MACHINERY group's numbering): - Carry 1 (STUDY K17; this group's part is 6): the page work extends `plan_page.py` and does not build a second page. The UNAVAILABLE page and the five mutation fixtures are kept. Rendering the flow section from the same model is residual, under `## Forward-carry`. - Carry 2 (from #2558): its precondition was re-measured at this merge base: 51 checks, 0 failed (`## Null control`). No shared builder with `plan_table.py` is built, because that premise is withdrawn. The out-of-tree `gen.py`/`tpl.html` retirement is the orchestrator's (`## Forward-carry`). - Carry 3 (item 3's premise): what it left for this stage is done here: driving the page from `state_docs.py`, the UNAVAILABLE page in place of no page, and the five generator-defect fixtures. - Carry 4 (`gen.py`/`tpl.html` retired once this merges): it has the same precondition, re-measured. The retirement itself happens out of tree, by design 8's N4 rule (`## Forward-carry`). - Carry 5 (the orchestrator.md line): the line is absent at the merge base, so nothing is edited (`## Forward-carry`). No standing seat's work moves into the orchestrator's turns: the page is drawn by the same `state_docs.py` call the record beat already runs. - Carry 6 (seam note: the Projected open issues section): kept unchanged. Its self-test arms still pass: `the issues chart is the first section, drawn from the open set`, and `no GitHub state: the chart is omitted with a note`. - Carry 7 (stamp cadence): residual. The count belongs in the replan's stamp planner, which the page then draws (`## Forward-carry`). - Carry 8 (the flow board is not a section of the page): still not met. It is residual and needs the orchestrator's ruling (`## Forward-carry`). - Carry 9 (the brief-versus-carry-3 contradiction): this PR again follows the brief. The board stays beside the page through `state_docs.py`, in the same commit. ## Head `92a57dd44cb9d137d6faa86a2fd281011c26d0d7` merges the authored code head `59598f9b783bff929b6c32a87bd34cd943b8d85d` and then merges origin/main `ca0a6cfbc` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head. dd93edd4316910b7362724692da2e1ad16cd9691, a fast-forward of the handoff a0abddcdf8de3ab983669b599c3a1d1d27770464: origin/main e77418f9b48f89421bd72b0ab511c057341c7fa4 merged in, then two repair commits (merge base e77418f9b48f89421bd72b0ab511c057341c7fa4, `date -u` 2026-10-30). Repair of open_pr's refusal: prepr's CI predict named `tests / closures` SELF-TEST READS INERT for `tools/plan/durations.json` and `tools/plan/replan.py`. `state_docs.py --self-test` (run by `tests/entities.py`) builds the plan page from the real roster, so it imports `replan` and opens `durations.json`: a real read, not an over-eager record. Re-classified rather than `--apply-inert` (which cannot clear a read the host really records): both go to `INERT_EXCEPT` in `tests/closure.py` and join `tests/entities.py`'s closure; the `tools/plan/` prefix stays INERT. The same record showed `tools/audit/seat/plan_page.py` read too (`closure.py merge` refused it), so it is excepted alike. The self-test is untouched. ## Mutation proof `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_plan_page_mutants.py` at the head. Each mutant is one exact replacement, restored byte for byte. The harness refuses a file with uncommitted edits. - New mutants, each killed with its FAIL lines: - `defect-1-hardcoded-override` (6 fails, among them `defect 1: every row's status is the roster's own stage` and `the fixture arms ran to the end`) - `defect-2-scratch-graph` (7, `defect 2: the blockers are the roster's after, never a scratch graph`) - `defect-3-count-wrong-set` (1, `defect 3: the open-issue count is the open set less the tracking issue`) - `defect-4-sha8-as-pr` (2, `defect 4: ...never #sha8`) - `defect-5-absorbed-as-done` (8, `defect 5: an absorbed group is not rendered done or delivered`) - `held-label` (2) - `unavailable-page-written`: deletes the write in `_refuse` (4, every refusal arm) - `unavailable-no-figures` (4) - `state-page-published` (1, `plan page: the first --plan call exits 0`) - `state-keeps-last-good` (1, `plan page: a stale plan keeps the last good page at the ref, exit 1`) - `state-unavailable-where-none` (1, `plan page: with no page at the ref, the UNAVAILABLE page is published`) - `state-unread-exits-1` (1) - The 19 pre-existing mutants are all still killed. - Final line: `RESULT survived=0`. - The harness now also runs the mutated file's own `--self-test`. For a `state_docs.py` mutant that is `state_docs.py --self-test`, whose comma-joined failure line the harness now counts as FAIL lines. ## Null control - At the merge base: `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/plan_page.py --self-test` prints `51 checks, 0 failed`, and the harness's `M0` prints `rc=0 fails=0 verdict=null`. This is the carry 15/39 precondition, re-measured at this merge base. The brief's 41 at fef4a1351 has since moved to 51. - The base self-test's own refusal arms pin "nothing written": `refused(...) == (1, False, True)`. That is the defect state 6.7 names. At the head the same arms pin `(1, True, True)` with the UNAVAILABLE page. - At the head, `M0` is null again, and a page that drew is checked not to be the UNAVAILABLE page. - In `state_docs.py`, `without --plan the write set holds no PLAN.html`. The pre-existing arms (write set exactly four docs, mirror exactly four files) pass unchanged. ## Figures - `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/plan_page.py --self-test` → `plan_page self-test: 60 checks, 0 failed` at the head, 51 at the merge base. The rule: one per `check(...)` evaluation. - `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/state_docs.py --self-test` → `state_docs self-test: all checks passed`. - `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_plan_page_mutants.py` → `RESULT survived=0` over its 32 entries (M0 plus 31 mutants), each with its verdict line. - Disposition-stage groups in the live roster. The rule is a stage in `roster_lib.DISPOSITION`, counted with `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools/audit/seat'); import roster_lib,json; r=json.load(open('dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json')); print(sum(1 for g in r['groups'] if (g.get('resume') or {}).get('stage') in roster_lib.DISPOSITION))"` → 11, all `carries-open`, at the merge base. These rendered `ready`/`blocked` at the base and render `held` at the head. The null control is `jq` over the same five words, which also gives 11. - `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` → `ALL 2484 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`. - `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff 507a9ec26`: `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run`, and `scope.run` names `tests/entities.py`. The `run_always` lines passed: `tests/env_drift.py --claims-only` (`claims hygiene: ... ok`), `tests/closure.py selftest` (`ALL 117 closure shrink pins PASSED`), `tests/layout.py` (`layout self-test: ok`) and `tests/harness_headers.py` (`ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`). - `python3 tests/structure.py` → `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`. - `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff 507a9ec26` → `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`. - `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/sweep_render.py --self-test` → `sweep_render self-test: 24 checks, 0 failed`. - Repair, rule: the INERT-vs-read pair is what `python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --only self-test-reads --record-self-tests` prints. Before: 2 PREDICT lines (durations.json, replan.py). After: `bash tools/pr/prepr.sh` → `ci predict ... no closures, fast, wave-script or instrument red predicted` and `PRE-PR: dd93edd4... rc=0` at this head. - Repair, recording: `tests/derive_closures.sh --single tests/entities.py` exited 1 because the one failing check was `every tracked file is either measured or deliberately classified` naming exactly durations.json and replan.py (all other `FAIL` lines in the log are planted null controls inside passing checks). Recorded with `--record-only --out-dir`, then `closure.py merge --partial --allow-failures` (the tool's documented two-step), which added three files to the closure (plan_page.py, durations.json, replan.py). The recorded `rc` was then restored to 0, because the same script re-run on the merged closure prints `ALL 2488 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` (null control: the same run before the merge printed `1 of 2488 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`). The recording was made on Linux in this container, not CI's canonical host; CI re-records `closures`, and `prepr` skips its closures step as unscoped (`tests/closure.py` changed). - `python3 tests/structure.py` at this head → `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`. `git log --format=%B origin/main..HEAD | grep -ci "claude\|co-authored"` → 0. ## Red checks none ## Unpinned sites Every production site this diff adds in `tools/audit/seat/plan_page.py` and `tools/audit/seat/state_docs.py` is pinned by the in-tree mutant harness `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_plan_page_mutants.py`. The `mutation-autofix` lane mutates `custom_components/` only, and this harness is the site's in-tree mutant harness under `fixer.md` step 2. The mutant names are under `## Mutation proof`. ## Forward-carry - **The replan schedules disposition-stage groups as open work.** `tools/plan/replan.py` `is_done` is `("done", "rca-done")`. The 11 `carries-open` groups at the merge base therefore get a duration and a bar, while the page now names them `held`. Whether a disposition is schedulable is the roster schema's and the planner's call, not the page's: the page draws the plan's bars unchanged. Carry: R10-ORCH-ROSTER-SCHEMA - **Stamp cadence (carry 7) is not built here.** Planning a stamp after about 3 merged production groups is `replan.py` `build_plan`'s stamp logic (`stamp_every`). The count shown on the page should be a field of the plan JSON replan writes that the page draws, because the page draws and does not plan. Built in the page, it would be a second answer. Carry: R10-ORCH-PLANPAGE (residual: lands with the replan stamp change, then one page row) - **The flow board as a section of the page (carries 8, 9 and 13(6)) is not built.** The board's model is `merge_throughput.py`'s `board(ctx)`, built from git history. Item (3)'s shared-model premise was withdrawn by carries 15 and 39, so there is no "same model" to render it from. The flow board document stays beside the plan page at the same ref, in the same commit. Carry 9 records the contradiction between the brief and carry 3; it needs the orchestrator's ruling. merges.body:
R10-FLY-GH-READ-RETRY carry 7, from triage w71's #2859 diagnosis: `tools/ci/ghapi.py`'s `get` retried a 5xx answer and let every transport failure through, so prelude at head 5135f0658 (run 40292248220, job 121469803963, step "Derive kind, PR, base, scope and legs") went red on one `http.client.IncompleteRead(0 bytes read, 48262 more expected)` out of `r.read()`. The same job was green twice at the next head. Every `tools/ci` module reads GitHub through `ghapi.get` (each glue binds it: `gate.py`, `prelude.py`, `codescan_wait.py`, `alert_list.py`), so this one seam covers all of them.

The fix: `TRANSPORT` = (`URLError`, `http.client.HTTPException`, `ConnectionError`, `TimeoutError`), which is `gh_read.urllib_wait`'s transport set. A GET retries a TRANSPORT failure on `RETRY_5XX`'s backoffs, just as it retries a 5xx, and raises the last failure once the budget is spent. A POST is never retried. A rate limit still raises `RateLimited` at once, and every other exception raises at once.

Alternatives considered:
- (a) Import `gh_read.retry`. Refused: contract item 2 makes `ghapi` the only urllib module under `tools/ci`, stdlib only, so it cannot import `tools/audit/seat`. Its 5/15/45 s schedule would also replace the (2, 6) schedule that P2 step 11a chose for gate latency.
- (b) Catch the error in each caller. Refused: that makes five copies of one concern.

Part of #2731.

The group's carries, at roster origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster 78c0bb77b. This diff is carry 7 alone:
- Carry 1 (PR 3, pr-contract.yml's body read): not here. That file is code-owned, and the carry gives it a PR of its own.
- Carry 2 (the App JWT curl GET and the carry path's `git fetch`): the JWT read landed in #2639. The `git fetch` is carry 5's.
- Carry 3 (PR 1's proof), applied to this diff's retry loop:
  - (a) Spent budget: the persists arms queue 4 transient failures for a 3-call budget, so only the budget stops them.
  - (b) Census: every member of TRANSPORT goes through the production `get` by an input it must retry. The near-misses it must refuse are a non-transport `ValueError` (1 call) and a 404 answer (1 call).
  - (c) Classifier alternatives: TRANSPORT is a 4-member tuple, not a regex. Each member has its own mutant (`ghapi-5`..`ghapi-8`), so the alternatives are enumerated in full by construction rather than by a source-reading rule.
  - (d) Sweep: no rule-generated sweep. The 7 mutants cover the arm, each member, the raise once the budget is spent, and the retry loop.
- Carry 4 (a spent hourly bucket waits for its reset and never loops): already true of `ghapi`, unchanged here. A rate limit raises `RateLimited` with `reset_epoch` before the 5xx/transport loop, and the `rate limit raises` arms still pass.
- Carry 5 (git fetch/push transport, 15 seams): not here. It needs its own classifier, written against measured git stderr.
- Carry 6 (`r10_codescan_wait_race.py` `pages()` per_page=100 502): not here. `pages()` reads through `ghapi.get`, which already retried that 502 twice, and the read failed 3 times. The fix it needs is a smaller page.
- Carry 7: this diff.

## Head

`c3413ae71659f835dcf44d19fa54c6b76b668efd` merges main `cc930cd` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

Body only: the get_rest forward-carry now names its roster destination (carry 1 at 5a8c3e64). Head unchanged at edf1cba7cda43790435d1d4b5aa1b3b24562912a.

`edf1cba7cda43790435d1d4b5aa1b3b24562912a` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/2995.md`. The authored code head is `0c66226e6ab85205f1ce69d2c9184181b3889c1f`.

`9fa53c46e23e15fd14985e4d28acd316df6b27b2` merges origin/main `e77418f9b` into the authored code head `0c66226e6ab85205f1ce69d2c9184181b3889c1f` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below).

0c66226e6ab85205f1ce69d2c9184181b3889c1f, on merge base 507a9ec264eb373b132248d752259254d8a9fa4d (origin/main's tip when measured, 2026-10-30).

## Mutation proof

The mutants are in the tree, in `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py` as `ghapi-4`..`ghapi-10`. Each one changes the predicate: the `except TRANSPORT` arm, each of the four TRANSPORT members, the raise once the budget is spent, and the retry loop itself. Run with `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py ghapi-1 ghapi-2 ghapi-3 ghapi-4 ghapi-5 ghapi-6 ghapi-7 ghapi-8 ghapi-9 ghapi-10`, which ends `RESULT survivors=0`. Every mutant is KILLED by a named FAIL, not by a crash. The FAIL lines:
- ghapi-4 (`except ():`): 8 failed, `a truncated read then a 200 on a GET answers the 200`, `... that persists raises the last failure after two retries` (got 1, want 3), the same pair for reset mid-read, timeout mid-read and connection reset.
- ghapi-5 (no URLError): `a connection reset then a 200 ...`, `a connection reset that persists ...`.
- ghapi-6 (no HTTPException): the truncated-read pair.
- ghapi-7 (no ConnectionError): the reset-mid-read pair.
- ghapi-8 (no TimeoutError): the timeout-mid-read pair.
- ghapi-9 (never raise after the budget): `<each of the 4> that persists raises: got 'returned', want 'raised'`.
- ghapi-10 (one try): 12 failed, including the pre-existing `a 502 then a 200 on a GET answers the 200` and `a 5xx that persists is returned after two retries, not looped`.

## Null control

At the base, the new self-test arms run against the base `get`. The control is built by splicing the merge base's `ghapi.py` up to `def self_test` with the head's `self_test`. It prints `ghapi self-test: 32 checks, 8 failed`, and the 8 are exactly the transient and persists arms of the four failures. At the head the same self-test prints `32 checks, 0 failed`. The self-test's own null controls hold at the head:
- a non-transport `ValueError` raises after 1 call;
- a 404 is not retried (1 call);
- each transport failure on a POST raises after 1 call.

## Figures

- `python3 -I tools/ci/ghapi.py --self-test`: `ghapi self-test: 32 checks, 0 failed` at the head (19 checks at the base).
- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py ghapi-1 ghapi-2 ghapi-3 ghapi-4 ghapi-5 ghapi-6 ghapi-7 ghapi-8 ghapi-9 ghapi-10`: `RESULT survivors=0`.
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff 507a9ec264eb373b132248d752259254d8a9fa4d --workdir "$D"`: `MODE: FULL`, reason `tools/ci/ghapi.py changes the gate itself`. I ran the run_always lines (`tests/structure.py`, `tests/closure.py selftest`, `tests/layout.py`, `tests/env_drift.py --claims-only origin/main`), `tests/entities.py`, and every `tools/ci/*.py --self-test`. All exited 0. The rest is left to CI.
- `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff 507a9ec264eb373b132248d752259254d8a9fa4d`: `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`.
- Class seams. The rule `git grep -n "urlopen(" -- tools dev/audit/harnesses .github` enumerates every urllib opener in the instrument trees. Each seam it returns, with its disposition:
  - `tools/ci/ghapi.py` `_open`: closed in this diff.
  - `tools/audit/seat/record_row.py` `urlopen` read: already guarded by `gh_read.retry` / `gh_read.urllib_wait` (#2639). The second hit is its self-test stub.
  - `tools/release/stamp.py` `get_rest`: an unretried GitHub REST read, open, carried to R10-FLY-STAMP-CHECK-NOTES (the live group owning that file).
  - `tools/release/stamp.py` `tests_gate`'s dispatch: a POST, outside the read rule.
  - `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_main_gate_replay.py`: a one-shot replay harness's read, open, and dismissed below: no live group owns it.
  - `dev/audit/harnesses/d6_page_anchors.py` `check`: fetches a documentation page given on its command line, not the GitHub API. Outside the class.
  - Reads through `ghapi.get` are covered by this diff for transport, including `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_codescan_wait_race.py`'s `pages()`. That harness's persistent per_page=100 502 is carry 6, which stays open (a later retry does not ride out a page-size 502).

## Red checks

none

## Forward-carry

- `tools/release/stamp.py` `get_rest` is the stamp's rule-2 REST source: one urlopen with no retry and no classifier (`git grep -nE "retry|urllib_wait" -- tools/release/stamp.py` names no read retry), so one transient read refuses a stamp. It is the class's seam outside this diff. Control: the same `urlopen(` enumerator returns `record_row.py`'s read already behind `gh_read.retry`. Brief to carry: put `get_rest` under `gh_read.urllib_wait`'s classes, failing test first (one transport error then an answer passes in 2 calls, a 404 refuses in 1, a spent budget refuses naming the last failure); `tests_gate`'s dispatch is a POST and stays out. Re-run the enumerator at that group's merge base. Written as the group's carry 1 (of 1) on `handoff/audit-r10-roster` at 5a8c3e6434a4b14a576bac280319b02086849d66, with this control and re-measure instruction. Carry: R10-FLY-STAMP-CHECK-NOTES

Carry: dismissed: a one-shot replay harness of a finished group; #2731, the class's issue, has no live roster group (R10-FLY-GH-READ-RETRY reads done at origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster 78c0bb77b while #2731 is open), so no destination exists; routed to the orchestrator in this handoff's result

merges.title: R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE part 3: park a base-policy refusal with its read reason; record-PR sweep on refusal and after a critical-path entry
merges.author: hpo-author[bot]
merges.body:
R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE part 3 (#2725), parts (1) and (2) of the brief: carries 1, 2, 3, 11b, 15 (refusal handling) and 13, 18 (record-PR sweep) in `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py`. Part (3), carries 7 and 10, is the remainder (`## Forward-carry`).

What the train does differently:

- **Policy refusal (carries 1, 2, 3; #2577, P4 s4).** On "the base branch policy prohibits the merge", `Train.policy_refusal` reads `gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup` against the head's required contexts. The whole refusal and the read reason are logged. A required context still pending, or a state it cannot read, retries as before. A red required context, a missing review, or BLOCKED with every required context green **parks** the car with `[BRANCH-POLICY]` and that reason after that attempt. The text starts `not merged after <k> attempt(s)`, so `at_head`'s #2290 recovery still recarries one whose head main has moved past.
- **Approval carry widened (carry 2, step 2).** A refusal an approval can answer (REVIEW_REQUIRED, or BLOCKED with every required context green) is offered, once, to `_carry_owner_approval`. Its conditions are unchanged: `--approval-carry`, a clean recarry, no branch-own file in h0..h, a prior owner APPROVED review citing one mandate, the mandate re-read in force at the merge, and a byte-identical read-back. Each refusal now leaves its reason in `item["carry_refused"]`, and the park names it.
- **P34 (carry 3).** The head wait reads the required set with `pr_head=True` inside `Train.serial`, the one path every serial head wait goes through (`one`, `one_overlap`, the batch's serial entries). The `req` parameter of `one` and `one_overlap` is gone, so no caller can hand a head wait main's set. This replaced a first cut that passed a second variable from `_batch`. That cut's mutant survived (`## Mutation proof`, M11), and the seam is the better fix (fixer.md step 17). At the merge base `PR_ONLY` is `()` (9262e6f43, the umbrella `gate`), and `gate.py` `REQUIRED["pr"]` holds `pr-contract`. So on today's ruleset a red pr-contract already reads as a red `gate`. This change makes the head wait independent of what `PR_ONLY` holds.
- **P231 (carry 15).** `sweep_bots` keeps `gh pr merge`'s output. A refused record PR now logs `BOT #<n> not merged at <h8> (<state>) refused: <gh's last non-empty line, up to 200 chars>`. `sweep_bots` returns the merged PR's number, else None.
- **P191 (carry 18).** After a refused attempt that is not BASE_MOVED, under `--bot-prs`, `land` sweeps once per landing. A record PR merged there raises `MainMoved('merge', 'the record PR #N merged under the batch')`, which the existing recovery recarries. No sweep runs on beats, and `add` still refuses the record branch.
- **P289 (carry 13).** A critical-path entry skips the sweep before its recarry, and `serial` sweeps after its merge (or when it stops). A batch holding one skips the sweep before reading its base and sweeps after its merges, before its serial entries. Critical path = `roster_lib.group_for_branch` on the entry's branch, checked against `roster_lib.critical_path_groups` at `roster_lib.reader_ref`, read once per run. Anything unread is nothing critical, which is today's order. `Train(critical=...)` takes a fixture reader, and both self-test drivers default it to "nothing critical", so no fixture reads the live roster.
- **P184 (b) (carry 11b).** `freeable` frees a clean holder whose HEAD is origin/<branch> or an ancestor of it (`git -C <holder> merge-base --is-ancestor`). A HEAD with commits origin lacks refuses with `has commits origin does not have`. HEAD or origin unreadable refuses as before. Keyed on commits, never a path.
- **P184's second caller, `queue_pre_flight` (round 2).** `PreFlight.worktree_holder` calls `Train.freeable` under the train's `--free-holders`. Its self-test stub answered every `merge-base` argv rc 0, so the new ancestor probe read the unpushed holder (HEAD 1.., origin 2..) as behind origin and passed it. The stub now answers `--is-ancestor` rc 1 unless the world says `behind`. A twin arm pins that a clean holder behind origin/<branch> passes, mirroring merge_train's P184 pair. The module docstring's `worktree` line now says `or an ancestor of it`.
- **Three policy survivors pinned (round 2).** The fix review's new survivors each get an arm in `merge_train`'s self-test. (a) A second approval-class refusal after a carried approval parks after attempt 2 with exactly one `approved (carry)` line. (b) A required context reading SKIPPED, or NEUTRAL, with a missing review parks at once as green rather than pending. (c) `--ignore`'d `nightly-status`, required and red, parks nothing: the running `fast` waits and the next attempt merges.

Alternatives not taken: a separate approval path for the policy class. It lost because carry 2 says to widen the existing carry under the same conditions, and a second path would be a second writer of the concept (fixer.md step 17). Parking on every policy refusal lost too: the pending-check case is the review-run race `review_settle` exists for (P86), and parking there would stop entries that merge one attempt later.

Closes nothing: #2725 stays open for part (3).

## Head

`ce7b452adf5353c8f7ea3a7f3de41ba7b28cb8dd` merges main `ca0a6cf` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`b173995ad456981d0736b74066126207f16949aa` merges the authored code head `ee438e5d173eac96f8ded452b1fa80fcc1f6bcad` and then merges origin/main `e77418f9b` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`d6300a3085dfdcca079f02e89533b7ae55758201` merges the authored code head `ee438e5d173eac96f8ded452b1fa80fcc1f6bcad` and then merges origin/main `e77418f9b` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

Measured at ee438e5d173eac96f8ded452b1fa80fcc1f6bcad, pushed to `handoff/r10-train-overlap-grade-p3`. It is one commit on the round-1 live head e456ff01323580d4390f964483a17dbdb6cff5bf. The merge base is 507a9ec264eb373b132248d752259254d8a9fa4d. origin/main was e77418f9b48f89421bd72b0ab511c057341c7fa4 at 2026-10-30 13:56Z, and `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0 there, so main was not merged (fixer.md step 6).

## Mutation proof

Each mutant is applied to a copy of the head's `merge_train.py` beside it, by an exact single-occurrence string replace, then `python3 <copy> --self-test` is run (driver: `$SCRATCH/mut.py`, a one-off probe, not in the tree). Every arm's mutant is the base's behaviour at that site.

- M1, policy park off (`if BRANCH_POLICY_SAID.search(said):` -> `if False:`, the base's loop): 7 failed. These are `policy refusal with a required context red ...`, `... still running waits ...`, `... missing review, no --approval-carry ...`, `carry 2: a policy refusal ... answered by the approval carry ...`, and the three `carry 2 null (...)` arms.
- M2, carry delta check dropped (`if own:` -> `if False:`): 2 failed, `approval-carry MUTATION (the diff-empty check)` and `carry 2 null (names branch-own)`.
- M3, live mandate read dropped (`if not live:` -> `if False:`): 2 failed, `approval-carry MUTATION (the mandate in-force check)` and `carry 2 null (is not in force at the merge)`.
- M4, park's carry off (`if approval and not carried:` -> `if False:`): 5 failed, the four `carry 2` arms and `... missing review, no --approval-carry ...`.
- M5, P231 text dropped from the BOT line: 1 failed, `P231: a record PR GitHub refuses logs ...`.
- M6, P191 sweep dropped (`bot = self.sweep_bots()` -> `bot = None`): 3 failed, `P191: a refused attempt with a record PR now green ...` and both `P191 null (...)` arms (they count the sweep).
- M7, P289 skip off (`if self.bot_prs and self.critical(item):` -> `if False:`): 2 failed, `P289 serial: a critical-path #7 merges, then the record PR, then #8` and `P289 serial, a critical-path entry alone ...`.
- M7b, the brief's mutation, skipping the sweep for every entry (`-> if self.bot_prs:`): 4 failed, among them `P289 serial: null, nothing critical: the record PR merges FIRST, as today` and the existing `--bot-prs: the open record PR ... merges FIRST`.
- M8, P289 batch (`cp = ...` -> `cp = False`): 1 failed, `P289 batch: with a critical-path entry the proof is built without the record PR ...`.
- M9, P34 (`req = self.required(pr_head=True)` in `serial` -> `self.required()`): 1 failed, `P34: pr-contract failure at the head (stops at ci naming it, no merge attempt)`.
- M10, P184 ancestor (`if here != there and not self.ok(... --is-ancestor ...):` -> `if here != there:`): 1 failed, `P184 --free-holders: a clean holder whose HEAD is an ancestor of origin/<branch> is freed ...`.
- M12, P289 post-merge sweep dropped: 1 failed, `P289 serial, a critical-path entry alone: the record PR still merges, after it`. With two entries, the next entry's recarry sweep masks this mutant, which is why the single-entry arm exists.
- S1, round 2 (`if approval and not carried:` -> `if approval:`): 1 failed, `carry 2: a second policy refusal after a carried approval parks without a second carry`.
- S2, round 2 (the green set `("SUCCESS", "SKIPPED", "NEUTRAL")` -> `("SUCCESS",)`): 2 failed, `policy refusal with the required context SKIPPED ...` and `... NEUTRAL ...`.
- S3, round 2 (`n not in self.ignore and ` dropped from `red`): 1 failed, `policy refusal null (--ignore): an ignored red required context parks nothing; ...`.
- Q1, round 2: queue_pre_flight's `--is-ancestor` stub is removed, which restores the round-1 fixture. Run with `python3 tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py --self-test`: `44 checks, 1 failed`, `... and one whose HEAD is not origin/<branch> still PARKs (unpushed work)`. This is the CI red, reproduced.
- Q2, round 2: M10 is applied to `merge_train.py`, then queue_pre_flight's self-test is run: `44 checks, 1 failed`, `... and one whose HEAD is an ancestor of origin/<branch> passes (P184: nothing origin lacks)`. The new twin arm reads `freeable`'s ancestor probe through the second caller.
- M11, from the first cut (`head_req = self.required(pr_head=True)` in `_batch` -> `head_req = req`): **survived**, 0 failed. Answered by removing the variable: the head set is now read in `serial` itself, where M9 kills it for the batch's serial entries too.

Baseline for every mutant: the unmutated head. It prints `merge_train self-test: 380 checks, 0 failed` and `queue_pre_flight self-test: 44 checks, 0 failed`. M1-M12 were run in round 1 against the 376-check head, and the fix reviewer re-ran them at e456ff01. Round 2 re-ran M10 at this head: 380 checks, 1 failed.

## Null control

- Policy: an unreadable merge state retries three times and stops `[BRANCH-POLICY] not merged after 3 attempts`, as today (`policy refusal null: ...`). The pre-existing `every refused merge attempt is logged ...`, `#2290 shape` and `... while the same refusals on a head that still contains main stop as before` arms pass unchanged.
- Carry: the three null worlds (a conflict-resolution delta, a prior review by the `hpo-approver` App, a mandate past its window) each park after one attempt naming their reason, with no `approved (carry)` line.
- P34: the same car with pr-contract green merges.
- P231: the existing `--bot-prs ... merges FIRST` arm still logs `BOT #9 MERGED`.
- P191: no open record PR (lookup 0), and a record PR still pending, each run three refused attempts with no MAIN-MOVED. Pending logs `BOT #9 pending` twice. Without `--bot-prs` nothing is looked up.
- P289: nothing critical merges the record PR first, serial and batch (the existing batch arm `batch --bot-prs: the record PR merges before the base is read` passes unchanged).
- P184: a holder at origin's tip is freed as today. A holder ahead of origin refuses. Without `--free-holders` nothing is detached. In queue_pre_flight the same three worlds hold: at origin's tip it passes, ahead of origin it PARKs, and without `--free-holders` the holder PARKs.
- S3's arm is itself a null control. Nothing red at the head parks, and the arm fails exactly when the ignore filter is dropped.

## Figures

- Self-test, merge_train: `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` prints `merge_train self-test: 380 checks, 0 failed` at the head. In a worktree at the merge base 507a9ec2 the same command prints `merge_train self-test: 355 checks, 0 failed`. At round 1's head e456ff01 it prints `376 checks, 0 failed`. The difference is checks executed, not call sites. `git diff 507a9ec2... HEAD -- tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py | grep -c '^+.*check('` prints 19 call sites, and some of them sit in loops.
- Self-test, queue_pre_flight: `python3 tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py --self-test` prints `queue_pre_flight self-test: 44 checks, 0 failed` at the head. At e456ff01 it prints `43 checks, 1 failed`, the CI red. At the merge base 507a9ec2 it prints `43 checks, 0 failed`. The same diff command on this file prints 1 added call site.
- Gate scope: `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff 507a9ec264eb373b132248d752259254d8a9fa4d --workdir "$D"` prints `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out`. It names `tests/entities.py`, and the 4 changed files are listed. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` prints `ALL 2484 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`.
- `run_always` lines: `python3 tests/env_drift.py --claims-only 507a9ec2...` exits 0, `python3 tests/closure.py selftest` exits 0 and `python3 tests/layout.py` exits 0. `python3 tests/harness_headers.py` prints `ALL 112 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py` prints `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`. Every metric is within budget and none was re-recorded.
- `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff 507a9ec264eb373b132248d752259254d8a9fa4d` prints `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`. The diff reaches no file the score reads, so no gain is claimed.
- Class rule, step 8. The instances are train logs on the orchestrator's host, not in the tree, so there is no finder harness to re-run, and the self-test fixtures model each instance. Let E be the line of `def _self_test` in merge_train.py.
  - Merge sites: `awk 'NR<E && /"gh", "pr", "merge"/' tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py` lists every production site that merges a pull request, and returns 2. `land`'s loop is closed in this diff (carries 1-3, 18). `sweep_bots` is closed (carry 15).
  - Head-set reads: `awk 'NR<E && /\.required\(/'` returns 3 sites. `serial` reads pr_head=True, closed here. `policy_refusal` reads pr_head=True, new. `_batch` reads main's set for `main_green`, `admit` and `settle`. `admit` is the distinct seam carried below. The CLI's `t.required(pr_head=not a.main)` in `main` is already right.
  - Sweeps: `awk 'NR<E && /self\.sweep_bots\(\)/'` returns 6 sites. `recarry` and `_batch`'s pre-base sweep are closed (P289 skip). Four are new: `serial` after the merge, `serial` on a stop, `_batch` after the merges, and `land` on refusal (P191).
  - P184, every caller of `Train.freeable`: `git grep -n '\.freeable(' -- tools tests dev` returns 2 sites. `Train.free_holder` in merge_train.py is closed in round 1, with the P184 pair. `PreFlight.worktree_holder` in queue_pre_flight.py is closed in round 2: its fixture answers the probe, and the twin arm pins the ancestor pass (Q2 kills it). This is the round-2 block's class. Its null control is the round-1 body: the same rule there would have returned the queue_pre_flight site undispositioned.

## Red checks

- `governance / instrument-self-tests` was red at e456ff01, job 124070275423: `queue_pre_flight self-test: 43 checks, 1 failed`. This diff caused it. Round 1 added the `--is-ancestor` probe to `Train.freeable`. queue_pre_flight, its second caller, has a fixture that answered every `merge-base` argv rc 0, so the unpushed-holder arm passed instead of parking.
  - Answer: the fixture now answers the probe, and a twin arm was added. At this head the self-test prints `44 checks, 0 failed`.
  - The cheaper detector exists: `python3 tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py --self-test`, which takes seconds locally. Round 1 ran only merge_train's self-test, and the class rule listed no caller of `freeable`. Its standing cost is one more self-test per edit to a shared `Train` method.
  - The P184 line in `## Figures` now enumerates every caller (`git grep -n '\.freeable('`), so a third caller is listed by the rule rather than found by CI. The analysis is `root-cause.md`'s seat, not this one.

## Forward-carry

- Part (3) of the brief, carries 7 (`add --front` / `add --remove` under `QUEUE_LOCK`, P112) and 10 (`stats`, and `--cap auto` only past 0.5 h/day lost, P164), is not built here. Reason: carry 10's `--cap auto` decision needs the train logs, and no train log is in the tree or reachable from this container (`git ls-files | grep -iE 'train[^/]*\.log|queue-add|skipped\.json'` prints nothing). The fixer.md rotation bound also applies. The two carries stay in the group's roster entry on `handoff/audit-r10-roster` as written. Carry: R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE
- `_batch` admission reads a PR head's CI with main's required set (`self.required()`, no `pr_head`). It is the P34 class's sibling seam, latent while `PR_ONLY` is `()`. A future non-empty `PR_ONLY` would admit a head whose PR-only context is red. Control: the M9 arm's world (`PR_ONLY=("pr-contract",)`, pr-contract red) driven through `batch` instead of the serial train. Carry: R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE
- Round-2 survivors. All three new survivors (S1-S3) are pinned here, so none is carried. The round-1 survivors R3, R5, R8 and R9 remain in carry 21 at `handoff/audit-r10-roster` 78c0bb77, as the fix review confirmed. Carry: R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE
- Carry 2's last sentence, "pass --approval-carry in the live launch", is the orchestrator's launch line, not this file. Without the flag every approval-class policy refusal parks naming `--approval-carry or --mandate is not given`. Carry: R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE

## Friction

- fixer.md-step-3: unclear: the carries' instances (train17, train27, s41, s44, #2665 run3) are train logs on the orchestrator's host, so "re-execute the finder's harness" has no harness to run. The self-test fixtures model each instance instead. Carry: dismissed: no finder harness exists for instrument carries; the fixtures are the measurement

## Block

Round 1. Measured at head e456ff01323580d4390f964483a17dbdb6cff5bf (still the live head of fix/r10-train-overlap-grade-p3 at verdict time, ev/head-live.txt).

fix-review.md step 10 / finding-propagation.md "Enforcement": the producing PR does not merge until its carry is in the tree, and the body names the file and the roster branch SHA. The body's second `## Forward-carry` item (`_batch` admission reads a PR head's CI with main's required set, `self.required()` at merge_train.py:3054 feeding `admit` at 3065/3068; the P34 class's sibling seam, latent while `PR_ONLY` is `()`, control: the M9 world driven through `batch`) ends `Carry: R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE`. But it is not written to that group. At `handoff/audit-r10-roster` 22622ddf6aab0651ca50c5e7d4d1d194bdaa886d, group R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE has 20 carries. The only one naming `pr_head` is carry 3 (the original P34 serial-wait finding). No carry names the admission head set (ev/roster-22622ddf.txt). The body gives no roster SHA for it. As finding-propagation.md says, a sibling seam in a running stage goes to a new issue filed by this PR or to a carry file. Neither exists, so this finding lives only in the PR body.

To clear: write the admission seam, with its control as a precondition, into the group's roster entry on handoff/audit-r10-roster (or file the issue or carry file), and name the SHA in the body. No code change is needed for this block. The other two forward-carry items are already in the tree: carries 7 and 10 (part 3), and carry 2's "pass --approval-carry in the live launch".

## Findings

- Surviving mutant R3: in `Train.serial`, the `except Stop:` arm's `if item.pop("sweep_after", False): self.sweep_bots()` replaced by `pass` leaves the self-test at 376 checks, 0 failed. The body claims "serial sweeps after its merge (or when it stops)", and the stop half is unpinned. Owed: a fixture where a critical-path entry stops (e.g. ci red) under --bot-prs and the record PR still merges. Carry: R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE
- Surviving mutant R9: `policy_refusal`'s `... or ms == "BLOCKED"` dropped leaves 0 failed. The body states that "BLOCKED with every required context green" parks and is offered to the approval carry, but every fixture arm uses reviewDecision REVIEW_REQUIRED or a red/pending context, so the BLOCKED+APPROVED+all-green branch (the #2580 train-27 instance itself) has no test. Owed: a pstate(rd="APPROVED") arm with all required contexts green, carried and not carried. Carry: R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE
- Surviving mutant R5: `rd != "CHANGES_REQUESTED"` changed to `True` leaves 0 failed. No arm pins that a CHANGES_REQUESTED refusal parks without an approval carry. Owed: one null arm. Carry: R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE
- Surviving mutant R8: `_critical`'s `except Exception: return False` changed to `return True` leaves 0 failed. Both self-test drivers inject `critical=lambda it: False`, so the live roster reader `_critical` (roster_lib.reader_ref / show_roster / group_for_branch / critical_path_groups, once-per-run cache) is never executed by any test. The "anything unread is nothing critical" claim is unmeasured. Owed: an arm driving `_critical` with a stub roster_lib, both a raising read and a critical/non-critical mapping. Carry: R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE
- No finder harness exists for these carries (the instances are train logs on the orchestrator's host). The body discloses this, and the self-test fixtures are the measurement. I built no harness of my own beyond the mutation driver named under Evidence. Carry: dismissed: instrument carries with no committed finder harness; fixtures are the measurement, as the body's Friction item records
